Dokumen: Accessibility Basics
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/accessibility/accessibility-basics/

# Accessibility Basics

10 examples to get you started with mobile accessibility - 7 basic and 3 intermediate. Every production screen should pass these VoiceOver and TalkBack checks before it ships.

Highlights / Accessibility Basics

* Every interactive control needs a name - visible text, accessibilityLabel, or labelledBy
* Test on a physical device with VoiceOver (iOS) and TalkBack (Android) before store submission
* Pressable and TextInput expose semantics through accessibilityRole and accessibilityState
* Decorative images set accessible={false} - meaningful images need a short label
* Touch targets need 44×44 pt effective size via padding or hitSlop, not tiny icons alone
* eslint-plugin-react-native-a11y catches missing labels in CI - it does not replace device testing

## Prerequisites

Accessibility is built into React Native core components. No extra install is required for labels, roles, and announcements on Expo SDK 57:

```bash
npx create-expo-app@latest MyA11yApp --template blank-typescript
cd MyA11yApp
```

Enable screen readers on a **physical device** - simulators work for smoke tests, but TalkBack timing and VoiceOver rotor behavior differ on real hardware.

| Platform | How to enable | Quick test gesture |
| --- | --- | --- |
| iOS | Settings → Accessibility → VoiceOver | Triple-click side button (if configured) |
| Android | Settings → Accessibility → TalkBack | Volume keys shortcut (device-dependent) |

> **Tooling:** These examples target **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4), **React Native 0.86.0**, and **React 19.2.3**. Semantics props apply to core `View`, `Text`, `Pressable`, `TextInput`, `Image`, and `Switch`.

---

## Basic Examples

### 1. Name Every Interactive Element

Screen readers announce the **accessible name** of a focused element. If a `Pressable` has no visible text and no label, users hear "button" with no context.

```tsx
import { Pressable, Text, StyleSheet } from "react-native";
 
export function SaveButton({ onPress }: { onPress: () => void }) {
  return (
    <Pressable
      accessibilityRole="button"
      accessibilityLabel="Save changes"
      onPress={onPress}
      style={styles.button}
    >
      <Text style={styles.label}>Save</Text>
    </Pressable>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  button: { backgroundColor: "#2563eb", padding: 14, borderRadius: 8 },
  label: { color: "#fff", fontWeight: "600", textAlign: "center" },
});
```

* Visible text inside a `Text` child often becomes the default name - **explicit `accessibilityLabel` is still recommended** for icon-only controls
* Keep labels **stable** across locales - do not embed dynamic counts unless they change meaning ("3 unread messages" is fine; "Button" is not)
* Pair with [accessibilityLabel & accessibilityRole](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/accessibility/accessibilitylabel-and-accessibilityrole/) when building custom components

---

### 2. Icon-Only Buttons Need Labels

Glyphs are meaningless to assistive tech unless you describe them.

```tsx
import { Pressable, Text, StyleSheet } from "react-native";
 
export function IconButton({
  label,
  onPress,
}: {
  label: string;
  onPress: () => void;
}) {
  return (
    <Pressable
      accessibilityRole="button"
      accessibilityLabel={label}
      hitSlop={12}
      onPress={onPress}
      style={styles.hit}
    >
      <Text style={styles.icon} accessibilityElementsHidden>
        ⋮
      </Text>
    </Pressable>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  hit: { minWidth: 44, minHeight: 44, alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "center" },
  icon: { fontSize: 22 },
});
```

* **`accessibilityElementsHidden`** on decorative glyph `Text` prevents double announcements ("more, more options")
* **`hitSlop`** or `minWidth` / `minHeight` of **44** achieves minimum touch target without bloating layout
* Add **`accessibilityHint`** only when the action is non-obvious - "Opens account settings" for a gear icon

---

### 3. accessibilityRole Tells Users What to Expect

Roles map to platform traits - button, link, header, switch, and more.

```tsx
import { Pressable, Text, View, StyleSheet } from "react-native";
 
export function ArticleCard({ title, onOpen }: { title: string; onOpen: () => void }) {
  return (
    <View style={styles.card}>
      <Text accessibilityRole="header" style={styles.title}>
        {title}
      </Text>
      <Pressable accessibilityRole="link" accessibilityLabel={`Read ${title}`} onPress={onOpen}>
        <Text style={styles.link}>Read article</Text>
      </Pressable>
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  card: { padding: 16, gap: 8 },
  title: { fontSize: 20, fontWeight: "700" },
  link: { color: "#2563eb" },
});
```

| Role | User expectation | Common mistake |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `button` | Activates an action | Using on static `Text` |
| `link` | Navigates to related content | Using on destructive delete |
| `header` | Section title, quick navigation | Skipping headings in long screens |
| `image` | Descriptive graphic | Leaving default on decorative icons |
| `switch` | Toggles on/off state | Using on `Pressable` instead of `Switch` |

---

### 4. accessibilityState for Toggles and Selection

Communicate `disabled`, `selected`, `checked`, and `expanded` explicitly - do not rely on color alone.

```tsx
import { Pressable, Text, StyleSheet } from "react-native";
 
type FilterChipProps = {
  label: string;
  selected: boolean;
  onPress: () => void;
};
 
export function FilterChip({ label, selected, onPress }: FilterChipProps) {
  return (
    <Pressable
      accessibilityRole="button"
      accessibilityLabel={label}
      accessibilityState={{ selected }}
      onPress={onPress}
      style={[styles.chip, selected && styles.chipSelected]}
    >
      <Text style={styles.chipText}>{label}</Text>
    </Pressable>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  chip: { paddingHorizontal: 12, paddingVertical: 8, borderRadius: 16, backgroundColor: "#e2e8f0" },
  chipSelected: { backgroundColor: "#2563eb" },
  chipText: { fontWeight: "600" },
});
```

* VoiceOver announces **"selected"** when `accessibilityState={{ selected: true }}`
* For native `Switch`, prefer the component itself - it wires `checked` state automatically
* Destructive actions: add **`accessibilityState={{ disabled: isLoading }}`** while async work runs

---

### 5. Hide Decorative Content from the Tree

Background ornaments, redundant icons, and visual dividers should not steal focus.

```tsx
import { Image, Text, View, StyleSheet } from "react-native";
 
export function PromoBanner() {
  return (
    <View style={styles.banner}>
      <Image
        source={require("./assets/sparkle.png")}
        style={styles.sparkle}
        accessible={false}
        importantForAccessibility="no"
      />
      <Text accessibilityRole="header">Summer sale - 20% off</Text>
      <View
        accessible={false}
        importantForAccessibility="no-hide-descendants"
        style={styles.rule}
      />
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  banner: { padding: 16, gap: 8 },
  sparkle: { width: 24, height: 24, position: "absolute", right: 8, top: 8 },
  rule: { height: 1, backgroundColor: "#cbd5e1" },
});
```

| Prop | Platform | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `accessible={false}` | iOS + Android | Removes element from accessibility focus |
| `importantForAccessibility="no"` | Android | Hides single view |
| `importantForAccessibility="no-hide-descendants"` | Android | Hides view and all children |
| `accessibilityElementsHidden` | iOS | Hides subtree from VoiceOver |

---

### 6. Meaningful Images Get Short Labels

Avatars, charts, and product photos need context; purely decorative assets do not.

```tsx
import { Image, StyleSheet } from "react-native";
 
export function UserAvatar({ uri, name }: { uri: string; name: string }) {
  return (
    <Image
      source={{ uri }}
      style={styles.avatar}
      accessibilityRole="image"
      accessibilityLabel={`${name} profile photo`}
    />
  );
}
 
export function DecorativeDivider() {
  return (
    <Image
      source={require("./assets/wave.png")}
      style={styles.wave}
      accessible={false}
      importantForAccessibility="no"
    />
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  avatar: { width: 48, height: 48, borderRadius: 24 },
  wave: { width: "100%", height: 8 },
});
```

* **One sentence max** for `accessibilityLabel` on images - "Bar chart showing revenue up 12% in Q3"
* Do not repeat information already in adjacent headings
* See [Images & Assets](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/rn-fundamentals/images-and-assets/) for `expo-image` performance patterns

---

### 7. Announce Dynamic Updates

When status changes without moving focus, tell screen reader users explicitly.

```tsx
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { AccessibilityInfo, Pressable, Text, View, StyleSheet } from "react-native";
 
export function CartBadge({ count }: { count: number }) {
  const [lastAnnounced, setLastAnnounced] = useState(count);
 
  useEffect(() => {
    if (count !== lastAnnounced) {
      AccessibilityInfo.announceForAccessibility(
        count === 0 ? "Cart is empty" : `${count} items in cart`,
      );
      setLastAnnounced(count);
    }
  }, [count, lastAnnounced]);
 
  return (
    <View
      accessibilityRole="text"
      accessibilityLabel={`Cart, ${count} items`}
      accessibilityLiveRegion="polite"
      style={styles.badge}
    >
      <Text>{count}</Text>
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  badge: { minWidth: 28, minHeight: 28, borderRadius: 14, backgroundColor: "#dc2626", alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "center" },
});
```

* **`AccessibilityInfo.announceForAccessibility`** pushes a one-shot message to VoiceOver/TalkBack
* **`accessibilityLiveRegion="polite"`** (Android) batches non-urgent text changes
* Use **`assertive`** for errors and time-sensitive alerts - see [Accessibility in Forms](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/forms-input/accessibility-in-forms/)

## Intermediate Examples

### 8. Group Related Content with accessible Containers

A card with title, price, and rating should be one logical unit - or deliberately split for scanning.

```tsx
import { Pressable, Text, View, StyleSheet } from "react-native";
 
export function ProductRow({
  name,
  price,
  rating,
  onPress,
}: {
  name: string;
  price: string;
  rating: string;
  onPress: () => void;
}) {
  return (
    <Pressable
      accessibilityRole="button"
      accessibilityLabel={`${name}, ${price}, rated ${rating} out of five`}
      onPress={onPress}
      style={styles.row}
    >
      <View importantForAccessibility="no-hide-descendants" accessibilityElementsHidden>
        <Text style={styles.name}>{name}</Text>
        <Text style={styles.price}>{price}</Text>
        <Text style={styles.rating}>{rating} ★</Text>
      </View>
    </Pressable>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  row: { padding: 16, borderBottomWidth: StyleSheet.hairlineWidth, borderColor: "#e2e8f0" },
  name: { fontSize: 16, fontWeight: "600" },
  price: { color: "#64748b" },
  rating: { color: "#f59e0b" },
});
```

* **Single focus stop** for tappable list rows - users swipe once per item, not three times
* Alternative pattern: leave children exposed when users should hear each field separately (data tables)
* Test both patterns with TalkBack **reading controls** vs **reading lines**

---

### 9. Detect Screen Reader and Adapt (Sparingly)

Query `AccessibilityInfo` for reader and reduce-motion settings - bake accessibility into default UI, do not ship a separate "accessible mode."

```tsx
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { AccessibilityInfo, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
export function useA11yPreferences() {
  const [screenReaderEnabled, setScreenReaderEnabled] = useState(false);
  const [reduceMotionEnabled, setReduceMotionEnabled] = useState(false);
 
  useEffect(() => {
    AccessibilityInfo.isScreenReaderEnabled().then(setScreenReaderEnabled);
    AccessibilityInfo.isReduceMotionEnabled().then(setReduceMotionEnabled);
 
    const screenReaderSub = AccessibilityInfo.addEventListener(
      "screenReaderChanged",
      setScreenReaderEnabled,
    );
    const motionSub = AccessibilityInfo.addEventListener(
      "reduceMotionChanged",
      setReduceMotionEnabled,
    );
 
    return () => {
      screenReaderSub.remove();
      motionSub.remove();
    };
  }, []);
 
  return { screenReaderEnabled, reduceMotionEnabled };
}
 
export function MotionAwareHint() {
  const { screenReaderEnabled } = useA11yPreferences();
 
  return (
    <View>
      <Text accessibilityRole="header">Orders</Text>
      {screenReaderEnabled ? (
        <Text>Swipe right through the list to hear each order.</Text>
      ) : null}
    </View>
  );
}
```

* Use detection to **skip decorative motion** or **simplify coaching UI** - not to hide features
* See [Reduced Motion](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/accessibility/reduced-motion/) and [Animations reduced motion](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/accessibility/reduced-motion/)

---

### 10. Smoke-Test a Screen with the Accessibility Inspector

Walk every screen with VoiceOver and TalkBack using a repeatable script.

```text
Per-screen checklist (5 minutes):
1. Turn on VoiceOver / TalkBack
2. Swipe through every focusable element - no unlabeled "button"
3. Activate primary action - hear confirmation or focus move
4. Rotate to landscape (tablet) - order still logical
5. Increase font scale to maximum - no clipped primary actions
6. Turn on Reduce Motion - no required animation to complete task
```

```tsx
// Dev-only helper - log the tree in __DEV__
import { AccessibilityInfo, Pressable, Text } from "react-native";
 
export function DevA11yLog({ label }: { label: string }) {
  if (!__DEV__) return null;
 
  return (
    <Pressable
      accessibilityRole="button"
      accessibilityLabel={`Log accessibility tree for ${label}`}
      onPress={() => AccessibilityInfo.isScreenReaderEnabled().then(console.log)}
    >
      <Text>Log a11y state ({label})</Text>
    </Pressable>
  );
}
```

* **Document failures** as P0/P1 in [Accessibility Audit Checklist](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/accessibility/accessibility-audit-checklist/)
* Add **Maestro** or **Detox** flows that query by `accessibilityLabel` - same selectors assistive tech relies on
* Design-system primitives should centralize roles - see [Design Systems Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/design-systems-basics/)

---

## Deep Dive

### How the Accessibility Tree Works

* React Native maps your component tree to **platform accessibility APIs** (UIAccessibility on iOS, AccessibilityNodeInfo on Android).
* Only views marked **`accessible={true}`** (default for `Text` and touchables) or containing accessible children become focus stops.
* **Reading order** follows the native view hierarchy - sibling order and nesting matter more than visual CSS-like layout.
* **`testID`** is for automation only - it does **not** replace labels for screen readers unless your tests mock it incorrectly.

### VoiceOver vs TalkBack Differences

| Behavior | VoiceOver (iOS) | TalkBack (Android) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Explore gesture | Swipe right / left | Swipe right / left |
| Activate | Double-tap | Double-tap |
| Reading modes | Rotor (headings, links) | Reading controls/granularity |
| Hints | `accessibilityHint` spoken after label | Hint less consistently used |
| Live regions | Limited vs web | `accessibilityLiveRegion` supported |

Test **both** platforms - passing iOS alone is not sufficient for Play Store accessibility expectations.

### Minimum Touch Targets

Apple HIG and Material recommend **44×44 pt / 48×48 dp** effective targets:

```tsx
<Pressable hitSlop={10} style={{ minHeight: 44, justifyContent: "center" }} />
```

Small visual icons are fine when the **hit region** is enlarged.

## Gotchas

* **Placeholder is not a label** - `TextInput` needs `accessibilityLabel` or `accessibilityLabelledBy`.
* **Duplicate announcements** - nested `accessible` views with overlapping text cause stutter.
* **Opacity-only disabled state** - still focusable unless `disabled` or `accessibilityState={{ disabled: true }}`.
* **Modal traps** - set `accessibilityViewIsModal` on overlay roots so background content is skipped.
* **Lint-only confidence** - `eslint-plugin-react-native-a11y` misses broken focus order and misleading hints.

## FAQs

Does Expo Go support full accessibility testing?

* Yes for core semantics, screen reader navigation, and font scaling.
* Custom native modules and some Reanimated edge cases need a dev build - test release candidates on device.

Should I use testID or accessibilityLabel for Detox?

* Prefer querying by **role + label** - matches real user and assistive-tech behavior.
* `testID` is fine for elements without a user-facing name, but do not let it replace missing labels.

Are web aria-\* props available?

* React Native 0.76+ maps some `aria-*` props to accessibility equivalents.
* Prefer documented RN props (`accessibilityLabel`, `accessibilityRole`) for cross-platform consistency on SDK 57.

Dokumen: accessibilityLabel & accessibilityRole

# accessibilityLabel & accessibilityRole

Correct semantics for custom components. A cookbook for wiring **names**, **roles**, **states**, and **hints** so VoiceOver and TalkBack understand your design-system primitives - not just raw `Pressable` calls scattered through features.

Highlights / accessibilityLabel & accessibilityRole

* Forward accessibility props from primitives - custom buttons must expose the same contract as Pressable
* Compose labels with accessibilityLabelledBy when visible text is split across elements
* Pick roles that match behavior - link for navigation, button for actions, header for section titles
* accessibilityHint explains how to act, not what the control is - keep hints short
* Hide decorative children so parents announce once - avoid triple-reading list rows
* Centralize semantics in design-system wrappers - features should not reinvent IconButton labels

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```tsx
import type { PressableProps } from "react-native";
import { Pressable, Text, StyleSheet } from "react-native";
 
type AppButtonProps = PressableProps & {
  label: string;
  hint?: string;
  variant?: "primary" | "ghost";
};
 
export function AppButton({
  label,
  hint,
  variant = "primary",
  accessibilityState,
  ...rest
}: AppButtonProps) {
  return (
    <Pressable
      accessibilityRole="button"
      accessibilityLabel={label}
      accessibilityHint={hint}
      accessibilityState={accessibilityState}
      style={[styles.base, variant === "primary" ? styles.primary : styles.ghost]}
      {...rest}
    >
      <Text style={styles.text} importantForAccessibility="no">
        {label}
      </Text>
    </Pressable>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  base: { minHeight: 44, paddingHorizontal: 16, borderRadius: 8, justifyContent: "center" },
  primary: { backgroundColor: "#2563eb" },
  ghost: { backgroundColor: "transparent" },
  text: { color: "#fff", fontWeight: "600", textAlign: "center" },
});
```

**When to reach for this:** Any time you wrap `Pressable`, `View`, or gesture handlers into reusable UI - cards, icon buttons, chips, steppers, and bottom-sheet actions all need an explicit semantic contract.

## Working Example

A compound **Settings row** with leading icon, title, subtitle, and chevron - announced once, activated once.

```tsx
import { Pressable, Text, View, StyleSheet } from "react-native";
 
type SettingsRowProps = {
  title: string;
  subtitle?: string;
  onPress: () => void;
};
 
export function SettingsRow({ title, subtitle, onPress }: SettingsRowProps) {
  const label = subtitle ? `${title}, ${subtitle}` : title;
 
  return (
    <Pressable
      accessibilityRole="button"
      accessibilityLabel={label}
      accessibilityHint="Opens settings"
      onPress={onPress}
      style={styles.row}
    >
      <View
        style={styles.content}
        importantForAccessibility="no-hide-descendants"
        accessibilityElementsHidden
      >
        <Text style={styles.title}>{title}</Text>
        {subtitle ? <Text style={styles.subtitle}>{subtitle}</Text> : null}
        <Text style={styles.chevron} accessible={false}>
          ›
        </Text>
      </View>
    </Pressable>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  row: { paddingVertical: 14, paddingHorizontal: 16, minHeight: 48 },
  content: { flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", gap: 8 },
  title: { flex: 1, fontSize: 16, fontWeight: "600" },
  subtitle: { fontSize: 14, color: "#64748b" },
  chevron: { fontSize: 20, color: "#94a3b8" },
});
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* Parent `Pressable` owns the **single accessible name**
* Visual children hidden from the tree - no "Notifications, Notifications, chevron"
* `accessibilityHint` adds purpose without repeating the title
* `minHeight: 48` satisfies touch target guidance

## Cookbook Patterns

### Pattern 1: Forward Props on Primitives

Design-system components should accept and forward accessibility props without stripping them.

```tsx
import type { PressableProps, ViewProps } from "react-native";
import { Pressable, View } from "react-native";
 
type CardProps = ViewProps & {
  onPress?: PressableProps["onPress"];
  accessibilityLabel: string;
};
 
export function Card({ onPress, accessibilityLabel, children, ...viewProps }: CardProps) {
  if (onPress) {
    return (
      <Pressable
        accessibilityRole="button"
        accessibilityLabel={accessibilityLabel}
        onPress={onPress}
        style={viewProps.style}
      >
        {children}
      </Pressable>
    );
  }
 
  return (
    <View
      accessibilityRole="summary"
      accessibilityLabel={accessibilityLabel}
      {...viewProps}
    >
      {children}
    </View>
  );
}
```

* Use `ComponentProps<typeof Pressable>` in TypeScript - see [Typing Components & Props](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/typescript-rn/typing-components-and-props/)
* Default **`accessibilityLabel` required** on interactive wrappers - make forgetting a label a type error

### Pattern 2: accessibilityLabelledBy for Visible Labels

When label text is visible, reference it by `nativeID` instead of duplicating strings.

```tsx
import { Text, TextInput, View, StyleSheet } from "react-native";
 
export function Field({ label, value, onChangeText }: { label: string; value: string; onChangeText: (t: string) => void }) {
  const labelId = `field-${label.replace(/\s/g, "-").toLowerCase()}`;
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.field}>
      <Text nativeID={labelId} style={styles.label}>
        {label}
      </Text>
      <TextInput
        value={value}
        onChangeText={onChangeText}
        accessibilityLabelledBy={labelId}
        accessibilityLabel={label}
      />
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  field: { gap: 4 },
  label: { fontWeight: "600" },
});
```

* Provide **both** `accessibilityLabelledBy` and `accessibilityLabel` for older OS targets
* `nativeID` must be **unique per screen** - prefix with screen or form id in wizards

### Pattern 3: Role Selection Table

| UI pattern | Role | Label source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Primary CTA | `button` | Visible text or `accessibilityLabel` |
| Text that navigates | `link` | Destination context - "View order details" |
| Section title | `header` | Heading text |
| Toggle row with `Switch` | `switch` on `Switch` | Row title; state on `Switch` |
| Checkbox custom | `checkbox` | Item name + `accessibilityState.checked` |
| Search field | `search` | "Search products" |
| Static paragraph | `text` or none | Usually auto from `Text` |
| Toolbar icon | `button` | **Required** `accessibilityLabel` |

### Pattern 4: accessibilityState Matrix

```tsx
<Pressable
  accessibilityRole="button"
  accessibilityLabel="Add to favorites"
  accessibilityState={{
    disabled: isLoading,
    selected: isFavorite,
    busy: isLoading,
  }}
/>
```

| State key | Announced as | Use when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `disabled` | "dimmed" / unavailable | Async or validation block |
| `selected` | "selected" | Tabs, filters, segmented controls |
| `checked` | "checked" / "unchecked" | Custom toggles |
| `expanded` | "expanded" / "collapsed" | Accordions |
| `busy` | In progress | Submit in flight |

### Pattern 5: Custom Actions (Steppers and Sliders)

```tsx
import { Pressable, Text, View, StyleSheet } from "react-native";
 
export function QuantityStepper({
  value,
  onIncrement,
  onDecrement,
}: {
  value: number;
  onIncrement: () => void;
  onDecrement: () => void;
}) {
  return (
    <View
      accessible
      accessibilityRole="adjustable"
      accessibilityLabel="Quantity"
      accessibilityValue={{ text: String(value) }}
      accessibilityActions={[
        { name: "increment", label: "Increase quantity" },
        { name: "decrement", label: "Decrease quantity" },
      ]}
      onAccessibilityAction={(e) => {
        if (e.nativeEvent.actionName === "increment") onIncrement();
        if (e.nativeEvent.actionName === "decrement") onDecrement();
      }}
      style={styles.row}
    >
      <Pressable accessibilityLabel="Decrease" onPress={onDecrement}>
        <Text>−</Text>
      </Pressable>
      <Text>{value}</Text>
      <Pressable accessibilityLabel="Increase" onPress={onIncrement}>
        <Text>+</Text>
      </Pressable>
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  row: { flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", gap: 12 },
});
```

* **`adjustable`** role suits iOS rotor adjustments - pair with `accessibilityActions` for custom steppers
* Physical buttons remain for sighted users - do not remove visible controls

### Pattern 6: Badges and Live Counts

```tsx
<Pressable
  accessibilityRole="button"
  accessibilityLabel={`Messages, ${unread} unread`}
  accessibilityHint="Opens inbox"
/>
```

* Include **dynamic counts in the label** when they convey status
* Do not call `announceForAccessibility` on every poll - reserve for meaningful transitions

## Deep Dive

### accessible={true} vs false

* Setting a container `accessible` merges children into **one** announcement on iOS.
* Leaving children exposed gives **granular** navigation - pick per UX intent.
* **`importantForAccessibility`** on Android overrides child visibility when parents are hidden.

### accessibilityHint Guidelines

* Hints describe **what happens next** - "Opens payment sheet", not "Button"
* Omit hints when the label is self-explanatory - verbosity slows expert screen reader users
* Localize hints with the same priority as labels

### Lint + Design System Integration

Enforce labels in CI with `eslint-plugin-react-native-a11y` - then ban raw `Pressable` in features:

```text
features/** → must import { AppButton, IconButton } from @/shared/ui
```

See [Custom ESLint Rules for RN](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/custom-eslint-rules-for-rn/) and [Building an Internal Component Library](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/building-an-internal-component-library/).

## Gotchas

* **Gesture-handler buttons** - `GestureDetector` wrappers are not accessible until an inner `Pressable` or `accessible` view exposes semantics.
* **Duplicate roles** - `accessibilityRole="button"` on both parent and child causes nested "button" announcements.
* **Icon fonts** - glyph codepoints are not spoken; always provide a text label.
* **Translated strings in labels** - interpolate values, not sentence order assumptions from English.
* **accessibilityElementsHidden on Android** - pair with `importantForAccessibility` for reliable hiding.

## FAQs

Should custom components set accessibilityLabel by default?

* Yes for interactive primitives - require `label` prop or sensible default from children text.
* Static layout containers usually need no label unless they summarize a complex card.

link or button for navigation?

* Use `link` when the action opens related content or another screen in a browsing context.
* Use `button` for modals, submits, and destructive confirmations - matches user mental model on mobile screen readers.

How do I test semantics without a device?

* React Native Testing Library: `getByRole("button", { name: "Save" })` - see [Mobile Testing Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/mobile-testing-basics/).
* Device testing still required for hints, grouping, and TalkBack granularity.

* [Accessibility in Forms](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/forms-input/accessibility-in-forms/) - `accessibilityLabelledBy` on inputs

Dokumen: Accessibility Best Practices
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/accessibility/best-practices/

# Accessibility Best Practices

A condensed summary of the 25 most important best practices drawn from every page in this section.

Highlights / Accessibility Best Practices

* Every interactive control needs a name - lint catches some gaps, devices catch the rest
* Design-system primitives own labels, roles, and scaling policy for the whole app
* VoiceOver and TalkBack on physical hardware are release gates, not nice-to-haves
* Maximum font scale and Reduce Motion belong in every RC test matrix
* Form errors must be announced and focus must move to the first invalid field
* Respect reduced motion in Reanimated with ReduceMotion.System - not animation-always marketing defaults

1. **Name every interactive control:** Provide `accessibilityLabel`, visible text, or `accessibilityLabelledBy` - icon-only buttons without names fail VoiceOver and store review.
2. **Set the correct `accessibilityRole`:** Use `button` for actions, `link` for navigation, `header` for section titles, and `switch` on native toggles - roles set user expectations.
3. **Expose state with `accessibilityState`:** Communicate `selected`, `disabled`, `checked`, and `expanded` - never rely on color alone for selection or errors.
4. **Hide decorative content:** Set `accessible={false}` and `importantForAccessibility="no-hide-descendants"` on ornaments, redundant chevrons, and background art.
5. **Enforce 44×44 pt targets:** Use `minHeight`, padding, or `hitSlop` on small visuals - touch and switch-control users need generous hit regions.
6. **Centralize semantics in design system:** `AppButton`, `IconButton`, and `Field` wrappers require labels at the type level - features should not reinvent raw `Pressable` patterns.
7. **Forward accessibility props on primitives:** Custom components accept and pass through `accessibilityLabel`, `accessibilityHint`, and `accessibilityState` like underlying `Pressable`.
8. **Placeholder is not a label:** `TextInput` needs a visible label or `accessibilityLabelledBy` - placeholder-only fields fail forms audits.
9. **Announce meaningful dynamic updates:** Use `AccessibilityInfo.announceForAccessibility` or `accessibilityLiveRegion` for cart counts, submit errors, and async completion - not every re-render.
10. **Group list rows into one focus stop:** Tappable cards should merge title, price, and metadata into a single label - reduce swipes for TalkBack and Switch Control.
11. **Test VoiceOver on a physical iPhone:** Simulator smoke is insufficient - rotor behavior, hint timing, and focus quirks appear on device.
12. **Test TalkBack on a physical Android:** `importantForAccessibility` and live regions differ from iOS - ship only after Android device walkthrough.
13. **Query tests by role and name:** React Native Testing Library `getByRole('button', { name: 'Save' })` aligns CI with assistive tech - `testID` alone hides label gaps.
14. **Run eslint-plugin-react-native-a11y in CI:** Catch missing labels before review - treat lint as necessary, not sufficient.
15. **Allow font scaling on body copy:** `allowFontScaling` defaults true - never disable globally; cap dense UI with `maxFontSizeMultiplier` instead.
16. **Use flexible layouts at large text sizes:** Prefer `minHeight`, `flexWrap`, and column reflow over fixed `height` + `numberOfLines={1}` on primary labels.
17. **Read font scale on app resume:** `PixelRatio.getFontScale()` after `AppState` active - users change text size while your app is backgrounded.
18. **Honor Reduce Motion:** Subscribe to `reduceMotionChanged` and pass `ReduceMotion.System` to Reanimated timing and entering animations.
19. **Never block tasks on animation:** Users with reduce motion enabled must reach final UI state instantly - provide non-gesture alternatives for swipe actions.
20. **Trap modal focus:** Set `accessibilityViewIsModal` on sheets and dialogs; restore focus to the trigger on dismiss with `setAccessibilityFocus`.
21. **Move focus on navigation changes:** Master-detail selection, wizard steps, and post-submit success should land screen reader focus on the new primary heading.
22. **Enable hardware keyboard traversal:** `focusable` on actionable `Pressable` controls and `returnKeyType="next"` chains on forms - critical for iPad and DeX.
23. **Run the audit checklist before RC:** Tier 1–2 every release; score P0/P1/P1 - see [Accessibility Audit Checklist](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/accessibility/accessibility-audit-checklist/).
24. **Coordinate with animations policy:** Pair `AccessibilityInfo` checks with Reanimated `ReduceMotion.System` - see [Reduced Motion](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/accessibility/reduced-motion/) and [Animations reduced motion](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/accessibility/reduced-motion/).
25. **Document known gaps for enterprise buyers:** Track checklist scores per release; publish accessibility contact and remediation timeline - procurement asks before users do.

## FAQs

Is accessibility only for screen reader users?

* Large text, reduced motion, keyboard navigation, and high-contrast system themes benefit many users.
* Semantic labels also stabilize Maestro, Detox, and RNTL tests.

What is the minimum bar before App Store / Play submission?

* Labeled controls on critical flows, device VoiceOver + TalkBack pass, max font scale without clipped CTAs, and modals that trap focus.
* Run the pre-release gate in the audit checklist.

Should we build a separate accessible mode?

* No - bake labels, scaling, motion policy, and focus management into default UI.
* Detection hooks adjust coaching or decorative motion only.

Where do design systems fit?

* Tokens and primitives fix whole classes of bugs - see [Design Systems Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/design-systems-basics/) and [Building an Internal Component Library](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/building-an-internal-component-library/).

How do forms differ from general a11y?

* Forms need labelled inputs, announced errors, and focus on first invalid field - [Accessibility in Forms](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/forms-input/accessibility-in-forms/) extends this section.

* [accessibilityLabel & accessibilityRole](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/accessibility/accessibilitylabel-and-accessibilityrole/) - semantics cookbook
* [Focus Order & Keyboard Navigation](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/accessibility/focus-order-and-keyboard-navigation/) - tablets and switch control
* [Dynamic Type & Font Scaling](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/accessibility/dynamic-type-and-font-scaling/) - font scale layouts

Dokumen: Dynamic Type & Font Scaling
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/accessibility/dynamic-type-and-font-scaling/

# Dynamic Type & Font Scaling

Respecting system text size without layout breaks. A cookbook for **`allowFontScaling`**, **`maxFontSizeMultiplier`**, and **layout patterns** that survive iOS Dynamic Type and Android font size settings.

Highlights / Dynamic Type & Font Scaling

* allowFontScaling defaults to true on Text - disabling app-wide breaks accessibility compliance
* maxFontSizeMultiplier caps growth on dense UI without blocking body copy scaling
* Flexible layouts with flexWrap and minHeight survive extreme Dynamic Type settings
* PixelRatio.getFontScale() helps adapt toolbars and chips at runtime
* Design-system Text primitives should own scaling policy per variant
* Test maximum font scale on smallest phone before store submission

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```tsx
import type { TextProps } from "react-native";
import { PixelRatio, StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
type AppTextProps = TextProps & {
  variant?: "body" | "caption" | "toolbar";
};
 
const SCALE_CAPS = {
  body: undefined,
  caption: 1.5,
  toolbar: 1.2,
} as const;
 
export function AppText({ variant = "body", style, ...rest }: AppTextProps) {
  const cap = SCALE_CAPS[variant];
 
  return (
    <Text
      allowFontScaling
      maxFontSizeMultiplier={cap}
      style={[typography[variant], style]}
      {...rest}
    />
  );
}
 
const typography = StyleSheet.create({
  body: { fontSize: 16, lineHeight: 24 },
  caption: { fontSize: 13, lineHeight: 18 },
  toolbar: { fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 18, fontWeight: "600" },
});
 
export function useFontScale() {
  return PixelRatio.getFontScale();
}
 
export function ScalableRow({ title, meta }: { title: string; meta: string }) {
  return (
    <View style={styles.row}>
      <AppText variant="body" style={styles.title}>
        {title}
      </AppText>
      <AppText variant="caption" style={styles.meta}>
        {meta}
      </AppText>
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  row: { flexDirection: "row", flexWrap: "wrap", gap: 8, paddingVertical: 12, alignItems: "center" },
  title: { flexShrink: 1 },
  meta: { color: "#64748b" },
});
```

**When to reach for this:** Any screen with fixed-height toolbars, chips, bottom tabs, or multi-column rows - users with large text settings will clip or overlap your UI unless you plan for scale.

## Working Example

Settings list that reflows from single-line to multi-line when font scale exceeds a threshold.

```tsx
import { useMemo } from "react";
import { PixelRatio, Pressable, StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
const LARGE_SCALE_THRESHOLD = 1.3;
 
export function SettingsScreen() {
  const fontScale = PixelRatio.getFontScale();
  const stacked = useMemo(() => fontScale >= LARGE_SCALE_THRESHOLD, [fontScale]);
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.screen}>
      <View style={[styles.toolbar, stacked && styles.toolbarStacked]}>
        <Text
          style={styles.toolbarTitle}
          maxFontSizeMultiplier={1.2}
          numberOfLines={stacked ? 2 : 1}
        >
          Settings
        </Text>
      </View>
 
      <Pressable style={[styles.row, stacked && styles.rowStacked]}>
        <Text style={styles.rowTitle} allowFontScaling>
          Notifications
        </Text>
        <Text style={styles.rowValue} maxFontSizeMultiplier={1.4}>
          Enabled
        </Text>
      </Pressable>
 
      <Pressable style={[styles.row, stacked && styles.rowStacked]}>
        <Text style={styles.rowTitle} allowFontScaling>
          Language
        </Text>
        <Text style={styles.rowValue} maxFontSizeMultiplier={1.4}>
          English
        </Text>
      </Pressable>
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  screen: { flex: 1, padding: 16, gap: 8 },
  toolbar: { minHeight: 44, justifyContent: "center" },
  toolbarStacked: { minHeight: 56, paddingVertical: 8 },
  toolbarTitle: { fontSize: 20, fontWeight: "700" },
  row: {
    flexDirection: "row",
    alignItems: "center",
    justifyContent: "space-between",
    minHeight: 48,
    paddingVertical: 8,
    gap: 12,
  },
  rowStacked: { flexDirection: "column", alignItems: "flex-start" },
  rowTitle: { fontSize: 16, fontWeight: "600", flexShrink: 1 },
  rowValue: { fontSize: 14, color: "#64748b" },
});
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* **`PixelRatio.getFontScale()`** drives layout mode switches at extreme scales
* **`maxFontSizeMultiplier`** on toolbar vs uncapped body text
* **`flexWrap` / column reflow** instead of `numberOfLines={1}` truncation on primary labels
* **`minHeight`** on rows preserves touch targets when text wraps

## Cookbook Patterns

### Pattern 1: Scaling Policy Table

| UI region | `allowFontScaling` | `maxFontSizeMultiplier` | Layout note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Body paragraphs | `true` | none (uncapped) | Let text wrap; avoid fixed heights |
| Buttons (primary) | `true` | `1.3`–`1.5` | `minHeight: 44`, vertical padding |
| Tab bar labels | `true` | `1.1`–`1.2` | Short labels; allow two lines if needed |
| Chips / badges | `true` | `1.1` | `flexWrap` on chip rows |
| Data table headers | `true` | `1.2` | Switch to card layout at high scale |
| Decorative icons | N/A | N/A | Icon size fixed; label carries meaning |

### Pattern 2: AppText in the Design System

Centralize typography tokens - see [Typography Scale & Font Loading](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/typography-scale-and-font-loading/) and [Design Systems Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/design-systems-basics/).

```tsx
// shared/ui/AppText.tsx - single scaling policy
export const typography = StyleSheet.create({
  display: { fontSize: 34, lineHeight: 40 },
  title: { fontSize: 22, lineHeight: 28 },
  body: { fontSize: 16, lineHeight: 24 },
  caption: { fontSize: 13, lineHeight: 18 },
});
```

* Ban raw `Text` in `features/**` via ESLint - force `AppText` variants
* Document which variants are **uncapped** in Storybook

### Pattern 3: Avoid Clipping with Flexible Layout

```tsx
// Fragile - fixed height clips large text
<View style={{ height: 40 }}>
  <Text numberOfLines={1}>Account settings and privacy controls</Text>
</View>
 
// Resilient - grows with content
<View style={{ minHeight: 44, paddingVertical: 8 }}>
  <Text style={{ flexShrink: 1 }}>Account settings and privacy controls</Text>
</View>
```

| Anti-pattern | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| `height: 32` on labels | `minHeight` + padding |
| `numberOfLines={1}` on titles | Wrap or stack layout |
| Horizontal row without `flexShrink` | `flexShrink: 1` on text side |
| Absolute-positioned badges over text | Move badge below title at high scale |

### Pattern 4: adjustsFontSizeToFit (iOS, Use Sparingly)

```tsx
<Text
  adjustsFontSizeToFit
  numberOfLines={1}
  minimumFontScale={0.85}
  maxFontSizeMultiplier={1.2}
  style={styles.tabLabel}
>
  Dashboard
</Text>
```

* Shrinks text to fit box - acceptable for **single-word tab labels**, not body copy
* Android ignores `adjustsFontSizeToFit` - do not rely on it cross-platform

### Pattern 5: Listen for Font Scale Changes

Font scale can change while the app is backgrounded (user adjusts system settings).

```tsx
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { PixelRatio, AppState } from "react-native";
 
export function useFontScale() {
  const [scale, setScale] = useState(PixelRatio.getFontScale());
 
  useEffect(() => {
    const sub = AppState.addEventListener("change", (state) => {
      if (state === "active") {
        setScale(PixelRatio.getFontScale());
      }
    });
    return () => sub.remove();
  }, []);
 
  return scale;
}
```

* Recompute layout flags when app returns active
* Pair with responsive breakpoints on tablets - [Split View & Tablet Layouts](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router-advanced/split-view-and-tablet-layouts/)

### Pattern 6: Do Not Disable Scaling Globally

```tsx
// Anti-pattern - rejects accessibility settings
<Text allowFontScaling={false}>Terms and conditions</Text>
 
// Prefer selective cap on dense chrome only
<Text maxFontSizeMultiplier={1.15} style={styles.badge}>
  PRO
</Text>
```

Disabling scaling app-wide is a **store-review and procurement risk** - cap selectively instead.

## Deep Dive

### iOS Dynamic Type vs Android Font Size

| Setting path | Effect in RN |
| --- | --- |
| iOS Display & Text Size → Larger Text | Scales `Text` when `allowFontScaling` is true |
| Android Display → Font size | Same via `PixelRatio.getFontScale()` |
| Per-app text size (iOS 15+) | Still flows through font scale APIs |

`lineHeight` should scale with `fontSize` - use token pairs (`16/24`, `22/28`), not arbitrary single values.

### Testing Procedure

```text
1. iOS: Settings → Accessibility → Display & Text Size → Larger Text → maximum
2. Android: Settings → Display → Font size → largest
3. Walk onboarding, form, tab bar, and checkout
4. Verify: no clipped CTAs, no overlapping tab icons, no truncated legal text
5. Screenshot failures for design review - not just engineering tickets
```

### Relationship to Screen Readers

Large text and screen readers often overlap - users may enable both. Layouts that survive font scaling usually help **zoom and reader** users too. Announce layout changes sparingly; reflow alone does not need `announceForAccessibility`.

## Gotchas

* **`allowFontScaling={false}` on `TextInput`** - users cannot enlarge field text; avoid unless duplicating preview text nearby.
* **Mixed font sizes in a row** - misaligned baselines when only one side scales; normalize variants.
* **Icons sized in dp only** - text grows, icons do not; leave gap between icon and label.
* **Bottom tabs with fixed tab bar height** - Expo Router native tabs may clip; test on device.
* **WebView content** - RN font scale does not propagate; native chrome still must scale.

## FAQs

What is a safe default for maxFontSizeMultiplier?

* Body: uncapped.
* Navigation chrome: `1.1`–`1.2`.
* Buttons and list titles: `1.3`–`1.5`.
* Tune per design system - document in Storybook knobs.

Should images and icons scale with text?

* Icons generally stay fixed size; increase tap padding.
* Illustrations with embedded text should use SVG/text overlays that scale - or provide accessible labels.

Does PixelRatio.getFontScale() update live?

* Not continuously - re-read on `AppState` active or dimension changes.
* Do not poll in a `setInterval` - event-driven refresh is enough.

* [Styling Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/best-practices/) - scaling caps on dense UI
* [Design Systems Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/design-systems-basics/) - `AppText` primitive ownership

Dokumen: Focus Order & Keyboard Navigation
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/accessibility/focus-order-and-keyboard-navigation/

# Focus Order & Keyboard Navigation

Hardware keyboard and switch control on tablets. A cookbook for **focus order**, **external keyboards**, and **switch navigation** on iPad, Android tablets, and foldables - where touch-first layouts break for non-touch users.

Highlights / Focus Order & Keyboard Navigation

* Focus order follows the native view hierarchy - DOM-like reordering does not exist
* focusable on Pressable enables hardware keyboard activation on Android and iPad
* Split views must move focus into the detail pane when selection changes
* Switch Control and TalkBack rely on logical grouping - one focus stop per tappable row
* Modals need accessibilityViewIsModal so background content leaves the focus loop
* Test iPad Magic Keyboard and Android Bluetooth keyboard before shipping tablet layouts

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```tsx
import { useRef } from "react";
import { FlatList, Pressable, Text, TextInput, View, StyleSheet } from "react-native";
 
export function KeyboardFriendlyForm() {
  const emailRef = useRef<TextInput>(null);
  const passwordRef = useRef<TextInput>(null);
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.form}>
      <Text nativeID="emailLabel" style={styles.label}>
        Email
      </Text>
      <TextInput
        ref={emailRef}
        accessibilityLabel="Email"
        accessibilityLabelledBy="emailLabel"
        returnKeyType="next"
        blurOnSubmit={false}
        onSubmitEditing={() => passwordRef.current?.focus()}
        style={styles.input}
      />
 
      <Text nativeID="passwordLabel" style={styles.label}>
        Password
      </Text>
      <TextInput
        ref={passwordRef}
        accessibilityLabel="Password"
        accessibilityLabelledBy="passwordLabel"
        secureTextEntry
        returnKeyType="done"
        style={styles.input}
      />
 
      <Pressable
        accessibilityRole="button"
        accessibilityLabel="Sign in"
        focusable
        style={styles.button}
      >
        <Text style={styles.buttonText}>Sign in</Text>
      </Pressable>
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  form: { padding: 16, gap: 8 },
  label: { fontWeight: "600" },
  input: { borderWidth: 1, borderColor: "#cbd5e1", borderRadius: 8, padding: 12 },
  button: { minHeight: 44, backgroundColor: "#2563eb", borderRadius: 8, justifyContent: "center", alignItems: "center" },
  buttonText: { color: "#fff", fontWeight: "600" },
});
```

**When to reach for this:** Tablet layouts, hardware keyboard accessories, Switch Control users, and any screen where assistive tech must traverse controls in a **predictable sequence** - especially master-detail and modal flows.

## Working Example

Master-detail on a tablet: selecting a list item moves screen reader focus and keyboard focus into the detail header.

```tsx
import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react";
import {
  AccessibilityInfo,
  FlatList,
  Pressable,
  Text,
  View,
  StyleSheet,
  findNodeHandle,
} from "react-native";
 
type Item = { id: string; title: string; body: string };
 
const DATA: Item[] = [
  { id: "1", title: "Invoice #1042", body: "Due April 12" },
  { id: "2", title: "Invoice #1043", body: "Paid" },
];
 
export function MasterDetail({ width }: { width: number }) {
  const isSplit = width >= 768;
  const [selectedId, setSelectedId] = useState(DATA[0].id);
  const detailTitleRef = useRef<Text>(null);
  const selected = DATA.find((d) => d.id === selectedId)!;
 
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!isSplit) return;
    const node = findNodeHandle(detailTitleRef.current);
    if (node) {
      AccessibilityInfo.setAccessibilityFocus(node);
    }
  }, [selectedId, isSplit]);
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.split}>
      <FlatList
        style={styles.list}
        data={DATA}
        keyExtractor={(item) => item.id}
        renderItem={({ item }) => (
          <Pressable
            accessibilityRole="button"
            accessibilityLabel={item.title}
            accessibilityState={{ selected: item.id === selectedId }}
            focusable
            onPress={() => setSelectedId(item.id)}
            style={[styles.row, item.id === selectedId && styles.rowSelected]}
          >
            <Text>{item.title}</Text>
          </Pressable>
        )}
      />
      {isSplit ? (
        <View style={styles.detail} accessibilityLabel="Invoice details">
          <Text
            ref={detailTitleRef}
            accessibilityRole="header"
            style={styles.detailTitle}
          >
            {selected.title}
          </Text>
          <Text>{selected.body}</Text>
        </View>
      ) : null}
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  split: { flex: 1, flexDirection: "row" },
  list: { flex: 1, maxWidth: 320 },
  row: { padding: 16, minHeight: 48 },
  rowSelected: { backgroundColor: "#e0f2fe" },
  detail: { flex: 2, padding: 24, gap: 8 },
  detailTitle: { fontSize: 22, fontWeight: "700" },
});
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* **`focusable`** on list rows for hardware keyboard traversal
* **`accessibilityState.selected`** exposes list selection to TalkBack
* **`AccessibilityInfo.setAccessibilityFocus`** moves VoiceOver to the detail header on selection change
* Split layout only on wide screens - phone stack navigation unchanged

## Cookbook Patterns

### Pattern 1: Reading Order Matches Visual Order

React Native does not support CSS `order`-style focus reordering. Structure JSX so the native tree matches the intended sequence.

```tsx
// Preferred - title before actions in JSX
<View>
  <Text accessibilityRole="header">Account</Text>
  <Pressable accessibilityRole="button" accessibilityLabel="Edit profile" />
  <Pressable accessibilityRole="button" accessibilityLabel="Sign out" />
</View>
 
// Avoid - actions visually positioned above title with absolute layout
// Screen readers still read in JSX order unless you hide/restructure
```

| Technique | When to use |
| --- | --- |
| Reorder JSX | Default - cheapest and most reliable |
| `importantForAccessibility="no-hide-descendants"` | Skip decorative columns |
| `setAccessibilityFocus` | After navigation or selection changes |
| Merge with `accessible` on parent | Single stop for complex tappable rows |

### Pattern 2: Hardware Keyboard on Tablets

| Key / action | Expected behavior | RN support |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Move between focusable controls | Android + iPad external keyboard (platform-dependent) |
| Enter / Space | Activate focused button | `Pressable` with `focusable` |
| Arrow keys in lists | Often maps to scroll, not item focus | Supplement with explicit list semantics |
| Escape | Close modal | Wire `BackHandler` + focus restore |

```tsx
<Pressable
  focusable
  accessibilityRole="button"
  accessibilityLabel="Close"
  onPress={onClose}
/>
```

* **`TextInput`** is focusable by default - chain fields with `returnKeyType="next"` and refs
* Test **iPad Magic Keyboard** and **Samsung DeX** if your app targets productivity tablets

### Pattern 3: Switch Control and Sequential Navigation

Switch Control (iOS) and Switch Access (Android) scan focusable elements. Reduce stops:

```tsx
<Pressable
  accessibilityRole="button"
  accessibilityLabel={`${productName}, ${price}, add to cart`}
  onPress={addToCart}
  style={styles.row}
>
  <View importantForAccessibility="no-hide-descendants" accessibilityElementsHidden>
    {/* visual layout */}
  </View>
</Pressable>
```

* Fewer focus stops = faster scanning for switch users
* Provide **`accessibilityActions`** on adjustable controls - see [accessibilityLabel & accessibilityRole](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/accessibility/accessibilitylabel-and-accessibilityrole/)
* Avoid **auto-advancing carousels** without pause - switch users cannot intercept fast timers

### Pattern 4: Modal Focus Trap

```tsx
import { Modal, Pressable, Text, View, StyleSheet } from "react-native";
 
export function ConfirmModal({ visible, onConfirm, onCancel }: {
  visible: boolean;
  onConfirm: () => void;
  onCancel: () => void;
}) {
  return (
    <Modal visible={visible} animationType="fade" transparent>
      <View style={styles.backdrop}>
        <View
          style={styles.sheet}
          accessibilityViewIsModal
          accessibilityLabel="Confirm delete"
        >
          <Text accessibilityRole="header">Delete item?</Text>
          <Pressable
            focusable
            accessibilityRole="button"
            accessibilityLabel="Confirm delete"
            onPress={onConfirm}
          >
            <Text>Delete</Text>
          </Pressable>
          <Pressable
            focusable
            accessibilityRole="button"
            accessibilityLabel="Cancel"
            onPress={onCancel}
          >
            <Text>Cancel</Text>
          </Pressable>
        </View>
      </View>
    </Modal>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  backdrop: { flex: 1, backgroundColor: "rgba(0,0,0,0.5)", justifyContent: "center", padding: 24 },
  sheet: { backgroundColor: "#fff", borderRadius: 12, padding: 20, gap: 12 },
});
```

* **`accessibilityViewIsModal`** prevents VoiceOver from reaching content under the sheet
* On dismiss, **`setAccessibilityFocus`** back to the triggering control
* First focusable in modal should be the **title or primary action** - document in QA scripts

### Pattern 5: Android nextFocusForward (Optional)

For deterministic hardware focus jumps on Android TV or custom keyboards:

```tsx
<Pressable
  nativeID="filterButton"
  focusable
  nextFocusDown="resultsList"
/>
```

* IDs must match `nativeID` on the target view
* Use sparingly - prefer natural tree order when possible

### Pattern 6: Tablet Split View with Expo Router

Cross-link layout patterns:

```tsx
// Wide: list + detail side by side - focus moves to detail on select
// Narrow: stack push to detail route - focus lands on detail header on mount
```

See [Split View & Tablet Layouts](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router-advanced/split-view-and-tablet-layouts/) for routing structure; this page covers **focus behavior** after layout splits.

## Deep Dive

### How Focus Differs from Web

* No `tabIndex` - use `focusable` and native hierarchy.
* **Radix-style roving tabindex** does not exist - simulate with stateful selection and `setAccessibilityFocus`.
* ScrollViews do not automatically move focus to off-screen children - announce route changes instead.

### Testing Matrix

| Setup | What to verify |
| --- | --- |
| VoiceOver + iPad keyboard | Tab through form; Enter activates buttons |
| TalkBack + Bluetooth keyboard | Focus order on master-detail |
| Switch Control (iOS) | Scan hits each actionable row once |
| TalkBack reading controls | Headings navigable via rotor-equivalent |

### Focus Restoration Checklist

1. User opens modal → focus inside modal title
2. User closes modal → focus returns to trigger
3. User deletes list item → focus moves to next row or empty state
4. User submits form with errors → focus on first invalid field - [Accessibility in Forms](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/forms-input/accessibility-in-forms/)

## Gotchas

* **FlatList reorder** - dynamic data changes can move nodes; re-test focus after sort/filter.
* **Gesture-handler overlays** - can intercept keys if not paired with accessible `Pressable`.
* **Hidden off-screen tabs** - mount all tabs and hide with `display: 'none'` traps focus; unmount inactive routes or hide descendants.
* **AutoFocus on every screen** - disorients screen reader users; focus first field only on empty forms.
* **WebView embeds** - separate focus loop; provide native escape hatch.

## FAQs

Does React Native support full keyboard navigation like the web?

* Partial - `TextInput` and `focusable` pressables are the core building blocks.
* Complex widgets (grids, trees) need explicit `accessibilityActions` and focus management.

How do I move TalkBack focus programmatically?

* `AccessibilityInfo.setAccessibilityFocus(reactTag)` with `findNodeHandle(ref.current)`.
* Prefer refs on `Text` or `View` with a clear `accessibilityRole="header"`.

Should list items be focusable on phone?

* Yes when the row is the actionable unit - switch and keyboard users benefit even without tablets.
* Ensure each row has a concise combined label.

## Related

* [Accessibility Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/accessibility/accessibility-basics/) - VoiceOver/TalkBack fundamentals
* [accessibilityLabel & accessibilityRole](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/accessibility/accessibilitylabel-and-accessibilityrole/) - roles and grouping for rows
* [Split View & Tablet Layouts](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router-advanced/split-view-and-tablet-layouts/) - master-detail routing
* [Accessibility in Forms](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/forms-input/accessibility-in-forms/) - submit focus and error focus
* [Modal & Presentation Routes](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router-advanced/modal-and-presentation-routes/) - sheet presentation patterns

# Accessibility Highlights Summary

Every highlight bullet from the 7 pages in this section, gathered on one page and grouped by the page it came from.

Highlights / Accessibility Highlights Summary

* Every interactive control needs a name - visible text, accessibilityLabel, or labelledBy
* Forward accessibility props from primitives - custom buttons must expose the same contract as Pressable
* Focus order follows the native view hierarchy - DOM-like reordering does not exist
* allowFontScaling defaults to true on Text - disabling app-wide breaks accessibility compliance
* AccessibilityInfo.isReduceMotionEnabled reflects iOS Reduce Motion and Android Remove animations
* Run Tier 1–2 on every release candidate; Tier 3–5 before major launches and compliance reviews

## [Accessibility Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/accessibility/accessibility-basics/)

* Every interactive control needs a name - visible text, accessibilityLabel, or labelledBy
* Test on a physical device with VoiceOver (iOS) and TalkBack (Android) before store submission
* Pressable and TextInput expose semantics through accessibilityRole and accessibilityState
* Decorative images set accessible={false} - meaningful images need a short label
* Touch targets need 44×44 pt effective size via padding or hitSlop, not tiny icons alone
* eslint-plugin-react-native-a11y catches missing labels in CI - it does not replace device testing

## [accessibilityLabel & accessibilityRole](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/accessibility/accessibilitylabel-and-accessibilityrole/)

* Forward accessibility props from primitives - custom buttons must expose the same contract as Pressable
* Compose labels with accessibilityLabelledBy when visible text is split across elements
* Pick roles that match behavior - link for navigation, button for actions, header for section titles
* accessibilityHint explains how to act, not what the control is - keep hints short
* Hide decorative children so parents announce once - avoid triple-reading list rows
* Centralize semantics in design-system wrappers - features should not reinvent IconButton labels

## [Focus Order & Keyboard Navigation](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/accessibility/focus-order-and-keyboard-navigation/)

* Focus order follows the native view hierarchy - DOM-like reordering does not exist
* focusable on Pressable enables hardware keyboard activation on Android and iPad
* Split views must move focus into the detail pane when selection changes
* Switch Control and TalkBack rely on logical grouping - one focus stop per tappable row
* Modals need accessibilityViewIsModal so background content leaves the focus loop
* Test iPad Magic Keyboard and Android Bluetooth keyboard before shipping tablet layouts

## [Dynamic Type & Font Scaling](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/accessibility/dynamic-type-and-font-scaling/)

* allowFontScaling defaults to true on Text - disabling app-wide breaks accessibility compliance
* maxFontSizeMultiplier caps growth on dense UI without blocking body copy scaling
* Flexible layouts with flexWrap and minHeight survive extreme Dynamic Type settings
* PixelRatio.getFontScale() helps adapt toolbars and chips at runtime
* Design-system Text primitives should own scaling policy per variant
* Test maximum font scale on smallest phone before store submission

## [Reduced Motion](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/accessibility/reduced-motion/)

* AccessibilityInfo.isReduceMotionEnabled reflects iOS Reduce Motion and Android Remove animations
* Reanimated 4 ReduceMotion.System delegates to platform settings on withTiming and entering animations
* Never require animation to complete a task - instant state transitions must remain available
* Subscribe to reduceMotionChanged - users toggle the setting without restarting the app
* Pair JS-thread checks with Reanimated reduceMotion for layout and gesture motion
* Cross-check gesture-heavy flows with the animations section reduced-motion page

## [Accessibility Audit Checklist](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/accessibility/accessibility-audit-checklist/)

* Run Tier 1–2 on every release candidate; Tier 3–5 before major launches and compliance reviews
* Score failures P0 (blocks ship), P1 (next sprint), P2 (backlog) with an owner
* Device testing with VoiceOver and TalkBack is mandatory - lint cannot gate alone
* Test maximum font scale and Reduce Motion on the smallest supported phone
* Walk checkout, auth, and delete flows - highest audit and legal exposure
* Pair with design-system review so primitives fix whole app classes of bugs

## [Accessibility Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/accessibility/best-practices/)

* Every interactive control needs a name - lint catches some gaps, devices catch the rest
* Design-system primitives own labels, roles, and scaling policy for the whole app
* VoiceOver and TalkBack on physical hardware are release gates, not nice-to-haves
* Maximum font scale and Reduce Motion belong in every RC test matrix
* Form errors must be announced and focus must move to the first invalid field
* Respect reduced motion in Reanimated with ReduceMotion.System - not animation-always marketing defaults

Dokumen: Android Basics for RN Devs
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/android-platform/android-basics-for-rn-devs/

# Android Basics for RN Devs

Android Studio, `adb`, and Gradle - the minimum native Android literacy every React Native developer needs without becoming a full-time Android engineer. On Expo SDK 57 you spend most days in JavaScript; this page is the map for when builds break, permissions misbehave, or Play Console asks questions Gradle can answer.

Highlights / Android Basics for RN Devs

* You rarely edit Gradle by hand in Expo CNG - config plugins and prebuild own the native project
* adb is the RN dev's terminal: devices, logcat, port reverse, and APK install
* settings.gradle registers modules; app/build.gradle is where app-level deps and signing live
* Run npx expo run:android instead of opening Android Studio for day-to-day JS work
* JAVA\_HOME and ANDROID\_HOME must point at JDK 17 and the Android SDK - wrong paths cause cryptic Gradle failures

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
# Verify toolchain before any native build
java -version          # expect 17.x (Temurin or Android Studio bundled JDK)
echo $ANDROID_HOME     # ~/Library/Android/sdk on macOS default install
 
# List devices and start Metro-backed debug build
adb devices
npx expo run:android
 
# Tail React Native + app logs (filter noise)
adb logcat '*:S' ReactNative:V ReactNativeJS:V AndroidRuntime:E
 
# Reverse Metro port when USB debugging (Wi-Fi dev client uses LAN IP instead)
adb reverse tcp:8081 tcp:8081
 
# Regenerate android/ from app.config (CNG workflow)
npx expo prebuild --platform android
```

```text
android/                          # generated by prebuild - treat as build output in CNG
├── settings.gradle               # includes app module + autolinked native libs
├── build.gradle                  # root project plugins (AGP, Kotlin)
├── gradle.properties             # JVM args, New Arch flags, caching toggles
└── app/
    ├── build.gradle              # applicationId, SDK versions, dependencies, signing
    └── src/main/
        ├── AndroidManifest.xml   # permissions, intent filters (from app.config)
        └── java/.../MainActivity.kt
```

**When to reach for this:**

* First `npx expo run:android` fails with JDK or SDK path errors.
* You need logcat to debug a native crash that never reaches the JS redbox.
* A teammate asks why `android/` exists and whether to commit it.
* You are tracing where a manifest permission or Gradle dependency came from.

## Working Example

**Step 1 - Confirm environment**

```bash
# macOS - typical Android Studio install paths
export ANDROID_HOME="$HOME/Library/Android/sdk"
export PATH="$PATH:$ANDROID_HOME/platform-tools:$ANDROID_HOME/emulator"
 
# Expo SDK 57 / RN 0.86 expects JDK 17
/usr/libexec/java_home -V
export JAVA_HOME=$(/usr/libexec/java_home -v 17)
 
npx expo-doctor
```

**Step 2 - Run on emulator or USB device**

```bash
# Start a recent API image (API 34–35) - not API 28 museum pieces
emulator -list-avds
emulator -avd Pixel_8_API_35 &
 
adb wait-for-device
npx expo run:android
```

**Step 3 - Debug a white screen**

```bash
# Terminal 1 - Metro already started by run:android; or:
npx expo start --dev-client
 
# Terminal 2 - native + JS logs
adb logcat '*:S' ReactNativeJS:V ReactNative:V SoLoader:E AndroidRuntime:E
```

**Step 4 - Install a CI/EAS APK locally**

```bash
adb install -r ./build.apk
adb shell am start -n com.example.shopapp/.MainActivity
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* **`adb devices`** - one authorized device/emulator before Gradle deploys.
* **`adb reverse`** - USB device reaches Metro on `localhost:8081`.
* **`logcat` filters** - surface JS `console.log` and native stack traces.
* **`android/` layout** - know which file to inspect vs which to regenerate with prebuild.

## Deep Dive

### How It Works

* **Expo CNG (Continuous Native Generation)** generates `android/` from `app.config.ts` + config plugins. You edit config, not hand-merge `build.gradle` on every upgrade.
* **`npx expo run:android`** invokes Gradle (`:app:installDebug`), installs the debug APK, and launches the dev client or debug build.
* **Autolinking** (via `expo-modules-autolinking`) injects native modules into `settings.gradle` - you do not manually `include` each library.
* **Android Studio** is for inspecting layouts, profiling, and editing Kotlin when you ship custom native code - not for daily JS iteration.
* **`adb`** bridges host machine and device: shell, file push/pull, intents, port forwarding.

### Gradle Mental Model

| File | Role | RN dev touch frequency |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `settings.gradle` | Declares included modules (`:app`, autolinked libs) | Rare - prebuild/plugin |
| Root `build.gradle` | AGP version, shared repos | Rare |
| `app/build.gradle` | `applicationId`, `minSdk`, `targetSdk`, deps, signing | Occasional via plugin |
| `gradle.properties` | JVM heap, `newArchEnabled`, caching | Tuning builds |
| `AndroidManifest.xml` | Permissions, activities, intent filters | Via `app.config` / plugins |

```gradle
// app/build.gradle (simplified mental model - actual file is prebuild-generated)
android {
    namespace "com.example.shopapp"
    defaultConfig {
        applicationId "com.example.shopapp"
        minSdkVersion rootProject.ext.minSdkVersion
        targetSdkVersion rootProject.ext.targetSdkVersion
    }
}
dependencies {
    implementation("com.facebook.react:react-android")
    // autolinked Expo modules appear here after prebuild
}
```

### Android Studio Essentials

| Task | Where in Android Studio |
| --- | --- |
| Open generated project | **File → Open** → `android/` folder |
| Sync Gradle | Elephant icon / **File → Sync Project with Gradle Files** |
| View merged manifest | **app → manifests → AndroidManifest.xml (Merged)** |
| Device Manager | **Tools → Device Manager** - create API 35 AVD |
| Logcat UI | **View → Tool Windows → Logcat** - same data as CLI |

You do **not** need Android Studio running for `npx expo run:android` - only the SDK + platform-tools on `PATH`.

### adb Commands RN Devs Use Weekly

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `adb devices` | List connected emulators/phones |
| `adb logcat` | Stream system and app logs |
| `adb reverse tcp:8081 tcp:8081` | USB → Metro |
| `adb install -r app.apk` | Sideload release/internal build |
| `adb shell pm clear com.pkg` | Reset app data (fresh permission prompts) |
| `adb shell am force-stop com.pkg` | Kill app process |
| `adb shell dumpsys package com.pkg` | Inspect granted permissions |

### CNG vs Committed `android/`

| Workflow | Commit `android/`? | Upgrade path |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Managed + EAS Build (no prebuild locally) | No | `eas build` runs prebuild in cloud |
| Local `expo run:android` | Optional - often gitignored | `npx expo prebuild --clean` on SDK bump |
| Bare / heavy native customization | Yes | Manual merge + plugins |

SDK 57 teams usually **gitignore** `android/` and regenerate - see [Prebuild Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/prebuild-basics/).

## Gotchas

* **Wrong JDK version** - AGP 8.x requires JDK 17; JDK 8 or 21 mismatches produce opaque "Could not resolve" errors. **Fix:** `export JAVA_HOME` to 17 before Gradle.
* **ANDROID\_HOME unset** - `sdkmanager` and Gradle cannot find build-tools. **Fix:** Point at Android Studio SDK path; add `platform-tools` to `PATH`.
* **Editing `android/` without a plugin** - Next `prebuild --clean` wipes manual edits. **Fix:** Move changes to a config plugin or `expo-build-properties`.
* **Ancient emulator API level** - API 24 emulators hide edge-to-edge, photo picker, and permission changes in RN 0.86. **Fix:** Test on API 34–35 images.
* **`adb device unauthorized`** - RSA fingerprint not accepted on phone. **Fix:** Revoke USB debugging authorizations on device; replug and accept prompt.
* **Assuming Android Studio Run ▶ replaces Expo** - Studio builds its own variant; Metro may not attach. **Fix:** Use `npx expo run:android` for dev-client workflow.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| EAS Build only (no local `android/`) | Team has no Android laptops | You need daily native debugging |
| Android Studio Logcat UI | Visual filtering, multi-process | Headless CI - use CLI `adb logcat` |
| `expo start` + Expo Go | Quick JS-only spikes on SDK 54 | SDK 57 dev clients with custom native modules |
| Physical device over Wi-Fi | USB port contention | Corporate networks block mDNS |

## FAQs

Do I need Android Studio installed?

* You need the **Android SDK** and **platform-tools** (`adb`). Android Studio is the easiest installer on macOS/Windows.
* Daily JS work uses VS Code/Cursor + terminal - Studio is for native inspection and profiling.

Why does my project have no android/ folder?

* Managed Expo workflow generates native projects at build time (`eas build` or `npx expo prebuild`).
* Run `npx expo prebuild --platform android` when you need local Gradle builds.

What is applicationId vs package name?

* `applicationId` in Gradle is the Play Store identity (`com.example.shopapp`).
* Kotlin package paths under `java/com/example/...` can differ in advanced setups - keep them aligned in Expo config (`android.package`).

How do I find my app's package name?

* `app.config.ts` → `expo.android.package`.
* Or `adb shell pm list packages | grep shop`.

Where do manifest permissions come from?

* Expo modules and `app.config` plugins merge permissions into `AndroidManifest.xml` at prebuild.
* Inspect merged manifest in Android Studio to see the final list.

Can I use Windows for Android development?

* Yes - Android is first-class on Windows. Set `ANDROID_HOME`, use JDK 17, enable Hyper-V/WSL2 for emulators.
* iOS builds still require macOS; Android-only devs are common on Windows/Linux.

What Gradle task does expo run:android execute?

* Typically `:app:installDebug` on the debug variant, then launches the main activity.
* Pass `--variant release` only when intentionally testing release builds locally.

How do I clear Gradle corruption?

* `cd android && ./gradlew clean` then rebuild.
* Nuclear: delete `android/`, run `npx expo prebuild --clean --platform android`.

Does New Architecture change the Gradle layout?

* `newArchEnabled=true` in `gradle.properties` toggles Fabric/TurboModules - default on RN 0.86.
* Folder layout is unchanged; native deps must ship New Arch-compatible binaries.

How does this relate to Play Console?

* Gradle produces the AAB/APK; Play Console consumes it. Signing and tracks are separate - see [Signing & Play App Signing](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/android-platform/signing-and-play-app-signing/) and [Internal Testing Tracks](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/android-platform/internal-testing-tracks/).
