Dokumen: Android Platform Best Practices
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/android-platform/best-practices/

# Android Platform Best Practices

A condensed summary of the 25 most important best practices drawn from every page in this section - Android Studio literacy, edge-to-edge, permissions, signing, testing tracks, 16 KB compliance, and Gradle performance for Expo SDK 57.

Highlights / Android Platform Best Practices

* Test on low-RAM devices, not just Pixel emulators
* Use Play internal track before production - policy and native bugs are cheaper there
* Play App Signing SHA-256 goes in assetlinks.json, not your upload key
* RN 0.86 edge-to-edge needs inset discipline - SafeAreaProvider at root
* 16 KB page size compliance is native - smoke test API 35 16 KB AVD before launch

1. **Set JDK 17 and ANDROID\_HOME before Gradle:** React Native 0.86 / AGP 8.x expect JDK 17. Point `ANDROID_HOME` at the Android SDK and add `platform-tools` to `PATH` - cryptic Gradle failures usually trace to toolchain drift.
2. **Use `npx expo run:android` for daily native loops:** Android Studio Run ▶ does not wire Metro the way Expo dev clients expect. Terminal-driven builds match how EAS and CI compile.
3. **Treat `android/` as generated in CNG:** Edit `app.config.ts` and config plugins, not hand-merge `build.gradle` on every SDK bump. Run `npx expo prebuild --clean` only when native config actually changed.
4. **Know the Gradle map:** `settings.gradle` registers modules, `app/build.gradle` holds `applicationId` and deps, `gradle.properties` holds JVM and New Arch flags. Inspect merged `AndroidManifest.xml` for final permissions.
5. **Filter `adb logcat` for RN signals:** `ReactNativeJS`, `ReactNative`, and `AndroidRuntime` tags surface JS logs and native crashes. USB debugging needs `adb reverse tcp:8081 tcp:8081` for Metro.
6. **Test on API 34–35 emulators:** Ancient API images hide edge-to-edge, photo picker, notification permission, and back-gesture behavior that RN 0.86 targets.
7. **Wrap the app in `SafeAreaProvider`:** Edge-to-edge Android (RN 0.86 default) draws behind system bars - inset hooks require a provider at the root layout.
8. **Pair `expo-status-bar` with inset padding:** Status bar modules style icon color; they do not pad content. Use `react-native-safe-area-context` for layout clearance.
9. **Theme the nav bar with `expo-navigation-bar`:** Transparent gesture nav bars need `setBackgroundColorAsync` and `setButtonStyleAsync` - often reapplied per screen on focus.
10. **Assign one inset owner per axis:** Do not stack `SafeAreaView` and manual `insets.top` on the same edge. Tab screens omit bottom safe edge when the tab bar handles it.
11. **Request permissions in context:** Explain why on a screen, then call `requestPermission` - never a splash-time permission dump. Play policy rejects "not core to app purpose" sensitive access.
12. **Prefer the system photo picker:** `expo-image-picker` one-off flows should avoid broad `READ_MEDIA_IMAGES` unless continuous gallery sync is a core feature.
13. **Audit the merged manifest after prebuild:** `rg uses-permission android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml` - catch transitive permissions from unused SDKs and strip with `blockedPermissions`.
14. **Keep Data safety aligned with SDKs:** Every analytics, crash, auth, or payment SDK must appear in Play Console Data safety and your privacy policy - "no data collected" with Sentry installed is a rejection path.
15. **Request `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` on API 33+:** Before `getExpoPushTokenAsync`, check and request notification permission - pushes silently fail without it.
16. **Enable Play App Signing on new listings:** Google holds the app signing key; you keep an upload key. Upload key loss is recoverable; app signing key loss is not.
17. **Let EAS manage upload keystores:** Use `eas credentials` as team source of truth - never commit `.jks` files or passwords to git. Vault a downloaded backup.
18. **Put Play App Signing SHA-256 in assetlinks.json:** Production [Android App Links](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/deep-linking/android-app-links/) verify against Google's re-signing cert - not your upload or debug fingerprint.
19. **Increment `versionCode` every Play upload:** Monotonic integers across all tracks. Use `autoIncrement: true` in `eas.json` or bump `android.versionCode` in `app.config.ts`.
20. **Ship internal track before production:** `eas submit` with `"track": "internal"` catches signing, Data safety, IAP, and App Links issues before public staged rollout.
21. **Test Play-delivered builds for store features:** EAS APK links and sideload debug builds do not fully exercise Play re-signing, billing, or verified App Links - install from internal track.
22. **Validate 16 KB page size on API 35:** Use 16 KB page size AVDs when available; cold-start smoke native libs before launch. Third-party `.so` SDKs are the usual compliance gap.
23. **Maintain a device matrix beyond Pixel:** Include low-RAM Samsung A-series, gesture vs 3-button nav, and a tablet or foldable width - emulator-only QA misses OEM inset and memory behavior.
24. **Tune Gradle JVM and caching:** Set `org.gradle.jvmargs`, `parallel`, and `caching` in `gradle.properties` - avoid habitual `prebuild --clean`. Enable EAS build cache for cloud compiles.
25. **Profile Gradle with `--scan` when builds regress:** Measure task time before guessing - CMake, codegen, and dex merges dominate RN 0.86; fix the actual slow task.

## FAQs

Should I read this page before or after the topic pages?

* Skim this list for orientation, then dive into topic pages as you hit each workflow (first Play upload, edge-to-edge bug, permission rejection).
* Return here as a release checklist before promoting internal → production.

Why exactly 25 items?

* Capped at 25 for one-sitting scanability - each maps to a dedicated page in Android Platform.
* Full recipes and commands live in the linked topic articles below.

Do these practices apply to bare React Native without Expo?

* Gradle, adb, Play policy, and 16 KB rules apply to all Android RN apps.
* EAS-specific items map to your CI signing and upload pipeline in bare workflows.

What is the single highest-risk Android mistake?

* **Shipping to production without internal track QA on a Play-installed build** - signing, App Links, and IAP surprises only appear with Play re-signing.

What is the most common edge-to-edge bug?

* **Bottom CTAs hidden under the gesture nav pill** - fix with `insets.bottom` on buttons and list footers, not opaque nav bar hacks.

Which permission triggers the most Play rejections?

* **Broad storage and background location** without core feature justification - use photo picker and foreground location only.

How does Android Platform relate to EAS Build docs?

* This section is Play- and device-centric; [EAS Build](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/eas-build/eas-build-basics/) covers cloud build profiles - use both for release trains.

When must I care about 16 KB page size?

* Targeting API 35 for Play submissions from **November 2025** onward - plan compliance on SDK 57 before the deadline, not after pre-launch blockers.

Where do App Links fit in the Android checklist?

* After first Play upload: register Play App Signing fingerprint, verify on internal track - [Android App Links](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/deep-linking/android-app-links/).

What device should every team own?

* At least one **low-RAM physical Android** (4 GB class) - Pixel emulators do not reproduce OOM and slow I/O your users hit daily.

Dokumen: Edge-to-Edge on Android
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/android-platform/edge-to-edge-on-android/

# Edge-to-Edge on Android

React Native 0.86 (Expo SDK 57) enables **edge-to-edge** Android by default - your app draws behind the status and navigation bars, matching Android 15 guidance. This cookbook covers the RN defaults, `expo-status-bar`, `expo-navigation-bar`, and the inset patterns that keep buttons tappable.

Highlights / Edge-to-Edge on Android

* RN 0.86 draws content behind status and navigation bars by default on Android
* Safe area insets - not opaque system bars - keep tappable UI out of the overlap zone
* expo-status-bar controls icon style; expo-navigation-bar controls Android nav bar color and visibility
* Test on API 35 emulators - classic opaque-bar assumptions break on modern devices
* Tab bars and FABs need bottom inset padding; full-bleed heroes can ignore top inset intentionally

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
npx expo install expo-status-bar expo-navigation-bar react-native-safe-area-context
```

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx - root shell for edge-to-edge Android
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
import { StatusBar } from "expo-status-bar";
import * as NavigationBar from "expo-navigation-bar";
import { useEffect } from "react";
import { Platform } from "react-native";
import { SafeAreaProvider } from "react-native-safe-area-context";
 
export default function RootLayout() {
  useEffect(() => {
    if (Platform.OS !== "android") return;
    NavigationBar.setBackgroundColorAsync("#ffffff00"); // transparent
    NavigationBar.setButtonStyleAsync("dark");
  }, []);
 
  return (
    <SafeAreaProvider>
      <StatusBar style="auto" translucent />
      <Stack screenOptions={{ headerShown: false }} />
    </SafeAreaProvider>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// Screen with tab bar - omit bottom safe edge; pad FAB manually
import { Platform, View } from "react-native";
import { SafeAreaView, useSafeAreaInsets } from "react-native-safe-area-context";
 
export function OrdersScreen() {
  const insets = useSafeAreaInsets();
 
  return (
    <SafeAreaView style={{ flex: 1 }} edges={["top", "left", "right"]}>
      <View style={{ flex: 1 }}>{/* content */}</View>
      {/* FAB clears gesture nav bar */}
      <View style={{ position: "absolute", right: 16, bottom: insets.bottom + 16 }} />
    </SafeAreaView>
  );
}
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Bottom buttons sit under the Android gesture navigation pill.
* Status bar icons are invisible on a dark hero image (or vice versa).
* QA reports layout differences between API 33 and API 35 emulators.
* You want immersive full-bleed headers without giving up safe tap targets.

## Working Example

**Step 1 - Install modules and wrap the app**

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
import { StatusBar } from "expo-status-bar";
import * as NavigationBar from "expo-navigation-bar";
import { useEffect } from "react";
import { Platform } from "react-native";
import { SafeAreaProvider } from "react-native-safe-area-context";
 
export default function RootLayout() {
  useEffect(() => {
    if (Platform.OS !== "android") return;
    void NavigationBar.setPositionAsync("absolute");
    void NavigationBar.setBackgroundColorAsync("#00000000");
    void NavigationBar.setButtonStyleAsync("light");
  }, []);
 
  return (
    <SafeAreaProvider>
      <StatusBar style="light" translucent />
      <Stack />
    </SafeAreaProvider>
  );
}
```

**Step 2 - Split hero (full bleed) and body (inset)**

```tsx
import { ImageBackground, Text, View, StyleSheet } from "react-native";
import { useSafeAreaInsets } from "react-native-safe-area-context";
import { StatusBar } from "expo-status-bar";
 
export function ProductScreen() {
  const insets = useSafeAreaInsets();
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.root}>
      <StatusBar style="light" />
      <ImageBackground source={{ uri: "https://pics.example/hero.jpg" }} style={styles.hero}>
        <Text style={[styles.heroTitle, { marginTop: insets.top + 8 }]}>Trail Runner Pro</Text>
      </ImageBackground>
      <View style={[styles.body, { paddingBottom: insets.bottom + 16 }]}>
        <Text style={styles.price}>$129.00</Text>
      </View>
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  root: { flex: 1, backgroundColor: "#fff" },
  hero: { height: 280, justifyContent: "flex-end", padding: 16 },
  heroTitle: { color: "#fff", fontSize: 28, fontWeight: "700" },
  body: { flex: 1, padding: 16 },
  price: { fontSize: 22, fontWeight: "600" },
});
```

**Step 3 - Theme nav bar per screen (optional)**

```tsx
import { useFocusEffect } from "expo-router";
import * as NavigationBar from "expo-navigation-bar";
import { useCallback } from "react";
import { Platform } from "react-native";
 
export function useAndroidNavBar(style: "light" | "dark", background = "#00000000") {
  useFocusEffect(
    useCallback(() => {
      if (Platform.OS !== "android") return;
      void NavigationBar.setBackgroundColorAsync(background);
      void NavigationBar.setButtonStyleAsync(style);
    }, [style, background]),
  );
}
```

**Step 4 - Verify on API 35 emulator**

```bash
npx expo run:android
# Device Manager → Pixel 8 API 35 → gesture navigation enabled
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* **`SafeAreaProvider`** at root - required for inset hooks on edge-to-edge Android.
* **`StatusBar translucent`** - content draws behind; you pad with insets.
* **`expo-navigation-bar`** - transparent nav bar with light/dark button style.
* **Split inset ownership** - hero bleeds; body and FAB respect `insets.bottom`.

## Deep Dive

### How It Works

* **RN 0.86** opts into edge-to-edge at the native activity/window level - the window extends under system bars.
* **Insets** from `react-native-safe-area-context` report how much of the screen is obscured by status bar, display cutout, and navigation bar (gesture or 3-button).
* **`expo-status-bar`** sets icon/text color (`light` | `dark` | `auto`) - it does not replace inset padding.
* **`expo-navigation-bar`** controls Android navigation bar background, button style, visibility, and position (`relative` vs `absolute`).
* **Keyboard** avoidance is separate - `KeyboardAvoidingView` / `react-native-keyboard-controller` still apply; bottom inset and keyboard may stack.

### Before vs After RN 0.86

| Concern | Pre–edge-to-edge | RN 0.86 edge-to-edge |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Status bar | Opaque system-reserved band | Content behind; top inset required |
| Nav bar | Opaque bar | Gesture pill overlays content; bottom inset |
| Background | Solid behind bars | Full-bleed possible |
| Tab navigator | Often "just worked" | May need `edges` without bottom |

### expo-navigation-bar API

| Method | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `setBackgroundColorAsync(color)` | Nav bar color - use `#RRGGBBAA` for transparency |
| `setButtonStyleAsync("light" | "dark")` | Contrast for 3-button/gesture icons |
| `setPositionAsync("absolute" | "relative")` | `absolute` overlays content (edge-to-edge) |
| `setVisibilityAsync("visible" | "hidden")` | Immersive readers - restore on blur |
| `getBackgroundColorAsync()` | Debug current color in dev menu scripts |

### Gradle / Window Flags (When Plugins Are Needed)

Most Expo SDK 57 templates enable edge-to-edge via prebuild. If you maintain a bare `android/` fork:

```ts
// app.config.ts - prefer config over hand-editing MainActivity
export default {
  expo: {
    android: {
      // RN 0.86 template sets edge-to-edge; confirm after prebuild
    },
    plugins: [
      [
        "expo-build-properties",
        {
          android: {
            // compileSdk / targetSdk 35 for latest bar behavior
            compileSdkVersion: 35,
            targetSdkVersion: 35,
          },
        },
      ],
    ],
  },
};
```

Inspect `android/app/src/main/res/values/styles.xml` after prebuild - `windowLayoutInDisplayCutoutMode` and transparent status/nav bar colors should be present in the RN 0.86 template.

### Screen Chrome Patterns

| UI element | Inset strategy |
| --- | --- |
| Stack header (custom) | `paddingTop: insets.top` |
| Tab screen content | `edges={["top","left","right"]}` - tab bar owns bottom |
| Modal / bottom sheet | `edges={["bottom"]}` or full inset |
| Map / camera fullscreen | Hide nav bar temporarily; restore on exit |
| `FlatList` footer CTA | `contentContainerStyle={{ paddingBottom: insets.bottom + 16 }}` |

## Gotchas

* **Padding `SafeAreaView` and manual `insets.top` together** - doubles top gap. **Fix:** One owner per axis.
* **White status icons on white header** - `StatusBar style="light"` on light background. **Fix:** Match `style` to background luminance per screen.
* **Tab bar overlaps home indicator** - React Navigation tabs may need `safeAreaInsets` tuning. **Fix:** Pass `tabBarStyle: { height: 56 + insets.bottom }` or use library defaults on SDK 57.
* **Testing only on 3-button nav** - Gesture nav changes bottom inset height. **Fix:** Toggle **Settings → System navigation** on emulator.
* **Opaque nav bar color fighting transparency** - Some OEM skins ignore alpha. **Fix:** `setPositionAsync("absolute")` + reapply on focus.
* **Assuming `expo-status-bar` adds padding** - It only styles icons. **Fix:** Always pair with `react-native-safe-area-context`.

Y29kZWd1aWRlcy5pb3xjZ2lvOTQ4fDIwMjYwNw

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SafeAreaView` only | Simple screens | FABs, split hero/body layouts |
| `useSafeAreaInsets()` everywhere | Fine-grained control | Repetitive four-edge padding |
| Immersive `setVisibilityAsync("hidden")` | Video, camera, games | Forms - users lose system back affordance |
| `android:fitsSystemWindows` in native XML | Legacy brownfield XML layouts | Greenfield Expo CNG - use JS insets |

## FAQs

Is edge-to-edge mandatory on RN 0.86?

* It is the **default** in the RN 0.86 Android template. Disabling it requires native theme changes and fights platform direction.
* Prefer learning inset patterns over opting out.

Do I need expo-navigation-bar if I only use SafeAreaView?

* **SafeAreaView** handles layout padding; **expo-navigation-bar** handles nav bar color and button contrast.
* Transparent nav bars usually need both.

Why does my content jump when the keyboard opens?

* Keyboard and safe area are independent. Combine `KeyboardAvoidingView` with bottom inset on the same screen carefully - avoid double bottom padding.

Does edge-to-edge affect iOS?

* iOS has always used safe areas for notches. Android now behaves similarly - cross-platform `SafeAreaProvider` helps both.

How do I test status bar icon contrast?

* Toggle light/dark hero backgrounds in Storybook or a dev menu screen.
* Run on physical Samsung/Pixel - OEM tinting differs from AVD.

Can Expo Router tabs handle insets automatically?

* Recent `@react-navigation/bottom-tabs` versions respect safe areas, but custom tab bars need manual `insets.bottom`.

What about Android 15 forced edge-to-edge?

* Targeting API 35 aligns with platform expectations. RN 0.86 template is ahead of the policy curve - still test on API 35.

How do I debug inset values?

* Log `useSafeAreaInsets()` in dev builds.
* Compare emulator vs device - gesture nav insets differ (~24–48dp).

Does navigation bar theming affect gesture pill only?

* `setButtonStyleAsync` affects 3-button and gesture modes; background color affects the bar area behind the pill.

Where is the layout deep dive for safe areas?

* See [Safe Areas & Notches](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/safe-areas-and-notches/) for `edges` patterns and iOS parity.

# Android Platform Highlights Summary

Every highlight bullet from the 8 pages in this section, gathered on one page and grouped by the page it came from.

Highlights / Android Platform Highlights Summary

* You rarely edit Gradle by hand in Expo CNG - config plugins and prebuild own the native project
* RN 0.86 draws content behind status and navigation bars by default on Android
* Dangerous permissions require runtime prompts - manifest declaration alone is not enough
* You sign AABs with an upload key; Google re-signs with the app signing key for users
* Internal → closed → open → production is the risk gradient - catch policy and native bugs early
* Google Play requires 16 KB memory page support for apps targeting Android 15+ (API 35)

## [Android Basics for RN Devs](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/android-platform/android-basics-for-rn-devs/)

* You rarely edit Gradle by hand in Expo CNG - config plugins and prebuild own the native project
* adb is the RN dev's terminal: devices, logcat, port reverse, and APK install
* settings.gradle registers modules; app/build.gradle is where app-level deps and signing live
* Run npx expo run:android instead of opening Android Studio for day-to-day JS work
* JAVA\_HOME and ANDROID\_HOME must point at JDK 17 and the Android SDK - wrong paths cause cryptic Gradle failures

## [Edge-to-Edge on Android](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/android-platform/edge-to-edge-on-android/)

* RN 0.86 draws content behind status and navigation bars by default on Android
* Safe area insets - not opaque system bars - keep tappable UI out of the overlap zone
* expo-status-bar controls icon style; expo-navigation-bar controls Android nav bar color and visibility
* Test on API 35 emulators - classic opaque-bar assumptions break on modern devices
* Tab bars and FABs need bottom inset padding; full-bleed heroes can ignore top inset intentionally

## [Permissions & Play Policy](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/android-platform/permissions-and-play-policy/)

* Dangerous permissions require runtime prompts - manifest declaration alone is not enough
* Android 13+ photo picker avoids broad storage READ permissions for one-off image selection
* POST\_NOTIFICATIONS is runtime on Android 13+ - request before sending FCM marketing pushes
* Play Console Data safety form must match actual SDK and API behavior - mismatches trigger rejection
* Declare only permissions you use - Play policy flags READ\_MEDIA\_IMAGES and location as high scrutiny

## [Signing & Play App Signing](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/android-platform/signing-and-play-app-signing/)

* You sign AABs with an upload key; Google re-signs with the app signing key for users
* Play App Signing certificate SHA-256 goes in assetlinks.json - not your upload key
* EAS manages keystores remotely - eas credentials is the source of truth for teams
* Losing an upload key is recoverable with Play App Signing; losing the app signing key is catastrophic
* Never commit keystore files or passwords to git - use EAS secrets or CI encrypted storage

## [Internal Testing Tracks](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/android-platform/internal-testing-tracks/)

* Internal → closed → open → production is the risk gradient - catch policy and native bugs early
* Internal track accepts builds in minutes; up to 100 testers - ideal for QA and founders
* Closed testing supports email lists and Google Groups before public open beta
* eas submit --track internal automates upload; versionCode must monotonically increase
* Production staged rollout percentage is separate - start at 5–10% after tracks pass

## [16 KB Page Size & Device Matrix](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/android-platform/16-kb-page-size-and-device-matrix/)

* Google Play requires 16 KB memory page support for apps targeting Android 15+ (API 35)
* Deadline: November 1, 2025 for new apps and updates targeting API 35; broader enforcement continues into 2026
* Failure mode is native crash at load time - .so alignment, not JavaScript
* Expo SDK 57 / RN 0.86 ship rebuilt native deps - third-party .so files are the usual gap
* Test on 16 KB Android 15 emulator images and at least one physical device class in your matrix

## [Gradle Performance & Caching](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/android-platform/gradle-performance-and-caching/)

* gradle.properties JVM heap and parallel workers dominate local clean build time
* Avoid expo prebuild --clean unless native config changed - it invalidates Gradle caches
* EAS remote build cache persists android/ Gradle outputs between cloud builds
* Configuration cache speeds sync; incompatible plugins break it - enable gradually
* Dependency resolution hits Maven on every cold CI node - lock versions and cache ~/.gradle

## [Android Platform Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/android-platform/best-practices/)

* Test on low-RAM devices, not just Pixel emulators
* Use Play internal track before production - policy and native bugs are cheaper there
* Play App Signing SHA-256 goes in assetlinks.json, not your upload key
* RN 0.86 edge-to-edge needs inset discipline - SafeAreaProvider at root
* 16 KB page size compliance is native - smoke test API 35 16 KB AVD before launch

Dokumen: Internal Testing Tracks
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/android-platform/internal-testing-tracks/

# Internal Testing Tracks

Closed and open testing tracks on Google Play - the cookbook for shipping Expo SDK 57 Android builds to real testers before production users see regressions. Tracks are Play Console distribution channels; EAS Submit pushes signed AABs into them.

Highlights / Internal Testing Tracks

* Internal → closed → open → production is the risk gradient - catch policy and native bugs early
* Internal track accepts builds in minutes; up to 100 testers - ideal for QA and founders
* Closed testing supports email lists and Google Groups before public open beta
* eas submit --track internal automates upload; versionCode must monotonically increase
* Production staged rollout percentage is separate - start at 5–10% after tracks pass

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```json
// eas.json
{
  "submit": {
    "production": {
      "android": {
        "serviceAccountKeyPath": "./secrets/play-service-account.json",
        "track": "internal"
      }
    },
    "closed-beta": {
      "android": {
        "serviceAccountKeyPath": "./secrets/play-service-account.json",
        "track": "alpha"
      }
    },
    "open-beta": {
      "android": {
        "serviceAccountKeyPath": "./secrets/play-service-account.json",
        "track": "beta"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

```bash
# Build release AAB
eas build --platform android --profile production
 
# Submit to internal testing (fastest feedback loop)
eas submit --platform android --profile production --latest
 
# Promote in Play Console UI: internal → closed → open → production
# Or submit directly to alpha/beta with matching eas.json profile
eas submit --platform android --profile closed-beta --latest
```

```ts
// app.config.ts - monotonic versionCode (required every upload)
export default {
  expo: {
    version: "2.4.0",
    android: {
      package: "com.example.shopapp",
      versionCode: 240012, // increment every Play upload
    },
  },
};
```

**When to reach for this:**

* First Play Store release - internal track validates signing, Data safety, and content rating before production.
* QA needs a Play-delivered build (not just EAS internal APK link) to test in-app purchases and App Links.
* You want 500 beta testers on closed track before 5% production staged rollout.
* Policy rejection - fix on internal, resubmit without touching production users.

## Working Example

**Step 1 - Create Play app and complete store listing basics**

1. Play Console → **Create app**.
2. Finish **Dashboard** required tasks: privacy policy, Data safety, content rating, target audience.
3. Enable **Play App Signing** on first upload.

**Step 2 - Service account for EAS Submit**

```bash
# Play Console → Users and permissions → Invite user → Service account
# Google Cloud → IAM → Create key JSON → save as secrets/play-service-account.json
# Grant Release manager (or minimum: Release to testing tracks)
```

**Step 3 - Internal track first upload**

```bash
eas build --platform android --profile production
eas submit --platform android --profile production --latest
```

Play Console → **Testing → Internal testing** → release appears after processing (~minutes to hours).

**Step 4 - Add testers**

| Track | Tester limit | How to add |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Internal | 100 | Email list in Internal testing → Testers tab |
| Closed (alpha) | Unlimited (invited) | Email lists or Google Groups |
| Open (beta) | Unlimited (public) | Opt-in URL anyone can join |
| Production | All users | Staged rollout % |

Share opt-in link from **Testers → Copy link** - testers accept invite, then install from Play Store.

**Step 5 - Promote after QA sign-off**

Play Console → **Promote release** from internal → closed → production.

Or submit a new build directly to production track with updated `eas.json` `"track": "production"` when ready.

**Step 6 - Verify App Links on internal build**

```bash
# After internal release is live on Play (re-signed with app signing key)
adb shell pm get-app-links com.example.shopapp
```

Use Play **App signing** SHA-256 in `assetlinks.json` - see [Android App Links](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/deep-linking/android-app-links/).

**What this demonstrates:**

* **Internal track** - fastest path from `eas submit` to installable Play build.
* **Service account** - CI-friendly non-interactive uploads.
* **versionCode** - must increase per upload across all tracks.
* **Promotion flow** - same artifact can climb tracks without rebuild.

## Deep Dive

### How It Works

* **Tracks** are Play Console release channels sharing one `applicationId` but different tester audiences.
* **AAB processing** - Google generates device-specific APKs after upload; testers download via Play Store, not sideload.
* **Same signing pipeline** - all tracks get Play App Signing; differences are visibility and rollout rules only.
* **EAS Submit** - uses Google Play Developer API (`edits.insert` + `bundles.upload`) to place AAB on chosen track.
* **Review** - Internal testing often skips lengthy review; **production** and sometimes **open testing** trigger policy review.

### Track Comparison

| Track | Play API name | Audience | Review speed | Typical use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Internal | `internal` | Up to 100 invited | Fastest | Engineering, PM, design QA |
| Closed | `alpha` | Invited lists / groups | Fast | Beta customers under NDA |
| Open | `beta` | Public opt-in | Medium | Public beta, scale testing |
| Production | `production` | Everyone | Full | Staged rollout 1% → 100% |

```json
// eas.json track mapping (common convention)
// "alpha"  → Closed testing
// "beta"   → Open testing
// "internal" → Internal testing
```

### Versioning Rules

| Field | Where | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | `app.config` `version` | User-visible semver (`2.4.0`) |
| `versionCode` | `app.config` `android.versionCode` | Integer - strictly increasing per upload |
| `versionName` | Derived from `version` in Gradle | Shown in Play listing |

```json
// eas.json - auto-increment versionCode on EAS Build
{
  "build": {
    "production": {
      "autoIncrement": true
    }
  }
}
```

### What to Test per Track

| Checkpoint | Internal | Closed | Open | Production |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cold start / login | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Push notifications | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| In-app purchases | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| App Links (verified) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Data safety accuracy | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| 16 KB page size devices | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Low-RAM phone | Optional | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |

### CI Pipeline Sketch

```yaml
# .github/workflows/android-release.yml (conceptual)
jobs:
  build-submit-internal:
    steps:
      - run: eas build --platform android --profile production --non-interactive
      - run: eas submit --platform android --profile production --latest --non-interactive
```

Gate production promotion on QA checklist + crash-free sessions in internal track.

## Gotchas

* **Same versionCode on resubmit** - Play rejects duplicate. **Fix:** Increment `versionCode` or enable `autoIncrement`.
* **Testers can't find app** - They must accept opt-in link with the Google account on device. **Fix:** Resend link; check account mismatch.
* **Testing debug APK instead of Play build** - IAP and App Links behave differently. **Fix:** Install from Play internal track after `eas submit`.
* **Skipping Data safety on internal** - Dashboard may block all tracks until complete. **Fix:** Finish compliance tasks first.
* **Open beta before closed validation** - Public one-star reviews on beta builds. **Fix:** Closed track with invited power users first.
* **Promote broken build to production** - Promotion copies release notes, not a new QA pass. **Fix:** Run checklist on each track promotion.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| EAS internal distribution (APK link) | Hourly dev QA, no Play needed | Testing Play billing or App Links |
| Firebase App Distribution | Cross-platform, non-Play | Play policy / IAP validation |
| Sideload `adb install` | Engineer-only smoke | PM/design testers without adb |
| Production 1% staged only | Tiny user base | No beta audience - risky |

## FAQs

How fast is internal testing available?

* Often minutes after processing; first app may take longer while Play completes setup tasks.
* Processing status appears in Play Console release dashboard.

Can I have multiple releases on one track?

* One active release per track at a time; new upload replaces or rolls forward depending on rollout state.
* Halt rollout before uploading conflicting version if needed.

Do internal testers need to pay for the app?

* Free apps: testers install at no cost.
* Paid apps: testers may need license testing configuration in Play Console.

What is the difference between alpha and beta tracks?

* **Alpha (closed)** - invite-only lists.
* **Beta (open)** - public opt-in link; anyone can join.
* Names are historical; think closed vs open.

Can EAS Submit go directly to production?

* Yes - set `"track": "production"` in `eas.json`.
* Recommended: internal first, then promote after QA for new apps.

How do release notes work per track?

* Enter per track in Play Console or via API metadata.
* Copy internal QA notes to closed/open when promoting - users read beta notes.

Does OTA (expo-updates) work on testing tracks?

* Yes - same binary; OTA targets runtime version policy.
* Native changes still need new AAB on a track.

How do I remove a tester?

* Play Console → track → Testers → remove email or disable opt-in link for open beta.

What permissions do the service account need?

* **Release to testing tracks** for internal/closed/open.
* **Release to production** for production submits - narrower IAM is better.

How does this connect to App Links?

* First Play upload establishes app signing cert for `assetlinks.json`.
* Verify links on internal track before production - [Android App Links](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/deep-linking/android-app-links/).

Dokumen: Permissions & Play Policy
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/android-platform/permissions-and-play-policy/

# Permissions & Play Policy

Runtime permissions, the system photo picker, and Google Play **Data safety** - the Android compliance cookbook for Expo SDK 57 apps. Manifest entries tell the OS what you *might* request; runtime prompts and Play Console forms must reflect what you *actually* do.

Highlights / Permissions & Play Policy

* Dangerous permissions require runtime prompts - manifest declaration alone is not enough
* Android 13+ photo picker avoids broad storage READ permissions for one-off image selection
* POST\_NOTIFICATIONS is runtime on Android 13+ - request before sending FCM marketing pushes
* Play Console Data safety form must match actual SDK and API behavior - mismatches trigger rejection
* Declare only permissions you use - Play policy flags READ\_MEDIA\_IMAGES and location as high scrutiny

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
npx expo install expo-image-picker expo-camera
```

```tsx
// features/media/pickAvatar.ts - photo picker without broad storage access
import * as ImagePicker from "expo-image-picker";
import { Alert, Linking, Platform } from "react-native";
 
export async function pickAvatar(): Promise<ImagePicker.ImagePickerAsset | null> {
  const { status } = await ImagePicker.requestMediaLibraryPermissionsAsync();
  if (status !== "granted") {
    Alert.alert(
      "Photos access needed",
      "Enable photo access in Settings to choose a profile picture.",
      [
        { text: "Cancel", style: "cancel" },
        { text: "Open Settings", onPress: () => Linking.openSettings() },
      ],
    );
    return null;
  }
 
  const result = await ImagePicker.launchImageLibraryAsync({
    mediaTypes: ["images"],
    allowsEditing: true,
    aspect: [1, 1],
    quality: 0.8,
    // Android 13+ uses system photo picker when available - no READ_MEDIA_IMAGES for one-off pick
  });
 
  if (result.canceled) return null;
  return result.assets[0] ?? null;
}
```

```ts
// app.config.ts - declare only what modules need; block accidental permissions
export default {
  expo: {
    android: {
      package: "com.example.shopapp",
      permissions: [
        "CAMERA", // expo-camera
        // Avoid legacy WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE - not needed for picker flows
      ],
      blockedPermissions: [
        "READ_MEDIA_VIDEO", // example: app never reads video library
      ],
    },
    plugins: [
      [
        "expo-image-picker",
        {
          photosPermission:
            "Allow ShopApp to access your photos for profile and receipt uploads.",
          cameraPermission: "Allow ShopApp to take photos for support tickets.",
        },
      ],
    ],
  },
};
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Play Console rejects the build for undeclared or overbroad permissions.
* Users see permission prompts at launch instead of in context.
* You are filling the **Data safety** questionnaire and need to map SDKs to collected data types.
* Android 14+ devices deny `READ_MEDIA_IMAGES` - picker-first flows still work.

## Working Example

**Step 1 - Contextual camera permission**

```tsx
import { CameraView, useCameraPermissions } from "expo-camera";
import { Button, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
export function ScanReceiptScreen() {
  const [permission, requestPermission] = useCameraPermissions();
 
  if (!permission) return <View />; // hook loading
 
  if (!permission.granted) {
    return (
      <View style={{ flex: 1, justifyContent: "center", padding: 24 }}>
        <Text>We need camera access to scan your receipt.</Text>
        <Button title="Continue" onPress={requestPermission} />
      </View>
    );
  }
 
  return <CameraView style={{ flex: 1 }} facing="back" />;
}
```

**Step 2 - Notifications (Android 13+)**

```tsx
import * as Notifications from "expo-notifications";
import { Platform } from "react-native";
 
export async function ensureNotificationPermission(): Promise<boolean> {
  if (Platform.OS !== "android" || Platform.Version < 33) return true;
 
  const { status: existing } = await Notifications.getPermissionsAsync();
  if (existing === "granted") return true;
 
  const { status } = await Notifications.requestPermissionsAsync();
  return status === "granted";
}
```

**Step 3 - Audit merged manifest after prebuild**

```bash
npx expo prebuild --platform android
rg "uses-permission" android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml
```

**Step 4 - Data safety alignment checklist**

| App behavior | Data safety declaration |
| --- | --- |
| `expo-image-picker` one-off photo | Photos/videos - **ephemeral** or **not collected** if never uploaded |
| Upload avatar to your API | Photos - **collected**, purpose Account management |
| `expo-location` foreground | Location - **approximate/precise**, purpose App functionality |
| Firebase Analytics | Device IDs, app interactions - declare per Firebase docs |
| Crash reporting (Sentry) | Diagnostics - crash logs |

**What this demonstrates:**

* **Just-in-time prompts** - explain *why* before `requestPermission`.
* **Plugin permission strings** - user-facing rationale on the system dialog.
* **`blockedPermissions`** - strip transitive permissions from dependencies.
* **Data safety** - map each Expo module to Play Console categories.

## Deep Dive

### How It Works

* **Install-time permissions** (`INTERNET`, `VIBRATE`) are granted at install - no runtime dialog.
* **Dangerous permissions** (`CAMERA`, `ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION`, `RECORD_AUDIO`, `POST_NOTIFICATIONS`) require runtime request on Android 6+.
* **Manifest merge** - Expo modules and config plugins add `<uses-permission>` entries; `npx expo prebuild` produces the merged manifest.
* **Photo picker (Android 13+)** - `ACTION_PICK_IMAGES` / system picker returns URIs without persistent broad storage access - preferred for profile photo, attachment flows.
* **Play policy** - Google reviews permission use against declared features; "feature not core to app purpose" is a common rejection for location and SMS.

### Permission Classes RN Apps Hit

| Permission | When needed | Expo module | Play scrutiny |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CAMERA` | QR scan, capture | `expo-camera` | Medium - justify in UI |
| `ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION` | Maps, delivery | `expo-location` | **High** - must be core feature |
| `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` | Push (API 33+) | `expo-notifications` | Medium |
| `READ_MEDIA_IMAGES` | Legacy gallery crawl | Avoid - use picker | **High** on Play |
| `RECORD_AUDIO` | Video, voice | `expo-av`, camera | Medium |
| `READ_CONTACTS` | Invite friends | Rare - avoid | **High** |

### Photo Picker vs Storage Permissions

| Approach | UX | Policy risk | Expo API |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| System photo picker | User selects specific items | Low | `launchImageLibraryAsync` |
| `READ_MEDIA_IMAGES` | App reads entire library | High - needs strong justification | Only if continuous gallery sync |
| `READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE` (≤ API 32) | Legacy | Deprecated path | Migrate on SDK bump |

```tsx
// Prefer picker - do not request broad storage for a single upload
const result = await ImagePicker.launchImageLibraryAsync({
  mediaTypes: ["images"],
  selectionLimit: 1,
});
```

### Data Safety Form Mental Model

1. **Data types** - location, photos, contacts, financial info, etc.
2. **Collected vs shared** - your servers vs third-party SDKs.
3. **Purpose** - app functionality, analytics, advertising (advertising triggers extra review).
4. **Security practices** - encryption in transit (HTTPS) at minimum.
5. **Deletion** - account settings or support email for erasure requests.

Cross-check against:

* Your privacy policy URL (required in Play Console).
* SDK privacy manifests / data collection docs (Sentry, Firebase, Stripe, etc.).
* Actual network traffic - undeclared analytics is a policy violation.

### Android 14+ Partial Grants

* Users can grant **selected photos** instead of full library access.
* Handle `permission.granted === false` and `canAskAgain === false` - route to Settings.
* Re-request only after user taps an action that needs access - not on cold start.

```tsx
import { Linking } from "react-native";
 
if (!permission.canAskAgain) {
  await Linking.openSettings();
}
```

## Gotchas

* **Requesting all permissions at splash** - Play policy and UX both punish this. **Fix:** Just-in-time, with rationale UI before the system dialog.
* **Transitive permissions from unused SDKs** - Analytics SDK adds location. **Fix:** `blockedPermissions` + remove unused deps; verify merged manifest.
* **Data safety says "no data collected" but Sentry ships** - Automatic rejection risk. **Fix:** Declare diagnostics; link SDK docs in internal compliance sheet.
* **Missing `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` on API 33+** - Push silently fails. **Fix:** Request before `getExpoPushTokenAsync`.
* **Legacy `WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE`** - Unnecessary for picker uploads on modern APIs. **Fix:** Remove from `app.config` permissions; use content URIs.
* **iOS parity assumptions** - iOS photo library wording differs; Android has picker + partial grants. **Fix:** Platform-specific copy in pre-permission screens.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| System photo picker | One-off image selection | Background sync of entire camera roll |
| `expo-document-picker` | PDFs, files | Camera capture |
| In-app browser for uploads | Zero storage permission | Native crop/edit UX required |
| Coarse location only | Weather, regional content | Turn-by-turn navigation |

## FAQs

Where do I declare Android permissions in Expo?

* `app.config.ts` → `expo.android.permissions` adds declarations.
* Config plugins (e.g. `expo-image-picker`) add permissions and rationale strings.
* Run prebuild and inspect merged manifest - source of truth for what ships.

Do I need READ\_MEDIA\_IMAGES for expo-image-picker?

* On Android 13+, the system picker path often avoids broad storage permission for single selection.
* If Play flags the permission, verify merged manifest and update to latest `expo-image-picker` - remove unused declarations.

How does Play verify permission usage?

* Automated scans of manifest + manual review for sensitive permissions.
* Declaration in **App content → Sensitive app permissions** must match feature videos and in-app flows.

What is the Data safety form?

* Mandatory Play Console questionnaire describing what user data the app collects and shares.
* Must align with privacy policy and actual SDK behavior - updated when you add analytics or auth.

Can I remove a permission added by a dependency?

* Yes - `expo.android.blockedPermissions` strips entries at merge time.
* Also remove the SDK if unused - blocked permissions do not stop JS from calling dead APIs.

How do I test permission denial paths?

* `adb shell pm clear com.example.shopapp` resets grants.
* Emulator **Settings → Apps → Your app → Permissions** toggles individual grants.

Does foreground location need a background permission?

* Only if you track location while app is backgrounded - requires separate `ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION` and heavy Play scrutiny.
* Maps on screen → foreground `ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION` only.

What about App Links and permissions?

* App Links ([Android App Links](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/deep-linking/android-app-links/)) do not require extra dangerous permissions - only intent filters and verification.

How often must Data safety be updated?

* On every release that adds SDKs, login, payments, or analytics.
* Treat it as part of the release checklist alongside version code bump.

Are permission strings localized?

* Plugin `photosPermission` strings are static in config - use `app.config.ts` with locale env for multi-language builds or per-flavor config.

Dokumen: Signing & Play App Signing
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/android-platform/signing-and-play-app-signing/

# Signing & Play App Signing

Upload keys, Play App Signing, and EAS credential sync - how Android release identity works for Expo SDK 57 teams. Signing proves updates come from you; Play App Signing adds Google's key custody so lost laptops do not end your app.

Highlights / Signing & Play App Signing

* You sign AABs with an upload key; Google re-signs with the app signing key for users
* Play App Signing certificate SHA-256 goes in assetlinks.json - not your upload key
* EAS manages keystores remotely - eas credentials is the source of truth for teams
* Losing an upload key is recoverable with Play App Signing; losing the app signing key is catastrophic
* Never commit keystore files or passwords to git - use EAS secrets or CI encrypted storage

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
# First Android production build - let EAS generate credentials
eas build --platform android --profile production
 
# Inspect and download credentials (admin)
eas credentials --platform android
 
# Build with existing remote keystore
eas build --platform android --profile production --non-interactive
```

```json
// eas.json
{
  "build": {
    "production": {
      "android": {
        "buildType": "app-bundle"
      }
    }
  },
  "submit": {
    "production": {
      "android": {
        "serviceAccountKeyPath": "./play-service-account.json",
        "track": "internal"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

```bash
# Local debug fingerprint (development / adb App Links testing only)
keytool -list -v -keystore ~/.android/debug.keystore \
  -alias androiddebugkey -storepass android -keypass android | grep SHA256
 
# Play Console → App integrity → App signing key certificate → SHA-256
# Use THAT fingerprint in assetlinks.json for production App Links
```

**When to reach for this:**

* First `eas build` for Android production asks about keystore generation.
* App Links verification fails - fingerprint mismatch between upload and Play signing cert.
* A teammate rotated off and only they had the `.jks` file on a laptop.
* Play Console rejects an AAB with "signed with wrong key."

## Working Example

**Step 1 - Enable Play App Signing (new app)**

1. Create app in Play Console.
2. On first AAB upload, accept **Google Play App Signing** (recommended - mandatory for new apps).
3. Google holds the **app signing key**; you keep an **upload key**.

**Step 2 - Generate upload credentials with EAS**

```bash
eas credentials --platform android
# Choose: Set up a new keystore (or upload existing if migrating)
# EAS stores keystore + passwords encrypted on Expo servers
```

**Step 3 - Production build and submit**

```bash
eas build --platform android --profile production
eas submit --platform android --profile production --latest
```

**Step 4 - Register App Links fingerprint**

```bash
# Play Console → Release → App integrity → App signing
# Copy SHA-256 certificate fingerprint
```

```json
// https://shop.example.com/.well-known/assetlinks.json
[
  {
    "relation": ["delegate_permission/common.handle_all_urls"],
    "target": {
      "namespace": "android_app",
      "package_name": "com.example.shopapp",
      "sha256_cert_fingerprints": ["PLAY_APP_SIGNING_SHA256_HERE"]
    }
  }
]
```

See [Android App Links](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/deep-linking/android-app-links/) for full verification setup.

**Step 5 - Rotate upload key (lost laptop scenario)**

1. Play Console → **App integrity** → **Upload key** → **Request upload key reset**.
2. Generate new upload keystore locally or via `eas credentials`.
3. Submit PEM certificate to Google; wait for approval.
4. Future EAS builds use new upload key; user-facing app signing key unchanged.

**What this demonstrates:**

* **Upload vs app signing** - two keys, two purposes.
* **EAS remote credentials** - team builds without passing `.jks` in Slack.
* **assetlinks.json** - must use Play App Signing cert for production links.
* **Upload key rotation** - supported; app signing key stays stable.

## Deep Dive

### How It Works

* **APK/AAB signing** - Gradle signs the release artifact with your **upload private key** before upload to Play.
* **Play App Signing** - Google strips your signature, re-signs with the **app signing key**, and serves that binary to users.
* **Certificate fingerprints** - SHA-256 of the public cert identifies your app for App Links, Firebase, Google Sign-In, and API key restrictions.
* **EAS Build** - pulls credentials from Expo's credential service at build time; injects `keystore`, `key alias`, and passwords into Gradle signing config.
* **Version code** - monotonic integer per `applicationId`; Play rejects duplicates. EAS can auto-increment via `eas.json`.

### Key Types

| Key | Who holds it | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Debug keystore | Your machine (`~/.android/debug.keystore`) | `npx expo run:android` local debug |
| Upload key | You / EAS | Signing AAB before Play upload |
| App signing key | Google Play | Signing APKs users download |
| Local release keystore (no Play Signing) | You only | Legacy - avoid for new apps |

### EAS Credentials Commands

| Command | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `eas credentials` | Interactive credential manager |
| `eas credentials --platform android` | Android keystore menu |
| Download keystore | Backup for disaster recovery - store in vault |
| Upload keystore | Migrate existing app to EAS |
| Remove credentials | Dangerous - only when rotating with Play support |

```bash
# Non-interactive CI - credentials already configured on Expo account
eas build --platform android --profile production --non-interactive
```

### Gradle Signing (Bare Reference)

Expo prebuild generates signing config; bare teams may see:

```gradle
// android/app/build.gradle (release) - EAS injects via env in cloud builds
signingConfigs {
    release {
        storeFile file(MYAPP_UPLOAD_STORE_FILE)
        storePassword MYAPP_UPLOAD_STORE_PASSWORD
        keyAlias MYAPP_UPLOAD_KEY_ALIAS
        keyPassword MYAPP_UPLOAD_KEY_PASSWORD
    }
}
```

Do not commit passwords - EAS uses encrypted secrets; local `gradle.properties` entries belong in `.gitignore`.

### Fingerprint Cheat Sheet

| Need | Which fingerprint |
| --- | --- |
| Production App Links | Play **App signing** SHA-256 |
| Internal EAS build App Links (before Play) | Upload or debug cert - test separately |
| Firebase Android app | Usually Play app signing SHA-256 + debug for dev |
| Google Sign-In OAuth | SHA-1 and SHA-256 of signing certs |

## Gotchas

* **assetlinks.json uses upload key fingerprint** - Production links fail verification. **Fix:** Play Console app signing SHA-256.
* **Committing `*.jks` to git** - Key compromise; Play may force rotation. **Fix:** EAS remote credentials + vault backup only.
* **Reusing debug keystore for release** - Play rejects; security disaster. **Fix:** Separate upload keystore via EAS.
* **Version code not incremented** - `eas submit` fails "version code already used." **Fix:** `autoIncrement: true` in `eas.json` or bump `android.versionCode` in `app.config`.
* **Package name mismatch** - `com.example.shopapp` in config vs keystore registered to old package. **Fix:** New Play listing or correct `applicationId` before first publish.
* **Opting out of Play App Signing** - Loses upload key recovery path. **Fix:** Accept Play App Signing on new listings.

WTI5a1pXZDFhV1JsY3k1cGIzeGpaMmx2T1RFNGZESXdNall3Tnc9PQ==

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| EAS managed credentials | Default for Expo teams | Air-gapped enterprise with HSM-only policy |
| Local keystore + manual upload | Legal requirement to hold keys on-prem | Small team without HSM discipline |
| Google Cloud KMS signing | Enterprise key custody | Standard indie/small SaaS overhead |
| APK instead of AAB | Legacy sideload channels | Play Store production - AAB required |

## FAQs

Does EAS store my keystore securely?

* Yes - encrypted at rest on Expo infrastructure; accessible to project members with credentials permission.
* Download a backup to your company vault after generation.

Can multiple apps share one keystore?

* Technically yes (same key, different `applicationId`) - **not recommended**. One compromise affects all apps; use per-app keystores.

What if I lose the upload key?

* With Play App Signing: request upload key reset in Play Console, register new cert, update EAS credentials.
* Without Play App Signing: you cannot ship updates - new listing with new package name.

How do I migrate from local Gradle signing to EAS?

* `eas credentials` → upload existing `.jks` + alias + passwords.
* Confirm next `eas build` fingerprint matches what Play expects.

Why did Google Sign-In break after first Play release?

* Debug SHA-1 was registered in Firebase; production uses Play app signing SHA-1.
* Add **both** debug and Play signing fingerprints in Firebase/Google Cloud console.

Do internal testing builds need the same key?

* Same upload key pipeline; Play re-signs all tracks with app signing key.
* Test App Links on internal track with Play signing fingerprint after first upload.

What is the difference between SHA-1 and SHA-256?

* App Links and modern APIs use SHA-256.
* Some Google Cloud console entries still ask for SHA-1 - provide both from the same cert.

Can I sign locally and upload to Play manually?

* Yes - `cd android && ./gradlew bundleRelease` with local keystore, then Play Console upload.
* EAS is preferred for reproducibility and credential sync across teammates.

How does signing relate to package name?

* Keystore does not encode package name - `applicationId` in Gradle must match Play listing.
* Changing package name after publish requires a new store listing.

Where do App Links fit?

* Verified links bind HTTPS URLs to your package + **signing certificate**.
* Full recipe: [Android App Links](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/deep-linking/android-app-links/).

## Related

* [Android App Links](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/deep-linking/android-app-links/) - SHA-256 fingerprint in assetlinks.json
* [Internal Testing Tracks](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/android-platform/internal-testing-tracks/) - ship signed AABs to testers before production
* [Permissions & Play Policy](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/android-platform/permissions-and-play-policy/) - Play Console compliance (separate from signing)
* [../eas-build/android-keystores-and-signing/android-keystores-and-signing.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/eas-build/android-keystores-and-signing/) - EAS-focused signing deep dive
* [../eas-build/eas-submit/eas-submit.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/eas-build/eas-submit/) - automated Play uploads

Dokumen: Animations Basics
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/animations-basics/

# Animations Basics

10 examples to get you started with React Native animations - 7 basic and 3 intermediate. You will learn when the built-in `Animated` API is enough, when **Reanimated 4** is the right tool, and how to keep motion at **60fps** on the UI thread.

Highlights / Animations Basics

* Install with npx expo install - Reanimated 4 and gesture-handler versions must match SDK 57
* react-native-reanimated/plugin must be the last entry in babel.config.js plugins
* Animated + useNativeDriver handles simple fades and springs on the native driver
* Reanimated 4 runs gesture-driven frames on the UI thread - the path to reliable 60fps
* Never animate layout properties with useNativeDriver: true - width, height, and flex need Reanimated or Layout animations
* Profile on a mid-tier Android device - simulators hide JS-thread jank during scroll + animation

## Prerequisites

Install Reanimated and Gesture Handler with Expo's version resolver - do not pin versions manually.

```bash
npx expo install react-native-reanimated react-native-gesture-handler
```

Confirm the SDK 57 pin before adding animation code:

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "expo": "~57.0.4",
    "react": "19.2.3",
    "react-native": "0.86.0",
    "react-native-reanimated": "~4.0.0",
    "react-native-gesture-handler": "~2.28.0"
  }
}
```

Wrap your root layout with `GestureHandlerRootView` (required for gestures; harmless for animation-only apps):

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
import { GestureHandlerRootView } from "react-native-gesture-handler";
 
export default function RootLayout() {
  return (
    <GestureHandlerRootView style={{ flex: 1 }}>
      <Stack />
    </GestureHandlerRootView>
  );
}
```

> **Tooling:** These examples target **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4), **React Native 0.86.0**, **React 19.2.3**, and **Reanimated 4**.

---

## Basic Examples

### 1. Babel Plugin Must Be Last

Reanimated's Babel plugin rewrites worklets at build time. It **must** be the final plugin in the array.

```js
// babel.config.js
module.exports = function (api) {
  api.cache(true);
  return {
    presets: ["babel-preset-expo"],
    plugins: [
      // other plugins first …
      "react-native-reanimated/plugin", // ← always last
    ],
  };
};
```

* If the plugin is missing or not last, worklets throw at runtime and animations silently fall back to the JS thread.
* After changing `babel.config.js`, restart Metro with cache cleared: `npx expo start --clear`.
* The `default@sdk-57` template ships this configuration - verify before copying snippets from older tutorials.

> **Related:** [react-native-reanimated 4](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/react-native-reanimated-4/) - shared values and UI-thread animations | [Worklets & Bundle Mode](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/worklets-and-bundle-mode/) - what the plugin actually does

---

### 2. Animated API - Opacity Fade

The built-in `Animated` API is fine for one-off fades that do not interact with gestures.

```tsx
import { useEffect, useRef } from "react";
import { Animated, StyleSheet, View } from "react-native";
 
export function FadeInBanner() {
  const opacity = useRef(new Animated.Value(0)).current;
 
  useEffect(() => {
    Animated.timing(opacity, {
      toValue: 1,
      duration: 300,
      useNativeDriver: true,
    }).start();
  }, [opacity]);
 
  return (
    <Animated.View style={[styles.banner, { opacity }]}>
      <View />
    </Animated.View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  banner: { padding: 16, backgroundColor: "#e8f4ff" },
});
```

* **`useNativeDriver: true`** offloads opacity and transform to the native driver - frames do not wait on React re-renders.
* `Animated.Value` lives in a ref - recreating it every render resets the animation.
* Good for toasts, skeleton reveals, and simple mount/unmount fades with no gesture coupling.

> **Related:** [Layout Animations](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/layout-animations/) - entering/exiting presets when items mount and unmount in lists

---

### 3. Animated.timing - Slide and Scale

Combine translate and scale for lightweight emphasis - still on the native driver.

```tsx
import { useEffect, useRef } from "react";
import { Animated, Pressable, Text } from "react-native";
 
export function PopInButton({ onPress }: { onPress: () => void }) {
  const scale = useRef(new Animated.Value(0.9)).current;
  const translateY = useRef(new Animated.Value(12)).current;
 
  useEffect(() => {
    Animated.parallel([
      Animated.spring(scale, {
        toValue: 1,
        friction: 6,
        useNativeDriver: true,
      }),
      Animated.timing(translateY, {
        toValue: 0,
        duration: 250,
        useNativeDriver: true,
      }),
    ]).start();
  }, [scale, translateY]);
 
  return (
    <Pressable onPress={onPress}>
      <Animated.View
        style={{
          transform: [{ scale }, { translateY }],
        }}
      >
        <Text>Continue</Text>
      </Animated.View>
    </Pressable>
  );
}
```

* **`Animated.parallel`** runs both tracks at once - order does not imply sequencing.
* `transform` (translate, scale, rotate) supports `useNativeDriver: true`; layout props do not.
* `Animated.spring` gives organic motion without hand-tuning easing curves for simple CTAs.

> **Related:** [react-native-reanimated 4](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/react-native-reanimated-4/) - `withSpring` on the UI thread for gesture-linked springs

---

### 4. Animated.loop and Sequence

Chain and repeat animations for loading indicators and pulsing badges.

```tsx
import { useEffect, useRef } from "react";
import { Animated, StyleSheet, View } from "react-native";
 
export function PulsingDot() {
  const opacity = useRef(new Animated.Value(0.4)).current;
 
  useEffect(() => {
    const pulse = Animated.loop(
      Animated.sequence([
        Animated.timing(opacity, {
          toValue: 1,
          duration: 600,
          useNativeDriver: true,
        }),
        Animated.timing(opacity, {
          toValue: 0.4,
          duration: 600,
          useNativeDriver: true,
        }),
      ])
    );
    pulse.start();
    return () => pulse.stop();
  }, [opacity]);
 
  return <Animated.View style={[styles.dot, { opacity }]} />;
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  dot: { width: 10, height: 10, borderRadius: 5, backgroundColor: "#3b82f6" },
});
```

* **Always stop loops in the effect cleanup** - leaked loops keep firing after unmount and waste battery.
* `Animated.sequence` runs steps one after another; `Animated.stagger` offsets parallel children.
* For complex loading skeletons tied to list layout, prefer Reanimated layout animations instead.

> **Related:** [Animations Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/best-practices/) - when pulsing indicators hurt list scroll performance

---

### 5. Animated.event - Scroll-Linked Opacity

Bind scroll position directly to animated values without per-frame `setState`.

```tsx
import { useRef } from "react";
import { Animated, ScrollView, StyleSheet, View } from "react-native";
 
const HEADER_HEIGHT = 56;
 
export function CollapsingHeaderScroll() {
  const scrollY = useRef(new Animated.Value(0)).current;
 
  const headerOpacity = scrollY.interpolate({
    inputRange: [0, HEADER_HEIGHT],
    outputRange: [1, 0],
    extrapolate: "clamp",
  });
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.screen}>
      <Animated.View style={[styles.header, { opacity: headerOpacity }]}>
        <View />
      </Animated.View>
      <Animated.ScrollView
        scrollEventThrottle={16}
        onScroll={Animated.event(
          [{ nativeEvent: { contentOffset: { y: scrollY } } }],
          { useNativeDriver: true }
        )}
      >
        {/* long content */}
      </Animated.ScrollView>
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  screen: { flex: 1 },
  header: { height: HEADER_HEIGHT, backgroundColor: "#111" },
});
```

* **`scrollEventThrottle={16}`** targets ~60fps scroll events - the default 400ms throttle feels laggy for parallax.
* `interpolate` maps scroll range to opacity - no React render per frame.
* For parallax tied to gestures beyond scroll (pull-to-refresh, bottom sheets), graduate to Reanimated + Gesture Handler.

> **Related:** [react-native-gesture-handler](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/react-native-gesture-handler/) - pan gestures that share values with Reanimated

---

### 6. What useNativeDriver Cannot Animate

Layout-affecting properties stay on the JS thread with the classic `Animated` API.

| Property family | `useNativeDriver: true` | Better approach |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `opacity`, `transform` | ✅ Supported | `Animated` or Reanimated |
| `width`, `height`, `top`, `left` | ❌ Not supported | Reanimated layout animations or `Layout` |
| `backgroundColor` | ❌ Not supported | Reanimated `useAnimatedStyle` + `interpolateColor` |
| Flex changes | ❌ Not supported | Reanimated `Layout` or conditional structure |

```tsx
// ❌ This warns and runs on the JS thread - jank during scroll
Animated.timing(width, { toValue: 200, useNativeDriver: true });
 
// ✅ Reanimated 4 - layout-aware animation on the UI thread
import Animated, { useAnimatedStyle, useSharedValue, withTiming } from "react-native-reanimated";
 
const progress = useSharedValue(0);
const style = useAnimatedStyle(() => ({
  width: withTiming(progress.value * 200),
}));
```

* The native driver boundary is the main reason teams adopt Reanimated for production motion.
* Animating layout on the JS thread during list scroll is a common source of dropped frames.

> **Related:** [Layout Animations](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/layout-animations/) - `Layout`, `FadeIn`, and list reorder without manual width tweens

---

### 7. When to Keep Animated vs Switch to Reanimated

| Scenario | `Animated` API | Reanimated 4 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One-shot fade on mount | ✅ | Overkill |
| Button press scale | ✅ | Either works |
| Finger-following drag | ❌ | ✅ `Gesture.Pan` + shared values |
| Swipe-to-delete row | ❌ | ✅ |
| Shared element hero | ❌ | ✅ `sharedTransitionTag` |
| List insert/delete motion | ❌ | ✅ entering/exiting + `Layout` |
| 60fps during fast scroll | Risky on JS thread | ✅ UI-thread worklets |

**Rule of thumb:** If the animation follows a finger or runs while a `FlatList` scrolls, use Reanimated 4. If it is a short, fire-and-forget transition on a static screen, `Animated` is acceptable.

> **Related:** [react-native-reanimated 4](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/react-native-reanimated-4/) - full cookbook for shared values | [Gesture Conflict Resolution](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/gesture-conflict-resolution/) - scroll vs swipe rows

---

## Intermediate Examples

### 8. Reanimated Shared Value - UI-Thread Fade

Shared values mutate off the React render path - the foundation of Reanimated 4.

```tsx
import { useEffect } from "react";
import { StyleSheet } from "react-native";
import Animated, {
  useAnimatedStyle,
  useSharedValue,
  withTiming,
} from "react-native-reanimated";
 
export function ReanimatedFadeIn({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  const opacity = useSharedValue(0);
 
  useEffect(() => {
    opacity.value = withTiming(1, { duration: 300 });
  }, [opacity]);
 
  const style = useAnimatedStyle(() => ({
    opacity: opacity.value,
  }));
 
  return <Animated.View style={[styles.card, style]}>{children}</Animated.View>;
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  card: { padding: 16, borderRadius: 12, backgroundColor: "#fff" },
});
```

* **`useSharedValue`** holds animation state on the UI thread - updating `.value` does not re-render React.
* **`useAnimatedStyle`** returns a style object recomputed every frame inside a worklet.
* Import `Animated` from `react-native-reanimated`, not `react-native`, when using worklet-driven styles.

> **Related:** [Worklets & Bundle Mode](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/worklets-and-bundle-mode/) - how worklets are compiled and debugged

---

### 9. withSpring - Gesture-Ready Motion

Springs feel responsive when linked to release velocity - Reanimated's default for interactive UI.

```tsx
import { Pressable, Text } from "react-native";
import Animated, {
  useAnimatedStyle,
  useSharedValue,
  withSpring,
} from "react-native-reanimated";
 
export function SpringChip({ label }: { label: string }) {
  const scale = useSharedValue(1);
 
  const style = useAnimatedStyle(() => ({
    transform: [{ scale: scale.value }],
  }));
 
  return (
    <Pressable
      onPressIn={() => {
        scale.value = withSpring(0.94, { damping: 15, stiffness: 400 });
      }}
      onPressOut={() => {
        scale.value = withSpring(1);
      }}
    >
      <Animated.View style={[{ padding: 12, borderRadius: 999, backgroundColor: "#dbeafe" }, style]}>
        <Text>{label}</Text>
      </Animated.View>
    </Pressable>
  );
}
```

* **`withSpring`** accepts `damping`, `stiffness`, and `mass` - tune once per design system, reuse via constants.
* Press handlers update shared values directly - still fine for simple chips; pans use Gesture Handler instead.
* Springs on the UI thread stay smooth even when JS is busy parsing a large API response.

> **Related:** [react-native-gesture-handler](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/react-native-gesture-handler/) - `Gesture.Pan().onUpdate` driving the same shared value

---

### 10. JS Thread vs UI Thread - Mental Model

Understanding where frames execute prevents "mysterious jank" in production.

```text
JS thread (React)                    UI thread (native)
─────────────────                    ───────────────────
React render → commit                Gesture recognition
setState every frame ❌              Shared value updates ✅
Animated without native driver ❌    useAnimatedStyle ✅
Business logic, networking         withTiming / withSpring
```

```tsx
// ❌ Runs on JS thread - competes with React reconciliation
const [offset, setOffset] = useState(0);
onPanResponderMove: (_, g) => setOffset(g.dx);
 
// ✅ Runs on UI thread - 60fps even during heavy JS work
const translateX = useSharedValue(0);
Gesture.Pan().onUpdate((e) => {
  translateX.value = e.translationX;
});
```

* **60fps means 16.7ms per frame** - one expensive JS render during a pan drops a frame visibly.
* Use React DevTools and the JS thread monitor; use Reanimated's debug logging for worklet issues.
* Profile on a **mid-tier Android device** - iPhone Pro simulators mask JS-thread contention.

> **Related:** [Animations Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/best-practices/) - profiling checklist before shipping motion | [../performance/best-practices/best-practices.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/performance/best-practices/) - device matrix for performance review

Dokumen: Animations Best Practices
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/best-practices/

# Animations Best Practices

A condensed summary of the 25 most important best practices drawn from every page in this section.

Highlights / Animations Best Practices

* Install Reanimated and Gesture Handler with npx expo install - never hand-pin versions on SDK 57
* react-native-reanimated/plugin must be the last babel.config.js plugin
* Finger-driven motion belongs on the UI thread via shared values - not setState per frame
* Profile on mid-tier Android before shipping gesture-heavy feeds
* Tune activeOffset and failOffset before rewriting scroll structures for swipe rows
* Respect reduced motion - provide instant state fallbacks when accessibility settings demand it

1. **Install with `npx expo install`:** `react-native-reanimated` and `react-native-gesture-handler` versions must match the SDK 57 matrix - manual npm pins cause native build failures.
2. **Babel plugin last:** `react-native-reanimated/plugin` is always the final entry in `babel.config.js` - other plugins after it break worklet transforms.
3. **Clear Metro after plugin changes:** Run `npx expo start --clear` whenever Babel or Reanimated versions change - stale caches produce "failed to create a worklet" errors.
4. **Wrap root with GestureHandlerRootView:** Required in `app/_layout.tsx` for pans, drawers, and stack-adjacent gestures - no compile-time warning when missing.
5. **Import Animated from Reanimated for worklets:** `react-native-reanimated`'s `Animated` supports `useAnimatedStyle`, entering/exiting, and shared transitions - not `react-native`'s `Animated`.
6. **Use shared values for interactive motion:** `useSharedValue` updates do not re-render React - the foundation of 60fps drags, springs, and scroll-linked styles.
7. **Never setState every animation frame:** `onPanResponderMove` or gesture `onUpdate` calling `setState` competes with React reconciliation - dropped frames on any mid-tier device.
8. **Prefer Reanimated for gesture-linked UI:** If motion follows a finger or runs during list scroll, graduate from the legacy `Animated` API to Reanimated 4.
9. **Keep Animated for simple one-shot fades:** Short opacity timing on static mount with `useNativeDriver: true` is acceptable - do not over-engineer toast fades.
10. **Know the native driver boundary:** `opacity` and `transform` support `useNativeDriver: true`; `width`, `height`, and `flex` need Reanimated layout animations or `useAnimatedStyle`.
11. **Pair RNGH with Reanimated:** Gesture recognition on the native thread plus shared-value updates on the UI thread - Pressable alone cannot match pan frequency.
12. **Tune pans before rewriting scroll trees:** `activeOffsetX` and `failOffsetY` fix most swipe-row vs `ScrollView` conflicts - see [Gesture Conflict Resolution](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/gesture-conflict-resolution/).
13. **Use simultaneousWithExternalGesture for swipe rows:** Wire the parent `ScrollView` / `FlatList` ref so horizontal row pans coexist with vertical scroll after offset qualification.
14. **Import inner scrollables from RNGH when nested scroll fails:** Switch the **inner** horizontal `FlatList` first - not both axes blindly ([Nested Scrollables](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/lists-scrolling/nested-scrollables/)).
15. **Stable keys for animated lists:** `keyExtractor` must return server ids - index keys make layout animations and shared transition tags jump between wrong rows.
16. **One entering/exiting wrapper per row:** Apply `FadeIn` / `SlideInRight` and `layout={Layout}` on a single `Animated.View` per `renderItem` - not on every nested `Text`.
17. **Shorten exiting duration:** Exiting at 150–220ms feels snappier than symmetric 400ms enter/exit - users perceive delete feedback faster.
18. **Cap stagger delays on long lists:** `FadeInDown.delay(index * 40)` beyond ~12–20 items adds noticeable mount latency - stagger only the first viewport.
19. **Unique sharedTransitionTag per entity:** Include stable ids in tag strings - duplicate tags across list rows break hero transitions ([Shared Element Transitions](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/shared-element-transitions/)).
20. **Match tags exactly across stack screens:** List cell and Expo Router detail route must use the same tag builder - pair with nested stacks ([Stack Navigation](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/stack-navigation/)).
21. **runOnJS sparingly:** Bridge to navigation, `setState`, and analytics on gesture **end** - not inside `onUpdate` every frame.
22. **Extract shared worklet helpers:** Clamp, rubber-band, and interpolate functions belong in `'worklet'` modules - reduces Hermes duplication and eases testing ([Worklets & Bundle Mode](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/worklets-and-bundle-mode/)).
23. **Profile release on mid-tier Android:** iPhone Pro simulators and Expo Go on Mac hide JS-thread contention - Flashlight or RN DevTools on a low-RAM device before ship.
24. **Respect reduced motion:** Check `AccessibilityInfo.isReduceMotionEnabled()` and skip or shorten entering/layout animations - provide instant state transitions as fallback.
25. **Run the gesture checklist before release:** Walk swipe-in-scroll, nested rails, sheet-over-feed, shared hero pop, and fast-list delete on Android - simulators miss scroll-vs-swipe races.

## FAQs

Animated API or Reanimated 4 for a new SDK 57 app?

* Default to Reanimated 4 for any interactive or list-adjacent motion.
* `Animated` remains fine for rare static fades with `useNativeDriver: true`.

What is the single most common animation bug?

* Updating React state every pan frame instead of shared values - visible as stutter during network or list work on the JS thread.

Do I need Gesture Handler without pans?

* Layout-only Reanimated (`FadeIn`, `Layout`) does not require RNGH.
* Add Gesture Handler the moment users swipe, pinch, or drag - and wrap the app root when you do.

When should I enable Reanimated bundle mode?

* After release profiling shows Hermes RAM climbing across many animated screens and shared worklet extraction is insufficient.

How do animations interact with list performance?

* Virtualized lists plus per-frame JS work is the worst combination - keep animation math on UI thread and avoid entering animations on every pagination page without profiling.

# Animations & Gestures Highlights Summary

Highlights / Animations & Gestures Highlights Summary

* Install with npx expo install - Reanimated 4 and gesture-handler versions must match SDK 57
* Shared values live on the UI thread - updating .value does not trigger React re-renders
* Gesture Handler runs recognition on the native thread - Pressable cannot match pan frequency
