## [Animations Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/animations-basics/)

* Install with npx expo install - Reanimated 4 and gesture-handler versions must match SDK 57
* react-native-reanimated/plugin must be the last entry in babel.config.js plugins
* Animated + useNativeDriver handles simple fades and springs on the native driver
* Reanimated 4 runs gesture-driven frames on the UI thread - the path to reliable 60fps
* Never animate layout properties with useNativeDriver: true - width, height, and flex need Reanimated or Layout animations
* Profile on a mid-tier Android device - simulators hide JS-thread jank during scroll + animation

## [react-native-reanimated 4](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/react-native-reanimated-4/)

* Shared values live on the UI thread - updating .value does not trigger React re-renders
* useAnimatedStyle recomputes styles inside worklets every frame at 60fps
* withTiming and withSpring are the two primitives for almost all motion curves
* Import Animated from react-native-reanimated, not react-native, for worklet components
* react-native-reanimated/plugin must remain the last babel.config.js plugin
* runOnJS bridges back to React only when you must call setState or navigation

## [react-native-gesture-handler](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/react-native-gesture-handler/)

* Gesture Handler runs recognition on the native thread - Pressable cannot match pan frequency
* Gesture.Pan and Gesture.Pinch are the two primitives for draggable and zoomable UI
* Wrap gestures in GestureDetector - one detector per composed gesture object
* Gesture.Simultaneous and Gesture.Race compose multi-gesture interactions
* GestureHandlerRootView at the app root is mandatory - drawers and stacks depend on it
* Pair every high-frequency gesture with Reanimated shared values, not setState

## [Layout Animations](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/layout-animations/)

* Entering and exiting props animate mount/unmount without manual opacity tweens
* FadeIn, SlideInRight, and FadeOut are the most common presets in production lists
* Layout prop animates position and size when siblings reorder or flex changes
* Customize presets with .duration(), .springify(), and .delay()
* Wrap list rows in Animated.View from reanimated - not react-native Animated
* Disable layout animations on huge lists if profiling shows mount pressure

## [Worklets & Bundle Mode](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/worklets-and-bundle-mode/)

* Worklets are JavaScript functions compiled to run on the UI thread via the Reanimated Babel plugin
* The 'worklet' directive marks custom functions safe for UI-thread execution
* Bundle mode pre-packages worklets to reduce Hermes memory duplication in large apps
* Never call setState, fetch, or navigation directly inside a worklet
* runOnJS is the controlled bridge back to the React JS thread
* Misconfigured plugins produce 'failed to create a worklet' at runtime - always clear Metro cache after fixes

## [Shared Element Transitions](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/shared-element-transitions/)

* sharedTransitionTag pairs the same logical element across two screens for hero motion
* Works with Expo Router stacks - both screens must mount Animated views with matching tags
* Use unique tags per list item - include stable id in the tag string
* Native stack performs better than JS stack for shared transitions
* Navigate after press - detail screen reuses the tag on the enlarged hero
* Fall back to fade or scale when tags mismatch or lists recycle unpredictably

## [Gesture Conflict Resolution](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/gesture-conflict-resolution/)

* Vertical ScrollView and horizontal Pan compete - tune activeOffsetX and failOffsetY first
* simultaneousWithExternalGesture lets row pans cooperate with parent scroll native handlers
* Bottom sheets need exclusive vertical pans - fail horizontal child gestures when sheet is mid-drag
* Use RNGH ScrollView on the inner rail before rewriting the whole tree
* Native scroll gestures beat JS PanResponder - always prefer RNGH composition APIs
* Test on Android mid-tier hardware - iOS simulators hide scroll vs swipe races

## [Animations Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/best-practices/)

* Install Reanimated and Gesture Handler with npx expo install - never hand-pin versions on SDK 57
* react-native-reanimated/plugin must be the last babel.config.js plugin
* Finger-driven motion belongs on the UI thread via shared values - not setState per frame
* Profile on mid-tier Android before shipping gesture-heavy feeds
* Tune activeOffset and failOffset before rewriting scroll structures for swipe rows
* Respect reduced motion - provide instant state fallbacks when accessibility settings demand it

Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/layout-animations/

# Layout Animations

Reanimated layout animations declaratively handle **entering**, **exiting**, and **layout** changes. Items fade or slide in when added, collapse out when removed, and glide when lists reorder - without `setState` every frame.

Highlights / Layout Animations

* Entering and exiting props animate mount/unmount without manual opacity tweens
* FadeIn, SlideInRight, and FadeOut are the most common presets in production lists
* Layout prop animates position and size when siblings reorder or flex changes
* Customize presets with .duration(), .springify(), and .delay()
* Wrap list rows in Animated.View from reanimated - not react-native Animated
* Disable layout animations on huge lists if profiling shows mount pressure

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
npx expo install react-native-reanimated
```

```tsx
import Animated, { FadeIn, FadeOut, Layout } from "react-native-reanimated";
 
export function AnimatedListItem({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <Animated.View
      entering={FadeIn.duration(220)}
      exiting={FadeOut.duration(180)}
      layout={Layout.springify()}
    >
      {children}
    </Animated.View>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// Slide from trailing edge - common for inbox rows
import { SlideInRight, SlideOutLeft } from "react-native-reanimated";
 
<Animated.View entering={SlideInRight.springify()} exiting={SlideOutLeft.duration(200)} />
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Todo lists, chat bubbles, and notification feeds with insert/delete
* Filter chips appearing/disappearing when toggling categories
* Grid reorder after drag-and-drop (with `Layout` on siblings)
* Accordion sections expanding/collapsing with sibling reflow

## Working Example

Filterable task list - items animate in on add, out on delete, and reposition on filter.

```tsx
// components/task-list.tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { FlatList, Pressable, StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
import Animated, {
  FadeInDown,
  FadeOutUp,
  Layout,
  SlideInRight,
  SlideOutLeft,
} from "react-native-reanimated";
 
type Task = { id: string; title: string; done: boolean };
 
const AnimatedPressable = Animated.createAnimatedComponent(Pressable);
 
export function TaskList() {
  const [tasks, setTasks] = useState<Task[]>([
    { id: "1", title: "Ship animations", done: false },
    { id: "2", title: "Profile on Android", done: false },
  ]);
  const [showDone, setShowDone] = useState(true);
 
  const visible = tasks.filter((t) => showDone || !t.done);
 
  const toggleDone = (id: string) => {
    setTasks((prev) =>
      prev.map((t) => (t.id === id ? { ...t, done: !t.done } : t))
    );
  };
 
  const remove = (id: string) => {
    setTasks((prev) => prev.filter((t) => t.id !== id));
  };
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.screen}>
      <Pressable onPress={() => setShowDone((v) => !v)} style={styles.filter}>
        <Text>{showDone ? "Hide completed" : "Show all"}</Text>
      </Pressable>
 
      <FlatList
        data={visible}
        keyExtractor={(item) => item.id}
        renderItem={({ item }) => (
          <AnimatedPressable
            entering={SlideInRight.duration(250)}
            exiting={SlideOutLeft.duration(200)}
            layout={Layout.springify().damping(18)}
            onPress={() => toggleDone(item.id)}
            onLongPress={() => remove(item.id)}
            style={[styles.row, item.done && styles.rowDone]}
          >
            <Text>{item.title}</Text>
          </AnimatedPressable>
        )}
        ItemSeparatorComponent={() => <View style={styles.separator} />}
      />
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  screen: { flex: 1, padding: 16 },
  filter: { marginBottom: 12 },
  row: { padding: 16, backgroundColor: "#f8fafc", borderRadius: 10 },
  rowDone: { opacity: 0.6 },
  separator: { height: 8 },
});
```

```tsx
// Staggered grid entrance - delay per index
import { FadeInDown } from "react-native-reanimated";
 
function GridCell({ index, children }: { index: number; children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <Animated.View entering={FadeInDown.delay(index * 40).springify()}>
      {children}
    </Animated.View>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// Accordion section - layout animates siblings when height changes
import { FadeIn, FadeOut, Layout } from "react-native-reanimated";
 
function AccordionPanel({ open, children }: { open: boolean; children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <Animated.View layout={Layout.springify()}>
      {open ? (
        <Animated.View entering={FadeIn} exiting={FadeOut}>
          {children}
        </Animated.View>
      ) : null}
    </Animated.View>
  );
}
```

## Deep Dive

### Entering animations

Import presets from `react-native-reanimated`:

| Preset | Motion |
| --- | --- |
| `FadeIn` / `FadeOut` | Opacity |
| `SlideInRight` / `SlideOutLeft` | Horizontal slide |
| `SlideInDown` / `SlideOutUp` | Vertical slide |
| `ZoomIn` / `ZoomOut` | Scale |
| `FadeInDown` | Combined fade + slide (popular for feeds) |

Chain modifiers:

```tsx
FadeIn.duration(300).delay(50).springify().damping(14)
```

* **Entering** runs when the view mounts with the animation prop present.
* Custom builders exist (`Entering` / `Exiting` factories) for design-system tokens.

### Exiting animations

* **Exiting** requires the view to unmount from React tree - conditional render or list filter removal.
* `FlatList` recycles rows - exiting animations fire only when the item leaves `data`, not on scroll off-screen.
* Keep exiting duration shorter than entering - 150–220ms feels snappy.

### Layout animations

`layout={Layout}` animates position and bounds when:

* Siblings reorder in flex layout
* Item height changes (accordion, multiline text wrap)
* Filter removes items and remaining rows reflow

```tsx
layout={Layout.springify().damping(15).stiffness(120)}
// or
layout={Layout.duration(250)}
```

* Apply `layout` on the **moving** container, not only inner text.
* For `FlatList`, put `layout` on the row wrapper returned from `renderItem`.

### List reorder

When drag-and-drop changes `data` order:

1. Update array order in state (or server-confirmed order).
2. Ensure **stable `keyExtractor`** - index keys break layout animation.
3. Add `layout={Layout.springify()}` on row `Animated.View`.

For drag gestures paired with reorder, combine RNGH pan + `runOnJS` reorder callback - see [react-native-gesture-handler](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/react-native-gesture-handler/).

### Performance notes

* Layout animations run on the UI thread but still cost GPU/CPU on large lists.
* Cap stagger `delay` on long lists - `index * 40` beyond ~20 items adds noticeable lag.
* Consider disabling entering on pagination append (page 2+) if mount jank appears.

## Gotchas

* **Using react-native Animated.View** - Entering/exiting props are ignored. **Fix:** Import `Animated` from `react-native-reanimated`.
* **No exiting on ScrollView map without key change** - React reconciler reuses nodes. **Fix:** Remove item from state array so React unmounts the row.
* **Index keys in lists** - Wrong row animates on delete. **Fix:** Stable string ids in `keyExtractor`.
* **layout on every nested Text** - Over-animates inner typography. **Fix:** One `Animated.View` wrapper per row.
* **Huge entering stagger** - List of 200 items each delays 50ms - UI feels frozen. **Fix:** Stagger only first screen (`index < 12`).
* **Combining Layout with flex wrap grids** - Unexpected jumps when line breaks change. **Fix:** Fixed cell widths or measure with `onLayout` before animating.
* **Modal unmount cuts exiting short** - Parent disappears before exit completes. **Fix:** Delay navigation pop until `exiting` duration elapses (`runOnJS` + timeout).

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Layout animations (Reanimated) | List insert/delete/reorder in RN | Web-only CSS transitions suffice |
| `Animated` timing on opacity | Single static fade | Sibling reflow or list removal |
| `LayoutAnimation` (RN core) | Legacy Android-only quick wins | Cross-platform consistency required |
| No animation | Very long virtualized feeds | User expects feedback on destructive delete |
| Lottie | Branded empty-state illustrations | Per-row list insert motion |

## FAQs

How do I install layout animations on Expo SDK 57?

```bash
npx expo install react-native-reanimated
```

Layout animations ship with Reanimated 4 - no extra package. Confirm Babel plugin is last in `babel.config.js`.

Why does exiting not run in my FlatList?

* Item still exists in `data` - you only scrolled away.
* Row unmounted without `exiting` prop on an Reanimated component.
* Parent list remounted (key change on `FlatList`) - exit cancelled.

FadeIn or SlideInRight for feed rows?

* `FadeIn` / `FadeInDown` for dense feeds (less visual noise).
* `SlideInRight` for inbox/action lists where directional metaphor helps.

What does layout={Layout.springify()} do?

When sibling views change position or size, the view animates to its new layout box with a spring physics curve instead of jumping instantly.

Can I use custom durations per design system?

Yes - centralize tokens:

```tsx
export const enterRow = FadeInDown.duration(220).springify().damping(16);
export const exitRow = FadeOutUp.duration(180);
```

Do layout animations work with FlashList?

Often yes with an `Animated.View` wrapper, but heavy entering on fast scroll can jank - profile on Android. Disable entering for off-screen prefetch if needed.

How do layout animations interact with swipe-to-delete?

Trigger remove from state on swipe end; `exiting` handles collapse. Coordinate with [Gesture Conflict Resolution](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/gesture-conflict-resolution/) so scroll and swipe do not fight.

# react-native-gesture-handler

Gesture Handler (RNGH) moves touch recognition to the native layer so pans, pinches, and multi-touch compositions stay at **60fps**. On Expo SDK 57, install it alongside Reanimated 4 and drive animated values from gesture callbacks on the UI thread.

Highlights / react-native-gesture-handler

* Gesture Handler runs recognition on the native thread - Pressable cannot match pan frequency
* Gesture.Pan and Gesture.Pinch are the two primitives for draggable and zoomable UI
* Wrap gestures in GestureDetector - one detector per composed gesture object
* Gesture.Simultaneous and Gesture.Race compose multi-gesture interactions
* GestureHandlerRootView at the app root is mandatory - drawers and stacks depend on it
* Pair every high-frequency gesture with Reanimated shared values, not setState

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
npx expo install react-native-gesture-handler react-native-reanimated
```

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
import { GestureHandlerRootView } from "react-native-gesture-handler";
 
export default function RootLayout() {
  return (
    <GestureHandlerRootView style={{ flex: 1 }}>
      <Stack />
    </GestureHandlerRootView>
  );
}
```

```tsx
import { StyleSheet } from "react-native";
import { Gesture, GestureDetector } from "react-native-gesture-handler";
import Animated, {
  useAnimatedStyle,
  useSharedValue,
  withSpring,
} from "react-native-reanimated";
 
export function SwipeableTile() {
  const translateX = useSharedValue(0);
 
  const pan = Gesture.Pan()
    .activeOffsetX([-12, 12])
    .onUpdate((e) => {
      translateX.value = e.translationX;
    })
    .onEnd(() => {
      translateX.value = withSpring(0);
    });
 
  const style = useAnimatedStyle(() => ({
    transform: [{ translateX: translateX.value }],
  }));
 
  return (
    <GestureDetector gesture={pan}>
      <Animated.View style={[styles.tile, style]} />
    </GestureDetector>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  tile: { height: 72, backgroundColor: "#e2e8f0", borderRadius: 12 },
});
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Swipe-to-delete rows, draggable cards, pull handles
* Pinch-to-zoom on images and maps overlays
* Bottom sheets and drawers that compete with scroll views
* Any gesture that must stay smooth while lists scroll

## Working Example

Pinch-to-zoom on an image with simultaneous pan - composed gestures on one detector.

```tsx
// components/zoomable-image.tsx
import { Image, StyleSheet, useWindowDimensions } from "react-native";
import { Gesture, GestureDetector } from "react-native-gesture-handler";
import Animated, {
  useAnimatedStyle,
  useSharedValue,
  withTiming,
} from "react-native-reanimated";
 
type Props = { uri: string };
 
export function ZoomableImage({ uri }: Props) {
  const { width } = useWindowDimensions();
  const scale = useSharedValue(1);
  const savedScale = useSharedValue(1);
  const translateX = useSharedValue(0);
  const translateY = useSharedValue(0);
  const savedX = useSharedValue(0);
  const savedY = useSharedValue(0);
 
  const pinch = Gesture.Pinch()
    .onUpdate((e) => {
      scale.value = savedScale.value * e.scale;
    })
    .onEnd(() => {
      if (scale.value < 1) {
        scale.value = withTiming(1);
        translateX.value = withTiming(0);
        translateY.value = withTiming(0);
        savedScale.value = 1;
        savedX.value = 0;
        savedY.value = 0;
      } else {
        savedScale.value = scale.value;
      }
    });
 
  const pan = Gesture.Pan()
    .minPointers(1)
    .maxPointers(2)
    .onUpdate((e) => {
      if (scale.value > 1) {
        translateX.value = savedX.value + e.translationX;
        translateY.value = savedY.value + e.translationY;
      }
    })
    .onEnd(() => {
      savedX.value = translateX.value;
      savedY.value = translateY.value;
    });
 
  const doubleTap = Gesture.Tap()
    .numberOfTaps(2)
    .onEnd(() => {
      if (scale.value > 1) {
        scale.value = withTiming(1);
        translateX.value = withTiming(0);
        translateY.value = withTiming(0);
        savedScale.value = 1;
        savedX.value = 0;
        savedY.value = 0;
      } else {
        scale.value = withTiming(2);
        savedScale.value = 2;
      }
    });
 
  const composed = Gesture.Simultaneous(
    pinch,
    pan,
    Gesture.Exclusive(doubleTap, Gesture.Tap())
  );
 
  const style = useAnimatedStyle(() => ({
    transform: [
      { translateX: translateX.value },
      { translateY: translateY.value },
      { scale: scale.value },
    ],
  }));
 
  return (
    <GestureDetector gesture={composed}>
      <Animated.View style={{ width, height: width * 0.75 }}>
        <Animated.Image
          source={{ uri }}
          style={[styles.image, style]}
          resizeMode="cover"
        />
      </Animated.View>
    </GestureDetector>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  image: { width: "100%", height: "100%" },
});
```

```tsx
// Swipe threshold with runOnJS - dismiss when pan passes -120px
import { runOnJS } from "react-native-reanimated";
 
const pan = Gesture.Pan()
  .onUpdate((e) => {
    translateX.value = Math.min(0, e.translationX);
  })
  .onEnd((e) => {
    if (e.translationX < -120) {
      runOnJS(onArchive)();
    } else {
      translateX.value = withSpring(0);
    }
  });
```

## Deep Dive

### Gesture.Pan

| Method | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `activeOffsetX/Y` | Require movement before activation - prevents stealing taps |
| `failOffsetY` | Fail pan when vertical movement dominates - scroll handoff |
| `minDistance` | Ignore micro-jitter |
| `onUpdate` | Per-frame translation - keep math only |
| `onEnd` | Snap, dismiss, or `runOnJS` side effects |

```tsx
Gesture.Pan()
  .activeOffsetX([-10, 10])
  .failOffsetY([-15, 15])
```

Use `failOffsetY` on horizontal swipe rows inside vertical `ScrollView` - see [Gesture Conflict Resolution](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/gesture-conflict-resolution/).

### Gesture.Pinch

* `event.scale` is relative to gesture start - multiply against a **saved** shared value on `onEnd`.
* Clamp min/max scale to avoid inverted or microscopic images.
* Pair with pan only when `scale > 1` so unzoomed images do not drift.

### GestureDetector

* One `GestureDetector` wraps one gesture object (simple or composed).
* Child must be a native view or Reanimated component - not a fragment with multiple roots.
* For lists, wrap the **row** content, not the entire `FlatList`.

### Composed gestures

| Composer | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `Gesture.Simultaneous(a, b)` | Both can recognize together (pinch + pan) |
| `Gesture.Race(a, b)` | First winner takes over |
| `Gesture.Exclusive(a, b)` | Higher-priority wins when both match |

```tsx
const drag = Gesture.Pan();
const longPress = Gesture.LongPress().minDuration(400);
const rowGesture = Gesture.Race(longPress, drag);
```

### RNGH ScrollView and FlatList

Import scrollables from `react-native-gesture-handler` when nested scroll causes native conflicts:

```tsx
import { ScrollView } from "react-native-gesture-handler";
```

Prefer this on the **inner** rail first - not both axes blindly (see [Nested Scrollables](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/lists-scrolling/nested-scrollables/)).

## Gotchas

* **No GestureHandlerRootView** - Gestures never activate; no compile-time error. **Fix:** Wrap `app/_layout.tsx` root.
* **setState in onUpdate** - Drops frames immediately. **Fix:** Shared values + `useAnimatedStyle`; `runOnJS` only on end.
* **Pan without activeOffset** - Horizontal row pans steal vertical scroll. **Fix:** `activeOffsetX` + `failOffsetY` tuning per layout.
* **Multiple GestureDetectors nested** - Parent may consume touches before child. **Fix:** Compose with `Simultaneous` / `Native` scroll refs instead of stacking detectors.
* **TouchableOpacity inside GestureDetector** - Double feedback or cancelled presses. **Fix:** Use `Gesture.Tap()` or `Pressable` with `pointerEvents` planning.
* **Reanimated plugin missing** - `onUpdate` throws worklet errors. **Fix:** `react-native-reanimated/plugin` last in Babel config.
* **Testing in Expo Go after native upgrade** - Old dev client lacks RNGH native bits. **Fix:** Rebuild dev client or use current Expo Go matching SDK 57.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Pressable` | Buttons, simple list row taps | Drag, swipe, multi-touch |
| PanResponder (RN core) | Legacy maintenance | New gesture code on SDK 57 |
| `react-native-gesture-handler` | Production pans/pinches | Static non-interactive UI |
| Platform native gestures only | Fully native screens in brownfield | Shared RN component library |
| `@gorhom/bottom-sheet` | Standard sheet physics | Simple modal with no drag |

## FAQs

How do I install Gesture Handler on Expo SDK 57?

```bash
npx expo install react-native-gesture-handler react-native-reanimated
```

Add `GestureHandlerRootView` to root layout. Ensure Reanimated Babel plugin is last.

Why use Gesture.Pan instead of PanResponder?

* RNGH recognizes on the native thread with better scroll handoff.
* API composes cleanly (`Simultaneous`, `Race`) and integrates with Reanimated worklets.

What is activeOffsetX for?

The finger must move horizontally by N pixels before the pan activates. This lets vertical scroll win when the user scrolls a list containing swipeable rows.

Can I attach multiple gestures to one view?

Yes - build one composed gesture and pass it to a single `GestureDetector`. Do not nest multiple detectors on the same view without a composition plan.

Should FlatList come from RNGH or react-native?

Start with RN `FlatList`. Switch the **inner** horizontal list to RNGH `FlatList` when nested scroll gestures fail on Android ([Nested Scrollables](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/lists-scrolling/nested-scrollables/)).

How do gestures interact with Expo Router stacks?

Stack swipe-back is a native gesture. Custom full-screen pans may need `gestureEnabled: false` on the screen or careful `simultaneousWithExternalGesture` - see [Gesture Conflict Resolution](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/gesture-conflict-resolution/).

Do I need react-native-reanimated for gestures?

Not strictly for recognition, but every high-frequency UI update should use Reanimated shared values. `setState` per pan frame will jank.

## Related

* [Animations Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/animations-basics/) - when to graduate from Pressable to RNGH
* [react-native-reanimated 4](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/react-native-reanimated-4/) - shared values driven by gestures
* [Gesture Conflict Resolution](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/gesture-conflict-resolution/) - ScrollView vs swipe rows vs sheets
* [Layout Animations](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/layout-animations/) - motion when rows mount/unmount after swipe

Dokumen: react-native-reanimated 4
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/react-native-reanimated-4/

# react-native-reanimated 4

Reanimated 4 is the default animation engine on Expo SDK 57. Shared values, `useAnimatedStyle`, and timing/spring helpers run on the **UI thread** so gestures and scroll do not stall when JavaScript is busy.

Highlights / react-native-reanimated 4

* Shared values live on the UI thread - updating .value does not trigger React re-renders
* useAnimatedStyle recomputes styles inside worklets every frame at 60fps
* withTiming and withSpring are the two primitives for almost all motion curves
* Import Animated from react-native-reanimated, not react-native, for worklet components
* react-native-reanimated/plugin must remain the last babel.config.js plugin
* runOnJS bridges back to React only when you must call setState or navigation

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
npx expo install react-native-reanimated react-native-gesture-handler
```

```js
// babel.config.js - plugin MUST be last
module.exports = function (api) {
  api.cache(true);
  return {
    presets: ["babel-preset-expo"],
    plugins: ["react-native-reanimated/plugin"],
  };
};
```

```tsx
import { StyleSheet, Text } from "react-native";
import Animated, {
  useAnimatedStyle,
  useSharedValue,
  withSpring,
  withTiming,
} from "react-native-reanimated";
 
export function ReanimatedCard() {
  const scale = useSharedValue(1);
  const opacity = useSharedValue(0);
 
  const animatedStyle = useAnimatedStyle(() => ({
    opacity: opacity.value,
    transform: [{ scale: scale.value }],
  }));
 
  const reveal = () => {
    opacity.value = withTiming(1, { duration: 250 });
    scale.value = withSpring(1, { damping: 14 });
  };
 
  return (
    <Animated.View style={[styles.card, animatedStyle]}>
      <Text onPress={reveal}>Tap to reveal</Text>
    </Animated.View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  card: { padding: 20, borderRadius: 12, backgroundColor: "#f0fdf4" },
});
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Finger-driven pans, pinches, and draggable sheets
* Animations that must stay smooth during list scroll or heavy JS work
* Layout-affecting motion (`width`, `borderRadius`, `backgroundColor`)
* Pairing with Gesture Handler for 60fps interactive UI

## Working Example

A draggable card that snaps back on release - shared value on the UI thread, spring on end.

```bash
npx expo install react-native-reanimated react-native-gesture-handler
```

```tsx
// components/draggable-card.tsx
import { StyleSheet, Text } from "react-native";
import { Gesture, GestureDetector } from "react-native-gesture-handler";
import Animated, {
  useAnimatedStyle,
  useSharedValue,
  withSpring,
} from "react-native-reanimated";
 
const SNAP_BACK = { damping: 18, stiffness: 220 };
 
export function DraggableCard({ title }: { title: string }) {
  const translateX = useSharedValue(0);
  const translateY = useSharedValue(0);
 
  const pan = Gesture.Pan()
    .onUpdate((e) => {
      translateX.value = e.translationX;
      translateY.value = e.translationY;
    })
    .onEnd(() => {
      translateX.value = withSpring(0, SNAP_BACK);
      translateY.value = withSpring(0, SNAP_BACK);
    });
 
  const style = useAnimatedStyle(() => ({
    transform: [
      { translateX: translateX.value },
      { translateY: translateY.value },
    ],
  }));
 
  return (
    <GestureDetector gesture={pan}>
      <Animated.View style={[styles.card, style]}>
        <Text>{title}</Text>
      </Animated.View>
    </GestureDetector>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  card: {
    padding: 20,
    borderRadius: 16,
    backgroundColor: "#fff",
    shadowColor: "#000",
    shadowOpacity: 0.08,
    shadowRadius: 8,
    elevation: 3,
  },
});
```

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx (excerpt)
import { GestureHandlerRootView } from "react-native-gesture-handler";
 
export default function RootLayout() {
  return (
    <GestureHandlerRootView style={{ flex: 1 }}>
      {/* Stack / providers */}
    </GestureHandlerRootView>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// Timing helper - progress bar driven by shared value
import Animated, {
  Easing,
  useAnimatedStyle,
  useSharedValue,
  withTiming,
} from "react-native-reanimated";
 
export function useProgressBar(progress: number) {
  const width = useSharedValue(0);
 
  width.value = withTiming(progress, {
    duration: 400,
    easing: Easing.out(Easing.cubic),
  });
 
  return useAnimatedStyle(() => ({
    width: `${width.value * 100}%`,
  }));
}
```

## Deep Dive

### Shared values

`useSharedValue(initial)` allocates a mutable slot readable and writable from worklets. Assign with `.value`:

```tsx
const offset = useSharedValue(0);
offset.value = 42;           // immediate
offset.value = withTiming(1); // animated transition
```

* Shared values are **not** React state - components do not re-render when they change.
* Read them inside `useAnimatedStyle`, `useDerivedValue`, or gesture callbacks marked as worklets.
* Prefer a small number of shared values per component - derive everything else with `useDerivedValue`.

### useAnimatedStyle

Returns a style object whose getters re-run on the UI thread each frame:

```tsx
const style = useAnimatedStyle(() => ({
  opacity: interpolate(progress.value, [0, 1], [0.4, 1]),
  transform: [{ translateX: offset.value }],
}));
```

* Do not call non-worklet functions inside the callback unless they are imported from Reanimated or marked `'worklet'`.
* Return only style-compatible keys - layout animations use separate `entering` / `exiting` props (see [Layout Animations](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/layout-animations/)).

### withTiming and withSpring

| Helper | Best for | Key options |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `withTiming` | Fades, precise durations, progress bars | `duration`, `easing` |
| `withSpring` | Drags, chips, bottom-sheet snap points | `damping`, `stiffness`, `mass` |

```tsx
opacity.value = withTiming(1, { duration: 200 });
translateY.value = withSpring(0, { damping: 15, stiffness: 120 });
```

* Chain with `withDelay`, `withRepeat`, and `withSequence` for staged motion.
* Cancel in-flight animation by assigning a new animation helper to the same shared value.

### runOnJS - crossing back to React

Worklets cannot call arbitrary JS (navigation, `setState`, analytics). Use `runOnJS`:

```tsx
import { runOnJS } from "react-native-reanimated";
 
const pan = Gesture.Pan().onEnd((e) => {
  if (e.translationX < -120) {
    runOnJS(onDismiss)();
  }
});
```

* Wrap only the minimal callback - keep gesture math on the UI thread.
* `runOnJS` schedules on the JS thread next tick - do not use it per-frame in `onUpdate`.

### Reanimated 4 on SDK 57

* Ships with the New Architecture path in mind - worklets compile via the Babel plugin and execute through JSI.
* Version ~4.x is the SDK 57 matrix entry - install with `npx expo install`, not npm guesses.
* **Bundle mode** (optional) reduces Hermes memory pressure for worklet-heavy apps - see [Worklets & Bundle Mode](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/worklets-and-bundle-mode/).

## Gotchas

* **Babel plugin not last** - Worklets fail to transform; animations stutter on JS thread. **Fix:** Move `react-native-reanimated/plugin` to the end of `plugins` and `npx expo start --clear`.
* **Importing Animated from react-native** - Mixing classic `Animated` with worklet styles causes type and runtime errors. **Fix:** `import Animated from 'react-native-reanimated'` for worklet components.
* **Reading shared values in React render** - `translateX.value` in JSX body does not subscribe to updates. **Fix:** Only read inside `useAnimatedStyle` or `useDerivedValue`; use `useAnimatedProps` for native props.
* **Calling setState inside useAnimatedStyle** - Triggers "Tried to synchronously call a function on a non-worklet thread" errors. **Fix:** `runOnJS(setState)` from gesture end handlers only.
* **Forgetting GestureHandlerRootView** - Gestures never fire; pans appear frozen. **Fix:** Wrap root layout (see [react-native-gesture-handler](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/react-native-gesture-handler/)).
* **Animating width as percentage strings incorrectly** - Some RN versions coerce oddly. **Fix:** Animate numeric width from `onLayout` measurement or use `flex` + `scaleX` for simple bars.
* **Heavy work in onUpdate** - JSON parsing or logging every pan frame drops frames. **Fix:** Keep `onUpdate` to shared-value math; defer work to `onEnd` via `runOnJS`.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Animated` API | One-shot fades on static screens | Finger-following drags or list scroll coupling |
| Reanimated 4 | Gestures, layout, 60fps interactive UI | trivial 200ms opacity fade with no gesture |
| `react-native-animatable` | Declarative CSS-like class animations | Custom gesture-linked physics |
| Lottie (`lottie-react-native`) | Designer-authored vector loops | Interactive draggable components |
| CSS transitions (Expo web only) | Web-only surfaces | Native iOS/Android shipping targets |

## FAQs

How do I install Reanimated 4 on Expo SDK 57?

```bash
npx expo install react-native-reanimated react-native-gesture-handler
```

Verify `babel.config.js` includes `react-native-reanimated/plugin` as the **last** plugin. Restart Metro with `--clear` after install.

What is the difference between useSharedValue and useState?

* `useSharedValue` - UI-thread slot; no React re-render on change; read in worklets.
* `useState` - JS-thread React state; triggers render; never update per animation frame.

When should I use withTiming vs withSpring?

* `withTiming` when design specifies exact duration (modals, progress, cross-fades).
* `withSpring` when motion should feel physical (drags, snap-back, bouncy toggles).

Can I use Reanimated without Gesture Handler?

Yes for mount animations, layout transitions, and press-driven timing. Any pan/pinch or scroll conflict scenario should add Gesture Handler.

Why does my animation work in dev but not in release?

* Missing Babel plugin is the top cause - production bundles skip worklet transforms.
* Also check Proguard rules on Android bare builds and stale Metro cache after upgrades.

How do I debug worklets?

* Enable Reanimated logger in dev: `configureReanimatedLogger` (see [Worklets & Bundle Mode](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/worklets-and-bundle-mode/)).
* If you see "failed to create a worklet", the Babel plugin is misconfigured.

Does Reanimated 4 require the New Architecture?

SDK 57 projects increasingly run New Architecture by default. Reanimated 4 targets that stack; older architecture may still work but team support focuses on Fabric + Hermes.

How do I animate colors?

Use `interpolateColor` inside `useAnimatedStyle`:

```tsx
backgroundColor: interpolateColor(progress.value, [0, 1], ["#ef4444", "#22c55e"])
```

Dokumen: Architecture Best Practices
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/best-practices/

# Architecture Best Practices

A condensed summary of the 25 most important best practices drawn from every page in this section.

Highlights / Architecture Best Practices

* Start with feature slices - add FSD layers and clean architecture when boundaries hurt
* Thin Expo Router routes; fat feature modules with public index.ts APIs
* TanStack Query for server state; Zustand for small global client state
* Factory functions and AppServicesProvider - no Java-style DI containers on day one
* Modular monolith + APP\_VARIANT before splitting into multiple apps
* Run the refactoring checklist on the five largest files before major releases

1. **Start with feature slices, not microservices:** Colocate screens, hooks, and components per product area in `features/<name>/` - evolve structure with team size, not day-one distributed systems.
2. **Keep Expo Router routes thin:** `app/**/*.tsx` re-exports feature screens and parses params - business logic belongs in `src/features/`, not route files.
3. **Expose a public API per feature:** Curate `features/<name>/index.ts` - sibling features import the barrel, never deep paths into `components/` or `model/`.
4. **Respect inward dependency flow:** `app → features → entities → shared` - shared code never imports features; entities never import features.
5. **Put shared primitives in `shared/ui`:** Generic `Button` and `Screen` live in shared; domain-specific `UserAvatar` lives in `entities/user/ui`.
6. **Model nouns in entities:** Plain types and pure functions for `User`, `Order` - zero React imports, testable in Node without a renderer.
7. **Hide IO behind adapters:** `createOrdersApi(client)` and `createSecureTokenStorage()` - screens and use cases never call `fetch` or `SecureStore` directly.
8. **Add use cases when tests need seams:** Extract `signIn`, `placeOrder` use cases when hooks mix IO, branching rules, and UI state - not for every button toggle.
9. **Return discriminated unions from use cases:** `{ ok: false, error: "network" }` beats thrown errors across layer boundaries - callers handle failures explicitly.
10. **Wire dependencies at the composition root:** `AppServicesProvider` in `app/_layout.tsx` binds production adapters - avoid module-scope singletons.
11. **Prefer factory injection over DI frameworks:** `createX(deps)` plus React context covers mobile needs - skip tsyringe/Inversify unless org mandates it.
12. **Default to TanStack Query for server state:** Lists, details, and mutations belong in Query cache - not Redux or Zustand slices duplicating API data.
13. **Use Zustand for small global client state:** Cart, preferences, and UI chrome - selectors prevent list re-render storms; not for server JSON blobs.
14. **Keep ephemeral UI state local:** Sheet open state and accordion index stay in the screen tree until a second unrelated route genuinely needs them.
15. **Put URL state in Expo Router params:** Filters and tabs via `useLocalSearchParams` - shareable deep links beat global store keys.
16. **Document navigation choice in an ADR:** Greenfield SDK 57 apps default to Expo Router; brownfield React Navigation stays valid - record the decision for onboarding.
17. **Map FSD layers pragmatically:** `app/`, `features/`, `entities/`, `shared/` - skip `widgets/` and `pages/` until a composite block repeats across routes.
18. **Enforce boundaries with ESLint:** `no-restricted-imports` blocking `@/features/*/components/*` - folder conventions alone fail at 10+ features.
19. **Modular monolith before multi-app:** One repo with `APP_VARIANT` and feature flags until bundle IDs, compliance, or release cadence truly diverge.
20. **Separate EAS Update channels per variant:** `production-consumer` vs `production-business` - wrong channel updates the wrong store listing.
21. **Centralize config in `getAppConfig()`:** Read `Constants.expoConfig?.extra` once - features do not scatter `process.env` and `__DEV__` branches.
22. **Orchestrate cross-feature flows at routes:** Pass `onAddToCart` callbacks from route files - features do not import sibling feature stores.
23. **Run the refactoring checklist before RC:** Audit top five files by line count and import fan-out - god modules block parallel PRs and SDK upgrades.
24. **Extract incrementally, one boundary per PR:** Move one hook or component per merge - abandon multi-week "cleanup" branches that diverge from `main`.
25. **Match architecture investment to risk:** Auth, payments, and offline sync earn ports and use cases - three-screen MVPs earn hooks and an API module until complexity proves otherwise.

## FAQs

When should we adopt full Clean Architecture?

When you need swappable IO (mock/staging/prod), compliance unit tests on business rules, or multiple adapters per feature - not on day one of a CRUD app.

Is Expo Router mandatory on SDK 57?

Default for greenfield apps. Brownfield React Navigation remains supported - migrate when deep linking pain exceeds migration cost.

How many global stores is too many?

More than Query + one client store (Zustand or Context) warrants an audit. Server data should not live in client stores.

Dokumen: Clean Architecture on Mobile
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/clean-architecture-on-mobile/

# Clean Architecture on Mobile

Clean Architecture separates **what the app does** (entities, use cases) from **how it talks to the world** (adapters). On React Native, that means testable use cases in TypeScript - not abstract factories for every button press.

Highlights / Clean Architecture on Mobile

* Entities are plain types + pure functions - zero React imports
* Use cases orchestrate one user intent - signIn, placeOrder, syncOfflineQueue
* Adapters implement ports - RestAuthGateway, SecureTokenStorage
* Screens call use cases through hooks - they never import fetch or AsyncStorage
* Add layers when tests need swappable IO - not on day one of a three-screen app
* One use case per file keeps mobile workflows readable without Java-style ceremony

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```text
src/features/auth/
├── domain/
│   ├── entities.ts          # User, Session
│   ├── ports.ts             # AuthGateway, TokenStorage (interfaces)
│   └── use-cases/
│       ├── signIn.ts
│       └── signOut.ts
├── adapters/
│   ├── restAuthGateway.ts
│   └── secureTokenStorage.ts
├── model/
│   └── useSignIn.ts         # hook wires use case + React state
└── ui/
    └── SignInScreen.tsx
```

```ts
// domain/ports.ts - interfaces only
import type { Session, User } from "./entities";
 
export type AuthGateway = {
  authenticate(email: string, password: string): Promise<User>;
};
 
export type TokenStorage = {
  save(session: Session): Promise<void>;
  load(): Promise<Session | null>;
  clear(): Promise<void>;
};
```

**When to reach for this:**

* You must swap API implementations (mock, staging, offline) without touching screens.
* Compliance or QA demands unit tests on business rules without a device farm.
* Multiple features share the same orchestration (`syncCart`, `validateCoupon`).
* A god hook mixes `fetch`, `AsyncStorage`, and navigation - and every change breaks tests.

## Working Example

```ts
// src/features/auth/domain/entities.ts
export type User = {
  id: string;
  email: string;
  displayName: string;
};
 
export type Session = {
  accessToken: string;
  user: User;
};
```

```ts
// src/features/auth/domain/ports.ts
import type { Session, User } from "./entities";
 
export type AuthGateway = {
  authenticate(email: string, password: string): Promise<User>;
};
 
export type TokenStorage = {
  save(session: Session): Promise<void>;
  load(): Promise<Session | null>;
  clear(): Promise<void>;
};
```

```ts
// src/features/auth/domain/use-cases/signIn.ts
import type { Session } from "../entities";
import type { AuthGateway, TokenStorage } from "../ports";
 
export type SignInDeps = {
  authGateway: AuthGateway;
  tokenStorage: TokenStorage;
  createSession: (user: Awaited<ReturnType<AuthGateway["authenticate"]>>) => Session;
};
 
export type SignInResult =
  | { ok: true; session: Session }
  | { ok: false; error: "invalid_credentials" | "network" | "unknown" };
 
export async function signIn(
  deps: SignInDeps,
  input: { email: string; password: string }
): Promise<SignInResult> {
  try {
    const user = await deps.authGateway.authenticate(input.email, input.password);
    const session = deps.createSession(user);
    await deps.tokenStorage.save(session);
    return { ok: true, session };
  } catch (e) {
    if (e instanceof Error && e.message === "INVALID_CREDENTIALS") {
      return { ok: false, error: "invalid_credentials" };
    }
    if (e instanceof Error && e.message === "NETWORK") {
      return { ok: false, error: "network" };
    }
    return { ok: false, error: "unknown" };
  }
}
```

```ts
// src/features/auth/adapters/restAuthGateway.ts
import type { AuthGateway } from "../domain/ports";
import type { User } from "../domain/entities";
 
export function createRestAuthGateway(baseUrl: string): AuthGateway {
  return {
    async authenticate(email, password) {
      const response = await fetch(`${baseUrl}/auth/login`, {
        method: "POST",
        headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
        body: JSON.stringify({ email, password }),
      });
      if (response.status === 401) throw new Error("INVALID_CREDENTIALS");
      if (!response.ok) throw new Error("NETWORK");
      return response.json() as Promise<User>;
    },
  };
}
```

```ts
// src/features/auth/adapters/secureTokenStorage.ts
import * as SecureStore from "expo-secure-store";
import type { TokenStorage } from "../domain/ports";
import type { Session } from "../domain/entities";
 
const KEY = "session";
 
export function createSecureTokenStorage(): TokenStorage {
  return {
    async save(session) {
      await SecureStore.setItemAsync(KEY, JSON.stringify(session));
    },
    async load() {
      const raw = await SecureStore.getItemAsync(KEY);
      return raw ? (JSON.parse(raw) as Session) : null;
    },
    async clear() {
      await SecureStore.deleteItemAsync(KEY);
    },
  };
}
```

```tsx
// src/features/auth/model/useSignIn.ts
import { useCallback, useState } from "react";
import { signIn } from "../domain/use-cases/signIn";
import { createRestAuthGateway } from "../adapters/restAuthGateway";
import { createSecureTokenStorage } from "../adapters/secureTokenStorage";
import { getAppConfig } from "@/shared/config/env";
import type { Session } from "../domain/entities";
 
const authGateway = createRestAuthGateway(getAppConfig().apiBaseUrl);
const tokenStorage = createSecureTokenStorage();
 
export function useSignIn() {
  const [pending, setPending] = useState(false);
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);
 
  const submit = useCallback(async (email: string, password: string): Promise<Session | null> => {
    setPending(true);
    setError(null);
    const result = await signIn(
      {
        authGateway,
        tokenStorage,
        createSession: (user) => ({ accessToken: `mock-token-${user.id}`, user }),
      },
      { email, password }
    );
    setPending(false);
    if (!result.ok) {
      setError(result.error);
      return null;
    }
    return result.session;
  }, []);
 
  return { submit, pending, error };
}
```

```tsx
// src/features/auth/ui/SignInScreen.tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { StyleSheet, Text, TextInput, View } from "react-native";
import { Button } from "@/shared/ui/Button";
import { Screen } from "@/shared/ui/Screen";
import { useSignIn } from "../model/useSignIn";
 
type Props = { onSignedIn: () => void };
 
export function SignInScreen({ onSignedIn }: Props) {
  const { submit, pending, error } = useSignIn();
  const [email, setEmail] = useState("");
  const [password, setPassword] = useState("");
 
  return (
    <Screen>
      <View style={styles.form}>
        <TextInput
          style={styles.input}
          autoCapitalize="none"
          keyboardType="email-address"
          placeholder="Email"
          value={email}
          onChangeText={setEmail}
        />
        <TextInput
          style={styles.input}
          secureTextEntry
          placeholder="Password"
          value={password}
          onChangeText={setPassword}
        />
        {error ? <Text style={styles.error}>{error}</Text> : null}
        <Button
          label={pending ? "Signing in…" : "Sign in"}
          disabled={pending}
          onPress={async () => {
            const session = await submit(email, password);
            if (session) onSignedIn();
          }}
        />
      </View>
    </Screen>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  form: { gap: 12, padding: 24 },
  input: { borderWidth: 1, borderColor: "#d1d5db", borderRadius: 8, padding: 12 },
  error: { color: "#dc2626" },
});
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* **`signIn` use case** is a pure async function - test it with in-memory gateway/storage doubles.
* **Adapters** own `fetch` and `expo-secure-store` - swappable per environment.
* **`useSignIn` hook** bridges React lifecycle to the use case - screens stay declarative.
* **Discriminated result** (`ok: true | false`) replaces thrown errors across layer boundaries.

## Deep Dive

### How It Works

#### Ring model on mobile

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
│  UI (screens, components)            │
├──────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Interface adapters (hooks, presenters)│
├──────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Use cases (application rules)       │
├──────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Entities (enterprise rules)         │
└──────────────────────────────────────┘
         adapters implement ports →
```

| Piece | Mobile home | Test strategy |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Entity | `domain/entities.ts` | Pure unit tests |
| Port | `domain/ports.ts` | Type-only; mocked in use-case tests |
| Use case | `domain/use-cases/*.ts` | Inject fake adapters |
| Adapter | `adapters/*.ts` | Integration tests sparingly |
| Hook | `model/use*.ts` | `@testing-library/react-native` with mocked use case |

#### Right-sizing ceremony

| App size | Recommended shape |
| --- | --- |
| 1–5 screens | Entities + hooks; skip formal ports until second IO backend |
| 5–20 screens | Ports for auth, payments, sync - the expensive seams |
| 20+ screens / compliance | Full use cases per intent; adapters per vendor |

#### Use case vs hook

* **Use case:** one user intent, no React, returns data or result unions.
* **Hook:** calls use case, owns `useState`/`useTransition`, exposes UI-friendly API.

Do not put `useEffect` inside use cases - that re-couples domain to the renderer.

### TypeScript Notes

```ts
// Test double - no framework required
const fakeGateway: AuthGateway = {
  authenticate: async () => ({ id: "1", email: "a@b.c", displayName: "Test" }),
};
 
const fakeStorage: TokenStorage = {
  saved: null as Session | null,
  async save(s) { this.saved = s; },
  async load() { return this.saved; },
  async clear() { this.saved = null; },
};
```

## Gotchas

* **Use case per button click** - Hundreds of one-liner "use cases" add noise. **Fix:** Use cases for multi-step intents; keep trivial toggles in hooks.
* **Ports for everything including `Date.now()`** - Abstract time only when tests prove flakiness. **Fix:** Inject clocks in payment/expiry flows only.
* **Throwing errors across layers** - Callers cannot distinguish network vs validation failures. **Fix:** Return discriminated unions (`{ ok: false, error: "network" }`).
* **Hooks that call `fetch` directly** - Bypasses use cases; tests need MSW for every screen. **Fix:** Move IO to adapters; hooks call use cases.
* **Entities importing adapters** - Inverts dependency rule. **Fix:** Adapters import entity types; use cases depend on port interfaces.
* **God `domain/` shared across all features** - Becomes a monolith. **Fix:** Per-feature `domain/` unless entity is truly global (`User` → `entities/user`).
* **TanStack Query inside use cases** - Query is a presentation-cache concern. **Fix:** Use case returns data; hook or repository adapter feeds the query client.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Clean Architecture (this page) | Swappable IO, compliance testing | 3-screen MVP with one API |
| Feature hooks + API module | Simple CRUD features | Multiple IO backends per feature |
| TanStack Query as data layer | Server state dominates | Complex offline merge rules need use-case orchestration |
| Redux Toolkit slices | Global event sourcing | Local feature workflows with few shared reducers |
| FSD only (no use cases) | Structure without heavy domain | Payment/auth flows need audited business rules |

## FAQs

Is Clean Architecture overkill for React Native?

Full ceremony is overkill for small apps. Adopt **entities + use cases + adapters** for features with real business rules (auth, payments, offline sync). CRUD lists can stay hook + API module.

Where do use cases live?

Inside the feature: `src/features/auth/domain/use-cases/`. Cross-feature rules belong in `src/entities/<name>/` or a shared domain package.

Do I need interfaces for every adapter?

Add a port interface when you have **two implementations** (live API + mock, or REST + GraphQL). A single adapter can use a concrete type until the second implementation exists.

How does this work with Expo Router?

Routes stay thin. `SignInScreen` receives `onSignedIn` from the route; navigation is an outer layer concern - not inside the use case.

Should use cases return entities or DTOs?

Return **entities** or feature-specific result types. Map API DTOs to entities inside adapters - DTO shapes never leak to UI.

Can use cases call other use cases?

Yes, compose them - `checkout` may call `validateCoupon` and `reserveInventory`. Keep composition in a parent use case, not in UI.

Where does Zustand fit?

Zustand holds **client UI state** or a **session cache** updated by use-case results. Do not put fetch logic inside store actions - call use cases from actions instead.

How do I test signIn without a device?

Pass fake `AuthGateway` and `TokenStorage` objects to `signIn()`. Assert on the discriminated union - no renderer required.

What about offline-first sync?

Model `SyncQueue` as a port. Use case `enqueueMutation` writes to queue adapter; background worker adapter drains queue - UI calls use cases, not SQLite directly.

Is Redux a clean architecture layer?

Redux is infrastructure/presentation state. Use cases should not dispatch Redux actions - hooks dispatch after use cases succeed.

How is this different from FSD?

FSD is **folder taxonomy**. Clean Architecture is **dependency direction** inside those folders. Use FSD segments (`domain/`, `adapters/`) to host clean rings.

When should I extract entities to src/entities/?

When two or more features import the same noun (`User`, `Order`). Feature-local entities stay in `features/<name>/domain/` until shared.

Do I need Dagger/Hilt-style DI?

No. Plain factory functions and React context are sufficient - see Dependency Injection in RN.

How many lines before a hook becomes a use case?

Line count is a weak signal. Extract when the hook mixes **IO + branching business rules + UI state** and tests require mounting React - typically 40+ lines of orchestration.

Dokumen: Dependency Injection in RN

# Dependency Injection in RN

Dependency injection on mobile means **passing dependencies in** - API clients, storage, analytics - instead of importing singletons. React Native teams get testable services with **factory functions**, **React context**, and **module boundaries** - not Dagger, Spring, or a global service locator.

Highlights / Dependency Injection in RN

* Factory functions (createOrdersApi) are DI - no container framework required
* React context wires production implementations at the app root
* Module boundaries expose ports; adapters are swappable in tests via props or overrides
* Prefer constructor injection via factories over service locator singletons
* expo-router root \_layout.tsx is the composition root for most Expo apps
* Jest module mocks replace adapters - keep use cases ignorant of React

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```tsx
// src/shared/di/AppServicesContext.tsx
import { createContext, useContext, type ReactNode } from "react";
import { createApiClient } from "@/shared/api/createApiClient";
import { createOrdersApi, type OrdersApi } from "@/features/orders/api/ordersApi";
import { getAppConfig } from "@/shared/config/env";
 
export type AppServices = {
  ordersApi: OrdersApi;
};
 
const AppServicesContext = createContext<AppServices | null>(null);
 
export function AppServicesProvider({ children, overrides }: { children: ReactNode; overrides?: Partial<AppServices> }) {
  const client = createApiClient(getAppConfig().apiBaseUrl);
  const value: AppServices = {
    ordersApi: overrides?.ordersApi ?? createOrdersApi(client),
  };
  return <AppServicesContext.Provider value={value}>{children}</AppServicesContext.Provider>;
}
 
export function useAppServices(): AppServices {
  const ctx = useContext(AppServicesContext);
  if (!ctx) throw new Error("AppServicesProvider missing - wrap app/_layout.tsx");
  return ctx;
}
```

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx (excerpt) - composition root
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
import { AppServicesProvider } from "@/shared/di/AppServicesContext";
 
export default function RootLayout() {
  return (
    <AppServicesProvider>
      <Stack />
    </AppServicesProvider>
  );
}
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Unit tests need fake APIs without `jest.mock("fetch")` in every file.
* Staging vs production clients must swap without `if (__DEV__)` scattered in features.
* Clean architecture ports need concrete adapters wired in one place.
* A `lib/api.ts` singleton imports `getAppConfig()` and creates hidden globals.

## Working Example

```ts
// src/shared/api/createApiClient.ts
export type ApiClient = {
  get<T>(path: string): Promise<T>;
};
 
export function createApiClient(baseUrl: string): ApiClient {
  return {
    async get<T>(path: string) {
      const response = await fetch(`${baseUrl}${path}`);
      if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`GET ${path} failed`);
      return response.json() as Promise<T>;
    },
  };
}
```

```ts
// src/features/orders/api/ordersApi.ts
import type { Order } from "@/entities/order";
import type { ApiClient } from "@/shared/api/createApiClient";
 
export type OrdersApi = {
  list(): Promise<Order[]>;
};
 
export function createOrdersApi(client: ApiClient): OrdersApi {
  return {
    list: () => client.get<Order[]>("/orders"),
  };
}
```

```tsx
// src/features/orders/model/useOrders.ts
import { useCallback, useEffect, useState } from "react";
import type { Order } from "@/entities/order";
import { useAppServices } from "@/shared/di/AppServicesContext";
 
export function useOrders() {
  const { ordersApi } = useAppServices();
  const [orders, setOrders] = useState<Order[]>([]);
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true);
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);
 
  const refresh = useCallback(async () => {
    try {
      setError(null);
      setOrders(await ordersApi.list());
    } catch (e) {
      setError(e instanceof Error ? e.message : "Failed to load");
    } finally {
      setLoading(false);
    }
  }, [ordersApi]);
 
  useEffect(() => {
    refresh();
  }, [refresh]);
 
  return { orders, loading, error, refresh };
}
```

```tsx
// src/features/orders/model/useOrders.test.tsx
import { renderHook, waitFor } from "@testing-library/react-native";
import type { ReactNode } from "react";
import { AppServicesProvider } from "@/shared/di/AppServicesContext";
import type { OrdersApi } from "../api/ordersApi";
import { useOrders } from "./useOrders";
 
const mockOrdersApi: OrdersApi = {
  list: jest.fn(() =>
    Promise.resolve([{ id: "1", title: "Test", totalCents: 100, status: "pending", placedAt: "" }])
  ),
};
 
function wrapper({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  return <AppServicesProvider overrides={{ ordersApi: mockOrdersApi }}>{children}</AppServicesProvider>;
}
 
it("loads orders from injected api", async () => {
  const { result } = renderHook(() => useOrders(), { wrapper });
  await waitFor(() => expect(result.current.loading).toBe(false));
  expect(mockOrdersApi.list).toHaveBeenCalled();
  expect(result.current.orders).toHaveLength(1);
});
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* **`createOrdersApi(client)`** receives its HTTP dependency - test with a fake `ApiClient` without network.
* **`AppServicesProvider`** is the **composition root** - one place binds production implementations.
* **`overrides`** prop injects test doubles without `jest.mock` on the hook file.
* Hooks call **`useAppServices()`** - not `createOrdersApi` directly.

## Deep Dive

### How It Works

#### DI patterns on RN (lightest → heaviest)

| Pattern | Mechanism | Best for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Factory functions** | `createX(deps)` | Adapters, use cases |
| **Parameter injection** | Pass deps as hook arguments | Storybook, isolated tests |
| **React context** | Provider at root | App-wide services (API, analytics) |
| **Module overrides** | `jest.mock` / Metro alias | Integration tests, e2e stubs |
| **DI container library** | tsyringe, Inversify | Rarely justified on mobile |

#### Composition root placement

| Location | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `app/_layout.tsx` | Global providers (API, auth session, theme) |
| `features/auth/model/AuthProvider.tsx` | Feature-scoped services |
| Test `wrapper` | Per-suite overrides via `overrides` prop |

#### Service locator anti-pattern

```ts
// ❌ Hidden global - hard to test, hard to swap per variant
export const ordersApi = createOrdersApi(createApiClient(getAppConfig().apiBaseUrl));
```

```ts
// ✅ Explicit wiring at composition root
const client = createApiClient(getAppConfig().apiBaseUrl);
const ordersApi = createOrdersApi(client);
```

#### Factory + use case wiring

```ts
// useSignIn hook - inject ports from context or factories
export function createSignInRunner(services: AppServices) {
  return (email: string, password: string) =>
    signIn(
      {
        authGateway: services.authGateway,
        tokenStorage: services.tokenStorage,
        createSession: services.createSession,
      },
      { email, password }
    );
}
```

Use cases stay framework-free; the hook pulls deps from context once.

### TypeScript Notes

```ts
// Narrow AppServices as the app grows - split contexts if needed
export type AppServices = {
  ordersApi: OrdersApi;
  authGateway: AuthGateway;
  tokenStorage: TokenStorage;
  analytics: AnalyticsPort;
};
 
// Feature-specific context avoids god provider
export const CheckoutServicesContext = createContext<CheckoutServices | null>(null);
```

## Gotchas

* **God context with 40 services** - Everything re-renders on any override change. **Fix:** Split by feature or use stable `useMemo` service objects.
* **Creating new service instances every render** - Breaks `useCallback` deps and refetches endlessly. **Fix:** Memoize services in provider with `useMemo(() => create..., [baseUrl])`.
* **Importing concrete adapters in use cases** - Inverts clean architecture. **Fix:** Use cases accept port interfaces; only composition root imports `restAuthGateway`.
* **jest.mock hoisting surprises** - Mock path must match exact import. **Fix:** Prefer `overrides` prop on provider over module mocks when possible.
* **Expo Go vs dev build service URLs** - Hidden `__DEV__` branches in factories. **Fix:** `getAppConfig().apiBaseUrl` from `app.config.ts` extra per variant.
* **Singleton analytics in every file** - Untestable event spam. **Fix:** `AnalyticsPort` injected; noop implementation in tests.
* **tsyringe for three services** - Reflection metadata pain in Metro. **Fix:** Plain factories until you have 20+ wired types.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Context + factories (this page) | Most Expo apps | - |
| Prop drilling deps | One screen tests, Storybook stories | App-wide API client |
| Module singleton | Throwaway spike only | Production features with tests |
| jest.mock per test file | Quick isolation | Consistent override story across suite |
| DI container (tsyringe) | Large brownfield porting from backend | Greenfield RN - adds Metro/babel complexity |
| Parametric hooks `useOrders(api)` | Library hooks reused outside your app | Internal app - verbose at every call site |

## FAQs

Do React Native apps need a DI framework?

No. Factory functions plus React context cover 95% of mobile needs. Containers add indirection without solving RN-specific problems (Metro bundling, Fast Refresh).

What is the composition root?

The single place where concrete implementations bind to abstractions - typically `app/_layout.tsx` or `AppServicesProvider`. No other file should call `createRestAuthGateway` with production URLs.

How do I test hooks that use API clients?

Wrap with `AppServicesProvider overrides={{ ordersApi: mock }}`. Alternatively pass the API as a hook argument in tests only.

Context vs Zustand for services?

Context wires **immutable service instances** (API, storage). Zustand holds **mutable app state** (cart, session). Do not store fetch clients in Zustand unless they hold session tokens that change.

Can I use expo-router loaders for DI?

Expo Router does not have RSC loaders. Wire services in root layout providers - not per-route unless route-scoped deps are truly isolated.

How do environment variants get different APIs?

`getAppConfig()` reads `extra` from `app.config.ts` - composition root passes the correct `baseUrl` when creating clients. No `if` in feature code.

What about @tanstack/react-query?

Inject a `QueryClient` via context (built-in `QueryClientProvider`). Repository adapters feed query functions - `queryFn: () => ordersApi.list()`.

Is jest.mock bad?

Acceptable for integration tests. Prefer provider `overrides` for unit tests - clearer and typed.

How do I avoid circular imports with DI?

Ports live in `domain/ports.ts`. Adapters import ports + entities. Composition root imports adapters. Features import ports through context - never adapters from domain.

Should SecureStore be injected?

Yes - wrap in `TokenStorage` port. Tests use in-memory storage; production uses `createSecureTokenStorage()`.

Fast Refresh with context providers?

Changing provider implementation hot-reloads fine. Changing context **shape** may need full reload - keep `AppServices` type stable.

Multiple apps in monorepo - shared DI?

Shared `packages/services` exports factories; each `apps/*` composition root passes app-specific config. Do not share a singleton across apps.

When does a DI library make sense?

Rarely on RN. Consider it when porting a large backend team’s patterns or when you have 30+ wired interfaces with automated contract tests - still evaluate Metro cost first.

How does DI relate to clean architecture?

Ports are interfaces; adapters are implementations; composition root binds them. Use cases receive deps as function arguments - the purest form of injection.
