Dokumen: Feature-Sliced Design for RN
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/feature-sliced-design-for-rn/

# Feature-Sliced Design for RN

Feature-Sliced Design (FSD) organizes front-end code into **layers** and **slices** with strict import rules. On Expo, map FSD to `app/`, `features/`, `entities/`, and `shared/` - you get the boundary benefits without seven top-level folders on day one.

Highlights / Feature-Sliced Design for RN

* Map FSD layers to app/, features/, entities/, and shared/ - skip pages/ and widgets/ until you need them
* Import rule: a layer may only import from layers below it
* Each slice exposes a public API via index.ts - @x notation is optional in RN
* Segments (ui, model, api, lib) group files inside a slice without inventing new top-level folders
* Expo Router lives in app/ - it is the FSD app layer, not a dumping ground for feature logic
* Enforce boundaries with ESLint no-restricted-imports before the graph becomes unmappable

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```text
src/
├── app/                    # FSD "app" layer - providers, init (NOT Expo Router's app/)
│   └── providers/
│       └── AppProviders.tsx
├── features/
│   ├── auth/
│   │   ├── index.ts        # public API
│   │   ├── ui/
│   │   ├── model/
│   │   └── api/
│   └── orders/
│       ├── index.ts
│       ├── ui/
│       ├── model/
│       └── api/
├── entities/
│   ├── user/
│   │   ├── index.ts
│   │   ├── model/
│   │   └── ui/             # UserAvatar - entity-scoped UI
│   └── order/
│       └── index.ts
└── shared/
    ├── ui/                 # Button, Screen
    ├── api/
    ├── config/
    └── lib/
 
app/                        # Expo Router - route files only
└── (tabs)/
    └── orders/
        └── index.tsx
```

```ts
// Import rule (enforced in ESLint):
// app → features → entities → shared
// features/auth must NOT import features/orders/ui/*
```

**When to reach for this:**

* The codebase has 10+ features and cross-imports are tangled.
* Onboarding requires a map ("where does checkout code live?").
* You want lint-enforceable boundaries without adopting Nx on day one.
* A web team already uses FSD and mobile should align.

## Working Example

```tsx
// src/entities/user/model/types.ts
export type User = {
  id: string;
  displayName: string;
  avatarUrl: string | null;
};
```

```tsx
// src/entities/user/ui/UserAvatar.tsx
import { Image, StyleSheet, View } from "react-native";
import type { User } from "../model/types";
 
type Props = { user: User; size?: number };
 
export function UserAvatar({ user, size = 40 }: Props) {
  return (
    <View style={[styles.circle, { width: size, height: size }]}>
      {user.avatarUrl ? (
        <Image source={{ uri: user.avatarUrl }} style={styles.image} />
      ) : null}
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  circle: { borderRadius: 999, overflow: "hidden", backgroundColor: "#e5e7eb" },
  image: { width: "100%", height: "100%" },
});
```

```ts
// src/entities/user/index.ts
export type { User } from "./model/types";
export { UserAvatar } from "./ui/UserAvatar";
```

```tsx
// src/features/orders/ui/OrderRow.tsx
import { Pressable, StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
import { UserAvatar, type User } from "@/entities/user";
import type { Order } from "@/entities/order";
 
type Props = {
  order: Order;
  placedBy: User;
  onPress: (orderId: string) => void;
};
 
export function OrderRow({ order, placedBy, onPress }: Props) {
  return (
    <Pressable style={styles.row} onPress={() => onPress(order.id)}>
      <UserAvatar user={placedBy} size={36} />
      <View style={styles.meta}>
        <Text style={styles.title}>{order.title}</Text>
        <Text style={styles.sub}>{placedBy.displayName}</Text>
      </View>
    </Pressable>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  row: { flexDirection: "row", gap: 12, padding: 16 },
  meta: { flex: 1 },
  title: { fontSize: 16, fontWeight: "600" },
  sub: { fontSize: 14, color: "#6b7280" },
});
```

```tsx
// src/features/orders/ui/OrdersScreen.tsx
import { FlatList, RefreshControl, StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
import { Screen } from "@/shared/ui/Screen";
import { useOrdersScreen } from "../model/useOrdersScreen";
import { OrderRow } from "./OrderRow";
 
export function OrdersScreen() {
  const { orders, usersById, loading, refresh, onOrderPress } = useOrdersScreen();
 
  return (
    <Screen>
      <FlatList
        data={orders}
        keyExtractor={(item) => item.id}
        refreshControl={<RefreshControl refreshing={loading} onRefresh={refresh} />}
        renderItem={({ item }) => (
          <OrderRow
            order={item}
            placedBy={usersById[item.placedById] ?? { id: "", displayName: "Unknown", avatarUrl: null }}
            onPress={onOrderPress}
          />
        )}
        ListEmptyComponent={<Text style={styles.empty}>No orders yet</Text>}
      />
    </Screen>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  empty: { textAlign: "center", marginTop: 48, color: "#6b7280" },
});
```

```ts
// src/features/orders/index.ts - public API
export { OrdersScreen } from "./ui/OrdersScreen";
```

```tsx
// app/(tabs)/orders/index.tsx
export { OrdersScreen as default } from "@/features/orders";
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* **`entities/user`** owns the `User` type and `UserAvatar` - reusable across features.
* **`features/orders`** composes entity UI into a product workflow without importing `features/auth`.
* **`shared/ui/Screen`** is a primitive with no domain knowledge.
* **Expo Router `app/`** re-exports the feature screen - the FSD `app` layer (`src/app/providers`) holds global providers separately from routes.

## Deep Dive

### How It Works

#### FSD layers adapted for Expo

| FSD layer | RN mapping | Contains |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **app** | `src/app/` + Expo `app/_layout.tsx` | Providers, analytics init, error boundaries |
| **pages** | Often skipped - Expo Router routes replace this | Thin route files in `app/` |
| **widgets** | Optional `src/widgets/` | Dashboard blocks reused on multiple routes |
| **features** | `src/features/<name>/` | User stories: auth, checkout, orders |
| **entities** | `src/entities/<name>/` | Business nouns: user, order, product |
| **shared** | `src/shared/` | UI kit, API client, config, utils |

#### Segments inside a slice

| Segment | Purpose | Example files |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ui/` | Components and screens | `OrdersScreen.tsx`, `OrderRow.tsx` |
| `model/` | State, hooks, stores | `useOrdersScreen.ts`, `cartStore.ts` |
| `api/` | IO adapters | `ordersApi.ts`, DTO mappers |
| `lib/` | Slice-local pure helpers | `sortOrders.ts` |

#### Import rules

```
shared     ← imported by everyone
  ↑
entities   ← features may import entities; entities never import features
  ↑
features   ← no cross-feature imports; use entities or app-layer orchestration
  ↑
app        ← wires providers; routes import feature public APIs
```

### TypeScript Notes

```ts
// tsconfig.json paths - mirror FSD layers
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "paths": {
      "@/*": ["./src/*"],
      "@/features/*": ["./src/features/*"],
      "@/entities/*": ["./src/entities/*"],
      "@/shared/*": ["./src/shared/*"]
    }
  }
}
```

```js
// eslint.config.js (excerpt) - block cross-feature deep imports
{
  rules: {
    "no-restricted-imports": ["error", {
      patterns: [
        {
          group: ["@/features/*/ui/*", "@/features/*/model/*", "@/features/*/api/*"],
          message: "Import from the feature public API (@/features/<name>) instead.",
        },
      ],
    }],
  },
}
```

### When to add widgets/ or pages/

| Signal | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Same dashboard header on 4 routes | Extract `src/widgets/dashboard-header/` |
| Marketing landing unrelated to features | `src/pages/landing/` or a `features/marketing` slice |
| Team confusion between `app/` and `src/app/` | Rename `src/app` → `src/providers` to avoid Expo collision |

## Gotchas

* **Putting feature logic in Expo `app/` routes** - Routes become god files. **Fix:** Re-export from `@/features/*`; parse params only.
* **Cross-feature imports for "just one component"** - Graph becomes cyclic within two sprints. **Fix:** Move shared UI to `entities/` or `shared/ui`; orchestrate in the route.
* **Empty `index.ts` barrels exporting everything** - Accidental public API bloat. **Fix:** Export deliberately; treat `index.ts` like a package manifest.
* **Creating `entities/` for every DTO** - Not every API response is a domain entity. **Fix:** Map DTOs in `api/`; promote to entity when two features need the type.
* **Skipping ESLint enforcement** - FSD without lint rules is folder theater. **Fix:** Add `no-restricted-imports` before feature count hits double digits.
* **Duplicating `shared/ui` and `entities/*/ui`** - Unclear ownership. **Fix:** Entity UI displays one noun (`UserAvatar`); shared UI is generic (`Button`).
* **Monolithic `features/orders/model/store.ts`** - Becomes a god module. **Fix:** Split by segment; one hook per screen orchestration.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FSD (this page) | 8+ features, multi-squad, import rules needed | Solo dev, 3-screen MVP |
| Simple feature folders (`features/orders/components`) | Team outgrew layers but FSD feels heavy | Cross-feature imports already uncontrolled |
| Nx module boundaries | Monorepo with enforced graph in CI | Single-package Expo app |
| Clean Architecture rings | Heavy test coverage, swappable adapters | Prototype without test investment |
| Flat `src/screens` + `src/components` | Spike or throwaway demo | Long-lived product with 20+ routes |

## FAQs

Do I need all seven FSD layers on mobile?

No. Most Expo apps use **app** (providers), **features**, **entities**, and **shared**. Skip **pages** (Expo Router replaces it) and **widgets** until a composite block repeats across routes.

Where does Expo Router's app/ folder fit?

Expo `app/` is the **routing shell** - file-based routes and layouts. FSD `src/app/` holds global providers and bootstrap. Keep route files thin; product code lives in `src/features/`.

Can features import other features?

No - FSD forbids slice-to-slice imports at the same layer. Share through **entities**, **shared**, or orchestrate at the **route** / `src/app` layer.

What is a segment?

A subfolder inside a slice: `ui`, `model`, `api`, `lib`. Segments group files by technical role without creating new top-level layers.

Should I use @x public API notation?

Optional. The `@x` cross-export pattern from web FSD is less common in RN. A plain `index.ts` barrel per slice is sufficient.

Where do Zustand stores live?

In `features/<name>/model/` for feature-local state. Global session state may live in `src/app/providers/` or `features/session/model/` depending on scope.

How does FSD work with TanStack Query?

Query hooks belong in `features/<name>/model/` or `entities/<name>/api/`. Entity-level queries (`useUser`) serve multiple features; feature-level queries (`useCheckout`) stay in the feature.

What goes in shared/ui vs entities/user/ui?

`shared/ui/Button` is generic. `entities/user/ui/UserAvatar` knows about `User` - it displays domain data and may be reused by many features.

Can I mix FSD with a monorepo?

Yes. Packages typically hold `shared` and `entities`; the Expo app holds `features` and routes. See shared-packages Metro guide for workspace resolution.

How do I migrate from flat folders to FSD?

One feature per PR: move `screens/OrdersScreen.tsx` → `features/orders/ui/`, add `index.ts`, update imports. Enable ESLint rules after the second migrated feature.

Is app/\_layout.tsx part of FSD app layer?

Yes - root layout wraps providers and navigation chrome. Register `AppProviders` from `src/app/providers/` in `app/_layout.tsx`, not business logic.

When is a widget not a feature?

When it has **no standalone user story** - e.g. a `StatsCard` reused on home and dashboard. Features deliver user value ("place order"); widgets compose entities for layout.

Does FSD replace Clean Architecture?

They complement each other. FSD organizes **file structure**; Clean Architecture organizes **dependency direction** inside a feature (use cases, adapters). Use both when complexity warrants it.

How many features is too many?

There is no hard cap - slices should match product domains. If `features/misc` appears, split by user journey or merge into an existing slice.

# Architecture & Design Highlights Summary

Every highlight bullet from the 9 pages in this section, gathered on one page and grouped by the page it came from.

Highlights / Architecture & Design Highlights Summary

* Keep app/ routes thin - they wire navigation; features/ owns product logic
* Map FSD layers to app/, features/, entities/, and shared/ - skip pages/ and widgets/ until you need them
* Entities are plain types + pure functions - zero React imports
* Modular monolith: one bundle ID, feature modules toggled by flags and build-time config
* Factory functions (createOrdersApi) are DI - no container framework required
* Expo Router is the default for new SDK 57 apps - file-based routes, typed routes, deep links

## [Mobile Architecture Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/mobile-architecture-basics/)

* Keep app/ routes thin - they wire navigation; features/ owns product logic
* Dependency direction flows inward: app → features → entities → shared
* Each feature exposes a public API through index.ts - no deep imports
* shared/ holds primitives and infra; features never import sibling feature internals
* Entities model domain nouns; use cases orchestrate verbs without UI imports
* Start with feature slices; add clean-architecture layers only when tests demand seams

## [Feature-Sliced Design for RN](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/feature-sliced-design-for-rn/)

* Map FSD layers to app/, features/, entities/, and shared/ - skip pages/ and widgets/ until you need them
* Import rule: a layer may only import from layers below it
* Each slice exposes a public API via index.ts - @x notation is optional in RN
* Segments (ui, model, api, lib) group files inside a slice without inventing new top-level folders
* Expo Router lives in app/ - it is the FSD app layer, not a dumping ground for feature logic
* Enforce boundaries with ESLint no-restricted-imports before the graph becomes unmappable

## [Clean Architecture on Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/clean-architecture-on-mobile/)

* Entities are plain types + pure functions - zero React imports
* Use cases orchestrate one user intent - signIn, placeOrder, syncOfflineQueue
* Adapters implement ports - RestAuthGateway, SecureTokenStorage
* Screens call use cases through hooks - they never import fetch or AsyncStorage
* Add layers when tests need swappable IO - not on day one of a three-screen app
* One use case per file keeps mobile workflows readable without Java-style ceremony

## [Modular Monolith vs Multi-App](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/modular-monolith-vs-multi-app/)

* Modular monolith: one bundle ID, feature modules toggled by flags and build-time config
* Multi-app: separate slugs, bundle IDs, and EAS projects per product surface
* APP\_VARIANT and app.config.ts branch identity without forking the repo
* Feature flags gate runtime behavior - they do not replace architectural module boundaries
* White-label is modular monolith with per-tenant config - not N separate codebases
* Split into multi-app when release cadence, compliance, or store listings truly diverge

## [Dependency Injection in RN](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/dependency-injection-in-rn/)

* Factory functions (createOrdersApi) are DI - no container framework required
* React context wires production implementations at the app root
* Module boundaries expose ports; adapters are swappable in tests via props or overrides
* Prefer constructor injection via factories over service locator singletons
* expo-router root \_layout.tsx is the composition root for most Expo apps
* Jest module mocks replace adapters - keep use cases ignorant of React

## [ADR: Navigation Library Choice](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/adr-navigation-library-choice/)

* Expo Router is the default for new SDK 57 apps - file-based routes, typed routes, deep links
* React Navigation fits brownfield apps already invested in imperative navigators
* Expo Router is built on React Navigation - you are not choosing different rendering engines
* Deep linking and universal links are simpler when routes match the filesystem
* Escape hatch: Expo Router supports custom navigators when file-based routing is insufficient
* Document the choice in an ADR when onboarding exceeds one sprint or multiple squads ship routes

## [ADR: State Management Selection](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/adr-state-management-selection/)

* Server state belongs in TanStack Query - not Redux, not Zustand
* Zustand fits client UI state and small global slices without provider nesting
* Redux Toolkit pays off when time-travel debugging and middleware ecosystems are required
* React 19 useOptimistic and useActionState cover local optimistic UI without a store
* One store per domain beats a single global atom for everything
* Document the default stack in an ADR before every squad picks a different library

## [Refactoring Checklist](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/refactoring-checklist/)

* Run this checklist on the five largest files before every major release
* God modules block parallel PRs - file length and import fan-out are objective signals
* Tier 1 items are cheap to fix early; Tier 4 items need dedicated refactor sprints
* Extract one boundary per PR - not a month-long cleanup branch
* Pair with ESLint import rules so regressions fail CI, not code review
* Score findings: P0 blocks release, P1 next sprint, P2 backlog

## [Architecture Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/best-practices/)

* Start with feature slices - add FSD layers and clean architecture when boundaries hurt
* Thin Expo Router routes; fat feature modules with public index.ts APIs
* TanStack Query for server state; Zustand for small global client state
* Factory functions and AppServicesProvider - no Java-style DI containers on day one
* Modular monolith + APP\_VARIANT before splitting into multiple apps
* Run the refactoring checklist on the five largest files before major releases

Dokumen: Mobile Architecture Basics
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/mobile-architecture-basics/

# Mobile Architecture Basics

10 examples to get you started with mobile architecture - 7 basic and 3 intermediate.

Highlights / Mobile Architecture Basics

* Keep app/ routes thin - they wire navigation; features/ owns product logic
* Dependency direction flows inward: app → features → entities → shared
* Each feature exposes a public API through index.ts - no deep imports
* shared/ holds primitives and infra; features never import sibling feature internals
* Entities model domain nouns; use cases orchestrate verbs without UI imports
* Start with feature slices; add clean-architecture layers only when tests demand seams

## Prerequisites

Scaffold a production-shaped Expo app with an explicit SDK 57 pin. The `default@sdk-57` template ships Expo Router, TypeScript, and the recommended folder layout to extend.

```bash
npx create-expo-app@latest MyApp --template default@sdk-57
cd MyApp
npm install
```

Add a `src/` tree beside `app/` for feature boundaries:

```text
MyApp/
├── app/                    # Expo Router - routes only
├── src/
│   ├── shared/             # UI primitives, API client, config
│   ├── entities/           # domain models (User, Order)
│   └── features/           # product slices (auth, orders, settings)
├── app.config.ts
└── package.json
```

Confirm the SDK pin before structuring features:

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "expo": "~57.0.4",
    "react": "19.2.3",
    "react-native": "0.86.0"
  }
}
```

> **Tooling:** These examples target **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4), **React Native 0.86.0**, and **React 19.2.3**.

---

## Basic Examples

### 1. Three-Layer Mental Model

Mobile apps benefit from a simple inward dependency flow: **presentation** (screens, components) calls **domain** (entities, use cases), which calls **data** (API adapters, storage).

```text
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  app/ + features/*/screens, components  │  ← presentation
├─────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  entities/ + features/*/model, hooks    │  ← domain
├─────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  shared/api, shared/storage, adapters   │  ← data / infra
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
         dependency direction: ↓ inward
```

```tsx
// src/features/orders/screens/OrdersScreen.tsx - presentation orchestrates
import { useOrders } from "../hooks/useOrders";
import { OrderList } from "../components/OrderList";
 
export function OrdersScreen() {
  const { orders, loading, error, refresh } = useOrders();
  return <OrderList orders={orders} loading={loading} error={error} onRefresh={refresh} />;
}
```

* **Presentation** never imports `fetch` directly - it calls hooks or use cases that hide IO
* **Domain** types (`Order`, `User`) live in `entities/` so multiple features share one shape
* **Data** adapters (`ordersApi.ts`, `secureStorage.ts`) sit in `shared/` or `features/*/api/`
* Violating direction (API client imported in a presentational `OrderRow`) makes unit tests painful

> **Related:** [Feature-Sliced Design for RN](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/feature-sliced-design-for-rn/) - formal slice layers adapted for Expo | [Clean Architecture on Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/clean-architecture-on-mobile/) - entities and use cases without ceremony

---

### 2. Thin Route Files

Expo Router maps filenames to URLs. Route files should **re-export** feature screens - not own business logic.

```tsx
// app/(tabs)/orders/index.tsx - one line when possible
export { OrdersScreen as default } from "@/features/orders";
```

```tsx
// src/features/orders/index.ts - public API for the feature
export { OrdersScreen } from "./screens/OrdersScreen";
export type { Order } from "./model/types";
```

* **`app/`** is navigation infrastructure - params parsing and layout nesting belong here at most
* **`features/orders/index.ts`** is the only import path other features should use
* Deep imports like `@/features/orders/components/OrderRow` couple consumers to internal refactors
* When a route needs param validation, parse once in the route file and pass typed props to the screen

> **Related:** [../project-setup/folder-structure-for-features/folder-structure-for-features.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/folder-structure-for-features/) - feature slice layout in growing codebases

---

### 3. Shared vs Feature-Local Code

`shared/` holds code with **no product opinion**. Feature folders hold product-specific UI and workflows.

```text
src/
├── shared/
│   ├── ui/              # Button, Screen, TextField - design-system primitives
│   ├── api/             # createApiClient(), error types
│   ├── config/          # env readers (no secrets in source)
│   └── lib/             # formatCurrency, date helpers
└── features/
    └── checkout/
        ├── components/  # PaymentSummary - checkout-specific
        └── hooks/       # useCheckout - checkout workflow
```

```tsx
// src/shared/ui/Button.tsx - primitive, no domain knowledge
import { Pressable, StyleSheet, Text, type PressableProps } from "react-native";
 
type ButtonProps = PressableProps & { label: string };
 
export function Button({ label, style, ...rest }: ButtonProps) {
  return (
    <Pressable style={[styles.base, style]} {...rest}>
      <Text style={styles.label}>{label}</Text>
    </Pressable>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  base: { paddingVertical: 12, paddingHorizontal: 20, borderRadius: 10, backgroundColor: "#2563eb" },
  label: { fontSize: 16, fontWeight: "600", color: "#fff" },
});
```

* Move code to **`shared/`** when two unrelated features need it **and** it has no product semantics
* Keep **checkout-specific** markup in `features/checkout/` even if only one screen uses it today
* **`shared/ui`** should not import from `features/` - dependency flows one way
* Resist a root-level `components/` junk drawer - unowned folders become god-module magnets

> **Related:** [Feature-Sliced Design for RN](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/feature-sliced-design-for-rn/) - `shared` layer rules and segment naming

---

### 4. Entity Types Without UI

Entities describe **nouns** in your domain - plain types and pure functions with zero React imports.

```tsx
// src/entities/order/model/types.ts
export type OrderStatus = "pending" | "shipped" | "delivered" | "cancelled";
 
export type Order = {
  id: string;
  title: string;
  totalCents: number;
  status: OrderStatus;
  placedAt: string;
};
```

```tsx
// src/entities/order/lib/formatOrderTotal.ts
import type { Order } from "../model/types";
 
export function formatOrderTotal(order: Order): string {
  return new Intl.NumberFormat("en-US", {
    style: "currency",
    currency: "USD",
  }).format(order.totalCents / 100);
}
```

* **Entities** are importable from any feature - `features/orders` and `features/tracking` both use `Order`
* Pure formatters and validators belong with the entity, not inside screen files
* No `useState`, no `fetch`, no `StyleSheet` in `entities/` - keeps them testable without a renderer
* Start with one file per entity; split `model/`, `lib/`, `api/` when the entity grows past ~200 lines

> **Related:** [Clean Architecture on Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/clean-architecture-on-mobile/) - when to add use cases around entities

---

### 5. Feature Public API

Every feature folder exposes an **`index.ts`** barrel. Cross-feature imports go through that file only.

```ts
// src/features/orders/index.ts
export { OrdersScreen } from "./screens/OrdersScreen";
export { OrderRow } from "./components/OrderRow";
export { useOrders } from "./hooks/useOrders";
export type { OrdersFilter } from "./model/types";
```

```tsx
// src/features/dashboard/screens/DashboardScreen.tsx - imports public API only
import { OrderRow } from "@/features/orders";
import type { Order } from "@/entities/order";
```

* **Public API** is a contract - adding exports is intentional; removing them is a breaking change
* Do not export internal helpers (`normalizeRawOrder`) unless another feature truly needs them
* ESLint `no-restricted-imports` can enforce `@/features/*/index` and block `@/features/*/components/*`
* Smaller features export one screen; larger features export screens + hooks + types selectively

> **Related:** [Refactoring Checklist](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/refactoring-checklist/) - audit items for boundary violations before release

---

### 6. API Adapter Boundary

Network and storage IO live behind adapters so screens swap implementations (mock, staging, prod) without edits.

```tsx
// src/shared/api/createApiClient.ts
type ApiClient = {
  get<T>(path: string): Promise<T>;
  post<T>(path: string, body: unknown): Promise<T>;
};
 
export function createApiClient(baseUrl: string): ApiClient {
  return {
    async get<T>(path: string) {
      const response = await fetch(`${baseUrl}${path}`);
      if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`GET ${path} failed: ${response.status}`);
      return response.json() as Promise<T>;
    },
    async post<T>(path: string, body: unknown) {
      const response = await fetch(`${baseUrl}${path}`, {
        method: "POST",
        headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
        body: JSON.stringify(body),
      });
      if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`POST ${path} failed: ${response.status}`);
      return response.json() as Promise<T>;
    },
  };
}
```

```tsx
// src/features/orders/api/ordersApi.ts
import type { Order } from "@/entities/order";
import type { ApiClient } from "@/shared/api/createApiClient";
 
export function createOrdersApi(client: ApiClient) {
  return {
    list: () => client.get<Order[]>("/orders"),
    byId: (id: string) => client.get<Order>(`/orders/${id}`),
  };
}
```

* **Factory functions** (`createOrdersApi`) accept dependencies - easy to inject mocks in tests
* Raw `fetch` URLs should not appear in screen components
* Map DTO shapes to entity types inside the adapter - API snake\_case stays out of UI
* One adapter module per bounded context (`ordersApi`, `authApi`) beats a single god `api.ts`

> **Related:** [Dependency Injection in RN](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/dependency-injection-in-rn/) - wiring adapters without a DI framework

---

### 7. Config and Environment Boundaries

Runtime configuration flows through a single reader - not scattered `process.env` calls in feature code.

```tsx
// src/shared/config/env.ts
import Constants from "expo-constants";
 
type AppConfig = {
  apiBaseUrl: string;
  appVariant: "development" | "staging" | "production";
};
 
export function getAppConfig(): AppConfig {
  const extra = Constants.expoConfig?.extra as Partial<AppConfig> | undefined;
  return {
    apiBaseUrl: extra?.apiBaseUrl ?? "https://api.staging.example.com",
    appVariant: extra?.appVariant ?? "development",
  };
}
```

```ts
// app.config.ts (excerpt)
export default {
  extra: {
    apiBaseUrl: process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL,
    appVariant: process.env.APP_VARIANT ?? "development",
  },
};
```

* **`EXPO_PUBLIC_*`** vars are embedded in the JS bundle - never put secrets there
* **`getAppConfig()`** is the only module that reads `Constants.expoConfig?.extra` for app settings
* Features import `getAppConfig()` or receive config via context - they do not read env directly
* Pair with EAS build profiles that set `env` per channel - see project-setup environment guides

> **Related:** [Modular Monolith vs Multi-App](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/modular-monolith-vs-multi-app/) - one binary with variants vs separate apps

---

## Intermediate Examples

### 8. Cross-Feature Communication

Features should not import each other's internals. Use **shared entities**, **events**, or **orchestration at the app layer**.

```tsx
// src/features/cart/hooks/useCart.ts - cart owns its state
import { create } from "zustand";
 
type CartItem = { productId: string; qty: number };
 
type CartStore = {
  items: CartItem[];
  add: (item: CartItem) => void;
  clear: () => void;
};
 
export const useCart = create<CartStore>((set) => ({
  items: [],
  add: (item) => set((s) => ({ items: [...s.items, item] })),
  clear: () => set({ items: [] }),
}));
```

```tsx
// app/(tabs)/catalog/[id].tsx - route orchestrates navigation + cart, not features importing features
import { useLocalSearchParams, router } from "expo-router";
import { ProductDetailScreen } from "@/features/catalog";
import { useCart } from "@/features/cart";
 
export default function ProductRoute() {
  const { id } = useLocalSearchParams<{ id: string }>();
  const add = useCart((s) => s.add);
 
  return (
    <ProductDetailScreen
      productId={id ?? ""}
      onAddToCart={(productId) => {
        add({ productId, qty: 1 });
        router.push("/(tabs)/cart");
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

* **Route-level orchestration** keeps `features/catalog` ignorant of cart navigation
* Pass **callbacks** (`onAddToCart`) into screens instead of importing sibling feature stores
* Shared **entity types** (`Product`, `Order`) live in `entities/` - both features import those
* If many features need pub/sub, add a thin `shared/events` module - not direct store imports

> **Related:** [ADR: State Management Selection](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/adr-state-management-selection/) - when global stores are justified

---

### 9. Testing Seams by Layer

Architecture pays off when each layer tests without booting the full app.

```tsx
// src/features/orders/hooks/useOrders.test.ts
import { renderHook, waitFor } from "@testing-library/react-native";
import { useOrders } from "./useOrders";
import type { Order } from "@/entities/order";
 
const mockOrders: Order[] = [
  { id: "1", title: "Widget", totalCents: 999, status: "pending", placedAt: "2026-01-01" },
];
 
jest.mock("../api/ordersApi", () => ({
  ordersApi: { list: jest.fn(() => Promise.resolve(mockOrders)) },
}));
 
it("loads orders on mount", async () => {
  const { result } = renderHook(() => useOrders());
  await waitFor(() => expect(result.current.loading).toBe(false));
  expect(result.current.orders).toHaveLength(1);
});
```

```tsx
// src/entities/order/lib/formatOrderTotal.test.ts - pure, no renderer
import { formatOrderTotal } from "./formatOrderTotal";
 
it("formats cents as USD", () => {
  expect(
    formatOrderTotal({ id: "1", title: "A", totalCents: 2500, status: "pending", placedAt: "" })
  ).toBe("$25.00");
});
```

* **Entity tests** run in Node - no React Native environment required
* **Hook tests** mock the API adapter, not `fetch` globally
* **Screen tests** pass props and assert composition - avoid mounting Expo Router for every case
* If you cannot mock a module, the boundary is in the wrong place - move IO behind a factory

> **Related:** [Dependency Injection in RN](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/dependency-injection-in-rn/) - injectable services for test doubles

---

### 10. When to Extract a Shared Package

Stay in a single repo until **two apps** or **CI isolation** force a workspace package.

```text
monorepo/
├── apps/
│   └── mobile/              # Expo app - imports @acme/orders
├── packages/
│   ├── orders/              # entity + API types shared with web admin
│   └── ui/                  # design system
└── pnpm-workspace.yaml
```

```json
// apps/mobile/package.json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "@acme/orders": "workspace:*",
    "expo": "~57.0.4",
    "react": "19.2.3",
    "react-native": "0.86.0"
  }
}
```

```ts
// packages/orders/src/index.ts
export type { Order, OrderStatus } from "./model/types";
export { formatOrderTotal } from "./lib/formatOrderTotal";
```

* Extract a package when the **same domain types** ship in mobile and another surface (web, widget)
* Keep **screens and hooks** in the app - packages hold entities, primitives, and isomorphic logic
* Run `npx expo-doctor` after adding workspace deps - Metro must resolve the symlink
* Do not extract prematurely - in-app `src/entities/` is free until a second consumer exists

> **Related:** [../project-setup/shared-packages-and-metro-resolution/shared-packages-and-metro-resolution.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/shared-packages-and-metro-resolution/) - Metro and workspace packages

Dokumen: Modular Monolith vs Multi-App
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/modular-monolith-vs-multi-app/

# Modular Monolith vs Multi-App

A **modular monolith** ships one installable binary with feature modules enabled by flags and config. **Multi-app** repos build separate store listings - different bundle IDs, icons, and often independent release trains. Pick based on release independence, not team preference.

Highlights / Modular Monolith vs Multi-App

* Modular monolith: one bundle ID, feature modules toggled by flags and build-time config
* Multi-app: separate slugs, bundle IDs, and EAS projects per product surface
* APP\_VARIANT and app.config.ts branch identity without forking the repo
* Feature flags gate runtime behavior - they do not replace architectural module boundaries
* White-label is modular monolith with per-tenant config - not N separate codebases
* Split into multi-app when release cadence, compliance, or store listings truly diverge

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```ts
// app.config.ts - one codebase, variant-driven identity
import { ExpoConfig, ConfigContext } from "expo/config";
 
const variant = process.env.APP_VARIANT ?? "consumer";
 
const variants: Record<string, { name: string; bundleId: string; enableB2B: boolean }> = {
  consumer: { name: "Shop", bundleId: "com.example.shop", enableB2B: false },
  business: { name: "Shop Business", bundleId: "com.example.shop.business", enableB2B: true },
};
 
const active = variants[variant] ?? variants.consumer;
 
export default ({ config }: ConfigContext): ExpoConfig => ({
  ...config,
  name: active.name,
  slug: "shop",
  ios: { bundleIdentifier: active.bundleId },
  android: { package: active.bundleId },
  extra: {
    appVariant: variant,
    featureFlags: {
      b2bPortal: active.enableB2B,
      newCheckout: process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_FF_NEW_CHECKOUT === "true",
    },
  },
});
```

```bash
# Same repo - different installable apps via EAS profiles
APP_VARIANT=consumer eas build --profile production-consumer --platform ios
APP_VARIANT=business eas build --profile production-business --platform ios
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Product asks for a "business app" alongside consumer - decide if it is a flag or a store listing.
* White-label tenants need custom bundle IDs but share 90% of code.
* Compliance requires isolating admin tooling from consumer-facing binaries.
* Release managers want one vs two App Store Connect records.

## Working Example

```tsx
// src/shared/config/featureFlags.ts
import Constants from "expo-constants";
 
type FeatureFlags = {
  b2bPortal: boolean;
  newCheckout: boolean;
};
 
export function getFeatureFlags(): FeatureFlags {
  const extra = Constants.expoConfig?.extra as { featureFlags?: FeatureFlags } | undefined;
  return {
    b2bPortal: extra?.featureFlags?.b2bPortal ?? false,
    newCheckout: extra?.featureFlags?.newCheckout ?? false,
  };
}
```

```tsx
// src/app/navigation/useAppRoutes.ts - modular monolith gates tabs at runtime
import { useMemo } from "react";
import { getFeatureFlags } from "@/shared/config/featureFlags";
 
export function useAppRoutes() {
  const flags = getFeatureFlags();
 
  return useMemo(() => {
    const tabs = [
      { name: "index", title: "Home" },
      { name: "orders", title: "Orders" },
    ];
    if (flags.b2bPortal) {
      tabs.push({ name: "b2b", title: "B2B Portal" });
    }
    return tabs;
  }, [flags.b2bPortal]);
}
```

```tsx
// app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx - render only enabled tabs
import { Tabs } from "expo-router";
import { useAppRoutes } from "@/app/navigation/useAppRoutes";
 
export default function TabLayout() {
  const routes = useAppRoutes();
 
  return (
    <Tabs>
      {routes.map((route) => (
        <Tabs.Screen key={route.name} name={route.name} options={{ title: route.title }} />
      ))}
    </Tabs>
  );
}
```

```json
// eas.json - multi-app: separate profiles per store listing
{
  "build": {
    "production-consumer": {
      "env": { "APP_VARIANT": "consumer" },
      "channel": "production-consumer"
    },
    "production-business": {
      "env": { "APP_VARIANT": "business" },
      "channel": "production-business"
    }
  }
}
```

```text
# Multi-app repo layout (when listings fully diverge)
apps/
├── consumer-mobile/     # slug: shop-consumer
└── business-mobile/     # slug: shop-business
packages/
├── features/            # shared feature modules
└── ui/
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* **Modular monolith** toggles `b2bPortal` tab via `extra.featureFlags` - one codebase, two EAS profiles.
* **`APP_VARIANT`** changes bundle ID and display name - users install two apps from one repo.
* **Multi-app** layout separates `apps/consumer-mobile` and `apps/business-mobile` when CI, icons, and native config diverge heavily.
* Feature flags **hide UI** - they do not remove dead code from the binary unless paired with build-time stripping.

## Deep Dive

### How It Works

#### Comparison matrix

| Dimension | Modular monolith | Multi-app repo |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Store listings | One or variants via bundle ID | Separate per `apps/*` |
| Code sharing | In-repo modules / flags | Workspace packages |
| Release cadence | Single train (flags gate risk) | Independent per app |
| Binary size | All modules compiled in\* | Each app ships only its graph |
| OTA updates | One channel per variant | Channel per app slug |
| Team ownership | Feature flags + module boundaries | Package boundaries + CODEOWNERS |

\*Use lazy routes and dead-code elimination; flags alone do not shrink native size.

#### Modular monolith patterns

| Pattern | Mechanism | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Runtime flag | `extra.featureFlags` | Show B2B tab |
| Build-time variant | `APP_VARIANT` in `app.config.ts` | Different bundle ID |
| Lazy route | Expo Router dynamic import | Load `b2b` screens only when enabled |
| Module boundary | `features/b2b/` isolated public API | Disable imports when flag off |

#### When multi-app wins

* **Different Apple/Google developer accounts** per product.
* **Regulatory isolation** - HIPAA admin app cannot ship consumer analytics SDKs.
* **Radically different native config** - dissimilar plugins, entitlements, or minimum OS.
* **Independent versioning** - business app on 3.2 while consumer is 8.0.

#### White-label

White-label is usually **modular monolith + per-tenant build profile**:

```ts
// app.config.ts (excerpt) - tenant from env at build time
const tenant = process.env.TENANT ?? "acme";
 
export default {
  name: process.env.APP_NAME ?? "Acme Shop",
  slug: `shop-${tenant}`,
  ios: { bundleIdentifier: `com.${tenant}.shop` },
  extra: { tenant, primaryColor: process.env.PRIMARY_COLOR },
};
```

Each tenant gets an EAS profile - not a forked Git branch.

### TypeScript Notes

```tsx
// Fail closed when required module is disabled
import { getFeatureFlags } from "@/shared/config/featureFlags";
 
export function B2BPortalScreen() {
  if (!getFeatureFlags().b2bPortal) {
    return null; // or redirect - route should also be unregistered
  }
  // ...
}
```

Prefer **excluding routes** from the navigator over rendering empty screens.

## Gotchas

* **Feature flags without module boundaries** - Disabled B2B still links if `features/b2b` imports leak. **Fix:** Isolate `features/b2b`; lint-import consumer-only apps away from it.
* **One slug, two bundle IDs** - Expo dashboard and OTA channels conflate. **Fix:** Separate EAS Update channels per `APP_VARIANT`.
* **Runtime flags for compliance** - Admin code still in the JS bundle. **Fix:** Multi-app or build-time exclusion for regulated SKUs.
* **Premature multi-app split** - Two apps, 99% shared code, double CI cost. **Fix:** Start monolith + variants; extract `apps/` when native config diverges.
* **Hard-coded API URLs per app** - Duplicated env logic. **Fix:** Central `getAppConfig()` keyed by `appVariant`.
* **Expo Go cannot test variants realistically** - Bundle IDs and icons need dev builds. **Fix:** EAS development profile per variant.
* **God `if (flags.x)` in every screen** - Unmaintainable branching. **Fix:** Register routes and navigators from a single `useAppRoutes()` / module manifest.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Modular monolith + flags | Same core product, optional modules | Compliance requires code separation |
| Multi-app monorepo | Independent releases, different native config | Only icon/name differs |
| Single app, server-driven flags | Remote experiments (LaunchDarkly, etc.) | Store listing must split |
| Flavors (Android) / schemes (iOS) bare | Brownfield native already flavorized | Greenfield managed Expo - use `app.config.ts` |
| Separate repos | Acquired products with no shared roadmap | Teams sharing features weekly |

## FAQs

What is a modular monolith on mobile?

One installable app binary containing multiple feature modules. Modules are bounded in code (`features/b2b`) and enabled via config or flags - not separate microservices.

When is one binary with flags enough?

When products share navigation, native plugins, and release cadence - only some tabs or flows differ (B2B portal, beta features, tenant branding).

When do I need separate apps in the repo?

When bundle IDs, store accounts, native entitlements, or release schedules are genuinely independent - not merely different themes.

Do feature flags remove code from the bundle?

Runtime flags hide UI; they do not tree-shake native modules. Use build-time variants or separate apps to exclude regulated SDKs.

How does Expo Updates work with variants?

Assign **one channel per variant** (`production-consumer`, `production-business`). Publishing to the wrong channel updates the wrong listing.

Can modular monolith support white-label?

Yes - `TENANT` env in `app.config.ts` per EAS profile. Shared `packages/features` hold code; tenant assets live in profile-specific env or `assets/tenants/<name>/`.

APP\_VARIANT vs EXPO\_PUBLIC feature flags?

`APP_VARIANT` typically drives **identity** (name, bundle ID) at build time. `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` flags suit **runtime experiments** embedded in JS - both can coexist.

How do I hide Expo Router routes when a flag is off?

Conditionally register `Tabs.Screen` / `Stack.Screen` entries from a route manifest - do not rely on users never deep-linking to disabled paths.

Is multi-app the same as monorepo?

No. Monorepo is repo layout. Multi-app means **multiple Expo apps** (`apps/a`, `apps/b`). A monorepo can host one app (modular monolith) or many.

What about Android applicationId vs iOS bundleIdentifier?

Both branch from `app.config.ts` per variant. Keep them in sync with `APP_VARIANT` - mismatched IDs break deep links and push credentials.

Can I merge consumer and business apps later?

Easier than splitting. Migrate business-only modules behind flags, unify bundle ID strategy deliberately - store listings may require user reinstall.

How does this relate to EAS build profiles?

Each profile sets `env` (`APP_VARIANT`, `TENANT`, flags). Profiles are the delivery mechanism for both monolith variants and multi-app targets.

Should B2B and consumer share analytics?

Architecturally separate event namespaces per `appVariant`. Multi-app may use different analytics projects - plan before merging dashboards.

Modular monolith vs feature flags service?

Local flags gate **compile-time modules and navigation**. Remote flag services gate **experiments** - use both: module boundaries locally, remote for A/B.

Dokumen: Authentication Best Practices
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/best-practices/

# Authentication Best Practices

A condensed summary of **25 authentication essentials** for Expo SDK 57 apps, mapped to **OWASP Mobile** themes: insecure storage (M2), insecure communication (M3), insecure authentication (M4), insufficient cryptography (M5), and insecure authorization (M6). Drawn from every page in this section.

Highlights / Authentication Best Practices

* 25 essentials mapped to OWASP Mobile - storage, transport, session, and OAuth
* Mobile clients are untrusted - short TTL, rotation, and server-side authorization
* Never AsyncStorage for tokens; never client secrets in EXPO\_PUBLIC\_
* Logout clears SecureStore, Query cache, and navigation - not React state alone
* OAuth uses PKCE + system browser - not implicit flow in WebView
* Account switch and compromised-device policies need explicit ADRs for regulated apps

1. **Treat the mobile client as untrusted:** Assume attackers can extract bundled values, hook native APIs, and replay tokens from compromised devices - design sessions that limit blast radius with short access TTL and refresh rotation.
2. **Never store refresh tokens in AsyncStorage:** Unencrypted SQLite is trivially readable on rooted devices - use `expo-secure-store` with `WHEN_UNLOCKED_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY` (OWASP M2: Insecure Data Storage).
3. **Keep access tokens short-lived:** 5–15 minute access token TTL limits damage from interception - refresh proactively before expiry, not only after 401 (OWASP M4: Insecure Authentication).
4. **Rotate refresh tokens on every exchange:** Issue a new refresh token and invalidate the previous one - detect reuse as a breach signal and revoke the entire token family (OWASP M4).
5. **Implement logout everywhere:** Local sign-out is insufficient for stolen devices - expose server-side refresh revocation that invalidates all sessions for the user (OWASP M4).
6. **Clear SecureStore, Query cache, and navigation on logout:** `deleteItemAsync` for all auth keys, `queryClient.clear()`, and `router.replace` to sign-in - Android back must not reveal authenticated screens (OWASP M2).
7. **Use Authorization Code + PKCE for OAuth:** Mobile is a public client - never implicit flow (`response_type=token`) or embedded WebViews; use `expo-auth-session` with `usePKCE: true` (OWASP M4).
8. **Exchange OAuth codes on your backend when secrets exist:** Client secrets do not belong in the app bundle - send `code` + `code_verifier` to your server for token exchange (OWASP M1: Improper Platform Usage).
9. **Register redirect URIs per build flavor:** `makeRedirectUri()` output must match Google, Apple, and IdP consoles for dev, preview, and production - `redirect_uri_mismatch` is the top OAuth integration failure.
10. **Never put OAuth client secrets in `EXPO_PUBLIC_*`:** Public env vars inline into the Hermes bundle - audit with `npx expo config --type public` before every release (OWASP M2).
11. **Attach tokens via `Authorization: Bearer` - not URL query params:** Query strings land in logs, analytics, and referrer headers - headers only for access tokens (OWASP M3: Insecure Communication).
12. **Use HTTPS for all auth and API endpoints:** No cleartext exceptions in production - system TLS on SDK 57 is the default; certificate pinning requires an ADR (OWASP M3).
13. **Single 401 retry with deduplicated refresh:** One in-flight refresh promise for parallel 401s - infinite retry loops mask misconfiguration and hammer the auth server (OWASP M4).
14. **Distinguish offline from revoked sessions:** Network failures during refresh should not force sign-out - `session_expired_offline` vs `session_expired` prevents airplane-mode logout rage (OWASP M7: Client Code Quality).
15. **Proactive refresh on foreground resume:** `AppState` listener refreshes when `shouldRefresh(session)` after background - users should not see hourly re-login prompts (OWASP M4).
16. **Apply clock skew buffer to client expiry:** Refresh 30–120 seconds before client `expiresAt` - prefer server `serverTime` in refresh responses over device clock alone (OWASP M5: Insufficient Cryptography).
17. **Biometrics prove presence - not identity to the server:** Use `expo-local-authentication` for step-up UX; high-risk endpoints still need server MFA or step-up tokens (OWASP M4).
18. **Offer passcode fallback for biometric flows:** `disableDeviceFallback: false` - trapping users without enrolled biometrics fails accessibility and App Review expectations (OWASP M1).
19. **Namespace SecureStore keys per account:** Multi-account apps use `auth.refresh_token.{accountId}` - switch account purges TanStack Query and Zustand before bootstrap (OWASP M2 / M6).
20. **Bind refresh tokens to device ID server-side:** Send stable `deviceId` on login and refresh - server rejects unknown devices; users can revoke lost devices from settings (OWASP M4).
21. **Include `userId` in TanStack Query cache keys:** Prevents cross-account data flash during switch even if purge races - `queryKey: ['orders', userId]` (OWASP M6: Insecure Authorization).
22. **Never trust client-side JWT claims for authorization:** Decode claims for display only - server validates roles and scopes on every request (OWASP M6).
23. **Scrub tokens from logs and crash reports:** Redact `Authorization` headers in Sentry breadcrumbs and structured logging - tokens in crash dumps are a common audit finding (OWASP M2).
24. **Degrade gracefully on jailbreak/root signals:** High-risk actions (payments, PII export) warrant blocks or MFA - do not hard-lock entire apps on spoofable signals without product/legal approval (OWASP M8: Code Tampering).
25. **Test auth on development builds - not only Expo Go:** OAuth redirect URIs, Keychain access groups, and Apple Sign In entitlements differ from Expo Go - E2E auth tests run against real bundle IDs before store submission (OWASP M9: Reverse Engineering).

## FAQs

Which OWASP Mobile categories does this section cover most?

* **M2** (storage), **M3** (transport), **M4** (authentication), **M5** (crypto), and **M6** (authorization) - the five categories most relevant to session handling.
* M7–M10 (code quality, tampering, reverse engineering, extraneous functionality) appear in lifecycle and integrity guidance.

What is the minimum auth stack for a new Expo app?

* `expo-secure-store` for refresh tokens.
* `expo-auth-session` + `expo-crypto` if OAuth.
* TanStack Query with user-scoped keys and `queryClient.clear()` on logout.
* `AuthProvider` with bootstrapping → authenticated → expired state machine.

Should I implement certificate pinning for auth?

* Default to system TLS - pinning is an ADR-level decision with operational cost (rotation, outages).
* See [Certificate Pinning](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/certificate-pinning/) before enabling.

How do I prioritize these 25 items?

* **Week 1:** Items 2, 3, 6, 7, 10, 11 - storage, TTL, logout, OAuth basics.
* **Before production:** Items 4, 5, 9, 12, 13, 25 - rotation, revocation, redirect URIs, E2E on dev builds.
* **Multi-account / fintech:** Items 19, 20, 21, 24 - account isolation, device binding, integrity policy.

Where do backend auth requirements fit?

* Client rules assume server supports refresh rotation, device binding, and revocation endpoints.
* Pair with backend OWASP API Security - mobile auth fails if server accepts long-lived opaque sessions without rotation.

Does Expo Go satisfy production auth testing?

* No - use `expo-dev-client` with production bundle ID and OAuth credentials before release.
* SecureStore works in Expo Go, but redirect URIs and Apple/Google console entries will not match store binaries.

Dokumen: Biometrics with LocalAuthentication
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/biometrics-with-localauthentication/

# Biometrics with LocalAuthentication

`expo-local-authentication` wraps **Face ID**, **Touch ID**, and **Android biometrics** for step-up authentication. Biometrics answer "is the person holding the phone the device owner?" - they do not replace your backend session.

Highlights / Biometrics with LocalAuthentication

* Biometrics prove user presence - they do not replace server authentication
* Use expo-local-authentication for Face ID, Touch ID, and Android fingerprint
* Step-up auth re-prompts biometrics before sensitive actions - transfers, password changes
* Offer passcode fallback - Apple requires it; never trap users without biometrics enrolled
* Store tokens in SecureStore; biometrics gate reading them - not a second password store
* Respect accessibility - always provide PIN/password path for users who cannot use biometrics

## Prerequisites

```bash
npx expo install expo-local-authentication expo-secure-store
```

Add the Face ID usage description on iOS:

```json
{
  "expo": {
    "ios": {
      "infoPlist": {
        "NSFaceIDUsageDescription": "Unlock MyApp and confirm sensitive actions."
      }
    }
  }
}
```

> **Tooling:** These examples target **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4), **React Native 0.86.0**, and **React 19.2.3**.

---

## Capability Check Before Prompting

Never call `authenticateAsync` without checking hardware and enrollment.

```ts
import * as LocalAuthentication from "expo-local-authentication";
 
export type BiometricCapability =
  | { available: false; reason: "no_hardware" | "not_enrolled" }
  | { available: true; types: LocalAuthentication.AuthenticationType[] };
 
export async function getBiometricCapability(): Promise<BiometricCapability> {
  const hasHardware = await LocalAuthentication.hasHardwareAsync();
  if (!hasHardware) {
    return { available: false, reason: "no_hardware" };
  }
 
  const enrolled = await LocalAuthentication.isEnrolledAsync();
  if (!enrolled) {
    return { available: false, reason: "not_enrolled" };
  }
 
  const types = await LocalAuthentication.supportedAuthenticationTypesAsync();
  return { available: true, types };
}
```

* **`hasHardwareAsync`** - device has biometric sensor (or secure enclave for Face ID)
* **`isEnrolledAsync`** - user has registered at least one fingerprint or face
* **`supportedAuthenticationTypesAsync`** - returns `FINGERPRINT`, `FACIAL_RECOGNITION`, `IRIS` bitmask
* When unavailable, fall back to **password re-entry** or **device passcode** - never brick the flow

---

## App Unlock Pattern

Gate access to stored refresh tokens behind biometrics on cold start.

```tsx
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { ActivityIndicator, View } from "react-native";
import * as LocalAuthentication from "expo-local-authentication";
import { secureTokenStorage } from "@/features/auth/adapters/secureTokenStorage";
import { refreshFromStoredToken } from "@/features/auth/api/refreshSession";
 
type UnlockState = "checking" | "locked" | "unlocked";
 
export function BiometricGate({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  const [state, setState] = useState<UnlockState>("checking");
 
  useEffect(() => {
    (async () => {
      const token = await secureTokenStorage.loadRefreshToken();
      if (!token) {
        setState("unlocked"); // no session - auth flow handles sign-in
        return;
      }
 
      const capability = await getBiometricCapability();
      if (!capability.available) {
        await refreshFromStoredToken();
        setState("unlocked");
        return;
      }
 
      const result = await LocalAuthentication.authenticateAsync({
        promptMessage: "Unlock MyApp",
        cancelLabel: "Sign out",
        disableDeviceFallback: false,
      });
 
      if (result.success) {
        await refreshFromStoredToken();
        setState("unlocked");
      } else {
        setState("locked");
      }
    })();
  }, []);
 
  if (state === "checking") {
    return (
      <View style={{ flex: 1, justifyContent: "center", alignItems: "center" }}>
        <ActivityIndicator />
      </View>
    );
  }
 
  if (state === "locked") {
    return <SignOutOrRetryScreen onRetry={() => setState("checking")} />;
  }
 
  return <>{children}</>;
}
```

* Prompt **after** confirming a refresh token exists - no biometrics on first-time users
* `disableDeviceFallback: false` allows device PIN - required for App Store accessibility expectations
* **Cancel → Sign out** is clearer than an infinite lock screen
* Refresh session **after** successful biometric - access token stays in memory until unlock

> **Related:** [SecureStore & Keychain/Keystore](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/securestore-and-keychain-keystore/) - where refresh tokens persist

---

## Step-Up Auth for Sensitive Actions

Re-prompt biometrics before high-risk operations even when the user is already signed in.

```ts
import * as LocalAuthentication from "expo-local-authentication";
 
export async function requireStepUpAuth(actionLabel: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const capability = await getBiometricCapability();
 
  if (!capability.available) {
    // Fall back to password modal or MFA challenge
    return promptPasswordModal(actionLabel);
  }
 
  const result = await LocalAuthentication.authenticateAsync({
    promptMessage: `Confirm ${actionLabel}`,
    fallbackLabel: "Use passcode",
  });
 
  return result.success;
}
```

```tsx
// Wire transfer screen
async function handleTransfer() {
  const confirmed = await requireStepUpAuth("wire transfer");
  if (!confirmed) return;
 
  await api.post("/transfers", { amount, toAccount });
}
```

* **Step-up** is time-bound - re-prompt if the sensitive screen was backgrounded > 60 seconds
* Server should accept a **step-up token** or recent MFA timestamp for high-risk endpoints - client biometrics alone are not proof for the backend
* Actions warranting step-up: money movement, password change, export PII, disable 2FA, add trusted device
* Log step-up failures without storing biometric data - only success/failure enum

---

## Settings Toggle: Opt-In Biometric Unlock

Let users enable or disable biometric unlock without affecting their server session.

```ts
import AsyncStorage from "@react-native-async-storage/async-storage";
 
const BIOMETRIC_PREF_KEY = "prefs.biometric_unlock_enabled";
 
export async function isBiometricUnlockEnabled() {
  return (await AsyncStorage.getItem(BIOMETRIC_PREF_KEY)) === "1";
}
 
export async function setBiometricUnlockEnabled(enabled: boolean) {
  if (enabled) {
    const capability = await getBiometricCapability();
    if (!capability.available) {
      throw new Error("Biometrics not available on this device");
    }
    // Prove enrollment works before saving preference
    const result = await LocalAuthentication.authenticateAsync({
      promptMessage: "Enable biometric unlock",
    });
    if (!result.success) return false;
  }
 
  await AsyncStorage.setItem(BIOMETRIC_PREF_KEY, enabled ? "1" : "0");
  return true;
}
```

* **Preference** in AsyncStorage is fine - it is not a secret, just a boolean flag
* Require a **successful biometric** when enabling - prevents toggling on without verifying it works
* Disabling biometrics does not sign the user out - only removes the unlock gate
* Re-prompt enrollment check after OS update - users may add/remove fingerprints

---

## Android vs iOS Behavior

```text
┌────────────────┬─────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┐
│ Concern        │ iOS                         │ Android                      │
├────────────────┼─────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────┤
│ Face           │ Face ID (TrueDepth)         │ Face unlock (vendor-dependent)│
│ Fingerprint    │ Touch ID (older devices)    │ Fingerprint / under-display  │
│ Fallback       │ Device passcode via system  │ Device PIN/pattern           │
│ Prompt         │ ASAuthorization-style sheet │ BiometricPrompt API          │
│ Cancel         │ User cancel ≠ failure lock  │ Vendor-specific              │
└────────────────┴─────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────┘
```

```ts
import { Platform } from "react-native";
 
const promptMessage = Platform.select({
  ios: "Unlock with Face ID",
  android: "Confirm with fingerprint",
  default: "Authenticate",
});
```

* Test on **physical devices** - simulators emulate biometrics with enrolled/not-enrolled toggles but miss vendor quirks
* Android **face unlock** security level varies by OEM - treat step-up on Android as UX convenience, not strong assurance
* iOS **Face ID** in simulator: Features → Face ID → Enrolled, then Matching Face
* Do not cache `authenticateAsync` results - each sensitive action gets a fresh prompt

---

## Security Limits

```text
What biometrics DO                    What biometrics DO NOT
────────────────────────────────────  ─────────────────────────────────────
Prove recent user presence            Replace server-side MFA
Speed up returning-user UX            Encrypt data (use SecureStore)
Reduce shoulder-surfing vs typing PIN   Survive jailbreak extraction alone
Meet some regulatory step-up UX       Prove identity to your API without backend
```

* Pair biometrics with **short access token TTL** and [refresh rotation](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/refresh-token-rotation/)
* For regulated apps, send a **backend step-up challenge** after local biometric success
* Never store biometric templates - Expo does not expose them; do not build custom biometric storage
* See [Security Rules for Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/security-rules-for-mobile/) for defense-in-depth expectations

---

## FAQs

Should I use biometrics instead of a login password?

* No - users still sign in with password/OAuth once.
* Biometrics unlock an existing session stored in SecureStore - they are not a credential replacement.

What happens after too many failed attempts?

* iOS/Android lock out biometrics temporarily - fall back to device passcode via `disableDeviceFallback: false`.
* Your app should offer explicit sign-out - do not implement custom lockout counters on top of OS behavior.

Can I require biometrics for every API call?

* Impractical - users would face dozens of prompts.
* Use step-up for sensitive mutations; rely on access tokens for routine reads.

Does expo-local-authentication work in background tasks?

* No - biometric UI requires foreground user interaction.
* Background refresh uses refresh tokens without biometric gate - see Auth Session Lifecycle.

## Related

* [SecureStore & Keychain/Keystore](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/securestore-and-keychain-keystore/) - token storage under biometric gate
* [Mobile Auth Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/mobile-auth-basics/) - session models and sign-out
* [Auth Session Lifecycle](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/auth-session-lifecycle/) - foreground unlock vs background refresh

Dokumen: expo-auth-session & OAuth
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/expo-auth-session-and-oauth/

# expo-auth-session & OAuth

Authorization Code with **PKCE** is the standard OAuth pattern for Expo apps. This page covers redirect URI setup, `expo-auth-session` wiring, and provider-specific quirks for **Google** and **Apple** on SDK 57.

Highlights / expo-auth-session & OAuth

* Mobile OAuth must use Authorization Code + PKCE - never implicit flow in a WebView
* Register redirect URIs per environment: Expo Go, dev client, and production scheme differ
* Exchange authorization codes on your backend - client secrets do not belong in the app
* Google requires platform-specific OAuth client IDs; Apple Sign In is mandatory for some App Store categories
* Use makeRedirectUri() - hardcoded redirect strings break across build flavors
* Test OAuth on development builds - Expo Go redirect behavior is not identical to store binaries

## Prerequisites

```bash
npx expo install expo-auth-session expo-crypto expo-web-browser
```

`expo-web-browser` opens the system browser (or ASWebAuthenticationSession on iOS) - prefer it over embedded WebViews for OAuth.

Register a custom URL scheme in `app.config.ts`:

```ts
// app.config.ts
export default {
  expo: {
    name: "MyApp",
    slug: "my-app",
    scheme: "myapp",
    ios: { bundleIdentifier: "com.example.myapp" },
    android: { package: "com.example.myapp" },
  },
};
```

> **Tooling:** These examples target **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4), **React Native 0.86.0**, and **React 19.2.3**.

---

## PKCE Fundamentals

PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange) prevents authorization code interception on public mobile clients.

```ts
import * as Crypto from "expo-crypto";
 
function base64UrlEncode(bytes: Uint8Array) {
  const base64 = btoa(String.fromCharCode(...bytes));
  return base64.replace(/\+/g, "-").replace(/\//g, "_").replace(/=+$/, "");
}
 
export async function createPkcePair() {
  const verifierBytes = await Crypto.getRandomBytesAsync(32);
  const codeVerifier = base64UrlEncode(verifierBytes);
 
  const digest = await Crypto.digestStringAsync(
    Crypto.CryptoDigestAlgorithm.SHA256,
    codeVerifier,
    { encoding: Crypto.CryptoEncoding.BASE64 },
  );
 
  const codeChallenge = digest
    .replace(/\+/g, "-")
    .replace(/\//g, "_")
    .replace(/=+$/, "");
 
  return { codeVerifier, codeChallenge };
}
```

* Generate a random **code\_verifier** and send its SHA-256 hash as **code\_challenge** on the authorize request
* Send the original **code\_verifier** when exchanging the authorization code for tokens
* `expo-auth-session` generates PKCE pairs automatically when `usePKCE: true` - manual generation is for custom backends
* Never use **implicit flow** (`response_type=token`) - access tokens in redirect URLs leak via logs and referrer headers

> **Related:** [Mobile Auth Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/mobile-auth-basics/) - normalizing OAuth tokens into your `Session` type

---

## Redirect URIs with makeRedirectUri

Redirect URIs must match exactly what you register with each OAuth provider.

```ts
import { makeRedirectUri } from "expo-auth-session";
import * as AuthSession from "expo-auth-session";
 
const redirectUri = makeRedirectUri({
  scheme: "myapp",
  path: "oauth",
});
 
// Examples by environment:
// Dev client / standalone:  myapp://oauth
// Expo Go (proxy):          https://auth.expo.io/@owner/slug  (legacy - avoid for production)
 
const discovery = {
  authorizationEndpoint: "https://accounts.example.com/oauth/authorize",
  tokenEndpoint: "https://accounts.example.com/oauth/token",
};
 
const [request, response, promptAsync] = AuthSession.useAuthRequest(
  {
    clientId: process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID!,
    redirectUri,
    scopes: ["openid", "profile", "email"],
    usePKCE: true,
    responseType: AuthSession.ResponseType.Code,
  },
  discovery,
);
```

* **`makeRedirectUri`** derives the correct URI from your `scheme`, `native`/`development` build, and Expo config
* Register **every** variant (dev, preview, production) in the provider console - mismatches cause `redirect_uri_mismatch`
* Prefer **custom scheme** redirects (`myapp://`) for production - not `exp://` or Expo Go proxy URLs
* Log `redirectUri` once in development to copy into Google Cloud Console and Apple Developer portal

---

## Complete Sign-In Flow

```tsx
import { useEffect } from "react";
import { Button, Text, View } from "react-native";
import * as AuthSession from "expo-auth-session";
import { makeRedirectUri } from "expo-auth-session";
import * as WebBrowser from "expo-web-browser";
import * as SecureStore from "expo-secure-store";
 
WebBrowser.maybeCompleteAuthSession();
 
const redirectUri = makeRedirectUri({ scheme: "myapp", path: "oauth" });
 
const discovery: AuthSession.DiscoveryDocument = {
  authorizationEndpoint: `${process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL}/oauth/authorize`,
  tokenEndpoint: `${process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL}/oauth/token`,
};
 
export function OAuthSignInButton() {
  const [request, response, promptAsync] = AuthSession.useAuthRequest(
    {
      clientId: process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID!,
      redirectUri,
      scopes: ["openid", "profile", "email"],
      usePKCE: true,
    },
    discovery,
  );
 
  useEffect(() => {
    if (response?.type !== "success") return;
 
    const { code } = response.params;
    exchangeCodeOnBackend(code, request?.codeVerifier);
  }, [response]);
 
  return (
    <View>
      <Button
        title="Sign in"
        disabled={!request}
        onPress={() => promptAsync({ preferEphemeralSession: true })}
      />
    </View>
  );
}
 
async function exchangeCodeOnBackend(code: string, codeVerifier?: string) {
  const res = await fetch(`${process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL}/auth/oauth/callback`, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
    body: JSON.stringify({ code, codeVerifier, redirectUri }),
  });
 
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error("OAuth exchange failed");
 
  const { refreshToken, accessToken, expiresAt, userId } = await res.json();
 
  await SecureStore.setItemAsync("auth.refresh_token", refreshToken, {
    keychainAccessible: SecureStore.WHEN_UNLOCKED_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY,
  });
 
  // Hydrate AuthProvider session state with { accessToken, refreshToken, expiresAt, userId }
}
```

* **`WebBrowser.maybeCompleteAuthSession()`** dismisses the browser tab when the redirect fires - call once at module scope
* Exchange the code on **your backend** when you have a confidential client or need to attach device metadata
* `preferEphemeralSession: true` on iOS avoids sharing cookies with Safari - good for shared devices
* Persist refresh tokens via [SecureStore](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/securestore-and-keychain-keystore/) after exchange

> **Related:** [../expo-rules/security-rules-for-mobile/security-rules-for-mobile.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/security-rules-for-mobile/) - never ship OAuth client secrets in the bundle

---

## Google Sign-In Quirks

Google requires **separate OAuth client IDs** per platform.

```text
Google Cloud Console → APIs & Services → Credentials
 
┌─────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Client type     │ Used for                                     │
├─────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ iOS             │ Bundle ID: com.example.myapp                 │
│ Android         │ Package + SHA-1 signing cert fingerprint     │
│ Web             │ Backend code exchange (client secret)        │
└─────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

```ts
// Use the iOS or Android client ID in the app - NOT the web client secret
const GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID = Platform.select({
  ios: process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_IOS_CLIENT_ID,
  android: process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_ANDROID_CLIENT_ID,
  default: process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID,
});
```

* **Android** requires the SHA-1 of your **upload key** and **app signing key** from Play Console - add both to Google Cloud
* **iOS** uses the reversed client ID as a URL scheme when using Google SDK - with `expo-auth-session`, your app `scheme` handles the redirect
* The **Web client ID** is for server-side token exchange - its secret stays on the backend
* Enable **Google People API** or relevant scopes only after privacy review - each scope triggers Play Data Safety declarations

Common errors:

| Error | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| `redirect_uri_mismatch` | Copy exact `makeRedirectUri()` output into Google console |
| `invalid_client` on Android | Add correct SHA-1 for the build profile you are testing |
| `access_denied` | OAuth consent screen in Testing mode - add test users |

---

## Apple Sign-In Quirks

Apple Sign In is required when you offer third-party sign-in on iOS for apps in certain categories.

```json
{
  "expo": {
    "ios": {
      "usesAppleSignIn": true,
      "bundleIdentifier": "com.example.myapp"
    },
    "plugins": ["expo-apple-authentication"]
  }
}
```

```bash
npx expo install expo-apple-authentication
```

```tsx
import * as AppleAuthentication from "expo-apple-authentication";
import { Platform } from "react-native";
 
export function AppleSignInButton() {
  if (Platform.OS !== "ios") return null;
 
  return (
    <AppleAuthentication.AppleAuthenticationButton
      buttonType={AppleAuthentication.AppleAuthenticationButtonType.SIGN_IN}
      buttonStyle={AppleAuthentication.AppleAuthenticationButtonStyle.BLACK}
      cornerRadius={8}
      style={{ width: "100%", height: 44 }}
      onPress={async () => {
        const credential = await AppleAuthentication.signInAsync({
          requestedScopes: [
            AppleAuthentication.AppleAuthenticationScope.FULL_NAME,
            AppleAuthentication.AppleAuthenticationScope.EMAIL,
          ],
        });
 
        await sendAppleCredentialToBackend(credential);
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

* **Full name and email** are returned only on the **first** sign-in - persist immediately server-side
* Apple may relay email via **Hide My Email** - your backend must accept `@privaterelay.appleid.com` addresses
* `expo-apple-authentication` uses native Sign in with Apple - distinct from generic OAuth browser flow
* Offer Apple alongside Google on iOS when Google is present - App Review enforces parity rules in many app categories

---

## Provider Discovery and Custom IdPs

For Auth0, Okta, or Keycloak, use built-in discovery:

```ts
import * as AuthSession from "expo-auth-session";
 
const discovery = await AuthSession.fetchDiscoveryAsync(
  "https://your-tenant.auth0.com",
);
 
const [request, response, promptAsync] = AuthSession.useAuthRequest(
  {
    clientId: process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_AUTH0_CLIENT_ID!,
    redirectUri: makeRedirectUri({ scheme: "myapp" }),
    scopes: ["openid", "profile", "offline_access"],
    usePKCE: true,
    extraParams: { audience: "https://api.example.com" },
  },
  discovery,
);
```

* **`offline_access`** scope is required on many IdPs to receive a refresh token
* **`audience`** (Auth0) ensures access tokens are minted for your API - not just the IdP userinfo endpoint
* Cache discovery documents - fetching on every render adds latency; store in module scope or context
* Custom IdPs may require **custom URL paths** - verify `authorizationEndpoint` and `tokenEndpoint` in discovery JSON

---

## Development vs Production Checklist

```text
Before shipping OAuth:
□ redirectUri logged and registered for prod scheme (myapp://)
□ Google Android SHA-1 matches EAS production keystore
□ Apple Sign In entitlement present in provisioning profile
□ Backend validates code_verifier (PKCE)
□ Refresh tokens stored in SecureStore - not AsyncStorage
□ Tested on physical device with development build - not only Expo Go
□ OAuth tested after app kill + relaunch (cold start refresh)
```

* **Expo Go** uses Expo's bundle identifier - Google/Apple prod credentials will not match
* Build a **development client** (`expo-dev-client`) with your real bundle ID before OAuth integration testing
* Staging and production should use **separate OAuth clients** - prevents staging tokens working against prod APIs

> **Related:** [Auth Session Lifecycle](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/auth-session-lifecycle/) - refresh after OAuth on app resume

---

## FAQs

Can I use a WebView for OAuth?

* No - embedded WebViews are vulnerable to MITM, violate provider policies, and cannot share system SSO state.
* Use `expo-auth-session` + `expo-web-browser` (system browser / ASWebAuthenticationSession).

Where does the OAuth client secret go?

* On your backend only - the mobile app sends the authorization code + code\_verifier to your server, which exchanges with the secret.

Why does Google work on iOS but fail on Android?

* Almost always a SHA-1 fingerprint mismatch - run `eas credentials` and add the correct fingerprint to Google Cloud Console.

Do I need universal links for OAuth?

* Custom URL schemes (`myapp://`) are sufficient for most apps.
* Universal links (`https://app.example.com/oauth`) add complexity but avoid scheme collision - optional for enterprise.

How do I handle OAuth cancel?

* `response.type === "cancel"` or `"dismiss"` - show nothing or a soft message; do not treat as an error worth logging to Sentry.
