# Auth Security Highlights Summary

Every highlight bullet from the 8 pages in this section, gathered on one page and grouped by the page it came from.

Highlights / Auth Security Highlights Summary

* Mobile apps are untrusted clients - assume tokens can be extracted from a compromised device
* Mobile OAuth must use Authorization Code + PKCE - never implicit flow in a WebView
* expo-secure-store maps to iOS Keychain and Android Keystore - hardware-backed on supported devices
* Biometrics prove user presence - they do not replace server authentication
* Rotate refresh tokens on every exchange - detect reuse as a breach signal
* Account switch must purge TanStack Query cache, Zustand slices, and in-memory tokens

## [Mobile Auth Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/mobile-auth-basics/)

* Mobile apps are untrusted clients - assume tokens can be extracted from a compromised device
* Prefer short-lived access tokens + refresh rotation; never infinite sessions on device
* Store refresh tokens in expo-secure-store - AsyncStorage is for preferences only
* Logout must clear secure storage, server session, and client caches - not just React state
* OAuth on mobile uses PKCE and custom URL schemes - not implicit flow in a WebView
* Pair auth with API client interceptors - see networking-api for 401 retry patterns

## [expo-auth-session & OAuth](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/expo-auth-session-and-oauth/)

* Mobile OAuth must use Authorization Code + PKCE - never implicit flow in a WebView
* Register redirect URIs per environment: Expo Go, dev client, and production scheme differ
* Exchange authorization codes on your backend - client secrets do not belong in the app
* Google requires platform-specific OAuth client IDs; Apple Sign In is mandatory for some App Store categories
* Use makeRedirectUri() - hardcoded redirect strings break across build flavors
* Test OAuth on development builds - Expo Go redirect behavior is not identical to store binaries

## [SecureStore & Keychain/Keystore](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/securestore-and-keychain-keystore/)

* expo-secure-store maps to iOS Keychain and Android Keystore - hardware-backed on supported devices
* Never store refresh tokens, PINs, or API secrets in AsyncStorage or plain MMKV
* SecureStore has a ~2 KB per-item limit - store tokens, not entire user profiles
* Use WHEN\_UNLOCKED\_THIS\_DEVICE\_ONLY so backups and iCloud Keychain do not export secrets
* Migrate legacy AsyncStorage tokens on upgrade - one-time read, write, delete
* Pair secure storage clears with navigation reset on logout

## [Biometrics with LocalAuthentication](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/biometrics-with-localauthentication/)

* Biometrics prove user presence - they do not replace server authentication
* Use expo-local-authentication for Face ID, Touch ID, and Android fingerprint
* Step-up auth re-prompts biometrics before sensitive actions - transfers, password changes
* Offer passcode fallback - Apple requires it; never trap users without biometrics enrolled
* Store tokens in SecureStore; biometrics gate reading them - not a second password store
* Respect accessibility - always provide PIN/password path for users who cannot use biometrics

## [Refresh Token Rotation](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/refresh-token-rotation/)

* Rotate refresh tokens on every exchange - detect reuse as a breach signal
* Deduplicate concurrent refresh calls - one in-flight promise for parallel 401s
* Silent refresh on cold start and foreground resume - users should not re-login hourly
* Forced re-login when rotation detects reuse, family revoked, or refresh TTL expired
* Clock skew breaks expiresAt checks - skew buffer and trust server 401 over client clock
* Never infinite-retry refresh - one 401 retry per request, then route to sign-in

## [Multi-Account & Device Binding](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/multi-account-and-device-binding/)

* Account switch must purge TanStack Query cache, Zustand slices, and in-memory tokens
* Use per-account SecureStore keys - not one shared refresh\_token key
* Device binding ties refresh tokens to a device ID - server rejects unknown devices
* Never show previous user's data while new user's session bootstraps - use purge + skeleton
* Add account is not sign-in - preserve existing accounts in storage until explicit removal
* Test account switch on slow networks - race conditions leak PII without ordered purge

## [Auth Session Lifecycle](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/auth-session-lifecycle/)

* AppState drives foreground refresh - resume from background triggers proactive token exchange
* Idle timeout may expire server sessions even when client expiresAt looks valid
* Background tasks cannot show biometric UI - refresh uses stored tokens without step-up
* Jailbreak/root detection is a risk signal - degrade gracefully, never false-lock legitimate users
* Combine lifecycle hooks with NetInfo - offline refresh failures should not force sign-out
* Document lifecycle ADR when banking/compliance mandates idle lock or compromised-device policy

## [Authentication Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/best-practices/)

* 25 essentials mapped to OWASP Mobile - storage, transport, session, and OAuth
* Mobile clients are untrusted - short TTL, rotation, and server-side authorization
* Never AsyncStorage for tokens; never client secrets in EXPO\_PUBLIC\_
* Logout clears SecureStore, Query cache, and navigation - not React state alone
* OAuth uses PKCE + system browser - not implicit flow in WebView
* Account switch and compromised-device policies need explicit ADRs for regulated apps

# Mobile Auth Basics

10 examples to get you started with mobile authentication - 7 basic and 3 intermediate. Covers session models, where tokens live on device, and what **logout everywhere** means when users switch accounts or revoke access.

Highlights / Mobile Auth Basics

* Mobile apps are untrusted clients - assume tokens can be extracted from a compromised device
* Prefer short-lived access tokens + refresh rotation; never infinite sessions on device
* Store refresh tokens in expo-secure-store - AsyncStorage is for preferences only
* Logout must clear secure storage, server session, and client caches - not just React state
* OAuth on mobile uses PKCE and custom URL schemes - not implicit flow in a WebView
* Pair auth with API client interceptors - see networking-api for 401 retry patterns

## Prerequisites

Scaffold an Expo app with SDK 57 and install the auth storage primitives you will use throughout this section:

```bash
npx create-expo-app@latest AuthBasics --template blank-typescript
cd AuthBasics
npx expo install expo-secure-store expo-auth-session expo-crypto
```

Confirm the SDK pin:

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "expo": "~57.0.4",
    "react": "19.2.3",
    "react-native": "0.86.0"
  }
}
```

> **Tooling:** These examples target **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4), **React Native 0.86.0**, and **React 19.2.3**.

---

## Basic Examples

### 1. Session Models on Mobile

Mobile apps typically use one of three session shapes. Pick based on your backend - do not invent a fourth unless compliance demands it.

```text
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Model              │ Access token │ Refresh │ Server session   │
├────────────────────┼──────────────┼─────────┼──────────────────┤
│ JWT + refresh      │ Short JWT    │ Rotating│ Optional sid     │
│ Opaque bearer      │ Opaque token │ Rotating│ Required         │
│ Cookie (rare RN)   │ HttpOnly*    │ HttpOnly│ Required         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
* HttpOnly cookies are awkward in RN - prefer Authorization header + secure store.
```

```ts
// src/features/auth/model/session.ts
export type Session = {
  accessToken: string;
  refreshToken: string;
  expiresAt: number; // epoch ms - client-side hint only; server validates
  userId: string;
};
```

* **JWT + refresh** is the most common Expo pattern - access token in memory or secure store, refresh in secure store only
* **Opaque bearer** pushes validation entirely server-side - client stores opaque strings, never parses claims
* **Cookie sessions** in React Native require cookie jars and are fragile with deep links - avoid unless you own a mature cookie stack
* Treat `expiresAt` as a **client hint** for proactive refresh - the server clock is authoritative

> **Related:** [Refresh Token Rotation](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/refresh-token-rotation/) - silent refresh and forced re-login | [../networking-api/networking-basics/networking-basics.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/networking-basics/) - attaching tokens to API calls

---

### 2. Access vs Refresh Token Roles

Access tokens authorize API calls. Refresh tokens obtain new access tokens - they are higher value and must be stored more carefully.

```ts
// src/shared/api/createApiClient.ts
type ApiClientOptions = {
  getAccessToken: () => Promise<string | null>;
};
 
export function createApiClient({ getAccessToken }: ApiClientOptions) {
  return async function apiFetch(path: string, init: RequestInit = {}) {
    const token = await getAccessToken();
    const headers = new Headers(init.headers);
 
    if (token) {
      headers.set("Authorization", `Bearer ${token}`);
    }
 
    return fetch(`${process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL}${path}`, {
      ...init,
      headers,
    });
  };
}
```

* **Access tokens** ride on every authenticated request via `Authorization: Bearer`
* **Refresh tokens** never appear in routine API headers - only in the dedicated `/refresh` endpoint
* Keep access tokens **short-lived** (5–15 minutes) so a leaked token has a narrow window
* Never log either token - scrub `Authorization` in crash reporters (see [Security Rules for Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/security-rules-for-mobile/))

> **Related:** [SecureStore & Keychain/Keystore](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/securestore-and-keychain-keystore/) - where refresh tokens live on device

---

### 3. Token Storage Overview

Mobile storage tiers have different threat models. Match sensitivity to the store.

```text
┌──────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Store            │ Appropriate for                                │
├──────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ React state      │ In-memory access token during active session   │
│ expo-secure-store│ Refresh tokens, long-lived secrets             │
│ AsyncStorage     │ Theme, onboarding flags, non-sensitive prefs   │
│ MMKV (encrypted) │ Large caches - not a substitute for Keychain   │
│ expo-file-system │ Files, media - never raw tokens                │
└──────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

```ts
import * as SecureStore from "expo-secure-store";
 
const REFRESH_KEY = "auth.refresh_token";
 
export async function saveRefreshToken(token: string) {
  await SecureStore.setItemAsync(REFRESH_KEY, token, {
    keychainAccessible: SecureStore.WHEN_UNLOCKED_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY,
  });
}
 
export async function loadRefreshToken() {
  return SecureStore.getItemAsync(REFRESH_KEY);
}
```

* **Secure Store** maps to iOS Keychain and Android Keystore - hardware-backed on supported devices
* **AsyncStorage** is unencrypted SQLite - fine for `hasSeenOnboarding`, fatal for refresh tokens
* **In-memory** access tokens disappear on process kill - pair with silent refresh on cold start
* Audit PRs for `AsyncStorage.setItem` with token-like key names

> **Related:** [SecureStore & Keychain/Keystore](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/securestore-and-keychain-keystore/) - keychain accessibility options and size limits

---

### 4. Cold Start: Restore Session from Secure Store

On launch, read the refresh token, exchange it for a fresh access token, then hydrate app state.

```tsx
// src/features/auth/AuthProvider.tsx
import { createContext, useContext, useEffect, useState, type ReactNode } from "react";
import * as SecureStore from "expo-secure-store";
import type { Session } from "./model/session";
 
type AuthContextValue = {
  session: Session | null;
  bootstrapping: boolean;
};
 
const AuthContext = createContext<AuthContextValue>({ session: null, bootstrapping: true });
 
async function refreshFromStoredToken(): Promise<Session | null> {
  const refreshToken = await SecureStore.getItemAsync("auth.refresh_token");
  if (!refreshToken) return null;
 
  const res = await fetch(`${process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL}/auth/refresh`, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
    body: JSON.stringify({ refreshToken }),
  });
 
  if (!res.ok) return null;
  return res.json() as Promise<Session>;
}
 
export function AuthProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  const [session, setSession] = useState<Session | null>(null);
  const [bootstrapping, setBootstrapping] = useState(true);
 
  useEffect(() => {
    refreshFromStoredToken()
      .then(setSession)
      .finally(() => setBootstrapping(false));
  }, []);
 
  return (
    <AuthContext.Provider value={{ session, bootstrapping }}>
      {children}
    </AuthContext.Provider>
  );
}
 
export function useAuth() {
  return useContext(AuthContext);
}
```

* Show a **splash or skeleton** while `bootstrapping` is true - do not flash the login screen for signed-in users
* Failed refresh on cold start means **no session** - route to sign-in without retry loops
* Persist the **new refresh token** if your backend rotates on every refresh call
* Wrap the root layout so every screen reads the same auth context

> **Related:** [Auth Session Lifecycle](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/auth-session-lifecycle/) - foreground refresh when returning from background

---

### 5. Sign-In: Persist Session After Password Login

After a successful credential exchange, write tokens to secure store and update context.

```ts
// src/features/auth/api/signInWithPassword.ts
import * as SecureStore from "expo-secure-store";
import type { Session } from "../model/session";
 
export async function signInWithPassword(email: string, password: string): Promise<Session> {
  const res = await fetch(`${process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL}/auth/login`, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
    body: JSON.stringify({ email, password }),
  });
 
  if (!res.ok) {
    throw new Error("Invalid credentials");
  }
 
  const session = (await res.json()) as Session;
 
  await SecureStore.setItemAsync("auth.refresh_token", session.refreshToken, {
    keychainAccessible: SecureStore.WHEN_UNLOCKED_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY,
  });
 
  return session;
}
```

* Write **refresh token only** to secure store - access token can live in React state until refresh
* Use `WHEN_UNLOCKED_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY` so backups and other devices do not export the keychain item
* Return the full `Session` to the caller so UI can navigate immediately without a second read
* Never store passwords locally - not even in secure store

> **Related:** [expo-auth-session & OAuth](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/expo-auth-session-and-oauth/) - when sign-in uses Google or Apple instead of passwords

---

### 6. Sign-Out: Local Logout

Local logout clears device artifacts and in-memory state. It is the minimum every app must implement.

```ts
// src/features/auth/api/signOutLocal.ts
import * as SecureStore from "expo-secure-store";
 
const AUTH_KEYS = ["auth.refresh_token", "auth.device_binding_id"] as const;
 
export async function signOutLocal() {
  await Promise.all(AUTH_KEYS.map((key) => SecureStore.deleteItemAsync(key)));
}
```

```tsx
// In your settings screen
import { useAuth } from "../AuthProvider";
import { signOutLocal } from "../api/signOutLocal";
 
async function handleSignOut() {
  await signOutLocal();
  setSession(null); // from AuthProvider state setter exposed via context
  router.replace("/sign-in");
}
```

* Delete **every** secure-store key your auth flow wrote - refresh, device binding, biometric unlock flags
* **Reset navigation** to the sign-in stack - Android back must not return to authenticated screens
* Clearing React state alone is insufficient - users relaunch into an authenticated shell with stale tokens
* Pair with TanStack Query `queryClient.clear()` when server-backed caches hold user PII

> **Related:** [Multi-Account & Device Binding](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/multi-account-and-device-binding/) - cache purge when switching users

---

### 7. Logout Everywhere (Server Revocation)

**Logout everywhere** revokes refresh tokens server-side so stolen devices cannot silently refresh.

```ts
// src/features/auth/api/signOutEverywhere.ts
import * as SecureStore from "expo-secure-store";
 
export async function signOutEverywhere(accessToken: string) {
  await fetch(`${process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL}/auth/revoke-all`, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}`,
      "Content-Type": "application/json",
    },
  });
 
  await SecureStore.deleteItemAsync("auth.refresh_token");
}
```

* Backend maintains a **refresh token family** or session table - `revoke-all` invalidates every device for that user
* Call **before** clearing local storage so you still have a valid access token for the revocation request
* Offer two UX paths: **Sign out** (this device) vs **Sign out everywhere** (all devices)
* After revocation, treat 401 on refresh as expected - route to sign-in without alarming error toasts

> **Related:** [Refresh Token Rotation](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/refresh-token-rotation/) - how rotation detects token reuse after a breach

---

## Intermediate Examples

### 8. Discriminated Auth State for Navigation

Model auth as a finite state so Expo Router layouts can gate routes without nested conditionals.

```ts
// src/features/auth/model/authState.ts
export type AuthState =
  | { status: "bootstrapping" }
  | { status: "unauthenticated" }
  | { status: "authenticated"; session: Session }
  | { status: "session_expired" };
```

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx (Expo Router)
import { Redirect, Stack } from "expo-router";
import { useAuth } from "@/features/auth/AuthProvider";
 
export default function RootLayout() {
  const { authState } = useAuth();
 
  if (authState.status === "bootstrapping") {
    return null; // or <SplashScreen />
  }
 
  if (authState.status === "unauthenticated" || authState.status === "session_expired") {
    return <Redirect href="/sign-in" />;
  }
 
  return <Stack screenOptions={{ headerShown: false }} />;
}
```

* **`bootstrapping`** prevents the login flash during cold-start refresh
* **`session_expired`** lets you show "Session expired - sign in again" instead of a generic error
* Keep route guards in **layout files** - individual screens should assume auth already passed
* `session_expired` often follows a failed silent refresh - do not infinite-retry

> **Related:** [Auth Session Lifecycle](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/auth-session-lifecycle/) - transitions between foreground and background refresh

---

### 9. OAuth vs Password: Same Session Shape

Whether users sign in with email or Google, normalize to one `Session` type so the rest of the app stays provider-agnostic.

```ts
// src/features/auth/model/mapOAuthToSession.ts
import type { Session } from "./session";
 
type OAuthTokenResponse = {
  access_token: string;
  refresh_token: string;
  expires_in: number;
  user: { id: string };
};
 
export function mapOAuthToSession(payload: OAuthTokenResponse): Session {
  return {
    accessToken: payload.access_token,
    refreshToken: payload.refresh_token,
    expiresAt: Date.now() + payload.expires_in * 1000,
    userId: payload.user.id,
  };
}
```

* OAuth and password flows **converge** at `Session` - features import one type
* Provider-specific code stays in `expo-auth-session` wiring - not in order lists or settings
* Store refresh tokens the same way regardless of sign-in method
* Backend should issue **your** tokens after OAuth code exchange - do not use Google access tokens as your API bearer long-term

> **Related:** [expo-auth-session & OAuth](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/expo-auth-session-and-oauth/) - PKCE and redirect URI setup

---

### 10. Auth-Aware API Client with Single 401 Retry

Centralize token refresh so feature code never hand-rolls retry logic.

```ts
// src/shared/api/authenticatedFetch.ts
let refreshPromise: Promise<Session | null> | null = null;
 
export function createAuthenticatedFetch(
  getSession: () => Session | null,
  setSession: (s: Session | null) => void,
  refreshSession: () => Promise<Session | null>,
) {
  return async function authenticatedFetch(path: string, init?: RequestInit) {
    const session = getSession();
    const headers = new Headers(init?.headers);
 
    if (session?.accessToken) {
      headers.set("Authorization", `Bearer ${session.accessToken}`);
    }
 
    let response = await fetch(`${process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL}${path}`, {
      ...init,
      headers,
    });
 
    if (response.status !== 401) return response;
 
    refreshPromise ??= refreshSession().finally(() => {
      refreshPromise = null;
    });
 
    const refreshed = await refreshPromise;
    if (!refreshed) return response;
 
    setSession(refreshed);
    headers.set("Authorization", `Bearer ${refreshed.accessToken}`);
 
    return fetch(`${process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL}${path}`, { ...init, headers });
  };
}
```

* **One retry** on 401 - infinite refresh loops mask server misconfiguration
* Deduplicate concurrent refreshes with a shared `refreshPromise` - ten parallel 401s should trigger one refresh
* Failed refresh sets session to `null` and routes to sign-in
* Wire this client into TanStack Query's `queryFn` for consistent behavior

> **Related:** [../networking-api/fetch-vs-axios/fetch-vs-axios.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/fetch-vs-axios/) - interceptor patterns | [Refresh Token Rotation](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/refresh-token-rotation/) - rotation edge cases

---

## FAQs

Should I store the access token in secure store too?

* In-memory is enough for most apps if cold start always refreshes.
* Persist access token only when your backend cannot refresh frequently and UX demands offline reads - still prefer short TTL.

Is Expo Go safe for testing auth flows?

* OAuth redirect URIs differ between Expo Go and standalone builds - test on a development build before release.
* Secure Store works in Expo Go, but custom URL schemes for OAuth require `expo-auth-session` redirect config per environment.

What is the difference between sign out and revoke?

* **Sign out** clears this device.
* **Revoke / logout everywhere** invalidates server-side refresh tokens for all devices - required for stolen-device scenarios.

Can I use JWT claims for authorization in the client?

* Decode claims for UX only (display name, avatar).
* Never trust client-side role checks for security - server validates every request.

Where do API keys go?

* Public keys in `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` only if designed for client exposure.
* Never put OAuth client secrets in the app - exchange codes on your backend.

Dokumen: SecureStore & Keychain/Keystore
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/securestore-and-keychain-keystore/

# SecureStore & Keychain/Keystore

`expo-secure-store` is the default token vault for Expo apps. It delegates to **iOS Keychain** and **Android Keystore**, keeping refresh tokens out of unencrypted SQLite (AsyncStorage) and out of your JS bundle.

Highlights / SecureStore & Keychain/Keystore

* expo-secure-store maps to iOS Keychain and Android Keystore - hardware-backed on supported devices
* Never store refresh tokens, PINs, or API secrets in AsyncStorage or plain MMKV
* SecureStore has a ~2 KB per-item limit - store tokens, not entire user profiles
* Use WHEN\_UNLOCKED\_THIS\_DEVICE\_ONLY so backups and iCloud Keychain do not export secrets
* Migrate legacy AsyncStorage tokens on upgrade - one-time read, write, delete
* Pair secure storage clears with navigation reset on logout

## Prerequisites

```bash
npx expo install expo-secure-store
```

No config plugin is required for basic usage on SDK 57 - install and import.

> **Tooling:** These examples target **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4), **React Native 0.86.0**, and **React 19.2.3**.

---

## Why Not AsyncStorage for Secrets

```text
Threat model comparison
 
AsyncStorage          SecureStore (Keychain / Keystore)
────────────────────  ─────────────────────────────────────────
Unencrypted SQLite    Hardware-backed encryption (device-dependent)
Readable on rooted    Requires device unlock + app entitlement
  devices with file     on iOS; Keystore-backed on Android
  browsers
Backed up as plain    WHEN_UNLOCKED_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY excludes
  app data in some      iCloud Keychain sync (iOS)
  Android backups
```

```ts
// ❌ Never do this
import AsyncStorage from "@react-native-async-storage/async-storage";
await AsyncStorage.setItem("refresh_token", token);
 
// ✅ Correct
import * as SecureStore from "expo-secure-store";
await SecureStore.setItemAsync("auth.refresh_token", token, {
  keychainAccessible: SecureStore.WHEN_UNLOCKED_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY,
});
```

* AsyncStorage is appropriate for **theme**, **last tab**, and **draft UI state** - not credentials
* Attackers with physical device access and jailbreak/root tools can dump AsyncStorage trivially
* Compliance frameworks (PCI, SOC2 mobile annexes) explicitly flag unencrypted local credential storage
* Grep PRs for `AsyncStorage` + `token` - automate in CI with a custom ESLint rule

> **Related:** [../expo-rules/security-rules-for-mobile/security-rules-for-mobile.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/security-rules-for-mobile/) - Tier 2 storage rules

---

## Token Storage Adapter

Wrap SecureStore behind an interface so tests swap in memory and migrations stay centralized.

```ts
// src/features/auth/adapters/secureTokenStorage.ts
import * as SecureStore from "expo-secure-store";
 
const KEYS = {
  refreshToken: "auth.refresh_token",
  lastUserId: "auth.last_user_id",
} as const;
 
const secureOptions: SecureStore.SecureStoreOptions = {
  keychainAccessible: SecureStore.WHEN_UNLOCKED_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY,
};
 
export const secureTokenStorage = {
  async saveRefreshToken(token: string) {
    await SecureStore.setItemAsync(KEYS.refreshToken, token, secureOptions);
  },
 
  async loadRefreshToken() {
    return SecureStore.getItemAsync(KEYS.refreshToken, secureOptions);
  },
 
  async clearAll() {
    await Promise.all(
      Object.values(KEYS).map((key) => SecureStore.deleteItemAsync(key)),
    );
  },
};
```

* **Namespaced keys** (`auth.refresh_token`) avoid collisions with other features using SecureStore
* Export a **single adapter** - screens never call `SecureStore` directly
* `clearAll` is the logout primitive - call from sign-out and account-switch flows
* Keep keys in one module - scattered string literals cause orphan secrets after refactors

> **Related:** [Mobile Auth Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/mobile-auth-basics/) - cold-start session restore

---

## Keychain Accessibility Options

iOS Keychain accessibility controls when items can be read.

```ts
import * as SecureStore from "expo-secure-store";
 
// Recommended for refresh tokens:
SecureStore.WHEN_UNLOCKED_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY
 
// Alternatives - use deliberately:
SecureStore.AFTER_FIRST_UNLOCK          // background fetch can read - higher risk
SecureStore.WHEN_UNLOCKED                 // may sync via iCloud Keychain
SecureStore.ALWAYS                        // avoid for auth secrets
```

| Option | Background read | iCloud sync | Use case |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `WHEN_UNLOCKED_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY` | No | No | Refresh tokens (default choice) |
| `AFTER_FIRST_UNLOCK` | Yes (until lock) | No | Background refresh before user unlocks |
| `WHEN_UNLOCKED` | No | Possible | Rare - cross-device keychain needs |

* Default to **`WHEN_UNLOCKED_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY`** for refresh tokens - matches banking app posture
* Choose `AFTER_FIRST_UNLOCK` only when you must refresh in background **before** first unlock and accept the tradeoff
* Android maps these to equivalent Keystore protection levels - Expo abstracts the platform differences
* Document the choice in an ADR if compliance asks why background refresh works pre-unlock

---

## Size Limits and What Not to Store

SecureStore is for **small secrets** - not arbitrary JSON caches.

```ts
// ❌ Too large - user object with avatar URL, preferences, roles
await SecureStore.setItemAsync("user", JSON.stringify(largeUserObject));
 
// ✅ Store token + non-sensitive ID; fetch profile from API
await SecureStore.setItemAsync("auth.refresh_token", refreshToken, secureOptions);
await SecureStore.setItemAsync("auth.last_user_id", userId, secureOptions);
```

* Expo documents a **~2048 byte** limit per value - oversized payloads fail at runtime
* Store **user profiles** in TanStack Query cache or encrypted MMKV if offline reads are required - not SecureStore
* Store **access tokens** in memory when possible - only persist refresh tokens unless offline demands otherwise
* If you need large encrypted blobs, evaluate `react-native-mmkv` with encryption key stored in SecureStore

---

## Migration from AsyncStorage

Ship a one-time migration for apps that previously stored tokens incorrectly.

```ts
// src/features/auth/adapters/migrateTokenStorage.ts
import AsyncStorage from "@react-native-async-storage/async-storage";
import * as SecureStore from "expo-secure-store";
 
const LEGACY_KEY = "refresh_token";
const SECURE_KEY = "auth.refresh_token";
const MIGRATION_FLAG = "auth.storage_migrated_v1";
 
export async function migrateLegacyTokens() {
  const done = await AsyncStorage.getItem(MIGRATION_FLAG);
  if (done) return;
 
  const legacy = await AsyncStorage.getItem(LEGACY_KEY);
  if (legacy) {
    await SecureStore.setItemAsync(SECURE_KEY, legacy, {
      keychainAccessible: SecureStore.WHEN_UNLOCKED_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY,
    });
    await AsyncStorage.removeItem(LEGACY_KEY);
  }
 
  await AsyncStorage.setItem(MIGRATION_FLAG, "1");
}
```

* Run migration **before** cold-start refresh in `AuthProvider` bootstrap
* Delete legacy AsyncStorage entries immediately after successful SecureStore write
* Set a **migration flag** so the path runs once - not on every launch
* Log migration success in analytics (without token values) to measure adoption

---

## Biometric-Gated Reads (Optional Layer)

SecureStore stores secrets; biometrics gate **access** to the app - see the dedicated biometrics page for step-up patterns.

```ts
// SecureStore holds the token; biometrics gate whether app unlocks session
import * as LocalAuthentication from "expo-local-authentication";
 
export async function unlockAppOrSignOut(
  loadRefresh: () => Promise<string | null>,
  signOut: () => Promise<void>,
) {
  const hasHardware = await LocalAuthentication.hasHardwareAsync();
  const enrolled = await LocalAuthentication.isEnrolledAsync();
 
  if (!hasHardware || !enrolled) {
    return loadRefresh();
  }
 
  const result = await LocalAuthentication.authenticateAsync({
    promptMessage: "Unlock MyApp",
    fallbackLabel: "Use passcode",
  });
 
  if (!result.success) {
    await signOut();
    return null;
  }
 
  return loadRefresh();
}
```

* Biometrics **do not replace** SecureStore - they add a user-presence check before reading tokens
* Failed biometric after N attempts should **not** delete tokens automatically - offer sign-out explicitly
* On Android, fingerprint and face unlock map to the same `authenticateAsync` API

> **Related:** [Biometrics with LocalAuthentication](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/biometrics-with-localauthentication/) - step-up auth patterns

---

## Logout and Key Deletion

```ts
export async function signOutCompletely(queryClient: { clear: () => void }) {
  await secureTokenStorage.clearAll();
  queryClient.clear();
  // Navigation reset handled by caller - router.replace("/sign-in")
}
```

* `deleteItemAsync` is idempotent - safe to call when key is already absent
* Missing logout cleanup is a top mobile security audit finding - test: logout → kill app → relaunch → no authenticated API calls
* Pair with [server revocation](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/mobile-auth-basics/) when user selects "Sign out everywhere"

## Testing SecureStore in Jest

Mock the module in Jest - SecureStore is not available in Node.

```ts
// jest.setup.ts
jest.mock("expo-secure-store", () => ({
  setItemAsync: jest.fn(),
  getItemAsync: jest.fn(),
  deleteItemAsync: jest.fn(),
  WHEN_UNLOCKED_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY: "WHEN_UNLOCKED_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY",
}));
```

* Unit-test your **adapter** logic with the mock - not Expo's native bridge
* E2E tests (Detox) should run on device/simulator for real Keychain behavior
* iOS Simulator Keychain persists across app deletes in some Xcode versions - reset simulator content when tests flake

## FAQs

Is SecureStore safe on jailbroken or rooted devices?

* No client storage survives a fully compromised device - treat SecureStore as raising the bar, not absolute protection.
* Combine with certificate pinning, jailbreak detection, and short token TTL for high-risk apps.

Does SecureStore work in Expo Go?

* Yes - it uses the device Keychain/Keystore under Expo Go's bundle ID.
* Production OAuth and Keychain access groups still require your standalone bundle ID - test on dev builds.

Can I share tokens between app extensions?

* Requires iOS Keychain access groups - custom native config beyond default Expo SecureStore.
* Prefer extension-to-host IPC or re-authentication instead of sharing refresh tokens.

What about expo-crypto for encryption?

* Use `expo-crypto` for hashing and random bytes - not as a replacement for SecureStore.
* Pattern: generate data encryption key with crypto, store key in SecureStore, encrypt blobs in MMKV.

Dokumen: Brownfield Best Practices
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/brownfield/best-practices/

# Brownfield Best Practices

A condensed summary of the 25 most important best practices drawn from every page in this section.

Highlights / Brownfield Best Practices

* One Metro project per embedded module - multiple runtimes need explicit iOS symbol planning
* Native owns session vault; RN reads shared state - never duplicate refresh logic silently
* Isolated artifacts decouple native CI from Node; integrated repos need prebuild in CI
* Version bridge contracts semver; bump Maven/SPM when message shapes change
* Debug artifacts + Metro for dev; release artifacts get offline smoke tests before host pin
* Strangler slices stay post-auth and off cold start until root navigation migrates

1. **Define brownfield explicitly:** If native `AppDelegate` / `Application` owns the root UI, RN is a guest - plan embed boundaries before choosing Expo Router routes.
2. **Score embed vs rewrite vs WebView per feature:** Use the three-way matrix in [Brownfield Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/brownfield/brownfield-basics/) - permanent WebView shells without an ADR sunset are a common failure mode.
3. **Default to isolated `expo-brownfield` artifacts:** AAR + Swift Package lets native CI skip Node when teams are split - integrated only when one squad edits both sides daily.
4. **One Metro bundler per embedded module:** Two RN runtimes in one process require `multipleFrameworks: true` on iOS and a deliberate symbol strategy - avoid accidental double Metro projects.
5. **Initialize `ReactNativeHostManager` once at app launch:** Late init causes blank RN screens and flaky Expo module lifecycle - mirror Expo docs in host `AppDelegate` / `Application`.
6. **Match `moduleName` to JS registration:** Host `ReactNativeViewController(moduleName:)` must align with `registerRootComponent` / `app.json` entry - mismatch shows white screen with no JS error.
7. **Pin Expo SDK across `expo` and `expo-brownfield`:** Use `npx expo install` on SDK 57 - Hermes and native binaries drift if versions diverge.
8. **Run `npx expo-doctor` on every artifact build:** Catches native module skew before publishing Maven/XCFramework consumers ingest bad artifacts.
9. **Version Android artifacts in plugin config:** `android.version` must match Maven coordinates - tag Git and Maven with the same semver.
10. **Ship iOS debug and release Swift Packages separately:** SPM binary targets are flavor-specific - QA and App Store pins must not cross wires.
11. **Document a bridge contract version:** `BRIDGE_CONTRACT_VERSION` in shared types - breaking `SharedStateKeys` or message `type` values require coordinated native + RN releases.
12. **Native keychain owns refresh tokens:** RN gets short-lived access tokens via `useSharedState` - refresh stays native unless auth strangler explicitly migrated.
13. **Mount a root `SessionBridge` listener:** `SESSION_UPDATED` / `LOGOUT` messages in `_layout.tsx` - per-screen listeners miss events on fast navigation.
14. **Never pass refresh tokens in `initialProps`:** Bootstrap props are logged and introspected - use shared state set by native after secure read.
15. **Use `Brownfield.popToNative()` at flow completion:** Checkout and wizard ends should return control to native chrome - do not leave orphan RN stacks under native tabs.
16. **Enable `setNativeBackEnabled` when native owns back:** Hardware back should exit RN module when stack is empty - prevents trapped users on Android.
17. **Pick strangler slices post-auth and off cold start:** First slice should not block app launch - home tab RN init is a performance and navigation ownership trap.
18. **Record slice order in ADRs:** [Incremental Adoption ADR](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/brownfield/incremental-adoption-adr/) ranked decisions prevent "random settings page" migrations with no journey cohesion.
19. **Separate release trains:** RN artifact pipeline, host store pipeline, optional OTA - semver them independently per [Brownfield CI/CD](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/brownfield/brownfield-ci-cd/).
20. **OTA only within `runtimeVersion`:** `eas update` on the RN project must not outpace the Hermes runtime embedded in the host's pinned artifact.
21. **Offline-test release artifacts:** Airplane mode on host Release build before bumping Maven/SPM - debug Metro paths hide missing embedded bundles.
22. **Use `@expo/ui` `RNHostView` for native chrome inside RN screens:** Distinct from full brownfield presentation - native toolbars around RN bodies without custom view managers.
23. **Keep RN routes thin; features fat:** Same as greenfield - `app/` re-exports feature screens per [Mobile Architecture Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/mobile-architecture-basics/).
24. **Prefer config plugins over hand-edited host plists:** `expo-brownfield` plugin regenerates targets on `prebuild --clean` - manual Gradle edits are lost.
25. **Treat brownfield as alpha-capable, not alpha-careless:** Expo documents brownfield support as alpha - budget native build debugging, read SDK release notes, and file upstream issues with reproduction artifacts.

## FAQs

Expo Go for brownfield QA?

No - use debug brownfield artifacts with Metro or internal host builds. Expo Go cannot load your host shell.

When is WebView acceptable long term?

Legal, marketing, and rarely updated read-only content - not core product flows with offline or native navigation requirements.

How many RN modules in one host app?

One unless legal or team boundaries force two - each adds artifact CI, bridge contracts, and iOS linker complexity.

Does Expo Router replace native navigation during strangler?

Expo Router owns navigation **inside** the embedded module only until ADR declares native root retired - see navigation ADR in architecture-design.

Who bumps the host app when RN adds `expo-camera`?

RN squad publishes new artifact; native squad integration PR bumps dependency - OTA alone is insufficient for new native modules.

Dokumen: Brownfield Basics
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/brownfield/brownfield-basics/

# Brownfield Basics

10 examples to decide when to **embed React Native**, **rewrite in RN**, or **fall back to WebView** - 7 basic and 3 intermediate.

Highlights / Brownfield Basics

* Brownfield apps have a native entry point - React Native is added as a screen or feature, not the root
* Embed React Native when you need native UX, offline, and shared logic - not for static marketing pages
* Full rewrite only when navigation, auth, and release cadence all justify the migration cost
* WebView is a valid fallback for low-interaction content - not a substitute for product screens
* Isolated approach (AAR/XCFramework) keeps native CI free of Node.js; integrated couples repos
* Expo SDK modules, Router, and EAS Build work in brownfield - Expo Go and some OTA paths do not

## Prerequisites

Brownfield work assumes you already ship a native iOS and/or Android app whose **main entry point is not React Native**. You add RN as a library, screen, or feature module.

For hands-on integration after these decisions, see [expo-brownfield Overview](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/brownfield/expo-brownfield-overview/). For architecture boundaries inside the RN slice, see [Mobile Architecture Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/mobile-architecture-basics/).

```bash
# Spike: minimal Expo project to validate embed feasibility
npx create-expo-app@latest RnSpike --template blank-typescript@sdk-57
cd RnSpike
npx expo install expo-brownfield
```

> **Tooling:** These examples target **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4), **React Native 0.86.0**, and **React 19.2.3**. Brownfield integration APIs are **alpha** - budget time for native build debugging.

---

## Basic Examples

### 1. Brownfield vs Greenfield

**Greenfield** means React Native (or Expo) is the app's root - every screen branches from a JS entry. **Brownfield** means UIKit/Swift, Jetpack Compose/Kotlin, or another native stack owns the shell; RN is embedded on demand.

```text
Greenfield                          Brownfield
┌─────────────────────┐            ┌─────────────────────┐
│  RN root (main)     │            │  Native root        │
│  ├─ Tab A           │            │  ├─ Home (native)   │
│  ├─ Tab B           │            │  ├─ Settings (nat.) │
│  └─ Modal           │            │  └─ Checkout (RN)   │  ← RN island
└─────────────────────┘            └─────────────────────┘
```

* If your **AppDelegate / Application class** launches a native storyboard first, you are brownfield
* Expo **Dev Client** does not target brownfield host apps today - use Metro + debug artifacts or integrated prebuild for local dev
* **Expo SDK modules**, **Expo Router**, **EAS Build**, and **EAS Submit** do support brownfield per Expo's compatibility matrix

> **Related:** [expo-brownfield Overview](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/brownfield/expo-brownfield-overview/) - packaging RN as AAR/XCFramework | [../architecture-design/mobile-architecture-basics/mobile-architecture-basics.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/mobile-architecture-basics/) - structuring the RN slice once embedded

---

### 2. Embed React Native - When It Wins

Embed RN when the feature needs **native-feeling UI**, **offline/cache behavior**, **device APIs**, or **shared TypeScript** with a web team - and the legacy native screen would take quarters to rebuild.

| Signal | Embed RN |
| --- | --- |
| Complex forms with validation | ✓ |
| Lists with gestures / Reanimated | ✓ |
| Camera, biometrics, BLE via Expo modules | ✓ |
| Reuse existing React design system | ✓ |
| One static FAQ page | ✗ (WebView or native) |

```tsx
// The RN slice can still use Expo Router inside the host-provided container
// app/_layout.tsx - RN navigation is internal to the embedded module
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
 
export default function RootLayout() {
  return (
    <Stack screenOptions={{ headerShown: false }}>
      <Stack.Screen name="checkout" />
      <Stack.Screen name="order-confirmation" />
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

* Embedding does **not** require rewriting the whole app - start with one high-churn flow (checkout, onboarding, support chat)
* Use **`expo-brownfield`** isolated artifacts when native teams refuse Node in CI
* Plan **one Metro project** per embedded module - avoid two RN runtimes in one process without `multipleFrameworks` planning on iOS

> **Related:** [RNHostView & Native UI Embedding](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/brownfield/rnhostview-and-native-ui-embedding/) - RN inside SwiftUI/Compose layouts | [../native-modules/native-modules-basics/native-modules-basics.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/native-modules/native-modules-basics/) - when JS alone is insufficient

---

### 3. Full Rewrite - When It Wins

A **rewrite** replaces the native shell with an Expo/RN app. Justified when **most screens** are changing anyway, **dual navigation** costs exceed migration, or you need **one OTA pipeline** for the entire product.

| Signal | Rewrite |
| --- | --- |
| >60% of roadmap touches UI shared with web | ✓ |
| Native codebase unmaintainable (no tests, no owners) | ✓ |
| Store compliance requires single binary identity | ✓ |
| One team owns one feature in an otherwise stable app | ✗ (embed) |

```text
Rewrite decision checklist (all "yes" → strong rewrite case):
□ Native and mobile web share a component library
□ Auth, push, and deep links need unified routing (Expo Router)
□ Native headcount cannot sustain two UI stacks
□ Leadership accepts 2–4 sprint migration freeze on affected flows
```

* Rewrites fail when treated as **big-bang** - use strangler fig (see [Incremental Adoption ADR](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/brownfield/incremental-adoption-adr/))
* Brownfield embed is often the **first phase** of a rewrite, not the alternative to one
* Document the choice in an ADR before re-platforming store listings or bundle IDs

> **Related:** [Incremental Adoption ADR](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/brownfield/incremental-adoption-adr/) - ranked strangler fig decisions | [../architecture-design/adr-navigation-library-choice/adr-navigation-library-choice.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/adr-navigation-library-choice/) - Expo Router vs React Navigation during migration

---

### 4. WebView Fallback - When It Wins

**WebView** ships mobile web inside the native shell. Best for **read-only**, **rarely updated**, or **legally hosted** content where native UX and offline are non-goals.

```tsx
import { WebView } from "react-native-webview";
 
export function HelpCenterWebView({ url }: { url: string }) {
  return (
    <WebView
      source={{ uri: url }}
      startInLoadingState
      sharedCookiesEnabled
      // Host app must inject auth cookie or token via injectedJavaScript
    />
  );
}
```

| Signal | WebView |
| --- | --- |
| Marketing / legal / help center | ✓ |
| Internal admin tools used monthly | ✓ |
| Checkout with PCI constraints | ✗ (native or RN + certified SDK) |
| Offline-first field app | ✗ |

* **Cookie/session sharing** with the native app is fragile - plan explicit token handoff (see [Shared Authentication & Bridges](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/brownfield/shared-authentication-and-bridges/))
* WebView **does not** give you Expo modules, Reanimated, or consistent offline - it is a browser tab with an app icon
* Prefer **Safari View Controller / Chrome Custom Tabs** for OAuth flows that forbid embedded WebViews

> **Related:** [Shared Authentication & Bridges](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/brownfield/shared-authentication-and-bridges/) - passing sessions into WebView and RN

---

### 5. Three-Way Decision Matrix

Score each candidate feature 1–5 on these axes; highest total suggests the column.

| Axis | Embed RN | Rewrite | WebView |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| UI complexity | High forms/lists | Entire app | Static HTML |
| Offline need | Required | Required | Optional |
| Release cadence | Weekly feature | Major version | Rare copy change |
| Native team capacity | Low | Willing to exit native UI | Any |
| Shared code with web | High | High | Already on web |
| Risk tolerance | Medium (island) | High (platform) | Low |

```text
Example: "Order tracking" in a native retail app
  UI complexity: 4  |  Offline: 3  |  Cadence: 5  |  Shared TS: 4
  → Embed RN (strangler fig on tracking stack)
 
Example: "Terms of service"
  UI: 1  |  Offline: 0  |  Cadence: 1
  → WebView or SFSafariViewController
```

* No column wins every row - **document the scoring** in your ADR repo
* Revisit when **EAS Update** or **store policy** changes - WebView-only checkout may fail review

> **Related:** [Incremental Adoption ADR](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/brownfield/incremental-adoption-adr/) - formal ranked decisions per scenario

---

### 6. Integrated vs Isolated Embedding

Expo documents two brownfield shapes:

| Approach | RN location | Native CI needs Node? | Best for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Integrated** | RN project wraps or neighbors native `ios/`/`android/` | Yes | Single team, frequent cross-boundary changes |
| **Isolated** | Separate repo/monorepo package → AAR + XCFramework | No (consumes artifacts) | Separate native and RN squads |

```json
// app.config.ts - isolated path uses expo-brownfield config plugin
export default {
  expo: {
    plugins: [
      [
        "expo-brownfield",
        {
          ios: { targetName: "CheckoutBrownfield" },
          android: {
            group: "com.example",
            libraryName: "checkout-brownfield",
            version: "2.1.0",
          },
        },
      ],
    ],
  },
};
```

```bash
# RN squad publishes artifacts; native squad consumes Maven / Swift Package
npx expo-brownfield build:android --release
npx expo-brownfield build:ios --release --package CheckoutPackage
```

* **Isolated** is the default recommendation when native release trains cannot absorb Yarn/Metro
* **Integrated** fits when you already run `npx expo prebuild` inside the host repo
* Both approaches still need **one Hermes + RN version** aligned with SDK 57

> **Related:** [expo-brownfield Overview](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/brownfield/expo-brownfield-overview/) - full cookbook | [../native-modules/config-plugins/config-plugins.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/native-modules/config-plugins/) - `expo-brownfield` plugin options

---

### 7. Presenting the First RN Screen (Host Side)

The host app initializes the RN runtime once, then presents a view controller or activity.

```swift
// iOS - call early in AppDelegate
import CheckoutBrownfield
 
@main
class AppDelegate: UIResponder, UIApplicationDelegate {
  func application(
    _ application: UIApplication,
    didFinishLaunchingWithOptions launchOptions: [UIApplication.LaunchOptionsKey: Any]?
  ) -> Bool {
    ReactNativeHostManager.shared.initialize()
    return true
  }
}
 
// UIKit - push RN checkout
let vc = ReactNativeViewController(
  moduleName: "main",
  initialProps: ["cartId": cartId]
)
navigationController?.pushViewController(vc, animated: true)
```

```kotlin
// Android - BrownfieldActivity + fragment
class CheckoutActivity : BrownfieldActivity() {
  override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
    super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
    showReactNativeFragment()
  }
}
```

* **`moduleName`** must match `registerRootComponent` / `app.json` `main` registration in the RN project
* **`initialProps`** seed route params - pair with shared auth keys (next article)
* Debug builds load from **Metro** (`npx expo start`); release builds use the **embedded bundle** inside the artifact

> **Related:** [Brownfield CI/CD](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/brownfield/brownfield-ci-cd/) - debug vs release artifact pipelines

---

## Intermediate Examples

### 8. Strangler Fig - First Slice Selection

Pick a flow that is **painful in native**, **bounded**, and **not** on the critical cold-start path.

```text
Good first slices:
  ✓ Post-login dashboard (auth already native)
  ✓ Settings sub-flow rarely opened at launch
  ✓ New feature with no legacy code
 
Poor first slices:
  ✗ App launch splash / home tab (cold start + RN init cost)
  ✗ Deep native navigation hub (back-stack ownership unclear)
  ✗ Background tasks / widgets (RN not in process)
```

```tsx
// RN side - listen for native "open slice" messages
import * as Brownfield from "expo-brownfield";
import { useEffect } from "react";
import { router } from "expo-router";
 
export function useNativeDeepLinks() {
  useEffect(() => {
    const sub = Brownfield.addMessageListener((event) => {
      if (event.type === "OPEN_TRACKING" && event.orderId) {
        router.push(`/orders/${event.orderId}`);
      }
    });
    return () => sub.remove();
  }, []);
}
```

* Native still owns **tab bar and root navigation** until the strangler retires those screens
* Use **`Brownfield.popToNative()`** when RN finishes a flow and returns control to UIKit/Compose
* Record slice order in [Incremental Adoption ADR](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/brownfield/incremental-adoption-adr/)

> **Related:** [Shared Authentication & Bridges](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/brownfield/shared-authentication-and-bridges/) - `BrownfieldMessaging` contract

---

### 9. WebView vs RN for the Same Product Screen

When PM asks for "just use the mobile website," run this comparison on one screen.

| Criterion | WebView | Embedded RN |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Scroll performance on low-end Android | Janky | Native list virtualization |
| Pull-to-refresh | Custom bridge | `RefreshControl` |
| Push deep link to row | URL fragility | Typed Expo Router path |
| App Store "minimum functionality" | Risk if thin shell | Stronger native presence |
| Engineering cost this quarter | Days | Weeks |

```tsx
// Compromise: WebView for MVP spike, RN for v2 - gate with feature flag
import { useFeatureFlag } from "@/shared/feature-flags";
 
export function LoyaltyScreen() {
  const useNative = useFeatureFlag("loyalty_rn_v2");
  return useNative ? <LoyaltyNative /> : <LoyaltyWebView uri="https://m.example.com/loyalty" />;
}
```

* Time-box WebView spikes - **do not** let temporary shells become permanent without an ADR
* If the web page needs **camera or file upload**, WebView permission plumbing often exceeds RN cost

> **Related:** [../architecture-design/modular-monolith-vs-multi-app/modular-monolith-vs-multi-app.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/modular-monolith-vs-multi-app/) - feature flags vs separate apps

---

### 10. Ownership Boundaries in a Hybrid App

Define who owns each layer before the first PR lands.

```text
Native squad owns:
  - App launch, push registration, keychain/session vault
  - Presenting ReactNativeViewController / BrownfieldActivity
  - Store binaries, signing, native crash triage
 
RN squad owns:
  - Metro project, Expo SDK pin, JS bundle quality
  - Screens inside the embedded module, OTA policy (if enabled)
  - expo-brownfield artifact version bumps
 
Shared contract (document in repo):
  - Message types: OPEN_*, SESSION_*, LOGOUT
  - Shared state keys: auth.accessToken, auth.userId
  - Semantic versioning on AAR/Maven + iOS Swift Package
```

```typescript
// Version the bridge contract - breaking changes require major artifact bump
export const BRIDGE_CONTRACT_VERSION = "1.2.0";
 
export type HostToRnMessage =
  | { type: "SESSION_UPDATED"; accessToken: string; userId: string }
  | { type: "OPEN_CHECKOUT"; cartId: string };
```

* **One Metro bundler** per embedded module - two RN instances without `multipleFrameworks: true` on iOS risk duplicate symbols
* Align with [Brownfield Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/brownfield/best-practices/) before scaling to multiple slices

> **Related:** [Brownfield Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/brownfield/best-practices/) - 25-item summary | [../native-modules/autolinking-and-expo-modules-core/autolinking-and-expo-modules-core.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/native-modules/autolinking-and-expo-modules-core/) - autolinking in monorepos

---

## FAQs

Can we use Expo Go to test brownfield?

No - Expo Go is a greenfield container. Use debug `expo-brownfield` artifacts with Metro, or an integrated dev client inside the host app.

Does EAS Update work for embedded bundles?

Yes for the RN module when runtime versions align - but the **host store binary** must still ship when native deps change. See [Brownfield CI/CD](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/brownfield/brownfield-ci-cd/).

WebView or RN for authenticated dashboards?

RN when you need offline, native navigation integration, or shared components with web. WebView when content is rarely updated and owned by a separate web team with no mobile capacity.

How many RN modules can one host app load?

One is simplest. Multiple isolated frameworks on iOS require `multipleFrameworks: true` and careful symbol mangling - plan in an ADR before duplicating Expo projects.

Dokumen: expo-brownfield Overview
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/brownfield/expo-brownfield-overview/

# expo-brownfield Overview

Cookbook for shipping **Expo modules inside existing iOS/Android shells** - from `expo-brownfield` install through artifact publish and host-app integration.

Highlights / expo-brownfield Overview

* expo-brownfield packages your Expo app as Android AAR and iOS XCFramework or Swift Package
* Config plugin generates BrownfieldActivity, ReactNativeViewController, and messaging APIs
* Isolated approach lets native CI consume Maven/Swift Package without Node.js
* Debug builds load from Metro; release artifacts embed the Hermes bundle
* build:ios --package produces a self-contained Swift Package for Xcode local dependencies
* Pair expo-build-properties usePrecompiledModules on iOS for faster artifact builds

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
# 1. Create RN module (separate repo or monorepo package)
npx create-expo-app@latest CheckoutModule --template default@sdk-57
cd CheckoutModule
npx expo install expo-brownfield
```

```json
// app.config.ts - plugin + optional iOS precompiled modules
{
  "expo": {
    "scheme": "checkout",
    "plugins": [
      ["expo-build-properties", { "ios": { "usePrecompiledModules": true } }],
      [
        "expo-brownfield",
        {
          "ios": { "targetName": "CheckoutBrownfield" },
          "android": {
            "group": "com.example",
            "libraryName": "checkout-brownfield",
            "package": "com.example.checkout.brownfield",
            "version": "1.0.0"
          }
        }
      ]
    ]
  }
}
```

```bash
# 2. Generate native brownfield targets (debug native code, CI codegen)
npx expo prebuild
 
# 3. Build artifacts
npx expo-brownfield build:android --release
npx expo-brownfield build:ios --release --package CheckoutPackage
 
# 4. Dev loop - Metro + host debug build
npx expo start
# Launch host app from Xcode / Android Studio → RN screen loads from Metro
```

```kotlin
// Android host - build.gradle.kts dependency (version from plugin config)
dependencies {
  implementation("com.example:checkout-brownfield:1.0.0")
}
```

```swift
// iOS host - AppDelegate + present RN
import CheckoutBrownfield
 
ReactNativeHostManager.shared.initialize()
 
let vc = ReactNativeViewController(moduleName: "main", initialProps: ["cartId": id])
navigationController?.pushViewController(vc, animated: true)
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Native squads **cannot** add Node/Yarn/Metro to their release pipeline - consume **pre-built AAR or Swift Package** instead.
* You want **Expo SDK 57 modules** (camera, secure store, router) inside a **UIKit / Compose** shell without rewriting the host app.
* Product strategy is **strangler fig** - ship one RN-powered flow while legacy native screens remain.
* You need **bi-directional messaging** (`BrownfieldMessaging`) between host and RN without writing a custom TurboModule on day one.

---

## Step-by-Step Cookbook

### 1. Scaffold the Expo module

The RN project does **not** have to live inside the native repo. A monorepo `packages/checkout-rn/` or a separate Git repository both work.

```bash
npx create-expo-app@latest CheckoutModule --template default@sdk-57
cd CheckoutModule
npx expo install expo-brownfield
```

Confirm SDK pin:

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "expo": "~57.0.4",
    "expo-brownfield": "~57.0.3",
    "react": "19.2.3",
    "react-native": "0.86.0"
  }
}
```

Structure screens with thin routes and fat features per [Mobile Architecture Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/mobile-architecture-basics/).

---

### 2. Configure the plugin

`expo-brownfield` adds a config plugin that generates:

* **Android:** library module with `BrownfieldActivity`, `ReactNativeFragment`, `ReactNativeHostManager`, `BrownfieldMessaging`
* **iOS:** framework target with `ReactNativeViewController`, `ReactNativeView` (SwiftUI), `ReactNativeHostManager`, `BrownfieldMessaging`

```typescript
// app.config.ts
import type { ExpoConfig } from "expo/config";
 
const config: ExpoConfig = {
  name: "Checkout Module",
  slug: "checkout-module",
  scheme: "checkout",
  plugins: [
    [
      "expo-brownfield",
      {
        ios: {
          targetName: "CheckoutBrownfield",
          bundleIdentifier: "com.example.checkout.brownfield",
        },
        android: {
          group: "com.example",
          libraryName: "checkout-brownfield",
          package: "com.example.checkout.brownfield",
          version: "1.0.0",
          publishing: [{ type: "localMaven" }],
        },
      },
    ],
  ],
};
 
export default config;
```

Run prebuild to materialize targets:

```bash
npx expo prebuild
```

See [Config Plugins](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/native-modules/config-plugins/) for idempotent plugin patterns when combining `expo-brownfield` with other native modifiers.

---

### 3. Build Android AAR

```bash
npx expo-brownfield build:android --release
```

Default publish target is **local Maven** (`~/.m2`). Host `build.gradle.kts` needs:

```kotlin
dependencyResolutionManagement {
  repositories {
    google()
    mavenCentral()
    mavenLocal()
  }
}
 
dependencies {
  implementation("com.example:checkout-brownfield:1.0.0")
}
```

Present RN from the host:

```kotlin
import com.example.checkout.brownfield.BrownfieldActivity
import com.example.checkout.brownfield.showReactNativeFragment
 
class CheckoutActivity : BrownfieldActivity() {
  override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
    super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
    showReactNativeFragment()
  }
}
```

`AndroidManifest.xml` entry needs a **NoActionBar** theme and `configChanges` for keyboard/orientation - the generated `BrownfieldActivity` docs list the full attribute set.

---

### 4. Build iOS XCFramework or Swift Package

```bash
# XCFrameworks in ./artifacts/
npx expo-brownfield build:ios --release
 
# Self-contained Swift Package (recommended for host Xcode integration)
npx expo-brownfield build:ios --release --package CheckoutPackage
```

**Swift Package path:** In Xcode → **Add Package Dependencies → Add Local** → select `artifacts/CheckoutPackage-release/`. Xcode links bundled `.xcframework` files (brownfield, Hermes, React, dependencies).

**XCFramework path:** Drag `{TargetName}.xcframework` and `hermesvm.xcframework` into the host project; set **Embed & Sign**.

Initialize early:

```swift
import CheckoutBrownfield
 
@main
class AppDelegate: UIResponder, UIApplicationDelegate {
  func application(
    _ application: UIApplication,
    didFinishLaunchingWithOptions launchOptions: [UIApplication.LaunchOptionsKey: Any]?
  ) -> Bool {
    ReactNativeHostManager.shared.initialize()
    return true
  }
}
```

SwiftUI presentation:

```swift
import SwiftUI
import CheckoutBrownfield
 
struct CheckoutButton: View {
  @State private var showCheckout = false
  var body: some View {
    Button("Checkout") { showCheckout = true }
      .fullScreenCover(isPresented: $showCheckout) {
        ReactNativeView(moduleName: "main", initialProps: ["cartId": cartId])
      }
  }
}
```

Build **debug and release** packages separately - SPM binary targets are flavor-specific.

---

### 5. Wire communication and navigation

```typescript
// RN module - send events to native
import * as Brownfield from "expo-brownfield";
 
export function completeCheckout(orderId: string) {
  Brownfield.sendMessage({ type: "CHECKOUT_COMPLETE", orderId });
  Brownfield.popToNative(true);
}
```

```kotlin
// Android - receive from RN
BrownfieldMessaging.addListener { event ->
  if (event["type"] == "CHECKOUT_COMPLETE") {
    // Refresh native order list, pop RN fragment
  }
}
```

Enable hardware back to return to native when appropriate:

```typescript
Brownfield.setNativeBackEnabled(true);
```

Full session patterns: [Shared Authentication & Bridges](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/brownfield/shared-authentication-and-bridges/).

---

### 6. Multiple frameworks in one host (iOS)

When two Expo brownfield modules coexist in one iOS app:

```json
{
  "plugins": [
    [
      "expo-brownfield",
      {
        "ios": {
          "targetName": "CheckoutBrownfield",
          "multipleFrameworks": true
        }
      }
    ]
  ]
}
```

This prefixes ObjC symbols to avoid duplicate linker errors. Treat as **advanced** - prefer one RN module with multiple routes until boundaries force a split.

---

## Working Example: Monorepo Layout

```text
acme-mobile/
├── apps/
│   ├── host-ios/          # Xcode - consumes Swift Package
│   └── host-android/      # Gradle - consumes Maven AAR
├── packages/
│   └── checkout-rn/       # Expo project with expo-brownfield
│       ├── app/
│       ├── app.config.ts
│       └── package.json
└── package.json           # workspace root
```

CI sketch:

```yaml
# packages/checkout-rn - publish artifacts on tag
- run: npx expo-brownfield build:android --release
- run: npx expo-brownfield build:ios --release --package CheckoutPackage
- run: aws s3 sync ./artifacts s3://ci-artifacts/checkout-rn/${{ github.sha }}/
```

Host pipelines download pinned artifact versions - no `npm install` on native runners. Details: [Brownfield CI/CD](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/brownfield/brownfield-ci-cd/).

## Tooling Compatibility

| Expo tool | Brownfield isolated host |
| --- | --- |
| Expo SDK modules | ✓ |
| Expo Router | ✓ (inside RN module) |
| `expo start` / Metro | ✓ (debug) |
| EAS Build (RN project) | ✓ |
| EAS Update | ✓ (with runtime version discipline) |
| Expo Go | ✗ |
| Expo Dev Client in host | ✗ (use debug artifacts + Metro) |

Brownfield support is **alpha** - pin `expo-brownfield` to the same SDK line as `expo` and read release notes each upgrade.

## FAQs

Integrated or isolated?

**Isolated** when native CI must stay Node-free. **Integrated** when one team edits native and RN in one repo daily. See [Brownfield Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/brownfield/brownfield-basics/).

What does prebuild generate?

Brownfield library targets alongside (not replacing) the app targets - use them to debug native glue and run `build:*` CLI commands.

How do native devs get a new RN version?

Bump `android.version` / iOS package tag, run `build:android` / `build:ios`, publish artifacts, update host dependency coordinates - same as any native library.

Can I use Expo Router in the embedded module?

Yes - routes live entirely inside the RN package. Native opens `moduleName: "main"`; Router handles internal paths.

Dokumen: Case Studies Best Practices
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/case-studies/best-practices/

# Case Studies Best Practices

A condensed summary of the **25 most important practices** for writing, reading, and applying mobile case studies in this documentation set. Mobile stacks age in quarters, not years - annotate **Expo SDK 57** explicitly or the lesson expires.

Highlights / Case Studies Best Practices

* Pin Expo SDK, React, and RN versions in every case study narrative
* Architecture diagrams in prose - boxes and arrows, not screenshot dumps
* Document decisions rejected, not only choices made
* Separate reference architectures from before/after migration stories
* Benchmarks need protocol: device, build type, cache state
* Cross-link cookbook pages - case studies are maps, not duplicates

## How to Use This List

* **Authors:** Apply items 1–12 when drafting a new case study; 13–20 when publishing; 21–25 when revisiting quarterly.
* **Readers:** Treat composite references as pattern libraries - verify constraints match your compliance, device matrix, and release model before copying.
* **Tech leads:** Link ADRs to case study decisions - "we chose X for the same reason as Reference: Fintech" beats tribal knowledge.

---

1. **Pin the stack in the opening paragraph:** State **React 19.2.3**, **React Native 0.86.0**, and **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4) - not "latest Expo."
2. **Declare composite vs shipped product:** These references blend real patterns; honesty prevents "Acme Bank shipped this" confusion.
3. **Use architecture diagrams in prose:** ASCII boxes and arrows survive doc theme changes; screenshots rot.
4. **Follow the case study spine:** Context → Architecture → Recipe → Decisions → Outcomes → Lessons → Related - matches cookbook depth without hiding narrative.
5. **Record rejected alternatives:** "We considered CRDT" teaches more than listing SQLite alone - see [Reference: Offline-First Field App](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/case-studies/reference-offline-first-field-app/).
6. **Separate reference from before/after:** Reference architectures show steady-state; migration stories show timeline and regressions - do not merge genres in one file.
7. **Quantify outcomes with caveats:** Pilot fleet size, date range, and attribution limits belong beside every metric table.
8. **Document honest upgrade paths:** SDK 54→57 means 55 and 56 checkpoints - [Before/After: Expo SDK Major Upgrade](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/case-studies/before-after-expo-sdk-major-upgrade/).
9. **Strangler migrations need invariants:** One root back stack, frozen marketing URLs, no dual `NavigationContainer` - [Before/After: React Navigation → Expo Router](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/case-studies/before-after-react-navigation-expo-router/).
10. **Benchmarks require a protocol:** Release vs dev, device model, cache warm/cold, duration - [Performance Case Study: Feed at Scale](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/case-studies/performance-case-study-feed-at-scale/).
11. **OTA vs store decisions are architecture:** B2C SaaS OTA-heavy and fintech store-only are both valid - document compliance trigger - compare [Reference: B2C Expo SaaS App](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/case-studies/reference-b2c-expo-saas-app/) and [Reference: Fintech Mobile Client](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/case-studies/reference-fintech-mobile-client/).
12. **Offline-first case studies need a UX contract:** Live, stale, syncing, unavailable - four states, not a single offline banner - [Offline-First Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/data-offline/offline-first-basics/).
13. **Cross-link cookbook pages:** Case studies point to recipes; they do not duplicate [EAS Build Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/eas-build/eas-build-basics/) or [TanStack Query](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/state-management/tanstack-query/) in full.
14. **Link ADRs for contested decisions:** Navigation, pinning, OTA policy - [Architecture Decision Records](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/architecture-decision-records/).
15. **End every page with the stack versions footer:** Last line, blockquote format - enables grep-based staleness audits across the site.
16. **Tag highlights in frontmatter:** Search and index cards surface decisions without opening the full article.
17. **Name devices in field and perf stories:** "Mid-tier Android" is vague; Pixel 6a API 34 and Zebra TC57 are actionable.
18. **Include incident classes avoided:** "No runtimeVersion mismatch strandings" is as valuable as latency milliseconds.
19. **Pin SDK in audit and support payloads:** Field IT and fraud ops correlate behavior months later - [Reference: Fintech Mobile Client](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/case-studies/reference-fintech-mobile-client/).
20. **Revisit case studies after SDK bumps:** expo-image, Reanimated, and Router APIs change - add a changelog note at top when refreshed.
21. **Do not treat case studies as mandates:** Brownfield React Navigation on SDK 57 remains valid per [ADR: Navigation Library Choice](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/adr-navigation-library-choice/).
22. **Pair case studies with checklists:** [Release & OTA Rules](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/release-and-ota-rules/) and [Security Rules for Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/security-rules-for-mobile/) operationalize reference architectures.
23. **Lessons section: six items max focus:** Long lesson lists dilute; prioritize what surprised the team.
24. **Recipe blocks stay copy-pasteable:** Even narrative case studies need one quick-reference card - cookbook spine requirement.
25. **Mobile ages fast - date the narrative:** "Twelve weeks on SDK 57" and "Q3 feature freeze" anchor reader judgment better than timeless claims.

## FAQs

Are these case studies real shipped apps?

No. They are **composite references** built from recurring production patterns across Expo SDK 57 teams. Names, metrics, and timelines are illustrative but technically consistent with the pinned stack.

Which case study should a greenfield SDK 57 team read first?

Start with [Reference: B2C Expo SaaS App](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/case-studies/reference-b2c-expo-saas-app/) for Router + Query + EAS shape. Add [Reference: Offline-First Field App](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/case-studies/reference-offline-first-field-app/) if connectivity is unreliable. Add [Reference: Fintech Mobile Client](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/case-studies/reference-fintech-mobile-client/) if compliance mandates pinning and audit trails.

Should we copy the benchmark numbers into our perf budget?

Use the **protocol**, not the absolute FPS values. Your row shapes, image CDN, and device matrix will differ. Adopt thresholds from [Performance Budget Rules](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/performance-budget-rules/).

How do case studies relate to brownfield docs?

Brownfield ADRs rank options; case studies narrate outcomes. Read [Incremental Adoption ADR](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/brownfield/incremental-adoption-adr/) alongside [Before/After: React Navigation → Expo Router](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/case-studies/before-after-react-navigation-expo-router/).

## [Reference: B2C Expo SaaS App](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/case-studies/reference-b2c-expo-saas-app/)

* Expo Router route groups split auth and app trees - one root gate in \_layout.tsx
* TanStack Query owns server snapshots; MMKV holds session prefs; SQLite is deferred until relational offline needs appear
* EAS profiles map development, preview, and production to channels and environments
* runtimeVersion policy appVersion ties OTA bundles to store binaries without drift
* OTA ships JS fixes weekly; native bumps ride monthly store trains

## [Reference: Offline-First Field App](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/case-studies/reference-offline-first-field-app/)

* SQLite is source of truth on device - TanStack Query mirrors server snapshots where online
* Outbox table replays mutations with Idempotency-Key on reconnect
* Background tasks flush outbox - foreground NetInfo reconnect remains primary
* Rugged Android (Zebra, Honeywell) tested on physical hardware, not simulators
* Four-state UX contract: live, stale, syncing, unavailable
* Server-authoritative reconciliation for inspection sign-off timestamps

## [Reference: Fintech Mobile Client](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/case-studies/reference-fintech-mobile-client/)

* OAuth PKCE via expo-auth-session - no client secrets in the mobile bundle
* Refresh tokens in SecureStore; access tokens in memory with proactive refresh
* Biometric step-up before transfers - not a substitute for secure storage
* Certificate pinning adopted with SPKI backup pins and rotation ADR
* Immutable client audit trail - who, what, when, device attestation level
* OTA cannot change pins or native payment SDK - store train for native bumps

## [Before/After: Expo SDK Major Upgrade](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/case-studies/before-after-expo-sdk-major-upgrade/)

* Upgrade one SDK at a time - 54→55→56→57, never a single leap PR
* CNG teams delete ios/ and android/ after each bump - EAS regenerates via prebuild
* Rebuild dev clients after every native-affecting step - Metro cache lies
* expo-doctor gates merge; device matrix catches what doctor misses
* Reanimated, expo-image, and New Architecture flags need explicit changelog reads
* Honest timeline: three sprint increments, not a one-weekend bump to 57

## [Before/After: React Navigation → Expo Router](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/case-studies/before-after-react-navigation-expo-router/)

* Strangler fig: new routes in app/; legacy screens wrapped, not rewritten day one
* Single root back stack - native-owned or Router-owned, never both
* Deep link manifest migrated path-by-path - marketing URLs stable throughout
* SDK 57 greenfield defaults to Router; brownfield migration is optional and incremental
* Analytics and auth gates consolidated in root \_layout.tsx over three sprints
* Big-bang rewrite rejected after dual-stack production incident in staging

## [Performance Case Study: Feed at Scale](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/case-studies/performance-case-study-feed-at-scale/)

* FlatList → FlashList cut frame drops 38% on mid-tier Android at 500+ rows
* expo-image recyclingKey eliminated wrong-thumbnail flash during scroll
* estimatedItemSize calibration from on-layout sampling - not guesses
* drawDistance tuned per device tier - not one global constant
* Benchmark protocol: release build, airplane-mode warm cache, 60s fast fling
* SDK 57 expo-image disk cache survives cold start - RN Image did not
