Dokumen: Reference: B2C Expo SaaS App
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/case-studies/reference-b2c-expo-saas-app/

# Reference: B2C Expo SaaS App

A composite reference architecture for a **B2C subscription SaaS** mobile client - team collaboration, habit tracking, or lightweight CRM. The stack is pinned to **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4), **React Native 0.86.0**, and **React 19.2.3**. This is not one shipped product; it distills patterns that recur across production SaaS apps on EAS.

Highlights / Reference: B2C Expo SaaS App

* Expo Router route groups split auth and app trees - one root gate in \_layout.tsx
* TanStack Query owns server snapshots; MMKV holds session prefs; SQLite is deferred until relational offline needs appear
* EAS profiles map development, preview, and production to channels and environments
* runtimeVersion policy appVersion ties OTA bundles to store binaries without drift
* OTA ships JS fixes weekly; native bumps ride monthly store trains
* Deep links, push payloads, and marketing URLs share the same file-based route manifest

## Context

**Constraints at kickoff:**

* Ship iOS and Android from one TypeScript codebase with **weekly JS releases** and **monthly native** cadence.
* Marketing needs **universal links** into paywalled content; push notifications must open the correct screen.
* Backend is REST + WebSocket; no offline mutation queue in v1 - reads should survive brief tunnel drops.
* Team of six engineers; no dedicated native squad; CI publishes through **EAS Build** and **EAS Update**.

**Non-goals for v1:** Certificate pinning, multi-tenant white-label flavors, brownfield native embedding.

---

## Architecture

```text
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                         B2C SaaS - logical layers                        │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  app/ (Expo Router)                                                      │
│    (auth)/sign-in, sign-up          ← unauthenticated route group        │
│    (app)/(tabs)/home|inbox|settings ← authenticated shell               │
│    (app)/paywall/[sku]              ← modal presentation                  │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  src/features/*                     ← screens, hooks, feature APIs       │
│  src/api/client.ts                  ← fetch wrapper + auth header        │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  TanStack Query (server state)      ← cache, staleTime, mutations        │
│  MMKV (prefs, flags)                ← theme, last tab, feature toggles     │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  expo-secure-store                  ← refresh token only                   │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  EAS Build (binaries)               development | preview | production   │
│  EAS Update (JS OTA)                channel per profile, runtimeVersion   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Request path (authenticated read):**

```text
Screen mount → useQuery(key) → Query cache hit?
  ├─ yes + fresh → render
  ├─ yes + stale → render + background refetch
  └─ no → client.ts fetch → API → cache write → render
```

**Release path:**

```text
Git tag v2.4.0 → eas build --profile production → store submit
       │
       └─ same runtime → eas update --channel production (JS hotfix)
```

Cold start loads the root `_layout.tsx`, which reads session from SecureStore, hydrates Query `queryClient`, and redirects between `(auth)` and `(app)` groups. Route files stay thin - they re-export feature screens per [Mobile Architecture Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/mobile-architecture-basics/).

> **Related:** [Expo Router Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/expo-router-basics/) - file-based routing on SDK 57

---

## Recipe

> Quick-reference stack card for a greenfield B2C SaaS on SDK 57.

```bash
npx create-expo-app@latest AcmeSaaS --template default@sdk-57
cd AcmeSaaS
npx expo install @tanstack/react-query expo-secure-store react-native-mmkv
eas build:configure
```

```json
// eas.json (excerpt) - profile → channel → environment
{
  "build": {
    "development": { "developmentClient": true, "channel": "development" },
    "preview": { "distribution": "internal", "channel": "preview" },
    "production": { "channel": "production" }
  }
}
```

```ts
// app.config.ts (excerpt) - runtime ties OTA to store version
export default {
  version: "2.4.0",
  runtimeVersion: { policy: "appVersion" },
  updates: { url: "https://u.expo.dev/<project-id>" },
};
```

**When this reference fits:** Subscription consumer apps with auth-gated tabs, REST backends, and EAS-managed release trains.

**When to diverge:** Offline mutation queues, regulated data, or brownfield native shells - see sibling case studies in this section.

---

## Decisions Made

| # | Decision | Choice | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Navigation | **Expo Router** with `(auth)` / `(app)` groups | File paths are the link manifest; typed routes reduce param bugs - [ADR: Navigation Library Choice](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/adr-navigation-library-choice/) |
| 2 | Server state | **TanStack Query** | Stale-while-revalidate matches SaaS dashboards; `onlineManager` wired to NetInfo - [TanStack Query](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/state-management/tanstack-query/) |
| 3 | Token storage | **expo-secure-store** for refresh; access token in memory | Meets [Security Rules for Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/security-rules-for-mobile/) Tier 2 |
| 4 | Local prefs | **MMKV** for flags and UI state | Faster than AsyncStorage for tab restoration; no tokens |
| 5 | Build system | **EAS Build + CNG** | No committed `ios/` / `android/`; prebuild on cloud runners - [EAS Build Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/eas-build/eas-build-basics/) |
| 6 | OTA policy | **`runtimeVersion: appVersion`** + channel per profile | Preview QA receives preview-channel OTAs; production OTAs cannot hit dev clients - [Release & OTA Rules](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/release-and-ota-rules/) |
| 7 | Deep links | **Universal links + Expo Router** | Push and email share `https://app.acme.com/inbox/[id]` paths - [iOS Universal Links](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/deep-linking/ios-universal-links/) |
| 8 | Observability | **Sentry + structured analytics** | Scrub `Authorization` breadcrumbs before upload - [Observability Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/observability/observability-basics/) |

**Rejected alternatives:**

* **Redux for server cache** - duplicated Query capabilities; team standardized on Query in week two.
* **Expo Go for QA sign-off** - preview dev clients on physical devices replaced Go before first store submission.
* **OTA on every commit** - production updates require preview soak and CI publish per Tier 2 release rules.

---

## Outcomes

After twelve weeks on SDK 57 (migrated from SDK 54 during sprint zero - see [Before/After: Expo SDK Major Upgrade](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/case-studies/before-after-expo-sdk-major-upgrade/)):

| Metric | Result |
| --- | --- |
| **Release cadence** | 3–4 `eas update` production promotions per month; 1 store binary per month |
| **Cold start (mid Android)** | ~1.8s to interactive home (TTI budget met per [Performance Budget Rules](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/performance-budget-rules/)) |
| **Deep link success** | 97% of marketing QA matrix paths land correct screen - [Deep Link Testing Matrix](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/deep-linking/deep-link-testing-matrix/) |
| **OTA rollback** | One production rollback in quarter one - bad paywall copy; reverted channel pointer in 12 minutes |
| **Incident class avoided** | No runtimeVersion mismatch strandings after adopting `appVersion` policy |

Paywall modal route (`presentation: "modal"`) shipped without navigator JSX churn - product could A/B SKU params via OTA while native StoreKit config stayed stable.

---

## Lessons

1. **Pin SDK 57 in the narrative and in `package.json`.** Upgrade notes belong in ADRs; case studies without version pins age badly - annotate every architecture diagram with the SDK that shaped it.
2. **Thin routes, fat features.** The highest churn was `src/features/inbox/`, not `app/(app)/(tabs)/inbox.tsx`. Onboarding improved when new engineers learned the filesystem for URLs only.
3. **Channels are environments, not engineers.** Renaming `jane-dev` to `preview` eliminated accidental production OTA publishes.
4. **Query `staleTime` is a product knob.** Inbox at 30s stale, settings at 5m - one global `staleTime` caused unnecessary battery drain.
5. **Rebuild dev clients after native-affecting bumps.** SDK 57 Reanimated and expo-image updates required new `development` profile binaries; Metro-only refreshes lied about native behavior.
6. **Document what OTA cannot change.** Marketing once requested a new camera permission via OTA - blocked until store build; now listed in release checklist Tier 1.

Dokumen: Reference: Fintech Mobile Client
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/case-studies/reference-fintech-mobile-client/

# Reference: Fintech Mobile Client

A composite reference for a **retail banking / wealth-lite** mobile client - balances, transfers, statements, card controls. Security and compliance constraints dominate architecture. Stack: **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4), **React Native 0.86.0**, **React 19.2.3**.

Highlights / Reference: Fintech Mobile Client

* OAuth PKCE via expo-auth-session - no client secrets in the mobile bundle
* Refresh tokens in SecureStore; access tokens in memory with proactive refresh
* Biometric step-up before transfers - not a substitute for secure storage
* Certificate pinning adopted with SPKI backup pins and rotation ADR
* Immutable client audit trail - who, what, when, device attestation level
* OTA cannot change pins or native payment SDK - store train for native bumps

## Context

**Regulatory and security drivers:**

* PCI-aligned mobile practices: no PAN in logs, screenshot policy on CVV flows, session idle timeout.
* Security team mandates **certificate pinning** for API and attestation endpoints.
* **Audit trail** required for authentication events, transfer confirmations, and policy overrides.
* Biometric unlock for app open; **step-up** biometric before wire transfers above threshold.

**Release model:** Store binaries monthly; **no production OTA** for this client (compliance chose artifact-only JS delivery via store). Preview channel OTA used for internal QA only.

---

## Architecture

```text
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                     Fintech client - security architecture                  │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Expo Router                                                               │
│    (auth)/login, (auth)/device-trust                                       │
│    (app)/(tabs)/accounts|transfer|more                                     │
│    (app)/transfer/confirm  ← biometric gate + audit event                │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Auth layer                                                                │
│    expo-auth-session (PKCE) → code exchange → SecureStore refresh          │
│    AuthProvider: bootstrapping → authenticated | session_expired           │
│    AppState foreground refresh - Auth Session Lifecycle                    │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Transport                                                                 │
│    api/client.ts → assertHttps → native TLS pin validator (release only)   │
│    Certificate Pinning config plugin - primary + backup SPKI hashes        │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Step-up                                                                   │
│    expo-local-authentication before high-risk mutations                    │
│    Server records step-up timestamp - client emits audit event             │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Audit pipeline                                                            │
│    audit.log(event) → batch queue → POST /audit (signed payload)           │
│    Sentry scrubbed - no tokens, no account numbers in breadcrumbs          │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Release                                                                   │
│    EAS Build production only; eas update disabled on production channel    │
│    Native payment SDK + pin set versioned with store semver                │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Authentication flow:**

```text
Cold start → SecureStore read refresh → silent refresh
  ├─ success → (app) tabs
  ├─ fail → (auth)/login → OAuth PKCE → store refresh → audit: LOGIN_SUCCESS
  └─ device risk elevated → (auth)/device-trust → audit: DEVICE_CHALLENGE
```

**Transfer flow (high risk):**

```text
User confirms amount → LocalAuthentication.authenticateAsync()
  ├─ fail → audit: STEP_UP_FAILED, remain on screen
  └─ success → POST /transfers + Idempotency-Key → audit: TRANSFER_INITIATED
```

> **Related:** [Security Rules for Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/security-rules-for-mobile/) - minimum bar before store submission

---

## Recipe

> Quick-reference security stack on SDK 57 - complete ADR checklist before pinning.

```bash
npx create-expo-app@latest AcmeBank --template default@sdk-57
npx expo install expo-auth-session expo-secure-store expo-local-authentication
# Pinning: config plugin + dev-client rebuild - not Expo Go
eas build --profile preview --platform all
```

```ts
// src/audit/auditLog.ts (excerpt) - structured, no PII in message body
type AuditEvent =
  | { type: "LOGIN_SUCCESS"; deviceId: string }
  | { type: "STEP_UP_FAILED"; reason: string }
  | { type: "TRANSFER_INITIATED"; transferId: string; amountBucket: string };
 
export function auditLog(event: AuditEvent) {
  const entry = {
    ...event,
    at: new Date().toISOString(),
    appVersion: Application.nativeApplicationVersion,
    sdk: "57",
  };
  queueForUpload(entry); // flush on foreground + before transfer POST
}
```

```text
Pinning ADR must include:
  1. Threat model (rogue CA, captive portal - not "prevent reverse engineering")
  2. Primary + backup SPKI pins
  3. 30-day cert renewal alerts
  4. Corporate MITM bypass policy (usually: no bypass - document help desk script)
  5. Native rebuild path when pins rotate
```

---

## Decisions Made

| # | Decision | Choice | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | OAuth | **PKCE via expo-auth-session** | Mobile public client - no embedded client secret - [Auth Session Lifecycle](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/auth-session-lifecycle/) |
| 2 | Token storage | **SecureStore refresh; memory access** | Tier 2 security rules; AsyncStorage grep-zero policy |
| 3 | Pinning | **Native SPKI pinning with backup pin** | Threat model included rogue CA; rotation runbook owned by security ops - [Certificate Pinning](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/certificate-pinning/) |
| 4 | Biometrics | **Step-up for transfers; app unlock optional** | Biometrics gate UI, not storage - [Biometrics with LocalAuthentication](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/biometrics-with-localauthentication/) |
| 5 | OTA | **Disabled on production channel** | Compliance required binary provenance; preview OTA for QA only - [Release & OTA Rules](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/release-and-ota-rules/) |
| 6 | Audit trail | **Client event queue + server immutability** | Device emits structured events; server is legal record |
| 7 | Jailbreak/root | **Risk signal → limited features** | No hard crash; audit `DEVICE_RISK_ELEVATED` - security rules Tier 4 |
| 8 | Logging | **Sentry with Authorization scrubber** | Test crash payload review in staging mandatory |
| 9 | Deep links | **No tokens in URLs** | Push opens `/accounts/[id]` - exchange short-lived server nonce - [Expo Linking API](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/deep-linking/expo-linking-api/) |

**Rejected alternatives:**

* **Pinning via JS-only fetch** - not possible on managed path; native module required.
* **AsyncStorage session cache** - failed internal audit in week three.
* **OTA for fraud-rule JS** - compliance required store submission hash for material risk logic.

---

## Outcomes

Internal launch on SDK 57 after migrating from SDK 55 (incremental path through 56 - see SDK upgrade case study).

| Control | Result |
| --- | --- |
| **Pen test findings (mobile)** | 0 critical after pinning + SecureStore migration |
| **Audit completeness** | 99.2% client events matched server ingest (gaps from offline queue - flushed on reconnect) |
| **Pin rotation drill** | Backup pin saved 48-hour outage window during primary cert renewal |
| **Biometric step-up opt-in** | 87% enabled; fallback PIN path audited |
| **False lockouts (root detect)** | <0.3% - degraded mode instead of crash |

One incident: engineer shipped debug `rejectUnauthorized: false` - CI grep rule added per [Security Rules for Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/security-rules-for-mobile/) #17.

---

## Lessons

1. **File pinning ADR before writing native code.** Rotation without backup pins bricks production until store approval - drill quarterly.
2. **Audit events are not analytics.** Separate pipeline, stricter retention, no third-party SDK sampling.
3. **Step-up timestamp must reach server.** Client-only biometric success is not evidence for disputes.
4. **OTA policy is a compliance decision, not a velocity decision.** This client chose store-only production; B2C SaaS sibling case study chose OTA - both valid with documentation.
5. **SecureStore migration is a release, not a refactor.** One-time AsyncStorage → SecureStore path ran before enabling refresh-on-resume.
6. **Annotate SDK 57 in audit payloads.** Fraud ops correlates behavior with `expo` and Hermes versions during incident review.

Dokumen: Reference: Offline-First Field App
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/case-studies/reference-offline-first-field-app/

# Reference: Offline-First Field App

A composite reference for **offline-first field operations** - utility inspections, warehouse audits, or municipal asset surveys. Technicians capture photos, GPS fixes, and checklist answers without reliable connectivity. Stack: **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4), **React Native 0.86.0**, **React 19.2.3**.

Highlights / Reference: Offline-First Field App

* SQLite is source of truth on device - TanStack Query mirrors server snapshots where online
* Outbox table replays mutations with Idempotency-Key on reconnect
* Background tasks flush outbox - foreground NetInfo reconnect remains primary
* Rugged Android (Zebra, Honeywell) tested on physical hardware, not simulators
* Four-state UX contract: live, stale, syncing, unavailable
* Server-authoritative reconciliation for inspection sign-off timestamps

## Context

**Operational reality:**

* 40% of work happens in basements, substations, and rural sites with **no signal for hours**.
* Losing a completed inspection because the app crashed before sync is a **contract failure**, not a UX annoyance.
* Devices are **rugged Android** (Zebra TC57, Honeywell CT40) plus a minority of corporate iPhones.
* Backend accepts REST batch uploads; conflict policy is **server-authoritative** on approval timestamps.

**Team constraints:** Four mobile engineers, one backend engineer, no on-call native specialist. Expo managed workflow with EAS internal distribution to fleet devices.

---

## Architecture

```text
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Field app - offline-first data plane                   │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Expo Router                                                             │
│    (app)/jobs/[jobId]/inspection/[id]   ← deep link from dispatch SMS    │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  UI layer                                                                │
│    DataFreshnessLabel (live|stale|syncing|unavailable)                   │
│    Optimistic save → SQLite immediately                                  │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  expo-sqlite (source of truth)                                           │
│    inspections, answers, attachments_meta                                │
│    outbox (mutation queue, idempotency_key, payload_json)                │
│    sync_cursor (last_server_seq)                                         │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  TanStack Query                                                          │
│    job list / reference data - stale-while-revalidate when online          │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  NetInfo → onlineManager + foreground flush                              │
│  expo-background-task → deferred outbox drain (≥15 min interval)         │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  expo-file-system + expo-image                                           │
│    attachment files on disk; upload in background worker                 │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Write path (offline create):**

```text
User taps Save → SQLite INSERT (synced=0) → outbox INSERT
  → UI shows "Pending upload" → (later) NetInfo online
  → flushOutbox() → POST /inspections + Idempotency-Key
  → server ack → UPDATE synced=1, tombstone outbox row
```

**Sync path (background safety net):**

```text
OS schedules BACKGROUND_SYNC_TASK
  → open SQLite → flushOutbox (max 50 rows, 25 MB attachments)
  → return Success | Failed
```

Boot gate in root `_layout.tsx` runs `PRAGMA user_version` migrations before any screen reads tables - see [expo-sqlite](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/data-offline/expo-sqlite/).

> **Related:** [Offline-First Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/data-offline/offline-first-basics/) - connectivity assumptions and UX contract

---

## Recipe

> Quick-reference stack card for field capture on SDK 57.

```bash
npx create-expo-app@latest FieldInspect --template default@sdk-57
npx expo install expo-sqlite expo-background-task expo-task-manager \
  @react-native-community/netinfo @tanstack/react-query expo-file-system expo-image
```

```ts
// src/sync/outboxFlush.ts (excerpt)
export async function flushOutbox(db: SQLiteDatabase) {
  const rows = await db.getAllAsync<OutboxRow>(
    `SELECT * FROM outbox ORDER BY created_at LIMIT 50`
  );
  for (const row of rows) {
    const res = await api.post("/inspections", row.payload_json, {
      headers: { "Idempotency-Key": row.idempotency_key },
    });
    if (res.ok) await markSynced(db, row.id);
  }
}
```

```ts
// index.ts - register background task in global scope
import "./src/background/syncTask";
import "expo-router/entry";
```

**Device lab minimum:** One rugged Android on Android 11+, one iPhone two generations behind current, both on **release** builds - not Expo Go.

---

## Decisions Made

| # | Decision | Choice | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Local source of truth | **expo-sqlite** with WAL | Relational inspections + outbox; not AsyncStorage blobs - [expo-sqlite](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/data-offline/expo-sqlite/) |
| 2 | Server snapshots | **TanStack Query** for job catalog | Reference lists can be stale; capture data cannot - [Sync Strategies](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/data-offline/sync-strategies/) |
| 3 | Conflict policy | **Server-authoritative** on `approved_at` | Inspector edits after supervisor approval are discarded with audit note in UX |
| 4 | Mutation replay | **Outbox + Idempotency-Key** | Reconnect must not duplicate rows - [Data Layer Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/data-offline/best-practices/) #19–20 |
| 5 | Background upload | **expo-background-task** supplement | Foreground flush on NetInfo is primary - [Background Sync & TaskManager](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/data-offline/background-sync-and-taskmanager/) |
| 6 | Attachments | **FileSystem paths in SQLite meta** | Upload worker streams files; DB stores `local_path`, `remote_url`, `bytes_uploaded` |
| 7 | UX contract | **Four visible states** | Technicians trust "Pending upload" over silent failure - [Offline-First Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/data-offline/offline-first-basics/) #2 |
| 8 | Rugged testing | **Physical Zebra on internal track** | Scanner intents and battery saver modes do not exist on emulators - [Android Basics for RN Devs](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/android-platform/android-basics-for-rn-devs/) |
| 9 | OTA scope | **JS-only fixes on `production` channel** | Schema migrations ship with store builds when `user_version` bumps |

**Rejected alternatives:**

* **CRDT for checklist answers** - backend had no merge engine; server-authoritative simpler for compliance.
* **Background sync as only path** - 15-minute minimum interval missed dispatch deadline; foreground flush mandatory.
* **AsyncStorage outbox** - 200+ pending items after multi-day outage exceeded comfortable JSON size.

---

## Outcomes

Pilot fleet: **120 rugged devices** on Android 11–14, SDK 57 build `1.6.0`.

| Metric | Before (online-first prototype) | After (SQLite + outbox) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Lost submissions / week** | 11 (user-reported) | 0 in 8-week pilot |
| **Median save latency offline** | N/A (blocked spinner) | <80ms local commit |
| **Sync within 5 min of connectivity** | 62% | 94% |
| **Background task success rate** | - | 78% (iOS stricter than Android) |
| **Support tickets: "frozen app"** | 23/month | 4/month |

Corruption recovery: one device with a failed OTA mid-migration triggered `safeParse` quarantine - app rendered last-known-good inspections without white-screening per [Data Layer Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/data-offline/best-practices/) #13.

---

## Lessons

1. **SQLite migrations before first paint.** A `user_version` bump shipped in an OTA without a store build bricked cold start once - now native schema changes require binary bump.
2. **Show pending state per row, not global spinner.** Inspectors work on job B while job A uploads; per-row `synced` flag beat a blocking modal.
3. **Rugged devices lie about battery.** `BatterySaver` on Zebra delayed background tasks; document that foreground flush is the real delivery path.
4. **Photo uploads need byte progress.** `expo-file-system` upload with `onUploadProgress` reduced "did it save?" calls to dispatch.
5. **Logout clears all layers.** Stale inspection cache on shared devices was a privacy incident class - `queryClient.clear()` + SQLite user tables + attachment dirs.
6. **Pin SDK 57 in runbooks.** Field IT installs APKs months later; support docs must state which `runtimeVersion` accepts which OTA.

---

Dokumen: CI/CD Best Practices
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/best-practices/

# CI/CD Best Practices

A condensed summary of the **25 most important CI/CD practices** for Expo SDK 57 mobile teams - drawn from every page in this section.

Highlights / CI/CD Best Practices

* One npm script surface for local dev and CI - lint, typecheck, test, format:check
* PR checks stay under ten minutes; native builds belong to release and preview lanes
* Pin build\_id from EAS through QA to eas submit - never promote a rebuilt binary
* OTA respects runtimeVersion; native changes always need eas build
* Maestro smoke gates automated submit - short flows, not mega-journeys
* Release calendar coordinates mobile, backend, and feature flags - not ad-hoc Friday tags

1. **Same scripts locally and in CI:** `npm run lint`, `typecheck`, `test`, and `format:check` must work on a fresh clone - CI should not invoke one-off tool commands developers never run.
2. **PR checks are fast gates:** Lint, TypeScript, and Jest on every pull request - target under ten minutes; block merge via branch protection.
3. **Release pipelines are separate:** Tag-driven `eas build` and submit workflows - different triggers, different failure budget than PR checks - [Mobile CI/CD Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/mobile-ci-cd-basics/).
4. **No laptop store builds:** Production binaries come from EAS Build with credentials in EAS - not Xcode archives on one engineer's MacBook.
5. **Same artifact CI to store:** QA signs off on `build_id`; `eas submit` uses that ID - not `--latest` after a rebuild - [Automated Store Promotion](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/automated-store-promotion/).
6. **EXPO\_TOKEN robot account:** CI uses an Expo access token stored in GitHub Secrets - never personal passwords or interactive `eas login` - [GitHub Actions + EAS](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/github-actions-plus-eas/).
7. **`npm ci` in CI always:** Lockfile-driven installs - `npm install` in workflows creates non-reproducible failures.
8. **Node 20 LTS in CI:** Align `engines.node` with GitHub Actions and EAS Workflows - matches SDK 57 tooling expectations.
9. **Run `npx expo customize` before `tsc`:** Typed routes need `.expo/types` on clean checkouts - [CI Quality Gates](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/ci-quality-gates/).
10. **Quality before `type: build`:** EAS Workflows chain `needs: [quality]` so native compiles do not start on broken TypeScript - [EAS Workflows](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/eas-workflows/).
11. **Preview builds are label-gated:** `needs-preview` label or path filters - not every typo spends EAS credits - [Preview Builds on PRs](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/preview-builds-on-prs/).
12. **Internal distribution for PR previews:** `distribution: internal` + Android `apk` - QR install for QA on real devices - [Internal Distribution](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/eas-build/internal-distribution/).
13. **Separate `preview` and `production` profiles:** Preview must not touch production signing credentials or auto-increment store build numbers - [Build Profiles & Flavors](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/eas-build/build-profiles-and-flavors/).
14. **Maestro smoke gates submit:** Two to four short flows on the production `build_id` before `type: submit` - [Maestro E2E](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/maestro-e2e/).
15. **E2E stays thin; Jest stays wide:** Critical paths in Maestro; branch coverage in unit tests - [Mobile Testing Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/mobile-testing-basics/).
16. **OTA only within `runtimeVersion`:** `eas update` ships JS compatible with installed store binaries - [Runtime Version Policy](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/runtime-version-policy/).
17. **Native changes require store build:** New Expo modules, config plugins, SDK bumps - never OTA alone - [OTA Updates Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/ota-updates-basics/).
18. **Explicit update channels:** `production`, `staging`, `preview` - no accidental cross-channel promotion - [Release Channels & Branches](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/release-channels-and-branches/).
19. **Document OTA rollback:** `eas update --roll-back` rehearsed before first production OTA - [Rollback Runbook](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/rollback-runbook/).
20. **Release train calendar is shared:** Mobile, backend, and QA see the same dependency checklist - API before breaking mobile, flags before visible features - [Release Train Calendar](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/release-train-calendar/).
21. **Contract tests in PR checks:** API shape drift caught before nightly - especially when backend deploys continuously - [Contract Tests for APIs](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/contract-tests-for-apis/).
22. **Nightlies catch integration drift:** Scheduled full build on `main` when PR volume is high - alert, do not block merges.
23. **Concurrency cancels stale PR runs:** `cancel-in-progress: true` - save minutes and reduce confusing red checks on outdated commits.
24. **Monorepo path filters or Turbo filter:** Mobile CI skips when only unrelated packages change - but nightlies still validate full `main`.
25. **Staged rollout after submit:** Automated upload ≠ 100% users immediately - Play staged % and phased TestFlight - [Staged Rollouts](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/staged-rollouts/).

## FAQs

GitHub Actions, EAS Workflows, or both?

Both is common: GitHub for PR checks; EAS Workflows for build → Maestro → submit chains. Keep npm scripts identical.

Minimum CI for a solo developer?

PR checks (lint + tsc + test) + manual `eas build` on tag. Add preview-on-PR and automated submit as the app grows.

How do I know if a change needs preview build?

Native module, config plugin, navigation shell, or camera/permissions - yes. Copy and unit-test-only - no.

What is the biggest CI/CD mistake?

QA testing one binary and stores receiving another. Pin `build_id` end-to-end.

Does expo-doctor belong in CI?

Yes - at least on release and nightly workflows. Catches dependency skew before expensive native builds.

Dokumen: EAS Workflows
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/eas-workflows/

# EAS Workflows

A **checklist** for YAML pipelines that **build**, **test**, **submit**, and **update** Expo SDK 57 apps on EAS infrastructure. Work through every item before calling your release train production-ready.

Highlights / EAS Workflows

* Workflow files live in `.eas/workflows/` - versioned beside `eas.json`
* Job types: custom steps, build, maestro, submit, update - chain with `needs`
* PR triggers use `pull\_request`; releases use `push` tags or `workflow\_dispatch`
* Quality gates run before `type: build` - same npm scripts as GitHub Actions
* Maestro jobs consume `build\_id` from an upstream build job - no manual APK upload
* Submit and update jobs promote artifacts already produced - never rebuild at submit time

## How to Use This Checklist

* Run **Tier 1–2** before your first `workflow:run`; **Tier 3–5** before store automation goes live.
* Keep **one workflow per intent** - `pr-quality.yml`, `preview-pr.yml`, `store-release.yml` - not one mega-file.
* Mirror npm scripts from [CI Quality Gates](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/ci-quality-gates/) - developers and workflows call the same commands.
* Re-run failed tiers after fixes; a green local `eas build` does not mean workflow YAML is wired correctly.

### Tier Overview

| Tier | Items | When | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **1** | 1–6 | First workflow | Mobile engineer |
| **2** | 7–12 | PR + preview automation | Mobile + QA |
| **3** | 13–18 | Store release train | EM + mobile lead |
| **4** | 19–24 | OTA + rollback readiness | Mobile + backend |
| **5** | 25–30 | Operations + cost control | Platform / EM |

---

## Tier 1: Project Setup (1–6)

1. **EAS project linked** - `app.json` / `app.config.ts` contains `extra.eas.projectId` after `eas init`.

   * **Signal:** `eas workflow:run` prompts to create a project interactively.
   * **Fix:** `npx eas-cli@latest init` on SDK 57; commit the generated project ID.
   * **Priority:** P0 - blocks all workflow runs.
2. **`eas.json` profiles exist for each intent** - at minimum `preview`, `production`, and `e2e-test`.

   * **Signal:** Workflow `params.profile` references a missing key.
   * **Fix:** [Build Profiles & Flavors](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/eas-build/build-profiles-and-flavors/).
   * **Priority:** P0.
3. **`.eas/workflows/` directory committed** - YAML is source code, reviewed like application changes.

   * **Signal:** Workflows only exist on one engineer's laptop.
   * **Fix:** Add `quality-gates.yml` first; expand from there.
   * **Priority:** P0.
4. **`EXPO_TOKEN` robot account in CI secrets** - not a personal access token tied to one developer.

   * **Signal:** Workflows fail when that developer is on vacation.
   * **Fix:** Expo dashboard → Access Tokens → machine user; store in GitHub / EAS secrets.
   * **Priority:** P0.
5. **Workflow CLI tested locally** - `npx eas-cli@latest workflow:run .eas/workflows/quality-gates.yml`.

   * **Signal:** First run fails on YAML syntax discovered only in cloud.
   * **Fix:** Run manually before wiring `on: pull_request`.
   * **Priority:** P1.
6. **Concurrency group configured** - cancel superseded runs on rapid PR pushes.

   * **Signal:** Five identical builds queue for one PR.
   * **Fix:**

```yaml
concurrency:
  cancel_in_progress: true
  group: ${{ workflow.filename }}-${{ github.ref }}
```

* **Priority:** P1.

---

## Tier 2: Quality & PR Workflows (7–12)

7. **Custom quality job before any `type: build`** - lint, typecheck, test on `eas/checkout`.
   * **Signal:** Native builds start while TypeScript is broken.
   * **Fix:**

```yaml
# .eas/workflows/quality-gates.yml
name: Quality Gates
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
 
jobs:
  quality:
    steps:
      - uses: eas/checkout
      - uses: eas/use_npm_token
      - uses: eas/install_node_modules
      - run: npx expo customize tsconfig.json
      - run: npm run format:check
      - run: npm run lint
      - run: npm run typecheck
      - run: npm run test -- --ci
```

* **Priority:** P0 on every PR.

8. **`needs: [quality]` on downstream build jobs** - builds wait for green scripts.

   * **Signal:** `build_ios` and `quality` run in parallel.
   * **Fix:** Add `needs` array on every `type: build` job.
   * **Priority:** P0.
9. **PR trigger matches branch policy** - `pull_request.branches: [main]` or `release/*`.

   * **Signal:** Workflows never fire on team forks or wrong base branch.
   * **Fix:** Align with GitHub branch protection targets.
   * **Priority:** P1.
10. **Preview build profile for PR workflows** - `distribution: internal` or `simulator` / `apk` as needed.

    * **Signal:** PR workflow tries `production` credentials.
    * **Fix:** Separate `preview` profile in `eas.json` - [Internal Distribution](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/eas-build/internal-distribution/).
    * **Priority:** P0 for PR previews.
11. **Build job outputs `build_id` consumed downstream** - Maestro and submit reference the same artifact.

    * **Signal:** Submit job calls `--latest` instead of pinned ID.
    * **Fix:**

```yaml
  build_android:
    needs: [quality]
    type: build
    params:
      platform: android
      profile: preview
 
  maestro_smoke:
    needs: [build_android]
    type: maestro
    params:
      build_id: ${{ needs.build_android.outputs.build_id }}
      flow_path: [".maestro/smoke.yml"]
```

```
- **Priority:** P0 before automated submit.
```

12. **Maestro `appId` matches `eas.json` bundle IDs** - flows launch the built app, not Expo Go.
- **Signal:** Maestro job succeeds locally but fails in workflow - wrong `appId`.
- **Fix:** [Maestro E2E](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/maestro-e2e/).
- **Priority:** P0 on first E2E workflow.

---

## Tier 3: Build, Submit & Release (13–18)

13. **Production build workflow triggered by semver tag** - `on.push.tags: ["v*"]`.

    * **Signal:** Every merge to `main` submits to stores.
    * **Fix:** Tag-driven release; manual `workflow_dispatch` for hotfixes.
    * **Priority:** P0.
14. **`type: build` with `profile: production` and `autoIncrement`** - build numbers advance without hand-editing plists.

    * **Signal:** Store rejects duplicate `versionCode` / build number.
    * **Fix:** `"autoIncrement": true` in `eas.json` production profile.
    * **Priority:** P0.
15. **`type: submit` references `build_id` from paired build job** - not `--latest`.

    * **Signal:** Store receives a build QA never tested.
    * **Fix:**

```yaml
  submit_ios:
    needs: [smoke_ios]
    type: submit
    params:
      platform: ios
      build_id: ${{ needs.build_ios.outputs.build_id }}
```

```
- **Priority:** P0 - [Automated Store Promotion](./automated-store-promotion.md).
```

16. **Maestro smoke gates submit** - at least login + one revenue-critical path.
- **Signal:** Submit runs immediately after build with no device verification.
- **Fix:** `needs: [maestro_smoke]` on submit jobs.
- **Priority:** P0 for automated promotion.

17. **iOS and Android submit jobs parallel after platform-specific smoke** - do not serialize unnecessarily.

    * **Signal:** Android waits for iOS TestFlight processing.
    * **Fix:** Separate build → smoke → submit chains per platform.
    * **Priority:** P1.
18. **Slack / email notification on workflow failure** - on-call knows before users do.

    * **Signal:** Failed release discovered Monday morning.
    * **Fix:** GitHub notifications or custom step posting to webhook.
    * **Priority:** P1.

---

## Tier 4: OTA Update Workflows (19–24)

19. **`type: update` job targets explicit channel** - `production`, `staging`, not implicit default.

    * **Signal:** Staging bundle promoted to production channel by typo.
    * **Fix:** [Release Channels & Branches](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/release-channels-and-branches/).
    * **Priority:** P0.
20. **OTA workflow runs quality gates first** - same lint/tsc/test as PR checks.

    * **Signal:** Broken TypeScript ships via OTA.
    * **Fix:** `needs: [quality]` before `type: update`.
    * **Priority:** P0.
21. **`runtimeVersion` policy documented** - OTA compatible only with matching store binaries.

    * **Signal:** OTA crashes on older app versions.
    * **Fix:** [Runtime Version Policy](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/runtime-version-policy/).
    * **Priority:** P0.
22. **OTA message includes Git SHA** - traceability in EAS dashboard.

    * **Signal:** Cannot correlate update with merged PR.
    * **Fix:** `message: ${{ github.sha }}` in update params.
    * **Priority:** P1.
23. **Rollback workflow documented and tested** - `eas update --roll-back` or channel republish.

    * **Signal:** First production incident has no runbook.
    * **Fix:** [Rollback Runbook](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/rollback-runbook/).
    * **Priority:** P0 before first OTA to production.
24. **Native-impacting changes blocked from OTA-only workflow** - config plugin edits trigger build workflow.

    * **Signal:** OTA imports `expo-camera` not in installed binary.
    * **Fix:** Path filters or required review label `native-change`.
    * **Priority:** P0.

---

## Tier 5: Operations & Cost (25–30)

25. **Skip tokens documented** - `[eas skip]` in commit message for docs-only pushes.

    * **Signal:** Team avoids workflows entirely because they cannot skip.
    * **Fix:** Document in CONTRIBUTING.md; do not overuse.
    * **Priority:** P2.
26. **PR preview builds label-gated or path-filtered** - not every typo triggers EAS build.

    * **Signal:** EAS credit burn exceeds budget mid-quarter.
    * **Fix:** [Preview Builds on PRs](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/preview-builds-on-prs/).
    * **Priority:** P1.
27. **Build profile matrix documented** - which profile runs on PR, nightly, release.

    * **Signal:** New engineer triggers production build from feature branch.
    * **Fix:** Table in README or [Mobile CI/CD Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/mobile-ci-cd-basics/).
    * **Priority:** P1.
28. **Secrets rotated on schedule** - `EXPO_TOKEN`, App Store Connect API key, Play service account.

    * **Signal:** Token leak requires emergency revoke with no backup.
    * **Fix:** Quarterly rotation calendar entry.
    * **Priority:** P1.
29. **Workflow duration monitored** - quality + build + Maestro p95 tracked.

    * **Signal:** Release train misses Friday window silently.
    * **Fix:** EAS dashboard build times; optimize `install_node_modules` caching.
    * **Priority:** P2.
30. **Disaster drill: failed Maestro blocks submit** - verified in staging, not assumed.

    * **Signal:** Submit job has loose `needs` wiring; smoke failure ignored.
    * **Fix:** Intentionally fail a flow in staging workflow quarterly.
    * **Priority:** P1.

---

## Reference: Job Types

| `type` | Purpose | Key `params` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| *(custom steps)* | lint, tsc, test, doctor | `run: npm run …` |
| `build` | Cloud native binary | `platform`, `profile` |
| `maestro` | E2E on built artifact | `build_id`, `flow_path` |
| `submit` | Store upload | `platform`, `build_id` |
| `update` | OTA bundle | `channel`, `message` |

### Full Release Workflow Sketch

```yaml
# .eas/workflows/store-release.yml
name: Store Release
on:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]
 
jobs:
  quality:
    steps:
      - uses: eas/checkout
      - uses: eas/install_node_modules
      - run: npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm run test -- --ci
 
  build_android:
    needs: [quality]
    type: build
    params: { platform: android, profile: production }
 
  smoke_android:
    needs: [build_android]
    type: maestro
    params:
      build_id: ${{ needs.build_android.outputs.build_id }}
      flow_path: [".maestro/smoke.yml"]
 
  submit_android:
    needs: [smoke_android]
    type: submit
    params:
      platform: android
      build_id: ${{ needs.build_android.outputs.build_id }}
 
  update_production:
    needs: [submit_android]
    type: update
    params:
      channel: production
      message: "Post-release OTA sync ${{ github.sha }}"
```

---

## FAQs

Where do workflow files live?

`.eas/workflows/*.yml` at the project root (sibling to `eas.json`). Name by intent: `quality-gates.yml`, `preview-pr.yml`, `store-release.yml`.

How do I run a workflow manually?

```bash
npx eas-cli@latest workflow:run .eas/workflows/quality-gates.yml
```

Use `workflow_dispatch` in `on:` for GitHub UI triggers.

GitHub Actions or EAS Workflows?

GitHub Actions excels at PR checks on every push. EAS Workflows excel at build → Maestro → submit chains on Expo infra. Many teams use both - keep npm scripts identical.

Can one workflow do build and OTA?

Yes - chain `type: build` then `type: update` with `needs`. OTA-only hotfixes can use a separate workflow with just quality + update jobs.

Dokumen: GitHub Actions + EAS
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/github-actions-plus-eas/

# GitHub Actions + EAS

A cookbook for wiring **GitHub Actions** to **EAS Build**, **Submit**, and **Update** - covering secrets, caching, monorepo triggers, and `expo-github-action`.

Highlights / GitHub Actions + EAS

* expo-github-action installs EAS CLI and authenticates with EXPO\_TOKEN
* npm ci + Node 20 + setup-node cache: npm for deterministic PR checks
* Monorepos use paths-filter or turbo --filter to skip unrelated packages
* Never store Apple passwords in YAML - EAS credentials and ASC API keys only
* Hybrid pattern: GitHub Actions for PR gates, EAS Workflows for build chains
* Concurrency groups cancel stale runs when contributors push fixup commits

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```yaml
# .github/workflows/eas-build.yml
name: EAS Build
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]
 
env:
  EXPO_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.EXPO_TOKEN }}
 
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: npm
      - uses: expo/expo-github-action@v8
        with:
          eas-version: latest
          token: ${{ secrets.EXPO_TOKEN }}
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run typecheck && npm run test -- --ci
      - run: eas build --profile production --platform all --non-interactive
```

```bash
# Create robot token (once, locally)
npx eas-cli@latest login
# Expo dashboard → Access Tokens → Create token → paste into GitHub Secrets as EXPO_TOKEN
```

**When to reach for this:**

* PR quality gates on GitHub free/cheap minutes; EAS cloud for native compiles.
* Tag-driven releases (`v*`) that must not depend on a developer laptop.
* Monorepos where only `apps/mobile` should trigger mobile workflows.
* Teams already using branch protection and required status checks on GitHub.

## Working Example

**Project layout:**

```text
your-expo-app/
  .github/workflows/
    pr-checks.yml
    eas-release.yml
  eas.json
  app.json
  package-lock.json
```

### PR checks (no EAS credits)

```yaml
# .github/workflows/pr-checks.yml
name: PR Checks
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
 
concurrency:
  group: pr-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
 
jobs:
  quality:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx expo customize tsconfig.json
      - run: npm run format:check
      - run: npm run lint
      - run: npm run typecheck
      - run: npm run test -- --ci --passWithNoTests
```

### Release build with expo-github-action

```yaml
# .github/workflows/eas-release.yml
name: EAS Release
on:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]
 
jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: npm
      - uses: expo/expo-github-action@v8
        with:
          eas-version: latest
          token: ${{ secrets.EXPO_TOKEN }}
          eas-cache: true
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx expo-doctor
      - run: npm run typecheck && npm run test -- --ci
      - name: Build production
        run: eas build --profile production --platform all --non-interactive --wait
      - name: Submit iOS
        run: eas submit --platform ios --latest --non-interactive
      - name: Submit Android
        run: eas submit --platform android --latest --non-interactive
```

### Monorepo path filter

```yaml
# .github/workflows/mobile-pr.yml
name: Mobile PR
on:
  pull_request:
 
jobs:
  changes:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      mobile: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.mobile }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dorny/paths-filter@v3
        id: filter
        with:
          filters: |
            mobile:
              - 'apps/mobile/**'
              - 'packages/ui/**'
              - 'packages/api-client/**'
              - 'package-lock.json'
 
  quality:
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.mobile == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: apps/mobile
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: package-lock.json
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm run test -- --ci
```

```bash
# Monorepo root alternative with Turborepo
npx turbo run lint typecheck test --filter=mobile
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* **`EXPO_TOKEN`** authenticates `eas build` / `submit` without interactive login.
* **`eas-cache: true`** on `expo-github-action` speeds repeated CLI invocations.
* **`npm ci`** + `cache: npm` restores `node_modules` between workflow runs.
* **Path filters** skip mobile CI when only `apps/web` changes.
* **`--non-interactive`** is mandatory in CI - no prompts.

## Deep Dive

### Secrets Matrix

| Secret | Where | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `EXPO_TOKEN` | GitHub Secrets | `eas build`, `submit`, `update`, workflow runs |
| `NPM_TOKEN` | GitHub Secrets | Private packages during `npm ci` |
| App Store Connect API key | EAS credentials | iOS submit - not duplicated in GitHub if using EAS Submit |
| Play service account JSON | EAS credentials | Android submit |

Create `EXPO_TOKEN` from an Expo **robot** or **CI** access token - not a developer's personal token tied to 2FA sessions.

```bash
# Verify token locally before adding to GitHub
EXPO_TOKEN=xxx npx eas-cli@latest whoami
```

### expo-github-action Options

| Input | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `eas-version` | Pin CLI (`latest` or `16.x.x`) |
| `token` | Maps to `EXPO_TOKEN` |
| `eas-cache` | Cache EAS CLI download between jobs |
| `packager` | `npm` / `yarn` / `pnpm` - match repo |

### Caching Strategies

```yaml
# npm - simplest
- uses: actions/setup-node@v4
  with:
    node-version: 20
    cache: npm
 
# Monorepo - point cache at root lockfile
- uses: actions/setup-node@v4
  with:
    node-version: 20
    cache: npm
    cache-dependency-path: package-lock.json
 
# Turborepo remote cache (optional, larger repos)
env:
  TURBO_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.TURBO_TOKEN }}
  TURBO_TEAM: ${{ vars.TURBO_TEAM }}
```

* **`npm ci`** always - not `npm install` - lockfile is the contract
* EAS Build has its own dependency install on Expo servers - GitHub cache does not speed cloud native compile
* Cache **saves PR check minutes**, not EAS build queue time

### Monorepo Trigger Patterns

| Pattern | Pros | Cons |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `paths:` on `on.pull_request` | Native GitHub, zero deps | Coarse - misses shared package renames |
| `dorny/paths-filter` | Per-job boolean outputs | Extra action dependency |
| `turbo --filter=[origin/main...]` | Affected-only in large repos | Requires Turbo graph setup |
| Always run root `turbo run lint` | Simple mental model | Slower on docs-only PRs |

For release tags, **always build from repo root** with full `npm ci` - path filters are PR-only optimizations.

### Hybrid: GitHub Actions + EAS Workflows

```text
PR opened → GitHub Actions (lint, tsc, test)     ← cheap, every push
Tag pushed  → EAS Workflow (build → Maestro → submit) ← native infra, gated chain
```

* Duplicate YAML is acceptable if **npm scripts stay identical**
* GitHub required checks: `quality` job from Actions
* EAS Workflows own `type: build` / `maestro` / `submit` - [EAS Workflows](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/eas-workflows/)

## Gotchas

* **Missing `EXPO_TOKEN`** - `eas build` hangs or prompts and fails. **Fix:** Organization secret available to the workflow; verify with `eas whoami` step.
* **`npm install` in CI** - Non-deterministic installs; "passes on CI, fails locally." **Fix:** `npm ci` when `package-lock.json` exists.
* **Running submit with `--latest` after QA tested older build** - Store gets untested binary. **Fix:** Pass `--id <BUILD_ID>` from the build step output.
* **Path filter ignores lockfile** - Dependency bump in root does not trigger mobile checks. **Fix:** Include `package-lock.json` / `pnpm-lock.yaml` in filter paths.
* **Apple ID password in GitHub Secrets** - Breaks on 2FA; security anti-pattern. **Fix:** EAS-managed credentials + App Store Connect API key.
* **No `concurrency` on PR workflows** - Six queued runs for rapid fixup pushes. **Fix:** `cancel-in-progress: true`.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GitHub Actions + expo-github-action | PR gates + tag releases on GH | You want build→Maestro→submit only on EAS infra |
| EAS Workflows only | Single YAML home on Expo | You need GH marketplace actions ecosystem |
| Bitrise / CircleCI | Enterprise standard already paid | Greenfield Expo team - EAS is lower ceremony |
| Local `eas build` | Emergency one-off | Normal release train - non-reproducible |

## FAQs

Where do I store EXPO\_TOKEN?

GitHub → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → `EXPO_TOKEN`. For monorepos, organization-level secret shared across mobile repos.

Should I pin eas-version?

Pin (`16.4.0`) for reproducibility; use `latest` when you want CLI fixes automatically. Align with `eas-cli` devDependency in `package.json` when possible.

How do I run EAS build only on labels?

```yaml
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled]
jobs:
  preview:
    if: contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'eas-preview')
```

See [Preview Builds on PRs](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/preview-builds-on-prs/).

pnpm monorepo?

```yaml
- uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
  with: { version: 9 }
- uses: actions/setup-node@v4
  with:
    node-version: 20
    cache: pnpm
- run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
```

Set `packager: pnpm` on `expo-github-action` when applicable.

Can GitHub Actions run Maestro?

Yes - but you manage emulator boot, APK install, and caching. EAS Workflows `type: maestro` is lower ceremony for Expo teams - [Maestro E2E](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/maestro-e2e/).

* [Preview Builds on PRs](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/preview-builds-on-prs/) - label-gated preview automation

## [Mobile CI/CD Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/mobile-ci-cd-basics/)

* PR checks are fast gates - lint, typecheck, unit tests - every merge request
* Release pipelines produce store binaries and OTA bundles from tagged commits
* Nightly builds catch integration drift when PR volume is high
* Same npm scripts locally and in CI - no special CI-only commands
* EAS Build replaces laptop Xcode/Android Studio for reproducible native artifacts
* Separate PR feedback (minutes) from release trains (hours/days) - different failure budgets

## [EAS Workflows](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/eas-workflows/)

* Workflow files live in `.eas/workflows/` - versioned beside `eas.json`
* Job types: custom steps, build, maestro, submit, update - chain with `needs`
* PR triggers use `pull_request`; releases use `push` tags or `workflow_dispatch`
* Quality gates run before `type: build` - same npm scripts as GitHub Actions
* Maestro jobs consume `build_id` from an upstream build job - no manual APK upload
* Submit and update jobs promote artifacts already produced - never rebuild at submit time

## [GitHub Actions + EAS](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/github-actions-plus-eas/)

* expo-github-action installs EAS CLI and authenticates with EXPO\_TOKEN
* npm ci + Node 20 + setup-node cache: npm for deterministic PR checks
* Monorepos use paths-filter or turbo --filter to skip unrelated packages
* Never store Apple passwords in YAML - EAS credentials and ASC API keys only
* Hybrid pattern: GitHub Actions for PR gates, EAS Workflows for build chains
* Concurrency groups cancel stale runs when contributors push fixup commits

## [Preview Builds on PRs](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/preview-builds-on-prs/)

* Preview profile produces internal-distribution binaries - install via QR, not the public store
* Label-gated or path-filtered triggers keep EAS credits under control
* expo-github-action or EAS Workflows both work - post install URL as PR comment
* Android APK previews install without Play Console; iOS uses ad hoc or simulator builds
* Pair preview builds with Maestro smoke when native navigation changed
* Document which PRs need previews - designers add a label, not every typo

## [Automated Store Promotion](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/automated-store-promotion/)

* Submit jobs reference build\_id from the same workflow - never --latest after manual QA on different ID
* Maestro smoke is the minimum gate - login, home, one revenue or data-loss path
* Human approval step optional between smoke and submit for regulated industries
* Staged Play rollout and phased TestFlight remain post-submit - automation stops at upload
* Failed smoke blocks submit via needs - no bypass without documented hotfix process
* Same workflow produces iOS and Android artifacts - parallel platform chains

## [Release Train Calendar](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/release-train-calendar/)

* Three clocks: store binary (native), OTA bundle (JS), backend API - document dependencies
* Backend breaking changes deploy before or with the mobile binary that requires them
* OTA-only weeks skip store submit but still need runtimeVersion discipline
* Code freeze windows protect Friday releases - hotfix lane documented separately
* Feature flags decouple binary live from feature visible to users
* Shared calendar visible to mobile, backend, and QA - not a spreadsheet only EM edits

## [CI/CD Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/best-practices/)

* One npm script surface for local dev and CI - lint, typecheck, test, format:check
* PR checks stay under ten minutes; native builds belong to release and preview lanes
* Pin build\_id from EAS through QA to eas submit - never promote a rebuilt binary
* OTA respects runtimeVersion; native changes always need eas build
* Maestro smoke gates automated submit - short flows, not mega-journeys
* Release calendar coordinates mobile, backend, and feature flags - not ad-hoc Friday tags

Dokumen: Mobile CI/CD Basics
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/mobile-ci-cd-basics/

# Mobile CI/CD Basics

10 examples to understand **PR checks**, **release pipelines**, and **nightly builds** for Expo SDK 57 apps - 7 basic and 3 intermediate.

Highlights / Mobile CI/CD Basics

* PR checks are fast gates - lint, typecheck, unit tests - every merge request
* Release pipelines produce store binaries and OTA bundles from tagged commits
* Nightly builds catch integration drift when PR volume is high
* Same npm scripts locally and in CI - no special CI-only commands
* EAS Build replaces laptop Xcode/Android Studio for reproducible native artifacts
* Separate PR feedback (minutes) from release trains (hours/days) - different failure budgets

## Prerequisites

CI/CD for React Native differs from web: you ship **native binaries** (store builds) and optionally **OTA JavaScript bundles** ([OTA Updates Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/ota-updates-basics/)). Cloud builds via [EAS Build Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/eas-build/eas-build-basics/) keep signing keys off laptops.

```bash
npx create-expo-app@latest ShipApp --template blank-typescript
cd ShipApp
npx expo install eas-cli --save-dev
npx eas-cli@latest build:configure
```

Standardize scripts CI will call:

```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "lint": "expo lint",
    "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit",
    "test": "jest",
    "format:check": "prettier --check ."
  }
}
```

> **Tooling:** These examples target **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4), **React Native 0.86.0**, and **React 19.2.3**. E2E snippets assume dev or preview builds - not Expo Go alone.

---

## Basic Examples

### 1. Three Pipeline Types

Mobile teams run **three distinct automation lanes** with different speed, cost, and blast-radius goals.

```text
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ PR checks        │ Every PR     │ 2–8 min  │ Block merge   │
├──────────────────┼──────────────┼──────────┼───────────────┤
│ Release pipeline │ Tag / main   │ 20–60 min│ Store + OTA   │
├──────────────────┼──────────────┼──────────┼───────────────┤
│ Nightly          │ Cron 02:00   │ 30–90 min│ Drift signal  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

| Lane | Triggers | Typical jobs | Blocks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PR checks | `pull_request` | lint, tsc, Jest | Merge to `main` |
| Release | `push` tag `v*`, manual | EAS build, Maestro smoke, submit | Store promotion |
| Nightly | `schedule: cron` | Full matrix build, contract tests | Nothing - alerts only |

* **PR checks fail fast** - no native compile until TypeScript and unit tests pass
* **Release pipelines** produce the **same artifact** QA signed off on and stores receive
* **Nightlies** catch "green PRs, broken together" when twenty branches land overnight

> **Related:** [CI Quality Gates](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/ci-quality-gates/) - script surface PR checks call

---

### 2. PR Checks - What Runs on Every Pull Request

PR automation answers: *"Is this diff safe to merge?"* - not *"Is this ready for the App Store?"*

```yaml
# .github/workflows/pr-checks.yml
name: PR Checks
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
 
jobs:
  quality:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: 20, cache: npm }
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx expo customize tsconfig.json
      - run: npm run format:check
      - run: npm run lint
      - run: npm run typecheck
      - run: npm run test -- --ci
```

* Runs on **every push** to an open PR - developers get feedback before review
* **No EAS build** on every PR unless preview builds are explicitly budgeted ([Preview Builds on PRs](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/preview-builds-on-prs/))
* Branch protection requires the `quality` check - policy, not honor system
* Same commands locally: `npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test`

> **Related:** [Mobile Testing Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/mobile-testing-basics/) - pyramid layers PR checks cover

---

### 3. Release Pipeline - Tag to Store Binary

Release automation answers: *"Build and ship the version we tagged."*

```yaml
# .github/workflows/release.yml
name: Release
on:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]
 
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: expo/expo-github-action@v8
        with:
          eas-version: latest
          token: ${{ secrets.EXPO_TOKEN }}
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run typecheck && npm run test -- --ci
      - run: eas build --profile production --platform all --non-interactive
```

```json
// eas.json (excerpt)
{
  "build": {
    "production": {
      "autoIncrement": true,
      "channel": "production"
    }
  }
}
```

* Trigger on **semver Git tags** (`v2.4.0`) - tag ↔ binary traceability
* `EXPO_TOKEN` robot account - never personal passwords in CI ([GitHub Actions + EAS](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/github-actions-plus-eas/))
* **`production` profile** maps to store signing credentials in EAS
* QA tests the **build ID** from this pipeline - not a laptop archive

> **Related:** [Build Profiles & Flavors](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/eas-build/build-profiles-and-flavors/) - `preview` vs `production`

---

### 4. Nightly Builds - Catch Integration Drift

When PR volume is high, individual green checks hide **cross-branch integration failures**. Nightlies run on a schedule without blocking merges.

```yaml
# .github/workflows/nightly.yml
name: Nightly Integration
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 6 * * 1-5"  # weekdays 06:00 UTC
  workflow_dispatch:
 
jobs:
  nightly:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with: { ref: main }
      - uses: expo/expo-github-action@v8
        with:
          eas-version: latest
          token: ${{ secrets.EXPO_TOKEN }}
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx expo-doctor
      - run: npm run test -- --ci
      - run: eas build --profile preview --platform android --non-interactive
```

* **Alerts channel** (`#mobile-ci`) on failure - do not block daytime merges
* Include `npx expo-doctor` - catches SDK skew nobody touched in today's PRs
* Build **one platform** nightly if credits are tight; rotate iOS/Android weekly
* Pair with **contract tests** against staging APIs ([Contract Tests for APIs](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/contract-tests-for-apis/))

---

### 5. PR Checks vs Preview Builds

Not every PR needs a native binary. Split **fast gates** from **optional preview builds**.

| Signal | PR check only | + Preview build |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Copy change in `Text` | ✓ | ✗ |
| New native module (`expo-camera`) | lint/tsc | ✓ |
| Navigation refactor | unit tests | ✓ (Maestro smoke) |
| Config plugin change | tsc + doctor | ✓ |

```yaml
# Label-gated preview - saves EAS credits
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled]
jobs:
  preview:
    if: contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'needs-preview')
    # ... eas build --profile preview
```

* Default: **quality gates only** - preview on label or `paths` filter for native-impacting dirs
* Preview builds install via **QR code** on real devices - see [Preview Builds on PRs](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/preview-builds-on-prs/)
* Document the label in CONTRIBUTING.md so designers know when to add `needs-preview`

---

### 6. OTA in the Release Train

JS-only fixes ship via `eas update` **inside** the release pipeline - native changes still need `eas build`.

```yaml
# .eas/workflows/release-ota.yml (excerpt)
jobs:
  quality:
    steps:
      - uses: eas/checkout
      - uses: eas/install_node_modules
      - run: npm run typecheck && npm run test -- --ci
 
  update_production:
    needs: [quality]
    type: update
    params:
      channel: production
      message: ${{ github.sha }}
```

* OTA runs **after** the same quality scripts as PR checks
* **`runtimeVersion`** must match the store binary users installed - [Runtime Version Policy](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/runtime-version-policy/)
* Never OTA a bundle that imports a native module absent from the installed binary
* Rollback path: `eas update --roll-back` - [Rollback Runbook](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/rollback-runbook/)

---

### 7. Artifact Promotion - Same Binary CI to Store

The anti-pattern: QA tests a laptop build; stores receive a different cloud build.

```text
❌ Laptop build → QA sign-off → CI rebuild → Store
✅ EAS build ID abc123 → QA sign-off → eas submit --id abc123 → Store
```

```bash
# Promote the exact build QA tested
eas submit --platform ios --id <BUILD_ID> --non-interactive
eas submit --platform android --id <BUILD_ID> --non-interactive
```

* Store **build IDs** in release notes and Slack threads
* `eas submit --latest` is convenient but risky if a newer build queued after QA
* [Automated Store Promotion](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/automated-store-promotion/) gates submit on Maestro smoke

> **Related:** [EAS Submit](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/eas-build/eas-submit/) - App Store Connect and Play Console handoff

---

## Intermediate Examples

### 8. Monorepo-Aware PR Triggers

Turborepo monorepos should not run mobile CI when only the marketing site changed.

```yaml
on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "apps/mobile/**"
      - "packages/ui/**"
      - "package-lock.json"
```

```yaml
# Or path filter action
- uses: dorny/paths-filter@v3
  id: changes
  with:
    filters: |
      mobile:
        - 'apps/mobile/**'
        - 'packages/**'
- if: steps.changes.outputs.mobile == 'true'
  run: npm run typecheck -w apps/mobile
```

* Root lockfile changes always trigger mobile - dependency graph may have shifted
* `turbo run lint typecheck test --filter=mobile` fans out with cache - [GitHub Actions + EAS](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/github-actions-plus-eas/)
* Nightly still builds **full main** - path filters are for PR speed, not integration coverage

---

### 9. Release Train with Staged Gates

Advanced teams chain **quality → build → E2E → submit** in one workflow file.

```yaml
# .eas/workflows/store-release.yml (sketch)
name: Store Release
on:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]
 
jobs:
  quality:
    steps:
      - uses: eas/checkout
      - uses: eas/install_node_modules
      - run: npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm run test -- --ci
 
  build_ios:
    needs: [quality]
    type: build
    params: { platform: ios, profile: production }
 
  smoke_ios:
    needs: [build_ios]
    type: maestro
    params:
      build_id: ${{ needs.build_ios.outputs.build_id }}
      flow_path: [".maestro/smoke.yml"]
 
  submit_ios:
    needs: [smoke_ios]
    type: submit
    params:
      platform: ios
      build_id: ${{ needs.build_ios.outputs.build_id }}
```

* **`needs`** chains enforce ordering - submit cannot run if Maestro failed
* Smoke flows stay **short** - login, home, one critical tab ([Maestro E2E](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/maestro-e2e/))
* Android and iOS can parallelize after quality - see [EAS Workflows](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/eas-workflows/) checklist

---

### 10. Coordinating JS, Native, and Backend

Mobile releases rarely ship alone. Document **deploy dependencies** in a release calendar.

```text
Week 12 release train
  Tue - Backend API v3 deploys to staging (contract tests green)
  Wed - eas build production (native + embedded JS)
  Thu - eas update production (JS hotfix if needed, same runtimeVersion)
  Fri - eas submit after Maestro + manual QA
  Mon - Staged rollout 10% → 50% → 100%
```

| Change type | Ships via | Backend dependency |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Button color | OTA | None |
| New API field (optional) | OTA | Backend live first |
| New native module | Store build | Feature flag off until binary live |
| Breaking API | Store + backend same window | Coordinate freeze |

* [Release Train Calendar](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/release-train-calendar/) expands the calendar model
* Feature flags decouple **binary live** from **feature visible** - [Feature Flags for Safe Rollout](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/error-resilience/feature-flags-for-safe-rollout/)
* Contract tests in PR checks catch API shape drift before nightly

---

## Anti-Patterns

| Anti-pattern | Why it fails |
| --- | --- |
| `eas build` on every PR commit | Burns credits; 20-minute feedback loops |
| Skipping tests on release tags | "Hotfix" tags ship regressions |
| Laptop archive to TestFlight | Non-reproducible; signing drift |
| OTA without channel discipline | Staging bundle hits production users |
| One pipeline for everything | PR waits 45 minutes; team disables CI |

---

## FAQs

What belongs in PR checks vs release?

PR: lint, format, tsc, unit tests, optional contract tests. Release: EAS build, E2E smoke, submit, OTA to production channel.

How often should nightlies run?

Weekdays for active teams; weekly for small apps. Increase frequency after SDK upgrades or monorepo migrations.

Can I skip CI with a commit message?

EAS Workflows honor `[eas skip]` on push triggers. Prefer label-gated previews over routine skip tokens - branch protection should still require PR checks.

Do I need both GitHub Actions and EAS Workflows?

Many teams use GitHub Actions for PR checks and EAS Workflows for build/test/submit chains. Keep npm scripts identical across both.
