Dokumen: Preview Builds on PRs
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/preview-builds-on-prs/

# Preview Builds on PRs

A cookbook for **QR distribution** of EAS preview builds on pull requests - so design and QA review on **real devices** before merge.

Highlights / Preview Builds on PRs

* Preview profile produces internal-distribution binaries - install via QR, not the public store
* Label-gated or path-filtered triggers keep EAS credits under control
* expo-github-action or EAS Workflows both work - post install URL as PR comment
* Android APK previews install without Play Console; iOS uses ad hoc or simulator builds
* Pair preview builds with Maestro smoke when native navigation changed
* Document which PRs need previews - designers add a label, not every typo

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```json
// eas.json - preview profile
{
  "build": {
    "preview": {
      "distribution": "internal",
      "channel": "preview",
      "android": { "buildType": "apk" },
      "ios": { "simulator": false }
    }
  }
}
```

```yaml
# .github/workflows/preview-pr.yml
name: Preview Build
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled]
 
jobs:
  preview:
    if: contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'needs-preview')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: expo/expo-github-action@v8
        with:
          eas-version: latest
          token: ${{ secrets.EXPO_TOKEN }}
      - run: npm ci
      - id: build
        run: |
          eas build --profile preview --platform android --non-interactive --json > build.json
          echo "url=$(jq -r '.[0].artifacts.buildUrl' build.json)" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
      - uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            github.rest.issues.createComment({
              issue_number: context.issue.number,
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              body: `## 📱 Preview build\n\nInstall: ${{ steps.build.outputs.url }}\n\nScan QR on device or open link.`
            })
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Native navigation, gestures, or camera flows designers must see on hardware.
* QA sign-off before merge on features that Jest cannot cover.
* Cross-platform UI review when web Storybook is not enough.
* Stakeholder demos without waiting for nightly or release train.

## Working Example

**Project layout:**

```text
your-expo-app/
  .github/workflows/preview-pr.yml
  .eas/workflows/preview-pr.yml   # optional EAS-native alternative
  eas.json
  app.json
```

### eas.json profiles

```json
{
  "build": {
    "preview": {
      "distribution": "internal",
      "channel": "preview",
      "env": {
        "APP_VARIANT": "preview"
      },
      "android": {
        "buildType": "apk"
      },
      "ios": {
        "simulator": false
      }
    },
    "preview-simulator": {
      "distribution": "internal",
      "ios": { "simulator": true },
      "android": { "buildType": "apk" }
    }
  }
}
```

```ts
// app.config.ts - optional variant banner
const IS_PREVIEW = process.env.APP_VARIANT === "preview";
 
export default {
  expo: {
    name: IS_PREVIEW ? "MyApp (Preview)" : "MyApp",
    // ...
  },
};
```

### GitHub Actions - comment with install link

```yaml
name: Preview on PR
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, labeled]
 
concurrency:
  group: preview-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
 
jobs:
  preview:
    if: contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'needs-preview')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: 20, cache: npm }
      - uses: expo/expo-github-action@v8
        with:
          eas-version: latest
          token: ${{ secrets.EXPO_TOKEN }}
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run typecheck
      - name: EAS preview build
        id: eas
        run: |
          eas build \
            --profile preview \
            --platform android \
            --non-interactive \
            --json > build-output.json
          BUILD_URL=$(jq -r '.[0].artifacts.buildUrl // .artifacts.buildUrl' build-output.json)
          QR_URL=$(jq -r '.[0].artifacts.applicationArchiveUrl // empty' build-output.json)
          echo "build_url=$BUILD_URL" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
      - name: Comment on PR
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const url = '${{ steps.eas.outputs.build_url }}';
            const body = [
              '## 📱 Android preview build',
              '',
              `**Install:** ${url}`,
              '',
              '1. Open the link on your Android device',
              '2. Scan the QR code or download the APK',
              '3. Allow install from unknown sources if prompted (internal testing only)',
              '',
              '_Built from commit `${{ github.sha }}` with profile `preview`._'
            ].join('\n');
            github.rest.issues.createComment({
              issue_number: context.issue.number,
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              body
            });
```

### EAS Workflows alternative

```yaml
# .eas/workflows/preview-pr.yml
name: Preview PR
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled]
 
jobs:
  quality:
    if: ${{ github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name contains 'needs-preview' }}
    steps:
      - uses: eas/checkout
      - uses: eas/install_node_modules
      - run: npm run typecheck
 
  build_preview:
    needs: [quality]
    type: build
    params:
      platform: android
      profile: preview
```

Trigger manually when testing:

```bash
npx eas-cli@latest workflow:run .eas/workflows/preview-pr.yml
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* **`distribution: internal`** - EAS hosts install page with QR ([Internal Distribution](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/eas-build/internal-distribution/)).
* **`buildType: apk`** on Android - sideload without Play internal track.
* **Label gate** - only PRs with `needs-preview` spend build credits.
* **PR comment** - QA and design get link without digging in EAS dashboard.
* **Concurrency** - latest push cancels stale preview for same PR number.

## Deep Dive

### Who Installs What

| Platform | Preview profile | Installer | Best for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Android | `apk` + internal | QR / APK link | QA on physical devices |
| iOS device | ad hoc / internal | QR via EAS | Registered UDIDs |
| iOS | `simulator: true` | `.app` tar | Designer on Mac simulator |
| Both | + `channel: preview` | + optional `eas update` | JS hotfix on same preview binary |

### Trigger Strategies

```yaml
# Label-gated (recommended)
if: contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'needs-preview')
 
# Path-filter - native-impacting changes only
on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "app/**"
      - "src/**"
      - "app.config.ts"
      - "plugins/**"
```

| Strategy | Credit cost | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Every PR push | High | Best coverage |
| Label `needs-preview` | Low | Requires discipline |
| Path filter | Medium | Misses shared package changes if filter too narrow |

Document in `CONTRIBUTING.md`:

```markdown
## Preview builds
Add label `needs-preview` when QA or design needs a device build.
Do **not** add for copy-only or test-only changes.
```

### OTA on Preview Channel

After the preview binary exists, JS fixes can ship without rebuilding:

```bash
eas update --channel preview --message "PR-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}"
```

* Preview binary must match `runtimeVersion` - [Runtime Version Policy](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/runtime-version-policy/)
* Comment on PR when OTA lands so QA refreshes the bundle
* Native changes still need a new preview build

### Pair with Maestro Smoke

When navigation changes, run a thin Maestro flow on the preview `build_id` before merge:

```yaml
  maestro_smoke:
    needs: [build_preview]
    type: maestro
    params:
      build_id: ${{ needs.build_preview.outputs.build_id }}
      flow_path: [".maestro/smoke.yml"]
```

* Fail the PR check if smoke fails - optional but valuable for routing refactors
* Keep smoke to 3–5 steps - [Maestro E2E](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/maestro-e2e/)

## Gotchas

* **Preview on every commit** - EAS credit exhaustion by mid-sprint. **Fix:** Label gate + concurrency cancel.
* **iOS preview without registered devices** - Ad hoc build installs nowhere. **Fix:** Maintain device list in Apple Developer portal or use simulator profile for designers.
* **QA tests Expo Go** - Bundle ID and native modules differ from preview build. **Fix:** Always distribute the EAS artifact link.
* **Stale PR comment** - Old install link after rebase. **Fix:** Edit comment or post new comment per build; include `github.sha` in body.
* **Production credentials on preview profile** - Accidental store signing on feature branch. **Fix:** Separate `preview` profile without `autoIncrement` production keys.
* **Missing `pull-requests: write` permission** - Comment step fails silently or errors. **Fix:** Add `permissions` block in workflow.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| EAS internal distribution QR | Default for device QA | You need Play internal track phased rollout |
| `eas update` on preview channel | JS-only PR tweaks | New native module added |
| TestFlight external + PR number | iOS-heavy team already on ASC | Fast Android APK feedback needed |
| Screenshot tests only | Pure layout/copy | Gestures, camera, haptics |

## FAQs

How does QA install on Android?

Open the EAS build page link from the PR comment → scan QR → install APK. Enable "install unknown apps" for the browser if prompted.

Can I build iOS and Android in one PR job?

```bash
eas build --profile preview --platform all --non-interactive
```

Costs two builds; comment both links or build Android-only for faster feedback.

How do designers get iOS preview without UDIDs?

Use `preview-simulator` profile - download simulator build; designer runs on Xcode simulator.

Should preview use a different API?

Set `env.API_URL` in preview profile to staging - never point preview builds at production write APIs.

Dokumen: adb & Android Devices
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cli/adb-and-android-devices/

# adb & Android Devices

`adb` (Android Debug Bridge) is the **terminal interface** to emulators and USB hardware - list devices, reverse Metro ports, tail `logcat`, and install dev builds without opening Android Studio. Expo SDK 57 wraps daily compiles in `npx expo run:android`; this page is the cookbook for when logcat, port forwarding, or APK installs need explicit control.

Highlights / adb & Android Devices

* adb devices -l confirms emulator and USB hardware before expo run:android
* adb reverse tcp:8081 tcp:8081 lets USB devices reach Metro without LAN IP hunting
* adb logcat '\*:S' ReactNativeJS:V filters JS console noise from system spam
* adb install -r pushes EAS APKs and local assembleDebug outputs
* adb shell am start opens deep links and cold-starts the dev client in one line
* Multiple devices require -s SERIAL on every adb subcommand

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
# Verify toolchain + device
export ANDROID_HOME="$HOME/Library/Android/sdk"
export PATH="$PATH:$ANDROID_HOME/platform-tools"
adb devices -l
 
# USB dev: Metro port reverse (8081 default)
adb reverse tcp:8081 tcp:8081
npx expo start --dev-client
 
# RN-focused logcat
adb logcat '*:S' ReactNative:V ReactNativeJS:V AndroidRuntime:E
 
# Install dev APK (EAS internal or local debug)
adb install -r ./build/app-debug.apk
adb shell am start -n com.example.app/.MainActivity
```

**When to reach for this:**

* `npx expo run:android` cannot see a device (`no devices/emulators found`).
* USB hardware cannot load the JS bundle - Metro works on emulator but not phone.
* You need native crash stack traces beyond the redbox.
* CI or QA installs a prebuilt APK without Gradle on the laptop.
* Deep link or notification cold-start must be scripted for Maestro prep.

## Working Example

**USB physical device: reverse Metro, install dev client, tail logs, open deep link.**

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
 
PACKAGE="com.example.shopapp"
APK="./shopapp-debug.apk"   # from eas build --profile development --platform android
 
# 1. Single device guard
SERIAL=$(adb devices | awk 'NR>1 && $2=="device" {print $1; exit}')
if [[ -z "$SERIAL" ]]; then
  echo "No adb device in 'device' state. Enable USB debugging." >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "Using device: $SERIAL"
 
# 2. Port reverse for Metro (USB)
adb -s "$SERIAL" reverse tcp:8081 tcp:8081
adb -s "$SERIAL" reverse --list
 
# 3. Install / upgrade dev client
adb -s "$SERIAL" install -r "$APK"
 
# 4. Cold start main activity
adb -s "$SERIAL" shell am force-stop "$PACKAGE"
adb -s "$SERIAL" shell am start -n "$PACKAGE/.MainActivity"
 
# 5. Deep link smoke
adb -s "$SERIAL" shell am start -a android.intent.action.VIEW \
  -d "shopapp://orders/42" "$PACKAGE"
 
# 6. Logs in second terminal - native crashes + JS console
adb -s "$SERIAL" logcat '*:S' ReactNative:V ReactNativeJS:V AndroidRuntime:E
```

**Start Metro (separate terminal):**

```bash
npx expo start --dev-client --clear
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* **`-s SERIAL`** - mandatory when emulator and phone are both connected.
* **`adb reverse`** - USB path to Metro without Wi-Fi IP alignment.
* **`install -r`** - replaces existing debug build while keeping app data (usually).
* **`am start -a VIEW -d`** - intent filter / deep link verification from bash.
* **Filtered `logcat`** - surfaces `ReactNativeJS` and fatal `AndroidRuntime` errors.

## Deep Dive

### How It Works

* **`adb`** speaks to `adbd` on the device/emulator over USB or TCP (wireless debugging).
* **Metro** serves JS on `localhost:8081` on your laptop - the device needs a path to that port (`reverse`, shared LAN IP, or tunnel).
* **`npx expo run:android`** invokes Gradle `installDebug` then launches the app - `adb install` skips compile when you already have an APK.
* **Dev clients** built with `expo-dev-client` still need Metro for JS - `adb reverse` is the USB shortcut.

### Device Discovery

```bash
adb devices -l                    # serial, state, model
adb kill-server && adb start-server # reset daemon when devices flap
adb -e <cmd>                        # only emulator
adb -d <cmd>                        # only USB device
```

| State | Meaning | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `device` | Ready | Proceed |
| `unauthorized` | RSA key not accepted on phone | Tap "Allow USB debugging" |
| `offline` | Cable/driver glitch | Replug, `adb kill-server` |
| empty list | No emulator running | Android Studio AVD or `emulator -avd <name>` |

```bash
# List AVDs and boot one (emulator binary is in ANDROID_HOME)
emulator -list-avds
emulator -avd Pixel_8_API_35 &
adb wait-for-device
```

### Port Reverse & Forward

```bash
# Metro (default 8081)
adb reverse tcp:8081 tcp:8081
 
# DevTools or custom packager port
adb reverse tcp:8082 tcp:8082
 
# Show active reverses
adb reverse --list
 
# Remove all reverses
adb reverse --remove-all
 
# Forward device port to laptop (less common in RN)
adb forward tcp:9000 tcp:9000
```

* **Wi-Fi dev** - skip `reverse`; use `npx expo start --dev-client --host lan` and ensure phone and laptop share subnet.
* **Corporate VPN** - often breaks LAN; try `--tunnel` on Metro or USB `reverse`.

### logcat Recipes

```bash
# RN daily driver
adb logcat '*:S' ReactNative:V ReactNativeJS:V AndroidRuntime:E
 
# Clear buffer before reproducing a crash
adb logcat -c && adb logcat '*:S' ReactNativeJS:V AndroidRuntime:E
 
# Save to file for CI artifact
adb logcat -d > android-logcat.txt
 
# Filter by PID after launch (adb shell pidof)
PID=$(adb shell pidof -s com.example.app)
adb logcat --pid="$PID"
 
# Kotlin/Java crash stack only
adb logcat '*:S' AndroidRuntime:E
```

### Install & Launch

```bash
# Debug APK from expo run:android
adb install -r android/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk
 
# EAS internal distribution APK
adb install -r ./downloads/shopapp.apk
 
# Uninstall clean
adb uninstall com.example.app
 
# Launch launcher activity
adb shell monkey -p com.example.app -c android.intent.category.LAUNCHER 1
 
# Force stop
adb shell am force-stop com.example.app
 
# Clear app data (logout / corrupted storage)
adb shell pm clear com.example.app
```

* **`applicationId`** in `app.config.ts` (`android.package`) must match `adb` package strings.
* **Play-signed AAB** from production `eas build` is not installable via `adb` - use internal APK/AAB track or `bundletool`.

### Shell Utilities

```bash
# Screenshot (PNG to stdout redirected)
adb exec-out screencap -p > screen.png
 
# Screen record (max 180s on many devices)
adb shell screenrecord /sdcard/demo.mp4
adb pull /sdcard/demo.mp4
 
# Input text (ASCII only - no spaces without %s)
adb shell input text "hello"
 
# Open system settings deep link
adb shell am start -a android.settings.APPLICATION_DETAILS_SETTINGS \
  -d package:com.example.app
```

### Bash Notes

```bash
# macOS default SDK path - align with Android Studio install
export ANDROID_HOME="$HOME/Library/Android/sdk"
export PATH="$PATH:$ANDROID_HOME/platform-tools:$ANDROID_HOME/emulator"
 
# JDK 17 required for RN 0.86 / Expo SDK 57 Gradle
export JAVA_HOME=$(/usr/libexec/java_home -v 17)
 
# Loop until device is ready (CI emulator boot)
adb wait-for-device shell 'while [[ -z $(getprop sys.boot_completed) ]]; do sleep 1; done'
```

## Gotchas

* **Forgot `adb reverse` on USB** - dev client shows "Unable to load script". **Fix:** `adb reverse tcp:8081 tcp:8081` after every reconnect.
* **Multiple devices, no `-s SERIAL`** - `adb: more than one device/emulator`. **Fix:** `adb devices` then suffix every command.
* **Installing release AAB with `adb install`** - fails; wrong artifact type. **Fix:** internal APK profile or Play internal track - [Internal Testing Tracks](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/android-platform/internal-testing-tracks/).
* **Logcat flood without filters** - thousands of lines/sec hide RN errors. **Fix:** `'*:S' ReactNativeJS:V` pattern above.
* **`npm install` native module without rebuild** - JS updates but native code stale. **Fix:** `npx expo run:android` or install fresh EAS dev APK.
* **Wireless debugging drops** - `adb disconnect` then re-pair. **Fix:** USB for reliable `reverse` during native debugging.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `npx expo run:android` | Daily Gradle compile + install | APK already built in CI |
| Android Studio Logcat GUI | Multi-filter UI, pinning threads | Headless CI - use `adb logcat` |
| `npx expo start --tunnel` | No USB, LAN blocked | USB available - `reverse` is faster |
| Wireless `adb connect` | Cable-free desk | Need stable Metro during long debug |

## FAQs

Why does emulator see Metro but USB phone does not?

* Emulator uses `10.0.2.2` to reach host localhost - physical devices do not.
* Use `adb reverse` on USB or `--host lan` with correct laptop IP on Wi-Fi.

How do I find the installable APK path after expo run:android?

* `android/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk` for standard debug builds.
* EAS artifacts download from `eas build:list` - see [jq, rg & JSON Logs](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cli/jq-rg-and-json-logs/).

adb unauthorized after macOS update?

* Revoke USB debugging authorizations on the phone (Developer options).
* Replug cable and accept the RSA fingerprint dialog.

Can I grant permissions from adb?

* `adb shell pm grant com.example.app android.permission.CAMERA`
* Runtime permissions still may need in-app prompts on Android 13+ for notifications.

Does adb work on iOS?

* No - use `xcrun simctl` and Xcode devices window for Apple platforms.

Dokumen: macOS & Linux CLI Best Practices
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cli/best-practices/

# macOS & Linux CLI Best Practices

A condensed summary of **25 macOS and Linux CLI essentials** for Expo SDK 57 teams - shared portable scripts, device tooling, and JSON automation drawn from every page in this section.

Highlights / macOS & Linux CLI Best Practices

* 25 portable CLI essentials for Expo SDK 57 teams on macOS and Linux
* Check scripts into scripts/ - same bash locally, on GitHub Actions, and EAS hooks
* Prefer npx expo and npx eas-cli over global CLI drift
* Pin jq/rg queries next to CI workflows - not copy-pasted Slack snippets
* Platform tools: simctl for iOS state, adb reverse for USB Metro
* Parse eas build:list --json - never scrape human tables in automation

1. **Check scripts into the repo:** Put `scripts/ci/` bash under version control - laptops, GitHub Actions, and EAS hooks run the same entrypoints, not one-off Slack snippets.
2. **Use `npx` for Expo and EAS CLIs:** `npx expo-doctor` and `npx eas-cli@latest` avoid global version drift between teammates and CI images.
3. **Standardize on `npm ci` in automation:** Lockfile-driven installs on CI; `npm install` only on local feature branches when intentionally updating deps.
4. **Run `npx expo-doctor` before native work:** Catches SDK 57 version skew before `expo run:*` or `eas build` waste twenty minutes on CocoaPods or Gradle.
5. **Pair `expo start --dev-client` with dev builds:** Custom native shells need the dev-client Metro flag - plain `expo start` targets Expo Go semantics.
6. **Clear Metro with intent:** `npx expo start --clear` after dependency upgrades; do not alias it to every save - it hides bundler bugs.
7. **Reserve `expo prebuild` for native changes:** Config plugins, entitlements, and new native modules - not every JS commit under CNG.
8. **Mirror CI gates locally:** `npm run lint && npx tsc --noEmit && npm test -- --ci` before `eas build --non-interactive` - same commands, same failure surface.
9. **Export `EXPO_TOKEN` on CI only:** Robot tokens in GitHub Secrets / EAS - never commit; verify with `eas whoami` in a dry-run job.
10. **Parse `eas build:list --json`:** Use `jq` for artifact URLs - human tables are not machine-readable and break when CLI formatting changes.
11. **Fail closed with `jq -er`:** Required JSON fields should exit non-zero when missing - prevents `curl` downloading HTML error pages as "APKs".
12. **Use `rg` for log triage:** Ripgrep JSONL and EAS logs with `-g` globs - faster than `grep -R` and respects `.gitignore`.
13. **Resolve iOS simulator UDIDs in scripts:** Device names collide across Xcode versions - `xcrun simctl list devices available -j | jq` is stable.
14. **Boot simulators before `simctl install`:** The `booted` alias targets nothing when Simulator is shut down - `simctl boot` then install.
15. **Screenshot with `simctl io` for evidence:** PNG artifacts for PRs, Maestro baselines, and App Store attachments - reproducible without Xcode UI.
16. **Set `ANDROID_HOME` and JDK 17 explicitly:** RN 0.86 Gradle expects JDK 17 - document paths in `README` and CI env blocks.
17. **`adb reverse tcp:8081` on USB Android:** Physical devices do not reach laptop `localhost` without reverse - do this after every cable reconnect.
18. **Suffix `adb -s SERIAL` with multiple devices:** Emulator plus phone causes ambiguous target errors - enumerate with `adb devices -l`.
19. **Filter logcat aggressively:** `'*:S' ReactNativeJS:V AndroidRuntime:E` surfaces JS and fatal native errors without system spam.
20. **Install APKs with `adb install -r`:** Reinstall dev clients from EAS or `assembleDebug` without Android Studio - verify `android.package` matches.
21. **Prefer LAN Metro; tunnel as fallback:** `--tunnel` is slower - use USB `adb reverse` or shared Wi-Fi before defaulting to tunnel.
22. **Chain commands with `&&` in scripts:** `set -euo pipefail` plus explicit gates - fail fast like CI, not silent partial success.
23. **Store jq filters beside workflows:** `scripts/jq/latest-apk.jq` reviewed in PRs - not inline one-liners duplicated across three YAML files.
24. **Linux CI for Android; macOS for iOS simctl:** Do not pretend `simctl` runs on `ubuntu-latest` - split jobs by platform capability.
25. **Cross-read platform docs when CLI is not enough:** Signing, entitlements, and Play tracks live in [EAS Build](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/eas-build/eas-build-basics/), [iOS Platform](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ios-platform/ios-basics-for-rn-devs/), and [Android Platform](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/android-platform/android-basics-for-rn-devs/) - CLI clears dev friction, not store policy.

## FAQs

Should we use Make or just bash scripts?

* Either works - pick one entry style (`make ci` or `npm run ci:android`).
* Bash scripts in `scripts/` are enough for most Expo teams; avoid macOS-only Makefile assumptions on Linux CI.

Where do shellcheck and shfmt fit?

* Run `shellcheck scripts/**/*.sh` in PR checks when scripts grow past trivial.
* Keeps `set -euo pipefail` scripts portable between macOS bash and Linux dash-linked environments.

Can Linux developers do all mobile CLI tasks?

* Android `adb`, Metro, and EAS JSON tooling run on Linux fully.
* iOS `simctl` and Xcode builds require macOS - use EAS cloud for iOS when Linux is the daily driver.

Dokumen: CLI Basics for RN
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cli/cli-basics-for-rn/

# CLI Basics for RN

The **20 terminal commands** you run daily building Expo SDK 57 apps - Metro, prebuild, local native runs, and EAS cloud workflows. Treat this page as a cookbook reference card; platform-specific debugging lives in [xcrun simctl](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cli/xcrun-simctl-and-ios-simulators/) and [adb](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cli/adb-and-android-devices/).

Highlights / CLI Basics for RN

* npx expo start is the daily entry - add --dev-client when native modules require your bundle ID
* npx expo install pins packages to the SDK 57 matrix - never raw npm install for Expo modules
* npx expo-doctor catches version skew before Metro throws obscure transform errors
* npx expo run:ios and run:android wrap prebuild + native compile for local dev clients
* eas build produces signed store binaries - eas update ships JS-only OTA bundles
* Same npm scripts locally and in CI - lint, typecheck, and test before eas build --non-interactive

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
# Morning startup (dev client on simulator)
npx expo start --dev-client
npx expo run:ios --simulator "iPhone 16 Pro"   # or: npx expo run:android
 
# Health check before a PR or release
npx expo-doctor
npm run lint && npx tsc --noEmit && npm test -- --ci
 
# Cloud build + submit (after eas.json is configured)
eas build --profile production --platform all --non-interactive
eas submit --platform all --latest --non-interactive
```

**When to reach for this:**

* You need the exact flag for tunnel vs LAN vs dev-client without opening docs.
* A new teammate asks "what do I run after `git clone`?"
* CI scripts should mirror laptop commands - no special-case YAML verbs.
* You are deciding between local `expo run:*` and cloud `eas build`.

## Working Example

**Typical SDK 57 day - from clone to TestFlight-shaped binary:**

```bash
# 1. Install deps (lockfile-driven)
npm ci
 
# 2. Verify SDK alignment
npx expo-doctor
 
# 3. Start Metro for a dev client (not Expo Go)
npx expo start --dev-client --clear
 
# 4. Compile and install native shell (first time or after native dep change)
npx expo run:ios --simulator "iPhone 16 Pro"
# npx expo run:android   # parallel Android path
 
# 5. Add a native-capable package the Expo way
npx expo install expo-camera
npx expo prebuild --platform ios   # only when plugin changes native project
npx expo run:ios
 
# 6. Pre-merge quality gate (same as CI)
npm run lint
npx tsc --noEmit
npm test -- --ci
 
# 7. Production-shaped cloud build
eas build --profile production --platform ios --non-interactive --wait
eas build:list --limit 1 --json > /tmp/last-build.json   # see jq page for parsing
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* **`npm ci`** - deterministic installs; CI and laptops share the same graph.
* **`expo-doctor`** - catches React/RN/Expo version skew before native compile.
* **`expo start --dev-client`** - pairs with a custom dev build, not Expo Go alone.
* **`expo install`** - resolves compatible semver for SDK 57 modules.
* **`eas build --wait`** - blocks until the artifact URL is ready for QA handoff.

## Deep Dive

### The 20 Daily Commands

| # | Command | What it does | When you run it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `npx expo start` | Starts Metro bundler and Dev Tools | Every JS iteration session |
| 2 | `npx expo start --dev-client` | Metro tuned for `expo-dev-client` launcher | Daily when using custom dev builds |
| 3 | `npx expo start --clear` | Metro with cache reset | Stale bundle, weird HMR, after dep upgrades |
| 4 | `npx expo start --tunnel` | Expo tunnel when LAN/firewall blocks device | QA on cellular, corporate Wi-Fi |
| 5 | `npx expo install <pkg>` | Adds deps pinned to SDK 57 matrix | Any new `expo-*` or RN community module |
| 6 | `npx expo-doctor` | Validates project against Expo compatibility rules | Before PR, after SDK bump, when builds fail mysteriously |
| 7 | `npx expo prebuild` | Generates `ios/` and `android/` from `app.config.ts` | After config plugin or native entitlement change |
| 8 | `npx expo run:ios` | Prebuild (if needed) + Xcode build + simulator/device install | Local iOS dev client iteration |
| 9 | `npx expo run:android` | Prebuild (if needed) + Gradle assemble + install | Local Android dev client iteration |
| 10 | `npx expo lint` | Runs ESLint with Expo's recommended config | Pre-commit and PR checks |
| 11 | `npx tsc --noEmit` | TypeScript compile check without output | Pre-commit and PR checks |
| 12 | `npm test -- --ci` | Jest in CI-safe mode (no watch) | Every PR and before `eas build` |
| 13 | `eas build` | Cloud native compile with EAS credentials | Store binaries, QA builds, simulator IPAs |
| 14 | `eas build:list` | Lists recent cloud builds (status, artifact URLs) | "Where is my IPA?" after CI |
| 15 | `eas build --local` | Runs EAS build recipe on your machine | Reproduce cloud signing/compile failures |
| 16 | `eas submit` | Uploads latest build to App Store Connect / Play Console | After green QA on production profile |
| 17 | `eas update` | Publishes JS bundle to EAS Update channel | Hotfix JS without store review |
| 18 | `eas credentials` | Manage iOS certs/profiles and Android keystores | Signing errors, new bundle ID, push setup |
| 19 | `npx expo export` | Static export of web or embedded bundle | Web deploy, size audits, offline bundle inspection |
| 20 | `watchman watch-del-all` | Clears Watchman roots (macOS/Linux) | Metro file-watcher stuck after branch switch |

### Command Families

```text
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Metro / JS loop     │ expo start*, expo export, eas update │
├─────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Native shell        │ expo prebuild, expo run:ios/android    │
├─────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Quality gates       │ expo-doctor, lint, tsc, jest --ci      │
├─────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Cloud ship          │ eas build*, eas submit, eas credentials│
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

* **Metro commands** are cheap - run dozens of times per day.
* **Native run commands** are expensive - run after native dep or entitlement changes.
* **EAS commands** cost build minutes - reserve for profiles that match store signing.

### Flags Worth Memorizing

```bash
# Simulator / device targeting
npx expo run:ios --simulator "iPhone 16 Pro"
npx expo run:ios --device
npx expo run:android --device
 
# Non-interactive CI (always pair with EXPO_TOKEN)
eas build --profile preview --platform android --non-interactive --wait
eas submit --platform ios --latest --non-interactive
 
# Inspect last build as JSON (feeds jq recipes)
eas build:list --limit 5 --json --status finished
```

### Bash Notes

```bash
# Prefer npx for one-off Expo/EAS CLIs - avoids global version drift
npx expo-doctor
npx eas-cli@latest build --profile production --platform all
 
# Export token for CI shells (GitHub Actions sets secrets.EXPO_TOKEN)
export EXPO_TOKEN="your-robot-token"
eas whoami   # verify auth before --non-interactive builds
 
# Chain gates the way CI does - fail fast
npx expo-doctor && npm run lint && npx tsc --noEmit && npm test -- --ci
```

## Gotchas

* **`npm install expo-camera` instead of `npx expo install`** - version may not match SDK 57; native build fails in CocoaPods or Gradle. **Fix:** always `npx expo install <pkg>`.
* **`expo start` without `--dev-client` on a custom native build** - launcher cannot find the right entry or dev menu. **Fix:** `npx expo start --dev-client` after `expo run:*`.
* **Running `eas build` without `eas login` / `EXPO_TOKEN` in CI** - interactive prompts hang the job. **Fix:** `eas login` locally; robot token in CI - see [EAS Build Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/eas-build/eas-build-basics/).
* **Skipping `expo-doctor` after merging dependabot** - green TypeScript but red native link step. **Fix:** doctor before every `expo run:*` or `eas build`.
* **`expo prebuild` on every JS save** - wipes hand-edited native files under CNG. **Fix:** prebuild only when `app.config.ts`, plugins, or native modules change.
* **Assuming `eas update` replaces entitlements or native modules** - OTA is JS-only. **Fix:** `eas build` when native code or config plugins change.
* **Different commands locally vs CI** - "works on my machine" release failures. **Fix:** npm scripts as single source of truth; CI calls `npm run` targets.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Expo Go (`expo start` + scan QR) | Learning RN, no custom native modules | Push, universal links, custom native SDKs |
| `eas build --local` | Reproduce cloud compile on a Mac with Xcode | You only need a quick Debug simulator run |
| `npx react-native run-ios` | Bare RN without Expo prebuild pipeline | Expo projects - loses config plugins |
| Global `eas` / `expo` install | You pin versions in every script anyway | Default - `npx` avoids team-wide CLI drift |

## FAQs

Do I need EAS CLI installed globally?

* No - `npx eas-cli@latest <command>` or `npm install eas-cli --save-dev` keeps versions in `package.json`.
* CI should use `expo/expo-github-action` or `npx eas-cli@latest` with `EXPO_TOKEN`.

expo start vs expo run:ios - which first?

* Run `expo run:ios` (or `run:android`) once to install the dev client binary.
* Then `expo start --dev-client` for daily JS reload - Metro stays up across saves.

When is --tunnel required?

* Device and laptop on different networks, or corporate firewall blocks LAN Metro.
* Tunnel is slower - prefer LAN or USB `adb reverse` on Android when possible.

What replaces expo start --ios in SDK 57?

* `npx expo start` plus press `i` in the terminal, or `npx expo run:ios` for native compile.
* There is no separate `expo start --ios` shortcut in modern Expo CLI.

How do I cancel a stuck cloud build?

* `eas build:cancel` - then `eas build:list` to confirm status before retrying.

Dokumen: jq, rg & JSON Logs
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cli/jq-rg-and-json-logs/

# jq, rg & JSON Logs

`jq` and `rg` (ripgrep) are the **fast inspection layer** for CI and EAS JSON - extract artifact URLs from `eas build:list`, grep JSONL logs for `Gradle failure`, and wire GitHub Actions outputs without a throwaway Node script. On Expo SDK 57 teams, these two tools turn cloud build metadata into bash you can check into the repo.

Highlights / jq, rg & JSON Logs

* eas build:list --json is the canonical EAS artifact feed for shell scripts
* jq -r selects fields without writing Node one-off parsers in CI
* rg searches JSONL build logs faster than grep - respects .gitignore, skips binaries
* Combine curl + jq to download the latest finished APK URL in one pipeline
* GitHub Actions step outputs pair with jq for downstream Maestro or adb install
* Keep jq filters in repo scripts - same query locally and on CI runners

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
# Latest finished production Android APK URL
eas build:list --platform android --status finished --limit 1 --json \
  | jq -r '.[0].artifacts.buildUrl // empty'
 
# iOS simulator .app download + bundle id from same JSON blob
eas build:list --platform ios --status finished --limit 1 --json \
  | jq -r '.[0] | "\(.applicationArchiveUrl // .artifacts.buildUrl)\t\(.buildDetails?.buildConfiguration ?? "n/a")"'
 
# Grep EAS/GitHub JSON log export for failure signature
rg -n '"level":"error"|Gradle failure|pod install' ./artifacts/build-logs.jsonl
 
# GitHub Actions: set output for downstream install step
echo "apk_url=$(jq -r '.[0].artifacts.buildUrl' build.json)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
```

**When to reach for this:**

* CI needs the **latest green build URL** after `eas build --wait`.
* You are triaging a 40 MB EAS log file for the first `error` line.
* A script must branch on `buildProfile` or `gitCommitHash` from JSON.
* You want portable queries that run on macOS and Linux agents identically.
* PR bots comment with preview build links parsed from `eas build:list`.

## Working Example

**GitHub Actions: wait for EAS, extract APK URL, install on emulator, grep logs on failure.**

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/ci/fetch-latest-apk.sh - run after eas build --wait
set -euo pipefail
 
PLATFORM="${1:-android}"
PROFILE="${2:-preview}"
OUT_JSON="${3:-./eas-last-build.json}"
 
eas build:list \
  --platform "$PLATFORM" \
  --buildProfile "$PROFILE" \
  --status finished \
  --limit 1 \
  --json > "$OUT_JSON"
 
# Fail loudly if no artifact
APK_URL=$(jq -er '.[0].artifacts.buildUrl' "$OUT_JSON")
BUILD_ID=$(jq -er '.[0].id' "$OUT_JSON")
GIT_SHA=$(jq -r '.[0].gitCommitHash // "unknown"' "$OUT_JSON")
 
echo "build_id=$BUILD_ID" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT:-/dev/null}"
echo "apk_url=$APK_URL" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT:-/dev/null}"
echo "git_sha=$GIT_SHA" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT:-/dev/null}"
 
curl -fsSL "$APK_URL" -o ./artifacts/app.apk
adb install -r ./artifacts/app.apk
```

**On failure - download logs and ripgrep:**

```bash
# EAS prints log URL in build JSON when available
LOG_URL=$(jq -r '.[0].logFiles[]? // empty' eas-last-build.json | head -1)
curl -fsSL "$LOG_URL" -o ./artifacts/build.log
 
rg -n --max-count 5 'FAILURE|error:|❌|Gradle failure|pod install' ./artifacts/build.log
jq -r 'select(.level=="error") | .message' ./artifacts/build.jsonl 2>/dev/null || true
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* **`jq -er`** - exit non-zero when field missing; CI fails instead of installing empty URL.
* **`eas build:list` filters** - `platform`, `buildProfile`, `status` narrow to the artifact you intend.
* **`curl -fsSL`** - silent fail on 404 HTML error pages masquerading as artifacts.
* **`rg --max-count`** - first five failure lines without scrolling megabytes.
* **GitHub `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`** - downstream `adb install` or Maestro steps consume parsed fields.

## Deep Dive

### How It Works

* **EAS CLI** can emit **JSON** (`--json`) for `build:list`, `build:view`, `submit:list`, and similar - stable for scripting.
* **`jq`** is a JSON query language - filters run in milliseconds on CI-sized files.
* **`rg`** recursively searches text with sane defaults - faster than `grep -R`, respects `.gitignore`.
* **JSONL** (one JSON object per line) appears in exported telemetry - `jq` reads line-by-line with `-c` or `inputs`.

### EAS build:list Field Map

| jq path | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `.[0].id` | Build UUID for `eas build:view` |
| `.[0].status` | `finished`, `errored`, `canceled`, `in-progress` |
| `.[0].platform` | `ios` or `android` |
| `.[0].buildProfile` | `development`, `preview`, `production` |
| `.[0].gitCommitHash` | Commit EAS built |
| `.[0].artifacts.buildUrl` | Installable artifact (APK/AAB/IPA/simulator) |
| `.[0].applicationArchiveUrl` | Alternate archive link on some profiles |
| `.[0].logFiles[]` | Remote log URLs when present |

```bash
# Pretty-print full latest build
eas build:list --limit 1 --json | jq '.[0]'
 
# Table of last 10 builds
eas build:list --limit 10 --json \
  | jq -r '.[] | [.id[0:8], .platform, .buildProfile, .status, .createdAt] | @tsv'
 
# Find last errored Android production build
eas build:list --platform android --status errored --limit 1 --json \
  | jq '.[0] | {id, error: .error.message}'
```

### jq Patterns for CI

```bash
# Safe default with // operator
jq -r '.[0].artifacts.buildUrl // "none"'
 
# Require field or exit 1
jq -er '.[0].artifacts.buildUrl' build.json > apk.url
 
# Map all artifact URLs (matrix builds)
jq -r '.[] | select(.status=="finished") | .artifacts.buildUrl'
 
# Extract nested Expo config from custom metadata (if your pipeline adds it)
jq -r '.[0].metadata | fromjson? | .updateGroup // empty'
 
# Slurp JSON array from file without stdin pipe
jq -r '.[0].id' < eas-last-build.json
```

### rg Patterns for Logs

```bash
# First Gradle OOM in EAS Android log
rg -m 1 'OutOfMemoryError|Java heap space' artifacts/android-build.log
 
# CocoaPods resolution failure (iOS)
rg -n 'CocoaPods could not find compatible versions|pod install' artifacts/ios-build.log
 
# JSONL: lines containing error level (literal ripgrep)
rg '"level":"error"' artifacts/telemetry.jsonl
 
# Search CI folder but only markdown/json
rg -g '*.{json,jsonl,log}' 'buildProfile' .github/
 
# Context lines around match (like grep -C)
rg -C 3 'Metro bundler' artifacts/expo-start.log
```

### Pipelines: Comment PR with Preview Links

```bash
# After eas build in GitHub Actions
eas build:list --buildProfile preview --status finished --limit 3 --json > previews.json
 
jq -r '
  .[] | "- [\(.platform) \(.buildProfile)](\(.artifacts.buildUrl)) - `\(.gitCommitHash[0:7])`"
' previews.json >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
```

### Bash Notes

```bash
# Install on macOS / Linux CI images
# brew install jq ripgrep   # macOS
# apt-get install -y jq     # Debian; rg from GitHub release or cargo
 
# Validate JSON before jq - catches eas CLI auth errors returned as text
jq empty < eas-last-build.json
 
# Avoid piping curl progress into jq
curl -fsSL "$URL" -o artifact.apk
 
# Large JSONL - stream with jq inputs
jq -c 'select(.level=="error")' < huge.jsonl | head -20
```

## Gotchas

* **Parsing `eas build:list` without `--json`** - human table is not machine-readable. **Fix:** always pass `--json`; pin `eas-cli` version in CI.
* **`jq` on empty array** - `.[0]` is `null`; silent bad deploys. **Fix:** `jq -er '.[0].artifacts.buildUrl'`.
* **Downloading IPA when CI needs APK** - wrong `platform` filter. **Fix:** `--platform android` and verify `buildProfile`.
* **`grep -R node_modules`** - slow and noisy. **Fix:** `rg` with `-g` globs or path limits.
* **Assuming log URL always exists** - older builds may omit `logFiles`. **Fix:** `eas build:view --json` fallback by `id`.
* **Secrets in JSON logs** - `EXPO_TOKEN` echo in debug steps. **Fix:** `rg` artifacts before uploading; mask secrets in CI.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `eas build:view --json` | You already have build UUID | Listing "latest green" across profiles |
| Node `JSON.parse` script | Complex transforms needing npm libs | One-field extraction - `jq` is simpler |
| `jless` / `fx` TUI | Interactive local exploration | GitHub Actions headless runners |
| Expo dashboard UI | Human QA browsing builds | Automated install pipelines |

## FAQs

jq vs python -m json.tool?

* `json.tool` pretty-prints only - no filtering.
* `jq` selects fields, maps arrays, and exits with errors for CI guards.

How do I get JSON for a specific build ID?

* `eas build:view <BUILD_ID> --json`
* Combine with `jq '.artifacts.buildUrl'`

rg not found on GitHub ubuntu-latest?

* `sudo apt-get install -y ripgrep` or `cargo install ripgrep`.
* Many teams add a setup step once per workflow.

Can jq parse eas submit output?

* `eas submit:list --json` - same patterns for submission status and ASC/Play links.

How do I search Metro logs in CI?

* Save Metro output as `metro.log` - `rg 'Bundling|ERROR|Unable to resolve' metro.log`.
* Pair with `npx expo export` failures logged in JSON wrappers.

## Related

* [CLI Basics for RN](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cli/cli-basics-for-rn/) - `eas build:list` and `--json` flags
* [adb & Android Devices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cli/adb-and-android-devices/) - install APK from parsed URL
* [xcrun simctl & iOS Simulators](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cli/xcrun-simctl-and-ios-simulators/) - install simulator `.app` from URL

Dokumen: xcrun simctl & iOS Simulators
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cli/xcrun-simctl-and-ios-simulators/

# xcrun simctl & iOS Simulators

`xcrun simctl` is the **bash-first control plane** for iOS Simulators - boot devices, install dev builds, tail logs, and capture screenshots without living in Xcode. On Expo SDK 57 you still run apps via `npx expo run:ios`; this page covers what to do when Simulator state is wrong, CI needs headless installs, or you need native logs beside Metro.

Highlights / xcrun simctl & iOS Simulators

* xcrun simctl list devices available shows bootable runtimes without opening Simulator.app
* simctl boot + open -a Simulator boots headlessly then brings up the GUI
* simctl install pushes dev-client IPAs and .app bundles without Xcode Run
* simctl io booted screenshot captures CI artifacts and bug reports
* log stream --predicate filters native noise - pair with Metro for JS+native triage
* Simulator is fast for UI; device is truth for push, universal links, and biometrics

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
# List bootable simulators (Apple Silicon: prefer arm64 devices)
xcrun simctl list devices available
 
# Boot + show Simulator.app
DEVICE="iPhone 16 Pro"
xcrun simctl boot "$DEVICE" 2>/dev/null || true
open -a Simulator --args -CurrentDeviceUDID "$(xcrun simctl list devices available | rg "$DEVICE" -m 1 | rg -o '[A-F0-9-]{36}')"
 
# Install a dev build or EAS simulator .app/.tar.gz artifact
xcrun simctl install booted ./build/YourApp.app
 
# Screenshot + logs
xcrun simctl io booted screenshot ./screenshots/home.png
xcrun simctl spawn booted log stream --level debug --predicate 'processImagePath CONTAINS "YourApp"'
```

**When to reach for this:**

* `npx expo run:ios` fails because no simulator is booted.
* You need to install an EAS **simulator build** without recompiling locally.
* QA wants reproducible screenshots for visual regression or App Store attachments.
* Native crash logs never reach the JS redbox - filter Simulator console from the terminal.
* Universal link or deep link smoke tests via `simctl openurl`.

## Working Example

**End-to-end: boot simulator, install EAS dev client, smoke test, capture evidence.**

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
 
APP_NAME="ShopApp"
BUNDLE_ID="com.example.shopapp"
SIM_NAME="iPhone 16 Pro"
ARTIFACT="./ShopApp.app"   # from eas build --profile development --platform ios (simulator)
 
# 1. Resolve UDID
UDID=$(xcrun simctl list devices available -j \
  | jq -r --arg name "$SIM_NAME" '
      .devices | to_entries[].value[] |
      select(.name == $name and .isAvailable == true) | .udid' \
  | head -1)
 
if [[ -z "$UDID" ]]; then
  echo "Simulator not found: $SIM_NAME" >&2
  exit 1
fi
 
# 2. Boot (idempotent) and focus Simulator UI
xcrun simctl boot "$UDID" 2>/dev/null || true
open -a Simulator --args -CurrentDeviceUDID "$UDID"
 
# 3. Clean install dev client
xcrun simctl uninstall "$UDID" "$BUNDLE_ID" 2>/dev/null || true
xcrun simctl install "$UDID" "$ARTIFACT"
 
# 4. Launch without Xcode
xcrun simctl launch "$UDID" "$BUNDLE_ID"
 
# 5. Deep link smoke (universal links still need device for full AASA chain)
xcrun simctl openurl "$UDID" "shopapp://orders/42"
 
# 6. Evidence for PR
mkdir -p ./screenshots
xcrun simctl io "$UDID" screenshot "./screenshots/${APP_NAME}-orders.png"
 
# 7. Tail native logs (Ctrl+C to stop) - run in second terminal
xcrun simctl spawn "$UDID" log stream \
  --style compact \
  --predicate "processImagePath CONTAINS \"$APP_NAME\"" \
  --level debug
```

**Pair with Metro in another terminal:**

```bash
npx expo start --dev-client --clear
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* **JSON device list + `jq`** - stable UDID lookup for scripts (see [jq, rg & JSON Logs](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cli/jq-rg-and-json-logs/)).
* **`simctl install`** - faster iteration when the native shell is unchanged.
* **`simctl openurl`** - route and scheme testing without tapping through UI.
* **`simctl io screenshot`** - PNG artifacts for CI or bug tickets.
* **`log stream --predicate`** - native-only filter; less noise than Console.app.

## Deep Dive

### How It Works

* **`xcrun`** selects the active Xcode toolchain - commands track your `xcode-select` path.
* **`simctl`** talks to `com.apple.CoreSimulator` - each simulator is a VM-like device with its own filesystem and keychain.
* **`booted`** is a magic alias for whichever simulator is currently booted (only one "primary" booted device in simple workflows).
* **Expo** wraps many flows in `npx expo run:ios --simulator "Name"` - `simctl` is the escape hatch when Expo cannot fix state.

### Boot & Lifecycle

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `xcrun simctl list devices available` | Human-readable inventory |
| `xcrun simctl list devices available -j` | JSON for scripting |
| `xcrun simctl boot <UDID>` | Power on device |
| `xcrun simctl shutdown <UDID>` | Power off |
| `xcrun simctl erase <UDID>` | Factory reset - fixes poisoned keychain / caches |
| `open -a Simulator` | GUI - required for some GPU rendering paths |

```bash
# Shutdown all simulators (free RAM before eas build --local)
xcrun simctl shutdown all
 
# Erase stuck Keychain or Associated Domains cache
xcrun simctl erase booted
```

### Install & Launch

```bash
# Install .app bundle (simulator builds only - not device IPA)
xcrun simctl install booted /path/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app
 
# Uninstall by bundle ID (matches app.config ios.bundleIdentifier)
xcrun simctl uninstall booted com.example.myapp
 
# Launch - prints PID
xcrun simctl launch booted com.example.myapp
 
# Terminate
xcrun simctl terminate booted com.example.myapp
```

* **Device IPAs** from `eas build --profile production` cannot install on simulator - use a **simulator** or **development** profile artifact.
* After `npx expo prebuild`, the `.app` path often lives under `ios/build/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/`.

### Logs

```bash
# Compact RN-friendly filter
xcrun simctl spawn booted log stream \
  --style compact \
  --predicate 'subsystem == "com.facebook.react.log" OR processImagePath CONTAINS "MyApp"'
 
# Historical crash reports
xcrun simctl spawn booted log show --last 5m --predicate 'eventType == "logEvent" AND messageType == "error"'
 
# Legacy alias (still works on many setups)
npx react-native log-ios
```

### Screenshots & Video

```bash
# PNG screenshot
xcrun simctl io booted screenshot ~/Desktop/sim-home.png
 
# Record short video (macOS 13+)
xcrun simctl io booted recordVideo ./demo.mov
# Ctrl+C stops recording
 
# Compare screenshots in CI with a known baseline path
mkdir -p artifacts && xcrun simctl io booted screenshot artifacts/ios-tab-bar.png
```

### Permissions & Settings

```bash
# Grant camera/microphone/photos for automated flows
xcrun simctl privacy booted grant camera com.example.myapp
xcrun simctl privacy booted grant photos com.example.myapp
 
# Simulate location
xcrun simctl location booted set 37.7749,-122.4194
 
# Pasteboard (clipboard) for copy/paste E2E
xcrun simctl pbcopy booted "coupon-code-123"
```

### Bash Notes

```bash
# simctl requires Xcode CLT - verify before scripting CI on self-hosted Mac
xcode-select -p
xcrun simctl help
 
# Prefer UDID over device name in scripts - names collide across runtimes
UDID=$(xcrun simctl list devices available -j | jq -r '...')
 
# Apple Silicon: pick arm64 simulator runtimes - x86_64 is slower and breaks some pods
xcrun simctl list devices available | rg "iPhone 16"
```

## Gotchas

* **Installing a device IPA on simulator** - `simctl install` fails with opaque errors. **Fix:** `eas build` with `ios.simulator: true` or local Debug `iphonesimulator` product.
* **No simulator booted** - `booted` alias targets nothing. **Fix:** `xcrun simctl boot <UDID>` before install/screenshot.
* **Assuming simulator proves push or universal links** - APNs and AASA edge cases need hardware. **Fix:** USB device testing - [iOS Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ios-platform/ios-basics-for-rn-devs/).
* **Name-based device selection in CI** - "iPhone 15" string changes with Xcode updates. **Fix:** resolve UDID from JSON; pin Xcode image on CI.
* **`erase booted` during active Metro session** - dev client uninstalled, Keychain cleared. **Fix:** reinstall with `simctl install` or `expo run:ios`.
* **Opening `.xcodeproj` instead of workspace** - unrelated to simctl but pairs with native rebuild pain. **Fix:** `open ios/*.xcworkspace` - see [CocoaPods & Pod Install](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ios-platform/cocoapods-and-pod-install/).

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `npx expo run:ios --simulator` | Daily compile + install + Metro | You already have a fresh `.app` artifact |
| Simulator.app GUI | Visual inspection, accessibility audit | Headless CI - use `simctl` |
| Xcode → Debug → Run | Native breakpoints in `AppDelegate` | Pure JS iteration - stay in Metro |
| Physical device (`expo run:ios --device`) | Push, camera, biometrics, performance truth | Fast UI layout iteration |

## FAQs

How do I list only booted simulators?

* `xcrun simctl list devices booted`
* JSON: `xcrun simctl list devices booted -j`

Can I run simctl on Linux CI?

* No - CoreSimulator is macOS + Xcode only.
* Use EAS macOS workers for iOS simulator builds; run Android on Linux agents.

Where does simctl put app data?

* `~/Library/Developer/CoreSimulator/Devices/<UDID>/data/`
* `erase` wipes this volume - treat it like factory reset.

simctl openurl vs universal links?

* Custom schemes (`myapp://`) work reliably.
* `https://` universal links may open Safari if AASA is not loaded - validate on device before release.

How do I free disk space from old simulators?

* Xcode → Settings → Platforms - delete unused runtimes.
* `xcrun simctl delete unavailable` removes orphaned device pairs.

Dokumen: Prebuild Best Practices
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/best-practices/

# Prebuild Best Practices

A condensed summary of the **25 most important best practices** drawn from every page in CNG & Prebuild - never hand-edit generated files you cannot reproduce.

Highlights / Prebuild Best Practices

* Gitignore ios/ and android/ under CNG - app.config.ts and plugins are source of truth
* SDK 57 expo prebuild cleans by default - encode every native change as a plugin
* Run prebuild twice when authoring plugins - second diff must be empty
* Rebuild dev clients and store binaries when fingerprint or native deps change
* Use npx expo install for native packages - never float versions past the SDK matrix
* EAS Build generates native projects when folders are absent from the upload

1. **Treat CNG as the default on SDK 57:** Maintain `app.config.ts`, config plugins, and `modules/` - not hand-edited `ios/` and `android/` folders.
2. **Gitignore native directories:** Add `ios/` and `android/` to `.gitignore` unless a brownfield ADR explicitly requires committed native projects.
3. **Understand clean regen default:** `npx expo prebuild` deletes existing native folders before generating - pass `--no-clean` only during controlled migration work.
4. **Never edit generated files you cannot reproduce:** If a change is not in config or a plugin, it will be lost on the next clean prebuild.
5. **Express permissions in plugins:** `NSCameraUsageDescription`, Android permissions, and entitlements belong in the `plugins` array - not post-prebuild Xcode edits.
6. **Write idempotent config plugins:** Running prebuild twice must not duplicate manifest entries or Gradle `apply` lines - existence checks before every add.
7. **Document plugin order in `app.config.ts`:** Multiple plugins touching the same native file depend on execution order - comment the rationale.
8. **Prefer library config plugins:** `expo-camera`, `expo-notifications`, and Expo modules ship maintained SDK 57 plugins - do not reinvent them.
9. **Use `npx expo install` for native dependencies:** Manual `npm install` can pull JS versions incompatible with SDK 57 native binaries.
10. **Run `expo-doctor` before prebuild:** Catch invalid config and version skew before wasting a compile cycle on EAS or locally.
11. **Use `npx expo config --type introspect` while developing plugins:** Inspect mod results without full native generation on every save.
12. **Port brownfield native diffs to plugins before cutover:** Inventory every Xcode/Gradle change vs fresh prebuild - spreadsheet with owners per row.
13. **Commit `modules/` for custom native code:** Local Expo modules are source of truth; generated `ios/MyApp/` is ephemeral under CNG.
14. **Use `expo run:ios` / `expo run:android` for local native iteration:** Wraps prebuild + compile - rebuild after Swift/Kotlin changes; Fast Refresh does not update native code.
15. **Rebuild dev clients after SDK bumps:** `expo-dev-client` embeds native runtime - OTA cannot upgrade it after an SDK or native dependency change.
16. **Delete stale native folders on upgrade:** After `npx expo install --fix` on a new SDK, `rm -rf ios android` before prebuild - old templates target the previous RN version.
17. **Upgrade SDKs sequentially:** One SDK per PR - prebuild templates and plugin APIs change per release; skipping versions compounds pain.
18. **Commit lockfiles with every native-affecting change:** CI, EAS, and fingerprint hashes must resolve the same dependency tree as local dev.
19. **Adopt fingerprint gates in CI:** `@expo/fingerprint` detects when a new native build is required - do not ship OTA to incompatible binaries.
20. **Use `runtimeVersion.policy: "fingerprint"` for CNG OTA:** Ties update eligibility to native inputs, not semver alone when plugins change between store releases.
21. **Let EAS Build run prebuild in CI:** Upload config + JS - not generated native folders - unless brownfield migration is incomplete.
22. **Map `eas.json` profiles to environments:** `development`, `preview`, and `production` must align credentials and env vars with fingerprint and build jobs.
23. **Physical device smoke test after plugin merges:** Simulators miss push entitlements, App Links, and signing issues that prebuild alone cannot catch.
24. **Pair native work with Native Module Rules:** Search Expo SDK packages and config plugins before writing Swift/Kotlin - custom modules need ADRs and owners.
25. **Schedule brownfield CNG migration before the next major SDK:** Manual native merge cost grows every release - cut over when audit spreadsheet is complete and clean prebuild passes.

## FAQs

Should we commit ios/ and android/?

* **No** for standard CNG SDK 57 apps - EAS Build regenerates them.
* **Yes** only with a brownfield ADR and a dated migration plan to plugins + gitignore.

When is --no-clean appropriate?

* Porting hand edits into a config plugin during brownfield migration.
* Never on SDK upgrade branches or CI validation gates - use default clean regen.

How do we know OTA is safe after a merge?

* Fingerprint unchanged since last store binary → JS-only fixes may use `eas update`.
* Fingerprint changed → new `eas build` for production and development clients.

What is the fastest prebuild validation loop?

1. Edit plugin or `app.config.ts`
2. `npx expo config --type introspect`
3. `npx expo prebuild --no-install` twice - zero diff on second run
4. `expo run:ios` or EAS development build for device proof

Does Expo Go replace prebuild for custom native code?

* No - Expo Go uses a fixed binary and ignores your plugins' entitlements.
* Custom native code requires prebuild + dev client - see [Custom Native Code in CNG](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/custom-native-code-in-cng/).

Dokumen: Config Plugins in CNG
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/config-plugins-in-cng/

# Config Plugins in CNG

Composable native changes that survive **`expo prebuild --clean`** (the SDK 57 default). Config plugins encode permissions, entitlements, Gradle dependencies, and manifest entries in version-controlled TypeScript - not hand-edited Xcode clicks.

Highlights / Config Plugins in CNG

* Config plugins mutate ios/ and android/ at prebuild time - not at Metro runtime
* Compose small plugins; chain with withPlugins from @expo/config-plugins
* Idempotent plugins produce zero diff on the second prebuild run
* Library plugins (expo-camera, etc.) ship with maintained SDK 57 support
* Plugin order matters when multiple mods touch Info.plist or build.gradle
* Pair with Native Module Rules before adding custom native patches

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
npx expo install @expo/config-plugins
mkdir -p plugins
```

```ts
// plugins/withMyFeature.ts
import {
  ConfigPlugin,
  withInfoPlist,
  withAndroidManifest,
  AndroidConfig,
} from "expo/config-plugins";
 
const withMyFeature: ConfigPlugin = (config) => {
  config = withInfoPlist(config, (cfg) => {
    cfg.modResults.NSMyFeatureUsageDescription =
      "Allow $(PRODUCT_NAME) to use My Feature.";
    return cfg;
  });
 
  config = withAndroidManifest(config, (cfg) => {
    const main = AndroidConfig.Manifest.getMainApplicationOrThrow(cfg.modResults);
    AndroidConfig.Manifest.addMetaDataItemToMainApplication(
      main,
      "com.example.MY_FEATURE_ENABLED",
      "true"
    );
    return cfg;
  });
 
  return config;
};
 
export default withMyFeature;
```

```ts
// app.config.ts
import type { ExpoConfig } from "expo/config";
import withMyFeature from "./plugins/withMyFeature";
 
const config: ExpoConfig = {
  name: "MyApp",
  slug: "my-app",
  plugins: [
    "expo-router",
    withMyFeature,
    [
      "expo-build-properties",
      { ios: { deploymentTarget: "15.1" } },
    ],
  ],
};
 
export default config;
```

```bash
npx expo prebuild --no-install
npx expo prebuild --no-install   # second run: git diff ios android must be empty
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Adding iOS usage descriptions or Android permissions
* Wiring third-party SDK keys into `Info.plist` / `AndroidManifest.xml`
* Adjusting Gradle `minSdkVersion`, iOS deployment target, or ProGuard rules
* Porting brownfield native edits into reproducible CNG

## Working Example

A composable plugin stack for an app that needs camera access, a custom URL scheme, and a shared deployment target - typical SDK 57 production setup.

```ts
// plugins/withAppLinks.ts
import { ConfigPlugin, withEntitlementsPlist } from "expo/config-plugins";
 
const withAppLinks: ConfigPlugin<{ domain: string }> = (config, { domain }) => {
  return withEntitlementsPlist(config, (cfg) => {
    const key = "com.apple.developer.associated-domains";
    const existing = (cfg.modResults[key] as string[] | undefined) ?? [];
    const entry = `applinks:${domain}`;
    if (!existing.includes(entry)) {
      cfg.modResults[key] = [...existing, entry];
    }
    return cfg;
  });
};
 
export default withAppLinks;
```

```ts
// app.config.ts
import type { ExpoConfig } from "expo/config";
import withAppLinks from "./plugins/withAppLinks";
 
const config: ExpoConfig = {
  name: "Shop",
  slug: "shop",
  scheme: "shop",
  ios: {
    bundleIdentifier: "com.example.shop",
  },
  android: {
    package: "com.example.shop",
  },
  plugins: [
    [
      "expo-camera",
      {
        cameraPermission: "Scan product barcodes in the store.",
      },
    ],
    [withAppLinks, { domain: "shop.example.com" }],
    [
      "expo-build-properties",
      {
        ios: { deploymentTarget: "15.1" },
        android: { minSdkVersion: 24 },
      },
    ],
  ],
};
 
export default config;
```

```bash
# Validate plugin output without full compile
npx expo config --type introspect
 
# Generate and verify idempotency
rm -rf ios android
npx expo prebuild --no-install
npx expo prebuild --no-install
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* **Library plugin first** - `expo-camera` owns camera permission strings
* **Parameterized custom plugin** - `withAppLinks` accepts `domain` and deduplicates entitlements
* **Build properties last** - `expo-build-properties` adjusts toolchain versions after feature plugins
* **Idempotency** - associated domain is appended only if missing

## Deep Dive

### How Config Plugins Work

```
app.config.ts  →  expo prebuild  →  @expo/prebuild-config  →  config plugins (mods)  →  ios/ android/
```

1. **Evaluation:** Expo loads `app.config.ts` and resolves the `plugins` array (strings, tuples, or functions).
2. **Mod pipeline:** Each plugin receives `ExpoConfig` and returns modified config via `with*` helpers (`withInfoPlist`, `withGradleProperties`, etc.).
3. **Template merge:** SDK 57 template files are copied, then mods apply in plugin order.
4. **Clean regen:** Default prebuild deletes folders first - only plugin-encoded changes persist.

### Composition Patterns

| Pattern | Use When |
| --- | --- |
| String plugin `"expo-router"` | Library ships a zero-config plugin |
| Tuple `["expo-camera", { ... }]` | Library plugin needs options |
| Function `withMyFeature` | Custom native mutation |
| Tuple + function `[withAppLinks, { domain }]` | Custom plugin with parameters |
| `withPlugins(config, [a, b, c])` | Group related mods in one file |

```ts
// plugins/index.ts - compose related mods
import { ConfigPlugin, withPlugins } from "expo/config-plugins";
import withAppLinks from "./withAppLinks";
import withPushEnvironment from "./withPushEnvironment";
 
const withNativeStack: ConfigPlugin = (config) =>
  withPlugins(config, [
    [withAppLinks, { domain: "shop.example.com" }],
    [withPushEnvironment, { env: "production" }],
  ]);
 
export default withNativeStack;
```

### Plugin Order Rules

* Plugins that **create base structure** run before plugins that **patch the same file**
* **Entitlements** before features that depend on them
* **`expo-build-properties`** often runs late - deployment target affects other pods
* When debugging, **bisect** the `plugins` array - remove half until prebuild succeeds

### Idempotency Checklist

| Anti-pattern | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| Append same XML every run | Check if node exists before `add` |
| Duplicate `NSCameraUsageDescription` keys | Merge into existing key or use library plugin |
| Regex replace without anchor | Use structured mods (`withInfoPlist`) not text files |
| Global Gradle `apply plugin` twice | Guard with `if (!contents.includes(...))` |

### Debugging

```bash
# See resolved mods without writing ios/android
npx expo config --type introspect
 
# Diff after plugin change
rm -rf ios android && npx expo prebuild --no-install
git diff ios   # if tracked; CNG teams inspect in IDE
 
# Doctor catches invalid plugin config
npx expo-doctor
```

## Gotchas

* **Editing `ios/` after prebuild** - SDK 57 clean default wipes changes. **Fix:** Encode in a plugin.
* **Wrong plugin order** - Later plugin overwrites earlier `Info.plist` key. **Fix:** Document order; use introspect.
* **Non-idempotent append** - Second prebuild duplicates manifest entries. **Fix:** Existence check before add.
* **`npm install` for plugin packages** - Version skew vs SDK 57 native binaries. **Fix:** `npx expo install`.
* **Testing only in Expo Go** - Plugins affecting entitlements need dev client rebuild. **Fix:** `expo run:ios` after plugin merge.
* **Importing from wrong path** - Use `expo/config-plugins` in app plugins; libraries use `@expo/config-plugins` per package docs.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Config plugin (recommended) | Any repeatable native change under CNG | One-off local experiment with no production path |
| Library built-in plugin | Package documents `plugins` entry | Library has no SDK 57 plugin - fork or ADR |
| `expo-build-properties` | SDK versions, ProGuard, deployment target | Complex manifest XML - write a custom plugin |
| Committed native folders (brownfield) | Legacy app with no plugin migration path | Greenfield SDK 57 apps - use CNG |
| `patch-package` on generated files | Emergency hotfix with ADR | Standard workflow - patches lost on clean prebuild |

## FAQs

Where do config plugins run?

At **prebuild time** on the machine running `expo prebuild` or EAS Build - not on every Metro reload. Rebuild native binaries after plugin changes that affect entitlements or native deps.

Can I use config plugins without committing ios/?

Yes - that is the CNG default. Plugins are the source of truth; native folders are ephemeral output.

How do I test a plugin without a full compile?

`npx expo config --type introspect` shows mod results. For final validation, run prebuild twice and confirm zero diff.

What is the difference between app.config plugins and native-modules config-plugins page?

This page focuses on **CNG workflow** - composition, idempotency, and prebuild survival. [../native-modules/config-plugins/config-plugins.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/native-modules/config-plugins/) covers the API surface for module authors.

## Related

* [Prebuild Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/prebuild-basics/) - what prebuild generates
* [expo prebuild Workflow](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/expo-prebuild-workflow/) - clean regen and local iteration checklist
* [../native-modules/config-plugins/config-plugins.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/native-modules/config-plugins/) - plugin API for native module authors
* [../native-modules/patching-native-projects/patching-native-projects.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/native-modules/patching-native-projects/) - when patches are unavoidable
