Dokumen: Custom Native Code in CNG
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/custom-native-code-in-cng/

# Custom Native Code in CNG

Local **`expo run:ios`** / **`expo run:android`** loops and the decision of **when to commit `ios/` and `android/`** in a Continuous Native Generation workflow. Custom native code belongs in `modules/`, config plugins, and EAS Build - not silent Xcode edits that vanish on clean prebuild.

Highlights / Custom Native Code in CNG

* expo run:ios and expo run:android run prebuild then compile locally
* Custom Expo modules live in modules/ and autolink via expo-modules-autolinking
* Default CNG: gitignore ios/ and android/ - commit modules/ and plugins/
* Commit native dirs only with ADR when CNG migration is blocked
* Rebuild dev client after every native code or SDK change
* Pair with create-expo-module before writing raw Swift/Kotlin patches

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
npx create-expo-app@latest CustomNative --template blank-typescript@sdk-57 --yes
cd CustomNative
npx expo install expo-dev-client expo-modules-core
```

```bash
# Scaffold a local Expo module (preferred over raw bridge code)
npx create-expo-module@latest expo-device-info-plus
# Move into modules/ if the CLI created a sibling folder
```

```text
CustomNative/
├── app.config.ts
├── modules/
│   └── expo-device-info-plus/   # Commit this - source of truth
├── plugins/                     # Commit custom config plugins
├── ios/                         # Gitignore under CNG
└── android/                     # Gitignore under CNG
```

```json
// package.json scripts
{
  "scripts": {
    "ios": "expo run:ios",
    "android": "expo run:android",
    "prebuild": "expo prebuild"
  }
}
```

```bash
npx expo run:ios
# or
npx expo run:android --device
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Debugging a custom Expo module on a physical device
* Iterating on Swift/Kotlin before publishing a module
* Validating autolinking after adding `modules/my-feature/`
* Deciding whether brownfield native folders must stay committed

## Working Example

An app with a local Expo module, a dev client, and CNG gitignore - the standard SDK 57 custom native loop.

```ts
// app.config.ts
import type { ExpoConfig } from "expo/config";
 
const config: ExpoConfig = {
  name: "CustomNative",
  slug: "custom-native",
  ios: { bundleIdentifier: "com.example.customnative" },
  android: { package: "com.example.customnative" },
  plugins: ["expo-dev-client"],
};
 
export default config;
```

```gitignore
# .gitignore - CNG default
ios/
android/
.expo/
```

```tsx
// App.tsx
import * as DeviceInfoPlus from "expo-device-info-plus";
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { Text, View } from "react-native";
 
export default function App() {
  const [model, setModel] = useState<string>("…");
 
  useEffect(() => {
    DeviceInfoPlus.getModelAsync().then(setModel);
  }, []);
 
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1, justifyContent: "center", alignItems: "center" }}>
      <Text>Device model: {model}</Text>
    </View>
  );
}
```

```bash
# First native compile on a fresh clone
npm install
npx expo run:ios
 
# After changing Swift/Kotlin in modules/
npx expo run:ios --no-build-cache
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* **`modules/` is committed** - native source survives clean prebuild
* **`ios/`/`android/` are generated** - recreated from config + autolinking on each prebuild
* **`expo run:ios`** orchestrates prebuild → pod install → Xcode build
* **Module changes require recompile** - Fast Refresh does not reload native code

## Deep Dive

### The Local Native Loop

```
Edit modules/*.swift or *.kt  →  expo run:<platform>  →  prebuild (if needed)  →  compile  →  device test
```

| Step | Command | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Generate native projects | `npx expo prebuild` | SDK 57 cleans by default |
| iOS compile + install | `npx expo run:ios` | Requires Xcode |
| Android compile + install | `npx expo run:android` | Requires Android SDK |
| Skip prebuild if folders exist | `expo run:ios --no-bundler` | Variants exist - see `expo run:ios --help` |
| Cloud compile | `eas build --profile development` | No local Xcode |

### What to Commit vs Gitignore

| Path | CNG default | Commit when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `app.config.ts` | ✅ Commit | Always |
| `plugins/` | ✅ Commit | Always |
| `modules/` | ✅ Commit | Custom Expo modules |
| `ios/` | ❌ Gitignore | Brownfield ADR - manual native maintenance |
| `android/` | ❌ Gitignore | Brownfield ADR - manual native maintenance |
| `patches/` (patch-package) | ⚠️ ADR | Last resort - prefer plugins |

### Integration Paths (Prefer Top to Bottom)

1. **Expo SDK package** - `npx expo install expo-*` with built-in plugin
2. **Community package + config plugin** - verify RN 0.86 / New Architecture support
3. **Local Expo module** - `npx create-expo-module@latest` in `modules/`
4. **Config plugin patch** - for thin native manifest/Gradle changes
5. **Committed native dirs** - brownfield only, with migration plan to CNG

See [Native Module Rules](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/native-module-rules/) Tier 1 for the decision tree.

### Autolinking After Prebuild

`expo-modules-autolinking` discovers:

* npm dependencies with `expo-module.config.json`
* Local `modules/*` folders
* Config plugin registrations

```bash
npx expo prebuild --no-install
# Verify Podfile contains expo autolinking script
# Verify android/settings.gradle includes useExpoModules()
```

Missing autolinking manifests as **undefined native module** at runtime - not a Metro error.

### When to Commit Native Directories

Commit `ios/` and `android/` **only** when:

* A **brownfield** app has native code that cannot yet be expressed as plugins
* An **ADR** names the owner, upgrade process, and CNG migration milestone
* **CI** runs `expo prebuild --check` or fingerprint diff to detect drift

Do **not** commit native dirs when:

* Starting a greenfield SDK 57 app
* All native changes live in plugins and `modules/`
* EAS Build generates native projects in CI ([CNG in CI](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/cng-in-ci/))

### Hybrid Migration Pattern

```bash
# 1. Inventory Xcode/Gradle diffs vs fresh prebuild
rm -rf ios android
npx expo prebuild --no-install
git diff  # against old committed ios/
 
# 2. Port each diff hunk to a config plugin or modules/ change
 
# 3. Final gate: clean prebuild matches behavior
rm -rf ios android && npx expo prebuild
```

Full runbook: [Migrating Manual Native Projects to CNG](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/migrating-manual-native-projects-to-cng/).

## Gotchas

* **Editing generated `AppDelegate` without a plugin** - Lost on SDK 57 clean prebuild. **Fix:** `expo-dev-client` plugin or custom config plugin.
* **Expecting Expo Go to load custom modules** - Expo Go binary is fixed. **Fix:** Dev client via `expo run:ios` or EAS development build.
* **Forgetting rebuild after Swift change** - Metro Fast Refresh only updates JS. **Fix:** Re-run `expo run:ios`.
* **Two copies of react-native in monorepo** - Autolinking picks wrong instance. **Fix:** `npx expo-doctor`, single hoisted `react-native`.
* **Committing `ios/Pods/`** - Massive repo bloat and merge conflicts. **Fix:** Gitignore Pods; `pod install` in CI/EAS.
* **Mixing CNG and hand-edited Gradle** - Prebuild overwrites unencoded edits. **Fix:** `expo-build-properties` or custom plugin.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Local `expo run:*` loop | Daily module development with Xcode/Android Studio | Team has no local toolchains - use EAS development builds |
| EAS development profile | Engineers without Macs; consistent CI binaries | You need sub-minute native iteration - local is faster |
| Committed native dirs | Brownfield blocked on plugin migration | Greenfield CNG apps |
| Published private npm module | Reuse native code across multiple apps | Single-app module - keep in `modules/` |
| Raw React Native TurboModule | Expo Modules API insufficient (rare) | Before trying `create-expo-module` |

## FAQs

Does expo run:ios always run prebuild?

If `ios/` is missing, yes. If `ios/` exists, it uses the existing project - which may be stale. After config plugin changes, run `npx expo prebuild` or delete `ios/` first.

Where should custom Swift code live?

In `modules/<module-name>/ios/` as an Expo module - autolinking wires it on prebuild. Avoid editing generated `ios/MyApp/` directly under CNG.

Can I use Xcode to debug then move changes to a plugin?

Yes - common brownfield migration path. Use `expo prebuild --no-clean` while iterating, then verify clean prebuild reproduces the behavior.

How do third-party native libraries fit CNG?

Install with `npx expo install`, add their config plugin to `app.config.ts`, run prebuild. See [../native-modules/using-third-party-native-libraries/using-third-party-native-libraries.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/native-modules/using-third-party-native-libraries/).

Dokumen: expo prebuild Workflow
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/expo-prebuild-workflow/

# expo prebuild Workflow

Operational checklist for **`npx expo prebuild`** on Expo SDK 57 - clean regeneration defaults, when to pass `--no-clean`, and how to iterate locally without corrupting native projects. Use this before SDK upgrades, config plugin PRs, and first-time dev-client setup.

Highlights / expo prebuild Workflow

* SDK 57 defaults to clean regen - expo prebuild deletes ios/ and android/ first
* Use --no-clean only when migrating hand edits into config plugins
* Run prebuild twice when authoring plugins - second diff must be empty
* expo run:ios/android wraps prebuild + compile for local native iteration
* Pair with expo-doctor before every prebuild on upgrade branches
* Gitignore native folders under CNG - EAS Build runs the same prebuild step

## How to Use This Checklist

* Run **Tier 1** before every SDK upgrade or fresh clone - stale `ios/`/`android/` from an older SDK block RN 0.86 templates.
* Apply **Tier 2** when authoring or reviewing config plugins - non-idempotent plugins destroy native projects on the second run.
* Use **Tier 3** for day-to-day local iteration with `expo run:ios` / `expo run:android`.
* Record brownfield exceptions (committed native dirs) in `docs/adr/` - CNG is the default path on SDK 57.
* Pair with [Native Module Rules](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/native-module-rules/) when adding packages with native code.

---

## Tier 1: Clean Regen & SDK 57 Defaults (1–6)

1. **Understand SDK 57 clean default:** `npx expo prebuild` **removes** existing `ios/` and `android/` before generating fresh projects.

   * **Opt out:** `npx expo prebuild --no-clean` layers template updates onto existing folders.
   * **After SDK bump:** Always use default clean - never `--no-clean` on upgrade branches.
2. **Delete stale native folders before upgrade prebuild:** Committed `ios/` from SDK 56 targets RN 0.85 Hermes and Pod versions.

   * **CNG pattern:** `rm -rf ios android` then `npx expo prebuild`.
   * **Verify:** `package.json` shows `expo` ~57.0.4 and `react-native` 0.86.0.
3. **Run expo-doctor before prebuild:** Invalid `app.config.ts` fields fail late - doctor catches schema drift early.

   * **Gate:** `npx expo-doctor` exits zero before `expo prebuild` in upgrade scripts.
   * **Fix:** `npx expo install --fix` when doctor reports version skew.
4. **Gitignore native dirs under CNG:** Standard teams do not commit `ios/` and `android/`.

   * **`.gitignore`:** Add `ios/` and `android/` at app root.
   * **Reject:** "Quick fix" Xcode edits that are not encoded in config plugins.
5. **Use `--no-install` for CI diff checks:** Skips `pod install` and Gradle sync - faster validation of plugin output.

   * **Local full build:** Omit `--no-install` when you need to compile immediately after prebuild.
   * **EAS Build:** Cloud builders run install steps automatically.
6. **Platform-scoped prebuild when iterating:** `--platform ios` or `--platform android` saves time on single-platform plugin work.

   * **Full release:** Run both platforms before merging plugin changes that touch shared config.
   * **Reject:** Merging iOS-only tested plugins without Android prebuild verification.

---

## Tier 2: Config Plugins & Idempotency (7–12)

7. **Express native changes as plugins:** Permissions, entitlements, Gradle dependencies, and manifest entries belong in `app.config.ts` `plugins` array.

   * **Inspect:** `npx expo config --type introspect` before full prebuild.
   * **Deep dive:** [Config Plugins in CNG](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/config-plugins-in-cng/).
8. **Run prebuild twice for every new plugin:** Second run must produce **zero diff** in native output.

   * **Test:** `npx expo prebuild && npx expo prebuild` - `git diff ios android` empty on second pass.
   * **Reject:** Regex-append plugins without existence checks.
9. **Document plugin order in comments:** Multiple plugins touching `Info.plist` or `build.gradle` depend on execution order.

   * **Pattern:** Base entitlements first, feature plugins second, custom patch plugin last.
   * **Debug:** Bisect by removing plugins one at a time when prebuild fails.
10. **Prefer library plugins over hand edits:** `expo-camera`, `expo-notifications`, and most Expo modules ship maintained plugins.

    * **Install:** `npx expo install <package>` - not `npm install @latest`.
    * **Reference:** [../native-modules/config-plugins/config-plugins.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/native-modules/config-plugins/).
11. **Migrate hand edits with `--no-clean` temporarily:** When porting brownfield Xcode changes, use `--no-clean` while developing the plugin, then verify with full clean.

    * **Done when:** Clean prebuild reproduces the same native behavior as the hand edit.
    * **Delete:** Temporary native patches once the plugin lands.
12. **Never edit generated files you cannot reproduce:** If a change is not in config or a plugin, it will be lost on clean prebuild.

    * **ADR required:** Any committed native file outside CNG must document the owner and upgrade path.
    * **Pair:** [../expo-rules/native-module-rules/native-module-rules.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/native-module-rules/) Tier 2.

---

## Tier 3: Local Iteration Loops (13–18)

13. **`expo run:ios` wraps prebuild + compile:** Generates `ios/` if missing, runs `pod install`, opens Xcode build.

    * **Script:** `"ios:native": "expo run:ios"` in `package.json`.
    * **Requires:** Xcode and CocoaPods for local iOS builds.
14. **`expo run:android` wraps prebuild + Gradle:** Same flow for Android - generates `android/` if absent.

    * **Device:** `expo run:android --device` for physical hardware testing.
    * **Emulator:** Ensure `ANDROID_HOME` and SDK platforms are installed.
15. **Rebuild dev client after native dependency changes:** `expo-dev-client` embeds native code - Metro reload is not enough.

    * **Trigger:** New native npm package, SDK bump, or plugin changing entitlements.
    * **OTA cannot replace:** `eas update` ships JS only within the same runtime.
16. **Clear Metro cache after prebuild config changes:** Stale caches mask autolinking and config resolution issues.

    * **Command:** `npx expo start --clear` after adding native modules.
    * **Nuclear:** `rm -rf node_modules/.cache` on stubborn bundler errors.
17. **Use `npx expo config` to debug without writing files:** Faster than full prebuild when validating env variants.

    * **Public manifest:** `npx expo config --type public` before store submission.
    * **Introspect:** See mod results plugins will apply.
18. **Physical device smoke test after prebuild:** Simulators do not catch entitlement, push, or App Links issues.

    * **Matrix:** One iOS device + one Android device minimum after plugin PRs.
    * **CI complement:** EAS `development` profile builds for teammates without Xcode.

---

## Tier 4: Upgrade & Release Gates (19–24)

19. **Sequential SDK upgrades:** Step one SDK at a time - prebuild templates change per SDK.

    * **Sequence:** `expo install expo@^<sdk>` → `--fix` → `expo-doctor` → delete native dirs → prebuild.
    * **Reference:** [../expo-platform/upgrading-expo-sdk-versions/upgrading-expo-sdk-versions.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-platform/upgrading-expo-sdk-versions/).
20. **Commit lockfiles with prebuild-related dep changes:** `expo install --fix` updates `package-lock.json` - CI must resolve the same tree.

    * **Reject:** Upgrade PRs that change `package.json` without lockfile.
    * **Check:** `npx expo install --check` in weekly hygiene scripts.
21. **EAS Build runs prebuild when native dirs are absent:** Upload without `ios/`/`android/` - cloud builder generates them.

    * **Local optional:** Teams without Xcode rely entirely on EAS for native compile.
    * **Deep dive:** [CNG in CI](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/cng-in-ci/).
22. **Fingerprint native changes for OTA/runtime version:** When native fingerprint changes, OTA updates must target a new runtime.

    * **Tool:** `@expo/fingerprint` - see [Fingerprint & Native Change Detection](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/fingerprint-and-native-change-detection/).
    * **Reject:** Shipping OTA to binaries built before a native plugin merge.
23. **New Architecture alignment:** SDK 57 prebuild templates enable New Architecture by default on RN 0.86.

    * **Verify:** Third-party native libs support TurboModules/Fabric before merging.
    * **Escape hatch:** `newArchEnabled: false` requires ADR and rebuild.
24. **Store release after native-affecting merges:** Production `eas build` must run on the same commit that passed local/EAS prebuild.

    * **Reject:** Merging plugin PRs without a green development build on CI.
    * **Rollback:** Single-purpose native PRs map cleanly to store version rollback.

---

## Tier 5: Brownfield & Migration (25–28)

25. **Inventory hand-maintained native diffs before CNG adoption:** List every Xcode and Gradle change not in config.

    * **Output:** Spreadsheet mapping file → config plugin or ADR exception.
    * **Runbook:** [Migrating Manual Native Projects to CNG](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/migrating-manual-native-projects-to-cng/).
26. **Use `--no-clean` only during migration, not in CI:** CI must prove clean prebuild is reproducible.

    * **Final gate:** `rm -rf ios android && npx expo prebuild` passes on migration branch.
    * **Done when:** Native dirs gitignored and clean prebuild is the only path.
27. **Autolinking verification after migration:** `expo-modules-autolinking` must appear in generated Podfile and `settings.gradle`.

    * **Fix:** `npx expo prebuild --clean` if autolinking entries are missing.
    * **Reference:** [../native-modules/autolinking-and-expo-modules-core/autolinking-and-expo-modules-core.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/native-modules/autolinking-and-expo-modules-core/).
28. **Document who owns native regressions post-CNG:** Platform engineer or mobile lead reviews plugin PRs.

    * **CODEOWNERS:** `app.config.ts`, `plugins/`, and any `modules/` native code.
    * **Onboarding:** README states CNG workflow - no silent Xcode edits.

---

## FAQs

When should I use --no-clean?

* Iterating on a config plugin while porting a brownfield native edit.
* Debugging incremental template updates without full delete/regen.
* **Never** on SDK upgrade branches or CI validation - use default clean.

Does expo prebuild run automatically on EAS Build?

* Yes, when `ios/` and `android/` are not uploaded or are gitignored.
* EAS runs the same config evaluation and plugin pipeline as local prebuild.

What is the fastest local native iteration loop?

1. Edit `app.config.ts` or plugin
2. `npx expo prebuild --platform <ios|android>`
3. `npx expo run:<platform>`
4. Repeat - use `--no-install` on prebuild only when skipping compile

Can I skip prebuild if I use Expo Go?

* Expo Go uses a fixed native binary - it ignores your config plugins for native entitlements.
* Custom native code requires prebuild + dev client - Expo Go is not a production test target.

# CNG & Prebuild Highlights Summary

Every highlight bullet from the 8 pages in this section, gathered on one page and grouped by the page it came from.

Highlights / CNG & Prebuild Highlights Summary

* CNG (Continuous Native Generation) turns app.config.ts + plugins into ios/ and android/
* SDK 57 defaults to clean regen - expo prebuild deletes ios/ and android/ first
* Config plugins mutate ios/ and android/ at prebuild time - not at Metro runtime
* expo run:ios and expo run:android run prebuild then compile locally
* @expo/fingerprint hashes everything that affects native binaries
* Inventory every ios/ and android/ diff vs a fresh SDK 57 prebuild

## [Prebuild Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/prebuild-basics/)

* CNG (Continuous Native Generation) turns app.config.ts + plugins into ios/ and android/
* SDK 57 runs expo prebuild with --clean by default - stale native folders are deleted first
* Gitignore ios/ and android/ under CNG; regenerate on EAS Build or local prebuild
* Every native permission, entitlement, and manifest entry should flow from config plugins
* expo run:ios and expo run:android invoke prebuild then compile a dev client locally
* Pair with Native Module Rules before adding packages that touch native code

## [expo prebuild Workflow](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/expo-prebuild-workflow/)

* SDK 57 defaults to clean regen - expo prebuild deletes ios/ and android/ first
* Use --no-clean only when migrating hand edits into config plugins
* Run prebuild twice when authoring plugins - second diff must be empty
* expo run:ios/android wraps prebuild + compile for local native iteration
* Pair with expo-doctor before every prebuild on upgrade branches
* Gitignore native folders under CNG - EAS Build runs the same prebuild step

## [Config Plugins in CNG](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/config-plugins-in-cng/)

* Config plugins mutate ios/ and android/ at prebuild time - not at Metro runtime
* Compose small plugins; chain with withPlugins from @expo/config-plugins
* Idempotent plugins produce zero diff on the second prebuild run
* Library plugins (expo-camera, etc.) ship with maintained SDK 57 support
* Plugin order matters when multiple mods touch Info.plist or build.gradle
* Pair with Native Module Rules before adding custom native patches

## [Custom Native Code in CNG](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/custom-native-code-in-cng/)

* expo run:ios and expo run:android run prebuild then compile locally
* Custom Expo modules live in modules/ and autolink via expo-modules-autolinking
* Default CNG: gitignore ios/ and android/ - commit modules/ and plugins/
* Commit native dirs only with ADR when CNG migration is blocked
* Rebuild dev client after every native code or SDK change
* Pair with create-expo-module before writing raw Swift/Kotlin patches

## [Fingerprint & Native Change Detection](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/fingerprint-and-native-change-detection/)

* @expo/fingerprint hashes everything that affects native binaries
* Runtime version policies can fingerprint instead of appVersion alone
* CI fingerprint diff gates catch accidental native drift before merge
* OTA updates must target binaries built with the same runtime fingerprint
* Pair fingerprint checks with CNG - generated ios/ is not the source of truth
* EAS Workflows can run fingerprint jobs per environment

## [Migrating Manual Native Projects to CNG](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/migrating-manual-native-projects-to-cng/)

* Inventory every ios/ and android/ diff vs a fresh SDK 57 prebuild
* Port hand edits to config plugins and modules/ before deleting committed native dirs
* Run expo prebuild --clean as the final migration gate
* Sequential SDK upgrade before CNG cutover reduces simultaneous variables
* ADR documents brownfield exceptions until full CNG parity
* Pair with Native Module Rules for third-party native library audit

## [CNG in CI](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/cng-in-ci/)

* EAS Build runs expo prebuild when ios/ and android/ are absent
* CNG CI uploads JS + config - not generated native folders
* Brownfield CI may diff committed native dirs against prebuild output
* Fingerprint jobs gate OTA vs native rebuild decisions in PRs
* eas.json profiles must match EAS environment for credential resolution
* Lockfiles and app.config.ts are the reproducible inputs - not ios/Pods

## [Prebuild Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/best-practices/)

* Gitignore ios/ and android/ under CNG - app.config.ts and plugins are source of truth
* SDK 57 expo prebuild cleans by default - encode every native change as a plugin
* Run prebuild twice when authoring plugins - second diff must be empty
* Rebuild dev clients and store binaries when fingerprint or native deps change
* Use npx expo install for native packages - never float versions past the SDK matrix
* EAS Build generates native projects when folders are absent from the upload

Dokumen: Prebuild Basics
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/prebuild-basics/

# Prebuild Basics

Ten examples for generating `ios/` and `android/` from **Expo config** without manual drift - the foundation of Continuous Native Generation (CNG) on Expo SDK 57 and React Native 0.86.

Highlights / Prebuild Basics

* CNG (Continuous Native Generation) turns app.config.ts + plugins into ios/ and android/
* SDK 57 runs expo prebuild with --clean by default - stale native folders are deleted first
* Gitignore ios/ and android/ under CNG; regenerate on EAS Build or local prebuild
* Every native permission, entitlement, and manifest entry should flow from config plugins
* expo run:ios and expo run:android invoke prebuild then compile a dev client locally
* Pair with Native Module Rules before adding packages that touch native code

## Prerequisites

Start from a blank Expo app with SDK 57 pinned. Prebuild reads `app.config.ts`, applies config plugins, and writes native projects:

```bash
npx create-expo-app@latest PrebuildBasics --template blank-typescript@sdk-57 --yes
cd PrebuildBasics
```

Confirm the stack pin before running prebuild:

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "expo": "~57.0.4",
    "react": "19.2.3",
    "react-native": "0.86.0"
  }
}
```

> **Tooling:** These examples target **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4), **React Native 0.86.0**, and **React 19.2.3**. Read [Native Module Rules](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/native-module-rules/) before adding native dependencies.

---

## Basic Examples

### 1. What Prebuild Does

`npx expo prebuild` is the bridge between your **JavaScript config** and **Xcode/Gradle projects**. It:

1. Evaluates `app.config.ts` (or `app.json`)
2. Runs registered **config plugins** in order
3. Copies the SDK 57 native template into `ios/` and `android/`
4. Applies plugin mutations to `Info.plist`, `AndroidManifest.xml`, Gradle, and Podfile

```bash
npx expo prebuild
```

After a successful run:

```text
PrebuildBasics/
├── app.config.ts
├── ios/                 # Generated - do not hand-edit under CNG
├── android/             # Generated - do not hand-edit under CNG
└── package.json
```

* **CNG teams gitignore** `ios/` and `android/` - EAS Build runs the same prebuild step in CI
* **Hand-edited native files** are overwritten on `expo prebuild --clean` (the SDK 57 default)
* Express durable changes as **config plugins**, not Xcode clicks - see [Config Plugins in CNG](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/config-plugins-in-cng/)

---

### 2. Minimal app.config.ts for Prebuild

Prebuild needs bundle identifiers, display name, and icon paths at minimum:

```ts
// app.config.ts
import type { ExpoConfig } from "expo/config";
 
const config: ExpoConfig = {
  name: "PrebuildBasics",
  slug: "prebuild-basics",
  version: "1.0.0",
  orientation: "portrait",
  icon: "./assets/icon.png",
  scheme: "prebuildbasics",
  userInterfaceStyle: "automatic",
  ios: {
    bundleIdentifier: "com.example.prebuildbasics",
    supportsTablet: true,
  },
  android: {
    package: "com.example.prebuildbasics",
    adaptiveIcon: {
      foregroundImage: "./assets/adaptive-icon.png",
      backgroundColor: "#ffffff",
    },
  },
};
 
export default config;
```

```bash
npx expo prebuild --no-install
```

* **`--no-install`** skips `pod install` and Gradle sync - useful for CI diff checks
* **`npx expo config --type public`** prints the resolved manifest without writing native folders
* Bundle ID and package name flow into generated `PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER` and `applicationId`

---

### 3. Gitignore Native Folders Under CNG

Standard CNG projects **do not commit** generated native directories:

```gitignore
# .gitignore (CNG pattern)
ios/
android/
```

```bash
# Verify prebuild reproduces the same tree locally
rm -rf ios android
npx expo prebuild --no-install
```

* **Committed `ios/` from SDK 56** blocks RN 0.86 templates on upgrade - delete and regenerate
* **EAS Build** runs prebuild automatically when folders are absent
* Brownfield teams that commit native dirs inherit manual merge work - see [Custom Native Code in CNG](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/custom-native-code-in-cng/)

> **Related:** [../expo-rules/expo-project-rules-checklist/expo-project-rules-checklist.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/expo-project-rules-checklist/) - CNG gitignore is a Tier 3 non-negotiable

---

### 4. SDK 57 Clean Regen Default

In SDK 57, `expo prebuild` **deletes existing `ios/` and `android/`** before regenerating:

```bash
# Default behavior (SDK 57): clean then generate
npx expo prebuild
 
# Opt out: layer changes onto existing native projects
npx expo prebuild --no-clean
```

| Flag | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| (default) | Remove `ios/` and `android/`, then generate fresh projects |
| `--no-clean` | Keep existing folders; apply template updates incrementally |
| `--platform ios` | Generate iOS only |
| `--platform android` | Generate Android only |

* Use **default clean** after SDK upgrades or when plugin output looks corrupted
* Use **`--no-clean`** when iterating on a local native patch you are migrating into a plugin
* Full workflow checklist: [expo prebuild Workflow](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/expo-prebuild-workflow/)

---

### 5. Inspecting Generated Output

Before merging plugin changes, diff what prebuild produced:

```bash
npx expo prebuild --no-install
git diff ios android   # only if folders are tracked (brownfield)
```

```bash
# Print resolved config without writing files
npx expo config --type introspect
```

* **`--type introspect`** shows mod results plugins would apply - faster than full prebuild during plugin development
* **`expo-doctor`** catches invalid config fields that fail silently until prebuild
* Plugin order in `app.config.ts` matters when multiple plugins touch the same file

---

### 6. Registering a Config Plugin

Native permissions and entitlements belong in **plugins**, not post-prebuild edits:

```ts
// app.config.ts
const config: ExpoConfig = {
  // ...name, slug, ios, android
  plugins: [
    [
      "expo-camera",
      {
        cameraPermission: "Allow $(PRODUCT_NAME) to scan barcodes.",
      },
    ],
  ],
};
```

```bash
npx expo install expo-camera
npx expo prebuild --platform ios --no-install
```

* **`expo-camera`** ships a config plugin that adds `NSCameraUsageDescription` to `Info.plist`
* Third-party libraries with native code often expose plugins - check their README for SDK 57 support
* Deep dive: [Config Plugins in CNG](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/config-plugins-in-cng/) and [../native-modules/config-plugins/config-plugins.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/native-modules/config-plugins/)

---

### 7. Prebuild + Development Client

Custom native modules require a **development build**, not Expo Go. Prebuild generates the native shell:

```bash
npx expo install expo-dev-client
npx expo prebuild
npx expo run:ios
```

```json
// package.json scripts
{
  "scripts": {
    "prebuild": "expo prebuild",
    "ios:native": "expo run:ios",
    "android:native": "expo run:android"
  }
}
```

* **`expo run:ios`** runs prebuild if `ios/` is missing, installs pods, then compiles
* **Rebuild the dev client** after every SDK bump or native dependency change - OTA cannot replace native code
* [../native-modules/native-modules-basics/native-modules-basics.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/native-modules/native-modules-basics/) - when JS-only is not enough

---

### 8. Platform-Specific Config

Prebuild reads platform keys and generates matching native settings:

```ts
// app.config.ts excerpt
ios: {
  bundleIdentifier: "com.example.prebuildbasics",
  infoPlist: {
    UIBackgroundModes: ["fetch"],
  },
  associatedDomains: ["applinks:shop.example.com"],
},
android: {
  package: "com.example.prebuildbasics",
  intentFilters: [
    {
      action: "VIEW",
      autoVerify: true,
      data: [{ scheme: "https", host: "shop.example.com", pathPrefix: "/orders" }],
      category: ["BROWSABLE", "DEFAULT"],
    },
  ],
},
```

```bash
npx expo prebuild --no-install
```

* **Universal Links and App Links** require native entitlements - config fields map to `associatedDomains` and intent filters
* Prefer **library config plugins** (e.g. `expo-router`, `expo-notifications`) over raw `infoPlist` when available
* Rebuild store binaries after changing domains or schemes - OTA cannot add entitlements

---

### 9. New Architecture Defaults

SDK 57 targets RN 0.86 with the **New Architecture** enabled in prebuild templates:

```ts
// app.config.ts
const config: ExpoConfig = {
  // ...
  newArchEnabled: true,
};
```

```bash
npx expo-doctor
npx expo prebuild --no-install
```

* **`newArchEnabled: false`** is a temporary escape hatch - document an ADR if you disable it
* Third-party native libraries must support TurboModules/Fabric on RN 0.86 - check GitHub issues before installing
* Clean rebuild after changing `newArchEnabled`: `rm -rf ios android && npx expo prebuild`

---

### 10. Prebuild in the Upgrade Path

SDK bumps delete stale native folders under CNG:

```bash
npx expo install expo@^57.0.0
npx expo install --fix
npx expo-doctor
rm -rf ios android
npx expo prebuild --no-install
```

* **Never bump `react-native` independently** - `expo install --fix` pins RN 0.86.0 for SDK 57
* **EAS Build** regenerates native projects when `ios/`/`android/` are absent from the upload
* Full upgrade recipe: [../expo-platform/upgrading-expo-sdk-versions/upgrading-expo-sdk-versions.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-platform/upgrading-expo-sdk-versions/)

---

## Intermediate Examples

### 11. Monorepo Prebuild from App Root

In a pnpm/Turborepo workspace, run prebuild from the **app package directory**:

```bash
cd apps/mobile
npx expo prebuild --no-install
```

```ts
// apps/mobile/app.config.ts
const config: ExpoConfig = {
  name: "Mobile",
  slug: "mobile",
  // ...
};
```

* Metro and prebuild both resolve from the app root - not the monorepo root
* Shared packages do not need their own `ios/` - only deployable apps run prebuild
* [../project-setup/shared-packages-and-metro-resolution/shared-packages-and-metro-resolution.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/shared-packages-and-metro-resolution/)

---

### 12. Environment Variants Without Forked Native Projects

Drive staging and production bundle IDs from env vars - one config file, multiple binaries:

```ts
// app.config.ts
const IS_DEV = process.env.APP_VARIANT === "development";
 
const config: ExpoConfig = {
  name: IS_DEV ? "PrebuildBasics (Dev)" : "PrebuildBasics",
  slug: "prebuild-basics",
  ios: {
    bundleIdentifier: IS_DEV
      ? "com.example.prebuildbasics.dev"
      : "com.example.prebuildbasics",
  },
  android: {
    package: IS_DEV
      ? "com.example.prebuildbasics.dev"
      : "com.example.prebuildbasics",
  },
};
 
export default config;
```

```bash
APP_VARIANT=development npx expo prebuild --no-install
APP_VARIANT=production npx expo prebuild --no-install
```

* **EAS profiles** set `env.APP_VARIANT` per build - prebuild runs with the correct bundle ID in CI
* Each bundle ID needs its own credentials and EAS `projectId` if binaries ship separately
* Never commit secrets into `app.config.ts` - use EAS Secrets for signing keys

---

### 13. Validating Prebuild Before Merge

Add a CI gate that proves config produces reproducible native output:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/verify-prebuild.sh
set -euo pipefail
 
npx expo-doctor
rm -rf ios android
npx expo prebuild --no-install
 
# Optional: fail if unexpected native diff when folders are tracked
if git diff --quiet ios android 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "Prebuild output matches committed native projects."
else
  echo "Native diff detected - migrate changes to config plugins."
  exit 1
fi
```

* CNG teams skip the git diff step - folders are gitignored
* Run twice locally when authoring plugins - second run should produce **zero diff**
* [CNG in CI](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/cng-in-ci/) - when EAS generates vs when you check in native dirs

---

## FAQs

What is the difference between prebuild and eject?

* **Prebuild** regenerates native projects from config on demand - you can delete `ios/` and recreate them.
* **Eject** (legacy) permanently copied native projects into your repo with no regeneration path.
* Modern Expo uses **CNG** - config + plugins, not one-way eject.

Do I need Xcode or Android Studio for prebuild?

* **Prebuild itself** only writes files - no compilers required.
* **`expo run:ios`** and **`expo run:android`** need platform toolchains to compile.
* **EAS Build** runs prebuild + compile in the cloud if local toolchains are unavailable.

Can I run prebuild without creating ios/ and android/ locally?

* Yes - delete local folders and let **EAS Build** run prebuild in CI.
* Many teams never commit native dirs and only prebuild locally when debugging plugins.

Why did my hand-edited Info.plist change disappear?

* SDK 57 default prebuild **cleans** native folders - unencoded edits are lost.
* Move the change into a **config plugin** or library plugin array entry.

## Related

* [Custom Native Code in CNG](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/custom-native-code-in-cng/) - `expo run:ios/android` and committing native dirs
* [../native-modules/autolinking-and-expo-modules-core/autolinking-and-expo-modules-core.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/native-modules/autolinking-and-expo-modules-core/) - how modules link after prebuild

Dokumen: Accessibility and Safe Area
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/code-reference/accessibility-and-safe-area/

# Accessibility and Safe Area

Screen reader semantics, safe areas for notches, and inclusive touch/typography defaults.

Highlights / Accessibility and Safe Area

* accessibilityLabel
* accessibilityRole
* useSafeAreaInsets
* Minimum Touch Target
* Reduce Motion Check

#### accessibilityLabel

Provide a spoken name when visible text is missing or incomplete (icon-only controls).

```tsx
<Pressable accessibilityLabel="Close dialog" onPress={onClose}>
  <Icon name="x" />
</Pressable>
```

#### accessibilityRole

Tell assistive tech what the control is: `button`, `link`, `header`, `image`, `checkbox`, and more.

```tsx
<Text accessibilityRole="header" style={styles.h1}>
  Settings
</Text>
```

#### accessibilityState

Expose selected, disabled, busy, checked, and expanded state to the OS.

```tsx
<Pressable
  accessibilityRole="button"
  accessibilityState={{ disabled: loading, busy: loading }}
  onPress={onSave}
>
  <Text>Save</Text>
</Pressable>
```

#### accessibilityHint

Optional extra guidance for what happens after activation - keep it short.

```tsx
<Pressable
  accessibilityLabel="Delete message"
  accessibilityHint="Removes this message from your inbox"
  onPress={onDelete}
>
  <Text>Delete</Text>
</Pressable>
```

#### accessible Grouping

Set `accessible` on a parent to merge children into one focusable unit for card-like rows.

```tsx
<View accessible accessibilityLabel={`${title}, ${subtitle}`}>
  <Text>{title}</Text>
  <Text>{subtitle}</Text>
</View>
```

#### importantForAccessibility

Hide decorative views from the accessibility tree on Android (`no-hide-descendants`).

```tsx
<Image
  source={bg}
  importantForAccessibility="no"
  accessibilityElementsHidden
  style={StyleSheet.absoluteFill}
/>
```

#### SafeAreaProvider

Wrap the app once (Expo Router templates already do) so inset hooks work.

```tsx
import { SafeAreaProvider } from "react-native-safe-area-context";
 
export default function Root() {
  return (
    <SafeAreaProvider>
      <App />
    </SafeAreaProvider>
  );
}
```

#### useSafeAreaInsets

Read pixel insets and apply padding manually when you need full control.

```tsx
import { useSafeAreaInsets } from "react-native-safe-area-context";
 
const insets = useSafeAreaInsets();
return <View style={{ paddingTop: insets.top, flex: 1 }}>{children}</View>;
```

#### edges on SafeAreaView

Only apply safe padding on selected edges so bottom tabs are not double-padded.

```tsx
import { SafeAreaView } from "react-native-safe-area-context";
 
<SafeAreaView style={{ flex: 1 }} edges={["top", "left", "right"]}>
  {children}
</SafeAreaView>
```

#### Minimum Touch Target

Aim for about 44x44 pt minimum hit areas. Expand with `hitSlop` when visuals are smaller.

```tsx
<Pressable
  hitSlop={8}
  style={{ minWidth: 44, minHeight: 44, alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "center" }}
  onPress={onPress}
>
  <Icon name="heart" />
</Pressable>
```

#### Reduce Motion Check

Skip non-essential motion when the user enables reduce motion.

```tsx
import { AccessibilityInfo } from "react-native";
 
const reduce = await AccessibilityInfo.isReduceMotionEnabled();
const duration = reduce ? 0 : 250;
```

#### Bold Text Enabled

React to accessibility bold text preferences when fine-tuning typography (iOS primarily).

```tsx
const bold = await AccessibilityInfo.isBoldTextEnabled();
const weight = bold ? "700" : "400";
```

#### Screen Reader Focus

Move accessibility focus after important UI changes (use sparingly).

```tsx
import { findNodeHandle, AccessibilityInfo } from "react-native";
 
const tag = findNodeHandle(ref.current);
if (tag) AccessibilityInfo.setAccessibilityFocus(tag);
```

#### Contrast Text Colors

Prefer high-contrast pairs for body text - especially on image overlays with scrims.

```tsx
const styles = {
  overlayText: { color: "#fff", textShadowColor: "rgba(0,0,0,0.5)", textShadowRadius: 4 },
};
```

#### Allow Font Scaling

System font scaling is on by default - prefer keeping it. Cap pathological sizes with `maxFontSizeMultiplier` on critical labels only.

```tsx
<Text maxFontSizeMultiplier={1.4} style={styles.title}>
  Balance
</Text>
```

* [StyleSheet and Flexbox](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/code-reference/stylesheet-and-flexbox/) - layout that respects insets

Dokumen: App State and Hooks
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/code-reference/app-state-and-hooks/

# App State and Hooks

Screen lifecycle, app foreground/background, system theme, and hook patterns that matter on mobile.

Highlights / App State and Hooks

* AppState Foreground
* useFocusEffect Expo Router
* useColorScheme Theme
* BackHandler Android
* InteractionManager After Interactions

#### useState Local UI

Local component state works the same as web React - ideal for form fields and ephemeral UI flags.

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
```

#### useEffect Mount Cleanup

Subscribe on mount and always clean up. Mobile apps background frequently - avoid leaked timers and listeners.

```tsx
useEffect(() => {
  const id = setInterval(tick, 1000);
  return () => clearInterval(id);
}, []);
```

#### AppState Foreground

`AppState` tells you active vs background. Pause video, sockets, or polling when inactive.

```tsx
import { AppState } from "react-native";
 
useEffect(() => {
  const sub = AppState.addEventListener("change", (next) => {
    if (next === "active") refresh();
  });
  return () => sub.remove();
}, []);
```

#### useFocusEffect Expo Router

Run an effect when a screen gains focus in the navigation tree (not only on mount).

```tsx
import { useFocusEffect } from "expo-router";
import { useCallback } from "react";
 
useFocusEffect(
  useCallback(() => {
    refresh();
    return () => abort();
  }, []),
);
```

#### useWindowDimensions Hook

React to orientation and split-view size changes without manual event wiring.

```tsx
import { useWindowDimensions } from "react-native";
 
const { width, height } = useWindowDimensions();
```

#### useColorScheme Theme

Read the system light/dark preference for theming.

```tsx
import { useColorScheme } from "react-native";
 
const scheme = useColorScheme(); // "light" | "dark" | null
const bg = scheme === "dark" ? "#0f172a" : "#ffffff";
```

#### Appearance Listener

Listen for theme changes if you need side effects beyond re-render.

```tsx
import { Appearance } from "react-native";
 
useEffect(() => {
  const sub = Appearance.addChangeListener(({ colorScheme }) => {
    analytics.theme(colorScheme);
  });
  return () => sub.remove();
}, []);
```

#### InteractionManager After Interactions

Defer expensive work until animations and gestures finish for smoother navigation transitions.

```tsx
import { InteractionManager } from "react-native";
 
useEffect(() => {
  const task = InteractionManager.runAfterInteractions(() => {
    warmCache();
  });
  return () => task.cancel();
}, []);
```

#### useRef for Timers

Store interval/timeout ids in refs so handlers always clear the latest timer.

```tsx
const timerRef = useRef<ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null>(null);
function schedule(fn: () => void) {
  if (timerRef.current) clearTimeout(timerRef.current);
  timerRef.current = setTimeout(fn, 300);
}
```

#### BackHandler Android

Intercept the hardware back button (and some gesture backs depending on setup).

```tsx
import { BackHandler } from "react-native";
 
useEffect(() => {
  const sub = BackHandler.addEventListener("hardwareBackPress", () => {
    if (dirty) {
      confirmDiscard();
      return true; // handled
    }
    return false;
  });
  return () => sub.remove();
}, [dirty]);
```

#### Dimensions Change Event

Prefer `useWindowDimensions` for UI; use the event API for imperative work on size change.

```tsx
import { Dimensions } from "react-native";
 
useEffect(() => {
  const sub = Dimensions.addEventListener("change", ({ window }) => {
    layoutEngine.relayout(window);
  });
  return () => sub.remove();
}, []);
```

#### Custom useToggle

Small shared hooks reduce boilerplate for boolean UI state.

```tsx
function useToggle(init = false) {
  const [on, setOn] = useState(init);
  const toggle = useCallback(() => setOn((v) => !v), []);
  return [on, toggle, setOn] as const;
}
```

#### Abort Fetch on Unmount

Cancel in-flight requests when leaving a screen so setState does not run after unmount.

```tsx
useEffect(() => {
  const ac = new AbortController();
  fetch(url, { signal: ac.signal })
    .then((r) => r.json())
    .then(setData)
    .catch((e) => {
      if (e.name !== "AbortError") setError(e);
    });
  return () => ac.abort();
}, [url]);
```

#### useCallback Stable Handlers

Stabilize callbacks passed into memoized list rows or navigation options.

```tsx
const onPressItem = useCallback((id: string) => {
  router.push(`/items/${id}`);
}, []);
```

#### useMemo Derived Lists

Memoize filtered/sorted lists when the derivation is non-trivial and inputs change often.

```tsx
const visible = useMemo(
  () => items.filter((i) => i.title.includes(query)),
  [items, query],
);
```

Dokumen: Core Views and Text
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/code-reference/core-views-and-text/

# Core Views and Text

Core host components every React Native screen is built from - layout boxes, text, images, and scroll containers.

Highlights / Core Views and Text

* Basic View Container
* Text Nesting and Nested Styles
* Image from URI
* ScrollView Vertical
* KeyboardAvoidingView

#### Basic View Container

`View` is the primary layout container (like a `div`). Nest views to build structure; style with Flexbox.

```tsx
import { View, Text } from "react-native";
 
export function Card({ title }: { title: string }) {
  return (
    <View style={{ padding: 16 }}>
      <Text>{title}</Text>
    </View>
  );
}
```

#### Text Nesting and Nested Styles

Only `Text` can nest text. Nested `Text` inherits and can override styles for spans of copy.

```tsx
<Text style={{ fontSize: 16 }}>
  Hello, <Text style={{ fontWeight: "700" }}>{name}</Text>
</Text>
```

#### Image from URI

Remote images need explicit width/height (or flex) or they collapse. Prefer `expo-image` for caching in production apps.

```tsx
import { Image } from "react-native";
 
<Image
  source={{ uri: "https://example.com/avatar.png" }}
  style={{ width: 48, height: 48, borderRadius: 24 }}
/>
```

#### Image from Require

Local assets are bundled via `require`. Metro resolves the path at build time.

```tsx
<Image source={require("../../assets/logo.png")} style={{ width: 120, height: 40 }} />
```

#### ScrollView Vertical

Use `ScrollView` for short, fixed trees. Prefer virtualized lists when item count is large or unknown.

```tsx
import { ScrollView, Text } from "react-native";
 
<ScrollView contentContainerStyle={{ padding: 16 }}>
  <Text>{longContent}</Text>
</ScrollView>
```

#### ScrollView Horizontal

Set `horizontal` for carousels and chip rows. Pair with `showsHorizontalScrollIndicator={false}` when the UI is self-explanatory.

```tsx
<ScrollView horizontal showsHorizontalScrollIndicator={false}>
  {chips.map((c) => (
    <Chip key={c.id} label={c.label} />
  ))}
</ScrollView>
```

#### SafeAreaView Edges

`SafeAreaView` from `react-native-safe-area-context` (Expo default) pads notches and home indicators. Prefer it over the legacy RN export for edge control.

```tsx
import { SafeAreaView } from "react-native-safe-area-context";
 
<SafeAreaView style={{ flex: 1 }} edges={["top", "left", "right"]}>
  {children}
</SafeAreaView>
```

#### ActivityIndicator Loading

Built-in indeterminate spinner for loading states. Size and color are platform-aware.

```tsx
import { ActivityIndicator, View } from "react-native";
 
<View style={{ padding: 24 }}>
  <ActivityIndicator size="large" color="#2563eb" />
</View>
```

#### Modal Presentation

`Modal` covers the window. Control visibility with state; handle Android back via `onRequestClose`.

```tsx
import { Modal, View, Text, Pressable } from "react-native";
 
<Modal visible={open} animationType="slide" onRequestClose={() => setOpen(false)}>
  <View style={{ flex: 1, padding: 16 }}>
    <Text>Details</Text>
    <Pressable onPress={() => setOpen(false)}><Text>Close</Text></Pressable>
  </View>
</Modal>
```

#### StatusBar Style

Style the system status bar per screen. With Expo, `expo-status-bar` is the usual import.

```tsx
import { StatusBar } from "expo-status-bar";
 
<StatusBar style="dark" />
```

#### KeyboardAvoidingView

Lift focused inputs above the keyboard. Behavior differs by platform - `padding` on iOS is a common default.

```tsx
import { KeyboardAvoidingView, Platform, TextInput } from "react-native";
 
<KeyboardAvoidingView
  style={{ flex: 1 }}
  behavior={Platform.OS === "ios" ? "padding" : undefined}
>
  <TextInput placeholder="Message" />
</KeyboardAvoidingView>
```

#### RefreshControl on ScrollView

Pull-to-refresh attaches via `refreshControl` on scrollable containers.

```tsx
import { ScrollView, RefreshControl } from "react-native";
 
<ScrollView
  refreshControl={
    <RefreshControl refreshing={loading} onRefresh={onRefresh} />
  }
>
  {children}
</ScrollView>
```

#### View Style Arrays

Later styles win on conflicts. Arrays are the idiomatic way to compose base + conditional styles.

```tsx
<View style={[styles.card, selected && styles.cardSelected, style]} />
```

#### pointerEvents Control

`pointerEvents` controls whether a view (and descendants) receive touches - useful for loading overlays.

```tsx
<View pointerEvents={blocking ? "none" : "auto"} style={styles.content}>
  {children}
</View>
```

#### testID for E2E

`testID` (and Android `accessibilityLabel` strategies) give Detox, Maestro, and Appium stable selectors.

```tsx
<Pressable testID="login-submit" onPress={onSubmit}>
  <Text>Sign in</Text>
</Pressable>
```

* [Lists and Virtualization](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/code-reference/lists-and-virtualization/) - when ScrollView is not enough
* [TextInput and Forms](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/code-reference/textinput-and-forms/) - inputs that live inside these containers

Dokumen: Expo Router Navigation
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/code-reference/expo-router-navigation/

# Expo Router Navigation

File-based routing idioms for Expo Router - stacks, tabs, params, and imperative navigation.

Highlights / Expo Router Navigation

* File-based Screen
* Link Component Navigate
* Dynamic Route Params
* Tabs Layout
* Redirect Auth Gate

#### File-based Screen

Routes map from the `app/` directory. `app/index.tsx` is the entry route for that segment.

```tsx
// app/index.tsx
import { Text, View } from "react-native";
 
export default function HomeScreen() {
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1, padding: 16 }}>
      <Text>Home</Text>
    </View>
  );
}
```

#### Stack Screen Options

Configure titles and headers in `_layout.tsx` with `Stack.Screen` options.

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
 
export default function Layout() {
  return (
    <Stack>
      <Stack.Screen name="index" options={{ title: "Home" }} />
      <Stack.Screen name="settings" options={{ title: "Settings" }} />
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

#### Link Component Navigate

Declarative navigation with `Link` - good for list rows and static menus.

```tsx
import { Link } from "expo-router";
import { Text } from "react-native";
 
<Link href="/settings">
  <Text>Open settings</Text>
</Link>
```

#### router.push Path

Imperative navigation from handlers after async work or validation.

```tsx
import { router } from "expo-router";
 
function onCreated(id: string) {
  router.push(`/items/${id}`);
}
```

#### Dynamic Route Params

Dynamic segments live in brackets: `app/items/[id].tsx` matches `/items/42`.

```tsx
// app/items/[id].tsx
import { useLocalSearchParams } from "expo-router";
 
export default function ItemScreen() {
  const { id } = useLocalSearchParams<{ id: string }>();
  return <Text>Item {id}</Text>;
}
```

#### useLocalSearchParams

Read path and query params for the focused route. Values may be `string | string[]` - normalize when needed.

```tsx
const { id, tab } = useLocalSearchParams<{ id: string; tab?: string }>();
const itemId = Array.isArray(id) ? id[0] : id;
```

#### Tabs Layout

Group tab screens under a `(tabs)` folder with a tabs `_layout`.

```tsx
// app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx
import { Tabs } from "expo-router";
 
export default function TabsLayout() {
  return (
    <Tabs>
      <Tabs.Screen name="index" options={{ title: "Home" }} />
      <Tabs.Screen name="profile" options={{ title: "Profile" }} />
    </Tabs>
  );
}
```

#### Redirect Auth Gate

Send unauthenticated users to sign-in without mounting protected UI.

```tsx
import { Redirect } from "expo-router";
 
if (!session) return <Redirect href="/sign-in" />;
return <AppShell />;
```

#### router.back and canGoBack

Pop the stack when possible; otherwise route to a safe fallback.

```tsx
import { router } from "expo-router";
 
function onBack() {
  if (router.canGoBack()) router.back();
  else router.replace("/");
}
```

#### replace vs push

`push` adds history; `replace` swaps the current entry - use after login so back does not return to the form.

```tsx
router.replace("/(tabs)");
```

#### Modal Presentation Route

Present a screen as a modal via stack options (`presentation: "modal"`).

```tsx
<Stack.Screen name="compose" options={{ presentation: "modal", title: "New" }} />
```

#### Href Object Params

Build hrefs as objects when you need query params without string concatenation.

```tsx
<Link href={{ pathname: "/search", params: { q: query } }}>
  <Text>Search</Text>
</Link>
```

#### useNavigation setOptions

Update the header from inside a screen when the title depends on loaded data.

```tsx
import { useNavigation } from "expo-router";
import { useLayoutEffect } from "react";
 
const navigation = useNavigation();
useLayoutEffect(() => {
  navigation.setOptions({ title: item?.name ?? "Item" });
}, [navigation, item?.name]);
```

#### Slot and Groups

Parentheses folders like `(auth)` group routes without affecting the URL path.

```tsx
// app/(auth)/sign-in.tsx -> /sign-in
// app/(auth)/_layout.tsx can wrap auth screens without a URL segment
```

#### Deep Link Path

Configure scheme in `app.json` / `app.config` so `/items/1` opens the matching route when the OS delivers a URL.

```tsx
// app.config: { expo: { scheme: "myapp" } }
// Opens: myapp://items/1  -> app/items/[id].tsx
```

Dokumen: Lists and Virtualization
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/code-reference/lists-and-virtualization/

# Lists and Virtualization

Virtualized lists for long data sets - FlatList, SectionList, and the knobs that keep scroll smooth.

Highlights / Lists and Virtualization

* FlatList Basic Data
* onEndReached Pagination
* SectionList Grouped
* getItemLayout Fixed Height
* Memoized Row Component

#### FlatList Basic Data

`data`, `renderItem`, and a stable `keyExtractor` are the minimum. Prefer string ids over indexes.

```tsx
import { FlatList, Text } from "react-native";
 
<FlatList
  data={items}
  keyExtractor={(item) => item.id}
  renderItem={({ item }) => <Text>{item.title}</Text>}
/>
```

#### Item Separator Component

Render dividers between items without putting borders on every row.

```tsx
const Separator = () => <View style={{ height: 1, backgroundColor: "#e5e7eb" }} />;
 
<FlatList ItemSeparatorComponent={Separator} data={items} renderItem={...} />
```

#### ListEmptyComponent

Show a dedicated empty state when `data` is empty (and not loading).

```tsx
<FlatList
  data={items}
  ListEmptyComponent={<Text>No results</Text>}
  renderItem={...}
/>
```

#### ListHeader Footer

Headers and footers scroll with the list (or stick with sticky header indices when configured).

```tsx
<FlatList
  ListHeaderComponent={<SearchBar />}
  ListFooterComponent={loadingMore ? <ActivityIndicator /> : null}
  data={items}
  renderItem={...}
/>
```

#### Pull to Refresh FlatList

Same `RefreshControl` pattern as ScrollView, via `refreshing` / `onRefresh` props or `refreshControl`.

```tsx
<FlatList
  data={items}
  refreshing={refreshing}
  onRefresh={onRefresh}
  renderItem={...}
/>
```

#### onEndReached Pagination

Load the next page when the user approaches the end. Guard with a loading flag to avoid duplicate fetches.

```tsx
<FlatList
  data={items}
  onEndReached={() => {
    if (!loadingMore && hasMore) loadMore();
  }}
  onEndReachedThreshold={0.4}
  renderItem={...}
/>
```

#### numColumns Grid

Set `numColumns` for simple grids. Item width should account for columns and gaps.

```tsx
<FlatList
  data={photos}
  numColumns={3}
  keyExtractor={(p) => p.id}
  renderItem={({ item }) => <Thumb photo={item} />}
/>
```

#### SectionList Grouped

Sectioned data needs `sections` with `{ title, data }` entries and section header renderers.

```tsx
import { SectionList, Text } from "react-native";
 
<SectionList
  sections={sections}
  keyExtractor={(item) => item.id}
  renderItem={({ item }) => <Text>{item.name}</Text>}
  renderSectionHeader={({ section }) => <Text>{section.title}</Text>}
/>
```

#### getItemLayout Fixed Height

When every row has a known height, provide `getItemLayout` so scroll-to-index skips measurement.

```tsx
const H = 56;
getItemLayout={(_, index) => ({ length: H, offset: H * index, index })}
```

#### extraData for Extra Renders

FlatList pure-renders from `data`. Pass `extraData` when selection state outside `data` should re-render rows.

```tsx
<FlatList data={items} extraData={selectedId} renderItem={renderItem} />
```

#### Memoized Row Component

Extract rows and wrap with `React.memo` so unchanged items skip work when the parent re-renders.

```tsx
const Row = memo(function Row({ item }: { item: Item }) {
  return <Text>{item.title}</Text>;
});
```

#### initialNumToRender Tuning

Control how many items render on first paint. Higher values reduce blank space; lower values speed TTI.

```tsx
<FlatList initialNumToRender={12} data={items} renderItem={...} />
```

#### windowSize Tuning

`windowSize` is a multiplier of the viewport for offscreen rendering. Lower values save memory; higher values reduce blank scroll.

```tsx
<FlatList windowSize={7} data={items} renderItem={...} />
```

#### removeClippedSubviews

On Android, clipping offscreen views can improve memory. Test carefully with sticky headers and absolute children.

```tsx
<FlatList removeClippedSubviews data={items} renderItem={...} />
```

#### FlashList Mental Model

For very large lists, Shopify FlashList recycles cells more aggressively than FlatList. Same data/render mental model; different performance characteristics - adopt when FlatList profiling shows jank.

```tsx
// import { FlashList } from "@shopify/flash-list";
// <FlashList data={items} estimatedItemSize={56} renderItem={...} />
```

Reviewed by Chris St. John·Last updated Jul 18, 2026

Dokumen: Networking Images Media
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/code-reference/networking-images-media/

# Networking Images Media

HTTP, cached images, pickers, and connectivity checks for mobile clients.

Highlights / Networking Images Media

* fetch JSON API
* AbortController Timeout
* expo-image Component
* ImagePicker Launch
* NetInfo Connectivity

#### fetch JSON API

`fetch` works in RN. Always check `response.ok` before assuming JSON success payloads.

```tsx
const res = await fetch(`${API}/items`, {
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` },
});
if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);
const data: Item[] = await res.json();
```

#### POST JSON Body

Send JSON with explicit `Content-Type` and stringified body.

```tsx
await fetch(`${API}/items`, {
  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`,
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({ title }),
});
```

#### AbortController Timeout

Cancel slow requests so UIs do not hang forever.

```tsx
const ac = new AbortController();
const t = setTimeout(() => ac.abort(), 12_000);
try {
  const res = await fetch(url, { signal: ac.signal });
  return await res.json();
} finally {
  clearTimeout(t);
}
```

#### expo-image Component

`expo-image` adds caching and better transitions than core `Image` for remote assets.

```tsx
import { Image } from "expo-image";
 
<Image
  source={{ uri }}
  style={{ width: 120, height: 120 }}
  contentFit="cover"
  transition={200}
/>
```

#### Image contentFit

Map CSS-like object-fit via `contentFit`: `cover`, `contain`, `fill`, `none`, `scale-down`.

```tsx
<Image source={{ uri }} style={styles.hero} contentFit="contain" />
```

#### Prefetch Image

Warm the cache before a screen that needs the asset immediately.

```tsx
import { Image } from "expo-image";
 
await Image.prefetch(uri);
```

#### ImagePicker Launch

Pick from the library with `expo-image-picker` after permissions.

```tsx
import * as ImagePicker from "expo-image-picker";
 
const result = await ImagePicker.launchImageLibraryAsync({
  mediaTypes: ["images"],
  quality: 0.8,
});
if (!result.canceled) setUri(result.assets[0].uri);
```

#### Camera Permission Flow

Request permissions and branch when denied - send users to settings if needed.

```tsx
const cam = await ImagePicker.requestCameraPermissionsAsync();
if (!cam.granted) {
  // show rationale / open settings
  return;
}
await ImagePicker.launchCameraAsync({ quality: 0.8 });
```

#### DocumentPicker File

Pick arbitrary documents for upload.

```tsx
import * as DocumentPicker from "expo-document-picker";
 
const res = await DocumentPicker.getDocumentAsync({ type: "application/pdf" });
if (!res.canceled) setFile(res.assets[0]);
```

#### MediaLibrary Save

Save a file into the user gallery when appropriate (requires permissions).

```tsx
import * as MediaLibrary from "expo-media-library";
 
const { status } = await MediaLibrary.requestPermissionsAsync();
if (status === "granted") await MediaLibrary.saveToLibraryAsync(localUri);
```

#### AV Video Playback

Play video with the Expo video stack you standardize on (e.g. `expo-video` / `expo-av` in your app). Keep players paused in background via AppState.

```tsx
// Conceptual controlled player:
// <VideoView player={player} style={{ width: "100%", height: 220 }} />
```

#### NetInfo Connectivity

Gate fetches and show offline banners with `@react-native-community/netinfo`.

```tsx
import NetInfo from "@react-native-community/netinfo";
 
const state = await NetInfo.fetch();
if (!state.isConnected) setOffline(true);
```

#### Upload multipart

Upload local files with `FormData` and the file URI shape RN expects.

```tsx
const form = new FormData();
form.append("file", {
  uri: localUri,
  name: "photo.jpg",
  type: "image/jpeg",
} as unknown as Blob);
await fetch(`${API}/upload`, { method: "POST", body: form, headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } });
```

#### Retry with Backoff

Retry idempotent GETs on transient failures with exponential delay.

```tsx
async function getWithRetry(url: string, attempts = 3) {
  let last: unknown;
  for (let i = 0; i < attempts; i++) {
    try {
      const res = await fetch(url);
      if (res.ok) return res.json();
      last = res.status;
    } catch (e) {
      last = e;
    }
    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 300 * 2 ** i));
  }
  throw last;
}
```

#### Absolute vs Relative Image URI

Remote URIs need `https://...`. Local picker URIs are device paths; do not prefix them as if they were web paths.

```tsx
const source = uri.startsWith("http") ? { uri } : { uri: localFileUri };
```

Dokumen: Performance and Lists
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/code-reference/performance-and-lists/

# Performance and Lists

Practical ways to keep JS and UI threads responsive - especially around long lists and navigation transitions.

Highlights / Performance and Lists

* React.memo Row
* getItemLayout Revisited
* Why Not ScrollView map
* Image Size Explicit
* Reanimated UI Thread Note

#### React.memo Row

Memoize pure row components so parent re-renders do not rebuild every cell.

```tsx
const Row = memo(function Row({ item }: { item: Item }) {
  return <Text>{item.title}</Text>;
});
```

#### useCallback onPress Item

Pass a stable handler into memoized rows (or close over id inside a memoized child).

```tsx
const onPressItem = useCallback((id: string) => {
  router.push(`/items/${id}`);
}, []);
```

#### Avoid Inline Style Objects in Rows

Create styles once with `StyleSheet.create`. Inline objects allocate every render and defeat shallow compares.

```tsx
// Prefer styles.row over style={{ padding: 12 }} inside renderItem
renderItem={({ item }) => <Row item={item} style={styles.row} />}
```

#### getItemLayout Revisited

Fixed-height rows unlock faster scroll-to-index and less measurement work.

```tsx
const H = 64;
const getItemLayout = (_: unknown, index: number) => ({
  length: H,
  offset: H * index,
  index,
});
```

#### InteractionManager Heavy Work

Schedule parsing or secondary fetches after the transition finishes.

```tsx
useEffect(() => {
  const task = InteractionManager.runAfterInteractions(() => hydrate());
  return () => task.cancel();
}, [id]);
```

#### startTransition Non Urgent

Mark non-urgent React updates (large filtered lists) so typing stays responsive when using concurrent features.

```tsx
import { startTransition, useState } from "react";
 
function onChangeText(text: string) {
  setQuery(text);
  startTransition(() => setFilter(text));
}
```

#### Hermes Engine Assumption

Modern RN/Expo defaults to Hermes. Write idiomatic modern JS; avoid assuming JSC-only quirks in new apps.

```tsx
// Prefer standard ES features supported by Hermes in your RN version
const id = crypto.randomUUID?.() ?? String(Date.now());
```

#### Why Not ScrollView map

Mapping hundreds of items into a `ScrollView` mounts every row at once. Use `FlatList` / FlashList for long data.

```tsx
// Avoid for large arrays:
// <ScrollView>{items.map(...)}</ScrollView>
// Prefer:
// <FlatList data={items} renderItem={...} />
```

#### Image Size Explicit

Always give images width/height or flex constraints so the list does not reflow as bits arrive.

```tsx
<Image source={{ uri }} style={{ width: 48, height: 48 }} contentFit="cover" />
```

#### console.log in Render Cost

Verbose logs in `renderItem` jank scroll on device. Strip or gate debug logging.

```tsx
if (__DEV__ && DEBUG_ROWS) console.log("row", item.id);
```

#### Profile with Perf Monitor

Use the dev menu perf monitor / React DevTools / native profilers before micro-optimizing.

```tsx
// Dev Menu -> Show Perf Monitor (FPS / JS frame time)
// Fix the measured bottleneck, not guessed ones
```

#### Reanimated UI Thread Note

Drive high-frequency animations with Reanimated shared values on the UI thread instead of `setState` per frame.

```tsx
// Conceptual: const x = useSharedValue(0);
// style useAnimatedStyle(() => ({ transform: [{ translateX: x.value }] }))
```

#### Batch setState Updates

Multiple updates inside one event handler batch automatically - avoid awaiting between related setters when you need a single paint.

```tsx
function onSuccess(data: Data) {
  setData(data);
  setError(null);
  setLoading(false);
}
```

#### Key Stability Across Filters

Keep stable ids when filtering so row state and images are not remounted incorrectly.

```tsx
keyExtractor={(item) => item.id}
```

#### Deferred Mount Screens

Do not mount every heavy tab eagerly. Lazy-load expensive screens so first paint stays light.

```tsx
// Expo Router: keep heavy routes as separate files; avoid importing huge modules in root layout
const Editor = React.lazy(() => import("../features/Editor"));
```

* [App State and Hooks](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/code-reference/app-state-and-hooks/) - InteractionManager and memo hooks
* [Networking Images Media](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/code-reference/networking-images-media/) - image caching and sizing

Dokumen: Platform Linking and Share
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/code-reference/platform-linking-and-share/

# Platform Linking and Share

Cross-platform branches, deep links out of the app, share sheets, and system dialogs.

Highlights / Platform Linking and Share

* Platform.OS Branch
* Linking openURL
* Share API
* Clipboard Set String
* Alert confirm

#### Platform.OS Branch

Branch on `"ios" | "android" | "web"` when APIs or UX truly differ.

```tsx
import { Platform, Text } from "react-native";
 
const label = Platform.OS === "ios" ? "Hold to reorder" : "Long-press to reorder";
return <Text>{label}</Text>;
```

#### Platform.select Values

Pick values (styles, components, numbers) per platform in one expression.

```tsx
const hit = Platform.select({ ios: 12, android: 16, default: 12 });
```

#### Platform.Version Check

Gate features that need a minimum OS version (Android API level is numeric; iOS is a string version).

```tsx
const supportsFeature =
  Platform.OS === "android" ? Number(Platform.Version) >= 33 : true;
```

#### Linking openURL

Open https, tel, mailto, or custom schemes in another app.

```tsx
import { Linking } from "react-native";
 
await Linking.openURL("https://expo.dev");
```

#### Linking canOpenURL

On iOS, declare schemes in `Info.plist` / app config and check before opening.

```tsx
const url = "twitter://user?screen_name=expo";
if (await Linking.canOpenURL(url)) await Linking.openURL(url);
else await Linking.openURL("https://twitter.com/expo");
```

#### Linking getInitialURL

Read the URL that launched a cold start (pair with Expo Router linking config).

```tsx
const initial = await Linking.getInitialURL();
if (initial) handleUrl(initial);
```

#### Linking addEventListener

Handle links while the app is already running.

```tsx
useEffect(() => {
  const sub = Linking.addEventListener("url", ({ url }) => handleUrl(url));
  return () => sub.remove();
}, []);
```

#### Share API

Present the OS share sheet with text and optional URL.

```tsx
import { Share } from "react-native";
 
await Share.share({ message: "Check this out", url: "https://example.com" });
```

#### Clipboard Set String

Copy text with `expo-clipboard` for a consistent Expo API.

```tsx
import * as Clipboard from "expo-clipboard";
 
await Clipboard.setStringAsync(inviteCode);
```

#### Open Settings App

Send users to system settings when permissions are blocked.

```tsx
import { Linking } from "react-native";
 
await Linking.openSettings();
```

#### Constants expo-constants

Read app config, `extra`, and execution environment from `expo-constants`.

```tsx
import Constants from "expo-constants";
 
const apiUrl = Constants.expoConfig?.extra?.apiUrl as string | undefined;
```

#### Device info expo-device

Query device name/model when useful for support diagnostics (avoid over-collecting PII).

```tsx
import * as Device from "expo-device";
 
const summary = `${Device.osName} ${Device.modelName ?? "unknown"}`;
```

#### Application app version

Surface native app version in settings/about screens.

```tsx
import Constants from "expo-constants";
 
const version = Constants.nativeAppVersion ?? Constants.expoConfig?.version;
```

#### Alert confirm

System alert with buttons - fine for destructive confirms without a custom modal.

```tsx
import { Alert } from "react-native";
 
Alert.alert("Delete item?", "This cannot be undone.", [
  { text: "Cancel", style: "cancel" },
  { text: "Delete", style: "destructive", onPress: onDelete },
]);
```

#### ActionSheetIOS

iOS-only action sheet for lightweight menus; use a cross-platform library on Android.

```tsx
import { ActionSheetIOS, Platform } from "react-native";
 
if (Platform.OS === "ios") {
  ActionSheetIOS.showActionSheetWithOptions(
    { options: ["Cancel", "Edit", "Delete"], cancelButtonIndex: 0, destructiveButtonIndex: 2 },
    (i) => {
      if (i === 1) onEdit();
      if (i === 2) onDelete();
    },
  );
}
```

Dokumen: Pressables and Touch
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/code-reference/pressables-and-touch/

# Pressables and Touch

Touch targets, press feedback, and patterns that keep taps reliable on phones.

Highlights / Pressables and Touch

* Pressable Basic
* Pressable Style Function
* hitSlop Expand Target
* Long Press Handler
* Android ripple android\_ripple

#### Pressable Basic

`Pressable` is the preferred primitive for custom buttons - more flexible than legacy Touchables.

```tsx
import { Pressable, Text } from "react-native";
 
<Pressable onPress={onSave}>
  <Text>Save</Text>
</Pressable>
```

#### Pressable Style Function

Style can be a function of `{ pressed }` for opacity or color feedback without extra state.

```tsx
<Pressable
  onPress={onPress}
  style={({ pressed }) => [{ opacity: pressed ? 0.7 : 1 }, styles.btn]}
>
  <Text>Continue</Text>
</Pressable>
```

#### hitSlop Expand Target

Expand the touch box without changing visuals - critical for small icons.

```tsx
<Pressable hitSlop={12} onPress={onClose}>
  <Icon name="x" />
</Pressable>
```

#### disabled Pressable

`disabled` blocks press handlers and should pair with muted styles and `accessibilityState`.

```tsx
<Pressable disabled={isPending} onPress={onSubmit} accessibilityState={{ disabled: isPending }}>
  <Text>Submit</Text>
</Pressable>
```

#### TouchableOpacity Legacy

Still common in older codebases. Prefer `Pressable` for new work unless a library requires Touchable.

```tsx
import { TouchableOpacity, Text } from "react-native";
 
<TouchableOpacity activeOpacity={0.7} onPress={onPress}>
  <Text>Legacy button</Text>
</TouchableOpacity>
```

#### Button Primitive

RN `Button` is a thin system control - fine for prototypes, limited for design systems.

```tsx
import { Button } from "react-native";
 
<Button title="OK" onPress={onOk} />
```

#### Long Press Handler

`onLongPress` opens context menus and secondary actions.

```tsx
<Pressable onPress={onOpen} onLongPress={onShowMenu}>
  <Text>{title}</Text>
</Pressable>
```

#### Delay Long Press

Tune how long the finger must stay down before long-press fires.

```tsx
<Pressable delayLongPress={400} onLongPress={onShowMenu}>
  <Row />
</Pressable>
```

#### Nested Pressables

Avoid wrapping pressable rows in another pressable parent. If you must nest, stop propagation patterns carefully - prefer separate hit targets.

```tsx
// Prefer sibling actions over Pressable inside Pressable rows
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row" }}>
  <Pressable onPress={onOpen} style={{ flex: 1 }}><Text>{title}</Text></Pressable>
  <Pressable onPress={onDelete}><Text>Delete</Text></Pressable>
</View>
```

#### Press Retention Offset

Allow the finger to drift slightly while still counting as a press.

```tsx
<Pressable pressRetentionOffset={20} onPress={onPress}>
  <Text>Drag-tolerant</Text>
</Pressable>
```

#### Android ripple android\_ripple

Material ripple on Android via the `android_ripple` prop.

```tsx
<Pressable
  android_ripple={{ color: "#dbeafe" }}
  onPress={onPress}
  style={styles.row}
>
  <Text>Row</Text>
</Pressable>
```

#### Haptic Feedback Expo

Light haptics improve perceived quality on supported devices (`expo-haptics`).

```tsx
import * as Haptics from "expo-haptics";
 
async function onPress() {
  await Haptics.impactAsync(Haptics.ImpactFeedbackStyle.Light);
  doAction();
}
```

#### Disable Double Submit

Guard async presses so double-taps do not fire two mutations.

```tsx
const busy = useRef(false);
async function onPress() {
  if (busy.current) return;
  busy.current = true;
  try {
    await submit();
  } finally {
    busy.current = false;
  }
}
```

#### Accessible Role Button

Expose the control as a button to VoiceOver/TalkBack and give it a spoken name.

```tsx
<Pressable
  accessibilityRole="button"
  accessibilityLabel="Save profile"
  onPress={onSave}
>
  <Icon name="check" />
</Pressable>
```

#### Gesture Handler Root

When using React Native Gesture Handler, wrap the app (Expo Router does this in templates) so gestures and native navigators cooperate.

```tsx
// Expo Router templates already wrap with GestureHandlerRootView.
// Bare RN: import { GestureHandlerRootView } from "react-native-gesture-handler";
// return <GestureHandlerRootView style={{ flex: 1 }}><App /></GestureHandlerRootView>;
```
