Dokumen: Storage and Secure Data
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/code-reference/storage-and-secure-data/

# Storage and Secure Data

Persistence options from simple key-value to secure tokens and local files/databases.

Highlights / Storage and Secure Data

* AsyncStorage Get Set
* SecureStore Token
* FileSystem Document Dir
* SQLite Open Database
* JSON Parse Guard

#### AsyncStorage Get Set

Unencrypted key-value storage for preferences and non-secret caches. Prefer `@react-native-async-storage/async-storage` (Expo-compatible).

```tsx
import AsyncStorage from "@react-native-async-storage/async-storage";
 
await AsyncStorage.setItem("theme", "dark");
const theme = await AsyncStorage.getItem("theme");
```

#### AsyncStorage Multi

Batch reads/writes to reduce bridge round-trips.

```tsx
await AsyncStorage.multiSet([
  ["onboarding.done", "1"],
  ["locale", "en"],
]);
const pairs = await AsyncStorage.multiGet(["onboarding.done", "locale"]);
```

#### SecureStore Token

Store secrets (session tokens, refresh tokens) in the platform keychain/keystore via `expo-secure-store`.

```tsx
import * as SecureStore from "expo-secure-store";
 
await SecureStore.setItemAsync("accessToken", token);
const token = await SecureStore.getItemAsync("accessToken");
```

#### SecureStore Delete

Clear credentials on logout.

```tsx
await SecureStore.deleteItemAsync("accessToken");
await SecureStore.deleteItemAsync("refreshToken");
```

#### FileSystem Document Dir

App document directory paths for durable user files with `expo-file-system`.

```tsx
import * as FileSystem from "expo-file-system";
 
const dir = FileSystem.documentDirectory; // string | null
const path = `${dir}notes.txt`;
```

#### Write Read Text File

Simple text file IO for exports and offline drafts.

```tsx
await FileSystem.writeAsStringAsync(path, contents, {
  encoding: FileSystem.EncodingType.UTF8,
});
const text = await FileSystem.readAsStringAsync(path);
```

#### Cache Directory Temp

Put disposable downloads in the cache directory so the OS may reclaim space.

```tsx
const cachePath = `${FileSystem.cacheDirectory}avatar-tmp.jpg`;
```

#### SQLite Open Database

Local relational storage with `expo-sqlite` for structured offline data.

```tsx
import * as SQLite from "expo-sqlite";
 
const db = await SQLite.openDatabaseAsync("app.db");
await db.execAsync("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS notes (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, body TEXT);");
```

#### MMKV Mental Model

MMKV (community module) is a fast synchronous key-value store often used with Zustand. Requires native code - fine in dev builds; not pure Expo Go unless supported by your workflow.

```tsx
// Conceptual: storage.set("key", value); const v = storage.getString("key");
```

#### Persist Zustand Slice

Sketch of persisting a slice - wire your storage engine in `persist` middleware.

```tsx
// persist( (set) => ({ token: null, setToken: (t) => set({ token: t }) }),
//   { name: "auth", storage: createJSONStorage(() => asyncStorage) } )
```

#### Clear on Logout

Namespace user keys and wipe them on logout so the next account never sees stale data.

```tsx
async function clearUserData() {
  await AsyncStorage.multiRemove(["user.profile", "user.prefs"]);
  await SecureStore.deleteItemAsync("accessToken");
}
```

#### JSON Parse Guard

Stored JSON can be corrupt - parse behind try/catch and fall back to defaults.

```tsx
function readJson<T>(raw: string | null, fallback: T): T {
  if (!raw) return fallback;
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw) as T;
  } catch {
    return fallback;
  }
}
```

#### Migration Version Key

Keep a schema version next to persisted state and run migrations when it changes.

```tsx
const VERSION = "2";
const v = await AsyncStorage.getItem("storage.version");
if (v !== VERSION) {
  await migrate(v);
  await AsyncStorage.setItem("storage.version", VERSION);
}
```

#### expo-crypto Random

Generate opaque ids with `expo-crypto` instead of weak `Math.random`.

```tsx
import * as Crypto from "expo-crypto";
 
const id = Crypto.randomUUID();
```

#### Keychain Availability

SecureStore can fail on restricted devices - catch errors and degrade gracefully (re-auth, in-memory session).

```tsx
try {
  await SecureStore.setItemAsync("accessToken", token);
} catch {
  // Fall back: keep token in memory only for this session
  memorySession.token = token;
}
```

Dokumen: StyleSheet and Flexbox
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/code-reference/stylesheet-and-flexbox/

# StyleSheet and Flexbox

Layout and styling idioms for React Native - Yoga Flexbox defaults, StyleSheet, and platform-aware styles.

Highlights / StyleSheet and Flexbox

* StyleSheet.create Basics
* Flex Direction Row
* justifyContent Alignment
* Gap in Flex Containers
* useWindowDimensions

#### StyleSheet.create Basics

`StyleSheet.create` validates keys at build time and lets you reference styles by name. Prefer it over huge inline objects for static styles.

```tsx
import { StyleSheet, View, Text } from "react-native";
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  box: { padding: 12, backgroundColor: "#fff" },
  title: { fontSize: 18, fontWeight: "600" },
});
```

#### Flex Direction Column

Default `flexDirection` is `column` (unlike web CSS). Children stack top to bottom unless you change it.

```tsx
<View style={{ flex: 1, flexDirection: "column" }}>
  <Header />
  <Content />
</View>
```

#### Flex Direction Row

Use `row` for toolbars, list rows with leading icons, and horizontal groups.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", gap: 8 }}>
  <Avatar />
  <Text>{name}</Text>
</View>
```

#### justifyContent Alignment

Main-axis distribution: `flex-start`, `center`, `flex-end`, `space-between`, `space-around`, `space-evenly`.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", justifyContent: "space-between" }}>
  <Text>Title</Text>
  <Text>Action</Text>
</View>
```

#### alignItems Cross Axis

Cross-axis alignment for children: `stretch` (default in column), `center`, `flex-start`, `flex-end`, `baseline`.

```tsx
<View style={{ alignItems: "center", padding: 16 }}>
  <Icon />
  <Text>Centered block</Text>
</View>
```

#### flex Grow Shrink

`flex: 1` makes a child fill remaining space on the main axis. Use it so body content consumes leftover height.

```tsx
<View style={{ flex: 1 }}>
  <Header />
  <View style={{ flex: 1 }}>{body}</View>
  <Footer />
</View>
```

#### Absolute Positioning

Position overlays with `position: "absolute"` and edge offsets. Parent usually needs non-static layout context.

```tsx
<View style={{ position: "relative" }}>
  <Image style={{ width: 64, height: 64 }} source={src} />
  <View style={{ position: "absolute", top: -4, right: -4 }}>
    <Badge />
  </View>
</View>
```

#### Gap in Flex Containers

Modern RN supports `gap`, `rowGap`, and `columnGap` on flex containers - cleaner than margin hacks.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", flexWrap: "wrap", gap: 8 }}>
  {tags.map((t) => (
    <Tag key={t} label={t} />
  ))}
</View>
```

#### Platform-Specific Styles

`Platform.select` picks values per OS without scattering `if (Platform.OS)` through JSX.

```tsx
import { Platform, StyleSheet } from "react-native";
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  shadow: Platform.select({
    ios: { shadowOpacity: 0.15, shadowRadius: 8 },
    android: { elevation: 3 },
    default: {},
  }),
});
```

#### Dynamic Style from Props

Compose with arrays: base styles, then conditionals, then overrides from props.

```tsx
function Pill({ active }: { active: boolean }) {
  return <View style={[styles.pill, active && styles.pillActive]} />;
}
```

#### Percent Width Height

Percentages are relative to the parent. Combine with `flex` carefully - know which constraint wins.

```tsx
<View style={{ width: "100%", maxWidth: 480, alignSelf: "center" }} />
```

#### Border Radius Shadows

iOS uses shadow\* props; Android uses `elevation`. Set both when you need cross-platform depth.

```tsx
const card = {
  borderRadius: 12,
  backgroundColor: "#fff",
  ...Platform.select({
    ios: { shadowColor: "#000", shadowOpacity: 0.12, shadowRadius: 6, shadowOffset: { width: 0, height: 2 } },
    android: { elevation: 4 },
  }),
};
```

#### useWindowDimensions

Subscribe to window size so layout updates on rotation and split-screen without a manual Dimensions listener.

```tsx
import { useWindowDimensions, View } from "react-native";
 
const { width } = useWindowDimensions();
const columns = width > 600 ? 2 : 1;
```

#### PixelRatio Rounding

Round layout numbers when you need crisp hairlines on high-DPI screens.

```tsx
import { PixelRatio, StyleSheet } from "react-native";
 
const hairline = StyleSheet.hairlineWidth; // or 1 / PixelRatio.get()
```

#### StyleSheet.flatten Compose

`StyleSheet.flatten` merges style arrays into one object - handy for debugging or third-party props that need a plain object.

```tsx
const flat = StyleSheet.flatten([styles.base, props.style]);
```

## Related

* [Core Views and Text](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/code-reference/core-views-and-text/) - components these styles attach to
* [Lists and Virtualization](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/code-reference/lists-and-virtualization/) - row layout at list scale
* [Performance and Lists](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/code-reference/performance-and-lists/) - avoid inline style thrash in hot paths

* [reactnative.dev/docs](https://reactnative.dev/docs/getting-started) - full RN documentation
* [reactnative.dev](https://reactnative.dev/) - official React Native site
* [react.dev](https://react.dev/) - core React concepts RN builds on

Dokumen: TextInput and Forms
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/code-reference/textinput-and-forms/

# TextInput and Forms

Text entry, keyboard configuration, focus management, and simple form state patterns on mobile.

Highlights / TextInput and Forms

* Controlled TextInput
* Secure Password Field
* Focus Next Field
* Switch Controlled
* Keyboard dismiss

#### Controlled TextInput

Drive `value` from state and update with `onChangeText` (string, not a DOM event).

```tsx
import { TextInput } from "react-native";
 
const [email, setEmail] = useState("");
return (
  <TextInput
    value={email}
    onChangeText={setEmail}
    autoCapitalize="none"
    keyboardType="email-address"
  />
);
```

#### Secure Password Field

`secureTextEntry` masks characters. Pair with a show/hide toggle via state.

```tsx
<TextInput
  value={password}
  onChangeText={setPassword}
  secureTextEntry={!visible}
  textContentType="password"
/>
```

#### Keyboard Types

Pick a keyboard that matches the data: `email-address`, `numeric`, `phone-pad`, `url`, and platform variants.

```tsx
<TextInput keyboardType="number-pad" value={code} onChangeText={setCode} />
```

#### returnKeyType Submit

Label the return key (`next`, `done`, `send`, `go`) so users know what happens next.

```tsx
<TextInput returnKeyType="next" onSubmitEditing={() => passwordRef.current?.focus()} />
```

#### Multiline TextInput

Set `multiline` for notes. Control height with styles; `textAlignVertical="top"` helps on Android.

```tsx
<TextInput
  multiline
  value={notes}
  onChangeText={setNotes}
  style={{ minHeight: 96, textAlignVertical: "top" }}
/>
```

#### Auto Capitalize Correct

Disable aggressive auto-correct for emails, codes, and usernames.

```tsx
<TextInput
  autoCapitalize="none"
  autoCorrect={false}
  autoComplete="email"
  value={email}
  onChangeText={setEmail}
/>
```

#### Focus Next Field

Hold refs to inputs and call `.focus()` from `onSubmitEditing` for multi-field forms.

```tsx
const passwordRef = useRef<TextInput>(null);
// email field:
onSubmitEditing={() => passwordRef.current?.focus()}
// password:
<TextInput ref={passwordRef} />
```

#### onSubmitEditing Form

Submit when the user hits the keyboard action on the last field.

```tsx
<TextInput
  returnKeyType="go"
  onSubmitEditing={onSubmit}
  blurOnSubmit
  value={query}
  onChangeText={setQuery}
/>
```

#### Placeholder and Selection Color

Theme placeholders and caret/selection colors for brand consistency.

```tsx
<TextInput
  placeholder="Search"
  placeholderTextColor="#9ca3af"
  selectionColor="#2563eb"
  value={q}
  onChangeText={setQ}
/>
```

#### Editable False ReadOnly

Disable editing without removing the field from layout - useful for review steps.

```tsx
<TextInput value={accountId} editable={false} selectTextOnFocus />
```

#### maxLength Counter

Cap input length and optionally show a live counter beside the field.

```tsx
const max = 120;
<TextInput maxLength={max} value={bio} onChangeText={setBio} />
<Text>{bio.length}/{max}</Text>
```

#### Switch Controlled

Boolean toggles use `value` and `onValueChange` on `Switch`.

```tsx
import { Switch } from "react-native";
 
<Switch value={enabled} onValueChange={setEnabled} />
```

#### Pressable as Checkbox

Build a custom checkbox row when design systems do not use stock controls.

```tsx
<Pressable
  onPress={() => setChecked((v) => !v)}
  accessibilityRole="checkbox"
  accessibilityState={{ checked }}
>
  <Text>{checked ? "☑" : "☐"} Agree to terms</Text>
</Pressable>
```

#### Form State Object

Group related fields when they submit together; spread previous state on each change.

```tsx
const [form, setForm] = useState({ name: "", email: "" });
const setField = (k: keyof typeof form, v: string) =>
  setForm((f) => ({ ...f, [k]: v }));
```

#### Keyboard dismiss

Dismiss the keyboard from a toolbar button or tap-outside handler.

```tsx
import { Keyboard } from "react-native";
 
function onDone() {
  Keyboard.dismiss();
  onSubmit();
}
```

* [Core Views and Text](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/code-reference/core-views-and-text/) - KeyboardAvoidingView wrappers
* [Accessibility and Safe Area](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/code-reference/accessibility-and-safe-area/) - labels for form fields

Dokumen: Component Patterns Best Practices
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/best-practices/

# Component Patterns Best Practices

A condensed summary of the 25 most important best practices drawn from every page in this section.

Highlights / Component Patterns Best Practices

* Split screens into container + presenter before files exceed ~300 lines
* Extract UI state into custom hooks; keep data fetching in containers
* Use compound components for tabs and field groups with shared context
* Prefer headless hooks that return accessibility prop bags
* Never nest Pressable inside Link - use asChild-style prop merging
* Co-locate feature code under features/<name>/ with a single public export

1. **Name the screen vs presenter split:** The screen (container) owns data, navigation, and side effects; the presenter renders props only - if you cannot test UI without mocking fetch, the boundary is wrong.
2. **Co-locate by feature, not by type:** Keep `features/orders/screens`, `hooks`, and `components` together - a global `components/` dump becomes a graveyard of one-off wrappers.
3. **One public export per feature:** Expose `OrdersScreen` from `features/orders/index.ts` - route files import one symbol; internals stay private to the folder.
4. **Extract UI hooks before the third `useState`:** Modal open state, disclosure toggles, and filter chips belong in `useDisclosure` / `useFilters` - not twenty `useState` calls at the top of a screen.
5. **Keep data hooks separate from UI hooks:** `useOrdersQuery` fetches; `useOrderFilters` shapes UI - mixing them makes hooks untestable and over-fetches on unrelated toggles.
6. **Use compound components for multi-part UI:** Tabs, accordions, and field groups share implicit state via context - prop-drilling `selectedIndex` through four layers is a maintenance tax.
7. **Expose intent methods on compound APIs:** Export `selectTab(id)` instead of raw `setIndex` - screens should not bypass validation or analytics hooks wired inside the compound root.
8. **Reach for render props when children need data the parent owns:** List empty states and row skeletons are classic render-prop slots - avoid cloning the parent just to read its state.
9. **Use Expo Router `<Slot />` for layout shells:** Slot patterns flatten deep navigation trees without wrapper hell - the layout owns chrome; leaf routes own content.
10. **Container/presenter naming is documentation:** Suffix `OrdersScreen` + `OrdersView` (or `OrdersPresenter`) so reviewers instantly know which file may call `fetch` or `router.push`.
11. **Test presenters with plain props:** Presenters should render from a props object with zero providers - snapshot and interaction tests run in milliseconds without MSW.
12. **Headless primitives return behavior, not styles:** `useDisclosure` exports `triggerProps` and `contentProps` bags - pre-styled output in the primitive couples every consumer to your design tokens.
13. **Mirror visual state in accessibility props:** Selected tabs and expanded accordions must set `accessibilityState` and `accessibilityRole` - VoiceOver does not read your CSS.
14. **Memoize accessibility prop bags:** Rebuilding `{ onPress, accessibilityRole, … }` inline every render defeats `memo` on list rows - `useMemo` keyed on `open` / `selected`.
15. **Never call hooks inside render props:** `children={() => useFoo()}` violates the Rules of Hooks - extract a named child component or call the hook in the parent.
16. **Use polymorphic `as` with generics:** `BoxProps<E extends ElementType>` preserves `href` vs `onPress` typing - bare `ElementType` erases the host contract.
17. **Prefer asChild over nested touchables:** Merging props onto Expo Router `Link` avoids invalid `Pressable > Link` trees and fixes focus order on web targets.
18. **Enforce a single child for asChild:** `Children.only` fails fast when designers wrap two nodes - document the constraint in Storybook examples.
19. **Chain onPress handlers deliberately:** Parent and child both fire by default - document precedence when navigation should swallow the parent handler.
20. **Split god screens at 300 lines, not 2,000:** Extract presenters and hooks incrementally - waiting until a file is unmaintainable guarantees a risky big-bang refactor.
21. **Move FlatList renderItem to a memoized row component:** Inline 200-line `renderItem` closures re-create every parent render and block virtualization wins.
22. **Validate route params at the container:** God screens branch on twelve raw string params - parse `useLocalSearchParams` with Zod in the screen container before passing typed props down.
23. **Keep platform switches in presenters or tokens:** Repeated `Platform.OS` ternaries through JSX signal a missing presenter split or design-system variant.
24. **Reserve global stores for cross-route state:** Bottom-sheet open state for one screen does not belong in Zustand - local state or a feature-scoped context is enough.
25. **Unit-test headless hooks, snapshot one skin:** Test `useDisclosure` behavior in isolation; integration-test a single styled reference component - not every consumer markup tree.

## FAQs

When should I reach for compound components vs context alone?

* Compound components when the public API is static parts (`Tabs.List`, `Tabs.Panel`) that must stay in sync.
* Raw context when only one wrapper exists and the API is a single provider + hook.

Is container/presenter overkill for small screens?

* A 80-line screen can stay combined - split when you add fetching, navigation, or a second presenter variant (loading/error).
* The split pays off the first time you write a presenter test without MSW.

How is asChild different from passing children?

* asChild merges accessibility and press props onto the child host - the child becomes the interactive element.
* Plain children render inside a wrapper `Pressable`, which breaks link semantics and nesting rules.

What is the first extraction from a god screen?

* The presentational JSX block into a `*View` component with typed props.
* Leave fetch and `router.push` in the screen file until the view stabilizes.

Should design-system buttons be headless?

* Primitives (disclosure, tabs, combobox) should be headless or compound.
* Opinionated branded buttons can ship styled - not every atom needs a hook twin.

Do render props still matter with hooks?

* Yes when the parent owns data the child layout should not fetch - hooks replace render props only when the child can call the hook directly at the top level.

What file belongs in app/ vs features/?

* `app/` routes stay thin - import `FeatureScreen` from `features/` and render it.
* Business logic never exports from route files for other features to import.

## Related

* [Component Patterns Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/component-patterns-basics/) - screen/presenter tour and folder conventions
* [Custom Hooks for UI Logic](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/custom-hooks-for-ui-logic/) - extracting stateful UI without prop drilling
* [Compound Components](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/compound-components/) - tabs, accordions, and field groups
* [Container/Presenter on Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/container-presenter-on-mobile/) - testable data/UI split
* [Headless Components](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/headless-components/) - logic-only primitives and a11y bags
* [Anti-Patterns: God Screens](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/anti-patterns-god-screens/) - how large screens fail and how to split them

Dokumen: Component Patterns Basics
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/component-patterns-basics/

# Component Patterns Basics

10 examples to get you started with Component Patterns - 7 basic and 3 intermediate.

Highlights / Component Patterns Basics

* Screens wire navigation and data; presentational components own layout and styles only
* Feature folders colocate screens, hooks, and UI so a module can be moved or deleted in one cut
* Custom hooks extract refresh, pagination, and form state without prop drilling through the tree
* Compound components share implicit state via context - ideal for tabs, cards, and field groups
* Container/presenter splits async work from pure UI so presenters are easy to snapshot-test
* Headless hooks return state and handlers; design-system components decide colors, spacing, and motion

## Prerequisites

These patterns apply to any React Native project. The snippets assume a standard **Expo SDK 57** TypeScript app scaffolded with create-expo-app.

```bash
npx create-expo-app@latest MyPatternsApp --template blank-typescript
cd MyPatternsApp
npx expo start
```

Replace `App.tsx` with each example to run it immediately. No extra packages are required beyond the default Expo template - patterns are about **how you structure components**, not which libraries you install.

> **Tooling:** These examples target **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4), **React Native 0.86.0**, and **React 19.2.3**.

---

## Basic Examples

### 1. Screen vs Presentational Split

A **screen** owns routing concerns, data loading, and side effects. A **presentational** component receives props and renders UI - no fetches, no navigation calls.

```tsx
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { ActivityIndicator, StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
type User = { id: string; name: string };
 
function ProfileView({ user }: { user: User }) {
  return (
    <View style={styles.card}>
      <Text style={styles.name}>{user.name}</Text>
      <Text style={styles.meta}>ID: {user.id}</Text>
    </View>
  );
}
 
export default function ProfileScreen() {
  const [user, setUser] = useState<User | null>(null);
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true);
 
  useEffect(() => {
    let cancelled = false;
    (async () => {
      const response = await fetch("https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users/1");
      const data = (await response.json()) as User;
      if (!cancelled) {
        setUser(data);
        setLoading(false);
      }
    })();
    return () => {
      cancelled = true;
    };
  }, []);
 
  if (loading) return <ActivityIndicator style={styles.loader} />;
  if (!user) return <Text style={styles.error}>User not found</Text>;
 
  return <ProfileView user={user} />;
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  loader: { flex: 1, justifyContent: "center" },
  error: { flex: 1, textAlign: "center", marginTop: 48, color: "#b91c1c" },
  card: { flex: 1, padding: 24, gap: 4 },
  name: { fontSize: 22, fontWeight: "700" },
  meta: { fontSize: 14, color: "#6b7280" },
});
```

* **`ProfileScreen`** decides *when* to show loading, error, or content - that orchestration belongs at the screen boundary
* **`ProfileView`** is pure presentation: given a `user`, it always renders the same tree - ideal for Storybook and snapshot tests
* Screens can live in `app/` (Expo Router) or a `screens/` folder; presenters live beside them under `components/`
* If a presentational component starts calling `fetch` or `router.push`, split it again - mixed responsibilities become god screens fast

> **Related:** [Container/Presenter on Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/container-presenter-on-mobile/) - naming, testing, and data boundaries | [Anti-Patterns: God Screens](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/anti-patterns-god-screens/) - when the split fails

---

### 2. Feature Folder Layout

Group everything a feature needs in one directory so engineers can onboard to "Orders" without hunting across the repo.

```text
src/features/orders/
├── index.ts                 # public exports for the feature
├── screens/
│   └── OrdersScreen.tsx     # route entry, wires hooks + presenter
├── components/
│   └── OrderList.tsx        # presentational list
├── hooks/
│   └── useOrders.ts         # fetch, refresh, pagination
└── types.ts                 # Order, OrderStatus, etc.
```

```ts
// src/features/orders/index.ts
export { OrdersScreen } from "./screens/OrdersScreen";
export type { Order } from "./types";
```

* **`screens/`** holds route-facing containers; **`components/`** holds reusable UI inside the feature
* **`hooks/`** keeps stateful behavior out of JSX - screens stay thin orchestration layers
* **`index.ts`** is the feature's public API - other features import from here, not deep paths
* Shared design tokens and primitives still live in `src/components/ui/`; feature folders own product-specific composition

> **Related:** [Component Patterns Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/best-practices/) - consistency without over-abstraction

---

### 3. Typed Presentational Props

Explicit prop types document what UI a component needs and prevent screens from leaking implementation details.

```tsx
import { Pressable, StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
type OrderRowProps = {
  title: string;
  total: string;
  status: "pending" | "shipped" | "delivered";
  onPress: () => void;
};
 
export function OrderRow({ title, total, status, onPress }: OrderRowProps) {
  return (
    <Pressable style={styles.row} onPress={onPress} accessibilityRole="button">
      <View style={styles.textBlock}>
        <Text style={styles.title}>{title}</Text>
        <Text style={styles.total}>{total}</Text>
      </View>
      <Text style={[styles.badge, styles[`badge_${status}`]]}>{status}</Text>
    </Pressable>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  row: {
    flexDirection: "row",
    alignItems: "center",
    padding: 16,
    borderBottomWidth: StyleSheet.hairlineWidth,
    borderBottomColor: "#e5e7eb",
  },
  textBlock: { flex: 1, gap: 2 },
  title: { fontSize: 16, fontWeight: "600" },
  total: { fontSize: 14, color: "#6b7280" },
  badge: { fontSize: 12, fontWeight: "600", textTransform: "capitalize" },
  badge_pending: { color: "#d97706" },
  badge_shipped: { color: "#2563eb" },
  badge_delivered: { color: "#16a34a" },
});
 
export default function App() {
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1, paddingTop: 48 }}>
      <OrderRow
        title="Wireless earbuds"
        total="$129.00"
        status="shipped"
        onPress={() => {}}
      />
    </View>
  );
}
```

* **Discriminated unions** (`status`) make impossible states unrepresentable - the badge style map stays exhaustive
* Presentational props should be **data and callbacks**, not raw `navigation` or `queryClient` objects
* `accessibilityRole="button"` on `Pressable` rows gives VoiceOver/TalkBack a correct role without extra wrappers
* Export prop types (`export type OrderRowProps`) so Storybook stories and tests share the same contract

> **Related:** [Container/Presenter on Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/container-presenter-on-mobile/) - which props cross the container boundary

---

### 4. Custom Hook for UI Logic

Move refresh, pagination, or toggle state into a hook so multiple screens reuse the same behavior without copy-pasting `useState` blocks.

```tsx
import { useCallback, useState } from "react";
import { Pressable, StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
function useRefresh(onRefresh: () => Promise<void>) {
  const [refreshing, setRefreshing] = useState(false);
 
  const refresh = useCallback(async () => {
    setRefreshing(true);
    try {
      await onRefresh();
    } finally {
      setRefreshing(false);
    }
  }, [onRefresh]);
 
  return { refreshing, refresh };
}
 
export default function App() {
  const [lastSynced, setLastSynced] = useState("Never");
 
  const { refreshing, refresh } = useRefresh(async () => {
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 800));
    setLastSynced(new Date().toLocaleTimeString());
  });
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.container}>
      <Text style={styles.label}>Last synced: {lastSynced}</Text>
      <Pressable
        style={[styles.button, refreshing && styles.buttonDisabled]}
        onPress={refresh}
        disabled={refreshing}
      >
        <Text style={styles.buttonText}>
          {refreshing ? "Refreshing…" : "Refresh"}
        </Text>
      </Pressable>
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  container: { flex: 1, justifyContent: "center", alignItems: "center", gap: 16 },
  label: { fontSize: 16, color: "#374151" },
  button: { backgroundColor: "#2563eb", paddingHorizontal: 20, paddingVertical: 12, borderRadius: 10 },
  buttonDisabled: { opacity: 0.6 },
  buttonText: { color: "#fff", fontWeight: "600" },
});
```

* Hooks named **`use*`** can hold UI state (refreshing, expanded, step index) - not only remote data
* Return a **stable `refresh` callback** via `useCallback` so `FlatList` `onRefresh` does not thrash child memoization
* The hook owns the `refreshing` flag; the screen wires it to `RefreshControl` or button `disabled`
* When logic grows (abort, error toast, retry), the hook file expands - the screen component does not

> **Related:** [Custom Hooks for UI Logic](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/custom-hooks-for-ui-logic/) - extraction rules and prop-drilling escape hatches

---

### 5. Compound Tabs

Share tab state through context so consumers compose `Tabs`, `TabList`, and `TabPanel` without prop drilling `activeTab` through every child.

```tsx
import {
  createContext,
  useContext,
  useState,
  type ReactNode,
} from "react";
import { Pressable, StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
type TabsContextValue = {
  active: string;
  setActive: (value: string) => void;
};
 
const TabsContext = createContext<TabsContextValue | null>(null);
 
function useTabsContext() {
  const ctx = useContext(TabsContext);
  if (!ctx) throw new Error("Tabs subcomponents must render inside <Tabs>");
  return ctx;
}
 
function Tabs({
  defaultValue,
  children,
}: {
  defaultValue: string;
  children: ReactNode;
}) {
  const [active, setActive] = useState(defaultValue);
  return (
    <TabsContext.Provider value={{ active, setActive }}>
      <View style={styles.root}>{children}</View>
    </TabsContext.Provider>
  );
}
 
function TabList({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  return <View style={styles.tabList}>{children}</View>;
}
 
function Tab({ value, children }: { value: string; children: ReactNode }) {
  const { active, setActive } = useTabsContext();
  const selected = active === value;
  return (
    <Pressable
      onPress={() => setActive(value)}
      style={[styles.tab, selected && styles.tabSelected]}
      accessibilityRole="tab"
      accessibilityState={{ selected }}
    >
      <Text style={[styles.tabText, selected && styles.tabTextSelected]}>
        {children}
      </Text>
    </Pressable>
  );
}
 
function TabPanel({ value, children }: { value: string; children: ReactNode }) {
  const { active } = useTabsContext();
  if (active !== value) return null;
  return <View style={styles.panel}>{children}</View>;
}
 
export default function App() {
  return (
    <Tabs defaultValue="upcoming">
      <TabList>
        <Tab value="upcoming">Upcoming</Tab>
        <Tab value="past">Past</Tab>
      </TabList>
      <TabPanel value="upcoming">
        <Text>No upcoming events.</Text>
      </TabPanel>
      <TabPanel value="past">
        <Text>Three past events.</Text>
      </TabPanel>
    </Tabs>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  root: { flex: 1, padding: 24, gap: 16 },
  tabList: { flexDirection: "row", gap: 8 },
  tab: { paddingHorizontal: 14, paddingVertical: 8, borderRadius: 999, backgroundColor: "#f3f4f6" },
  tabSelected: { backgroundColor: "#dbeafe" },
  tabText: { color: "#4b5563", fontWeight: "600" },
  tabTextSelected: { color: "#1d4ed8" },
  panel: { padding: 12, backgroundColor: "#f9fafb", borderRadius: 12 },
});
```

* The **parent coordinates** (`Tabs` holds `active`); children read/write through context - the hallmark compound-component API
* Throwing when context is missing catches **`Tab` rendered outside `Tabs`** at dev time instead of silently failing
* `TabPanel` returns `null` for inactive panels - swap for lazy mounting if panels are expensive
* Mobile tabs often scroll horizontally; keep `TabList` as a separate subcomponent so teams can swap layout without changing state logic

> **Related:** [Compound Components](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/compound-components/) - cards, field groups, and API design

### 6. Container and Presenter Names

Make the split obvious in filenames so code review instantly shows which file is allowed to fetch and which is pure UI.

```tsx
// Presenter - no side effects
import { StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
export type WeatherPresenterProps = {
  city: string;
  temperature: number;
  unit: "C" | "F";
};
 
export function WeatherPresenter({ city, temperature, unit }: WeatherPresenterProps) {
  return (
    <View style={styles.card}>
      <Text style={styles.city}>{city}</Text>
      <Text style={styles.temp}>
        {temperature}°{unit}
      </Text>
    </View>
  );
}
 
// Container - loads data, maps to presenter props
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { ActivityIndicator, StyleSheet, Text } from "react-native";
import { WeatherPresenter } from "./WeatherPresenter";
 
export function WeatherContainer() {
  const [data, setData] = useState<WeatherPresenterProps | null>(null);
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true);
 
  useEffect(() => {
    const timer = setTimeout(() => {
      setData({ city: "Austin", temperature: 72, unit: "F" });
      setLoading(false);
    }, 400);
    return () => clearTimeout(timer);
  }, []);
 
  if (loading) return <ActivityIndicator style={styles.loader} />;
  if (!data) return <Text>Weather unavailable</Text>;
 
  return <WeatherPresenter {...data} />;
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  loader: { flex: 1, justifyContent: "center" },
  card: { flex: 1, justifyContent: "center", alignItems: "center", gap: 8 },
  city: { fontSize: 18, color: "#6b7280" },
  temp: { fontSize: 48, fontWeight: "700" },
});
 
export default function App() {
  return <WeatherContainer />;
}
```

* **`WeatherPresenter`** never imports `fetch`, `useEffect`, or navigation - if it does, rename it; it is a screen now
* **`WeatherContainer`** maps remote shapes to presenter props so API churn does not ripple into styles
* Spread `{...data}` only when field names align; prefer explicit mapping when API names differ from UI vocabulary
* In tests, mount the presenter with fixture props; test the container with mocked data layers

> **Related:** [Container/Presenter on Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/container-presenter-on-mobile/) - async boundaries and test doubles

---

### 7. Composition with Children

Accept `children` for flexible layout shells instead of adding a prop for every possible slot.

```tsx
import { type ReactNode } from "react";
import { StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
function Screen({
  title,
  children,
}: {
  title: string;
  children: ReactNode;
}) {
  return (
    <View style={styles.screen}>
      <Text style={styles.title}>{title}</Text>
      <View style={styles.body}>{children}</View>
    </View>
  );
}
 
function Card({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  return <View style={styles.card}>{children}</View>;
}
 
export default function App() {
  return (
    <Screen title="Inbox">
      <Card>
        <Text style={styles.row}>Shipment delayed - tap for details.</Text>
      </Card>
      <Card>
        <Text style={styles.row}>Your refund was processed.</Text>
      </Card>
    </Screen>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  screen: { flex: 1, padding: 24, gap: 16, backgroundColor: "#f9fafb" },
  title: { fontSize: 28, fontWeight: "700" },
  body: { gap: 12 },
  card: {
    backgroundColor: "#fff",
    borderRadius: 12,
    padding: 16,
    borderWidth: StyleSheet.hairlineWidth,
    borderColor: "#e5e7eb",
  },
  row: { fontSize: 15, lineHeight: 22 },
});
```

* **`children`** keeps `Screen` and `Card` APIs small - consumers decide what goes inside without new props per layout
* `ReactNode` accepts elements, strings, fragments, and `null` - the widest renderable type for slot props
* When you need fixed regions (header, footer, actions), add **named props** (`footer={<Actions />}`) alongside `children`
* Deep navigation trees benefit from composition: stack headers and tab badges stay declarative without wrapper hell

> **Related:** [Render Props & Slot Patterns](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/render-props-and-slot-patterns/) - named slots and list renderers

## Intermediate Examples

### 8. Feature Screen Wiring Hook + Presenter

A complete feature slice: the screen is a thin glue layer; the hook owns async work; the presenter renders props.

```tsx
import { useCallback, useEffect, useState } from "react";
import {
  ActivityIndicator,
  FlatList,
  Pressable,
  RefreshControl,
  StyleSheet,
  Text,
  View,
} from "react-native";
 
type Todo = { id: number; title: string; completed: boolean };
 
function useTodos() {
  const [todos, setTodos] = useState<Todo[]>([]);
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true);
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);
 
  const load = useCallback(async () => {
    const response = await fetch("https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/todos?_limit=8");
    if (!response.ok) throw new Error("Failed to load todos");
    return (await response.json()) as Todo[];
  }, []);
 
  const refresh = useCallback(async () => {
    try {
      setError(null);
      setTodos(await load());
    } catch (e) {
      setError(e instanceof Error ? e.message : "Unknown error");
    } finally {
      setLoading(false);
    }
  }, [load]);
 
  useEffect(() => {
    refresh();
  }, [refresh]);
 
  return { todos, loading, error, refresh };
}
 
function TodoListPresenter({
  todos,
  refreshing,
  onRefresh,
}: {
  todos: Todo[];
  refreshing: boolean;
  onRefresh: () => void;
}) {
  return (
    <FlatList
      data={todos}
      keyExtractor={(item) => String(item.id)}
      contentContainerStyle={styles.list}
      refreshControl={
        <RefreshControl refreshing={refreshing} onRefresh={onRefresh} />
      }
      renderItem={({ item }) => (
        <View style={styles.row}>
          <Text style={styles.title}>{item.title}</Text>
          <Text style={styles.meta}>{item.completed ? "Done" : "Open"}</Text>
        </View>
      )}
    />
  );
}
 
export default function TodoScreen() {
  const { todos, loading, error, refresh } = useTodos();
  const [refreshing, setRefreshing] = useState(false);
 
  const handleRefresh = useCallback(async () => {
    setRefreshing(true);
    await refresh();
    setRefreshing(false);
  }, [refresh]);
 
  if (loading) return <ActivityIndicator style={styles.centered} />;
  if (error) {
    return (
      <View style={styles.centered}>
        <Text style={styles.error}>{error}</Text>
        <Pressable style={styles.button} onPress={refresh}>
          <Text style={styles.buttonText}>Retry</Text>
        </Pressable>
      </View>
    );
  }
 
  return (
    <TodoListPresenter
      todos={todos}
      refreshing={refreshing}
      onRefresh={handleRefresh}
    />
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  centered: { flex: 1, justifyContent: "center", alignItems: "center", gap: 12 },
  list: { padding: 16, gap: 8 },
  row: {
    padding: 14,
    backgroundColor: "#fff",
    borderRadius: 10,
    borderWidth: StyleSheet.hairlineWidth,
    borderColor: "#e5e7eb",
    gap: 4,
  },
  title: { fontSize: 15, fontWeight: "600" },
  meta: { fontSize: 13, color: "#6b7280" },
  error: { color: "#b91c1c", fontSize: 16 },
  button: { backgroundColor: "#2563eb", paddingHorizontal: 16, paddingVertical: 10, borderRadius: 8 },
  buttonText: { color: "#fff", fontWeight: "600" },
});
```

* **`useTodos`** is the feature's data hook - screens and tests import the same module
* **`TodoScreen`** handles loading/error branches; **`TodoListPresenter`** assumes happy-path list data
* Pull-to-refresh UI state (`refreshing`) can live in the screen or a dedicated `useRefresh` hook - keep it out of the presenter when possible
* This triad scales: add `types.ts`, move files into `features/todos/`, export `TodoScreen` from `index.ts`

> **Related:** [Custom Hooks for UI Logic](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/custom-hooks-for-ui-logic/) - when to merge or split hooks | [Anti-Patterns: God Screens](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/anti-patterns-god-screens/) - signs the screen is doing too much

---

### 9. Render Prop for List Empty States

Hand list rendering back to the parent when empty, loading, and error UIs differ per screen but pagination logic stays shared.

```tsx
import { type ReactNode } from "react";
import { FlatList, StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
type PaginatedListProps<T> = {
  data: T[];
  loading: boolean;
  renderItem: (item: T) => ReactNode;
  renderEmpty: () => ReactNode;
  keyExtractor: (item: T) => string;
};
 
function PaginatedList<T>({
  data,
  loading,
  renderItem,
  renderEmpty,
  keyExtractor,
}: PaginatedListProps<T>) {
  if (loading) {
    return <View style={styles.centered}>{renderEmpty()}</View>;
  }
 
  return (
    <FlatList
      data={data}
      keyExtractor={keyExtractor}
      contentContainerStyle={data.length === 0 ? styles.centered : styles.list}
      ListEmptyComponent={renderEmpty}
      renderItem={({ item }) => <>{renderItem(item)}</>}
    />
  );
}
 
type Message = { id: string; body: string };
 
export default function App() {
  const messages: Message[] = [];
 
  return (
    <PaginatedList
      data={messages}
      loading={false}
      keyExtractor={(item) => item.id}
      renderItem={(item) => (
        <View style={styles.row}>
          <Text>{item.body}</Text>
        </View>
      )}
      renderEmpty={() => (
        <View style={styles.empty}>
          <Text style={styles.emptyTitle}>Inbox zero</Text>
          <Text style={styles.emptyBody}>New messages will appear here.</Text>
        </View>
      )}
    />
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  list: { padding: 16, gap: 8 },
  centered: { flexGrow: 1, justifyContent: "center", alignItems: "center" },
  row: { padding: 12, backgroundColor: "#fff", borderRadius: 8 },
  empty: { alignItems: "center", gap: 8, padding: 24 },
  emptyTitle: { fontSize: 18, fontWeight: "700" },
  emptyBody: { fontSize: 14, color: "#6b7280", textAlign: "center" },
});
```

* **Render props** (`renderItem`, `renderEmpty`) let each screen customize row and empty UI without forking the list shell
* Generic `<T>` keeps the list reusable across `Message`, `Order`, and `Notification` types
* Custom hooks replaced many render-prop use cases, but **list and slot APIs** still favor render props for flexibility
* `ListEmptyComponent` and an early `loading` branch cover the two empty paths `FlatList` needs on mobile

> **Related:** [Render Props & Slot Patterns](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/render-props-and-slot-patterns/) - slot props vs render props on deep trees

### 10. Headless Hook + Styled Presenter

Return state and event handlers from a logic-only hook; let design-system components own colors, spacing, and platform feedback.

```tsx
import { useCallback, useState, type ReactNode } from "react";
import { Pressable, StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
function useDisclosure(initial = false) {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(initial);
  const toggle = useCallback(() => setOpen((value) => !value), []);
  const close = useCallback(() => setOpen(false), []);
  return { open, toggle, close };
}
 
function AccordionRow({
  title,
  children,
}: {
  title: string;
  children: ReactNode;
}) {
  const { open, toggle } = useDisclosure();
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.row}>
      <Pressable
        onPress={toggle}
        style={styles.header}
        accessibilityRole="button"
        accessibilityState={{ expanded: open }}
      >
        <Text style={styles.title}>{title}</Text>
        <Text style={styles.chevron}>{open ? "−" : "+"}</Text>
      </Pressable>
      {open ? <Text style={styles.body}>{children}</Text> : null}
    </View>
  );
}
 
export default function App() {
  return (
    <View style={styles.screen}>
      <AccordionRow title="Shipping">Arrives in 3–5 business days.</AccordionRow>
      <AccordionRow title="Returns">Free returns within 30 days.</AccordionRow>
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  screen: { flex: 1, padding: 24, gap: 12 },
  row: {
    backgroundColor: "#fff",
    borderRadius: 12,
    borderWidth: StyleSheet.hairlineWidth,
    borderColor: "#e5e7eb",
    overflow: "hidden",
  },
  header: {
    flexDirection: "row",
    justifyContent: "space-between",
    alignItems: "center",
    padding: 16,
  },
  title: { fontSize: 16, fontWeight: "600" },
  chevron: { fontSize: 20, color: "#6b7280" },
  body: { paddingHorizontal: 16, paddingBottom: 16, color: "#4b5563", lineHeight: 20 },
});
```

* **`useDisclosure`** is headless - no `View` imports required, so the same hook powers modals, menus, and accordions
* Presentational components choose **Pressable feedback, typography, and motion**; swap styles per brand without touching logic
* `accessibilityState={{ expanded: open }}` wires accordion semantics for screen readers
* Export headless hooks from your design system package; keep styled wrappers in the app or a themed layer

> **Related:** [Headless Components](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/headless-components/) - logic-only primitives for design systems | [Polymorphic & AsChild Patterns](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/polymorphic-and-aschild-patterns/) - flexible host elements for primitives

Dokumen: Compound Components
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/compound-components/

# Compound Components

Compound components let callers assemble flexible UIs - tabs, cards, form field groups - from named parts that share implicit state. The parent owns `activeIndex` or `isExpanded`; children like `Tabs.List` and `Tabs.Panel` read it through context instead of prop drilling through every slot.

Highlights / Compound Components

* Parent owns state; children declare structure - consumers compose the UI they need
* React Context shares implicit state without long prop lists
* Tabs, accordions, and form fields are the classic mobile compound wins
* Static properties (Tabs.List, Tabs.Panel) document the API in TypeScript
* Throw in development when a sub-component is used outside its provider
* Prefer layout primitives (View, Pressable) inside parts - not opinionated styling

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```tsx
import { createContext, useContext, useState, type ReactNode } from "react";
import { Pressable, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
interface TabsContextValue {
  activeIndex: number;
  setActiveIndex: (index: number) => void;
}
 
const TabsContext = createContext<TabsContextValue | null>(null);
 
function useTabsContext() {
  const ctx = useContext(TabsContext);
  if (!ctx) throw new Error("Tabs.* must be used inside <Tabs>");
  return ctx;
}
 
function Tabs({ defaultIndex = 0, children }: { defaultIndex?: number; children: ReactNode }) {
  const [activeIndex, setActiveIndex] = useState(defaultIndex);
  return (
    <TabsContext.Provider value={{ activeIndex, setActiveIndex }}>
      <View>{children}</View>
    </TabsContext.Provider>
  );
}
 
function TabList({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  return <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", gap: 8 }}>{children}</View>;
}
 
function Tab({ index, children }: { index: number; children: ReactNode }) {
  const { activeIndex, setActiveIndex } = useTabsContext();
  const active = activeIndex === index;
  return (
    <Pressable onPress={() => setActiveIndex(index)}>
      <Text style={{ fontWeight: active ? "700" : "400" }}>{children}</Text>
    </Pressable>
  );
}
 
function TabPanel({ index, children }: { index: number; children: ReactNode }) {
  const { activeIndex } = useTabsContext();
  if (activeIndex !== index) return null;
  return <View>{children}</View>;
}
 
Tabs.List = TabList;
Tabs.Tab = Tab;
Tabs.Panel = TabPanel;
 
// Consumer - reorder, omit, or restyle parts freely
export function SettingsScreen() {
  return (
    <Tabs defaultIndex={0}>
      <Tabs.List>
        <Tabs.Tab index={0}>Account</Tabs.Tab>
        <Tabs.Tab index={1}>Privacy</Tabs.Tab>
      </Tabs.List>
      <Tabs.Panel index={0}>
        <Text>Account settings</Text>
      </Tabs.Panel>
      <Tabs.Panel index={1}>
        <Text>Privacy settings</Text>
      </Tabs.Panel>
    </Tabs>
  );
}
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Several child pieces need the same parent state (active tab, open section, field error)
* Prop lists like `tabLabels`, `tabContents`, `onTabChange` fight flexible layouts
* Design system primitives should stay unstyled while product teams compose structure
* You want an API that reads like JSX - `<Card.Header>` not `renderHeader()`
* Mobile layouts need to reorder chrome (tabs on bottom on phone, side on tablet) without API changes

## Working Example

```tsx
import {
  createContext,
  useCallback,
  useContext,
  useId,
  useMemo,
  useState,
  type ReactNode,
} from "react";
import { Pressable, StyleSheet, Text, TextInput, View } from "react-native";
 
interface AccordionContextValue {
  openId: string | null;
  toggle: (id: string) => void;
}
 
const AccordionContext = createContext<AccordionContextValue | null>(null);
 
function useAccordion() {
  const ctx = useContext(AccordionContext);
  if (!ctx) throw new Error("Accordion.* must be used inside <Accordion>");
  return ctx;
}
 
interface AccordionProps {
  children: ReactNode;
  defaultOpenId?: string | null;
}
 
function Accordion({ children, defaultOpenId = null }: AccordionProps) {
  const [openId, setOpenId] = useState<string | null>(defaultOpenId);
 
  const toggle = useCallback((id: string) => {
    setOpenId((current) => (current === id ? null : id));
  }, []);
 
  const value = useMemo(() => ({ openId, toggle }), [openId, toggle]);
 
  return (
    <AccordionContext.Provider value={value}>
      <View style={styles.accordion}>{children}</View>
    </AccordionContext.Provider>
  );
}
 
interface ItemProps {
  title: string;
  children: ReactNode;
}
 
function AccordionItem({ title, children }: ItemProps) {
  const id = useId();
  const { openId, toggle } = useAccordion();
  const open = openId === id;
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.item}>
      <Pressable
        onPress={() => toggle(id)}
        style={styles.trigger}
        accessibilityRole="button"
        accessibilityState={{ expanded: open }}
      >
        <Text style={styles.triggerText}>{title}</Text>
        <Text style={styles.chevron}>{open ? "▾" : "▸"}</Text>
      </Pressable>
      {open ? <View style={styles.panel}>{children}</View> : null}
    </View>
  );
}
 
interface FieldGroupContextValue {
  error?: string;
}
 
const FieldGroupContext = createContext<FieldGroupContextValue>({});
 
interface FieldGroupProps {
  label: string;
  error?: string;
  children: ReactNode;
}
 
function FieldGroup({ label, error, children }: FieldGroupProps) {
  const value = useMemo(() => ({ error }), [error]);
  return (
    <FieldGroupContext.Provider value={value}>
      <View style={styles.fieldGroup}>
        <Text style={styles.label}>{label}</Text>
        {children}
        {error ? <Text style={styles.error}>{error}</Text> : null}
      </View>
    </FieldGroupContext.Provider>
  );
}
 
function FieldInput(props: React.ComponentProps<typeof TextInput>) {
  const { error } = useContext(FieldGroupContext);
  return (
    <TextInput
      {...props}
      style={[styles.input, error && styles.inputError, props.style]}
      placeholderTextColor="#94a3b8"
    />
  );
}
 
FieldGroup.Input = FieldInput;
 
export default function ProfileFormScreen() {
  const [name, setName] = useState("");
  const nameError = name.length > 0 && name.length < 2 ? "Name is too short" : undefined;
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.screen}>
      <Text style={styles.heading}>Profile</Text>
 
      <Accordion defaultOpenId={null}>
        <AccordionItem title="Personal info">
          <FieldGroup label="Display name" error={nameError}>
            <FieldGroup.Input
              value={name}
              onChangeText={setName}
              placeholder="Jane Doe"
              autoCapitalize="words"
            />
          </FieldGroup>
        </AccordionItem>
 
        <AccordionItem title="Notifications">
          <Text style={styles.body}>
            Push and email preferences live here. The accordion keeps the screen
            short on small phones.
          </Text>
        </AccordionItem>
      </Accordion>
    </View>
  );
}
 
Accordion.Item = AccordionItem;
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  screen: { flex: 1, padding: 16, backgroundColor: "#f8fafc", gap: 16 },
  heading: { fontSize: 24, fontWeight: "700", color: "#0f172a" },
  accordion: { gap: 8 },
  item: { backgroundColor: "#fff", borderRadius: 12, overflow: "hidden" },
  trigger: {
    flexDirection: "row",
    alignItems: "center",
    justifyContent: "space-between",
    padding: 16,
  },
  triggerText: { fontSize: 16, fontWeight: "600", color: "#0f172a" },
  chevron: { fontSize: 14, color: "#64748b" },
  panel: { paddingHorizontal: 16, paddingBottom: 16, gap: 12 },
  fieldGroup: { gap: 6 },
  label: { fontSize: 14, fontWeight: "600", color: "#334155" },
  input: {
    borderWidth: 1,
    borderColor: "#cbd5e1",
    borderRadius: 10,
    padding: 12,
    fontSize: 16,
    backgroundColor: "#fff",
    color: "#0f172a",
  },
  inputError: { borderColor: "#dc2626" },
  error: { fontSize: 13, color: "#dc2626" },
  body: { fontSize: 15, color: "#475569", lineHeight: 22 },
});
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* `Accordion` owns `openId`; `AccordionItem` generates a stable `useId()` and reads shared toggle logic
* `FieldGroup` + `FieldGroup.Input` share error styling without passing `error` into every input prop
* Static properties (`Accordion.Item`, `FieldGroup.Input`) expose a discoverable namespace API
* Consumers control order and nesting - notification copy can sit beside the name field without API changes
* Context values are memoized to avoid re-rendering every item when unrelated state changes

## Deep Dive

### How It Works

* The **root compound component** holds state (`activeIndex`, `openId`, `variant`) and provides it via `React.createContext`.
* **Sub-components** call `useContext` (wrapped in a custom hook) to read and update shared state.
* Children are composed in JSX - the parent does not map over configuration arrays to render slots.
* Static assignment (`Tabs.List = TabList`) attaches parts to the root export for a single import ergonomics.
* React 19 still reconciles children normally; compound parts are ordinary function components.
* Throwing when context is `null` fails fast in development if a part is used outside its provider.

### Compound API Building Blocks

| Piece | Responsibility | RN note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Root (`<Tabs>`) | State, provider, optional layout shell | Often a `View` with `gap` - no ScrollView unless needed |
| List / chrome (`Tabs.List`) | Groups triggers | Use `flexDirection: "row"` or column for bottom tabs |
| Trigger (`Tabs.Tab`) | `Pressable` + `accessibilityRole` | Mark `accessibilityState={{ selected: active }}` |
| Panel (`Tabs.Panel`) | Conditional render or `display: "none"` | Unmount hidden panels to save memory on heavy screens |
| Leaf input (`FieldGroup.Input`) | Forwards refs/props to primitive | Spread `TextInput` props; do not hard-code keyboard types |

### Context Value Stability

```tsx
// Unstable - new object every render re-renders all consumers
<TabsContext.Provider value={{ activeIndex, setActiveIndex }}>
 
// Stable - memoize; stabilize setters with useCallback in the root
const value = useMemo(
  () => ({ activeIndex, setActiveIndex }),
  [activeIndex, setActiveIndex]
);
```

* Only descendants that **read** a changed field re-render when context updates.
* Split hot and cold context if needed: `TabsStateContext` + `TabsActionsContext` for large trees.
* For high-frequency updates (animated scrubbers), prefer a hook or ref instead of context.

### TypeScript Notes

```tsx
import type { ReactNode } from "react";
 
// Namespace typing with static parts
type TabsComponent = ((props: TabsProps) => JSX.Element) & {
  List: typeof TabList;
  Tab: typeof Tab;
  Panel: typeof TabPanel;
};
 
const Tabs = RootTabs as TabsComponent;
Tabs.List = TabList;
Tabs.Tab = Tab;
Tabs.Panel = TabPanel;
 
// Discriminated props on items - invalid combos fail at compile time
type FormFieldProps =
  | { kind: "text"; value: string; onChangeText: (t: string) => void }
  | { kind: "switch"; value: boolean; onValueChange: (v: boolean) => void };
```

* Export context hooks as `useTabsContext` - do not export raw context unless testing.
* Type static parts with intersection types so `Tabs.List` autocompletes in the IDE.
* See [Typing Components & Props](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/typescript-rn/typing-components-and-props/) for discriminated unions on variant parts.

## Gotchas

* **Missing provider guard** - Using `Tabs.Tab` outside `<Tabs>` reads `null` context and silently misbehaves. **Fix:** Throw in `useTabsContext()` with a clear error message.
* **Unstable context value** - Inline `value={{ activeIndex, setActiveIndex }}` re-renders every consumer each parent render. **Fix:** `useMemo` the value; wrap setters in `useCallback`.
* **Index-based tabs break on reorder** - Hard-coded `index={2}` shifts when marketing inserts a tab. **Fix:** Key tabs by string id (`"account"`) internally; map to index if needed.
* **Mounting all panels at once** - Heavy charts in hidden tabs still run effects and hurt scroll perf. **Fix:** Return `null` from inactive `TabPanel` or lazy-mount on first activation.
* **God compound** - One mega-`<Form>` with 20 sub-parts becomes harder than props. **Fix:** Split into `FieldGroup`, `SelectField`, and `DateField` compounds rather than one export.
* **Styling inside primitives** - Baking brand colors into `Tabs.Tab` blocks white-label apps. **Fix:** Accept `style` / `textStyle` props or a `className` hook for NativeWind consumers.
* **Accessibility state not wired** - Tabs without `accessibilityRole="tab"` and `selected` state confuse VoiceOver/TalkBack. **Fix:** Mirror web ARIA roles on `Pressable` per platform guidance.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Compound components | Flexible layout of related parts sharing state | Single self-contained button with no children |
| Custom hook + dumb parts | One screen needs behavior; no shared child API | External teams compose varied tab layouts from your library |
| Render props | Caller owns markup entirely | JSX readability matters - nested functions get noisy |
| Configuration arrays | Fixed-order tabs from CMS JSON | Designers reorder chrome per platform frequently |
| Single component + many props | ≤3 variants, no structural flexibility | Prop list exceeds ~8 optional layout props |
| Headless + slots | Design system needs total style control | Internal app with one visual language |

## FAQs

What makes a component compound?

* A parent provides **shared state** through context (or cloneElement in older patterns).
* Children are **named parts** composed in JSX, not opaque configuration objects.
* The caller controls **structure and order** - the library does not hard-code one layout.

Compound components vs React Context - what is the difference?

* Compound components are a **pattern** built on context (or scoped state).
* Raw context exports a provider and hook; compound wraps that into ergonomic sub-components.
* Prefer compounds for design-system APIs; raw context for app-level theme or auth.

Should inactive tab panels stay mounted?

* **Unmount** when panels run heavy effects, map views, or video players.
* **Keep mounted** when switching back must preserve scroll position or form input.
* Expose `unmountOnBlur?: boolean` on the root if both use cases matter.

How do I type static properties like Tabs.List?

* Define the root function, then intersect with `{ List: typeof TabList; ... }`.
* Cast once when attaching parts, or build an object literal and assert the namespace type.
* Re-export a single `Tabs` symbol so consumers import one name.

Gotcha: Why do all accordion items re-render on toggle?

* A new context value object each render notifies every `useContext` subscriber.
* Memoize the provider value and split state vs actions if lists are large.
* Wrap item bodies in `memo` when the panel content is expensive.

Can compound components work with Expo Router layouts?

* Yes - a layout can render `<Tabs>` around a `<Slot />` for nested routes.
* Route-driven tabs still benefit from compound triggers that call `router.push`.
* See [Render Props & Slot Patterns](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/render-props-and-slot-patterns/) for slot composition.

How do form field compounds integrate with validation libraries?

* Root `FieldGroup` accepts `error` from React Hook Form's `fieldState.error?.message`.
* Keep validation logic outside the compound - it only displays error chrome.
* Pass `onChangeText` / `value` through `FieldGroup.Input` unchanged.

Is cloneElement still used for compound components?

* Context is the modern default - less fragile than reaching into child props.
* `cloneElement` appears in legacy libraries; new RN design systems should use context.
* React 19 `ref` as a prop simplifies forwarding without `cloneElement`.

How many sub-components is too many?

* If consumers routinely use only one sub-part, the API may be over-factored.
* Aim for 3–6 parts per compound (`Root`, `List`, `Trigger`, `Panel`, `Input`).
* Split into multiple compounds linked by shared hooks when namespaces grow unwieldy.

Gotcha: useId collisions across servers?

* `useId` is per React tree - safe for accordion item ids on mobile.
* Do not persist `useId` output to storage; generate server ids separately for APIs.

How do bottom tabs differ from compound tabs?

* React Navigation / Expo Router bottom tabs are **navigators** with route state.
* Compound tabs are **in-screen** UI for settings, filters, or wizard steps.
* Use navigators when each tab is a route; use compounds for local panel switching.

Can I forward styles to every part?

```tsx
function Tab({ index, children, style }: TabProps) {
  const { activeIndex, setActiveIndex } = useTabsContext();
  const active = activeIndex === index;
  return (
    <Pressable onPress={() => setActiveIndex(index)} style={[styles.tab, style]}>
      <Text>{children}</Text>
    </Pressable>
  );
}
```

* Accept optional `style` / `textStyle` on each part for brand overrides.
* Document which styles merge with defaults vs replace them.

How does this relate to custom hooks?

* Extract state logic into `useTabsState()` when multiple roots need the same behavior.
* Compound root calls the hook and passes the result into context.
* See [Custom Hooks for UI Logic](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/custom-hooks-for-ui-logic/) for the hook layer.

Should compound roots render a ScrollView?

* Default to `View` - callers wrap in `ScrollView` when content overflows.
* Built-in `ScrollView` fights nested scroll and keyboard-aware layouts.
* Document max-height behavior for accordion panels inside parent scroll views.
