# Container/Presenter on Mobile

The container/presenter split separates **data and side effects** (fetching, mutations, navigation, analytics) from **pure UI** (layout, styles, conditional rendering from props). On mobile, route screens usually act as containers while reusable list rows, sheets, and empty states stay presenters - which makes Jest tests and Storybook-style previews far cheaper than mounting full navigation trees.

Highlights / Container/Presenter on Mobile

* Containers own data, navigation side effects, and platform wiring
* Presenters are pure UI - props in, JSX out, easy to snapshot test
* Screens are often containers; shared lists and cards are presenters
* TanStack Query belongs in the container layer, not inside design-system atoms
* Co-locate container + presenter per feature before splitting across packages
* Expo Router route files are thin containers that delegate to feature presenters

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```tsx
import { useCallback } from "react";
import { ActivityIndicator, FlatList, Pressable, Text, View } from "react-native";
import { useQuery } from "@tanstack/react-query";
 
interface User {
  id: string;
  name: string;
}
 
interface UserListProps {
  users: User[];
  onSelect: (id: string) => void;
}
 
// Presenter - no fetch, no router, no global stores
export function UserList({ users, onSelect }: UserListProps) {
  return (
    <FlatList
      data={users}
      keyExtractor={(item) => item.id}
      renderItem={({ item }) => (
        <Pressable onPress={() => onSelect(item.id)}>
          <Text>{item.name}</Text>
        </Pressable>
      )}
    />
  );
}
 
// Container - wires data + navigation
export function UserListScreen() {
  const { data, isPending, isError, refetch } = useQuery({
    queryKey: ["users"],
    queryFn: fetchUsers,
  });
 
  const handleSelect = useCallback((id: string) => {
    // router.push(`/users/${id}`);
  }, []);
 
  if (isPending) return <ActivityIndicator />;
  if (isError) return <Text>Failed to load users</Text>;
 
  return <UserList users={data ?? []} onSelect={handleSelect} />;
}
 
async function fetchUsers(): Promise<User[]> {
  const res = await fetch("https://example.com/api/users");
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error("Network error");
  return res.json();
}
```

**When to reach for this:**

* A screen mixes `useQuery`, `useRouter`, and 200 lines of JSX styling
* You want to snapshot-test UI states (loading, empty, error) without mocking fetch
* Designers iterate on layout while engineers stabilize data contracts
* The same list UI appears in a modal and a full screen with different data sources
* E2E tests should hit containers; unit tests should hit presenters

## Working Example

```tsx
import { useCallback } from "react";
import {
  ActivityIndicator,
  FlatList,
  Pressable,
  RefreshControl,
  StyleSheet,
  Text,
  View,
} from "react-native";
import { useRouter } from "expo-router";
import { useQuery } from "@tanstack/react-query";
 
interface Project {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  status: "active" | "archived";
  openTasks: number;
}
 
type LoadState = "loading" | "error" | "empty" | "ready";
 
interface ProjectsPresenterProps {
  state: LoadState;
  projects: Project[];
  refreshing: boolean;
  errorMessage?: string;
  onRefresh: () => void;
  onPressProject: (id: string) => void;
}
 
export function ProjectsPresenter({
  state,
  projects,
  refreshing,
  errorMessage,
  onRefresh,
  onPressProject,
}: ProjectsPresenterProps) {
  if (state === "loading") {
    return (
      <View style={styles.center}>
        <ActivityIndicator size="large" />
        <Text style={styles.muted}>Loading projects…</Text>
      </View>
    );
  }
 
  if (state === "error") {
    return (
      <View style={styles.center}>
        <Text style={styles.error}>{errorMessage ?? "Something went wrong"}</Text>
        <Pressable onPress={onRefresh} style={styles.button}>
          <Text style={styles.buttonText}>Try again</Text>
        </Pressable>
      </View>
    );
  }
 
  if (state === "empty") {
    return (
      <View style={styles.center}>
        <Text style={styles.heading}>No projects yet</Text>
        <Text style={styles.muted}>Pull to refresh after your first sync.</Text>
      </View>
    );
  }
 
  return (
    <FlatList
      data={projects}
      keyExtractor={(item) => item.id}
      refreshControl={
        <RefreshControl refreshing={refreshing} onRefresh={onRefresh} />
      }
      renderItem={({ item }) => (
        <Pressable
          onPress={() => onPressProject(item.id)}
          style={styles.card}
        >
          <View style={styles.cardHeader}>
            <Text style={styles.title}>{item.name}</Text>
            <Text
              style={[
                styles.badge,
                item.status === "archived" && styles.badgeMuted,
              ]}
            >
              {item.status}
            </Text>
          </View>
          <Text style={styles.meta}>{item.openTasks} open tasks</Text>
        </Pressable>
      )}
      ItemSeparatorComponent={() => <View style={styles.separator} />}
      contentContainerStyle={styles.list}
    />
  );
}
 
const MOCK_PROJECTS: Project[] = [
  { id: "p1", name: "Expo SDK 57 upgrade", status: "active", openTasks: 4 },
  { id: "p2", name: "Checkout redesign", status: "active", openTasks: 11 },
  { id: "p3", name: "Legacy billing", status: "archived", openTasks: 0 },
];
 
async function fetchProjects(): Promise<Project[]> {
  await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 400));
  return MOCK_PROJECTS;
}
 
function toLoadState(
  isPending: boolean,
  isError: boolean,
  count: number
): LoadState {
  if (isPending) return "loading";
  if (isError) return "error";
  if (count === 0) return "empty";
  return "ready";
}
 
export default function ProjectsScreen() {
  const router = useRouter();
  const query = useQuery({
    queryKey: ["projects"],
    queryFn: fetchProjects,
  });
 
  const projects = query.data ?? [];
  const state = toLoadState(query.isPending, query.isError, projects.length);
 
  const handleRefresh = useCallback(() => {
    void query.refetch();
  }, [query]);
 
  const handlePressProject = useCallback(
    (id: string) => {
      router.push(`/projects/${id}`);
    },
    [router]
  );
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.screen}>
      <ProjectsPresenter
        state={state}
        projects={projects}
        refreshing={query.isFetching && !query.isPending}
        errorMessage={query.error instanceof Error ? query.error.message : undefined}
        onRefresh={handleRefresh}
        onPressProject={handlePressProject}
      />
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  screen: { flex: 1, backgroundColor: "#f8fafc" },
  center: {
    flex: 1,
    alignItems: "center",
    justifyContent: "center",
    padding: 24,
    gap: 12,
  },
  heading: { fontSize: 20, fontWeight: "700", color: "#0f172a" },
  muted: { fontSize: 15, color: "#64748b", textAlign: "center" },
  error: { fontSize: 15, color: "#dc2626", textAlign: "center" },
  button: {
    backgroundColor: "#2563eb",
    paddingHorizontal: 16,
    paddingVertical: 10,
    borderRadius: 8,
  },
  buttonText: { color: "#fff", fontWeight: "600" },
  list: { padding: 16 },
  card: {
    backgroundColor: "#fff",
    borderRadius: 12,
    padding: 16,
    gap: 6,
  },
  cardHeader: {
    flexDirection: "row",
    alignItems: "center",
    justifyContent: "space-between",
  },
  title: { fontSize: 17, fontWeight: "600", color: "#0f172a", flex: 1 },
  badge: {
    fontSize: 12,
    fontWeight: "700",
    color: "#2563eb",
    textTransform: "uppercase",
  },
  badgeMuted: { color: "#94a3b8" },
  meta: { fontSize: 14, color: "#475569" },
  separator: { height: 10 },
});
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* `ProjectsScreen` maps TanStack Query flags into a simple `LoadState` union for the presenter
* `ProjectsPresenter` handles every visual branch - loading, error, empty, list - with no fetch imports
* Navigation (`router.push`) stays in the container; the presenter only calls `onPressProject(id)`
* `RefreshControl` wiring lives in the presenter; the container supplies `onRefresh` tied to `refetch`
* Tests can render `ProjectsPresenter` with `state="empty"` without a `QueryClientProvider`

## Deep Dive

### How It Works

* **Container** (smart / screen component): subscribes to remote data, global stores, route params, and platform APIs; maps them to a **view model** passed as props.
* **Presenter** (dumb / pure component): renders JSX from props; avoids `useQuery`, `useRouter`, and implicit globals.
* The boundary is a **typed props interface** - that contract is what you snapshot-test and what design tools consume.
* Containers may call custom hooks (`useProjectsQuery`) to stay thin - hooks are not presenters.
* Expo Router files (`app/projects/index.tsx`) should default-export a container that imports a colocated presenter from `features/projects/`.
* Multiple containers can reuse one presenter when the UI is identical but data sources differ (search modal vs tab screen).

### Responsibility Split

| Concern | Container | Presenter |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `useQuery` / mutations | ✓ |  |
| `useRouter` / deep links | ✓ |  |
| Analytics events | ✓ (or hook called by container) |  |
| `StyleSheet` / layout | Optional shell | ✓ primary |
| Empty / error / loading UI | Maps flags to `state` prop | ✓ renders branches |
| `FlatList` performance | Passes stable callbacks | ✓ `memo` on rows |
| Form validation schema | ✓ loads defaults from API | ✓ shows field errors from props |

### Folder Layout on Mobile

```
features/
  projects/
    projects-screen.tsx          # container (default export for route)
    projects-presenter.tsx       # pure UI
    use-projects-query.ts        # optional data hook
    project-card.tsx             # smaller presenter
    __tests__/
      projects-presenter.test.tsx
app/
  projects/
    index.tsx                    # re-export ProjectsScreen
```

* Keep presenters next to their primary container - not in a distant `components/` dump.
* Share presenters across features only when the props contract is truly identical.
* Route files stay one line when possible: `export { default } from "@/features/projects/projects-screen";`

### View Model Props

```tsx
// Prefer explicit unions over many booleans
type ProjectsViewModel =
  | { status: "loading" }
  | { status: "error"; message: string }
  | { status: "empty" }
  | { status: "ready"; projects: Project[]; refreshing: boolean };
 
interface ProjectsPresenterProps extends ProjectsViewModel {
  onRefresh: () => void;
  onPressProject: (id: string) => void;
}
```

* Discriminated unions make impossible states unrepresentable - no `isLoading && isError`.
* See [Typing Components & Props](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/typescript-rn/typing-components-and-props/) for union typing patterns.
* Callback props are always named `on*` and defined in the container with `useCallback`.

### TypeScript Notes

```tsx
// Presenter props document the full visual contract
interface ProjectCardProps {
  project: Project;
  onPress: (id: string) => void;
}
 
// Container maps API DTO → view model
function mapProjectDto(dto: ProjectDto): Project {
  return {
    id: dto.project_id,
    name: dto.display_name,
    status: dto.is_archived ? "archived" : "active",
    openTasks: dto.open_task_count,
  };
}
```

* Map snake\_case API fields before they reach presenters - UI types match design language.
* Export presenter props types for tests and Storybook-style harnesses.
* Route params typed via [Typing Navigation & Route Params](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/typescript-rn/typing-navigation-and-route-params/) stay in the container.

## Gotchas

* **Presenter sneaks in `useQuery`** - A "dumb" list that imports TanStack Query cannot render in isolation. **Fix:** Lift query to the container; pass `projects` and `state` down.
* **Leaky navigation in presenters** - `router.push` inside a card component couples UI to Expo Router. **Fix:** Pass `onPressProject`; let the container decide the route.
* **Boolean prop soup** - `isLoading`, `isError`, `hasData`, `isRefreshing` combos explode. **Fix:** Single discriminated `state` or `status` union prop.
* **Container still 800 lines of JSX** - Splitting the file but leaving all markup in the container defeats the pattern. **Fix:** Move visual branches to the presenter; container returns one JSX element.
* **Over-splitting tiny screens** - Two static labels do not need two files. **Fix:** Apply the split when fetch, navigation, or three+ UI states appear.
* **Unstable callback props** - Inline `onPress={() => router.push(...)}` in the container recreates each render. **Fix:** `useCallback` in the container so presenter children can `memo`.
* **Testing the container by default** - Mocking `QueryClient`, `expo-router`, and native modules in every test is slow. **Fix:** Test the presenter for UI; reserve one integration test per critical container path.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Container / presenter | Screens with network + several UI states | Static marketing page with no data |
| Custom hook + single component | Medium screens where file split feels heavy | Presenter reuse across modal and route |
| TanStack Query in presenter via HOC | Legacy migration only | Greenfield - explicit container is clearer |
| Server Components | N/A on RN today | - |
| MVVM with view models in hooks | Large teams formalize contracts | Small feature with one list |
| God screen (no split) | Prototype or throwaway | Long-lived production feature |

## FAQs

What is the difference between a container and a screen?

* On mobile, the **screen** is often the container - the file tied to a route.
* The **presenter** is usually not a route; it is imported by one or more containers.
* A screen can render multiple presenters (header + list + footer).

Can presenters use useState?

* **Ephemeral UI state** (expanded row, pressed chip) can live in presenters.
* **Server or route-derived state** belongs in containers.
* If modal open state triggers navigation, keep it in the container.

Where does TanStack Query go?

* In the container or a dedicated `useProjectsQuery` hook called by the container.
* Presenters receive mapped data and status - not raw `UseQueryResult`.
* Pull-to-refresh calls `refetch` in the container, passed as `onRefresh`.

How do I test a presenter without a device?

```tsx
import { render, screen } from "@testing-library/react-native";
import { ProjectsPresenter } from "../projects-presenter";
 
test("shows empty state", () => {
  render(
    <ProjectsPresenter
      state="empty"
      projects={[]}
      refreshing={false}
      onRefresh={jest.fn()}
      onPressProject={jest.fn()}
    />
  );
  expect(screen.getByText("No projects yet")).toBeTruthy();
});
```

* No `QueryClientProvider`, no router mock - only props.
* Snapshot the four `LoadState` branches for regression safety.

Gotcha: Presenter imports useRouter by accident?

* Any router hook forces tests to mock `expo-router`.
* Pass `onPress` callbacks from the container instead.
* Search the presenter for `expo-router`, `@tanstack`, and `zustand` - they should be absent.

How thin should an Expo Router route file be?

* Ideal: re-export the feature container - `export { default } from "@/features/projects/projects-screen";`
* Acceptable: tiny container when the route only adds `Stack.Screen` options.
* Avoid business logic in `app/` - keeps file-based routing a map, not a junk drawer.

Container/presenter vs hooks - what goes where?

* **Hook**: reusable data + effect logic (`useProjectsQuery`).
* **Container**: composes hooks, router, analytics; maps to view props.
* **Presenter**: renders props; may use small local UI state.
* See [Custom Hooks for UI Logic](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/custom-hooks-for-ui-logic/) for UI-only hooks in presenters.

Should error boundaries wrap container or presenter?

* Wrap at the **container / route** level so the whole screen can fall back.
* Presenters can render inline error UI when `state="error"` - that is expected data failure, not a render crash.
* Use React error boundaries for unexpected throws in either layer.

How do I share a presenter between a modal and a screen?

* Export the same `ProjectsPresenter` from `features/projects/`.
* `ProjectsModalContainer` and `ProjectsScreen` differ only in data source and `onPress` routing.
* Modals still benefit from the split - test the presenter once.

Gotcha: Mapping query flags wrong?

* `isFetching` is true during background refresh - not the same as initial `isPending`.
* Pass `refreshing={isFetching && !isPending}` to `RefreshControl`.
* Initial load should not show the pull spinner and the full-screen loader simultaneously.

Is this the same as atomic design?

* Presenters overlap with **molecules/organisms** but the split is about **data boundaries**, not size.
* A large presenter is fine if it stays prop-driven.
* Containers map domain data; atoms stay style-only.

How does this help performance?

* Presenters wrapped in `memo` re-render only when view props change.
* Containers isolate query subscription churn from deep presenter subtrees when props are stable.
* Pair with guidance in [Props, State & Re-renders on Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/rn-fundamentals/props-state-and-re-renders-on-mobile/).

Can generated API clients live in presenters?

* No - keep OpenAPI/Zod parsing in the container or a `api/` module.
* Presenters receive already-validated view models.
* See [Typing API Responses & Zod](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/typescript-rn/typing-api-responses-and-zod/).

When is one file enough?

* Read-only UI with no network and no navigation side effects.
* Prototypes exploring layout before the data contract exists.
* Split once you add the second state branch (error/empty) or second consumer.

## Related

* [Component Patterns Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/component-patterns-basics/) - screen vs presentational conventions
* [Custom Hooks for UI Logic](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/custom-hooks-for-ui-logic/) - hooks containers call before passing props
* [Render Props & Slot Patterns](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/render-props-and-slot-patterns/) - optional handoff from container to presenter
* [Anti-Patterns: God Screens](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/anti-patterns-god-screens/) - when the split was skipped too long
* [Typing API Responses & Zod](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/typescript-rn/typing-api-responses-and-zod/) - validate in the container layer

Dokumen: Custom Hooks for UI Logic
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/custom-hooks-for-ui-logic/

# Custom Hooks for UI Logic

Custom hooks let you extract stateful UI behavior - keyboard offsets, sheet open state, debounced search, scroll-driven headers - into reusable functions that any screen or presentational component can call. You keep JSX in components and move the "how it works" into hooks, which cuts prop drilling without hiding business rules in visual trees.

Highlights / Custom Hooks for UI Logic

* Custom hooks bundle state + effects + handlers into one reusable unit
* Return a small object or tuple - consumers pick only what they need
* UI hooks differ from data hooks: no fetch/cache, only presentation behavior
* Keyboard, sheet, and scroll hooks are the highest-ROI extractions on mobile
* Prefix with use and keep hooks pure - no JSX inside the hook body
* Colocate hooks next to the feature until a second screen needs the same logic

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```tsx
import { useCallback, useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { Keyboard, TextInput, View, type KeyboardEvent } from "react-native";
 
export function useKeyboardHeight() {
  const [height, setHeight] = useState(0);
 
  useEffect(() => {
    const show = (e: KeyboardEvent) => setHeight(e.endCoordinates.height);
    const hide = () => setHeight(0);
 
    const showSub = Keyboard.addListener("keyboardDidShow", show);
    const hideSub = Keyboard.addListener("keyboardDidHide", hide);
 
    return () => {
      showSub.remove();
      hideSub.remove();
    };
  }, []);
 
  return height;
}
 
// Consumer - no prop drilling from a parent
export function CommentComposer() {
  const keyboardHeight = useKeyboardHeight();
 
  return (
    <View style={{ paddingBottom: keyboardHeight }}>
      <TextInput placeholder="Add a comment" />
    </View>
  );
}
```

**When to reach for this:**

* The same `useState` + `useEffect` + handler trio appears in two or more screens
* A parent only exists to pass `isOpen`, `onOpen`, `onClose` through three layers
* Mobile-specific listeners (keyboard, app state, dimensions) clutter a screen component
* You want to unit-test UI behavior without mounting full component trees
* A presentational component should stay dumb while behavior lives beside it

## Working Example

```tsx
import { useCallback, useMemo, useState } from "react";
import {
  FlatList,
  Pressable,
  StyleSheet,
  Text,
  TextInput,
  View,
} from "react-native";
import { useSafeAreaInsets } from "react-native-safe-area-context";
 
type Filter = "all" | "open" | "done";
 
interface Todo {
  id: string;
  title: string;
  done: boolean;
}
 
const SEED: Todo[] = [
  { id: "1", title: "Extract keyboard hook", done: true },
  { id: "2", title: "Wire filter chips", done: false },
  { id: "3", title: "Ship presentational list", done: false },
];
 
function useTodoFilters(initial: Todo[]) {
  const [query, setQuery] = useState("");
  const [filter, setFilter] = useState<Filter>("all");
 
  const visible = useMemo(() => {
    const normalized = query.trim().toLowerCase();
    return initial.filter((todo) => {
      const matchesFilter =
        filter === "all" ||
        (filter === "open" && !todo.done) ||
        (filter === "done" && todo.done);
      const matchesQuery =
        normalized.length === 0 ||
        todo.title.toLowerCase().includes(normalized);
      return matchesFilter && matchesQuery;
    });
  }, [initial, query, filter]);
 
  const counts = useMemo(
    () => ({
      all: initial.length,
      open: initial.filter((t) => !t.done).length,
      done: initial.filter((t) => t.done).length,
    }),
    [initial]
  );
 
  return {
    query,
    setQuery,
    filter,
    setFilter,
    visible,
    counts,
  };
}
 
function useDisclosure(initial = false) {
  const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState(initial);
 
  const open = useCallback(() => setIsOpen(true), []);
  const close = useCallback(() => setIsOpen(false), []);
  const toggle = useCallback(() => setIsOpen((v) => !v), []);
 
  return { isOpen, open, close, toggle };
}
 
interface TodoListProps {
  data: Todo[];
  onToggle: (id: string) => void;
}
 
function TodoList({ data, onToggle }: TodoListProps) {
  return (
    <FlatList
      data={data}
      keyExtractor={(item) => item.id}
      renderItem={({ item }) => (
        <Pressable
          onPress={() => onToggle(item.id)}
          style={[styles.row, item.done && styles.rowDone]}
        >
          <Text style={styles.title}>{item.title}</Text>
          <Text style={styles.badge}>{item.done ? "Done" : "Open"}</Text>
        </Pressable>
      )}
      ItemSeparatorComponent={() => <View style={styles.separator} />}
      contentContainerStyle={styles.list}
      keyboardShouldPersistTaps="handled"
    />
  );
}
 
export default function TodoScreen() {
  const insets = useSafeAreaInsets();
  const [todos, setTodos] = useState(SEED);
  const filters = useTodoFilters(todos);
  const search = useDisclosure(false);
 
  const handleToggle = useCallback((id: string) => {
    setTodos((prev) =>
      prev.map((t) => (t.id === id ? { ...t, done: !t.done } : t))
    );
  }, []);
 
  return (
    <View style={[styles.screen, { paddingTop: insets.top }]}>
      <View style={styles.header}>
        <Text style={styles.heading}>Todos</Text>
        <Pressable onPress={search.toggle} style={styles.iconButton}>
          <Text style={styles.iconButtonText}>{search.isOpen ? "✕" : "⌕"}</Text>
        </Pressable>
      </View>
 
      {search.isOpen ? (
        <TextInput
          autoFocus
          value={filters.query}
          onChangeText={filters.setQuery}
          placeholder="Search todos"
          style={styles.search}
        />
      ) : null}
 
      <View style={styles.chips}>
        {(["all", "open", "done"] as const).map((key) => (
          <Pressable
            key={key}
            onPress={() => filters.setFilter(key)}
            style={[styles.chip, filters.filter === key && styles.chipActive]}
          >
            <Text
              style={[
                styles.chipText,
                filters.filter === key && styles.chipTextActive,
              ]}
            >
              {key} ({filters.counts[key]})
            </Text>
          </Pressable>
        ))}
      </View>
 
      <TodoList data={filters.visible} onToggle={handleToggle} />
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  screen: { flex: 1, backgroundColor: "#f8fafc" },
  header: {
    flexDirection: "row",
    alignItems: "center",
    justifyContent: "space-between",
    paddingHorizontal: 16,
    paddingVertical: 12,
  },
  heading: { fontSize: 22, fontWeight: "700", color: "#0f172a" },
  iconButton: {
    width: 36,
    height: 36,
    borderRadius: 18,
    backgroundColor: "#e2e8f0",
    alignItems: "center",
    justifyContent: "center",
  },
  iconButtonText: { fontSize: 16, fontWeight: "700", color: "#334155" },
  search: {
    marginHorizontal: 16,
    marginBottom: 8,
    padding: 12,
    borderRadius: 10,
    backgroundColor: "#fff",
    borderWidth: 1,
    borderColor: "#cbd5e1",
  },
  chips: { flexDirection: "row", gap: 8, paddingHorizontal: 16, marginBottom: 8 },
  chip: {
    paddingHorizontal: 12,
    paddingVertical: 6,
    borderRadius: 999,
    backgroundColor: "#e2e8f0",
  },
  chipActive: { backgroundColor: "#2563eb" },
  chipText: { fontSize: 13, fontWeight: "600", color: "#334155" },
  chipTextActive: { color: "#fff" },
  list: { paddingHorizontal: 16, paddingBottom: 24 },
  row: {
    flexDirection: "row",
    alignItems: "center",
    backgroundColor: "#fff",
    padding: 14,
    borderRadius: 10,
    gap: 8,
  },
  rowDone: { opacity: 0.7 },
  title: { flex: 1, fontSize: 16, color: "#0f172a" },
  badge: { fontSize: 12, fontWeight: "600", color: "#2563eb" },
  separator: { height: 8 },
});
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* `useTodoFilters` owns search + chip filter state and derived `visible` data - the screen stays readable
* `useDisclosure` replaces three props (`isOpen`, `onOpen`, `onClose`) with one hook call
* `TodoList` is presentational: it receives data and a stable callback, no filter logic inside
* `useMemo` inside the hook keeps derived lists cheap without pushing computation into JSX
* Hooks compose at the screen level; no intermediate wrapper passes behavior down

## Deep Dive

### How It Works

* A custom hook is a **function whose name starts with `use`** and that may call other hooks (`useState`, `useEffect`, `useCallback`, …).
* React associates hook state with the **component instance** that called the hook - not with the hook function globally.
* Each call site gets its own isolated state; two screens calling `useDisclosure()` do not share `isOpen`.
* Hooks run during render on the JS thread; effects registered inside run after paint (or on cleanup).
* Return values are plain objects, tuples, or primitives - consumers destructure what they need.
* Custom hooks are **not** a new React feature - they are the composition pattern for the Rules of Hooks.

### UI Hooks vs Data Hooks

| Kind | Owns | Examples | Usually lives in |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| UI hook | Presentation behavior | `useDisclosure`, `useKeyboardHeight`, `useCollapsibleHeader` | `hooks/use-*.ts` next to the feature |
| Data hook | Remote/cache state | TanStack Query `useQuery`, `useMutation` | `api/` or `queries/` module |
| Domain hook | Business rules | `useCartTotals`, `useCanCheckout` | `features/checkout/hooks/` |
| Platform hook | RN / Expo APIs | `useAppState`, `useNetInfo` wrappers | `lib/platform/` |

* Keep fetch and cache in TanStack Query - wrap it in a thin `useTodosQuery()` if needed, but do not mix keyboard listeners into query hooks.
* UI hooks should be **synchronous from the consumer's perspective** except where they intentionally mirror async platform events.

### Return Shape Conventions

| Pattern | Shape | Good for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Object return | `{ isOpen, open, close }` | Named fields; easy to extend without breaking call sites |
| Tuple return | `[value, setValue]` | Mirrors `useState`; familiar for simple state |
| Split actions | `{ state, actions }` | Large hooks where UI and handlers should not interleave |
| Ref + setter | `{ ref, scrollToTop }` | Scroll views, flat lists, imperative handles |

```tsx
// Prefer stable action references inside the hook
export function useCounter(initial = 0) {
  const [count, setCount] = useState(initial);
 
  const increment = useCallback(() => setCount((c) => c + 1), []);
  const reset = useCallback(() => setCount(initial), [initial]);
 
  return { count, increment, reset };
}
```

### TypeScript Notes

```tsx
import type { Dispatch, SetStateAction } from "react";
 
interface UseTodoFiltersResult {
  query: string;
  setQuery: Dispatch<SetStateAction<string>>;
  filter: "all" | "open" | "done";
  setFilter: Dispatch<SetStateAction<"all" | "open" | "done">>;
  visible: Todo[];
  counts: Record<"all" | "open" | "done", number>;
}
 
// Generic hook - preserves item type through the pipeline
export function useDebouncedValue<T>(value: T, delayMs: number): T {
  const [debounced, setDebounced] = useState(value);
 
  useEffect(() => {
    const id = setTimeout(() => setDebounced(value), delayMs);
    return () => clearTimeout(id);
  }, [value, delayMs]);
 
  return debounced;
}
```

* Export the return type when multiple screens share the hook - see [Typing Components & Props](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/typescript-rn/typing-components-and-props/).
* Type listener events with React Native's exported event types (`KeyboardEvent`, `AppStateStatus`).
* Avoid `any` on hook parameters; generics preserve item types for list filters and selectors.

## Gotchas

* **Calling hooks conditionally** - `if (show) useFoo()` violates the Rules of Hooks and crashes in dev. **Fix:** Call the hook unconditionally; gate behavior inside it or in the consumer.
* **Returning unstable objects every render** - `return { open, close, state: { isOpen } }` where the inner object is recreated causes needless child re-renders. **Fix:** Memoize nested objects or flatten the return shape; stabilize callbacks with `useCallback`.
* **Mixing data fetching into UI hooks** - `useProductSheet` that fetches and manages keyboard height is hard to test and reuse. **Fix:** Split into `useProductQuery` + `useBottomSheet`; compose at the screen.
* **Forgetting native listener cleanup** - Keyboard and `Dimensions` listeners leak if `remove()` is skipped. **Fix:** Return a cleanup function from `useEffect` and call `.remove()` on subscriptions.
* **Sharing mutable refs across instances** - Module-level `let lastOffset = 0` bleeds state between screens. **Fix:** Keep mutable values in `useRef` inside the hook body.
* **Hooks that return JSX** - A hook returning `<Modal />` is a component, not a hook. **Fix:** Return state + handlers; let the caller render JSX (headless pattern - see [Headless Components](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/headless-components/)).
* **Over-abstracting one-off logic** - A hook used exactly once adds indirection without reuse. **Fix:** Inline until the second consumer appears; then extract with a name that describes behavior, not the screen.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Custom UI hook | Reused behavior across screens or fat screens needing clarity | One-off toggle used in a single 20-line component |
| Colocated `useState` in screen | Simple, local state with no reuse | Same listener/effect block copied to three files |
| React Context | Many descendants need the same UI state (theme, wizard step) | Only one child needs `isOpen` |
| Compound components | Related UI pieces share implicit state (tabs, accordion) | Behavior is flat - a single hook return is enough |
| Zustand slice | Cross-tab UI flags (global toast queue, mini-player) | Screen-scoped sheet open state |
| Container component | Behavior tightly coupled to one tree's lifecycle | Multiple presenters need the same logic |

## FAQs

What is the difference between a custom hook and a utility function?

* Custom hooks **may call other hooks**; plain functions may not.
* Hooks participate in React's render cycle - state, effects, and memoization are tied to a component instance.
* Utility functions (`formatCurrency`, `clamp`) belong in `lib/` with no `use` prefix.

Can I call the same custom hook twice in one component?

* Yes - each call creates **independent state**.
* `const a = useDisclosure(); const b = useDisclosure();` gives two unrelated `isOpen` values.
* Name them distinctly: `const header = useDisclosure(); const menu = useDisclosure();`.

Where should I put custom hooks in an Expo Router project?

* Start colocated: `features/inbox/hooks/use-thread-filters.ts`.
* Promote to `hooks/use-keyboard-height.ts` when two unrelated features need it.
* Avoid a single `hooks/` junk drawer until patterns stabilize.

How do custom hooks reduce prop drilling?

* Instead of a parent owning `isOpen` and passing `onClose` through intermediaries, the leaf calls `useDisclosure()` directly.
* Shared behavior moves to the hook; components keep only the props their **layout** needs.
* Context is the alternative when many deep descendants need the same value.

Gotcha: Why does my keyboard hook report zero on Android?

* Some Android keyboards fire `keyboardDidShow` with different timing than iOS.
* Use `keyboardDidShow` / `keyboardDidHide` for layout adjustments; avoid `Will` events unless animating.
* Test on a physical device - emulators often misreport keyboard height.

Should UI hooks accept configuration objects or positional args?

* Prefer a single options object when there are three or more optional parameters.
* Positional args are fine for `(initialValue, delayMs)`-style hooks.
* Default sensibly so call sites stay one line for the common case.

How do I test a custom UI hook?

```tsx
import { renderHook, act } from "@testing-library/react-native";
import { useDisclosure } from "./use-disclosure";
 
test("toggle flips isOpen", () => {
  const { result } = renderHook(() => useDisclosure());
  act(() => result.current.open());
  expect(result.current.isOpen).toBe(true);
});
```

* Use `@testing-library/react-native`'s `renderHook` - no full screen mount required.
* Mock native modules (`Keyboard`, `Dimensions`) at the test boundary.

Can custom hooks replace TanStack Query?

* No - query hooks solve **server state**: caching, stale times, retries.
* UI hooks solve **client presentation**: sheets, filters, animation progress.
* Compose them: `const { data } = useTodosQuery(); const filters = useTodoFilters(data ?? []);`.

What naming convention should I follow?

* Prefix with `use` - `useSearchFilters`, not `searchFilters`.
* Name after **behavior**, not implementation: `useCollapsibleHeader` beats `useScrollYState`.
* File name kebab-case: `use-collapsible-header.ts`.

Gotcha: Why does eslint complain about missing dependencies?

* Effects must list every value from the component scope that they read.
* Stabilize callbacks with `useCallback` or move logic inside the effect.
* Do not disable `exhaustive-deps` to silence real stale-closure bugs.

How do custom hooks interact with React 19 batching?

* Multiple `setState` calls inside a hook's event handler batch into one re-render - same as inline state.
* Hooks do not change batching semantics; they only relocate where updates originate.
* See [Props, State & Re-renders on Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/rn-fundamentals/props-state-and-re-renders-on-mobile/) for the full update path.

When should I return a tuple vs an object?

* Tuple mirrors `useState` - good for `[value, setValue]` ergonomics.
* Object scales better when you add a third or fourth field later.
* Document the return shape in a named exported type for shared hooks.

Can I use custom hooks inside FlatList renderItem?

* **No** - `renderItem` is a nested function, not a component; hooks cannot be called there.
* Extract a `TodoRow` component and call hooks at the top of that component instead.
* List rows that need hooks must be proper function components.

How is this different from headless components?

* Hooks return **data and functions**; headless components return **no UI** but may use context to wire children.
* Start with a hook when one consumer needs behavior; graduate to headless when multiple sub-parts share implicit state.
* See [Headless Components](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/headless-components/) for the compound-style variant.

Dokumen: Component Patterns Highlights Summary
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/highlights-summary/

# Component Patterns Highlights Summary

Every highlight bullet from the 9 pages in this section, gathered on one page and grouped by the page it came from.

Highlights / Component Patterns Highlights Summary

* Screens wire navigation and data; presentational components own layout and styles only
* Custom hooks bundle state + effects + handlers into one reusable unit
* Parent owns state; children declare structure - consumers compose the UI they need
* Render props pass state to a function - the caller owns all markup
* Containers own data, navigation side effects, and platform wiring
* Headless primitives own state, events, and accessibility - consumers own layout and StyleSheet

## [Component Patterns Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/component-patterns-basics/)

* Screens wire navigation and data; presentational components own layout and styles only
* Feature folders colocate screens, hooks, and UI so a module can be moved or deleted in one cut
* Custom hooks extract refresh, pagination, and form state without prop drilling through the tree
* Compound components share implicit state via context - ideal for tabs, cards, and field groups
* Container/presenter splits async work from pure UI so presenters are easy to snapshot-test
* Headless hooks return state and handlers; design-system components decide colors, spacing, and motion

## [Custom Hooks for UI Logic](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/custom-hooks-for-ui-logic/)

* Custom hooks bundle state + effects + handlers into one reusable unit
* Return a small object or tuple - consumers pick only what they need
* UI hooks differ from data hooks: no fetch/cache, only presentation behavior
* Keyboard, sheet, and scroll hooks are the highest-ROI extractions on mobile
* Prefix with use and keep hooks pure - no JSX inside the hook body
* Colocate hooks next to the feature until a second screen needs the same logic

## [Compound Components](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/compound-components/)

* Parent owns state; children declare structure - consumers compose the UI they need
* React Context shares implicit state without long prop lists
* Tabs, accordions, and form fields are the classic mobile compound wins
* Static properties (Tabs.List, Tabs.Panel) document the API in TypeScript
* Throw in development when a sub-component is used outside its provider
* Prefer layout primitives (View, Pressable) inside parts - not opinionated styling

## [Render Props & Slot Patterns](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/render-props-and-slot-patterns/)

* Render props pass state to a function - the caller owns all markup
* Slot patterns (Expo Router Slot) swap child routes without nested wrappers
* Prefer children-as-function only when the parent owns non-trivial state
* Flatten navigation layouts - logic components should not wrap every screen
* Typed render props preserve item types through lists and async data
* Combine with memoized row components to keep list render props fast

## [Container/Presenter on Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/container-presenter-on-mobile/)

* Containers own data, navigation side effects, and platform wiring
* Presenters are pure UI - props in, JSX out, easy to snapshot test
* Screens are often containers; shared lists and cards are presenters
* TanStack Query belongs in the container layer, not inside design-system atoms
* Co-locate container + presenter per feature before splitting across packages
* Expo Router route files are thin containers that delegate to feature presenters

## [Headless Components](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/headless-components/)

* Headless primitives own state, events, and accessibility - consumers own layout and StyleSheet
* Return prop bags (triggerProps, contentProps) instead of rendering Pressable or View yourself
* Custom hooks are the RN default; render props remain useful when JSX shape varies per screen
* Spread accessibilityRole and accessibilityState onto the consumer's host element
* Context wires compound headless parts without exporting internal state setters
* Test behavior through the hook API - not snapshotting styled output

## [Polymorphic & AsChild Patterns](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/polymorphic-and-aschild-patterns/)

* Polymorphic `as` lets one primitive render as Pressable, Link, or Text with correct prop types
* asChild merges event and accessibility props onto a single child - no Pressable wrapping Link
* Implement Slot with React.Children.only and cloneElement - RN has no built-in Radix Slot
* Default to Pressable; promote to Link only when navigation is the primary action
* Omit conflicting keys (onPress vs href) at the type level with discriminated unions
* Forward refs with React 19 ref-as-prop on custom components that wrap hosts

## [Anti-Patterns: God Screens](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/anti-patterns-god-screens/)

* A screen file over 400 lines is a refactor ticket - not a style preference
* Screens should orchestrate; they should not own fetch parsers, modal markup, and list cells
* Colocate by feature folder, not by file type spread across the repo
* Extract when a second screen needs the same block - not when line count feels ugly
* One screen-level data hook beats five chained useEffects
* God screens fail review because nobody can reason about the whole diff

## [Component Patterns Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/best-practices/)

* Split screens into container + presenter before files exceed ~300 lines
* Extract UI state into custom hooks; keep data fetching in containers
* Use compound components for tabs and field groups with shared context
* Prefer headless hooks that return accessibility prop bags
* Never nest Pressable inside Link - use asChild-style prop merging
* Co-locate feature code under features// with a single public export

Dokumen: Render Props & Slot Patterns
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/render-props-and-slot-patterns/

# Render Props & Slot Patterns

Render props and slot patterns let parents own behavior while children own markup - so you compose deep navigation trees without stacking wrapper components around every screen. Render props pass state through a function; slot patterns (as in Expo Router layouts) reserve a hole where the active child route renders.

Highlights / Render Props & Slot Patterns

* Render props pass state to a function - the caller owns all markup
* Slot patterns (Expo Router Slot) swap child routes without nested wrappers
* Prefer children-as-function only when the parent owns non-trivial state
* Flatten navigation layouts - logic components should not wrap every screen
* Typed render props preserve item types through lists and async data
* Combine with memoized row components to keep list render props fast

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```tsx
import type { ReactNode } from "react";
import { useCallback, useState } from "react";
import { Pressable, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
interface ToggleRenderProps {
  isOn: boolean;
  toggle: () => void;
}
 
interface ToggleProps {
  initial?: boolean;
  children: (state: ToggleRenderProps) => ReactNode;
}
 
export function Toggle({ initial = false, children }: ToggleProps) {
  const [isOn, setIsOn] = useState(initial);
  const toggle = useCallback(() => setIsOn((v) => !v), []);
  return <>{children({ isOn, toggle })}</>;
}
 
// Caller paints the UI - no Toggle.Button export required
export function NotificationRow() {
  return (
    <Toggle initial={true}>
      {({ isOn, toggle }) => (
        <Pressable onPress={toggle} style={{ flexDirection: "row", gap: 8 }}>
          <Text>Push alerts</Text>
          <Text>{isOn ? "On" : "Off"}</Text>
        </Pressable>
      )}
    </Toggle>
  );
}
```

**When to reach for this:**

* A parent owns state or subscriptions but product teams must control layout (lists, settings rows)
* Expo Router / React Navigation layouts need a single outlet for nested routes (`<Slot />`)
* You want to avoid exporting five styled sub-components for one small behavior
* Third-party libraries expose `children` as a function (`KeyboardAvoidingView`-style APIs)
* Deep navigator trees suffer "wrapper hell" - five HOCs before the actual screen

## Working Example

```tsx
import type { ReactNode } from "react";
import { useCallback, useEffect, useState } from "react";
import {
  ActivityIndicator,
  FlatList,
  Pressable,
  StyleSheet,
  Text,
  View,
} from "react-native";
import { Stack, Slot } from "expo-router";
 
interface AsyncState<T> {
  status: "idle" | "loading" | "success" | "error";
  data: T | null;
  error: string | null;
}
 
interface AsyncListProps<T> {
  load: () => Promise<T[]>;
  keyExtractor: (item: T) => string;
  children: (ctx: {
    items: T[];
    status: AsyncState<T[]>["status"];
    error: string | null;
    reload: () => void;
  }) => ReactNode;
}
 
function AsyncList<T>({ load, keyExtractor, children }: AsyncListProps<T>) {
  const [state, setState] = useState<AsyncState<T[]>>({
    status: "idle",
    data: null,
    error: null,
  });
 
  const reload = useCallback(async () => {
    setState((prev) => ({ status: "loading", data: prev.data, error: null }));
    try {
      const data = await load();
      setState({ status: "success", data, error: null });
    } catch (e) {
      setState({
        status: "error",
        data: null,
        error: e instanceof Error ? e.message : "Request failed",
      });
    }
  }, [load]);
 
  useEffect(() => {
    void reload();
  }, [reload]);
 
  const items = state.data ?? [];
 
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1 }}>
      {children({
        items,
        status: state.status,
        error: state.error,
        reload,
      })}
    </View>
  );
}
 
interface InboxItem {
  id: string;
  subject: string;
  unread: boolean;
}
 
const MOCK: InboxItem[] = [
  { id: "1", subject: "Release train Friday", unread: true },
  { id: "2", subject: "Design review notes", unread: false },
  { id: "3", subject: "Crash-free rate 99.2%", unread: true },
];
 
function InboxListUI({
  items,
  status,
  error,
  reload,
}: {
  items: InboxItem[];
  status: AsyncState<InboxItem[]>["status"];
  error: string | null;
  reload: () => void;
}) {
  if (status === "loading" && items.length === 0) {
    return <ActivityIndicator style={{ marginTop: 32 }} />;
  }
 
  if (status === "error") {
    return (
      <View style={styles.center}>
        <Text style={styles.error}>{error}</Text>
        <Pressable onPress={reload} style={styles.retry}>
          <Text style={styles.retryText}>Retry</Text>
        </Pressable>
      </View>
    );
  }
 
  return (
    <FlatList
      data={items}
      keyExtractor={(item) => item.id}
      renderItem={({ item }) => (
        <View style={[styles.row, item.unread && styles.unread]}>
          <Text style={styles.subject}>{item.subject}</Text>
          {item.unread ? <Text style={styles.dot}>•</Text> : null}
        </View>
      )}
      ItemSeparatorComponent={() => <View style={styles.separator} />}
      contentContainerStyle={styles.list}
    />
  );
}
 
export function InboxScreen() {
  const loadInbox = useCallback(
    () => new Promise<InboxItem[]>((r) => setTimeout(() => r(MOCK), 500)),
    []
  );
 
  return (
    <AsyncList load={loadInbox} keyExtractor={(item) => item.id}>
      {(ctx) => <InboxListUI {...ctx} />}
    </AsyncList>
  );
}
 
// Expo Router layout - slot avoids wrapping every child screen manually
export function InboxLayout() {
  return (
    <View style={styles.layout}>
      <Stack.Screen options={{ title: "Inbox" }} />
      <View style={styles.banner}>
        <Text style={styles.bannerText}>Team mobile updates</Text>
      </View>
      <View style={styles.slot}>
        <Slot />
      </View>
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  layout: { flex: 1, backgroundColor: "#f8fafc" },
  banner: {
    backgroundColor: "#0f172a",
    paddingHorizontal: 16,
    paddingVertical: 10,
  },
  bannerText: { color: "#fff", fontWeight: "600" },
  slot: { flex: 1 },
  list: { padding: 16 },
  row: {
    flexDirection: "row",
    alignItems: "center",
    backgroundColor: "#fff",
    padding: 14,
    borderRadius: 10,
  },
  unread: { borderLeftWidth: 3, borderLeftColor: "#2563eb" },
  subject: { flex: 1, fontSize: 16, color: "#0f172a" },
  dot: { color: "#2563eb", fontSize: 20, lineHeight: 20 },
  separator: { height: 8 },
  center: { flex: 1, alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "center", gap: 12 },
  error: { color: "#dc2626", fontSize: 15 },
  retry: {
    backgroundColor: "#2563eb",
    paddingHorizontal: 16,
    paddingVertical: 10,
    borderRadius: 8,
  },
  retryText: { color: "#fff", fontWeight: "600" },
});
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* `AsyncList` owns fetch status; the render prop paints loading, error, and `FlatList` UI
* Generics preserve `InboxItem` type through the render callback - no `any` in `renderItem`
* `InboxLayout` uses Expo Router's `<Slot />` so child routes render without per-screen wrappers
* Behavior component (`AsyncList`) stays free of brand styles; UI component (`InboxListUI`) stays free of fetch logic
* One layout file adds banner chrome around every inbox child route

## Deep Dive

### How It Works

* **Render prop** - `children` (or a named prop like `renderItem`) is a **function** the parent calls with state: `children({ isOn, toggle })`.
* The parent renders `<> {children(state)} </>` - it does not choose which `Pressable` or `Text` to show.
* **Slot pattern** - a layout renders shared chrome and inserts `<Slot />` where the matched child route's component should appear.
* Expo Router resolves the active child from the URL; the layout does not import screen files directly.
* Both patterns **invert control**: library owns logic; app owns structure and styling.
* Deep navigation benefits because layouts replace stacks of HOC wrappers (`withAuth(withTheme(Screen))`).

### Render Prop vs Compound vs Hook

| Pattern | Caller provides | Parent provides | Best on mobile when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Render prop | Function that returns JSX | State + callbacks | One-off layouts, list row customization |
| Compound | Named JSX children | Context + sub-parts | Design-system tabs, accordion, fields |
| Custom hook | Component body calls `useX()` | Returned state/actions | Same logic, totally different trees |
| Slot (`<Slot />`) | Child route files | Layout chrome | Expo Router / file-based nesting |

### Expo Router Slot Layout

```tsx
// app/(app)/settings/_layout.tsx
import { Stack, Slot } from "expo-router";
import { View, Text } from "react-native";
 
export default function SettingsLayout() {
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1 }}>
      <Stack.Screen options={{ headerShown: false }} />
      <Text style={{ padding: 16, fontWeight: "700" }}>Settings</Text>
      <Slot />
    </View>
  );
}
```

* `Slot` renders the active child route - analogous to `children` in a layout component.
* Use nested `_layout.tsx` files instead of manually composing navigators in every screen.
* Pair with typed routes - see [Expo Router Typed Routes](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/typescript-rn/expo-router-typed-routes/).

### List Render Props and Performance

```tsx
<FlatList
  data={items}
  renderItem={({ item }) => (
    <UserRow item={item} onPress={handlePress} />
  )}
/>
```

* `renderItem` is a render prop built into React Native lists.
* Extract `UserRow` as a `memo`ized component - do not call hooks inside `renderItem`.
* Stabilize `handlePress` with `useCallback` so row memoization works.

### TypeScript Notes

```tsx
import type { ReactNode } from "react";
 
type RenderProp<T> = (value: T) => ReactNode;
 
interface DataRendererProps<T> {
  data: T;
  children: RenderProp<T>;
}
 
// Named render prop when children is already used for composition
interface ListProps<T> {
  items: T[];
  renderRow: RenderProp<{ item: T; index: number }>;
  keyExtractor: (item: T) => string;
}
```

* Prefer explicit names (`renderHeader`, `renderEmpty`) when `children` is also a valid React node.
* Generic parents (`AsyncList<T>`) keep item types flowing to the callback parameter.
* Type the render argument as an interface so screens get autocomplete on `reload`, `status`, etc.

## Gotchas

* **Inline render functions in lists** - `children={(ctx) => <Row {...ctx} />}` defined inside a parent re-creates the function every render and can defeat `memo`. **Fix:** Hoist a stable child component or pass `renderRow` from `useCallback`.
* **Wrapper hell in navigators** - Nesting five providers in every `_layout.tsx` obscures the actual screen. **Fix:** Push cross-cutting providers to the root layout; use slots for route-level chrome only.
* **Using render props when a hook suffices** - `Toggle` with only `isOn`/`toggle` does not need a function child if every caller renders the same row. **Fix:** Export `useToggle` and a dumb row - see [Custom Hooks for UI Logic](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/custom-hooks-for-ui-logic/).
* **Calling hooks inside render props** - `children={() => { const x = useFoo(); ... }}` violates the Rules of Hooks. **Fix:** Move hook calls into a child component rendered by the function.
* **Slot without flex** - Forgetting `flex: 1` on the slot container yields blank or clipped child screens. **Fix:** Give the slot wrapper `flex: 1` in full-screen layouts.
* **Async render prop reload loops** - `useEffect(() => reload(), [items])` when `reload` sets `items` causes infinite fetch. **Fix:** Depend on stable keys; load once on mount or on explicit user action.
* **Untyped `children` as Function** - `children: Function` loses type safety. **Fix:** `children: (state: ToggleRenderProps) => ReactNode`.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Render props | Caller must own all markup; few structural conventions | Team prefers consistent compound sub-parts |
| Compound components | Repeated multi-part UI (tabs, fields) | Only one layout ever consumes the behavior |
| Custom hooks | Identical state, arbitrary JSX trees | You need a single component boundary for error boundaries |
| Expo Router `<Slot />` | File-based child routes under shared chrome | Modal overlays that are not routes |
| HOCs (`withTheme`) | Legacy codebase already standardized on them | Greenfield - layouts + hooks are clearer |
| Inline JSX children | Static composition, no shared state function | Parent must inject dynamic state into the child |

## FAQs

What is a render prop?

* A prop (often `children`) whose value is a **function** that returns React elements.
* The parent component calls the function with its internal state.
* The caller decides which native primitives to render.

How is Slot different from children in a layout?

* `children` in classic React are elements passed by the direct parent.
* `<Slot />` renders the **matched child route** from the router - not manually passed JSX.
* Expo Router wires the slot to the file system under the layout's directory.

Why does wrapper hell happen in navigation?

* Each concern (auth, theme, analytics, safe area) adds a layout or HOC layer.
* Without slots, every screen import path grows and shared chrome duplicates.
* Root + group layouts should own providers; leaf layouts own only local chrome.

Gotcha: Can I use hooks inside a render prop callback?

* **No** - the callback is not a component body.
* Return `<MyRow />` from the callback and call hooks inside `MyRow`.
* Same rule as `FlatList` `renderItem`.

Render props vs compound components - which wins for tabs?

* **Compound** when your design system ships `Tabs.List` / `Tabs.Tab` and teams reuse that structure.
* **Render props** when every product screen lays out tabs differently (bottom vs segmented control).
* Hybrid: compound parts internally, optional `renderTab` override for advanced cases.

How do I avoid recreating render functions?

```tsx
function InboxBody(props: InboxRenderProps) {
  return <InboxListUI {...props} />;
}
 
<AsyncList load={loadInbox} keyExtractor={(i) => i.id}>
  {InboxBody}
</AsyncList>
```

* Pass a stable function reference instead of an inline arrow in JSX.
* Or wrap with `useCallback` when the function closes over props.

Does FlatList use a render prop?

* Yes - `renderItem`, `ListHeaderComponent`, and `ListEmptyComponent` are all render-style APIs.
* `ListEmptyComponent` can be a component type or a function returning JSX.
* Treat list rows as first-class components for hooks and memoization.

How do slots interact with Stack navigators?

* A `_layout.tsx` can render `<Stack />` for headers and still use `<Slot />` in tab-style nested layouts.
* `Stack.Screen options` in layouts set shared header config for child routes.
* Deep links target child routes; the layout slot updates automatically.

Gotcha: Blank screen below my layout banner?

* The slot container likely has no height - add `flex: 1`.
* Child screens should also use `flex: 1` on their root `View`.
* Check that the matched route file has a default export.

Are render props deprecated?

* React docs favor hooks for many cases, but render props remain valid - especially in libraries.
* React Native list APIs still center on `renderItem`.
* Choose readability: if a hook + component is clearer, use that instead.

How do I type children as a function in TypeScript?

* `children: (state: State) => ReactNode` - not `Function` or `any`.
* Export the state interface so consumers annotate extracted render components.
* See [Typing Components & Props](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/typescript-rn/typing-components-and-props/).

Can render props help with platform-specific UI?

* A `MediaQuery` or `Platform.select` wrapper can expose `{ isTablet }` to its render child.
* Caller returns different trees for phone vs tablet without forking the data layer.
* Pair with [Platform-Specific Code](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/rn-fundamentals/platform-specific-code/) for file splits when trees diverge heavily.

How many layout layers should an Expo Router app have?

* Root: providers, fonts, splash, analytics.
* Group `(app)` / `(auth)`: session gates.
* Feature `_layout`: local banner, segment tabs, `<Slot />`.
* Avoid duplicating the same provider at every level.

How does this relate to container/presenter?

* Containers often use render props to hand async state to presenters.
* `AsyncList` is container-like; `InboxListUI` is presenter-like.
* See [Container/Presenter on Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/container-presenter-on-mobile/).

* [Component Patterns Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/component-patterns-basics/) - folder conventions that keep layouts thin
* [Compound Components](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/compound-components/) - named parts instead of function children
* [Custom Hooks for UI Logic](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/custom-hooks-for-ui-logic/) - hook alternative to render props
* [Container/Presenter on Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/container-presenter-on-mobile/) - split data logic from slot-friendly UI
* [Expo Router Typed Routes](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/typescript-rn/expo-router-typed-routes/) - type-safe params with slot layouts

Dokumen: AsyncStorage Patterns
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/data-offline/asyncstorage-patterns/

# AsyncStorage Patterns

Small key-value persistence and migration versioning. `@react-native-async-storage/async-storage` is the default **string KV store** for Expo SDK 57 - ideal for preferences, small outboxes, feature flags, and TanStack Query persistence. It is not a database.

Highlights / AsyncStorage Patterns

* Use @react-native-async-storage/async-storage for small JSON blobs - not relational data
* Version every persisted schema with a meta key and stepwise migrations
* Wrap read/write in try/catch - corrupted JSON should reset to defaults, not crash boot
* Namespace keys by domain: prefs:v1, sync:outbox:v1 - never one global dump
* Pair with TanStack Query persister for server-state hydration on cold start
* AsyncStorage is async and relatively slow - batch writes and avoid hot-path reads

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
npx expo install @react-native-async-storage/async-storage
```

```ts
// src/storage/keys.ts
export const STORAGE_KEYS = {
  meta: "app:storage:meta:v1",
  preferences: "user:preferences:v1",
  outbox: "sync:outbox:v1",
} as const;
 
export type StorageMeta = { schemaVersion: number };
```

```ts
// src/storage/safeJson.ts
export function safeParse<T>(raw: string | null, fallback: T): T {
  if (!raw) return fallback;
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw) as T;
  } catch {
    return fallback;
  }
}
```

```ts
// src/storage/preferences.ts
import AsyncStorage from "@react-native-async-storage/async-storage";
import { STORAGE_KEYS } from "./keys";
import { safeParse } from "./safeJson";
 
export type Preferences = { theme: "light" | "dark"; locale: string };
 
const DEFAULTS: Preferences = { theme: "light", locale: "en" };
 
export async function loadPreferences(): Promise<Preferences> {
  const raw = await AsyncStorage.getItem(STORAGE_KEYS.preferences);
  return safeParse(raw, DEFAULTS);
}
 
export async function savePreferences(prefs: Preferences) {
  await AsyncStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEYS.preferences, JSON.stringify(prefs));
}
```

**When to reach for this:**

* User preferences, onboarding progress, small offline outboxes (< few hundred KB)
* TanStack Query `createAsyncStoragePersister` for last-known-good API cache
* Feature-flag defaults and last-sync timestamps
* Anything that fits in JSON and does not need SQL queries

## Working Example

```bash
npx expo install @react-native-async-storage/async-storage
```

```ts
// src/storage/keys.ts
export const STORAGE_KEYS = {
  meta: "app:storage:meta:v1",
  preferences: "user:preferences:v1",
  outbox: "sync:outbox:v1",
} as const;
 
export const CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION = 2;
 
export type StorageMeta = { schemaVersion: number };
```

```ts
// src/storage/migrations.ts
import AsyncStorage from "@react-native-async-storage/async-storage";
import { CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION, STORAGE_KEYS, type StorageMeta } from "./keys";
import { safeParse } from "./safeJson";
 
async function readMeta(): Promise<StorageMeta> {
  const raw = await AsyncStorage.getItem(STORAGE_KEYS.meta);
  return safeParse(raw, { schemaVersion: 0 });
}
 
async function writeMeta(meta: StorageMeta) {
  await AsyncStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEYS.meta, JSON.stringify(meta));
}
 
async function migrateV0ToV1() {
  // v0 had unversioned key "preferences"
  const legacy = await AsyncStorage.getItem("preferences");
  if (legacy) {
    await AsyncStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEYS.preferences, legacy);
    await AsyncStorage.removeItem("preferences");
  }
}
 
async function migrateV1ToV2() {
  const raw = await AsyncStorage.getItem(STORAGE_KEYS.preferences);
  const prefs = safeParse(raw, { theme: "light" });
  const next = { ...prefs, locale: prefs.locale ?? "en" };
  await AsyncStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEYS.preferences, JSON.stringify(next));
}
 
const STEPS: Record<number, () => Promise<void>> = {
  0: migrateV0ToV1,
  1: migrateV1ToV2,
};
 
export async function runStorageMigrations() {
  const meta = await readMeta();
  let version = meta.schemaVersion;
 
  while (version < CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION) {
    const step = STEPS[version];
    if (!step) throw new Error(`Missing migration for schema v${version}`);
    await step();
    version += 1;
    await writeMeta({ schemaVersion: version });
  }
}
```

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx (excerpt)
import AsyncStorage from "@react-native-async-storage/async-storage";
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { runStorageMigrations } from "@/storage/migrations";
 
export default function RootLayout() {
  const [ready, setReady] = useState(false);
 
  useEffect(() => {
    runStorageMigrations()
      .then(() => setReady(true))
      .catch(async () => {
        // Corruption recovery: reset non-critical keys and boot
        await AsyncStorage.clear();
        setReady(true);
      });
  }, []);
 
  if (!ready) return null;
  return <Stack />;
}
```

```ts
// src/storage/outbox.ts
import AsyncStorage from "@react-native-async-storage/async-storage";
import { STORAGE_KEYS } from "./keys";
import { safeParse } from "./safeJson";
 
export type OutboxItem = {
  id: string;
  type: string;
  payload: unknown;
  idempotencyKey: string;
  createdAt: number;
};
 
export async function readOutbox(): Promise<OutboxItem[]> {
  const raw = await AsyncStorage.getItem(STORAGE_KEYS.outbox);
  return safeParse(raw, []);
}
 
export async function appendOutbox(item: OutboxItem) {
  const queue = await readOutbox();
  queue.push(item);
  await AsyncStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEYS.outbox, JSON.stringify(queue));
}
 
export async function writeOutbox(queue: OutboxItem[]) {
  await AsyncStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEYS.outbox, JSON.stringify(queue));
}
```

```bash
# Optional: TanStack Query persistence
npx expo install @tanstack/react-query-persist-client @tanstack/query-async-storage-persister
```

## Deep Dive

### Key namespacing

Treat every domain as an isolated document with a version suffix in the key:

| Key | Contents | Max size guidance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `user:preferences:v1` | Theme, locale | < 4 KB |
| `sync:outbox:v1` | Pending mutations | < 500 KB - flush often |
| `REACT_QUERY_OFFLINE_CACHE` | Dehydrated Query cache | Monitor growth; exclude secrets |
| `app:storage:meta:v1` | `{ schemaVersion }` | Tiny |

Bump the `:v1` suffix when the **shape** changes irreversibly - migrations handle in-place upgrades; key renames handle breaking rewrites.

### Stepwise migrations

```text
Boot sequence:
 
1. Read app:storage:meta:v1 → schemaVersion (default 0)
2. While version < CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION:
     run STEPS[version]()
     version++
     persist meta
3. App renders - no screen reads un-migrated keys
```

* Migrations run **once per version step** - idempotent steps are safer for crash mid-migration
* Log migration failures to your crash reporter - silent `clear()` loses user data
* For large transforms, write to a **new key** then swap - avoids half-written JSON on kill

### Corruption recovery

```ts
export async function loadWithRecovery<T>(
  key: string,
  fallback: T,
  onCorrupt?: () => void
): Promise<T> {
  try {
    const raw = await AsyncStorage.getItem(key);
    return safeParse(raw, fallback);
  } catch {
    onCorrupt?.();
    await AsyncStorage.removeItem(key);
    return fallback;
  }
}
```

* **Preferences corruption** → reset to defaults and show a one-time toast
* **Outbox corruption** → quarantine to `sync:outbox:corrupt:<timestamp>` for support export before clearing
* Never call **`AsyncStorage.clear()`** on auth errors only - scope clears to affected namespaces

### Batching and multi-set

```ts
import AsyncStorage from "@react-native-async-storage/async-storage";
 
export async function saveDraftBundle(draft: object, updatedAt: number) {
  await AsyncStorage.multiSet([
    ["draft:composer:v1", JSON.stringify(draft)],
    ["draft:composer:meta:v1", JSON.stringify({ updatedAt })],
  ]);
}
```

`multiSet` reduces bridge round-trips compared to sequential `setItem` calls - still async, not synchronous like MMKV.

## Gotchas

* **Storing large lists in one JSON array** - Parsing 5 MB on the JS thread blocks UI. **Fix:** Move relational data to [expo-sqlite](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/data-offline/expo-sqlite/); keep AsyncStorage for metadata and outbox pointers.
* **No schema version** - Shipping a new shape without migration crashes `JSON.parse` assumptions. **Fix:** Always maintain `app:storage:meta:v1` and step migrations.
* **Storing secrets in AsyncStorage** - It is not encrypted. **Fix:** Tokens in `expo-secure-store`; only non-sensitive prefs in AsyncStorage.
* **Race on concurrent writes** - Two screens appending to the same outbox can drop items. **Fix:** Read-modify-write in one function; serialize flushes with a mutex or queue service.
* **Assuming persistence is synchronous** - `await getItem` on every render causes jank. **Fix:** Load once at boot or hydrate Zustand/Query; use MMKV for sync hot paths.
* **Unbounded Query persister growth** - Dehydrating every query fills disk. **Fix:** `shouldDehydrateQuery` filter + `maxAge`; see [../state-management/tanstack-query/tanstack-query.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/state-management/tanstack-query/).
* **Forgetting logout cleanup** - Prior user's cache leaks to the next login. **Fix:** `multiRemove` on session keys + `queryClient.clear()` on sign-out.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@react-native-async-storage/async-storage` | Small JSON, prefs, Query persister | You need SQL, full-text search, or sync joins |
| `expo-sqlite/kv-store` | Already on SQLite; want AsyncStorage-compatible API + sync reads | You only need a few keys and no DB yet |
| `react-native-mmkv` | Hot-path flags, session-adjacent cache, frequent reads | Expo Go without a dev build; multi-MB blobs |
| `expo-secure-store` | Tokens, refresh secrets | Large payloads (> ~2 KB per key on some platforms) |
| TanStack Query cache only | Pure server-state with no local-only writes | Offline-created rows that never hit the server |

## FAQs

How do I install AsyncStorage on Expo SDK 57?

```bash
npx expo install @react-native-async-storage/async-storage
```

Always use `expo install` - manual npm versions may not match the SDK native module matrix.

When should I bump schema version vs rename the key?

* **Bump `schemaVersion`** when you can migrate data in place (add field, rename property).
* **Rename key** (`:v1` → `:v2`) when the old data is unusable or migration cost exceeds re-download.
* Never read new code against old keys without running migrations at boot.

How big is too big for AsyncStorage?

Stay under **~500 KB per key** for smooth boot. Multi-megabyte JSON parse blocks the JS thread for hundreds of milliseconds. Split large datasets into SQLite tables or paginated cache keys.

Can AsyncStorage replace a server database?

No. It is a local convenience layer. Treat contents as **best-effort cache** with TTL, version, and server reconciliation - see [Sync Strategies](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/data-offline/sync-strategies/).

How do I persist TanStack Query offline?

```bash
npx expo install @tanstack/react-query-persist-client @tanstack/query-async-storage-persister
```

Wire `PersistQueryClientProvider` with `createAsyncStoragePersister`. Exclude auth and PII queries from dehydration.

What if migration throws mid-boot?

* Retry once - transient I/O errors happen on low storage.
* On second failure, quarantine corrupt keys, reset non-critical namespaces, and log to telemetry.
* Offer support export for outbox quarantine before wipe in field apps.

Should I use Zustand persist with AsyncStorage?

Yes for client UI state (filters, draft forms). Use `createJSONStorage(() => AsyncStorage)` and the same migration/version discipline. Server API data still belongs in TanStack Query.

Is AsyncStorage encrypted?

Not by default. Assume rooted/jailbroken devices can read it. Secrets → SecureStore; sensitive PII → minimize retention or encrypt at rest with a server-derived key.

## Related

* [Offline-First Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/data-offline/offline-first-basics/) - connectivity UX and SWR patterns
* [expo-sqlite](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/data-offline/expo-sqlite/) - relational data and typed queries
* [MMKV & High-Performance KV](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/data-offline/mmkv-and-high-performance-kv/) - when AsyncStorage is too slow
* [../state-management/tanstack-query/tanstack-query.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/state-management/tanstack-query/) - cache persistence and mobile lifecycle

Dokumen: Background Sync & TaskManager
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/data-offline/background-sync-and-taskmanager/

# Background Sync & TaskManager

`expo-background-task` and `expo-task-manager` for deferred uploads. Mobile OSes **kill foreground network work** when users switch apps. Register a background worker to flush SQLite outboxes, upload attachments, and pull deltas - within strict battery and scheduling limits.

Highlights / Background Sync & TaskManager

* TaskManager.defineTask must run in global scope - before React mounts
* expo-background-task schedules deferrable work via WorkManager (Android) and BGTaskScheduler (iOS)
* Minimum interval is 15 minutes - not real-time; foreground flush still required
* Return BackgroundTaskResult.Success or Failed - failed tasks may retry per OS policy
* iOS background tasks require a physical device - simulators do not run BGTaskScheduler
* Use for outbox flush and attachment upload - not user-visible latency-critical paths

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
npx expo install expo-background-task expo-task-manager
```

```ts
// src/background/syncTask.ts - import this file at app entry (global scope)
import * as BackgroundTask from "expo-background-task";
import * as TaskManager from "expo-task-manager";
 
export const SYNC_TASK = "offline-sync-worker";
 
TaskManager.defineTask(SYNC_TASK, async () => {
  try {
    // Open DB, flush outbox, upload files - keep work short
    console.log("[sync] background worker ran");
    return BackgroundTask.BackgroundTaskResult.Success;
  } catch (error) {
    console.error("[sync] background worker failed", error);
    return BackgroundTask.BackgroundTaskResult.Failed;
  }
});
```

```ts
// src/background/registerSyncTask.ts
import * as BackgroundTask from "expo-background-task";
import * as TaskManager from "expo-task-manager";
import { SYNC_TASK } from "./syncTask";
 
export async function registerSyncTask() {
  const status = await BackgroundTask.getStatusAsync();
  if (status === BackgroundTask.BackgroundTaskStatus.Restricted) return;
 
  const registered = await TaskManager.isTaskRegisteredAsync(SYNC_TASK);
  if (!registered) {
    await BackgroundTask.registerTaskAsync(SYNC_TASK, {
      minimumInterval: 15, // minutes - OS may delay further
    });
  }
}
```

```ts
// index.ts or app/_layout.tsx - side-effect import at top
import "@/background/syncTask";
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Flushing pending SQLite / AsyncStorage outbox when app is backgrounded
* Uploading inspection photos after field capture
* Incremental catalog pull that should not block foreground UX

**When to avoid:**

* User waiting for immediate confirmation - flush on reconnect in foreground
* Sub-minute polling - OS will not honor it; use push notifications or foreground refetch

## Working Example

Deferred outbox flush with expo-sqlite and development-build testing hook.

```bash
npx expo install expo-background-task expo-task-manager expo-sqlite
```

```ts
// src/background/syncTask.ts
import * as BackgroundTask from "expo-background-task";
import * as TaskManager from "expo-task-manager";
import * as SQLite from "expo-sqlite";
import { flushWorkOrders } from "@/sync/flushOutbox";
 
export const SYNC_TASK = "offline-sync-worker";
 
TaskManager.defineTask(SYNC_TASK, async () => {
  try {
    const db = await SQLite.openDatabaseAsync("field.db");
    // flushWorkOrders without QueryClient - background has no React tree
    await flushWorkOrders(db, null);
    return BackgroundTask.BackgroundTaskResult.Success;
  } catch (error) {
    console.error("[sync] failed", error);
    return BackgroundTask.BackgroundTaskResult.Failed;
  }
});
```

```ts
// src/sync/flushOutbox.ts (excerpt) - tolerate null queryClient in background
export async function flushWorkOrders(
  db: SQLiteDatabase,
  queryClient: QueryClient | null
) {
  // ... push pending rows ...
  if (queryClient) {
    await queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ["work-orders"] });
  }
}
```

```tsx

  useEffect(() => {
    setupMobileQuery();
    registerSyncTask();
  }, []);
 
  return <Stack />;
```
