Dokumen: Deep Linking Basics
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/deep-linking/deep-linking-basics/

# Deep Linking Basics

10 examples to wire custom schemes, universal links, and Expo config - the foundation every SDK 57 app needs before routing users from email, SMS, QR codes, or push notifications into the right screen.

Highlights / Deep Linking Basics

* Custom schemes (myapp://) work everywhere but show an 'Open in app?' prompt on the web
* Universal Links (iOS) and App Links (Android) open https:// URLs directly in the installed app
* Declare scheme and associated domains in app.config.ts before shipping deep links
* Expo Router maps file paths to URLs - app/orders/[id].tsx becomes /orders/:id
* expo-linking parses URLs into path, queryParams, and hostname for custom handlers
* Test cold-start links on development builds - Expo Go scheme behavior differs from store binaries

## Prerequisites

Scaffold an Expo app with file-based routing and install the linking primitives:

```bash
npx create-expo-app@latest DeepLinkBasics --template tabs
cd DeepLinkBasics
npx expo install expo-linking expo-router
```

Confirm the SDK pin:

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "expo": "~57.0.4",
    "react": "19.2.3",
    "react-native": "0.86.0",
    "expo-router": "~6.0.0"
  }
}
```

> **Tooling:** These examples target **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4), **React Native 0.86.0**, and **React 19.2.3**.

---

## Basic Examples

### 1. Custom Scheme vs HTTPS Link

Mobile deep links arrive in two shapes. Pick based on whether you need verified HTTPS routing or a quick dev-only path.

```text
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Type              │ Example URL                    │ Opens without prompt │
├───────────────────┼────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────┤
│ Custom scheme     │ myapp://orders/42              │ Yes (if app installed) │
│ Universal/App Link│ https://shop.example.com/o/42  │ Yes (when verified)  │
│ Web fallback      │ https://shop.example.com/o/42  │ Browser (no app)     │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

* **Custom schemes** are fastest to ship - register `scheme` in `app.config.ts` and handle paths in code
* **Universal/App Links** require server-hosted verification files but feel native - no disambiguation sheet on iOS
* Marketing emails and social posts should prefer **HTTPS links** with web fallbacks for users without the app
* OAuth redirects and dev tooling often use **custom schemes** - see [../auth-session/expo-auth-session-and-oauth/expo-auth-session-and-oauth.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/expo-auth-session-and-oauth/)

> **Related:** [iOS Universal Links](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/deep-linking/ios-universal-links/) - `apple-app-site-association` setup | [Android App Links](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/deep-linking/android-app-links/) - `assetlinks.json` verification

---

### 2. Register a Custom Scheme in app.config.ts

The `scheme` property tells iOS and Android which URL prefix belongs to your app.

```ts
// app.config.ts
import type { ExpoConfig } from "expo/config";
 
const config: ExpoConfig = {
  name: "ShopApp",
  slug: "shop-app",
  scheme: "shopapp",
  ios: {
    bundleIdentifier: "com.example.shopapp",
  },
  android: {
    package: "com.example.shopapp",
  },
};
 
export default config;
```

* A single lowercase scheme (`shopapp`) produces URLs like `shopapp://orders/42`
* Multiple schemes use an array: `scheme: ["shopapp", "com.example.shopapp"]`
* **Rebuild native binaries** after changing `scheme` - OTA updates cannot add new URL handlers
* Match scheme strings across OAuth consoles, email templates, and QR codes - typos cause silent no-ops

> **Related:** [../expo-rules/navigation-and-routing-rules/navigation-and-routing-rules.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/navigation-and-routing-rules/) - scheme and domain rules for review

---

### 3. Build Outbound Links with createURL

`expo-linking` generates URLs that respect your configured scheme and optional path prefix.

```ts
import * as Linking from "expo-linking";
 
const orderUrl = Linking.createURL("orders/42", {
  queryParams: { ref: "email" },
});
 
// Dev client / production: shopapp://orders/42?ref=email
```

* **`createURL`** prepends the app scheme and normalizes slashes - prefer it over string concatenation
* Pass `isTripleSlashed: true` only when integrating with legacy Android intent filters
* Share links from in-app "Invite friend" flows using `createURL` so dev and prod stay consistent
* Log `orderUrl` in `__DEV__` to copy into Maestro flows and marketing spreadsheets

> **Related:** [expo-linking API](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/deep-linking/expo-linking-api/) - parsing inbound URLs and event listeners

---

### 4. Parse an Inbound URL

When a link opens your app, parse it into structured parts before navigating.

```ts
import * as Linking from "expo-linking";
 
function handleDeepLink(url: string) {
  const parsed = Linking.parse(url);
 
  // shopapp://orders/42?ref=email
  // parsed.path        → "orders/42"
  // parsed.queryParams → { ref: "email" }
  // parsed.hostname    → null (custom scheme)
 
  const segments = (parsed.path ?? "").split("/").filter(Boolean);
  const [screen, id] = segments;
 
  if (screen === "orders" && id) {
    // router.push(`/orders/${id}`);
  }
}
```

* **`Linking.parse`** handles both custom schemes and `https://` URLs - hostname is set for universal links
* Strip leading slashes from `path` before splitting - Android and iOS sometimes differ on trailing slashes
* Never trust query params for authorization - validate IDs server-side before showing sensitive data
* With Expo Router, prefer file-based routes over manual parsing - Router maps paths automatically

> **Related:** [../expo-router/expo-router-basics/expo-router-basics.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/expo-router-basics/) - file paths become URL segments

---

### 5. Listen for Links While the App Is Open (Warm Start)

Warm-start links arrive while JavaScript is already running - subscribe in a root layout.

```tsx
import * as Linking from "expo-linking";
import { useEffect } from "react";
 
export function useDeepLinkListener(onUrl: (url: string) => void) {
  useEffect(() => {
    const subscription = Linking.addEventListener("url", ({ url }) => {
      onUrl(url);
    });
 
    return () => subscription.remove();
  }, [onUrl]);
}
```

* **`addEventListener("url")`** fires when the user taps a link and the app is foregrounded or backgrounded
* Return `subscription.remove()` in the effect cleanup - leaks cause duplicate navigations after fast refresh
* Debounce rapid duplicate events - some OEMs fire the listener twice on Android
* Pair with Expo Router's built-in linking - only add custom listeners for analytics or non-route URLs

> **Related:** [expo-linking API](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/deep-linking/expo-linking-api/) - cold-start vs warm-start handling

---

### 6. Handle Cold-Start Links on Launch

Cold-start links open the app from a killed state - read the initial URL once before rendering routes.

```tsx
import * as Linking from "expo-linking";
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
 
export function useInitialDeepLink() {
  const [initialUrl, setInitialUrl] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [ready, setReady] = useState(false);
 
  useEffect(() => {
    Linking.getInitialURL()
      .then((url) => setInitialUrl(url))
      .finally(() => setReady(true));
  }, []);
 
  return { initialUrl, ready };
}
```

* **`getInitialURL`** returns the link that launched the app, or `null` if opened from the home screen
* Gate splash screen hide on `ready` - navigating before Router mounts drops the initial URL
* Call `getInitialURL` **once** at startup - subsequent opens use the event listener
* Expo Router reads the initial URL automatically when `scheme` is configured - custom hooks are for side effects

> **Related:** [expo-linking API](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/deep-linking/expo-linking-api/) - complete cold + warm bootstrap pattern

---

### 7. Map File Routes to URL Paths (Expo Router)

Expo Router turns your `app/` directory into a URL tree - deep links map to screens without manual wiring.

```text
app/
  (tabs)/
    index.tsx          → /
    orders/
      index.tsx        → /orders
      [id].tsx         → /orders/:id
  product/
    [slug].tsx         → /product/:slug
```

```tsx
// app/orders/[id].tsx
import { useLocalSearchParams } from "expo-router";
import { Text, View } from "react-native";
 
export default function OrderDetailScreen() {
  const { id } = useLocalSearchParams<{ id: string }>();
 
  return (
    <View>
      <Text>Order {id}</Text>
    </View>
  );
}
```

* **Dynamic segments** (`[id].tsx`) become URL params - `shopapp://orders/42` lands on `OrderDetailScreen`
* **Route groups** `(tabs)` do not appear in the URL - keeps tab URLs clean
* Validate `id` with Zod at the screen boundary - malformed deep links should show a fallback, not crash
* Typed routes (`experiments.typedRoutes`) catch invalid `href` at compile time

> **Related:** [../expo-router/link-and-href/link-and-href.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/link-and-href/) - `Link` and `href` objects

---

### 8. Declare a Web Host for Universal Links

HTTPS deep links need a domain association - add `associatedDomains` (iOS) and `intentFilters` (Android) via config plugins or `app.config.ts`.

```ts
// app.config.ts
const config = {
  expo: {
    name: "ShopApp",
    slug: "shop-app",
    scheme: "shopapp",
    ios: {
      bundleIdentifier: "com.example.shopapp",
      associatedDomains: ["applinks:shop.example.com"],
    },
    android: {
      package: "com.example.shopapp",
      intentFilters: [
        {
          action: "VIEW",
          autoVerify: true,
          data: [
            {
              scheme: "https",
              host: "shop.example.com",
              pathPrefix: "/orders",
            },
          ],
          category: ["BROWSABLE", "DEFAULT"],
        },
      ],
    },
  },
};
 
export default config;
```

* **`applinks:`** prefix on iOS tells the system to fetch `apple-app-site-association` from your CDN
* **`autoVerify: true`** on Android triggers Digital Asset Links verification at install time
* Host only the paths your app owns - `/orders`, `/product`, not the entire marketing site root unless intended
* Changes require a **new native build** - verify on TestFlight and internal tracks before wide release

> **Related:** [iOS Universal Links](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/deep-linking/ios-universal-links/) - AASA file format and CDN headers

---

### 9. Test a Custom Scheme from the Terminal

Use `npx uri-scheme` to fire links into simulators and connected devices without rebuilding marketing pages.

```bash
# iOS Simulator
npx uri-scheme open "shopapp://orders/42?ref=cli" --ios
 
# Android emulator / device
npx uri-scheme open "shopapp://orders/42?ref=cli" --android
```

* Install `uri-scheme` globally or use `npx` - no app code changes required
* Test **cold start** by killing the app first, then running the command
* Test **warm start** with the app backgrounded - confirms the event listener path
* Universal links need Safari/Chrome or `xcrun simctl openurl` with `https://` - see [Deep Link Testing Matrix](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/deep-linking/deep-link-testing-matrix/)

> **Related:** [Deep Link Testing Matrix](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/deep-linking/deep-link-testing-matrix/) - simulator, device, and CI coverage

---

### 10. Provide a Web Fallback for Users Without the App

Deep links should degrade to your marketing site or app store - never a blank error page.

```html
<!-- Hosted at https://shop.example.com/orders/42 -->
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <title>Order 42 - ShopApp</title>
    <meta name="apple-itunes-app" content="app-id=123456789, app-argument=https://shop.example.com/orders/42" />
    <script>
      const isIOS = /iPhone|iPad|iPod/i.test(navigator.userAgent);
      const isAndroid = /Android/i.test(navigator.userAgent);
      if (isIOS || isAndroid) {
        window.location = "shopapp://orders/42";
        setTimeout(() => {
          window.location = isIOS
            ? "https://apps.apple.com/app/id123456789"
            : "https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.example.shopapp";
        }, 1500);
      }
    </script>
  </head>
  <body>
    <p>Opening ShopApp… <a href="https://shop.example.com/orders/42">View in browser</a></p>
  </body>
</html>
```

* **Smart banners** (`apple-itunes-app`) improve iOS web-to-app handoff when universal links are not yet verified
* Timeout fallback prevents users from staring at a blank page when the app is not installed
* Deferred deep links (install → first open) need attribution SDKs or custom install-referrer plumbing - see [Deferred Deep Links](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/deep-linking/deferred-deep-links/)
* Keep web and app paths aligned - `/orders/42` should mean the same entity on both surfaces

> **Related:** [Deferred Deep Links](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/deep-linking/deferred-deep-links/) - attribution after fresh install

---

## Intermediate Examples

### 11. Prefix Paths for Staging vs Production

Use `expo-linking` path prefixes when multiple build flavors share one scheme but different route roots.

```ts
import Constants from "expo-constants";
import * as Linking from "expo-linking";
 
const prefix = Constants.expoConfig?.extra?.linkingPrefix ?? "";
 
export function appPath(route: string) {
  return Linking.createURL(`${prefix}${route}`);
}
 
// Staging extra: linkingPrefix = "staging/"
// → shopapp://staging/orders/42
```

* **Flavor-specific prefixes** isolate staging deep links from production analytics
* Document prefix rules in marketing UTM spreadsheets - conflating staging and prod links skews attribution
* Expo Router supports `linking` config with prefixes in `expo-router` advanced setups - keep one source of truth

> **Related:** [Push Notification Deep Links](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/deep-linking/push-notification-deep-links/) - embedding paths in notification payloads

---

## FAQs

Do I need both a custom scheme and universal links?

* **Scheme only** is fine for OAuth, dev testing, and internal tools.
* **Production consumer apps** should add verified HTTPS links for email and web - schemes show disambiguation UI and break when another app registers the same scheme.
* Keep the scheme as a fallback during universal-link rollout.

Does Expo Go handle my production scheme?

* Expo Go uses the `exp://` scheme - your `shopapp://` links open the dev client or a standalone build, not Expo Go.
* Test deep links on `expo-dev-client` or preview builds with the real bundle ID before release.

Can I change the scheme after App Store submission?

* Yes, but existing marketing links break until you ship a new binary and update every outbound URL.
* Treat scheme changes as a breaking API change - version your links or maintain redirects on the web host.

Who parses the URL - Expo Router or expo-linking?

* **Expo Router** maps paths to screens when using file-based routing - default choice.
* **`Linking.parse`** is for analytics, legacy React Navigation setups, or non-route URLs (e.g. `shopapp://reset-password?token=…`).

Why does my link open the browser instead of the app?

* Universal/App link verification failed - check AASA and `assetlinks.json` hosting.
* User long-pressed and chose "Open in Safari" - iOS remembers per-domain.
* Link uses `http://` instead of `https://` - verification requires TLS.

# expo-linking API

Parsing URLs, listeners, and cold-start vs warm-start handling - the `expo-linking` cookbook for Expo SDK 57 apps that receive links from email, SMS, QR codes, and other apps.

Highlights / expo-linking API

* Linking.parse breaks any inbound URL into path, hostname, and queryParams
* getInitialURL handles cold start - addEventListener handles warm start
* createURL builds outbound links that respect your configured scheme
* Gate navigation until Router and auth state are ready - or initial links are dropped
* Call canOpenURL before opening third-party schemes - returns false when app is missing
* Expo Router subsumes most parsing when using file-based routes - use Linking for side effects

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```tsx
import * as Linking from "expo-linking";
import { useEffect } from "react";
import { router } from "expo-router";
 
function routeFromUrl(url: string) {
  const { path, queryParams } = Linking.parse(url);
  const cleanPath = `/${(path ?? "").replace(/^\/+/, "")}`;
  router.push({ pathname: cleanPath as never, params: queryParams ?? {} });
}
 
export function useDeepLinkBootstrap() {
  useEffect(() => {
    Linking.getInitialURL().then((url) => {
      if (url) routeFromUrl(url);
    });
 
    const sub = Linking.addEventListener("url", ({ url }) => routeFromUrl(url));
    return () => sub.remove();
  }, []);
}
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Custom analytics or attribution before Expo Router navigates.
* Non–file-based routes (password reset tokens, magic links).
* OAuth return URLs handled outside Router - see auth-session.
* Opening external apps (`maps://`, `mailto:`) with `openURL`.
* Building share sheets and referral links with `createURL`.

## Working Example

```tsx
// src/linking/useAppLinking.ts
import * as Linking from "expo-linking";
import { router } from "expo-router";
import { useEffect, useRef } from "react";
import { z } from "zod";
 
const orderParams = z.object({
  id: z.string().min(1),
  ref: z.string().optional(),
});
 
function navigateFromUrl(url: string) {
  const parsed = Linking.parse(url);
  const segments = (parsed.path ?? "").split("/").filter(Boolean);
 
  if (segments[0] === "orders" && segments[1]) {
    const result = orderParams.safeParse({
      id: segments[1],
      ref: parsed.queryParams?.ref,
    });
 
    if (!result.success) {
      router.replace("/");
      return;
    }
 
    router.push({
      pathname: "/orders/[id]",
      params: { id: result.data.id, ref: result.data.ref ?? "" },
    });
    return;
  }
 
  router.replace("/");
}
 
type Options = {
  enabled: boolean;
};
 
export function useAppLinking({ enabled }: Options) {
  const handledInitial = useRef(false);
 
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!enabled) return;
 
    Linking.getInitialURL().then((url) => {
      if (!url || handledInitial.current) return;
      handledInitial.current = true;
      navigateFromUrl(url);
    });
 
    const subscription = Linking.addEventListener("url", ({ url }) => {
      navigateFromUrl(url);
    });
 
    return () => subscription.remove();
  }, [enabled]);
}
```

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
import { useAppLinking } from "../src/linking/useAppLinking";
import { useAuthReady } from "../src/auth/useAuthReady";
 
export default function RootLayout() {
  const authReady = useAuthReady();
 
  useAppLinking({ enabled: authReady });
 
  return (
    <Stack>
      <Stack.Screen name="(tabs)" options={{ headerShown: false }} />
      <Stack.Screen name="orders/[id]" options={{ title: "Order" }} />
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* **Cold start** via `getInitialURL` with a ref guard against double handling.
* **Warm start** via `addEventListener` with cleanup on unmount.
* **Auth gating** - links wait until `authReady` so protected routes do not flash.
* **Zod validation** at the linking boundary - malformed URLs fall back to home.
* **Expo Router** `router.push` with dynamic pathname and params.

## Deep Dive

### How It Works

* The OS delivers URLs to your app through **custom scheme handlers** or **verified HTTPS intent filters**.
* On launch, the native layer queues the URL; `getInitialURL` reads it once JavaScript starts.
* While running, new URLs arrive as events on the `url` channel - same shape `{ url: string }`.
* Expo Router registers its own linking config from `app/` - your listener runs in parallel for side effects.
* `Linking.parse` uses the WHATWG URL parser - invalid URLs return `{ path: null, queryParams: null }`.

### Cold Start vs Warm Start

| Scenario | App state | API | Pitfall |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cold start | Process killed | `getInitialURL()` | Navigating before auth/Router ready drops the URL |
| Warm start (background) | JS running | `addEventListener("url")` | Duplicate handler if layout remounts without cleanup |
| Warm start (foreground) | JS running | `addEventListener("url")` | Same URL may fire twice on some Android OEMs |
| User opened from icon | No link | `getInitialURL()` → `null` | Do not treat `null` as an error |

### Key API Surface

| Method / Event | Returns | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Linking.parse(url)` | `{ scheme, hostname, path, queryParams }` | Inspect inbound URLs |
| `Linking.createURL(path, opts?)` | `string` | Build share/referral links |
| `Linking.getInitialURL()` | `Promise<string | null>` | Cold-start bootstrap |
| `Linking.addEventListener("url", fn)` | `Subscription` | Warm-start listener |
| `Linking.openURL(url)` | `Promise<true>` | Open external apps |
| `Linking.canOpenURL(url)` | `Promise<boolean>` | Check if target app exists |
| `Linking.getLinkingURL()` | `string | null` | Dev-only Expo Go URL (avoid in prod) |

### TypeScript Notes

```ts
import * as Linking from "expo-linking";
 
type ParsedLink = ReturnType<typeof Linking.parse>;
 
function queryParam(
  parsed: ParsedLink,
  key: string
): string | undefined {
  const value = parsed.queryParams?.[key];
  return Array.isArray(value) ? value[0] : value;
}
```

* `queryParams` values may be `string | string[]` - normalize before Zod parsing.
* `path` omits leading slash for custom schemes - normalize before concatenation.
* Use `router.push` typed routes when `experiments.typedRoutes` is enabled - invalid paths fail at compile time.

## Gotchas

* **Handling initial URL before auth resolves** - protected screens mount, then redirect, losing deep-link context. **Fix:** gate `useAppLinking({ enabled: authReady })` as shown above.
* **Double navigation on cold start** - both Expo Router and your hook push the same route. **Fix:** disable custom navigation when Router linking suffices, or set `initialRouteName` explicitly.
* **Forgetting listener cleanup** - Fast Refresh stacks listeners; one link triggers five navigations. **Fix:** `return () => subscription.remove()` in `useEffect`.
* **Hardcoding `myapp://` strings** - breaks across flavors and Expo Go. **Fix:** always `Linking.createURL("orders/42")`.
* **Trusting query params for auth** - `?token=` in URLs lands in analytics and logs. **Fix:** exchange tokens server-side; use short-lived one-time codes in links.
* **`canOpenURL` blocked on iOS without LSApplicationQueriesSchemes** - always returns false for unlisted schemes. **Fix:** declare queried schemes in `app.config.ts` `ios.infoPlist`.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Expo Router linking only | File-based routes cover all paths | You need pre-navigation analytics or token exchange |
| React Navigation `linking` config | Brownfield React Navigation app | Greenfield Expo Router project |
| Branch / AppsFlyer SDK | Deferred deep links + attribution | Simple custom-scheme-only app |
| Manual `Linking.parse` in every screen | Legacy codebase | New code - centralize in one hook |

## FAQs

Does Expo Router replace expo-linking?

* Router uses linking under the hood for path mapping.
* Keep `expo-linking` for `createURL`, `openURL`, `canOpenURL`, and custom pre-navigation logic.

When should I call getInitialURL?

* Once at app startup - typically in root `_layout.tsx` or an auth provider.
* Do not poll it - the value does not change until the next cold start.

Why is getInitialURL null but the app opened from a link?

* Listener-only setup with no cold-start handler.
* Navigation ran before the effect - gate on splash until linking hook completes.
* Expo Go vs dev client scheme mismatch - link targeted wrong binary.

How do I open WhatsApp or Maps from my app?

```ts
const url = "maps://?q=Coffee+Shop";
if (await Linking.canOpenURL(url)) {
  await Linking.openURL(url);
}
```

* Add target schemes to `LSApplicationQueriesSchemes` on iOS.

Can I use expo-linking on web?

* `parse` and `createURL` work on web with `http`/`https` origins.
* `getInitialURL` returns the page URL on first load - guard with `Platform.OS !== "web"` if sharing code.

How do query params with duplicate keys parse?

* `?tag=a&tag=b` yields `queryParams.tag` as `string[]`.
* Normalize to a single string before validation.

Should warm-start links use replace or push?

* **Push** when the user should back-navigate to the previous screen.
* **Replace** for magic links and password resets - prevent back into unauthenticated stacks.

How do I log links without leaking PII?

* Log `path` only - strip `token`, `email`, and `code` query keys before analytics.
* Hash order IDs if your policy treats them as sensitive.

Does addEventListener fire for universal links?

* Yes - verified `https://` links trigger the same event once the app opens.
* Failed verification opens Safari instead - your JS never runs.

How do I test getInitialURL in Jest?

```ts
jest.spyOn(Linking, "getInitialURL").mockResolvedValue("shopapp://orders/1");
```

* Mock `addEventListener` to invoke the callback manually in integration tests.

# Deep Linking Highlights Summary

Every highlight bullet from the 8 pages in this section, gathered on one page and grouped by the page it came from.

Highlights / Deep Linking Highlights Summary

* Custom schemes (myapp://) work everywhere but show an 'Open in app?' prompt on the web
* Linking.parse breaks any inbound URL into path, hostname, and queryParams
* Universal Links open https:// URLs directly in your app when AASA verification passes
* App Links verify https:// URLs at install time via Digital Asset Links
* Deferred deep links route users to the intended screen after first install
* Put routing paths in notification data payload - not only in title/body text

## [Deep Linking Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/deep-linking/deep-linking-basics/)

* Custom schemes (myapp://) work everywhere but show an 'Open in app?' prompt on the web
* Universal Links (iOS) and App Links (Android) open https:// URLs directly in the installed app
* Declare scheme and associated domains in app.config.ts before shipping deep links
* Expo Router maps file paths to URLs - app/orders/[id].tsx becomes /orders/:id
* expo-linking parses URLs into path, queryParams, and hostname for custom handlers
* Test cold-start links on development builds - Expo Go scheme behavior differs from store binaries

## [expo-linking API](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/deep-linking/expo-linking-api/)

* Linking.parse breaks any inbound URL into path, hostname, and queryParams
* getInitialURL handles cold start - addEventListener handles warm start
* createURL builds outbound links that respect your configured scheme
* Gate navigation until Router and auth state are ready - or initial links are dropped
* Call canOpenURL before opening third-party schemes - returns false when app is missing
* Expo Router subsumes most parsing when using file-based routes - use Linking for side effects

## [iOS Universal Links](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/deep-linking/ios-universal-links/)

* Universal Links open https:// URLs directly in your app when AASA verification passes
* associatedDomains in app.config.ts must use the applinks: prefix
* apple-app-site-association must be served over HTTPS with no redirects and application/json
* CDN caching mistakes are the top production failure - stale AASA blocks new paths
* Users can force Safari with long-press - design web fallbacks for the same URLs
* Rebuild and reinstall after entitlement changes - OTA cannot add associated domains

## [Android App Links](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/deep-linking/android-app-links/)

* App Links verify https:// URLs at install time via Digital Asset Links
* intentFilters with autoVerify: true trigger Android domain verification
* assetlinks.json must list your signing certificate SHA-256 fingerprint
* Play App Signing uses Google's cert - register Play Console fingerprint, not only upload key
* Verification failures fall back to a disambiguation chooser - users pick browser or app
* Rebuild after intent filter changes - manifest updates require a new native binary

## [Deferred Deep Links](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/deep-linking/deferred-deep-links/)

* Deferred deep links route users to the intended screen after first install
* iOS does not expose a reliable install referrer - attribution SDKs or server-side matching required
* Android Play Install Referrer API provides campaign metadata - respect user privacy disclosures
* SKAdNetwork and ATT limit deterministic user-level attribution on iOS
* Store pending deep-link intent in memory + SecureStore - not AsyncStorage for sensitive targets
* Always offer a manual fallback path when deferred matching fails

## [Push Notification Deep Links](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/deep-linking/push-notification-deep-links/)

* Put routing paths in notification data payload - not only in title/body text
* Handle cold start (getLastNotificationResponseAsync) and warm tap (addNotificationResponseReceivedListener)
* Gate navigation on auth ready - order notifications must not flash before login
* Use router.push for browsable stacks, router.replace for transactional one-shots
* Validate payload paths with Zod - malformed push data should not crash the app
* Expo Go push credentials differ from production - test on dev client builds

## [Deep Link Testing Matrix](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/deep-linking/deep-link-testing-matrix/)

* Test matrix spans link type, app state, platform, and build flavor - not a single happy path
* Cold start and warm start behave differently - both need explicit rows
* Universal links fail silently in Safari when verification breaks - device testing is mandatory
* CI can smoke-test custom schemes via Maestro; HTTPS verification needs hosted JSON checks
* Expo Go is not a substitute for dev-client or store builds in deep-link QA
* Log path + query in test builds only - redact tokens before analytics

## [Deep Linking Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/deep-linking/best-practices/)

* 25 essentials for schemes, universal links, push taps, and deferred routing
* Validate every inbound path and query param - URLs are untrusted input
* Gate navigation on auth and onboarding - cold-start links wait for ready state
* Test cold and warm starts on dev clients - Expo Go is not production parity
* Host AASA and assetlinks.json with CI checks - CDN regressions fail silently
* Idempotent routes and safe fallbacks prevent crashes from malformed marketing links

# iOS Universal Links

Associated domains, `apple-app-site-association`, and CDN hosting - the iOS cookbook for opening `https://` marketing URLs directly in your Expo SDK 57 app without a custom scheme disambiguation sheet.

Highlights / iOS Universal Links

* Universal Links open https:// URLs directly in your app when AASA verification passes
* associatedDomains in app.config.ts must use the applinks: prefix
* apple-app-site-association must be served over HTTPS with no redirects and application/json
* CDN caching mistakes are the top production failure - stale AASA blocks new paths
* Users can force Safari with long-press - design web fallbacks for the same URLs
* Rebuild and reinstall after entitlement changes - OTA cannot add associated domains

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```ts
// app.config.ts
export default {
  expo: {
    scheme: "shopapp",
    ios: {
      bundleIdentifier: "com.example.shopapp",
      associatedDomains: ["applinks:shop.example.com"],
    },
  },
};
```

```json
// https://shop.example.com/.well-known/apple-app-site-association
{
  "applinks": {
    "apps": [],
    "details": [
      {
        "appID": "TEAMID.com.example.shopapp",
        "paths": ["/orders/*", "/product/*", "/invite/*"]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Email and SMS campaigns use `https://` links that should open the app when installed.
* You want seamless handoff from your marketing site without `myapp://` prompts.
* App Store listings and smart banners reference the same canonical URLs as the app.
* You need iOS to verify domain ownership before opening links in-app.

## Working Example

End-to-end setup for `https://shop.example.com/orders/*` on an Expo prebuild app.

**Step 1 - Entitlements via app.config.ts**

```ts
// app.config.ts
import type { ExpoConfig } from "expo/config";
 
const config: ExpoConfig = {
  name: "ShopApp",
  slug: "shop-app",
  scheme: "shopapp",
  ios: {
    bundleIdentifier: "com.example.shopapp",
    associatedDomains: ["applinks:shop.example.com"],
  },
  android: {
    package: "com.example.shopapp",
  },
};
 
export default config;
```

**Step 2 - Host AASA on your CDN**

```json
{
  "applinks": {
    "apps": [],
    "details": [
      {
        "appID": "ABCDE12345.com.example.shopapp",
        "paths": [
          "/orders/*",
          "/product/*",
          "NOT /admin/*",
          "NOT /api/*"
        ]
      }
    ]
  },
  "webcredentials": {
    "apps": ["ABCDE12345.com.example.shopapp"]
  }
}
```

Serve at **both** paths (Apple checks either):

* `https://shop.example.com/apple-app-site-association`
* `https://shop.example.com/.well-known/apple-app-site-association`

**Step 3 - CDN response headers**

```http
Content-Type: application/json
Cache-Control: max-age=3600
```

* No **301/302 redirects** on the AASA URL - Apple rejects redirected association files.
* File must be **unsigned** - no `.json` extension required; raw JSON body.
* Replace `ABCDE12345` with your Apple Team ID from the Developer portal.

**Step 4 - Expo Router screen**

```tsx
// app/orders/[id].tsx
import { useLocalSearchParams } from "expo-router";
import { Text, View } from "react-native";
 
export default function OrderScreen() {
  const { id } = useLocalSearchParams<{ id: string }>();
  return (
    <View style={{ padding: 16 }}>
      <Text>Order {id}</Text>
    </View>
  );
}
```

**Step 5 - Build and verify**

```bash
npx expo prebuild --platform ios
npx expo run:ios
# Simulator: open universal link
xcrun simctl openurl booted "https://shop.example.com/orders/42"
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* **associatedDomains** entitlement generated at prebuild.
* **AASA** path rules limiting which URLs open the app.
* **CDN headers** required for Apple's crawler.
* **Expo Router** dynamic route matching `/orders/42`.
* **Simulator testing** before TestFlight.

## Deep Dive

### How It Works

* At install, iOS fetches AASA from each `applinks:` domain in your entitlements.
* Apple caches association data on device - updates propagate slowly (hours, sometimes days).
* When the user taps a matching `https://` link, iOS opens your app and passes the URL to React Native.
* If verification fails or the path is excluded, Safari handles the URL normally.
* Custom schemes still work in parallel - universal links are preferred for marketing.

### AASA Path Rules

| Pattern | Matches |
| --- | --- |
| `/orders/*` | `/orders/42`, `/orders/42/receipt` |
| `/product/*` | `/product/widget` |
| `NOT /admin/*` | Excludes admin URLs even if parent would match |
| `*` | Everything on the domain - avoid unless app owns entire host |

### CDN Checklist

| Check | Pass criteria |
| --- | --- |
| TLS | Valid certificate; no mixed `http://` |
| Redirects | AASA URL returns 200 directly |
| Content-Type | `application/json` or `application/pkcs7-mime` (signed) |
| Size | Under 128 KB |
| Accessibility | Public internet - no VPN or IP allowlist |

### iOS Notes

```bash
# Validate AASA with Apple's CDN (device will eventually see same data)
curl -s "https://app-site-association.cdn-apple.com/a/v1/shop.example.com" | jq .
```

* After changing AASA, bump CDN cache or purge edge nodes - stale files cause "works in staging, broken in prod."
* **TestFlight** builds use the production bundle ID - match `appID` exactly.
* Users who chose "Open in Safari" disable universal links per site until reset in Settings.

## Gotchas

* **Wrong Team ID in appID** - link opens Safari silently. **Fix:** `TEAMID.bundleIdentifier` from Apple Developer → Membership.
* **AASA behind redirect** - `www` → apex redirect breaks fetch. **Fix:** serve AASA on the exact host in `associatedDomains`.
* **Forgetting to rebuild after adding associatedDomains** - entitlement missing in IPA. **Fix:** `eas build --platform ios` after config change.
* **Including `/api/*` in paths** - API JSON responses should not open the app. **Fix:** explicit `NOT` rules or narrow prefixes.
* **Expecting instant AASA updates** - iOS caches aggressively. **Fix:** change paths only with versioned marketing campaigns; keep old paths during transition.
* **Universal link from same domain in WKWebView** - in-app browser may not hand off. **Fix:** use `SFSafariViewController` or `<a target="_blank">` for external open.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Custom scheme only | Internal tools, OAuth redirects | Consumer email campaigns |
| Firebase Dynamic Links (deprecated) | Legacy projects already integrated | Greenfield - Google shut down Aug 2025 |
| Branch.io / AppsFlyer OneLink | Deferred deep links + attribution | Simple verified links suffice |
| Smart App Banner only | Web-to-app nudge without full universal links | You need tap-to-open without Safari |

## FAQs

Where do I find my Apple Team ID?

* Apple Developer → Account → Membership details → **Team ID**.
* Format in AASA: `TEAMID.com.example.shopapp` - no spaces.

Do I need a separate AASA per build flavor?

* One file can list multiple `details` entries with different `appID` values for dev and prod bundle IDs.
* Domains can differ per flavor - `applinks:staging.example.com` vs `applinks:shop.example.com`.

Why does long-press show "Open in ShopApp" but tap opens Safari?

* AASA verification failed or path not listed - long-press uses heuristics; tap requires verification.
* Check CDN with `curl -I` for redirects and content type.

Can I use wildcard subdomains?

* Use `applinks:*.example.com` in entitlements and separate `details` per subdomain in AASA.
* `*.example.com` in paths is not valid - list each subdomain explicitly.

Does Expo Go support universal links for my bundle ID?

* No - universal links require your signed bundle ID and entitlements in a dev client or store build.

What is webcredentials in AASA?

* Enables Password AutoFill association between your app and website - optional but recommended for login flows.

How do I debug on a physical device?

* Install build → tap link in Notes app (not Messages preview).
* Settings → Developer → diagnose associated domains (iOS 17+).

Should marketing use query strings?

* Yes - `/orders/42?ref=email` works if `/orders/*` matches; query does not affect path rules.
* Strip tracking params before routing if they are not in your Zod schema.

Can one domain point to multiple apps?

* AASA supports multiple `details` entries - iOS picks the installed app matching `appID`.
* Watch for conflicts when sister apps share a domain.

How does this interact with Expo Router?

* Router maps `https://shop.example.com/orders/42` to `app/orders/[id].tsx` automatically when scheme/host are configured.
* See [../expo-router/link-and-href/link-and-href.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/link-and-href/).

Dokumen: Design Systems Best Practices
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/best-practices/

# Design Systems Best Practices

A condensed summary of the 25 most important best practices drawn from every page in this section.

Highlights / Design Systems Best Practices

* Tokens before libraries - semantic roles beat raw hex in feature screens
* Component APIs stay small: variant, size, disabled - not style soup per screen
* Pick one styling strategy per app - NativeWind, Tamagui, Paper, or tokens + StyleSheet
* Bake accessibilityRole and accessibilityLabel into primitives, not per-screen patches
* On-device Storybook is the RN catalog - semver the package that screens import
* White-label flavors swap config - never fork repos for logo and primary color

1. **Start with tokens, not a library:** Define color, spacing, and typography roles in a module before adopting NativeWind, Tamagui, or Paper - libraries consume tokens; they do not replace design decisions.
2. **Name tokens by semantic role:** Use `surface`, `textPrimary`, and `accent` instead of `gray700` - palette overhauls and white-label flavors swap values without renaming every screen.
3. **Keep spacing on a fixed scale:** A 4px grid (`4, 8, 16, 24`) beats ad-hoc `13` and `17` padding - designers and engineers share one rhythm.
4. **Expose small component APIs:** Primitives accept `variant`, `size`, and `disabled` - not open-ended style props that recreate one-off buttons per feature.
5. **One ThemeProvider at the root:** Centralize scheme and brand selection - nested providers cause split-brain colors and double fetches on theme change.
6. **Apply dynamic colors at render:** Module-level `StyleSheet.create` with hard-coded hex does not react to dark mode - pair static layout with `useTheme()` or `dark:` utilities.
7. **Pick one styling strategy per app:** Mixing Tamagui screens, NativeWind screens, and raw `StyleSheet` without boundaries creates bundle bloat and inconsistent motion - choose a spine and wrap legacy incrementally.
8. **Profile before adopting a compiler:** NativeWind and Tamagui solve scale problems - a five-screen MVP does not need Metro transformers or `tamagui.config.ts` maintenance.
9. **NativeWind: static class strings in lists:** Dynamic `` `bg-${x}` `` breaks compile-time extraction - use fixed variant maps on row components.
10. **Tamagui: typed variants over inline hex:** `styled()` variants encode design states - `$brand` tokens keep dark mode and flavors coherent.
11. **React Native Paper: always wrap PaperProvider:** MD3 theme, ripple, and icons flow from context - screens that skip the provider silently fall back to defaults.
12. **Paper + Navigation: use adaptNavigationTheme:** Header and tab colors should match `primary` and `surface` - mismatched chrome reads as two different apps.
13. **@expo/ui for native chrome, RN for density:** Universal `Host`/`Button`/`Switch` excel at platform feel - virtualized lists and custom charts stay in RN (`RNHostView` islands).
14. **SwiftUI modifiers are not RN styles:** Widget and glass layouts use `@expo/ui/swift-ui/modifiers` - do not paste `StyleSheet` into extension targets.
15. **Accessibility belongs in primitives:** Set `accessibilityRole="button"` and labels on library `Button`/`Pressable` once - feature teams forget per-screen patches.
16. **Support dynamic type on text primitives:** Forward `maxFontSizeMultiplier` and test long German strings on `Text` wrappers - dense toolbars cap scaling; body copy should not.
17. **Honor reduced motion in animated primitives:** Loading skeletons and entrance transitions should respect system settings - gate Reanimated entering animations when reduced motion is on.
18. **Contrast-test every brand flavor:** White-label `primary`/`onPrimary` pairs must pass audit per tenant - one passing Acme palette does not certify Globex green.
19. **Storybook documents states, not just happy path:** Empty, loading, error, disabled, and long-text stories catch layout bugs before they reach production auth flows.
20. **Keep Storybook out of production bundles:** Use `STORYBOOK_ENABLED` entry swapping - never import `.rnstorybook` unconditionally in `App.tsx`.
21. **Semver the UI package like any dependency:** Renaming `title` → `label` is a **major** bump - mobile apps pin versions; document breaking visual changes in CHANGELOG.
22. **Export a narrow public API:** Barrel-export only primitives and hooks from `index.ts` - internal helpers prefixed or unexported prevent unsupported coupling.
23. **White-label with flavor config, not git forks:** `BRAND_FLAVOR` in EAS profiles + `brands` registry scales security patches - forks multiply SDK upgrade cost.
24. **Isolate OTA channels per flavor:** Publishing one client's JS bundle to another tenant's channel is a branding and data incident - map channels in `eas.json`.
25. **Cross-review tokens in CI:** Block new raw hex in feature folders and new inline styles in list `renderItem` - design system discipline erodes one PR at a time without lint gates.

## FAQs

When should we adopt NativeWind or Tamagui?

When you have **many screens** sharing tokens and utility or variant ergonomics measurably beats `StyleSheet` maintenance. Stay on tokens + `StyleSheet` until copy-paste drift appears - see [Design Systems Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/design-systems-basics/).

Paper or custom primitives?

Choose **Paper** for MD3 Android-first products with standard forms and dialogs. Choose **custom + tokens** when brand language is not Material. See [React Native Paper](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/react-native-paper/).

Where does @expo/ui fit?

Drop-in **native** controls and hybrid layouts - not a full replacement for lists and navigation. See [Expo UI Drop-Ins](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/expo-ui-drop-ins/).

How do dark mode and brand flavors compose?

**Flavor** picks brand primary and assets; **scheme** picks neutral backgrounds and borders. Merge in one provider - see [Theming & Brand Flavors](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/theming-and-brand-flavors/).

Do we need an internal npm package?

Extract when **two apps** share primitives or when Storybook and semver matter. Single-app teams can use `components/` until the second consumer appears - see [Building an Internal Component Library](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/building-an-internal-component-library/).

What is the minimum a11y gate for primitives?

`accessibilityRole`, visible label (or `accessibilityLabel` on icon-only controls), contrast on text, and VoiceOver/TalkBack smoke on each new primitive - see [Accessibility Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/accessibility/accessibility-basics/).

## Related

* [Design Systems Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/design-systems-basics/) - tokens, spacing, and component API examples
* [NativeWind (Tailwind for RN)](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/nativewind-tailwind-for-rn/) - utility classes and dark mode on Expo
* [Tamagui](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/tamagui/) - compiled tokens and styled primitives
* [React Native Paper](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/react-native-paper/) - MD3 theming and PaperProvider
* [Expo UI Drop-Ins](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/expo-ui-drop-ins/) - universal vs SwiftUI/Compose surfaces
* [Building an Internal Component Library](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/building-an-internal-component-library/) - Storybook and semver
* [Theming & Brand Flavors](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/theming-and-brand-flavors/) - white-label without forks
* [Dark Mode & Color Schemes](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/dark-mode-and-color-schemes/) - semantic palettes and system sync
* [Accessibility Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/accessibility/accessibility-basics/) - assistive tech fundamentals

Dokumen: Design Systems Basics
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/design-systems-basics/

# Design Systems Basics

10 examples to get you started with Design Systems - 7 basic and 3 intermediate.

Highlights / Design Systems Basics

* Design tokens are named constants - colors, spacing, type - not raw values in screens
* Semantic tokens (surface, textPrimary) survive palette overhauls better than gray-500
* A spacing scale on a 4px grid keeps padding and gaps consistent across components
* Component APIs expose variant, size, and disabled - not one-off style props per screen
* ThemeProvider centralizes active palette; screens call useTheme() instead of hard-coded hex
* Type token objects with as const and derive union types for variant props

## Prerequisites

Every example below uses built-in React Native primitives and a small token module - no third-party design library required. Scaffold a standard **Expo SDK 57** TypeScript app and replace `App.tsx` to run each snippet.

```bash
npx create-expo-app@latest MyDesignApp --template blank-typescript
cd MyDesignApp
npx expo start
```

> **Tooling:** These examples target **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4), **React Native 0.86.0**, and **React 19.2.3**. Tokens pair naturally with [Styling Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/styling-basics/) and [Dark Mode & Color Schemes](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/dark-mode-and-color-schemes/).

---

## Basic Examples

### 1. Color Tokens as Named Constants

Replace scattered hex values with a single palette object. Components reference **roles**, not literals.

```tsx
// theme/colors.ts
export const colors = {
  brand: {
    primary: "#2563eb",
    primaryMuted: "#93c5fd",
    onPrimary: "#ffffff",
  },
  neutral: {
    50: "#f8fafc",
    100: "#f1f5f9",
    700: "#334155",
    900: "#0f172a",
  },
  feedback: {
    success: "#16a34a",
    danger: "#dc2626",
  },
} as const;
```

```tsx
import { Pressable, StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
import { colors } from "./theme/colors";
 
export default function App() {
  return (
    <View style={styles.screen}>
      <Pressable style={styles.cta}>
        <Text style={styles.ctaLabel}>Continue</Text>
      </Pressable>
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  screen: { flex: 1, justifyContent: "center", padding: 24, backgroundColor: colors.neutral[50] },
  cta: { backgroundColor: colors.brand.primary, padding: 16, borderRadius: 10, alignItems: "center" },
  ctaLabel: { color: colors.brand.onPrimary, fontWeight: "700", fontSize: 16 },
});
```

* **`as const`** narrows types so typos fail at compile time
* Name tokens by **intent** (`onPrimary`) not by value (`white`)
* Keep palette in one module - screens import tokens, never `#2563eb` directly
* When you adopt NativeWind or Tamagui later, this object becomes your `tailwind.config` or theme source

> **Related:** [Styling Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/styling-basics/) - StyleSheet vs inline and token promotion

---

### 2. Spacing Scale on a 4px Grid

A spacing scale removes magic numbers. Most mobile design systems use multiples of **4**.

```tsx
// theme/spacing.ts
export const spacing = {
  xs: 4,
  sm: 8,
  md: 16,
  lg: 24,
  xl: 32,
  xxl: 48,
} as const;
```

```tsx
import { StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
import { spacing } from "./theme/spacing";
 
export default function App() {
  return (
    <View style={styles.card}>
      <Text style={styles.title}>Order summary</Text>
      <Text style={styles.body}>3 items · arrives tomorrow</Text>
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  card: {
    margin: spacing.md,
    padding: spacing.lg,
    gap: spacing.sm,
    borderRadius: 12,
    backgroundColor: "#fff",
  },
  title: { fontSize: 18, fontWeight: "600" },
  body: { fontSize: 15, lineHeight: 22 },
});
```

* **`gap`** on flex containers uses the same scale as `padding` and `margin`
* Document the grid in your design handoff - engineers and designers share `md = 16`
* Avoid odd values (`13`, `17`) unless correcting optical alignment on a specific component
* Spacing tokens compose with [Safe Areas & Notches](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/safe-areas-and-notches/) - safe area is additive, not a replacement for the scale

> **Related:** [Flexbox Deep Dive](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/flexbox-deep-dive/) - `gap` vs margin on first/last child

---

### 3. Typography Scale

Map **roles** (`title`, `body`, `label`) to `fontSize` + `lineHeight` pairs. Screens reference roles, not raw numbers.

```tsx
// theme/typography.ts
export const typography = {
  display: { fontSize: 32, lineHeight: 40, fontWeight: "700" as const },
  title: { fontSize: 20, lineHeight: 28, fontWeight: "600" as const },
  body: { fontSize: 16, lineHeight: 24, fontWeight: "400" as const },
  label: { fontSize: 13, lineHeight: 18, fontWeight: "500" as const },
} as const;
```

```tsx
import { StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
import { typography } from "./theme/typography";
 
export default function App() {
  return (
    <View style={styles.screen}>
      <Text style={styles.display}>Welcome back</Text>
      <Text style={styles.body}>Your saved items are ready to checkout.</Text>
      <Text style={styles.label}>LAST UPDATED · 2 MIN AGO</Text>
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  screen: { flex: 1, padding: 24, gap: 8 },
  display: typography.display,
  body: typography.body,
  label: { ...typography.label, letterSpacing: 0.6, color: "#64748b" },
});
```

* Pair every `fontSize` with an explicit **`lineHeight`** - default line heights clip descenders on Android
* Load custom font families in one place - see [Typography Scale & Font Loading](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/typography-scale-and-font-loading/)
* Respect dynamic type: primitives should accept `maxFontSizeMultiplier` - see [Dynamic Type & Font Scaling](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/accessibility/dynamic-type-and-font-scaling/)

> **Related:** [Typography Scale & Font Loading](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/typography-scale-and-font-loading/) - expo-font and accessible text

---

### 4. Semantic Color Roles

Semantic tokens decouple components from palette values. `surface` means "card background" in both light and dark schemes.

```tsx
// theme/semantic.ts
export const light = {
  background: "#f8fafc",
  surface: "#ffffff",
  textPrimary: "#0f172a",
  textSecondary: "#64748b",
  border: "#e2e8f0",
  accent: "#2563eb",
} as const;
 
export const dark = {
  background: "#020617",
  surface: "#0f172a",
  textPrimary: "#f8fafc",
  textSecondary: "#94a3b8",
  border: "#334155",
  accent: "#60a5fa",
} as const;
```

```tsx
import { StyleSheet, Text, useColorScheme, View } from "react-native";
import { dark, light } from "./theme/semantic";
 
export default function App() {
  const scheme = useColorScheme() ?? "light";
  const theme = scheme === "dark" ? dark : light;
 
  return (
    <View style={[styles.screen, { backgroundColor: theme.background }]}>
      <View style={[styles.card, { backgroundColor: theme.surface, borderColor: theme.border }]}>
        <Text style={{ color: theme.textPrimary, fontSize: 17, fontWeight: "600" }}>Inbox</Text>
        <Text style={{ color: theme.textSecondary, fontSize: 15 }}>12 unread messages</Text>
      </View>
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  screen: { flex: 1, padding: 16 },
  card: { padding: 16, borderRadius: 12, borderWidth: 1, gap: 4 },
});
```

* Components reference **`theme.textPrimary`**, not `dark.textPrimary` - selection happens once at the screen or provider
* Static layout keys stay in `StyleSheet.create`; **colors apply at render** when they follow the scheme
* Semantic naming is the bridge to [Dark Mode & Color Schemes](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/dark-mode-and-color-schemes/) and white-label flavors

> **Related:** [Dark Mode & Color Schemes](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/dark-mode-and-color-schemes/) - `useColorScheme` and `Appearance.setColorScheme`

---

### 5. Radius and Elevation Tokens

Corner radius and shadow/elevation belong in the token layer - cards, chips, and sheets share the same values.

```tsx
// theme/shape.ts
import { Platform } from "react-native";
 
export const radius = {
  sm: 6,
  md: 12,
  lg: 20,
  full: 999,
} as const;
 
export const elevation = {
  card: Platform.select({
    ios: {
      shadowColor: "#000",
      shadowOffset: { width: 0, height: 2 },
      shadowOpacity: 0.08,
      shadowRadius: 8,
    },
    android: { elevation: 3 },
    default: {},
  }),
  modal: Platform.select({
    ios: {
      shadowColor: "#000",
      shadowOffset: { width: 0, height: 8 },
      shadowOpacity: 0.15,
      shadowRadius: 24,
    },
    android: { elevation: 8 },
    default: {},
  }),
} as const;
```

```tsx
import { StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
import { elevation, radius } from "./theme/shape";
 
export default function App() {
  return (
    <View style={styles.screen}>
      <View style={styles.card}>
        <Text style={styles.title}>Delivery ETA</Text>
        <Text style={styles.body}>Arrives by 6:30 PM</Text>
      </View>
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  screen: { flex: 1, justifyContent: "center", padding: 24, backgroundColor: "#f1f5f9" },
  card: {
    backgroundColor: "#fff",
    borderRadius: radius.md,
    padding: 20,
    gap: 6,
    ...elevation.card,
  },
  title: { fontSize: 17, fontWeight: "600" },
  body: { fontSize: 15, color: "#475569" },
});
```

* iOS uses **shadow props**; Android uses **`elevation`** - `Platform.select` in tokens keeps components clean
* Elevated surfaces need an **opaque `backgroundColor`** - transparent cards produce invisible depth
* See [Shadows, Elevation & Borders](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/shadows-elevation-and-borders/) for wrapper vs clip patterns

> **Related:** [Shadows, Elevation & Borders](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/shadows-elevation-and-borders/) - cross-platform depth

---

### 6. ThemeProvider and useTheme

Centralize theme selection in a React context so nested components avoid prop drilling.

```tsx
// theme/ThemeProvider.tsx
import { createContext, useContext, useMemo } from "react";
import { useColorScheme } from "react-native";
import { dark, light } from "./semantic";
 
type Theme = typeof light;
const ThemeContext = createContext<Theme>(light);
 
export function ThemeProvider({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  const scheme = useColorScheme() ?? "light";
  const theme = useMemo(() => (scheme === "dark" ? dark : light), [scheme]);
  return <ThemeContext.Provider value={theme}>{children}</ThemeContext.Provider>;
}
 
export function useTheme() {
  return useContext(ThemeContext);
}
```

```tsx
// App.tsx
import { StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
import { ThemeProvider, useTheme } from "./theme/ThemeProvider";
 
function ProfileCard() {
  const theme = useTheme();
  return (
    <View style={[styles.card, { backgroundColor: theme.surface, borderColor: theme.border }]}>
      <Text style={{ color: theme.textPrimary, fontWeight: "600" }}>Alex Kim</Text>
      <Text style={{ color: theme.textSecondary }}>Pro member</Text>
    </View>
  );
}
 
export default function App() {
  return (
    <ThemeProvider>
      <View style={styles.screen}>
        <ProfileCard />
      </View>
    </ThemeProvider>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  screen: { flex: 1, padding: 16 },
  card: { padding: 16, borderRadius: 12, borderWidth: 1, gap: 4 },
});
```

* Wrap the app root (inside `SafeAreaProvider`) - one provider for the whole tree
* `useMemo` on the palette object avoids re-rendering consumers when the reference is stable across schemes
* Extend with **brand flavor** keys later - see [Theming & Brand Flavors](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/theming-and-brand-flavors/)

> **Related:** [Theming & Brand Flavors](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/theming-and-brand-flavors/) - multi-brand without forks

---

### 7. Button Variant and Size API

Design-system components expose a **small, typed API** - `variant`, `size`, `disabled` - instead of per-screen style overrides.

```tsx
// components/Button.tsx
import { Pressable, StyleSheet, Text, type PressableProps } from "react-native";
import { spacing } from "../theme/spacing";
 
type Variant = "primary" | "secondary" | "ghost";
type Size = "sm" | "md" | "lg";
 
type Props = PressableProps & {
  label: string;
  variant?: Variant;
  size?: Size;
};
 
const variantStyles: Record<Variant, { container: object; label: object }> = {
  primary: { container: { backgroundColor: "#2563eb" }, label: { color: "#fff" } },
  secondary: { container: { backgroundColor: "#e2e8f0" }, label: { color: "#0f172a" } },
  ghost: { container: { backgroundColor: "transparent" }, label: { color: "#2563eb" } },
};
 
const sizeStyles: Record<Size, { container: object; label: object }> = {
  sm: { container: { paddingVertical: spacing.xs, paddingHorizontal: spacing.sm }, label: { fontSize: 14 } },
  md: { container: { paddingVertical: spacing.sm, paddingHorizontal: spacing.md }, label: { fontSize: 16 } },
  lg: { container: { paddingVertical: spacing.md, paddingHorizontal: spacing.lg }, label: { fontSize: 17 } },
};
 
export function Button({ label, variant = "primary", size = "md", disabled, style, ...rest }: Props) {
  return (
    <Pressable
      accessibilityRole="button"
      disabled={disabled}
      style={[
        styles.base,
        variantStyles[variant].container,
        sizeStyles[size].container,
        disabled && styles.disabled,
        style,
      ]}
      {...rest}
    >
      <Text style={[styles.label, variantStyles[variant].label, sizeStyles[size].label]}>{label}</Text>
    </Pressable>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  base: { borderRadius: 10, alignItems: "center" },
  label: { fontWeight: "600" },
  disabled: { opacity: 0.45 },
});
```

```tsx
import { View } from "react-native";
import { Button } from "./components/Button";
 
export default function App() {
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1, justifyContent: "center", gap: 12, padding: 24 }}>
      <Button label="Continue" variant="primary" size="lg" />
      <Button label="Back" variant="ghost" size="md" />
      <Button label="Delete" variant="secondary" size="sm" disabled />
    </View>
  );
}
```

* **`accessibilityRole="button"`** is mandatory on custom pressables - see [accessibilityLabel & accessibilityRole](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/accessibility/accessibilitylabel-and-accessibilityrole/)
* Accept `style` last in the array so callers can override - document whether overrides are supported
* Map variants to tokens, not inline hex, before the component library grows

> **Related:** [accessibilityLabel & accessibilityRole](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/accessibility/accessibilitylabel-and-accessibilityrole/) - semantics on custom controls

---

## Intermediate Examples

### 8. Box Primitive with Token Props

A low-level **Box** (or `Stack`) primitive maps token props to style arrays - higher components compose it instead of raw `View`.

```tsx
// components/Box.tsx
import { View, type ViewProps } from "react-native";
import { spacing, type spacing as SpacingScale } from "../theme/spacing";
 
type SpacingKey = keyof typeof SpacingScale;
 
type Props = ViewProps & {
  p?: SpacingKey;
  px?: SpacingKey;
  gap?: SpacingKey;
  bg?: string;
};
 
export function Box({ p, px, gap, bg, style, ...rest }: Props) {
  return (
    <View
      style={[
        p != null && { padding: spacing[p] },
        px != null && { paddingHorizontal: spacing[px] },
        gap != null && { gap: spacing[gap] },
        bg != null && { backgroundColor: bg },
        style,
      ]}
      {...rest}
    />
  );
}
```

```tsx
import { Text } from "react-native";
import { Box } from "./components/Box";
 
export default function App() {
  return (
    <Box p="lg" gap="sm" bg="#f8fafc" style={{ flex: 1 }}>
      <Text style={{ fontSize: 20, fontWeight: "600" }}>Notifications</Text>
      <Box px="md" p="md" bg="#fff" style={{ borderRadius: 12 }}>
        <Text>Your order shipped.</Text>
      </Box>
    </Box>
  );
}
```

* Primitives stay **thin** - no business logic, only layout and surface tokens
* Prop names (`p`, `px`, `gap`) mirror design-tool shorthand designers already use
* Libraries like Tamagui formalize this pattern with compiled styles - see [Tamagui](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/tamagui/)

> **Related:** [Tamagui](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/tamagui/) - optimized token props at scale

---

### 9. Text Primitive with Tone and Role

Centralize text styling so screens pass **`tone="muted"`** instead of duplicating `fontSize` and `color`.

```tsx
// components/Text.tsx
import { Text as RNText, type TextProps } from "react-native";
import { typography } from "../theme/typography";
import { useTheme } from "../theme/ThemeProvider";
 
type Role = "display" | "title" | "body" | "label";
type Tone = "default" | "muted" | "accent" | "danger";
 
type Props = TextProps & { role?: Role; tone?: Tone };
 
export function Text({ role = "body", tone = "default", style, ...rest }: Props) {
  const theme = useTheme();
  const toneColor = {
    default: theme.textPrimary,
    muted: theme.textSecondary,
    accent: theme.accent,
    danger: "#dc2626",
  }[tone];
 
  return <RNText style={[typography[role], { color: toneColor }, style]} {...rest} />;
}
```

```tsx
import { ThemeProvider } from "./theme/ThemeProvider";
import { Text } from "./components/Text";
import { View } from "react-native";
 
export default function App() {
  return (
    <ThemeProvider>
      <View style={{ flex: 1, padding: 24, gap: 8 }}>
        <Text role="title">Payment method</Text>
        <Text tone="muted">Visa ending in 4242</Text>
        <Text role="label" tone="accent">
          CHANGE
        </Text>
      </View>
    </ThemeProvider>
  );
}
```

* Forward `...rest` so **`accessibilityLabel`** and **`maxFontSizeMultiplier`** pass through to the native `Text`
* `tone="danger"` should eventually map to `theme.feedback.danger` - keep feedback colors in tokens
* Pair with [Dynamic Type & Font Scaling](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/accessibility/dynamic-type-and-font-scaling/) on dense UI roles

> **Related:** [Dynamic Type & Font Scaling](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/accessibility/dynamic-type-and-font-scaling/) - `maxFontSizeMultiplier` on labels

---

### 10. Extending Tokens Without Breaking Callers

When design adds a new brand color, **extend** the token object and keep old keys - semver for tokens mirrors semver for npm packages.

```tsx
// theme/colors.v2.ts - additive change
import { colors as v1 } from "./colors";
 
export const colors = {
  ...v1,
  brand: {
    ...v1.brand,
    secondary: "#7c3aed", // new token - old screens unaffected
  },
} as const;
 
/** @deprecated Use colors.brand.primary - removed in v2.0 */
export const legacyPrimary = v1.brand.primary;
```

```tsx
// components/Badge.tsx - optional new variant, default unchanged
type Variant = "neutral" | "brand" | "brandSecondary";
 
const bg: Record<Variant, string> = {
  neutral: "#e2e8f0",
  brand: "#2563eb",
  brandSecondary: "#7c3aed",
};
 
export function Badge({ label, variant = "neutral" }: { label: string; variant?: Variant }) {
  return (
    <View style={{ backgroundColor: bg[variant], paddingHorizontal: 10, paddingVertical: 4, borderRadius: 999 }}>
      <Text style={{ color: variant === "neutral" ? "#0f172a" : "#fff", fontSize: 12, fontWeight: "600" }}>
        {label}
      </Text>
    </View>
  );
}
```

* **Additive** token keys are safe; **renaming** keys is a breaking change for every screen
* Deprecate with JSDoc and lint rules before removal - internal libraries use semver; see [Building an Internal Component Library](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/building-an-internal-component-library/)
* Document token changes in Storybook stories so designers see new variants in isolation

> **Related:** [Building an Internal Component Library](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/building-an-internal-component-library/) - semver and Storybook for UI packages
