Dokumen: Expo UI Drop-Ins
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/expo-ui-drop-ins/

# Expo UI Drop-Ins

Universal components vs SwiftUI/Compose-specific surfaces.

Highlights / Expo UI Drop-Ins

* @expo/ui Host is the required root for universal layouts - Column, Row, Text, Button
* Universal components render native UI on iOS and Android from one import path
* SwiftUI-specific APIs live under @expo/ui/swift-ui - modifiers, not RN style props
* Jetpack Compose APIs live under @expo/ui/jetpack-compose for Android-only surfaces
* RNHostView embeds standard RN subtrees inside native @expo/ui chrome
* Expo Go supports @expo/ui for prototyping - widgets and extensions need dev builds

**`@expo/ui`** lets Expo apps render **native UI** - SwiftUI on iOS, Jetpack Compose on Android - from React components. Use **universal** imports (`Host`, `Column`, `Button`) when one API should work on both platforms; reach for **`@expo/ui/swift-ui`** or **`@expo/ui/jetpack-compose`** when you need platform-specific modifiers, materials, or controls that have no cross-platform equivalent.

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
npx create-expo-app@latest MyExpoUIApp --template blank-typescript
cd MyExpoUIApp
npx expo install @expo/ui
```

```tsx
// screens/SettingsNativeScreen.tsx
import { Host, Column, Row, Text, Switch, Button, Spacer } from "@expo/ui";
 
export default function SettingsNativeScreen() {
  return (
    <Host style={{ flex: 1 }}>
      <Column spacing={16} padding={16}>
        <Text style={{ fontSize: 28, fontWeight: "700" }}>Notifications</Text>
 
        <Row spacing={12} alignment="center">
          <Column style={{ flex: 1 }}>
            <Text style={{ fontSize: 17, fontWeight: "600" }}>Push alerts</Text>
            <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, opacity: 0.7 }}>Order updates and promos</Text>
          </Column>
          <Switch defaultValue={true} label="Push alerts" />
        </Row>
 
        <Spacer />
 
        <Button label="Save preferences" variant="borderedProminent" onPress={() => {}} />
      </Column>
    </Host>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// Platform-specific enhancement (iOS only file pattern)
// components/GlassHeader.ios.tsx
import { Host, Text, VStack } from "@expo/ui/swift-ui";
import { background, glassEffect, padding } from "@expo/ui/swift-ui/modifiers";
 
export function GlassHeader({ title }: { title: string }) {
  return (
    <Host matchContents>
      <VStack modifiers={[padding({ all: 16 }), glassEffect({ glass: { variant: "regular" } })]}>
        <Text modifiers={[background("transparent")]}>{title}</Text>
      </VStack>
    </Host>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// components/GlassHeader.tsx - Android fallback
import { Text, View } from "react-native";
 
export function GlassHeader({ title }: { title: string }) {
  return (
    <View style={{ padding: 16, backgroundColor: "#f1f5f9" }}>
      <Text style={{ fontSize: 22, fontWeight: "700" }}>{title}</Text>
    </View>
  );
}
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Product wants **platform-native feel** - iOS switches, materials, Compose ripples - without maintaining two native codebases.
* You are building **hybrid screens**: native toolbar + RN body via `RNHostView`.
* **Widgets or Live Activities** need SwiftUI layouts - see [App Extensions & Widgets](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ios-platform/app-extensions-and-widgets/).
* Designers reference **Apple HIG** or **Material 3 native** patterns, not custom flat RN chrome.

## Working Example

Hybrid settings screen: universal layout, `RNHostView` for a React Native chart island, and iOS-only glass header.

```tsx
// screens/HybridDashboardScreen.tsx
import { Host, Column, Row, Text, Button, RNHostView } from "@expo/ui";
import { useColorScheme } from "react-native";
import { GlassHeader } from "../components/GlassHeader";
import { SpendingChart } from "../components/SpendingChart"; // standard RN component
 
export default function HybridDashboardScreen() {
  const scheme = useColorScheme() ?? "light";
 
  return (
    <Host style={{ flex: 1, backgroundColor: scheme === "dark" ? "#0f172a" : "#f8fafc" }}>
      <Column spacing={0} style={{ flex: 1 }}>
        <GlassHeader title="Spending" />
 
        <Column spacing={16} padding={16} style={{ flex: 1 }}>
          <Row spacing={8} alignment="center">
            <Text style={{ fontSize: 15, opacity: 0.75 }}>This month</Text>
            <Text style={{ fontSize: 28, fontWeight: "700" }}>$1,284.00</Text>
          </Row>
 
          {/* RN island inside native layout */}
          <Host style={{ flex: 1, minHeight: 220, borderRadius: 12, overflow: "hidden" }}>
            <RNHostView style={{ flex: 1 }}>
              <SpendingChart />
            </RNHostView>
          </Host>
 
          <Button
            label="View transactions"
            variant="bordered"
            onPress={() => {}}
            accessibilityLabel="View transactions"
          />
        </Column>
      </Column>
    </Host>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// components/SpendingChart.tsx - ordinary React Native
import { View, Text, StyleSheet } from "react-native";
 
const BARS = [40, 65, 30, 80, 55];
 
export function SpendingChart() {
  return (
    <View style={styles.chart}>
      {BARS.map((h, i) => (
        <View key={i} style={[styles.bar, { height: h }]} />
      ))}
      <Text style={styles.caption}>RN chart inside RNHostView</Text>
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  chart: { flex: 1, flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "flex-end", gap: 8, padding: 16, backgroundColor: "#fff" },
  bar: { flex: 1, backgroundColor: "#2563eb", borderRadius: 4 },
  caption: { position: "absolute", bottom: 8, left: 16, fontSize: 12, color: "#64748b" },
});
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* **`Host`** roots every `@expo/ui` tree - universal layouts do not work without it.
* **`Column` / `Row`** use native stack layouts with `spacing` and `alignment` props instead of flexbox style objects.
* **`Button` / `Switch`** from `@expo/ui` are **native controls**, not `Pressable` wrappers.
* **`RNHostView`** embeds existing RN components inside native chrome - migration path for hybrid design systems.
* **`.ios.tsx` fallback pattern** for SwiftUI-only APIs (`glassEffect`) with RN fallback on Android.

## Deep Dive

### How It Works

* **`@expo/ui`** bridges React props to SwiftUI / Compose views via Expo Modules - rendering happens on the native UI thread where supported.
* **Universal imports** (`@expo/ui`) pick the platform implementation at build time - one component tree, two native backends.
* **Platform-specific imports** expose modifiers and views with no cross-platform mirror - use `*.ios.tsx` / `*.android.tsx` fallbacks.
* **`RNHostView`** creates a nested RN root inside a native layout - distinct from brownfield full-screen embed; see [RNHostView & Native UI Embedding](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/brownfield/rnhostview-and-native-ui-embedding/).
* **Styling model** - universal components accept limited `style` objects; SwiftUI surfaces prefer **modifiers** from `@expo/ui/swift-ui/modifiers`.

### Universal vs Platform-Specific

| Import | Renders | Use for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@expo/ui` (`Host`, `Column`, `Button`) | SwiftUI + Compose | Cross-platform native chrome |
| `@expo/ui/swift-ui` | SwiftUI only | Glass, materials, widget layouts |
| `@expo/ui/jetpack-compose` | Compose only | Android Material widgets |
| `react-native` (`View`, `Pressable`) | RN layout | Custom DS, lists, Skia, legacy screens |

### Modifier Pattern (SwiftUI)

```tsx
import { Text, VStack } from "@expo/ui/swift-ui";
import { font, foregroundStyle, padding } from "@expo/ui/swift-ui/modifiers";
 
<Text
  modifiers={[
    font({ weight: "semibold", size: 17 }),
    foregroundStyle("#111111"),
    padding({ horizontal: 16 }),
  ]}
>
  Hello
</Text>
```

Modifiers are **not** RN `style` - they map to SwiftUI modifier chains. Widget extensions use the same vocabulary - see [App Extensions & Widgets](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ios-platform/app-extensions-and-widgets/).

### When to Mix with a Design System Library

| Layer | Tool |
| --- | --- |
| Native chrome (toolbar, toggles) | `@expo/ui` |
| Dense lists and forms | RN + Paper / Tamagui / NativeWind |
| Brand tokens | Your token module - see [Design Systems Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/design-systems-basics/) |
| White-label flavors | Theme config - see [Theming & Brand Flavors](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/theming-and-brand-flavors/) |

## Gotchas

* **Missing `Host` wrapper** - Layout children fail to mount. **Fix:** Every `@expo/ui` screen starts with `<Host>`.
* **Using `<View>` inside SwiftUI widget files** - Widget targets reject RN primitives. **Fix:** `@expo/ui/swift-ui` only in extension bundles.
* **Expecting identical pixels on iOS and Android** - Universal components map to platform idioms; spacing may differ. **Fix:** Design for roles, not pixel parity.
* **RNHostView without bounded height** - Chart island collapses to zero. **Fix:** Set `minHeight` or `flex: 1` on the `Host` wrapper.
* **Importing SwiftUI modifiers on Android** - Build failure. **Fix:** Platform-specific files or universal components only.
* **Replacing entire app with @expo/ui** - Lists, navigation, and third-party RN libs still need RN layout. **Fix:** Drop-in native chrome selectively, not wholesale replacement.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **@expo/ui universal** | Native switches, buttons, hybrid screens | Every screen is a complex virtualized list |
| **@expo/ui/swift-ui** | iOS materials, widgets, Live Activities | Android-only app |
| **React Native Paper** | Material Design in RN views | You need true Compose widgets |
| **Tamagui / NativeWind** | Custom branded DS across RN tree | Platform-native toggle and glass effects |
| **Custom TurboModule views** | Bespoke native control not in @expo/ui | @expo/ui already ships the primitive |

## FAQs

Does @expo/ui work in Expo Go on SDK 57?

Yes for universal components and `RNHostView` prototyping. Widget extensions and some platform-only targets require `expo prebuild` and dev builds.

What is Host?

The root container that bridges React children to native SwiftUI/Compose hierarchies. Wrap every `@expo/ui` layout tree with `<Host>`.

When should I use RNHostView?

When native chrome (toolbar, segmented control) should wrap **existing RN screens** without rewriting them. See [RNHostView & Native UI Embedding](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/brownfield/rnhostview-and-native-ui-embedding/).

Can I use StyleSheet with @expo/ui?

Universal components accept limited style props. Prefer layout props (`spacing`, `padding`, `alignment`). Keep `StyleSheet` for `RNHostView` children.

SwiftUI modifiers vs RN style?

Modifiers compile to SwiftUI chains (`font`, `padding`, `glassEffect`). They do not cascade like CSS. Use platform files when modifiers have no Android equivalent.

How does @expo/ui relate to React Native Paper?

Paper renders **Material in RN views**. `@expo/ui` renders **native Compose/SwiftUI**. You can combine them - Paper forms below a native `@expo/ui` header.

Accessibility with native components?

Set `label` / `accessibilityLabel` props where exposed. Test with VoiceOver and TalkBack - native controls behave differently from `Pressable`. See [Accessibility Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/accessibility/accessibility-basics/).

## Related

* [App Extensions & Widgets](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ios-platform/app-extensions-and-widgets/) - SwiftUI widget layouts

# Design Systems Highlights Summary

Every highlight bullet from the 8 pages in this section, gathered on one page and grouped by the page it came from.

Highlights / Design Systems Highlights Summary

* Design tokens are named constants - colors, spacing, type - not raw values in screens
* NativeWind v4 maps Tailwind classes to RN style objects at build time via Metro
* Tamagui compiles style props to flat RN objects - fewer allocations in hot paths
* Paper ships Material Design 3 components - Button, TextInput, FAB, Snackbar
* @expo/ui Host is the required root for universal layouts - Column, Row, Text, Button
* Treat the UI package like any npm library - explicit peerDependencies on react and react-native

## [Design Systems Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/design-systems-basics/)

* Design tokens are named constants - colors, spacing, type - not raw values in screens
* Semantic tokens (surface, textPrimary) survive palette overhauls better than gray-500
* A spacing scale on a 4px grid keeps padding and gaps consistent across components
* Component APIs expose variant, size, and disabled - not one-off style props per screen
* ThemeProvider centralizes active palette; screens call useTheme() instead of hard-coded hex
* Type token objects with as const and derive union types for variant props

## [NativeWind (Tailwind for RN)](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/nativewind-tailwind-for-rn/)

* NativeWind v4 maps Tailwind classes to RN style objects at build time via Metro
* global.css + tailwind.config content paths must include app/ and components/
* dark: variants follow useColorScheme when darkMode is set to class
* Prefer semantic tokens in tailwind.config theme.extend - not arbitrary values in screens
* className composes like style arrays - later classes override earlier ones
* Profile bundle size before adopting on small apps - config cost has a floor

## [Tamagui](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/tamagui/)

* Tamagui compiles style props to flat RN objects - fewer allocations in hot paths
* Define tokens once in tamagui.config.ts - colors, space, size, radius
* Styled components accept variant props mapped to token keys, not raw numbers
* TamaguiProvider wraps the app - theme and media queries flow through context
* @tamagui/config provides a sensible default theme to fork, not adopt blindly
* Expo requires react-native-reanimated and a Metro resolver tweak for optional deps

## [React Native Paper](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/react-native-paper/)

* Paper ships Material Design 3 components - Button, TextInput, FAB, Snackbar
* PaperProvider must wrap the app - theme, icons, and ripple settings flow from context
* MD3Theme maps color roles: primary, onPrimary, surface, onSurface, elevation
* adaptNavigationTheme bridges React Navigation colors with Paper's MD3 palette
* Custom fonts and roundness extend MD3LightTheme / MD3DarkTheme - do not fork per screen
* Paper excels on Android-first apps; iOS still works but reads Material, not Cupertino

## [Expo UI Drop-Ins](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/expo-ui-drop-ins/)

* @expo/ui Host is the required root for universal layouts - Column, Row, Text, Button
* Universal components render native UI on iOS and Android from one import path
* SwiftUI-specific APIs live under @expo/ui/swift-ui - modifiers, not RN style props
* Jetpack Compose APIs live under @expo/ui/jetpack-compose for Android-only surfaces
* RNHostView embeds standard RN subtrees inside native @expo/ui chrome
* Expo Go supports @expo/ui for prototyping - widgets and extensions need dev builds

## [Building an Internal Component Library](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/building-an-internal-component-library/)

* Treat the UI package like any npm library - explicit peerDependencies on react and react-native
* Semver major bumps when removing or renaming public component props
* On-device Storybook is the RN catalog - web Storybook misses native fonts and safe areas
* STORYBOOK\_ENABLED entry swap keeps Storybook out of production bundles
* Publish from packages/ui with changesets or semver tags - apps pin exact versions
* Visual regression pairs Storybook with Maestro screenshots - Jest alone misses layout drift

## [Theming & Brand Flavors](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/theming-and-brand-flavors/)

* Brand flavor is config data - primary hex, logo asset, app name - not a git fork
* EAS build profiles map FLAVOR env to the active brand at compile time
* expo-constants extra.brandFlavor reads the selected flavor in runtime code
* One ThemeProvider accepts flavor + scheme - components never branch on app id
* Shared JS bundle + per-flavor native icons/splash via app.config dynamic config
* Semver token keys across flavors - flavors swap values, not prop names

## [Design Systems Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/best-practices/)

* Tokens before libraries - semantic roles beat raw hex in feature screens
* Component APIs stay small: variant, size, disabled - not style soup per screen
* Pick one styling strategy per app - NativeWind, Tamagui, Paper, or tokens + StyleSheet
* Bake accessibilityRole and accessibilityLabel into primitives, not per-screen patches
* On-device Storybook is the RN catalog - semver the package that screens import
* White-label flavors swap config - never fork repos for logo and primary color

# NativeWind (Tailwind for RN)

Utility classes, dark mode, and build setup on Expo.

Highlights / NativeWind (Tailwind for RN)

* NativeWind v4 maps Tailwind classes to RN style objects at build time via Metro
* global.css + tailwind.config content paths must include app/ and components/
* dark: variants follow useColorScheme when darkMode is set to class
* Prefer semantic tokens in tailwind.config theme.extend - not arbitrary values in screens
* className composes like style arrays - later classes override earlier ones
* Profile bundle size before adopting on small apps - config cost has a floor

NativeWind brings **Tailwind CSS ergonomics** to React Native: `className="flex-1 p-4 bg-white dark:bg-slate-900"` instead of sprawling `StyleSheet` objects. On **Expo SDK 57**, NativeWind v4 hooks into Metro and compiles utilities to RN styles at build time - not a runtime CSS parser on device.

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
npx create-expo-app@latest MyWindApp --template blank-typescript
cd MyWindApp
npx expo install nativewind tailwindcss@^3.4.0 react-native-reanimated react-native-safe-area-context
npm install --save-dev prettier-plugin-tailwindcss
npx tailwindcss init
```

```js
// tailwind.config.js
/** @type {import('tailwindcss').Config} */
module.exports = {
  content: ["./app/**/*.{js,jsx,ts,tsx}", "./components/**/*.{js,jsx,ts,tsx}"],
  presets: [require("nativewind/preset")],
  theme: {
    extend: {
      colors: {
        brand: { DEFAULT: "#2563eb", muted: "#93c5fd" },
      },
    },
  },
  plugins: [],
};
```

```css
/* global.css */
@tailwind base;
@tailwind components;
@tailwind utilities;
```

```js
// metro.config.js
const { getDefaultConfig } = require("expo/metro-config");
const { withNativeWind } = require("nativewind/metro");
 
const config = getDefaultConfig(__dirname);
module.exports = withNativeWind(config, { input: "./global.css" });
```

```ts
// nativewind-env.d.ts
/// <reference types="nativewind/types" />
```

```tsx

import "../global.css";

  return <Stack screenOptions={{ headerShown: false }} />;
```

```tsx
// components/Card.tsx
import { Text, View } from "react-native";
 
export function Card({ title, body }: { title: string; body: string }) {
  return (
    <View className="rounded-xl border border-slate-200 bg-white p-4 dark:border-slate-700 dark:bg-slate-900">
      <Text className="text-base font-semibold text-slate-900 dark:text-slate-50">{title}</Text>
      <Text className="mt-1 text-sm text-slate-600 dark:text-slate-400">{body}</Text>
    </View>
  );
}
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Designers and engineers already use **Tailwind on web** and want the same utility vocabulary on mobile.
* You have **dozens of screens** where `StyleSheet` duplication is slowing velocity.
* Dark mode needs **`dark:` variants** tied to system scheme without hand-maintaining two palettes per component.
* You want **responsive-ish** utilities (`md:`, `lg:`) for tablet layouts alongside phone defaults.

## Working Example

Settings screen with system dark mode, semantic brand tokens, and a pressed-state button.

```tsx
// app/settings.tsx
import { Pressable, ScrollView, Text, useColorScheme, View } from "react-native";
import { SafeAreaView } from "react-native-safe-area-context";
import { StatusBar } from "expo-status-bar";
 
const ROWS = [
  { id: "profile", label: "Edit profile" },
  { id: "notifications", label: "Notifications" },
  { id: "privacy", label: "Privacy" },
] as const;
 
export default function SettingsScreen() {
  const scheme = useColorScheme() ?? "light";
 
  return (
    <SafeAreaView className="flex-1 bg-slate-50 dark:bg-slate-950">
      <StatusBar style={scheme === "dark" ? "light" : "dark"} />
      <ScrollView contentContainerClassName="gap-3 p-4">
        <Text className="text-2xl font-bold text-slate-900 dark:text-slate-50">Settings</Text>
 
        <View className="overflow-hidden rounded-xl border border-slate-200 bg-white dark:border-slate-800 dark:bg-slate-900">
          {ROWS.map((row) => (
            <Pressable
              key={row.id}
              accessibilityRole="button"
              className="border-b border-slate-100 px-4 py-3.5 active:bg-slate-100 dark:border-slate-800 dark:active:bg-slate-800"
            >
              <Text className="text-base text-slate-900 dark:text-slate-100">{row.label}</Text>
            </Pressable>
          ))}
        </View>
 
        <Pressable
          accessibilityRole="button"
          className="items-center rounded-xl bg-brand px-4 py-3.5 active:opacity-80"
        >
          <Text className="text-base font-semibold text-white">Save changes</Text>
        </Pressable>
      </ScrollView>
    </SafeAreaView>
  );
}
```

```js
// tailwind.config.js - darkMode for class-based dark: utilities
module.exports = {
  content: ["./app/**/*.{js,jsx,ts,tsx}", "./components/**/*.{js,jsx,ts,tsx}"],
  presets: [require("nativewind/preset")],
  darkMode: "class",
  theme: {
    extend: {
      colors: {
        brand: { DEFAULT: "#2563eb", foreground: "#ffffff" },
      },
    },
  },
};
```

```tsx
// providers/ThemeModeProvider.tsx - optional in-app override
import { createContext, useContext, useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { Appearance, useColorScheme } from "react-native";
import { colorScheme } from "nativewind";
 
type Mode = "light" | "dark" | "system";
 
const ThemeModeContext = createContext<{ mode: Mode; setMode: (m: Mode) => void }>({
  mode: "system",
  setMode: () => {},
});
 
export function ThemeModeProvider({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  const system = useColorScheme();
  const [mode, setMode] = useState<Mode>("system");
 
  useEffect(() => {
    if (mode === "system") {
      Appearance.setColorScheme(null);
      colorScheme.set(system === "dark" ? "dark" : "light");
    } else {
      Appearance.setColorScheme(mode);
      colorScheme.set(mode);
    }
  }, [mode, system]);
 
  return (
    <ThemeModeContext.Provider value={{ mode, setMode }}>{children}</ThemeModeContext.Provider>
  );
}
 
export function useThemeMode() {
  return useContext(ThemeModeContext);
}
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* **`withNativeWind`** in Metro compiles `global.css` and wires `className` on RN primitives.
* **`dark:`** variants respond to NativeWind's `colorScheme` API synced with `useColorScheme`.
* **`contentContainerClassName`** on `ScrollView` applies utilities to the scroll content wrapper.
* **Semantic `brand`** color in `theme.extend` - screens use `bg-brand`, not raw hex.
* **`active:`** pseudo-utility for press feedback without inline `StyleSheet` state.

## Deep Dive

### How It Works

* **NativeWind v4** uses a Metro transformer to parse Tailwind classes and emit React Native style objects at bundle time.
* **`nativewind/preset`** maps web Tailwind utilities to RN-supported properties - unsupported CSS is stripped or warned in dev.
* **`className`** is not a native prop - NativeWind patches supported components (`View`, `Text`, `Pressable`, etc.) via the `jsxImportSource` or Babel plugin depending on setup.
* **Dark mode** - with `darkMode: "class"`, call `colorScheme.set("dark")` from `nativewind` when overriding system appearance; `dark:` classes activate accordingly.
* **Tokens** - define design decisions in `tailwind.config.js` `theme.extend`; screens consume utilities, not one-off `text-[#334155]` arbitrary values.

### NativeWind vs StyleSheet

| Concern | StyleSheet + tokens | NativeWind |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Learning curve | RN-native | Tailwind vocabulary |
| Bundle overhead | Minimal | Config + compiler floor |
| Dark mode | Manual theme object | `dark:` variants |
| List hot paths | Stable references easy | Keep class strings static |
| Designer handoff | Token table | Utility class spec |

### TypeScript Notes

```ts
// nativewind-env.d.ts
/// <reference types="nativewind/types" />
```

* Add the reference file so `className` is typed on RN components.
* For third-party components without `className`, use `cssInterop` from NativeWind to map `className` → `style`.
* Keep **static class strings** in list `renderItem` - dynamic template literals defeat compile-time extraction.

### Expo Router Layout

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx
import "../global.css";
import { ThemeModeProvider } from "../providers/ThemeModeProvider";
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
 
export default function RootLayout() {
  return (
    <ThemeModeProvider>
      <Stack />
    </ThemeModeProvider>
  );
}
```

Import `global.css` **once** at the root layout - child routes inherit compiled utilities.

## Gotchas

* **Missing `content` paths** - Tailwind purges unused classes; if `./app/**` is omitted, styles silently disappear. **Fix:** Include every folder with `className` strings.
* **Forgot `global.css` import** - Utilities never register. **Fix:** Import at root `App.tsx` or `app/_layout.tsx`.
* **Metro cache stale after config change** - Old styles persist. **Fix:** `npx expo start --clear` after `tailwind.config.js` edits.
* **Arbitrary values everywhere** - `p-[13px]` bypasses your scale. **Fix:** Extend `theme.spacing` and enforce in code review.
* **Dynamic class concatenation in lists** - `` `bg-${color}-500` `` breaks compile-time extraction. **Fix:** Use a fixed map: `const bg = { red: "bg-red-500", blue: "bg-blue-500" }`.
* **`dark:` without syncing colorScheme** - In-app toggle changes `Appearance` but not NativeWind. **Fix:** Call `colorScheme.set()` in your theme provider.
* **Third-party `TextInput` ignores className** - Not all components are patched. **Fix:** `cssInterop(TextInput, { className: "style" })` in a setup file.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **NativeWind v4** | Tailwind team, many screens, dark variants | Two-screen app with five styles |
| **StyleSheet + tokens** | Minimal deps, full control | Designers mandate utility workflow |
| **Tamagui** | Compiled tokens + components + web | You only want class strings, not a component kit |
| **React Native Paper** | Material components out of the box | Custom brand unrelated to MD3 |
| **Unistyles** | Runtime themes with breakpoints | Team has zero RN styling library experience |

## FAQs

Does NativeWind work with Expo SDK 57?

Yes. Install via `npx expo install nativewind tailwindcss react-native-reanimated`, wrap Metro with `withNativeWind`, and import `global.css` at the app root. Clear Metro cache after config changes.

Where do I put design tokens?

In `tailwind.config.js` under `theme.extend` - colors, spacing, fontSize, borderRadius. Screens reference `text-brand`, `p-md`, not raw values. Align names with [Design Systems Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/design-systems-basics/).

How does dark mode work?

Set `darkMode: "class"` and use `dark:bg-slate-900` utilities. Sync with system via `useColorScheme`, or override with `colorScheme.set("dark")` from `nativewind` when the user picks an in-app theme. See [Dark Mode & Color Schemes](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/dark-mode-and-color-schemes/).

Can I use NativeWind with Expo Router?

Yes. Import `global.css` in `app/_layout.tsx`. Add `./app/**/*` to Tailwind `content` paths.

className vs style - which wins?

Treat `className` like a base layer and pass `style` for truly dynamic values (animated width). Avoid duplicating the same property in both.

Does NativeWind work on web (Expo web)?

NativeWind targets React Native views. Expo web may render some utilities, but validate layout separately - web-specific issues belong in [Styling Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/styling-basics/).

How do I add custom fonts?

Load fonts with `expo-font`, then map `fontFamily` in `tailwind.config.js` `theme.extend`. See [Typography Scale & Font Loading](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/typography-scale-and-font-loading/).

Performance in FlatList?

Keep **static** `className` strings on row components. Extract rows to `memo()` children. Profile before assuming utilities are free - see [Style Performance](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/style-performance/).

## Related

* [Design Systems Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/design-systems-basics/) - tokens and component APIs before adopting a library
* [Dark Mode & Color Schemes](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/dark-mode-and-color-schemes/) - semantic palettes and `Appearance` API
* [Styling Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/styling-basics/) - StyleSheet fundamentals NativeWind compiles toward
* [Tamagui](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/tamagui/) - compiled design system alternative
* [Style Performance](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/style-performance/) - list hot paths and style reference stability

# React Native Paper

Material Design components and theming for Android-first UX.

Highlights / React Native Paper

* Paper ships Material Design 3 components - Button, TextInput, FAB, Snackbar
* PaperProvider must wrap the app - theme, icons, and ripple settings flow from context
* MD3Theme maps color roles: primary, onPrimary, surface, onSurface, elevation
* adaptNavigationTheme bridges React Navigation colors with Paper's MD3 palette
* Custom fonts and roundness extend MD3LightTheme / MD3DarkTheme - do not fork per screen
* Paper excels on Android-first apps; iOS still works but reads Material, not Cupertino

**React Native Paper** implements **Material Design 3** for React Native: buttons, text fields, dialogs, chips, and surfaces with built-in accessibility roles and ripple feedback. On **Expo SDK 57**, pair `PaperProvider` with **MD3 themes** and optionally **adapt React Navigation** so headers and tabs match your palette.

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
npx create-expo-app@latest MyPaperApp --template blank-typescript
cd MyPaperApp
npx expo install react-native-paper react-native-safe-area-context
npm install @react-navigation/native
```

```tsx
// theme/paper.ts
import {
  MD3DarkTheme,
  MD3LightTheme,
  adaptNavigationTheme,
  configureFonts,
} from "react-native-paper";
import {
  DarkTheme as NavDarkTheme,
  DefaultTheme as NavDefaultTheme,
} from "@react-navigation/native";
 
const fontConfig = configureFonts({ config: { fontFamily: "System" } });
 
export const lightTheme = {
  ...MD3LightTheme,
  fonts: fontConfig,
  colors: {
    ...MD3LightTheme.colors,
    primary: "#2563eb",
    secondary: "#7c3aed",
  },
  roundness: 10,
};
 
export const darkTheme = {
  ...MD3DarkTheme,
  fonts: fontConfig,
  colors: {
    ...MD3DarkTheme.colors,
    primary: "#60a5fa",
    secondary: "#a78bfa",
  },
  roundness: 10,
};
 
export const { LightTheme: NavLight, DarkTheme: NavDark } = adaptNavigationTheme({
  reactNavigationLight: NavDefaultTheme,
  reactNavigationDark: NavDarkTheme,
  materialLight: lightTheme,
  materialDark: darkTheme,
});
```

```tsx
// App.tsx
import { useColorScheme } from "react-native";
import { PaperProvider } from "react-native-paper";
import { NavigationContainer } from "@react-navigation/native";
import { createNativeStackNavigator } from "@react-navigation/native-stack";
import { HomeScreen } from "./screens/HomeScreen";
import { darkTheme, lightTheme, NavDark, NavLight } from "./theme/paper";
 
const Stack = createNativeStackNavigator();
 
export default function App() {
  const scheme = useColorScheme() ?? "light";
  const paperTheme = scheme === "dark" ? darkTheme : lightTheme;
  const navTheme = scheme === "dark" ? NavDark : NavLight;
 
  return (
    <PaperProvider theme={paperTheme}>
      <NavigationContainer theme={navTheme}>
        <Stack.Navigator>
          <Stack.Screen name="Home" component={HomeScreen} options={{ title: "Inbox" }} />
        </Stack.Navigator>
      </NavigationContainer>
    </PaperProvider>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// screens/HomeScreen.tsx
import { View } from "react-native";
import { Button, Card, Text, TextInput } from "react-native-paper";
 
export function HomeScreen() {
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1, padding: 16, gap: 12 }}>
      <Card mode="elevated">
        <Card.Title title="Welcome" subtitle="Material 3 on Expo" />
        <Card.Content>
          <Text variant="bodyMedium">Compose forms and actions from Paper primitives.</Text>
        </Card.Content>
        <Card.Actions>
          <Button mode="text">Dismiss</Button>
          <Button mode="contained">Continue</Button>
        </Card.Actions>
      </Card>
      <TextInput mode="outlined" label="Email" placeholder="you@example.com" />
    </View>
  );
}
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Product targets **Android-first** or explicitly adopts **Material Design 3**.
* You need **accessible inputs, dialogs, and snackbars** without building from scratch.
* Navigation chrome should **match Paper colors** via `adaptNavigationTheme`.
* Timeline is tight - Paper's `Button`, `FAB`, and `Searchbar` ship production-ready patterns.

## Working Example

Login flow with MD3 theming, icon provider, snackbar feedback, and dark mode.

```tsx
// providers/AppProviders.tsx
import { useMemo } from "react";
import { useColorScheme } from "react-native";
import { PaperProvider, MD3Theme } from "react-native-paper";
import { NavigationContainer, Theme } from "@react-navigation/native";
import { darkTheme, lightTheme, NavDark, NavLight } from "../theme/paper";
 
export function AppProviders({
  children,
  navigationRef,
}: {
  children: React.ReactNode;
  navigationRef?: React.RefObject<object>;
}) {
  const scheme = useColorScheme() ?? "light";
  const paperTheme = useMemo<MD3Theme>(
    () => (scheme === "dark" ? darkTheme : lightTheme),
    [scheme],
  );
  const navTheme = useMemo<Theme>(
    () => (scheme === "dark" ? NavDark : NavLight),
    [scheme],
  );
 
  return (
    <PaperProvider theme={paperTheme}>
      <NavigationContainer ref={navigationRef} theme={navTheme}>
        {children}
      </NavigationContainer>
    </PaperProvider>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// screens/LoginScreen.tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { KeyboardAvoidingView, Platform, View } from "react-native";
import { Button, HelperText, Snackbar, Text, TextInput } from "react-native-paper";
 
export function LoginScreen() {
  const [email, setEmail] = useState("");
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [snack, setSnack] = useState(false);
 
  function handleSubmit() {
    if (!email.includes("@")) {
      setError("Enter a valid email");
      return;
    }
    setError(null);
    setSnack(true);
  }
 
  return (
    <KeyboardAvoidingView
      style={{ flex: 1 }}
      behavior={Platform.OS === "ios" ? "padding" : undefined}
    >
      <View style={{ flex: 1, padding: 24, justifyContent: "center", gap: 12 }}>
        <Text variant="headlineMedium">Sign in</Text>
        <TextInput
          mode="outlined"
          label="Email"
          value={email}
          onChangeText={setEmail}
          keyboardType="email-address"
          autoCapitalize="none"
          error={!!error}
          accessibilityLabel="Email address"
        />
        <HelperText type="error" visible={!!error}>
          {error}
        </HelperText>
        <Button mode="contained" onPress={handleSubmit} accessibilityLabel="Sign in">
          Sign in
        </Button>
      </View>
      <Snackbar visible={snack} onDismiss={() => setSnack(false)} duration={3000}>
        Signed in as {email}
      </Snackbar>
    </KeyboardAvoidingView>
  );
}
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* **`PaperProvider`** supplies MD3 theme to all Paper components - colors, roundness, fonts, ripple.
* **`adaptNavigationTheme`** aligns React Navigation header/tab colors with Paper's `primary` and `surface` roles.
* **`Text variant="headlineMedium"`** uses MD3 typography scale - not raw `fontSize`.
* **`HelperText` + `error` prop** on `TextInput` - accessible validation pattern.
* **`Snackbar`** for transient feedback without custom toast infrastructure.

## Deep Dive

### How It Works

* **MD3 color roles** - `primary`, `onPrimary`, `primaryContainer`, `surface`, `onSurface`, `outline`, etc. Paper components consume roles, not arbitrary hex.
* **`PaperProvider`** - React context for theme, icons (`settings.icon`), and ripple configuration.
* **`useTheme()`** hook from Paper returns the active `MD3Theme` inside any child component.
* **`mode` props** - `Button mode="contained|outlined|text|elevated"`, `Card mode="elevated|outlined|contained"`.
* **Icons** - Paper uses `react-native-vector-icons` MaterialCommunityIcons by default; override via `settings.icon` in provider.

### MD3 Theme Structure

```tsx
import { MD3LightTheme } from "react-native-paper";
 
const theme = {
  ...MD3LightTheme,
  colors: {
    ...MD3LightTheme.colors,
    primary: "#2563eb",       // brand actions
    onPrimary: "#ffffff",     // text on primary buttons
    surface: "#ffffff",       // cards, sheets
    onSurface: "#1c1b1f",     // body text on surface
    background: "#f8fafc",    // screen backdrop
  },
  roundness: 10,              // global corner radius baseline
};
```

Map your semantic tokens from [Design Systems Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/design-systems-basics/) to MD3 roles - do not invent parallel naming.

### React Navigation Integration

```tsx
import { adaptNavigationTheme } from "react-native-paper";
import { DefaultTheme, DarkTheme } from "@react-navigation/native";
 
const { LightTheme, DarkTheme: NavDark } = adaptNavigationTheme({
  reactNavigationLight: DefaultTheme,
  reactNavigationDark: DarkTheme,
  materialLight: lightTheme,
  materialDark: darkTheme,
});
```

Navigation headers pick up `primary` and `card` from Paper - avoids mismatched blues between app bar and buttons.

### TypeScript Notes

```tsx
import type { MD3Theme } from "react-native-paper";
 
export const lightTheme: MD3Theme = { ... };
```

* Type the theme export so custom color keys added incorrectly surface compile errors.
* `Text` `variant` is a union of MD3 typography names - autocomplete in IDE.

## Gotchas

* **Missing `PaperProvider`** - Components render with default theme; custom colors ignored. **Fix:** Wrap at root, inside `SafeAreaProvider`.
* **Hard-coded hex in screens** - Breaks dark mode. **Fix:** Use `useTheme().colors.primary` or Paper components that read theme automatically.
* **iOS users expecting Cupertino** - Paper reads Material on both platforms. **Fix:** Use Paper for Android-primary apps; consider `@expo/ui` or custom primitives for iOS-native chrome.
* **TextInput behind keyboard** - Outlined fields need `KeyboardAvoidingView` on iOS. **Fix:** Wrap form screens; test on small iPhones.
* **Ripple on iOS** - Paper simulates feedback; it is not identically Material Android. **Fix:** Accept platform differences or customize `android_ripple` via theme.
* **Mixing Paper and unstyled RN `Text`** - Typography rhythm drifts. **Fix:** Use Paper `Text` with `variant` inside Paper screens.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **React Native Paper** | MD3, Android-first, forms and dialogs | Fully custom non-Material brand |
| **Tamagui / NativeWind** | Custom design language | You want prebuilt MD3 widgets |
| **@expo/ui** | Native SwiftUI/Compose controls | Material-specific elevation and ripple |
| **react-native-elements** | Legacy projects already on RNE | Greenfield MD3 apps - prefer Paper |

## FAQs

Does React Native Paper work with Expo SDK 57?

Yes. `npx expo install react-native-paper react-native-safe-area-context`. No native config plugin required for standard usage.

Where does PaperProvider go?

Outside navigation but inside safe area - typically wrapping `NavigationContainer` in `App.tsx` or root layout. One provider per app.

How do I change the primary brand color?

Override `colors.primary` (and `onPrimary`) in `MD3LightTheme` / `MD3DarkTheme` spreads. Keep contrast ratios for accessibility - see [Accessibility Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/accessibility/accessibility-basics/).

Can I use custom fonts?

Pass `configureFonts({ config: { fontFamily: "Inter-Regular" } })` into the theme after loading fonts with expo-font. See [Typography Scale & Font Loading](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/typography-scale-and-font-loading/).

How does dark mode work?

Build `darkTheme` from `MD3DarkTheme`, select with `useColorScheme`, pass to `PaperProvider`. Sync `StatusBar` and navigation via `adaptNavigationTheme`.

Paper vs Tamagui?

Paper ships **opinionated MD3 components**. Tamagui ships **token primitives you style**. Choose Paper when Material patterns are the product; Tamagui when the brand is custom.

Are Paper components accessible?

Paper sets roles on many primitives, but you still must provide `accessibilityLabel` on icon-only buttons and test with VoiceOver/TalkBack. See [accessibilityLabel & accessibilityRole](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/accessibility/accessibilitylabel-and-accessibilityrole/).

Dokumen: Tamagui

# Tamagui

Cross-platform design system with optimized style compilation.

Highlights / Tamagui

* Tamagui compiles style props to flat RN objects - fewer allocations in hot paths
* Define tokens once in tamagui.config.ts - colors, space, size, radius
* Styled components accept variant props mapped to token keys, not raw numbers
* TamaguiProvider wraps the app - theme and media queries flow through context
* @tamagui/config provides a sensible default theme to fork, not adopt blindly
* Expo requires react-native-reanimated and a Metro resolver tweak for optional deps

Tamagui is a **universal design system** for React Native (and web): typed tokens, styled primitives (`Stack`, `Text`, `Button`), and a compiler that flattens style props into optimized objects. On **Expo SDK 57**, it fits teams that want **component + token discipline** beyond utility classes - with performance tuned for list-heavy apps.

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
npx create-expo-app@latest MyTamaguiApp --template blank-typescript
cd MyTamaguiApp
npx expo install tamagui @tamagui/config @tamagui/core react-native-reanimated react-native-safe-area-context
```

```ts
// tamagui.config.ts
import { config as defaultConfig } from "@tamagui/config";
import { createTamagui } from "tamagui";
 
export const config = createTamagui({
  ...defaultConfig,
  tokens: {
    ...defaultConfig.tokens,
    color: {
      ...defaultConfig.tokens.color,
      brand: "#2563eb",
      brandMuted: "#93c5fd",
    },
  },
  themes: {
    ...defaultConfig.themes,
    light: {
      ...defaultConfig.themes.light,
      brand: "#2563eb",
    },
    dark: {
      ...defaultConfig.themes.dark,
      brand: "#60a5fa",
    },
  },
});
 
export type AppConfig = typeof config;
declare module "tamagui" {
  // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-empty-object-type
  interface TamaguiCustomConfig extends AppConfig {}
}
```

```tsx
// App.tsx
import { TamaguiProvider, Theme, YStack, Text, Button } from "tamagui";
import { useColorScheme } from "react-native";

  return (
    <TamaguiProvider config={config} defaultTheme={scheme}>
      <Theme name={scheme}>

          <Text fontSize="$6" fontWeight="700" color="$color">
            Tamagui on Expo
          </Text>

            Continue
          </Button>

      </Theme>
    </TamaguiProvider>
```

**When to reach for this:**

* You need **typed variants** (`size="$4"`, `color="$brand"`) with compile-time validation.
* Lists and feeds are performance-sensitive - Tamagui's **style flattening** reduces per-render work.
* Design system spans **mobile and web** from one token file.
* You want **styled primitives** (`Button`, `Card`) rather than only utility classes.

## Working Example

Product card with variants, dark theme, and a memoized list row built on Tamagui tokens.

```tsx
// components/ProductCard.tsx
import { Card, H4, Paragraph, XStack, YStack, styled } from "tamagui";
 
const Badge = styled(Paragraph, {
  name: "Badge",
  fontSize: "$1",
  fontWeight: "700",
  paddingHorizontal: "$2",
  paddingVertical: "$1",
  borderRadius: "$10",
  variants: {
    tone: {
      sale: { backgroundColor: "$red4", color: "$red11" },
      new: { backgroundColor: "$green4", color: "$green11" },
    },
  } as const,
  defaultVariants: { tone: "new" },
});
 
type Props = {
  title: string;
  price: string;
  badge?: "sale" | "new";
};
 
export function ProductCard({ title, price, badge = "new" }: Props) {
  return (
    <Card elevate bordered padding="$4" backgroundColor="$background">
      <YStack gap="$2">
        <XStack justifyContent="space-between" alignItems="center">
          <H4 color="$color" numberOfLines={1}>
            {title}
          </H4>
          {badge && <Badge tone={badge}>{badge === "sale" ? "SALE" : "NEW"}</Badge>}
        </XStack>
        <Paragraph color="$color11" fontSize="$5" fontWeight="600">
          {price}
        </Paragraph>
      </YStack>
    </Card>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// screens/CatalogScreen.tsx
import { FlatList } from "react-native";
import { YStack, Text } from "tamagui";
import { ProductCard } from "../components/ProductCard";
 
const PRODUCTS = [
  { id: "1", title: "Trail Runner Pro", price: "$129", badge: "new" as const },
  { id: "2", title: "Merino Base Layer", price: "$79", badge: "sale" as const },
  { id: "3", title: "Softshell Jacket", price: "$199", badge: "new" as const },
];
 
export function CatalogScreen() {
  return (
    <YStack flex={1} padding="$4" backgroundColor="$background" gap="$3">
      <Text fontSize="$8" fontWeight="800" color="$color">
        Catalog
      </Text>
      <FlatList
        data={PRODUCTS}
        keyExtractor={(item) => item.id}
        ItemSeparatorComponent={() => <YStack height="$3" />}
        renderItem={({ item }) => (
          <ProductCard title={item.title} price={item.price} badge={item.badge} />
        )}
      />
    </YStack>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx
import { TamaguiProvider, Theme } from "tamagui";
import { Slot } from "expo-router";
import { useColorScheme } from "react-native";
import { config } from "../tamagui.config";
 
export default function RootLayout() {
  const scheme = useColorScheme() ?? "light";
  return (
    <TamaguiProvider config={config} defaultTheme={scheme}>
      <Theme name={scheme}>
        <Slot />
      </Theme>
    </TamaguiProvider>
  );
}
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* **`$` token shorthand** - `$4` resolves to spacing token `4` from config.
* **`styled()` with `variants`** - `tone="sale"` maps to theme-aware colors, not inline hex.
* **`Theme name={scheme}`** swaps light/dark theme objects from `tamagui.config.ts`.
* **`Card elevate bordered`** - Tamagui shorthand props compile to platform-appropriate elevation.
* **FlatList + Tamagui** - row component uses stable variant props; separator uses token height.

## Deep Dive

### How It Works

* **`createTamagui`** merges your tokens, themes, fonts, and media into one config object.
* **`TamaguiProvider`** supplies config and active theme to the React tree.
* **Styled components** resolve props like `padding="$4"` to numeric values at compile/runtime and flatten to RN style objects.
* **Themes** are maps of token name → value per appearance (`light`, `dark`). Components reference `$color`, `$background`, not hard-coded hex.
* **Optional compiler** (`@tamagui/compiler` or Babel plugin) can further optimize static trees - evaluate when bundle size matters.

### Token Layers

| Layer | Example | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tokens.color.brand` | `#2563eb` | Raw palette |
| `themes.light.brand` | `#2563eb` | Theme-specific role |
| Component prop | `backgroundColor="$brand"` | Consumption in JSX |

### TypeScript Notes

```ts
declare module "tamagui" {
  interface TamaguiCustomConfig extends AppConfig {}
}
```

* The module augmentation enables **autocomplete** on `$` tokens and variant names.
* Use `as const` on `variants` objects so `tone` is `"sale" | "new"`, not `string`.
* Export `AppConfig` from `tamagui.config.ts` for Storybook decorators that need typed themes.

### Metro on Expo

Some Tamagui optional packages need explicit resolution. If Metro fails on `@tamagui/*` subpaths:

```js
// metro.config.js
const { getDefaultConfig } = require("expo/metro-config");
const config = getDefaultConfig(__dirname);
config.resolver.unstable_enablePackageExports = true;
module.exports = config;
```

Run `npx expo start --clear` after adding Tamagui to an existing project.

## Gotchas

* **Missing `TamaguiProvider`** - `$` tokens resolve to undefined styles. **Fix:** Wrap root layout, same placement as other theme providers.
* **Theme name mismatch** - `Theme name="dark"` without a `dark` key in `themes`. **Fix:** Fork `@tamagui/config` themes or define both `light` and `dark`.
* **Mixing Tamagui and raw `View`** - Spacing rhythm breaks. **Fix:** Use `YStack`/`XStack` for layout islands; migrate incrementally.
* **Inline hex on Tamagui components** - Defeats theming. **Fix:** Add token + theme entry, reference `$brand`.
* **Reanimated plugin order** - Reanimated Babel plugin must be **last** in `babel.config.js`. **Fix:** Follow Expo Reanimated docs when enabling animations alongside Tamagui.
* **Web-only props on native** - Some shorthand props target web CSS. **Fix:** Test on both platforms; use `Platform.select` in custom styled components when needed.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Tamagui** | Token-typed components + web sharing | Team wants only Tailwind strings |
| **NativeWind** | Utility-class ergonomics | You need first-class variant APIs on primitives |
| **React Native Paper** | Material Design out of the box | Heavily custom brand language |
| **StyleSheet + tokens** | Minimal dependencies | Large DS with many variant matrices |
| **@expo/ui** | Native SwiftUI/Compose chrome | Custom design language unrelated to platform widgets |

## FAQs

Does Tamagui work with Expo SDK 57?

Yes. Install `tamagui`, `@tamagui/config`, and `react-native-reanimated` via `npx expo install`. Wrap the app in `TamaguiProvider` and load `tamagui.config.ts` at the root layout.

What does the $ prefix mean?

`$4` references the `space` token `4`. `$color` references the active theme's `color` role. It is Tamagui's shorthand for token lookup - not a string literal.

How do I customize the default theme?

Spread `defaultConfig` from `@tamagui/config`, override `tokens` and `themes`, and keep `createTamagui` types via module augmentation. Do not copy the entire default theme blindly - trim unused tokens to reduce bundle size.

Tamagui vs NativeWind?

NativeWind maps **Tailwind classes** to styles. Tamagui provides **styled components + tokens** with a variant system. Teams allergic to `className` often prefer Tamagui; teams from web Tailwind often prefer NativeWind.

How does dark mode work?

Define `light` and `dark` in `themes`, wrap with `<Theme name={scheme}>`, and drive `scheme` from `useColorScheme`. See [Dark Mode & Color Schemes](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/dark-mode-and-color-schemes/).

Can I use Tamagui with FlatList?

Yes. Keep `renderItem` lean; extract `ProductCard` as a separate component. Avoid creating new style objects inline in the render callback.

Does Tamagui help accessibility?

Tamagui components forward props to RN primitives - set `accessibilityRole`, `accessibilityLabel`, and test with VoiceOver/TalkBack. See [Accessibility Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/accessibility/accessibility-basics/).

## Related

* [Design Systems Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/design-systems-basics/) - token and variant patterns Tamagui formalizes
* [NativeWind (Tailwind for RN)](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/nativewind-tailwind-for-rn/) - utility-class alternative
* [Style Performance](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/style-performance/) - why flattened styles matter in lists
* [Dark Mode & Color Schemes](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/dark-mode-and-color-schemes/) - system scheme sync

Dokumen: Android Keystores & Signing
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/eas-build/android-keystores-and-signing/

# Android Keystores & Signing

Upload keys and **Play App Signing** interplay - the EAS-focused cookbook for Android release identity on Expo SDK 57.

Highlights / Android Keystores & Signing

* EAS generates and stores upload keystores encrypted - eas credentials is team source of truth
* Play App Signing holds the app signing key; you sign AABs with the upload key
* assetlinks.json must use Play App Signing SHA-256 - not the upload key fingerprint
* Losing an upload key is recoverable with Play App Signing enabled
* Never commit .jks, .keystore, or passwords to git
* versionCode must increase monotonically on every Play upload

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
# First production build - let EAS generate the keystore
eas build --platform android --profile production
 
# Inspect remote credentials (admin)
eas credentials --platform android
 
# CI production build
eas build --platform android --profile production --non-interactive
```

```json
// eas.json
{
  "build": {
    "production": {
      "distribution": "store",
      "android": {
        "buildType": "app-bundle"
      }
    },
    "preview": {
      "distribution": "internal",
      "android": {
        "buildType": "apk"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

```ts
// app.config.ts
export default {
  expo: {
    version: "2.4.0",
    android: {
      package: "com.example.shopapp",
      versionCode: 240001,
    },
  },
};
```

**When to reach for this:**

* First `eas build --platform android` prompts for keystore generation.
* Play Console rejects an AAB: "signed with the wrong key."
* App Links verification fails - fingerprint mismatch in `assetlinks.json`.
* Migrating from a legacy keystore on a former employee's laptop.

## Working Example

**Step 1 - Enable Play App Signing (new app)**

1. Create the app in Google Play Console.
2. On first AAB upload, accept **Google Play App Signing** (mandatory for new apps).
3. Google holds the **app signing key**; your team keeps the **upload key**.

**Step 2 - Generate upload credentials with EAS**

```bash
eas credentials --platform android
```

```text
? What do you want to do? › Set up a new keystore
? Generate a new Android Keystore? › Yes
```

EAS stores:

* **Keystore file** (encrypted)
* **Keystore password**, **key alias**, **key password**

**Step 3 - Production AAB build**

```bash
eas build --profile production --platform android
eas submit --platform android --profile production --latest
```

**Step 4 - Register App Links with Play signing fingerprint**

```bash
# Play Console → Release → App integrity → App signing key certificate
# Copy SHA-256 - NOT the upload key fingerprint
```

```json
// https://shop.example.com/.well-known/assetlinks.json
[
  {
    "relation": ["delegate_permission/common.handle_all_urls"],
    "target": {
      "namespace": "android_app",
      "package_name": "com.example.shopapp",
      "sha256_cert_fingerprints": ["PLAY_APP_SIGNING_SHA256_HERE"]
    }
  }
]
```

See [Signing & Play App Signing](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/android-platform/signing-and-play-app-signing/) for the full Play Console walkthrough.

---

## Upload Key vs App Signing Key

| Key | Who holds it | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Upload key** | Your team / EAS | Signing AABs you upload to Play |
| **App signing key** | Google (Play App Signing) | Signing APKs users download from Play |

```bash
# Upload key fingerprint (EAS credentials download - admin only)
eas credentials --platform android
 
# Debug keystore - local development ONLY
keytool -list -v -keystore ~/.android/debug.keystore \
  -alias androiddebugkey -storepass android -keypass android | grep SHA256
```

* **Never** put the debug keystore fingerprint in production `assetlinks.json`
* If Play App Signing is disabled (legacy apps), the upload key **is** the app signing key - treat loss as catastrophic

---

## Migrating an Existing Keystore

Brownfield apps already on Play must upload the **same upload key** EAS will use:

```bash
eas credentials --platform android
# Choose: Upload existing keystore
# Provide: .jks path, store password, key alias, key password
```

Checklist:

1. Export keystore from the previous CI system or developer machine
2. Confirm fingerprint matches Play Console → **App integrity** → **Upload key certificate**
3. Run a test `eas build` and `eas submit` to internal track before production
4. Revoke local copies after EAS upload succeeds - EAS is now source of truth

---

## Credential Recovery

### Lost upload key (Play App Signing enabled)

1. Play Console → **App integrity** → **Request upload key reset**
2. Generate a new upload key via `eas credentials --platform android`
3. Submit the new certificate to Google for approval
4. Rebuild and upload AAB - users unaffected (app signing key unchanged)

### Lost upload key (Play App Signing disabled)

* **No recovery path** - you cannot publish updates to the same package name
* This is why Play App Signing is mandatory for new apps

### Rotating off a teammate

```bash
# Admin downloads credentials backup (one-time export) and stores in team vault
eas credentials --platform android
 
# Remove local .jks from laptops - CI uses EAS remote credentials only
```

---

## eas.json Signing Options

```json
{
  "build": {
    "production": {
      "android": {
        "buildType": "app-bundle",
        "gradleCommand": ":app:bundleRelease"
      }
    },
    "development": {
      "android": {
        "buildType": "apk",
        "withoutCredentials": false
      }
    }
  }
}
```

* **`buildType": "app-bundle"`** - required for Play production
* **`buildType": "apk"`** - preview / internal sideload without Play
* **`withoutCredentials": true`** - unsigned debug-style builds only; rare for RN apps

---

## FAQs

Should EAS generate our keystore or should we bring our own?

* **Greenfield** - let EAS generate; simplest team onboarding.
* **Existing Play app** - upload the current upload keystore; fingerprint must match Play records.
* Never generate a second upload key for a live app without Play Console reset workflow.

Where does the keystore live?

* Encrypted on Expo servers, referenced by `eas credentials`.
* Optional one-time download for disaster recovery - store in a team password manager vault.
* Not in your git repo.

How do I auto-increment versionCode?

```json
{
  "cli": { "appVersionSource": "remote" },
  "build": {
    "production": { "autoIncrement": true }
  }
}
```

* Remote version source keeps CI and local builds aligned
* Play rejects duplicate `versionCode` - always increment on upload

APK or AAB for internal QA?

* **APK** - direct download link from EAS; no Play Console required.
* **AAB + internal track** - closer to production delivery; see [Internal Testing Tracks](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/android-platform/internal-testing-tracks/).

Dokumen: EAS Build Best Practices
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/eas-build/best-practices/

# EAS Build Best Practices

A condensed summary of the **25 most important best practices** drawn from every page in EAS Build - reproducible builds with locked dependencies, fingerprint gates, and credential hygiene on Expo SDK 57.

Highlights / EAS Build Best Practices

* Commit lockfiles - EAS resolves the same tree as local and CI
* Gitignore ios/ and android/ under CNG - let EAS run prebuild
* Map eas.json profiles to EAS environments - never rely on laptop .env
* Fingerprint gates decide rebuild vs eas update - not gut feel
* Use autoIncrement and appVersionSource remote for monotonic store versions
* Document eas-build hooks and non-obvious eas.json in README

1. **Run `eas build:configure` early:** Link `projectId` in `app.config.ts` before the first cloud compile - builds without it fail with opaque config errors.
2. **Commit lockfiles with every native-affecting change:** `package-lock.json` / `yarn.lock` / `pnpm-lock.yaml` must match what EAS installs - floating ranges cause non-reproducible binaries.
3. **Gitignore `ios/` and `android/` under CNG:** Upload JS + config - EAS runs `expo prebuild` when native folders are absent. See [Prebuild Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/prebuild-basics/).
4. **Use three baseline profiles:** `development`, `preview`, `production` in `eas.json` - avoid engineer-named one-off profiles that rot undocumented.
5. **Bind every profile to an EAS environment:** `environment: "production"` pulls vars from Expo dashboard - local `.env.local` is ignored on build runners.
6. **Align `channel` with `eas update`:** Production binaries on `channel: "production"` must receive updates published to the same channel - [Release & OTA Rules](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/release-and-ota-rules/).
7. **Set explicit `runtimeVersion` policy:** Use `appVersion`, `sdkVersion`, or `fingerprint` consistently - mismatch strands users on stale JS silently.
8. **Adopt fingerprint CI gates:** `@expo/fingerprint` diff before merge tells you whether OTA is safe or a new `eas build` is mandatory.
9. **Rebuild dev clients after native changes:** SDK bumps, new native modules, and config plugin edits require new `development` profile builds - OTA cannot upgrade embedded native code.
10. **Let EAS manage iOS credentials:** Distribution certs and provisioning profiles stored encrypted - teammates use `--non-interactive` without Xcode signing exports.
11. **Let EAS generate Android keystores for greenfield apps:** Upload existing keystores only when migrating a live Play app - fingerprint must match Play Console upload certificate.
12. **Enable Play App Signing:** Google holds the app signing key - upload key loss is recoverable; app signing key loss is catastrophic.
13. **Use `buildType: "app-bundle"` for Play production:** APK is for internal sideload preview - AAB is required for store production uploads.
14. **Enable `autoIncrement` on store profiles:** Remote `buildNumber` / `versionCode` prevents "redundant binary" and "version code already used" rejections.
15. **Register iOS devices before ad hoc builds:** `eas device:create` → tester enrollment → rebuild - profiles embed UDIDs at compile time.
16. **Prefer TestFlight internal over ad hoc for iOS QA:** Production signing, easier installs, no per-device profile rebuild for ASC team members - [TestFlight Distribution](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ios-platform/testflight-distribution/).
17. **Submit to Play internal track before production:** Catch signing and policy issues on up to 100 testers - promote through closed → open → staged rollout.
18. **Store submit secrets in CI vaults:** App Store Connect `.p8` and Play service account JSON - never in git; reference paths in `eas.json` submit profiles.
19. **Use `EXPO_TOKEN` for CI builds and submits:** Machine tokens from expo.dev - personal session tokens expire and break pipelines.
20. **Run `npx expo-doctor` before `eas build`:** Catch invalid config and SDK version skew before spending EAS minutes on a doomed compile.
21. **Express native changes in config plugins:** Hand-editing generated `Info.plist` or `build.gradle` is lost on prebuild `--clean` - hooks are not a substitute.
22. **Document `eas-build-pre-install` / `post-install` hooks:** Non-obvious pipeline steps belong in README - future engineers will not read `package.json` scripts first.
23. **Keep hooks fast:** Private registry auth and codegen are fine - 20-minute E2E suites belong in CI gates before triggering EAS, not on the worker.
24. **Pin `cli.version` in eas.json:** Ensures local and CI use compatible EAS CLI semantics - bump deliberately when adopting new flags.
25. **Physical device smoke test after credential or plugin changes:** Simulators miss push entitlements, App Links, and signing edge cases that only appear on signed IPAs and release APKs.

## FAQs

When is OTA safe after a merged PR?

* Fingerprint unchanged since last store binary → JS-only fixes may use `eas update`.
* Fingerprint changed → new `eas build` for production and development clients.
* See [Fingerprint & Native Change Detection](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/fingerprint-and-native-change-detection/).

Should preview builds use internal or store distribution?

* **internal** - fastest APK/ad hoc loops for daily QA.
* **store** + TestFlight when you need production-identical signing and push environment.
* Both are release-compiled - preview is not a debug binary.

How do we onboard a new engineer to EAS builds?

1. `eas login` + clone repo with lockfile
2. `eas build --profile development --platform ios` (simulator) or Android APK
3. Install dev client → `npx expo start --dev-client`
4. Read [EAS Build Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/eas-build/eas-build-basics/) and credential pages before touching production profiles.

What is the fastest validation loop before EAS?

1. `npx expo-doctor`
2. `npx expo prebuild --no-install` (twice - zero diff on second run)
3. `eas build --profile preview --platform <one>` for device proof
4. Promote to production profile only after QA sign-off.

Does Expo Go replace EAS Build for custom native code?

* No - Expo Go uses a fixed binary and ignores your entitlements and custom modules.
* Custom native code requires prebuild + dev client or store build - [Prebuild Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/prebuild-basics/).

Dokumen: Build Profiles & Flavors
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/eas-build/build-profiles-and-flavors/

# Build Profiles & Flavors

Dev, preview, production, and **white-label variants** - the cookbook for structuring `eas.json` profiles and dynamic `app.config.ts` on Expo SDK 57.

Highlights / Build Profiles & Flavors

* eas.json profiles are named build recipes - not the same as Android product flavors
* Map development, preview, and production to EAS environments for env var parity
* White-label apps use app.config.ts variants with distinct bundle IDs per brand
* channel on a profile ties store binaries to eas update promotion paths
* APP\_VARIANT env vars drive dynamic app.config.ts for staging vs production
* Each flavor needs separate credentials - one keystore per package name

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```json
// eas.json - three-environment baseline
{
  "cli": { "version": ">= 16.0.0", "appVersionSource": "remote" },
  "build": {
    "development": {
      "developmentClient": true,
      "distribution": "internal",
      "environment": "development",
      "channel": "development"
    },
    "preview": {
      "distribution": "internal",
      "environment": "preview",
      "channel": "preview"
    },
    "production": {
      "distribution": "store",
      "environment": "production",
      "channel": "production",
      "autoIncrement": true
    }
  }
}
```

```ts
// app.config.ts - APP_VARIANT from eas.json env
import type { ExpoConfig } from "expo/config";
 
const variant = process.env.APP_VARIANT ?? "production";
 
const bundleIds: Record<string, string> = {
  development: "com.example.shopapp.dev",
  preview: "com.example.shopapp.staging",
  production: "com.example.shopapp",
};
 
const config: ExpoConfig = {
  name: variant === "production" ? "Shop" : `Shop (${variant})`,
  slug: "shop-app",
  ios: { bundleIdentifier: bundleIds[variant] },
  android: { package: bundleIds[variant] },
  extra: {
    apiUrl: process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL,
    eas: { projectId: "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000" },
  },
};
 
export default config;
```

```json
// eas.json - pass variant into prebuild
{
  "build": {
    "preview": {
      "env": { "APP_VARIANT": "preview" },
      "environment": "preview"
    }
  }
}
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Staging and production must install side-by-side on the same device.
* White-label brands share one codebase with different icons and bundle IDs.
* QA needs preview API URLs without risking production data.
* EAS Update channels must not cross-pollinate environments.

## Working Example

**Step 1 - Define profile responsibilities**

| Profile | Audience | Distribution | Typical binary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **development** | Engineers | internal | Dev client + simulator/APK |
| **preview** | QA / stakeholders | internal | Release-shaped IPA/APK |
| **production** | End users | store | AAB + App Store IPA |

```bash
eas build --profile development --platform all
eas build --profile preview --platform ios
eas build --profile production --platform android
```

**Step 2 - Bind EAS environments**

Create variables in Expo dashboard → **Project** → **Environment variables**:

```text
development   EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL=https://api.dev.example.com
preview       EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL=https://api.staging.example.com
production    EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL=https://api.example.com
```

```json
{
  "build": {
    "preview": { "environment": "preview" }
  }
}
```

* **`environment`** pulls vars from EAS - not laptop `.env.local`
* `eas update --environment production` must match production profile - [Release & OTA Rules](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/release-and-ota-rules/)

**Step 3 - White-label with app.config.ts**

```ts
// app.config.ts - multi-brand from BRAND env
type Brand = "acme" | "contoso";
 
const brand = (process.env.BRAND ?? "acme") as Brand;
 
const brands: Record<Brand, { name: string; bundleId: string; icon: string }> = {
  acme: {
    name: "Acme Shop",
    bundleId: "com.acme.shop",
    icon: "./brands/acme/icon.png",
  },
  contoso: {
    name: "Contoso Market",
    bundleId: "com.contoso.market",
    icon: "./brands/contoso/icon.png",
  },
};
 
const config: ExpoConfig = {
  name: brands[brand].name,
  slug: `shop-${brand}`,
  icon: brands[brand].icon,
  ios: { bundleIdentifier: brands[brand].bundleId },
  android: {
    package: brands[brand].bundleId,
    adaptiveIcon: { foregroundImage: brands[brand].icon, backgroundColor: "#fff" },
  },
};
 
export default config;
```

```json
// eas.json - one profile per brand for production
{
  "build": {
    "production-acme": {
      "extends": "production",
      "env": { "BRAND": "acme" },
      "environment": "production-acme"
    },
    "production-contoso": {
      "extends": "production",
      "env": { "BRAND": "contoso" },
      "environment": "production-contoso"
    }
  }
}
```

```bash
eas build --profile production-acme --platform all
eas build --profile production-contoso --platform all
```

* Each brand needs **separate** `projectId` or careful channel isolation per bundle ID
* Separate **iOS certs** and **Android keystores** per `bundleIdentifier` / `package`

---

## Profile Inheritance with extends

DRY shared settings across profiles:

```json
{
  "build": {
    "base": {
      "node": "22.11.0",
      "resourceClass": "medium"
    },
    "development": {
      "extends": "base",
      "developmentClient": true,
      "distribution": "internal"
    },
    "production": {
      "extends": "base",
      "distribution": "store",
      "autoIncrement": true
    },
    "production-ios-simulator": {
      "extends": "production",
      "ios": { "simulator": true },
      "distribution": "internal"
    }
  }
}
```

* **`extends`** merges parent keys - child overrides win
* Use for Detox simulator builds, Maestro CI, and shared Node version pins

---

## Profiles vs Android Product Flavors

Expo CNG typically uses **one Gradle applicationId** per prebuild driven by `app.config.ts`:

```text
eas.json profile  →  APP_VARIANT env  →  app.config.ts  →  applicationId
```

Native Android **product flavors** in `build.gradle` are possible in brownfield projects but fight CNG regeneration. Prefer:

1. Dynamic `app.config.ts` for bundle ID, name, and icons
2. Separate EAS profiles per variant
3. Config plugins for flavor-specific native resources if unavoidable

See [Prebuild Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/prebuild-basics/) - hand-edited `android/app/build.gradle` product flavors are lost on clean prebuild.

---

## Channel and Runtime Alignment

```ts
// app.config.ts
runtimeVersion: {
  policy: "fingerprint",
},
updates: {
  url: "https://u.expo.dev/<project-id>",
},
```

```json
{
  "build": {
    "preview": { "channel": "preview" },
    "production": { "channel": "production" }
  }
}
```

```bash
eas update --channel preview --environment preview --message "QA fix"
eas update --channel production --environment production --message "Hotfix"
```

* Channel on the **binary** must match channel on **`eas update`**
* Different flavors with different native fingerprints need different runtime versions

---

## FAQs

Can development and production install on the same phone?

* **Yes** if `bundleIdentifier` / `package` differ - use `APP_VARIANT` suffixes like `.dev` and `.staging`.
* **No** if they share the same ID - the new install replaces the old app.

How many profiles should we have?

* Start with **three**: development, preview, production.
* Add brand-specific or platform-specific profiles with `extends` when needed.
* Avoid engineer-named profiles (`"jane-debug"`) - use environments and channels instead.

Should preview use store or internal distribution?

* **internal** for APK/ad hoc and fast iteration.
* **store** + TestFlight internal when QA needs production-identical signing - [TestFlight Distribution](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ios-platform/testflight-distribution/).

How do white-label apps share one repo?

* Single codebase + `BRAND` env + separate credentials per package name.
* Separate EAS projects or strict channel isolation per brand.
* Document which profile maps to which Play Console / App Store Connect app.
