# Network Failure UX

Offline banners, retry queues, and stale-while-revalidate displays.

Highlights / Network Failure UX

* Detect connectivity with @react-native-community/netinfo - not a one-time fetch probe
* Show a persistent offline banner; distinguish offline from server errors
* TanStack Query onlineManager ties query retries to real network state
* Stale-while-revalidate: keep showing cached data with a clear last-updated label
* Queue failed mutations locally and flush when isConnected returns
* Retry buttons should call refetch - not reload the entire app

Mobile networks drop constantly - elevators, tunnels, flaky Wi‑Fi. Good network failure UX **detects connectivity**, **communicates state**, **shows cached data when possible**, and **retries safely** when the device is back online.

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```tsx
import NetInfo, { useNetInfo } from "@react-native-community/netinfo";
import { onlineManager, useQuery } from "@tanstack/react-query";
import { useEffect } from "react";
import { Pressable, StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
// Sync TanStack Query's online state with the device
onlineManager.setEventListener((setOnline) =>
  NetInfo.addEventListener((state) => {
    setOnline(!!state.isConnected && state.isInternetReachable !== false);
  })
);
 
function OfflineBanner() {
  const net = useNetInfo();
  const offline = net.isConnected === false || net.isInternetReachable === false;
  if (!offline) return null;
  return (
    <View style={styles.banner}>
      <Text style={styles.bannerText}>You are offline. Showing saved data where available.</Text>
    </View>
  );
}
 
async function fetchPosts() {
  const res = await fetch("https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts?_limit=5");
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);
  return res.json() as Promise<{ id: number; title: string }[]>;
}
 
export function FeedScreen() {
  const { data, error, isError, isFetching, refetch, dataUpdatedAt } = useQuery({
    queryKey: ["posts"],
    queryFn: fetchPosts,
    staleTime: 60_000,
    retry: 2,
  });
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.screen}>
      <OfflineBanner />
      {data && (
        <Text style={styles.stale}>
          {isFetching ? "Updating…" : `Updated ${new Date(dataUpdatedAt).toLocaleTimeString()}`}
        </Text>
      )}
      {isError && (
        <View style={styles.errorBox}>
          <Text style={styles.errorText}>{error instanceof Error ? error.message : "Request failed"}</Text>
          <Pressable onPress={() => refetch()} style={styles.retry}>
            <Text style={styles.retryLabel}>Retry</Text>
          </Pressable>
        </View>
      )}
      {data?.map((post) => (
        <Text key={post.id} style={styles.row}>{post.title}</Text>
      ))}
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  screen: { flex: 1, padding: 16, backgroundColor: "#fff" },
  banner: { backgroundColor: "#fef3c7", padding: 10, borderRadius: 8, marginBottom: 12 },
  bannerText: { color: "#92400e", fontWeight: "600" },
  stale: { fontSize: 12, color: "#64748b", marginBottom: 8 },
  errorBox: { padding: 12, backgroundColor: "#fee2e2", borderRadius: 8, marginBottom: 12 },
  errorText: { color: "#991b1b", marginBottom: 8 },
  retry: { alignSelf: "flex-start", backgroundColor: "#dc2626", paddingHorizontal: 12, paddingVertical: 8, borderRadius: 6 },
  retryLabel: { color: "#fff", fontWeight: "600" },
  row: { fontSize: 14, marginBottom: 6 },
});
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Feed, catalog, or profile screens that should remain readable offline with cached data.
* Forms or actions that must **not** silently fail when the device loses connectivity.
* Apps using TanStack Query (or similar) that need correct pause/resume of retries.
* Any screen where users blame the app for "spinning forever" on a dead network.
* Mutation flows (post, pay, save) that should queue and flush when online returns.

## Working Example

```tsx
import AsyncStorage from "@react-native-async-storage/async-storage";
import NetInfo, { useNetInfo } from "@react-native-community/netinfo";
import { onlineManager, useMutation, useQuery, useQueryClient } from "@tanstack/react-query";
import { useCallback, useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { FlatList, Pressable, StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
const QUEUE_KEY = "offline-mutation-queue-v1";
 
type Todo = { id: string; title: string; pending?: boolean };
type QueuedCreate = { id: string; title: string };
 
onlineManager.setEventListener((setOnline) =>
  NetInfo.addEventListener((state) => {
    setOnline(!!state.isConnected && state.isInternetReachable !== false);
  })
);
 
async function loadTodos(): Promise<Todo[]> {
  const raw = await AsyncStorage.getItem("todos-cache");
  return raw ? (JSON.parse(raw) as Todo[]) : [];
}
 
async function saveTodos(todos: Todo[]) {
  await AsyncStorage.setItem("todos-cache", JSON.stringify(todos));
}
 
async function readQueue(): Promise<QueuedCreate[]> {
  const raw = await AsyncStorage.getItem(QUEUE_KEY);
  return raw ? (JSON.parse(raw) as QueuedCreate[]) : [];
}
 
async function writeQueue(items: QueuedCreate[]) {
  await AsyncStorage.setItem(QUEUE_KEY, JSON.stringify(items));
}
 
async function createTodoOnServer(title: string): Promise<Todo> {
  const net = await NetInfo.fetch();
  if (!net.isConnected) throw new TypeError("OFFLINE");
 
  // Simulated API - replace with your backend
  await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 400));
  return { id: `srv-${Date.now()}`, title };
}
 
function ConnectivityChrome() {
  const net = useNetInfo();
  const offline = net.isConnected === false;
  const captive = net.isConnected && net.isInternetReachable === false;
 
  if (offline) {
    return (
      <View style={[styles.banner, styles.offline]}>
        <Text style={styles.bannerText}>Offline - changes will sync when you reconnect.</Text>
      </View>
    );
  }
  if (captive) {
    return (
      <View style={[styles.banner, styles.captive]}>
        <Text style={styles.bannerText}>Connected, but no internet reachability.</Text>
      </View>
    );
  }
  return null;
}
 
export default function App() {
  const queryClient = useQueryClient();
  const [title, setTitle] = useState("");
  const [queueLen, setQueueLen] = useState(0);
 
  const todosQuery = useQuery({
    queryKey: ["todos"],
    queryFn: loadTodos,
    staleTime: 30_000,
    // Stale-while-revalidate: show cached list immediately; refresh when online
    placeholderData: (prev) => prev,
  });
 
  const flushQueue = useCallback(async () => {
    const queue = await readQueue();
    if (queue.length === 0) return;
 
    const remaining: QueuedCreate[] = [];
    let todos = (await loadTodos()) ?? [];
 
    for (const item of queue) {
      try {
        const created = await createTodoOnServer(item.title);
        todos = todos.map((t) => (t.id === item.id ? created : t));
      } catch {
        remaining.push(item);
      }
    }
 
    await saveTodos(todos);
    await writeQueue(remaining);
    setQueueLen(remaining.length);
    queryClient.setQueryData(["todos"], todos);
  }, [queryClient]);
 
  useEffect(() => {
    const unsub = NetInfo.addEventListener((state) => {
      if (state.isConnected && state.isInternetReachable !== false) {
        void flushQueue();
      }
    });
    void readQueue().then((q) => setQueueLen(q.length));
    return () => unsub();
  }, [flushQueue]);
 
  const createMutation = useMutation({
    mutationFn: async (newTitle: string) => {
      const optimistic: Todo = { id: `local-${Date.now()}`, title: newTitle, pending: true };
      const current = (await loadTodos()) ?? [];
      const next = [optimistic, ...current];
      await saveTodos(next);
      queryClient.setQueryData(["todos"], next);
 
      try {
        const created = await createTodoOnServer(newTitle);
        const synced = next.map((t) => (t.id === optimistic.id ? created : t));
        await saveTodos(synced);
        queryClient.setQueryData(["todos"], synced);
        return created;
      } catch (e) {
        if (e instanceof TypeError && e.message === "OFFLINE") {
          const queue = await readQueue();
          await writeQueue([...queue, { id: optimistic.id, title: newTitle }]);
          setQueueLen((n) => n + 1);
          return optimistic;
        }
        throw e;
      }
    },
  });
 
  const todos = todosQuery.data ?? [];
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.screen}>
      <ConnectivityChrome />
      {todosQuery.isFetching && <Text style={styles.meta}>Refreshing…</Text>}
      {queueLen > 0 && (
        <Text style={styles.meta}>{queueLen} change(s) waiting to sync</Text>
      )}
 
      <Pressable
        style={styles.add}
        onPress={() => {
          const next = title.trim() || `Todo ${Date.now()}`;
          setTitle("");
          createMutation.mutate(next);
        }}
      >
        <Text style={styles.addLabel}>Add todo</Text>
      </Pressable>
 
      <FlatList
        data={todos}
        keyExtractor={(item) => item.id}
        renderItem={({ item }) => (
          <Text style={styles.row}>
            {item.pending ? "⏳ " : ""}
            {item.title}
          </Text>
        )}
        ListEmptyComponent={<Text style={styles.meta}>No todos yet.</Text>}
      />
 
      {todosQuery.isError && (
        <Pressable onPress={() => todosQuery.refetch()} style={styles.retry}>
          <Text style={styles.retryLabel}>Retry load</Text>
        </Pressable>
      )}
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  screen: { flex: 1, padding: 16, backgroundColor: "#f8fafc" },
  banner: { padding: 10, borderRadius: 8, marginBottom: 10 },
  offline: { backgroundColor: "#fef3c7" },
  captive: { backgroundColor: "#ffedd5" },
  bannerText: { fontWeight: "600", color: "#78350f" },
  meta: { fontSize: 12, color: "#64748b", marginBottom: 8 },
  add: { backgroundColor: "#2563eb", padding: 12, borderRadius: 8, marginBottom: 12 },
  addLabel: { color: "#fff", fontWeight: "600", textAlign: "center" },
  row: { fontSize: 16, paddingVertical: 8, borderBottomWidth: StyleSheet.hairlineWidth, borderColor: "#e2e8f0" },
  retry: { marginTop: 12, padding: 12, backgroundColor: "#dc2626", borderRadius: 8, alignItems: "center" },
  retryLabel: { color: "#fff", fontWeight: "600" },
});
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* `useNetInfo` drives a **connectivity banner** with distinct offline vs captive-portal messaging.
* `onlineManager` syncs TanStack Query retry behavior with real device connectivity.
* **Stale-while-revalidate**: cached todos render immediately via `placeholderData` while a background refetch runs.
* **Optimistic UI** plus a persisted **retry queue** for creates that fail while offline.
* Automatic **queue flush** when `NetInfo` reports the device is back online.
* Per-screen **Retry** calls `refetch()` - not an app restart.

## Deep Dive

### How It Works

* **`@react-native-community/netinfo`** listens to OS connectivity events (Wi‑Fi, cellular, airplane mode). `isConnected` means a network interface exists; `isInternetReachable` adds a reachability probe (can be `null` while checking).
* **Offline banner** is a global or screen-level chrome element - always visible when offline so users understand why actions stall.
* **TanStack Query** pauses retries when `onlineManager` reports offline and resumes when online. Pair with `staleTime` and `gcTime` so cached data survives short outages.
* **Stale-while-revalidate (SWR)** shows the last successful payload while `isFetching` is true. Label it with `dataUpdatedAt` so users know data may be old.
* **Retry queue** persists failed mutations (AsyncStorage, MMKV, SQLite) and replays them idempotently when connectivity returns.
* Distinguish **offline** (no network), **timeout** (slow/dead server), and **HTTP errors** (4xx/5xx) - copy and actions differ for each.

### Connectivity Signals

| Signal | Meaning | UX response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `isConnected === false` | Airplane mode, no interface | Offline banner; queue mutations |
| `isInternetReachable === false` | Wi‑Fi without DNS/captive portal | "Connected but no internet" banner |
| `isInternetReachable === null` | Probe in flight | Do not flash offline UI - keep previous state |
| Fetch throws `TypeError` / timeout | Server or DNS failure while "online" | Inline error + Retry; not the offline banner |
| HTTP 5xx | Server error | "Service unavailable" + Retry with backoff |

```bash
npx expo install @react-native-community/netinfo @react-native-async-storage/async-storage @tanstack/react-query
```

### TanStack Query Mobile Defaults

```tsx
import { AppState, Platform } from "react-native";
import { focusManager, QueryClient } from "@tanstack/react-query";
 
// Refetch on app foreground (pairs with network recovery)
focusManager.setEventListener((handleFocus) => {
  const sub = AppState.addEventListener("change", (state) => {
    if (state === "active") handleFocus();
  });
  return () => sub.remove();
});
 
export const queryClient = new QueryClient({
  defaultOptions: {
    queries: {
      retry: 2,
      staleTime: 30_000,
      gcTime: 24 * 60 * 60_000,
    },
  },
});
```

See [TanStack Query on Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/tanstack-query-on-mobile/) for full `focusManager` / `onlineManager` setup.

### Retry Queue Design

| Concern | Recommendation |
| --- | --- |
| Storage | AsyncStorage for small queues; MMKV/SQLite for high volume |
| Idempotency | Send client-generated idempotency keys to your API |
| Ordering | Process FIFO per entity; parallelize independent entities |
| Conflict | On 409, drop or merge using server version |
| UI | Show `pending` state on optimistic rows until flush succeeds |
| Failure cap | After N failures, surface item to user for manual retry/discard |

```tsx
type QueueItem = {
  idempotencyKey: string;
  operation: "create" | "update" | "delete";
  payload: unknown;
  attempts: number;
};
```

### Stale-While-Revalidate Display Patterns

| Pattern | User sees | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cached list + banner | Last feed + "Offline" | `isConnected === false` |
| Cached + spinner | Old data + subtle "Updating…" | `isFetching && data` |
| Empty + error | Illustration + Retry | `isError && !data` |
| Skeleton first load | Placeholder rows | `isLoading && !data` |

Always show **when** data was last fresh: `dataUpdatedAt`, "Updated 2 min ago", or "Showing saved copy".

### TypeScript Notes

```tsx
import type { NetInfoState } from "@react-native-community/netinfo";
 
function isEffectivelyOffline(state: NetInfoState): boolean {
  if (state.isConnected === false) return true;
  if (state.isInternetReachable === false) return true;
  return false;
}
 
type NetworkFailure =
  | { kind: "offline" }
  | { kind: "timeout" }
  | { kind: "http"; status: number };
 
function classifyFetchError(error: unknown): NetworkFailure {
  if (error instanceof TypeError) return { kind: "offline" };
  return { kind: "timeout" };
}
```

* Treat `isInternetReachable === null` as **unknown**, not offline - avoids banner flicker.
* Type mutation queue items narrowly so replay logic stays exhaustive.

## Gotchas

* **Using a single failed fetch to mean "offline"** - Servers return 500 while Wi‑Fi is fine. **Fix:** Combine `NetInfo` with error type; show different copy for offline vs server errors.
* **Flashing the offline banner when `isInternetReachable` is `null`** - NetInfo probes take a moment on launch. **Fix:** Only show offline UI when `isConnected === false` or `isInternetReachable === false`, not during `null`.
* **Infinite retry spinners** - `retry: true` without `onlineManager` drains battery on airplane mode. **Fix:** Wire `onlineManager` to NetInfo and cap retries.
* **Reloading the app on Retry** - `Updates.reloadAsync()` discards in-memory state and feels broken. **Fix:** Call `refetch()` or replay the queue item.
* **Silent mutation loss offline** - Users think saves succeeded. **Fix:** Optimistic UI with `pending` marker + persisted queue until server ack.
* **Showing stale data without labeling it** - Users make decisions on outdated prices or balances. **Fix:** Display `dataUpdatedAt` or "Showing saved data from …".
* **Queue replay without idempotency** - Reconnect creates duplicate charges or posts. **Fix:** Idempotency keys on client and server; see [Retries, Backoff & Idempotency](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/retries-backoff-and-idempotency/).

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NetInfo + manual banners | Full control, any data layer | You already standardize on TanStack Query's `isFetching` / `isError` alone |
| TanStack Query only (no NetInfo) | Read-only apps with tolerant caching | You must gate mutations or explain offline state clearly |
| Full offline-first (SQLite sync) | Field apps with long offline windows | Simple CRUD apps that only need graceful failure |
| Expo `Network` module | Legacy Expo docs reference | Greenfield apps - prefer `@react-native-community/netinfo` |
| Background sync (TaskManager) | Large uploads that must finish later | Immediate user feedback on the same screen is enough |

## FAQs

How do I install NetInfo in an Expo SDK 57 app?

```bash
npx expo install @react-native-community/netinfo
```

Expo supports this module in development builds and production; no config plugin is required for basic connectivity listeners.

What is the difference between isConnected and isInternetReachable?

* `isConnected` - device has a network interface (Wi‑Fi or cellular).
* `isInternetReachable` - NetInfo probed actual internet access (can be `false` on captive portals).

Use both: show offline when disconnected; show a different message when connected but unreachable.

Why hook onlineManager to NetInfo?

TanStack Query pauses automatic retries when offline and resumes when `onlineManager` flips to true. Without this, queries retry uselessly in airplane mode.

What is stale-while-revalidate in mobile terms?

Show the last successful response immediately (`placeholderData` or persisted cache), fetch fresh data in the background, and label the timestamp. Users stay productive during slow or flaky networks.

Should the offline banner block interaction?

Usually no - use a slim non-blocking banner. Disable only actions that truly cannot work offline (e.g. payment capture), not entire read-only screens with cached data.

How do I persist query cache across app restarts?

Use TanStack Query's `persistQueryClient` with AsyncStorage or MMKV for read-mostly screens. Pair with `staleTime` and manual invalidation on logout.

What should a Retry button do?

```tsx
<Pressable onPress={() => refetch()}>
  <Text>Retry</Text>
</Pressable>
```

Refetch the failed query or replay the specific queue item - do not restart the app unless a fatal native error requires it.

How do I queue mutations offline?

On mutation failure when offline: write `{ idempotencyKey, payload }` to storage, show optimistic `pending` UI, subscribe to NetInfo, and flush the queue when connected. Increment `attempts` and stop after a cap.

How is a server 500 different from offline UX?

Offline: yellow banner, queue actions, show cache. Server 500: inline error on the affected section ("Service unavailable"), Retry with exponential backoff, no offline banner.

Should I use pull-to-refresh on error screens?

Yes - `RefreshControl` wired to `refetch()` is idiomatic on mobile and matches user expectations alongside an explicit Retry button.

Does NetInfo fire when the app is backgrounded?

Yes - subscribe in a root provider or hook and update global state. Flush queues on reconnect even if the user returns later; pair with `AppState` foreground refetch.

How long should staleTime be on mobile?

Start with 30–60 seconds for frequently changing feeds, longer for catalogs and profile shells. Balance freshness with battery - see [Networking Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/networking-basics/).

Can I show cached data and an error at the same time?

Yes - keep stale list visible, show a compact error bar ("Could not refresh"), and let Retry call `refetch()`. Hiding good cache on transient refresh failure feels worse than partial degradation.

How does this relate to offline-first architecture?

This page covers **failure UX** on networked screens. Full offline-first adds local databases, sync engines, and conflict resolution - see [Offline-First Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/data-offline/offline-first-basics/).

Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/error-resilience/user-facing-error-copy/

# User-Facing Error Copy

Actionable messages vs opaque stack traces on mobile.

Highlights / User-Facing Error Copy

* Users need what happened, what is safe, and what to do next - not a stack trace
* Map internal errors to a small set of user messages at the network and boundary edges
* Primary action first: Retry, Check connection, or Contact support - one clear CTA
* accessibilityLiveRegion announces errors without moving focus away from the task
* \_\_DEV\_\_ shows diagnostics; production shows the same calm copy on every screen
* Never echo raw API bodies - 'Request failed with status 500' is not actionable

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```tsx
// src/errors/userMessages.ts
export type UserFacingError = {
  title: string;
  body: string;
  action: "retry" | "settings" | "support" | "dismiss";
  actionLabel: string;
};
 
const NETWORK: UserFacingError = {
  title: "You're offline",
  body: "Check your connection and try again. Your changes are saved on this device.",
  action: "retry",
  actionLabel: "Try again",
};
 
const UNKNOWN: UserFacingError = {
  title: "Something went wrong",
  body: "We could not complete that. Try again in a moment.",
  action: "retry",
  actionLabel: "Try again",
};
 
export function toUserFacingError(error: unknown): UserFacingError {
  if (error instanceof TypeError && /network/i.test(error.message)) {
    return NETWORK;
  }
  if (isHttpError(error, 401)) {
    return {
      title: "Session expired",
      body: "Sign in again to continue.",
      action: "dismiss",
      actionLabel: "Sign in",
    };
  }
  if (isHttpError(error, 503)) {
    return {
      title: "Service busy",
      body: "Our servers are temporarily overloaded. Wait a few seconds and retry.",
      action: "retry",
      actionLabel: "Try again",
    };
  }
  return UNKNOWN;
}
 
function isHttpError(error: unknown, status: number): boolean {
  return (
    typeof error === "object" &&
    error !== null &&
    "status" in error &&
    (error as { status: number }).status === status
  );
}
```

```tsx
// src/components/ErrorCallout.tsx
import { Button, StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
import type { UserFacingError } from "@/errors/userMessages";
 
type Props = {
  error: UserFacingError;
  onAction: () => void;
};
 
export function ErrorCallout({ error, onAction }: Props) {
  return (
    <View
      style={styles.box}
      accessibilityRole="alert"
      accessibilityLiveRegion="polite"
    >
      <Text style={styles.title}>{error.title}</Text>
      <Text style={styles.body}>{error.body}</Text>
      <Button title={error.actionLabel} onPress={onAction} />
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  box: {
    padding: 16,
    borderRadius: 8,
    backgroundColor: "#fef2f2",
    borderWidth: StyleSheet.hairlineWidth,
    borderColor: "#fecaca",
    gap: 8,
  },
  title: { fontSize: 16, fontWeight: "700", color: "#991b1b" },
  body: { color: "#7f1d1d", lineHeight: 20 },
});
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Any catch block, error boundary fallback, or failed fetch that would otherwise show `error.message` or a redbox.
* Offline and timeout states where the user can fix the problem without contacting support.
* Form submission failures where retry is safe and duplicate side effects are prevented.
* Empty states after errors - replace spinners that never resolve with honest copy.

## Working Example

```tsx
// src/errors/reportError.ts
import type { UserFacingError } from "./userMessages";
 
export function reportError(
  scope: string,
  cause: unknown,
  user: UserFacingError,
): void {
  if (__DEV__) {
    console.group(`[${scope}]`);
    console.error(cause);
    console.log("User copy:", user);
    console.groupEnd();
    return;
  }
  // Production: Sentry/Crashlytics with scope + cause; never attach user.title to analytics PII
}
 
// src/screens/ProfileScreen.tsx
import { useCallback, useEffect, useState } from "react";
import {
  ActivityIndicator,
  Button,
  StyleSheet,
  Text,
  View,
} from "react-native";
import { ErrorCallout } from "@/components/ErrorCallout";
import { reportError } from "@/errors/reportError";
import { toUserFacingError } from "@/errors/userMessages";
 
async function fetchProfile(): Promise<{ name: string }> {
  const response = await fetch("https://api.example.com/me");
  if (!response.ok) {
    throw { status: response.status, message: await response.text() };
  }
  return (await response.json()) as { name: string };
}
 
export function ProfileScreen() {
  const [name, setName] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true);
  const [userError, setUserError] = useState<ReturnType<
    typeof toUserFacingError
  > | null>(null);
 
  const load = useCallback(async () => {
    setLoading(true);
    setUserError(null);
    try {
      const data = await fetchProfile();
      setName(data.name);
    } catch (cause) {
      const user = toUserFacingError(cause);
      setUserError(user);
      reportError("ProfileScreen.load", cause, user);
    } finally {
      setLoading(false);
    }
  }, []);
 
  useEffect(() => {
    void load();
  }, [load]);
 
  if (loading) {
    return <ActivityIndicator accessibilityLabel="Loading profile" />;
  }
 
  if (userError) {
    return (
      <View style={styles.screen}>
        <ErrorCallout
          error={userError}
          onAction={() => {
            if (userError.action === "retry") void load();
            // wire sign-in / support / settings per action enum
          }}
        />
      </View>
    );
  }
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.screen}>
      <Text style={styles.title}>Hello, {name}</Text>
      <Button title="Refresh" onPress={() => void load()} />
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  screen: { flex: 1, padding: 24, justifyContent: "center", gap: 12 },
  title: { fontSize: 22, fontWeight: "700" },
});
 
// src/components/ScreenErrorBoundary.tsx - boundary copy matches the same tone
import { Component, type ReactNode } from "react";
import { Button, StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
type Props = { children: ReactNode };
type State = { hasError: boolean };
 
export class ScreenErrorBoundary extends Component<Props, State> {
  state: State = { hasError: false };
 
  static getDerivedStateFromError(): State {
    return { hasError: true };
  }
 
  componentDidCatch(error: Error) {
    if (__DEV__) console.error(error);
    // report to crash service in production
  }
 
  render() {
    if (this.state.hasError) {
      return (
        <View style={boundaryStyles.wrap} accessibilityRole="alert">
          <Text style={boundaryStyles.title}>This screen hit a snag</Text>
          <Text style={boundaryStyles.body}>
            The rest of the app still works. Try again or go back.
          </Text>
          <Button
            title="Try again"
            onPress={() => this.setState({ hasError: false })}
          />
        </View>
      );
    }
    return this.props.children;
  }
}
 
const boundaryStyles = StyleSheet.create({
  wrap: { flex: 1, justifyContent: "center", padding: 24, gap: 12 },
  title: { fontSize: 18, fontWeight: "700" },
  body: { color: "#64748b", lineHeight: 22 },
});
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* `toUserFacingError` maps messy internals to a fixed vocabulary of titles, bodies, and actions.
* `reportError` logs full detail in `__DEV__` only - production users never see stack traces.
* `ErrorCallout` uses `accessibilityRole="alert"` and `accessibilityLiveRegion` for VoiceOver/TalkBack.
* Error boundary copy matches fetch-error copy - same calm tone, same "Try again" pattern.

## Deep Dive

### How It Works

* **Single mapping layer** - Screens call `toUserFacingError(cause)` once; they never branch on `error.message` in JSX.
* **Structured user object** - `title`, `body`, `action`, `actionLabel` drive UI and analytics without leaking internals.
* **Separate reporting** - Crash reporters and log pipelines receive the raw `cause`; the UI receives only `UserFacingError`.
* **Action enum** - One primary CTA per error - retry, open settings, contact support, or dismiss. Secondary actions go in body copy as text links.
* **Consistent voice** - Short sentences, active voice, no blame ("Check your connection" not "You failed to connect").

### Message Formula

| Part | Guideline | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Title | 3–6 words, no jargon | "You're offline" |
| Body | What happened + what is safe + hint | "Check your connection. Your draft is saved." |
| Action | One verb, matches recovery | "Try again" |
| Avoid | Status codes, exception names, URLs | Not "HTTP 503" or "TypeError: undefined" |

### Error Categories on Mobile

| Category | User title | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Offline / timeout | You're offline | Retry |
| Auth expired | Session expired | Sign in |
| Server 5xx | Service busy | Retry |
| Permission denied | Permission needed | Open settings |
| Validation | Check highlighted fields | Dismiss |
| Unknown | Something went wrong | Retry or support |

### Dev vs Production

```tsx
export function DevDiagnostics({ error }: { error: unknown }) {
  if (!__DEV__) return null;
  return (
    <Text style={{ fontFamily: "monospace", fontSize: 11 }}>
      {error instanceof Error ? error.stack : String(error)}
    </Text>
  );
}
```

Render `DevDiagnostics` below `ErrorCallout` in development builds only. Strip it from release binaries - `__DEV__` is false in production.

### TypeScript Notes

```tsx
// Keep action handling exhaustive
function handleErrorAction(
  user: UserFacingError,
  handlers: Record<UserFacingError["action"], () => void>,
) {
  handlers[user.action]();
}
```

## Gotchas

* **Showing `error.message` from fetch** - Often `"Network request failed"` or raw HTML. **Fix:** Map to `UserFacingError`; log raw body in `reportError` only.
* **Stack traces in Alert.alert** - Common debug habit left in production. **Fix:** `Alert` gets `user.title` and `user.body` only.
* **Blaming the user** - "You entered invalid data" feels accusatory. **Fix:** "Check the highlighted fields" or "Use a valid email address."
* **Two competing CTAs** - "Retry" and "Contact support" with equal weight paralyzes mobile users. **Fix:** One primary `Button`; support as tertiary text link.
* **Silent failures** - Spinner stops with no message. **Fix:** Every failed async path sets `userError` or an inline field error.
* **Announcing errors aggressively** - `accessibilityLiveRegion="assertive"` on every keystroke validation interrupts screen readers. **Fix:** `polite` for form errors; `assertive` only for blocking screen-level failures.
* **Localized strings inline** - Hard-coded English in mappers blocks i18n. **Fix:** Return message keys (`errors.offline.title`) and resolve with `i18n.t` in the component.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Centralized mapper (this page) | Most app errors share a small vocabulary | Highly domain-specific errors needing unique UX per screen |
| Toast-only errors | Non-blocking background sync failures | Blocking errors - toasts disappear before users read them |
| Raw API `message` field | Backend owns trusted, user-tested copy end-to-end | Third-party APIs or verbose developer messages |
| Error codes in UI ("E1042") | Support-heavy B2B with trained agents | Consumer apps - codes feel like blame |
| Redbox / LogBox in production | Never | Development only - redboxes are not user-facing copy |

## FAQs

Should I ever show technical details to users?

No in production. In `__DEV__`, show stacks below the friendly callout for engineers. Support staff can look up incidents by timestamp/user ID in your dashboard - users do not need a fault code on screen.

How long should error body copy be?

One or two short sentences (roughly 120 characters). Mobile screens are narrow; long apologies push the action button below the fold.

What tone should error copy use?

Calm, direct, and helpful. Acknowledge the problem, state what is preserved ("your draft is saved"), and give one next step. Avoid humor for payment, health, or auth errors.

How do error boundaries differ from fetch error copy?

Boundaries catch render errors - copy should reassure that the **rest of the app works** and offer "Try again" or navigation back. Fetch errors are **operation** failures - copy can be specific (offline, session expired).

Should retry buttons auto-retry?

Let the user tap retry - auto-retry loops frustrate users on airplane mode and waste battery. Exception: background sync with exponential backoff, invisible to the user.

How do I handle form field errors?

Inline under the field for validation ("Enter a valid email"). Screen-level `ErrorCallout` for submit failures (server rejected the form). Do not duplicate the same message in both places.

What about i18n?

Store translation keys in the mapper, not literal strings, before the app ships multiple locales. Keep English strings as defaults for early-stage apps.

Should I include a support link on every error?

Reserve support for `UNKNOWN` or repeated failures after retry. Offline and session-expired errors are user-fixable - support links add noise.

How does this relate to network failure UX?

Network failure UX covers banners, queues, and stale-while-revalidate. User-facing copy is the **wording layer** inside those patterns - same tone whether in a banner or a full-screen error.

Can I use the API error message if it is user-friendly?

Only if you control the API and test the strings. Wrap even trusted messages in a whitelist map - unexpected deploys can leak SQL fragments or internal service names.

What accessibility props matter most?

`accessibilityRole="alert"`, `accessibilityLiveRegion="polite"` (or `assertive` for critical blockers), and a visible focus order that lands on the action button after announcement.

How do global error handlers fit in?

`ErrorUtils.setGlobalHandler` catches unhandled native/JS fatals - pair with a generic "Something went wrong" screen and restart prompt. See [Global Error Handlers](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/error-resilience/global-error-handlers/) for wiring; this page owns the copy.

Dokumen: Essential Libraries Best Practices
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/essential-libraries/best-practices/

# Essential Libraries Best Practices

A condensed summary of the **25 most important essential-library practices** for Expo SDK 57 mobile teams - drawn from every page in this section.

Highlights / Essential Libraries Best Practices

* npx expo install for every native module - SDK 57 matrix, not npm latest
* TanStack Query for server state; Zustand for client UI - never duplicate API caches
* MMKV for hot-path sync KV; AsyncStorage for boot hydration; SQLite for relational
* FlashList after profiling - not preemptive migration of every FlatList
* Reanimated plugin last in Babel; GestureHandlerRootView at root
* One crash reporter with source maps on every EAS production build

1. **`npx expo install` for native modules:** `react-native-reanimated`, `react-native-gesture-handler`, `react-native-mmkv`, `@shopify/flash-list`, and `@sentry/react-native` must match the SDK 57 compatibility table - manual npm pins cause EAS native build failures.
2. **Audit native transitive deps before adopting:** Every native library is autolinking surface, install size, and an SDK upgrade reconciliation item - run `npx expo-doctor` and `npx expo prebuild --dry-run` on dependency PRs.
3. **TanStack Query owns server state:** API lists, profiles, and settings with loading/error/cache belong in Query - not Zustand, Context, or `useEffect` fetches - [@tanstack/react-query](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/essential-libraries/tanstack-react-query/).
4. **Zustand owns client UI state:** Cart badges, theme prefs, onboarding flags, and filter chips - one store per domain with selectors - [zustand](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/essential-libraries/zustand/).
5. **Never duplicate API data in global stores:** If Query already caches `products`, do not mirror them in Zustand - invalidation becomes manual and logout cleanup fails.
6. **Wire mobile Query lifecycle at bootstrap:** `onlineManager` + NetInfo and `focusManager` + AppState in `_layout` - without this, foreground refetch and offline retry behave like web defaults - [TanStack Query](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/state-management/tanstack-query/).
7. **One QueryClient per app:** Create in root layout with `useState(createQueryClient)` - never per screen or per navigator.
8. **Zustand selectors always:** `useStore((s) => s.field)` - bare `useStore()` re-renders on every slice change.
9. **Secrets never in Zustand persist or MMKV plaintext:** Tokens and refresh credentials live in `expo-secure-store` - MMKV holds non-secret prefs and drafts only.
10. **Pick storage by data shape:** AsyncStorage for small JSON at boot; MMKV for synchronous hot-path reads; SQLite for relational offline data - not one store for everything - [react-native-mmkv](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/essential-libraries/react-native-mmkv/).
11. **Version every persisted schema:** `meta:schemaVersion` for MMKV, `PRAGMA user_version` for SQLite, keyed migrations before new shapes reach production.
12. **FlashList after profiling, not by default:** Migrate feeds when Android profiling shows scroll jank - keep FlatList for short settings screens - [@shopify/flash-list](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/essential-libraries/shopify-flash-list/).
13. **`estimatedItemSize` is mandatory on FlashList:** Wrong estimates cause scroll jump and blank gaps - set `minHeight` on rows to match.
14. **Memoize recycled list rows:** `memo` on row components, stable `renderItem` via `useCallback`, props-only state - recycled views expose stale closure bugs.
15. **Install Reanimated and Gesture Handler as a pair:** SDK 57 matrix - `react-native-reanimated` ~4.0.0 and `react-native-gesture-handler` ~2.28.0 - [react-native-reanimated & gesture-handler](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/essential-libraries/react-native-reanimated-and-gesture-handler/).
16. **Babel plugin last:** `react-native-reanimated/plugin` is always the final entry in `babel.config.js` - then `npx expo start --clear`.
17. **GestureHandlerRootView at root:** Wrap `app/_layout.tsx` - pans and sheets fail silently without it.
18. **Import Animated from Reanimated for worklets:** Not from `react-native` - mixing APIs breaks gesture-driven UI.
19. **Rebuild dev client after native library changes:** MMKV, FlashList, Sentry, and Reanimated require EAS or dev client rebuild - Metro restart alone is not enough.
20. **One crash reporter:** `@sentry/react-native` with wizard setup - not `sentry-expo` (deprecated) and not two vendors - [sentry-expo / @sentry/react-native](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/essential-libraries/sentry-expo-sentry-react-native/).
21. **Sentry.init before other imports:** Top of `_layout.tsx`; `Sentry.wrap` on root once - pair with source map upload on every EAS production build.
22. **Set release and dist correctly:** `release` = native version + build; `dist` = OTA update id - aligns crash reports with the binary users run - [Sentry for React Native](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/observability/sentry-for-react-native/).
23. **Sunset unused libraries before SDK upgrades:** Run `npx knip` and `npx depcheck` - dead native modules inflate autolinking and break reconciliation - [Essential Libraries Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/essential-libraries/essential-libraries-basics/).
24. **Dependency PR checklist:** `npx expo install`, `expo-doctor` clean, device test note, no duplicate problem-class library, ADR updated if team default changes.
25. **Logout clears all layers:** `queryClient.clear()`, Zustand reset, MMKV user instance wipe, SecureStore token delete, and SQLite user tables - stale cache is a security defect.

## FAQs

What is the default essential stack for SDK 57?

TanStack Query + NetInfo, Zustand, MMKV (when profiled), FlashList (for feeds), Reanimated 4 + Gesture Handler, and @sentry/react-native - installed via `npx expo install`.

Can I use npm install for any of these?

JS-only: `@tanstack/react-query`, `zustand`. Native modules: always `npx expo install`. Commit lockfile changes with every dependency PR.

When do I need MMKV vs AsyncStorage?

Start with AsyncStorage. Add MMKV when profiling shows async `getItem` on the critical path - composer drafts, feature flags read every mount, Zustand persist flicker.

Do I need FlashList on day one?

No - profile first. Short lists and settings screens stay on FlatList until scroll performance fails on target Android hardware.

Where do I go deeper on each library?

State Management and Observability sections have full cookbooks - Essential Libraries pages are the install-and-defaults cards with links inward.

Dokumen: Essential Libraries Basics
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/essential-libraries/essential-libraries-basics/

# Essential Libraries Basics

10 examples to understand how we **pick**, **pin**, and **sunset** dependencies on mobile - 7 basic and 3 intermediate. These are the team defaults for Expo SDK 57 apps; deeper cookbooks for each library follow in this section.

Highlights / Essential Libraries Basics

* npx expo install pins native modules to the SDK 57 compatibility table - not npm guesses
* Every native dependency is autolinking surface, install size, and an EAS rebuild trigger
* Server state → TanStack Query; client UI → Zustand; never duplicate API caches in global stores
* Sunset unused libraries before SDK upgrades - knip and depcheck catch dead weight early
* ADR or team defaults beat per-feature library roulette - one list stack, one crash reporter
* Lockfile + expo-doctor in CI catches version skew before expensive native builds

## Prerequisites

Start from a pinned SDK 57 project. Essential libraries are **curated defaults** - not every npm package that solves a problem belongs in a shipping app.

```bash
npx create-expo-app@latest LibBasics --template default@sdk-57
cd LibBasics
npx expo install @tanstack/react-query @react-native-community/netinfo zustand
npx expo-doctor
```

Confirm the baseline pin before adding native modules:

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "expo": "~57.0.4",
    "react": "19.2.3",
    "react-native": "0.86.0"
  }
}
```

> **Tooling:** These examples target **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4), **React Native 0.86.0**, and **React 19.2.3**. Native modules require a **development build** or EAS build - not stock Expo Go alone when the package ships custom native code.

---

## Basic Examples

### 1. Pick by Problem Class - Not by GitHub Stars

Mobile dependency decisions start with **what kind of state or I/O** you need - not trending repos.

```text
┌────────────────────┬─────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────┐
│ Problem            │ Default library         │ Do not use for           │
├────────────────────┼─────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────┤
│ API / server cache │ @tanstack/react-query   │ Cart badge, theme toggle │
│ Global client UI   │ zustand                 │ Product catalog rows     │
│ Fast local KV      │ react-native-mmkv       │ Relational offline data  │
│ Long lists         │ @shopify/flash-list     │ 8-row settings screen    │
│ Gestures / motion  │ Reanimated 4 + RNGH     │ One-shot 200ms fade      │
│ Crash reporting    │ @sentry/react-native    │ Console.log in prod      │
└────────────────────┴─────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────┘
```

* **One library per problem class** - two list libraries or two global stores creates migration debt
* **Prefer Expo-first packages** - `npx expo install` resolves versions; fewer native build surprises
* Document exceptions in an ADR - not in a Slack thread nobody finds during onboarding

> **Related:** [State Management Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/state-management/state-management-basics/) - server vs client split

---

### 2. Pin with `npx expo install` - Not Raw npm

Expo maintains a **compatibility matrix** per SDK. Hand-pinning `react-native-reanimated@latest` breaks EAS builds when the native ABI does not match RN 0.86.

```bash
# Correct - resolves SDK 57-compatible version
npx expo install react-native-reanimated react-native-gesture-handler
 
# Risky for native modules - may install incompatible semver
npm install react-native-reanimated
```

```bash
# Verify after any dependency change
npx expo-doctor
```

* **`npx expo install`** writes the tilde-pinned range Expo tested against your SDK
* **JS-only packages** (`zod`, `@tanstack/react-query`, `zustand`) can use `npm install` - no native bridge
* Run **`expo-doctor`** on release and nightly CI - catches skew before `eas build`
* Commit **lockfile changes** with the dependency PR - reproducible installs on EAS

> **Related:** [Expo SDK Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-sdk/expo-sdk-basics/) - when `npm install` is acceptable

---

### 3. Audit Native Transitive Deps Before Adopting

Every library with native code pulls in **autolinking**, **config plugins**, and **store binary size**. Read the install docs before merging.

```bash
# After adding a candidate library
npx expo install react-native-mmkv
npx expo prebuild --dry-run   # surfaces config plugin changes
npx expo-doctor
```

Checklist before merge:

| Question | Pass | Fail → defer or find alternative |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Works in Expo managed workflow? | Yes | Requires bare fork |
| Needs config plugin in `app.config`? | Documented | Surprise native diff |
| Requires dev client rebuild? | Planned in sprint | Blocked on Expo Go-only QA |
| Duplicates existing library? | No overlap | Consolidate first |

* **MMKV, FlashList, Sentry, Reanimated** all require a dev build or EAS binary - plan rebuild time
* `expo prebuild --dry-run` previews native project changes without writing `ios/` / `android/`
* Count **total native modules** - each one is an SDK upgrade reconciliation item

> **Related:** [Dead Code & Dependency Analysis](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/dead-code-and-dependency-analysis/) - keep the graph lean

---

### 4. Lock the Team Default Stack in package.json

Pin the **essential stack** in one PR during project bootstrap so every feature branch inherits the same versions.

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "expo": "~57.0.4",
    "react": "19.2.3",
    "react-native": "0.86.0",
    "@tanstack/react-query": "^5.0.0",
    "zustand": "^5.0.0",
    "react-native-reanimated": "~4.0.0",
    "react-native-gesture-handler": "~2.28.0",
    "@sentry/react-native": "^6.0.0"
  }
}
```

Native list/storage pins (`@shopify/flash-list`, `react-native-mmkv`, `@react-native-community/netinfo`) are written by `npx expo install` - do not hand-edit those ranges.

```bash
npx expo install @tanstack/react-query @react-native-community/netinfo zustand \
  @shopify/flash-list react-native-mmkv react-native-reanimated \
  react-native-gesture-handler @sentry/react-native
```

* Let **`npx expo install`** set exact compatible ranges - do not hand-edit native pins
* **One crash reporter** - Sentry or an enterprise alternative, never both
* **One list implementation** per app - FlashList for feeds; FlatList for short static screens is fine
* Document the stack in README or ADR - onboarding copies `package.json`, not tribal knowledge

---

### 5. Separate Server State from Client State

The most expensive library mistake is **duplicating API data** in Zustand or Context when TanStack Query already owns it.

```tsx
// ❌ Anti-pattern - manual fetch + global store for server data
const useProductStore = create((set) => ({
  products: [] as Product[],
  load: async () => {
    const res = await fetch("/products");
    set({ products: await res.json() });
  },
}));
 
// ✅ Pattern - Query owns server cache; Zustand owns UI-only flags
const { data: products } = useQuery({ queryKey: ["products"], queryFn: fetchProducts });
const filter = useFilterStore((s) => s.category); // client-only
```

* **TanStack Query** - loading, error, stale time, dedupe, background refetch, persistence
* **Zustand** - cart, onboarding flags, composer drafts, filter chips - synchronous client UI
* **Never** store JWTs or refresh tokens in Zustand persist - use `expo-secure-store`
* See [@tanstack/react-query](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/essential-libraries/tanstack-react-query/) and [zustand](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/essential-libraries/zustand/) cookbooks

> **Related:** [TanStack Query](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/state-management/tanstack-query/) - full server-state deep dive

---

### 6. Know When AsyncStorage Is Enough - Before MMKV

Not every app needs `react-native-mmkv` on day one. Start with AsyncStorage; upgrade when profiling proves sync reads matter.

```text
Storage pick order:
1. In-memory React state / Query cache     → ephemeral
2. @react-native-async-storage/async-storage → small JSON, boot hydration
3. react-native-mmkv                       → hot-path sync reads every frame
4. expo-sqlite                             → relational rows, migrations, queries
5. expo-secure-store                       → tokens, secrets
```

```bash
npx expo install @react-native-async-storage/async-storage
# Add MMKV only after React DevTools Profiler shows storage await on critical path
npx expo install react-native-mmkv
```

* **AsyncStorage** is async - `await getItem` on every render causes jank
* **MMKV** is synchronous - ideal for Zustand persist and feature flags read every mount
* **MMKV is not a database** - no SQL, no joins; use SQLite for offline relational data
* MMKV requires a **dev build** - not available in stock Expo Go

> **Related:** [react-native-mmkv](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/essential-libraries/react-native-mmkv/) - fast KV cookbook

---

### 7. List Library: FlatList First, FlashList When Profiled

`@shopify/flash-list` is a performance upgrade - not a day-one requirement for every screen.

```tsx
// Short settings list - FlatList is fine
import { FlatList } from "react-native";
 
// Image-heavy feed with scroll jank on Android - migrate
import { FlashList } from "@shopify/flash-list";
```

Migration trigger checklist:

* Profiler shows **frame drops** during fast flick scroll on a mid-range Android device
* List has **50+ rows** with images or variable content
* `windowSize` tuning on FlatList did not fix blank flashes

```bash
npx expo install @shopify/flash-list
```

* Do not migrate **every** `FlatList` preemptively - estimate tuning has a cost
* See [@shopify/flash-list](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/essential-libraries/shopify-flash-list/) for the full migration checklist

> **Related:** [FlashList vs FlatList](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/lists-scrolling/flashlist-vs-flatlist/) - trade-offs before adopting

---

## Intermediate Examples

### 8. Sunset a Library - Remove Before SDK Upgrade

Sunsetting is a **planned removal** - not letting a package rot in `package.json` until the upgrade explodes.

```bash
# 1. Confirm zero imports
npx knip
npx depcheck
 
# 2. Remove package and lockfile entry
npm uninstall legacy-state-library
 
# 3. Remove native config plugin from app.config.ts if present
# 4. Rebuild dev client - autolinking must drop the native module
eas build --profile development --platform all
 
# 5. Verify on device
npx expo-doctor
```

```ts
// app.config.ts - remove plugin stanza when sunsetting
export default {
  plugins: [
    // ["legacy-library-expo-plugin"],  ← delete
    "expo-router",
  ],
};
```

* **Sunset in a dedicated PR** - easier to bisect than bundled with a feature
* Run **knip** before removal - orphaned files often hide the last import
* **Rebuild native** after removing any package with native code - stale dev clients crash mysteriously
* Document **why** it was removed in the PR description - prevents re-introduction next quarter

> **Related:** [Dead Code & Dependency Analysis](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/dead-code-and-dependency-analysis/)

---

### 9. Dependency PR Review Template

Standardize review questions so every new library gets the same scrutiny.

```markdown
## Dependency PR: @shopify/flash-list
 
- [ ] Problem class documented (list performance - feed screen)
- [ ] Installed with `npx expo install`
- [ ] `npx expo-doctor` clean
- [ ] Native rebuild scheduled / completed
- [ ] No duplicate library (FlatList remains for settings)
- [ ] Bundle impact noted (source size + native)
- [ ] Test plan on physical Android device
- [ ] ADR updated if this changes team default
```

```yaml
# .github/workflows/pr-checks.yml - add on dependency-label PRs
- name: Expo doctor
  if: contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'dependencies')
  run: npx expo-doctor
```

* Label dependency PRs **`dependencies`** - triggers extra CI steps
* **Block merge** if `expo-doctor` fails - version skew is cheaper to fix in PR than in EAS queue
* Require **device test note** for native modules - simulators miss autolinking failures
* Link to the **cookbook** in this section when adopting a standard library

---

### 10. SDK Upgrade Reconciliation Pass

SDK bumps are when unpinned or duplicate libraries hurt most. Run a reconciliation pass **before** merging the SDK PR.

```bash
# Upgrade workflow (simplified)
npx expo install expo@~57.0.4 --fix
npx expo-doctor
npx knip
npm run typecheck && npm test
 
# Reinstall essential native stack against new matrix
npx expo install react-native-reanimated react-native-gesture-handler \
  react-native-mmkv @shopify/flash-list @sentry/react-native
 
eas build --profile preview --platform all
```

| Step | Goal |
| --- | --- |
| `expo install --fix` | Align all `expo-*` modules to SDK 57 |
| `expo-doctor` | Catch incompatible peer deps |
| `knip` | Remove libraries that died during the last release cycle |
| Preview EAS build | Validate native compile before production tag |
| Re-read Babel config | Reanimated plugin must stay **last** |

* **Do not upgrade SDK and add new libraries in one PR** - bisect failures
* Check **config plugin changelogs** - Sentry and notifications plugins move between SDKs
* Re-run **Maestro smoke** on preview binary - gestures and lists break silently on native bumps

> **Related:** [Upgrading Expo SDK Versions](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-platform/upgrading-expo-sdk-versions/)

---

## Anti-Patterns

| Anti-pattern | Why it fails |
| --- | --- |
| `npm install` every native module | Version skew → EAS native compile errors |
| Redux + Zustand + Context for same cart | Three sources of truth; logout cleanup nightmare |
| FlashList everywhere on day one | Estimate tuning cost with no measurable gain |
| Keeping unused native modules "just in case" | Autolinking bloat; SDK upgrade pain |
| Skipping dev client rebuild after native add | "Works in Metro" but crashes on device |
| Two crash reporters | Duplicate events; double SDK overhead |

---

## FAQs

Which libraries are in the Essential Libraries section?

TanStack Query, Zustand, MMKV, FlashList, Reanimated + Gesture Handler, and Sentry - the default production stack for Expo SDK 57 apps in this docs site.

Can I use npm install for @tanstack/react-query?

Yes - it is JS-only with no Expo native module. Still pin a semver range and commit the lockfile. For any package Expo documents in the SDK reference, prefer `npx expo install`.

How many global stores should I have?

One Zustand store per **domain** (cart, preferences, onboarding) - not one mega-store. See [zustand](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/essential-libraries/zustand/).

When do I need a new EAS build after adding a library?

Whenever the package adds **native code** or a **config plugin** - MMKV, FlashList, Sentry, Reanimated. JS-only packages need Metro restart only.

How do I justify a non-default library to the team?

Write a short ADR: problem, alternatives considered, native cost, sunset plan. Link it from the dependency PR.

## [Essential Libraries Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/essential-libraries/essential-libraries-basics/)

* npx expo install pins native modules to the SDK 57 compatibility table - not npm guesses
* Every native dependency is autolinking surface, install size, and an EAS rebuild trigger
* Server state → TanStack Query; client UI → Zustand; never duplicate API caches in global stores
* Sunset unused libraries before SDK upgrades - knip and depcheck catch dead weight early
* ADR or team defaults beat per-feature library roulette - one list stack, one crash reporter
* Lockfile + expo-doctor in CI catches version skew before expensive native builds

## [@tanstack/react-query](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/essential-libraries/tanstack-react-query/)

* QueryClient defaults: staleTime 30s, gcTime 5min, retry 2 - tuned for mobile LTE
* Wire onlineManager to NetInfo and focusManager to AppState at bootstrap
* One QueryClient per app - create in \_layout, never per screen
* Mutations invalidate related query keys - not manual Zustand cache copies
* JS-only install - npx expo install @tanstack/react-query plus NetInfo
* Full patterns in state-management/tanstack-query - this page is the defaults card

## [zustand](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/essential-libraries/zustand/)

* No Provider tree - import useStore hook anywhere in the JS bundle
* Selectors prevent list screens from re-rendering on unrelated slice updates
* One store per domain: cart, preferences, onboarding flags
* persist + MMKV or AsyncStorage for non-secret preferences only
* Never store API responses - TanStack Query owns server cache
* Full patterns in state-management/zustand - this page is the minimal cookbook

## [react-native-mmkv](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/essential-libraries/react-native-mmkv/)

* Synchronous mmap reads - orders of magnitude faster than AsyncStorage await
* Ideal for feature flags, drafts, Zustand persist on hot paths
* Requires a development build - not available in stock Expo Go
* Multiple named instances isolate domains: app, cache, experiments
* Not a database - no queries; use expo-sqlite for relational offline data
* Secrets need encryption key from expo-secure-store

## [@shopify/flash-list](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/essential-libraries/shopify-flash-list/)

* estimatedItemSize is required - wrong estimates cause scroll jump and blank gaps
* View recycling demands memoized rows with props-only state
* Migration: install, swap import, add estimate, audit variable heights
* drawDistance tunes pre-render distance ahead of the viewport
* FlatList remains fine for short settings screens - profile before migrating
* Trade-offs and tuning in lists-scrolling/flashlist-vs-flatlist

## [react-native-reanimated & gesture-handler](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/essential-libraries/react-native-reanimated-and-gesture-handler/)

* SDK 57 matrix: react-native-reanimated ~4.0.0, gesture-handler ~2.28.0
* Install both together with npx expo install - never hand-pin native versions
* react-native-reanimated/plugin must be the last babel.config.js plugin
* GestureHandlerRootView wraps the root layout - required for pans and sheets
* Import Animated from react-native-reanimated for worklet components
* Deep patterns in animations-gestures section - this page is install + matrix

## [sentry-expo / @sentry/react-native](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/essential-libraries/sentry-expo-sentry-react-native/)

* Initialize Sentry before other app imports in \_layout or index.js
* Upload source maps on every EAS production build - Hermes stacks need symbolication
* Set release to native version+build and dist to OTA update id when applicable
* Sentry.wrap on root component - one wrap, not duplicate captureException
* Wizard configures Metro plugin and EAS build hooks for SDK 57
* Full observability patterns in sentry-for-react-native deep guide

## [Essential Libraries Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/essential-libraries/best-practices/)

* npx expo install for every native module - SDK 57 matrix, not npm latest
* TanStack Query for server state; Zustand for client UI - never duplicate API caches
* MMKV for hot-path sync KV; AsyncStorage for boot hydration; SQLite for relational
* FlashList after profiling - not preemptive migration of every FlatList
* Reanimated plugin last in Babel; GestureHandlerRootView at root
* One crash reporter with source maps on every EAS production build

Dokumen: react-native-mmkv
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/essential-libraries/react-native-mmkv/

# react-native-mmkv

Fast storage when AsyncStorage is too slow. `react-native-mmkv` is a **memory-mapped synchronous KV store** - ideal for feature flags, composer drafts, and Zustand persist middleware on screens that read storage every render. Reach for it when profiling shows AsyncStorage `await` on the critical path.

Highlights / react-native-mmkv

* Synchronous mmap reads - orders of magnitude faster than AsyncStorage await
* Ideal for feature flags, drafts, Zustand persist on hot paths
* Requires a development build - not available in stock Expo Go
* Multiple named instances isolate domains: app, cache, experiments
* Not a database - no queries; use expo-sqlite for relational offline data
* Secrets need encryption key from expo-secure-store

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
npx expo install react-native-mmkv
```

```ts
// src/storage/mmkv.ts
import { MMKV } from "react-native-mmkv";
 
export const storage = new MMKV({ id: "app-storage" });
export const cacheStorage = new MMKV({ id: "hot-cache" });
 
export function getJson<T>(key: string, fallback: T, instance = storage): T {
  const raw = instance.getString(key);
  if (!raw) return fallback;
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw) as T;
  } catch {
    return fallback;
  }
}
 
export function setJson(key: string, value: unknown, instance = storage) {
  instance.set(key, JSON.stringify(value));
}
```

```ts
// src/stores/draftStore.ts - Zustand persist adapter
import { create } from "zustand";
import { createJSONStorage, persist, type StateStorage } from "zustand/middleware";
import { storage } from "@/storage/mmkv";
 
const mmkvStorage: StateStorage = {
  getItem: (name) => storage.getString(name) ?? null,
  setItem: (name, value) => { storage.set(name, value); },
  removeItem: (name) => { storage.delete(name); },
};
 
type DraftStore = { text: string; setText: (text: string) => void };
 
export const useDraftStore = create<DraftStore>()(
  persist(
    (set) => ({
      text: "",
      setText: (text) => set({ text }),
    }),
    { name: "composer-draft", storage: createJSONStorage(() => mmkvStorage) }
  )
);
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Synchronous read on every keystroke or animation frame.
* Zustand persist where AsyncStorage hydration flickers empty state.
* Small encrypted blobs with key from SecureStore.
* Replacing repeated `AsyncStorage.getItem` in list `renderItem` paths.

**When to avoid:**

* Relational data, full-text search, or server sync queues → `expo-sqlite`.
* Secrets without encryption wrapper → `expo-secure-store`.
* Expo Go-only workflows without a dev build.

## Working Example

```bash
npx expo install react-native-mmkv expo-secure-store
```

```ts
// src/storage/flags.ts
import { getJson, setJson, storage } from "./mmkv";
 
export type FeatureFlags = {
  offlineChecklist: boolean;
  newComposer: boolean;
};
 
const FLAGS_KEY = "flags:v1";
const DEFAULTS: FeatureFlags = { offlineChecklist: true, newComposer: false };
 
export function readFlags(): FeatureFlags {
  return getJson(FLAGS_KEY, DEFAULTS);
}
 
export function writeFlags(flags: FeatureFlags) {
  setJson(FLAGS_KEY, flags);
}
 
// Synchronous read in render - no await, no flash
export function isNewComposerEnabled(): boolean {
  return readFlags().newComposer;
}
```

```tsx
// src/components/Composer.tsx
import { TextInput } from "react-native";
import { useDraftStore } from "@/stores/draftStore";
 
export function Composer() {
  const text = useDraftStore((s) => s.text);
  const setText = useDraftStore((s) => s.setText);
 
  return (
    <TextInput
      value={text}
      onChangeText={setText}
      placeholder="Draft saves instantly"
      multiline
    />
  );
}
```

```ts
// src/storage/migrations.ts - MMKV has no PRAGMA; use explicit version keys
import { storage } from "./mmkv";
 
const VERSION_KEY = "meta:schemaVersion";
const CURRENT_VERSION = 2;
 
export function runMmkvMigrations() {
  const version = storage.getNumber(VERSION_KEY) ?? 0;
 
  if (version < 1) {
    const legacy = storage.getString("flags");
    if (legacy) {
      storage.set("flags:v1", legacy);
      storage.delete("flags");
    }
    storage.set(VERSION_KEY, 1);
  }
 
  if (version < 2) {
    const raw = storage.getString("flags:v1");
    if (raw) {
      const parsed = JSON.parse(raw);
      storage.set("flags:v1", JSON.stringify({ ...parsed, newComposer: false }));
    }
    storage.set(VERSION_KEY, 2);
  }
}
```

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx (excerpt) - run migrations before UI reads flags
import { useEffect } from "react";
import { runMmkvMigrations } from "@/storage/migrations";
 
export default function RootLayout() {
  useEffect(() => {
    runMmkvMigrations();
  }, []);
 
  return /* routes */;
}
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* **`getJson` / `setJson`** - typed helpers avoid parse boilerplate in every caller.
* **Zustand + MMKV** - rehydrates synchronously; no empty-state flash after persist.
* **Feature flags** - read synchronously in render without `useEffect` hydration.
* **Explicit migrations** - version key + incremental transforms; no SQL migrations.
* **Named instances** - `app-storage` vs `hot-cache` isolate eviction domains.

## Deep Dive

### Storage Decision Matrix

| Store | Latency | Shape | Expo Go |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AsyncStorage | Async | Small JSON blobs | Yes |
| MMKV | Sync | Key-value strings/numbers/bools | No - dev build |
| expo-sqlite | Async SQL | Relational rows | Dev build |
| expo-secure-store | Async | Secrets | Yes (limited) |

### Optional Encryption

```ts
import * as SecureStore from "expo-secure-store";
import { MMKV } from "react-native-mmkv";
 
const KEY_ID = "mmkv-encryption-key";
 
export async function createSecureStorage(): Promise<MMKV> {
  let key = await SecureStore.getItemAsync(KEY_ID);
  if (!key) {
    key = crypto.randomUUID();
    await SecureStore.setItemAsync(KEY_ID, key);
  }
  return new MMKV({ id: "user-secure", encryptionKey: key });
}
```

Encryption key lives in SecureStore; MMKV holds encrypted blobs - not raw tokens in plaintext.

### Logout

```ts
import { storage, cacheStorage } from "@/storage/mmkv";
 
export function clearUserMmkv() {
  storage.clearAll();
  cacheStorage.clearAll();
  // Also: queryClient.clear(), SecureStore.deleteItemAsync for tokens
}
```

## Gotchas

* **Using MMKV for large catalogs** - Multi-MB JSON blocks the JS thread on parse. **Fix:** SQLite or TanStack Query persistence with eviction.
* **Skipping migrations** - Renamed keys strand users on old shapes. **Fix:** `meta:schemaVersion` + incremental migration functions.
* **Storing JWTs unencrypted** - MMKV is fast plaintext storage. **Fix:** SecureStore for tokens; MMKV for non-secret prefs only.
* **Testing in Expo Go** - Native module missing. **Fix:** `eas build --profile development` or Expo dev client.
* **Reading MMKV in every list row without memoization** - Sync is fast but parse still costs. **Fix:** Read once at screen level; pass props down.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MMKV | Hot-path sync KV | Relational queries |
| AsyncStorage | Infrequent boot hydration | Every-frame reads |
| expo-sqlite | Offline relational data | Single boolean flag |
| TanStack Query persist | Server cache offline reads | UI-only draft text |
| SecureStore | Tokens, small secrets | Feature flag JSON |

## FAQs

How do I install MMKV on Expo SDK 57?

```bash
npx expo install react-native-mmkv
eas build --profile development --platform all
```

Rebuild the dev client after install - autolinking adds the native module.

MMKV vs AsyncStorage for Zustand persist?

AsyncStorage is fine for settings loaded once at boot. MMKV when users see a flash of empty state before async rehydration completes.

Can I use MMKV in Expo Go?

No - it requires custom native code. Use a development build.

Where is the full MMKV guide?

[MMKV & High-Performance KV](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/data-offline/mmkv-and-high-performance-kv/) - encryption bootstrap, multi-instance patterns, and Zustand integration.

Does MMKV need a config plugin?

Standard Expo autolinking handles install for SDK 57 - no custom plugin in most apps. Run `npx expo-doctor` after adding.

# react-native-reanimated & gesture-handler

Version matrix tied to Expo SDK 57. Reanimated 4 runs animations on the **UI thread**; Gesture Handler moves touch recognition to native so pans stay at **60fps**. Install them as a pair. For shared values, springs, and composed gestures, see [react-native-reanimated 4](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/react-native-reanimated-4/) and [react-native-gesture-handler](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/react-native-gesture-handler/).

Highlights / react-native-reanimated & gesture-handler

* SDK 57 matrix: react-native-reanimated ~4.0.0, gesture-handler ~2.28.0
* Install both together with npx expo install - never hand-pin native versions
* react-native-reanimated/plugin must be the last babel.config.js plugin
* GestureHandlerRootView wraps the root layout - required for pans and sheets
* Import Animated from react-native-reanimated for worklet components
* Deep patterns in animations-gestures section - this page is install + matrix

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

### SDK 57 Version Matrix

| Package | SDK 57 pin | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `react-native-reanimated` | `~4.0.0` | Reanimated 4 - New Architecture baseline |
| `react-native-gesture-handler` | `~2.28.0` | Install alongside Reanimated |
| `react` | `19.2.3` | Bundled with Expo SDK 57 |
| `react-native` | `0.86.0` | Fabric + Hermes default |

```bash
npx expo install react-native-reanimated react-native-gesture-handler
npx expo-doctor
```

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "expo": "~57.0.4",

```

```js
// babel.config.js - plugin MUST be last
module.exports = function (api) {
  api.cache(true);
  return {
    presets: ["babel-preset-expo"],

  };

```

```tsx

  return (

  );
}
```

```bash
# After install or babel change - clear Metro cache

```

**When to reach for this:**

* Finger-driven pans, pinches, draggable sheets, and swipe actions.
* Animations that must stay smooth during list scroll or heavy JS work.
* Replacing `PanResponder` or JS-thread `Animated` for interactive UI.

## Working Example

Draggable card - shared values on the UI thread, spring on release.

```tsx
// components/draggable-card.tsx
import { StyleSheet, Text } from "react-native";
import { Gesture, GestureDetector } from "react-native-gesture-handler";
import Animated, {
  useAnimatedStyle,
  useSharedValue,
  withSpring,
} from "react-native-reanimated";
 
const SNAP_BACK = { damping: 18, stiffness: 220 };
 
export function DraggableCard({ title }: { title: string }) {
  const translateX = useSharedValue(0);
  const translateY = useSharedValue(0);
 
  const pan = Gesture.Pan()
    .onUpdate((e) => {
      translateX.value = e.translationX;
      translateY.value = e.translationY;
    })
    .onEnd(() => {
      translateX.value = withSpring(0, SNAP_BACK);
      translateY.value = withSpring(0, SNAP_BACK);
    });
 
  const style = useAnimatedStyle(() => ({
    transform: [
      { translateX: translateX.value },
      { translateY: translateY.value },
    ],
  }));
 
  return (
    <GestureDetector gesture={pan}>
      <Animated.View style={[styles.card, style]}>
        <Text>{title}</Text>
      </Animated.View>
    </GestureDetector>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  card: {
    padding: 20,
    borderRadius: 12,
    backgroundColor: "#f0fdf4",
    margin: 16,
  },
});
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* **`useSharedValue`** - updates on UI thread without React re-renders.
* **`Gesture.Pan()`** - native touch recognition via Gesture Handler.
* **`useAnimatedStyle`** - worklet reads shared values every frame.
* **`withSpring` on end** - physics-based snap-back.
* **`GestureDetector` + Reanimated `Animated.View`** - the standard SDK 57 pairing.

## Deep Dive

### Install Verification Checklist

```markdown
## Reanimated + RNGH install verification
 
- [ ] npx expo install react-native-reanimated react-native-gesture-handler
- [ ] package.json shows ~4.0.0 and ~2.28.0 (via expo install)
- [ ] babel.config.js - reanimated/plugin is LAST plugin
- [ ] GestureHandlerRootView wraps root layout
- [ ] npx expo start --clear after babel change
- [ ] eas build --profile development after native version bump
- [ ] Pan gesture tested on physical device (not just simulator)
- [ ] npx expo-doctor passes
```

### Rebuild Triggers

| Change | Metro restart | Dev client / EAS rebuild |
| --- | --- | --- |
| JS-only animation code | Yes | No |
| Babel plugin added/changed | `--clear` required | No |
| Native version bump | `--clear` | **Yes** |
| SDK upgrade | `--clear` | **Yes** |

### Import Rules

```tsx
// ✅ Worklet components and styles
import Animated, { useAnimatedStyle, useSharedValue } from "react-native-reanimated";
 
// ❌ Do not mix for gesture-driven UI
import { Animated } from "react-native";
```

### Scroll + Gesture Conflicts

When nested scroll steals pans, import scrollables from Gesture Handler for the inner rail:

```tsx
import { ScrollView } from "react-native-gesture-handler";
```

See [Gesture Conflict Resolution](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/gesture-conflict-resolution/).

## Gotchas

* **Babel plugin not last** - Worklets fail; animations stutter on JS thread. **Fix:** Move `react-native-reanimated/plugin` to end of `plugins`; `npx expo start --clear`.
* **Hand-pinning versions** - `npm install react-native-reanimated@latest` breaks native ABI. **Fix:** Always `npx expo install`.
* **Missing GestureHandlerRootView** - Gestures never fire. **Fix:** Wrap `app/_layout.tsx` root.
* **Reading shared values in React render** - `translateX.value` in JSX does not subscribe. **Fix:** Only read inside `useAnimatedStyle`.
* **Testing in stale Expo Go** - Old client lacks native bits after upgrade. **Fix:** Rebuild dev client matching SDK 57.
* **Calling setState inside useAnimatedStyle** - Worklet thread errors. **Fix:** `runOnJS(setState)` from gesture `onEnd` only.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reanimated 4 + RNGH | Gestures, 60fps interactive UI | One-shot 200ms fade |
| RN `Animated` API | Simple opacity on static screens | Finger-following drags |
| `PanResponder` | Legacy maintenance | New gesture code on SDK 57 |
| Lottie | Designer vector loops | Interactive draggable UI |

## FAQs

What versions does Expo SDK 57 pin?

`react-native-reanimated` **~4.0.0** and `react-native-gesture-handler` **~2.28.0**. Run `npx expo install` - do not copy versions from older blog posts.

Do I need both packages?

Install both together. Gesture Handler is required for `Gesture.Pan` and native scroll conflicts; Reanimated drives UI-thread values from gesture callbacks.

Where does the Babel plugin go?

Last entry in `babel.config.js` `plugins` array - after all other plugins. Restart Metro with `--clear`.

Does Reanimated require New Architecture?

SDK 57 projects increasingly run Fabric + Hermes by default. Reanimated 4 targets that stack.

Where are the full animation guides?

[react-native-reanimated 4](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/react-native-reanimated-4/) and [react-native-gesture-handler](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/react-native-gesture-handler/).
