Dokumen: Environments & EAS Environment Variables
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-platform/environments-and-eas-environment-variables/

# Environments & EAS Environment Variables

Separate dev, staging, and production configuration without committing secrets - using local `.env` files for development and EAS environment variables for cloud builds, updates, and workflows.

Highlights / Environments & EAS Environment Variables

* EAS provides three built-in environments: development, preview, and production
* Map eas.json build profiles to EAS environments with the `environment` field
* Only `EXPO\_PUBLIC\_` variables are safe to embed in client JavaScript - treat them as public
* `eas env:pull` syncs cloud variables to `.env.local` for local dev without committing secrets
* SDK 55+ requires `--environment` on `eas update` so OTA bundles match build-time config
* Secret visibility variables are for build-time tooling (NPM tokens), not client-side API keys

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```json
// eas.json - wire each build profile to an EAS environment
{
  "build": {
    "development": {
      "developmentClient": true,
      "distribution": "internal",
      "environment": "development"
    },
    "preview": {
      "distribution": "internal",
      "environment": "preview"
    },
    "production": {
      "distribution": "store",
      "environment": "production"
    }
  }
}
```

```bash
# Create cloud variables (repeat per environment)
eas env:create --name EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL \
  --value https://api.staging.example.com \
  --environment preview \
  --visibility plaintext
 
# Pull preview vars locally (writes .env.local - keep gitignored)
eas env:pull --environment preview
 
# Publish an OTA update using the same environment as the build
eas update --environment production --message "Hotfix auth redirect"
```

```tsx
// src/config.ts - only EXPO_PUBLIC_ vars are inlined into the bundle
export const config = {
  apiUrl: process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL ?? "http://localhost:3000",
  appEnv: process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_APP_ENV ?? "development",
} as const;
```

**When to reach for this:**

* You ship **multiple app variants** (dev client, internal QA, App Store) that need different API endpoints or bundle identifiers.
* Your team runs **EAS Build or EAS Update** and cannot rely on uncommitted local `.env` files on remote runners.
* You need **role-based visibility** - plaintext for public config, sensitive for obfuscated logs, secret for NPM tokens and signing keys.
* You want **one source of truth** so a preview build and a preview OTA update resolve the same `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` values.

## Working Example

```tsx
// app.config.ts - branch native config per environment without hardcoding secrets
import type { ExpoConfig } from "expo/config";
 
const APP_ENV = process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_APP_ENV ?? "development";
 
const bundleIds: Record<string, string> = {
  development: "com.example.myapp.dev",
  preview: "com.example.myapp.staging",
  production: "com.example.myapp",
};
 
const apiUrls: Record<string, string> = {
  development: "http://localhost:3000",
  preview: "https://api.staging.example.com",
  production: "https://api.example.com",
};
 
const config: ExpoConfig = {
  name: APP_ENV === "production" ? "My App" : `My App (${APP_ENV})`,
  slug: "my-app",
  version: "1.0.0",
  ios: {
    bundleIdentifier: bundleIds[APP_ENV] ?? bundleIds.development,
  },
  android: {
    package: bundleIds[APP_ENV] ?? bundleIds.development,
  },
  extra: {
    appEnv: APP_ENV,
    apiUrl: process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL ?? apiUrls[APP_ENV],
    eas: {
      projectId: "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000",
    },
  },
};
 
export default config;
```

```tsx
// App.tsx - read runtime config from inlined public vars and app.config extra
import Constants from "expo-constants";
import { StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
export default function App() {
  const apiUrl =
    process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL ??
    (Constants.expoConfig?.extra?.apiUrl as string | undefined) ??
    "not configured";
 
  const appEnv =
    process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_APP_ENV ??
    (Constants.expoConfig?.extra?.appEnv as string | undefined) ??
    "unknown";
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.container}>
      <Text style={styles.title}>Environment: {appEnv}</Text>
      <Text style={styles.body}>API: {apiUrl}</Text>
      <Text style={styles.hint}>
        EAS builds inject EXPO_PUBLIC_* at bundle time. Secrets never appear here.
      </Text>
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  container: { flex: 1, justifyContent: "center", padding: 24, gap: 8 },
  title: { fontSize: 20, fontWeight: "700" },
  body: { fontSize: 15, color: "#374151" },
  hint: { fontSize: 13, color: "#6b7280", marginTop: 12 },
});
```

```bash
# .gitignore - never commit local overrides or pulled secrets
.env*.local
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* Mapping **EAS environments** (`development`, `preview`, `production`) to `eas.json` build profiles.
* Using **`EXPO_PUBLIC_*`** for client-safe values that Metro inlines at bundle time.
* Keeping **bundle identifiers and display names** environment-specific via `app.config.ts`.
* Separating **build-time secrets** (NPM tokens, signing keys) from anything referenced in JavaScript.

## Deep Dive

### How It Works

* **Local development:** Expo CLI loads `.env`, `.env.local`, and other standard dotenv files. Variables prefixed with `EXPO_PUBLIC_` are statically replaced in your source during bundling.
* **EAS Build:** When `environment` is set on a build profile, EAS injects that environment's variables into the build worker. Plaintext and sensitive variables are available when resolving `app.config.ts`; secret variables are available only on the server during the job.
* **EAS Update (SDK 55+):** `eas update --environment <name>` is **required**. Only variables from that EAS environment are used - local `.env` files are ignored, keeping OTA bundles aligned with store builds.
* **Scope:** Variables can be **project-wide** (one app) or **account-wide** (shared across apps in an organization).

### EAS Environment Mapping

| EAS environment | Typical use | `eas.json` signal (if `environment` omitted) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `development` | Dev client, local API, debug tooling | `developmentClient: true` |
| `preview` | Internal QA, staging API, TestFlight/Play internal | Everything else (default fallback) |
| `production` | App Store / Play Store releases | `distribution: "store"` |

Explicit `environment` fields are recommended - auto-detection is convenient but easy to misconfigure when profiles share similar flags.

### Visibility Settings

| Visibility | Readable in dashboard/CLI | In build logs | Client bundle |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Plain text | Yes | Yes | Only if referenced as `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` |
| Sensitive | Toggle on dashboard | Obfuscated | Only if referenced as `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` |
| Secret | No (server-only) | Obfuscated | **Never** - build-time tooling only |

> Anything embedded in client JavaScript is extractable from the compiled app. Use secrets for `NPM_TOKEN`, `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`, and similar build-time values - not for "private" API keys shipped to users.

### Built-in EAS Build Variables

These are set automatically on EAS Build workers (not part of your project environments):

| Variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `EAS_BUILD` | `true` |
| `EAS_BUILD_PROFILE` | Profile name from `eas.json` |
| `EAS_BUILD_PLATFORM` | `android` or `ios` |
| `EAS_BUILD_ID` | Unique build UUID |
| `EAS_BUILD_PROJECT_ID` | Linked EAS project ID |

Use `EAS_BUILD_PROFILE` in `app.config.ts` when you need profile-specific logic beyond the three standard environments.

### TypeScript Notes

```tsx
// env.d.ts - document expected public variables for the team
declare namespace NodeJS {
  interface ProcessEnv {
    EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL: string;
    EXPO_PUBLIC_APP_ENV: "development" | "preview" | "production";
  }
}
 
// Static access only - Metro will NOT inline bracket notation or destructuring
const url = process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL; // ✓ inlined
// const url = process.env["EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL"]; // ✗ not inlined
```

## Gotchas

* **Putting API secrets in `EXPO_PUBLIC_*`** - Any value inlined into JavaScript is visible in the app binary. **Fix:** Keep secrets server-side; use short-lived tokens from your backend.
* **Omitting `--environment` on `eas update` (SDK 55+)** - Updates may not match the variables used in your production build. **Fix:** Always pass `--environment` matching the target build profile.
* **Using `NODE_ENV` to switch `.env` files** - `npx expo export` forces `NODE_ENV=production`, so test/staging files won't load as expected. **Fix:** Use `eas env:pull --environment <name>` or explicit `EXPO_PUBLIC_APP_ENV`.
* **Bracket notation for env vars** - `process.env['EXPO_PUBLIC_KEY']` is not statically analyzable and won't be inlined. **Fix:** Use dot notation: `process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_KEY`.
* **Assuming secrets are available in `app.config.ts` locally** - Secret-type variables are unreadable outside EAS servers. **Fix:** Use sensitive/plaintext for values needed during local config resolution, or provide dev defaults.
* **Committing `.env.local` after `eas env:pull`** - Pulled files often contain staging/production values. **Fix:** Add `.env*.local` to `.gitignore` and use separate pull commands per developer machine.
* **Mismatched environments across workflow jobs** - A fingerprint job on `production` paired with a preview build causes wrong secrets. **Fix:** Set `jobs.<id>.environment` to match the build profile's environment in EAS Workflows.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| EAS environment variables | Cloud builds, updates, team-wide config | You need zero Expo account dependency |
| Local `.env` files only | Solo dev, no EAS, open-source samples | Remote CI/CD or EAS Build - files won't be on the runner |
| `eas env:pull` + `.env.local` | Local dev parity with cloud environments | You want fully offline config with no Expo CLI |
| `app.config.ts` + `extra` field | Values needed before JS bundle (icons, bundle ID) | Simple runtime flags - prefer `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` |
| `react-native-config` | Legacy bare RN apps not on Expo env vars | New Expo SDK 57 projects - migrate to `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` |
| Runtime remote config (Firebase, LaunchDarkly) | Feature flags that change without a new build | Static API URLs known at build time |

## FAQs

What are the three default EAS environments?

`development`, `preview`, and `production`. Each is an independent set of variables. Custom environment names are available on Enterprise and Production EAS plans.

How do I connect an eas.json build profile to an environment?

Add the `environment` field to the profile:

```json
{
  "build": {
    "production": {
      "environment": "production"
    }
  }
}
```

All variables assigned to that environment are injected during the build.

What is the difference between project-wide and account-wide variables?

* **Project-wide:** Scoped to one EAS project (one app). Managed in project settings.
* **Account-wide:** Available to all projects under an Expo account or organization. Useful for shared tooling tokens.

Which variables are safe to use in client JavaScript?

Only variables prefixed with `EXPO_PUBLIC_`. They are inlined into the bundle at build time and are extractable from the compiled app. Never prefix private keys or admin tokens with `EXPO_PUBLIC_`.

How do I load EAS variables for local development?

```bash
eas env:pull --environment development
```

This writes a `.env.local` file. Restart Metro or reload the app to pick up changes. Keep `.env.local` gitignored.

Why is --environment required for eas update in SDK 55+?

To guarantee OTA bundles use the same EAS environment variables as cloud builds - not whatever `.env` file happens to exist on the machine running the update command.

Gotcha: Why does process.env["EXPO\_PUBLIC\_API\_URL"] not work?

Expo's Metro config only inlines **static dot notation** (`process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL`). Bracket access and destructuring are not supported. Use dot notation everywhere.

What are secret-type variables for?

Build-time values like `NPM_TOKEN` or private registry credentials. They are unreadable outside EAS servers and are not available during local `app.config.ts` evaluation. They do **not** protect values you embed in client code.

How does EAS pick an environment if I omit the environment field?

Automatically: `production` when `distribution` is `store`, `development` when `developmentClient` is `true`, and `preview` for everything else. Explicit configuration is safer for teams with many profiles.

Can I use environment variables in EAS Workflows?

Yes. Build jobs inherit `environment` from the matching `eas.json` profile. Other job types (update, fingerprint, Maestro) accept `jobs.<id>.environment`. Keep environments consistent across jobs in the same workflow.

How do file-type environment variables work?

Upload a file (for example `google-services.json`) as an environment variable. EAS exposes it as a file path on the build runner. Useful for credentials that must exist as files during native compilation.

Should I commit .env to git?

Commit a `.env` with safe defaults or placeholder `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` values if helpful for onboarding. Never commit `.env.local` or files containing real secrets. Use EAS for production values.

How do I run a one-off command with EAS environment variables?

```bash
eas env:exec --environment production 'npx sentry-expo-upload-sourcemaps dist'
```

`eas env:exec` loads the environment before executing the shell command.

How does app.config.ts read environment variables during EAS Build?

Node evaluates `app.config.ts` on the build worker. Plaintext and sensitive EAS variables are available as `process.env.*`. Use them to set `bundleIdentifier`, `name`, plugins, and `extra` fields per environment.

What is the relationship between EXPO\_PUBLIC\_APP\_ENV and EAS environments?

They are independent concepts that you align by convention. `EXPO_PUBLIC_APP_ENV` is a variable you define. EAS `development`/`preview`/`production` are containers for variables. Set `EXPO_PUBLIC_APP_ENV=preview` inside the preview EAS environment for consistency.

* [Expo Platform Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-platform/expo-platform-basics/) - `APP_VARIANT` branching and EAS project linking

Dokumen: Expo Account, Projects & Permissions
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-platform/expo-account-projects-and-permissions/

# Expo Account, Projects & Permissions

Structure Expo accounts, EAS projects, and role-based access so teams can ship multiple apps under one organization - with clear ownership, credential isolation, and least-privilege permissions.

Highlights / Expo Account, Projects & Permissions

* Personal accounts suit solo work; organizations enable team RBAC and shared credentials
* Four org roles: Owner, Admin, Developer, Viewer - least privilege for day-to-day work
* Set expo.owner in app.json so builds and credentials land under the correct account
* extra.eas.projectId is the stable identifier for EAS Build, Update, and env vars
* Account-wide environment variables share tooling tokens across multiple apps
* Project transfers require Owner/Admin on both source and destination accounts

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
# Log in and link a new app to an organization project
eas login
eas init
```

```json
// app.json - route the app to an organization and pin the EAS project
{
  "expo": {
    "name": "Retail App",
    "slug": "retail-app",
    "owner": "acme-mobile",
    "extra": {
      "eas": {
        "projectId": "bd2f7e21-1ee7-47f2-8357-d7c4b50622fb"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

```bash
# Verify which account owns the linked project
eas project:info
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Your team has **more than one developer** touching builds, credentials, or environment variables.
* You ship **multiple apps** (per client, brand, or platform) and need isolated credentials with shared billing.
* You need **auditability** - who can submit to the store, rotate secrets, or invite members.
* You are moving from a **personal account** to an **organization** without breaking production apps.

## Working Example

```json
// app.config.ts - multi-app org: shared projectId pattern, distinct slugs per app
import type { ExpoConfig } from "expo/config";
 
const APP_SLUG = "retail-consumer";
const ORG_OWNER = "acme-mobile";
 
const config: ExpoConfig = {
  name: "Acme Retail",
  slug: APP_SLUG,
  owner: ORG_OWNER,
  version: "3.1.0",
  ios: {
    bundleIdentifier: "com.acme.retail",
  },
  android: {
    package: "com.acme.retail",
  },
  extra: {
    eas: {
      projectId: "bd2f7e21-1ee7-47f2-8357-d7c4b50622fb",
    },
    appFamily: "retail",
  },
};
 
export default config;
```

```json
// eas.json - profiles inherit org credentials via the linked projectId
{
  "cli": {
    "version": ">= 16.0.0",
    "appVersionSource": "remote"
  },
  "build": {
    "development": {
      "developmentClient": true,
      "distribution": "internal",
      "environment": "development"
    },
    "preview": {
      "distribution": "internal",
      "environment": "preview"
    },
    "production": {
      "distribution": "store",
      "environment": "production",
      "autoIncrement": true
    }
  },
  "submit": {
    "production": {
      "ios": {
        "appleTeamId": "ABCDE12345"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

```bash
# CI: use a robot token with minimal scope - not a personal password
# Expo dashboard → Account Settings → Access Tokens → Create token
export EXPO_TOKEN="xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"
eas build --profile production --platform ios --non-interactive
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* **`owner`** routes the app to an organization - builds, credentials, and env vars scope to `acme-mobile`.
* **`projectId`** is the durable key EAS services use across slug or bundle ID changes.
* **Build profiles** map to environments without duplicating credential stores per developer.
* **Robot tokens** for CI preserve least privilege - no shared personal passwords.

## Deep Dive

### How It Works

#### Account types

| Type | Best for | Collaboration |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Personal** | Solo projects, learning, prototypes | Share credentials manually (discouraged) |
| **Organization** | Teams, agencies, multi-app companies | RBAC, shared credentials, audit logs |

Every `expo.dev` signup creates a Personal account. Create an Organization when more than one person needs build, submit, or credential access.

#### EAS project linking

```
eas init  →  creates/links project under active account
          →  writes extra.eas.projectId to app config
          →  EAS Build / Update / env vars key off projectId
```

* **`slug`** is human-readable and used in URLs - it can change.
* **`projectId`** is a UUID - stable for the lifetime of the project.
* **`owner`** determines which account's credential store and billing apply.

#### Organization roles

| Role | Builds & updates | Credentials | Billing & invites | Delete account/projects |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Owner** | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| **Admin** | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ (no Owner grant) | ✗ |
| **Developer** | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ |
| **Viewer** | View in Expo Go only | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ |

Assign **Developer** for engineers who ship daily. Reserve **Owner** for leads and billing contacts. Use **Viewer** for stakeholders who only need to open preview builds in Expo Go.

#### Multi-app governance patterns

| Pattern | Structure |
| --- | --- |
| **One org, many projects** | `acme-mobile` org with `retail-app`, `warehouse-app`, `driver-app` - each with its own `projectId` |
| **Org per client (agency)** | `client-a-mobile` org isolates credentials and billing per customer |
| **Account-wide env vars** | Shared `NPM_TOKEN` or Sentry org token at account scope; app-specific API URLs at project scope |
| **Escrow transfer** | Temporary org holds a project during acquisition - both parties need Owner on escrow |

#### Programmatic access

* **Personal access tokens** - tied to a user; inherit that user's org memberships and roles.
* **Robot users / tokens** - for CI/CD; assign to an org with Developer role minimum for builds.
* **SSO** - Enterprise orgs can enforce single sign-on (see Expo SSO docs).

### TypeScript Notes

```tsx
// Reading linked project metadata at runtime (diagnostics only - not for auth)
import Constants from "expo-constants";
 
const projectId = Constants.expoConfig?.extra?.eas?.projectId;
const owner = Constants.expoConfig?.owner; // available in static config
 
export function DiagnosticsBanner() {
  if (!__DEV__) return null;
  return (
    <Text>
      EAS {projectId ?? "unlinked"} · owner: {owner ?? "personal"}
    </Text>
  );
}
```

Never use `projectId` or `owner` for in-app authorization - they are build-time identifiers, not security boundaries.

## Gotchas

* **Sharing a personal account password** - No audit trail, no per-person revocation, violates Expo ToS. **Fix:** Create an Organization and invite members with appropriate roles.
* **Omitting `owner` on org projects** - `eas build` may target your personal account instead of the team. **Fix:** Set `"owner": "org-slug"` in `app.json` before `eas init` or transfer the project.
* **Hardcoding credentials per developer machine** - Apple/Google keys stored locally break CI and onboarding. **Fix:** Let EAS host credentials under the org project; use `eas credentials` for rotation.
* **Granting Owner to every engineer** - One mistaken click can delete production credentials. **Fix:** Default to Developer; keep two Owners for bus-factor coverage.
* **Reusing one EAS project for unrelated apps** - Credentials, env vars, and update channels collide. **Fix:** One `projectId` per app binary (bundle ID / package).
* **Transferring without Admin on both sides** - Project moves require Owner or Admin on source **and** destination. **Fix:** Use an escrow organization for third-party transfers.
* **CI tokens on personal accounts** - Token inherits personal project scope; leaves when the employee departs. **Fix:** Create a robot token under the organization.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Organization account | Any team ≥ 2 people | Solo hobby project with no CI |
| Personal account | Learning, single-developer prototypes | Production apps with shared credentials |
| One org per client | Agency isolation and offboarding | Single-product company - unnecessary overhead |
| Account-wide env vars | Shared tokens across all org apps | App-specific API URLs - use project scope |
| Personal access token (CI) | Quick CI setup on a small team | Long-lived production pipelines - prefer robot tokens |
| Convert personal → org | Solo dev becoming a team | You need a clean client separation - create a new org instead |

## FAQs

When should I create an Organization instead of using my personal account?

When anyone besides you needs to run builds, manage credentials, configure environment variables, or submit to app stores. Organizations provide RBAC, shared credential stores, and member management.

What are the four organization roles?

* **Owner** - full control including deletion
* **Admin** - settings, billing, invites (cannot grant Owner)
* **Developer** - builds, updates, credentials
* **Viewer** - read-only via Expo Go, no modifications

What does the owner field in app.json do?

It sets which Expo account (personal username or organization slug) owns the project. Builds, credentials, and dashboard URLs resolve under that account. Required when the project belongs to an organization you are a member of.

What is extra.eas.projectId?

A stable UUID written by `eas init` that links your repo to an EAS project. EAS Build, Update, environment variables, and credentials all scope to this ID - not to `slug` or bundle identifier.

How do I link an existing repo to EAS?

```bash
eas login
eas init
```

Follow prompts to create a new project or link to an existing one. The command writes `projectId` into your app config.

Gotcha: Why did my build run on my personal account instead of the team org?

The active `eas whoami` account or a missing `owner` field defaults to personal scope. Set `"owner": "your-org-slug"` in app config and confirm `eas project:info` shows the organization.

Can I convert a personal account into an organization?

Yes - User Settings → "Convert your account into an organization." Projects, credentials, EAS subscriptions, and webhooks transfer. Plan a maintenance window and confirm integrations using your access token still work.

How do project transfers work?

Project Settings → General → Transfer project. You must be Owner or Admin on **both** source and destination accounts. For transfers to a third party without shared access, use an escrow organization.

Who can invite new members?

Owners and Admins. Admins can assign any role except Owner. Owners can assign any role including Owner.

What is the difference between project-wide and account-wide environment variables?

* **Project-wide:** Scoped to one EAS project (one app).
* **Account-wide:** Available to all projects in the organization. Configure under Account Settings → Environment variables.

How should CI authenticate to EAS?

Create an access token (robot user for organizations). Set `EXPO_TOKEN` in CI secrets. Use `--non-interactive` on `eas build` and `eas submit`. Do not store personal passwords in CI.

Can multiple apps share one EAS project?

Technically yes, but not recommended. Credentials, update channels, and environment variables collide. Use one EAS project per distinct app (unique bundle ID / package).

What permissions does a Developer need for day-to-day work?

Developer role covers `eas build`, `eas update`, `eas credentials`, and environment variable reads (per visibility). Developers cannot manage billing, invite members, or change org settings.

How do I structure an agency with many clients?

Create a separate Organization per client (`client-a-mobile`, `client-b-mobile`). Each org holds its own projects, credentials, and billing. Developers receive invites only to the orgs they serve.

Where do I audit account security changes?

Account Overview → User settings → Security activity. Shows password, email, and 2FA changes. Organization Owners should enforce 2FA for all members on production accounts.

Dokumen: Expo Go vs Development Builds
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-platform/expo-go-vs-development-builds/

# Expo Go vs Development Builds

Expo Go is a fast playground with a fixed native surface. A **development build** is your own debug binary with `expo-dev-client`, carrying every native module your project installs - the environment production apps are actually built from.

Highlights / Expo Go vs Development Builds

* Expo Go is a fixed native binary - only its preinstalled native modules are callable from your JS
* Development builds include expo-dev-client and YOUR native dependencies
* Switch before custom native modules, push credentials, or universal/app links
* npx expo install expo-dev-client then eas build --profile development
* JS hot reload works in both; native code changes require a new native build

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
# Still prototyping with only Expo SDK modules? Expo Go is enough:
npx expo start
# Scan QR with Expo Go (simulator/emulator or device with matching SDK)
 
# Need custom native code? Add the dev client and create a development build:
npx expo install expo-dev-client
eas build --profile development --platform ios
# Install the .ipa/.apk, then:
npx expo start --dev-client
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Deciding whether day-one Expo Go is sufficient for your SDK 57 spike.
* Hitting `Native module cannot be null` after `npm install`ing a library not bundled in Expo Go.
* Testing push notifications, app/universal links, or custom splash/icon behavior realistically.
* Onboarding teammates who confuse Expo Go limitations with Expo platform limitations.

## Working Example

```bash
# 1. Add expo-dev-client to an existing SDK 57 project
npx expo install expo-dev-client
```

```json
// eas.json - development profile (installable debug build)
{
  "cli": { "version": ">= 16.0.0" },
  "build": {
    "development": {
      "developmentClient": true,
      "distribution": "internal",
      "ios": { "simulator": true }
    },
    "production": {
      "autoIncrement": true
    }
  }
}
```

```bash
# 2. Build and install (simulator example)
eas build --profile development --platform ios
# Download/install the build, then start Metro for dev-client:
npx expo start --dev-client
```

```tsx
// App.tsx - detect runtime for conditional diagnostics
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { Button, StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
import * as Expo from "expo";
import Constants from "expo-constants";
 
export default function App() {
  const [inGo, setInGo] = useState<boolean | null>(null);
 
  useEffect(() => {
    setInGo(Expo.isRunningInExpoGo());
  }, []);
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.container}>
      <Text style={styles.title}>Runtime probe</Text>
      <Text>expo-dev-client: {Constants.expoConfig?.plugins?.includes("expo-dev-client") ? "configured" : "n/a"}</Text>
      <Text>Running in Expo Go: {inGo === null ? "…" : inGo ? "yes" : "no"}</Text>
      <Text style={styles.hint}>
        Development builds load your native modules. Expo Go only loads modules shipped inside Expo Go.
      </Text>
      <Button title="Reload" onPress={() => Expo.reloadAppAsync("manual")} />
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  container: { flex: 1, justifyContent: "center", padding: 24, gap: 8 },
  title: { fontSize: 20, fontWeight: "700" },
  hint: { fontSize: 14, color: "#555", marginTop: 8 },
});
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* `expo-dev-client` turns your app into a development client with a launcher UI and network inspector.
* `eas build --profile development` produces an installable binary with your native dependency graph.
* `npx expo start --dev-client` serves JS to the custom binary instead of Expo Go.
* `Expo.isRunningInExpoGo()` branches diagnostics or feature gates during migration.

## Deep Dive

### How It Works

#### Two layers: native app vs JavaScript bundle

| Layer | What it is | Changes when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Native app** | Binary on device (Expo Go or your dev build) | New native module, icon, entitlements, SDK upgrade |
| **JavaScript bundle** | Metro output from `npx expo start` | Every Fast Refresh / reload |

Your JS can only call native APIs that exist in the **installed native app**. Installing `react-native-foo` adds JS stubs to `node_modules`, but until the native code is compiled into your binary, calls fail at runtime.

#### Expo Go

* Prebuilt app from the store with a **fixed set** of native modules (the Expo SDK subset Expo Go ships).
* Loads your JS bundle over the network - instant iteration for learning and early UI work.
* **Cannot** gain new native modules after install.
* Shows an **emulated** splash (app icon on solid color) - not your real `app.json` splash assets.
* Supports **one SDK version** on iOS App Store builds - older SDKs require simulator/Android sideload from expo.dev/go.

#### Development build (`expo-dev-client`)

* **Your** debug binary with the same native modules you ship to TestFlight / Play Internal Testing.
* Includes a **launcher** to switch Metro servers, open updates, and inspect network traffic.
* Rebuild required when native dependencies or `app.config` native fields change - JS-only work still hot-reloads.
* Required for realistic push notification, app/universal link, and custom native module testing.

```
┌─────────────────────┐         ┌──────────────────────────────┐
│     Expo Go         │         │   Development build          │
│  Fixed native mods  │         │  Your native mods + dev-client│
│  + your JS bundle   │         │  + your JS bundle            │
└─────────────────────┘         └──────────────────────────────┘
         │                                    │
         └────────── npx expo start ──────────┘
                    (Metro serves JS)
```

### Decision Matrix

| Need | Expo Go | Development build |
| --- | --- | --- |
| UI with Expo SDK modules only | ✓ | ✓ (overkill early) |
| `expo-camera`, `expo-router`, etc. in SDK 57 | ✓ if included in Expo Go | ✓ |
| `@react-native-firebase/*`, custom native SDKs | ✗ | ✓ |
| Remote push notifications (APNs/FCM) | ✗ | ✓ |
| iOS Universal Links / Android App Links | ✗ | ✓ |
| Custom app icon / splash on device | Limited / emulated | ✓ |
| Native code you wrote (Expo Modules API) | ✗ | ✓ |
| Same binary as production CI | ✗ | ✓ (debug variant) |

### Migration Path (Expo Go → dev client)

```bash
npx expo install expo-dev-client
# Ensure plugins includes expo-dev-client (auto-added by install)
 
eas build:configure   # if eas.json missing
eas build --profile development --platform all
 
# Daily loop after install:
npx expo start --dev-client
```

Local alternative when you have Xcode/Android Studio:

```bash
npx expo run:ios
npx expo run:android
```

These compile a debug binary with `expo-dev-client` embedded.

### TypeScript Notes

```tsx
import * as Expo from "expo";
 
export function RuntimeBanner() {
  if (Expo.isRunningInExpoGo()) {
    return <Text>Expo Go - some native features disabled</Text>;
  }
  return <Text>Development / production native binary</Text>;
}
```

Use runtime detection only for diagnostics - do not fork product logic permanently on `isRunningInExpoGo()` unless the feature is genuinely unavailable.

## Gotchas

* **Installing a native library and expecting Expo Go to work** - JS installs succeed but native calls throw. **Fix:** `npx expo install expo-dev-client` and create a development build.
* **Testing push notifications in Expo Go** - Remote push requires your certificates in **your** binary. **Fix:** Development build with configured push credentials.
* **Assuming splash/icon changes appear in Expo Go** - Expo Go shows its own shell; your branding ships with native builds. **Fix:** Validate assets in a development or preview build.
* **Forgetting `--dev-client` flag** - Metro defaults to Expo Go QR flow; your custom binary won't connect correctly. **Fix:** `npx expo start --dev-client` after installing a dev build.
* **iOS device stuck on wrong SDK Expo Go** - App Store only offers the latest Expo Go. **Fix:** Development build, or use simulator with a downloadable Expo Go build from expo.dev/go.
* **Rebuilding for every JS change** - Unnecessary. Native rebuilds are only for native dependency or config plugin changes. **Fix:** Keep Metro running; reload JS for component edits.
* **Shipping `expo-dev-client` to production stores** - Dev client belongs in debug/internal profiles. **Fix:** Separate `development` and `production` EAS profiles; production omits dev-client launcher UI.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Expo Go | Learning, UI spikes, SDK-only modules | Custom native modules or store-realistic testing |
| EAS development build | Team distribution, no local Xcode/Android setup | You need instant native iteration with no cloud queue |
| `npx expo run:ios/android` (local) | Fast native iteration on one machine | CI-only teams without local native toolchains |
| Preview build (release config, internal dist) | QA testing performance near production | Daily dev loop - slower than dev client + Metro |
| Production build only | Tiny apps with no native customizations | Any project that iterated in Expo Go and hit native walls |
| Simulator web (`expo start --web`) | Component logic without native APIs | Camera, push, sensors, or platform-specific native code |

## FAQs

What is Expo Go?

Expo Go is a prebuilt Expo playground app from the app stores. It loads your JavaScript bundle over the network so you can preview UI quickly without compiling native code yourself.

What is a development build?

A development build is a debug version of **your** app with the `expo-dev-client` library installed. It includes your native dependencies and connects to Metro for JavaScript hot reload - the same architecture production uses, minus release optimizations.

When is Expo Go enough?

When you only use native modules already bundled inside Expo Go (most `expo-*` SDK packages), you are learning RN, or you are building UI that does not depend on custom native code, push, or app links.

When must I switch to a development build?

Before integrating libraries with native code outside Expo Go's bundle, testing remote push, configuring universal/app links, or validating real icons, splash screens, and entitlements.

What does expo-dev-client add?

A development launcher, switchable Metro URLs, network inspection, and support for loading your custom native module graph - capabilities Expo Go cannot replicate because its native binary is fixed.

How do I create a development build on EAS?

```bash
npx expo install expo-dev-client
eas build --profile development --platform ios
```

Set `"developmentClient": true` in the EAS profile. Install the artifact, then run `npx expo start --dev-client`.

Do I need to rebuild for every code change?

No. JavaScript and React changes hot-reload through Metro in both Expo Go and development builds. Rebuild when you add/remove native modules or change native config plugins.

Gotcha: Why does my new native package work on npm install but crash at runtime?

`npm install` adds JavaScript and native source to `node_modules`, but Expo Go's binary does not include that native code. Create a development build so the native module is compiled into your app.

Can I use Expo Go with SDK 57?

Yes on simulators/emulators and Android devices when Expo Go versions align. iOS physical devices must use the App Store Expo Go version compatible with SDK 57 - if mismatched, use a development build.

What command starts Metro for a development build?

```bash
npx expo start --dev-client
```

Without `--dev-client`, the CLI optimizes for Expo Go QR codes.

How do I detect Expo Go at runtime?

```tsx
import * as Expo from "expo";
Expo.isRunningInExpoGo(); // boolean
```

Use for diagnostics, not as a permanent feature flag strategy.

Are development builds the same as production builds?

They share native modules and config plugins, but development builds include dev-client tooling, debug symbols, and internal distribution. Production profiles strip dev-only code and apply release signing.

Can I test deep links in Expo Go?

Custom URL schemes partially work, but **App Links / Universal Links** need two-way association baked into your native binary - impossible in Expo Go. Use a development build.

What is the daily workflow after I have a dev build installed?

Start Metro once (`npx expo start --dev-client`), open the dev client app, pick your server, iterate on JS with Fast Refresh. Rebuild native only when native dependencies change.

Does expo-dev-client ship to the App Store?

No. Keep it in development/internal profiles. Production store builds use a `production` EAS profile without the dev launcher.

## Related

* [create-expo-app Quickstart](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-platform/create-expo-app-quickstart/) - scaffold the project before choosing a runtime
* [app.json & app.config.js](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-platform/app-json-and-app-config-js/) - native fields dev builds actually apply
* [Expo Modules Core](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-platform/expo-modules-core/) - how native modules register in your binary

Dokumen: Expo Modules Core
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-platform/expo-modules-core/

# Expo Modules Core

The `expo` package is more than a version pin - it bootstraps **Expo Modules Core**, the JSI-native runtime that registers Expo SDK modules, exposes `requireNativeModule`, and connects JavaScript to Swift/Kotlin implementations in every Expo and bare React Native app.

Highlights / Expo Modules Core

* The expo package installs ExpoModulesCore native infrastructure at app launch
* requireNativeModule resolves JSI bindings first, then falls back to legacy bridge proxies
* registerRootComponent wires AppRegistry and dev-only Fast Refresh helpers
* NativeModule and SharedObject extend EventEmitter over JSI - same API on iOS and Android
* Works in managed, bare, and brownfield apps once the native entry point is configured

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```tsx
// index.ts (custom entry) or App.tsx root
import { registerRootComponent } from "expo";
import { requireNativeModule, requireOptionalNativeModule } from "expo-modules-core";
import App from "./App";
 
// Optional: probe a native module at startup (dev diagnostics)
const ExpoDevice = requireOptionalNativeModule("ExpoDevice");
if (__DEV__ && ExpoDevice) {
  console.log("ExpoDevice native module loaded via JSI");
}
 
registerRootComponent(App);
```

```bash
# Ensure the core package matches SDK 57
npx expo install expo expo-modules-core
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Understanding why `import { Camera } from 'expo-camera'` works after only `npx expo install`.
* Debugging `Cannot find native module 'Expo…'` in bare or brownfield setups.
* Calling `requireNativeModule` from shared libraries without React components.
* Authoring or integrating native modules built with the Expo Modules API.

## Working Example

```tsx
// src/native/brightness.ts - thin typed wrapper over an Expo native module
import { requireNativeModule, NativeModule } from "expo-modules-core";
 
type BrightnessModule = NativeModule & {
  getBrightnessAsync: () => Promise<number>;
  setBrightnessAsync: (value: number) => Promise<void>;
};
 
const Brightness = requireNativeModule<BrightnessModule>("ExpoBrightness");
 
export async function dimToHalf(): Promise<number> {
  const current = await Brightness.getBrightnessAsync();
  await Brightness.setBrightnessAsync(0.5);
  return current;
}
```

```tsx
// App.tsx - root registration + runtime probe
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { Button, StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
import { registerRootComponent } from "expo";
import * as Device from "expo-device";
import { dimToHalf } from "./src/native/brightness";
 
function App() {
  const [model, setModel] = useState<string>("…");
  const [restored, setRestored] = useState<string>("");
 
  useEffect(() => {
    setModel(Device.modelName ?? "unknown");
  }, []);
 
  async function handleDim() {
    const previous = await dimToHalf();
    setRestored(`was ${previous.toFixed(2)}`);
  }
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.container}>
      <Text style={styles.title}>Expo Modules Core</Text>
      <Text>Device: {model}</Text>
      <Text>expo-device uses the same JSI registry as requireNativeModule</Text>
      <Button title="Dim screen to 50%" onPress={handleDim} />
      {restored ? <Text>{restored}</Text> : null}
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  container: { flex: 1, justifyContent: "center", padding: 24, gap: 8 },
  title: { fontSize: 20, fontWeight: "700" },
});
 
registerRootComponent(App);
```

```java
// android/app/src/main/java/.../MainActivity.java (bare) - required component name
@Override
protected String getMainComponentName() {
  return "main"; // matches registerRootComponent → AppRegistry.registerComponent("main", ...)
}
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* `registerRootComponent` registers `"main"` with React Native and web runtimes.
* `requireNativeModule` loads the JSI host object exported by Expo Modules Core.
* High-level packages (`expo-device`) and low-level `requireNativeModule` share the same native registry.
* Bare projects must align `MainActivity` / `AppDelegate` `moduleName` with `"main"`.

## Deep Dive

### How It Works

#### Bootstrap sequence (app launch)

1. Native app starts → **ExpoModulesCore** initializes the JSI host object (`global.expo.modules…`).
2. Each installed Expo module's native code **registers** itself (name → class) during native startup.
3. JavaScript loads → `expo` polyfills (`registerRootComponent`, web globals) run.
4. When JS calls `requireNativeModule("ExpoCamera")`, Core looks up the JSI binding and returns a **NativeModule** proxy.
5. If JSI binding is missing (legacy path), Core falls back to a bridge proxy - some sync APIs may be unavailable.

```
Native launch
    │
    ▼
ExpoModulesCore (Swift / Kotlin / C++)
    │ registers ExpoCamera, ExpoDevice, …
    ▼
JS bundle loads (Metro)
    │
    ▼
requireNativeModule("ExpoCamera") ──JSI──▶ native method calls
```

#### Key `expo` / `expo-modules-core` APIs

| API | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `registerRootComponent` | Registers root component as `"main"`; web entry + dev helpers |
| `requireNativeModule(name)` | Loads native module; throws if missing |
| `requireOptionalNativeModule(name)` | Same, returns `null` when absent |
| `requireNativeView` | Drop-in replacement for `requireNativeComponent` |
| `NativeModule` | Base class for native modules; extends `EventEmitter` |
| `SharedObject` / `SharedRef` | Long-lived native handles (video players, image refs) over JSI |
| `isRunningInExpoGo()` | Runtime check for Expo Go vs custom binary |

```tsx
import { EventEmitter, requireNativeModule } from "expo-modules-core";
 
// NativeModule methods are async by default unless marked sync in native code
const module = requireNativeModule("ExpoFileSystem");
```

#### Relationship to React Native New Architecture

* Expo Modules API targets **JSI** and supports **TurboModules / Fabric** on the New Architecture.
* Backwards compatible with older architecture - bridge proxy fallback exists but lacks sync JSI features.
* SDK 57 / RN 0.86 default to New Architecture; Expo modules auto-link through `expo-modules-autolinking`.

#### Package layout in SDK 57

| Package | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `expo` | App entry helpers, re-exports, web polyfills, `expo/fetch` |
| `expo-modules-core` | `requireNativeModule`, `NativeModule`, `EventEmitter`, JSI types |
| `expo-modules-autolinking` | Gradle/Pod resolution of Expo modules at build time |
| `expo-*` libraries | Feature modules (camera, file-system, etc.) registering via Core |

```bash
# Autolinking inspect (debug missing modules)
npx expo-modules-autolinking resolve --platform ios
```

### Bare / Brownfield Setup Requirements

Expo Modules Core runs in **any** React Native app that:

1. Depends on `expo` and `expo-modules-core` (`npx expo install expo expo-modules-core`).
2. Applies **expo-modules-autolinking** in `settings.gradle` / Podfile (added by `npx install-expo-modules` or Expo prebuild).
3. Registers the JS root component name **`main`** via `registerRootComponent`.
4. Calls native entry setup in `AppDelegate` / `MainApplication` (prebuild templates do this automatically).

```bash
# Add Expo modules to an existing bare RN app
npx install-expo-modules@latest
```

### NativeModule Events

```tsx
import { useEventListener } from "expo";
import { requireNativeModule } from "expo-modules-core";
 
const ExpoAccelerometer = requireNativeModule("ExpoAccelerometer");
 
export function AccelerometerListener() {
  useEventListener(ExpoAccelerometer, "accelerometerDidUpdate", (event) => {
    console.log(event.x, event.y, event.z);
  });
  return null;
}
```

`EventEmitter` in Core is implemented in C++ shared across platforms - listeners fire synchronously on the JS thread.

### TypeScript Notes

```tsx
import type { NativeModule } from "expo-modules-core";
import { requireNativeModule } from "expo-modules-core";
 
interface ExpoHapticsModule extends NativeModule {
  impactAsync(style: "light" | "medium" | "heavy"): Promise<void>;
  selectionAsync(): Promise<void>;
}
 
export const Haptics = requireNativeModule<ExpoHapticsModule>("ExpoHaptics");
```

Typing the interface documents available native methods and catches typos at compile time.

## Gotchas

* **Wrong `MainComponent` name in bare apps** - Native entry still says `"MyApp"` while JS registers `"main"`. **Fix:** Set `getMainComponentName()` / `moduleName` to `"main"` or match your `registerRootComponent` name.
* **Missing autolinking after adding `expo-camera`** - Native build never compiles the module. **Fix:** Run `npx expo prebuild` or verify `expo-modules-autolinking` in Gradle/Podfile; rebuild native.
* **Calling `requireNativeModule` in Expo Go for unbundled modules** - Core works, but the native class was never shipped in Expo Go. **Fix:** Development build with the module installed.
* **Assuming bridge sync methods on fallback proxy** - When JSI binding is missing, some sync APIs noop or throw. **Fix:** Rebuild with New Architecture enabled; verify module supports sync functions.
* **Importing from `expo` vs `expo-modules-core`** - App authors can use either for `requireNativeModule`; library packages should import from `expo-modules-core` to avoid peer-dep cycles. **Fix:** Libraries → `expo-modules-core`; apps → `expo` re-exports.
* **Leaking SharedObjects** - Long-lived native handles (video players) retain memory until `release()` or hook cleanup. **Fix:** Use package hooks (`useVideoPlayer`) or call `release()` when done.
* **Skipping `npx expo install`** - Manual npm versions mismatch native binaries vs JS stubs. **Fix:** Always `npx expo install <pkg>` so autolinking resolves SDK 57-compatible builds.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Expo Modules API (`expo-modules-core`) | Expo SDK libraries, shared Swift/Kotlin modules | You need heavy C++ shared across platforms (consider Turbo Modules) |
| React Native Turbo Modules | C++ core, RN-first libraries without `expo` dep | You want Expo autolinking and Config Plugins integration |
| Legacy NativeModules bridge | Maintaining very old libraries | New SDK 57 projects - prefer JSI |
| `react-native-web` shims only | Web builds without native APIs | Device features (camera, sensors) |
| Direct `NativeModules` import | Quick spike in legacy code | Long-term - misses optional JSI sync APIs |

## FAQs

What is Expo Modules Core?

The native + JavaScript infrastructure behind the Expo Modules API. It registers native modules on a JSI host object, exposes `requireNativeModule`, and provides `NativeModule`, `EventEmitter`, and `SharedObject` primitives used by every `expo-*` package.

How is the expo package different from expo-modules-core?

`expo` is the umbrella runtime - `registerRootComponent`, `isRunningInExpoGo`, web polyfills, and re-exports. `expo-modules-core` is the low-level module loader and type layer library authors depend on.

What does registerRootComponent do?

It calls `AppRegistry.registerComponent("main", …)`, sets up web rendering, polyfills `process.nextTick`, and enables dev-only Fast Refresh helpers. Every Expo app ultimately registers `"main"` as the root component name.

How does requireNativeModule find native code?

It queries the JSI host object populated at native launch. If absent, it falls back to a bridge proxy module - still functional but missing some synchronous JSI methods.

Why do I get Cannot find native module ExpoSomething?

Common causes: native project not rebuilt after install, autolinking misconfigured in bare app, module not included in Expo Go, or typo in module name. Rebuild native and verify with `npx expo-modules-autolinking resolve`.

Does Expo Modules Core require Expo Go?

No. It runs in development builds, production binaries, and bare React Native apps once autolinking and the `"main"` entry name are configured.

How does this relate to the New Architecture?

Expo modules are JSI-first and support TurboModules/Fabric. SDK 57 defaults to New Architecture on RN 0.86; Core handles both paths with bridge fallback for older setups.

What is a SharedObject?

A JSI-backed native instance with methods and events - e.g. a video player. It extends `EventEmitter` and persists across JS calls until `release()` or hook teardown.

Gotcha: Why do high-level imports work but requireNativeModule fails?

You may be in Expo Go where the high-level JS package exists but the native module is not bundled, or the native name differs (`ExpoDevice` vs `Device`). Verify the exact native module name in the package docs and use a development build.

Can I use Expo Modules in a brownfield app?

Yes. Run `npx install-expo-modules`, align the root component name, rebuild native, and install SDK packages with `npx expo install`.

What is expo-modules-autolinking?

Build-time tooling that scans dependencies and wires Gradle/Podspec entries so native Expo modules compile into your app without manual linking.

How do native events reach JavaScript?

`NativeModule` extends `EventEmitter`. Native code emits events; JS subscribes via `addListener`, `useEventListener`, or `useEvent` from `expo`.

Should library code import from expo or expo-modules-core?

Library packages should depend on `expo-modules-core` for `requireNativeModule` to avoid circular peers. Application code may import from `expo` for ergonomics.

Does expo bundle global fetch in SDK 57?

Yes. SDK 57 installs WinterCG-compliant `fetch` globally on native unless `EXPO_PUBLIC_USE_RN_FETCH=1` is set. Named `import { fetch } from 'expo/fetch'` always uses the Expo implementation.

How do I inspect which modules will link?

```bash
npx expo-modules-autolinking resolve --platform android
npx expo-modules-autolinking resolve --platform ios
```

Compare output with `requireNativeModule` names your app uses.

Dokumen: Expo Platform Basics
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-platform/expo-platform-basics/

# Expo Platform Basics

10 examples to get you started with Expo Platform - 7 basic and 3 intermediate.

Highlights / Expo Platform Basics

* Expo is a platform layer on React Native - you still write RN components, Expo handles native project wiring
* The managed workflow keeps ios/ and android/ generated; you opt into native folders only when needed
* Pin `expo` ~57.0.4 in package.json - every Expo module version is validated against that SDK
* `npx expo install` resolves compatible semver ranges; plain npm install can drift from the SDK matrix
* Expo Go is fastest for learning; custom native modules require a development build with expo-dev-client
* app.config.ts can branch on APP\_VARIANT without committing secrets to app.json
* Linking an EAS projectId early keeps builds, updates, and environment variables scoped to one Expo project

## Prerequisites

Expo projects are scaffolded with **create-expo-app**, which pins the SDK, Metro config, and default TypeScript layout in one step.

```bash
npx create-expo-app@latest MyExpoApp --template blank-typescript
cd MyExpoApp
```

Confirm the SDK pin in `package.json` before installing anything else:

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "expo": "~57.0.4",
    "react": "19.2.3",
    "react-native": "0.86.0"
  }
}
```

Start the dev server and open the app on a device or simulator:

```bash
npx expo start
```

Press `i` for the iOS Simulator, `a` for Android, or scan the QR code with **Expo Go**. Every runnable example below can replace `App.tsx` in the project you just created.

> **Tooling:** These examples target **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4), **React Native 0.86.0**, and **React 19.2.3**.

---

## Basic Examples

### 1. Expo as a Platform Layer

Expo wraps React Native with tooling, a curated module set, and a managed native project - your UI code stays standard RN.

```tsx
import { StatusBar } from "expo-status-bar";
import { StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
export default function App() {
  return (
    <View style={styles.container}>
      <Text style={styles.title}>Expo + React Native</Text>
      <Text style={styles.body}>
        Same View/Text primitives - Expo supplies the dev server, config, and
        native bootstrap.
      </Text>
      <StatusBar style="auto" />
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  container: { flex: 1, justifyContent: "center", padding: 24, gap: 8 },
  title: { fontSize: 22, fontWeight: "700" },
  body: { fontSize: 15, color: "#4b5563", lineHeight: 22 },
});
```

* You still author **React Native components** - Expo is not a separate UI framework
* Packages like `expo-status-bar` ship as **Expo modules** with native code precompiled for the SDK
* The **managed workflow** means Expo owns `ios/` and `android/` generation via prebuild unless you eject or run bare
* Adopt Expo when you want faster iteration, consistent upgrades, and EAS Build/Update without maintaining native projects day one

> **Related:** [create-expo-app Quickstart](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-platform/create-expo-app-quickstart/) - templates and first-run verification | [Expo Modules Core](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-platform/expo-modules-core/) - how native modules bootstrap

---

### 2. Default Project Layout

A fresh Expo app is a small, predictable tree - learn these files before adding features.

```text
MyExpoApp/
├── App.tsx              # Root component (entry UI)
├── app.json             # Static manifest (or app.config.ts)
├── package.json         # SDK-pinned dependencies and scripts
├── tsconfig.json
├── assets/              # Icons, splash, images bundled at build time
└── node_modules/
```

* **`App.tsx`** is the default root - Expo Router projects swap this for an `app/` directory instead
* **`app.json`** (or `app.config.ts`) is the single source of truth for app identity, icons, and native permissions
* **`assets/`** files are referenced by URI in config (`icon`, `splash`) and imported in components
* No `ios/` or `android/` folders yet in pure managed mode - they appear after `npx expo prebuild` or an EAS build

> **Related:** [create-expo-app Quickstart](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-platform/create-expo-app-quickstart/) - template choices and script reference

---

### 3. SDK Pin in package.json

The `expo` package version is the contract every other Expo module must satisfy.

```json
{
  "name": "my-expo-app",
  "main": "expo/AppEntry.js",
  "scripts": {
    "start": "expo start",
    "android": "expo start --android",
    "ios": "expo start --ios"
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "expo": "~57.0.4",
    "react": "19.2.3",
    "react-native": "0.86.0"
  }
}
```

* **`expo` ~57.0.4** locks the project to SDK 57 - mixing SDK 56 modules with SDK 57 `expo` causes native build failures
* `main: "expo/AppEntry.js"` wires Metro to Expo's bootstrap, which registers your root component
* Default scripts delegate to **`expo start`** so LAN, tunnel, and dev-client flags stay consistent across the team
* After cloning, run `npm install` then `npx expo doctor` to catch version skew before your first build

> **Related:** [Upgrading Expo SDK Versions](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-platform/upgrading-expo-sdk-versions/) - intentional bumps and `expo install --fix`

---

### 4. app.json Identity Fields

These manifest keys define how the binary appears on device home screens and in app stores.

```json
{
  "expo": {
    "name": "My Expo App",
    "slug": "my-expo-app",
    "version": "1.0.0",
    "scheme": "myexpoapp",
    "orientation": "portrait",
    "icon": "./assets/icon.png",
    "splash": {
      "image": "./assets/splash-icon.png",
      "resizeMode": "contain",
      "backgroundColor": "#ffffff"
    },
    "ios": {
      "bundleIdentifier": "com.example.myexpoapp"
    },
    "android": {
      "package": "com.example.myexpoapp"
    }
  }
}
```

* **`name`** is the user-visible label; **`slug`** is the URL-safe Expo project identifier
* **`scheme`** registers a custom URL scheme for deep links (`myexpoapp://`)
* **`bundleIdentifier` / `package`** must be unique per app - changing them after store release creates a new listing
* Icons and splash paths are resolved at **build time**, not fetched over the network

> **Related:** [app.json & app.config.js](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-platform/app-json-and-app-config-js/) - dynamic config and multi-environment manifests

---

### 5. Start the Dev Server

`expo start` launches Metro, prints a QR code, and hot-reloads `App.tsx` on save.

```bash
# Default: LAN URL for devices on the same network
npx expo start
 
# Clear Metro cache after dependency or babel changes
npx expo start --clear
 
# Tunnel when LAN/firewall blocks device ↔ laptop (slower, but reliable)
npx expo start --tunnel
```

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { Pressable, StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
export default function App() {
  const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.container}>
      <Text style={styles.count}>{count}</Text>
      <Pressable style={styles.button} onPress={() => setCount((c) => c + 1)}>
        <Text style={styles.buttonText}>Increment - save to hot reload</Text>
      </Pressable>
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  container: { flex: 1, justifyContent: "center", alignItems: "center", gap: 16 },
  count: { fontSize: 48, fontWeight: "700" },
  button: { backgroundColor: "#2563eb", paddingHorizontal: 20, paddingVertical: 12, borderRadius: 10 },
  buttonText: { color: "#fff", fontWeight: "600" },
});
```

* Metro bundles JavaScript on demand - **Fast Refresh** preserves component state when possible
* Use **`--clear`** when imports resolve incorrectly after adding packages or changing `babel.config.js`
* **LAN** is fastest; **tunnel** trades latency for reachability on corporate Wi-Fi or remote devices
* The terminal also accepts `i` / `a` to boot simulators without retyping flags

> **Related:** [Expo Go vs Development Builds](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-platform/expo-go-vs-development-builds/) - which client opens from this command

---

### 6. Version-Safe Installs with expo install

Always add Expo modules through the CLI so semver ranges match the SDK compatibility table.

```bash
# Adds a module tested against SDK 57
npx expo install expo-camera expo-file-system
 
# After a manual package.json edit or SDK bump - reconcile all Expo deps
npx expo install --fix
```

* **`npx expo install`** reads your pinned `expo` version and chooses compatible native module releases
* Plain **`npm install expo-camera@latest`** can pull a module built for a newer SDK and break iOS/Android compile
* **`--fix`** is the first command to run after upgrading `expo` in `package.json`
* Config plugins for some modules (camera, notifications) also require entries in `app.json` - installing is only step one

> **Related:** [Upgrading Expo SDK Versions](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-platform/upgrading-expo-sdk-versions/) - doctor, changelog, and RN alignment

---

### 7. Preview with Expo Go

Expo Go is a sandbox app with prebuilt native modules - ideal for learning and UI work without compiling native code.

```tsx
import { CameraView, useCameraPermissions } from "expo-camera";
import { Pressable, StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
export default function App() {
  const [permission, requestPermission] = useCameraPermissions();
 
  if (!permission?.granted) {
    return (
      <View style={styles.center}>
        <Text style={styles.message}>Camera access is required.</Text>
        <Pressable style={styles.button} onPress={requestPermission}>
          <Text style={styles.buttonText}>Grant permission</Text>
        </Pressable>
      </View>
    );
  }
 
  return <CameraView style={styles.camera} facing="back" />;
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  center: { flex: 1, justifyContent: "center", alignItems: "center", gap: 12, padding: 24 },
  message: { fontSize: 16, textAlign: "center" },
  button: { backgroundColor: "#2563eb", paddingHorizontal: 20, paddingVertical: 10, borderRadius: 8 },
  buttonText: { color: "#fff", fontWeight: "600" },
  camera: { flex: 1 },
});
```

* Scan the QR from `npx expo start` with **Expo Go** - no Xcode or Android Studio required for this loop
* Expo Go only includes modules shipped in its store build; **custom native code or unreleased modules won't run**
* Permission APIs (`useCameraPermissions`) still execute real OS prompts inside the Expo Go shell
* When you outgrow Expo Go's module set, move to a **development build** - same JS bundle, your own native binary

> **Related:** [Expo Go vs Development Builds](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-platform/expo-go-vs-development-builds/) - decision checklist and `expo-dev-client`

---

## Intermediate Examples

### 8. Environment-Aware app.config.ts

Replace static `app.json` with TypeScript config when bundle IDs, names, or API hosts differ per environment.

```ts
import { ExpoConfig, ConfigContext } from "expo/config";
 
const APP_VARIANT = process.env.APP_VARIANT ?? "development";
 
export default ({ config }: ConfigContext): ExpoConfig => {
  const isProd = APP_VARIANT === "production";
 
  return {
    ...config,
    name: isProd ? "My Expo App" : "My Expo App (Dev)",
    slug: "my-expo-app",
    ios: {
      ...config.ios,
      bundleIdentifier: isProd
        ? "com.example.myexpoapp"
        : "com.example.myexpoapp.dev",
    },
    android: {
      ...config.android,
      package: isProd ? "com.example.myexpoapp" : "com.example.myexpoapp.dev",
    },
    extra: {
      apiUrl: isProd ? "https://api.example.com" : "https://staging.example.com",
      appVariant: APP_VARIANT,
    },
  };
};
```

```bash
APP_VARIANT=development npx expo start
APP_VARIANT=production npx eas build --profile production
```

* **`app.config.ts`** is evaluated at build and prebuild time - not on every Metro reload
* Spread `...config` so Expo CLI merges defaults (plugins, updates) instead of silently dropping them
* Put **non-secret** environment switches in `extra` - read them with `expo-constants` in app code
* Never embed private API keys here; use **EAS environment variables** or CI secrets for sensitive values

> **Related:** [app.json & app.config.js](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-platform/app-json-and-app-config-js/) - config plugins and secrets-safe patterns | [Environments & EAS Environment Variables](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-platform/environments-and-eas-environment-variables/) - dev/staging/prod separation

---

### 9. When Expo Go Is Not Enough

Libraries with custom native code, private native modules, or config plugins not in Expo Go require a development build.

```bash
npx expo install expo-dev-client
npx expo run:ios
# or produce a installable dev client via EAS:
npx eas build --profile development --platform ios
```

```json
{
  "expo": {
    "plugins": [
      [
        "expo-build-properties",
        {
          "ios": { "deploymentTarget": "15.1" },
          "android": { "minSdkVersion": 24 }
        }
      ]
    ]
  }
}
```

* **`expo-dev-client`** replaces Expo Go as the native shell while keeping Metro fast refresh
* **`npx expo run:ios` / `run:android`** generates native projects locally via prebuild, then compiles a dev client
* **Config plugins** mutate native projects at prebuild - they are ignored by Expo Go even if JavaScript imports succeed
* Stay on the managed workflow: commit `app.config.ts` and let EAS Build run prebuild in CI instead of hand-editing `ios/` when possible

> **Related:** [Expo Go vs Development Builds](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-platform/expo-go-vs-development-builds/) - feature matrix | [Managed to Bare Migration](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-platform/managed-to-bare-migration/) - keeping upgrade paths when native folders exist

---

### 10. Link an Expo Account and EAS Project

Associating the app with an Expo project unlocks cloud builds, submit, updates, and org-scoped secrets.

```bash
npx expo login
npx eas init
```

```json
{
  "expo": {
    "name": "My Expo App",
    "slug": "my-expo-app",
    "owner": "my-org",
    "extra": {
      "eas": {
        "projectId": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

```tsx
import Constants from "expo-constants";
import { Text, View } from "react-native";
 
export default function App() {
  const projectId = Constants.expoConfig?.extra?.eas?.projectId;
 
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1, justifyContent: "center", alignItems: "center" }}>
      <Text>EAS project: {projectId ?? "not linked"}</Text>
    </View>
  );
}
```

* **`eas init`** creates or links a project under your Expo account and writes `extra.eas.projectId`
* **`owner`** set to an organization slug routes builds and credentials to the team, not a personal account
* The **projectId** is stable across bundle ID changes - EAS services key off it, not `slug` alone
* Link early in greenfield projects so preview, staging, and production build profiles share one credential store

> **Related:** [Expo Account, Projects & Permissions](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-platform/expo-account-projects-and-permissions/) - roles and multi-app governance | [Environments & EAS Environment Variables](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-platform/environments-and-eas-environment-variables/) - per-environment secrets

Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-platform/highlights-summary/

# Expo Platform Highlights Summary

Every highlight bullet from the 10 pages in this section, gathered on one page and grouped by the page it came from.

Highlights / Expo Platform Highlights Summary

* Expo is a platform layer on React Native - you still write RN components, Expo handles native project wiring
* Pin SDK 57 explicitly with --template default@sdk-57 - bare @latest may scaffold SDK 54 during the transition
* Static app.json for tooling edits; app.config.ts when you need env branches and typed config
* Expo Go is a fixed native binary - only its preinstalled native modules are callable from your JS
* The expo package installs ExpoModulesCore native infrastructure at app launch
* EAS provides three built-in environments: development, preview, and production

## [Expo Platform Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-platform/expo-platform-basics/)

* Expo is a platform layer on React Native - you still write RN components, Expo handles native project wiring
* The managed workflow keeps ios/ and android/ generated; you opt into native folders only when needed
* Pin `expo` ~57.0.4 in package.json - every Expo module version is validated against that SDK
* `npx expo install` resolves compatible semver ranges; plain npm install can drift from the SDK matrix
* Expo Go is fastest for learning; custom native modules require a development build with expo-dev-client
* app.config.ts can branch on APP\_VARIANT without committing secrets to app.json
* Linking an EAS projectId early keeps builds, updates, and environment variables scoped to one Expo project

## [create-expo-app Quickstart](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-platform/create-expo-app-quickstart/)

* Pin SDK 57 explicitly with --template default@sdk-57 - bare @latest may scaffold SDK 54 during the transition
* default template ships Expo Router, TypeScript, and the recommended Expo CLI scripts
* Verify the pin in package.json: expo ~57.0.4 and react-native 0.86.0
* Run npx expo-doctor after scaffold to catch version skew before you write feature code
* bare-minimum runs prebuild immediately - choose it only when you need android/ and ios/ on day one

## [app.json & app.config.js](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-platform/app-json-and-app-config-js/)

* Static app.json for tooling edits; app.config.ts when you need env branches and typed config
* EXPO\_PUBLIC\_ vars inline at bundle time - never put secrets there
* extra passes non-secret runtime config via Constants.expoConfig.extra
* npx expo config --type public shows exactly what ships in the client bundle
* Config plugins in app.config mutate native projects at prebuild/EAS build time

## [Expo Go vs Development Builds](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-platform/expo-go-vs-development-builds/)

* Expo Go is a fixed native binary - only its preinstalled native modules are callable from your JS
* Development builds include expo-dev-client and YOUR native dependencies
* Switch before custom native modules, push credentials, or universal/app links
* npx expo install expo-dev-client then eas build --profile development
* JS hot reload works in both; native code changes require a new native build

## [Expo Modules Core](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-platform/expo-modules-core/)

* The expo package installs ExpoModulesCore native infrastructure at app launch
* requireNativeModule resolves JSI bindings first, then falls back to legacy bridge proxies
* registerRootComponent wires AppRegistry and dev-only Fast Refresh helpers
* NativeModule and SharedObject extend EventEmitter over JSI - same API on iOS and Android
* Works in managed, bare, and brownfield apps once the native entry point is configured

## [Environments & EAS Environment Variables](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-platform/environments-and-eas-environment-variables/)

* EAS provides three built-in environments: development, preview, and production
* Map eas.json build profiles to EAS environments with the `environment` field
* Only `EXPO_PUBLIC_` variables are safe to embed in client JavaScript - treat them as public
* `eas env:pull` syncs cloud variables to `.env.local` for local dev without committing secrets
* SDK 55+ requires `--environment` on `eas update` so OTA bundles match build-time config
* Secret visibility variables are for build-time tooling (NPM tokens), not client-side API keys

## [Upgrading Expo SDK Versions](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-platform/upgrading-expo-sdk-versions/)

* Upgrade one SDK version at a time - never skip majors in a single PR
* `npx expo install --fix` realigns every Expo module to the SDK compatibility matrix
* `npx expo-doctor` catches unmet peer deps, config plugin drift, and New Architecture mismatches
* CNG projects delete ios/ and android/ after a bump - EAS Build regenerates them via prebuild
* SDK 57 targets React Native 0.86 with no intentional breaking changes from 0.85
* Rebuild development clients after every native-affecting SDK upgrade

## [Managed to Bare Migration](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-platform/managed-to-bare-migration/)

* Managed vs bare workflow is deprecated - Continuous Native Generation (CNG) is the modern model
* CNG generates ios/ and android/ on demand; you maintain app.config + config plugins, not native diffs
* Committing native folders opts out of automatic EAS prebuild - upgrades require manual native merges
* SDK 57 runs expo prebuild --clean by default; pass --no-clean to layer incremental changes
* Migrate native customizations to config plugins before deleting hand-edited native code
* Bare RN CLI projects can adopt prebuild without losing Expo modules or EAS services

## [Expo Account, Projects & Permissions](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-platform/expo-account-projects-and-permissions/)

* Personal accounts suit solo work; organizations enable team RBAC and shared credentials
* Four org roles: Owner, Admin, Developer, Viewer - least privilege for day-to-day work
* Set expo.owner in app.json so builds and credentials land under the correct account
* extra.eas.projectId is the stable identifier for EAS Build, Update, and env vars
* Account-wide environment variables share tooling tokens across multiple apps
* Project transfers require Owner/Admin on both source and destination accounts

## [Expo Platform Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-platform/best-practices/)

* Pin SDK at scaffold time with default@sdk-57 and verify with expo-doctor
* Use app.config.ts and EXPO\_PUBLIC\_ for env - never commit secrets to extra
* Adopt expo-dev-client when you need native modules beyond Expo Go
* Let npx expo install resolve SDK-compatible native dependency versions
* Gitignore ios/ and android/ under CNG; regenerate with prebuild on upgrades
* Scope EAS projects, credentials, and env vars per app under an organization
