Dokumen: Expo Router Fundamentals Best Practices
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/best-practices/

# Expo Router Fundamentals Best Practices

A condensed summary of the 25 most important best practices drawn from every page in this section.

Highlights / Expo Router Fundamentals Best Practices

* Route files re-export feature screens - no business logic beside \_layout.tsx
* One root \_layout.tsx owns providers; nested layouts handle stack/tab chrome only
* Enable experiments.typedRoutes and run tsc --noEmit when app/ changes
* Auth gates wait for session hydration - then Redirect or router.replace, never push
* Prefer href objects and centralized builders over stringly-typed router.push paths
* Validate URL params with Zod at screen entry - typed routes do not secure deep links

1. **Scaffold with Expo Router from day one:** `default@sdk-57` sets `main: "expo-router/entry"` - retrofitting file-based routing costs more than starting with `app/`.
2. **Install router through Expo:** `npx expo install expo-router` pins versions compatible with SDK 57's React Navigation peers - manual npm ranges cause native/JS skew.
3. **Treat file names as URLs:** `app/settings.tsx` → `/settings` - design paths for deep links and analytics before folders proliferate.
4. **Keep route files thin:** Under ~20 lines; re-export screens from `features/<name>/` - reviewers grep `app/` to understand navigation, not business rules.
5. **One root `_layout.tsx` for providers:** Theme, query client, auth session, and error boundaries mount once - never duplicate `QueryClientProvider` in tab layouts.
6. **Nested layouts own chrome only:** Stack headers, tab icons, drawer labels - not data fetching. `useFocusEffect` refetch belongs in screens.
7. **Use route groups for structure:** `(auth)`, `(app)`, `(tabs)`, `(modals)` - parentheses organize without polluting URLs.
8. **Private folders use underscore prefix:** `_components/` colocated with layouts is not routable - never create accidental `/components` screens.
9. **Index routes for list hubs:** `orders/index.tsx` lists; `orders/[id].tsx` details - predictable REST-like paths aid linking.
10. **Single redirect hub at `app/index.tsx`:** Auth and role routing live in one place - avoid duplicate `/` index files across groups.
11. **Wait for session hydration before redirect:** Show splash or spinner while SecureStore reads - premature `<Redirect>` causes login/home flicker.
12. **`router.replace` after login and logout:** Preserves back-stack hygiene - `push` leaves credential screens behind swipe-back.
13. **Guard authenticated groups in layout:** `(app)/_layout.tsx` redirects guests - deep links to `/settings` must not bypass auth.
14. **Prefer `Link` for declarative navigation:** Lists, inline links, and prefetch - reserve `router.push` for post-async side effects.
15. **Centralize href builders:** `orderDetailHref(id)` in `navigation/hrefs.ts` - one typo fix updates every feature callsite.
16. **Enable typed routes early:** `experiments: { typedRoutes: true }` in `app.config.ts` - invalid paths fail `tsc`, not production.
17. **Validate params with Zod at runtime:** `useLocalSearchParams()` input is untrusted from deep links and push payloads - types alone are insufficient.
18. **Nest stacks inside tabs for drill-down:** One tab pushes detail screens while the tab bar stays - cap nesting at drawer → tabs → stack.
19. **Hide non-tab routes with `href: null`:** Helper screens stay navigable via `router.push` without cluttering the tab bar.
20. **Modal routes are explicit:** `(modals)` group or `presentation: "modal"` - half-overlays break Android back and accessibility.
21. **Declare `scheme` before shipping deep links:** `app.config.ts` scheme and associated domains pair with file paths - test Maestro flows per critical URL.
22. **Run `tsc --noEmit` when `app/` changes:** Regenerated `.expo/types` catches stale hrefs - add to CI alongside `expo-doctor`.
23. **Align `app/` with feature slices:** `features/orders/` maps to `app/(tabs)/orders/` - import rule: routes import features, not the reverse.
24. **Document non-standard patterns in ADRs:** Modals as overlays, custom tab bars, or React Navigation escape hatches - before the third squad copies them.
25. **Revisit route map at ~30 screens:** Flatten deep trees, split modals, and audit duplicate paths - schedule before import cycles and duplicate `/` routes force a rewrite.

## FAQs

When should we adopt Expo Router over manual React Navigation?

* **Default for new SDK 57 greenfield apps** - template, linking, and typed routes align.
* Brownfield apps with heavy custom navigators may stay on React Navigation until a migration sprint is scheduled.
* See [ADR: Navigation Library Choice](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/adr-navigation-library-choice/).

Where should business logic live?

In `features/<name>/` - hooks, API, and screen UI. `app/` files re-export only. Global providers live in root `_layout.tsx` or `app-providers.tsx`.

How do we enforce thin route files in review?

* Reject PRs with hooks or fetch calls in `app/*.tsx` unless auth redirect guards.
* Pair with [Navigation & Routing Rules](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/navigation-and-routing-rules/) Tier 1 checklist.

Tabs or drawer for primary navigation?

* **Tabs** for 3–5 daily destinations on phones.
* **Drawer wrapping tabs** when you have 6+ sections or tablet-first IA.
* Avoid competing drawer and tab patterns for the same destinations.

How do typed routes fit with CI?

```bash
npx expo start --non-interactive &
npm run typecheck
```

Ensure `.expo/types` generates before `tsc` in CI when `app/` changes.

Dokumen: Expo Router Basics
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/expo-router-basics/

# Expo Router Basics

10 examples to get you started with Expo Router - 7 basic and 3 intermediate. File-based routes, `_layout.tsx`, and the mental model vs React Navigation.

Highlights / Expo Router Basics

* File names in app/ map to URLs - settings.tsx becomes /settings without a central route table
* app/\_layout.tsx is the root navigator: wrap providers once, then export Stack, Tabs, or Slot
* Expo Router is React Navigation under the hood - you gain file-based routes, not a different renderer
* main: expo-router/entry in package.json wires Metro to the router bootstrap instead of App.tsx
* Dynamic segments [id].tsx and catch-all [...slug].tsx power entity detail and CMS-style URLs
* Thin route files re-export feature screens - logic belongs in features/, not beside \_layout.tsx

## Prerequisites

Scaffold an SDK 57 app with the default template - it ships Expo Router, TypeScript, and the recommended entry point.

```bash
npx create-expo-app@latest MyRouterApp --template default@sdk-57
cd MyRouterApp
npm install
npx expo install expo-router
```

Confirm the router entry and SDK pin:

```json
{
  "main": "expo-router/entry",
  "dependencies": {
    "expo": "~57.0.4",
    "expo-router": "~6.0.8",
    "react": "19.2.3",
    "react-native": "0.86.0"
  }
}
```

> **Tooling:** These examples target **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4), **React Native 0.86.0**, and **React 19.2.3**.

---

## Basic Examples

### 1. File-Based Routes Map to URLs

Every file under `app/` becomes a route segment. The file name is the path - no central `linking` config required for standard screens.

```text
app/
├── index.tsx           → /
├── settings.tsx        → /settings
├── profile/
│   └── index.tsx       → /profile
└── orders/
    ├── index.tsx       → /orders
    └── [id].tsx        → /orders/:id
```

```tsx
// app/settings.tsx
import { Text, View } from "react-native";
 
export default function SettingsScreen() {
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1, padding: 16 }}>
      <Text>Settings</Text>
    </View>
  );
}
```

* **`app/index.tsx`** is the `/` route - the app's default landing screen
* **Nested folders** add path segments (`app/profile/index.tsx` → `/profile`)
* **`[id].tsx`** is a dynamic segment - access `id` via `useLocalSearchParams()`
* Route files should stay **thin** - import screens from `features/` when logic grows

> **Related:** [Route Groups & Organizing `app/`](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/route-groups-and-organizing-app/) - `(auth)` and `(tabs)` without changing URLs | [../expo-rules/navigation-and-routing-rules/navigation-and-routing-rules.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/navigation-and-routing-rules/) - team routing conventions

---

### 2. Root `_layout.tsx` Owns the Navigator

`_layout.tsx` files define navigators (Stack, Tabs, Drawer) for their directory. The root layout wraps global providers and exports the top-level navigator.

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
import { StatusBar } from "expo-status-bar";
 
export default function RootLayout() {
  return (
    <>
      <StatusBar style="auto" />
      <Stack>
        <Stack.Screen name="index" options={{ title: "Home" }} />
        <Stack.Screen name="settings" options={{ title: "Settings" }} />
      </Stack>
    </>
  );
}
```

* **`Stack` from `expo-router`** is a file-based wrapper around `@react-navigation/native-stack`
* **`<Stack.Screen name="settings">`** configures the screen that matches `app/settings.tsx`
* Child routes **inherit** the parent navigator - `app/orders/[id].tsx` pushes onto the root stack unless a nested `_layout.tsx` says otherwise
* Mount **providers once** here (theme, query client, auth) - not in every nested layout

> **Related:** [Stack Navigation](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/stack-navigation/) - headers, `screenOptions`, and push/pop | [../architecture-design/feature-sliced-design-for-rn/feature-sliced-design-for-rn.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/feature-sliced-design-for-rn/) - keep `app/` as the FSD app layer

---

### 3. Mental Model: Files vs React Navigation Config

React Navigation builds a **navigator tree in code**. Expo Router builds the **same tree from the filesystem** - you trade imperative `createNativeStackNavigator` for declarative file names.

```tsx
// React Navigation (imperative tree)
const Stack = createNativeStackNavigator();
 
function AppNavigator() {
  return (
    <Stack.Navigator>
      <Stack.Screen name="Home" component={HomeScreen} />
      <Stack.Screen name="Settings" component={SettingsScreen} />
    </Stack.Navigator>
  );
}
```

```text
// Expo Router (filesystem tree)
app/
├── _layout.tsx      → Stack navigator for this folder
├── index.tsx        → "Home" screen (name derived from file)
└── settings.tsx     → "Settings" screen
```

| Concept | React Navigation | Expo Router |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Screen registration | `<Stack.Screen name="Settings" />` | `app/settings.tsx` exists |
| Nested navigator | Navigator inside a screen | `app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx` |
| Deep link path | Manual `linking` config | File path ≈ URL path |
| Screen options | `options` prop on `Screen` | `export const options` or `<Stack.Screen options>` |

* Expo Router **is** React Navigation - `useNavigation`, `useFocusEffect`, and header APIs still apply
* File names become **route names** - `settings.tsx` registers as `"settings"` in the stack
* Brownfield apps can adopt Expo Router incrementally - see [ADR: Navigation Library Choice](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/adr-navigation-library-choice/)

> **Related:** [Link & href](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/link-and-href/) - declarative navigation without memorizing route names | [Typed Routes](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/typed-routes/) - compile-time path safety

---

### 4. `expo-router/entry` Bootstrap

`package.json` `main` points Metro at Expo Router's entry instead of `expo/AppEntry.js` or a hand-written `App.tsx`.

```json
{
  "main": "expo-router/entry",
  "scripts": {
    "start": "expo start",
    "android": "expo start --android",
    "ios": "expo start --ios"
  }
}
```

```tsx
// You do NOT need App.tsx - the entry loads app/_layout.tsx automatically
// app/_layout.tsx is the true application root
import { Slot } from "expo-router";
 
export default function RootLayout() {
  return <Slot />;
}
```

* **`expo-router/entry`** registers the root component, linking handlers, and error boundaries
* **`Slot`** renders the matched child route - use it when you want a layout **without** forcing a Stack/Tabs wrapper
* Removing `main: "expo-router/entry"` breaks routing - the bundler will not discover `app/` routes
* `npx expo install expo-router` ensures the router version matches SDK 57's React Navigation peers

> **Related:** [../project-setup/project-setup-basics/project-setup-basics.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/project-setup-basics/) - SDK pin and default template layout

---

### 5. Dynamic Segments and Params

Bracket syntax creates dynamic URL segments. Read params with `useLocalSearchParams` - validate before use.

```tsx
// app/orders/[id].tsx
import { useLocalSearchParams } from "expo-router";
import { Text, View } from "react-native";
 
export default function OrderDetailScreen() {
  const { id } = useLocalSearchParams<{ id: string }>();
 
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1, padding: 16 }}>
      <Text>Order #{id}</Text>
    </View>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// Navigate programmatically (imperative)
import { router } from "expo-router";
 
router.push({ pathname: "/orders/[id]", params: { id: "42" } });
```

* **`[id]`** matches one segment - `/orders/42` sets `id: "42"` (always strings from URLs)
* **Multiple dynamics** - `app/users/[userId]/posts/[postId].tsx` exposes both params
* **Validate params** at the feature boundary with Zod - URLs are untrusted input
* Prefer **path segments** over query strings for entity IDs - clearer deep links and analytics

> **Related:** [Typed Routes](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/typed-routes/) - generated `Href` types for param-safe navigation | [../expo-rules/navigation-and-routing-rules/navigation-and-routing-rules.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/navigation-and-routing-rules/) - param validation rules

---

### 6. Index Routes as Folder Defaults

`index.tsx` inside a folder is the default screen for that path segment - like `index.html` on the web.

```text
app/
├── index.tsx              → /
└── orders/
    ├── _layout.tsx        → Stack for /orders/*
    ├── index.tsx          → /orders (list)
    └── [id].tsx           → /orders/:id (detail)
```

```tsx
// app/orders/index.tsx
import { Link } from "expo-router";
import { Text, View } from "react-native";
 
const ORDERS = [{ id: "1" }, { id: "2" }];
 
export default function OrdersListScreen() {
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1, padding: 16, gap: 12 }}>
      {ORDERS.map((order) => (
        <Link key={order.id} href={{ pathname: "/orders/[id]", params: { id: order.id } }}>
          Order #{order.id}
        </Link>
      ))}
    </View>
  );
}
```

* **`/orders`** resolves to `orders/index.tsx`, not `orders.tsx` - pick one pattern per feature
* Nested **`_layout.tsx`** wraps all siblings in that folder (`index.tsx` and `[id].tsx`)
* Use index routes for **list hubs**; dynamic segments for **entity detail** - predictable REST-like URLs

> **Related:** [Redirects & Index Routes](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/redirects-and-index-routes/) - default landing and auth-gated entry | [Link & href](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/link-and-href/) - `Link` vs `router.push`

---

### 7. Screen Options from Route Files

Export `options` from a route file or configure screens in `_layout.tsx` - both feed React Navigation's screen options API.

```tsx
// app/settings.tsx
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
import { Text, View } from "react-native";
 
export const options = {
  title: "Settings",
  headerLargeTitle: true,
};
 
export default function SettingsScreen() {
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1, padding: 16 }}>
      <Text>Settings</Text>
    </View>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx (alternative - centralize chrome)
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
 
export default function RootLayout() {
  return (
    <Stack
      screenOptions={{
        headerShown: true,
        animation: "slide_from_right",
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

* **`screenOptions`** on the navigator sets defaults; per-file **`options`** overrides for one screen
* **`Stack.Screen name="settings" options={{...}}`** in `_layout.tsx` is equivalent to exporting `options` from `settings.tsx`
* Dynamic titles use **`useNavigation().setOptions()`** inside the screen when data loads
* Header buttons and modals are configured the same way as React Navigation - Expo Router forwards the API

> **Related:** [Stack Navigation](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/stack-navigation/) - cookbook for headers, gestures, and presentation modes

---

## Intermediate Examples

### 8. Nested Stack Inside Tabs

The default SDK 57 template nests stacks under tabs - each tab folder can push detail screens without losing the tab bar.

```text
app/
├── _layout.tsx
└── (tabs)/
    ├── _layout.tsx        → Tabs navigator
    ├── index.tsx          → Home tab
    └── orders/
        ├── _layout.tsx    → Stack inside the Orders tab
        ├── index.tsx      → /orders list (tab root)
        └── [id].tsx       → /orders/:id (pushed, tab bar stays)
```

```tsx
// app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx
import { Tabs } from "expo-router";
import { Ionicons } from "@expo/vector-icons";
 
export default function TabLayout() {
  return (
    <Tabs screenOptions={{ headerShown: false }}>
      <Tabs.Screen
        name="index"
        options={{ title: "Home", tabBarIcon: ({ color }) => <Ionicons name="home" size={24} color={color} /> }}
      />
      <Tabs.Screen
        name="orders"
        options={{ title: "Orders", tabBarIcon: ({ color }) => <Ionicons name="list" size={24} color={color} /> }}
      />
    </Tabs>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// app/(tabs)/orders/_layout.tsx
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
 
export default function OrdersStackLayout() {
  return (
    <Stack>
      <Stack.Screen name="index" options={{ title: "Orders" }} />
      <Stack.Screen name="[id]" options={{ title: "Order" }} />
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

* **Tabs at `(tabs)/_layout.tsx`** - each immediate child folder or file becomes a tab
* **Stack inside `orders/`** - pushes `[id]` on top of `orders/index` while the tab bar remains visible
* Parentheses in **`(tabs)`** are a route group - they organize files without adding `/tabs` to the URL
* Deep nesting increases mental load - flatten when a tab has only one screen

> **Related:** [Tabs & Drawers](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/tabs-and-drawers/) - tab bar styling, drawer composition | [Route Groups & Organizing `app/`](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/route-groups-and-organizing-app/) - `(tabs)` conventions

---

### 9. Route Groups for Auth vs App Shell

Route groups `(auth)` and `(app)` separate login flows from the main shell without changing URL paths.

```text
app/
├── _layout.tsx
├── index.tsx              → Redirect hub (see redirects article)
├── (auth)/
│   ├── _layout.tsx        → Stack for login/signup
│   ├── login.tsx          → /login
│   └── register.tsx       → /register
└── (app)/
    ├── _layout.tsx          → Authenticated shell (tabs or stack)
    └── (tabs)/
        ├── _layout.tsx
        └── index.tsx        → / (when signed in)
```

```tsx
// app/(auth)/_layout.tsx
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
 
export default function AuthLayout() {
  return (
    <Stack screenOptions={{ headerShown: false }}>
      <Stack.Screen name="login" />
      <Stack.Screen name="register" />
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

* **`(auth)` and `(app)`** do not appear in URLs - `/login` not `/auth/login`
* Split layouts let you apply **different transitions and headers** per flow
* Auth gates usually live in root `_layout.tsx` or `index.tsx` with `<Redirect />` - see the redirects cookbook
* Keep redirect logic **minimal** in layouts - session state comes from a provider, not fetches in `_layout.tsx`

> **Related:** [Redirects & Index Routes](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/redirects-and-index-routes/) - auth-gated entry | [../auth-session/mobile-auth-basics/mobile-auth-basics.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/mobile-auth-basics/) - session providers

---

### 10. Thin Routes Re-Exporting Feature Screens

Production apps keep `app/` as a routing layer - screens, hooks, and API calls live in `features/`.

```text
features/
└── orders/
    ├── index.ts
    ├── ui/
    │   ├── OrdersListScreen.tsx
    │   └── OrderDetailScreen.tsx
    └── model/
        └── useOrder.ts
 
app/
└── (tabs)/
    └── orders/
        ├── index.tsx      → re-export only
        └── [id].tsx       → re-export only
```

```tsx
// features/orders/index.ts
export { OrdersListScreen } from "./ui/OrdersListScreen";
export { OrderDetailScreen } from "./ui/OrderDetailScreen";
```

```tsx
// app/(tabs)/orders/index.tsx
export { OrdersListScreen as default } from "@/features/orders";
```

```tsx
// app/(tabs)/orders/[id].tsx
export { OrderDetailScreen as default } from "@/features/orders";
```

* Route files stay **under ~20 lines** - easy to grep and review in PRs
* Features remain **testable without the router** - import screens directly in RNTL tests
* One **public export per feature** via `index.ts` - no cross-feature deep imports
* Aligns with [Feature-Sliced Design](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/feature-sliced-design-for-rn/) - `app/` is the app layer, not a god folder

> **Related:** [Expo Router Fundamentals Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/best-practices/) - full section summary | [../project-setup/folder-structure-for-features/folder-structure-for-features.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/folder-structure-for-features/) - scaling past the starter tree

---

> **Stack versions:** This page was written for **React 19.2.3**, **React Native 0.86.0**, and **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4).

# Expo Router Highlights Summary

Every highlight bullet from the 8 pages in this section, gathered on one page and grouped by the page it came from.

Highlights / Expo Router Highlights Summary

* File names in app/ map to URLs - settings.tsx becomes /settings without a central route table
* Stack from expo-router wraps native-stack - file names become pushable screens automatically
* Tabs from expo-router maps each child file or folder to a tab - icons live in \_layout.tsx
* Parentheses folders are route groups - they organize files without adding URL segments
* Link is the default navigation primitive - it preserves accessibility and web-like href semantics
* experiments.typedRoutes: true generates .expo/types/router.d.ts from your app/ tree

## [Expo Router Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/expo-router-basics/)

* File names in app/ map to URLs - settings.tsx becomes /settings without a central route table
* app/\_layout.tsx is the root navigator: wrap providers once, then export Stack, Tabs, or Slot
* Expo Router is React Navigation under the hood - you gain file-based routes, not a different renderer
* main: expo-router/entry in package.json wires Metro to the router bootstrap instead of App.tsx
* Dynamic segments [id].tsx and catch-all [...slug].tsx power entity detail and CMS-style URLs
* Thin route files re-export feature screens - logic belongs in features/, not beside \_layout.tsx

## [Stack Navigation](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/stack-navigation/)

* Stack from expo-router wraps native-stack - file names become pushable screens automatically
* screenOptions on \_layout.tsx sets team-wide header defaults; per-route options override
* presentation: modal and headerShown: false are the two most common stack tweaks in production
* useNavigation().setOptions updates titles after async data loads without remounting
* Nested stacks under tabs keep the tab bar visible while detail screens push on top
* Android hardware back and iOS swipe-back follow React Navigation stack rules - test both

## [Tabs & Drawers](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/tabs-and-drawers/)

* Tabs from expo-router maps each child file or folder to a tab - icons live in \_layout.tsx
* Nest a Stack inside a tab folder when that section needs list → detail push without losing the tab bar
* Drawer requires @react-navigation/drawer - install with npx expo install and wrap in app/(drawer)/
* href: null hides a route from the tab bar while keeping it addressable via router.push
* Lazy tabs mount on first visit - prefetch heavy tabs with Link prefetch when UX demands
* Three-level nesting (drawer → tabs → stack) is the practical ceiling before flattening

## [Route Groups & Organizing `app/`](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/route-groups-and-organizing-app/)

* Parentheses folders are route groups - they organize files without adding URL segments
* (auth), (app), (tabs), and (modals) are the four groups most production apps need
* Leading underscore marks private files - \_components/ is not a route
* Multiple groups at the same level compose URLs from non-group segments only
* Split auth and app shells with separate \_layout.tsx files per group
* Mirror features/ in src/ - app/ stays a thin routing map, not a feature dump

## [Link & href](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/link-and-href/)

* Link is the default navigation primitive - it preserves accessibility and web-like href semantics
* href accepts strings or objects with pathname and params - prefer objects for dynamic routes
* router.push, replace, and back are imperative - use after mutations and auth redirects
* Link prefetch loads lazy routes early - valuable for heavy tab screens and detail views
* asChild merges Link behavior into Pressable or custom components without wrapper views
* Centralize href builders in routes.ts - features import orderDetailHref(id) not raw strings

## [Typed Routes](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/typed-routes/)

* experiments.typedRoutes: true generates .expo/types/router.d.ts from your app/ tree
* Href and Route types catch invalid pathnames at compile time - not at runtime in production
* Dynamic routes require params objects - /orders/[id] needs { id: string } in the href
* Run tsc --noEmit in CI after every app/ restructure - generated types drift silently otherwise
* Central href builders return Href - one typo fix updates every callsite
* Validate URL params with Zod at screen entry - types do not prove runtime deep-link input

## [Redirects & Index Routes](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/redirects-and-index-routes/)

* app/index.tsx is the / route - use it as a redirect hub, not a 200-line home screen
* Redirect component declaratively sends users based on session - replace for auth transitions
* router.replace after login prevents swipe-back to credential screens
* Index routes inside folders default that path segment - orders/index.tsx is /orders
* Never duplicate index.tsx across route groups - both (auth) and (app) cannot own /
* Gate on session hydration first - redirecting before AsyncStorage/SecureStore reads causes flicker

## [Expo Router Fundamentals Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/best-practices/)

* Route files re-export feature screens - no business logic beside \_layout.tsx
* One root \_layout.tsx owns providers; nested layouts handle stack/tab chrome only
* Enable experiments.typedRoutes and run tsc --noEmit when app/ changes
* Auth gates wait for session hydration - then Redirect or router.replace, never push
* Prefer href objects and centralized builders over stringly-typed router.push paths
* Validate URL params with Zod at screen entry - typed routes do not secure deep links

Dokumen: Link & href
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/link-and-href/

# Link & href

Declarative navigation and prefetch-friendly links. `Link` maps to anchor-like navigation on web and accessible press targets on native - `router` handles imperative flows after side effects.

Highlights / Link & href

* Link is the default navigation primitive - it preserves accessibility and web-like href semantics
* href accepts strings or objects with pathname and params - prefer objects for dynamic routes
* router.push, replace, and back are imperative - use after mutations and auth redirects
* Link prefetch loads lazy routes early - valuable for heavy tab screens and detail views
* asChild merges Link behavior into Pressable or custom components without wrapper views
* Centralize href builders in routes.ts - features import orderDetailHref(id) not raw strings

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```tsx
import { Link, router, type Href } from "expo-router";
import { Pressable, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
// String href - static paths only
<Link href="/settings">Settings</Link>
 
// Object href - dynamic segments (preferred)
<Link href={{ pathname: "/orders/[id]", params: { id: "42" } }}>
  Order 42
</Link>
 
// Imperative after mutation
router.replace("/(tabs)");
 
// Prefetch on hover/focus (web) or manually
<Link href="/orders" prefetch />
```

```ts
// src/navigation/routes.ts
import type { Href } from "expo-router";
 
export const routes = {
  home: "/" as Href,
  settings: "/settings" as Href,
  orderDetail: (id: string): Href => ({
    pathname: "/orders/[id]",
    params: { id },
  }),
};
```

**When to reach for this:**

* **`Link`** - list rows, inline text links, tab-adjacent navigation, SEO-friendly web anchors
* **`router.push`** - navigate after form submit, scan QR, or timer callback
* **`router.replace`** - post-login, post-logout, onboarding completion
* **`prefetch`** - screens with heavy bundles or slow data waterfalls

## Working Example

List screen with `Link`, custom `Pressable` via `asChild`, imperative navigation, and centralized href builders.

```ts
// src/navigation/routes.ts
import type { Href } from "expo-router";
 
export function orderDetailHref(id: string): Href {
  return { pathname: "/orders/[id]", params: { id } };
}
 
export function settingsHref(): Href {
  return "/settings";
}
```

```tsx
// features/orders/ui/OrdersListScreen.tsx
import { Link, router } from "expo-router";
import { Pressable, Text, View } from "react-native";
import { orderDetailHref } from "@/navigation/routes";
 
const ORDERS = [
  { id: "101", label: "Widget shipment" },
  { id: "102", label: "Replacement part" },
];
 
export function OrdersListScreen() {
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1, padding: 16, gap: 12 }}>
      {ORDERS.map((order) => (
        <Link key={order.id} href={orderDetailHref(order.id)} prefetch asChild>
          <Pressable style={{ padding: 12, backgroundColor: "#f1f5f9", borderRadius: 8 }}>
            <Text>{order.label}</Text>
          </Pressable>
        </Link>
      ))}
 
      <Link href="/settings">Account settings</Link>
 
      <Pressable
        onPress={() => router.push(orderDetailHref("draft"))}
        accessibilityRole="button"
      >
        <Text>Create draft (imperative)</Text>
      </Pressable>
    </View>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// After successful form submit - replace avoids back stack to form
import { router } from "expo-router";
 
async function onSubmit() {
  await saveProfile();
  router.replace("/(tabs)/profile");
}
```

```tsx
// Dismiss modal flow
import { router } from "expo-router";
 
function closeModal() {
  if (router.canGoBack()) {
    router.back();
  } else {
    router.replace("/");
  }
}
```

## Deep Dive

### `href` shapes

| Form | Example | Typed routes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| String path | `"/settings"` | Static routes |
| Object | `{ pathname: "/orders/[id]", params: { id } }` | Dynamic routes |
| Relative | `"./details"` | Sibling within folder |
| External | `"https://expo.dev"` | Opens browser / external app |

```tsx
// Relative navigation within app/orders/
<Link href="./[id]" params={{ id: "5" }}>Relative</Link>
```

* **Params are always strings** when parsed from URLs - coerce numbers in the screen
* **Query params** - `href="/search?q=shoes"` or `params: { q: "shoes" }` depending on route shape
* Enable **typed routes** so invalid `pathname` values fail at compile time - see [Typed Routes](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/typed-routes/)

### `Link` vs `router`

| API | Style | Best for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<Link href>` | Declarative | Lists, inline navigation, prefetch |
| `router.push` | Imperative | Post-async, programmatic redirects |
| `router.replace` | Imperative | Auth transitions, no back |
| `router.back` | Imperative | Cancel, modal dismiss |
| `router.navigate` | Imperative | Go to route if exists, else push (web-like) |

```tsx
// Link props that matter in production
<Link
  href="/orders"
  prefetch                    // preload route module
  replace                     // replace history instead of push
  push                        // force push even when replace might default
  asChild                     // merge into child Pressable
  disabled={!isReady}
/>
```

### Prefetch behavior

* **`prefetch` on `Link`** - Expo Router loads the target route's JavaScript bundle ahead of navigation
* Most impactful for **lazy tabs** and **heavy screens** with large dependency trees
* On web, prefetch may hook **focus/hover** depending on version - verify in your target SDK
* Do not prefetch **auth-gated** routes before session is known - wasted bandwidth and flicker

### `asChild` pattern

```tsx
<Link href="/settings" asChild>
  <Pressable style={styles.row}>
    <Text>Settings</Text>
  </Pressable>
</Link>
```

* Child must **forward props** (`onPress`, `href` on web) - use `Pressable` or custom components that spread props
* Avoid nesting **buttons inside buttons** - one pressable per `Link`
* Set **`accessibilityRole="link"`** on web; `Pressable` inherits link behavior from `Link`

### Centralized href builders

```ts
// packages/navigation/src/hrefs.ts (monorepo)
export const orderDetailHref = (id: string) =>
  ({ pathname: "/orders/[id]", params: { id } }) as const;
```

* One module prevents **typo drift** across features
* White-label apps share **`packages/navigation`** when route shapes match
* Pair with **Zod** validating params at screen entry - href builders do not validate runtime input

## Gotchas

* **String concatenation for dynamic paths** - `href={'/orders/' + id}` bypasses typed routes and breaks when segments change. **Fix:** Object form or `orderDetailHref(id)`.
* **`router.push` after login** - back gesture returns to login. **Fix:** `router.replace`.
* **`Link` wrapping non-forwarding components** - custom rows ignore press. **Fix:** `asChild` + spread props, or use `Pressable`.
* **External URLs in `router.push`** - may not open browser. **Fix:** `import { openURL } from "expo-linking"` for `https://` links.
* **Prefetching protected routes** - flashes unauthorized content. **Fix:** Gate prefetch behind session check or skip on auth screens.
* **Missing `accessibilityRole` on imperative Pressable** - screen readers announce "button" for navigation. **Fix:** `accessibilityRole="link"` or prefer `Link`.
* **Huge param payloads in href** - navigation state bloat, logs leak data. **Fix:** Pass IDs only; load bodies from store or API.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<Link href>` | Default list/inline navigation | After async mutation before navigate |
| `router.push` / `replace` | Imperative control | You need prefetch and link semantics |
| `useNavigation().navigate` | React Navigation escape hatch | Standard Expo Router paths exist |
| `Redirect` component | Declarative auth gate in layout | Button-triggered navigation |
| Deep link URL manually | Push notifications payload | In-app taps - use typed href |
| `href` string | Quick prototypes | Production dynamic routes |

## FAQs

When should I use Link vs router.push?

* **`Link`** for user-tappable UI that navigates to a known route.
* **`router.push`** after async work completes (save, scan, permission grant).
* **`router.replace`** when back should not return to the current screen.

How do I navigate with query parameters?

```tsx
router.push({ pathname: "/search", params: { q: "shoes", sort: "price" } });
```

Read with `useLocalSearchParams()`. Prefer path segments for entity IDs; query for filters.

Does Link work on web?

Yes - `Link` renders an anchor on web with client-side navigation. String `href` values improve crawlability for public web builds.

How do I disable a Link?

```tsx
<Link href="/checkout" disabled={!cartReady} asChild>
  <Pressable disabled={!cartReady}>
    <Text>Checkout</Text>
  </Pressable>
</Link>
```

Set `disabled` on both `Link` and child when using `asChild`.

What is router.canGoBack()?

Returns whether the stack has a prior screen. Use before `router.back()` in modals opened via deep link - fall back to `router.replace("/")`.

How do I open an external URL?

```tsx
import * as Linking from "expo-linking";
 
await Linking.openURL("https://docs.expo.dev/router/introduction/");
```

Do not pass external URLs to `router.push` unless you've configured external linking handlers.

Can I prefetch programmatically?

Prefer `<Link prefetch />`. For advanced cases, consult Expo Router SDK 57 docs for `prefetch` utilities on the router instance - availability evolves per minor release.

How do relative hrefs work?

`./[id]` resolves relative to the current route's directory - useful inside `app/orders/` siblings. Prefer absolute builders in shared modules for clarity.

Should I use router.navigate vs push?

`navigate` deduplicates if the route is already focused (web-like). `push` always adds a stack entry. Use `push` for intentional duplicate detail stacks; `navigate` for tab-like behavior.

How do href builders work with typed routes?

Return type `Href` from `expo-router`. With `experiments.typedRoutes`, invalid pathnames error at compile time. See [Typed Routes](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/typed-routes/).

## Related

* [Typed Routes](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/typed-routes/) - compile-time `Href` safety
* [Redirects & Index Routes](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/redirects-and-index-routes/) - `Redirect` vs `router.replace`
* [Stack Navigation](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/stack-navigation/) - back stack behavior
* [Expo Router Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/expo-router-basics/) - route file layout
* [../expo-rules/navigation-and-routing-rules/navigation-and-routing-rules.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/navigation-and-routing-rules/) - `Link` vs imperative rules
* [../architecture-design/adr-navigation-library-choice/adr-navigation-library-choice.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/adr-navigation-library-choice/) - deep linking rationale

> **Stack versions:** This page was written for **React 19.2.3**, **React Native 0.86.0**, and **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4).

Dokumen: Redirects & Index Routes
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/redirects-and-index-routes/

# Redirects & Index Routes

Default landing screens and auth-gated entry points. `index.tsx` files define default routes for their folder; `<Redirect />` and `router.replace` send users to the right shell without polluting the back stack.

Highlights / Redirects & Index Routes

* app/index.tsx is the / route - use it as a redirect hub, not a 200-line home screen
* Redirect component declaratively sends users based on session - replace for auth transitions
* router.replace after login prevents swipe-back to credential screens
* Index routes inside folders default that path segment - orders/index.tsx is /orders
* Never duplicate index.tsx across route groups - both (auth) and (app) cannot own /
* Gate on session hydration first - redirecting before AsyncStorage/SecureStore reads causes flicker

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```text
app/
├── _layout.tsx
├── index.tsx              # / - auth redirect hub
├── (auth)/
│   ├── login.tsx          # /login
│   └── register.tsx
└── (app)/
    └── (tabs)/
        ├── _layout.tsx
        └── index.tsx      # / - real home when signed in
```

```tsx
// app/index.tsx - redirect hub
import { Redirect } from "expo-router";
import { useSession } from "@/features/auth";
 
export default function Index() {
  const { session, isLoading } = useSession();
 
  if (isLoading) return null;
 
  if (session) {
    return <Redirect href="/(tabs)" />;
  }
 
  return <Redirect href="/login" />;
}
```

```tsx
// After login - imperative replace
import { router } from "expo-router";
 
router.replace("/(tabs)");
```

**When to reach for this:**

* **Auth-gated entry** - signed-in users skip login; guests skip tabs
* **Marketing `/` → `/home`** - legacy path support
* **Onboarding completion** - `replace` to main app
* **Role-based landing** - admin vs user default tab

## Working Example

Session provider, root redirect hub, protected app group layout, and post-login replace.

```tsx
// features/auth/model/useSession.tsx (simplified)
import { createContext, useContext, useEffect, useState } from "react";
 
type Session = { userId: string } | null;
 
const SessionContext = createContext<{
  session: Session;
  isLoading: boolean;
  signIn: () => void;
  signOut: () => void;
}>({ session: null, isLoading: true, signIn: () => {}, signOut: () => {} });
 
export function SessionProvider({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  const [session, setSession] = useState<Session>(null);
  const [isLoading, setLoading] = useState(true);
 
  useEffect(() => {
    // Hydrate from SecureStore - see auth-session section
    const timer = setTimeout(() => {
      setSession(null);
      setLoading(false);
    }, 300);
    return () => clearTimeout(timer);
  }, []);
 
  return (
    <SessionContext.Provider
      value={{
        session,
        isLoading,
        signIn: () => setSession({ userId: "1" }),
        signOut: () => setSession(null),
      }}
    >
      {children}
    </SessionContext.Provider>
  );
}
 
export const useSession = () => useContext(SessionContext);
```

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
import { SessionProvider } from "@/features/auth";
 
export default function RootLayout() {
  return (
    <SessionProvider>
      <Stack screenOptions={{ headerShown: false }}>
        <Stack.Screen name="index" />
        <Stack.Screen name="(auth)" />
        <Stack.Screen name="(app)" />
      </Stack>
    </SessionProvider>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// app/index.tsx
import { Redirect } from "expo-router";
import { ActivityIndicator, View } from "react-native";
import { useSession } from "@/features/auth";
 
export default function RootIndex() {
  const { session, isLoading } = useSession();
 
  if (isLoading) {
    return (
      <View style={{ flex: 1, justifyContent: "center", alignItems: "center" }}>
        <ActivityIndicator />
      </View>
    );
  }
 
  if (session) {
    return <Redirect href="/(tabs)" />;
  }
 
  return <Redirect href="/login" />;
}
```

```tsx
// app/(app)/_layout.tsx - belt-and-suspenders guard
import { Redirect, Stack } from "expo-router";
import { useSession } from "@/features/auth";
 
export default function AppGroupLayout() {
  const { session, isLoading } = useSession();
 
  if (isLoading) return null;
  if (!session) return <Redirect href="/login" />;
 
  return <Stack screenOptions={{ headerShown: false }} />;
}
```

```tsx
// app/(auth)/login.tsx (excerpt)
import { router } from "expo-router";
import { Pressable, Text, View } from "react-native";
import { useSession } from "@/features/auth";
 
export default function LoginScreen() {
  const { signIn } = useSession();
 
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1, justifyContent: "center", padding: 16 }}>
      <Pressable
        onPress={() => {
          signIn();
          router.replace("/(tabs)");
        }}
      >
        <Text>Sign in</Text>
      </Pressable>
    </View>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// app/(app)/(tabs)/index.tsx - actual home content
import { Text, View } from "react-native";
 
export default function HomeScreen() {
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1, padding: 16 }}>
      <Text>Home</Text>
    </View>
  );
}
```

## Deep Dive

### Index route resolution

```text
app/index.tsx                    → /
app/orders/index.tsx             → /orders
app/(app)/(tabs)/index.tsx       → /   (when (app) group is active)
```

* Only **one file** should own `/` for a given navigation state - use root `app/index.tsx` as hub
* **Folder index** is the list/default screen for that segment
* **`index.tsx` vs `orders.tsx`** - choose one; mixing creates confusing duplicates

### Redirect mechanisms

| Mechanism | API | Back stack | Use case |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<Redirect href>` | Declarative in render | Replaces current entry | Auth hub, layout guards |
| `router.replace` | Imperative | No back to prior | Post-login, logout |
| `router.push` | Imperative | Preserves back | Not for auth gates |
| `<Link replace>` | Declarative tap | Replace on navigate | Rare; prefer router after async |

```tsx
// Layout guard pattern
if (!session) return <Redirect href="/login" />;
```

### Auth-gated entry sequence

```text
1. Root _layout mounts SessionProvider
2. app/index.tsx waits for isLoading === false
3. session ? Redirect → /(tabs) : Redirect → /login
4. (app)/_layout.tsx re-checks session (deep link protection)
5. Login success → router.replace("/(tabs)")
6. Logout → router.replace("/login")
```

* **Double guard** - root hub + `(app)/_layout` catches deep links to `/settings` when logged out
* **Loading UI** - never redirect while session hydrates; prevents flash of login screen
* **Signed-in user on `/login`** - optionally redirect to `/(tabs)` from `(auth)/_layout.tsx`

### Logout and stack reset

```tsx
function signOut() {
  clearSession();
  router.replace("/login");
}
```

For stubborn stack state, remount navigators:

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx
const { session } = useSession();
return <Stack key={session?.userId ?? "guest"} />;
```

## Gotchas

* **Redirect before session hydration** - users flash through login → home → login. **Fix:** `isLoading` gate with spinner or splash.
* **Two index routes at `/`** - `(auth)/index.tsx` and `(app)/index.tsx` conflict. **Fix:** Single `app/index.tsx` hub.
* **`router.push` after login** - swipe back exposes credentials. **Fix:** `router.replace`.
* **Infinite redirect loop** - `(app)` layout redirects to `/login` while login redirects to `/(tabs)` before session updates. **Fix:** Ensure `signIn` sets session **before** `router.replace`.
* **Deep link to protected route** - `/settings` bypasses hub. **Fix:** Guard in `(app)/_layout.tsx`, not only `app/index.tsx`.
* **Redirect in every child screen** - duplicated logic drifts. **Fix:** Layout-level `<Redirect>` once per group.
* **`href="/(tabs)"` vs `href="/"`** - both may work but mean different things when groups change. **Fix:** Prefer explicit tab root path; use typed `Href`.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `app/index.tsx` + `<Redirect>` | Standard auth gate | You need async server-side redirect (use web middleware) |
| `(app)/_layout` guard only | Simple apps | Deep links must also be protected - hub still recommended |
| `router.replace` post-login | Imperative after mutation | Initial cold start routing |
| Splash screen hold | Long hydration (1s+) | Fast SecureStore read - spinner enough |
| React Navigation `initialRouteName` | Manual RN without files | Expo Router file-based entry |
| Feature flag redirect | Maintenance mode | Per-user auth routing |

## FAQs

What is the difference between index and redirect?

**Index** is a real screen at the default path for a folder. **Redirect** sends navigation elsewhere without rendering content. Use `app/index.tsx` as a thin redirect hub; put home UI in `(tabs)/index.tsx`.

Redirect vs router.replace?

`<Redirect>` is declarative - render when condition is true. `router.replace` is imperative - call after `signIn()` completes. Both avoid back-stack entries when configured correctly.

How do I prevent back to login after sign-in?

```tsx
router.replace("/(tabs)");
```

Never `push` to the main app from login. Clear auth stack with `replace`.

How do I handle logout?

```tsx
await clearTokens();
router.replace("/login");
```

Also `queryClient.clear()` and reset tab stacks - remount with `key` on root layout if needed.

Can I redirect to an external URL?

Use `expo-linking` `openURL` for external sites. `<Redirect>` is for in-app routes only.

How do role-based redirects work?

```tsx
if (session?.role === "admin") return <Redirect href="/admin" />;
return <Redirect href="/(tabs)" />;
```

Keep role logic in session model - index hub reads one `useSession()` hook.

What about onboarding flows?

```tsx
if (!session) return <Redirect href="/login" />;
if (!session.onboardingDone) return <Redirect href="/onboarding" />;
return <Redirect href="/(tabs)" />;
```

Chain conditions in `app/index.tsx` - ordered from most specific to default.

How do index routes work in nested folders?

`app/orders/index.tsx` serves `/orders`. Navigating to `/orders` shows the list; `/orders/42` pushes `[id].tsx` on the orders stack.

Should signed-in users access /login?

Optionally redirect in `(auth)/_layout.tsx`:

```tsx
if (session) return <Redirect href="/(tabs)" />;
```

Prevents bookmarked login screen when already authenticated.

How do I test redirect logic?

Use `expo-router/testing-library` `renderRouter` with mock session providers. Assert `Redirect` targets by inspecting navigation state after `waitFor`.

Dokumen: Route Groups & Organizing app/
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/route-groups-and-organizing-app/

# Route Groups & Organizing `app/`

`(auth)`, `(tabs)`, and private folder conventions. Route groups keep large `app/` trees navigable without polluting URLs or deep-link paths.

Highlights / Route Groups & Organizing `app/`

* Parentheses folders are route groups - they organize files without adding URL segments
* (auth), (app), (tabs), and (modals) are the four groups most production apps need
* Leading underscore marks private files - \_components/ is not a route
* Multiple groups at the same level compose URLs from non-group segments only
* Split auth and app shells with separate \_layout.tsx files per group
* Mirror features/ in src/ - app/ stays a thin routing map, not a feature dump

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```text
app/
├── _layout.tsx                 # Root providers + top navigator
├── index.tsx                   # Entry redirect hub
├── (auth)/
│   ├── _layout.tsx             # Auth stack (no header)
│   ├── login.tsx               # /login
│   └── register.tsx            # /register
├── (app)/
│   ├── _layout.tsx             # Authenticated guard shell
│   └── (tabs)/
│       ├── _layout.tsx
│       ├── index.tsx           # /
│       └── settings.tsx        # /settings
├── (modals)/
│   ├── _layout.tsx             # presentation: modal
│   └── compose.tsx             # /compose
└── _components/                # Private - NOT a route
    └── ScreenChrome.tsx
```

```tsx
// app/(app)/_layout.tsx - minimal auth shell
import { Redirect, Stack } from "expo-router";
import { useSession } from "@/features/auth";
 
export default function AppShellLayout() {
  const { session, isLoading } = useSession();
 
  if (isLoading) return null;
  if (!session) return <Redirect href="/login" />;
 
  return <Stack screenOptions={{ headerShown: false }} />;
}
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Separating **auth** vs **authenticated** flows with different layouts
* Grouping **modals** for shared `presentation: "modal"` options
* Organizing **tabs** without `/tabs` in every URL
* Colocating **non-route helpers** in `_components/` next to layouts

## Working Example

A production-shaped tree with auth group, app shell, tabs, modals, and private folders.

```tsx

        <Stack.Screen name="(modals)" options={{ presentation: "modal" }} />
      </Stack>
    </AppProviders>
  );
}
```

    <Stack
      screenOptions={{
        presentation: "modal",

```text
URL map (groups omitted from path):
 
/login           → (auth)/login.tsx
/register        → (auth)/register.tsx
/                → (app)/(tabs)/index.tsx
/settings        → (app)/(tabs)/settings.tsx
/compose         → (modals)/compose.tsx
```

## Deep Dive

### Route group syntax

| Pattern | URL impact | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `(auth)/login.tsx` | `/login` | Group name omitted from URL |
| `(tabs)/index.tsx` | `/` | Organize tab files |
| `[id].tsx` | `/:id` | Dynamic segment (not a group) |
| `_layout.tsx` | - | Navigator for folder |
| `_components/` | - | Private folder (underscore prefix) |

* Groups can **nest**: `(app)/(tabs)/` is valid - both names are stripped from the URL
* **Sibling groups** at the same level merge into one route tree - avoid duplicate route names across groups
* **Route groups are not layout groups** - you still need `_layout.tsx` per folder for navigators

### Organizing principles

```text
app/                          features/
├── routing & layouts only    ├── business logic
├── re-exports                ├── hooks & API
├── redirects                 └── UI screens
└── _components/ (private)
```

1. **One concern per group** - `(auth)` for sign-in, `(app)` for signed-in shell, `(modals)` for overlays
2. **Mirror feature names** - `app/(app)/(tabs)/orders/` maps to `features/orders/`
3. **Keep root `index.tsx` thin** - redirect hub only; see [Redirects & Index Routes](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/redirects-and-index-routes/)
4. **Cap folder depth at 4** - `app/(app)/(tabs)/orders/[id].tsx` is enough; deeper paths signal refactor time

### Private folders and colocation

```text
app/(tabs)/
├── _layout.tsx
├── _components/
│   └── TabIcon.tsx
├── index.tsx
└── profile.tsx
```

* **`_prefix`** marks files/folders **non-routable** - Expo Router ignores them for URL generation
* Colocate layout-only components in `_components/` - do not put them in `features/` unless reused
* **`+html.tsx`**, **`+not-found.tsx`** are special files - learn their roles before customizing web/not-found

### Multiple root groups pattern

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx - explicit registration prevents ambiguous auto-discovery
<Stack>
  <Stack.Screen name="(auth)" />
  <Stack.Screen name="(app)" />
</Stack>
```

Explicit `<Stack.Screen name="(auth)" />` documents top-level segments for reviewers and keeps screen options centralized.

## Gotchas

* **Duplicate routes across groups** - `(auth)/index.tsx` and `(app)/index.tsx` both map to `/`. **Fix:** Single `app/index.tsx` redirect hub; one group owns `/`.
* **Forgetting group parentheses** - `auth/login.tsx` creates `/auth/login`, breaking marketing links. **Fix:** Rename to `(auth)/login.tsx`.
* **Business logic in `_layout.tsx`** - data fetching in layouts runs on every child navigation. **Fix:** Auth redirect only; screens own data.
* **God `(app)` group** - every screen dumped under one group. **Fix:** Sub-groups `(tabs)`, `(modals)`, feature folders.
* **`_components` without underscore** - `components/Header.tsx` becomes `/components/Header` route. **Fix:** Prefix private folders with `_`.
* **Cross-group `router.push` with wrong path** - pushing `/(app)/settings` includes group in some APIs. **Fix:** Use URL paths `/settings` or typed `Href` objects.
* **Monorepo shared `app/`** - white-label apps diverge in route trees. **Fix:** Separate `apps/brand-a/app/` per binary - see [../project-setup/multiple-apps-in-one-repo/multiple-apps-in-one-repo.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/multiple-apps-in-one-repo/).

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Route groups `(name)` | Organize without URL segments | You need `/auth/login` in the public URL |
| Flat `app/` tree | <10 routes total | Parallel squads editing one folder daily |
| `src/routes` manual React Navigation | Brownfield without file-based routing | New SDK 57 greenfield apps |
| Feature flags for sections | Seasonal tabs | Permanent auth vs app split |
| Separate Expo apps | Truly different products | White-label variants - use config instead |
| Deep folder mirroring org chart | Never recommended | - |

## FAQs

Do parentheses appear in URLs?

No. `(auth)/login.tsx` maps to `/login`, not `/auth/login`. Groups exist purely for filesystem organization and layout boundaries.

Can I nest multiple route groups?

Yes - `app/(app)/(tabs)/(hidden)/` is valid. Each group name is stripped. Avoid unnecessary nesting that obscures the route map.

What is a private folder?

Files and folders starting with `_` (except `_layout.tsx`) are not turned into routes. Use `_components/`, `_hooks/`, etc., for colocated non-route code.

How do groups interact with deep links?

Deep links target **URL paths**, not group names. `/settings` opens `(app)/(tabs)/settings.tsx` regardless of group folders. Configure `scheme` in `app.config.ts` once at the app level.

Should auth and app share a root layout?

Yes - one `app/_layout.tsx` mounts providers for both groups. Split **navigators** per group (`(auth)/_layout`, `(app)/_layout`), not duplicate provider trees.

How do I organize modals?

Create `(modals)/` with its own `_layout.tsx` setting `presentation: "modal"`. Register `(modals)` on the root stack. URLs stay `/compose`, not `/modals/compose`.

Can two groups each have an index route?

Both would resolve to `/` - a conflict. Use a single `app/index.tsx` as the entry redirect instead.

How does this map to Feature-Sliced Design?

`app/` is the FSD **app layer** (routing only). `features/`, `entities/`, `shared/` live outside `app/`. Route groups segment flows; feature slices segment business domains - see [../architecture-design/feature-sliced-design-for-rn/feature-sliced-design-for-rn.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/feature-sliced-design-for-rn/).

When should URLs include the segment explicitly?

When marketing, SEO (web), or support docs publish the path - e.g. `/pricing` for a public web page. Use normal folders, not groups, when the segment must appear in the URL.

How do I document the route map for new hires?

Maintain a `docs/routes.md` table: URL → file path → feature owner. Update on every new group. Pair with typed routes so TypeScript catches drift.

## Related

* [Expo Router Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/expo-router-basics/) - file-based routing fundamentals
* [Redirects & Index Routes](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/redirects-and-index-routes/) - `app/index.tsx` redirect hub
* [Tabs & Drawers](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/tabs-and-drawers/) - `(tabs)` and `(drawer)` layout patterns
* [Stack Navigation](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/stack-navigation/) - per-group stack options
* [../architecture-design/feature-sliced-design-for-rn/feature-sliced-design-for-rn.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/feature-sliced-design-for-rn/) - feature boundaries vs `app/`
* [../expo-rules/navigation-and-routing-rules/navigation-and-routing-rules.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/navigation-and-routing-rules/) - structure review checklist

> **Stack versions:** This page was written for **React 19.2.3**, **React Native 0.86.0**, and **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4).

Dokumen: Stack Navigation
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/stack-navigation/

# Stack Navigation

Push/pop, headers, and screen options in `app/` directories. `Stack` from `expo-router` is the file-based face of `@react-navigation/native-stack` - every sibling route file under a folder with `_layout.tsx` becomes a stack screen.

Highlights / Stack Navigation

* Stack from expo-router wraps native-stack - file names become pushable screens automatically
* screenOptions on \_layout.tsx sets team-wide header defaults; per-route options override
* presentation: modal and headerShown: false are the two most common stack tweaks in production
* useNavigation().setOptions updates titles after async data loads without remounting
* Nested stacks under tabs keep the tab bar visible while detail screens push on top
* Android hardware back and iOS swipe-back follow React Navigation stack rules - test both

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
npx expo install expo-router
```

```text
app/
├── _layout.tsx           # Root stack
├── index.tsx
├── settings.tsx
└── orders/
    ├── _layout.tsx       # Nested stack for /orders/*
    ├── index.tsx
    └── [id].tsx
```

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
 
export default function RootLayout() {
  return (
    <Stack
      screenOptions={{
        headerShown: true,
        animation: "slide_from_right",
      }}
    >
      <Stack.Screen name="index" options={{ title: "Home" }} />
      <Stack.Screen name="settings" options={{ title: "Settings" }} />
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// app/orders/_layout.tsx
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
 
export default function OrdersLayout() {
  return (
    <Stack>
      <Stack.Screen name="index" options={{ title: "Orders" }} />
      <Stack.Screen name="[id]" options={{ title: "Order" }} />
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Linear drill-down flows (list → detail → edit)
* Full-screen modals via `presentation: "modal"`
* Hiding headers on splash/auth screens with `headerShown: false`
* Nested stacks inside tabs when one tab needs its own push history

## Working Example

A root stack with a hidden-header splash, a settings screen with a dynamic title, and a nested orders stack.

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
import { ThemeProvider } from "@/shared/theme";
 
export default function RootLayout() {
  return (
    <ThemeProvider>
      <Stack>
        <Stack.Screen name="index" options={{ headerShown: false }} />
        <Stack.Screen name="(tabs)" options={{ headerShown: false }} />
        <Stack.Screen
          name="settings"
          options={{
            title: "Settings",
            presentation: "card",
          }}
        />
      </Stack>
    </ThemeProvider>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// app/settings.tsx
import { useNavigation } from "expo-router";
import { useEffect } from "react";
import { ActivityIndicator, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
export default function SettingsScreen() {
  const navigation = useNavigation();
 
  useEffect(() => {
    navigation.setOptions({ title: "Account Settings" });
  }, [navigation]);
 
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1, padding: 16 }}>
      <Text>Settings content</Text>
    </View>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// app/orders/[id].tsx
import { useLocalSearchParams, Stack } from "expo-router";
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { ActivityIndicator, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
export default function OrderDetailScreen() {
  const { id } = useLocalSearchParams<{ id: string }>();
  const [title, setTitle] = useState(`Order #${id}`);
 
  useEffect(() => {
    // Simulate fetch - then update header via layout child
    const timer = setTimeout(() => setTitle(`Order ${id} - Shipped`), 400);
    return () => clearTimeout(timer);
  }, [id]);
 
  return (
    <>
      <Stack.Screen options={{ title }} />
      <View style={{ flex: 1, padding: 16 }}>
        <Text>Detail for order {id}</Text>
      </View>
    </>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// Navigate between stack screens
import { Link, router } from "expo-router";
import { Pressable, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
export function HomeActions() {
  return (
    <View style={{ gap: 12 }}>
      <Link href="/settings">Settings (declarative)</Link>
      <Pressable onPress={() => router.push("/orders/42")}>
        <Text>Order 42 (imperative)</Text>
      </Pressable>
    </View>
  );
}
```

## Deep Dive

### How the filesystem becomes a stack

```text
app/orders/_layout.tsx  →  <Stack> wraps this folder
app/orders/index.tsx    →  initial route (bottom of stack)
app/orders/[id].tsx     →  pushed when navigating to /orders/:id
app/orders/new.tsx      →  pushed when navigating to /orders/new
```

* Expo Router **auto-registers** every route file as a `Stack.Screen` - explicit `<Stack.Screen name="...">` is optional but recommended for options
* The **initial route** is the first matching screen on navigation; deep links can open `[id]` directly
* **Sibling files** share one stack history - folders without `_layout.tsx` inherit the parent navigator

### Header configuration layers

| Layer | API | Precedence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Navigator default | `screenOptions` on `<Stack>` | Lowest |
| Layout child | `<Stack.Screen options={...}>` | Medium |
| Route file | `export const options = {...}` | Medium |
| Runtime | `navigation.setOptions()` or `<Stack.Screen options>` in render | Highest |

```tsx
// Per-route static options (co-located)
export const options = {
  title: "Profile",
  headerBackTitle: "Back",
};
```

### Presentation modes

```tsx
<Stack.Screen
  name="compose"
  options={{
    presentation: "modal",        // iOS card modal; Android full-screen
    gestureEnabled: true,
    headerShown: true,
  }}
/>
```

* **`card`** (default) - standard push animation
* **`modal`** - modal presentation; pair with a `(modals)` route group for organization
* **`transparentModal`** - overlays previous screen (use sparingly - accessibility and Android back differ)
* **`fullScreenModal`** - edge-to-edge modal on iOS

### Nesting stacks under tabs

```text
(tabs)/_layout.tsx     → Tabs (tab bar always visible)
(tabs)/orders/_layout  → Stack (push within Orders tab only)
```

Each tab maintains an **independent stack history** - switching tabs preserves each tab's stack state by default. Reset stacks on logout with `router.replace` or remounting the navigator key.

## Gotchas

* **Missing `_layout.tsx` in a folder with multiple screens** - siblings may flatten into the parent stack unexpectedly. **Fix:** Add `orders/_layout.tsx` with `<Stack />` when a folder has `index` + `[id]`.
* **Duplicate screen names from index files** - `orders.tsx` and `orders/index.tsx` conflict. **Fix:** Pick one URL shape per feature.
* **`headerShown: false` on root stack but expecting nested headers** - child stacks must set `headerShown: true` explicitly. **Fix:** Configure headers at the nested `_layout.tsx` where screens live.
* **Dynamic title flicker** - default title shows before fetch completes. **Fix:** Use a skeleton title or `headerLargeTitle: false` until data loads; set options in `useEffect`.
* **`router.push` after login duplicates auth on back stack** - users swipe back to login. **Fix:** `router.replace('/(tabs)')` after successful auth.
* **Modal without Android back handling** - `presentation: "modal"` still respects hardware back, but custom overlays may not. **Fix:** Test Android back; prefer real routes over absolute-position overlays.
* **Deep link opens stack mid-tree without index** - `/orders/99` may skip list screen. **Fix:** Acceptable for notifications; use `router.back()` fallback UI when stack is empty.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Stack` (native-stack) | Default push/pop, native headers, gestures | You need cross-stack shared element transitions (limited) |
| `Tabs` | Top-level sections with persistent tab bar | Linear wizard with no section switching |
| `Drawer` | Many sections, tablet-first navigation | Phone apps with ≤4 primary destinations |
| Modal as route (`presentation: "modal"`) | Full-screen forms, compose flows | Tiny tooltips or dropdowns |
| Imperative overlay (`react-native` Modal) | Blocking alerts, one-off pickers | Navigation that should appear in history/deep links |
| React Navigation JS stack (`@react-navigation/stack`) | Custom card animations on older setups | New SDK 57 projects - native-stack is default |

## FAQs

How do I hide the header on one screen?

```tsx
// In _layout.tsx
<Stack.Screen name="login" options={{ headerShown: false }} />
 
// Or export from the route file
export const options = { headerShown: false };
```

Set `headerShown: false` on the specific screen - parent `screenOptions` can still apply to siblings.

How do I add a header right button?

```tsx
import { Stack, router } from "expo-router";
import { Pressable, Text } from "react-native";
 
export default function EditScreen() {
  return (
    <>
      <Stack.Screen
        options={{
          headerRight: () => (
            <Pressable onPress={() => router.push("/preview")}>
              <Text>Preview</Text>
            </Pressable>
          ),
        }}
      />
      {/* screen body */}
    </>
  );
}
```

Use `headerLeft`, `headerRight`, or `headerTitle` render props - same API as React Navigation.

Can I use a custom header component?

Yes - `header: () => <MyHeader />` in screen options. Prefer design-system headers for consistency. Hide the default with `headerShown: false` and render your own in the screen body only when the stack header is insufficient.

How does Android hardware back work?

Hardware back pops the current stack. At the root stack's first screen, back exits the app (or moves to background). Test nested stacks inside tabs - back should pop detail before switching tabs.

How do I reset the stack on logout?

```tsx
import { router } from "expo-router";
 
router.replace("/(auth)/login");
```

`replace` removes prior routes from history. For complex resets, remount the navigator with a `key` tied to `userId` on the root layout.

Should modals be routes or React Native Modal?

**Routes** when the modal has a URL, deep link, or should appear in navigation history. **RN `Modal`** for ephemeral UI with no shareable path. Document team choice in an ADR when both patterns appear.

How do I pass data between stack screens?

* **URL params** for IDs and shallow state (`params: { id }`)
* **Global store** (Zustand, TanStack Query) for shared entities
* **Avoid** large JSON in params - URLs are logged and persisted in navigation state

See [Typed Routes](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/typed-routes/) for param typing.

What animation options does native-stack support?

`animation: "slide_from_right" | "fade" | "fade_from_bottom" | "flip" | "simple_push" | "none"` in `screenOptions`. Platform defaults differ - verify on both iOS and Android simulators.

Can I nest a stack inside another stack?

Yes - `app/settings/_layout.tsx` can export `<Stack>` while sitting inside the root stack. Limit depth to **two stacks** (root + feature) before UX and debugging suffer.

How do I disable swipe-back on a sensitive screen?

```tsx
<Stack.Screen name="confirm-payment" options={{ gestureEnabled: false }} />
```

Use for irreversible actions. Pair with an explicit cancel button for accessibility.

* [Expo Router Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/expo-router-basics/) - filesystem mental model and `_layout.tsx`

* [Link & href](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/link-and-href/) - declarative push targets
* [Route Groups & Organizing `app/`](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/route-groups-and-organizing-app/) - `(modals)` group pattern
* [../expo-rules/navigation-and-routing-rules/navigation-and-routing-rules.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/navigation-and-routing-rules/) - review checklist
