Dokumen: Tabs & Drawers
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/tabs-and-drawers/

# Tabs & Drawers

Tab bars, drawer gestures, and nested layout composition. `Tabs` and `Drawer` from `expo-router` wrap React Navigation navigators - file names under the layout folder become destinations automatically.

Highlights / Tabs & Drawers

* Tabs from expo-router maps each child file or folder to a tab - icons live in \_layout.tsx
* Nest a Stack inside a tab folder when that section needs list → detail push without losing the tab bar
* Drawer requires @react-navigation/drawer - install with npx expo install and wrap in app/(drawer)/
* href: null hides a route from the tab bar while keeping it addressable via router.push
* Lazy tabs mount on first visit - prefetch heavy tabs with Link prefetch when UX demands
* Three-level nesting (drawer → tabs → stack) is the practical ceiling before flattening

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
npx expo install expo-router
# Drawer only:
npx expo install @react-navigation/drawer react-native-gesture-handler react-native-reanimated
```

```text
app/
├── _layout.tsx
└── (tabs)/
    ├── _layout.tsx       → Tabs
    ├── index.tsx         → Home tab
    ├── explore.tsx       → Explore tab
    └── orders/
        ├── _layout.tsx     → Stack nested in Orders tab
        ├── index.tsx
        └── [id].tsx
```

```tsx
// app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx
import { Tabs } from "expo-router";
import { Ionicons } from "@expo/vector-icons";
 
export default function TabLayout() {
  return (
    <Tabs
      screenOptions={{
        tabBarActiveTintColor: "#2563eb",
        headerShown: true,
      }}
    >
      <Tabs.Screen
        name="index"
        options={{
          title: "Home",
          tabBarIcon: ({ color, size }) => <Ionicons name="home" size={size} color={color} />,
        }}
      />
      <Tabs.Screen
        name="explore"
        options={{
          title: "Explore",
          tabBarIcon: ({ color, size }) => <Ionicons name="compass" size={size} color={color} />,
        }}
      />
      <Tabs.Screen
        name="orders"
        options={{
          title: "Orders",
          headerShown: false,
          tabBarIcon: ({ color, size }) => <Ionicons name="list" size={size} color={color} />,
        }}
      />
    </Tabs>
  );
}
```

**When to reach for this:**

* **Tabs** - 3–5 peer destinations users switch between constantly (home, search, profile)
* **Drawer** - 6+ sections, tablet layouts, or hamburger-first IA
* **Nested stack** - one tab has drill-down flows while siblings stay flat

## Working Example

Tabs with a nested orders stack and an optional drawer shell for wider navigation.

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
 
export default function RootLayout() {
  return (
    <Stack screenOptions={{ headerShown: false }}>
      <Stack.Screen name="(drawer)" />
      <Stack.Screen name="(auth)" options={{ presentation: "modal" }} />
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// app/(drawer)/_layout.tsx
import { Drawer } from "expo-router/drawer";
import { GestureHandlerRootView } from "react-native-gesture-handler";
 
export default function DrawerLayout() {
  return (
    <GestureHandlerRootView style={{ flex: 1 }}>
      <Drawer screenOptions={{ headerShown: false }}>
        <Drawer.Screen name="(tabs)" options={{ title: "Main" }} />
        <Drawer.Screen name="settings" options={{ title: "Settings" }} />
      </Drawer>
    </GestureHandlerRootView>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// app/(drawer)/(tabs)/orders/_layout.tsx
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
 
export default function OrdersStack() {
  return (
    <Stack>
      <Stack.Screen name="index" options={{ title: "Orders" }} />
      <Stack.Screen name="[id]" options={{ title: "Order Detail" }} />
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// Hide a screen from tab bar but keep it navigable
// app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx (excerpt)
<Tabs.Screen
  name="hidden-settings"
  options={{
    href: null,
    title: "Hidden",
  }}
/>
```

```tsx
// app/(tabs)/hidden-settings.tsx - reachable via router.push("/hidden-settings")
import { Text, View } from "react-native";
 
export default function HiddenSettingsScreen() {
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1, padding: 16 }}>
      <Text>Not shown in tab bar</Text>
    </View>
  );
}
```

## Deep Dive

### Tabs layout rules

```text
app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx
├── index.tsx      → tab 1 (often Home)
├── explore.tsx    → tab 2
└── profile.tsx    → tab 3
```

* Every **immediate child** of `(tabs)/` becomes a tab unless `href: null`
* **Folders** become a single tab - the folder's `_layout.tsx` chooses stack/drawer inside that tab
* **`tabBarButton`** customizes press behavior - use for special center FAB tabs
* **`lazy: true`** (default) defers mounting until first focus - improves cold start

### Drawer layout rules

```tsx
import { Drawer } from "expo-router/drawer";
```

* Import from **`expo-router/drawer`**, not `expo-router` - drawer has extra native dependencies
* Wrap the tree in **`GestureHandlerRootView`** at the drawer layout or root
* **`drawerPosition`**, **`drawerType`**, and **`overlayColor`** match React Navigation drawer options
* On phones, many teams use **tabs primary + drawer for secondary** - not both competing for thumb reach

### Composition patterns

| Pattern | Structure | Best for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tabs only | `(tabs)/` at root | Consumer apps, 3–5 sections |
| Drawer → Tabs | `(drawer)/(tabs)/` | Many sections; tabs for daily use |
| Stack → Tabs | Root stack pushes modals over tabs | Auth modal, global compose |
| Tabs → Stack | Stack inside one tab folder | List/detail in one section |

```text
Recommended max depth:
 
Root Stack
  └── Drawer (optional)
        └── Tabs
              └── Stack (per heavy tab)
```

### Tab bar styling

```tsx
<Tabs
  screenOptions={{
    tabBarStyle: { backgroundColor: "#0f172a" },
    tabBarLabelStyle: { fontSize: 12 },
    tabBarHideOnKeyboard: true,
  }}
/>
```

* **`tabBarHideOnKeyboard`** prevents the bar from covering text inputs on Android
* Safe area insets apply automatically - test on iPhone with home indicator
* **`tabBarBadge`** for unread counts - keep badges in sync with push notification state

## Gotchas

* **Every file in `(tabs)/` shows as a tab** - helper routes leak into the bar. **Fix:** `href: null` or move non-tab screens into a nested stack folder.
* **Drawer without gesture-handler root** - swipes silently fail. **Fix:** `GestureHandlerRootView` wrapping drawer layout; ensure `react-native-reanimated` Babel plugin is configured (default in SDK 57 template).
* **Double headers (tabs + stack)** - tab layout and nested stack both show headers. **Fix:** `headerShown: false` on tabs for folders that own a nested stack (`orders` tab pattern).
* **Tab state survives logout** - previous user's stack remains in memory. **Fix:** Remount `(tabs)` with `key={userId}` on the layout or `router.replace` to auth.
* **Deep link to `/orders/5` with wrong tab focused** - user lands on detail but wrong tab highlighted. **Fix:** Ensure route lives under the correct tab folder; test universal links per tab.
* **Too many tabs (6+)** - iOS tab bar truncates labels. **Fix:** Move rare destinations to drawer, profile menu, or "More" stack.
* **Drawer on iPhone as primary nav** - thumb reach and discoverability suffer vs bottom tabs. **Fix:** Reserve drawer for tablet or 6+ destinations.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bottom `Tabs` | 3–5 daily destinations | Flat IA with one linear flow |
| `Drawer` | Many sections, tablet-first | Simple 3-tab consumer app |
| Top material tabs (`@react-navigation/material-top-tabs`) | Swipeable content sections inside one area | App-wide primary navigation |
| Single `Stack` + hub screen | Very small apps, wizards | Users need one-tap section switching |
| Custom tab bar (`tabBar: () => <MyBar />`) | Branded FAB, animated bar | You only need tint colors - use `screenOptions` |
| iOS sidebar (`@react-navigation/drawer` permanent on iPad) | Split-view tablet layouts | Phone-only MVP |

## FAQs

How do I install drawer support?

```bash
npx expo install @react-navigation/drawer react-native-gesture-handler react-native-reanimated
```

Use `import { Drawer } from "expo-router/drawer"`. The SDK 57 template already includes Reanimated's Babel plugin.

How do I hide a route from the tab bar?

```tsx
<Tabs.Screen name="secret" options={{ href: null }} />
```

The route remains navigable via `router.push("/secret")` or `Link href="/secret"`.

Can one tab have a stack and others stay flat?

Yes - add `app/(tabs)/orders/_layout.tsx` with `<Stack />` while `explore.tsx` stays a single screen. Set `headerShown: false` on the orders tab entry in tabs layout.

How do I change the active tab programmatically?

```tsx
import { router } from "expo-router";
 
router.push("/(tabs)/explore");
```

Navigate to the tab's root path. Use `router.replace` when you should not preserve back history.

How do I add a middle FAB tab?

```tsx
<Tabs.Screen
  name="create"
  options={{
    tabBarButton: (props) => (
      <Pressable {...props} style={[props.style, styles.fab]}>
        <Ionicons name="add" size={28} color="#fff" />
      </Pressable>
    ),
  }}
/>
```

Style the custom button - ensure hit slop and accessibility label.

Should the drawer wrap tabs or the reverse?

**Drawer wrapping tabs** is most common - drawer for app sections, tabs for high-frequency subset. Tabs wrapping drawer is rare and confuses back behavior.

How do badges work on tab icons?

```tsx
<Tabs.Screen
  name="inbox"
  options={{
    tabBarBadge: 3,
    tabBarBadgeStyle: { backgroundColor: "#ef4444" },
  }}
/>
```

Update badge values from notification store or query cache - clear on tab focus if appropriate.

Do tabs preserve scroll position?

Yes - inactive tabs stay mounted by default (`lazy` only delays first mount). Use `unmountOnBlur: true` in screen options if memory pressure requires tearing down heavy tabs.

How do I test tab navigation in RNTL?

Use `expo-router/testing-library` `renderRouter` with a fixture `app` directory. Assert tab switches via `user.press` on tab labels and verify URL segments.

Can I use native iOS tab bar APIs?

Expo Router tabs use React Navigation's JS tab bar by default. For fully native UITabBar experiments, you'd leave file-based tabs - uncommon for most Expo teams. Prefer styling via `screenOptions` first.

Dokumen: Typed Routes
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/typed-routes/

# Typed Routes

Generated types and safe param passing between screens. Typed routes turn your `app/` filesystem into a TypeScript `Href` union - invalid paths fail `tsc` before they ship.

Highlights / Typed Routes

* experiments.typedRoutes: true generates .expo/types/router.d.ts from your app/ tree
* Href and Route types catch invalid pathnames at compile time - not at runtime in production
* Dynamic routes require params objects - /orders/[id] needs { id: string } in the href
* Run tsc --noEmit in CI after every app/ restructure - generated types drift silently otherwise
* Central href builders return Href - one typo fix updates every callsite
* Validate URL params with Zod at screen entry - types do not prove runtime deep-link input

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```ts
// app.config.ts
export default {
  experiments: {
    typedRoutes: true,
  },
} satisfies import("expo/config").ExpoConfig;
```

```bash
# Regenerate types after adding routes
npx expo start
# or
npm run typecheck   # tsc --noEmit
```

```tsx
import { Link, router, type Href } from "expo-router";
 
// ✅ Static route - string href
const settings: Href = "/settings";
 
// ✅ Dynamic route - object with params
const order: Href = { pathname: "/orders/[id]", params: { id: "42" } };
 
<Link href={order}>Open order</Link>
router.push(order);
```

```ts
// src/navigation/hrefs.ts
import type { Href } from "expo-router";
 
export const orderDetailHref = (id: string): Href => ({
  pathname: "/orders/[id]",
  params: { id },
});
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Any production app with **more than ~10 routes**
* Teams using **`router.push` in hooks** - typos are invisible at runtime
* **Monorepos** sharing navigation helpers across white-label apps
* CI pipelines that already run **`tsc --noEmit`**

## Working Example

Enable typed routes, define href builders, consume in screens, and validate runtime params.

```ts
// app.config.ts
import type { ExpoConfig, ConfigContext } from "expo/config";
 
export default ({ config }: ConfigContext): ExpoConfig => ({
  ...config,
  name: "TypedRoutesApp",
  slug: "typed-routes-app",
  experiments: {
    typedRoutes: true,
  },
});
```

```text
app/
├── _layout.tsx
├── settings.tsx
└── orders/
    ├── index.tsx
    └── [id].tsx
```

```ts
// src/navigation/hrefs.ts
import type { Href } from "expo-router";
 
export const hrefs = {
  settings: "/settings" as Href,
  orders: "/orders" as Href,
  orderDetail: (id: string): Href => ({
    pathname: "/orders/[id]",
    params: { id },
  }),
} as const;
```

```tsx
// features/orders/ui/OrdersListScreen.tsx
import { Link } from "expo-router";
import { Text, View } from "react-native";
import { hrefs } from "@/navigation/hrefs";
 
export function OrdersListScreen() {
  return (
    <View style={{ padding: 16 }}>
      <Link href={hrefs.orderDetail("99")}>
        <Text>Order 99</Text>
      </Link>
    </View>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// features/orders/ui/OrderDetailScreen.tsx
import { useLocalSearchParams } from "expo-router";
import { z } from "zod";
import { Text, View } from "react-native";
 
const paramsSchema = z.object({
  id: z.string().min(1),
});
 
export function OrderDetailScreen() {
  const raw = useLocalSearchParams();
  const parsed = paramsSchema.safeParse(raw);
 
  if (!parsed.success) {
    return (
      <View style={{ padding: 16 }}>
        <Text>Invalid order link</Text>
      </View>
    );
  }
 
  const { id } = parsed.data;
 
  return (
    <View style={{ padding: 16 }}>
      <Text>Order {id}</Text>
    </View>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// Compile-time failure examples (do not ship):
// router.push("/orders");           // ❌ missing params for [id] route
// router.push("/settigns");          // ❌ typo in static path
// <Link href="/unknown" />          // ❌ route does not exist in app/
```

## Deep Dive

### Generated types location

```text
.expo/types/router.d.ts    # Auto-generated - do not hand-edit
```

* Types regenerate when **Metro starts** or when Expo CLI scans `app/`
* **Commit or gitignore?** - gitignore `.expo/`; CI runs `expo start` or `npx expo customize tsconfig` flow so types exist before `tsc`
* `tsconfig.json` should include Expo's types:

```json
{
  "extends": "expo/tsconfig.base",
  "compilerOptions": {
    "strict": true
  },
  "include": ["**/*.ts", "**/*.tsx", ".expo/types/**/*.ts"]
}
```

### Core types

| Type | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `Href` | Union of all valid `href` values for `Link` and `router` |
| `Href<T>` | Narrow href for a specific route |
| Route path strings | Literal union of static segments |

```tsx
import type { Href } from "expo-router";
 
function navigate(href: Href) {
  router.push(href);
}
```

### Dynamic segment typing

```text
app/users/[userId]/posts/[postId].tsx
```

```tsx
const href: Href = {
  pathname: "/users/[userId]/posts/[postId]",
  params: { userId: "1", postId: "9" },
};
```

* **All dynamic params required** in the object - partial params fail `tsc`
* **Optional search params** follow the generated shape for your route - consult generated `router.d.ts` when unsure
* **Catch-all routes** `[...slug].tsx` generate array or string param types depending on configuration

### Runtime vs compile-time safety

```text
Compile-time (typed routes):     Developer typos in router.push / Link
Runtime (Zod):                 Deep links, push notifications, malformed URLs
```

Typed routes **do not validate** external input - always parse `useLocalSearchParams()` before fetching.

### CI checklist

```bash
npx expo customize tsconfig.json   # first-time setup if needed
npx expo start --non-interactive & # generate .expo/types
sleep 5
npm run typecheck
```

Add to PR checks when `app/` changes - route renames without updated hrefs break builds loudly (desired).

## Gotchas

* **Types stale after rename** - `tsc` passes locally with old `.expo/types` until Metro restarts. **Fix:** Restart dev server or run typecheck in CI fresh each time.
* **Assuming types validate notification payloads** - push opens `/orders/abc` with extra query junk. **Fix:** Zod at screen boundary.
* **String interpolation bypasses checks** - `router.push(\`/orders/${id}` as Href)`defeats the system. **Fix:** Object href builders without`as Href` casts.
* **Monorepo app path not scanned** - types generated for wrong workspace root. **Fix:** Run Expo CLI from the app package directory.
* **Missing `experiments.typedRoutes`** - `Href` widens to `string`. **Fix:** Enable in `app.config.ts` on day one.
* **Shared package imports app types** - coupling the wrong direction. **Fix:** `packages/navigation` exports builders; app owns generated types.
* **Route groups in pathname** - typed hrefs use **URL paths**, not `(tabs)` group names. **Fix:** `/settings` not `/(tabs)/settings` in href objects.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `experiments.typedRoutes` | Expo Router apps on SDK 57 | Non-Expo React Navigation codebases |
| Manual `routes.ts` const object | Tiny apps (<8 routes) | Fast-growing `app/` trees |
| Zod-only validation | Untyped brownfield | Greenfield - add typed routes too |
| Codegen from OpenAPI paths | Backend-driven web parity | Mobile-first file-based routing |
| ESLint `no-restricted-syntax` on string push | Enforcing migration | You have typed routes enabled already |

## FAQs

How do I enable typed routes?

```ts
// app.config.ts
experiments: { typedRoutes: true }
```

Restart Metro. Confirm `.expo/types/router.d.ts` exists. Run `tsc --noEmit`.

Where are types generated?

`.expo/types/router.d.ts` - auto-generated from files in `app/`. Do not edit manually; restart the dev server after route changes.

Why does tsc fail after adding a route?

Generated types updated - existing string hrefs may now be invalid. Update callsites to use the new path or add missing `params` for dynamic segments.

Do typed routes work with route groups?

Yes - groups like `(tabs)` are omitted from URL types. `/settings` is valid; `/(tabs)/settings` is typically not in the `Href` union.

How do I type useLocalSearchParams?

```tsx
const { id } = useLocalSearchParams<{ id: string }>();
```

Generated types may also export route-specific param maps - inspect `router.d.ts`. Still validate with Zod for external entry points.

Can I use typed routes in a monorepo?

Yes - run type generation per app package (`apps/mobile`). Share **href builder functions** from `packages/navigation`; each app validates against its own `app/` tree.

What about catch-all routes?

`app/docs/[...slug].tsx` generates href types requiring `slug` - often `string | string[]`. Test deep links with multiple segments in Maestro smoke flows.

Should I cast string paths as Href?

Avoid `as Href` casts - they silence real errors. Fix the path or use object form with required params.

Do typed routes affect runtime bundle size?

No - types are compile-time only. Zero production JS cost.

How do href builders interact with features?

Features import `orderDetailHref` from `@/navigation/hrefs` - never import from `.expo/types` directly. The builder return type is `Href`.

Dokumen: Expo Router Advanced Best Practices
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router-advanced/best-practices/

# Expo Router Advanced Best Practices

A condensed summary of the 25 most important best practices drawn from every page in this section.

Highlights / Expo Router Advanced Best Practices

* Model navigation as URLs - every screen worth restoring must have a file route
* Stack.Protected at root owns auth - avoid competing Redirect chains in nested layouts
* Anchor modal stacks for deep links - unstable\_settings.anchor preserves tab context
* Per-tab stacks preserve back history - do not expect one global pop order
* Treat alpha APIs (NativeTabs, SplitView, RSC) as feature-flagged experiments
* Test cold-start deep links on both platforms before every release

1. **Nest one navigator per `_layout.tsx`:** Each folder layout exports exactly one `Stack`, `Tabs`, `NativeTabs`, `SplitView`, or headless `Slot`/`Navigator` - mixing two navigators in one layout file creates ambiguous history.
2. **Give every tab its own stack when pushing detail:** Put `home/_layout.tsx` → `<Stack />` under each tab that needs list → detail; flat tab folders lose independent back stacks.
3. **Navigate with absolute hrefs across tab boundaries:** Prefer `router.push('/inbox/t2')` over `../` relative paths when crossing tabs - relative segments resolve against the current navigator context.
4. **Anchor modal routes for deep links:** Export `unstable_settings = { anchor: '(tabs)' }` on the stack that owns modals so cold-start `/compose` does not wipe the tab shell.
5. **Use `router.replace` after auth transitions:** Login, logout, and role changes should replace history - `push` lets users swipe back into credential or stale-role screens.
6. **Hydrate session before rendering `Stack.Protected`:** Keep splash visible until SecureStore / token read completes - rendering guards while `isLoading` causes redirect flicker and loops.
7. **Single authority for auth gates:** Root `Stack.Protected` groups beat sprinkling `<Redirect />` in every nested layout - competing redirects cause infinite bounce between `/` and `/sign-in`.
8. **Never duplicate screens across Protected groups:** A route file may appear in only one `Stack.Protected` declaration - nest guards for roles instead of copying `profile` into two groups.
9. **Treat Protected as UX, not security:** Client guards do not remove routes from the bundle - validate every API call server-side; see [../auth-session/](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/).
10. **Choose Expo Router modals over RN `<Modal>` for linkable flows:** `presentation: 'modal'` routes participate in deep links and Android back - reserve RN `Modal` for ephemeral alerts with no URL.
11. **Render form sheet chrome in content on Android:** Native stack headers and nested stacks inside `formSheet` do not render on Android - title and actions belong in the sheet body.
12. **Cap form sheet detents at three on Android:** `sheetAllowedDetents` with more than three values is truncated - design cross-platform sheets with ≤3 snap points.
13. **Declare every native tab with `NativeTabs.Trigger`:** Unlike JavaScript `Tabs`, files are not auto-added to the bar - missing triggers mean routes exist but are unreachable from the tab UI.
14. **Do not use `disabled` on native tabs for authorization:** `disabled` blocks tab bar taps only - `router.push` still navigates; use `Stack.Protected` or `hidden` for true removal.
15. **Resolve feature-flag tab visibility before first mount:** Toggling `hidden` on `NativeTabs.Trigger` at runtime remounts the navigator and clears stacks - decide tab sets at boot.
16. **Drive tablet master-detail from URL segments:** Selection state belongs in `[id].tsx` routes, not `useState(selectedId)` - deep links and rotation restore correctly.
17. **Ship responsive split fallback for Android tablets:** `SplitView` is iOS-native alpha - use `useWindowDimensions` + row layout and per-section `Stack` on Android and narrow widths.
18. **Show an empty detail placeholder on tablet:** `/orders` without an id should render "Select an order" in the secondary pane - mail-client parity prevents confusing blank columns.
19. **Limit yourself to one `SplitView` per app:** Nesting split views or placing them inside tabs throws - split belongs at root with sidebar sections replacing bottom tabs on iPad.
20. **Start RSC with Server Functions only in SDK 57:** Enable `reactServerFunctions` inside normal client routes - avoid `reactServerComponentRoutes` in production until Stack/Tabs support returns.
21. **Wrap streamed Server Function UI in Suspense:** Every `renderX()` call from `"use server"` needs `<React.Suspense fallback={…}>` - otherwise loading states block the whole screen.
22. **Reach for `<Slot />` before custom `Navigator`:** Headless chrome (headers, onboarding progress) rarely needs `useNavigationBuilder` - custom navigators increase maintenance and SDK import surface.
23. **Import navigation primitives from `expo-router` paths:** SDK 56+ routes `@react-navigation/*` through `expo-router` and `expo-router/react-navigation` - direct package imports break on upgrade.
24. **Pass `redirect` query param through sign-in:** Deep link to protected content should resume post-login via `router.replace(redirect ?? '/(tabs)')` - do not drop the intended destination.
25. **Test cold-start deep links in CI matrices:** Verify `myapp://inbox/t2`, modal anchors, logged-out redirects, and Android hardware back on each release - navigation regressions are production incidents.

## FAQs

What is the first fix when back behavior feels wrong?

* Identify which navigator owns the current URL (`useSegments()`).
* Back pops the innermost stack; tab roots stop before exiting the app.
* See [Nested Navigators](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router-advanced/nested-navigators/).

Stack.Protected or Redirect - which should new apps use?

* **SDK 57+:** `Stack.Protected` / `Tabs.Protected` at root.
* **Redirect hub:** `app/index.tsx` only for default landing path.
* Do not duplicate both patterns on the same route condition.

When should I adopt NativeTabs?

* When system tab bar fidelity (liquid glass, badges, native a11y) outweighs alpha API risk.
* Keep JavaScript `Tabs` when you need `Tabs.Protected` inside the tab layout or fully custom tab bar JSX.

Are server components ready for my shipping app?

* **Not for primary navigation** in SDK 57 - EAS Update and full layouts are incomplete.
* Experiment on branches; keep production on client routes + standard navigators.

How do I avoid auth redirect loops?

1. `isLoading` gate before any navigator.
2. One root `Stack.Protected` authority.
3. `router.replace` after login.
4. No duplicate `index.tsx` in competing groups.

What should integration tests cover for advanced routing?

* `renderRouter` for href navigation and Protected redirects.
* Device tests for modal presentation, form sheet detents, and Android back.
* Cold-start deep link fixtures per platform.

Dokumen: Expo Router Advanced Highlights Summary
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router-advanced/highlights-summary/

# Expo Router Advanced Highlights Summary

Every highlight bullet from the 8 pages in this section, gathered on one page and grouped by the page it came from.

Highlights / Expo Router Advanced Highlights Summary

* Each \_layout.tsx owns one navigator - Stack, Tabs, or NativeTabs at that folder level
* Modal routes are files in app/ - set presentation on Stack.Screen, not a separate navigator
* Stack.Protected / Tabs.Protected guard screens by session - SDK 57+ preferred over redirect-only layouts
* NativeTabs from expo-router/unstable-native-tabs - alpha in SDK 57, uses system tab bars
* SplitView from expo-router/unstable-split-view - alpha, iOS-native; falls back to Slot on Android
* RSC in Expo Router is experimental/beta in SDK 57 - not production-default

## [Nested Navigators](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router-advanced/nested-navigators/)

* Each \_layout.tsx owns one navigator - Stack, Tabs, or NativeTabs at that folder level
* Back pops the innermost stack first; only when that stack is at root does back leave the tab
* Deep links use full paths (/home/messages) - no nested screen params object required
* Nest Stack inside each tab when tabs need headers and push screens
* Export unstable\_settings.anchor on modal stacks so deep links keep navigation context
* Avoid duplicate route files across groups - one screen belongs in one navigator tree

## [Modal & Presentation Routes](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router-advanced/modal-and-presentation-routes/)

* Modal routes are files in app/ - set presentation on Stack.Screen, not a separate navigator
* presentation: 'modal' slides up on iOS; Android back dismisses the modal stack
* formSheet supports detents - sheetAllowedDetents, sheetInitialDetentIndex, grabber on iOS
* Anchor deep-linked modals with unstable\_settings.anchor so background routes survive
* Prefer router.back() or href='../' on web - Android hardware back is automatic
* React Native Modal is for ephemeral UI; Expo Router modals belong in navigation history

## [Protected Routes & Middleware](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router-advanced/protected-routes-and-middleware/)

* Stack.Protected / Tabs.Protected guard screens by session - SDK 57+ preferred over redirect-only layouts
* All routes exist on disk; guards control client-side access, not file deletion
* Hydrate session before rendering navigators - SplashScreen until SecureStore read completes
* Never duplicate the same screen in two Protected groups - declare once with nested guards
* router.replace after login - push lets users swipe back to credential screens
* Expo Router has no native middleware on mobile - web server middleware is future; use client guards today

## [Native Tabs](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router-advanced/native-tabs/)

* NativeTabs from expo-router/unstable-native-tabs - alpha in SDK 57, uses system tab bars
* Unlike Stack/Tabs, routes are NOT auto-added - declare each NativeTabs.Trigger explicitly
* Nest Stack inside each tab folder for headers and push navigation
* SDK 55+ uses NativeTabs.Trigger.Icon / .Label / .Badge compound API
* hidden on Trigger removes a tab; disabled only blocks tab bar taps - router.push still works
* Fall back to JavaScript Tabs when you need fully custom tab bar UI

## [Split View & Tablet Layouts](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router-advanced/split-view-and-tablet-layouts/)

* SplitView from expo-router/unstable-split-view - alpha, iOS-native; falls back to Slot on Android
* Master-detail maps to URL segments - /orders and /orders/42, not parallel local state
* On iPhone, SplitView collapses to one column - topColumnForCollapsing picks the visible pane
* Responsive fallback: useWindowDimensions + conditional Stack or two-pane layout on Android tablet
* Only one SplitView per app - cannot nest inside other navigators except Slot
* Empty detail state needs [type]/index.tsx placeholder - Mail-style 'nothing selected'

## [Server Components Experiments](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router-advanced/server-components-experiments/)

* RSC in Expo Router is experimental/beta in SDK 57 - not production-default
* reactServerFunctions enables Server Functions; full route RSC needs reactServerComponentRoutes
* Server Functions stream RSC payloads to client - wrap in React.Suspense
* Full RSC mode breaks Stack/Tabs/Drawer layouts today - no stack routing yet
* EAS Update and DOM components do not support RSC in production yet
* Protected routes and API auth remain server-side - RSC does not replace mobile auth guards

## [Custom Navigators & Headless Router](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router-advanced/custom-navigators-and-headless-router/)

* Slot renders the active child route without adding a navigator - layout chrome only
* Navigator + useNavigationBuilder powers fully custom routers with file-based routes
* withLayoutContext ports existing React Navigation navigators into Expo Router
* Navigator.Slot renders the focused route inside custom navigator context
* Protected works with custom navigators via withLayoutContext
* Prefer Slot until you truly need custom transition or history semantics

## [Expo Router Advanced Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router-advanced/best-practices/)

* Model navigation as URLs - every screen worth restoring must have a file route
* Stack.Protected at root owns auth - avoid competing Redirect chains in nested layouts
* Anchor modal stacks for deep links - unstable\_settings.anchor preserves tab context
* Per-tab stacks preserve back history - do not expect one global pop order
* Treat alpha APIs (NativeTabs, SplitView, RSC) as feature-flagged experiments
* Test cold-start deep links on both platforms before every release

Dokumen: Modal & Presentation Routes
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router-advanced/modal-and-presentation-routes/

# Modal & Presentation Routes

Sheet modals, form sheets, and Android back handling. In Expo Router, modals are regular routes declared in `app/` with `presentation` set on `Stack.Screen`. They participate in deep linking, back stacks, and typed hrefs - unlike React Native's `<Modal>` component, which sits outside the router.

Highlights / Modal & Presentation Routes

* Modal routes are files in app/ - set presentation on Stack.Screen, not a separate navigator
* presentation: 'modal' slides up on iOS; Android back dismisses the modal stack
* formSheet supports detents - sheetAllowedDetents, sheetInitialDetentIndex, grabber on iOS
* Anchor deep-linked modals with unstable\_settings.anchor so background routes survive
* Prefer router.back() or href='../' on web - Android hardware back is automatic
* React Native Modal is for ephemeral UI; Expo Router modals belong in navigation history

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```text
app/
├── _layout.tsx
├── index.tsx
└── (app)/
    ├── _layout.tsx
    └── compose.tsx          # /compose - modal route
```

```tsx
// app/(app)/_layout.tsx
export const unstable_settings = {
  anchor: "(tabs)",
};
 
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
 
export default function AppLayout() {
  return (
    <Stack>
      <Stack.Screen name="(tabs)" options={{ headerShown: false }} />
      <Stack.Screen
        name="compose"
        options={{
          presentation: "modal",
          title: "New message",
        }}
      />
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// app/(app)/compose.tsx
import { router } from "expo-router";
import { Button, TextInput, View } from "react-native";
 
export default function ComposeModal() {
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1, padding: 16 }}>
      <TextInput placeholder="Write something…" style={{ flex: 1 }} />
      <Button title="Close" onPress={() => router.back()} />
    </View>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// Open from any screen
import { Link, router } from "expo-router";
 
<Link href="/compose" asChild>
  <Button title="Compose" />
</Link>
 
router.push("/compose");
```

**When to reach for this:**

* **Multi-step flows** that must be linkable (`/compose`, `/checkout`)
* **Form sheets** with draggable detents (filters, quick actions)
* **Auth sign-in overlay** while preserving deep link context behind the modal
* **Transparent overlays** (`transparentModal`) for lightweight pickers

## Working Example

Full-screen modal, form sheet with detents, and Android-aware dismiss.

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
import { SessionProvider } from "@/features/auth";
 
export default function RootLayout() {
  return (
    <SessionProvider>
      <Stack>
        <Stack.Screen name="(app)" options={{ headerShown: false }} />
        <Stack.Screen
          name="sign-in"
          options={{
            presentation: "modal",
            title: "Sign in",
          }}
        />
      </Stack>
    </SessionProvider>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// app/(app)/_layout.tsx
export const unstable_settings = {
  anchor: "(tabs)",
};
 
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
 
export default function AppLayout() {
  return (
    <Stack>
      <Stack.Screen name="(tabs)" options={{ headerShown: false }} />
      <Stack.Screen
        name="filters"
        options={{
          presentation: "formSheet",
          sheetAllowedDetents: [0.35, 0.6, 1],
          sheetInitialDetentIndex: 1,
          sheetGrabberVisible: true,
          sheetCornerRadius: 20,
          sheetLargestUndimmedDetentIndex: 0,
        }}
      />
      <Stack.Screen
        name="share"
        options={{
          presentation: "modal",
        }}
      />
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// app/(app)/filters.tsx - form sheet content
import { router } from "expo-router";
import { Button, ScrollView, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
export default function FiltersSheet() {
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1, backgroundColor: "white" }}>
      {/* Render title/actions in content - native headers unsupported in Android form sheets */}
      <Text style={{ fontSize: 18, fontWeight: "600", padding: 16 }}>Filters</Text>
      <ScrollView contentContainerStyle={{ padding: 16, gap: 12 }}>
        <Text>Status: Open</Text>
        <Text>Sort: Newest</Text>
      </ScrollView>
      <Button title="Apply" onPress={() => router.back()} />
    </View>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// app/sign-in.tsx - dismiss respects platform
import { Link, router } from "expo-router";
import { Platform, Pressable, Text, View } from "react-native";
import { StatusBar } from "expo-status-bar";
 
export default function SignInModal() {
  const canDismiss = router.canGoBack();
 
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1, justifyContent: "center", alignItems: "center" }}>
      <StatusBar style={Platform.OS === "ios" ? "light" : "auto"} />
      <Text>Sign in to continue</Text>
      {canDismiss && (
        <Link href="../" asChild>
          <Pressable style={{ marginTop: 24 }}>
            <Text>Dismiss</Text>
          </Pressable>
        </Link>
      )}
    </View>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// Android: hardware back calls router.back() automatically on modal routes.
// Optional explicit handler when intercepting back for dirty forms:
import { useEffect } from "react";
import { BackHandler } from "react-native";
import { router } from "expo-router";
 
export function useConfirmBackOnDirty(isDirty: boolean) {
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!isDirty) return;
    const sub = BackHandler.addEventListener("hardwareBackPress", () => {
      // Show discard dialog; return true to block default back
      router.back();
      return true;
    });
    return () => sub.remove();
  }, [isDirty]);
}
```

## Deep Dive

### Presentation modes

| `presentation` | iOS | Android |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `card` | Push from side (default) | Platform default push |
| `modal` | Slide from bottom | Slide over; **back dismisses** |
| `formSheet` | Detented bottom sheet | Bottom sheet (max 3 detents) |
| `transparentModal` | Previous screen visible | Falls back to `transparentModal` |
| `fullScreenModal` | Full screen cover | Falls back to `modal` |

Set options on `Stack.Screen` in the owning `_layout.tsx` - leaf files should stay thin.

### Form sheet detents

```tsx
options={{
  presentation: "formSheet",
  sheetAllowedDetents: [0.25, 0.5, 1],       // fractions of screen height
  sheetInitialDetentIndex: 0,                 // or 'last'
  sheetGrabberVisible: true,                  // iOS grabber
  sheetCornerRadius: 24,
  sheetLargestUndimmedDetentIndex: 1,         // dimming below this detent
}}
```

* **`fitToContents`** - auto height; content cannot use `flex: 1` (must size explicitly).
* **Numeric detents (SDK 55+)** - `flex: 1` works on iOS inside the sheet.
* **Android** - native stack headers and nested stacks inside form sheets are **not** supported; render chrome in sheet content.

### Android sheet footer (experimental)

```tsx
options={{
  presentation: "formSheet",
  sheetAllowedDetents: [0.5, 1],
  unstable_sheetFooter: () => (
    <View style={{ padding: 16 }}>
      <Button title="Confirm" onPress={() => router.back()} />
    </View>
  ),
}}
```

### Modal vs React Native `<Modal>`

|  | Expo Router modal route | RN `<Modal>` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| URL / deep link | Yes | No |
| Back stack | Yes | No |
| Android back | Automatic dismiss | Manual `onRequestClose` |
| Best for | Flows users may link to | Alerts, blocking loaders |

## Gotchas

* **Deep link to modal without anchor** - Background route is wiped. **Fix:** `export const unstable_settings = { anchor: 'index' }` on the stack layout.
* **Expecting stack headers inside Android form sheets** - They do not render. **Fix:** Custom header row in the sheet body.
* **More than three detents on Android** - Only first three apply. **Fix:** Cap `sheetAllowedDetents` at three for cross-platform parity.
* **Using `push` after modal dismiss for auth** - User can swipe back to login. **Fix:** `router.replace('/(tabs)')` after successful sign-in.
* **Nested modal stacks without planning** - Modal presenting another modal confuses back order. **Fix:** Single modal stack at one layout level; use steps inside one route or `fullScreenModal` for sub-steps.
* **Web modal with no dismiss UI** - No swipe-down on web. **Fix:** Check `router.canGoBack()` and render `<Link href="../">`.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `presentation: 'modal'` | Standard overlay flow | You need partial-height sheet |
| `presentation: 'formSheet'` | Filters, pickers, quick forms | Full-screen wizard with stack headers on Android |
| `transparentModal` | Toast-style panels over content | Opaque full workflows |
| React Native `<Modal>` | Confirm dialogs, blocking spinners | Route must appear in history / deep links |
| Bottom sheet library (Gorhom) | Highly custom gestures outside router | You want file-based `/sheet` URLs |

## FAQs

How does Android hardware back interact with modals?

* On a modal route, back pops the modal (same as `router.back()`).
* When the modal is dismissed, focus returns to the anchored route underneath.
* Intercept with `BackHandler` only when you need unsaved-change prompts.

Can I present a modal from inside a tab stack?

* Yes - define the modal on the **parent** stack that wraps the tabs.
* Modals declared inside a tab stack only cover that tab (valid for tab-scoped flows).

How do I style the iOS modal status bar?

```tsx
import { Platform } from "react-native";
import { StatusBar } from "expo-status-bar";
 
<StatusBar style={Platform.OS === "ios" ? "light" : "auto"} />
```

iOS modals default to dark backgrounds behind the status bar.

What is sheetLargestUndimmedDetentIndex?

* Detents at or below this index keep the background **undimmed**.
* Use when users should interact with content behind a partial sheet (maps, media).
* Set to `'none'` to always dim, `'last'` to never dim at largest detent.

Should sign-in be a modal or a separate auth stack?

* **Modal** - preserve deep link destination; dismiss after login.
* **Separate `(auth)` group** - cleaner back stack; use `router.replace` into app.
* See [Protected Routes & Middleware](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router-advanced/protected-routes-and-middleware/).

How do I test modal presentation?

Use `renderRouter` and assert navigation state after `router.push('/compose')`. Snapshot tests rarely capture native presentation - prefer integration tests on device/simulator.

Dokumen: Native Tabs
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router-advanced/native-tabs/

# Native Tabs

Platform tab bars via Expo Router native tabs API. `NativeTabs` from `expo-router/unstable-native-tabs` renders **UIKit / Material** tab bars - including iOS liquid glass styling - instead of JavaScript-drawn tabs. The API is **alpha** in SDK 57; pin behavior in QA before shipping production UX that depends on edge cases.

Highlights / Native Tabs

* NativeTabs from expo-router/unstable-native-tabs - alpha in SDK 57, uses system tab bars
* Unlike Stack/Tabs, routes are NOT auto-added - declare each NativeTabs.Trigger explicitly
* Nest Stack inside each tab folder for headers and push navigation
* SDK 55+ uses NativeTabs.Trigger.Icon / .Label / .Badge compound API
* hidden on Trigger removes a tab; disabled only blocks tab bar taps - router.push still works
* Fall back to JavaScript Tabs when you need fully custom tab bar UI

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```text
app/
├── _layout.tsx              # NativeTabs root
├── index.tsx                # first tab
├── explore.tsx
└── settings/
    ├── _layout.tsx          # Stack inside tab
    └── index.tsx
```

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx - SDK 57 (SDK 55+ compound API)
import { NativeTabs } from "expo-router/unstable-native-tabs";
 
export default function TabLayout() {
  return (
    <NativeTabs>
      <NativeTabs.Trigger name="index">
        <NativeTabs.Trigger.Label>Home</NativeTabs.Trigger.Label>
        <NativeTabs.Trigger.Icon
          sf={{ default: "house", selected: "house.fill" }}
          md="home"
        />
      </NativeTabs.Trigger>
 
      <NativeTabs.Trigger name="explore">
        <NativeTabs.Trigger.Label>Explore</NativeTabs.Trigger.Label>
        <NativeTabs.Trigger.Icon sf="safari" md="explore" />
      </NativeTabs.Trigger>
 
      <NativeTabs.Trigger name="settings">
        <NativeTabs.Trigger.Label>Settings</NativeTabs.Trigger.Label>
        <NativeTabs.Trigger.Icon sf="gear" md="settings" />
        <NativeTabs.Trigger.Badge>2</NativeTabs.Trigger.Badge>
      </NativeTabs.Trigger>
    </NativeTabs>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// app/settings/_layout.tsx - stack per tab (headers + push)
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
 
export default function SettingsStack() {
  return (
    <Stack>
      <Stack.Screen name="index" options={{ title: "Settings" }} />
      <Stack.Screen name="account" options={{ title: "Account" }} />
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

**When to reach for this:**

* **Platform-native tab chrome** - liquid glass, SF Symbols, system blur
* **Accessibility** - system tab bar VoiceOver / TalkBack behavior
* **Performance** - less JS layout work vs custom tab bars
* **Badges and native scroll-to-top** on tab re-tap (Android SDK 55+)

## Working Example

Native tabs with per-tab stacks, dynamic badge, conditional tab visibility, and iOS dynamic colors.

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx
import { DynamicColorIOS } from "react-native";
import { NativeTabs } from "expo-router/unstable-native-tabs";
import { useUnreadCount } from "@/features/inbox";
 
export default function TabLayout() {
  const unread = useUnreadCount();
  const showInbox = true; // feature flag - set before mount, not toggled live
 
  return (
    <NativeTabs
      labelStyle={{
        color: DynamicColorIOS({ dark: "white", light: "black" }),
      }}
      tintColor={DynamicColorIOS({ dark: "white", light: "#007AFF" })}
    >
      <NativeTabs.Trigger name="index" disablePopToTop={false}>
        <NativeTabs.Trigger.Label>Home</NativeTabs.Trigger.Label>
        <NativeTabs.Trigger.Icon
          sf={{ default: "house", selected: "house.fill" }}
          md={{ default: "home", selected: "home" }}
        />
      </NativeTabs.Trigger>
 
      <NativeTabs.Trigger name="inbox" hidden={!showInbox}>
        <NativeTabs.Trigger.Label>Inbox</NativeTabs.Trigger.Label>
        <NativeTabs.Trigger.Icon sf="tray" md="inbox" />
        {unread > 0 && <NativeTabs.Trigger.Badge>{unread > 9 ? "9+" : unread}</NativeTabs.Trigger.Badge>}
      </NativeTabs.Trigger>
 
      <NativeTabs.Trigger name="settings">
        <NativeTabs.Trigger.Label hidden />
        <NativeTabs.Trigger.Icon sf="gear" md="settings" />
      </NativeTabs.Trigger>
    </NativeTabs>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// app/inbox/_layout.tsx
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
 
export default function InboxStack() {
  return (
    <Stack>
      <Stack.Screen name="index" options={{ title: "Inbox" }} />
      <Stack.Screen name="[id]" options={{ title: "Message" }} />
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// Hiding tab bar on focused screen (SDK 55+ hidden prop on NativeTabs)
import { createContext, use, useState } from "react";
import { NativeTabs } from "expo-router/unstable-native-tabs";
import { useFocusEffect } from "expo-router";
 
export const TabBarContext = createContext({
  setTabBarHidden: (_hidden: boolean) => {},
});
 
export default function TabLayout() {
  const [hidden, setTabBarHidden] = useState(false);
 
  return (
    <TabBarContext value={{ setTabBarHidden }}>
      <NativeTabs hidden={hidden}>
        <NativeTabs.Trigger name="index">
          <NativeTabs.Trigger.Label>Home</NativeTabs.Trigger.Label>
        </NativeTabs.Trigger>
      </NativeTabs>
    </TabBarContext>
  );
}
 
// In immersive screen:
export function useHideTabBarOnFocus() {
  const { setTabBarHidden } = use(TabBarContext);
  useFocusEffect(() => {
    setTabBarHidden(true);
    return () => setTabBarHidden(false);
  });
}
```

## Deep Dive

### Native tabs vs JavaScript tabs

|  | `NativeTabs` | `Tabs` (expo-router) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tab bar rendering | Native system | React Navigation JS |
| Route registration | Manual `Trigger` per route | Auto from `app/` files |
| Custom tab bar UI | Limited | `tabBar` prop, full custom |
| Stack inside tab | ✅ Recommended | ✅ |
| `Tabs.Protected` | Use root `Stack.Protected` wrapping tabs | ✅ Built-in |
| Status | Alpha (SDK 54+) | Stable |

### Icon sources

```tsx
<NativeTabs.Trigger.Icon
  sf={{ default: "star", selected: "star.fill" }}  // SF Symbols (iOS)
  md={{ default: "star", selected: "star" }}     // Material Symbols (Android)
  src={require("@/assets/icon.png")}             // Custom image
  xcasset="home-icon"                            // iOS asset catalog (SDK 55+)
  renderingMode="template"                       // iOS tint vs original colors
/>
```

* **`sf` takes precedence on iOS** over `src`; Android uses `src` / `md`.
* **Distinct selected icons on Android** need SDK 56+ / `react-native-screens` 4.25+.
* **Vector icon fonts** - rasterize with `@react-native-vector-icons/get-image` at module scope.

### Tab interaction props (SDK 55+)

| Prop | Platform | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `disablePopToTop` | Android | Re-tap does not pop stack to root |
| `disableScrollToTop` | Android | Re-tap does not scroll list to top |
| `hidden` | Both | Tab not shown; **not navigable** |
| `disabled` | SDK 56+ | Tab visible but not tappable; **JS navigation still works** |

> Dynamically hiding tabs **remounts** the navigator and resets state. Toggle visibility before first mount or when the tab bar is not visible.

### Nesting with root stack

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx at project root is often a Stack, not NativeTabs
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
 
export default function RootLayout() {
  return (
    <Stack screenOptions={{ headerShown: false }}>
      <Stack.Screen name="(tabs)" />
      <Stack.Screen name="compose" options={{ presentation: "modal" }} />
    </Stack>
  );
}
 
// app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx - NativeTabs live one level down
```

See [Nested Navigators](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router-advanced/nested-navigators/).

## Gotchas

* **Forgetting `NativeTabs.Trigger`** - Files in `app/` do not appear in the tab bar automatically. **Fix:** Add a `Trigger` for every routable tab.
* **Using `disabled` for auth gating** - `router.push('/settings')` bypasses disabled. **Fix:** `Stack.Protected` at root.
* **Toggling `hidden` at runtime** - Remounts navigator; loses stack state. **Fix:** Feature flags resolved before first render.
* **Custom tab bar branding** - Native tabs follow system chrome. **Fix:** JavaScript [custom tabs](https://docs.expo.dev/router/advanced/custom-tabs/) or `Tabs` with `tabBar` prop.
* **Expecting `Tabs.Protected` on NativeTabs** - Use outer stack guards. **Fix:** Wrap `(tabs)` group in `Stack.Protected`.
* **Alpha API breaking changes** - Pin `expo-router` and read SDK changelog before upgrade. **Fix:** QA tab icons, badges, and back behavior each SDK bump.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `NativeTabs` | System-native look, liquid glass iOS | Fully custom tab bar design |
| JavaScript `Tabs` | `Tabs.Protected`, custom `tabBar` | You need UIKit tab bar fidelity |
| Custom tabs (`expo-router/ui`) | Marketing-heavy branded chrome | You want zero maintenance of tab primitives |
| Bottom sheet nav | Single primary action surface | Standard 3–5 section app |
| No tabs - drawer only | Many sections, few top-level | Phone-first 4-tab product pattern |

## FAQs

How do I migrate from JavaScript Tabs to NativeTabs?

1. Replace `import { Tabs }` with `NativeTabs` from `expo-router/unstable-native-tabs`.
2. Add `NativeTabs.Trigger` for each former `Tabs.Screen`.
3. Move icons into `NativeTabs.Trigger.Icon` (SDK 55+ compound API).
4. Keep per-tab `_layout.tsx` stacks unchanged.

Can native tabs use expo-router typed routes?

* Yes - `name` on `Trigger` matches the route file (`index`, `settings`, folder names).
* `Link href="/settings/account"` works the same as with JavaScript tabs.

How do badges update with new messages?

* Re-render `NativeTabs.Trigger.Badge` when unread count changes.
* Badge is declarative - no imperative API.
* Empty badge dot: `<NativeTabs.Trigger.Badge />` with no children.

Why do selected icons look the same on Android?

* Distinct `selected` variants for `src` / `md` require SDK 56+ and `react-native-screens` 4.25+.
* Upgrade or use `@react-native-vector-icons/get-image` with separate glyphs.

Native tabs vs compound in-screen tabs?

* **NativeTabs** - route-level navigation; each tab is a URL.
* **Compound tabs** (component patterns) - local panel switching inside one screen.
* See [../component-patterns/compound-components/compound-components.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/compound-components/).

Is NativeTabs production-ready?

* Documented as **alpha** - API may change.
* Suitable for teams that accept SDK churn and test on real devices each release.
* Use stable JavaScript `Tabs` when compliance requires frozen navigation APIs.

## Related

* [Split View & Tablet Layouts](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router-advanced/split-view-and-tablet-layouts/) - tablet patterns beyond bottom tabs

Dokumen: Nested Navigators
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router-advanced/nested-navigators/

# Nested Navigators

Stacks inside tabs inside stacks without losing back behavior. Each `app/**/_layout.tsx` declares a navigator; child routes inherit that shell. Expo Router maps URLs to the correct nested screen - you navigate with full paths like `/orders/42`, not React Navigation's `{ screen, params }` objects.

Highlights / Nested Navigators

* Each \_layout.tsx owns one navigator - Stack, Tabs, or NativeTabs at that folder level
* Back pops the innermost stack first; only when that stack is at root does back leave the tab
* Deep links use full paths (/home/messages) - no nested screen params object required
* Nest Stack inside each tab when tabs need headers and push screens
* Export unstable\_settings.anchor on modal stacks so deep links keep navigation context
* Avoid duplicate route files across groups - one screen belongs in one navigator tree

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```text
app/
├── _layout.tsx              # Root Stack
├── index.tsx
└── (app)/
    ├── _layout.tsx          # Tabs (or NativeTabs)
    └── (tabs)/
        ├── _layout.tsx      # Tab bar
        ├── home/
        │   ├── _layout.tsx  # Stack per tab
        │   ├── index.tsx    # /home
        │   └── feed.tsx     # /home/feed
        └── settings/
            ├── _layout.tsx
            └── index.tsx
```

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx - root stack wraps the tab group
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
 
export default function RootLayout() {
  return (
    <Stack screenOptions={{ headerShown: false }}>
      <Stack.Screen name="(app)" />
      <Stack.Screen
        name="compose"
        options={{ presentation: "modal", title: "New post" }}
      />
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// app/(app)/(tabs)/_layout.tsx - tabs own four stacks
import { Tabs } from "expo-router";
 
export default function TabLayout() {
  return (
    <Tabs>
      <Tabs.Screen name="home" options={{ title: "Home" }} />
      <Tabs.Screen name="search" options={{ title: "Search" }} />
      <Tabs.Screen name="inbox" options={{ title: "Inbox" }} />
      <Tabs.Screen name="profile" options={{ title: "Profile" }} />
    </Tabs>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// app/(app)/(tabs)/home/_layout.tsx - stack inside one tab
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
 
export default function HomeStackLayout() {
  return (
    <Stack>
      <Stack.Screen name="index" options={{ title: "Home" }} />
      <Stack.Screen name="feed" options={{ title: "Feed" }} />
      <Stack.Screen name="[id]" options={{ title: "Post" }} />
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

**When to reach for this:**

* **Tabs + detail pushes** - each tab keeps its own back stack
* **Modal over tabs** - root stack presents `compose` above the tab shell
* **Auth group inside root stack** - `(auth)` and `(app)` as sibling stacks
* **Native tabs + headers** - nest `<Stack />` inside each native tab folder

## Working Example

Root stack → tabs → per-tab stacks, with predictable back behavior and deep-link targets.

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
import { SessionProvider } from "@/features/auth";
 
export default function RootLayout() {
  return (
    <SessionProvider>
      <Stack>
        <Stack.Screen name="(app)" options={{ headerShown: false }} />
        <Stack.Screen name="(auth)" options={{ headerShown: false }} />
      </Stack>
    </SessionProvider>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// app/(app)/(tabs)/_layout.tsx
import { Tabs } from "expo-router";
 
export default function TabsLayout() {
  return (
    <Tabs screenOptions={{ headerShown: false }}>
      <Tabs.Screen name="home" options={{ tabBarLabel: "Home" }} />
      <Tabs.Screen name="inbox" options={{ tabBarLabel: "Inbox" }} />
    </Tabs>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// app/(app)/(tabs)/inbox/_layout.tsx
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
 
export default function InboxStackLayout() {
  return (
    <Stack>
      <Stack.Screen name="index" options={{ title: "Inbox" }} />
      <Stack.Screen name="[threadId]" options={{ title: "Thread" }} />
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// app/(app)/(tabs)/inbox/index.tsx
import { Link, router } from "expo-router";
import { FlatList, Pressable, Text } from "react-native";
 
const threads = [{ id: "t1", subject: "Hello" }, { id: "t2", subject: "Ship it" }];
 
export default function InboxListScreen() {
  return (
    <FlatList
      data={threads}
      keyExtractor={(item) => item.id}
      renderItem={({ item }) => (
        <Pressable onPress={() => router.push(`/inbox/${item.id}`)}>
          <Text style={{ padding: 16 }}>{item.subject}</Text>
        </Pressable>
      )}
    />
  );
}
```

```tsx
// app/(app)/(tabs)/inbox/[threadId].tsx
import { Link, useLocalSearchParams, useRouter } from "expo-router";
import { Button, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
export default function ThreadScreen() {
  const { threadId } = useLocalSearchParams<{ threadId: string }>();
  const router = useRouter();
 
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1, padding: 16 }}>
      <Text>Thread: {threadId}</Text>
      <Button title="Back" onPress={() => router.back()} />
      <Link href="/compose" asChild>
        <Button title="Reply (modal)" />
      </Link>
    </View>

}
```

```tsx
// Deep link - lands on thread inside inbox tab, back returns to inbox list
// myapp://inbox/t2
import { router } from "expo-router";
router.push("/inbox/t2");
```

## Deep Dive

### Back stack mental model

React Navigation nests navigators; Expo Router expresses the same tree through folders:

```text
User on /inbox/t2 presses Android back:
 
1. Inbox Stack pops t2 → /inbox (list)
2. User presses back again → stays on Inbox tab (tab root has nowhere to pop)
3. User switches to Home tab → Inbox stack state is preserved (default)
4. User opens /compose modal → back dismisses modal, tabs remain underneath
```

Control tab reset behavior with `unmountOnBlur` on `Tabs.Screen` when stale stacks are unacceptable (e.g. wizard flows).

### Stack inside native tabs

When using [Native Tabs](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router-advanced/native-tabs/), each tab folder gets its own `_layout.tsx` exporting `<Stack />`:

```tsx
// app/(app)/(native-tabs)/inbox/_layout.tsx
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
 
export default function InboxStack() {
  return <Stack />;
}
```

Native tab triggers do not auto-pop nested stacks unless `disablePopToTop` is false (default on Android SDK 55+).

### Modal anchoring for nested stacks

Deep-linking directly to a modal route without an anchor wipes the screen behind it. Export `unstable_settings` on the stack that owns the modal:

```tsx
// app/(app)/_layout.tsx
export const unstable_settings = {
  anchor: "(tabs)",
};
 
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
 
export default function AppLayout() {
  return (
    <Stack>
      <Stack.Screen name="(tabs)" />
      <Stack.Screen name="filters" options={{ presentation: "modal" }} />
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

### Navigating across nested boundaries

| Goal | Expo Router |
| --- | --- |
| Open thread in inbox tab | `router.push("/inbox/t2")` |
| Switch tab and reset its stack | `router.replace("/home")` |
| Open modal above tabs | `router.push("/compose")` |
| Pop to tab root | `router.dismissTo("/inbox")` or tab re-tap (native tabs) |

Prefer `router.replace` after auth transitions so users cannot swipe back into credential screens - see [../expo-router/redirects-and-index-routes/redirects-and-index-routes.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/redirects-and-index-routes/).

## Gotchas

* **Expecting one global back stack** - Each tab maintains its own stack. **Fix:** Design URLs per tab; document which flows use `replace` vs `push`.
* **Modal deep link with no anchor** - Opening `/compose` cold starts with no tab context. **Fix:** Set `unstable_settings.anchor` on the parent stack.
* **Duplicating screens across navigators** - Same `profile.tsx` in two tab folders causes ambiguous routes. **Fix:** One file per URL; use [shared routes](https://docs.expo.dev/router/advanced/shared-routes/) if truly needed.
* **Returning `null` from root layout** - Blocks static rendering and can break nested hydration. **Fix:** Splash screen + session provider; render `<Stack />` once ready.
* **Pushing with relative paths across tabs** - `../settings` from `/inbox/t2` may not land where you expect. **Fix:** Use absolute hrefs (`/settings`) with typed routes.
* **Nesting Drawer inside Tabs without planning** - Gesture conflicts and double headers. **Fix:** Drawer at root or tabs inside drawer - pick one primary pattern per app.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Single root stack (no tabs) | Linear flows, onboarding wizards | Four+ top-level destinations |
| Tabs without per-tab stacks | Flat tab content, no detail pushes | Each tab needs list → detail |
| Native tabs + per-tab stacks | Platform tab bar + headers | You need fully custom tab UI |
| One stack + segment-based UI | Simple two-pane tablet layout | True independent back stacks per section |
| React Native `Modal` component | Ephemeral alerts, no URL needed | Flow must be deep-linkable or in history |

## FAQs

Why does Android back stay on the tab instead of leaving the app?

* Back pops the **innermost** navigator first.
* At a tab's root screen, there is nothing left to pop inside that tab.
* Use `BackHandler` at true app exit points (e.g. home tab root) if product requires double-back-to-exit.

How do I reset a tab's stack when re-selecting it?

* JavaScript tabs: configure tab press listeners via React Navigation options.
* Native tabs: default re-tap pops to root; use `disablePopToTop` on `NativeTabs.Trigger` to keep depth.

Can I nest a Drawer inside Tabs?

```text
app/(app)/_layout.tsx     → Drawer
app/(app)/(drawer)/_layout.tsx → Stack or Tabs child
```

Yes - but prefer **one** primary shell. Deep nesting increases back-stack confusion and bundle size.

How do typed routes work with nesting?

* Enable `experiments.typedRoutes` in app config.
* Hrefs like `/(app)/(tabs)/inbox/[threadId]` generate compile-time checks.
* See [../expo-router/typed-routes/typed-routes.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/typed-routes/).

Should modals live in the root stack or inside a tab stack?

* **Root stack** - global compose, filters, media picker (visible from any tab).
* **Tab stack** - detail actions scoped to one section (edit single inbox thread).
* Root modals need `anchor` for deep links.

How do I test nested navigation?

```tsx
import { renderRouter, screen } from "expo-router/testing-library";
 
renderRouter({
  "inbox/index": () => <InboxListScreen />,
  "inbox/[threadId]": () => <ThreadScreen />,
});
```

Assert pathname segments after `router.push` - see [../testing/react-native-testing-library/react-native-testing-library.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/react-native-testing-library/).

Dokumen: Protected Routes & Middleware
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router-advanced/protected-routes-and-middleware/

# Protected Routes & Middleware

Auth gates, role checks, and redirect loop prevention. Expo Router SDK 57 introduces `Stack.Protected` and `Tabs.Protected` with `guard` booleans - the recommended pattern over sprinkling `<Redirect />` in every layout. Session hydration still lives in React context backed by [../auth-session/](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/) storage; protected routes react when `guard` flips.

Highlights / Protected Routes & Middleware

* Stack.Protected / Tabs.Protected guard screens by session - SDK 57+ preferred over redirect-only layouts
* All routes exist on disk; guards control client-side access, not file deletion
* Hydrate session before rendering navigators - SplashScreen until SecureStore read completes
* Never duplicate the same screen in two Protected groups - declare once with nested guards
* router.replace after login - push lets users swipe back to credential screens
* Expo Router has no native middleware on mobile - web server middleware is future; use client guards today

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```text
app/
├── _layout.tsx          # SessionProvider + Stack.Protected
├── sign-in.tsx          # guard={!session}
└── (app)/
    ├── _layout.tsx      # authenticated stack
    └── (tabs)/...
```

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
import { SplashScreen } from "expo-router";
import { SessionProvider, useSession } from "@/features/auth";
 
SplashScreen.preventAutoHideAsync();
 
export default function RootLayout() {
  return (
    <SessionProvider>
      <SplashScreenController />
      <RootNavigator />
    </SessionProvider>
  );
}
 
function SplashScreenController() {
  const { isLoading } = useSession();
  if (!isLoading) SplashScreen.hideAsync();
  return null;
}
 
function RootNavigator() {
  const { session } = useSession();
 
  return (
    <Stack>
      <Stack.Protected guard={!!session}>
        <Stack.Screen name="(app)" />
      </Stack.Protected>
 
      <Stack.Protected guard={!session}>
        <Stack.Screen name="sign-in" />
      </Stack.Protected>
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// app/sign-in.tsx
import { router } from "expo-router";
import { Button, View } from "react-native";
import { useSession } from "@/features/auth";
 
export default function SignInScreen() {
  const { signIn } = useSession();
 
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1, justifyContent: "center", alignItems: "center" }}>
      <Button
        title="Sign in"
        onPress={async () => {
          await signIn();
          router.replace("/(app)/(tabs)");
        }}
      />
    </View>
  );
}
```

**When to reach for this:**

* **Binary auth** - signed-in vs guest route sets
* **Role gates** - nested `Stack.Protected` for admin-only screens
* **Tab visibility** - hide `profile` tab until authenticated
* **Session expiry** - `guard` flips false → user redirected off protected screens automatically

## Working Example

Session provider, nested role protection, redirect hub fallback, and loop-safe patterns.

```tsx
// features/auth/model/SessionProvider.tsx
import { createContext, use, useEffect, useState, type PropsWithChildren } from "react";
import * as SecureStore from "expo-secure-store";
 
type Session = { userId: string; role: "user" | "admin" } | null;
 
const AuthContext = createContext<{
  session: Session;
  isLoading: boolean;
  signIn: () => Promise<void>;
  signOut: () => Promise<void>;
} | null>(null);
 
export function useSession() {
  const ctx = use(AuthContext);
  if (!ctx) throw new Error("useSession requires SessionProvider");
  return ctx;
}
 
export function SessionProvider({ children }: PropsWithChildren) {
  const [session, setSession] = useState<Session>(null);
  const [isLoading, setLoading] = useState(true);
 
  useEffect(() => {
    SecureStore.getItemAsync("session")
      .then((raw) => setSession(raw ? JSON.parse(raw) : null))
      .finally(() => setLoading(false));
  }, []);
 
  const signIn = async () => {
    const next: Session = { userId: "u1", role: "user" };
    await SecureStore.setItemAsync("session", JSON.stringify(next));
    setSession(next);
  };
 
  const signOut = async () => {
    await SecureStore.deleteItemAsync("session");
    setSession(null);
  };
 
  return (
    <AuthContext value={{ session, isLoading, signIn, signOut }}>
      {children}
    </AuthContext>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx - root guards
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
import { SessionProvider, useSession } from "@/features/auth";
 
function RootNavigator() {
  const { session, isLoading } = useSession();
 
  if (isLoading) return null;
 
  const isLoggedIn = !!session;
  const isAdmin = session?.role === "admin";
 
  return (
    <Stack>
      <Stack.Protected guard={isLoggedIn}>
        <Stack.Protected guard={isAdmin}>
          <Stack.Screen name="admin" />
        </Stack.Protected>
        <Stack.Screen name="(app)" />
      </Stack.Protected>
 
      <Stack.Protected guard={!isLoggedIn}>
        <Stack.Screen name="sign-in" />
      </Stack.Protected>
    </Stack>
  );
}
 
export default function RootLayout() {
  return (
    <SessionProvider>
      <RootNavigator />
    </SessionProvider>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// app/index.tsx - optional redirect hub (avoid fighting Stack.Protected)
import { Redirect } from "expo-router";
import { useSession } from "@/features/auth";
 
export default function Index() {
  const { session, isLoading } = useSession();
  if (isLoading) return null;
  if (session) return <Redirect href="/(app)/(tabs)" />;
  return <Redirect href="/sign-in" />;
}
```

```tsx
// app/(app)/(tabs)/_layout.tsx - protect individual tabs
import { Tabs } from "expo-router";
import { useSession } from "@/features/auth";
 
export default function TabsLayout() {
  const { session } = useSession();
  const isLoggedIn = !!session;
 
  return (
    <Tabs>
      <Tabs.Screen name="home" options={{ title: "Home" }} />
      <Tabs.Protected guard={isLoggedIn}>
        <Tabs.Screen name="inbox" options={{ title: "Inbox" }} />
        <Tabs.Screen name="profile" options={{ title: "Profile" }} />
      </Tabs.Protected>
    </Tabs>
  );
}
```

## Deep Dive

### How `guard` redirects work

When `guard` is `false`:

1. User cannot **client-navigate** to protected screens (Link, `router.push`).
2. If already on a protected screen when `guard` becomes false, router redirects to the **anchor** route (usually `index`) or the **first available** screen in the stack.
3. History entries for that protected subtree are **removed** when guard flips false.

Place the sign-in screen **outside** the authenticated `Stack.Protected` group so guests always have a fallback target.

### Avoiding redirect loops

| Anti-pattern | Loop | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `index` redirects to `/sign-in` while sign-in redirects to `/` | Infinite bounce | Use `Stack.Protected` - only one authority decides fallback |
| Both `(auth)` and `(app)` own `index.tsx` at `/` | Ambiguous `/` | Single `app/index.tsx` hub |
| Redirect before `isLoading === false` | Flash sign-in → home → sign-in | `return null` until hydration completes |
| `sign-in` inside authenticated group | No fallback when logged out | `guard={!session}` group for auth screens |
| `router.push` after login | Back to sign-in | `router.replace` |

```tsx
// ❌ Loop risk - two layouts both redirect on /
// (auth)/_layout.tsx
if (!session) return <Redirect href="/sign-in" />;
// (app)/_layout.tsx
if (!session) return <Redirect href="/sign-in" />;
 
// ✅ Single source of truth
// app/_layout.tsx - Stack.Protected only
```

### Middleware: what exists in SDK 57

Expo Router **does not** ship Next.js-style route middleware on native. On web, routing is primarily static generation today - **no custom server middleware** for per-request auth redirects.

| Layer | Native | Web (SDK 57) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Stack.Protected` | ✅ Client guard | ✅ Client guard |
| `<Redirect />` in layouts | ✅ | ✅ |
| Server middleware | ❌ | ❌ (not yet) |
| API route auth | Separate concern | `app/api/**` + your server |

Treat protected routes as **UX gates**, not security boundaries. Validate tokens on every API call - see [../auth-session/mobile-auth-basics/mobile-auth-basics.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/mobile-auth-basics/) and [../auth-session/securestore-and-keychain-keystore/securestore-and-keychain-keystore.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/securestore-and-keychain-keystore/).

### Deep links while logged out

A user opening `myapp://inbox/42` while logged out hits a protected screen → router redirects to the first available unguarded screen (`sign-in`). After login, `router.replace` to the intended href:

```tsx
const redirect = useGlobalSearchParams<{ redirect?: string }>();
 
await signIn();
router.replace((redirect as `/${string}`) ?? "/(app)/(tabs)");
```

Pass `redirect` query param when sending users to sign-in.

### Sign-out behavior

Calling `signOut()` flips `guard` to false. Protected history is cleared automatically - user should land on `sign-in` without manual `router.replace` if layouts are wired correctly.

## Gotchas

* **Protected routes ≠ server security** - URLs are still in the bundle. **Fix:** API authorization, token expiry, certificate pinning for sensitive apps.
* **Duplicating screens across Protected groups** - Same `profile` in two groups throws. **Fix:** One declaration; nest guards for roles.
* **Rendering navigators before hydration** - Brief false `guard` causes redirect flicker. **Fix:** SplashScreen + `isLoading` gate.
* **Using `disabled` on native tabs as auth** - `disabled` only blocks tab bar taps; `router.push` still works. **Fix:** `Tabs.Protected` or root `Stack.Protected`.
* **Static web export of protected routes** - Protected screens are skipped at build time; direct URL access may still fetch JS. **Fix:** Do not rely on SSG for secrecy.
* **Modal sign-in without anchor** - Deep link context lost. **Fix:** `unstable_settings.anchor` - see [Modal & Presentation Routes](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router-advanced/modal-and-presentation-routes/).

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Stack.Protected` | SDK 57+ auth shells | You must support Expo Router < 5 |
| `<Redirect />` in layouts | Simple hub, legacy code | Complex role matrix (prefer nested Protected) |
| Imperative `router.replace` only | One-off post-login | Ongoing session enforcement |
| Feature-level guards in screens | Extra sensitive action (delete account) | Replacing layout-level auth entirely |
| Server session (web API routes) | Token refresh, RBAC on server | Expecting it to block native navigation alone |

## FAQs

Stack.Protected vs Redirect - which wins?

* Prefer **`Stack.Protected`** for navigator-level access in SDK 57+.
* Use **`<Redirect />`** in `app/index.tsx` as a landing hub, not in every nested layout.
* Do not combine conflicting rules on the same route.

How do nested role guards compose?

```tsx
<Stack.Protected guard={isLoggedIn}>
  <Stack.Protected guard={isAdmin}>
    <Stack.Screen name="admin" />
  </Stack.Protected>
  <Stack.Screen name="(app)" />
</Stack.Protected>
```

`/admin` requires both guards true. `/about` under the outer group requires login only.

What happens when guard changes while user is on a protected screen?

* Router redirects to anchor or first available screen.
* Protected screen history is **removed** from the stack.
* No manual `router.replace('/sign-in')` required if sign-in is the unguarded fallback.

Can I use expo-auth-session with protected routes?

* Yes - OAuth completes in `sign-in.tsx`; persist tokens in SecureStore; set session state.
* See [../auth-session/expo-auth-session-and-oauth/expo-auth-session-and-oauth.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/expo-auth-session-and-oauth/).

How do I prevent the sign-in ↔ home loop?

1. Wait for `isLoading === false` before any redirect.
2. Single guard authority at root `Stack.Protected`.
3. `router.replace` after login, never `push`.
4. One `app/index.tsx` - no competing index routes in groups.

Is there Expo Router middleware like Next.js?

* **Not on native** - use client guards.
* **Web** - middleware-style server redirects are not supported yet; use client `Stack.Protected` and loading states.
* API routes authenticate separately on the server.
