Dokumen: Forms Basics
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/forms-input/forms-basics/

# Forms Basics

Controlled TextInput, focus flow, and mobile keyboard types.

Highlights / Forms Basics

* Controlled inputs store value in React state and update via onChangeText
* keyboardType picks the correct software keyboard - email, numeric, phone
* returnKeyType labels the action key - next, done, go, search
* blurOnSubmit=false keeps focus moving between fields without dismissing the keyboard
* Refs call .focus() for autofocus, error recovery, and programmatic focus chains
* onSubmitEditing wires the keyboard action key to focus the next field or submit
* keyboardShouldPersistTaps="handled" lets submit buttons work on the first tap

## Prerequisites

Every example below uses built-in React Native primitives - no form libraries. Scaffold a standard **Expo SDK 57** TypeScript app and replace `App.tsx` to run each snippet.

```bash
npx create-expo-app@latest MyFormsApp --template blank-typescript
cd MyFormsApp
npx expo start
```

> **Tooling:** These examples target **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4), **React Native 0.86.0**, and **React 19.2.3**.

---

## Basic Examples

### 1. Controlled TextInput

On mobile, `TextInput` is **always controlled** when you care about validation, submission, or resetting fields. Mirror web React: hold `value` in state and update it in `onChangeText`.

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { StyleSheet, Text, TextInput, View } from "react-native";
 
export default function App() {
  const [name, setName] = useState("");
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.screen}>
      <Text style={styles.label}>Display name</Text>
      <TextInput
        style={styles.input}
        value={name}
        onChangeText={setName}
        placeholder="Alex Chen"
        placeholderTextColor="#94a3b8"
      />
      <Text style={styles.preview}>
        {name.length === 0 ? "Type to preview" : `Hello, ${name}`}
      </Text>
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  screen: { flex: 1, padding: 16, gap: 8 },
  label: { fontSize: 14, fontWeight: "600", color: "#334155" },
  input: {
    borderWidth: 1,
    borderColor: "#cbd5e1",
    borderRadius: 10,
    paddingHorizontal: 14,
    paddingVertical: 12,
    fontSize: 16,
    backgroundColor: "#fff",
  },
  preview: { fontSize: 15, color: "#64748b", marginTop: 4 },
});
```

* `onChangeText` receives a **string** - not a synthetic event like web `onChange`
* `value={name}` makes the native field a controlled component; omit `value` only for fully uncontrolled prototypes
* Reset a field by calling `setName("")` from a button or after successful submit
* Pair controlled state with validation libraries later - see react-hook-form and Zod guides when forms grow past a few fields

> **Related:** [react-hook-form on Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/forms-input/react-hook-form-on-mobile/) - fewer re-renders when many inputs share one screen

---

### 2. keyboardType and autoCapitalize

`keyboardType` selects the **software keyboard layout**. Combine it with `autoCapitalize` and `autoCorrect` so users get the right keys and autocorrect behavior per field.

```tsx
import { useState, type ReactNode } from "react";
import { StyleSheet, Text, TextInput, View } from "react-native";
 
export default function App() {
  const [email, setEmail] = useState("");
  const [age, setAge] = useState("");
  const [phone, setPhone] = useState("");
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.screen}>
      <Field label="Email">
        <TextInput
          style={styles.input}
          value={email}
          onChangeText={setEmail}
          keyboardType="email-address"
          autoCapitalize="none"
          autoCorrect={false}
          textContentType="emailAddress"
          placeholder="you@example.com"
        />
      </Field>
 
      <Field label="Age">
        <TextInput
          style={styles.input}
          value={age}
          onChangeText={setAge}
          keyboardType="number-pad"
          placeholder="25"
        />
      </Field>
 
      <Field label="Phone">
        <TextInput
          style={styles.input}
          value={phone}
          onChangeText={setPhone}
          keyboardType="phone-pad"
          textContentType="telephoneNumber"
          placeholder="(555) 010-2030"
        />
      </Field>
    </View>
  );
}
 
function Field({ label, children }: { label: string; children: ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <View style={styles.field}>
      <Text style={styles.label}>{label}</Text>
      {children}
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  screen: { flex: 1, padding: 16, gap: 16 },
  field: { gap: 6 },
  label: { fontSize: 14, fontWeight: "600", color: "#334155" },
  input: {
    borderWidth: 1,
    borderColor: "#cbd5e1",
    borderRadius: 10,
    paddingHorizontal: 14,
    paddingVertical: 12,
    fontSize: 16,
    backgroundColor: "#fff",
  },
});
```

* Common `keyboardType` values: `default`, `email-address`, `numeric`, `number-pad`, `phone-pad`, `decimal-pad`, `url`
* `email-address` and `url` keyboards include `@` and `/` - still set `autoCapitalize="none"` because sentence-case defaults are annoying in those fields
* `number-pad` and `phone-pad` have **no Return key** - plan submit via an on-screen button or move focus with refs
* `textContentType` (iOS) and `autoComplete` (Android) improve password-manager and SMS autofill - expand in the password example below

> **Related:** [Pickers, Date/Time & Native Inputs](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/forms-input/pickers-date-time-and-native-inputs/) - when a native picker beats free-text entry

---

### 3. returnKeyType

`returnKeyType` relabels the keyboard's **action key** - "Next", "Done", "Go", "Search". Match the label to what actually happens when the user taps it.

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { StyleSheet, Text, TextInput, View } from "react-native";
 
export default function App() {
  const [query, setQuery] = useState("");
  const [note, setNote] = useState("");
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.screen}>
      <Text style={styles.label}>Search</Text>
      <TextInput
        style={styles.input}
        value={query}
        onChangeText={setQuery}
        returnKeyType="search"
        onSubmitEditing={() => console.log("search:", query)}
        placeholder="Find articles"
      />
 
      <Text style={styles.label}>Bio</Text>
      <TextInput
        style={[styles.input, styles.multiline]}
        value={note}
        onChangeText={setNote}
        multiline
        returnKeyType="default"
        blurOnSubmit={false}
        placeholder="A short bio - Return inserts a new line"
      />
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  screen: { flex: 1, padding: 16, gap: 8 },
  label: { fontSize: 14, fontWeight: "600", color: "#334155" },
  input: {
    borderWidth: 1,
    borderColor: "#cbd5e1",
    borderRadius: 10,
    paddingHorizontal: 14,
    paddingVertical: 12,
    fontSize: 16,
    backgroundColor: "#fff",
  },
  multiline: { minHeight: 96, textAlignVertical: "top" },
});
```

* Use `next` between fields in a wizard, `done` on the last single-line field, `go` when submitting to a server, `send` in chat UIs
* On **multiline** inputs, Return normally inserts a newline - keep `blurOnSubmit={false}` so the action key does not dismiss the keyboard unexpectedly
* `onSubmitEditing` fires when the user taps the action key - wire it to focus the next field or run submit logic
* Android honors `returnKeyType` inconsistently on some OEM keyboards - always provide an on-screen fallback button

> **Related:** [Multi-Step & Wizard Flows](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/forms-input/multi-step-and-wizard-flows/) - `returnKeyType="next"` across step boundaries

---

### 4. blurOnSubmit

`blurOnSubmit` controls whether tapping the action key **dismisses the keyboard** after `onSubmitEditing`. For multi-field forms, set `blurOnSubmit={false}` on every field except the last so focus can move without the keyboard collapsing.

```tsx
import { useRef, useState } from "react";
import { StyleSheet, Text, TextInput, View, type TextInput as TextInputType } from "react-native";
 
export default function App() {
  const [city, setCity] = useState("");
  const [zip, setZip] = useState("");
  const zipRef = useRef<TextInputType>(null);
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.screen}>
      <Text style={styles.label}>City</Text>
      <TextInput
        style={styles.input}
        value={city}
        onChangeText={setCity}
        returnKeyType="next"
        blurOnSubmit={false}
        onSubmitEditing={() => zipRef.current?.focus()}
        placeholder="Portland"
      />
 
      <Text style={styles.label}>ZIP code</Text>
      <TextInput
        ref={zipRef}
        style={styles.input}
        value={zip}
        onChangeText={setZip}
        keyboardType="number-pad"
        returnKeyType="done"
        blurOnSubmit
        placeholder="97201"
      />
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  screen: { flex: 1, padding: 16, gap: 8 },
  label: { fontSize: 14, fontWeight: "600", color: "#334155" },
  input: {
    borderWidth: 1,
    borderColor: "#cbd5e1",
    borderRadius: 10,
    paddingHorizontal: 14,
    paddingVertical: 12,
    fontSize: 16,
    backgroundColor: "#fff",
  },
});
```

* Default is `true` for single-line inputs - fine for a one-field search bar, wrong for "Next" chains
* `blurOnSubmit={false}` + `onSubmitEditing` → `nextRef.focus()` is the standard **two-field pattern**
* On the **last** field, leave `blurOnSubmit` at default (`true`) or set it explicitly so Done dismisses the keyboard
* Number pads lack a Return key - `blurOnSubmit` matters less there; rely on a visible Submit button

> **Related:** [Keyboard Controller](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/forms-input/keyboard-controller/) - keep inputs visible when the keyboard is open

---

### 5. Refs and Programmatic Focus

Attach a **ref** to `TextInput` to call `.focus()`, `.blur()`, or `.clear()` imperatively. Use this for autofocus on mount, jumping to the first invalid field, or "Edit" shortcuts.

```tsx
import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react";
import { Pressable, StyleSheet, Text, TextInput, View, type TextInput as TextInputType } from "react-native";
 
export default function App() {
  const inputRef = useRef<TextInputType>(null);
  const [code, setCode] = useState("");
 
  useEffect(() => {
    const timer = setTimeout(() => inputRef.current?.focus(), 300);
    return () => clearTimeout(timer);
  }, []);
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.screen}>
      <Text style={styles.heading}>Enter verification code</Text>
      <TextInput
        ref={inputRef}
        style={styles.input}
        value={code}
        onChangeText={setCode}
        keyboardType="number-pad"
        maxLength={6}
        placeholder="000000"
      />
      <Pressable style={styles.button} onPress={() => inputRef.current?.focus()}>
        <Text style={styles.buttonText}>Focus input</Text>
      </Pressable>
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  screen: { flex: 1, padding: 16, gap: 12 },
  heading: { fontSize: 20, fontWeight: "700", color: "#0f172a" },
  input: {
    borderWidth: 1,
    borderColor: "#cbd5e1",
    borderRadius: 10,
    paddingHorizontal: 14,
    paddingVertical: 12,
    fontSize: 24,
    letterSpacing: 8,
    textAlign: "center",
    backgroundColor: "#fff",
  },
  button: {
    alignSelf: "flex-start",
    backgroundColor: "#2563eb",
    paddingHorizontal: 16,
    paddingVertical: 10,
    borderRadius: 8,
  },
  buttonText: { color: "#fff", fontWeight: "600" },
});
```

* `useRef<TextInput>(null)` - call `ref.current?.focus()` with optional chaining because the node may not be mounted yet
* Delay autofocus slightly (`setTimeout` ~300ms) after navigation transitions so the keyboard does not fight screen animations
* After validation fails, `firstErrorRef.current?.focus()` brings screen readers and sighted users to the problem field
* React 19 still passes refs to native components the same way - `ref={inputRef}` on `TextInput` is the idiomatic pattern

> **Related:** [Accessibility in Forms](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/forms-input/accessibility-in-forms/) - announcing errors and managing VoiceOver/TalkBack focus

---

### 6. Focus Chain with onSubmitEditing

Chain fields by combining **`returnKeyType="next"`**, **`blurOnSubmit={false}`**, refs, and **`onSubmitEditing`**. The keyboard's Next key should land on the logical next field every time.

```tsx
import { useRef, useState } from "react";
import { StyleSheet, Text, TextInput, View, type TextInput as TextInputType } from "react-native";
 
export default function App() {
  const [first, setFirst] = useState("");
  const [last, setLast] = useState("");
  const [company, setCompany] = useState("");
 
  const lastRef = useRef<TextInputType>(null);
  const companyRef = useRef<TextInputType>(null);
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.screen}>
      <Text style={styles.label}>First name</Text>
      <TextInput
        style={styles.input}
        value={first}
        onChangeText={setFirst}
        returnKeyType="next"
        blurOnSubmit={false}
        onSubmitEditing={() => lastRef.current?.focus()}
        textContentType="givenName"
        autoComplete="given-name"
        placeholder="Alex"
      />
 
      <Text style={styles.label}>Last name</Text>
      <TextInput
        ref={lastRef}
        style={styles.input}
        value={last}
        onChangeText={setLast}
        returnKeyType="next"
        blurOnSubmit={false}
        onSubmitEditing={() => companyRef.current?.focus()}
        textContentType="familyName"
        autoComplete="family-name"
        placeholder="Chen"
      />
 
      <Text style={styles.label}>Company</Text>
      <TextInput
        ref={companyRef}
        style={styles.input}
        value={company}
        onChangeText={setCompany}
        returnKeyType="done"
        blurOnSubmit
        textContentType="organizationName"
        placeholder="Acme Inc."
      />
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  screen: { flex: 1, padding: 16, gap: 8 },
  label: { fontSize: 14, fontWeight: "600", color: "#334155" },
  input: {
    borderWidth: 1,
    borderColor: "#cbd5e1",
    borderRadius: 10,
    paddingHorizontal: 14,
    paddingVertical: 12,
    fontSize: 16,
    backgroundColor: "#fff",
  },
});
```

* Order refs to match **visual tab order** - do not jump randomly because it is convenient in code
* `textContentType` / `autoComplete` help OS autofill insert values without breaking your focus chain
* For the last field in a chain, switch to `returnKeyType="done"` and call your submit handler in `onSubmitEditing`
* Long forms belong in a `ScrollView` - scroll the focused field into view before calling `.focus()` on lower fields (see example 9)

> **Related:** [Forms Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/forms-input/best-practices/) - reducing taps and preventing data loss on back navigation

---

### 7. Submit Handler

Wire an on-screen **Submit** button to validate state, call your API, and dismiss the keyboard. Use `keyboardShouldPersistTaps` on parent scrollables so the button responds on the first tap.

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import {
  Alert,
  Keyboard,
  Pressable,
  ScrollView,
  StyleSheet,
  Text,
  TextInput,
  View,
} from "react-native";
 
export default function App() {
  const [email, setEmail] = useState("");
  const [submitting, setSubmitting] = useState(false);
 
  async function handleSubmit() {
    if (!email.includes("@")) {
      Alert.alert("Invalid email", "Enter a valid email address.");
      return;
    }
 
    setSubmitting(true);
    Keyboard.dismiss();
 
    try {
      await fakeSubscribe(email);
      Alert.alert("Subscribed", `Confirmation sent to ${email}`);
      setEmail("");
    } finally {
      setSubmitting(false);
    }
  }
 
  return (
    <ScrollView
      contentContainerStyle={styles.screen}
      keyboardShouldPersistTaps="handled"
    >
      <Text style={styles.heading}>Newsletter</Text>
      <TextInput
        style={styles.input}
        value={email}
        onChangeText={setEmail}
        keyboardType="email-address"
        autoCapitalize="none"
        returnKeyType="go"
        onSubmitEditing={handleSubmit}
        placeholder="you@example.com"
      />
      <Pressable
        style={[styles.button, submitting && styles.buttonDisabled]}
        onPress={handleSubmit}
        disabled={submitting}
      >
        <Text style={styles.buttonText}>{submitting ? "Submitting…" : "Subscribe"}</Text>
      </Pressable>
    </ScrollView>
  );
}
 
async function fakeSubscribe(_email: string) {
  await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 600));
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  screen: { padding: 16, gap: 12 },
  heading: { fontSize: 22, fontWeight: "700", color: "#0f172a" },
  input: {
    borderWidth: 1,
    borderColor: "#cbd5e1",
    borderRadius: 10,
    paddingHorizontal: 14,
    paddingVertical: 12,
    fontSize: 16,
    backgroundColor: "#fff",
  },
  button: {
    backgroundColor: "#2563eb",
    paddingVertical: 14,
    borderRadius: 10,
    alignItems: "center",
  },
  buttonDisabled: { opacity: 0.6 },
  buttonText: { color: "#fff", fontSize: 16, fontWeight: "600" },
});
```

* Call `Keyboard.dismiss()` at the start of submit so the keyboard does not cover success UI
* `keyboardShouldPersistTaps="handled"` lets `Pressable` receive taps **without** requiring a second tap to dismiss the keyboard first
* Disable the button and show inline loading copy while `submitting` - prevents double posts on slow networks
* Replace the inline `includes("@")` check with Zod or your API schema before shipping - see the validation guide

> **Related:** [Validation with Zod](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/forms-input/validation-with-zod/) - schema-first errors surfaced next to each field

---

## Intermediate Examples

### 8. secureTextEntry and Password Autofill

Password fields need `secureTextEntry`, sensible `textContentType` / `autoComplete`, and often a **visibility toggle** - users cannot proofread masked text.

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { Pressable, StyleSheet, Text, TextInput, View } from "react-native";
 
export default function App() {
  const [password, setPassword] = useState("");
  const [visible, setVisible] = useState(false);
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.screen}>
      <Text style={styles.label}>Password</Text>
      <View style={styles.row}>
        <TextInput
          style={styles.input}
          value={password}
          onChangeText={setPassword}
          secureTextEntry={!visible}
          textContentType="password"
          autoComplete="password"
          autoCapitalize="none"
          autoCorrect={false}
          returnKeyType="done"
          placeholder="••••••••"
        />
        <Pressable
          style={styles.toggle}
          onPress={() => setVisible((v) => !v)}
          accessibilityRole="button"
          accessibilityLabel={visible ? "Hide password" : "Show password"}
        >
          <Text style={styles.toggleText}>{visible ? "Hide" : "Show"}</Text>
        </Pressable>
      </View>
      <Text style={styles.hint}>Minimum 8 characters</Text>
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  screen: { flex: 1, padding: 16, gap: 6 },
  label: { fontSize: 14, fontWeight: "600", color: "#334155" },
  row: { flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", gap: 8 },
  input: {
    flex: 1,
    borderWidth: 1,
    borderColor: "#cbd5e1",
    borderRadius: 10,
    paddingHorizontal: 14,
    paddingVertical: 12,
    fontSize: 16,
    backgroundColor: "#fff",
  },
  toggle: { paddingHorizontal: 8, paddingVertical: 10 },
  toggleText: { color: "#2563eb", fontWeight: "600" },
  hint: { fontSize: 13, color: "#64748b" },
});
```

* `secureTextEntry` masks characters on screen and in some screenshots - still treat the value as sensitive in logs
* iOS Keychain / Android Autofill use `textContentType="password"` and `autoComplete="password"` - use `newPassword` on sign-up flows
* Toggling visibility flips `secureTextEntry` only - the state value stays the same
* Never store plaintext passwords in AsyncStorage - collect, validate, hash or tokenize server-side

> **Related:** [Accessibility in Forms](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/forms-input/accessibility-in-forms/) - labeling secure fields for assistive tech

---

### 9. ScrollView, KeyboardAvoidingView, and Taps

Full-screen forms need a **scroll container**, keyboard avoidance, and tap handling so fields near the bottom stay reachable and buttons stay tappable.

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import {
  KeyboardAvoidingView,
  Platform,
  Pressable,
  ScrollView,
  StyleSheet,
  Text,
  TextInput,
  View,
} from "react-native";
 
export default function App() {
  const [subject, setSubject] = useState("");
  const [orderId, setOrderId] = useState("");
  const [details, setDetails] = useState("");
 
  return (
    <KeyboardAvoidingView
      style={styles.flex}
      behavior={Platform.OS === "ios" ? "padding" : undefined}
      keyboardVerticalOffset={Platform.OS === "ios" ? 64 : 0}
    >
      <ScrollView
        contentContainerStyle={styles.content}
        keyboardShouldPersistTaps="handled"
        keyboardDismissMode="on-drag"
      >
        <Text style={styles.heading}>Support request</Text>
 
        <View style={styles.field}>
          <Text style={styles.label}>Subject</Text>
          <TextInput
            style={styles.input}
            value={subject}
            onChangeText={setSubject}
            returnKeyType="next"
            blurOnSubmit={false}
            placeholder="Brief summary"
          />
        </View>
 
        <View style={styles.field}>
          <Text style={styles.label}>Order ID</Text>
          <TextInput
            style={styles.input}
            value={orderId}
            onChangeText={setOrderId}
            returnKeyType="next"
            blurOnSubmit={false}
            placeholder="ORD-12345"
          />
        </View>
 
        <View style={styles.field}>
          <Text style={styles.label}>Details</Text>
          <TextInput
            style={[styles.input, styles.multiline]}
            value={details}
            onChangeText={setDetails}
            multiline
            blurOnSubmit={false}
            placeholder="What happened?"
          />
        </View>
 
        <Pressable style={styles.button} onPress={() => {}}>
          <Text style={styles.buttonText}>Send request</Text>
        </Pressable>
      </ScrollView>
    </KeyboardAvoidingView>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  flex: { flex: 1 },
  content: { padding: 16, gap: 12, paddingBottom: 40 },
  heading: { fontSize: 22, fontWeight: "700", marginBottom: 4 },
  field: { gap: 6 },
  label: { fontSize: 14, fontWeight: "600", color: "#334155" },
  input: {
    borderWidth: 1,
    borderColor: "#cbd5e1",
    borderRadius: 10,
    paddingHorizontal: 14,
    paddingVertical: 12,
    fontSize: 16,
    backgroundColor: "#fff",
  },
  multiline: { minHeight: 120, textAlignVertical: "top" },
  button: {
    marginTop: 8,
    backgroundColor: "#2563eb",
    paddingVertical: 14,
    borderRadius: 10,
    alignItems: "center",
  },
  buttonText: { color: "#fff", fontWeight: "600", fontSize: 16 },
});
```

* `KeyboardAvoidingView` with `behavior="padding"` on iOS lifts content when the keyboard opens - tune `keyboardVerticalOffset` for your header height
* `keyboardDismissMode="on-drag"` lets users drag the scroll view to dismiss the keyboard - expected on long forms
* `keyboardShouldPersistTaps="handled"` is **required** when submit buttons sit inside the same `ScrollView` as inputs
* For pixel-perfect keyboard tracking and sticky footers, graduate to `react-native-keyboard-controller` - linked below

> **Related:** [Keyboard Controller](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/forms-input/keyboard-controller/) - `KeyboardAwareScrollView` and consistent cross-platform offsets

---

### 10. Complete Sign-In Form

This example combines **controlled inputs**, keyboard types, a **focus chain**, password masking, validation, and submit - the baseline pattern most apps extend.

```tsx
import { useRef, useState } from "react";
import {
  Alert,
  Keyboard,
  KeyboardAvoidingView,
  Platform,
  Pressable,
  ScrollView,
  StyleSheet,
  Text,
  TextInput,
  View,
  type TextInput as TextInputType,
} from "react-native";
 
export default function App() {
  const [email, setEmail] = useState("");
  const [password, setPassword] = useState("");
  const [submitting, setSubmitting] = useState(false);
 
  const passwordRef = useRef<TextInputType>(null);
 
  async function handleSignIn() {
    if (!email.includes("@")) {
      Alert.alert("Check email", "Enter a valid email address.");
      return;
    }
    if (password.length < 8) {
      Alert.alert("Check password", "Password must be at least 8 characters.");
      passwordRef.current?.focus();
      return;
    }
 
    setSubmitting(true);
    Keyboard.dismiss();
 
    try {
      await fakeSignIn(email, password);
      Alert.alert("Signed in", `Welcome back, ${email}`);
    } catch {
      Alert.alert("Sign-in failed", "Check your credentials and try again.");
    } finally {
      setSubmitting(false);
    }
  }
 
  return (
    <KeyboardAvoidingView
      style={styles.flex}
      behavior={Platform.OS === "ios" ? "padding" : undefined}
    >
      <ScrollView
        contentContainerStyle={styles.content}
        keyboardShouldPersistTaps="handled"
      >
        <Text style={styles.heading}>Sign in</Text>
 
        <Text style={styles.label}>Email</Text>
        <TextInput
          style={styles.input}
          value={email}
          onChangeText={setEmail}
          keyboardType="email-address"
          autoCapitalize="none"
          autoCorrect={false}
          textContentType="username"
          autoComplete="email"
          returnKeyType="next"
          blurOnSubmit={false}
          onSubmitEditing={() => passwordRef.current?.focus()}
          placeholder="you@example.com"
        />
 
        <Text style={styles.label}>Password</Text>
        <TextInput
          ref={passwordRef}
          style={styles.input}
          value={password}
          onChangeText={setPassword}
          secureTextEntry
          textContentType="password"
          autoComplete="password"
          returnKeyType="go"
          onSubmitEditing={handleSignIn}
          placeholder="••••••••"
        />
 
        <Pressable
          style={[styles.button, submitting && styles.buttonDisabled]}
          onPress={handleSignIn}
          disabled={submitting}
        >
          <Text style={styles.buttonText}>{submitting ? "Signing in…" : "Sign in"}</Text>
        </Pressable>
      </ScrollView>
    </KeyboardAvoidingView>
  );
}
 
async function fakeSignIn(_email: string, _password: string) {
  await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 800));
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  flex: { flex: 1 },
  content: { padding: 16, gap: 8, paddingBottom: 32 },
  heading: { fontSize: 28, fontWeight: "700", color: "#0f172a", marginBottom: 8 },
  label: { fontSize: 14, fontWeight: "600", color: "#334155", marginTop: 4 },
  input: {
    borderWidth: 1,
    borderColor: "#cbd5e1",
    borderRadius: 10,
    paddingHorizontal: 14,
    paddingVertical: 12,
    fontSize: 16,
    backgroundColor: "#fff",
  },
  button: {
    marginTop: 16,
    backgroundColor: "#2563eb",
    paddingVertical: 14,
    borderRadius: 10,
    alignItems: "center",
  },
  buttonDisabled: { opacity: 0.6 },
  buttonText: { color: "#fff", fontSize: 16, fontWeight: "600" },
});
```

* Validation failures call `passwordRef.current?.focus()` so the user lands on the field that needs attention
* `returnKeyType="next"` on email and `go` on password mirror the on-screen primary action
* `Keyboard.dismiss()` before async work avoids the keyboard reappearing under loading overlays
* Swap `Alert` for inline error text under each field - Zod + react-hook-form make that scalable across larger forms

> **Related:** [react-hook-form on Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/forms-input/react-hook-form-on-mobile/) - same UX with less manual state | [Validation with Zod](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/forms-input/validation-with-zod/) - reusable schemas for email and password rules

# Forms & Input Highlights Summary

Every highlight bullet from the 8 pages in this section, gathered on one page and grouped by the page it came from.

Highlights / Forms & Input Highlights Summary

* Controlled inputs store value in React state and update via onChangeText
* Use Controller for every TextInput - React Native has no native form element to register by ref
* z.infer<typeof Schema> is the single source of truth for form values and API payloads
* KeyboardProvider at the app root enables consistent keyboard events on iOS and Android
* Use @react-native-community/datetimepicker for dates and times - it renders the OS-native control
* Keep one form object across steps - split UI, not state, unless steps are independent domains

## [Forms Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/forms-input/forms-basics/)

* Controlled inputs store value in React state and update via onChangeText
* keyboardType picks the correct software keyboard - email, numeric, phone
* returnKeyType labels the action key - next, done, go, search
* blurOnSubmit=false keeps focus moving between fields without dismissing the keyboard
* Refs call .focus() for autofocus, error recovery, and programmatic focus chains
* onSubmitEditing wires the keyboard action key to focus the next field or submit
* keyboardShouldPersistTaps="handled" lets submit buttons work on the first tap

## [react-hook-form on Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/forms-input/react-hook-form-on-mobile/)

* Use Controller for every TextInput - React Native has no native form element to register by ref
* defaultValues must list every field or isDirty and reset behave incorrectly
* mode: onTouched validates after blur, reducing keyboard-dismiss churn on small screens
* formState is a Proxy - destructure only the flags you read or you opt into extra re-renders
* setFocus jumps between fields for wizard steps and accessible error recovery
* Pair with Zod via zodResolver so validation schemas stay the single source of truth

## [Validation with Zod](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/forms-input/validation-with-zod/)

* z.infer is the single source of truth for form values and API payloads
* zodResolver bridges Zod into react-hook-form - errors map to field paths automatically
* TextInput always yields strings - use z.coerce.number() or preprocess before comparing numbers
* Show errors only after touch or submit to avoid shouting at users mid-keystroke
* Use .refine() and .superRefine() for cross-field rules like password confirmation
* Map server fieldErrors with setError so API failures appear inline, not in alerts

## [Keyboard Controller](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/forms-input/keyboard-controller/)

* KeyboardProvider at the app root enables consistent keyboard events on iOS and Android
* KeyboardAwareScrollView scrolls the focused TextInput above the keyboard with native timing
* bottomOffset accounts for fixed footers, toolbars, and safe-area padding
* KeyboardToolbar adds Previous / Next / Done without custom focus bookkeeping
* Prefer keyboard-controller over KeyboardAvoidingView for multi-field forms
* Pair with react-hook-form setFocus for return-key and toolbar navigation

## [Pickers, Date/Time & Native Inputs](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/forms-input/pickers-date-time-and-native-inputs/)

* Use @react-native-community/datetimepicker for dates and times - it renders the OS-native control
* Android pickers are modal dialogs; iOS pickers are inline spinners unless you wrap them
* @react-native-picker/picker maps to UIPickerView and Android Spinner - not a dropdown menu
* Store Date objects in state; format for display with Intl or date-fns at the edge
* Custom wheel pickers look consistent cross-platform but lose accessibility and locale behavior
* Always pair picker triggers with visible labels and accessibilityLabel on the Pressable

## [Multi-Step & Wizard Flows](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/forms-input/multi-step-and-wizard-flows/)

* Keep one form object across steps - split UI, not state, unless steps are independent domains
* Validate per step on Next; run full-schema validation only on final submit
* Back navigation must not discard entered data - persist to memory, MMKV, or AsyncStorage
* Hardware back on Android and swipe-back on iOS need explicit guards when a step is dirty
* react-hook-form FormProvider shares one methods instance across step components
* Show progress (step N of M) and disable Next until the current step schema passes

## [Accessibility in Forms](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/forms-input/accessibility-in-forms/)

* Every TextInput needs an accessibilityLabel - placeholder text is not a label
* Expose validation errors with accessibilityLiveRegion or AccessibilityInfo.announceForAccessibility
* Move focus to the first invalid field after submit - screen reader users miss visual-only error summaries
* Group related inputs with accessibilityRole and accessibilityState, not visual proximity alone
* accessibilityHint carries format guidance; keep labels short and stable
* Test with VoiceOver and TalkBack on device - eslint-plugin-react-native-a11y catches only a fraction

## [Forms Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/forms-input/best-practices/)

* Keep TextInput controlled with value and onChangeText
* Use react-hook-form Controller - register does not wire RN inputs
* Validate with Zod at submit and map server errors with setError
* Wrap the app in KeyboardProvider for keyboard-controller layouts
* Persist multi-step drafts and confirm before discarding dirty wizards
* Announce validation failures to VoiceOver and TalkBack

# Keyboard Controller

`react-native-keyboard-controller` replaces the guesswork in `KeyboardAvoidingView` with keyboard height synced to the native animation. On form screens, that means the active `TextInput` stays visible, the scroll feels like a system sheet, and Android behaves the same as iOS - without per-platform `behavior` props.

Highlights / Keyboard Controller

* KeyboardProvider at the app root enables consistent keyboard events on iOS and Android
* KeyboardAwareScrollView scrolls the focused TextInput above the keyboard with native timing
* bottomOffset accounts for fixed footers, toolbars, and safe-area padding
* KeyboardToolbar adds Previous / Next / Done without custom focus bookkeeping
* Prefer keyboard-controller over KeyboardAvoidingView for multi-field forms
* Pair with react-hook-form setFocus for return-key and toolbar navigation

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx - provider once at the root
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
import { KeyboardProvider } from "react-native-keyboard-controller";
 
export default function RootLayout() {
  return (
    <KeyboardProvider>
      <Stack />
    </KeyboardProvider>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// app/contact.tsx - scroll + toolbar for a short form
import { StyleSheet, TextInput, View } from "react-native";
import { KeyboardAwareScrollView, KeyboardToolbar } from "react-native-keyboard-controller";
 
export default function ContactScreen() {
  return (
    <>
      <KeyboardAwareScrollView
        bottomOffset={48}
        contentContainerStyle={styles.container}
        keyboardShouldPersistTaps="handled"
      >
        <TextInput placeholder="Name" style={styles.input} />
        <TextInput placeholder="Email" keyboardType="email-address" style={styles.input} />
        <TextInput placeholder="Message" multiline style={styles.multiline} />
      </KeyboardAwareScrollView>
      <KeyboardToolbar />
    </>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  container: { padding: 16, gap: 12 },
  input: {
    borderWidth: 1,
    borderColor: "#d1d5db",
    borderRadius: 8,
    paddingHorizontal: 12,
    paddingVertical: 10,
    fontSize: 16,
  },
  multiline: { minHeight: 120, textAlignVertical: "top" },
});
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Any screen with more than two text fields stacked vertically.
* Forms with a fixed footer button or tab bar that the keyboard would otherwise cover.
* Chat-style inputs where content must rise in sync with keyboard animation.
* Android builds where `KeyboardAvoidingView` padding feels jumpy or inconsistent.
* Flows that need Previous / Next / Done traversal across inputs.

## Working Example

```tsx
// app/(auth)/sign-up.tsx - keyboard-aware form wired to react-hook-form
import { zodResolver } from "@hookform/resolvers/zod";
import { useForm } from "react-hook-form";
import { Pressable, StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
import {
  KeyboardAwareScrollView,
  KeyboardToolbar,
} from "react-native-keyboard-controller";
import { z } from "zod";
import { TextField } from "../../components/form/TextField";
 
const SignUpSchema = z
  .object({
    fullName: z.string().trim().min(1, "Name is required"),
    email: z.string().email("Enter a valid email"),
    password: z.string().min(8, "At least 8 characters"),
  });
 
type SignUpValues = z.infer<typeof SignUpSchema>;
 
export default function SignUpScreen() {
  const {
    control,
    handleSubmit,
    setFocus,
    formState: { isSubmitting },
  } = useForm<SignUpValues>({
    resolver: zodResolver(SignUpSchema),
    defaultValues: { fullName: "", email: "", password: "" },
    mode: "onTouched",
  });
 
  async function onSubmit(values: SignUpValues) {
    await fetch("https://api.example.com/v1/sign-up", {
      method: "POST",
      headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
      body: JSON.stringify(values),
    });
  }
 
  return (
    <>
      <KeyboardAwareScrollView
        bottomOffset={72}
        contentContainerStyle={styles.scroll}
        keyboardShouldPersistTaps="handled"
      >
        <Text style={styles.title}>Create account</Text>
 
        <TextField
          control={control}
          name="fullName"
          label="Full name"
          autoComplete="name"
          returnKeyType="next"
          onSubmitEditing={() => setFocus("email")}
        />
 
        <TextField
          control={control}
          name="email"
          label="Email"
          keyboardType="email-address"
          autoCapitalize="none"
          autoComplete="email"
          returnKeyType="next"
          onSubmitEditing={() => setFocus("password")}
        />
 
        <TextField
          control={control}
          name="password"
          label="Password"
          secureTextEntry
          returnKeyType="done"
          onSubmitEditing={handleSubmit(onSubmit)}
        />
 
        <Pressable
          onPress={handleSubmit(onSubmit)}
          disabled={isSubmitting}
          style={styles.button}
        >
          <Text style={styles.buttonText}>{isSubmitting ? "Creating…" : "Sign up"}</Text>
        </Pressable>
      </KeyboardAwareScrollView>
 
      <KeyboardToolbar />
    </>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  scroll: { padding: 16, gap: 16, paddingBottom: 32 },
  title: { fontSize: 22, fontWeight: "700" },
  button: {
    backgroundColor: "#2563eb",
    borderRadius: 8,
    paddingVertical: 12,
    alignItems: "center",
    marginTop: 8,
  },
  buttonText: { color: "#fff", fontWeight: "600" },
});
```

```tsx
// app/chat.tsx - frame-synced lift for a composer above FlatList
import { FlatList, StyleSheet, TextInput, View } from "react-native";
import Animated, { useAnimatedStyle, useSharedValue } from "react-native-reanimated";
import { useKeyboardHandler } from "react-native-keyboard-controller";
import { MessageBubble } from "../../components/MessageBubble";
 
const messages = [{ id: "1", text: "Hello" }];
 
function useKeyboardSpacer() {
  const height = useSharedValue(0);
 
  useKeyboardHandler(
    {
      onMove: (event) => {
        "worklet";
        height.value = Math.max(event.height, 0);
      },
    },
    []
  );
 
  return height;
}
 
export default function ChatScreen() {
  const keyboardHeight = useKeyboardSpacer();
 
  const spacerStyle = useAnimatedStyle(() => ({
    height: keyboardHeight.value,
  }));
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.container}>
      <FlatList
        data={messages}
        keyExtractor={(item) => item.id}
        renderItem={({ item }) => <MessageBubble message={item} />}
        contentContainerStyle={styles.list}
        keyboardDismissMode="interactive"
      />
      <TextInput placeholder="Message" style={styles.composer} />
      <Animated.View style={spacerStyle} />
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  container: { flex: 1 },
  list: { padding: 16, gap: 8 },
  composer: {
    marginHorizontal: 16,
    marginBottom: 8,
    borderWidth: 1,
    borderColor: "#d1d5db",
    borderRadius: 20,
    paddingHorizontal: 16,
    paddingVertical: 10,
  },
});
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* `KeyboardProvider` in the root layout unlocks all keyboard-controller hooks and components.
* `KeyboardAwareScrollView` auto-scrolls to the focused field with `bottomOffset` clearing the toolbar.
* `KeyboardToolbar` ships Previous / Next / Done without manual ref arrays.
* `keyboardShouldPersistTaps="handled"` lets submit `Pressable`s work while the keyboard is open.
* `useKeyboardHandler` + Reanimated lifts chat content frame-by-frame for composer UIs.
* `setFocus` from react-hook-form aligns Return-key navigation with toolbar behavior.

## Deep Dive

### How It Works

* The native module reports keyboard height and animation progress on every frame.
* `KeyboardAwareScrollView` measures the focused input and adjusts scroll offset to keep it visible.
* `KeyboardProvider` supplies context so hooks and toolbars share the same keyboard state.
* Unlike `KeyboardAvoidingView`, the scroll view approach handles **many** inputs without shrinking the whole screen.
* Reanimated worklets in `useKeyboardHandler` read keyboard height off the JS thread for smooth chat lifts.

### Setup Checklist

| Step | Action |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | `npx expo install react-native-keyboard-controller` |
| 2 | Ensure `react-native-reanimated` is installed (Expo SDK 57 template includes it) |
| 3 | Wrap the app in `<KeyboardProvider>` at the root layout |
| 4 | Replace `KeyboardAvoidingView` + `ScrollView` with `KeyboardAwareScrollView` on form screens |
| 5 | Tune `bottomOffset` for toolbars, sticky CTAs, and safe-area padding |

```bash
npx expo install react-native-keyboard-controller react-native-reanimated
```

### Components at a Glance

| Component / Hook | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `KeyboardProvider` | Required root wrapper - enables keyboard events |
| `KeyboardAwareScrollView` | Scrolls focused `TextInput` into view |
| `KeyboardToolbar` | Previous / Next / Done bar above the keyboard |
| `KeyboardStickyView` | Pins a footer (e.g. submit bar) to the keyboard top edge |
| `useKeyboardHandler` | Frame-synced keyboard height for custom animations |
| `Keyboard.dismiss()` | Same RN API - still works alongside the library |

### bottomOffset and Safe Area

```tsx
import { useSafeAreaInsets } from "react-native-safe-area-context";
 
const insets = useSafeAreaInsets();
const TOOLBAR_HEIGHT = 44;
 
<KeyboardAwareScrollView
  bottomOffset={insets.bottom + TOOLBAR_HEIGHT}
  ...
/>
```

* `bottomOffset` is extra space **below** the focused input when scrolled into view.
* Include fixed footer height, `KeyboardToolbar` height, and bottom safe inset.
* Safe area alone does not move when the keyboard opens - keyboard and inset are separate concerns (see [Safe Areas & Notches](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/safe-areas-and-notches/)).

### Android Tab Bar and `softwareKeyboardLayoutMode`

When bottom tabs jump above the keyboard on Android, add to `app.config.ts`:

```ts
export default {
  expo: {
    android: {
      softwareKeyboardLayoutMode: "pan",
    },
  },
};
```

* `pan` resizes the window instead of pushing tab chrome unpredictably.
* Alternatively set `tabBarHideOnKeyboard: true` on Expo Router `Tabs` to hide tabs while typing.

### TypeScript Notes

```tsx
import type { KeyboardAwareScrollViewProps } from "react-native-keyboard-controller";
 
type FormScrollProps = Pick<
  KeyboardAwareScrollViewProps,
  "bottomOffset" | "keyboardShouldPersistTaps"
>;
 
const formScrollDefaults: FormScrollProps = {
  bottomOffset: 48,
  keyboardShouldPersistTaps: "handled",
};
```

* The library exports props types for scroll views and toolbar customization.
* Wrap shared form screens with a `FormScreen` component that applies consistent `bottomOffset` and toolbar slots.

## Gotchas

* **Missing `KeyboardProvider`** - `KeyboardAwareScrollView` falls back to inconsistent behavior or zero keyboard height. **Fix:** Wrap the root layout, not individual screens.
* **`bottomOffset` left at 0 with a toolbar** - The focused field hides under `KeyboardToolbar`. **Fix:** Set `bottomOffset` to toolbar height + safe area (often 44–62 px before inset).
* **`keyboardShouldPersistTaps` omitted** - Taps on submit buttons dismiss the keyboard without firing `onPress`. **Fix:** `keyboardShouldPersistTaps="handled"` on the scroll view.
* **Nesting `KeyboardAvoidingView` inside `KeyboardAwareScrollView`** - Double adjustment overshoots and causes bounce. **Fix:** Pick one strategy - keyboard-controller OR avoiding view, not both.
* **FlatList inside KeyboardAwareScrollView** - Virtualized lists inside scroll views break measurement and performance. **Fix:** Put inputs in `ListHeaderComponent` / `ListFooterComponent`, or use `useKeyboardHandler` for chat layouts.
* **Android tab bar resize** - Bottom tabs slide up with the keyboard and squash the form. **Fix:** `softwareKeyboardLayoutMode: "pan"` or `tabBarHideOnKeyboard: true`.
* **Reanimated not configured** - `useKeyboardHandler` worklets fail silently or throw on Android. **Fix:** Verify `react-native-reanimated` babel plugin per [Expo Reanimated docs](https://docs.expo.dev/versions/latest/sdk/reanimated/).

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `react-native-keyboard-controller` | Multi-field forms, chat composers, cross-platform parity | A single full-screen search input with no overlap risk |
| `KeyboardAvoidingView` | Quick prototype, one or two inputs | Long forms - platform-specific `behavior` tuning exhausts quickly |
| `KeyboardAvoidingView` + `ScrollView` | Medium forms without adding a dependency | You need toolbar navigation or frame-synced animation |
| `android:windowSoftInputMode` only | Legacy native Android tuning | iOS parity - still need an iOS strategy |
| Nothing (let keyboard cover) | Full-screen modal search a la spotlight | Data entry where users cannot see what they type |

## FAQs

How do I install react-native-keyboard-controller in Expo SDK 57?

```bash
npx expo install react-native-keyboard-controller
```

* Also ensure `react-native-reanimated` is present - the Expo template ships it by default.
* Wrap your root layout with `KeyboardProvider` after install.

Where does KeyboardProvider go?

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx
<KeyboardProvider>
  <Stack />
</KeyboardProvider>
```

* Place it above navigators so every screen can use keyboard hooks.
* One provider per app - do not nest providers per screen.

What should bottomOffset be set to?

* Start with `48`–`62` when using `KeyboardToolbar`.
* Add `useSafeAreaInsets().bottom` on devices with home indicators.
* If a sticky submit bar sits above the keyboard, include its height too.
* Tune on a real device - simulators are close but not exact.

KeyboardAwareScrollView vs KeyboardAvoidingView?

* **KeyboardAwareScrollView** scrolls to the focused input - best for forms with many fields.
* **KeyboardAvoidingView** shrinks or pads the whole container - OK for one or two inputs.
* Keyboard Controller tracks native keyboard animation timing on both platforms.

Why are my submit buttons not firing while the keyboard is open?

* Default scroll views swallow taps to dismiss the keyboard.
* Set `keyboardShouldPersistTaps="handled"` on `KeyboardAwareScrollView`.
* Use `Pressable` - not `TouchableWithoutFeedback` wrapping the whole screen.

How do I add Previous and Next buttons above the keyboard?

```tsx
<>
  <KeyboardAwareScrollView ... />
  <KeyboardToolbar />
</>
```

* `KeyboardToolbar` discovers registered text inputs and wires navigation automatically.
* Works alongside `returnKeyType="next"` and react-hook-form `setFocus`.

Can I use keyboard-controller with react-hook-form?

* Yes - wrap RHF fields in `KeyboardAwareScrollView`.
* Use `setFocus("fieldName")` in `onSubmitEditing` to chain Return-key navigation.
* See [react-hook-form on Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/forms-input/react-hook-form-on-mobile/) for the field wiring pattern.

How do I handle chat-style keyboard lift?

* Use `useKeyboardHandler` with Reanimated `useSharedValue` for per-frame height.
* Add an `Animated.View` spacer below the composer that matches keyboard height.
* Keep the message list in `FlatList` - do not wrap it in `KeyboardAwareScrollView`.

Does safe area padding replace keyboard handling?

* No - safe area insets are static per device orientation; keyboard height is dynamic.
* Apply both: safe area for notches, keyboard-controller for text input visibility.

My Android bottom tabs move when the keyboard opens - what do I do?

```ts
// app.config.ts
android: { softwareKeyboardLayoutMode: "pan" }
```

* Or hide tabs while typing: `tabBarHideOnKeyboard: true` on `Tabs` `screenOptions`.
* Restart the dev server after changing `app.config.ts`.

Do I need a development build?

* Expo documents keyboard-controller as installable via `npx expo install` on SDK 57.
* Production apps should use development builds for native modules you ship to stores.
* Run `npx expo prebuild` and EAS Build when moving beyond quick Expo Go spikes.

Can I dismiss the keyboard programmatically?

```ts
import { Keyboard } from "react-native";
 
Keyboard.dismiss();
```

* Works alongside keyboard-controller - no API conflict.
* Call after successful form submit or when closing a modal sheet.

How do I pin a footer button to the top of the keyboard?

* Use `KeyboardStickyView` from the library for footers that track keyboard height.
* Alternatively place the CTA inside the scroll content and rely on `bottomOffset`.
* Sticky views suit single primary actions; scroll content suits long forms with inline submit.

* [react-hook-form on Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/forms-input/react-hook-form-on-mobile/) - `setFocus` chains that match toolbar navigation

Dokumen: Pickers, Date/Time & Native Inputs
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/forms-input/pickers-date-time-and-native-inputs/

# Pickers, Date/Time & Native Inputs

Platform pickers vs custom UI trade-offs.

Highlights / Pickers, Date/Time & Native Inputs

* Use @react-native-community/datetimepicker for dates and times - it renders the OS-native control
* Android pickers are modal dialogs; iOS pickers are inline spinners unless you wrap them
* @react-native-picker/picker maps to UIPickerView and Android Spinner - not a dropdown menu
* Store Date objects in state; format for display with Intl or date-fns at the edge
* Custom wheel pickers look consistent cross-platform but lose accessibility and locale behavior
* Always pair picker triggers with visible labels and accessibilityLabel on the Pressable

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
npx expo install @react-native-community/datetimepicker @react-native-picker/picker
```

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { Platform, Pressable, Text, View } from "react-native";
import DateTimePicker, {
  DateTimePickerEvent,
} from "@react-native-community/datetimepicker";
import { Picker } from "@react-native-picker/picker";
 
export function AppointmentFields() {
  const [date, setDate] = useState(new Date());
  const [showDate, setShowDate] = useState(false);
  const [timezone, setTimezone] = useState("America/New_York");
 
  const onDateChange = (_event: DateTimePickerEvent, selected?: Date) => {
    if (Platform.OS === "android") setShowDate(false);
    if (selected) setDate(selected);
  };
 
  return (
    <View>
      <Pressable
        onPress={() => setShowDate(true)}
        accessibilityRole="button"
        accessibilityLabel="Appointment date"
        accessibilityHint="Opens the date picker"
      >
        <Text>{date.toLocaleDateString()}</Text>
      </Pressable>
 
      {showDate && (
        <DateTimePicker
          value={date}
          mode="date"
          display={Platform.OS === "ios" ? "spinner" : "default"}
          onChange={onDateChange}
        />
      )}
 
      <Picker
        selectedValue={timezone}
        onValueChange={setTimezone}
        accessibilityLabel="Time zone"
      >
        <Picker.Item label="Eastern" value="America/New_York" />
        <Picker.Item label="Pacific" value="America/Los_Angeles" />
      </Picker>
    </View>
  );
}
```

**When to reach for this:** Any form field where free-text entry is error-prone - birth dates, appointment slots, country/region selection, or enumerated options with more than a handful of values.

## Working Example

```tsx
import { useCallback, useState } from "react";
import {
  Modal,
  Platform,
  Pressable,
  StyleSheet,
  Text,
  View,
} from "react-native";
import DateTimePicker, {
  DateTimePickerEvent,
} from "@react-native-community/datetimepicker";
import { Picker } from "@react-native-picker/picker";
 
type FormState = {
  date: Date;
  time: Date;
  durationMinutes: number;
};
 
const DURATIONS = [15, 30, 45, 60] as const;
 
const formatDate = (d: Date) =>
  new Intl.DateTimeFormat(undefined, {
    weekday: "short",
    month: "short",
    day: "numeric",
    year: "numeric",
  }).format(d);
 
const formatTime = (d: Date) =>
  new Intl.DateTimeFormat(undefined, {
    hour: "numeric",
    minute: "2-digit",
  }).format(d);
 
export function BookingForm({
  onSubmit,
}: {
  onSubmit: (value: FormState) => void;
}) {
  const [form, setForm] = useState<FormState>({
    date: new Date(),
    time: new Date(),
    durationMinutes: 30,
  });
  const [activePicker, setActivePicker] = useState<
    "date" | "time" | null
  >(null);
 
  const closePicker = useCallback(() => setActivePicker(null), []);
 
  const onPickerChange = useCallback(
    (field: "date" | "time") =>
      (_event: DateTimePickerEvent, selected?: Date) => {
        if (Platform.OS === "android") closePicker();
        if (!selected) return;
        setForm((prev) => ({ ...prev, [field]: selected }));
      },
    [closePicker],
  );
 
  const iosPicker = activePicker ? (
    <Modal transparent animationType="slide" onRequestClose={closePicker}>
      <Pressable style={styles.backdrop} onPress={closePicker} />
      <View style={styles.sheet}>
        <View style={styles.sheetHeader}>
          <Pressable onPress={closePicker} accessibilityRole="button">
            <Text style={styles.done}>Done</Text>
          </Pressable>
        </View>
        <DateTimePicker
          value={form[activePicker]}
          mode={activePicker}
          display="spinner"
          onChange={onPickerChange(activePicker)}
        />
      </View>
    </Modal>
  ) : null;
 
  const androidPicker =
    Platform.OS === "android" && activePicker ? (
      <DateTimePicker
        value={form[activePicker]}
        mode={activePicker}
        onChange={onPickerChange(activePicker)}
      />
    ) : null;
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.container}>
      <Text style={styles.label}>Date</Text>
      <Pressable
        style={styles.field}
        onPress={() => setActivePicker("date")}
        accessibilityRole="button"
        accessibilityLabel={`Date, ${formatDate(form.date)}`}
      >
        <Text>{formatDate(form.date)}</Text>
      </Pressable>
 
      <Text style={styles.label}>Time</Text>
      <Pressable
        style={styles.field}
        onPress={() => setActivePicker("time")}
        accessibilityRole="button"
        accessibilityLabel={`Time, ${formatTime(form.time)}`}
      >
        <Text>{formatTime(form.time)}</Text>
      </Pressable>
 
      <Text style={styles.label}>Duration</Text>
      <View style={styles.pickerWrap}>
        <Picker
          selectedValue={form.durationMinutes}
          onValueChange={(durationMinutes) =>
            setForm((prev) => ({ ...prev, durationMinutes }))
          }
          accessibilityLabel="Duration"
        >
          {DURATIONS.map((m) => (
            <Picker.Item key={m} label={`${m} minutes`} value={m} />
          ))}
        </Picker>
      </View>
 
      <Pressable
        style={styles.submit}
        onPress={() => onSubmit(form)}
        accessibilityRole="button"
      >
        <Text style={styles.submitText}>Book</Text>
      </Pressable>
 
      {iosPicker}
      {androidPicker}
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  container: { padding: 16, gap: 8 },
  label: { fontSize: 14, fontWeight: "600", color: "#374151" },
  field: {
    padding: 14,
    borderWidth: 1,
    borderColor: "#d1d5db",
    borderRadius: 8,
    backgroundColor: "#fff",
  },
  pickerWrap: {
    borderWidth: 1,
    borderColor: "#d1d5db",
    borderRadius: 8,
    overflow: "hidden",
  },
  submit: {
    marginTop: 12,
    padding: 14,
    borderRadius: 8,
    backgroundColor: "#2563eb",
    alignItems: "center",
  },
  submitText: { color: "#fff", fontWeight: "600" },
  backdrop: { flex: 1, backgroundColor: "rgba(0,0,0,0.35)" },
  sheet: {
    backgroundColor: "#fff",
    borderTopLeftRadius: 16,
    borderTopRightRadius: 16,
    paddingBottom: 24,
  },
  sheetHeader: {
    alignItems: "flex-end",
    paddingHorizontal: 16,
    paddingVertical: 12,
    borderBottomWidth: StyleSheet.hairlineWidth,
    borderBottomColor: "#e5e7eb",
  },
  done: { color: "#2563eb", fontWeight: "600", fontSize: 16 },
});
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* **Trigger + native picker** - visible `Pressable` fields open OS pickers instead of asking users to type dates.
* **Platform branching** - Android uses the system dialog; iOS wraps the spinner in a bottom sheet with an explicit Done action.
* **Date in state, string at the edge** - `Date` objects in React state; `Intl.DateTimeFormat` for display.
* **Enumerated duration** - `@react-native-picker/picker` for a short fixed list.
* **Accessibility labels** - each trigger announces its current value to VoiceOver/TalkBack.

## Deep Dive

### How It Works

* **Date/time pickers** delegate to `@react-native-community/datetimepicker`, which bridges to `UIDatePicker` on iOS and `DatePickerDialog` / `TimePickerDialog` on Android.
* **Value pickers** use `@react-native-picker/picker`, which renders `UIPickerView` (iOS) or `Spinner` (Android) - not an HTML-style `<select>` dropdown.
* **Android modals** - `DateTimePicker` on Android is typically shown once and dismissed on selection or cancel; you control visibility with local state.
* **iOS inline spinners** - the same component can render inline in your layout or inside a `Modal` / bottom sheet for a compact trigger pattern.
* **Locale and 12/24-hour** - the native control respects system locale and clock preference; you do not reimplement AM/PM logic unless you build a custom picker.

### Platform Display Modes

| Platform | `mode` | Common `display` | UX |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| iOS | `date` | `spinner`, `inline`, `compact` | Inline calendar (iOS 14+) or wheel |
| iOS | `time` | `spinner`, `compact` | Wheel or compact clock chip |
| Android | `date` | `default`, `calendar`, `spinner` | System dialog |
| Android | `time` | `default`, `clock`, `spinner` | System dialog |

On Android, prefer `default` unless design requires a specific variant. On iOS, `compact` works well in dense forms; `spinner` inside a sheet is familiar for booking flows.

### Storing and Submitting Values

```tsx
// Store native Date objects in form state
const [startsAt, setStartsAt] = useState(new Date());
 
// Serialize only at the API boundary
const payload = {
  startsAt: startsAt.toISOString(), // UTC ISO-8601
  dateOnly: startsAt.toISOString().slice(0, 10), // YYYY-MM-DD when time is irrelevant
};
 
// Parse API responses back to Date
const restored = new Date(payload.startsAt);
```

* Keep **time zones explicit** in your API contract - the picker returns a local `Date`; servers usually want UTC or an IANA zone string.
* For **date-only** fields (birthday), zero out time components before submit or use a dedicated `YYYY-MM-DD` string to avoid off-by-one bugs across zones.
* Pair with [Validation with Zod](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/forms-input/validation-with-zod/) to reject impossible dates (e.g., appointment in the past).

### TypeScript Notes

```tsx
import type { DateTimePickerEvent } from "@react-native-community/datetimepicker";
 
type PickerField = "date" | "time";
 
function handleChange(
  field: PickerField,
  event: DateTimePickerEvent,
  selected?: Date,
) {
  // event.type: "set" | "dismissed" (Android)
  if (event.type === "dismissed") return;
  if (selected) {
    // narrow field-specific updates
  }
}
```

* `DateTimePickerEvent.type` distinguishes confirm vs dismiss on Android - do not update state on `dismissed`.
* `Picker.Item` `value` can be `string | number`; keep types consistent with your form schema.
* Wrap picker state in a small hook (`useDatePickerField`) so screens stay readable.

## Gotchas

* **Typing dates into TextInput** - Users enter `01/02/03` and parsers disagree on month vs day. **Fix:** Use a native or sheet picker; reserve text fields for search, not calendar entry.
* **Android picker left open** - Forgetting to set `showPicker` to `false` after `onChange` leaves an invisible modal blocking touches. **Fix:** Close on every `onChange` on Android; guard with `event.type === "dismissed"`.
* **iOS spinner without Done** - Inline iOS spinners update on every wheel tick, which can fire validation mid-gesture. **Fix:** Use a sheet with Done/Cancel; commit value only on Done.
* **Picker as a hidden dropdown** - `@react-native-picker/picker` always occupies layout height - it is not a collapsed menu. **Fix:** Use a `Pressable` trigger + modal picker pattern, or a design-system bottom sheet, for long lists.
* **Storing formatted strings in state** - Saving `"Mar 8, 2026"` makes comparisons and API mapping fragile. **Fix:** Store `Date` or ISO strings; format at render time.
* **Time zone surprises on submit** - `toISOString()` converts to UTC and can shift the calendar day. **Fix:** Send `date-fns-tz` / `Temporal` (when available) normalized values, or date-only strings for birthdays.
* **Missing accessibility on custom triggers** - Icon-only calendar buttons announce as "button" with no context. **Fix:** Set `accessibilityLabel` including the current value; add `accessibilityHint` for the action.
* **Huge Picker lists** - Rendering 200 `<Picker.Item>` rows hurts mount time and scroll performance. **Fix:** Native picker for < ~20 items; searchable modal list (`FlatList` + filter) for countries or airports.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@react-native-community/datetimepicker` | Standard date/time; you want OS locale, accessibility, and store-review-safe UX | You need pixel-identical wheels on iOS and Android |
| `@react-native-picker/picker` | Short fixed enumerations (duration, salutation, US state) | Long searchable lists or multi-select |
| Custom wheel (`react-native-wheely`, Reanimated) | Brand-mandated cross-platform visual | You can ship native pickers - a11y and locale cost is high |
| Bottom sheet + `FlatList` | 50+ options, search, multi-select tags | Three-option enums where a native picker is faster to ship |
| `TextInput` + mask (`inputMode`, regex) | Currency, phone, postal codes - not calendar data | Dates, times, or enumerated policy fields |
| `expo-document-picker` / `expo-image-picker` | Files and media - different "native input" family | Scalar form fields |

## FAQs

Should I use native pickers or a custom bottom sheet?

* Native pickers win on accessibility, locale, and maintenance - the OS handles VoiceOver/TalkBack and 12/24-hour clocks.
* Custom sheets win when design requires identical visuals on iOS and Android or advanced features (range selection, blocked dates).
* Hybrid is common: native on phone, custom calendar grid on tablet - see [Responsive & Adaptive Layout](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/responsive-and-adaptive-layout/).

How do I install pickers in an Expo SDK 57 project?

* Run `npx expo install @react-native-community/datetimepicker @react-native-picker/picker` so versions match RN 0.86.
* Rebuild dev clients after adding native modules - Expo Go includes these modules; custom dev clients need a rebuild.
* Import from the package root; no manual linking in managed workflow.

Why does Android show a dialog but iOS shows a spinner?

* Each platform exposes its idiomatic control - Android `DatePickerDialog`, iOS `UIDatePicker`.
* You normalize the UX in your layer with triggers, sheets, and Done buttons - do not fight the underlying widget.
* `display="compact"` on iOS 14+ yields a tappable chip that expands inline - good for dense settings screens.

How do I pick both date and time for one appointment?

* Use two fields with `mode="date"` and `mode="time"`, then merge into one `Date` before submit.
* Alternatively, pick date first, then time in a second step - clearer for thumb reach on small phones.
* Validate the combined instant is in the future with Zod `refine` on the merged value.

What is the difference between datetimepicker and Picker?

* `datetimepicker` is for calendar clock values - returns a `Date` through `onChange`.
* `Picker` is for choosing among discrete string/number options - think duration, category, prefix.
* Do not use `Picker` for dates; do not use `datetimepicker` for enum lists.

How do I disable past dates or weekends?

* `@react-native-community/datetimepicker` supports `minimumDate` and `maximumDate` props on both platforms.
* Blocking arbitrary weekdays (e.g., no Sundays) is not built in - validate on submit or use a custom calendar.
* Document blocked rules in inline helper text so users understand why a day is rejected.

How do pickers interact with react-hook-form?

* Register a `Controller` whose `render` wraps your trigger + picker; call `field.onChange(date)` when the user confirms.
* Use `value={field.value ?? new Date()}` and validate with Zod `z.coerce.date()` or `z.date()`.
* See [react-hook-form on Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/forms-input/react-hook-form-on-mobile/) for `Controller` patterns that avoid re-renders.

Can I show a picker inline without a Pressable trigger?

* Yes on iOS - render `DateTimePicker` with `display="inline"` directly in the form.
* Android still prefers dialog mode for date/time - inline calendar is iOS-biased.
* Inline pickers consume vertical space; pair with [Keyboard Controller](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/forms-input/keyboard-controller/) so fields above are not obscured.

How do I format dates for US vs EU users?

* Use `Intl.DateTimeFormat(undefined, options)` - `undefined` locale follows the device setting.
* Store ISO or epoch in state/API; never persist locale-formatted strings.
* For i18n-heavy apps, centralize format helpers - see the i18n section when those articles ship.

What about pickers in dark mode?

* Native pickers follow system appearance automatically.
* Custom trigger borders and sheet backgrounds need theme tokens - see [Dark Mode & Color Schemes](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/dark-mode-and-color-schemes/).
* Test compact iOS chips in both schemes - contrast on `surface` containers matters.

Do pickers work inside a ScrollView?

* Inline iOS spinners inside `ScrollView` can cause gesture conflicts - nest carefully or use modal presentation.
* Android dialogs are outside the scroll tree - no conflict.
* For long forms, dismiss the keyboard before opening pickers so layout does not jump.

How do I test pickers in Jest?

* Mock `@react-native-community/datetimepicker` to a `Pressable` that calls `onChange` with a fixed date.
* Mock `Picker` as a `View` that exposes `onValueChange` via `testID`.
* Assert your trigger `accessibilityLabel` and submitted ISO string - not native wheel semantics.
