# react-hook-form on Mobile

React Native `TextInput` components are always controlled from the native side, but you still want uncontrolled *form state* on the JS thread. **react-hook-form** subscribes to field changes instead of re-rendering the whole screen on every keystroke - the pattern that keeps multi-field signup and checkout flows smooth on mid-range Android devices.

Highlights / react-hook-form on Mobile

* Use Controller for every TextInput - React Native has no native form element to register by ref
* defaultValues must list every field or isDirty and reset behave incorrectly
* mode: onTouched validates after blur, reducing keyboard-dismiss churn on small screens
* formState is a Proxy - destructure only the flags you read or you opt into extra re-renders
* setFocus jumps between fields for wizard steps and accessible error recovery
* Pair with Zod via zodResolver so validation schemas stay the single source of truth

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```tsx
import { Controller, useForm } from "react-hook-form";
import { Pressable, StyleSheet, Text, TextInput, View } from "react-native";
 
interface SignInValues {
  email: string;
  password: string;
}
 
export function SignInForm() {
  const {
    control,
    handleSubmit,
    formState: { errors, isSubmitting },
  } = useForm<SignInValues>({
    defaultValues: { email: "", password: "" },
    mode: "onTouched",
  });
 
  async function onSubmit(values: SignInValues) {
    await fetch("https://api.example.com/auth/login", {
      method: "POST",
      headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
      body: JSON.stringify(values),
    });
  }
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.form}>
      <Controller
        control={control}
        name="email"
        rules={{ required: "Email is required" }}
        render={({ field: { onChange, onBlur, value, ref } }) => (
          <TextInput
            ref={ref}
            value={value}
            onChangeText={onChange}
            onBlur={onBlur}
            keyboardType="email-address"
            autoCapitalize="none"
            placeholder="Email"
            style={styles.input}
          />
        )}
      />
      {errors.email && <Text style={styles.error}>{errors.email.message}</Text>}
 
      <Controller
        control={control}
        name="password"
        rules={{ minLength: { value: 8, message: "At least 8 characters" } }}
        render={({ field: { onChange, onBlur, value, ref } }) => (
          <TextInput
            ref={ref}
            value={value}
            onChangeText={onChange}
            onBlur={onBlur}
            secureTextEntry
            placeholder="Password"
            style={styles.input}
          />
        )}
      />
      {errors.password && <Text style={styles.error}>{errors.password.message}</Text>}
 
      <Pressable
        onPress={handleSubmit(onSubmit)}
        disabled={isSubmitting}
        style={styles.button}
      >
        <Text style={styles.buttonText}>{isSubmitting ? "Signing in…" : "Sign in"}</Text>
      </Pressable>
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  form: { gap: 12, padding: 16 },
  input: {
    borderWidth: 1,
    borderColor: "#d1d5db",
    borderRadius: 8,
    paddingHorizontal: 12,
    paddingVertical: 10,
    fontSize: 16,
  },
  error: { color: "#dc2626", fontSize: 13 },
  button: {
    backgroundColor: "#2563eb",
    borderRadius: 8,
    paddingVertical: 12,
    alignItems: "center",
  },
  buttonText: { color: "#fff", fontWeight: "600" },
});
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Screens with more than three `TextInput` fields where `useState` per field causes visible jank.
* Dynamic field lists (addresses, line items) via `useFieldArray`.
* Forms that share validation with your web app through Zod schemas.
* Multi-step wizards that need one form instance across steps.
* Any flow where you need `isDirty` guards before navigating back.

## Working Example

```tsx
// components/form/TextField.tsx - reusable RN field wired to RHF
import { Controller, type Control, type FieldPath, type FieldValues } from "react-hook-form";
import { StyleSheet, Text, TextInput, type TextInputProps, View } from "react-native";
 
interface TextFieldProps<T extends FieldValues> extends Omit<TextInputProps, "value" | "onChangeText"> {
  control: Control<T>;
  name: FieldPath<T>;
  label: string;
}
 
export function TextField<T extends FieldValues>({
  control,
  name,
  label,
  ...inputProps
}: TextFieldProps<T>) {
  return (
    <Controller
      control={control}
      name={name}
      render={({ field: { onChange, onBlur, value, ref }, fieldState: { error, isTouched } }) => (
        <View style={styles.field}>
          <Text style={styles.label}>{label}</Text>
          <TextInput
            ref={ref}
            value={value ?? ""}
            onChangeText={onChange}
            onBlur={onBlur}
            style={[styles.input, isTouched && error && styles.inputError]}
            accessibilityLabel={label}
            {...inputProps}
          />
          {error && <Text style={styles.error}>{error.message}</Text>}
        </View>
      )}
    />
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  field: { gap: 6 },
  label: { fontSize: 14, fontWeight: "600", color: "#374151" },
  input: {
    borderWidth: 1,
    borderColor: "#d1d5db",
    borderRadius: 8,
    paddingHorizontal: 12,
    paddingVertical: 10,
    fontSize: 16,
    backgroundColor: "#fff",
  },
  inputError: { borderColor: "#dc2626" },
  error: { color: "#dc2626", fontSize: 13 },
});
```

```tsx
// app/(auth)/register.tsx - profile form with focus chain and submit guard
import { useForm } from "react-hook-form";
import { Alert, Pressable, StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
import { KeyboardAwareScrollView } from "react-native-keyboard-controller";
import { useRouter } from "expo-router";
import { TextField } from "../../components/form/TextField";
 
interface RegisterValues {
  fullName: string;
  email: string;
  phone: string;
}
 
export default function RegisterScreen() {
  const router = useRouter();
 
  const {
    control,
    handleSubmit,
    setFocus,
    formState: { isSubmitting, isDirty },
  } = useForm<RegisterValues>({
    defaultValues: { fullName: "", email: "", phone: "" },
    mode: "onTouched",
  });
 
  async function onSubmit(values: RegisterValues) {
    const res = await fetch("https://api.example.com/v1/register", {
      method: "POST",
      headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
      body: JSON.stringify(values),
    });
    if (!res.ok) {
      Alert.alert("Registration failed", "Check your details and try again.");
      return;
    }
    Alert.alert("Account created", "You can sign in now.");
  }
 
  function handleBack() {
    if (isDirty) {
      Alert.alert("Discard changes?", "You have unsaved edits.", [
        { text: "Stay", style: "cancel" },
        { text: "Discard", style: "destructive", onPress: () => router.back() },
      ]);
      return;
    }
    router.back();
  }
 
  return (
    <KeyboardAwareScrollView
      bottomOffset={24}
      contentContainerStyle={styles.scroll}
      keyboardShouldPersistTaps="handled"
    >
      <Text style={styles.title}>Create account</Text>
 
      <TextField
        control={control}
        name="fullName"
        label="Full name"
        autoComplete="name"
        returnKeyType="next"
        onSubmitEditing={() => setFocus("email")}
      />
 
      <TextField
        control={control}
        name="email"
        label="Email"
        keyboardType="email-address"
        autoCapitalize="none"
        autoComplete="email"
        returnKeyType="next"
        onSubmitEditing={() => setFocus("phone")}
      />
 
      <TextField
        control={control}
        name="phone"
        label="Phone"
        keyboardType="phone-pad"
        autoComplete="tel"
        returnKeyType="done"
        onSubmitEditing={handleSubmit(onSubmit)}
      />
 
      <View style={styles.actions}>
        <Pressable onPress={handleBack} style={styles.secondary}>
          <Text style={styles.secondaryText}>Back</Text>
        </Pressable>
        <Pressable
          onPress={handleSubmit(onSubmit)}
          disabled={isSubmitting}
          style={styles.primary}
        >
          <Text style={styles.primaryText}>{isSubmitting ? "Saving…" : "Continue"}</Text>
        </Pressable>
      </View>
    </KeyboardAwareScrollView>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  scroll: { padding: 16, gap: 16 },
  title: { fontSize: 22, fontWeight: "700", marginBottom: 4 },
  actions: { flexDirection: "row", gap: 12, marginTop: 8 },
  secondary: {
    flex: 1,
    borderWidth: 1,
    borderColor: "#d1d5db",
    borderRadius: 8,
    paddingVertical: 12,
    alignItems: "center",
  },
  secondaryText: { fontWeight: "600", color: "#374151" },
  primary: {
    flex: 1,
    backgroundColor: "#2563eb",
    borderRadius: 8,
    paddingVertical: 12,
    alignItems: "center",
  },
  primaryText: { color: "#fff", fontWeight: "600" },
});
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* `Controller` bridges react-hook-form to every `TextInput` - the required pattern on React Native.
* A reusable `TextField` keeps error styling and accessibility labels consistent across screens.
* `setFocus` and `returnKeyType="next"` chain the software keyboard without extra state.
* `mode: "onTouched"` validates after blur, not on every character - better for mobile typing.
* `isDirty` powers a discard-changes guard before the user leaves the screen.
* `KeyboardAwareScrollView` keeps the active field visible above the keyboard.

## Deep Dive

### How It Works

* `useForm` holds field values in a ref-backed store - updating a field does not re-render the parent unless you subscribe to that slice of `formState`.
* `Controller` registers the field, wires `onChange` to `onChangeText`, and attaches the `ref` so `setFocus` can call `TextInput.focus()`.
* Validation runs through `rules` on the `Controller`, a custom `resolver`, or `zodResolver` (see [Validation with Zod](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/forms-input/validation-with-zod/)).
* `handleSubmit` runs validation first; your `onSubmit` only fires when the form is valid.
* `formState` uses a Proxy - reading `errors.email` subscribes the component to email errors; reading the entire `formState` object subscribes to everything.

### Controller vs register on Mobile

| Approach | React Native | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `register` + spread props | Does not work | No `<input>` ref; `TextInput` needs `onChangeText` |
| `Controller` | Default | Full control over `TextInput` props and styling |
| `useController` | Custom field components | Same as `Controller`, better for design-system wrappers |

On web you can `{...register("email")}` on a native input. On RN, always use `Controller` or `useController`.

### Validation Modes for Mobile

| `mode` | When validation runs | Mobile fit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onSubmit` | On button press | Simple one-field forms |
| `onTouched` | After first blur, then on change | **Recommended default** for multi-field screens |
| `onBlur` | Every blur | Good for long text areas |
| `onChange` | Every keystroke | Use sparingly - can fight the keyboard and cause jank |

Combine with `reValidateMode: "onChange"` so corrected fields clear errors immediately after the first submit attempt.

### FormProvider and Multi-Step Flows

```tsx
import { FormProvider, useForm } from "react-hook-form";
 
const methods = useForm<WizardValues>({ defaultValues: { /* all steps */ } });
 
return (
  <FormProvider {...methods}>
    {step === 1 ? <AccountStep /> : <AddressStep />}
  </FormProvider>
);
```

* Declare **all step fields** in `defaultValues` even if the current step only renders a subset - `isDirty` and `reset` stay accurate.
* Child steps call `useFormContext()` instead of receiving `control` through props.
* Persist `methods.getValues()` to AsyncStorage between steps for wizard recovery (see [Multi-Step & Wizard Flows](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/forms-input/multi-step-and-wizard-flows/)).

### TypeScript Notes

```tsx
import { useForm, type SubmitHandler } from "react-hook-form";
import { z } from "zod";
import { zodResolver } from "@hookform/resolvers/zod";
 
const ProfileSchema = z.object({
  fullName: z.string().min(1),
  email: z.string().email(),
});
 
type ProfileValues = z.infer<typeof ProfileSchema>;
 
const onSubmit: SubmitHandler<ProfileValues> = async (values) => {
  // values is fully typed
};
 
const form = useForm<ProfileValues>({
  resolver: zodResolver(ProfileSchema),
  defaultValues: { fullName: "", email: "" },
});
```

* Install with `npx expo install react-hook-form @hookform/resolvers zod`.
* Use `FieldPath<ProfileValues>` on reusable field `name` props so typos fail at compile time.
* `TextInput` values are always strings - coerce numbers in Zod with `z.coerce.number()` rather than typing fields as `number` in `defaultValues`.

### Parameters & Return Values

| API | Purpose on RN |
| --- | --- |
| `useForm({ defaultValues })` | Required - every field key must appear |
| `control` | Pass to `Controller` / `useFieldArray` |
| `handleSubmit(onValid, onInvalid?)` | Wraps `Pressable.onPress`; `onInvalid` can call `setFocus` on first error |
| `setFocus(name)` | Moves keyboard focus to a field by name |
| `reset(values?)` | Clears after success or restores draft |
| `watch(name)` | Subscribe to one field - avoid watching the whole form in render |
| `useFieldArray({ control, name })` | Dynamic rows - key list items with `field.id`, not array index |

## Gotchas

* **Spreading `register` on `TextInput`** - `register` returns web-centric props (`onChange`, `name`) that do not map to `onChangeText`. **Fix:** Use `Controller` and map `onChange` → `onChangeText`.
* **Missing `defaultValues` keys** - New fields show `undefined`, `isDirty` stays false after edits, and `reset()` skips them. **Fix:** List every field in `defaultValues`, including empty strings and empty arrays.
* **Destructuring all of `formState`** - `const { formState } = useForm()` then reading `formState.isSubmitting` in render still works, but `const { isSubmitting, errors, isDirty, isValid } = formState` subscribes to four signals at once. **Fix:** Destructure only what the component displays.
* **`watch()` in the parent render** - `watch()` without arguments re-renders on every keystroke across all fields - the problem RHF solves. **Fix:** `watch("email")` for one field, or move watched UI into an isolated child.
* **`undefined` TextInput value** - Passing `value={undefined}` triggers warnings and clears cursor position. **Fix:** `value={value ?? ""}` in the `Controller` render.
* **`onSubmit` without `handleSubmit`** - Pressing the button skips validation and sends partial data. **Fix:** `onPress={handleSubmit(onSubmit)}` on `Pressable`, never `onPress={onSubmit}`.
* **Server errors not mapped to fields** - API returns `{ fieldErrors: { email: "Taken" } }` but the UI shows a generic alert. **Fix:** Loop `setError("email", { type: "server", message })` and `setFocus("email")`.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| react-hook-form + `Controller` | Default for 4+ fields, dynamic lists, shared Zod schemas | A single search box with one piece of local state |
| Plain `useState` per field | 1–3 fields, no validation, prototype screens | Checkout, onboarding, or any form with cross-field rules |
| Formik | Brownfield app already on Formik | Greenfield Expo apps - heavier re-render profile |
| React 19 `useActionState` | Web-style server actions in Expo Router API routes | Complex client-only validation and masked inputs on device |
| TanStack Form | You want headless form primitives with fine-grained subscriptions | Team already standardized on RHF across web and mobile |

## FAQs

Why can't I use register() like on the web?

* React Native has no DOM `<input>` - `register` relies on ref + native change events that `TextInput` does not expose the same way.
* `TextInput` uses `onChangeText`, not `onChange`.
* `Controller` is the supported bridge and gives you full control over keyboard props.

What validation mode should I use on mobile?

* Start with `mode: "onTouched"` - errors appear after the user leaves a field, not mid-word.
* Add `reValidateMode: "onChange"` so fixed fields clear errors without another submit.
* Reserve `mode: "onChange"` for short fields like promo codes where instant feedback helps.

How do I move focus to the next field when the user taps Return?

```tsx
<TextField
  name="email"
  returnKeyType="next"
  onSubmitEditing={() => setFocus("password")}
/>
```

* `setFocus` is built into `useForm` - no manual ref map required when field names are registered.
* Set `returnKeyType="done"` on the last field and call `handleSubmit(onSubmit)` in `onSubmitEditing`.

How do I focus the first invalid field after submit?

```tsx
handleSubmit(onSubmit, (invalid) => {
  const first = Object.keys(invalid)[0] as keyof RegisterValues;
  setFocus(first);
})();
```

* The second argument to `handleSubmit` runs when validation fails.
* Combine with `scrollTo` from a ref on `KeyboardAwareScrollView` for long forms.

Does react-hook-form work with TypeScript on Expo?

* Yes - pass a generic to `useForm<FormValues>()` and to `Control<FormValues>` on field components.
* Pair with `zodResolver` and `z.infer<typeof Schema>` for end-to-end typed forms.
* Install via `npx expo install react-hook-form @hookform/resolvers zod`.

How do I show a loading state on the submit button?

* Destructure `isSubmitting` from `formState`.
* `handleSubmit` sets it true while your async `onSubmit` promise is pending.
* Disable the `Pressable` and change label text while `isSubmitting` is true.

Can I use react-hook-form inside a FlatList?

* Yes for the form wrapper - put fields inside `ListHeaderComponent` or `ListFooterComponent`.
* Do not put uncontrolled `TextInput` inside `renderItem` without `Controller` - recycling will reset values.
* For dynamic rows, prefer `useFieldArray` over manual index state.

How do I reset the form after a successful API call?

```tsx
async function onSubmit(values: RegisterValues) {
  await createAccount(values);
  reset(); // back to defaultValues
}
```

* `reset()` clears errors, dirty state, and values.
* Pass `reset(partialValues)` to keep some fields after success (e.g. email for a confirmation step).

Should I use FormProvider?

* Use it when multiple child components need `useFormContext()` - wizard steps, modal field groups, or design-system form sections.
* For a single-screen form, passing `control` to `TextField` is enough.

How does react-hook-form compare to controlled useState on RN?

* `useState` re-renders the owning component on every `onChangeText`.
* RHF stores values in refs and only re-renders subscribed `formState` slices.
* For 1–2 fields the difference is negligible; past ~4 fields RHF wins on mid-tier hardware.

How do I handle secure text and password visibility toggles?

* Keep `secureTextEntry` on `TextInput` inside `Controller` - do not fork a second uncontrolled input.
* Toggle visibility with local `useState` in the field component; the RHF value stays the same string.

Can I combine react-hook-form with KeyboardAwareScrollView?

* Yes - wrap the form in `KeyboardAwareScrollView` from `react-native-keyboard-controller`.
* Set `keyboardShouldPersistTaps="handled"` so submit buttons work while the keyboard is open.
* See [Keyboard Controller](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/forms-input/keyboard-controller/) for `bottomOffset` and toolbar setup.

How do I install react-hook-form in an Expo SDK 57 project?

```bash
npx expo install react-hook-form
```

* Add `@hookform/resolvers` and `zod` when you wire schema validation.
* No native config plugin required - pure JavaScript.

* [Validation with Zod](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/forms-input/validation-with-zod/) - `zodResolver`, inline errors, and schema-first mobile UX

# Validation with Zod

Zod describes what valid data looks like at runtime and infers the same TypeScript type your IDE autocompletes. On mobile, that matters twice: `TextInput` always delivers strings, and users expect inline errors under the field they just left - not a modal after tapping Submit.

Highlights / Validation with Zod

* z.infer<typeof Schema> is the single source of truth for form values and API payloads
* zodResolver bridges Zod into react-hook-form - errors map to field paths automatically
* TextInput always yields strings - use z.coerce.number() or preprocess before comparing numbers
* Show errors only after touch or submit to avoid shouting at users mid-keystroke
* Use .refine() and .superRefine() for cross-field rules like password confirmation
* Map server fieldErrors with setError so API failures appear inline, not in alerts

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```tsx
import { zodResolver } from "@hookform/resolvers/zod";
import { Controller, useForm } from "react-hook-form";
import { z } from "zod";
import { Pressable, StyleSheet, Text, TextInput, View } from "react-native";
 
const SignUpSchema = z
  .object({
    email: z.string().min(1, "Email is required").email("Enter a valid email"),
    password: z.string().min(8, "At least 8 characters"),
    confirmPassword: z.string().min(1, "Confirm your password"),
  })
  .refine((data) => data.password === data.confirmPassword, {
    message: "Passwords must match",
    path: ["confirmPassword"],
  });
 
type SignUpValues = z.infer<typeof SignUpSchema>;
 
export function SignUpForm() {
  const {
    control,
    handleSubmit,
    formState: { errors, isSubmitting },
  } = useForm<SignUpValues>({
    resolver: zodResolver(SignUpSchema),
    defaultValues: { email: "", password: "", confirmPassword: "" },
    mode: "onTouched",
  });
 
  function onSubmit(values: SignUpValues) {
    console.log(values);
  }
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.form}>
      <Controller
        control={control}
        name="email"
        render={({ field: { onChange, onBlur, value, ref } }) => (
          <TextInput
            ref={ref}
            value={value}
            onChangeText={onChange}
            onBlur={onBlur}
            keyboardType="email-address"
            autoCapitalize="none"
            placeholder="Email"
            style={styles.input}
          />
        )}
      />
      {errors.email && <Text style={styles.error}>{errors.email.message}</Text>}
 
      <Controller
        control={control}
        name="password"
        render={({ field: { onChange, onBlur, value, ref } }) => (
          <TextInput
            ref={ref}
            value={value}
            onChangeText={onChange}
            onBlur={onBlur}
            secureTextEntry
            placeholder="Password"
            style={styles.input}
          />
        )}
      />
      {errors.password && <Text style={styles.error}>{errors.password.message}</Text>}
 
      <Controller
        control={control}
        name="confirmPassword"
        render={({ field: { onChange, onBlur, value, ref } }) => (
          <TextInput
            ref={ref}
            value={value}
            onChangeText={onChange}
            onBlur={onBlur}
            secureTextEntry
            placeholder="Confirm password"
            style={styles.input}
          />
        )}
      />
      {errors.confirmPassword && (
        <Text style={styles.error}>{errors.confirmPassword.message}</Text>
      )}
 
      <Pressable onPress={handleSubmit(onSubmit)} disabled={isSubmitting} style={styles.button}>
        <Text style={styles.buttonText}>Create account</Text>
      </Pressable>
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  form: { gap: 12, padding: 16 },
  input: {
    borderWidth: 1,
    borderColor: "#d1d5db",
    borderRadius: 8,
    paddingHorizontal: 12,
    paddingVertical: 10,
    fontSize: 16,
  },
  error: { color: "#dc2626", fontSize: 13 },
  button: {
    backgroundColor: "#2563eb",
    borderRadius: 8,
    paddingVertical: 12,
    alignItems: "center",
  },
  buttonText: { color: "#fff", fontWeight: "600" },
});
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Any form where validation rules should match your API request schema.
* Cross-field rules - password confirmation, date ranges, conditional required fields.
* Sharing schemas between mobile forms and fetch-layer parsing (see [Typing API Responses & Zod](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/typescript-rn/typing-api-responses-and-zod/)).
* Localized error messages derived from one schema definition.
* Preventing `TextInput` string quirks from breaking numeric or boolean validation.

## Working Example

```ts
// lib/schemas/profile.ts - shared between form and API client
import { z } from "zod";
 
export const ProfileSchema = z.object({
  displayName: z
    .string()
    .trim()
    .min(1, "Display name is required")
    .max(40, "Keep it under 40 characters"),
  bio: z
    .string()
    .max(280, "Bio must be 280 characters or fewer")
    .optional()
    .or(z.literal("")),
  age: z
    .string()
    .min(1, "Age is required")
    .pipe(
      z.coerce
        .number({ invalid_type_error: "Enter a number" })
        .int("Whole numbers only")
        .min(13, "You must be at least 13")
        .max(120, "Enter a realistic age")
    ),
  newsletter: z.boolean().default(false),
});
 
export type ProfileValues = z.infer<typeof ProfileSchema>;
 
export const ProfileUpdateSchema = ProfileSchema.pick({
  displayName: true,
  bio: true,
  newsletter: true,
});
 
export type ProfileUpdateValues = z.infer<typeof ProfileUpdateSchema>;
```

```tsx
// components/form/ValidatedTextField.tsx
import { Controller, type Control, type FieldPath, type FieldValues } from "react-hook-form";
import { StyleSheet, Text, TextInput, type TextInputProps, View } from "react-native";
 
interface ValidatedTextFieldProps<T extends FieldValues>
  extends Omit<TextInputProps, "value" | "onChangeText"> {
  control: Control<T>;
  name: FieldPath<T>;
  label: string;
}
 
export function ValidatedTextField<T extends FieldValues>({
  control,
  name,
  label,
  ...inputProps
}: ValidatedTextFieldProps<T>) {
  return (
    <Controller
      control={control}
      name={name}
      render={({ field: { onChange, onBlur, value, ref }, fieldState: { error, isTouched } }) => (
        <View style={styles.field}>
          <Text style={styles.label}>{label}</Text>
          <TextInput
            ref={ref}
            value={value ?? ""}
            onChangeText={onChange}
            onBlur={onBlur}
            style={[styles.input, isTouched && error && styles.inputError]}
            accessibilityLabel={label}
            accessibilityHint={error?.message}
            {...inputProps}
          />
          {isTouched && error && (
            <Text style={styles.error} accessibilityLiveRegion="polite">
              {error.message}
            </Text>
          )}
        </View>
      )}
    />
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  field: { gap: 6 },
  label: { fontSize: 14, fontWeight: "600", color: "#374151" },
  input: {
    borderWidth: 1,
    borderColor: "#d1d5db",
    borderRadius: 8,
    paddingHorizontal: 12,
    paddingVertical: 10,
    fontSize: 16,
    backgroundColor: "#fff",
  },
  inputError: { borderColor: "#dc2626" },
  error: { color: "#dc2626", fontSize: 13 },
});
```

```tsx
// app/settings/profile.tsx - submit with server error mapping
import { zodResolver } from "@hookform/resolvers/zod";
import { useForm } from "react-hook-form";
import { Controller } from "react-hook-form";
import { Alert, Pressable, StyleSheet, Switch, Text, View } from "react-native";
import { KeyboardAwareScrollView } from "react-native-keyboard-controller";
import { ProfileSchema, type ProfileValues } from "../../lib/schemas/profile";
import { ValidatedTextField } from "../../components/form/ValidatedTextField";
 
type ApiFieldErrors = Partial<Record<keyof ProfileValues, string>>;
 
async function saveProfile(
  values: ProfileValues
): Promise<{ ok: true } | { ok: false; fieldErrors?: ApiFieldErrors; message?: string }> {
  const res = await fetch("https://api.example.com/v1/profile", {
    method: "PUT",
    headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
    body: JSON.stringify(values),
  });
  const json: unknown = await res.json();
  if (!res.ok) {
    const body = json as { fieldErrors?: ApiFieldErrors; message?: string };
    return { ok: false, fieldErrors: body.fieldErrors, message: body.message };
  }
  return { ok: true };
}
 
export default function ProfileScreen() {
  const {
    control,
    handleSubmit,
    setError,
    setFocus,
    formState: { isSubmitting, isDirty },
  } = useForm<ProfileValues>({
    resolver: zodResolver(ProfileSchema),
    defaultValues: {
      displayName: "",
      bio: "",
      age: "",
      newsletter: false,
    },
    mode: "onTouched",
    reValidateMode: "onChange",
  });
 
  async function onSubmit(values: ProfileValues) {
    const result = await saveProfile(values);
    if (result.ok) {
      Alert.alert("Saved", "Your profile was updated.");
      return;
    }
    if (result.fieldErrors) {
      for (const [field, message] of Object.entries(result.fieldErrors)) {
        setError(field as keyof ProfileValues, { type: "server", message });
      }
      const first = Object.keys(result.fieldErrors)[0] as keyof ProfileValues;
      setFocus(first);
      return;
    }
    Alert.alert("Save failed", result.message ?? "Try again.");
  }
 
  return (
    <KeyboardAwareScrollView contentContainerStyle={styles.scroll} keyboardShouldPersistTaps="handled">
      <ValidatedTextField control={control} name="displayName" label="Display name" />
 
      <ValidatedTextField
        control={control}
        name="bio"
        label="Bio"
        multiline
        numberOfLines={3}
        style={styles.multiline}
      />
 
      <ValidatedTextField
        control={control}
        name="age"
        label="Age"
        keyboardType="number-pad"
      />
 
      <View style={styles.switchRow}>
        <Text style={styles.switchLabel}>Email newsletter</Text>
        <Controller
          control={control}
          name="newsletter"
          render={({ field: { value, onChange } }) => (
            <Switch value={value} onValueChange={onChange} />
          )}
        />
      </View>
 
      <Pressable
        onPress={handleSubmit(onSubmit)}
        disabled={isSubmitting || !isDirty}
        style={[styles.button, (!isDirty || isSubmitting) && styles.buttonDisabled]}
      >
        <Text style={styles.buttonText}>{isSubmitting ? "Saving…" : "Save changes"}</Text>
      </Pressable>
    </KeyboardAwareScrollView>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  scroll: { padding: 16, gap: 16 },
  multiline: { minHeight: 88, textAlignVertical: "top" },
  switchRow: { flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "space-between" },
  switchLabel: { fontSize: 16 },
  button: {
    backgroundColor: "#2563eb",
    borderRadius: 8,
    paddingVertical: 12,
    alignItems: "center",
    marginTop: 8,
  },
  buttonDisabled: { opacity: 0.5 },
  buttonText: { color: "#fff", fontWeight: "600" },
});
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* One `ProfileSchema` drives both compile-time types and runtime validation.
* `.trim()`, `.coerce.number()`, and `.optional().or(z.literal(""))` handle `TextInput` string realities.
* `ValidatedTextField` shows errors only after touch - better mobile UX than validating on every character.
* `setError` + `setFocus` maps server `fieldErrors` to inline messages under the right input.
* `ProfileUpdateSchema.pick()` reuses field definitions for a partial edit form without duplicating rules.

## Deep Dive

### How It Works

* You define a Zod schema describing the shape, constraints, and error messages.
* `zodResolver(Schema)` adapts that schema to react-hook-form's `resolver` slot.
* On submit (or per `mode`), RHF passes current values to Zod; failures become `formState.errors` keyed by field path.
* `z.infer<typeof Schema>` exports the TypeScript type - no parallel `interface` to drift.
* Zod runs in plain `.ts` files with no JSX, so Metro can import schemas from API clients, background tasks, and tests.

### Rules at a Glance

| Zod helper | Mobile form use |
| --- | --- |
| `z.string().min(1)` | Required text fields (after `.trim()`) |
| `z.string().email()` | Email `TextInput` with `keyboardType="email-address"` |
| `z.coerce.number()` | Numeric fields - `TextInput` always returns strings |
| `z.boolean()` | `Switch` values via `Controller` |
| `z.enum(["a", "b"])` | Segmented controls and picker selections |
| `.optional()` | Field may be absent from the object |
| `.nullable()` | Field may be explicit `null` from the API |
| `.default(false)` | Checkbox off without registering `undefined` |
| `.refine()` | Cross-field rules with `path` targeting one field |
| `.superRefine()` | Multiple errors or array-index paths |

### Empty Strings and Optional Fields

```ts
const OptionalBioSchema = z.object({
  bio: z
    .string()
    .trim()
    .max(280)
    .transform((s) => (s === "" ? undefined : s))
    .optional(),
});
```

* Users leave optional fields blank as `""`, not `undefined`.
* Transform empty strings once in the schema instead of cleaning in `onSubmit`.
* For required fields, chain `.trim().min(1, "Required")` so whitespace-only input fails.

### Cross-Field Validation

```ts
const ChangePasswordSchema = z
  .object({
    currentPassword: z.string().min(1, "Enter your current password"),
    newPassword: z.string().min(8, "At least 8 characters"),
    confirmPassword: z.string().min(1, "Confirm your new password"),
  })
  .refine((data) => data.newPassword === data.confirmPassword, {
    message: "Passwords must match",
    path: ["confirmPassword"],
  })
  .refine((data) => data.currentPassword !== data.newPassword, {
    message: "New password must differ from current",
    path: ["newPassword"],
  });
```

* `.refine()` runs after base field parsing - ideal for password confirmation.
* Set `path` so the error attaches to the correct `TextInput`, not the form root.
* Use `.superRefine()` when one validation produces multiple errors on different paths.

### TypeScript Notes

```ts
import { z } from "zod";
 
const OrderSchema = z.object({
  quantity: z.coerce.number().positive(),
  note: z.string().optional(),
});
 
type OrderInput = z.input<typeof OrderSchema>;   // before transforms/coerce
type OrderOutput = z.output<typeof OrderSchema>; // after - same as z.infer when no transforms
type OrderValues = z.infer<typeof OrderSchema>;
```

* Install with `npx expo install zod @hookform/resolvers react-hook-form`.
* Export `Schema`, `type Values = z.infer<typeof Schema>`, and `safeParse` helpers from one module.
* Reuse API response schemas with `.pick()` / `.omit()` / `.extend()` so list, detail, and form shapes stay aligned.

### Error Display Patterns

| Pattern | Behavior | Best for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Show on touch | `isTouched && error` | Default mobile UX |
| Show after first submit | `isSubmitted && error` | Short forms with one CTA |
| Always show | `error && message` | Accessibility-critical compliance forms |
| Summary banner | Root `errors.root` message | Non-field server failures |

```tsx
// Surface a non-field server error
setError("root", { type: "server", message: "Network unavailable. Try again." });
{errors.root && <Text style={styles.banner}>{errors.root.message}</Text>}
```

## Gotchas

* **Duplicating types and schemas** - Maintaining a `interface Profile` separate from `ProfileSchema` drifts on the first API change. **Fix:** Export only `z.infer<typeof ProfileSchema>`.
* **Validating numbers without coercion** - `z.number()` fails when `TextInput` delivers `"25"` as a string. **Fix:** `z.coerce.number()` or `z.string().regex(/^\d+$/).transform(Number)`.
* **`.optional()` vs empty string** - Optional bio field with `""` fails `z.string().email()` chained after. **Fix:** Trim and transform `""` → `undefined`, or use `.or(z.literal(""))`.
* **Showing errors before touch** - Validating `onChange` on every keystroke frustrates mobile users. **Fix:** `mode: "onTouched"` and render `isTouched && error`.
* **Password match on wrong path** - `.refine()` without `path` puts the error on `_form` root. **Fix:** `path: ["confirmPassword"]` so the message sits under the right field.
* **Nullable API fields in forms** - Backend sends `middleName: null` but form uses `""`. **Fix:** Normalize in `defaultValues` and schema with `.nullable().transform(v => v ?? "")`.
* **Giant monolithic schema** - One 40-field schema makes error paths hard to read. **Fix:** Compose step schemas and merge with `.merge()` for wizards, or validate per step with `.pick()`.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Zod + `zodResolver` | Default for typed RN forms shared with API layer | Single checkbox with one local `useState` |
| Yup + `yupResolver` | Team already standardized on Yup | Greenfield apps where Zod matches your fetch schemas |
| Inline `rules` on `Controller` | 1–2 trivial fields (`required: true`) | Cross-field rules or schemas reused server-side |
| Valibot / ArkType | Bundle size is the top constraint | You already share Zod schemas with the backend and web app |
| Manual `safeParse` in `onSubmit` | Prototype without RHF | Production forms needing per-field touch state and `setError` |

## FAQs

How do I install Zod and the resolver in Expo SDK 57?

```bash
npx expo install zod @hookform/resolvers react-hook-form
```

* `expo install` pins versions compatible with your lockfile.
* Import schemas from plain `.ts` files - no native module setup.

What is the difference between parse and safeParse in forms?

* `zodResolver` uses `parse` internally - validation failures become RHF field errors automatically.
* Use `safeParse` in API clients when you want to branch without throwing.
* In `onSubmit`, values are already validated - trust the type RHF passes through.

How do I validate optional fields that users leave blank?

```ts
bio: z.string().trim().max(280).optional().or(z.literal(""))
```

* Empty `TextInput` yields `""`, not `undefined`.
* Either accept `""` with `.or(z.literal(""))` or transform to `undefined`.

How do I show errors only after the user submits once?

```tsx
const { isSubmitted } = formState;
{ (isTouched || isSubmitted) && error && <Text>{error.message}</Text> }
```

* Combine `isTouched` and `isSubmitted` for a forgiving first edit, strict after submit attempt.
* `mode: "onTouched"` still validates early fields before the first submit - adjust `mode` if needed.

How do I handle numeric TextInput fields?

```ts
quantity: z.coerce.number().positive("Enter a positive number")
```

* `keyboardType="number-pad"` does not change the JS type - value is still a string until coercion.
* Empty string coerces to `NaN` - add `.min(1)` on a string step or custom error map for clearer copy.

Can I reuse the same schema for forms and API responses?

* Yes - parse API JSON with `UserSchema.parse(json)` and validate forms with `zodResolver(UserSchema)`.
* Use `.pick()` for edit forms that submit a subset of fields.
* See [Typing API Responses & Zod](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/typescript-rn/typing-api-responses-and-zod/) for fetch-boundary patterns.

How do I attach a refine error to a specific field?

```ts
.refine((data) => data.startDate <= data.endDate, {
  message: "End date must be after start date",
  path: ["endDate"],
})
```

* Without `path`, the error lands on the form root - invisible next to inputs.
* Multiple refines can target different `path` values.

How do I map server validation errors to fields?

```tsx
setError("email", { type: "server", message: "Email already registered" });
setFocus("email");
```

* Loop `fieldErrors` from the API response.
* Use `type: "server"` so client-side rules can coexist.

Should I use z.input or z.infer for useForm generics?

* Use `z.infer` (output type) when the schema uses `.coerce`, `.default`, or `.transform`.
* Use `z.input` when the form holds pre-transform shapes (rare on mobile).
* When unsure, `z.infer` matches what `onSubmit` receives after validation.

How do I validate a dynamic list of fields?

```ts
const InviteSchema = z.object({
  emails: z.array(z.string().email("Invalid email")).min(1, "Add at least one invite"),
});
```

* Pair with `useFieldArray` from react-hook-form.
* Zod reports array-index paths like `emails.2` - map them to the correct row in UI.

Can I localize Zod error messages?

* Pass custom strings to every constraint: `.min(8, t("password.min"))`.
* Or use `z.setErrorMap()` globally for shared message templates.
* Keep message strings in your i18n layer - Zod only stores the final string RHF displays.

What validation mode pairs best with Zod on mobile?

* `mode: "onTouched"` + `reValidateMode: "onChange"` is the usual combination.
* First blur runs Zod; subsequent edits re-validate as the user fixes mistakes.
* Avoid `onChange` for long free-text fields - it fights autocorrect and multiline typing.

How is form Zod different from API Zod?

* Form schemas accept `TextInput` strings and coerce before compare.
* API schemas validate JSON shapes from the wire - numbers may already be numbers.
* Share a core object definition, then `.extend()` or wrap with form-specific coercion at the edge.

> **Stack versions:** This page was written for **React 19.2.3**, **React Native 0.86.0**, and **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4).

Dokumen: Git & GitHub Best Practices
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/git/best-practices/

# Git & GitHub Best Practices

A condensed summary of the **25 most important Git and GitHub practices** for Expo SDK 57 mobile teams - drawn from every page in this section.

Highlights / Git & GitHub Best Practices

* main stays shippable - feature branches are days, not months
* release/\* freezes during store review; hotfix/\* branches from tags, not main
* Production OTA publishes from hotfix lanes - not unvetted main tip
* git worktree for SDK spikes; interactive rebase only on private feat/\* branches
* PR templates require device evidence - iOS and Android with build\_id
* Same npm scripts locally, in hooks, and in GitHub Actions - one command surface

1. **`main` is always integration truth:** Every merged PR must pass CI; never leave `main` broken overnight - store and OTA pipelines assume a green tip ([Git Basics for Mobile Teams](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/git/git-basics-for-mobile-teams/)).
2. **Commit the lockfile:** `package-lock.json` (or `pnpm-lock.yaml`) is required for reproducible `npm ci` in [Mobile CI/CD Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/mobile-ci-cd-basics/) - never gitignore it.
3. **Ticket IDs in every commit:** `feat(checkout): summary sheet [SHIP-412]` - cherry-picks to `release/*` and `hotfix/*` depend on traceable messages.
4. **Squash merge features to `main`:** One ticket, one commit on integration branch - simplifies cherry-pick to release and hotfix lanes.
5. **Short-lived feature branches:** Target 1–3 days; rebase or merge `main` daily to avoid `app.json`, native folder, and `eas.json` conflicts.
6. **Cut `release/X.Y` before freeze:** Release branch holds the store candidate; new features land on `main` only until the train ships ([Release Train Calendar](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/release-train-calendar/)).
7. **Code freeze is a Git policy:** During App Review, `release/*` accepts bugfixes only - enforce with branch protection, not Slack reminders.
8. **Cherry-pick - never merge `main` into `release/*`:** Merging pulls un-QA'd features into the store candidate; pick explicit SHAs listed in the release ticket.
9. **Tag from `release/*` after QA sign-off:** `v2.6.0` triggers EAS release CI; tag message includes `build_id` QA tested ([Automated Store Promotion](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/automated-store-promotion/)).
10. **Merge `release/*` back to `main` after rollout:** Fast-forward or merge commit preserves train boundary; delete the release branch when 100% rollout completes.
11. **Hotfix branches from tags:** `git checkout -b hotfix/2.4.2 v2.4.1` - not from `main` or `release/2.5.0` - guarantees correct `runtimeVersion` and native baseline ([GitHub Flow & Release Branches](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/git/github-flow-and-release-branches/)).
12. **Parallel hotfix lanes per live minor:** When 2.4.x and 2.5.0 RC coexist, separate `hotfix/2.4.*` and `release/2.5.0` - one open hotfix per minor at a time.
13. **Backport every hotfix:** Cherry-pick fix SHA to `main` (if not already there) and to open `release/*` - production OTA alone does not protect the next store binary.
14. **Map Git branches to OTA channels:** Production channel publishes from `hotfix/*` or documented production branch - never from `feat/*` ([Release Channels & Branches](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/release-channels-and-branches/)).
15. **Never force-push `main`, `release/*`, or `hotfix/*`:** Rewriting shared history breaks audit trails, tags, and OTA bundle lineage.
16. **SDK upgrades on `spike/*` + worktrees:** `git worktree add` keeps `main` open for features while `expo upgrade` runs in isolation ([Interactive Rebase & Worktrees](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/git/interactive-rebase-and-worktrees/)).
17. **Interactive rebase on private branches only:** Squash WIP before PR with `git rebase -i origin/main`; use `--force-with-lease`, never `--force` on shared branches.
18. **Separate Metro ports per worktree:** `EXPO_PACKAGER_PORT=8082` in spike worktree - avoids packager collisions with daily feature work.
19. **Pre-commit hooks mirror CI:** Husky runs `format:check`, `lint`, `typecheck` - same scripts as `pr-checks.yml` ([GitHub Actions Integration](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/git/github-actions-integration/)).
20. **PR template requires device evidence:** iOS and Android rows with `PASS`, test paths, and EAS `build_id` or install link - not "tested locally" placeholders.
21. **Auto-label UI and native paths:** `needs-device-qa` on `src/**`, `ios/**`, `android/**` changes; `skip-device-qa` for docs-only PRs.
22. **Branch protection requires `quality` + `evidence`:** GitHub Actions gates merge - policy beats honor system; pair with [Preview Builds on PRs](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/preview-builds-on-prs/) for QR installs.
23. **Never commit signing secrets:** No `.p8`, `.jks`, or `.env` with API keys - EAS credentials and [EAS environment variables](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-platform/environments-and-eas-environment-variables/) only.
24. **Review native diffs on SDK bumps:** `git diff main -- ios/ android/ app.json eas.json` before merge; run `npx expo-doctor` in CI on spike PRs.
25. **Document rollback in PR and tag messages:** OTA channel, feature flag, or hotfix branch plan - ties Git history to [Rollback Runbook](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/rollback-runbook/) and on-call actions.

## FAQs

GitFlow develop branch or trunk + release?

Prefer **trunk (`main`) + short `release/*` + `hotfix/*`**. Long-lived `develop` diverges from store binaries and OTA channels on mobile teams.

Minimum Git setup for a solo developer?

`main` + feature branches + squash merge + Husky hooks + tag-driven `eas build`. Add release branches and PR evidence when QA or a second engineer joins.

Merge commit or rebase onto main before PR?

**Squash merge** at PR time is enough for most teams. Rebase onto `main` before review if you want linear history; avoid rebasing after review starts.

How do Git practices connect to CI/CD?

Tags trigger release pipelines; PRs trigger quality gates; branch protection connects both. Git choices define what CI builds - see [CI/CD Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/best-practices/).

Biggest Git mistake on mobile teams?

Publishing production OTA from `main` while two store versions with different `runtimeVersion` values are live - use hotfix lanes mapped to channels.

## Related

* [Git Basics for Mobile Teams](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/git/git-basics-for-mobile-teams/) - freeze windows, cherry-picks, repo hygiene
* [GitHub Flow & Release Branches](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/git/github-flow-and-release-branches/) - hotfix parallel to OTA channels
* [Interactive Rebase & Worktrees](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/git/interactive-rebase-and-worktrees/) - SDK spikes without stashing
* [GitHub Actions Integration](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/git/github-actions-integration/) - PR templates and evidence workflows
* [Mobile CI/CD Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/mobile-ci-cd-basics/) - what runs on each Git event
* [GitHub Actions + EAS](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/github-actions-plus-eas/) - secrets and release triggers
* [Release Train Calendar](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/release-train-calendar/) - shared freeze calendar
* [Testing Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/best-practices/) - device vs unit test boundaries

> **Stack versions:** This page was written for **React 19.2.3**, **React Native 0.86.0**, and **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4).

Dokumen: Git Basics for Mobile Teams
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/git/git-basics-for-mobile-teams/

# Git Basics for Mobile Teams

A cookbook for a **branching model that respects store release freezes** - trunk-based integration on `main`, short-lived feature branches, and release lanes that do not collide with App Store or Play review windows.

Highlights / Git Basics for Mobile Teams

* main is always shippable - release branches cut from tags, not long-lived forks
* Code freeze windows block feature merges into release/\* during store review
* Separate lanes for store binaries (tags) and OTA bundles (channel branches)
* Lockfiles and native folders committed - never gitignore package-lock.json
* Conventional commits with ticket IDs make cherry-picks and hotfixes traceable
* Pre-commit hooks run lint and typecheck - same scripts CI will call

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
# Daily feature work
git checkout main && git pull --ff-only
git checkout -b feat/SHIP-412-checkout-summary
# ... commits ...
git push -u origin feat/SHIP-412-checkout-summary
# Open PR → squash merge to main after review + CI green
```

```bash
# Release cut (Tuesday - before Thursday freeze)
git checkout main && git pull --ff-only
git checkout -b release/2.6.0
git push -u origin release/2.6.0
# Only bugfixes cherry-picked or PRs targeting release/2.6.0 until tag
```

```bash
# Tag after QA sign-off (post-review)
git checkout release/2.6.0
git tag -a v2.6.0 -m "Release 2.6.0 - build_id abc123"
git push origin v2.6.0
```

```text
Branch lanes (mobile)
  main              ← integration; always green CI
  feat/*            ← days, squash merge
  release/X.Y       ← weeks; freeze during store review
  hotfix/X.Y.Z      ← hours; from tag, cherry-pick to main
  ota/production    ← optional long-lived for channel-only JS (see GitHub Flow page)
```

**When to reach for this:**

* First mobile team adopting Git after ad-hoc laptop builds.
* Store submission windows where merging features mid-review risks rejection.
* Coordinating OTA JavaScript updates with tagged store binaries.
* Onboarding engineers who know web Git but not native artifact discipline.

**When to avoid:**

* Solo side project with no QA or store cadence - `main` + tags may be enough.
* GitFlow with `develop` lasting months - mobile store review punishes drift.

## Working Example

End-to-end **feature → release → freeze → tag** for an Expo SDK 57 app shipping through EAS.

**Step 1 - Bootstrap repo hygiene**

```bash
npx create-expo-app@latest ShipApp --template blank-typescript
cd ShipApp
git init
```

```gitignore
# .gitignore - mobile essentials (do NOT ignore lockfile)
node_modules/
.expo/
dist/
*.jks
*.p8
*.p12
*.mobileprovision
ios/Pods/
android/.gradle/
android/app/build/
```

```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "lint": "expo lint",
    "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit",
    "test": "jest",
    "format:check": "prettier --check .",
    "prepare": "husky"
  }
}
```

```bash
# .husky/pre-commit
npm run format:check && npm run lint && npm run typecheck
```

* Commit `package-lock.json` - CI uses `npm ci` ([Mobile CI/CD Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/mobile-ci-cd-basics/))
* Never commit signing keys - EAS stores credentials ([GitHub Actions + EAS](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/github-actions-plus-eas/))

**Step 2 - Feature branch with ticket-scoped commits**

```bash
git checkout main && git pull --ff-only
git checkout -b feat/SHIP-412-checkout-summary
 
git add src/screens/CheckoutSummary.tsx
git commit -m "feat(checkout): add order summary sheet [SHIP-412]"
 
git push -u origin feat/SHIP-412-checkout-summary
```

PR targets `main`. Squash merge preserves one commit per feature - easier cherry-picks to `release/*` later.

**Step 3 - Cut release branch before freeze**

```markdown
<!-- docs/release-calendar.md (excerpt) -->
| Week | Event                          | Git rule                          |
|------|--------------------------------|-----------------------------------|
| W12  | Cut release/2.6.0 Tue 10:00    | New features → main only          |
| W12  | Code freeze Thu 18:00 UTC      | release/2.6.0: bugfixes only      |
| W12  | Submit Fri after Maestro       | Tag v2.6.0 from release branch    |
| W13  | Store review in flight         | No native changes on release/2.6.0|
```

```bash
git checkout main && git pull --ff-only
git checkout -b release/2.6.0
git push -u origin release/2.6.0
```

Branch protection on `release/2.6.0`:

* Require PR reviews
* Require status checks (`quality` from [GitHub Actions Integration](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/git/github-actions-integration/))
* Block direct pushes except release managers

**Step 4 - Cherry-pick a bugfix during freeze**

A critical fix lands on `main` after the cut. Cherry-pick - do not merge all of `main`.

```bash
git checkout release/2.6.0 && git pull --ff-only
git cherry-pick <sha-from-main>
git push origin release/2.6.0
```

```bash
# Verify the cherry-pick is the only diff vs tag candidate
git log --oneline main..release/2.6.0
git diff main...release/2.6.0 --stat
```

**Step 5 - Tag triggers release pipeline**

```bash
git checkout release/2.6.0
git tag -a v2.6.0 -m "Release 2.6.0 - QA build_id abc123"
git push origin v2.6.0
```

Tag `v*` triggers `eas build` in CI - same artifact QA tested ([Automated Store Promotion](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/automated-store-promotion/)).

**Step 6 - Merge release back to main**

After store approval and staged rollout:

```bash
git checkout main && git pull --ff-only
git merge --ff-only release/2.6.0
git push origin main
git branch -d release/2.6.0
git push origin --delete release/2.6.0
```

## Mobile-Specific Git Rules

| Rule | Web habit | Mobile reality |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lockfile | Sometimes ignored | **Always commit** - reproducible native builds |
| `ios/` / `android/` | N/A | Commit after `prebuild`; review native diffs on SDK bumps |
| Long `develop` branch | Common | **Avoid** - OTA and store binaries diverge from `main` |
| Merge Friday 5 p.m. | Acceptable | **Risky** - no on-call for broken store binary |
| Force-push `main` | Rare disaster | **Never** - breaks release tags and OTA audit trail |

```bash
# Inspect what changed in native folders before merging SDK bump
git diff main -- ios/ android/ app.json eas.json
npx expo-doctor
```

## Gotchas

* **Merging `main` into `release/*` during review** - Pulls in un-QA'd features; store rejection risk. **Fix:** Cherry-pick only listed SHAs.
* **Feature branch from stale `main`** - Rebase before PR; outdated `runtimeVersion` conflicts surface late. **Fix:** `git fetch && git rebase origin/main` weekly.
* **`.env` committed "just for CI"** - Secrets in Git forever. **Fix:** EAS environment variables ([Environments and EAS Environment Variables](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-platform/environments-and-eas-environment-variables/)).
* **Binary assets in Git without LFS** - Repo bloat slows CI checkout. **Fix:** `git lfs track "*.psd"` or host in CDN.
* **Squash merge loses cherry-pick metadata** - Ticket ID in commit body still required for release picks.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Trunk-only (`main` + tags) | Solo dev, weekly store releases | Parallel QA on next version during review |
| GitFlow `develop` | Legacy enterprise mandate | Greenfield mobile - prefer release branches |
| Monorepo `apps/mobile` | Shared packages | Without path filters in CI - burns minutes |
| Fork-based OSS workflow | External contributors | Internal team - branch on same repo |

## FAQs

How long should feature branches live?

Target **1–3 days**. Longer branches conflict with `app.json` version bumps, native folder changes, and EAS profile edits. Rebase or merge `main` daily.

What merges are allowed during code freeze?

Bugfixes with QA evidence, copy tweaks that do not change native code, and security patches. No new screens, permissions, or Expo modules - those need a new store binary and reset review clock.

Should OTA updates come from main or release branches?

**JS-only hotfixes** on the same `runtimeVersion` can publish from `main` to the production channel after soak. **Store-bound code** must match the tagged `release/*` commit QA signed off on. See [Release Channels & Branches](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/release-channels-and-branches/).

Merge commit or squash merge?

**Squash** for `feat/*` → `main` - one ticket, one commit. **Merge commit** optional for `release/*` → `main` if you want to preserve release boundary. Never squash a release branch without team agreement - loses cherry-pick SHAs.

How do I handle SDK upgrade branches?

Use a dedicated long-lived spike branch or [git worktrees](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/git/interactive-rebase-and-worktrees/) - do not block `main` for two weeks while `expo upgrade` runs.

## Related

* [GitHub Flow & Release Branches](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/git/github-flow-and-release-branches/) - hotfix lanes parallel to OTA channels
* [Interactive Rebase & Worktrees](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/git/interactive-rebase-and-worktrees/) - parallel SDK spikes without stashing
* [GitHub Actions Integration](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/git/github-actions-integration/) - PR templates and required checks
* [Release Train Calendar](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/release-train-calendar/) - freeze windows on a shared calendar
* [Mobile CI/CD Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/mobile-ci-cd-basics/) - what CI runs on each branch
* [Release Channels & Branches](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/release-channels-and-branches/) - Git branch vs EAS Update branch
* [Git & GitHub Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/git/best-practices/) - 25-item summary

Dokumen: GitHub Actions Integration
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/git/github-actions-integration/

# GitHub Actions Integration

A cookbook for **GitHub Actions + PR templates** that require **device test evidence** - so "tested on simulator" does not merge native navigation changes without a real iPhone and Android QA path.

Highlights / GitHub Actions Integration

* PR template checkboxes force device OS, build\_id, and test path evidence
* GitHub Actions validates template sections - empty placeholders fail the check
* Branch protection requires quality + pr-evidence before merge
* Device matrix table in PR body - iOS and Android both required for UI changes
* Links EAS preview QR and Maestro recording attach to the PR thread
* Same npm scripts in Actions as local - no CI-only test commands

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```markdown
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->
## Summary
<!-- What changed and why -->
 
## Ticket
<!-- SHIP-___ -->
 
## Device test evidence (required for UI / native / navigation)
| Platform | Device / OS        | Build source     | Result |
|----------|--------------------|------------------|--------|
| iOS      | e.g. iPhone 14 / 17| EAS preview QR   | PASS   |
| Android  | e.g. Pixel 7 / 14  | EAS preview QR   | PASS   |
 
## Test paths exercised
- [ ] Cold start / login
- [ ] Changed screen(s): ___
- [ ] Deep link / push (if applicable)
 
## Screenshots / recordings
<!-- Drag Maestro cloud link, screen recording, or screenshot -->
 
## CI
- [ ] `quality` check green
- [ ] Preview build ID noted: ___
```

```yaml
# .github/workflows/pr-evidence.yml
name: PR Evidence
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, edited, synchronize, reopened]
 
jobs:
  evidence:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Validate PR template
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const body = context.payload.pull_request.body ?? '';
            const needsDevice = /native|navigation|gesture|camera|ui/i.test(body)
              || context.payload.pull_request.labels.some(l => l.name === 'needs-device-qa');
            if (!needsDevice) {
              core.info('No device-heavy paths detected - evidence check skipped');
              return;
            }
            const required = ['Device test evidence', 'Test paths exercised', 'iOS', 'Android', 'PASS'];
            const missing = required.filter(r => !body.includes(r));
            if (missing.length) {
              core.setFailed(`PR body missing: ${missing.join(', ')}`);
            }
```

```yaml
# .github/workflows/pr-checks.yml (excerpt - pair with evidence)
name: PR Checks
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
jobs:
  quality:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: 20, cache: npm }
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx expo customize tsconfig.json
      - run: npm run format:check && npm run lint && npm run typecheck
      - run: npm run test -- --ci
```

**When to reach for this:**

* UI regressions slipped through because PRs only listed "Jest green."
* [Preview builds on PRs](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/preview-builds-on-prs/) exist but nobody records which `build_id` they tested.
* Maestro or Detox runs locally but evidence is not attached to the PR.
* Branch protection needs a **second gate** beyond lint and TypeScript.

**When to avoid:**

* Docs-only PRs - label `skip-device-qa` or path-filter workflows.
* Automated Maestro on every preview build already posts results - template can be lighter.

## Working Example

**Step 1 - Add PR template and labels**

```bash
mkdir -p .github
```

```markdown
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->
## Summary
 
## Ticket
SHIP-
 
## Change type
- [ ] JS / copy only (OTA-safe)
- [ ] UI layout / styling
- [ ] Navigation / gestures
- [ ] Native module / config plugin
- [ ] SDK upgrade
 
## Device test evidence
> Required when any box above except "JS / copy only" is checked.
 
| Platform | Device / OS | Build (`build_id` or preview link) | Result |
|----------|-------------|-----------------------------------|--------|
| iOS      |             |                                   | PASS / FAIL |
| Android  |             |                                   | PASS / FAIL |
 
## Test paths exercised
- [ ] Cold start
- [ ] Auth / session restore
- [ ] Feature under change: ___
 
## Automation
- [ ] Maestro flow: `flows/smoke.yaml` (link or CI artifact)
- [ ] Screenshot / screen recording attached
 
## Rollback notes (if production-impacting)
<!-- OTA channel, feature flag, or hotfix branch plan -->
```

```bash
# Create GitHub labels (gh CLI)
gh label create "needs-device-qa" --color B60205 --description "Requires device evidence in PR"
gh label create "skip-device-qa" --color C5DEF5 --description "Docs or CI-only - no device matrix"
```

**Step 2 - Path-based auto-label**

```yaml
# .github/workflows/pr-labeler.yml
name: PR Labeler
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize]
 
jobs:
  label:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/labeler@v5
        with:
          repo-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
```

```yaml
# .github/labeler.yml
needs-device-qa:
  - changed-files:
      - any-glob-to-any-file:
          - 'app/**'
          - 'src/**/*.tsx'
          - 'ios/**'
          - 'android/**'
          - 'app.json'
          - 'eas.json'
```

**Step 3 - Evidence validation workflow**

```yaml
# .github/workflows/pr-evidence.yml
name: PR Evidence
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, edited, synchronize, reopened]
 
permissions:
  pull-requests: read
 
jobs:
  evidence:
    if: >-
      !contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'skip-device-qa')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const pr = context.payload.pull_request;
            const body = pr.body ?? '';
            const title = pr.title ?? '';
 
            const uiPaths = /(src\/|app\/|\.tsx|navigation|gesture|native|plugin)/i;
            const needsEvidence =
              pr.labels.some(l => l.name === 'needs-device-qa') ||
              uiPaths.test(body) ||
              uiPaths.test(title);
 
            if (!needsEvidence) {
              core.info('Skipping device evidence - JS/docs-only change');
              return;
            }
 
            const fail = (msg) => core.setFailed(msg);
 
            if (!/\| iOS \|.*\|.*\|.*PASS/i.test(body.replace(/\n/g, ' '))) {
              fail('iOS row with PASS missing in device table');
            }
            if (!/\| Android \|.*\|.*\|.*PASS/i.test(body.replace(/\n/g, ' '))) {
              fail('Android row with PASS missing in device table');
            }
            if (!body.includes('Test paths exercised')) {
              fail('Test paths exercised section missing');
            }
            const buildRef = /build_id|eas\.dev|expo\.dev\/accounts/i;
            if (!buildRef.test(body)) {
              fail('No EAS preview build_id or install link in PR body');
            }
```

**Step 4 - Branch protection**

```text
GitHub → Settings → Branches → main:
  Require status checks:
    - quality          (pr-checks.yml)
    - evidence         (pr-evidence.yml)
  Require pull request reviews: 1
```

Document in `CONTRIBUTING.md` - reviewers reject PRs with placeholder `e.g. iPhone` text.

**Step 5 - Contributor workflow with preview build**

```bash
# Author adds label after opening PR (or labeler adds automatically)
gh pr create --fill
gh pr edit --add-label needs-device-qa
```

Request preview from [Preview Builds on PRs](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/preview-builds-on-prs/):

```bash
gh pr edit 42 --add-label needs-preview
# CI posts QR - author installs on physical devices
```

```bash
# Run Maestro locally against preview binary
maestro test flows/checkout-smoke.yaml
# Attach recording; paste build_id into PR table
```

Example filled PR table:

```markdown
| Platform | Device / OS        | Build source                          | Result |
|----------|----------------------|---------------------------------------|--------|
| iOS      | iPhone 14 / iOS 17.4 | build_id 8f3a2c (PR #42 preview)      | PASS   |
| Android  | Pixel 7 / API 34     | build_id 8f3a2c (PR #42 preview)      | PASS   |
```

**Step 6 - Optional Maestro upload on preview success**

```yaml
# .github/workflows/preview-maestro.yml (excerpt)
- name: Maestro smoke on preview artifact
  if: success()
  run: |
    maestro test flows/smoke.yaml --format junit --output maestro.xml
- uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
  with:
    name: maestro-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
    path: maestro.xml
```

Link artifact in PR - satisfies "Automation" checkbox.

## Integration with EAS and CI/CD

| Check | Workflow | Blocks merge |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lint / tsc / Jest | `pr-checks.yml` | Yes |
| Template evidence | `pr-evidence.yml` | Yes (UI paths) |
| Preview build | `preview-build.yml` | No - informs evidence |
| Maestro on EAS | EAS Workflow | Release only |

```bash
# Robot token for preview workflows - never personal account
# GitHub Secret: EXPO_TOKEN (see GitHub Actions + EAS)
```

Hybrid pattern: GitHub Actions for PR gates; [EAS Workflows](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/eas-workflows/) for tag release chains.

## Gotchas

* **Regex too strict on table formatting** - Minor markdown spacing fails check. **Fix:** Loosen regex or use a small validation script with clear error messages.
* **Evidence workflow on draft PRs** - Authors cannot fill template yet. **Fix:** `if: github.event.pull_request.draft == false`.
* **Simulator-only "PASS"** - Misses Android manufacturer skins and iOS safe areas. **Fix:** Policy: physical device for `needs-device-qa`.
* **Stale preview build\_id** - Author rebased but table references old binary. **Fix:** Re-run preview on `synchronize`; CI comment with latest `build_id`.
* **Skipping evidence with empty summary** - Label `skip-device-qa` misuse. **Fix:** CODEOWNERS review for label removal.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Honor-system template | Tiny team, high trust | Store submissions failing QA |
| Required Maestro in EAS only | Budget for cloud devices | Need fast PR feedback |
| Manual QA sign-off in Jira | Regulated industries | No link between ticket and PR |
| Danger JS PR linter | Complex custom rules | Team prefers YAML-only |

## FAQs

Should docs-only PRs run evidence check?

No. Use `skip-device-qa` label or path filters excluding `docs/**` and `*.md`. Keep `quality` check for all PRs.

What if QA owns device testing, not the author?

Allow QA to edit PR body or comment with evidence table; `pull_request_target` on `edited` re-runs validation. Better: QA posts comment template author copies into body.

Is Expo Go enough for evidence?

Not for native modules, config plugins, or SDK upgrades. Record **EAS preview** or dev client `build_id` - [Maestro E2E](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/maestro-e2e/).

How does this relate to Jest in CI?

Jest proves logic; device evidence proves layout, gestures, and native bridges. Both required for UI PRs - [Mobile Testing Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/mobile-testing-basics/).

Can I use issue forms instead of markdown template?

Yes - GitHub Issue Forms support required fields. Convert the device table to required form inputs; Actions still validates PR body if contributors use `Closes #` linking.
