Dokumen: GitHub Flow & Release Branches
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/git/github-flow-and-release-branches/

# GitHub Flow & Release Branches

A cookbook for **GitHub Flow adapted to mobile** - continuous integration on `main`, **release branches** for store trains, and **hotfix branches parallel to OTA channels** so production JavaScript and live store binaries stay aligned.

Highlights / GitHub Flow & Release Branches

* GitHub Flow on main - open PR, review, merge, deploy from tip or tag
* release/\* branches hold store candidates; hotfix/\* branches patch live versions
* OTA channels map to Git branches - production OTA never from unmerged feat/\*
* Hotfix cherry-picks flow release → main → optional OTA publish
* Parallel hotfix lanes when 2.4 and 2.5 are both in market
* Branch protection enforces freeze rules - not Slack honor system

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```text
GitHub Flow (mobile adaptation)
  1. Branch from main     → feat/SHIP-220-dark-mode
  2. Open PR              → CI + device evidence required
  3. Merge to main        → squash preferred
  4. Deploy               → OTA to preview channel OR tag for store build
```

```bash
# Hotfix for live store version 2.4.x (parallel to 2.5 RC on release/2.5.0)
git fetch --tags
git checkout -b hotfix/2.4.2 v2.4.1
git cherry-pick <fix-sha>
git tag -a v2.4.2 -m "Hotfix: crash on cold start [SHIP-991]"
git push origin hotfix/2.4.2 v2.4.2
```

```bash
# JS-only hotfix on same runtimeVersion - OTA from hotfix branch
git checkout hotfix/2.4.2
eas update --branch production --channel production --environment production \
  --message "hotfix: cold start crash [SHIP-991]"
```

```text
Parallel lanes example
  main              ← integration
  release/2.5.0     ← RC in TestFlight review
  hotfix/2.4.2      ← production store 2.4.x users
  (OTA production channel ← hotfix/2.4.2 commits only)
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Users on **two store versions** simultaneously (staged rollout lag).
* **OTA production channel** must not receive commits meant for next store release.
* Team outgrows "tag everything from `main`" but does not want GitFlow `develop`.
* Hotfix needed while `release/2.5.0` is frozen in App Review.

**When to avoid:**

* Single version in market, OTA disabled - simpler trunk + tags may suffice.
* Hotfix requires new native module - must be store build, not OTA-only lane.

## Working Example

**Scenario:** `v2.4.1` is live in production (50% Play rollout). `release/2.5.0` waits in App Review. A cold-start crash affects 2.4.x users only.

**Step 1 - Map Git branches to EAS channels**

```markdown
<!-- docs/branch-channel-map.md -->
| Git branch       | Store version | EAS Update branch | EAS channel  |
|------------------|---------------|-------------------|--------------|
| main             | (next)        | preview           | preview      |
| release/2.5.0    | 2.5.0 RC      | staging           | staging      |
| hotfix/2.4.2     | 2.4.2 live    | production        | production   |
```

```bash
eas channel:view production
# Confirm channel points at production branch - not main
```

See [Release Channels & Branches](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/release-channels-and-branches/) for channel semantics.

**Step 2 - Land fix on main first (integration truth)**

```bash
git checkout main && git pull --ff-only
git checkout -b fix/SHIP-991-cold-start
# ... fix ...
git commit -m "fix(app): guard null session on cold start [SHIP-991]"
git push -u origin fix/SHIP-991-cold-start
# PR → squash merge to main
```

**Step 3 - Open hotfix branch from live tag**

```bash
git fetch --tags
git checkout -b hotfix/2.4.2 v2.4.1
git cherry-pick <squashed-sha-from-main>
npm run typecheck && npm run test -- --ci
git push -u origin hotfix/2.4.2
```

* Branch from **tag** `v2.4.1`, not from `main` - guarantees same `runtimeVersion` and native code
* Cherry-pick one commit - not `git merge main`

**Step 4 - Store submit for native hotfix (if required)**

```bash
# Bump app version on hotfix branch only
# app.json → version 2.4.2, ios.buildNumber++, android.versionCode++
 
git commit -am "chore(release): bump to 2.4.2 [SHIP-991]"
git tag -a v2.4.2 -m "Hotfix 2.4.2 - build_id xyz789"
git push origin hotfix/2.4.2 v2.4.2
```

Tag triggers [EAS release workflow](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/github-actions-plus-eas/) - expedited profile, same `build_id` QA tested.

**Step 5 - OTA parallel lane (JS-only path)**

If the fix is JavaScript-only and `runtimeVersion` matches `v2.4.1`:

```bash
git checkout hotfix/2.4.2
eas update --branch production --channel production --environment production \
  --message "hotfix: cold start [SHIP-991]"
```

```bash
# Verify production channel head matches hotfix tip
git rev-parse hotfix/2.4.2
eas update:list --branch production --limit 1
```

**Step 6 - Backport to main and release/2.5.0**

```bash
# main already has fix from step 2
git checkout release/2.5.0 && git pull --ff-only
git cherry-pick <same-sha>
git push origin release/2.5.0
```

2.5.0 users get the fix when the store binary ships - not from production OTA channel.

## GitHub Flow vs Release Branch - Decision Table

| Situation | Flow | Branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New feature | GitHub Flow | `feat/*` → `main` |
| Weekly store train | Release branch | `release/X.Y.0` from `main` |
| Live crash on old version | Hotfix lane | `hotfix/X.Y.Z` from tag |
| JS typo on production | OTA | `hotfix/*` or `main` if same runtime |
| SDK bump | Spike | `spike/sdk-57` or worktree |

```bash
# List branches still receiving OTA
git branch -r | grep -E 'hotfix|release'
eas channel:list
```

## Branch Protection Template

```yaml
# Document in CONTRIBUTING.md - enforce in GitHub Settings
main:
  required_checks: [quality, pr-template]
  required_reviews: 1
  allow_force_push: false
 
release/*:
  required_checks: [quality, maestro-smoke]
  required_reviews: 2
  restrict_push: [release-managers]
 
hotfix/*:
  required_checks: [quality]
  required_reviews: 2  # expedited but not solo
```

## Gotchas

* **OTA from `main` while 2.4 and 2.5 differ in native code** - 2.5 binary may load incompatible JS. **Fix:** Publish production OTA only from `hotfix/*` tied to live `runtimeVersion`.
* **Hotfix branch from `release/2.5.0` for 2.4 users** - Wrong native baseline. **Fix:** `git checkout -b hotfix/2.4.2 v2.4.1`.
* **Forgetting cherry-pick to `release/2.5.0`** - Fix ships to old users only; 2.5 regresses. **Fix:** Backport checklist in PR template.
* **Deleting hotfix branch before channel repoint** - Production channel orphaned. **Fix:** `eas channel:edit` only after new tag lane documented.
* **Parallel hotfixes same version** - Second branch from wrong tag. **Fix:** Sequential tags `v2.4.2`, `v2.4.3`; one open hotfix at a time per major.minor.

cGJxcnRodnFyZi52YnxwdHZiOTc0fDIwMjYwNw==

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Trunk + tag only | One version in market | Staged rollout leaves two versions live |
| GitFlow `develop` | Mandated by org | OTA channel mapping becomes unclear |
| Long-lived `production` Git branch | Strict OTA audit | Drifts from `main` without discipline |
| Fork hotfix per platform | iOS/Android ship different patches | Adds merge burden - prefer one hotfix |

## FAQs

Is GitHub Flow enough without release branches?

For small apps with continuous store submission - often yes. Add `release/*` when review windows, RC soak, or parallel versions demand a frozen candidate branch.

How many hotfix branches can be open?

One per **live store minor** (e.g. one `hotfix/2.4.x` lane). Multiple patches chain as `v2.4.2`, `v2.4.3`. A separate `hotfix/2.3.x` only if you still support that cohort.

Does hotfix merge to main or only cherry-pick?

Fix lands on `main` via normal PR first. Hotfix branch **cherry-picks** that SHA - never merge hotfix → main (brings version bump noise backward).

Who owns production OTA publishes?

CI on tag or release manager with `EXPO_TOKEN` - not feature developers from laptops. Matches [Release Train Calendar](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/release-train-calendar/) policy.

What if hotfix needs native code?

Store build from `hotfix/*`, new tag, expedited submit - OTA alone is insufficient. Bump `runtimeVersion` if native ABI changes ([Runtime Version Policy](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/runtime-version-policy/)).

* [Interactive Rebase & Worktrees](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/git/interactive-rebase-and-worktrees/) - clean history before hotfix cherry-pick
* [GitHub Actions Integration](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/git/github-actions-integration/) - PR checks on hotfix PRs
* [Release Channels & Branches](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/release-channels-and-branches/) - channel ↔ branch mapping
* [Rollback Runbook](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/rollback-runbook/) - revert bad OTA on production channel

Dokumen: Interactive Rebase & Worktrees
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/git/interactive-rebase-and-worktrees/

# Interactive Rebase & Worktrees

A cookbook for **parallel SDK upgrade spikes** using `git worktree` and **interactive rebase** - so `expo upgrade` does not freeze `main` and your stash list does not become archaeology.

Highlights / Interactive Rebase & Worktrees

* git worktree add runs two branches with separate node\_modules - no stash stack
* Interactive rebase squashes WIP commits before PR - reviewers see one logical change
* SDK upgrade spikes live on spike/\* branches without blocking main feature work
* Never rebase public release or hotfix branches - only feat/\* and spike/\*
* Each worktree gets its own Metro port - avoid packager collisions
* Cherry-pick finished upgrade commits back to main as one squash merge

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
# From primary clone - add SDK spike worktree (sibling directory)
cd ~/WEBDEV/ShipApp
git fetch origin
git worktree add ../ShipApp-sdk57-spike -b spike/sdk-57-upgrade origin/main
```

```bash
# Spike worktree - upgrade in isolation
cd ../ShipApp-sdk57-spike
npm ci
npx expo install expo@~57.0.4 --fix
npx expo-doctor
npm run typecheck && npm run test -- --ci
```

```bash
# Primary clone - keep shipping features on main
cd ~/WEBDEV/ShipApp
git checkout main
git checkout -b feat/SHIP-501-settings-redesign
# Metro on default 8081 - spike uses 8082 (see below)
```

```bash
# Before PR - squash fixup commits on feature branch
git checkout feat/SHIP-501-settings-redesign
git fetch origin && git rebase -i origin/main
# Mark WIP commits as squash/fixup; keep one feat commit
```

```bash
# After spike validated - remove worktree
cd ~/WEBDEV/ShipApp
git worktree remove ../ShipApp-sdk57-spike
```

**When to reach for this:**

* **Expo SDK upgrade** spanning days while features must merge to `main`.
* **Native prebuild diff** you need to compare side-by-side with production branch.
* **Long-running spike** (new navigation library) without blocking teammates' `npm ci`.
* **PR cleanup** - ten "fix lint" commits should be one commit before review.

**When to avoid:**

* Shared `release/*` or `hotfix/*` branches others have checked out - rebase rewrites history.
* Already-pushed branch others based work on - coordinate or merge instead of rebase.
* Disk-constrained laptop - two full `node_modules` trees cost gigabytes.

## Working Example

**Scenario:** ShipApp runs Expo SDK 56 in production. Team needs SDK 57 spike while `feat/*` branches land daily on `main`.

**Step 1 - Create spike worktree**

```bash
cd ~/WEBDEV/ShipApp
git pull --ff-only origin main
git worktree add ../ShipApp-sdk57-spike -b spike/sdk-57-upgrade origin/main
git worktree list
```

```text
/Users/csjcode/WEBDEV/ShipApp              abc1234 [main]
/Users/csjcode/WEBDEV/ShipApp-sdk57-spike  abc1234 [spike/sdk-57-upgrade]
```

Both directories share one `.git` object store - branches differ, disks separate.

**Step 2 - Isolate Metro ports**

```bash
# ../ShipApp-sdk57-spike/.env.local (gitignored)
EXPO_PACKAGER_PORT=8082
```

```bash
cd ../ShipApp-sdk57-spike
npm ci
npx expo start --port 8082
```

Primary clone keeps `npx expo start` on 8081 - no "port already in use" collisions.

**Step 3 - Run upgrade with checkpoint commits**

```bash
cd ../ShipApp-sdk57-spike
 
npx expo install expo@~57.0.4 --fix
git add package.json package-lock.json
git commit -m "chore(sdk): bump expo to SDK 57 [SPIKE-57]"
 
npx expo prebuild --clean
git add ios android
git commit -m "chore(native): prebuild after SDK 57 [SPIKE-57]"
 
npm run typecheck
# fix breaks...
git commit -am "fix(types): navigation params after RN 0.86 [SPIKE-57]"
```

WIP commits are fine **on spike branch** - interactive rebase before opening PR.

**Step 4 - Parallel feature work in primary clone**

```bash
cd ~/WEBDEV/ShipApp
git checkout -b feat/SHIP-501-settings-redesign
# unaffected by spike's package.json - separate node_modules
npm ci
npm run test -- --ci
git push -u origin feat/SHIP-501-settings-redesign
```

Teammates never pull half-upgraded SDK from `main`.

**Step 5 - Interactive rebase before PR**

Feature branch accumulated noise:

```bash
git checkout feat/SHIP-501-settings-redesign
git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD
```

```text
a1b2c3d fix typo
d4e5f6g fix lint
g7h8i9j feat(settings): redesign layout [SHIP-501]
j1k2l3m wip
```

```bash
git rebase -i origin/main
```

In the editor, reorder and mark:

```text
pick g7h8i9j feat(settings): redesign layout [SHIP-501]
squash j1k2l3m wip
squash d4e5f6g fix lint
squash a1b2c3d fix typo
```

```bash
git push --force-with-lease origin feat/SHIP-501-settings-redesign
```

* `--force-with-lease` - safer than `--force`; fails if remote advanced
* Only rewrite **your** feature branches - never `main`, `release/*`, `hotfix/*`

**Step 6 - Finish spike and land on main**

```bash
cd ../ShipApp-sdk57-spike
npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm run test -- --ci
npx expo-doctor
```

Squash spike commits for review:

```bash
git rebase -i origin/main
# squash all SPIKE-57 commits into one:
# chore(sdk): upgrade to Expo SDK 57 [SPIKE-57]
```

```bash
git push -u origin spike/sdk-57-upgrade
# Open PR → main; full device matrix + EAS preview build required
```

After merge:

```bash
cd ~/WEBDEV/ShipApp
git pull --ff-only origin main
git worktree remove ../ShipApp-sdk57-spike
git branch -d spike/sdk-57-upgrade   # if merged
```

Trigger [preview build on PR](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/preview-builds-on-prs/) for SDK PRs - Expo Go alone misses native changes.

## Rebase Safety Matrix

| Branch type | Interactive rebase? | Force push? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `feat/*` (solo) | Yes | `--force-with-lease` OK |
| `spike/*` | Yes | `--force-with-lease` OK |
| `main` | **No** | **Never** |
| `release/*` | **No** | Breaks RC audit |
| `hotfix/*` | **No** | Cherry-pick instead |
| Shared `feat/*` | Coordinate | Prefer merge |

```bash
# Abort a rebase gone wrong
git rebase --abort
 
# Recovery reflog
git reflog | head -20
git checkout -b recovery-branch HEAD@{3}
```

## Worktree Commands Reference

```bash
git worktree list
git worktree add ../path -b new-branch start-point
git worktree remove ../path
git worktree prune   # clean stale metadata
 
# Cannot remove worktree with uncommitted changes
git -C ../ShipApp-sdk57-spike status
```

```bash
# Optional: shared node_modules via pnpm (advanced)
# Prefer full npm ci per worktree for fidelity with CI
```

## Gotchas

* **One branch checked out in two worktrees** - Git forbids this. **Fix:** Different branch per worktree directory.
* **Rebasing after PR review started** - Invalidates review comments on old SHAs. **Fix:** Rebase before requesting review, or merge `main` instead.
* **Spike merges without `expo-doctor` in CI** - Hidden dependency skew. **Fix:** Add doctor step to [PR checks](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/mobile-ci-cd-basics/).
* **Forgotten worktree consumes disk** - `git worktree list` monthly. **Fix:** `git worktree remove` + `git worktree prune`.
* **Interactive rebase on merge commits** - Confusing conflicts. **Fix:** `git rebase -i --rebase-merges` or avoid merge commits on feature branches.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `git stash` | 30-minute context switch | Multi-day SDK spike |
| Second full clone | Simple mental model | Double fetch time and disk |
| Feature flags on main | Small SDK delta | Native folder overhaul |
| Draft PR from spike | Visibility without merge | Still blocks CI if targeting main early |

## FAQs

worktree vs second git clone?

Worktrees share object database - faster, less disk. Second clone is simpler but duplicates `.git` history. Prefer worktrees for same-repo parallel branches.

How many worktrees are practical?

Two or three (main + spike + hotfix investigation). More than that - disk and mental overhead exceed benefit.

Should spike branch merge or rebase onto main before PR?

`git merge origin/main` into spike before PR is safer for long spikes. Interactive rebase **onto** main produces linear history but costs conflict resolution time.

Can CI run on worktree branches?

Yes - worktrees push to same `origin`. Branch `spike/sdk-57-upgrade` triggers same GitHub Actions as any remote branch.

What commits belong in one squash?

One logical unit: one ticket or one SDK bump. Separate `feat` from `chore(sdk)` if reviewers need to bisect later.

## Related

* [Git Basics for Mobile Teams](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/git/git-basics-for-mobile-teams/) - when not to touch release branches
* [GitHub Flow & Release Branches](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/git/github-flow-and-release-branches/) - hotfix lanes avoid rebase
* [GitHub Actions Integration](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/git/github-actions-integration/) - SDK PR requires preview build evidence
* [Preview Builds on PRs](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/preview-builds-on-prs/) - native validation for SDK upgrades

Dokumen: Governance Best Practices
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/governance/best-practices/

# Governance Best Practices

A condensed summary of the **25 most important governance practices** for Expo SDK 57 mobile teams - drawn from every page in this section.

Highlights / Governance Best Practices

* Written standards + CI gates - docs without enforcement decay by month two
* N-1 SDK window and named upgrade champions - not whoever is free in crunch week
* EOL registry with owners and dates - deprecation without deadline is permanent
* Spikes are time-boxed with ADR outcomes - never merge spike code without flags and QA
* Supply-chain: lockfile, audit, SBOM per release tag - legal asks 'what shipped?' once
* Staff+ impact is durable policy adopted by squads you do not manage

1. **Publish standards in `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md`:** Naming, folders, and native touch rules live in git - not Slack pins that new hires never see ([Standards Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/governance/standards-basics/)).
2. **Feature barrels are merge blockers:** Import only from `@/features/<name>` - deep imports couple refactors; enforce with ESLint `no-restricted-imports` ([Coding Standards & Style Guides](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/governance/coding-standards-and-style-guides/)).
3. **Thin `app/`, fat `src/features/`:** Route files re-export screens; business logic never lives in Expo Router filenames - aligns with [Expo Project Rules Checklist](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/expo-project-rules-checklist/).
4. **Native touch rules have named owners:** `plugins/`, `app.config.ts`, and checked-in `ios/` / `android/` require platform CODEOWNERS - CNG teams regenerate, never hand-edit ([Native Module Rules](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/native-module-rules/)).
5. **One command surface for quality:** `format:check`, `lint`, `typecheck`, `test` - identical in Husky, laptop, and GitHub Actions ([CI Quality Gates](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/ci-quality-gates/)).
6. **Zero-warning ESLint on `main`:** `expo lint -- --max-warnings 0` in CI - warnings become ignored debt within one sprint ([Linting Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/linting-basics/)).
7. **Prettier and ESLint do not fight:** Pick Prettier for formatting and import order; disable overlapping ESLint stylistic rules ([Prettier & Import Sorting](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/prettier-and-import-sorting/)).
8. **PR template encodes human gates:** Device evidence, native diff attachments, and standards checkboxes - policy beats honor system ([Coding Standards & Style Guides](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/governance/coding-standards-and-style-guides/)).
9. **ADR for every intentional exception:** "Temporary" native edits or architecture violations without ADR become permanent - use [Architecture Decision Records](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/architecture-decision-records/).
10. **Commit lockfiles; CI uses `npm ci`:** Floating installs hide native/JS skew until TestFlight - never gitignore `package-lock.json` ([Dependency & Supply-Chain Governance](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/governance/dependency-and-supply-chain-governance/)).
11. **`npx expo install` for Expo packages:** Manual version pins cause doctor failures and production native crashes - [Expo Rules Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/best-practices/).
12. **npm audit fails on high/critical in CI:** Document accepted risk in `docs/security-exceptions.md` with expiry - exceptions without dates are not accepted ([Dependency & Supply-Chain Governance](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/governance/dependency-and-supply-chain-governance/)).
13. **SBOM per store release tag:** CycloneDX from lockfile archived with EAS `build_id` - enterprise audits ask what shipped in build `abc123`, not today's `main`.
14. **Native OSS licenses ship in-app:** iOS Settings bundle and Android OSS screen updated on every native bump - legal review on GPL-class additions.
15. **N-1 SDK support window only:** Production supports current SDK and one prior - three SDK generations in the wild breaks OTA and support ([SDK Upgrade Policy](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/governance/sdk-upgrade-policy/)).
16. **Named upgrade champion per SDK bump:** Accountable for branch, `expo-doctor`, preview matrix, and `runtimeVersion` ADR - not a volunteer in sprint 47 ([SDK Upgrade Skill](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/skills/sdk-upgrade-skill/)).
17. **SDK upgrades on dedicated branches + worktrees:** Never mix `expo upgrade` with feature work on `main` - hotfixes stay possible on parallel worktree ([Interactive Rebase & Worktrees](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/git/interactive-rebase-and-worktrees/)).
18. **`expo-doctor` and preview `eas build` are merge gates:** OTA cannot fix native skew from a bad SDK merge - full build matrix before production ([Release and OTA Rules](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/release-and-ota-rules/)).
19. **EOL registry with owners and deadlines:** RN architecture, Expo SDK, OS floors, and API deprecations in `docs/eol-registry.md` - reviewed quarterly ([Deprecation & EOL Tracking](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/governance/deprecation-and-end-of-life-tracking/)).
20. **OS floor bumps are product decisions:** ASC / Play analytics + ADR before raising `deploymentTarget` / `minSdkVersion` - engineering preference alone is insufficient.
21. **Spikes are time-boxed with ADR outcomes:** ADOPT, DEFER, or REJECT documented; spike branches deleted after demo - no Friday merge without flags and QA ([Spikes, PoCs & New Architecture](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/governance/spikes-pocs-and-new-architecture/)).
22. **Brownfield spikes use isolated artifacts:** `expo-brownfield` AAR/XCFramework - never copy-paste JS bundles into host assets ([Brownfield Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/brownfield/brownfield-basics/)).
23. **New Architecture validated on release-like builds:** Expo Go is not proof - EAS preview + device smoke before org-wide NA enablement on RN 0.86.
24. **Risk calendar aligns three clocks:** Store binary, OTA bundle, and backend API deprecation on one shared doc - mobile EOL must not lag API removal ([Release Train Calendar](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/release-train-calendar/)).
25. **Staff+ governance is measured by durability:** Policies, runbooks, and ADRs adopted by squads after you move on - not lines of code or heroic release weekends ([Career Growth: Senior → Lead → Staff](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/governance/career-growth-senior-lead-staff/)).

## FAQs

Minimum governance for a two-person mobile team?

`CONTRIBUTING.md`, lockfile + `npm ci`, `expo lint` + `tsc` in CI, PR template with device evidence, and one `docs/eol-registry.md` row per SDK. Add champions and SBOM when a third app or enterprise customer appears.

How do governance and expo-rules differ?

**Governance** is process (who, when, how decisions are recorded). **expo-rules** are technical non-negotiables (secrets, OTA, navigation). Both appear in PR review; violations of either can block merge.

Biggest governance failure on RN teams?

**Undocumented SDK drift** - multiple `runtimeVersion` families in production with no EOL calendar, leading to OTA bricks and security patches that never reach the oldest app.

Who maintains governance docs?

**Staff / platform lead authors**; **Lead enforces** in review; **EM sponsors** calendar time. Everyone proposes ADR updates when reality diverges from policy.

Dokumen: Coding Standards & Style Guides
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/governance/coding-standards-and-style-guides/

# Coding Standards & Style Guides

A cookbook for **RN/Expo style guide enforcement** - ESLint, Prettier, TypeScript, PR review, and CODEOWNERS wired so standards survive turnover without a style sheriff in every thread.

Highlights / Coding Standards & Style Guides

* One command surface: format:check, lint, typecheck, test - local, hooks, and CI call the same scripts
* eslint-config-expo/flat + Prettier + tsc --noEmit - three gates, three failure classes
* PR template checkboxes beat Slack reminders - standards without enforcement decay in month two
* Custom ESLint rules encode RN-specific bans: deep feature imports, inline styles on hot paths
* CODEOWNERS on app.config.ts, plugins/, eas.json - style guide extends to config files
* Zero-warning ESLint policy requires CI --max-warnings 0 - warnings become errors on main

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```json
// package.json - the four scripts every gate calls
{
  "scripts": {
    "lint": "expo lint",
    "lint:ci": "expo lint -- --max-warnings 0",
    "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit",
    "format:check": "prettier --check .",
    "test": "jest"
  }
}
```

```bash
# Local pre-push (identical sequence to CI)
npm run format:check && npm run lint:ci && npm run typecheck && npm run test
```

```text
Enforcement stack
  Prettier     → formatting (quotes, commas, import order)
  ESLint       → RN/React patterns, hooks, restricted imports
  TypeScript   → types strict - no implicit any in src/
  PR template  → human gates ESLint cannot cover
  CODEOWNERS   → native-touch and release config paths
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Team size crossed two engineers and PRs debate formatting weekly.
* Onboarding hires from web React who import `div` habits into RN.
* You have [Standards Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/governance/standards-basics/) written but nobody reads them.
* CI green but production still ships `any`, inline styles on lists, and deep feature imports.
* Monorepo needs the same gates on `apps/mobile` and `packages/ui`.

**When to avoid:**

* Solo prototype with no CI - run `npx expo lint` and ship; formalize when a second contributor joins.
* Replacing architecture review with lint rules - ESLint cannot enforce feature boundaries without custom rules.

## Working Example

End-to-end enforcement for an Expo SDK 57 app from scaffold through merged PR.

**Step 1 - Scaffold lint and format**

```bash
npx create-expo-app@latest StyleApp --template default@sdk-57
cd StyleApp
npx expo lint
npm install --save-dev prettier @ianvs/prettier-plugin-sort-imports eslint-config-prettier
```

```js
// eslint.config.js - extend expo flat config
import expo from "eslint-config-expo/flat";
import prettier from "eslint-config-prettier";
 
export default [
  { ignores: [".expo/", "dist/", "ios/", "android/"] },
  ...expo,
  prettier,
  {
    rules: {
      "@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars": ["error", { argsIgnorePattern: "^_" }],
      "react-hooks/rules-of-hooks": "error",
      "react-hooks/exhaustive-deps": "warn",
    },
  },
];
```

* Full ESLint setup: [Linting Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/linting-basics/)
* Import order: [Prettier & Import Sorting](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/prettier-and-import-sorting/)

**Step 2 - TypeScript strict baseline**

```json
// tsconfig.json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "strict": true,
    "noUncheckedIndexedAccess": true,
    "paths": { "@/*": ["./src/*"] }
  },
  "include": ["**/*.ts", "**/*.tsx", ".expo/types/**/*.ts", "expo-env.d.ts"]
}
```

```bash
npm run typecheck   # must pass before every PR merge
```

* Stricter options: [TypeScript Strict Mode](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/typescript-strict-mode/)
* `tsc` and ESLint catch different bugs - run both in CI

**Step 3 - Husky pre-commit (optional accelerator)**

```bash
npm install --save-dev husky
npx husky init
```

```bash
# .husky/pre-commit
npm run format:check && npm run lint && npm run typecheck
```

* Hooks **mirror CI** - never run different commands locally vs GitHub Actions
* Hooks are not a substitute for branch protection - developers can `--no-verify`
* CI gate: [CI Quality Gates](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/ci-quality-gates/)

**Step 4 - Custom RN rules for architecture**

```js
// eslint.config.js - add restricted imports (see full recipes in custom rules page)
{
  rules: {
    "no-restricted-imports": [
      "error",
      {
        patterns: [
          {
            group: ["@/features/*/*"],
            message: "Import from @/features/<name> barrel only - see CONTRIBUTING.md",
          },
        ],
      },
    ],
  },
}
```

* Ban `StyleSheet.create` in list `renderItem` hot paths via custom rule or review checklist
* Ban `console.log` in `src/` - use structured logging adapter
* Full rule pack: [Custom ESLint Rules for RN](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/custom-eslint-rules-for-rn/)

**Step 5 - GitHub Actions quality workflow**

```yaml
# .github/workflows/quality.yml
name: Quality Gates
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
 
jobs:
  quality:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run format:check
      - run: npm run lint:ci
      - run: npm run typecheck
      - run: npm run test -- --ci
```

* Branch protection requires `quality` check - red lint cannot merge
* Monorepo: `turbo run lint typecheck test` fans out across packages

**Step 6 - PR template human gates**

```markdown
## Style & standards
- [ ] Imports use feature barrels only (`@/features/<name>`)
- [ ] No new `any` without `// eslint-disable-next-line` + ticket comment
- [ ] Lists use FlashList/FlatList - no ScrollView for dynamic feeds
- [ ] Native-touch files: prebuild diff attached (if applicable)
 
## Evidence
- [ ] iOS tested - build_id or screenshot
- [ ] Android tested - build_id or screenshot
```

* Template items reference [Expo Project Rules Checklist](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/expo-project-rules-checklist/)
* Reviewers reject "I'll fix in follow-up" on standards violations - follow-up PRs rarely land

**Step 7 - CODEOWNERS for config and native touch**

```text
# .github/CODEOWNERS
app.config.ts           @mobile-platform
eas.json                @mobile-release
plugins/                @mobile-platform
ios/                    @mobile-platform
android/                @mobile-platform
.github/workflows/      @mobile-infra
```

* CODEOWNERS auto-requests reviewers - complements ESLint for files lint does not parse
* Release config changes need [Release and OTA Rules](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/release-and-ota-rules/) reviewer

---

## Style Guide Essentials

Publish these bullets in `docs/STYLE.md` - link from PR template.

### TypeScript

| Rule | Do | Don't |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Props | `type ButtonProps = { label: string }` | `any` props |
| Components | Named export or default export per file - pick one per folder | Mixed patterns |
| Nullability | `order?.id` with strict null checks | `as` casts to silence errors |
| Enums | `as const` objects | TypeScript `enum` (tree-shaking) |

### React / RN components

```tsx
// ✅ Pressable + accessibility
<Pressable
  accessibilityRole="button"
  accessibilityLabel="Submit order"
  onPress={onSubmit}
>
  <Text>Submit</Text>
</Pressable>
 
// ❌ TouchableOpacity without a11y props on interactive controls
```

* **Prefer `Pressable`** over legacy touchables for new code
* **`StyleSheet.create`** at module scope - not inline objects in list rows
* **Hooks rules:** [React Hooks Lint Rules](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/react-hooks-lint-rules/)

### Imports order (Prettier plugin)

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { View, Text } from "react-native";
import { useRouter } from "expo-router";
 
import { Button } from "@/shared/ui";
import { useOrders } from "@/features/orders";
 
import { styles } from "./styles";
```

### File size and complexity

* **Screen files** target < 200 lines - extract hooks and subcomponents
* **One component per file** unless small colocated helpers (< 20 lines)
* Cyclomatic complexity: flag functions with > 10 branches in review - optional ESLint `complexity` rule

---

## Review Enforcement Rubric

| Severity | Example | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Block** | Secret in `EXPO_PUBLIC_*`, deep feature import, missing `expo-doctor` on SDK PR | Request changes |
| **Block** | `ScrollView` + `.map()` for unbounded list | Request changes |
| **Discuss** | `exhaustive-deps` warning with documented exception | Comment + ticket |
| **Nit** | Variable rename outside PR scope | Approve or optional follow-up |

* **Blockers reference a doc link** - not reviewer preference
* **ADR exceptions** override blockers when linked - [Architecture Decision Records](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/architecture-decision-records/)
* **Escalation:** repeated violations → pair programming session, not public call-out

## Monorepo Extension

```json
// turbo.json
{
  "pipeline": {
    "lint": { "dependsOn": ["^lint"] },
    "typecheck": { "dependsOn": ["^typecheck"] },
    "test": { "dependsOn": ["^test"] }
  }
}
```

```bash
# Root package.json
turbo run format:check lint typecheck test
```

* **Shared `packages/eslint-config`** exports flat config consumed by all apps
* **One Prettier config** at root - `.prettierignore` skips `ios/`, `android/`, `.expo/`
* Dead code scan monthly: [Dead Code & Dependency Analysis](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/dead-code-and-dependency-analysis/)

## FAQs

Prettier or ESLint for import sorting?

**Pick one.** This cookbook uses Prettier + `@ianvs/prettier-plugin-sort-imports`. Do not also enable `eslint-plugin-import` order rules - they fight on every save.

Warnings in CI - fail or allow?

**Fail on `main` and `release/*`** with `--max-warnings 0`. Feature branches may tolerate warnings during migration sprints - but merge gate is zero warnings.

How do style guides relate to expo-rules?

**expo-rules** are product/architecture non-negotiables (secrets, OTA, navigation). **Style guides** are code hygiene. Both appear in PR template; expo-rules violations are always blockers.

# Governance Highlights Summary

Every highlight bullet from the 8 pages in this section, gathered on one page and grouped by the page it came from.

Highlights / Governance Highlights Summary

* ESLint catches syntax; standards catch architecture - naming and folders need a written doc
* One command surface: format:check, lint, typecheck, test - local, hooks, and CI call the same scripts
* Lockfile is the contract - npm ci in CI; no floating installs on release branches
* N-1 window: production supports current SDK and one prior - not three years of drift
* One registry: docs/eol-registry.md - RN arch, Expo SDK, OS floors, and API deprecations
* Spike branches are time-boxed - ADR outcome required before any merge to main

## [Standards Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/governance/standards-basics/)

* ESLint catches syntax; standards catch architecture - naming and folders need a written doc
* PascalCase components, camelCase hooks, kebab-case route folders - one table in CONTRIBUTING.md
* features//index.ts is the only public import path - deep imports are merge blockers
* Native touch rules: who edits ios/, android/, plugins/, and when prebuild --clean is mandatory
* ADR required for every native folder commit under CNG - otherwise drift becomes permanent
* Pair standards with expo-rules checklist and lint CI gates - docs alone do not enforce

## [Coding Standards & Style Guides](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/governance/coding-standards-and-style-guides/)

* One command surface: format:check, lint, typecheck, test - local, hooks, and CI call the same scripts
* eslint-config-expo/flat + Prettier + tsc --noEmit - three gates, three failure classes
* PR template checkboxes beat Slack reminders - standards without enforcement decay in month two
* Custom ESLint rules encode RN-specific bans: deep feature imports, inline styles on hot paths
* CODEOWNERS on app.config.ts, plugins/, eas.json - style guide extends to config files
* Zero-warning ESLint policy requires CI --max-warnings 0 - warnings become errors on main

## [Dependency & Supply-Chain Governance](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/governance/dependency-and-supply-chain-governance/)

* Lockfile is the contract - npm ci in CI; no floating installs on release branches
* npm audit gates critical/high in CI; document accepted risk in docs/security-exceptions.md
* SBOM per store release - CycloneDX from lockfile + native Podfile.lock / Gradle lock
* Native SDK licenses: iOS Settings bundle, Android OSS licenses screen, legal review on bumps
* Dependabot/Renovate with expo-doctor smoke - never auto-merge native-affecting bumps
* Supply-chain incidents need rollback binary + OTA plan - not only npm override

## [SDK Upgrade Policy](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/governance/sdk-upgrade-policy/)

* N-1 window: production supports current SDK and one prior - not three years of drift
* Named upgrade champion per bump - not 'whoever has time' in sprint 47
* Dedicated upgrade branch + spike worktree - never SDK bump mixed with feature on main
* expo-doctor + eas build matrix are merge gates - OTA cannot fix native skew
* runtimeVersion and OTA channels reviewed on every SDK PR - silent bricking is common
* Risk calendar aligns SDK train with store freeze and backend API deprecation

## [Deprecation & End-of-Life Tracking](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/governance/deprecation-and-end-of-life-tracking/)

* One registry: docs/eol-registry.md - RN arch, Expo SDK, OS floors, and API deprecations
* OS floor is a product decision - iOS 15 / Android API 26 minimums belong in app.config.ts + ADR
* Old Architecture sunset tracked per RN release - RN 0.86 defaults New Architecture on greenfield
* Expo SDK EOL tied to N-1 policy - not 'we'll upgrade when Apple complains'
* Deprecation without removal date is permanent - every entry needs owner + deadline
* Store analytics (% OS version) feeds floor bumps - not only engineering preference

## [Spikes, PoCs & New Architecture](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/governance/spikes-pocs-and-new-architecture/)

* Spike branches are time-boxed - ADR outcome required before any merge to main
* PoC success criteria written before code - 'looks cool' is not a metric
* Expo UI and experimental Router APIs belong on spike/\* with feature flags off in production
* Brownfield spikes use isolated worktree + artifact publish - not copy-paste into host main
* New Architecture validation needs release-like eas build - Expo Go is not proof
* Kill spikes loudly - document why not to pursue saves future sprint debates

## [Career Growth: Senior → Lead → Staff](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/governance/career-growth-senior-lead-staff/)

* Senior ships reliably; Lead multiplies the team; Staff shapes systems across squads
* Principal path on mobile = deep RN/Expo + release trains + governance others adopt
* Scope proof: ADRs, SDK calendar, and incident runbooks you wrote that outlive your tenure
* Staff impact is measurable - crash-free, upgrade lead time, PR cycle time, not lines of code
* Avoid 'staff as senior++' - cross-team policy without authority to say no is burnout
* T-shaped: one spike (NA, brownfield, perf) + breadth (CI, security, observability)

## [Governance Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/governance/best-practices/)

* Written standards + CI gates - docs without enforcement decay by month two
* N-1 SDK window and named upgrade champions - not whoever is free in crunch week
* EOL registry with owners and dates - deprecation without deadline is permanent
* Spikes are time-boxed with ADR outcomes - never merge spike code without flags and QA
* Supply-chain: lockfile, audit, SBOM per release tag - legal asks 'what shipped?' once
* Staff+ impact is durable policy adopted by squads you do not manage

Dokumen: Spikes, PoCs & New Architecture
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/governance/spikes-pocs-and-new-architecture/

# Spikes, PoCs & New Architecture

A cookbook for evaluating **Expo UI**, **brownfield embed**, and **experimental flags** safely - time-boxed branches, clear success criteria, and ADR outcomes so exploration does not become permanent production debt.

Highlights / Spikes, PoCs & New Architecture

* Spike branches are time-boxed - ADR outcome required before any merge to main
* PoC success criteria written before code - 'looks cool' is not a metric
* Expo UI and experimental Router APIs belong on spike/\* with feature flags off in production
* Brownfield spikes use isolated worktree + artifact publish - not copy-paste into host main
* New Architecture validation needs release-like eas build - Expo Go is not proof
* Kill spikes loudly - document why not to pursue saves future sprint debates

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
# Spike bootstrap (never on main)
git checkout main && git pull --ff-only
git worktree add ../MyApp-spike-ui spike/expo-ui-tabs
cd ../MyApp-spike-ui
EXPO_PACKAGER_PORT=8082 npx expo start
```

```markdown
# docs/spikes/TEMPLATE.md - copy per spike
## Spike: <name>
- **Owner:** @engineer
- **Time box:** 3 days (hard stop)
- **Hypothesis:** <what we learn>
- **Success criteria:** <measurable>
- **Out of scope:** production merge, perf sign-off, a11y audit
- **Outcome:** ADOPT | DEFER | REJECT + link to ADR
```

```text
Spike lifecycle
  charter (30 min) → branch → time box → demo → ADR → delete branch
                              ↓
                    never merge without ADR + flags + QA matrix
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Evaluating **Expo UI** (SwiftUI/Jetpack Compose interop) for a new screen class.
* **Brownfield** embed feasibility before native squad commits CI changes.
* **New Architecture** validation after adding a bridge-only native module.
* **Experimental** `app.config.ts` or Expo Router APIs flagged unstable in docs.
* Leadership asks for PoC "this sprint" without success criteria - charter first.

**When to avoid:**

* Production bug fix - use `fix/*` branch, not `spike/*`.
* Already-adopted pattern (Expo Router file routes) - ship in feature branch with normal QA.
* Re-litigating decided ADR without new constraints - read `docs/adr/` first.

## Working Example A - Expo UI Spike

Evaluate whether **Expo UI** components can replace a custom native tab chrome for tablet layouts.

**Step 1 - Charter (before code)**

```markdown
## Spike: expo-ui-tablet-tabs
- **Time box:** 3 days
- **Hypothesis:** Expo UI tab primitives reduce native PRs for iPad split view
- **Success:** Tab switch &lt; 100ms on iPad 10th gen; TypeScript types compile SDK 57
- **Fail:** Crash on Android API 26 or requires hand-edited ios/ outside CNG
- **Outcome doc:** docs/adr/0012-expo-ui-tabs.md
```

**Step 2 - Isolated branch + flag**

```ts
// src/shared/config/featureFlags.ts
export const flags = {
  expoUiTabs: __DEV__ && process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_SPIKE_EXPO_UI === "1",
};
```

```bash
EXPO_PUBLIC_SPIKE_EXPO_UI=1 EXPO_PACKAGER_PORT=8082 npx expo start
```

* **Never enable spike flags** in `production` EAS profile
* Pair with [Navigation and Routing Rules](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/navigation-and-routing-rules/) - one navigator owner

**Step 3 - Validation matrix**

| Check | Command / action |
| --- | --- |
| Doctor | `npx expo-doctor` |
| Types | `npx tsc --noEmit` |
| Release-like perf | `eas build --profile preview` + Flashlight |
| Tablet layout | Physical iPad or ASC screenshot sizes |
| Android parity | API 26 device - not emulator-only |

**Step 4 - Outcome ADR**

```markdown
# ADR 0012: Expo UI for tablet tabs - DEFER
- **Reason:** Android parity gaps; team lacks SwiftUI reviewer
- **Revisit:** SDK 58 or when Expo UI hits stable in changelog
- **Branch deleted:** spike/expo-ui-tabs
```

* **DEFER** is valid - link calendar reminder in [Deprecation & EOL Tracking](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/governance/deprecation-and-end-of-life-tracking/)
* **ADOPT** requires feature flag rollout plan - [Feature Flags for Safe Rollout](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/error-resilience/feature-flags-for-safe-rollout/)

---

## Working Example B - Brownfield Embed PoC

Prove **expo-brownfield** artifact loads in existing native host without Node on host CI.

**Step 1 - Two-repo spike layout**

```text
rn-checkout/          # Expo module repo (spike branch)
  expo-brownfield build → AAR + XCFramework
host-ios-android/     # Native host (spike/brownfield-checkout branch)
  consumes artifact v0.0.1-spike.1
```

```bash
# RN repo
npx create-expo-app@latest CheckoutRn --template blank-typescript@sdk-57
npx expo install expo-brownfield
# build artifacts per expo-brownfield docs
```

* Follow [Brownfield Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/brownfield/brownfield-basics/) - isolated vs integrated decision first
* PoC **does not merge** into host `main` until CI publishes artifacts automatically - [Brownfield CI/CD](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/brownfield/brownfield-ci-cd/)

**Step 2 - Success criteria**

```markdown
- [ ] Host launches RN checkout screen from native button
- [ ] Cold start RN surface &lt; 2s on mid-tier Android
- [ ] Back navigation returns to native without leak (Instruments / LeakCanary)
- [ ] Auth token passed via bridge contract v1 - document in ADR
- [ ] No manual copy of JS bundle into host assets
```

**Step 3 - Bridge contract version**

```ts
// Document in ADR - host and RN must bump together
export const BRIDGE_CONTRACT_VERSION = "1.0.0-spike";
```

> **Related:** [Shared Authentication and Bridges](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/brownfield/shared-authentication-and-bridges/)

---

## Working Example C - New Architecture Validation

Third-party camera module claims NA support - validate before store release.

**Step 1 - Enable NA on spike only**

```bash
git checkout -b spike/new-arch-camera
npx expo prebuild --clean
```

```ts
// app.config.ts - spike documents explicit NA (SDK 57 greenfield may default true)
export default {
  expo: {
    plugins: ["expo-camera", "expo-build-properties"],
  },
};
```

**Step 2 - Build matrix (required)**

```bash
npx expo-doctor
eas build --profile preview --platform ios
eas build --profile preview --platform android
```

| Test | Pass criteria |
| --- | --- |
| Open camera | No redbox on NA build |
| Take photo | File URI returned |
| Background / resume | No crash |
| Flashlight score | No regression vs Old Arch baseline |

* **Expo Go is invalid** for NA proof - custom dev client or EAS preview
* If fail: registry row in [Deprecation & EOL Tracking](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/governance/deprecation-and-end-of-life-tracking/); evaluate alternate module

**Step 3 - Merge criteria if ADOPT**

```markdown
- [ ] ADR: New Architecture enabled project-wide
- [ ] All native modules NA-compatible or replaced
- [ ] eas build production matrix green
- [ ] 72h crash-free on preview channel
```

---

## Experimental Flags and Config

| Surface | Safe spike pattern | Production rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` spike toggles | `.env.local` only | Never in EAS production env |
| `experiments` in app config | spike branch | Remove or ADR before merge |
| Expo Router unstable API | `spike/*` | Pin to documented API version |
| React 19 experimental | Match SDK 57 template | No manual canary override |

```ts
// ❌ Never merge to main without ADR
export default {
  expo: {
    experiments: {
      // typedRoutes, reactCompiler, etc. - spike only until stable
    },
  },
};
```

* Read Expo changelog **Experimental** section each SDK bump
* [Expo Project Rules Checklist](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/expo-project-rules-checklist/) - config source of truth in `app.config.ts`

---

## Spike Governance Rules

| Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- |
| Max **5 active spikes** per squad | Focus dilution |
| Hard **time box** (3–5 days default) | Spikes expand to fill sprint |
| **Demo on day N** - even if fail | Forces articulation of learning |
| **No spike code in release branch** | Cherry-pick poison |
| **ADR for ADOPT, DEFER, REJECT** | Institutional memory |
| Delete branch after outcome | Prevents accidental merge months later |

```bash
# After REJECT - delete worktree
git worktree remove ../MyApp-spike-ui
git branch -D spike/expo-ui-tabs
```

---

## PoC vs Spike vs Production Pilot

| Type | Duration | Ships to users? | Doc |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Spike** | 3–5 days | No | Short ADR |
| **PoC** | 1–2 sprints | Internal TestFlight / internal track only | ADR + test plan |
| **Pilot** | 1 release | Flagged 1–5% production | Full QA + rollback runbook |

Promotion path: **Spike → ADR → PoC → Pilot → GA** - skipping steps requires EM + platform sign-off.

---

## FAQs

Spike succeeded - can we merge Friday?

Only with **ADR**, **feature flag off by default**, normal **PR template evidence**, and **no spike-only hacks** left in `app.config.ts`. Otherwise schedule PoC sprint.

Who approves brownfield spike merging into host repo?

**Native platform lead** + **mobile lead** + CI owner. RN-only approval is insufficient - host binary ships to stores.

New Architecture spike failed - do we block SDK 57?

**No** - document module replacement plan. SDK 57 / RN 0.86 still ships; failing module gets registry EOL row and swap timeline.

* [Incremental Adoption ADR](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/brownfield/incremental-adoption-adr/) - strangler pattern
* [SDK Upgrade Policy](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/governance/sdk-upgrade-policy/) - upgrade spikes
* [Architecture Decision Records](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/architecture-decision-records/) - ADR format
* [Interactive Rebase & Worktrees](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/git/interactive-rebase-and-worktrees/) - parallel spike work

Dokumen: Standards Basics
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/governance/standards-basics/

# Standards Basics

10 examples for team conventions **beyond ESLint** - naming, folders, and **native touch rules** that survive SDK churn and new hires. Seven basic and three intermediate.

Highlights / Standards Basics

* ESLint catches syntax; standards catch architecture - naming and folders need a written doc
* PascalCase components, camelCase hooks, kebab-case route folders - one table in CONTRIBUTING.md
* features/<name>/index.ts is the only public import path - deep imports are merge blockers
* Native touch rules: who edits ios/, android/, plugins/, and when prebuild --clean is mandatory
* ADR required for every native folder commit under CNG - otherwise drift becomes permanent
* Pair standards with expo-rules checklist and lint CI gates - docs alone do not enforce

## Prerequisites

Start from an Expo SDK 57 project with TypeScript and Expo Router. Standards live in `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` (or `docs/standards.md`) and are enforced in PR review - not only in chat.

```bash
npx create-expo-app@latest MyApp --template default@sdk-57
cd MyApp
npx expo lint
```

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "expo": "~57.0.4",
    "react": "19.2.3",
    "react-native": "0.86.0"
  }
}
```

> **Tooling:** These examples target **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4), **React Native 0.86.0**, and **React 19.2.3**. ESLint setup is in [Linting Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/linting-basics/); project rules are in [Expo Project Rules Checklist](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/expo-project-rules-checklist/).

---

## Basic Examples

### 1. Naming Conventions Table

Publish one table - debate once, reference forever.

| Artifact | Convention | Example | Avoid |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| React components | PascalCase | `OrderSummaryCard.tsx` | `orderSummary.tsx` |
| Hooks | `use` + camelCase | `useOrders.ts` | `OrdersHook.ts` |
| Route folders (Expo Router) | kebab-case | `app/order-history/` | `app/orderHistory/` |
| Feature folders | kebab-case | `src/features/order-history/` | `src/features/OrderHistory/` |
| Constants (module scope) | SCREAMING\_SNAKE | `MAX_RETRY_COUNT` | `maxRetry` |
| Test files | `.test.ts(x)` suffix | `useOrders.test.ts` | `useOrders.spec.js` |
| Env-specific config | `development`, `preview`, `production` | EAS profile names | `dev`, `prod2` |

```tsx
// src/features/order-history/components/OrderSummaryCard.tsx
export function OrderSummaryCard({ orderId }: { orderId: string }) {
  return null;
}
```

* **File name matches default export** for components - grep and IDE jump-to-definition stay predictable
* **Hooks live in `hooks/`** inside the feature or in `src/shared/hooks/` when cross-feature
* **Route param names** in Expo Router use camelCase in code (`orderId`) even when URL segment is kebab-case

> **Related:** [Prettier & Import Sorting](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/prettier-and-import-sorting/) - formatting is not naming | [Coding Standards & Style Guides](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/governance/coding-standards-and-style-guides/) - enforcement cookbook

---

### 2. Folder Layout - Greenfield Expo

Align with [Mobile Architecture Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/mobile-architecture-basics/): thin `app/`, fat `src/features/`.

```text
MyApp/
├── app/                          # routes only - no business logic
│   ├── (tabs)/
│   │   ├── index.tsx
│   │   └── orders/
│   │       └── [id].tsx
│   └── _layout.tsx
├── src/
│   ├── shared/                   # api, ui primitives, config helpers
│   ├── entities/                 # User, Order - domain nouns
│   └── features/
│       ├── auth/
│       │   ├── index.ts          # public API
│       │   ├── screens/
│       │   ├── components/
│       │   ├── hooks/
│       │   └── model/
│       └── orders/
├── plugins/                      # config plugins - native touch zone
├── app.config.ts
├── eas.json
└── docs/
    ├── CONTRIBUTING.md           # standards live here
    └── adr/
```

* **`app/`** files should re-export feature screens - one line when possible
* **`src/features/<name>/index.ts`** is the only import path other modules use
* **`plugins/`** and **`app.config.ts`** changes trigger native review - see native touch rules below
* Do not create `src/utils/` junk drawer - promote to `shared/` with a named purpose

> **Related:** [Expo Project Rules Checklist](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/expo-project-rules-checklist/) - Tier 2 folder rules

---

### 3. Feature Public API - No Deep Imports

```tsx
// ✅ Correct - consumer imports from feature barrel
import { OrdersScreen, type Order } from "@/features/orders";
 
// ❌ Wrong - couples to internal refactor
import { OrderRow } from "@/features/orders/components/OrderRow";
```

```ts
// src/features/orders/index.ts
export { OrdersScreen } from "./screens/OrdersScreen";
export type { Order } from "./model/types";
// Do not export OrderRow unless another feature truly needs it
```

* **Barrel exports are intentional** - internal components stay private until a second feature needs them
* **ESLint `no-restricted-imports`** can enforce `@/features/*/*` paths - see [Custom ESLint Rules for RN](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/custom-eslint-rules-for-rn/)
* When two features share UI, move the component to `src/shared/ui/` - do not export sibling internals

---

### 4. Route File Discipline

```tsx
// app/(tabs)/orders/index.tsx
export { OrdersScreen as default } from "@/features/orders";
```

```tsx
// app/orders/[id].tsx - param parsing stays in the route layer
import { useLocalSearchParams } from "expo-router";
import { OrderDetailScreen } from "@/features/orders";
 
export default function OrderDetailRoute() {
  const { id } = useLocalSearchParams<{ id: string }>();
  if (!id) return null;
  return <OrderDetailScreen orderId={id} />;
}
```

* **Parse params once** in the route file; pass typed props to the screen
* **Layouts** (`_layout.tsx`) own providers and stack/tab config - not feature business rules
* **Modal routes** follow [Navigation and Routing Rules](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/navigation-and-routing-rules/) - one presentation pattern per app

---

### 5. Native Touch Rules - Who May Edit What

| Path / action | Default owner | PR requirement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ios/`, `android/` (CNG gitignored) | EAS Build / `expo prebuild` | No manual commits - regenerate |
| `ios/`, `android/` (checked in) | Mobile platform squad | Two reviewers + device build\_id |
| `plugins/*.ts` | Platform + feature lead | `expo prebuild --clean` diff attached |
| `app.config.ts` plugins array | Same as plugins | `npx expo config --type public` output in PR |
| `eas.json` credentials | Release manager | No drive-by profile edits |
| `metro.config.js`, `babel.config.js` | Infra / senior mobile | Explain bundle impact |

```bash
# After plugin or SDK change - mandatory on CNG teams
npx expo prebuild --clean
git diff ios/ android/
```

* **CNG teams gitignore native folders** - hand-editing `Info.plist` guarantees EAS overwrite
* **Brownfield** host repos follow [Brownfield Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/brownfield/brownfield-basics/) - artifact version bumps, not copy-paste bundles
* Any exception needs an **ADR** in `docs/adr/` - "temporary" without ADR becomes years of drift

> **Related:** [Native Module Rules](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/native-module-rules/) - when JS is not enough

---

### 6. Branch and Ticket Naming

```text
feat/SHIP-412-order-summary-sheet
fix/SHIP-419-crash-on-logout
chore/upgrade-expo-sdk-57
spike/expo-ui-tab-bar
release/2.6.0
hotfix/2.5.1
```

* **Prefix matches conventional commit type** - `feat`, `fix`, `chore`, `spike`
* **Ticket ID required** when your org uses Jira/Linear - cherry-picks depend on traceability
* **`spike/*` never merges to `main` without ADR outcome** - see [Spikes, PoCs & New Architecture](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/governance/spikes-pocs-and-new-architecture/)
* **SDK upgrades** use dedicated `chore/upgrade-*` branches - not mixed with feature work

> **Related:** [Git Basics for Mobile Teams](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/git/git-basics-for-mobile-teams/)

---

### 7. Environment and Secret Naming

```text
EAS environment:     development | preview | production
.env files:          .env.local (gitignored), .env.example (committed)
Public runtime vars: EXPO_PUBLIC_* only - never secrets
Config:              app.config.ts reads process.env at build time
```

```ts
// app.config.ts - pattern
const IS_DEV = process.env.APP_ENV === "development";
 
export default {
  expo: {
    extra: {
      apiUrl: process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL,
    },
  },
};
```

* **`EXPO_PUBLIC_*` inlines at bundle time** - treat as visible to users; see [Security Rules for Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/security-rules-for-mobile/)
* **`.env.example`** documents every required key with placeholder values - onboarding copies to `.env.local`
* **Profile names in `eas.json`** match `development` / `preview` / `production` - no `staging2`

---

## Intermediate Examples

### 8. Monorepo Package Naming

```text
apps/
  mobile/                 # Expo app - primary consumer
packages/
  ui/                     # @myorg/ui - shared RN components
  api-client/             # @myorg/api-client - fetch layer
  tsconfig/               # @myorg/tsconfig - shared bases
```

```json
{
  "name": "@myorg/ui",
  "main": "src/index.ts",
  "peerDependencies": {
    "react": "19.2.3",
    "react-native": "0.86.0"
  }
}
```

* **One lockfile at repo root** - apps do not float independent trees
* **Packages expose `src/index.ts`** - same barrel rule as features
* **Peer deps pin RN/React** - workspace package must not bundle duplicate React
* **Turbo pipeline** runs same `lint` / `typecheck` scripts - [CI Quality Gates](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/ci-quality-gates/)

---

### 9. Native Module and Config Plugin Standards

When adding a config plugin or custom native module:

```text
plugins/
  withMySdk.ts            # config plugin
src/modules/
  my-sdk/                 # optional local Expo module
    expo-module.config.json
    ios/
    android/
```

```bash
# PR checklist for native-touch PRs
npx expo prebuild --clean
npx expo-doctor
eas build --profile preview --platform all
```

* **Plugin id** matches npm package or `with*` function name - one plugin per file
* **Document iOS/Android permissions** added in PR template - store review reads these strings
* **New Architecture compatibility** noted in ADR - RN 0.86 defaults NA on greenfield
* Follow [Native Module Rules](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/native-module-rules/) before `expo prebuild`

---

### 10. Standards Document Template

Commit `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` with enforceable bullets - link from PR template.

```markdown

## Naming
- Components: PascalCase files matching export
- Routes: kebab-case folders under app/
 
## Imports
- Features: import only from @/features/<name>
- No default exports in hooks/utils - named exports only
 
## Native touch
- No manual ios/ android/ edits under CNG
- plugins/ changes require prebuild --clean diff in PR
 
## Review
- UI PRs: iOS + Android screenshot or build_id
- Native-touch PRs: platform reviewer required
 
## Exceptions
- Record in docs/adr/NNNN-title.md - link in PR
```

* **Revisit quarterly** and after every SDK bump - [Deprecation & EOL Tracking](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/governance/deprecation-and-end-of-life-tracking/)
* **PR template checkbox** - "I read CONTRIBUTING.md" beats Slack reminders
* **Onboarding day one** - assign reading [Expo Rules Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/best-practices/) + this doc

## FAQs

ESLint already enforces style - why a separate standards doc?

ESLint catches **syntax and selected anti-patterns**. It does not know your feature boundaries, native ownership, or spike merge policy. Standards document **architecture and process** ESLint cannot express without unmaintainable custom rules.

Can we use snake\_case for API field mapping?

**External API shapes** may use snake\_case in adapters (`mapOrderFromApi`). **TypeScript/React layer** stays camelCase - transform at the `shared/api` boundary, not in components.

Who approves breaking a native touch rule?

Staff or lead mobile engineer + written ADR. Emergency hotfix may merge with retroactive ADR within one sprint - not "we'll document later" indefinitely.

Dokumen: i18n Best Practices
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/i18n/best-practices/

# i18n Best Practices

A condensed summary of the 25 most important best practices drawn from every page in this section.

Highlights / i18n Best Practices

* Externalize every user-visible string - literals block translation and RTL QA
* One key per complete sentence - never concatenate t() fragments
* expo-localization for device default; AsyncStorage for user override
* i18next namespaces and lazy packs for catalogs past ~100 keys
* I18nManager + start/end edges for RTL - reload on direction change
* Translation CI verifies key parity before EAS production builds

1. **Externalize all user-visible copy:** Literals in JSX block translators, break plural rules, and prevent RTL truncation QA - use `t()` from day one.
2. **One key per complete phrase:** Never concatenate `t("welcome") + name + t("exclaim")` - word order differs in Arabic, Japanese, and German.
3. **Context-aware keys:** Duplicate English homographs (`close` dialog vs `close` account) need distinct keys - translators cannot guess from `"close"`.
4. **English JSON is the source locale:** Ship `en` changes in the same PR as new `t()` calls - TMS uploads and verify scripts treat English as authoritative.
5. **Resolve locale at boot before navigation:** Gate root layout until device default and AsyncStorage override resolve - avoid English flash on Arabic devices.
6. **Device default from expo-localization:** Use `getLocales()[0].languageTag` and walk the preference list - not `Intl` guesses or hard-coded `en-US`.
7. **User override beats device locale:** Settings persistence in AsyncStorage (or server profile) wins over OS language on next launch.
8. **Map BCP 47 tags to supported app locales:** `es-419` → `es`, `pt-PT` → `pt` - explicit tables beat bare language-code truncation.
9. **Fallback chains to English:** Configure `fallbackLng` (`fr-CA` → `fr` → `en`) - missing keys must never render blank in production.
10. **Format with Intl at the display edge:** Store ISO dates and raw numbers in state/API; format with `languageTag` and `currencyCode` from expo-localization.
11. **Never parse locale-formatted input:** Users type decimals with `,` or `.` - parse with known separators or structured pickers, not reversed display strings.
12. **Adopt i18next past ~100 keys:** Namespaces, plurals, lazy language packs, and TMS workflows outgrow hand-rolled `t()` helpers.
13. **Split namespaces by feature:** `common`, `auth`, `billing` - not one monolithic `translation.json` that conflicts on every merge.
14. **Lazy-load non-default languages:** Dynamic `import()` per locale keeps startup small - preload on Wi‑Fi after user selects a language.
15. **`escapeValue: false` in react-i18next:** React Native `Text` already escapes - `escapeValue: true` mangles apostrophes and ICU markup.
16. **Plural keys in JSON, not JSX branches:** Use `count` with `_one` / `_other` suffixes - Arabic and Polish need more than two forms.
17. **Error mappers return message keys:** Not literal English strings - resolve with `t()` in components so offline and auth copy translates.
18. **RTL is layout, not just translation:** Enable `I18nManager`, use `marginStart`/`paddingEnd`, mirror directional icons - reload when crossing LTR ↔ RTL.
19. **Do not mirror logos, media, or maps:** Chevrons and back arrows flip; brand marks and play buttons do not.
20. **Refresh locale on Android foreground:** `AppState` + `getLocales()` when returning active - users change language in Settings without restart.
21. **Pseudolocale before long locales ship:** `en-XA` or padded strings surface truncation in buttons and tabs before German copy arrives.
22. **Translation CI on every PR:** `i18next-parser` extract + `verify-locales` parity - block merge when `en` drifts or required locales miss keys.
23. **TMS for non-English writes:** Crowdin/Lokalise download into git - translators do not edit `es.json` in pull requests manually.
24. **testID for E2E, not copy assertions:** Detox and Maestro survive locale changes when selectors decouple from translated labels.
25. **Brand flavors may scope locales and RTL:** White-label tenants ship different language lists and direction rules without forking code - coordinate with design-system theming.

## FAQs

What is the default greenfield i18n stack?

`expo-localization` + `i18next` / `react-i18next` + AsyncStorage override + `I18nManager` for RTL + `i18next-parser` and verify script in CI. Start with [i18n Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/i18n/i18n-basics/), graduate to [i18next / react-i18next](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/i18n/i18next-react-i18next/).

When is a minimal t() helper enough?

Two locales, fewer than ~100 keys, no plurals, and no TMS. Replace before plurals, lazy packs, or translator workflows - see [i18n Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/i18n/i18n-basics/).

How do i18n and theming interact?

Locale choice is independent of light/dark theme, but **brand flavors** may fix supported locales, default language, and RTL policy per tenant - [Theming & Brand Flavors](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/theming-and-brand-flavors/).

Do I need separate App Store listings per language?

Store metadata is separate from in-app i18n. In-app locales come from JSON bundles or OTA updates - [Translation CI](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/i18n/translation-ci/) gates production catalogs.

* [Locale Fallbacks & Pseudolocale](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/i18n/locale-fallbacks-and-pseudolocale/) - fallback chains and truncation QA
* [../design-systems/theming-and-brand-flavors/theming-and-brand-flavors.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/theming-and-brand-flavors/) - per-brand locale and RTL policy
