Dokumen: CocoaPods & Pod Install
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ios-platform/cocoapods-and-pod-install/

# CocoaPods & Pod Install

Podfile.lock hygiene and Apple Silicon simulator quirks - the CocoaPods cookbook React Native developers need when `npx expo run:ios` fails in `Pods/`, EAS Build reports a pod resolution error, or an M-series Mac picks the wrong simulator architecture.

Highlights / CocoaPods & Pod Install

* Run npx pod-install from the repo root - it picks the right Ruby/CocoaPods env
* Commit Podfile.lock when ios/ is in git; regenerate when ios/ is CNG-gitignored
* Apple Silicon: use arm64 simulators; avoid Rosetta-only x86\_64 simulator runtimes
* expo-modules-autolinking writes Podfile entries - do not hand-edit for standard packages
* CDN trunk failures are transient - retry pod install before chasing phantom header errors
* Clean pods when upgrades hallucinate: rm -rf Pods Podfile.lock && npx pod-install

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
# Preferred entry point from project root (Expo wraps CocoaPods)
npx pod-install
 
# Equivalent when already in ios/
cd ios && pod install && cd ..
 
# Full native regen (CNG) then pods
npx expo prebuild --platform ios
npx pod-install
 
# Nuclear reset when pods are corrupted after an SDK bump
rm -rf ios/Pods ios/Podfile.lock ios/build
npx expo prebuild --platform ios
npx pod-install
npx expo run:ios
```

**When to reach for this:**

* `The sandbox is not in sync with the Podfile.lock` after a git pull.
* Adding or removing a native module (`expo-camera`, `react-native-maps`, etc.).
* Upgrading Expo SDK or React Native - pod versions shift.
* Simulator build fails with architecture errors on Apple Silicon.
* EAS Build passes locally but fails - lockfile drift between teammates.

## Working Example

**Step 1 - Know what owns the Podfile**

Under Expo SDK 57, `npx expo prebuild` generates:

```ruby
# ios/Podfile (excerpt - do not hand-maintain autolinking block)
require File.join(File.dirname(`node --print "require.resolve('expo/package.json')"`), "scripts/autolinking")
require File.join(File.dirname(`node --print "require.resolve('react-native/package.json')"`), "scripts/react_native_pods")
 
target 'ShopApp' do
  use_expo_modules!
  config = use_native_modules!
  use_react_native!(:path => config[:reactNativePath], :hermes_enabled => true)
end
```

Native modules from `package.json` appear via **autolinking** - not manual `pod 'SomeLibrary'` lines unless a library's docs explicitly require it.

**Step 2 - Add a native dependency the right way**

```bash
npx expo install expo-camera
npx expo prebuild --platform ios   # applies plugin + Podfile entries
npx pod-install
npx expo run:ios
```

**Step 3 - Podfile.lock hygiene**

| `ios/` in git? | Podfile.lock policy |
| --- | --- |
| **Yes** (bare / committed native) | **Commit** `Podfile.lock` - CI and EAS must resolve identical pod versions |
| **No** (CNG / gitignored) | Lockfile is **ephemeral** - EAS regenerates on each build; still commit `package-lock.json` |

```bash
# After intentional pod upgrades on committed ios/
git add ios/Podfile.lock
git commit -m "chore(ios): pin pods after expo-camera add"
```

**Step 4 - Apple Silicon simulator selection**

```bash
# List runtimes - prefer arm64 (Apple Silicon) simulators
xcrun simctl list devices available | grep -E "iPhone|Booted"
 
# Run on a named arm64 simulator
npx expo run:ios --simulator "iPhone 16 Pro"
```

In Xcode → Product → Destination: avoid simulators marked **Rosetta** unless a legacy pod forces x86\_64 (rare on SDK 57).

**Step 5 - Fix "building for iOS Simulator, but linking in object file built for iOS"**

```bash
# 1. Ensure no mixed-arch caches
rm -rf ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData
rm -rf ios/Pods ios/build
 
# 2. Reinstall pods
npx pod-install
 
# 3. Rebuild
npx expo run:ios --simulator "iPhone 16 Pro"
```

If a **third-party** pod ships prebuilt x86\_64 binaries only, options are: upgrade the pod, pick an arm64-compatible version, or temporarily use a Rosetta simulator as a bridge - not a long-term fix.

**What this demonstrates:**

* **`npx pod-install`** is the cross-platform entry point Expo documents.
* **Lockfile discipline** prevents "works on my Mac" EAS failures.
* **Architecture alignment** between simulator runtime and compiled pods.
* **Autolinking** replaces manual Podfile edits for ecosystem modules.

## Deep Dive

### pod install vs pod update

| Command | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `pod install` | Resolves from **Podfile.lock** when present; adds/removes pods to match Podfile |
| `pod update SomePod` | Bumps `SomePod` to latest allowed by Podfile - **changes lockfile** |
| `pod update` | Updates everything - avoid on release branches |

On teams with committed `ios/`, run `pod install` after pull - not `pod update` - unless you intend to upgrade native deps.

### Expo prebuild and pods

```
package.json deps
      ↓
expo-modules-autolinking + RN autolinking
      ↓
ios/Podfile (generated)
      ↓
pod install → Pods/ + Podfile.lock
      ↓
YourApp.xcworkspace
```

Config plugins may inject pod subspecs or `use_frameworks!` - see [Config Plugins](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/native-modules/config-plugins/). If a plugin and manual Podfile edit conflict, **plugin wins on next prebuild**.

### Apple Silicon notes (M1/M2/M3/M4)

* **Host**: CocoaPods and Xcode run natively on Apple Silicon - Rosetta for CocoaPods is not required on modern Expo/RN.
* **Simulator**: Default iOS simulators are **arm64** - matches device ARM architecture, faster than Rosetta x86\_64.
* **"My Mac (Designed for iPad)"** - Mac Catalyst destination; not your RN iOS app target.
* **`USE_FRAMEWORKS=static`** - some CI scripts set this for Firebase; match EAS `eas.json` `env` with local builds.

### CDN and network failures

```text
[!] CDN: trunk URL couldn't be downloaded: https://cdn.cocoapods.org/...
```

```bash
# Retry with repo update
cd ios && pod install --repo-update && cd ..
 
# Persistent corporate proxy: set HTTP_PROXY / HTTPS_PROXY for the shell running pod install
```

### Ruby environment

EAS Build manages Ruby/CocoaPods on cloud workers. Locally:

* macOS system Ruby is deprecated - Homebrew Ruby or `rbenv` is fine.
* `npx pod-install` uses the project's expected path; prefer it over guessing `pod` on PATH.
* `sudo gem install cocoapods` causes permission pain - use user-level gem installs.

### New Architecture (SDK 57 default)

React Native 0.86 enables New Architecture by default. Pods compile as Fabric/TurboModule-aware. If a **legacy** library is not compatible, `expo-doctor` and compile errors surface early - fix by upgrading or replacing the library, not by disabling New Arch in production without an ADR.

## Gotchas

* **Manual `pod 'ExpoModulesCore'` lines** - duplicated with autolinking, duplicate symbol errors. **Fix:** remove hand edits; `npx expo prebuild --clean`.
* **Committing `Pods/` directory** - bloated repo, merge hell. **Fix:** commit `Podfile.lock` only; ignore `Pods/` in `.gitignore` (Expo default).
* **Stale lockfile after branch switch** - sandbox sync errors. **Fix:** `npx pod-install` or delete `Pods/` and reinstall.
* **Running pod from wrong directory** - creates stray `Pods/` at repo root. **Fix:** only run inside `ios/` or use `npx pod-install` from root.
* **x86\_64 simulator on arm64 Mac for daily dev** - slow and architecture mismatch errors. **Fix:** use arm64 simulator runtimes from Xcode → Settings → Platforms.
* **Different CocoaPods versions across teammates** - lockfile churn. **Fix:** document CocoaPods version in README; EAS ignores local drift by clean prebuild.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Swift Package Manager | Pure Swift deps, no RN ecosystem | React Native pods - ecosystem is CocoaPods-first |
| `eas build --local` | Reproduce cloud pod resolution | Quick JS-only iteration |
| `npx expo prebuild --clean` | ios/ is generated and haunted | Committed native with hand merges you must preserve |
| `use_frameworks! :linkage => :static` | Firebase / gRPC docs require it | Default RN apps - adds build time |

## FAQs

Should I run pod install before or after npm install?

* Always **`npm install` first** - autolinking reads `node_modules`.
* Then `npx expo prebuild` (if using CNG) then `npx pod-install`.

Does EAS Build run pod install for me?

* Yes - when `ios/` is absent, EAS runs `expo prebuild` which includes pod installation.
* When `ios/` is committed, EAS uses your folder and runs `pod install` on the worker.

Why does expo prebuild --clean delete my Podfile edits?

* CNG assumes native is generated - hand Podfile edits are not durable.
* Encode changes in a **config plugin** or maintain committed `ios/` without `--clean`.

Can I use Bundler for CocoaPods?

* Yes - some teams add `Gemfile` with `cocoapods` pin and run `bundle exec pod install`.
* `npx pod-install` remains the simplest Expo default.

What about use\_modular\_headers!?

* Occasionally required for Swift pods in mixed targets.
* Prefer `expo-build-properties` or a config plugin over one-off manual Podfile hacks.

## Related

* [iOS Basics for RN Devs](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ios-platform/ios-basics-for-rn-devs/) - workspace, schemes, Xcode entry
* [Prebuild Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/prebuild-basics/) - when `ios/` regenerates

Dokumen: Entitlements & Capabilities
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ios-platform/entitlements-and-capabilities/

# Entitlements & Capabilities

Push, associated domains, keychain, and background modes - configuring iOS entitlements through `app.config.ts` and config plugins so Expo prebuild writes the correct `.entitlements` file before EAS Build or TestFlight.

Highlights / Entitlements & Capabilities

* Entitlements are signed capabilities - they ship in the IPA, not via OTA
* Declare push, associated domains, and background modes in app.config.ts or plugins
* associatedDomains uses applinks: prefix for universal links - rebuild after changes
* Keychain access groups require matching entitlements for expo-secure-store sharing
* UIBackgroundModes must match real behavior - App Review rejects speculative entries
* Expo Go cannot represent your production entitlements - test on dev clients

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```ts
// app.config.ts - common entitlements via Expo config
import type { ExpoConfig } from "expo/config";
 
const config: ExpoConfig = {
  name: "ShopApp",
  slug: "shop-app",
  ios: {
    bundleIdentifier: "com.example.shopapp",
    // Universal Links
    associatedDomains: ["applinks:shop.example.com"],
    // Keychain access group (optional - Secure Store)
    entitlements: {
      "keychain-access-groups": ["$(AppIdentifierPrefix)com.example.shopapp.shared"],
    },
    infoPlist: {
      UIBackgroundModes: ["remote-notification"],
    },
  },
  plugins: [
    "expo-router",
    [
      "expo-notifications",
      {
        icon: "./assets/notification-icon.png",
        color: "#ffffff",
        sounds: ["./assets/notification.wav"],
      },
    ],
  ],
};
 
export default config;
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Adding push notifications or universal links to a production bundle.
* Sharing tokens between app and widget extension via keychain / app groups.
* Enabling background fetch, processing, or `remote-notification` for silent push.
* App Review rejects with "missing entitlement" or "background modes without justification."
* Migrating entitlements from hand-edited Xcode tabs to CNG-friendly config.

## Working Example

### Push notifications

**Step 1 - Plugin + permission strings**

```ts
// app.config.ts
export default {
  expo: {
    plugins: ["expo-notifications"],
    ios: {
      infoPlist: {
        UIBackgroundModes: ["remote-notification"],
      },
    },
  },
};
```

**Step 2 - Apple Developer portal**

1. Identifiers → your App ID → enable **Push Notifications**.
2. Keys → create APNs key (`.p8`) - upload to EAS or your push provider.
3. EAS credentials: `eas credentials` → iOS → Push Key.

**Step 3 - Rebuild and test on device**

```bash
npx expo prebuild --platform ios
eas build --profile development --platform ios
# Push does not deliver to simulators - use USB device
```

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx (excerpt)
import * as Notifications from "expo-notifications";
 
Notifications.setNotificationHandler({
  handleNotification: async () => ({
    shouldShowBanner: true,
    shouldPlaySound: true,
    shouldSetBadge: true,
    shouldShowList: true,
  }),
});
```

### Associated domains (Universal Links)

```ts
ios: {
  associatedDomains: [
    "applinks:shop.example.com",
    "webcredentials:shop.example.com", // Password AutoFill (optional)
  ],
},
```

* Host `apple-app-site-association` on the domain - see [iOS Universal Links](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/deep-linking/ios-universal-links/).
* Prefix must be `applinks:` - not bare hostnames.
* **Rebuild** after changes - OTA cannot add associated domains.

```bash
xcrun simctl openurl booted "https://shop.example.com/orders/42"
```

### Keychain and app groups

```ts
ios: {
  entitlements: {
    "keychain-access-groups": [
      "$(AppIdentifierPrefix)com.example.shopapp.shared",
    ],
    "com.apple.security.application-groups": [
      "group.com.example.shopapp",
    ],
  },
},
```

```tsx
import * as SecureStore from "expo-secure-store";
 
await SecureStore.setItemAsync("refresh_token", token, {
  keychainAccessible: SecureStore.WHEN_UNLOCKED,
  // accessGroup: "group.com.example.shopapp", // when extension must read same secret
});
```

* App group identifiers must match between main app and extensions (widgets).
* Keychain sharing requires identical access group in both targets' entitlements.

### Background modes

| Mode | Legitimate use | Config |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `remote-notification` | Silent push wakes app | `infoPlist.UIBackgroundModes` + push entitlement |
| `fetch` | Legacy background fetch | Plugin + real periodic sync implementation |
| `processing` | `BGTaskScheduler` deferred work | `expo-background-task` plugin |
| `audio` | Playback continues backgrounded | `expo-av` / audio plugin |
| `location` | Turn-by-turn / approved tracking | `expo-location` + usage strings |

```ts
plugins: [
  "expo-background-task", // adds processing + BGTaskSchedulerPermittedIdentifiers
],
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* **Entitlements** flow from config → `.entitlements` at prebuild.
* **Push** needs portal + binary rebuild + device testing.
* **Associated domains** pair with hosted AASA files.
* **Background modes** must reflect actual code paths - not copy-paste from Stack Overflow.

## Deep Dive

### What entitlements are

Entitlements are **key-value pairs** in `YourApp.entitlements` that Apple code-signs into the IPA. They gate APIs:

```xml
<!-- Generated excerpt - do not hand-edit under CNG -->
<key>com.apple.developer.associated-domains</key>
<array>
  <string>applinks:shop.example.com</string>
</array>
<key>aps-environment</key>
<string>development</string> <!-- production in App Store builds -->
```

| Capability | Entitlement key | Set via |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Push | `aps-environment` | `expo-notifications` + EAS credentials |
| Universal Links | `com.apple.developer.associated-domains` | `ios.associatedDomains` |
| App Groups | `com.apple.security.application-groups` | `ios.entitlements` or widget plugin |
| Keychain groups | `keychain-access-groups` | `ios.entitlements` |
| Sign in with Apple | `com.apple.developer.applesignin` | `expo-apple-authentication` plugin |

### Development vs production push

| Build type | `aps-environment` | APNs endpoint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Debug / dev client | `development` | `api.sandbox.push.apple.com` |
| TestFlight / App Store | `production` | `api.push.apple.com` |

EAS sets this from the distribution profile. Mismatch symptoms: token registers but notifications never arrive.

### Config plugins vs `ios.entitlements`

```ts
// Prefer high-level config fields when Expo documents them
ios: { associatedDomains: ["applinks:example.com"] }
 
// Use ios.entitlements for keys without first-class fields
ios: {
  entitlements: {
    "com.apple.developer.networking.networkextension": ["app-proxy-provider"],
  },
}
 
// Or a local config plugin with withEntitlementsPlist
```

See [Config Plugins](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/native-modules/config-plugins/) - `withEntitlementsPlist` is the escape hatch.

### Verifying entitlements in a built IPA

```bash
# After eas build --local or Xcode Archive
unzip -q ShopApp.ipa -d /tmp/shop
codesign -d --entitlements :- /tmp/shop/Payload/ShopApp.app > /tmp/entitlements.plist
/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c Print /tmp/entitlements.plist
```

Compare output to `app.config.ts` before blaming application code.

## Gotchas

* **Editing Signing & Capabilities in Xcode under CNG** - overwritten on prebuild. **Fix:** `app.config.ts` only.
* **Missing `applinks:` prefix** - associated domain silently ignored. **Fix:** `applinks:host.example.com`.
* **Expecting OTA to add push or domains** - entitlements are native. **Fix:** new `eas build`.
* **UIBackgroundModes without implementation** - Guideline 2.5.4 rejection. **Fix:** remove unused modes.
* **Expo Go for universal link QA** - wrong bundle ID. **Fix:** dev client with your `bundleIdentifier`.
* **Widget reads keychain but no app group** - extension cannot see main app data. **Fix:** matching `group.` identifiers - see [App Extensions & Widgets](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ios-platform/app-extensions-and-widgets/).

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Xcode Capabilities GUI | One-off brownfield rescue | CNG projects - not durable |
| `withEntitlementsPlist` plugin | Custom enterprise entitlements | Simple push - use `expo-notifications` |
| Custom scheme only | Internal OAuth | Marketing HTTPS links - use associated domains |
| FCM-only on Android | Cross-platform push backend | iOS still needs APNs entitlements |

## FAQs

Where do permission usage strings go?

* `ios.infoPlist.NSCameraUsageDescription`, etc. - often set automatically by Expo module plugins (`expo-camera`, `expo-location`).
* Missing strings crash at runtime on first permission request.

Do I need Sign in with Apple?

* Required when offering third-party social login (Google, Facebook) for account creation - App Review enforces Guideline 4.8.
* Add `expo-apple-authentication` plugin and entitlement via config.

Can I use wildcard associated domains?

* Entitlements support `applinks:*.example.com` - AASA still requires per-host files.
* See [iOS Universal Links](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/deep-linking/ios-universal-links/).

How do entitlements interact with EAS?

* `eas build` runs prebuild (unless `ios/` committed) and signs with credentials matching the App ID capabilities enabled in Apple Developer portal.
* Portal capability must be ON **and** config must declare the entitlement.

What about iCloud or HealthKit?

* Enable in Apple Developer portal, add entitlement via config plugin, provide Review notes and usage justification.
* HealthKit requires explicit feature need - speculative entitlements trigger rejection.

## Related

* [iOS Universal Links](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/deep-linking/ios-universal-links/) - AASA hosting and verification
* [Push Notification Deep Links](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/deep-linking/push-notification-deep-links/) - tap → route wiring
* [App Extensions & Widgets](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ios-platform/app-extensions-and-widgets/) - app groups and extension entitlements
* [Config Plugins](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/native-modules/config-plugins/) - `withEntitlementsPlist`
* [iOS Credentials & Provisioning](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/eas-build/ios-credentials-and-provisioning/) - APNs keys and profiles
* [Background Sync & TaskManager](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/data-offline/background-sync-and-taskmanager/) - `processing` background mode

> **Stack versions:** This page was written for **React 19.2.3**, **React Native 0.86.0**, and **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4).

Dokumen: iOS Basics for RN Devs
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ios-platform/ios-basics-for-rn-devs/

# iOS Basics for RN Devs

Xcode essentials without becoming an iOS engineer full-time - the minimum mental model React Native developers need when `npx expo run:ios`, EAS Build, or a native crash log pulls you into Apple's toolchain on SDK 57.

Highlights / iOS Basics for RN Devs

* Open the .xcworkspace - never the .xcodeproj when CocoaPods is present
* Schemes select which target builds; Debug vs Release changes signing and optimizations
* npx expo run:ios wraps prebuild + xcodebuild - you rarely open Xcode daily
* Simulator is fast; device is truth for push, camera, universal links, and performance
* Signing lives in Apple Developer + EAS - local Xcode signing is for USB debugging
* When ios/ is gitignored (CNG), treat Xcode as a debugger - not the source of truth

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
# Generate ios/ from app.config.ts (CNG) and run on simulator
npx expo prebuild --platform ios
npx expo run:ios
 
# Pick a specific simulator
npx expo run:ios --simulator "iPhone 16 Pro"
 
# USB device (requires Apple Developer account + Xcode)
npx expo run:ios --device
 
# Open the workspace when you must inspect native build settings
open ios/*.xcworkspace
 
# List simulators and connected devices
xcrun simctl list devices available
xcrun xctrace list devices
```

**When to reach for this:**

* First time opening `ios/` after `npx expo prebuild`.
* A native build fails in EAS and you need to reproduce locally in Xcode.
* QA reports a device-only bug (push, camera, biometrics, universal links).
* You need to read a crash log or attach the native debugger to a Hermes issue.
* Someone on the team asks "which file do I edit?" - answer: usually `app.config.ts`, not `pbxproj`.

## Working Example

**Step 1 - Understand what prebuild generated**

```text
ios/
├── Podfile                 ← CocoaPods dependency manifest (autolinking writes here)
├── Podfile.lock            ← Pinned pod versions (commit if ios/ is in git)
├── YourApp.xcworkspace     ← OPEN THIS in Xcode (includes Pods project)
├── YourApp.xcodeproj       ← App target only - wrong entry when Pods exist
└── YourApp/
    ├── AppDelegate.swift   ← RN entry; rarely hand-edit under CNG
    ├── Info.plist          ← Permissions strings; prefer app.config plugins
    └── YourApp.entitlements ← Push, associated domains, app groups
```

**Step 2 - Run from CLI (daily path)**

```bash
npx expo install expo-dev-client
npx expo prebuild --platform ios
npx expo run:ios --simulator "iPhone 16 Pro"
npx expo start --dev-client
```

**Step 3 - Open Xcode only when needed**

```bash
open ios/ShopApp.xcworkspace
```

In Xcode:

1. **Scheme** (toolbar): `ShopApp` → selects the app target to build.
2. **Destination**: simulator or plugged-in iPhone.
3. **Product → Run** (`⌘R`): same as `npx expo run:ios` but with GUI breakpoints in native code.
4. **Signing & Capabilities** tab: bundle ID, team, entitlements mirror - should match `app.config.ts`.

**Step 4 - Read a native build failure**

```text
▸ Compiling SomePod.m
❌ 'SomeHeader.h' file not found
```

Typical RN/Expo fix order:

```bash
cd ios && pod install && cd ..
npx expo prebuild --platform ios --no-clean   # only if ios/ is committed
npx expo run:ios
```

If the error is signing:

```text
error: No profiles for 'com.example.app' were found
```

Fix in [EAS iOS credentials](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/eas-build/ios-credentials-and-provisioning/) or Xcode → Signing → select your Team - not by disabling signing.

**What this demonstrates:**

* **Workspace vs project** - CocoaPods requires `.xcworkspace`.
* **CLI-first workflow** - Expo commands wrap Xcode; you do not live in Interface Builder.
* **Config is source of truth** - entitlements and Info.plist keys should flow from `app.config.ts` plugins.
* **Simulator vs device** - choose the right hardware for the feature under test.

## Deep Dive

### Xcode concepts mapped to RN

| Xcode term | RN / Expo equivalent |
| --- | --- |
| **Target** | The `.app` binary (your app, or a widget extension) |
| **Scheme** | Build + run configuration for a target (Debug/Release) |
| **Workspace** | App project + `Pods.xcodeproj` |
| **Bundle Identifier** | `ios.bundleIdentifier` in `app.config.ts` |
| **Provisioning Profile** | Apple-signed permission slip tying cert + bundle ID + devices |
| **Capabilities / Entitlements** | `ios.associatedDomains`, push, keychain - see [Entitlements & Capabilities](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ios-platform/entitlements-and-capabilities/) |
| **Info.plist** | Permission usage strings, URL schemes, background modes |
| **Archive** | Release build for TestFlight - `eas build` does this in CI |

### Debug vs Release

|  | Debug | Release |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hermes | Dev tools enabled | Optimized bytecode |
| JS bundle | Metro dev server | Embedded production bundle |
| Signing | Development cert | Distribution cert |
| Use when | Daily dev, USB debugging | TestFlight, App Store |

`npx expo run:ios` builds **Debug** by default. Store binaries come from `eas build --profile production`.

### Simulator essentials

```bash
# Boot a simulator without running the app
xcrun simctl boot "iPhone 16 Pro"
 
# Open a URL (universal link smoke test)
xcrun simctl openurl booted "https://shop.example.com/orders/42"
 
# Erase state (stuck keychain / cached AASA)
xcrun simctl erase booted
```

* Apple Silicon Macs run **arm64 simulators** natively - prefer them over Rosetta-x86\_64 simulators.
* Simulators **cannot** receive real APNs push, do not run BGTaskScheduler faithfully, and fake some sensors.
* iOS **16+** physical devices require **Developer Mode** (Settings → Privacy & Security).

### CNG vs committed `ios/`

| Model | You edit | Xcode role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **CNG** (gitignored `ios/`) | `app.config.ts`, plugins | Debugger only; regenerated on prebuild |
| **Committed native** | `ios/` + plugins | Merge native changes carefully on SDK bumps |

SDK 57 default: `npx expo prebuild` runs `--clean` - see [Prebuild Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/prebuild-basics/).

### When you actually need Xcode

* Native module compile errors in a specific pod.
* Inspecting **Signing & Capabilities** after a rejection.
* Attaching to a **native** crash (not JS redbox) in `AppDelegate` or a third-party SDK.
* Profiling with Instruments (memory leaks in native image pipelines).

For JS debugging, prefer React Native DevTools and Metro - not Xcode breakpoints in application code.

## Gotchas

* **Opening `.xcodeproj` instead of `.xcworkspace`** - `Pods` headers missing, build fails. **Fix:** always `open ios/*.xcworkspace`.
* **Editing `Info.plist` / entitlements by hand under CNG** - wiped on next prebuild. **Fix:** config plugin or `app.config.ts` `ios` fields.
* **Assuming simulator proves push or Live Activities** - APNs requires device + proper entitlements. **Fix:** USB device testing.
* **Bundle ID mismatch** - `app.config.ts`, Apple Developer portal, and AASA `appID` must match exactly.
* **Chasing Xcode UI on every RN upgrade** - if `ios/` is generated, delete and `prebuild --clean` before deep manual merges.
* **Using Expo Go for iOS entitlement features** - universal links, Sign in with Apple, and app groups need your bundle ID in a dev client or store build.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `eas build --local` | Reproduce cloud iOS build on your Mac | You only need a quick simulator Debug run |
| Xcode Cloud | Team already on Apple CI | Standard Expo teams - EAS Build is simpler |
| `npx react-native run-ios` | Bare RN without Expo prebuild | Expo projects - loses config plugin pipeline |
| VS Code + sweetpad | Lighter editor integration | Complex signing issues - use Xcode GUI |

## FAQs

Do I need a paid Apple Developer account for simulator builds?

* No - simulator builds work with free Apple ID.
* Physical device, TestFlight, and App Store require the **$99/year** program.

Where is the iOS version / deployment target set?

* `expo.ios.deploymentTarget` in `app.config.ts`, or `expo-build-properties` plugin.
* Rebuild native after changing - not an OTA change.

Why does Metro say "No bundle URL present" on device?

* Phone and Mac not on same network, or dev client cannot reach Metro.
* Try `npx expo start --dev-client --tunnel` or USB with appropriate hostname flags.

How do I see native logs?

* Xcode → Window → Devices and Simulators → Open Console.
* CLI: `npx react-native log-ios` or `xcrun simctl spawn booted log stream --predicate 'processImagePath contains "YourApp"'`.

Can I delete DerivedData?

* Yes when builds act haunted: `rm -rf ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData`.
* Then `cd ios && pod install && cd ..` and rebuild.

What folder do I commit?

* **CNG:** commit `app.config.ts`, not `ios/`.
* **Bare:** commit `ios/` including `Podfile.lock` - see [CocoaPods & Pod Install](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ios-platform/cocoapods-and-pod-install/).

Dokumen: TestFlight Distribution
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ios-platform/testflight-distribution/

# TestFlight Distribution

Internal/external testers and build expiration handling - the TestFlight cookbook for shipping Expo SDK 57 IPAs to QA, stakeholders, and beta users before App Store release.

Highlights / TestFlight Distribution

* Internal testers: up to 100 App Store Connect users - no Beta App Review
* External testers: up to 10,000 - requires Beta App Review per build
* TestFlight builds expire after 90 days - plan rebuild cadence for long QA cycles
* eas build + eas submit uploads IPAs; Connect distributes to TestFlight groups
* TestFlight uses production APNs - match push entitlements before push QA
* Universal links and associated domains need TestFlight builds, not Expo Go

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
# Build production-shaped IPA for TestFlight
eas build --profile production --platform ios
 
# Upload to App Store Connect (TestFlight tab)
eas submit --platform ios --latest
 
# Or build + submit in one workflow (eas.json)
eas build --profile production --platform ios --auto-submit
```

```json
// eas.json - production profile for TestFlight
{
  "build": {
    "production": {
      "distribution": "store",
      "ios": {
        "simulator": false
      }
    },
    "preview": {
      "distribution": "internal",
      "ios": {
        "simulator": false
      }
    }
  },
  "submit": {
    "production": {
      "ios": {
        "appleId": "you@example.com",
        "ascAppId": "1234567890",
        "appleTeamId": "ABCDE12345"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

**When to reach for this:**

* QA needs an installable iOS build without public App Store release.
* Validating universal links, push, Sign in with Apple, or IAP on real devices.
* Stakeholder demos on physical iPhones outside your USB cable.
* Dogfooding a release candidate before `eas submit` to App Review.
* Managing beta groups across marketing, QA, and executive teams.

## Working Example

**Step 1 - Configure EAS credentials**

```bash
eas credentials --platform ios
# Distribution cert + App Store provisioning profile for bundle ID
```

Ensure App Store Connect has an app record matching `ios.bundleIdentifier`.

**Step 2 - Build and submit**

```bash
eas build --profile production --platform ios
eas submit --platform ios --latest
```

App Store Connect → **TestFlight** tab → build shows **Processing** (5–30 minutes) then **Ready to Test**.

**Step 3 - Internal testing (fast path)**

| Property | Internal testers |
| --- | --- |
| Who | App Store Connect users with Admin/Developer/Marketing/Customer Support role |
| Limit | 100 users |
| Beta App Review | **Not required** |
| Expiration | **90 days** from upload |
| Use for | Engineering, PM, design - daily QA |

1. TestFlight → **Internal Testing** → default group or create group.
2. Add builds - latest upload auto-available to internal group.
3. Testers install **TestFlight** app from App Store → accept invite → install build.

**Step 4 - External testing (wider beta)**

| Property | External testers |
| --- | --- |
| Who | Email invites or public link |
| Limit | 10,000 testers |
| Beta App Review | **Required** per build (first external) |
| What Apple checks | Crashes, placeholder content, obvious guideline violations |
| Use for | Beta program, friendly customers, UAT |

1. TestFlight → **External Testing** → create group (e.g. `Public Beta`).
2. Add build → fill **What to Test** notes for reviewers.
3. Submit for Beta App Review - usually hours, not days.
4. Share **Public Link** or email invites.

**Step 5 - Handle 90-day expiration**

```text
TestFlight build expires: 2026-04-08
Today: 2026-04-01
Action: schedule eas build this week; notify testers before lapse
```

```bash
# Rebuild same git tag or release branch
eas build --profile production --platform ios
eas submit --platform ios --latest
# External groups: new build may need Beta App Review if material changes
```

Automate reminders:

```yaml
# .github/workflows/testflight-expiry-reminder.yml (conceptual)
# Parse Connect API for earliest expiring build; Slack when < 14 days
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* **Internal** path skips Beta App Review - fastest loop for engineering.
* **External** path scales to thousands with Apple gate.
* **90-day expiration** is hard - plan rebuilds for marathons QA.
* **Production profile** matches App Store signing and entitlements.

## Deep Dive

### TestFlight vs other iOS distribution

| Channel | Profile | Install method | Expires |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **TestFlight internal** | `production` / `store` | TestFlight app | 90 days |
| **TestFlight external** | `production` / `store` | TestFlight app | 90 days |
| **Ad hoc** | `preview` / `internal` | Direct IPA / QR (EAS) | 1 year cert |
| **Development** | `development` | USB / dev client | 7-day cert (dev) |
| **App Store** | `production` | Public store | Until replaced |

For universal links and push, prefer **TestFlight** (production `aps-environment`) over dev clients when validating production behavior.

### Processing states

```text
Upload received → Processing → Ready to Test → (External) Waiting for Review → Testing
                     ↓ fail
                  Invalid Binary / Missing Compliance
```

**Missing Compliance:** Answer encryption questions in Connect - same as App Store.

**Invalid Binary:** Often privacy manifest (ITMS-91053) - fix before testers see anything.

### Tester experience

1. Receive email or public link.
2. Install Apple **TestFlight** app (if missing).
3. Accept invite → **Install** → app appears on home screen.
4. TestFlight shows **What to Test** release notes you provide.
5. Automatic updates when you assign newer builds to their group.

Crash logs and screenshots flow back to Connect → TestFlight → build → **Crashes**.

### What to Test notes (template)

```text
Build 1.4.0 (42) - March 2026 beta
 
Focus:
- Universal link: https://shop.example.com/orders/demo opens Order screen
- Push: enable notifications on login; tap notification routes to inbox
- Account deletion: Settings → Delete Account
 
Known issues:
- iPad layout minor clipping in cart - fix scheduled 1.4.1
 
Credentials: review@example.com / BetaDemo2026!
```

### Pairing with CI

```bash
# Non-interactive CI submit
EXPO_TOKEN=xxx eas build --profile production --platform ios --non-interactive
EXPO_TOKEN=xxx eas submit --platform ios --latest --non-interactive
```

Gate submit on `expo-doctor`, tests, and internal TestFlight soak time before external beta.

### Simulator builds

```json
"ios": { "simulator": true }
```

* Produces `.app` for Simulator - **cannot** upload to TestFlight.
* TestFlight requires device IPAs (`simulator: false`).

## Gotchas

* **Using `developmentClient: true` for TestFlight** - wrong binary type for store distribution. **Fix:** production profile without dev client flag for TestFlight track.
* **Expecting push on sandbox with TestFlight build** - TestFlight uses **production** APNs. **Fix:** production push key in provider; correct `aps-environment`.
* **Build expired mid-UAT** - testers cannot install or update. **Fix:** rebuild before day 90; communicate in Slack.
* **External beta blocked on first crash** - Beta App Review rejects unstable builds. **Fix:** internal soak first.
* **Wrong bundle ID in Connect** - upload succeeds to wrong app. **Fix:** match `ascAppId` in `eas.json` submit profile.
* **Universal links "work in simulator" but fail TestFlight** - AASA / `appID` mismatch with production bundle. **Fix:** [iOS Universal Links](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/deep-linking/ios-universal-links/).

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| EAS internal distribution (ad hoc) | Quick QR install, no TestFlight | Need 500+ testers or crash analytics in Connect |
| Xcode Organizer upload | Manual one-off without EAS | Team already standardized on `eas submit` |
| Firebase App Distribution | Cross-platform Android+iOS informal QA | You want Apple-native tester management |
| App Store phased release | Post-approval gradual rollout | Pre-release validation |

## FAQs

How many builds can I have active?

* Connect keeps a rolling window of builds; expired builds drop off TestFlight.
* Practical limit: rebuild monthly for active beta programs.

Can testers stay on an old build?

* Yes - TestFlight does not force upgrade unless you expire old builds or stop distributing them.
* Communicate minimum build for API compatibility.

Does TestFlight use the same IPA as App Store?

* Yes - same `production` artifact; App Review is a separate gate after TestFlight validation.

Public link vs email invite?

* Public link: anyone with link can join (up to 10,000) - good for open beta.
* Email: controlled list - good for NDAs and enterprise pilots.

Can I test IAP in TestFlight?

* Yes - Sandbox Apple ID for purchases; TestFlight builds use sandbox StoreKit environment.

What about App Store Connect API keys?

* Prefer API key for CI `eas submit` over Apple ID password + 2FA.
* Create in Users and Access → Integrations → App Store Connect API.

Dokumen: Linting Best Practices
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/best-practices/

# Linting Best Practices

A condensed summary of the 25 most important best practices drawn from every page in this section.

Highlights / Linting Best Practices

* Start with npx expo lint and eslint-config-expo flat config
* Run Prettier and ESLint as separate concerns with eslint-config-prettier
* Enable TypeScript strict incrementally - do not flip everything in one PR
* Treat react-hooks/exhaustive-deps seriously on mobile lifecycle code
* Gate CI on lint, typecheck, format:check, and test scripts
* Run Knip and depcheck quarterly - native deps bloat binaries

1. **Start from eslint-config-expo:** `npx expo lint` scaffolds the flat config - do not cargo-cult a 2019 `.eslintrc` from a web repo.
2. **Use ESLint flat config in new projects:** `eslint.config.js` with `eslint-config-expo/flat` - legacy eslintrc is a migration tax, not a feature.
3. **Script lint in package.json:** `expo lint` or `eslint .` - every PR runs the same command locally and in CI.
4. **Separate Prettier from ESLint:** Format with Prettier; lint with ESLint - `eslint-config-prettier` prevents rule fights.
5. **Sort imports with a Prettier plugin:** `@ianvs/prettier-plugin-sort-imports` - consistent import order beats bike-shedding in review.
6. **Extend expo/tsconfig.base before strict:** Official base includes paths and JSX settings - strict flags layer on a working foundation.
7. **Enable strict incrementally:** `noImplicitAny` per folder beats a thousand-error wall - track progress in a living ADR.
8. **Add noUncheckedIndexedAccess deliberately:** Catches `params[0]` bugs in router code - enable after nullability cleanup in shared utils.
9. **Run tsc --noEmit in CI:** Types are not optional on mobile - ESLint does not replace the compiler.
10. **Install eslint-plugin-react-hooks:** `rules-of-hooks` and `exhaustive-deps` are non-negotiable - mobile code uses effects for AppState, focus, and NetInfo.
11. **Audit exhaustive-deps for focus effects:** `useFocusEffect` callbacks need stable deps - stale closures cause duplicate fetches on tab switch.
12. **Avoid eslint-disable on hooks rules:** If deps are "too noisy," fix the effect design - suppression hides real stale-data bugs.
13. **Ban console.log in production paths:** `no-console` with `allow: ["warn", "error"]` - use a logger wrapper for debug tiers.
14. **Enforce a11y props with eslint-plugin-react-native-a11y:** `accessibilityLabel` on icon-only Pressables - catch in CI, not in App Store review.
15. **Restrict cross-feature imports:** `no-restricted-paths` or Nx boundaries - `features/billing` must not import `features/orders/internals`.
16. **Custom local rules for org invariants:** Small `createRule` plugins for banned APIs (`AsyncStorage` in wrong layer) - document in CONTRIBUTING.
17. **CI runs lint, typecheck, format:check, test:** Four scripts, one `validate` meta-script - PRs do not merge on partial green.
18. **Cache ESLint in GitHub Actions:** `actions/cache` on `.eslintcache` - monorepos need cache keys per package.
19. **Mirror gates in EAS Workflows:** Same `validate` before `eas build` - native binaries should not ship from unlinted branches.
20. **Run Knip on a schedule:** Unused exports and dead files accumulate in RN apps with Expo Router entrypoints - quarterly Knip PRs stay small.
21. **Pair Knip with depcheck:** Knip finds unused code; depcheck finds unused package.json deps - native modules left installed inflate prebuild time.
22. **Whitelist Expo Router entries in Knip:** `app/**` routes are dynamic - configure `entry` patterns or false positives block adoption.
23. **Zero-warning policy with a sunset list:** New warnings fail CI; legacy warnings have ticket IDs - velocity without infinite debt.
24. **Auto-fix on save in editor, full check in CI:** Developers get fast feedback; CI remains authoritative - do not skip CI because "it looked fine locally."
25. **Document suppressions with why comments:** `eslint-disable-next-line` requires a one-line justification - `@ts-expect-error` preferred over `@ts-ignore` for the same reason.

## FAQs

Should Prettier run in a pre-commit hook?

* Optional for individuals; CI `format:check` is the enforcement layer.
* Hooks that auto-fix can hide unreviewed formatting churn - team preference.

Is strict TypeScript required on day one?

* Greenfield apps: yes for new `src/` and `features/`.
* Brownfield: incremental per module - see TypeScript in RN gradual typing page.

## Related

* [Linting Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/linting-basics/) - eslint-config-expo and first-pass setup
* [Prettier & Import Sorting](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/prettier-and-import-sorting/) - formatting across packages
* [TypeScript Strict Mode](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/typescript-strict-mode/) - incremental strict flags
* [React Hooks Lint Rules](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/react-hooks-lint-rules/) - exhaustive-deps checklist
* [CI Quality Gates](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/ci-quality-gates/) - GitHub Actions and EAS Workflows
* [Dead Code & Dependency Analysis](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/dead-code-and-dependency-analysis/) - Knip and depcheck

Dokumen: CI Quality Gates
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/ci-quality-gates/

# CI Quality Gates

CI quality gates run the same `lint`, `typecheck`, `format:check`, and `test` scripts on every pull request - catching hook dependency mistakes and cross-package type breaks before EAS spends minutes on a native build.

Highlights / CI Quality Gates

* Standardize scripts: lint (expo lint), typecheck, format:check, test - CI calls the same npm scripts as local
* npm ci + Node 20 for deterministic GitHub Actions installs
* Run tsc --noEmit before EAS build jobs - native compile is too late to catch TS errors
* EAS Workflows use eas/checkout and eas/install\_node\_modules for cloud quality gates
* Branch protection requires status checks so red lint cannot merge to main
* Monorepos: turbo run lint typecheck test fans out across apps and packages

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```json
// package.json - scripts CI will call
{
  "scripts": {
    "lint": "expo lint",
    "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit",
    "format:check": "prettier --check .",
    "test": "jest"
  }
}
```

```bash
# Local pre-push (same sequence as CI)
npm run format:check && npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm run test
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Every team using pull requests to merge into `main` or `release/*`.
* Expo apps where a type error currently surfaces only during `eas build`.
* Monorepos that need lint and `tsc` across `apps/mobile` and `packages/*`.
* Projects adopting EAS Workflows and wanting quality checks before `type: build` jobs.
* Enforcing a zero-warning ESLint policy without relying on honor-system pre-commit hooks.

## Working Example

```yaml
# .github/workflows/quality.yml
name: Quality Gates
 
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  push:
    branches: [main]
 
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
 
jobs:
  quality:
    name: Lint, Format, Types, Tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
 
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
 
      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: npm
 
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci
 
      - name: Generate Expo types
        run: npx expo customize tsconfig.json
 
      - name: Prettier
        run: npm run format:check
 
      - name: ESLint
        run: npm run lint
 
      - name: TypeScript
        run: npm run typecheck
 
      - name: Unit tests
        run: npm run test -- --ci --passWithNoTests
```

```yaml
# .eas/workflows/quality-gates.yml - same scripts on Expo infrastructure
name: Quality Gates
 
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  push:
    branches: [main]
 
concurrency:
  cancel_in_progress: true
  group: ${{ workflow.filename }}-${{ github.ref }}
 
jobs:
  quality:
    name: Lint, Format, Types, Tests
    steps:
      - uses: eas/checkout
      - uses: eas/use_npm_token
      - uses: eas/install_node_modules
 
      - name: Generate Expo types
        run: npx expo customize tsconfig.json
 
      - name: Format check
        run: npm run format:check
 
      - name: Lint
        run: npm run lint
 
      - name: Typecheck
        run: npm run typecheck
 
      - name: Unit tests
        run: npm run test -- --ci --passWithNoTests
 
  build_ios:
    name: iOS build (after quality)
    needs: [quality]
    type: build
    params:
      platform: ios
      profile: preview
```

```json
// turbo.json - monorepo fans out the same gates
{
  "$schema": "https://turbo.build/schema.json",
  "tasks": {
    "lint": {
      "dependsOn": ["^lint"]
    },
    "typecheck": {
      "dependsOn": ["^typecheck"]
    },
    "test": {
      "dependsOn": ["^test"]
    },
    "format:check": {
      "outputs": []
    }
  }
}
```

```yaml
# .github/workflows/quality-monorepo.yml
name: Monorepo Quality
 
on:
  pull_request:
 
jobs:
  quality:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx turbo run format:check lint typecheck test
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* One `package.json` script surface - developers and CI run identical commands.
* GitHub Actions uses `npm ci`, Node 20, and concurrency cancellation to save minutes.
* `npx expo customize tsconfig.json` ensures `.expo/types` exists before `tsc --noEmit`.
* EAS Workflows reuse the same scripts, then `needs: [quality]` blocks native builds on failure.
* Turborepo runs lint/typecheck/test across workspaces with dependency-aware ordering.

## Deep Dive

### How It Works

* Each CI step is a shell command that exits non-zero on failure - GitHub and EAS mark the run failed.
* `expo lint` wraps ESLint with `eslint-config-expo` - errors fail the job unless you pass `--max-warnings` intentionally.
* `tsc --noEmit` validates the entire TypeScript graph, including workspace packages imported by the app.
* `prettier --check` fails on formatting drift without mutating the runner filesystem.
* Branch protection rules can require the `quality` check before merge - policy enforcement, not suggestions.

### Scripts CI Should Call

| Script | Command | Catches |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `format:check` | `prettier --check .` | Inconsistent quotes, imports, trailing commas |
| `lint` | `expo lint` | Hooks deps, unused vars, RN a11y gaps |
| `typecheck` | `tsc --noEmit` | Broken exports, bad route params, API types |
| `test` | `jest` / `vitest` | Regressions in hooks, utils, reducers |

### GitHub Actions vs EAS Workflows

| Platform | Best for | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GitHub Actions | PR checks on every push; open-source; monorepo turbo | Familiar YAML; free tier limits apply |
| EAS Workflows | Quality gate **before** `type: build` on Expo infra | Lives in `.eas/workflows/`; shares secrets with EAS Build |
| Both | Teams that want GH PR status **and** gated cloud builds | Keep scripts identical; duplicate YAML is acceptable |

### Gate Ordering

```text
format:check → lint → typecheck → test → (optional) eas build
```

* **Format first** - fastest signal; fails in seconds on small diffs.
* **Lint second** - catches RN-specific issues ESLint owns.
* **Typecheck third** - slower but finds cross-file breaks.
* **Tests last** - most expensive; still before native compile.
* **EAS build** - only after quality passes; saves queue time and build credits.

### Monorepo Notes

```json
// apps/mobile/package.json
{
  "scripts": {
    "lint": "expo lint",
    "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit",
    "test": "jest"
  }
}
```

* Root `turbo run lint typecheck` respects `dependsOn: ["^lint"]` so `packages/ui` lints before `apps/mobile`.
* Pin one Node version in `engines` and CI - RN tooling assumes Node 20 LTS.
* For pnpm, swap `npm ci` for `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and `cache: pnpm` on `setup-node`.

## Gotchas

* **Skipping `expo customize` before `tsc`** - Typed routes fail with missing `.expo/types` on a clean CI checkout. **Fix:** Add an explicit step before `typecheck`, or commit generated types only if your team policy requires it (usually do not).
* **`npm install` instead of `npm ci` in CI** - Lockfile drift produces "works on CI, fails locally" flakiness. **Fix:** Always `npm ci` when `package-lock.json` exists.
* **Running `prettier --write` in CI** - Runner formats files that never get committed; main stays dirty. **Fix:** Use `--check` only in workflows.
* **Lint warnings allowed to merge** - `--max-warnings 0` is not the default everywhere; warnings accumulate. **Fix:** Treat warnings as errors in CI when adopting a zero-warning policy, or fix warnings before enabling the gate.
* **Quality job not required in branch protection** - Developers merge with admin bypass while checks are red. **Fix:** GitHub → Settings → Branches → require the `quality` status check.
* **EAS build without `needs: [quality]`** - Native builds start while lint is still failing. **Fix:** Chain `needs` so `type: build` jobs wait for the custom quality job.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Husky + lint-staged only | Solo dev prototyping | You need enforceable gates reviewers can trust |
| `turbo run` remote cache | Large monorepo CI is slow | Single-app repo with <30s checks already |
| Nx affected targets | Huge repo; only lint changed projects | Simple Expo app without Nx graph |
| EAS Build without prior lint | Emergency hotfix bypass (documented) | Normal feature development - too slow to fail |

## FAQs

What scripts should every Expo app expose for CI?

* `lint` → `expo lint`
* `typecheck` → `tsc --noEmit`
* `format:check` → `prettier --check .`
* `test` → your unit test runner

CI should call these by name, not inline tool commands.

Why run typecheck if expo lint already runs TypeScript ESLint?

* ESLint analyzes per-file patterns; `tsc` validates exports, generics, and cross-package imports.
* A broken type in `packages/ui` may not appear until the app imports it - `tsc` catches that.

How do I add quality gates to EAS Workflows?

* Create `.eas/workflows/quality-gates.yml`.
* Use `eas/checkout`, `eas/install_node_modules`, then `run: npm run <script>` steps.
* Add `needs: [quality]` on downstream `type: build` jobs.

Gotcha: Why does CI fail on typed routes but local passes?

* Local `.expo/types` exists after `expo start`; CI checkout is clean.
* Run `npx expo customize tsconfig.json` or `expo export` step that generates types before `tsc`.

Should lint and typecheck run in parallel jobs?

* Parallel jobs install `node_modules` twice - slower for small repos.
* Single sequential job is simpler until total runtime exceeds ~5 minutes.
* Split when monorepo packages justify parallel fan-out via Turbo.

How do I gate merges on GitHub?

1. Open repo **Settings → Branches**.
2. Add rule for `main`.
3. Enable **Require status checks to pass**.
4. Select your `quality` job name.

Can I skip CI with a commit message?

* EAS Workflows honor `[eas skip]` / `[skip eas]` in commit messages for push triggers.
* Prefer branch protection exceptions for hotfixes instead of routine skip tokens.

What Node version should CI use?

* Node 20 LTS matches Expo SDK 57 tooling expectations.
* Align `engines.node` in root `package.json` with CI `node-version`.

How do monorepos run tests in CI?

```bash
npx turbo run test --filter=mobile
# or all packages:
npx turbo run test
```

* Mark `test` `dependsOn: ["^test"]` when packages must build/typecheck first.

Does expo lint work in CI without a simulator?

* Yes. ESLint is static analysis - no device or emulator required.
* Maestro / Detox jobs are separate gates for UI integration tests.

How long should I set timeout-minutes?

* 10–15 minutes covers install + lint + tsc + unit tests for typical Expo apps.
* Increase when monorepo `turbo` fan-out grows; decrease when only running affected packages.

Should I run expo-doctor in CI?

* Yes as an optional weekly or PR gate - catches SDK mismatch before native builds.
* Add `npx expo-doctor` as a step after install; fail on incompatible dependency versions.

> **Stack versions:** This page was written for **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4), **React Native 0.86.0**, and **React 19.2.3**. 383k393a3c3q3e393a3o1r3e3k3x383c3e3k221w1u3x1v1t1v1z1t20

# Linting & Formatting Highlights Summary

Every highlight bullet from the 8 pages in this section, gathered on one page and grouped by the page it came from.

Highlights / Linting & Formatting Highlights Summary

* SDK 57 scaffolds ESLint 9 flat config via `npx expo lint` - no legacy `.eslintrc`
* One root .prettierrc covers apps/mobile and packages/ui - Metro does not care about import order, but humans do
* Extend expo/tsconfig.base - SDK 57 already sets jsx and moduleResolution Metro expects
* eslint-config-expo ships react-hooks/rules-of-hooks and exhaustive-deps - verify both are on before tuning
* Standardize scripts: lint (expo lint), typecheck, format:check, test - CI calls the same npm scripts as local
* Start with built-in no-restricted-syntax and no-restricted-imports before writing custom rule modules

## [Linting Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/linting-basics/)

* SDK 57 scaffolds ESLint 9 flat config via `npx expo lint` - no legacy `.eslintrc`
* `eslint-config-expo/flat` bundles React, hooks, import, and Expo-aware globals out of the box
* The `lint` npm script delegates to `expo lint` so CI and laptops share the same entry point
* Put global `ignores` in their own config object - mixing ignores with rules changes ESLint semantics
* Prefix intentionally unused params with `_` to satisfy `@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars`
* Metro and Babel config files need Node globals - `eslint-config-expo` handles most of them automatically
* Pair `npm run lint` with `tsc --noEmit` before EAS builds - types and lint catch different failure classes

## [Prettier & Import Sorting](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/prettier-and-import-sorting/)

* One root .prettierrc covers apps/mobile and packages/ui - Metro does not care about import order, but humans do
* Use prettier --check in CI and --write locally; never format in CI without committing
* @ianvs/prettier-plugin-sort-imports groups react, react-native, expo, then relative paths
* eslint-config-prettier disables ESLint formatting rules so lint and format stay separate
* .prettierignore must skip .expo/, ios/, android/, and lock files
* Import sorting via Prettier plugin or ESLint import/order - pick one, not both fighting

## [TypeScript Strict Mode](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/typescript-strict-mode/)

* Extend expo/tsconfig.base - SDK 57 already sets jsx and moduleResolution Metro expects
* strict: true enables eight checks; noUncheckedIndexedAccess is separate and high-value for RN
* Type route params and API JSON at boundaries - not every StyleSheet line at once
* npx tsc --noEmit in CI catches cross-file breaks ESLint cannot see
* Enable strictNullChecks first when tightening a brownfield app
* Pair compiler strictness with @typescript-eslint/no-floating-promises for async screens

## [React Hooks Lint Rules](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/react-hooks-lint-rules/)

* eslint-config-expo ships react-hooks/rules-of-hooks and exhaustive-deps - verify both are on before tuning
* rules-of-hooks is always error; exhaustive-deps stays warn until the team trusts suppressions
* AppState, useFocusEffect, and NetInfo subscriptions are the top mobile stale-closure sources
* Never call hooks inside FlatList renderItem - extract a row component so lint and React agree
* Prefer functional setState and AbortController cleanup over blanket eslint-disable comments
* TanStack Query hook results belong in deps; the stable queryClient ref usually does not

## [CI Quality Gates](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/ci-quality-gates/)

* Standardize scripts: lint (expo lint), typecheck, format:check, test - CI calls the same npm scripts as local
* npm ci + Node 20 for deterministic GitHub Actions installs
* Run tsc --noEmit before EAS build jobs - native compile is too late to catch TS errors
* EAS Workflows use eas/checkout and eas/install\_node\_modules for cloud quality gates
* Branch protection requires status checks so red lint cannot merge to main
* Monorepos: turbo run lint typecheck test fans out across apps and packages

## [Custom ESLint Rules for RN](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/custom-eslint-rules-for-rn/)

* Start with built-in no-restricted-syntax and no-restricted-imports before writing custom rule modules
* Ban console.log in src/ but allow structured logging wrappers in lib/logger.ts
* eslint-plugin-react-native-a11y catches missing accessibilityLabel on TextInput - not a device-test substitute
* import/no-restricted-paths enforces feature → feature boundaries without a custom AST visitor
* Local rules live in tools/eslint/rules/ and load via @typescript-eslint/utils createRule
* Scope test-only relaxations with files globs - never weaken a11y rules globally

## [Dead Code & Dependency Analysis](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/dead-code-and-dependency-analysis/)

* Knip finds unused files, exports, and dependencies from the module graph
* depcheck lists package.json deps Metro never imports - fast first pass
* Every unused native module is install size and autolinking surface - delete aggressively
* Ignore .expo/, ios/, android/, and config-only packages in knip.json
* False positives: expo plugins in app.config, jest setupFiles, side-effect imports
* Run knip in CI monthly or on dependency PRs - not every commit if noisy

## [Linting Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/best-practices/)

* Start with npx expo lint and eslint-config-expo flat config
* Run Prettier and ESLint as separate concerns with eslint-config-prettier
* Enable TypeScript strict incrementally - do not flip everything in one PR
* Treat react-hooks/exhaustive-deps seriously on mobile lifecycle code
* Gate CI on lint, typecheck, format:check, and test scripts
* Run Knip and depcheck quarterly - native deps bloat binaries

Dokumen: Linting Basics
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/linting-basics/

# Linting Basics

10 examples to get you started with Linting & Formatting - 7 basic and 3 intermediate.

Highlights / Linting Basics

* SDK 57 scaffolds ESLint 9 flat config via `npx expo lint` - no legacy `.eslintrc`
* `eslint-config-expo/flat` bundles React, hooks, import, and Expo-aware globals out of the box
* The `lint` npm script delegates to `expo lint` so CI and laptops share the same entry point
* Put global `ignores` in their own config object - mixing ignores with rules changes ESLint semantics
* Prefix intentionally unused params with `\_` to satisfy `@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars`
* Metro and Babel config files need Node globals - `eslint-config-expo` handles most of them automatically
* Pair `npm run lint` with `tsc --noEmit` before EAS builds - types and lint catch different failure classes

## Prerequisites

Start from an Expo SDK 57 project. The `default@sdk-57` template already includes TypeScript and the recommended scripts - you only need to add ESLint once.

```bash
npx create-expo-app@latest MyApp --template default@sdk-57
cd MyApp
npx expo lint
```

`npx expo lint` installs `eslint`, `eslint-config-expo`, and writes `eslint.config.js` at the project root. Confirm the SDK pin before customizing rules:

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "expo": "~57.0.4",
    "react": "19.2.3",
    "react-native": "0.86.0"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "eslint": "^9.0.0",
    "eslint-config-expo": "~57.0.0"
  }
}
```

> **Tooling:** These examples target **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4), **React Native 0.86.0**, and **React 19.2.3**. Install the [ESLint VS Code extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=dbaeumer.vscode-eslint) so violations surface while you edit.

---

## Basic Examples

### 1. Scaffold with `npx expo lint`

The Expo CLI is the supported path to a working flat config - it pins compatible `eslint` and `eslint-config-expo` versions for your SDK.

```bash
# First run: installs devDependencies and creates eslint.config.js
npx expo lint
 
# Subsequent runs: lint the whole project
npx expo lint
 
# Auto-fix safe violations
npx expo lint --fix
```

* **`npx expo lint`** reads the `lint` script from `package.json` and forwards flags to ESLint
* First run may take a moment while packages install - commit the generated `eslint.config.js` and lockfile changes together
* Warnings do not fail CI by default - treat warnings as errors locally if your team runs a zero-warning policy
* Delete any leftover `.eslintrc.*` files before adopting flat config - ESLint 9 prefers flat config but falls back to legacy when both exist

> **Related:** [../project-setup/project-setup-basics.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/project-setup-basics/) - SDK pin and first-run verification checklist

---

### 2. Default `eslint-config-expo` Flat Config

SDK 53+ projects use ESLint flat config. The scaffolded file extends Expo's preset - React, hooks, TypeScript, and import rules are already wired.

```js
// eslint.config.js
const { defineConfig } = require("eslint/config");
const expoConfig = require("eslint-config-expo/flat");
 
module.exports = defineConfig([
  expoConfig,
  {
    ignores: ["dist/*"],
  },
]);
```

* **`eslint-config-expo/flat`** exports a `defineConfig` array - spread or reference it as the first block so Expo defaults load before your overrides
* The preset registers **browser and React Native globals** (`__DEV__`, `fetch`, Hermes-friendly APIs) so screen files lint without `/* global */` comments
* **`@typescript-eslint`** rules apply to `.ts` and `.tsx` files when TypeScript is present in the project
* Keep custom rules in a **separate object after** `expoConfig` so you override rather than replace the preset

> **Related:** [Prettier & Import Sorting](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/prettier-and-import-sorting/) - layer Prettier without fighting ESLint formatting rules

---

### 3. `npm run lint` Script

Wire linting into `package.json` so teammates, pre-commit hooks, and CI all invoke the same command.

```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "start": "expo start",
    "lint": "expo lint",
    "lint:fix": "expo lint --fix",
    "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit"
  }
}
```

```bash
npm run lint
npm run lint:fix
```

* **`"lint": "expo lint"`** is what `npx expo lint` executes under the hood - prefer the npm script in docs and CI YAML so the entry point stays obvious
* Add **`lint:fix`** for local cleanup; avoid auto-fix in CI unless your pipeline is idempotent and fast
* Pair **`typecheck`** with lint - ESLint catches patterns TypeScript ignores (hooks deps, import order) and vice versa
* EAS Build does not run lint for you - scripts must be explicit in GitHub Actions or EAS Workflows

> **Related:** [CI Quality Gates](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/ci-quality-gates/) - fail builds on lint and typecheck together

---

### 4. First Custom Rules

Start with a small rules block after the Expo preset. These two adjustments cover most new Expo teams without turning lint into a rewrite project.

```js
// eslint.config.js
const { defineConfig } = require("eslint/config");
const expoConfig = require("eslint-config-expo/flat");
 
module.exports = defineConfig([
  expoConfig,
  {
    rules: {
      "@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars": [
        "error",
        { argsIgnorePattern: "^_", varsIgnorePattern: "^_" },
      ],
      "react/react-in-jsx-scope": "off",
    },
  },
  {
    ignores: ["dist/*", ".expo/*"],
  },
]);
```

```tsx
// app/index.tsx - `_event` is intentionally unused; lint passes
import { Pressable, Text } from "react-native";
 
export default function Home() {
  return (
    <Pressable onPress={(_event) => console.warn("pressed")}>
      <Text>Tap me</Text>
    </Pressable>
  );
}
```

* **`argsIgnorePattern: "^_"`** is the standard escape hatch for event handlers you must accept but do not read
* **`react/react-in-jsx-scope: off`** is correct for React 17+ JSX transform - Expo's Babel preset already enables it
* Add rules **one at a time** and fix the resulting violations before piling on stricter settings
* Prefer `"warn"` temporarily when rolling out a rule across a large brownfield codebase

> **Related:** [TypeScript Strict Mode](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/typescript-strict-mode/) - align compiler strictness with lint rules over time

---

### 5. Global Ignores for Expo Artifacts

Generated and vendored paths should never block a merge. In flat config, put ignores in a dedicated object with `ignores` as the only key.

```js
// eslint.config.js
const { defineConfig, globalIgnores } = require("eslint/config");
const expoConfig = require("eslint-config-expo/flat");
 
module.exports = defineConfig([
  globalIgnores([
    "node_modules/**",
    ".expo/**",
    "dist/**",
    "web-build/**",
    "ios/**",
    "android/**",
  ]),
  expoConfig,
  {
    rules: {
      "@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars": [
        "error",
        { argsIgnorePattern: "^_", varsIgnorePattern: "^_" },
      ],
    },
  },
]);
```

* **`globalIgnores`** (or a standalone `{ ignores: [...] }` object) skips files entirely - faster runs and fewer false positives
* Ignore **`.expo/`** - local dev server state, not source
* Ignore **`ios/` and `android/`** in managed workflow until you intentionally commit native projects (CNG / bare)
* Mixing `ignores` with `rules` in the same object creates a **file-scoped filter**, not a global skip - keep ignores isolated

> **Related:** [Dead Code & Dependency Analysis](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/dead-code-and-dependency-analysis/) - find unused files lint never touches

---

### 6. Lint One Path with `--fix`

Target a feature folder while iterating so feedback stays fast on large apps.

```bash
# Lint only the app router tree
npx expo lint app
 
# Lint a shared package in a monorepo
npx expo lint packages/ui/src
 
# Fix auto-fixable issues in one screen
npx expo lint app/(tabs)/index.tsx --fix
```

```tsx
// app/(tabs)/index.tsx - missing hook dep flagged before you open a PR
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { Text, View } from "react-native";
 
export default function TabHome() {
  const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
 
  useEffect(() => {
    const id = setInterval(() => setCount((c) => c + 1), 1000);
    return () => clearInterval(id);
  }, []); // eslint may warn: react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
 
  return (
    <View>
      <Text>Count: {count}</Text>
    </View>
  );
}
```

* Scoping to **`app/`** matches how Expo Router teams organize features - lint the folder you are actively changing
* **`--fix`** rewrites import order and simple style issues; it will not invent hook dependency arrays for you
* `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` warnings often surface **stale closures** in timers and subscriptions - read the message before silencing it
* Full-project `npm run lint` remains the merge gate even when you lint locally by path

> **Related:** [React Hooks Lint Rules](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/react-hooks-lint-rules/) - exhaustive-deps patterns in async mobile code

---

### 7. Node Globals for Config Files

App screens run in Hermes or the browser; `metro.config.js` and `app.config.ts` run in Node. Expo's preset already relaxes Node globals for common config filenames - extend the list when you add custom tooling files.

```js
// eslint.config.js
const { defineConfig } = require("eslint/config");
const expoConfig = require("eslint-config-expo/flat");
const globals = require("globals");
 
module.exports = defineConfig([
  expoConfig,
  {
    files: ["metro.config.js", "app.config.ts", "babel.config.js"],
    languageOptions: {
      globals: globals.node,
    },
  },
  {
    ignores: ["dist/*"],
  },
]);
```

```js
// metro.config.js - __dirname is valid under Node globals
const { getDefaultConfig } = require("expo/metro-config");
 
/** @type {import('expo/metro-config').MetroConfig} */
const config = getDefaultConfig(__dirname);
 
module.exports = config;
```

* Without Node globals, ESLint flags **`__dirname`**, `require`, and `module` as undefined in config files
* **`eslint-config-expo`** already special-cases several config paths - add explicit `files` blocks only for custom names (`tailwind.config.js`, `scripts/**`)
* Use **`/* eslint-env node */`** as a last resort in a single legacy file - prefer centralized `languageOptions` in flat config
* Keep config files **plain `.js` or `.ts`** at the repo root so the `files` glob stays simple

> **Related:** [../project-setup/project-setup-basics.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/project-setup-basics/) - `metro.config.js` and `app.config.ts` layout

---

## Intermediate Examples

### 8. RN-Specific Rule Layer

After the baseline passes, add mobile-focused rules: ban raw text outside `<Text>`, discourage `console.log` in shipping code, and require testID on pressables you cover in E2E.

```js
// eslint.config.js
const { defineConfig } = require("eslint/config");
const expoConfig = require("eslint-config-expo/flat");
 
module.exports = defineConfig([
  expoConfig,
  {
    rules: {
      "no-console": ["warn", { allow: ["warn", "error"] }],
      "react-native/no-raw-text": [
        "error",
        { skip: ["Trans", "Animated.Text"] },
      ],
    },
  },
  {
    ignores: ["dist/*", ".expo/*"],
  },
]);
```

```tsx
// Violation: bare string as a child of View - wrap with Text
import { View, Text, Pressable } from "react-native";
 
export function SettingsRow({ label }: { label: string }) {
  return (
    <Pressable accessibilityRole="button" testID="settings-row">
      <View>
        <Text>{label}</Text>
      </View>
    </Pressable>
  );
}
```

* **`react-native/no-raw-text`** catches a common crash class on Android - strings must live inside `<Text>`
* **`no-console`** as `warn` keeps debug logs visible in review without blocking merges on day one
* Install **`eslint-plugin-react-native`** when you enable RN-specific rules: `npx expo install eslint-plugin-react-native --dev`
* Custom team rules (import boundaries, design-system-only colors) belong in a shared config package - see the dedicated checklist page

> **Related:** [Custom ESLint Rules for RN](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/custom-eslint-rules-for-rn/) - ban `console.log`, a11y props, and import boundaries

---

### 9. Monorepo Lint Scope

In a Turborepo or npm-workspaces layout, point ESLint at each app's source roots and share one base config from `packages/eslint-config`.

```json
{
  "name": "mobile",
  "private": true,
  "scripts": {
    "lint": "expo lint app src",
    "lint:all": "turbo run lint"
  }
}
```

```js
// apps/mobile/eslint.config.js
const { defineConfig } = require("eslint/config");
const expoConfig = require("eslint-config-expo/flat");
const baseRules = require("@myorg/eslint-config/expo");
 
module.exports = defineConfig([
  expoConfig,
  baseRules,
  {
    ignores: ["dist/*", ".expo/*", "ios/**", "android/**"],
  },
]);
```

* Pass **explicit directories** to `expo lint` when app code lives outside `app/` (e.g. `src/features/`)
* Extract shared overrides to **`packages/eslint-config`** so mobile and web apps inherit the same unused-var and import rules
* Run **`lint:all` from the repo root** in CI so a shared hook change in `packages/ui` fails before publish
* Each app still owns its **`ignores`** block - native folders and build output differ per target

> **Related:** [../project-setup/monorepo-with-turborepo.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/monorepo-with-turborepo/) - workspace layout and task graph | [CI Quality Gates](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/ci-quality-gates/) - matrix builds per app

---

### 10. Lint + Typecheck Pre-Build Gate

Treat lint and TypeScript as complementary gates before `eas build` or a store submission - they catch different defect classes.

```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "lint": "expo lint",
    "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit",
    "validate": "npm run typecheck && npm run lint"
  }
}
```

```bash
npm run validate
```

```tsx
// TypeScript passes; ESLint flags the hook - validate catches both
import { useCallback, useState } from "react";
import { Button, View } from "react-native";
 
export function Counter() {
  const [n, setN] = useState(0);
  const increment = useCallback(() => setN(n + 1), []); // stale closure risk
 
  return (
    <View>
      <Button title={`${n}`} onPress={increment} />
    </View>
  );
}
```

* **`tsc --noEmit`** validates types without emitting JS - fast enough for every PR
* **`expo lint`** runs the hooks plugin - stale closures like `useCallback(..., [])` reading `n` are lint findings, not type errors
* Name the combo script **`validate`** or **`check`** and call it from CI, pre-push hooks, and local pre-release rituals
* Metro may still bundle code that fails `validate` - never skip the gate because the simulator launched

> **Related:** [TypeScript Strict Mode](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/typescript-strict-mode/) - tighten `strict` incrementally | [Linting Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/best-practices/) - zero-warning policy without slowing velocity

---

> **Stack versions:** This page was written for **React 19.2.3**, **React Native 0.86.0**, and **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4).
