Dokumen: Prettier & Import Sorting
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/prettier-and-import-sorting/

# Prettier & Import Sorting

Prettier removes formatting debates across your Expo app and any shared packages in a monorepo. Import sorting keeps `react-native` above local feature imports so diffs stay readable when screens grow past a dozen dependencies.

Highlights / Prettier & Import Sorting

* One root .prettierrc covers apps/mobile and packages/ui - Metro does not care about import order, but humans do
* Use prettier --check in CI and --write locally; never format in CI without committing
* @ianvs/prettier-plugin-sort-imports groups react, react-native, expo, then relative paths
* eslint-config-prettier disables ESLint formatting rules so lint and format stay separate
* .prettierignore must skip .expo/, ios/, android/, and lock files
* Import sorting via Prettier plugin or ESLint import/order - pick one, not both fighting

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
npm install --save-dev prettier @ianvs/prettier-plugin-sort-imports eslint-config-prettier
 
# Check formatting (CI)
npx prettier --check .
 
# Fix formatting locally
npx prettier --write .
```

```json
// package.json scripts
{
  "scripts": {
    "format": "prettier --write .",
    "format:check": "prettier --check ."
  }
}
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Two or more contributors touching the same `.tsx` screens and shared UI packages.
* A Turborepo or Nx monorepo where `apps/mobile` and `packages/ui` must share one style.
* PRs that currently mix quote style, trailing commas, and import reordering in every review.
* CI that should fail when someone forgets to run format before pushing.
* Teams that want import groups (`react` → `expo` → `@repo/*` → relative) without manual cleanup.

## Working Example

```json
// .prettierrc
{
  "semi": true,
  "singleQuote": false,
  "tabWidth": 2,
  "trailingComma": "all",
  "printWidth": 80,
  "endOfLine": "lf",
  "plugins": ["@ianvs/prettier-plugin-sort-imports"],
  "importOrder": [
    "<BUILTIN_MODULES>",
    "",
    "^react$",
    "^react-native$",
    "^expo",
    "^@react-navigation",
    "<THIRD_PARTY_MODULES>",
    "",
    "^@repo/(.*)$",
    "",
    "^@/(.*)$",
    "",
    "^[./]"
  ],
  "importOrderType": "mixed"
}
```

```gitignore
# .prettierignore
node_modules/
.expo/
dist/
coverage/
ios/
android/
*.lock
package-lock.json
pnpm-lock.yaml
```

```javascript
// eslint.config.js - disable ESLint formatting; keep import/order optional
const { defineConfig } = require("eslint/config");
const expoConfig = require("eslint-config-expo/flat");
const eslintConfigPrettier = require("eslint-config-prettier");
 
module.exports = defineConfig([
  expoConfig,
  eslintConfigPrettier,
  {
    ignores: [".expo/**", "ios/**", "android/**"],
  },
]);
```

```tsx
// apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/index.tsx - after Prettier + import plugin
import { useCallback } from "react";
import { Pressable, StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
import { useRouter } from "expo-router";
 
import { Button } from "@repo/ui/button";
 
import { useSession } from "@/hooks/useSession";
 
import { HomeHero } from "../../components/HomeHero";
 
export default function HomeScreen() {
  const router = useRouter();
  const { user } = useSession();
 
  const onContinue = useCallback(() => {
    router.push("/settings");
  }, [router]);
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.container}>
      <HomeHero name={user?.displayName ?? "Guest"} />
      <Button variant="primary" onPress={onContinue}>
        Continue
      </Button>
      <Pressable onPress={() => router.push("/help")}>
        <Text style={styles.link}>Help</Text>
      </Pressable>
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  container: { flex: 1, padding: 16, gap: 12 },
  link: { color: "#2563eb", textAlign: "center" },
});
```

```json
// Root package.json in a monorepo - one format command for every workspace
{
  "scripts": {
    "format": "prettier --write \"**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx,json,md}\"",
    "format:check": "prettier --check \"**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx,json,md}\""
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@ianvs/prettier-plugin-sort-imports": "^4.4.0",
    "eslint-config-prettier": "^10.0.0",
    "prettier": "^3.5.0"
  }
}
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* A single `.prettierrc` at the repo root formats both the Expo app and shared packages.
* `@ianvs/prettier-plugin-sort-imports` enforces stable import groups tuned for RN (`expo`, `@repo/*`, `@/*`).
* `.prettierignore` skips generated native folders and Expo cache so CI stays fast.
* `eslint-config-prettier` turns off ESLint rules that duplicate Prettier - run `lint` and `format:check` as separate scripts.
* Monorepo scripts use explicit globs so Prettier does not walk `node_modules` in every package.

## Deep Dive

### How It Works

* Prettier parses each file into an AST and reprints it with fixed rules - it does not "suggest" style, it enforces it.
* Import-sort plugins run **after** Prettier's printer pass, reordering `import` statements to match `importOrder` regex groups.
* Metro bundles whatever import order you ship; sorting is a **maintainability** win, not a runtime optimization.
* `eslint-config-prettier` is a one-way gate: ESLint handles correctness (`react-hooks/exhaustive-deps`), Prettier handles whitespace and quotes.
* In monorepos, put config at the root and run Prettier from the root so `packages/ui` and `apps/mobile` never drift.

### Config at a Glance

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `.prettierrc` | Quote style, trailing commas, import-order plugin |
| `.prettierignore` | Skip `.expo/`, `ios/`, `android/`, lock files |
| `eslint.config.js` | `eslint-config-expo` + `eslint-config-prettier` last |
| `package.json` scripts | `format` (local) vs `format:check` (CI) |

### Import Sorting Strategies

| Approach | Pros | Cons |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@ianvs/prettier-plugin-sort-imports` | One command formats + sorts; works in editors | Competes with ESLint `import/order` if both enabled |
| `prettier-plugin-organize-imports` | Uses TypeScript's organize-imports | Can remove "unused" imports you meant to keep for side effects |
| ESLint `import/order` only | Sort on `eslint --fix` without Prettier plugin | Two tools to configure; import order not applied by format-on-save alone |

**Recommendation:** Pick Prettier plugin **or** ESLint `import/order`, not both with conflicting group rules.

### Monorepo Notes

```yaml
# turbo.json - cache format check like lint
{
  "tasks": {
    "format:check": {
      "outputs": []
    }
  }
}
```

```json
// apps/mobile/package.json
{
  "scripts": {
    "format:check": "prettier --check ."
  }
}
```

* Share one `.prettierrc` via the repo root; avoid per-package copies that diverge on `printWidth`.
* When `packages/ui` publishes through `exports` maps, sorted imports make public entry points obvious in reviews.
* Run `prettier --check` from CI at the root with a glob - faster than spawning per-package jobs for small teams.

### TypeScript Notes

```tsx
// Prettier preserves type-only imports when importOrderType is "mixed"
import type { Href } from "expo-router";
import { useRouter } from "expo-router";
 
// importOrderType: "inline" merges type and value from the same module
// importOrderType: "mixed" keeps type imports grouped with their module
```

## Gotchas

* **Prettier vs ESLint formatting fight** - Both try to control quotes and semicolons, producing an infinite fix loop in the editor. **Fix:** Add `eslint-config-prettier` after `eslint-config-expo` in flat config; never use `eslint-plugin-prettier` as a rule runner.
* **Formatting `.expo/types` or `ios/`** - Generated route types and prebuild folders create huge noisy diffs. **Fix:** Add `.expo/`, `ios/`, and `android/` to `.prettierignore` unless you intentionally format committed native projects.
* **Two import sorters** - Prettier plugin and ESLint `import/order` with different group rules reshuffle imports on every save. **Fix:** Disable `import/order` in ESLint when the Prettier plugin owns sorting.
* **`--write` in CI** - CI formats files on the runner but does not commit them, so the job passes while `main` stays unformatted. **Fix:** Use `prettier --check` in CI; reserve `--write` for local runs and lint-staged hooks.
* **Lock files formatted by mistake** - Without `.prettierignore`, Prettier touches `package-lock.json` and creates merge conflicts. **Fix:** Ignore `*lock*` files explicitly.
* **Editor uses wrong formatter** - VS Code may default to the built-in TypeScript formatter for `.tsx`. **Fix:** Set `"editor.defaultFormatter": "esbenp.prettier-vscode"` for `[typescriptreact]` and install the Prettier extension.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ESLint `import/order` only | You refuse Prettier plugins and already run `eslint --fix` on commit | You want format-on-save to also sort imports |
| `prettier-plugin-organize-imports` | You trust TS to drop unused imports | Imports exist only for side effects (polyfills, gesture handler setup) |
| [Biome](https://biomejs.dev/) | Greenfield repo wants one linter + formatter | You rely on Expo's `eslint-config-expo` presets and RN-specific plugins |
| Editor-only Prettier | Solo developer, no CI | Team needs enforceable gates on every PR |

## FAQs

Does Prettier work with Expo Router file-based routes?

* Yes. Prettier formats `.tsx` screens under `app/` like any other React file.
* Ignore `.expo/types/**/*.ts` in `.prettierignore` - those files are generated, not hand-edited.
* Import sorting still applies; keep `expo-router` in your `importOrder` group for consistency.

What is the difference between --check and --write?

* `--check` exits with code 1 when any file differs - use in CI and `npm run format:check`.
* `--write` mutates files in place - use locally before committing.
* Never run `--write` in CI unless a bot commits the result.

How do I share Prettier config across apps/mobile and packages/ui?

* Place `.prettierrc` and `.prettierignore` at the monorepo root.
* Run `prettier --check .` from the root with globs, or add `format:check` to each package's `package.json` pointing at the same config.
* See [Monorepo with Turborepo](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/monorepo-with-turborepo/) for workspace layout.

Should I sort imports with Prettier or ESLint?

* **Prettier plugin:** one `format` command, works with format-on-save.
* **ESLint `import/order`:** sorts on lint fix; better if you skip Prettier entirely for imports.
* Pick one authority; disabling the other avoids ping-pong diffs.

Gotcha: Why does format-on-save not run Prettier in VS Code?

* Another formatter is set as default for `typescriptreact`.
* The Prettier extension is not installed or is disabled in workspace settings.
* **Fix:** Add `.vscode/settings.json` with `editor.defaultFormatter` set to `esbenp.prettier-vscode`.

Does printWidth force every line under 80 characters?

* No. `printWidth` is a target; long strings, URLs, and import paths may exceed it.
* Prettier prefers readable breaks over strict column limits.

How do I add a blank line between import groups?

```json
"importOrder": ["^react$", "", "^expo", "", "^@repo/(.*)$", "", "^[./]"]
```

* Empty strings in the `importOrder` array insert blank lines between groups.

Do I need prettier for JSON and Markdown in an RN repo?

* Optional but common for `app.config.ts` companions (`eas.json`, `package.json` formatting on save).
* Limit CI globs to `*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx,json,md}` so you do not format assets or native project files.

How does eslint-config-prettier fit with eslint-config-expo?

* `eslint-config-expo` ships RN-aware lint rules including stylistic defaults.
* `eslint-config-prettier` disables any rule that overlaps with Prettier.
* Load Prettier's config **last** in flat config so overrides win.

Will import sorting break Metro barrel files?

* Sorting only reorders import lines at the top of a file.
* It does not change re-export graphs or `packages/ui` `exports` maps.
* Side-effect imports (`import "react-native-gesture-handler"`) stay in place when listed in `importOrder`.

Can I run format:check in Turborepo?

```json
// turbo.json
{
  "tasks": {
    "format:check": {
      "cache": true,
      "outputs": []
    }
  }
}
```

* Add `format:check` scripts to each package or run once at the root in CI.

What RN paths belong in importOrder regexes?

* `^react-native$` - core primitives before feature code.
* `^expo` - SDK modules (`expo-router`, `expo-font`, …).
* `^@react-navigation` - when using React Navigation outside Expo Router.
* `^@repo/` or `^@/` - monorepo aliases before relative `./` imports.

Dokumen: React Hooks Lint Rules
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/react-hooks-lint-rules/

# React Hooks Lint Rules

A verification checklist for `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` in Expo React Native apps - catching illegal hook calls, stale closures in async mobile code, and missing cleanup before they ship to backgrounded devices.

Highlights / React Hooks Lint Rules

* eslint-config-expo ships react-hooks/rules-of-hooks and exhaustive-deps - verify both are on before tuning
* rules-of-hooks is always error; exhaustive-deps stays warn until the team trusts suppressions
* AppState, useFocusEffect, and NetInfo subscriptions are the top mobile stale-closure sources
* Never call hooks inside FlatList renderItem - extract a row component so lint and React agree
* Prefer functional setState and AbortController cleanup over blanket eslint-disable comments
* TanStack Query hook results belong in deps; the stable queryClient ref usually does not

## How to Use This Checklist

* Run **Tier 1** when scaffolding or upgrading ESLint - confirm `eslint-config-expo` registers the hooks plugin before adding overrides.
* Apply **Tiers 2–3** per screen or custom hook during PR review; mobile listeners and navigation focus effects fail more often than web `fetch` tutorials suggest.
* Treat every `eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` as a **documented exception** - note why the dep is stable or why stale data is acceptable.
* Revisit **Tier 4** after SDK upgrades - React 19 batching and New Architecture do not remove the need for correct dependency arrays.
* Device-test screens that pass lint but still show stale UI after backgrounding - lint cannot prove runtime subscription hygiene.

## Plugin & Baseline Severity (1–5)

1. **Confirm `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` is active:** `eslint-config-expo` bundles the plugin in flat config - run `npx eslint --print-config app/index.tsx` and verify `react-hooks/` rules appear.

   * **Missing plugin:** Add `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` and extend its recommended preset explicitly.
   * **Duplicate registration:** Do not install the plugin twice via overlapping presets - duplicate configs produce conflicting severities.
2. **`react-hooks/rules-of-hooks` severity:** Keep at **`error`** - illegal hook order breaks React in production and cannot be downgraded to warn without hiding ship-stoppers.

   * **CI gate:** `error` fails `expo lint` and GitHub Actions the same way as TypeScript errors.
   * **Never global-off:** A single `off` for this rule lets conditional hooks merge silently.
3. **`react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` severity:** Default to **`warn`** in active codebases; promote to **`error`** only after the team has a written suppression policy.

   * **Warn in CI:** Pair with `--max-warnings 0` when you want zero warnings without fighting stable-ref false positives on day one.
   * **Error for new modules:** Scope `error` to `src/features/**` once greenfield folders are clean.
4. **Flat config file targeting:** Ensure `app/`, `src/`, and `components/` are inside ESLint `files` globs - hooks in route files are linted the same as shared hooks.

   * **Monorepo:** Extend the same hooks block to shared `packages/ui` - stale closures in a design-system hook affect every screen.
   * **Ignore only generated dirs:** Do not ignore `app/` because Expo Router filenames confuse the linter.
5. **Editor integration:** Enable ESLint in the IDE with flat-config support so `exhaustive-deps` surfaces while typing effects, not only in CI.

   * **On-save fix:** Auto-fix handles import order, not dependency arrays - developers must edit deps manually.
   * **Pre-commit:** Run `expo lint` via lint-staged on changed `.tsx` files.

## Rules of Hooks Enforcement (6–10)

6. **No hooks inside `renderItem`:** `FlatList` / `SectionList` `renderItem` is a callback, not a component - extract `TodoRow` and call hooks at the top of that component.

   * **Lint signal:** `rules-of-hooks` flags hook calls inside nested functions.
   * **Fix pattern:** `renderItem={({ item }) => <TodoRow item={item} />}`.
7. **No hooks after early returns:** Guard clauses above `useState` / `useEffect` violate hook order when the guard toggles between renders.

   * **Common in RN:** `if (!fontsLoaded) return null` placed before hooks in a screen.
   * **Fix:** Move loading gates below all hooks or split into a wrapper shell component.
8. **Prefix custom hooks with `use`:** `getFilters()` can call `useState` illegally; `useFilters()` triggers `rules-of-hooks` on the custom hook body.

   * **File convention:** `use-app-state.ts` exporting `useAppState`.
   * **Test helpers:** `renderHook` from Testing Library still requires a proper `use*` hook.
9. **No hooks inside `useMemo` / `useCallback` factories:** The factory runs during render; hooks belong at component top level only.

   * **Smell:** Creating a subscription inside `useMemo(() => { useEffect(...) })`.
   * **Fix:** Plain `useEffect` with cleanup, or a dedicated custom hook.
10. **No hooks in Reanimated worklets or non-React callbacks:** Worklets and native module callbacks are outside React's render cycle - use shared values and `runOnJS` instead.

    * **Lint gap:** ESLint may not analyze worklet bodies - enforce via code review and `// eslint-disable` is not the answer.
    * **See:** [Custom Hooks for UI Logic](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/custom-hooks-for-ui-logic/) for platform hook extraction.

## exhaustive-deps - Mobile Patterns (11–18)

11. **`AppState` listeners:** Effects that subscribe to `AppState.addEventListener` must list every closed-over value used inside the handler, or read fresh values from refs.

    * **Stale pattern:** Handler reads `userId` from render when app returns from background after logout.
    * **Fix:** Include `userId` in deps, or `const userIdRef = useRef(userId)` synced in a separate effect.
12. **`useFocusEffect` from Expo Router / React Navigation:** The callback identity matters - wrap work in `useCallback` with correct deps or eslint flags the effect wrapper.

    * **Stale pattern:** Refetch uses `route.params.id` omitted from deps; wrong record flashes after deep link.
    * **Fix:** `[route.params.id]` in `useCallback` deps; return cleanup to cancel in-flight fetch.
13. **NetInfo / connectivity subscriptions:** `NetInfo.addEventListener` callbacks that enqueue mutations must see current auth and queue state.

    * **Stale pattern:** Replay offline queue with an expired token captured at mount.
    * **Fix:** Dep on `accessToken` or read from a ref updated on refresh.
14. **Keyboard and dimension listeners:** `Keyboard.addListener` and `Dimensions.addEventListener` effects need cleanup and deps for values used when firing.

    * **Stale pattern:** `keyboardVerticalOffset` computed once; lint-clean but wrong after rotation.
    * **Fix:** Dep on `layout` state or re-read `Dimensions.get` inside the handler.
15. **Async effects and `AbortController`:** `useEffect` that calls `async function load()` must abort on cleanup and list deps that change the request.

    * **Stale pattern:** Fast tab switches apply an older response - not caught by deps alone without abort.
    * **Fix:** `const ac = new AbortController(); … return () => ac.abort();` plus full dep array.
16. **Timers (`setInterval`, `setTimeout`):** Effects scheduling timers must clear them in cleanup and include delay-driving deps.

    * **Stale pattern:** Polling interval still hits API after screen blurs because `useFocusEffect` cleanup was forgotten.
    * **Fix:** Clear timer in both `useEffect` return and focus-effect cleanup.
17. **Stable refs vs missing deps:** `dispatch` from `useReducer`, `setState` from `useState`, and refs are stable - omitting them is fine; omitting **props and derived state** is not.

    * **False positive:** Lint wants `dispatch` - safe to leave; do not disable the rule for it.
    * **Real bug:** Omitting `filter` when effect posts `filter` to analytics - add `filter`.
18. **TanStack Query and context:** Include `data`, `isFetching`, and query-key inputs in deps when effects react to them; `queryClient` from `useQueryClient()` is stable.

    * **Stale pattern:** `useEffect` on `data` but missing `dataUpdatedAt` when only freshness matters.
    * **Fix:** Dep on the specific fields the effect reads, or derive a memoized primitive first.

## Suppression, Custom Hooks & CI (19–24)

19. **One-line disable policy:** `eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` requires an inline comment explaining stability or intentional staleness.

    * **Reject:** Blank disables to silence lint during a rush.
    * **Accept:** `// deps intentionally empty - mount-only analytics ping`.
20. **Never disable `rules-of-hooks`:** If the rule fires, refactor - conditional hooks are never a lint false positive.

    * **God-screen smell:** Multiple disables in one screen file - extract hooks per [Anti-Patterns: God Screens](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/anti-patterns-god-screens/).
21. **Custom hooks export a coherent dep story:** Hooks wrapping `AppState` / NetInfo should document which values callers must pass in so caller effects stay lint-clean.

    * **Pattern:** `useOnAppForeground(onForeground, deps)` internally mirrors `useEffect` deps.
    * **Anti-pattern:** Hidden global module state inside a hook - callers cannot satisfy exhaustive-deps honestly.
22. **Functional updates for rapid events:** `setCount(c => c + 1)` removes `count` from handler deps - prefer over disabling lint on press handlers.

    * **RN batching:** React 19 batches multiple `setState` in the same gesture - functional form stays correct.
    * **See:** [Props, State & Re-renders on Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/rn-fundamentals/props-state-and-re-renders-on-mobile/).
23. **`useCallback` / `useMemo` dependency lint:** Nested hooks lint their own factories - if `useCallback` omits a closed-over prop, the bug is in the callback deps, not `exhaustive-deps` on the effect alone.

    * **Smell:** `useEffect(() => { doWork(cb) }, [cb])` where `cb` recreates every render anyway.
    * **Fix:** Stabilize `cb` with correct `useCallback` deps or inline the work in the effect.
24. **CI enforcement:** Add `expo lint` (or `eslint .`) to PR checks with `--max-warnings 0` when policy matures.

    * **Gradual:** Start with `rules-of-hooks` as error only; flip `exhaustive-deps` to error per package.
    * **See:** [CI Quality Gates](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/ci-quality-gates/) for script wiring.

## Applying the Checklist in Order

* **Tier 1 (1–5):** Plugin and severity - do once per repo or ESLint upgrade.
* **Tier 2 (6–10):** Hook placement - fix before reviewing deps; illegal hooks cannot be patched with dep tweaks.
* **Tier 3 (11–18):** Mobile async and subscriptions - highest ROI for production stale UI on background/resume.
* **Tier 4 (19–24):** Suppression discipline and CI - lock in after the codebase is mostly green.

## FAQs

Does eslint-config-expo include react-hooks rules?

Yes - the Expo flat config preset registers `eslint-plugin-react-hooks`. Confirm with `npx eslint --print-config` on a screen file before adding a duplicate plugin install.

Should exhaustive-deps be error or warn?

Start at **warn** so stable-ref false positives do not block velocity. Move to **error** (or `--max-warnings 0`) once the team documents acceptable one-line suppressions. Keep `rules-of-hooks` at **error** always.

Why does lint pass but my screen shows stale data after resume?

`exhaustive-deps` is static analysis - it cannot verify your `AppState` handler reads fresh auth state. Audit Tier 3 listeners manually and test background → foreground on a physical device.

Can I call useFocusEffect without useCallback?

You can, but the effect re-runs every render if the callback identity changes. Wrap the body in `useCallback` with the same deps you would put on a `useEffect`, or accept redundant refetches.

Is omitting dispatch from deps correct?

Yes - `useReducer` dispatch is stable for the component lifetime. The same applies to `useState` setters. Do not disable the rule solely to silence `dispatch`; add real missing values instead.

How do I fix hooks inside FlatList renderItem?

Extract a row component: `function Row({ item }) { const theme = useTheme(); … }`. Pass `renderItem={({ item }) => <Row item={item} />}`. Hooks then run in a real component.

Should queryClient be in my effect deps?

Usually no - `useQueryClient()` returns a stable client. Include query **results** and variables that change fetch behavior (`id`, `filter`), not the client singleton.

When is eslint-disable-next-line acceptable?

When you can state in one line why the dependency is stable (mount-only, ref-backed, or intentional empty deps). Never blanket-disable for a whole file or directory.

Do React 19 and New Architecture change these rules?

Batching and concurrent rendering make stale closures *more* visible, not less. Hook rules and `exhaustive-deps` semantics are unchanged - still enforce them on SDK 57.

How do I lint hooks in a monorepo shared package?

Apply the same `react-hooks` rules block to `packages/**` TypeScript sources. A stale hook in `packages/ui` ships to every app in the workspace.

What about useEffectEvent or experimental React APIs?

If your SDK ships an official stable API, follow its lint guidance. Until then, prefer refs for stable handlers inside effects rather than turning off `exhaustive-deps` globally.

Does useMemo remove the need for exhaustive-deps?

No - `useMemo` has its own dependency array. Effects that read memoized values still need those values (or their deps) listed on the effect.

How do I test hook cleanup?

Use `renderHook` with `@testing-library/react-native`, unmount the hook, and assert listeners are removed (mock `AppState.addEventListener`). Strict Mode double-mount in dev helps surface missing cleanup during manual runs.

Can I use a global eslint override for screens?

Avoid folder-wide disables for `app/`. Route screens are where `useFocusEffect` and param-driven effects concentrate - they need lint most, not least.

Where do custom platform hooks fit?

Wrap `AppState`, NetInfo, and Keyboard in `use*` hooks with explicit parameters for closed-over values. See [Custom Hooks for UI Logic](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/custom-hooks-for-ui-logic/).

Dokumen: TypeScript Strict Mode
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/typescript-strict-mode/

# TypeScript Strict Mode

`strict: true` turns on the compiler checks that catch undefined route params, stale API shapes, and implicit `any` in native bridges - before Metro bundles a broken screen. On Expo SDK 57, you extend `expo/tsconfig.base` and tighten incrementally instead of fighting a thousand-error wall.

Highlights / TypeScript Strict Mode

* Extend expo/tsconfig.base - SDK 57 already sets jsx and moduleResolution Metro expects
* strict: true enables eight checks; noUncheckedIndexedAccess is separate and high-value for RN
* Type route params and API JSON at boundaries - not every StyleSheet line at once
* npx tsc --noEmit in CI catches cross-file breaks ESLint cannot see
* Enable strictNullChecks first when tightening a brownfield app
* Pair compiler strictness with @typescript-eslint/no-floating-promises for async screens

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
# Verify types without emitting JS (CI-friendly)
npx tsc --noEmit
 
# Track remaining errors while migrating
npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | rg "error TS" | wc -l
```

```json
// tsconfig.json - Expo SDK 57 baseline
{
  "extends": "expo/tsconfig.base",
  "compilerOptions": {
    "strict": true,
    "noUncheckedIndexedAccess": true
  },
  "include": ["**/*.ts", "**/*.tsx", ".expo/types/**/*.ts", "expo-env.d.ts"]
}
```

**When to reach for this:**

* New Expo TypeScript projects - keep `strict: true` from day one.
* Apps reading `useLocalSearchParams()` or push notification payloads without validation.
* API helpers that `JSON.parse` into typed objects without runtime checks.
* Brownfield migrations moving `.js` screens to `.tsx` without a feature freeze.
* CI gates that need to block merges when a shared hook change breaks distant screens.

## Working Example

```json
// tsconfig.json - production-shaped Expo app
{
  "extends": "expo/tsconfig.base",
  "compilerOptions": {
    "strict": true,
    "noUncheckedIndexedAccess": true,
    "noImplicitReturns": true,
    "noFallthroughCasesInSwitch": true,
    "verbatimModuleSyntax": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true
  },
  "include": ["**/*.ts", "**/*.tsx", ".expo/types/**/*.ts", "expo-env.d.ts"]
}
```

```json
// package.json scripts
{
  "scripts": {
    "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit",
    "lint": "expo lint"
  }
}
```

```tsx
// app/orders/[id].tsx - strictNullChecks + typed route params
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { ActivityIndicator, Text, View, StyleSheet } from "react-native";
import { useLocalSearchParams } from "expo-router";
 
import { fetchOrder, type Order } from "@/lib/api/orders";
 
type OrderParams = {
  id: string;
};
 
function parseOrderParams(raw: Record<string, string | string[] | undefined>): OrderParams {
  const value = raw.id;
  const id = Array.isArray(value) ? value[0] : value;
  if (!id) {
    throw new Error("Missing route param: id");
  }
  return { id };
}
 
export default function OrderDetailScreen() {
  const params = useLocalSearchParams();
  const { id } = parseOrderParams(params);
 
  const [order, setOrder] = useState<Order | null>(null);
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);
 
  useEffect(() => {
    let cancelled = false;
 
    fetchOrder(id)
      .then((data) => {
        if (!cancelled) setOrder(data);
      })
      .catch((err: unknown) => {
        if (!cancelled) {
          setError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : "Failed to load order");
        }
      });
 
    return () => {
      cancelled = true;
    };
  }, [id]);
 
  if (error) {
    return (
      <View style={styles.center}>
        <Text style={styles.error}>{error}</Text>
      </View>
    );
  }
 
  if (!order) {
    return (
      <View style={styles.center}>
        <ActivityIndicator />
      </View>
    );
  }
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.screen}>
      <Text style={styles.title}>Order {order.id}</Text>
      <Text>Status: {order.status}</Text>
      <Text>Total: ${(order.totalCents / 100).toFixed(2)}</Text>
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  screen: { flex: 1, padding: 16 },
  center: { flex: 1, alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "center" },
  title: { fontSize: 20, fontWeight: "600" },
  error: { color: "#dc2626" },
});
```

```ts
// lib/api/orders.ts - unknown at the boundary, typed after validation
import { z } from "zod";
 
const OrderSchema = z.object({
  id: z.string(),
  totalCents: z.number().int().nonnegative(),
  status: z.enum(["pending", "shipped", "delivered"]),
});
 
export type Order = z.infer<typeof OrderSchema>;
 
export async function fetchOrder(id: string): Promise<Order> {
  const res = await fetch(`https://api.example.com/orders/${id}`);
  if (!res.ok) {
    throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);
  }
  const json: unknown = await res.json();
  return OrderSchema.parse(json);
}
```

```ts
// components/TagList.tsx - noUncheckedIndexedAccess in action
import { Text, View, StyleSheet } from "react-native";
 
const TAGS = ["mobile", "expo", "typescript"] as const;
 
export function TagList() {
  const first = TAGS[0]; // type: "mobile" | "typescript" | "expo" | undefined
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.row}>
      {first ? <Text style={styles.chip}>{first}</Text> : <Text>No tags</Text>}
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  row: { flexDirection: "row", gap: 8 },
  chip: { paddingHorizontal: 8, paddingVertical: 4, backgroundColor: "#e2e8f0", borderRadius: 6 },
});
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* `expo/tsconfig.base` supplies SDK-correct `jsx` and `moduleResolution`; you add strict flags on top.
* Route params are parsed once at the screen boundary - `useLocalSearchParams()` is not trusted blindly.
* API responses flow through `unknown` → Zod → `Order`, satisfying `strictNullChecks` without `as Order`.
* `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` forces a guard before using `TAGS[0]`.
* `typecheck` script runs the same command locally and in CI.

## Deep Dive

### How It Works

* `"strict": true` is an umbrella flag enabling `strictNullChecks`, `noImplicitAny`, `strictFunctionTypes`, and five related checks.
* Flags like `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` are **not** part of `strict` - enable them explicitly when you want stricter indexed access.
* `tsc --noEmit` typechecks the whole project graph; one broken export in `packages/ui` fails every consumer.
* Expo generates route types under `.expo/types` when typed routes are enabled - include that path in `tsconfig.json`.
* ESLint catches patterns (`react-hooks/exhaustive-deps`); TypeScript catches impossible types - both belong in quality gates.

### Strict Flags at a Glance

| Option | What it catches in RN apps |
| --- | --- |
| `strictNullChecks` | Undefined route params, optional API fields, `user?.name` gaps |
| `noImplicitAny` | Untyped event handlers, `fetch` results, legacy `.js` imports |
| `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` | `array[i]` and `record[key]` without guards |
| `noImplicitReturns` | Screen components that sometimes return `undefined` instead of `null` |
| `verbatimModuleSyntax` | Value/type import mix-ups that confuse Metro tree-shaking |
| `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` | Distinguishes "missing" vs "explicitly undefined" props - strict; optional |

### Incremental Enablement

```json
// Phase 1 - highest ROI per error fixed (brownfield)
{
  "extends": "expo/tsconfig.base",
  "compilerOptions": {
    "allowJs": true,
    "strict": false,
    "strictNullChecks": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true
  },
  "include": ["**/*.ts", "**/*.tsx", "**/*.js", ".expo/types/**/*.ts", "expo-env.d.ts"]
}
```

```json
// Phase 2 - flip the umbrella when Phase 1 is clean
{
  "extends": "expo/tsconfig.base",
  "compilerOptions": {
    "strict": true,
    "noUncheckedIndexedAccess": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true
  },
  "include": ["**/*.ts", "**/*.tsx", ".expo/types/**/*.ts", "expo-env.d.ts"]
}
```

| Phase | Enable | Stop when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `strictNullChecks` | `tsc` errors trend to zero in `app/` and `lib/` |
| 2 | `noImplicitAny` | Legacy `.js` is migrated or shimmed |
| 3 | `strict: true` | Remaining individual strict flags are clean |
| 4 | `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` | Indexed access sites have guards or helpers |

### TypeScript Notes

```tsx
// Prefer import type for types-only - verbatimModuleSyntax enforces clarity
import type { Order } from "@/lib/api/orders";
import { fetchOrder } from "@/lib/api/orders";
 
// StyleProp<ViewStyle> for components accepting style overrides
import type { StyleProp, ViewStyle } from "react-native";
 
interface CardProps {
  title: string;
  style?: StyleProp<ViewStyle>;
}
```

```ts
// Temporary suppression - prefer @ts-expect-error with a ticket over @ts-ignore
// @ts-expect-error RN-204 - LegacyDeviceModule untyped until bridge wrapper lands
const reading = NativeModules.LegacyDeviceModule.getLastReading();
```

## Gotchas

* **Disabling `strict` to green CI** - The build passes while `any` leaks into navigation and fetch layers. **Fix:** Fix boundaries first; use `@ts-expect-error` with ticket IDs for known legacy gaps.
* **`noUncheckedIndexedAccess` noise on safe indexes** - Every `items[0]` becomes `T | undefined`. **Fix:** Narrow with `if (item)`, use `.at(0)` with a guard, or a small `function first<T>(arr: T[]): T | undefined` helper - avoid blanket `!` assertions.
* **Untyped `useLocalSearchParams()`** - Deep links deliver strings; missing keys become `undefined` at runtime. **Fix:** Parse params in one function per screen; throw or redirect when required keys are absent.
* **`skipLibCheck: false` during SDK upgrades** - Conflicts inside `@types/react` and RN typings block merges unrelated to your code. **Fix:** Keep `skipLibCheck: true` (Expo default) unless you maintain custom DefinitelyTyped forks.
* **`tsc` not seeing Expo Router types** - Generated files live under `.expo/types`. **Fix:** Add `.expo/types/**/*.ts` to `include` and run `npx expo customize tsconfig.json` after enabling typed routes.
* **Type-aware ESLint rules without `parserOptions.project`** - Rules like `@typescript-eslint/no-floating-promises` silently skip or error. **Fix:** Point ESLint at `tsconfig.json` or run those rules only in a dedicated CI job.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| JavaScript + JSDoc `@ts-check` | Tiny Expo module or config-only package | App code with navigation, async storage, and API layers |
| `strict: false` + Zod only at runtime | Prototyping with heavy `any` tolerance | You need compile-time guarantees on refactors |
| [Gradual Typing in Brownfield Apps](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/typescript-rn/gradual-typing-in-brownfield-apps/) | Large `.js` codebase mid-migration | Greenfield SDK 57 app - start strict immediately |
| Flow or PropTypes | Legacy RN codebase already on Flow | New Expo TypeScript project - TS is the default template |

## FAQs

Does Expo SDK 57 enable strict mode by default?

* The `blank-typescript` and `default@sdk-57` templates extend `expo/tsconfig.base` with `strict: true`.
* Verify your `tsconfig.json` after ejecting or merging branches - brownfield apps often ship with `strict: false`.

What is the difference between strict and noUncheckedIndexedAccess?

* `strict` is an umbrella of eight compiler options.
* `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` is separate - array and index-signature access becomes `T | undefined`.
* Enable it when you want safer list and map access in screens and reducers.

Should I run tsc or rely on expo lint?

* `expo lint` runs ESLint - fast, per-file, great for hooks and imports.
* `tsc --noEmit` validates the whole type graph - catches broken exports across packages.
* Run both in CI; they overlap minimally.

How do I enable strict mode incrementally?

1. Turn on `strictNullChecks` only.
2. Fix errors folder by folder (`lib/`, then `app/`).
3. Enable `noImplicitAny`, then `strict: true`.
4. Add `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` last.

See [Gradual Typing in Brownfield Apps](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/typescript-rn/gradual-typing-in-brownfield-apps/).

Gotcha: Why do I get errors after adding typed Expo Router routes?

* Typed routes generate `.expo/types/router.d.ts`.
* Without that path in `include`, param types stay `string | string[]`.
* Run `npx expo start` once to regenerate types, then `tsc --noEmit`.

Does strict mode slow Metro?

* Typechecking is separate from Metro bundling - `tsc` runs in CI and editor, not on every fast refresh.
* Type-aware ESLint rules are slower; keep them in CI if editor performance suffers.

When should I use @ts-expect-error vs any?

* `@ts-expect-error` on the **next line** with a ticket comment - fails when the error is fixed (good).
* `any` propagates and disables checking downstream (bad).
* Prefer typed wrappers around native modules instead of either when possible.

How do TextInput strings interact with strict typing?

* `TextInput` values are always `string`.
* Use `z.coerce.number()` or explicit `parseInt` before numeric comparison.
* See [Validation with Zod](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/forms-input/validation-with-zod/).

Is exactOptionalPropertyTypes worth enabling?

* It breaks `{ foo?: string }` assignments of `undefined` unless types distinguish missing vs undefined.
* Most RN apps skip it - enable only if your API models require that distinction.

What belongs in include for an Expo Router app?

```json
"include": ["**/*.ts", "**/*.tsx", ".expo/types/**/*.ts", "expo-env.d.ts"]
```

* Add `**/*.js` only during brownfield migration with `allowJs: true`.

Can monorepo packages share one strict tsconfig?

* Yes - `packages/typescript-config/base.json` extended by `apps/mobile` and `packages/ui`.
* See [Monorepo with Turborepo](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/monorepo-with-turborepo/).

Which ESLint rules complement strict tsconfig?

```js
"@typescript-eslint/no-floating-promises": "error",
"@typescript-eslint/no-misused-promises": "error",
"react-hooks/exhaustive-deps": "warn",
```

* Type-aware `@typescript-eslint/*` rules need `parserOptions.project` pointing at your `tsconfig.json`.

Dokumen: Lists Best Practices
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/lists-scrolling/best-practices/

# Lists Best Practices

A condensed summary of the 25 most important best practices drawn from every page in this section.

Highlights / Lists Best Practices

* Use ScrollView only for short static content; virtualize feeds with FlatList or FlashList
* Stable string keys from server ids - never index keys on sorted or filtered lists
* Memoize row components and stabilize renderItem with useCallback
* Provide getItemLayout when row height is fixed - skips measurement jank
* Guard onEndReached with loading flags and cursor exhaustion
* Set estimatedItemSize when adopting FlashList on SDK 57

1. **Choose ScrollView for small static content:** Fewer than ~20 non-growing items with mixed layout types - once the list grows or paginates, switch to virtualization.
2. **Default to FlatList for feeds:** `FlatList` recycles rows off-screen - mapping hundreds of items inside `ScrollView` allocates every row in memory and blocks the JS thread.
3. **Evaluate FlashList for heavy feeds:** On SDK 57, Shopify FlashList improves recycling throughput when profiles show frame drops - migrate with `estimatedItemSize` and a measured migration checklist.
4. **Keys must be stable strings:** `keyExtractor` should return server ids - index keys break selection, animation, and state when items sort, filter, or paginate.
5. **Never key on array index for dynamic data:** `key={index}` causes wrong row content to flash during insert/delete - users see likes jump between posts.
6. **Extract `renderItem` to a memoized row:** Inline `renderItem` closures recreate every parent render - `const Row = memo(function Row…)` plus stable `useCallback` handler.
7. **Pass `extraData` when selection drives UI:** Without `extraData`, `FlatList` may skip re-rendering visible rows after `selectedId` changes - pass the minimal state slice that affects row appearance.
8. **Hoist list styles to StyleSheet:** Fresh `contentContainerStyle={{ padding: 16 }}` on every parent render invalidates list optimizations - cache wrapper styles.
9. **Use `getItemLayout` for fixed-height rows:** Inbox and settings rows with uniform height skip async measurement - scrolling to index becomes instant.
10. **Do not lie to `getItemLayout`:** Wrong `length` or `offset` produces blank gaps and jumpy scroll - measure once in design review and keep height in sync with separators.
11. **Separate empty and loading states:** `ListEmptyComponent` should not spin forever - branch `ListEmptyComponent` vs `ListFooterComponent` skeletons while the first page loads.
12. **Pull-to-refresh resets pagination:** `onRefresh` should clear cursor state and refetch page one - appending to a stale cursor after refresh duplicates items.
13. **Guard `onEndReached`:** Fire only when `!isFetching && hasNextPage` - otherwise momentum scroll triggers duplicate page fetches at the bottom.
14. **Show footer skeletons for pagination:** A small loading row at `ListFooterComponent` beats a full-screen spinner for page two - users keep context on the feed.
15. **Precompute SectionList sections in `useMemo`:** Grouping hundreds of items in render allocates every pass - derive `sections` when source data or sort order changes.
16. **Use sticky headers intentionally:** `stickySectionHeadersEnabled` helps alphabet lists - disable when headers overlap complex hero content at the top.
17. **Enable `nestedScrollEnabled` for horizontal rails:** Vertical feed + horizontal shelf needs explicit nested scroll on Android - test gesture handoff on real devices.
18. **Avoid vertical FlatList inside vertical ScrollView:** Double scroll containers fight gestures and break virtualization - one axis should own scrolling; use horizontal inner lists only.
19. **Tune `windowSize` after profiling:** Lower `windowSize` reduces memory; too low causes blank rows during fast flings - start with defaults, adjust with Flashlight or RN DevTools.
20. **Set FlashList `estimatedItemSize` close to reality:** Estimates far from measured height cause layout thrash and blank frames - measure average row height from production content.
21. **Avoid anonymous functions in `renderItem`:** `onPress={() => toggle(item.id)}` inside rows defeats `memo` - pass `id` to rows that call stable handlers.
22. **Validate dynamic row heights:** Variable-height rows without measurement cause virtualization to mount wrong content - use FlashList `overrideItemLayout` or accept non-virtualized sections.
23. **Test rotation and font scaling on lists:** Larger accessibility fonts change row height - fixed `getItemLayout` may need dynamic measurement or updated constants.
24. **Scroll to top on tab re-tap via ref:** Expose `flatListRef.current?.scrollToOffset({ offset: 0 })` from navigation events - feed apps expect this behavior.
25. **Run the virtualization gotchas checklist before release:** Walk keys, heights, empty states, and nested scroll cases on a low-end Android device - simulators hide blank-row bugs.

## FAQs

When is ScrollView still the right choice?

* Settings screens with ~10 heterogeneous rows (toggles, text, links) that never paginate.
* Legal copy or onboarding with mixed blocks, not a homogeneous data array.

FlatList or FlashList for a new Expo SDK 57 app?

* Start with `FlatList` until profiling proves jank on target devices.
* Adopt FlashList when feed scroll FPS drops or team already standardized on Shopify's package.

What is the most common shipping bug in feeds?

* Unstable keys combined with optimistic updates - rows show wrong avatars or counts after mutations.

Should infinite scroll use offset or cursor pagination?

* Prefer opaque cursors from the API - offset pagination breaks when items insert at the top of the feed.

How do I fix blank rows while scrolling fast?

* Check `getItemLayout` accuracy, increase `windowSize` slightly, or improve FlashList `estimatedItemSize` - blanks are almost always height math, not "React being slow."

Dokumen: FlashList vs FlatList
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/lists-scrolling/flashlist-vs-flatlist/

# FlashList vs FlatList

Shopify FlashList trade-offs, recycling, and migration checklist - when the default list is not fast enough.

Highlights / FlashList vs FlatList

* FlashList recycles a small pool of views - FlatList mounts more off-screen rows
* estimatedItemSize is required - wrong estimates cause scroll jump and blank gaps
* Drop-in migration: swap import, add estimatedItemSize, audit variable row heights
* FlashList shines on image-heavy feeds and fast scroll - overkill for short settings lists
* drawDistance tunes how far ahead rows are pre-rendered

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```tsx
import { FlashList } from "@shopify/flash-list";
import { StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
interface Post {
  id: string;
  title: string;
}
 
const ESTIMATED_ROW_HEIGHT = 88;
 
export function PostFeed({ posts }: { posts: Post[] }) {
  return (
    <FlashList
      data={posts}
      estimatedItemSize={ESTIMATED_ROW_HEIGHT}
      keyExtractor={(item) => item.id}
      renderItem={({ item }) => (
        <View style={styles.row}>
          <Text style={styles.title} numberOfLines={2}>
            {item.title}
          </Text>
        </View>
      )}
      ItemSeparatorComponent={() => <View style={styles.separator} />}
    />
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  row: { paddingHorizontal: 16, paddingVertical: 12, backgroundColor: "#fff" },
  title: { fontSize: 16, fontWeight: "600", color: "#0f172a" },
  separator: { height: 8 },
});
```

**When to reach for this:** Image-heavy feeds, chat timelines, or any list where profiling shows frame drops during fast scroll on mid-range Android devices.

## Working Example

```tsx
import { memo, useCallback } from "react";
import { FlashList } from "@shopify/flash-list";
import { Image, StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
interface Product {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  price: string;
  imageUrl: string;
}
 
const PRODUCTS: Product[] = Array.from({ length: 200 }, (_, i) => ({
  id: `p-${i}`,
  name: `Product ${i + 1}`,
  price: `$${(9.99 + (i % 50)).toFixed(2)}`,
  imageUrl: `https://picsum.photos/seed/${i}/120/120`,
}));
 
const ESTIMATED_ROW_HEIGHT = 96;
 
const ProductRow = memo(function ProductRow({ item }: { item: Product }) {
  return (
    <View style={styles.row}>
      <Image source={{ uri: item.imageUrl }} style={styles.thumb} />
      <View style={styles.meta}>
        <Text style={styles.name} numberOfLines={1}>
          {item.name}
        </Text>
        <Text style={styles.price}>{item.price}</Text>
      </View>
    </View>
  );
});
 
export default function ProductFeedScreen() {
  const renderItem = useCallback(
    ({ item }: { item: Product }) => <ProductRow item={item} />,
    [],
  );
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.screen}>
      <FlashList
        data={PRODUCTS}
        estimatedItemSize={ESTIMATED_ROW_HEIGHT}
        keyExtractor={(item) => item.id}
        renderItem={renderItem}
        drawDistance={250}
        contentContainerStyle={styles.list}
      />
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  screen: { flex: 1, backgroundColor: "#f8fafc" },
  list: { paddingVertical: 8 },
  row: {
    flexDirection: "row",
    alignItems: "center",
    gap: 12,
    paddingHorizontal: 16,
    paddingVertical: 10,
    backgroundColor: "#fff",
    minHeight: ESTIMATED_ROW_HEIGHT,
  },
  thumb: { width: 72, height: 72, borderRadius: 8, backgroundColor: "#e2e8f0" },
  meta: { flex: 1 },
  name: { fontSize: 16, fontWeight: "600", color: "#0f172a" },
  price: { fontSize: 14, color: "#2563eb", marginTop: 4 },
});
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* `estimatedItemSize` set to the typical row height - required for FlashList layout math.
* `minHeight` on the row aligns rendered size with the estimate for stable scroll.
* `memo` on `ProductRow` pairs with view recycling - rows must tolerate reuse without stale state.
* `drawDistance={250}` pre-renders slightly ahead of the viewport to reduce blank flashes during fast flick scroll.
* Same `keyExtractor` / `renderItem` patterns as `FlatList` - migration is mostly prop additions.

## Deep Dive

### How It Works

* **FlatList** virtualizes by mounting/unmounting row subtrees as they enter and leave the render window. Fast scroll can still allocate many views per second.
* **FlashList** maintains a **recycled pool** of row containers - new data is bound to existing native views instead of creating fresh trees each time.
* FlashList needs `estimatedItemSize` because it lays out content **before** every row is measured - the estimate drives offset calculations until real measurement arrives.
* Wrong estimates cause **scroll jump** (content shifts when true height differs) or brief **blank gaps** during fast scroll.
* FlashList supports the same mental model: `data`, `renderItem`, `keyExtractor`, separators, headers, `onEndReached`.
* Under the hood, FlashList still runs on React Native's scroll infrastructure - it is not a separate native list implementation.

### FlatList vs FlashList

| Aspect | FlatList | FlashList |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Recycling | Mount/unmount rows | Rebinds a fixed pool of views |
| Size hint | Optional `getItemLayout` | Required `estimatedItemSize` |
| Variable height | Works; remeasures as needed | Works; tune estimate + `overrideItemLayout` |
| Bundle | Built into RN | `@shopify/flash-list` dependency |
| API surface | Superset (mature) | Near drop-in; some prop differences |
| Best fit | Short/medium lists, settings | Long feeds, images, chat, marketplace grids |

### Migration Checklist

1. **Install:** `npx expo install @shopify/flash-list`
2. **Swap import:** `FlatList` → `FlashList` from `@shopify/flash-list`
3. **Add `estimatedItemSize`:** Measure a typical row in DevTools or design specs (include padding).
4. **Audit row components:** Remove local state that survives recycling; derive UI from `item` props only.
5. **Match min heights:** Set `minHeight` or fixed height close to the estimate when possible.
6. **Variable heights:** Use `overrideItemLayout` per item type or separate lists per layout variant.
7. **Test fast scroll:** Flick-scroll on a low-end Android device; watch for blanks and jump.
8. **Re-test `onEndReached`:** Threshold behavior is similar but verify pagination guards.
9. **Section lists:** Use `FlashList` with sticky headers or keep `SectionList` until you need the perf win.
10. **Profile before/after:** React Native DevTools performance monitor or `console.time` around scroll sessions.

```tsx
// Before
import { FlatList } from "react-native";
<FlatList data={items} renderItem={...} keyExtractor={...} />
 
// After
import { FlashList } from "@shopify/flash-list";
<FlashList
  data={items}
  estimatedItemSize={72}
  renderItem={...}
  keyExtractor={...}
/>
```

### Tuning Props

| Prop | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `estimatedItemSize` | Average row height in dp - required |
| `drawDistance` | Pixels beyond viewport to pre-render (default ~250) |
| `overrideItemLayout` | Per-index size override for heterogeneous rows |
| `estimatedListSize` | `{ height, width }` when list size is known early |
| `getItemType` | Return a type string so recycling pools separate layouts |

```tsx
<FlashList
  data={items}
  estimatedItemSize={120}
  getItemType={(item) => (item.pinned ? "pinned" : "normal")}
  overrideItemLayout={(layout, item) => {
    layout.size = item.pinned ? 160 : 96;
  }}
  renderItem={renderItem}
/>
```

### Recycling Gotchas

* Recycled rows **reuse the same component instance** - `useState` inside a row can show the previous item's state for a frame.
* Side effects in `useEffect` without proper deps fire on the wrong item.
* **Fix:** Keep row state in `item` data or parent maps (`expandedIds`); rows should be pure functions of props.

### TypeScript Notes

```tsx
import type { FlashListProps, ListRenderItem } from "@shopify/flash-list";
 
interface Article {
  id: string;
  headline: string;
}
 
type ArticleListProps = Pick<
  FlashListProps<Article>,
  "data" | "onEndReached" | "refreshing" | "onRefresh"
> & {
  onPress: (article: Article) => void;
};
 
function ArticleList({ data, onPress, ...rest }: ArticleListProps) {
  const renderItem: ListRenderItem<Article> = useCallback(
    ({ item }) => <ArticleRow article={item} onPress={() => onPress(item)} />,
    [onPress],
  );
 
  return (
    <FlashList
      data={data}
      estimatedItemSize={104}
      keyExtractor={(item) => item.id}
      renderItem={renderItem}
      {...rest}
    />
  );
}
```

* Import types from `@shopify/flash-list`, not `react-native`.
* `FlashListProps<T>` mirrors `FlatListProps<T>` for most list props.

### Parameters & Return Values

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `estimatedItemSize` | `number` | Average item height in density-independent pixels - **required** |
| `data` | `readonly T[]` | Source array (same as FlatList) |
| `renderItem` | `ListRenderItem<T>` | Row renderer - must be stable for recycling |
| `drawDistance` | `number` | Pre-render distance beyond viewport edges |
| `overrideItemLayout` | `(layout, item, index) => void` | Set `layout.size` for known per-item heights |
| `getItemType` | `(item, index) => string` | Separates recycle pools per layout variant |

## Gotchas

* **Missing `estimatedItemSize`** - FlashList warns and falls back to poor layout guesses; scroll feels broken. **Fix:** Always set it; measure real rows in the simulator.
* **Estimate far from reality** - A 200px estimate on 80px rows causes jump when measurement corrects. **Fix:** Measure p50 row height; use `overrideItemLayout` for outliers.
* **Stateful row components** - `useState` for "liked" inside the row shows the previous item's like state after recycle. **Fix:** Store interaction state in parent/`item` or `extraData` maps.
* **Migrating without `memo`** - Recycling magnifies unnecessary re-renders inside rows. **Fix:** `memo` row components; stable `renderItem` with `useCallback`.
* **Using FlashList for 10 settings rows** - Extra dependency and tuning for no measurable gain. **Fix:** Keep `FlatList` or `ScrollView` until profiling proves need.
* **Ignoring image dimensions** - Images loading async change row height after first layout, causing jump on both list types; worse when estimate is wrong. **Fix:** Fixed `width`/`height` on `Image`, placeholder background, or known aspect ratio.
* **Assuming 100% API parity** - Some edge props differ; test `ListHeaderComponent`, `numColumns`, and nested scroll. **Fix:** Read `@shopify/flash-list` docs for your version; run migration checklist on device.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `FlatList` | Default lists, settings, < 100 rows, no perf complaints | Profiling shows scroll jank on target devices |
| `FlashList` | Long feeds, images, chat, marketplace | Trivial lists where bundle size matters more |
| `SectionList` | Grouped data with sticky section headers | Single-type flat feed - FlashList is simpler |
| `Legend List` / other community lists | Evaluating alternatives to FlashList | You want Shopify-maintained Expo compatibility first |
| `ScrollView` + `map` | Very short static content | Any list that scrolls for seconds at 60 fps |

## FAQs

Is FlashList a drop-in replacement for FlatList?

Nearly - swap the import, add `estimatedItemSize`, and audit row components for recycling safety. Most props (`data`, `renderItem`, `keyExtractor`, `onEndReached`, refresh) work the same. Test your specific header/footer and multi-column layouts.

Why is estimatedItemSize required?

FlashList positions rows before all are measured. The estimate drives scroll offset math until each row's true height is known. Without it, the list cannot virtualize efficiently.

How do I pick the right estimatedItemSize?

Measure a typical rendered row in the layout inspector, including padding and separators. Use the median height if rows vary slightly. For mixed types, use `getItemType` + `overrideItemLayout`.

What is view recycling?

Instead of destroying a row view when it scrolls off screen, FlashList rebinds it to a new item's data. The same native view tree is reused - like `UITableView` cell reuse on iOS. Row components must not hold stale local state.

Does FlashList work with Expo?

Yes - `npx expo install @shopify/flash-list` pins a compatible version for your SDK. No custom native code required in standard Expo workflows.

FlatList or FlashList for SectionList-style data?

FlashList supports sticky headers and heterogeneous layouts, but `SectionList` is still the ergonomic choice for `{ title, data }` grouping. Migrate item rendering to FlashList patterns when the flat feed is the bottleneck.

What is drawDistance?

Distance in pixels beyond the visible viewport where FlashList pre-renders items. Higher values reduce blank flashes during fast scroll at the cost of more work per frame. Default is usually fine; raise on image-heavy feeds if you see flicker.

Can I use getItemLayout with FlashList?

FlashList uses `estimatedItemSize` and `overrideItemLayout` instead. `overrideItemLayout` lets you set per-index `layout.size` when heights are known without measuring.

Does FlashList support numColumns?

Yes - grid layouts are supported. Set `numColumns` and ensure `estimatedItemSize` reflects row height (not cell width). Test horizontal spacing and recycle pools for grid cells.

How do I fix scroll jumping?

* Bring `estimatedItemSize` closer to real height.
* Use fixed image dimensions.
* Set `minHeight` on rows.
* Use `overrideItemLayout` for known tall/short variants.

Should row components use memo?

Yes - especially with recycling. Combine `memo` on the row, stable `renderItem`, and props-only state. See [List Performance Tuning](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/lists-scrolling/list-performance-tuning/).

Does extraData exist on FlashList?

FlashList supports the same pattern - pass external state that affects row rendering so recycled views update when selection or theme changes.

When is FlatList actually faster?

For very short lists, FlatList avoids estimate tuning and the extra package. Measure - do not migrate preemptively.

Where is the full FlashList library reference?

See [@shopify/flash-list](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/essential-libraries/shopify-flash-list/) in Essential Libraries for install, config plugins, and advanced props.

How does FlashList interact with infinite scroll?

Same `onEndReached` / `onEndReachedThreshold` pattern as FlatList. Guard fetches with a loading ref. See [Infinite Scroll & Pagination](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/lists-scrolling/infinite-scroll-and-pagination/).
