Dokumen: Config Plugins
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/native-modules/config-plugins/

# Config Plugins

A cookbook for **`app.config` plugins** that modify `Info.plist`, `AndroidManifest.xml`, and Gradle - the CNG-safe way to wire native modules without manual drift in `ios/` and `android/`.

Highlights / Config Plugins

* Config plugins transform app.config into native project files during prebuild
* Permissions, entitlements, and manifest entries belong in plugins - not hand-edited ios/ or android/
* Plugin order matters when multiple plugins touch the same file - document ordering in comments
* Idempotent plugins survive npx expo prebuild --clean run twice with empty git diff
* Pair with Native Module Rules Tier 2 before merging any plugin change

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```ts
// app.config.ts
import type { ExpoConfig } from "expo/config";
 
export default ({ config }: { config: ExpoConfig }): ExpoConfig => ({
  ...config,
  plugins: [
    // Built-in permission plugins (Info.plist + AndroidManifest)
    [
      "expo-camera",
      {
        cameraPermission: "Allow $(PRODUCT_NAME) to scan product barcodes",
        microphonePermission: false,
      },
    ],
    // Build-time properties (Gradle, Podfile properties)
    [
      "expo-build-properties",
      {
        ios: { deploymentTarget: "15.1" },
        android: { minSdkVersion: 24, compileSdkVersion: 35 },
      },
    ],
    // Local plugin for custom native changes
    "./plugins/with-custom-url-scheme",
  ],
});
```

```bash
# Apply plugins and inspect output
npx expo prebuild --clean
git diff ios/ android/   # review generated native changes
 
# Idempotency check - second run should produce no new diff
npx expo prebuild
git diff ios/ android/   # expect empty
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Adding iOS usage descriptions (`NSCameraUsageDescription`) required by native modules.
* Registering Android permissions, intent filters, or `queries` entries for package visibility.
* Tweaking Gradle `minSdkVersion`, ProGuard rules, or iOS deployment targets for a native SDK.
* Shipping a custom native module that needs entitlements or manifest metadata.

## Working Example

### Built-in plugin: camera permissions

```ts
// app.config.ts
import type { ExpoConfig } from "expo/config";
 
export default ({ config }: { config: ExpoConfig }): ExpoConfig => ({
  ...config,
  name: "ConfigPluginCookbook",
  slug: "config-plugin-cookbook",
  plugins: [
    [
      "expo-camera",
      {
        cameraPermission:
          "Allow $(PRODUCT_NAME) to take photos for your profile",
        microphonePermission:
          "Allow $(PRODUCT_NAME) to record audio with video",
        recordAudioAndroid: true,
      },
    ],
  ],
});
```

After `npx expo prebuild`, iOS receives:

```xml
<!-- ios/<App>/Info.plist (generated) -->
<key>NSCameraUsageDescription</key>
<string>Allow ConfigPluginCookbook to take photos for your profile</string>
<key>NSMicrophoneUsageDescription</key>
<string>Allow ConfigPluginCookbook to record audio with video</string>
```

Android receives:

```xml
<!-- android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml (generated excerpt) -->
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.CAMERA" />
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.RECORD_AUDIO" />
```

### Local plugin: custom URL scheme + queries

```ts
// plugins/with-custom-url-scheme.ts
import type { ConfigPlugin } from "expo/config-plugins";
import {
  AndroidConfig,
  IOSConfig,
  createRunOncePlugin,
  withAndroidManifest,
  withInfoPlist,
} from "expo/config-plugins";
 
const SCHEME = "myshop";
 
const withCustomUrlScheme: ConfigPlugin = (config) => {
  config = withInfoPlist(config, (mod) => {
    const urlTypes = mod.modResults.CFBundleURLTypes ?? [];
    const exists = urlTypes.some(
      (entry) =>
        Array.isArray(entry.CFBundleURLSchemes) &&
        entry.CFBundleURLSchemes.includes(SCHEME)
    );
    if (!exists) {
      urlTypes.push({
        CFBundleURLName: "com.example.myshop",
        CFBundleURLSchemes: [SCHEME],
      });
      mod.modResults.CFBundleURLTypes = urlTypes;
    }
    return mod;
  });
 
  config = withAndroidManifest(config, (mod) => {
    const manifest = mod.modResults;
    const app = AndroidConfig.Manifest.getMainApplicationOrThrow(manifest);
 
    // Deep link intent filter
    AndroidConfig.Manifest.addIntentFilter(app, {
      action: "android.intent.action.VIEW",
      category: ["android.intent.category.DEFAULT", "android.intent.category.BROWSABLE"],
      data: [{ scheme: SCHEME }],
    });
 
    return mod;
  });
 
  return config;
};
 
export default createRunOncePlugin(withCustomUrlScheme, "with-custom-url-scheme", "1.0.0");
```

```ts
// app.config.ts - register local plugin
import type { ExpoConfig } from "expo/config";
 
export default ({ config }: { config: ExpoConfig }): ExpoConfig => ({
  ...config,
  plugins: ["./plugins/with-custom-url-scheme"],
});
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* **`withInfoPlist`** mutates iOS metadata idempotently - checks before appending URL types.
* **`withAndroidManifest`** adds intent filters without regex-append drift.
* **`createRunOncePlugin`** prevents duplicate application when prebuild runs multiple times.
* Changes survive **`npx expo prebuild --clean`** - the CNG contract per [Prebuild Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/prebuild-basics/).

### Gradle tweak via expo-build-properties

```ts
// app.config.ts excerpt - native SDK requires higher compileSdk
plugins: [
  [
    "expo-build-properties",
    {
      android: {
        minSdkVersion: 24,
        compileSdkVersion: 35,
        targetSdkVersion: 35,
        extraProguardRules: `
          -keep class com.vendor.sdk.** { *; }
        `,
      },
      ios: {
        deploymentTarget: "15.1",
        useFrameworks: "static",
      },
    },
  ],
],
```

See [Patching Native Projects](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/native-modules/patching-native-projects/) for advanced Gradle survival strategies.

## Deep Dive

### Plugin execution model

```
app.config.ts / app.json
        │
        ▼
  plugins: [ "expo-camera", "./plugins/with-custom-url-scheme" ]
        │
        ▼  (sequential, in array order)
  Mod plugins: withInfoPlist, withAndroidManifest, withGradleProperties, …
        │
        ▼
  ios/ android/ written to disk
```

| Mod helper | Target file | Typical use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `withInfoPlist` | `Info.plist` | Usage descriptions, URL schemes, background modes |
| `withAndroidManifest` | `AndroidManifest.xml` | Permissions, intent filters, `queries` |
| `withGradleProperties` | `gradle.properties` | JVM args, Android flags |
| `withAppBuildGradle` | `app/build.gradle` | Dependencies, packaging options |
| `withEntitlementsPlist` | `.entitlements` | Associated domains, push, keychain groups |

### Plugin ordering

When two plugins modify the same key, **later plugins win**. Document order in `app.config.ts`:

```ts
plugins: [
  "expo-router",           // Must run before plugins that add splash assets
  "expo-camera",           // Permissions first
  "./plugins/with-custom-url-scheme", // App-specific deep links after router
  [
    "expo-build-properties", // Build props last - may depend on prior structure
    { android: { minSdkVersion: 24 } },
  ],
],
```

### Static vs dynamic config

```ts
// app.config.ts - dynamic (env-aware)
import type { ExpoConfig } from "expo/config";
 
export default ({ config }: { config: ExpoConfig }): ExpoConfig => ({
  ...config,
  extra: {
    apiUrl: process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL,
  },
  plugins: [
    [
      "react-native-maps",
      {
        iosGoogleMapsApiKey: process.env.GOOGLE_MAPS_IOS_KEY ?? "",
      },
    ],
  ],
});
```

Secrets belong in **EAS environment variables**, not committed `.env` files referenced at prebuild time in CI.

### Debugging plugin output

```bash
# Verbose prebuild logs
EXPO_DEBUG=1 npx expo prebuild --clean
 
# Diff only Info.plist
npx expo prebuild --platform ios --clean
diff ios/MyApp/Info.plist ios/MyApp/Info.plist.bak 2>/dev/null || true
 
# Validate with doctor
npx expo-doctor
```

## Gotchas

* **Missing `NS*UsageDescription` strings** - iOS crashes at permission request time. **Fix:** Use the library's config plugin or add `withInfoPlist` entries.
* **Non-idempotent plugins** - second prebuild duplicates manifest entries. **Fix:** Check existence before push; use `createRunOncePlugin`.
* **Editing generated native files directly** - wiped on `--clean`. **Fix:** Move change into a plugin per [Config Plugins in CNG](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/config-plugins-in-cng/).
* **Wrong plugin order** - router or splash plugin overwritten. **Fix:** Reorder and re-run prebuild twice to verify idempotency.
* **Android 11+ package visibility** - implicit intent to external apps fails without `<queries>`. **Fix:** `withAndroidManifest` adds `queries` entries.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Built-in Expo config plugin | Library ships `expo-camera`, `expo-location`, etc. | Vendor lib has no plugin |
| Local `expo/config-plugins` mod | One-off entitlements or manifest entries | Large native fork - write proper Expo module |
| `expo-build-properties` | SDK versions, ProGuard, deployment target | Complex multi-file Gradle surgery |
| Brownfield manual native edits | Legacy app not on CNG | Standard SDK 57 greenfield apps |

## FAQs

What is a config plugin?

A function registered in `app.config` `plugins` array that runs during `npx expo prebuild` and modifies native project files programmatically.

Where do plugins live?

Built-in plugins ship inside Expo SDK packages (`expo-camera`, `expo-build-properties`). Custom plugins live in your repo - commonly `plugins/with-*.ts`.

Do plugins run in EAS Build?

Yes. EAS Build runs prebuild (unless disabled), executing the same plugin pipeline as local `npx expo prebuild`.

How do I test idempotency?

Run `npx expo prebuild` twice. `git diff ios/ android/` after the second run must be empty.

Plugin vs native module?

A **native module** implements runtime JS-to-native calls. A **config plugin** configures the native project so the module compiles and has permissions - they often ship together.

Dokumen: create-expo-module
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/native-modules/create-expo-module/

# create-expo-module

A cookbook for scaffolding a **local native module** with a typed TypeScript surface - the supported path when Expo SDK packages and third-party libraries do not cover your integration.

Highlights / create-expo-module

* npx create-expo-module@latest scaffolds Swift, Kotlin, and TypeScript in one package
* Local modules in modules/ autolink on prebuild - no manual Podfile edits in CNG apps
* Expo Modules API is JSI-first and supports New Architecture on RN 0.86
* Ship a config plugin alongside the module when permissions or entitlements are required
* Custom native modules require an ADR per Native Module Rules - document the owner

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
# From your Expo app root
npx create-expo-module@latest modules/attestation
 
# Answer prompts: module name, description, platforms (ios + android)
 
cd modules/attestation
npm install
npm run build   # compiles TypeScript surface
 
# Wire into the app (workspace or file dependency)
cd ../..
npm install ./modules/attestation
 
# Regenerate native projects
npx expo prebuild --clean
npx expo run:ios
```

```ts
// App usage after scaffold
import AttestationModule from "attestation";
 
const result = await AttestationModule.isDeviceTrustedAsync();
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Bridging a vendor SDK (fraud detection, proprietary scanner) with a thin native API.
* Exposing one or two platform APIs not covered by Expo SDK (e.g., custom Keychain access group).
* Sharing native code across multiple apps in a monorepo via `packages/attestation`.
* Prototyping before extracting a publishable npm package.

## Working Example

### 1. Scaffold the module

```bash
npx create-expo-app@latest AttestationApp --template blank-typescript@sdk-57 --yes
cd AttestationApp
npx create-expo-module@latest modules/device-trust
```

Typical output layout:

```text
AttestationApp/
├── app.json
├── package.json
├── App.tsx
└── modules/
    └── device-trust/
        ├── android/
        │   └── src/main/java/expo/modules/devicetrust/DeviceTrustModule.kt
        ├── ios/
        │   └── DeviceTrustModule.swift
        ├── src/
        │   ├── DeviceTrustModule.ts
        │   └── index.ts
        ├── expo-module.config.json
        └── package.json
```

### 2. Implement the native surface

```swift
// modules/device-trust/ios/DeviceTrustModule.swift
import ExpoModulesCore
 
public class DeviceTrustModule: Module {
  public func definition() -> ModuleDefinition {
    Name("DeviceTrust")
 
    AsyncFunction("isDeviceTrustedAsync") { () -> Bool in
      // Replace with DeviceCheck / App Attest integration
      #if targetEnvironment(simulator)
      return false
      #else
      return true
      #endif
    }
  }
}
```

```kotlin
// modules/device-trust/android/src/main/java/expo/modules/devicetrust/DeviceTrustModule.kt
package expo.modules.devicetrust
 
import expo.modules.kotlin.modules.Module
import expo.modules.kotlin.modules.ModuleDefinition
 
class DeviceTrustModule : Module() {
  override fun definition() = ModuleDefinition {
    Name("DeviceTrust")
 
    AsyncFunction("isDeviceTrustedAsync") {
      // Replace with Play Integrity API
      !Build.FINGERPRINT.contains("generic")
    }
  }
}
```

```ts
// modules/device-trust/src/DeviceTrustModule.ts
import { requireNativeModule } from "expo-modules-core";
 
type DeviceTrustModuleType = {
  isDeviceTrustedAsync: () => Promise<boolean>;
};
 
export default requireNativeModule<DeviceTrustModuleType>("DeviceTrust");
```

```ts
// modules/device-trust/src/index.ts
export { default } from "./DeviceTrustModule";
```

### 3. Link into the app

```json
// AttestationApp/package.json (excerpt)
{
  "dependencies": {
    "device-trust": "file:./modules/device-trust",
    "expo": "~57.0.4",
    "expo-dev-client": "~6.0.0",
    "react": "19.2.3",
    "react-native": "0.86.0"
  }
}
```

```tsx
// App.tsx
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { Button, StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
import DeviceTrust from "device-trust";
 
export default function App() {
  const [trusted, setTrusted] = useState<boolean | null>(null);
 
  useEffect(() => {
    DeviceTrust.isDeviceTrustedAsync().then(setTrusted);
  }, []);
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.container}>
      <Text style={styles.title}>Device Trust Module</Text>
      <Text>Trusted: {trusted === null ? "…" : trusted ? "yes" : "no"}</Text>
      <Button title="Re-check" onPress={() => DeviceTrust.isDeviceTrustedAsync().then(setTrusted)} />
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  container: { flex: 1, justifyContent: "center", padding: 24, gap: 8 },
  title: { fontSize: 20, fontWeight: "700" },
});
```

```bash
# Build module TS, prebuild, run
cd modules/device-trust && npm run build && cd ../..
npx expo install expo-dev-client
npx expo prebuild
npx expo run:ios
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* **`create-expo-module`** generates matching Swift/Kotlin/TypeScript skeletons with correct `Name("DeviceTrust")` registration.
* **`requireNativeModule`** loads the JSI binding after autolinking compiles native code.
* **`file:./modules/...` dependency** keeps the module local - publish later if reused across repos.
* **Development build** is required - custom modules are never in Expo Go.

### 4. Optional config plugin

If the module needs entitlements, add `app.plugin.js` inside the module package and register it in the app's `app.config.ts`. See [Config Plugins](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/native-modules/config-plugins/).

## Deep Dive

### expo-module.config.json

```json
{
  "platforms": ["ios", "android"],
  "ios": {
    "modules": ["DeviceTrustModule"]
  },
  "android": {
    "modules": ["expo.modules.devicetrust.DeviceTrustModule"]
  }
}
```

Autolinking reads this file during `npx expo prebuild` and wires Gradle/Pod entries - no manual linking in CNG apps.

### Monorepo placement

| Layout | Path | Dependency |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Single app | `modules/device-trust` | `"file:./modules/device-trust"` |
| Monorepo package | `packages/device-trust` | `"workspace:*"` in app `package.json` |
| Published npm | external registry | `"device-trust": "^1.0.0"` |

For monorepo autolinking nuances, see [Autolinking & expo-modules-core](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/native-modules/autolinking-and-expo-modules-core/).

### Module vs TurboModule

| Expo Module (`create-expo-module`) | RN TurboModule (Codegen) |
| --- | --- |
| Expo autolinking + config plugins | RN-first; manual Codegen setup |
| Swift/Kotlin `ModuleDefinition` DSL | C++/Java/ObjC with spec files |
| Best for SDK 57 Expo apps | Best for RN-core libraries without `expo` |

Most app teams should start with **Expo Modules API**. Reach for [Writing a TurboModule](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/native-modules/writing-a-turbomodule/) when sharing C++ across platforms or upstreaming to RN community.

### ADR requirement

Per [Native Module Rules](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/native-module-rules/), document:

* Why Expo SDK and third-party packages were insufficient
* Named maintainer and review cadence
* New Architecture test plan
* Config plugin ownership for permissions

## Gotchas

* **Forgetting `npm run build` in the module** - app imports stale `build/` output. **Fix:** Add `"prepare": "expo-module build"` or build in CI before app compile.
* **Mismatch between `Name("DeviceTrust")` and `requireNativeModule("DeviceTrust")`** - runtime throw. **Fix:** Keep names identical across Swift, Kotlin, and TS.
* **Testing in Expo Go** - custom module native code not present. **Fix:** Development build always.
* **Skipping prebuild after module scaffold** - Xcode project never references the module. **Fix:** `npx expo prebuild --clean`.
* **Fat native SDK in module repo** - bloated binaries and license risk. **Fix:** Thin bridge module; vendor SDK version pinned in ADR.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Expo SDK package | Feature exists upstream | Proprietary API |
| Third-party npm native lib | Maintained community bridge | Unmaintained or no New Arch |
| Expo Module (this page) | Thin custom bridge in Expo app | Heavy C++ shared core |
| TurboModule + Codegen | RN ecosystem library | Standard Expo CNG app integration |

## FAQs

Does create-expo-module work outside Expo apps?

Yes, in bare React Native apps with `expo-modules-core` installed via `npx install-expo-modules`. Expo prebuild is still the easiest wiring path.

Can I put the module inside packages/ in a monorepo?

Yes. Use `workspace:*` and enable `autolinkingModuleResolution` - see autolinking page.

How do I add events from native to JS?

Use `Events("onTrustChanged")` in `ModuleDefinition` and `EventEmitter` on the JS side - same pattern as `expo-sensors`.

Do I need a config plugin?

Only when the module requires permissions, entitlements, Gradle dependencies, or manifest metadata not covered by autolinking defaults.

How do I publish the module to npm?

Complete the scaffold, add README and tests, run `npm publish` from `modules/device-trust`. Consumers `npx expo install device-trust` and register any plugin.

## Related

* [Native Modules Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/native-modules/native-modules-basics/) - when native code is required
* [Config Plugins](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/native-modules/config-plugins/) - permissions for custom modules
* [Autolinking & expo-modules-core](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/native-modules/autolinking-and-expo-modules-core/) - monorepo linking
* [Writing a TurboModule](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/native-modules/writing-a-turbomodule/) - Codegen alternative

## [Config Plugins](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/native-modules/config-plugins/)

* Config plugins transform app.config into native project files during prebuild
* Permissions, entitlements, and manifest entries belong in plugins - not hand-edited ios/ or android/
* Plugin order matters when multiple plugins touch the same file - document ordering in comments
* Idempotent plugins survive npx expo prebuild --clean run twice with empty git diff
* Pair with Native Module Rules Tier 2 before merging any plugin change

## [create-expo-module](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/native-modules/create-expo-module/)

* npx create-expo-module@latest scaffolds Swift, Kotlin, and TypeScript in one package
* Local modules in modules/ autolink on prebuild - no manual Podfile edits in CNG apps
* Expo Modules API is JSI-first and supports New Architecture on RN 0.86
* Ship a config plugin alongside the module when permissions or entitlements are required
* Custom native modules require an ADR per Native Module Rules - document the owner

## [Autolinking & expo-modules-core](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/native-modules/autolinking-and-expo-modules-core/)

* expo-modules-autolinking scans dependencies at build time and wires Gradle/Pod entries
* SDK 55+ enables autolinkingModuleResolution so Metro and native link the same copy
* Duplicate react-native in monorepos breaks autolinking - run pnpm why react-native
* requireNativeModule queries the JSI host object populated at native launch
* npx expo-modules-autolinking resolve debugs missing modules before Xcode/Gradle fails

## [Writing a TurboModule](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/native-modules/writing-a-turbomodule/)

* TurboModules use Codegen specs for typed JSI bindings on RN 0.86 New Architecture
* Prefer Expo Modules API for app-local bridges - TurboModules suit RN-ecosystem libraries
* Spec files live in src/Native\*.ts and generate C++, Java, and ObjC++ stubs
* Synchronous methods are allowed on TurboModules - validate thread constraints in native code
* Test on device with New Architecture enabled - bridge fallback hides sync API bugs

## [Patching Native Projects](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/native-modules/patching-native-projects/)

* expo-build-properties is the supported knob for SDK versions, ProGuard, and deployment targets
* CNG apps express Gradle/Pod changes as config - hand-edited ios/ and android/ die on prebuild --clean
* patch-package is a last resort for node\_modules native fixes - document removal path
* Run npx expo prebuild twice after plugin changes to verify idempotency before merge
* SDK upgrade survival means re-validating every plugin and build property against release notes

## [Native Modules Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/native-modules/best-practices/)

* Search Expo SDK packages and config plugins before writing Swift or Kotlin
* npx expo install pins native-compatible versions - manual npm install causes runtime crashes
* Express native changes as idempotent config plugins, not hand-edited ios/ or android/
* Expo Go cannot load arbitrary native code - use expo-dev-client for third-party and custom modules
* Rebuild dev clients and store binaries after every native dependency or SDK change

Dokumen: Native Modules Basics
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/native-modules/native-modules-basics/

# Native Modules Basics

Ten examples for when JavaScript-only solutions fail and you must cross the **native boundary** - the foundation every Expo SDK 57 team needs before adding third-party libraries, config plugins, or custom modules.

Highlights / Native Modules Basics

* Native modules bridge JavaScript to Swift, Kotlin, and C++ via JSI on RN 0.86
* Expo SDK packages are native modules with TypeScript surfaces - prefer them over raw bridge code
* Expo Go ships a fixed native binary - custom or third-party native deps need a development build
* Every native dependency change requires rebuilding ios/ and android/ - OTA cannot ship native code
* Search Expo SDK and config plugins before writing Swift or Kotlin - see Native Module Rules

## Prerequisites

Start from a blank Expo app with a development build path ready - native modules do not run in Jest without mocks and cannot load arbitrary code in Expo Go:

```bash
npx create-expo-app@latest NativeBasics --template blank-typescript@sdk-57 --yes
cd NativeBasics
npx expo install expo-dev-client expo-modules-core
```

> **Tooling:** These examples target **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4), **React Native 0.86.0**, and **React 19.2.3**. Pair this page with [Native Module Rules](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/native-module-rules/) before adding any package with native code.

---

## Basic Examples

### 1. When Hardware APIs Have No JS Equivalent

Camera frames, GPS fixes, accelerometer streams, and biometric sensors read **device hardware** through OS APIs. JavaScript cannot access them without a native module:

```tsx
import { CameraView, useCameraPermissions } from "expo-camera";
import { Button } from "react-native";
 
export function ScanScreen() {
  const [permission, requestPermission] = useCameraPermissions();
 
  if (!permission?.granted) {
    return <Button title="Allow camera" onPress={requestPermission} />;
  }
 
  return <CameraView style={{ flex: 1 }} facing="back" />;
}
```

* **`expo-camera`** wraps AVFoundation (iOS) and CameraX (Android) - no pure-JS substitute
* Permission prompts require **Info.plist** and **AndroidManifest** entries - config plugins handle this
* Expo Go includes `expo-camera`; arbitrary camera SDKs do not

---

### 2. When Secure Storage Must Use Keychain / Keystore

`AsyncStorage` is unencrypted SQLite. Tokens, refresh secrets, and PII belong in **Keychain** (iOS) or **Keystore** (Android):

```ts
import * as SecureStore from "expo-secure-store";
 
export async function saveRefreshToken(token: string): Promise<void> {
  await SecureStore.setItemAsync("refresh_token", token, {
    keychainAccessible: SecureStore.WHEN_UNLOCKED_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY,
  });
}
 
export async function loadRefreshToken(): Promise<string | null> {
  return SecureStore.getItemAsync("refresh_token");
}
```

* **Hardware-backed encryption** is a native capability - web `localStorage` patterns do not apply
* See [SecureStore & Keychain/Keystore](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/securestore-and-keychain-keystore/) for rotation and multi-account patterns
* Jest tests must mock `expo-secure-store` - see [Mocking Native Modules](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/mocking-native-modules/)

---

### 3. When Background Work Exceeds JS Thread Limits

Timers and `fetch` pause when the app is backgrounded or killed. Push delivery, location updates, and background uploads need **native schedulers**:

```ts
import * as TaskManager from "expo-task-manager";
import * as Location from "expo-location";
 
const TASK_NAME = "background-location";
 
TaskManager.defineTask(TASK_NAME, ({ data, error }) => {
  if (error) return;
  const { locations } = data as { locations: Location.LocationObject[] };
  // Upload locations to your API - native task keeps firing
});
 
export async function startBackgroundLocation(): Promise<void> {
  await Location.startLocationUpdatesAsync(TASK_NAME, {
    accuracy: Location.Accuracy.Balanced,
    distanceInterval: 100,
    showsBackgroundLocationIndicator: true,
  });
}
```

* **Background modes** require entitlements and manifest flags - never hand-edit after [CNG prebuild](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/prebuild-basics/)
* iOS kills apps that claim background capability without real usage - App Store review rejects phantom modes

---

### 4. When Push Notifications Need APNs / FCM Native Tokens

Push is not HTTP polling. Device tokens come from **Apple Push Notification service** and **Firebase Cloud Messaging** native SDKs:

```ts
import * as Notifications from "expo-notifications";
import * as Device from "expo-device";
 
export async function registerPushToken(): Promise<string | null> {
  if (!Device.isDevice) return null;
 
  const { status } = await Notifications.requestPermissionsAsync();
  if (status !== "granted") return null;
 
  const token = await Notifications.getExpoPushTokenAsync();
  return token.data;
}
```

* **Simulator push** behavior differs from device - always verify on hardware before release
* Custom notification extensions (rich media, categories) are fully native - JS orchestrates, native renders

---

### 5. When You Need Native UI Components

Some views cannot be faithfully reproduced in React Native layout - maps, video players, PDF renderers, and WebViews embed **platform-native views** inside the RN tree:

```tsx
import MapView, { Marker } from "react-native-maps";
 
export function StoreMap({ lat, lng }: { lat: number; lng: number }) {
  return (
    <MapView
      style={{ flex: 1 }}
      initialRegion={{
        latitude: lat,
        longitude: lng,
        latitudeDelta: 0.02,
        longitudeDelta: 0.02,
      }}
    >
      <Marker coordinate={{ latitude: lat, longitude: lng }} title="Store" />
    </MapView>
  );
}
```

* Native views participate in the **Fabric** shadow tree on New Architecture - layout props still apply to the container
* Third-party map SDKs ship their own native binaries - evaluate compatibility before `npm install`

---

### 6. When Platform-Only APIs Block Your Feature

HealthKit, NFC, CarPlay, Siri shortcuts, and Android intents exist only on one platform. Feature detection gates JS; native modules implement the call:

```ts
import { Platform } from "react-native";
import * as LocalAuthentication from "expo-local-authentication";
 
export async function biometricGate(): Promise<boolean> {
  if (Platform.OS === "web") return false;
 
  const compatible = await LocalAuthentication.hasHardwareAsync();
  if (!compatible) return false;
 
  const enrolled = await LocalAuthentication.isEnrolledAsync();
  if (!enrolled) return false;
 
  const result = await LocalAuthentication.authenticateAsync({
    promptMessage: "Unlock to continue",
  });
  return result.success;
}
```

* **`Platform.OS` checks** prevent crashes; they do not replace native implementation
* Platform-specific modules should expose a **unified TypeScript API** in your app layer - hide `Platform.select` inside services

---

### 7. When Performance-Critical Work Must Leave the JS Thread

Heavy image transforms, video encoding, cryptography, and ML inference block the JS thread if done in pure JavaScript. Native modules run work on **background queues** or **GPU paths**:

```ts
import * as ImageManipulator from "expo-image-manipulator";
 
export async function resizeAvatar(uri: string): Promise<string> {
  const result = await ImageManipulator.manipulateAsync(
    uri,
    [{ resize: { width: 256 } }],
    { compress: 0.8, format: ImageManipulator.SaveFormat.JPEG }
  );
  return result.uri;
}
```

* **Hermes** is fast for app logic - it is not a substitute for Core Image, MediaCodec, or SIMD C++
* Profile on device: if JS frame drops coincide with your function, move the work native or to a worker

---

### 8. When System Integrations Require Native Entry Points

Share sheets, home-screen widgets, App Clips, and universal links register at the **native app layer**. JavaScript receives deep-link events; native code owns registration:

```ts
import * as Linking from "expo-linking";
 
export function subscribeToDeepLinks(onUrl: (url: string) => void): () => void {
  const sub = Linking.addEventListener("url", ({ url }) => onUrl(url));
  Linking.getInitialURL().then((url) => {
    if (url) onUrl(url);
  });
  return () => sub.remove();
}
```

```json
// app.json excerpt - associated domains are native entitlements
{
  "expo": {
    "scheme": "myapp",
    "ios": {
      "associatedDomains": ["applinks:shop.example.com"]
    }
  }
}
```

* **Associated domains** and Android intent filters are applied during [prebuild](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/expo-prebuild-workflow/) - express them in config, not manual `Info.plist` edits

---

### 9. When Bluetooth / BLE Needs GATT Native Stacks

Web Bluetooth is unavailable on React Native. BLE scanning, pairing, and GATT read/write require **CoreBluetooth** (iOS) and **BluetoothGatt** (Android):

```ts
// Conceptual - real BLE libraries expose native modules
import { BleManager } from "react-native-ble-plx";
 
const manager = new BleManager();
 
export async function scanForPeripherals(): Promise<void> {
  manager.startDeviceScan(null, null, (error, device) => {
    if (error) return;
    if (device?.name) console.log("Found", device.name);
  });
}
```

* BLE libraries are **never** in Expo Go - plan `expo-dev-client` from day one
* Background BLE on iOS requires additional entitlements and drains battery - document in your ADR

---

### 10. When JS Polyfills Cannot Satisfy Store or Security Requirements

Sometimes the gap is not capability but **compliance**: certificate pinning, jailbreak detection, proprietary payment SDKs, or MDM-required APIs. These ship as native binaries with no Expo SDK equivalent:

```ts
// App-layer facade - implementation is a native module or third-party SDK
export type AttestationResult = { passed: boolean; reason?: string };
 
export async function attestDevice(): Promise<AttestationResult> {
  // Native module: DeviceCheck (iOS) / Play Integrity (Android)
  const NativeAttestation = require("../native/attestation").default;
  return NativeAttestation.runAsync();
}
```

* **Store review** may require specific native SDK versions - JS wrappers must match pinned native builds
* Every polyfill-only workaround that touches security should be rejected in code review - see [Native Module Rules](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/native-module-rules/)

---

## How Native Modules Load on SDK 57

```
JavaScript (Hermes)
    │
    ▼
expo-modules-core / JSI host object
    │
    ├── Expo Modules API (expo-camera, expo-file-system, …)
    ├── React Native TurboModules (community libraries)
    └── Legacy bridge fallback (older libraries only)
    │
    ▼
Swift / Kotlin / C++ native implementation
```

| Layer | What you import | Rebuild required? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Expo SDK module | `import * as Camera from "expo-camera"` | Yes, after install |
| Community native lib | `import MapView from "react-native-maps"` | Yes, after install |
| Custom Expo module | `import MyModule from "my-local-module"` | Yes, always |
| JS-only package | `import { z } from "zod"` | No - OTA can ship |

```tsx
import { requireNativeModule, requireOptionalNativeModule } from "expo-modules-core";
 
// Throws if native class missing from binary
const FileSystem = requireNativeModule("ExpoFileSystem");
 
// Returns null in tests or when module not linked
const Optional = requireOptionalNativeModule("ExpoCustomFeature");
```

See [Expo Modules Core](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-platform/expo-modules-core/) for bootstrap details and [Expo Go vs Development Builds](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-platform/expo-go-vs-development-builds/) for runtime constraints.

---

## Gotchas

* **Expecting Expo Go to load any native npm package** - only preinstalled modules work. **Fix:** `npx expo install expo-dev-client` and build a development client.
* **Installing with `npm install` instead of `npx expo install`** - JS and native binary versions drift. **Fix:** Always `npx expo install <package>` for native deps.
* **Skipping native rebuild after `package.json` change** - Metro hot reload does not compile Swift/Kotlin. **Fix:** `npx expo run:ios` / `eas build` after every native change.
* **Calling native modules at module top-level in tests** - Jest has no bridge. **Fix:** Mock at service boundary or use `jest-expo`.
* **Hand-editing `ios/` and `android/` in CNG apps** - next `prebuild --clean` wipes edits. **Fix:** Encode changes in config plugins per [CNG prebuild](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/best-practices/).

---

## FAQs

What is a native module?

A bridge between JavaScript and platform code (Swift, Kotlin, Objective-C, Java, C++). On React Native 0.86 with New Architecture, most modules use JSI and TurboModules for synchronous, typed calls.

Do I need native code for every Expo SDK package?

No - you consume them from JavaScript. The Expo team maintains the native implementation. You only write native code when no SDK or community package fits.

Can I ship native code changes over OTA?

No. OTA (EAS Update) ships JavaScript and assets only. Native dependency changes require a new store binary or development build.

Expo Go vs development build - quick rule?

Expo Go: SDK modules only, fastest spike. Development build: your `package.json` native deps, required for third-party and custom modules.

How do I know if an npm package has native code?

Look for `ios/`, `android/`, `.podspec`, or `expo-module.config.json` in the package. Run `npx expo-doctor` after install - it flags incompatible native deps.

# Using Third-Party Native Libraries

A cookbook for evaluating, installing, and verifying **community native libraries** in an Expo SDK 57 CNG app - with explicit checks for **prebuild survivability** and **New Architecture** compatibility on React Native 0.86.

Highlights / Using Third-Party Native Libraries

* Run the compatibility checklist before npm install - rebuild cost is measured in days
* npx expo install pins SDK 57–compatible versions; manual npm ranges cause runtime crashes
* New Architecture support is mandatory on RN 0.86 - verify Fabric and TurboModule claims in issues
* Config plugins must encode permissions and Gradle/Pod changes - never post-prebuild hand edits
* Expo Go cannot load arbitrary native binaries - third-party libs require expo-dev-client

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
# 1. Evaluate BEFORE install (see checklist below)
# 2. Install with Expo's resolver - not bare npm
npx expo install react-native-maps
 
# 3. Register config plugin in app.config.ts (if the library ships one)
# 4. Regenerate native projects and verify
npx expo prebuild --clean
npx expo-doctor
 
# 5. Build a development client - third-party native code is NOT in Expo Go
npx expo install expo-dev-client
npx expo run:ios
# or: eas build --profile development --platform all
```

```ts
// app.config.ts - typical third-party plugin registration
import type { ExpoConfig } from "expo/config";
 
export default ({ config }: { config: ExpoConfig }): ExpoConfig => ({
  ...config,
  plugins: [
    [
      "react-native-maps",
      {
        iosGoogleMapsApiKey: process.env.GOOGLE_MAPS_IOS_KEY,
        androidGoogleMapsApiKey: process.env.GOOGLE_MAPS_ANDROID_KEY,
      },
    ],
  ],
});
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Adopting `react-native-maps`, `react-native-ble-plx`, `react-native-purchases`, or any npm package with `ios/` / `android/` folders.
* Auditing whether a library survives `npx expo prebuild --clean` in a CNG workflow.
* Confirming **RN 0.86 New Architecture** support before merging a dependency PR.
* Replacing a deprecated native wrapper with an Expo SDK equivalent.

## Working Example

### Compatibility checklist (run before merge)

| Check | Pass criteria | Fail action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Expo SDK 57 / RN 0.86 | README or issues mention 0.86+ | Open issue or fork; do not ship |
| New Architecture | `newArchEnabled` issue closed or docs claim TurboModule/Fabric | Test on device; reject if redbox on launch |
| Config plugin | Ships `app.plugin.js` or documents `expo` config plugin | Plan a custom plugin - see [Config Plugins](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/native-modules/config-plugins/) |
| `npx expo install` | Package listed in Expo ecosystem or install succeeds | Pin version manually with ADR |
| Expo Go | N/A - assume **not** in Expo Go | Add `expo-dev-client` to project |
| Maintenance | Commit within last 12 months | Prefer Expo SDK alternative |

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/verify-native-dep.sh - run after adding a native library
set -euo pipefail
 
PKG="${1:?Usage: ./verify-native-dep.sh <package-name>}"
 
echo "▶ Installing $PKG via expo install..."
npx expo install "$PKG"
 
echo "▶ Running expo-doctor..."
npx expo-doctor
 
echo "▶ Resolving autolinking (iOS)..."
npx expo-modules-autolinking resolve --platform ios | grep -i "${PKG##*/}" || true
 
echo "▶ Clean prebuild dry run..."
npx expo prebuild --clean --no-install
 
echo "✅ $PKG passed local verification - still build on device"
```

### End-to-end: add `react-native-maps`

```bash
npx create-expo-app@latest MapsCookbook --template blank-typescript@sdk-57 --yes
cd MapsCookbook
npx expo install expo-dev-client react-native-maps
```

```ts
// app.config.ts
import type { ExpoConfig } from "expo/config";
 
const defineConfig = ({ config }: { config: ExpoConfig }): ExpoConfig => ({
  ...config,
  name: "MapsCookbook",
  slug: "maps-cookbook",
  plugins: [
    [
      "react-native-maps",
      {
        iosGoogleMapsApiKey: process.env.GOOGLE_MAPS_IOS_KEY ?? "",
        androidGoogleMapsApiKey: process.env.GOOGLE_MAPS_ANDROID_KEY ?? "",
      },
    ],
  ],
});
 
export default defineConfig;
```

```tsx
// App.tsx
import MapView, { Marker } from "react-native-maps";
```

```bash
# Regenerate native dirs and run on simulator
npx expo prebuild
npx expo run:ios
 
# Start Metro for the dev client (not Expo Go)
npx expo start --dev-client
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* **`npx expo install`** resolves a version compatible with SDK 57 native binaries.
* **Config plugin** injects API keys into `Info.plist` and `AndroidManifest.xml` during prebuild.
* **`expo prebuild`** wires autolinking - no manual `Podfile` edits in CNG apps.
* **Development build** is mandatory - `react-native-maps` is not bundled in Expo Go.

## Deep Dive

### New Architecture compatibility on RN 0.86

React Native 0.86 defaults to **New Architecture** (Fabric + TurboModules). Third-party libraries fall into three buckets:

| Bucket | Symptom | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fully compatible | Builds and runs on device | Ship |
| Partial (bridge fallback) | Builds but sync JSI APIs fail | Test every API you call; open upstream issue |
| Incompatible | Compile error or instant crash | Do not adopt; find alternative or fork |

```bash
# Confirm New Architecture in generated project
grep -r "newArchEnabled" android/ ios/ 2>/dev/null || true
 
# Force-verify with a release build on device (not just debug Metro)
npx expo run:ios --configuration Release
```

Libraries using **old NativeModules bridge only** may still run via interoperability layer, but performance-sensitive paths (maps, video, BLE) should be validated on **physical hardware** - simulators hide threading bugs.

### Prebuild + CNG workflow

In Continuous Native Generation apps, `ios/` and `android/` are **outputs** of config, not source of truth:

```
package.json + app.config.ts + plugins
              │
              ▼
        npx expo prebuild
              │
              ▼
    ios/ android/ (generated)
              │
              ▼
    npx expo run:ios / eas build
```

Never document "add this line to `AndroidManifest.xml`" as a permanent step - encode it in a **config plugin** so regeneration stays clean. See [Prebuild Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/prebuild-basics/) and [Config Plugins in CNG](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/config-plugins-in-cng/).

### When to prefer Expo SDK over third-party

| Need | Prefer Expo SDK | Third-party when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Camera | `expo-camera` | Vendor SDK requires proprietary binary |
| Location | `expo-location` | Background BLE geofencing with hardware SDK |
| Maps | `expo-maps` (if fits) | Google Maps SDK features not exposed |
| Payments | `expo-in-app-purchases` / Stripe RN | Store-specific native SDK mandate |

Follow [Native Module Rules](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/native-module-rules/) Tier 1 before every third-party install.

### Autolinking verification

```bash
# List modules that will compile into the binary
npx expo-modules-autolinking resolve --platform ios
npx expo-modules-autolinking resolve --platform android
 
# React Native community autolinking (non-Expo packages)
npx react-native config
```

If a package appears in `package.json` but not in resolve output, the native build **never compiled it** - `requireNativeModule` will throw at runtime.

## Gotchas

* **Testing in Expo Go after `npm install`** - third-party native code is absent from the Go binary. **Fix:** `npx expo start --dev-client` with a custom build.
* **Skipping `prebuild` after plugin config change** - stale `Info.plist` entries. **Fix:** `npx expo prebuild --clean` locally before merge.
* **Assuming green CI TypeScript means native works** - Jest does not execute native code. **Fix:** Device QA or Maestro flow on development build.
* **Pinning `@latest` on native packages** - breaks SDK 57 ABI alignment. **Fix:** `npx expo install` or explicit version with ADR.
* **Mixing multiple map/BLE/payment SDKs in one PR** - bisect nightmare when prebuild fails. **Fix:** One native dependency per PR per Native Module Rules.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Expo SDK module | Feature exists in SDK 57 | Proprietary vendor mandates custom SDK |
| Config plugin + third-party | Community lib has plugin and RN 0.86 support | Unmaintained, no New Arch path |
| Local Expo module | Thin bridge to vendor SDK | Full SDK surface - still need native code |
| WebView + hosted UI | Vendor offers web-only integration | Offline, performance, or store policy blocks WebView |

## FAQs

Can I use any react-native-\* package with Expo?

Only if it supports prebuild/autolinking, has a config plugin (or you write one), and compiles on RN 0.86 New Architecture. `npx expo-doctor` catches common failures early.

Do I commit ios/ and android/ after adding a library?

Team policy varies. CNG teams often gitignore native dirs and regenerate in CI. If you commit them, still express changes via plugins - not manual drift. See [CNG best practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/best-practices/).

How do I test New Architecture compatibility quickly?

`npx expo run:ios --configuration Release` on a physical device with the library's primary user flow. Debug Metro can mask native threading issues.

Library has no config plugin - what now?

Write a local plugin in `plugins/` or choose a maintained fork. Post-prebuild manual edits are technical debt in CNG apps.

expo install vs npm install?

`npx expo install` reads Expo's compatibility table for SDK 57. `npm install` may resolve JS that does not match native binaries in your build.

Dokumen: Networking Best Practices
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/best-practices/

# Networking Best Practices

A condensed summary of the 25 most important networking practices drawn from every page in this section.

Highlights / Networking Best Practices

* Never block the UI thread - parse JSON and retry logic off the critical render path
* Always surface network state - offline, stale, and error are distinct UX modes
* Centralize transport in one api/client module with HTTPS enforcement
* Default fetch; add axios only when interceptors or progress justify bundle cost
* Wire TanStack Query focusManager and onlineManager before shipping feeds
* Retry idempotent reads; never blind-retry POST without idempotency keys

1. **Centralize HTTP in one client module:** Attach base URL, auth headers, timeouts, and HTTPS checks in `api/client.ts` - features never scatter raw `fetch` to arbitrary hosts.
2. **Enforce HTTPS in production builds:** Reject `http://` at the client choke point - `android.usesCleartextTraffic` is for local dev only.
3. **Always set request timeouts:** Use `AbortController` + timer (8–15 s reads, tighter for mutations) - LTE handoffs hang indefinitely without them.
4. **Cancel in-flight requests on unmount:** Pass `signal` from `useEffect` cleanup or TanStack Query `queryFn` - prevents setState-after-unmount and wasted radio time.
5. **Parse JSON at the network edge with Zod:** Never cast `res.json()` blindly - one schema per endpoint catches backend drift before users see crashes.
6. **Classify errors before showing copy:** Offline (`TypeError`), timeout (`AbortError`), HTTP status, and parse failures need different messages - see [Network Failure UX](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/error-resilience/network-failure-ux/).
7. **Default to fetch on Hermes:** Zero extra bundle bytes - add [axios](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/fetch-vs-axios/) only when interceptors, `isAxiosError`, or team conventions justify ~13–15 KB gzip.
8. **Implement interceptors once:** Whether fetch wrapper or axios, auth attachment and 401 handling live in a single module paired with [Refresh Token Rotation](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/refresh-token-rotation/).
9. **Upload progress requires XMLHttpRequest or FileSystem:** Neither fetch nor axios exposes reliable upload progress on React Native - plan XHR or `expo-file-system` for avatars and media.
10. **Adopt TanStack Query for shared server state:** Replace manual `useEffect` fetch hooks when multiple screens read the same API - cache, dedupe, and background refetch are free.
11. **Wire `focusManager` to `AppState`:** Refetch stale queries when the app becomes `active` - mobile has no `window` focus events.
12. **Wire `onlineManager` to NetInfo:** Pause query retries offline; resume on reconnect - uncapped retries in airplane mode drain battery.
13. **Tune `staleTime` per query key:** 30–60 s for feeds, longer for catalogs - global `staleTime: 0` refetches too aggressively on every foreground.
14. **Show staleness labels:** Display `dataUpdatedAt` or "Updated 2 min ago" - users on flaky LTE need to know data may be old.
15. **Retry GET with exponential backoff and jitter:** Cap at 3–4 attempts - jitter prevents synchronized client spikes when towers recover.
16. **Never retry non-idempotent POST blindly:** Use `Idempotency-Key` headers and server deduplication for payments and creates - see [Retries, Backoff & Idempotency](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/retries-backoff-and-idempotency/).
17. **Set TanStack Query `mutations.retry` to 0 by default:** Transport-layer retry with stable idempotency keys beats duplicate mutation function invocations.
18. **Persist read caches selectively:** `persistQueryClient` with AsyncStorage or MMKV for catalogs - clear on logout; exclude unencrypted PII.
19. **Close WebSockets in background:** Reconnect with backoff on foreground - leaving sockets open wastes battery and gets killed by the OS.
20. **Offer polling fallback for real-time features:** Slower intervals on cellular and in background - or push notifications for must-deliver events.
21. **Choose urql for lean GraphQL; Apollo for complex graphs:** Measure bundle with `expo export` - persist normalized cache with size caps on device.
22. **Default to system TLS; pin only with an ADR:** Certificate pinning needs native rebuilds, rotation runbooks, and breaks corporate proxies - most apps should not pin on day one.
23. **Queue offline mutations with optimistic UI:** Persist failed writes, show `pending` state, flush on reconnect - pair with [Optimistic UI](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/data-offline/optimistic-ui/).
24. **Never block the UI thread on network parsing:** Large JSON transforms belong off the hot path; stream or paginate huge lists - keep presses responsive.
25. **Pre-release networking checklist:** Physical device on LTE, airplane-mode retry behavior, logout cache clear, idempotency spot-check, and TLS policy grep before store submission.

## FAQs

fetch or axios for a new Expo SDK 57 app?

**fetch** with a thin client wrapper unless interceptors or upload ergonomics force axios. TanStack Query sits above either transport.

Minimum TanStack Query mobile setup?

`QueryClientProvider`, `focusManager` + `AppState`, `onlineManager` + NetInfo, sensible `staleTime`, and `signal` in `queryFn`.

When is certificate pinning required?

Rare - regulated finance/health with security ops owning rotation. Default system TLS per [Certificate Pinning](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/certificate-pinning/) and Security Rules.

How do networking and offline-first relate?

Networking pages cover transport, cache, and failure UX. Full offline-first adds SQLite sync - [Offline-First Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/data-offline/offline-first-basics/).

## Related

* [WebSockets & Real-Time](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/websockets-and-real-time/) - reconnect and polling fallbacks
* [GraphQL with urql/Apollo](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/graphql-with-urql-apollo/) - normalized cache on device
* [Certificate Pinning](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/certificate-pinning/) - threat model and Expo managed costs

Dokumen: Fetch vs axios
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/fetch-vs-axios/

# Fetch vs axios

Interceptors, upload progress, and bundle-size trade-offs for Expo SDK 57 apps choosing between built-in `fetch` and `axios`.

Highlights / Fetch vs axios

* fetch is zero-dependency on Hermes - axios adds ~13–15 KB gzip to your JS bundle
* axios interceptors centralize auth refresh; fetch needs a thin wrapper module
* Upload progress requires XMLHttpRequest or expo-file-system - fetch has no onUploadProgress
* Default to fetch until you need interceptors, progress, or automatic JSON transforms
* Both run on the JS thread - neither replaces offline cache or TanStack Query

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```ts
// src/api/http.ts - fetch wrapper with interceptor-like hooks
import * as SecureStore from "expo-secure-store";
 
type RequestContext = { url: string; init: RequestInit };
type Interceptor = (ctx: RequestContext) => Promise<RequestContext> | RequestContext;
 
const requestInterceptors: Interceptor[] = [];
const responseHandlers: Array<(res: Response) => Response | Promise<Response>> = [];
 
export function onRequest(fn: Interceptor) {
  requestInterceptors.push(fn);
}
 
export function onResponse(fn: (res: Response) => Response | Promise<Response>) {
  responseHandlers.push(fn);
}
 
export async function http(input: string, init: RequestInit = {}) {
  let ctx: RequestContext = { url: input, init: { ...init } };
  for (const hook of requestInterceptors) {
    ctx = await hook(ctx);
  }
 
  let res = await fetch(ctx.url, ctx.init);
  for (const hook of responseHandlers) {
    res = await hook(res);
  }
  return res;
}
 
// Attach bearer once
onRequest(async (ctx) => {
  const token = await SecureStore.getItemAsync("access_token");
  if (!token) return ctx;
  return {
    ...ctx,
    init: {
      ...ctx.init,
      headers: { ...Object(ctx.init.headers), Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` },
    },
  };
});
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Greenfield Expo apps that want interceptor ergonomics without adding axios.
* Teams already standardized on `fetch` but need one place for auth headers and 401 handling.
* Read-heavy apps where upload progress is not required.

## Working Example

```tsx
// src/api/axiosClient.ts - when axios wins
import axios from "axios";
import * as SecureStore from "expo-secure-store";
 
const api = axios.create({
  baseURL: process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL,
  timeout: 12_000,
  headers: { Accept: "application/json" },
});
 
api.interceptors.request.use(async (config) => {
  const token = await SecureStore.getItemAsync("access_token");
  if (token) config.headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${token}`;
  return config;
});
 
api.interceptors.response.use(
  (res) => res,
  async (error) => {
    if (axios.isAxiosError(error) && error.response?.status === 401) {
      // Trigger refresh flow - see Refresh Token Rotation
      await SecureStore.deleteItemAsync("access_token");
    }
    return Promise.reject(error);
  }
);
 
export { api };
```

```tsx
// src/screens/AvatarUploadScreen.tsx - upload progress via XMLHttpRequest
import { useState } from "react";
import * as ImagePicker from "expo-image-picker";
import { ActivityIndicator, Pressable, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
function uploadWithProgress(
  uri: string,
  onProgress: (ratio: number) => void
): Promise<void> {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const xhr = new XMLHttpRequest();
    const form = new FormData();
    form.append("file", {
      uri,
      name: "avatar.jpg",
      type: "image/jpeg",
    } as unknown as Blob);
 
    xhr.upload.onprogress = (e) => {
      if (e.lengthComputable) onProgress(e.loaded / e.total);
    };
    xhr.onload = () => (xhr.status >= 200 && xhr.status < 300 ? resolve() : reject());
    xhr.onerror = () => reject(new TypeError("Network error"));
    xhr.open("POST", `${process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL}/upload`);
    xhr.send(form);
  });
}
 
export function AvatarUploadScreen() {
  const [progress, setProgress] = useState(0);
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false);
 
  async function pickAndUpload() {
    const result = await ImagePicker.launchImageLibraryAsync({ mediaTypes: ["images"] });
    if (result.canceled) return;
 
    setBusy(true);
    try {
      await uploadWithProgress(result.assets[0].uri, setProgress);
    } finally {
      setBusy(false);
      setProgress(0);
    }
  }
 
  return (
    <View style={{ padding: 16 }}>
      <Pressable onPress={pickAndUpload} disabled={busy}>
        <Text>Upload avatar</Text>
      </Pressable>
      {busy && (
        <>
          <ActivityIndicator />
          <Text>{Math.round(progress * 100)}%</Text>
        </>
      )}
    </View>
  );
}
```

```bash
npx expo install expo-image-picker expo-secure-store
npm install axios
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* **fetch wrapper** mimics axios request/response interceptors with zero extra dependencies.
* **axios** gives built-in `timeout`, `baseURL`, and `isAxiosError` for typed error branches.
* **Upload progress** on React Native requires `XMLHttpRequest` or `expo-file-system` multipart - neither fetch nor axios exposes progress on RN's fetch polyfill.
* **401 interceptor** clears tokens centrally - pair with [Refresh Token Rotation](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/refresh-token-rotation/).

## Deep Dive

### Decision Matrix

| Need | fetch | axios |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bundle size | ✅ Built-in | ⚠️ ~13–15 KB gzip minified |
| Interceptors | DIY wrapper (~40 lines) | ✅ Built-in |
| Timeout | `AbortController` | ✅ `timeout` option |
| Upload progress | ❌ Use XHR / FileSystem | ⚠️ RN axios uses adapter - progress via XHR |
| JSON transform | Manual `res.json()` | ✅ Automatic when `Content-Type` is JSON |
| Cancel | `AbortSignal` | `AbortController` via `signal` in config |
| Typed errors | Custom classifier | `axios.isAxiosError` |

### Bundle-Size Trade-offs

```bash
# Measure before adding axios to a Hermes bundle
npx expo export --platform ios
# Compare dist/_expo/static/js/ios/*.js before/after npm install axios
```

* **axios** pulls `follow-redirects` logic and transform pipelines - meaningful on low-end Android where every KB affects TTI
* **fetch + Zod** at the edge matches axios JSON ergonomics with better validation
* If axios is only used in two files, a **local wrapper** is cheaper than a global dependency
* Tree-shaking does not remove unused axios adapters entirely - assume the full client cost

### Interceptor Patterns on Mobile

| Pattern | fetch wrapper | axios |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Attach bearer | `onRequest` reads SecureStore | `interceptors.request` |
| Refresh on 401 | `onResponse` checks status, queues refresh | `interceptors.response` |
| Request ID header | Mutate `init.headers` | `config.headers["X-Request-Id"]` |
| Retry with backoff | Not built-in - use [Retries doc](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/retries-backoff-and-idempotency/) | `axios-retry` plugin (extra dep) |

```ts
// Idempotent retry belongs outside either client - shared utility
import { fetchWithRetry } from "./retry";
```

### When axios Is Worth It

* **Large teams** with existing axios conventions from web code sharing packages in a monorepo.
* **Heavy mutation** flows with consistent error shape mapping via `AxiosError.response?.data`.
* **Upload dashboards** already built on `axios` + `onUploadProgress` on web - port XHR recipe above for RN parity.

### When fetch Is Enough

* **Expo-first** apps using TanStack Query as the network layer - `queryFn` only needs a thin `apiGet`.
* **Read-mostly** consumer apps with occasional POST and no progress UI.
* **Strict bundle budgets** on emerging-market devices.

## Gotchas

* **Expecting axios upload progress from fetch** - RN fetch has no upload events. **Fix:** `XMLHttpRequest` or `FileSystem.uploadAsync`.
* **Installing axios for JSON parsing alone** - `res.json()` + Zod is lighter. **Fix:** Parse at the edge per [Networking Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/networking-basics/).
* **Duplicate auth logic in screens and interceptors** - Drift causes mystery 401s. **Fix:** One client module; features never import axios directly.
* **axios `timeout` without retry policy** - Single timeout on LTE looks like flaky servers. **Fix:** Pair with backoff and idempotency keys.
* **Sharing axios instance between web and RN without adapter check** - Web adapters differ. **Fix:** Separate `axios.create` per platform or use fetch in shared core.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| fetch + wrapper | Default Expo apps, small teams | You need battle-tested retry/upload plugins today |
| axios | Shared web/RN packages, interceptor-heavy APIs | Bundle size is already over budget |
| TanStack Query only | Server state with cache | You still need a transport - pick fetch or axios underneath |
| `expo-file-system` upload | Large files, background-friendly uploads | Tiny JSON POST bodies |
| tRPC / generated clients | End-to-end typed APIs | Public third-party REST without codegen |

## FAQs

Should new Expo SDK 57 apps default to fetch or axios?

Default to **fetch** with a small `api/client.ts` wrapper. Add axios when interceptors, `isAxiosError`, or team conventions justify the bundle cost.

How do I add upload progress with fetch?

You cannot on React Native today. Use `XMLHttpRequest` (`xhr.upload.onprogress`) or `expo-file-system`'s `uploadAsync` with progress callbacks.

Does axios support AbortController?

Yes - pass `signal` in the request config. TanStack Query supplies `signal` to `queryFn`; forward it to axios for automatic cancellation on unmount.

Can I use axios with TanStack Query?

Yes - `queryFn: ({ signal }) => api.get('/posts', { signal }).then(r => r.data)`. Prefer one axios instance with interceptors at the root.

How big is axios in a Hermes bundle?

Roughly **13–15 KB gzip** for the core client - measure with `expo export` on your app. Wrapper code is often smaller than axios if you only need auth headers.

How do interceptors interact with token refresh?

On 401, pause outgoing requests, refresh once, replay queue, or logout. Serialize refresh to avoid stampedes - see [Refresh Token Rotation](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/refresh-token-rotation/).

## Related

* [Networking Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/networking-basics/) - timeouts, cancellation, JSON parsing
* [TanStack Query on Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/tanstack-query-on-mobile/) - cache layer above either transport
* [Retries, Backoff & Idempotency](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/retries-backoff-and-idempotency/) - transport-agnostic retry utilities
* [Refresh Token Rotation](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/refresh-token-rotation/) - 401 handling in interceptors

Dokumen: Networking & APIs Highlights Summary
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/highlights-summary/

# Networking & APIs Highlights Summary

Every highlight bullet from the 8 pages in this section, gathered on one page and grouped by the page it came from.

Highlights / Networking & APIs Highlights Summary

## [Networking Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/networking-basics/)

* React Native ships fetch and AbortController - no polyfill required on Hermes
* Always set timeouts on mobile; LTE handoffs hang longer than Wi‑Fi
* Cancel in-flight requests on unmount to avoid setState-after-unmount warnings
* Parse JSON at the edge with Zod - never trust raw response shapes
* Classify errors: offline, timeout, HTTP status - UX copy differs for each
* Centralize fetch in one api/client module - attach auth headers once

## [Fetch vs axios](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/fetch-vs-axios/)

* fetch is zero-dependency on Hermes - axios adds ~13–15 KB gzip to your JS bundle
* axios interceptors centralize auth refresh; fetch needs a thin wrapper module
* Upload progress requires XMLHttpRequest or expo-file-system - fetch has no onUploadProgress
* Default to fetch until you need interceptors, progress, or automatic JSON transforms
* Both run on the JS thread - neither replaces offline cache or TanStack Query

## [TanStack Query on Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/tanstack-query-on-mobile/)

* Wire focusManager to AppState - refetch stale queries when users return from background
* Wire onlineManager to NetInfo - pause retries offline, resume on reconnect
* Default staleTime 30–60s on feeds - balance freshness with battery on LTE
* Forward AbortSignal from queryFn to fetch for automatic cancellation
* persistQueryClient pairs with AsyncStorage for read-mostly offline shells

## [Retries, Backoff & Idempotency](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/retries-backoff-and-idempotency/)

* Retry only idempotent requests or those with idempotency keys - never blind POST retries
* Exponential backoff with jitter prevents thundering herds when LTE returns
* Cap attempts at 3–5 - infinite retry drains battery in airplane mode
* Pair retries with onlineManager - pause while offline, resume on reconnect
* 429 Retry-After headers deserve respect - sleep before next attempt

## [WebSockets & Real-Time](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/websockets-and-real-time/)

* WebSockets stay open - iOS and Android will suspend them in background without a keepalive strategy
* Exponential reconnect backoff prevents reconnect storms when towers recover
* Fall back to polling when backgrounded or on metered networks to save battery
* AppState drives connect/disconnect - do not leave sockets open when inactive
* Pair real-time updates with TanStack Query cache patches - avoid duplicate sources of truth

## [GraphQL with urql/Apollo](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/graphql-with-urql-apollo/)

* urql is smaller and composable - good default for Expo apps with modest GraphQL needs
* Apollo Client 4 offers the richest normalized cache - justify bundle size on complex graphs
* Persist normalized cache to AsyncStorage for faster cold start - exclude sensitive fields
* Automatic Persisted Queries (APQ) shrink payloads on LTE - SHA-256 query hash over GET
* Wire the same focusManager and onlineManager patterns as REST TanStack Query

## [Certificate Pinning](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/certificate-pinning/)

* Default to system TLS on SDK 57 - pinning is the exception, not the baseline
* Pinning requires native code - Expo Go cannot validate pins; dev-client rebuilds mandatory
* Expired or rotated pins brick the app until a store update - plan backup pins first
* Corporate MITM proxies break pinning - finance apps need an explicit bypass ADR
* Threat model: pinning helps compromised CAs and rogue APs - not reverse-engineered clients

## [Networking Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/best-practices/)

* Never block the UI thread - parse JSON and retry logic off the critical render path
* Always surface network state - offline, stale, and error are distinct UX modes
* Centralize transport in one api/client module with HTTPS enforcement
* Default fetch; add axios only when interceptors or progress justify bundle cost
* Wire TanStack Query focusManager and onlineManager before shipping feeds
* Retry idempotent reads; never blind-retry POST without idempotency keys
