Dokumen: Networking Basics
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/networking-basics/

# Networking Basics

10 examples for timeouts, cancellation, and parsing at the mobile edge - the foundation every Expo SDK 57 app needs before adding TanStack Query or axios.

Highlights / Networking Basics

* React Native ships fetch and AbortController - no polyfill required on Hermes
* Always set timeouts on mobile; LTE handoffs hang longer than Wi‑Fi
* Cancel in-flight requests on unmount to avoid setState-after-unmount warnings
* Parse JSON at the edge with Zod - never trust raw response shapes
* Classify errors: offline, timeout, HTTP status - UX copy differs for each
* Centralize fetch in one api/client module - attach auth headers once

## Prerequisites

React Native 0.86 includes a **WHATWG fetch** implementation backed by native networking stacks. Start from a blank Expo app:

```bash
npx create-expo-app@latest MyNetworkApp --template blank-typescript
cd MyNetworkApp
npx expo install zod @react-native-community/netinfo
```

Create a small API module so screens never call raw URLs:

```ts
// src/api/config.ts
export const API_BASE =
  process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL ?? "https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com";
```

> **Tooling:** These examples target **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4), **React Native 0.86.0**, and **React 19.2.3**. Test on a physical device over cellular - simulators hide LTE handoff pain.

---

## Basic Examples

### 1. A Minimal GET with fetch

Mobile `fetch` mirrors web APIs. Always check `response.ok` before parsing - HTTP 404 still resolves the promise.

```ts
async function getPost(id: number) {
  const res = await fetch(`${API_BASE}/posts/${id}`);
  if (!res.ok) {
    throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);
  }
  return res.json() as Promise<{ id: number; title: string; body: string }>;
}
```

* **`fetch` never throws on 4xx/5xx** - you must inspect `res.ok` or `res.status`
* **DNS and TLS errors throw** `TypeError` - often indistinguishable from offline on first glance
* Keep URLs in `API_BASE` - never scatter production hosts across feature folders

> **Related:** [Fetch vs axios](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/fetch-vs-axios/) - when interceptors justify the bundle cost

---

### 2. Request Timeouts with AbortController

Unlike browsers, React Native fetch has **no built-in `timeout` option**. Combine `AbortController` with `setTimeout`:

```ts
export async function fetchWithTimeout(
  input: RequestInfo | URL,
  init: RequestInit = {},
  timeoutMs = 10_000
) {
  const controller = new AbortController();
  const timer = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), timeoutMs);
 
  try {
    const res = await fetch(input, { ...init, signal: controller.signal });
    return res;
  } finally {
    clearTimeout(timer);
  }
}
```

```ts
// Usage
const res = await fetchWithTimeout(`${API_BASE}/posts/1`, {}, 8_000);
```

* **Default 8–15 s on reads** - subway tunnels and elevator dead zones exceed 3 s regularly
* **Shorter for mutations** - users perceive stalled POSTs as broken; fail fast and offer Retry
* `AbortError` on timeout is distinct from network `TypeError` - classify before showing copy

---

### 3. Cancel In-Flight Requests on Unmount

Screens unmount when users navigate away mid-request. Wire `AbortController` to `useEffect` cleanup:

```tsx
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { ActivityIndicator, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
export function PostDetail({ postId }: { postId: number }) {
  const [post, setPost] = useState<{ title: string } | null>(null);
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);
 
  useEffect(() => {
    const controller = new AbortController();
 
    (async () => {
      try {
        const res = await fetch(`${API_BASE}/posts/${postId}`, {
          signal: controller.signal,
        });
        if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);
        setPost(await res.json());
      } catch (e) {
        if (e instanceof Error && e.name === "AbortError") return;
        setError(e instanceof Error ? e.message : "Request failed");
      }
    })();
 
    return () => controller.abort();
  }, [postId]);
 
  if (error) return <Text>{error}</Text>;
  if (!post) return <ActivityIndicator />;
  return <Text>{post.title}</Text>;
}
```

* **Ignore `AbortError` in catch** - cancellation is expected, not a user-facing failure
* Changing `postId` aborts the previous request automatically via effect re-run
* With TanStack Query, prefer `queryKey` + built-in cancellation - see [TanStack Query on Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/tanstack-query-on-mobile/)

---

### 4. Parse JSON Safely at the Edge

Never cast `res.json()` blindly. Validate once at the network boundary:

```ts
import { z } from "zod";
 
const postSchema = z.object({
  id: z.number(),
  title: z.string(),
  body: z.string(),
});
 
export type Post = z.infer<typeof postSchema>;
 
export async function getPostSafe(id: number): Promise<Post> {
  const res = await fetchWithTimeout(`${API_BASE}/posts/${id}`);
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);
 
  const raw: unknown = await res.json();
  return postSchema.parse(raw);
}
```

* **Zod `.parse` throws `ZodError`** - map to "unexpected server response" in UI, not a stack trace
* Shared schemas power contract tests - see [Contract Tests for APIs](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/contract-tests-for-apis/)
* Parse **arrays** with `z.array(schema)` - list endpoints drift more often than detail endpoints

---

### 5. Classify Network Errors for UX

Mobile users need different copy for offline, timeout, and server errors:

```ts
export type NetworkErrorKind = "offline" | "timeout" | "http" | "parse" | "unknown";
 
export function classifyFetchError(error: unknown, status?: number): NetworkErrorKind {
  if (status && status >= 400) return "http";
  if (error instanceof Error) {
    if (error.name === "AbortError") return "timeout";
    if (error instanceof TypeError) return "offline";
  }
  return "unknown";
}
 
export function userMessage(kind: NetworkErrorKind): string {
  switch (kind) {
    case "offline":
      return "No connection. Check airplane mode or try again when online.";
    case "timeout":
      return "This is taking too long. Try again on a stronger signal.";
    case "http":
      return "The server could not complete this request.";
    case "parse":
      return "Received an unexpected response. Try again later.";
    default:
      return "Something went wrong. Please retry.";
  }
}
```

* Pair with **NetInfo** for connectivity banners - see [Network Failure UX](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/error-resilience/network-failure-ux/)
* Do not show the offline banner on HTTP 500 - Wi‑Fi is fine; the server is not

---

### 6. JSON POST with Content-Type and Body

Mutations need explicit headers. `JSON.stringify` on plain objects - FormData is separate (multipart uploads):

```ts
export async function createPost(title: string, body: string) {
  const res = await fetchWithTimeout(
    `${API_BASE}/posts`,
    {
      method: "POST",
      headers: {
        Accept: "application/json",
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
      },
      body: JSON.stringify({ title, body, userId: 1 }),
    },
    12_000
  );
 
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);
  return postSchema.parse(await res.json());
}
```

* **`Content-Type: application/json`** is required - omitting it breaks many Rails/Express parsers
* **Idempotency keys** on POST belong in headers for payment flows - see [Retries, Backoff & Idempotency](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/retries-backoff-and-idempotency/)
* Attach auth tokens in a shared client - see [Mobile Auth Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/mobile-auth-basics/)

---

### 7. Query Parameters Without String Bugs

Build search URLs with `URLSearchParams` - avoids `?foo=undefined` and encoding mistakes:

```ts
export async function searchPosts(query: string, limit = 20) {
  const params = new URLSearchParams({
    q: query,
    _limit: String(limit),
  });
 
  const res = await fetchWithTimeout(`${API_BASE}/posts?${params}`);
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);
 
  const raw: unknown = await res.json();
  return z.array(postSchema).parse(raw);
}
```

* **Encode user input** - `URLSearchParams` handles `&`, spaces, and Unicode
* Omit empty optional params - `params.delete("q")` when query is blank
* For cursor pagination, pass `cursor` as a string param; validate shape with Zod

---

### 8. Central API Client with Auth Headers

One module attaches bearer tokens, base URL, and default timeout - features import `apiGet` / `apiPost`:

```ts
// src/api/client.ts
import * as SecureStore from "expo-secure-store";
import { fetchWithTimeout } from "./fetchWithTimeout";
import { API_BASE } from "./config";
 
async function authHeaders(): Promise<HeadersInit> {
  const token = await SecureStore.getItemAsync("access_token");
  return {
    Accept: "application/json",
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    ...(token ? { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } : {}),
  };
}
 
export async function apiGet<T>(path: string, parse: (raw: unknown) => T): Promise<T> {
  const res = await fetchWithTimeout(`${API_BASE}${path}`, {
    headers: await authHeaders(),
  });
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);
  return parse(await res.json());
}
```

```bash
npx expo install expo-secure-store
```

* **Never read tokens in every screen** - rotation and logout become impossible to audit
* On **401**, trigger refresh or session clear - see [Refresh Token Rotation](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/refresh-token-rotation/)
* Reject non-HTTPS URLs in production builds at this choke point

---

### 9. Handle Empty and Non-JSON Responses

DELETE and some PATCH endpoints return **204 No Content**. Calling `res.json()` throws:

```ts
export async function deletePost(id: number, headers: HeadersInit): Promise<void> {
  const res = await fetchWithTimeout(`${API_BASE}/posts/${id}`, {
    method: "DELETE",
    headers,
  });
 
  if (res.status === 204) return;
 
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);
 
  const text = await res.text();
  if (!text) return;
  // Some APIs return JSON bodies on DELETE - parse only when present
  JSON.parse(text);
}
```

* **Check `Content-Type`** before parsing - `text/html` error pages arrive as 200 from misconfigured proxies
* Use `res.text()` then `JSON.parse` when bodies are optional - clearer errors than `res.json()` on empty
* Log parse failures in dev only - never ship raw response bodies to users

---

### 10. Typed Hook with Loading, Error, and Retry

Before adopting TanStack Query, understand the manual pattern - then replace it:

```tsx
import { useCallback, useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { Pressable, Text, View } from "react-native";
import { API_BASE } from "../api/config";
import { fetchWithTimeout } from "../api/fetchWithTimeout";
import { postSchema, type Post } from "../api/posts";
 
export function PostScreen({ id }: { id: number }) {
  const [data, setData] = useState<Post | null>(null);
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true);
 
  const load = useCallback(async (signal?: AbortSignal) => {
    setLoading(true);
    setError(null);
    try {
      const res = await fetchWithTimeout(`${API_BASE}/posts/${id}`, { signal });
      if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);
      setData(postSchema.parse(await res.json()));
    } catch (e) {
      if (e instanceof Error && e.name === "AbortError") return;
      setError(e instanceof Error ? e.message : "Failed");
    } finally {
      setLoading(false);
    }
  }, [id]);
 
  useEffect(() => {
    const controller = new AbortController();
    void load(controller.signal);
    return () => controller.abort();
  }, [load]);
 
  return (
    <View style={{ padding: 16 }}>
      {loading && <Text>Loading…</Text>}
      {error && (
        <>
          <Text>{error}</Text>
          <Pressable onPress={() => load()}>
            <Text>Retry</Text>
          </Pressable>
        </>
      )}
      {data && <Text>{data.title}</Text>}
    </View>
  );
}
```

* **Retry calls `load()`** - not `Updates.reloadAsync()` or app restart
* Graduate to `useQuery` when you need cache, dedupe, and background refetch - [TanStack Query on Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/tanstack-query-on-mobile/)
* Persist read models offline with [Offline-First Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/data-offline/offline-first-basics/)

---

## Intermediate Patterns

### Combine Timeout + Cancellation + Parse

```ts
export async function requestJson<T>(
  path: string,
  options: RequestInit & { timeoutMs?: number; parse: (raw: unknown) => T }
): Promise<T> {
  const { timeoutMs = 10_000, parse, ...init } = options;
  const res = await fetchWithTimeout(`${API_BASE}${path}`, init, timeoutMs);
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);
  return parse(await res.json());
}
```

### React 19 `use` with Suspense (Optional)

If your team adopts Suspense for data, keep the same timeout wrapper - only the consumption site changes. Most Expo apps still prefer TanStack Query for cache semantics on mobile.

---

## Gotchas

* **Assuming fetch throws on 404** - It resolves; check `res.ok`. **Fix:** Central client throws on `!res.ok`.
* **No timeout on cellular** - Requests hang until OS kills them. **Fix:** `AbortController` + 8–15 s default.
* **Parsing before checking status** - Error HTML bodies crash JSON parse. **Fix:** Check `res.ok` first.
* **setState after unmount** - Forgot abort cleanup. **Fix:** `useEffect` return `() => controller.abort()`.
* **Trusting `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL` in prod without HTTPS guard** - Cleartext leaks tokens. **Fix:** Assert `https://` in production client.

Dokumen: Retries, Backoff & Idempotency
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/retries-backoff-and-idempotency/

# Retries, Backoff & Idempotency

Resilient calls on flaky LTE and subway mode - when to retry, how to back off, and how idempotency keys prevent duplicate charges.

Highlights / Retries, Backoff & Idempotency

* Retry only idempotent requests or those with idempotency keys - never blind POST retries
* Exponential backoff with jitter prevents thundering herds when LTE returns
* Cap attempts at 3–5 - infinite retry drains battery in airplane mode
* Pair retries with onlineManager - pause while offline, resume on reconnect
* 429 Retry-After headers deserve respect - sleep before next attempt

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```ts
// src/api/retry.ts
export type RetryOptions = {
  maxAttempts?: number;
  baseDelayMs?: number;
  maxDelayMs?: number;
  shouldRetry?: (error: unknown, attempt: number) => boolean;
};
 
function jitter(ms: number): number {
  return ms * (0.5 + Math.random() * 0.5);
}
 
export async function fetchWithRetry(
  input: RequestInfo | URL,
  init?: RequestInit,
  opts: RetryOptions = {}
): Promise<Response> {
  const {
    maxAttempts = 4,
    baseDelayMs = 500,
    maxDelayMs = 8_000,
    shouldRetry = defaultShouldRetry,
  } = opts;
 
  let lastError: unknown;
 
  for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= maxAttempts; attempt++) {
    try {
      const res = await fetch(input, init);
      if (res.status === 429) {
        const retryAfter = res.headers.get("Retry-After");
        const waitSec = retryAfter ? Number(retryAfter) : 2 ** attempt;
        await sleep(jitter(waitSec * 1000));
        continue;
      }
      if (res.ok || !shouldRetry(res, attempt)) return res;
      lastError = new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);
    } catch (error) {
      lastError = error;
      if (!shouldRetry(error, attempt)) throw error;
    }
 
    if (attempt < maxAttempts) {
      const delay = Math.min(baseDelayMs * 2 ** (attempt - 1), maxDelayMs);
      await sleep(jitter(delay));
    }
  }
 
  throw lastError;
}
 
function defaultShouldRetry(error: unknown, attempt: number): boolean {
  if (attempt >= 4) return false;
  if (error instanceof Response) {
    const status = error.status;
    return status >= 500 || status === 408 || status === 429;
  }
  if (error instanceof Error) {
    if (error.name === "AbortError") return false;
    return error instanceof TypeError; // network blip
  }
  return false;
}
 
function sleep(ms: number) {
  return new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));
}
```

**When to reach for this:**

* GET and safe HEAD requests on unreliable cellular.
* Idempotent PUT/DELETE with server-side deduplication.
* Background sync replay after offline queues drain.

## Working Example

```tsx
import NetInfo from "@react-native-community/netinfo";
import { useMutation, useQueryClient } from "@tanstack/react-query";
import { useCallback } from "react";
import { fetchWithRetry } from "../api/retry";
 
const API = process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL ?? "https://api.example.com";
 
function idempotencyKey(): string {
  return `idem-${Date.now()}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 9)}`;
}
 
async function createOrder(items: { sku: string; qty: number }[], key: string) {
  const res = await fetchWithRetry(
    `${API}/orders`,
    {
      method: "POST",
      headers: {
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
        "Idempotency-Key": key,
      },
      body: JSON.stringify({ items }),
    },
    {
      maxAttempts: 3,
      shouldRetry: (err, attempt) => {
        if (err instanceof Response) return err.status >= 500 && attempt < 3;
        return err instanceof TypeError && attempt < 3;
      },
    }
  );
 
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);
  return res.json();
}
 
export function useCreateOrder() {
  const queryClient = useQueryClient();
 
  const waitForOnline = useCallback(async () => {
    const state = await NetInfo.fetch();
    if (state.isConnected && state.isInternetReachable !== false) return;
    await new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
      const unsub = NetInfo.addEventListener((s) => {
        if (s.isConnected && s.isInternetReachable !== false) {
          unsub();
          resolve();
        }
      });
    });
  }, []);
 
  return useMutation({
    mutationFn: async (items: { sku: string; qty: number }[]) => {
      await waitForOnline();
      const key = idempotencyKey();
      return createOrder(items, key);
    },
    retry: false, // retries handled in fetchWithRetry with idempotency key
    onSuccess: () => queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ["orders"] }),
  });
}
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* **Exponential backoff + jitter** spaces retries when a cell tower recovers and many clients reconnect at once.
* **Idempotency-Key header** lets the server return the same order if the client retries a POST after timeout.
* **429 handling** reads `Retry-After` when present.
* **`retry: false` on useMutation** when transport-layer retry already runs with keys - avoids duplicate mutation fn calls with new keys.
* **waitForOnline** gates user-initiated checkout - optional; background queues use different patterns in [Network Failure UX](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/error-resilience/network-failure-ux/).

## Deep Dive

### What Is Safe to Retry?

| Method / case | Retry? | Condition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET, HEAD | ✅ Yes | Bounded attempts + backoff |
| PUT with stable id | ✅ Usually | Server upserts by resource id |
| DELETE | ✅ Usually | Second delete should 404 safely |
| POST payment | ⚠️ Only with idempotency key | Server stores key → same response |
| POST without key | ❌ No | Risk duplicate rows/charges |
| 401 / 403 | ❌ No | Refresh auth first |
| 400 validation | ❌ No | Payload is wrong - fix client |
| 409 conflict | ❌ No | Merge or show UI |

### Idempotency Key Contract

```ts
type IdempotentRequest = {
  idempotencyKey: string; // client-generated UUID
  operation: "createOrder" | "capturePayment";
  payload: unknown;
};
```

* **Generate once per user action** - store with offline queue item; replay same key on flush
* **Server stores key → response** for 24–72 h - document TTL with backend
* **Stripe, Adyen, and many REST APIs** accept `Idempotency-Key` - align header name with provider
* Client keys complement server **[Optimistic UI](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/data-offline/optimistic-ui/)** - pending rows map to keys

### TanStack Query Retry Tuning

```tsx
export const queryClient = new QueryClient({
  defaultOptions: {
    queries: {
      retry: (failureCount, error) => {
        if (failureCount >= 3) return false;
        if (error instanceof Error && error.message.startsWith("HTTP 4")) return false;
        return true;
      },
      retryDelay: (attempt) => Math.min(1000 * 2 ** attempt, 30_000),
    },
    mutations: {
      retry: 0,
    },
  },
});
```

* Wire **onlineManager** so retries pause offline - see [TanStack Query on Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/tanstack-query-on-mobile/)
* **Mutations default `retry: 0`** - explicit idempotency at transport layer instead

### LTE / Subway Failure Modes

| Symptom | Likely cause | Retry strategy |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TypeError: Network request failed` | Handoff, tunnel, airplane | Backoff; pause if offline |
| Hang then timeout | Weak signal | AbortController + retry |
| HTTP 502/503 | Gateway recovery | Retry with jitter |
| Intermittent 200 + empty body | CDN glitch | Parse guard; retry once |
| Success on server, timeout on client | Slow ACK | Idempotency key on POST |

### Offline Queue Replay

```ts
for (const item of queue) {
  try {
    await fetchWithRetry(url, { headers: { "Idempotency-Key": item.key }, ... });
    dequeue(item);
  } catch {
    incrementAttempts(item);
    if (item.attempts > 5) surfaceToUser(item);
  }
}
```

* **FIFO per entity** - two updates to same row should not race
* After max attempts, **show manual Retry/Discard** - silent loss erodes trust
* Full queue design in [Sync Strategies](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/data-offline/sync-strategies/)

## Gotchas

* **Retrying POST without idempotency** - Double charges on timeout. **Fix:** Key per action; server dedupes.
* **Retrying 401** - Amplifies auth outage. **Fix:** Refresh token once; logout on failure.
* **No jitter** - LTE recovery causes synchronized client spikes. **Fix:** Randomize delay 50–100%.
* **Infinite TanStack Query retry** - Battery drain in airplane mode. **Fix:** Cap at 2–3 + onlineManager.
* **New idempotency key on each retry attempt** - Server creates duplicates. **Fix:** Same key for all attempts of one action.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Transport `fetchWithRetry` | Custom fetch client | Already using axios-retry with same rules |
| TanStack Query `retry` | GET queries | Non-idempotent mutations |
| Background TaskManager replay | Large uploads hours later | Immediate user feedback required |
| Server long-polling | Client retry budget exhausted | Normal REST with short timeouts |

## FAQs

How many retry attempts on mobile?

**3–4** for reads with exponential backoff. **0–1** for mutations unless idempotency keys are guaranteed.

What is jitter?

Randomizing delay (e.g. 500–1000 ms instead of exactly 750 ms) so thousands of devices do not retry in the same millisecond when a tower comes back.

Should I retry 404?

No - the resource is missing or the URL is wrong. Retrying wastes battery and obscures bugs.

How do idempotency keys differ from client-generated IDs?

Idempotency keys tell the **server** to dedupe within a TTL. Client IDs become the resource id in the payload - use both for offline creates when possible.

Does axios-retry replace this pattern?

It can, if configured with the same idempotency and status rules. Transport-agnostic utilities keep fetch and axios consistent.

## Related

* [Networking Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/networking-basics/) - timeouts and AbortController
* [TanStack Query on Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/tanstack-query-on-mobile/) - onlineManager and query retry defaults
* [Network Failure UX](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/error-resilience/network-failure-ux/) - offline queues and user-facing retry
* [Optimistic UI](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/data-offline/optimistic-ui/) - pending state until idempotent ack
* [Sync Strategies](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/data-offline/sync-strategies/) - ordered replay and conflict handling
* [Networking Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/best-practices/) - section summary

Dokumen: TanStack Query on Mobile
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/tanstack-query-on-mobile/

# TanStack Query on Mobile

`focusManager`, `onlineManager`, and refetch on app foreground - the mobile-specific wiring TanStack Query needs beyond web tutorials.

Highlights / TanStack Query on Mobile

* Wire focusManager to AppState - refetch stale queries when users return from background
* Wire onlineManager to NetInfo - pause retries offline, resume on reconnect
* Default staleTime 30–60s on feeds - balance freshness with battery on LTE
* Forward AbortSignal from queryFn to fetch for automatic cancellation
* persistQueryClient pairs with AsyncStorage for read-mostly offline shells

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```tsx
// src/lib/queryClient.ts
import NetInfo from "@react-native-community/netinfo";
import { QueryClient, focusManager, onlineManager } from "@tanstack/react-query";
import { AppState, Platform } from "react-native";
 
// Refetch when app returns to foreground
focusManager.setEventListener((handleFocus) => {
  const sub = AppState.addEventListener("change", (state) => {
    if (state === "active") handleFocus();
  });
  return () => sub.remove();
});
 
// Pause retries when offline; resume when connected
onlineManager.setEventListener((setOnline) => {
  return NetInfo.addEventListener((state) => {
    const online =
      state.isConnected !== false && state.isInternetReachable !== false;
    setOnline(online);
  });
});
 
export const queryClient = new QueryClient({
  defaultOptions: {
    queries: {
      retry: 2,
      staleTime: 30_000,
      gcTime: 24 * 60 * 60_000,
      refetchOnWindowFocus: true,
      refetchOnReconnect: true,
    },
  },
});
```

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx
import { QueryClientProvider } from "@tanstack/react-query";
import { queryClient } from "../src/lib/queryClient";
 
export default function RootLayout() {
  return (
    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
      {/* routes */}
    </QueryClientProvider>
  );
}
```

```bash
npx expo install @tanstack/react-query @react-native-community/netinfo
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Any Expo app with multiple screens reading the same API data.
* Feeds, profiles, or settings that should refresh when users foreground the app.
* Apps that must stop useless retries in airplane mode.

## Working Example

```tsx
import NetInfo from "@react-native-community/netinfo";
import {
  QueryClient,
  QueryClientProvider,
  focusManager,
  onlineManager,
  useQuery,
} from "@tanstack/react-query";
import { useEffect } from "react";
import {
  AppState,
  FlatList,
  Pressable,
  RefreshControl,
  StyleSheet,
  Text,
  View,
} from "react-native";
 
const API = "https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com";
 
focusManager.setEventListener((handleFocus) => {
  const sub = AppState.addEventListener("change", (s) => {
    if (s === "active") handleFocus();
  });
  return () => sub.remove();
});
 
onlineManager.setEventListener((setOnline) =>
  NetInfo.addEventListener((state) => {
    setOnline(!!state.isConnected && state.isInternetReachable !== false);
  })
);
 
const queryClient = new QueryClient({
  defaultOptions: {
    queries: { staleTime: 45_000, retry: 2, refetchOnReconnect: true },
  },
});
 
async function fetchPosts({ signal }: { signal?: AbortSignal }) {
  const res = await fetch(`${API}/posts?_limit=12`, { signal });
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);
  return res.json() as Promise<{ id: number; title: string }[]>;
}
 
function PostsScreen() {
  const { data, error, isError, isFetching, refetch, dataUpdatedAt } = useQuery({
    queryKey: ["posts"],
    queryFn: fetchPosts,
  });
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.screen}>
      <Text style={styles.meta}>
        {isFetching ? "Updating…" : `Updated ${new Date(dataUpdatedAt).toLocaleTimeString()}`}
      </Text>
 
      <FlatList
        data={data}
        keyExtractor={(item) => String(item.id)}
        refreshControl={<RefreshControl refreshing={isFetching} onRefresh={refetch} />}
        renderItem={({ item }) => <Text style={styles.row}>{item.title}</Text>}
        ListEmptyComponent={isError ? null : <Text>Loading…</Text>}
      />
 
      {isError && (
        <View style={styles.error}>
          <Text>{error instanceof Error ? error.message : "Failed"}</Text>
          <Pressable onPress={() => refetch()}>
            <Text style={styles.retry}>Retry</Text>
          </Pressable>
        </View>
      )}
    </View>
  );
}
 
export default function App() {
  return (
    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
      <PostsScreen />
    </QueryClientProvider>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  screen: { flex: 1, padding: 16, backgroundColor: "#fff" },
  meta: { fontSize: 12, color: "#64748b", marginBottom: 8 },
  row: { paddingVertical: 10, borderBottomWidth: StyleSheet.hairlineWidth, borderColor: "#e2e8f0" },
  error: { padding: 12, backgroundColor: "#fee2e2", borderRadius: 8 },
  retry: { color: "#2563eb", fontWeight: "600", marginTop: 8 },
});
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* **`focusManager` + `AppState`** refetches stale queries when the app becomes `active`.
* **`onlineManager` + NetInfo** pauses retries offline and triggers `refetchOnReconnect` when LTE returns.
* **`signal` in `queryFn`** cancels fetch when the query unmounts or key changes.
* **Pull-to-refresh** calls `refetch()` - idiomatic mobile UX alongside foreground refetch.
* **`dataUpdatedAt`** labels staleness for users on flaky networks.

## Deep Dive

### focusManager and App Foreground

| AppState | TanStack behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `active` | `handleFocus()` - refetch stale queries if `refetchOnWindowFocus` |
| `background` | Queries stay cached; in-flight requests may complete |
| `inactive` (iOS) | Treat like brief interruption - same listener |

```tsx
// Optional: only refetch "important" queries on focus
queryClient.refetchQueries({ queryKey: ["inbox"], type: "active" });
```

* Users **expect fresh inbox counts** after switching back from another app - `staleTime: 0` for those keys only
* **Do not refetch everything** on every focus - battery and API rate limits suffer; tune per `queryKey`
* Pair with [Network Failure UX](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/error-resilience/network-failure-ux/) banners when refetch fails offline

### onlineManager and NetInfo

```tsx
onlineManager.setEventListener((setOnline) => {
  return NetInfo.addEventListener((state) => {
    // null reachability = unknown - do not force offline
    if (state.isConnected === false) {
      setOnline(false);
      return;
    }
    if (state.isInternetReachable === false) {
      setOnline(false);
      return;
    }
    setOnline(true);
  });
});
```

* **`refetchOnReconnect: true`** (default) refetches stale queries when `onlineManager` flips true
* Mutations should use `networkMode: "offlineFirst"` only when you have a persisted queue - see [Offline-First Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/data-offline/offline-first-basics/)
* Flush offline mutation queues in a NetInfo listener **in addition to** onlineManager - queues are app logic, not built into Query

### Mobile QueryClient Defaults

| Option | Suggested mobile value | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `staleTime` | 30–60 s feeds; 5–15 min catalogs | Reduces LTE chatter |
| `gcTime` | 24 h | Survive short offline sessions |
| `retry` | 2 | LTE blips recover; cap avoids battery drain |
| `retryDelay` | exponential 1s → 4s | See [Retries doc](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/retries-backoff-and-idempotency/) |
| `refetchOnWindowFocus` | `true` with focusManager | Mobile "window" = app foreground |
| `refetchOnReconnect` | `true` with onlineManager | Catch up after subway |

### Persist Cache to Device Storage

```bash
npx expo install @tanstack/react-query-persist-client @react-native-async-storage/async-storage
```

```tsx
import AsyncStorage from "@react-native-async-storage/async-storage";
import { createAsyncStoragePersister } from "@tanstack/query-async-storage-persister";
import { PersistQueryClientProvider } from "@tanstack/react-query-persist-client";
 
const persister = createAsyncStoragePersister({ storage: AsyncStorage });
 
// Wrap QueryClientProvider with PersistQueryClientProvider in root layout
```

* Persist **read-mostly** keys only - exclude PII-heavy queries unless encrypted
* **Clear persister on logout** - pair with [Mobile Auth Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/mobile-auth-basics/)
* For high-performance KV, swap AsyncStorage for MMKV - [MMKV patterns](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/data-offline/mmkv-and-high-performance-kv/)

### Auth-Aware Queries

```tsx
useQuery({
  queryKey: ["profile", userId],
  queryFn: fetchProfile,
  enabled: !!userId,
});
```

* **`enabled: false`** until session exists - avoids 401 storms on launch
* Invalidate `["profile"]` on logout: `queryClient.clear()` or `removeQueries`
* Attach tokens in `queryFn` via shared client - not inside every hook

## Gotchas

* **Skipping focusManager** - Data looks stale after users return from background. **Fix:** `AppState` listener in app bootstrap.
* **Treating `isInternetReachable: null` as offline** - Banner and retry flicker on launch. **Fix:** Only set offline on explicit `false`.
* **No `signal` in queryFn** - Requests complete after unmount. **Fix:** `fetch(url, { signal })` with Query's injected signal.
* **`staleTime: 0` globally** - Refetch on every focus drains battery. **Fix:** Per-query tuning.
* **Persisting auth errors** - Cached 401 profile survives restarts. **Fix:** Clear cache on logout and failed refresh.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TanStack Query + managers | Default server state for Expo | Pure local state with no network |
| SWR | Team already on SWR from web | Greenfield Expo - Query has richer RN docs in this site |
| Redux + thunks | Legacy store already central | New apps - duplicate cache logic |
| Manual useEffect fetch | One screen, no shared cache | Multiple screens reading same API |

## FAQs

Where do I call focusManager.setEventListener?

Once at module load in `queryClient.ts` or root `_layout.tsx` before any queries run - not inside individual screens.

Does refetchOnWindowFocus work without focusManager on RN?

No - React Native has no `window` focus events. You must wire `AppState` to `focusManager`.

Should mutations retry automatically?

Only **idempotent** mutations with server-side keys. Default `retry: 0` for POST payments - see [Retries, Backoff & Idempotency](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/retries-backoff-and-idempotency/).

How do I prefetch for the next screen?

```tsx
queryClient.prefetchQuery({ queryKey: ["post", id], queryFn: () => fetchPost(id) });
```

Call on `onPressIn` of list rows for snappy navigation.

How does this relate to offline-first?

TanStack Query gives **stale-while-revalidate** and optional persistence. Full offline-first adds SQLite sync - [Offline-First Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/data-offline/offline-first-basics/).

Dokumen: WebSockets & Real-Time
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/websockets-and-real-time/

# WebSockets & Real-Time

Reconnect strategies and battery-aware polling fallbacks for live data on Expo SDK 57 without draining battery in background.

Highlights / WebSockets & Real-Time

* WebSockets stay open - iOS and Android will suspend them in background without a keepalive strategy
* Exponential reconnect backoff prevents reconnect storms when towers recover
* Fall back to polling when backgrounded or on metered networks to save battery
* AppState drives connect/disconnect - do not leave sockets open when inactive
* Pair real-time updates with TanStack Query cache patches - avoid duplicate sources of truth

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```ts
// src/realtime/useReconnectingSocket.ts
import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react";
import { AppState, type AppStateStatus } from "react-native";
 
type Options = {
  url: string;
  onMessage: (data: unknown) => void;
  maxBackoffMs?: number;
};
 
export function useReconnectingSocket({ url, onMessage, maxBackoffMs = 30_000 }: Options) {
  const wsRef = useRef<WebSocket | null>(null);
  const attemptRef = useRef(0);
  const [connected, setConnected] = useState(false);
  const appState = useRef<AppStateStatus>(AppState.currentState);
 
  useEffect(() => {
    let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;
    let closed = false;
 
    function connect() {
      if (closed || appState.current !== "active") return;
 
      const ws = new WebSocket(url);
      wsRef.current = ws;
 
      ws.onopen = () => {
        attemptRef.current = 0;
        setConnected(true);
      };
 
      ws.onmessage = (event) => {
        try {
          onMessage(JSON.parse(String(event.data)));
        } catch {
          onMessage(event.data);
        }
      };
 
      ws.onclose = () => {
        setConnected(false);
        if (closed || appState.current !== "active") return;
        const delay = Math.min(1000 * 2 ** attemptRef.current, maxBackoffMs);
        attemptRef.current += 1;
        timer = setTimeout(connect, delay * (0.5 + Math.random() * 0.5));
      };
 
      ws.onerror = () => ws.close();
    }
 
    const sub = AppState.addEventListener("change", (next) => {
      appState.current = next;
      if (next === "active") {
        connect();
      } else {
        wsRef.current?.close();
        wsRef.current = null;
        setConnected(false);
      }
    });
 
    connect();
 
    return () => {
      closed = true;
      if (timer) clearTimeout(timer);
      wsRef.current?.close();
      sub.remove();
    };
  }, [url, maxBackoffMs, onMessage]);
 
  return { connected };
}
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Chat, live scores, collaborative cursors, or order-status streams.
* Foreground-first experiences where sub-second latency matters.
* Apps that can **degrade to polling** when backgrounded.

## Working Example

```tsx
import NetInfo from "@react-native-community/netinfo";
import { useQueryClient } from "@tanstack/react-query";
import { useCallback, useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react";
import { AppState, FlatList, StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
type Message = { id: string; text: string; ts: number };
 
const WS_URL = "wss://echo.websocket.events"; // replace with your gateway
const POLL_MS_FOREGROUND = 15_000;
const POLL_MS_BACKGROUND = 120_000;
 
export function ChatScreen() {
  const queryClient = useQueryClient();
  const [messages, setMessages] = useState<Message[]>([]);
  const [mode, setMode] = useState<"socket" | "poll">("socket");
  const pollRef = useRef<ReturnType<typeof setInterval> | null>(null);
 
  const appendMessage = useCallback(
    (msg: Message) => {
      setMessages((prev) => [...prev, msg]);
      queryClient.setQueryData<Message[]>(["inbox"], (old = []) => [...old, msg]);
    },
    [queryClient]
  );
 
  // WebSocket path (foreground)
  useEffect(() => {
    if (mode !== "socket") return;
 
    let ws: WebSocket | null = null;
    let reconnectTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;
    let attempt = 0;
    let disposed = false;
 
    function connect() {
      if (disposed || AppState.currentState !== "active") return;
      ws = new WebSocket(WS_URL);
 
      ws.onopen = () => {
        attempt = 0;
      };
 
      ws.onmessage = (e) => {
        appendMessage({
          id: String(Date.now()),
          text: String(e.data),
          ts: Date.now(),
        });
      };
 
      ws.onclose = () => {
        if (disposed) return;
        const delay = Math.min(1000 * 2 ** attempt++, 20_000);
        reconnectTimer = setTimeout(connect, delay);
      };
    }
 
    connect();
 
    return () => {
      disposed = true;
      if (reconnectTimer) clearTimeout(reconnectTimer);
      ws?.close();
    };
  }, [mode, appendMessage]);
 
  // Battery-aware fallback: polling when backgrounded or on cellular policy
  useEffect(() => {
    async function pickMode() {
      const net = await NetInfo.fetch();
      const background = AppState.currentState !== "active";
      const expensive = net.type === "cellular";
 
      if (background || expensive) {
        setMode("poll");
      } else {
        setMode("socket");
      }
    }
 
    void pickMode();
 
    const appSub = AppState.addEventListener("change", () => void pickMode());
    const netSub = NetInfo.addEventListener(() => void pickMode());
 
    return () => {
      appSub.remove();
      netSub.remove();
    };
  }, []);
 
  useEffect(() => {
    if (pollRef.current) clearInterval(pollRef.current);
 
    if (mode !== "poll") return;
 
    const interval =
      AppState.currentState === "active" ? POLL_MS_FOREGROUND : POLL_MS_BACKGROUND;
 
    pollRef.current = setInterval(async () => {
      // Replace with your REST delta endpoint
      const res = await fetch("https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/comments?_limit=1");
      if (!res.ok) return;
      const data = await res.json();
      appendMessage({
        id: `poll-${Date.now()}`,
        text: data[0]?.body ?? "poll tick",
        ts: Date.now(),
      });
    }, interval);
 
    return () => {
      if (pollRef.current) clearInterval(pollRef.current);
    };
  }, [mode, appendMessage]);
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.screen}>
      <Text style={styles.badge}>
        Transport: {mode === "socket" ? "WebSocket" : "polling"} ({mode === "poll" ? "battery-aware" : "live"})
      </Text>
      <FlatList
        data={messages}
        keyExtractor={(m) => m.id}
        renderItem={({ item }) => <Text style={styles.row}>{item.text}</Text>}
      />
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  screen: { flex: 1, padding: 16, backgroundColor: "#fff" },
  badge: { fontSize: 12, color: "#64748b", marginBottom: 8 },
  row: { paddingVertical: 8, borderBottomWidth: StyleSheet.hairlineWidth, borderColor: "#e2e8f0" },
});
```

```bash
npx expo install @react-native-community/netinfo @tanstack/react-query
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* **Reconnect with exponential backoff** when the socket drops on LTE handoff.
* **AppState disconnect** in background - avoids iOS watchdog kills and wasted radio time.
* **Polling fallback** with slower interval when backgrounded or on cellular - battery-aware degradation.
* **TanStack Query cache patch** via `setQueryData` - one inbox source for list screens.
* **NetInfo policy** toggles transport mode - product decision, not one-size-fits-all.

## Deep Dive

### Reconnect Strategy

| Phase | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `onclose` / `onerror` | Close socket, schedule reconnect |
| Backoff | `min(1000 * 2^attempt, 30s)` + jitter |
| App background | Cancel reconnect timer; close socket |
| App foreground | Reset attempt counter optional; connect immediately |
| Auth expiry | Send refresh token over REST first - see [Auth Session](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/auth-session-lifecycle/) |

```ts
// Heartbeat - detect half-open connections
const ping = setInterval(() => {
  if (ws.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN) ws.send(JSON.stringify({ type: "ping" }));
}, 25_000);
```

* Servers should respond to **ping/pong** or close idle connections
* **Do not heartbeat in background** if you disconnected intentionally

### Battery-Aware Polling Fallback

| State | Suggested interval | Transport |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Foreground + Wi‑Fi | WebSocket or 10–15 s poll | Real-time |
| Foreground + cellular | WebSocket or 30 s poll | Product choice |
| Background | 60–300 s poll or none | Polling only if business requires |
| Offline | Stop both | Queue events locally |

* **iOS suspends JS timers** in background - use push notifications for must-deliver events
* **Android Doze** delays network - do not assume socket survival overnight
* For must-sync offline events, use [Background Sync](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/data-offline/background-sync-and-taskmanager/)

### Server- Sent Events and Socket.io

| Technology | RN support | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Native WebSocket | ✅ Built-in | Lowest overhead |
| Socket.io client | ✅ JS client | Extra protocol + bundle; match server |
| SSE (`EventSource`) | ⚠️ Limited | Often polyfilled; WS is simpler on RN |
| Firebase / Supabase realtime | ✅ SDKs | Managed reconnect; vendor lock-in |

### Merge Real-Time into Cached State

```tsx
queryClient.setQueryData<Thread>(["thread", id], (old) => {
  if (!old) return old;
  return { ...old, messages: [...old.messages, incoming] };
});
```

* **Invalidate** on reconnect gap: `refetchQueries` after `onopen` to backfill missed events
* **Version vectors** or `since=cursor` query params close the gap - document with backend
* Avoid maintaining parallel `useState` and Query cache - pick Query as source of truth

## Gotchas

* **Leaving WebSocket open in background** - Battery drain and iOS kill. **Fix:** Close on `background`; poll or push instead.
* **Reconnect without backoff** - Thundering herd on tower recovery. **Fix:** Exponential delay + jitter.
* **No gap fill after reconnect** - Missed messages while disconnected. **Fix:** REST delta with `since` cursor on `onopen`.
* **Duplicate messages** - Server replay + client append. **Fix:** Dedupe by `message.id`.
* **Ignoring auth token expiry on WS** - Silent disconnect loops. **Fix:** Refresh session before reconnect.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| WebSocket + reconnect hook | Chat, live dashboards | Rare updates - polling is simpler |
| Long polling | Corporate proxies block WS | You need sub-second latency |
| FCM / APNs push | Background must-know events | In-app typing indicators |
| TanStack Query refetch interval | Low-frequency stock prices | High-frequency streams |

## FAQs

Does React Native support WebSocket?

Yes - global `WebSocket` is available in Hermes. Use `wss://` in production; avoid cleartext `ws://` except local dev.

Should I use WebSockets on cellular?

Often yes for foreground chat. For background or metered-only features, degrade to slower polling or push notifications.

How do I authenticate a WebSocket?

Pass a short-lived token in query string (`wss://api.example.com/ws?token=`) or send an auth frame immediately after `onopen`. Refresh via REST before reconnect - [Mobile Auth Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/mobile-auth-basics/).

What interval for polling fallback?

Foreground: **15–30 s**. Background: **2–5 min** or stop entirely and rely on push. Measure battery with profiling tools on mid-tier Android.

Can Expo Go test WebSockets?

Yes for `wss` endpoints. Production auth and custom native gateways need dev-client builds - same as REST.

## Related

* [TanStack Query on Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/tanstack-query-on-mobile/) - cache updates from socket events
* [Retries, Backoff & Idempotency](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/retries-backoff-and-idempotency/) - backoff shared with HTTP
* [Background Sync](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/data-offline/background-sync-and-taskmanager/) - defer work when socket unavailable
* [Network Failure UX](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/error-resilience/network-failure-ux/) - offline banners during reconnect
* [Networking Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/best-practices/) - section summary

Dokumen: Analytics & Privacy
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/observability/analytics-and-privacy/

# Analytics & Privacy

**Segment** and **Amplitude** with **consent gates** and **ATT alignment** on Expo SDK 57. Product analytics belongs in the observability program, but it follows privacy rules crash reporters do not.

Highlights / Analytics & Privacy

* Analytics is not crash reporting - separate consent, retention, and vendor contracts
* Gate all product analytics behind explicit consent resolved before first track call
* iOS ATT applies to tracking that links user data across apps - align SDK config with legal review
* Segment is a router - one identify() fans out to Amplitude, Braze, etc. with transformations
* Reset analytics identity on logout - same discipline as auth token clearing
* Use coarse event schemas - stable names, typed properties, no PII in property keys

## Prerequisites

```bash
npm install @segment/analytics-react-native @segment/sovran-react-native
# or Amplitude directly:
npm install @amplitude/analytics-react-native
npx expo install expo-tracking-transparency
```

> **Tooling:** These examples target **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4), **React Native 0.86.0**, and **React 19.2.3**.

---

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

**1. Consent state**

```ts
// src/privacy/consent.ts
import AsyncStorage from "@react-native-async-storage/async-storage";
 
export type ConsentState = {
  analytics: boolean;
  crashReporting: boolean; // often separate - may default on for stability
  marketing: boolean;
  decidedAt: string | null;
};
 
const KEY = "consent_v1";
 
const defaultState: ConsentState = {
  analytics: false,
  crashReporting: true,
  marketing: false,
  decidedAt: null,
};
 
export async function getConsent(): Promise<ConsentState> {
  const raw = await AsyncStorage.getItem(KEY);
  return raw ? JSON.parse(raw) : defaultState;
}
 
export async function setConsent(patch: Partial<ConsentState>) {
  const next = { ...(await getConsent()), ...patch, decidedAt: new Date().toISOString() };
  await AsyncStorage.setItem(KEY, JSON.stringify(next));
  return next;
}
```

**2. ATT prompt (iOS)**

```ts
// src/privacy/att.ts
import { Platform } from "react-native";
import * as TrackingTransparency from "expo-tracking-transparency";
 
export async function requestAttIfNeeded() {
  if (Platform.OS !== "ios") return "unavailable";
 
  const { status: existing } = await TrackingTransparency.getTrackingPermissionsAsync();
  if (existing === "granted" || existing === "denied") return existing;
 
  const { status } = await TrackingTransparency.requestTrackingPermissionsAsync();
  return status;
}
```

**3. Gated analytics facade**

```ts
// src/analytics/index.ts
import { getConsent } from "@/privacy/consent";
 
type Props = Record<string, string | number | boolean | null>;
 
let segmentClient: { track: (e: string, p?: Props) => void; identify: (id: string, t?: Props) => void; reset: () => void } | null = null;
 
export async function initAnalytics() {
  const consent = await getConsent();
  if (!consent.analytics) return;
 
  const { createClient } = await import("@segment/analytics-react-native");
  segmentClient = createClient({
    writeKey: process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_SEGMENT_WRITE_KEY!,
    trackAppLifecycleEvents: true,
  });
}
 
export async function track(event: string, properties?: Props) {
  const consent = await getConsent();
  if (!consent.analytics || !segmentClient) return;
  segmentClient.track(event, sanitize(properties));
}
 
export async function identify(userId: string, traits?: Props) {
  const consent = await getConsent();
  if (!consent.analytics || !segmentClient) return;
  segmentClient.identify(userId, sanitize(traits));
}
 
export async function resetAnalytics() {
  segmentClient?.reset();
}
 
function sanitize(props?: Props): Props | undefined {
  if (!props) return props;
  const blocked = ["email", "phone", "name", "address"];
  return Object.fromEntries(
    Object.entries(props).filter(([k]) => !blocked.includes(k.toLowerCase()))
  );
}
```

**4. Consent UI gate in root layout**

```tsx
// src/privacy/ConsentGate.tsx
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { Button, Text, View } from "react-native";
import { getConsent, setConsent } from "./consent";
import { requestAttIfNeeded } from "./att";
import { initAnalytics } from "@/analytics";
 
export function ConsentGate({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  const [ready, setReady] = useState(false);
  const [showBanner, setShowBanner] = useState(false);
 
  useEffect(() => {
    (async () => {
      const consent = await getConsent();
      setShowBanner(!consent.decidedAt);
      if (consent.analytics) await initAnalytics();
      setReady(true);
    })();
  }, []);
 
  if (!ready) return null;
 
  if (showBanner) {
    return (
      <View style={{ padding: 24, gap: 12 }}>
        <Text>We use analytics to improve the app. You can change this in Settings.</Text>
        <Button
          title="Accept analytics"
          onPress={async () => {
            await requestAttIfNeeded();
            await setConsent({ analytics: true });
            await initAnalytics();
            setShowBanner(false);
          }}
        />
        <Button
          title="Decline"
          onPress={async () => {
            await setConsent({ analytics: false });
            setShowBanner(false);
          }}
        />
      </View>
    );
  }
 
  return <>{children}</>;
}
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Legal requires **opt-in** analytics in EU/UK and transparent ATT flows on iOS
* You route events to multiple destinations via **Segment** transformations
* **Amplitude** is your product source of truth - funnels, retention, experiments
* You must **reset identity on logout** alongside [Mobile Auth Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/mobile-auth-basics/)

// app/_layout.tsx

export async function logout() {

  await resetAnalytics();
  // clear React state, invalidate queries...

## Segment vs Amplitude

| Approach | Pros | Cons |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Segment router** | One SDK, many destinations, server-side filtering | Extra cost, another vendor |
| **Amplitude direct** | Rich product analytics UI, experimentation | Each new tool needs another SDK |
| **Both** | Segment → Amplitude common in enterprise | Two configs to keep in sync |

```ts
// Amplitude direct (when Segment is not required)
import { init, track, identify, reset } from "@amplitude/analytics-react-native";
 
export async function initAmplitude() {
  await init(process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_AMPLITUDE_API_KEY!, undefined, {
    trackingOptions: { ipAddress: false },
  });
}
```

* Disable **IP collection** on mobile when policy requires
* Use **Amplitude** groups for B2B `account_id` - not for PII
* Mirror `release` and `otaUpdateId` as super-properties for release correlation - [OTA Updates Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/ota-updates-basics/)

---

## ATT Alignment Checklist

1. **Info.plist** string explains *why* you request tracking - vague copy fails review
2. Request ATT **after** consent banner when analytics requires IDFA-linked data
3. If user denies ATT, **still allow** first-party analytics without cross-app tracking where legal permits
4. Document decision in privacy policy - link from Settings
5. Crash reporting (Sentry) is typically **not** ATT-gated - separate from marketing analytics

> **Related:** [Observability Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/observability/observability-basics/) - do not conflate `track()` with `captureException()`

---

## Event Design Rules

* **Past tense verbs**: `checkout_completed`, not `completeCheckout`
* **Stable names** - renaming breaks year-over-year charts; version with `schema_version` property if needed
* **No PII** in keys or values - use opaque `user_id` from auth, never email
* **One event per user action** - avoid duplicate `screen_view` from both router and screen `useEffect`
* Coarse **performance** events (`cold_start_ms`) belong here or in [Performance Monitoring](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/observability/performance-monitoring/) - pick one owner

---

## FAQs

Can I fire analytics before consent?

* Only strictly necessary **technical** events (if legal approves) - not funnels or ads measurement.
* Default **off** until `decidedAt` is set.

Does GDPR require opt-in for all analytics?

* Jurisdiction and interpretation vary - this doc shows opt-in patterns common in EU-facing apps.
* Involve legal/compliance; engineering implements the gate, not the law.

Should crash reporting respect analytics consent?

* Often **no** - stability telemetry may run under legitimate interest with separate disclosure.
* Document two toggles in Settings: "Share crash reports" vs "Share usage analytics".

How do I test ATT in Simulator?

* Settings → Privacy → Tracking - reset and re-test.
* Physical device behavior is authoritative for release sign-off.

Dokumen: Observability Best Practices
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/observability/best-practices/

# Observability Best Practices

A condensed summary of the 25 most important best practices drawn from every page in this section.

Highlights / Observability Best Practices

* Correlate release, OTA update id, sessionId, and route on every signal
* Crash reporting, structured logs, performance traces, and analytics serve different questions
* Upload source maps and native symbols on every production build - unsymbolicated stacks waste incidents
* Gate product analytics behind consent; crash stability telemetry may use separate policy
* Define SLOs with error budgets before launch week - not after the first spike
* Mid-tier Android validates performance SLOs - flagship phones hide cold start and jank regressions

1. **Know the four signals:** Crashes/fatals, handled errors, performance transactions, and product analytics - one vendor rarely replaces all four.
2. **Tag every report with release identity:** Native `version+build`, `otaUpdateId`, `runtimeVersion`, and `channel` - triage without reproducing on device.
3. **Generate sessionId on cold start:** Rotate on logout - same lifecycle discipline as [Mobile Auth Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/mobile-auth-basics/) tokens.
4. **Attach route to crashes and logs:** Expo Router `pathname` beats component display names - refactors rename components, routes stay stable.
5. **Separate native crashes from JS errors:** Different symbolication pipelines - Hermes maps and iOS dSYM / Android ProGuard are all required.
6. **Chain ErrorUtils handlers:** Never replace the previous global handler wholesale - dev redbox and SDK integrations depend on chaining.
7. **Initialize Sentry before routes mount:** Earliest `_layout` or `index.js` side effect - late init misses startup failures.
8. **Upload source maps on every EAS production build:** Unsymbolicated stacks are a release blocker, not a nice-to-have.
9. **Set Sentry `dist` to OTA update id:** Distinguish JS regressions from native regressions on the same store version.
10. **Enable native crash capture:** `@sentry/react-native` native modules - JS-only wrappers miss SIGABRT and OOM kills.
11. **Cap breadcrumbs and log buffers:** Unbounded rings OOM on chatty screens - drop `debug` first under pressure.
12. **Batch structured logs; ship on foreground:** Per-line HTTPS wastes battery - flush on `active` and best-effort on `background`.
13. **Never log tokens, emails, or card data:** Hash user ids; strip PII in `beforeSend` and analytics `sanitize()`.
14. **Gate analytics behind explicit consent:** Separate toggles for crash reporting vs product analytics - legal owns the policy, engineering implements gates.
15. **Request ATT only when needed on iOS:** Align `NSUserTrackingUsageDescription` with actual cross-app tracking - vague copy fails review.
16. **Reset analytics identity on logout:** `segment.reset()` / Amplitude `reset()` alongside secure store clearing.
17. **Use stable analytics event names:** `checkout_completed` not `completeCheckout` - renames break year-over-year charts.
18. **Sample production traces at 10–20%:** 100% capture overwhelms cost; 100% on checkout/payment routes is fine.
19. **Instrument navigation at the router layer:** One navigation span per pathname - not per leaf `useEffect`.
20. **Propagate trace headers on API calls:** `sentry-trace` or W3C `traceparent` - mobile-only latency hides backend blame.
21. **Define crash-free sessions SLO with session rules:** Align with Sentry session tracking - exclude dev and preview environments from production numerators.
22. **Track OTA apply success explicitly:** Silent `fetchUpdateAsync` failures erode trust - measure check → download → apply → next-launch `updateId`.
23. **Pair cold start SLO with reference device:** p95 on Pixel 6a class per [Performance Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/performance/performance-basics/) - iPhone Pro lies.
24. **Use error budgets to gate releases:** Burn > 50% in a week → feature freeze; 0% → halt store and OTA per [Rollback Runbook](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/rollback-runbook/).
25. **Run observability review before major OTAs:** Staged rollout + Release Health + OTA success SLO - rollback channel before store emergency.

## FAQs

Can one tool replace Sentry, Segment, and OpenTelemetry?

* Unified platforms exist but rarely excel at all four signal types on day one.
* Start with crash + logs + consent-gated analytics; add OTel when backend tracing matures.

What is the minimum viable observability for v1?

* Sentry with source maps, release tags, route breadcrumbs, and crash-free dashboard.
* Structured log buffer shipping on foreground is a close second for offline-first apps.

Should observability run in Expo Go?

* No - validate on development builds and EAS preview binaries; Expo Go shell skews crashes and performance.

How do observability and performance sections differ?

* [Performance](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/observability/performance-monitoring/) defines **budgets and optimization** - observability **measures and alerts** against those budgets in production.

Dokumen: Observability Highlights Summary
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/observability/highlights-summary/

# Observability Highlights Summary

Every highlight bullet from the 8 pages in this section, gathered on one page and grouped by the page it came from.

Highlights / Observability Highlights Summary

* Mobile observability spans native crashes, JS fatals, ANRs, and product analytics - not one SDK
* Initialize Sentry before any other app imports in \_layout or index.js
* Structured logs are JSON lines with stable keys - grep-friendly in any backend
* Analytics is not crash reporting - separate consent, retention, and vendor contracts
* Transactions span a user-perceived operation - screen load, checkout, not every setState
* OpenTelemetry is vendor-neutral - export to Honeycomb, Datadog, Grafana Tempo, or OTLP collector

## [Observability Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/observability/observability-basics/)

* Mobile observability spans native crashes, JS fatals, ANRs, and product analytics - not one SDK
* Crash-free sessions measure user impact; raw crash counts hide low-traffic screens
* JS errors and native crashes need separate pipelines - Hermes stacks differ from iOS native frames
* Tag every event with release, OTA update id, and route - triage without reproducing on device
* ANRs on Android are slow main-thread work - profile before blaming React
* Pair crash reporters with structured logs - breadcrumbs alone miss offline-first failures

## [Sentry for React Native](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/observability/sentry-for-react-native/)

* Initialize Sentry before any other app imports in \_layout or index.js
* Upload source maps on every EAS build - unsymbolicated Hermes stacks are unreadable
* Set release to native version+build and dist to OTA update id when applicable
* Enable native crash capture - @sentry/react-native includes iOS and Android native layers
* Breadcrumbs from navigation and fetch beat post-mortem guesswork
* Release Health tracks crash-free sessions - align numerators with your SLO doc

## [Structured Logging On Device](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/observability/structured-logging-on-device/)

* Structured logs are JSON lines with stable keys - grep-friendly in any backend
* Buffer on device; ship batches on foreground and before background - not per log line
* Cap buffer size and drop verbose levels first - unbounded logs OOM low-RAM Android
* Attach release, OTA id, sessionId, and route to every batch header
* Never persist access tokens or PII in log payloads - hash user ids
* Pair with crash reporters - logs uploaded on prior foreground explain native crashes

## [Analytics & Privacy](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/observability/analytics-and-privacy/)

* Analytics is not crash reporting - separate consent, retention, and vendor contracts
* Gate all product analytics behind explicit consent resolved before first track call
* iOS ATT applies to tracking that links user data across apps - align SDK config with legal review
* Segment is a router - one identify() fans out to Amplitude, Braze, etc. with transformations
* Reset analytics identity on logout - same discipline as auth token clearing
* Use coarse event schemas - stable names, typed properties, no PII in property keys

## [Performance Monitoring](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/observability/performance-monitoring/)

* Transactions span a user-perceived operation - screen load, checkout, not every setState
* Instrument navigation at the router layer - leaf screens should not each start spans
* Propagate trace headers on API calls to join mobile TT with backend latency
* Sample production traces - 100% capture overwhelms cost and obscures p99
* Name spans with op codes: navigation, http.client, ui.load - dashboards group by op
* Compare traces against TTI budgets from Performance Basics - observability without budgets is noise

## [OpenTelemetry on Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/observability/opentelemetry-on-mobile/)

* OpenTelemetry is vendor-neutral - export to Honeycomb, Datadog, Grafana Tempo, or OTLP collector
* Mobile spans must propagate W3C traceparent to your API - otherwise traces stop at the device
* Batch and compress OTLP exports - mobile radios punish per-span HTTPS
* Resource attributes carry service.name, app.version, and deployment.environment
* Sample aggressively in production - head sampling at 1–10% is typical on client
* Align span names with Performance Monitoring - one taxonomy across Sentry and OTel if both run

## [SLOs for Mobile Apps](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/observability/slos-for-mobile-apps/)

* SLOs are user-facing promises with error budgets - not aspirational dashboard targets
* Crash-free sessions is the default reliability SLO - define session end rules explicitly
* Cold start SLOs must name reference device and percentile - p95 on Pixel 6a class
* OTA success rate measures download+apply - failed silent updates erode trust invisibly
* Burn-rate alerts fire before budget exhaustion - 2% crash rate for 1h matters more than 28-day average
* Correlate SLO regressions with release, dist, and channel - native vs JS attribution

## [Observability Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/observability/best-practices/)

* Correlate release, OTA update id, sessionId, and route on every signal
* Crash reporting, structured logs, performance traces, and analytics serve different questions
* Upload source maps and native symbols on every production build - unsymbolicated stacks waste incidents
* Gate product analytics behind consent; crash stability telemetry may use separate policy
* Define SLOs with error budgets before launch week - not after the first spike
* Mid-tier Android validates performance SLOs - flagship phones hide cold start and jank regressions
