Dokumen: Observability Basics
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/observability/observability-basics/

# Observability Basics

10 examples to get you started with mobile observability - 7 basic and 3 intermediate. Covers **native crashes**, **ANRs**, **JavaScript errors**, and how they fit into the **signal stack** every Expo team ships before store release.

Highlights / Observability Basics

* Mobile observability spans native crashes, JS fatals, ANRs, and product analytics - not one SDK
* Crash-free sessions measure user impact; raw crash counts hide low-traffic screens
* JS errors and native crashes need separate pipelines - Hermes stacks differ from iOS native frames
* Tag every event with release, OTA update id, and route - triage without reproducing on device
* ANRs on Android are slow main-thread work - profile before blaming React
* Pair crash reporters with structured logs - breadcrumbs alone miss offline-first failures

## Prerequisites

Scaffold a blank TypeScript app. Examples use built-in APIs and patterns that work on **Expo SDK 57** release builds - no vendor SDK required until you wire Sentry in a later page.

```bash
npx create-expo-app@latest MyObservabilityApp --template blank-typescript
cd MyObservabilityApp
npx expo start
```

> **Tooling:** These examples target **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4), **React Native 0.86.0**, and **React 19.2.3**.

The mobile **signal stack** has four layers teams instrument in order:

| Layer | What it catches | Typical tool |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Crash / fatal** | Native SIGSEGV, fatal JS, process death | Sentry, Firebase Crashlytics |
| **Error / handled** | Caught API failures, boundary trips, global JS | Sentry + your logger |
| **Performance** | Cold start, navigation TT, API latency | Sentry transactions, OTel |
| **Product analytics** | Funnels, retention, feature usage | Amplitude, Segment |

Use all four. A crash-free dashboard with zero performance budgets still ships slow releases.

---

## Basic Examples

### 1. Define Crash vs Error vs ANR

Mobile platforms classify failures differently - your dashboards should too.

```ts
// src/observability/taxonomy.ts
export type MobileFailureKind =
  | "native_crash"      // process terminated - iOS/Android native
  | "js_fatal"          // ErrorUtils isFatal - bundle may be unhealthy
  | "js_non_fatal"      // caught, reported, app continues
  | "anr"               // Android: main thread blocked ~5s+ (Application Not Responding)
  | "handled_error";    // API 5xx surfaced in UI - still worth logging
 
export type FailureReport = {
  kind: MobileFailureKind;
  message: string;
  screen?: string;
  release: string;       // native build: 1.4.2 (42)
  otaUpdateId?: string;    // expo-updates manifest id
  sessionId: string;
};
```

* **Native crash** ends the session - user must relaunch
* **JS fatal** may or may not kill the process depending on engine and error site
* **ANR** is Android-specific - iOS watchdog kills are closer to native crash taxonomy
* **Handled errors** belong in logs and non-fatal issue trackers - not the crash-free rate numerator

> **Related:** [Global Error Handlers](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/error-resilience/global-error-handlers/) - `ErrorUtils.setGlobalHandler` for JS fatals

---

### 2. Attach Release Context to Every Report

Without build identity, you cannot tie a spike to an OTA or a store build.

```ts
// src/observability/releaseContext.ts
import * as Application from "expo-application";
import * as Updates from "expo-updates";
 
export async function getReleaseContext() {
  const nativeVersion = Application.nativeApplicationVersion ?? "unknown";
  const buildNumber = Application.nativeBuildVersion ?? "unknown";
  const ota = Updates.updateId ?? "embedded";
  const channel = Updates.channel ?? "none";
 
  return {
    release: `${nativeVersion}+${buildNumber}`,
    otaUpdateId: ota,
    channel,
    runtimeVersion: Updates.runtimeVersion ?? "unknown",
  };
}
```

```bash
npx expo install expo-application expo-updates
```

* **`release`** should match what Sentry and your backend expect - `version+build` is a common shape
* **OTA update id** distinguishes a bad JavaScript bundle from a bad native binary - see [OTA Updates Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/ota-updates-basics/)
* **Runtime version** gates which OTAs apply - mismatches look like mysterious "old bug" reports
* Log context once at session start and attach to every error, log batch, and trace

---

### 3. Session ID for Correlation

Tie crashes, logs, and API traces to one user journey.

```ts
// src/observability/session.ts
import * as Crypto from "expo-crypto";
 
let sessionId: string | null = null;
 
export async function getSessionId() {
  if (!sessionId) {
    const bytes = await Crypto.getRandomBytesAsync(16);
    sessionId = Array.from(bytes)
      .map((b) => b.toString(16).padStart(2, "0"))
      .join("");
  }
  return sessionId;
}
```

* Generate a new session id on **cold start** - not on every foreground
* Rotate on **logout** when PII boundaries change - pair with [Mobile Auth Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/mobile-auth-basics/)
* Send `sessionId` as a header (`X-Session-Id`) on API calls for server-side join
* Never use session id as user id - sessions are anonymous until auth

---

### 4. Screen Name as a Dimension

Route-aware crash grouping cuts triage time dramatically.

```tsx
// src/observability/useActiveRoute.ts
import { usePathname, useSegments } from "expo-router";
import { useEffect } from "react";
 
type RouteReporter = (route: string) => void;
 
export function useActiveRoute(report: RouteReporter) {
  const pathname = usePathname();
  const segments = useSegments();
 
  useEffect(() => {
    const route = pathname || segments.join("/") || "unknown";
    report(route);
  }, [pathname, segments, report]);
}
```

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx - wire once at root
import { useCallback, useRef } from "react";
import { useActiveRoute } from "@/observability/useActiveRoute";
 
const currentRoute = { value: "boot" };
 
export default function RootLayout() {
  const report = useCallback((route: string) => {
    currentRoute.value = route;
    // crashSdk.setTag("route", route);
  }, []);
 
  useActiveRoute(report);
  return null; // Stack in real app
}
```

* Prefer **pathname** over component display names - refactors rename components, routes stay stable
* Update route tag on **every navigation** - stale route tags mis-attribute crashes
* For modals and nested stacks, include segments: `checkout/payment`
* Performance transactions should use the same route key - see [Performance Monitoring](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/observability/performance-monitoring/)

---

### 5. Breadcrumb Shape for Mobile

Breadcrumbs are a time-ordered trail - keep them small and structured.

```ts
// src/observability/breadcrumbs.ts
export type Breadcrumb = {
  ts: number;
  category: "navigation" | "network" | "auth" | "user" | "console";
  message: string;
  data?: Record<string, string | number | boolean>;
};
 
const MAX_BREADCRUMBS = 50;
const ring: Breadcrumb[] = [];
 
export function addBreadcrumb(crumb: Omit<Breadcrumb, "ts">) {
  ring.push({ ...crumb, ts: Date.now() });
  if (ring.length > MAX_BREADCRUMBS) ring.shift();
}
 
export function getBreadcrumbs() {
  return [...ring];
}
```

```ts
addBreadcrumb({
  category: "network",
  message: "GET /v1/feed failed",
  data: { status: 503, durationMs: 4200 },
});
```

* Cap ring size - unbounded arrays OOM on chatty screens
* **Never** put tokens, emails, or card numbers in `data` - hashes or booleans only
* Categories map cleanly to Sentry and structured log indexes
* Auth breadcrumbs (`login_success`, `logout`) help reproduce session bugs without storing credentials

---

### 6. Distinguish JS Errors from Native Crashes

Your dashboard needs two ingestion paths.

```ts
// src/observability/report.ts
import type { FailureReport } from "./taxonomy";
 
type Reporter = (report: FailureReport) => void;
 
export function reportJsError(
  report: Reporter,
  error: Error,
  meta: { isFatal: boolean; screen: string; release: string }
) {
  report({
    kind: meta.isFatal ? "js_fatal" : "js_non_fatal",
    message: error.message,
    screen: meta.screen,
    release: meta.release,
    sessionId: "…", // from getSessionId()
  });
}
 
// Native crashes are captured by @sentry/react-native / Crashlytics native SDKs.
// JS layer only sees them as "previous session ended unexpectedly" on next launch.
```

* Install the **React Native SDK** with native modules enabled - JS-only wrappers miss SIGABRT
* Symbolicate **both** Hermes bytecode maps and native dSYMs / ProGuard mappings
* After a native crash, **on-device logs are gone** unless you shipped them on prior foreground - see [Structured Logging On Device](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/observability/structured-logging-on-device/)
* JS fatals may still allow `componentDidCatch` on sibling trees - native crashes do not

---

### 7. Crash-Free Sessions (Concept)

Product and engineering should agree on one north-star reliability metric.

```ts
// src/observability/metrics.ts
export type SessionOutcome = "clean" | "crashed" | "unknown";
 
export function crashFreeRate(sessions: SessionOutcome[]) {
  const known = sessions.filter((s) => s !== "unknown");
  const clean = known.filter((s) => s === "clean").length;
  return known.length === 0 ? 1 : clean / known.length;
}
 
// Example SLO: 99.5% crash-free sessions over 28 days (see slos-for-mobile-apps)
```

* A **session** ends on crash, force-quit, or background timeout - define the rule explicitly
* **Crash-free users** is a stricter metric - one bad device should not dominate
* Exclude **development** and **internal** builds from production SLO numerators
* Pair with **cold start** and **OTA success** SLOs - [SLOs for Mobile Apps](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/observability/slos-for-mobile-apps/)

---

## Intermediate Examples

### 8. Global Handler + Enriched Payload

Chain the previous handler and attach release context before forwarding to your reporter.

```tsx
// src/bootstrap/installObservability.ts
import { getReleaseContext } from "@/observability/releaseContext";
import { getBreadcrumbs } from "@/observability/breadcrumbs";
 
type GlobalHandler = (error: Error, isFatal?: boolean) => void;
 
declare const ErrorUtils: {
  getGlobalHandler(): GlobalHandler;
  setGlobalHandler(handler: GlobalHandler): void;
};
 
export function installGlobalObservability(
  send: (payload: Record<string, unknown>) => void
) {
  const previous = ErrorUtils.getGlobalHandler();
 
  ErrorUtils.setGlobalHandler(async (error, isFatal = false) => {
    const release = await getReleaseContext();
    send({
      kind: isFatal ? "js_fatal" : "js_non_fatal",
      message: error.message,
      stack: error.stack,
      isFatal,
      breadcrumbs: getBreadcrumbs(),
      ...release,
    });
    previous(error, isFatal);
  });
}
```

* Call **once** at bootstrap - before providers and navigation
* Always **chain** `previous` - dev redbox and vendor SDKs depend on it
* Async work in the handler must be fire-and-forget - do not block the runtime
* Mirror the same payload shape in Sentry `beforeSend` for consistent dashboards

> **Related:** [Error Handling Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/error-resilience/error-handling-basics/) - three-layer error model

---

### 9. Detect Main-Thread Risk (ANR Prevention)

ANRs come from synchronous work on the UI thread - often JSON parse, logging floods, or heavy `useMemo` on large arrays.

```tsx
import { useEffect, useRef } from "react";
import { InteractionManager } from "react-native";
 
export function useMainThreadWatchdog(thresholdMs = 2000) {
  const lastTick = useRef(Date.now());
 
  useEffect(() => {
    const id = setInterval(() => {
      const now = Date.now();
      const gap = now - lastTick.current;
      lastTick.current = now;
      if (gap > thresholdMs) {
        console.warn("[perf] event loop gap ms", gap);
        // report non-fatal: possible ANR / JS thread stall
      }
    }, 500);
    return () => clearInterval(id);
  }, [thresholdMs]);
}
 
// Defer heavy work off the critical path
export function deferAfterInteractions(task: () => void) {
  InteractionManager.runAfterInteractions(task);
}
```

* **2000ms** gaps on a 500ms timer suggest JS thread blockage - investigate before users see ANR dialogs
* Large **FlatList** datasets without virtualization are a common ANR source - [Performance Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/performance/performance-basics/)
* Image decode on the JS thread during scroll causes stalls - use appropriately sized assets
* Android Vitals reports ANRs in Play Console - correlate with your release and OTA tags

---

### 10. Minimal Signal Stack Bootstrap

Wire crash reporting, logging, and analytics behind one facade so screens stay clean.

```ts
// src/observability/index.ts
import { getReleaseContext } from "./releaseContext";
import { getSessionId } from "./session";
import { addBreadcrumb, getBreadcrumbs } from "./breadcrumbs";
 
export const observability = {
  async baseContext() {
    const [release, sessionId] = await Promise.all([
      getReleaseContext(),
      getSessionId(),
    ]);
    return { ...release, sessionId };
  },
  breadcrumb: addBreadcrumb,
  getBreadcrumbs,
  captureException(error: Error, extra?: Record<string, unknown>) {
    // forward to Sentry + log buffer
    console.error("[capture]", error.message, extra);
  },
  track(event: string, props?: Record<string, string | number | boolean>) {
    // forward to analytics with consent gate - see analytics-and-privacy
  },
};
```

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx
import { useEffect } from "react";
import { installGlobalObservability } from "@/bootstrap/installObservability";
import { observability } from "@/observability";
 
installGlobalObservability((payload) => {
  observability.captureException(new Error(payload.message as string), payload);
});
 
export default function RootLayout() {
  useEffect(() => {
    observability.baseContext().then((ctx) => {
      observability.track("app_open", { channel: ctx.channel });
    });
  }, []);
  return null;
}
```

* One **facade** prevents every screen from importing three SDKs
* `baseContext()` runs once per session - cache internally
* **Analytics** calls must respect consent - stub `track` until gates resolve
* Expand this facade in [Sentry for React Native](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/observability/sentry-for-react-native/) and [Structured Logging On Device](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/observability/structured-logging-on-device/)

---

## FAQs

What is the difference between observability and analytics?

* **Observability** answers "what broke and why" - crashes, errors, latency, traces.
* **Analytics** answers "what did users do" - funnels, retention, experiments.
* Share release context and session ids; do not duplicate vendors without reason.

Do I need separate tools for iOS and Android crashes?

* Modern RN SDKs (Sentry, Crashlytics) ship **one package** with native modules for both platforms.
* You still need **platform-specific** symbol files - dSYM (iOS) and ProGuard/R8 mapping (Android).

Can Expo Go report production-like crashes?

* No - Expo Go uses a different native shell and bundle id. Validate on **development builds** and **EAS preview** binaries.

How do OTA updates affect crash attribution?

* Tag reports with `expo-updates` `updateId` and `runtimeVersion`.
* A spike after OTA publish without a store release almost always points to JavaScript - roll back the update channel first.

Dokumen: Sentry for React Native

# Sentry for React Native

`@sentry/react-native` on Expo SDK 57 - initialization, **source maps**, **release health**, and **breadcrumbs** wired for EAS builds. This cookbook assumes you already understand the signal stack from [Observability Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/observability/observability-basics/).

Highlights / Sentry for React Native

* Initialize Sentry before any other app imports in \_layout or index.js
* Upload source maps on every EAS build - unsymbolicated Hermes stacks are unreadable
* Set release to native version+build and dist to OTA update id when applicable
* Enable native crash capture - @sentry/react-native includes iOS and Android native layers
* Breadcrumbs from navigation and fetch beat post-mortem guesswork
* Release Health tracks crash-free sessions - align numerators with your SLO doc

## Prerequisites

```bash
npx expo install @sentry/react-native
npx @sentry/wizard@latest -i reactNative
```

The wizard adds Metro plugin config, native hooks, and EAS build steps. For manual setup, pin versions compatible with RN 0.86:

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "@sentry/react-native": "^6.0.0",
    "expo": "~57.0.4",
    "react": "19.2.3",
    "react-native": "0.86.0"
  }
}
```

> **Tooling:** These examples target **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4), **React Native 0.86.0**, and **React 19.2.3**.

---

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

**1. Initialize at the earliest entry point**

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx - must run before other imports side effects
import * as Sentry from "@sentry/react-native";
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
import * as Application from "expo-application";
import * as Updates from "expo-updates";
 
const nativeVersion = Application.nativeApplicationVersion ?? "0.0.0";
const buildNumber = Application.nativeBuildVersion ?? "0";
const release = `${nativeVersion}+${buildNumber}`;
const dist = Updates.updateId ?? buildNumber;
 
Sentry.init({
  dsn: process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN,
  environment: process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_APP_ENV ?? "development",
  release,
  dist,
  enableAutoSessionTracking: true,
  tracesSampleRate: 0.2,
  attachStacktrace: true,
  beforeSend(event) {
    // Strip PII - never send raw emails or tokens
    if (event.user?.email) delete event.user.email;
    return event;
  },
});
 
function RootLayout() {
  return <Stack />;
}
 
export default Sentry.wrap(RootLayout);
```

**2. EAS build - upload source maps**

```json
// eas.json excerpt
{
  "build": {
    "production": {
      "env": {
        "SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN": "@sentry-auth-token",
        "SENTRY_ORG": "your-org",
        "SENTRY_PROJECT": "your-rn-app"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

```bash
# After EAS Build completes, sentry-expo / wizard hooks upload:
# - Hermes source maps (JS)
# - Debug symbols for native frames (iOS dSYM, Android NDK if used)
eas build --platform all --profile production
```

**3. Navigation breadcrumbs (Expo Router)**

```tsx
import { useEffect } from "react";
import { usePathname } from "expo-router";
import * as Sentry from "@sentry/react-native";
 
export function useSentryRouteBreadcrumb() {
  const pathname = usePathname();
 
  useEffect(() => {
    Sentry.addBreadcrumb({
      category: "navigation",
      message: pathname,
      level: "info",
    });
    Sentry.setTag("route", pathname);
  }, [pathname]);
}
```

**4. Network breadcrumb wrapper**

```ts
export async function sentryFetch(input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit) {
  const start = Date.now();
  const url = typeof input === "string" ? input : input.url;
 
  try {
    const res = await fetch(input, init);
    Sentry.addBreadcrumb({
      category: "http",
      message: `${init?.method ?? "GET"} ${url}`,
      data: { status: res.status, durationMs: Date.now() - start },
      level: res.ok ? "info" : "warning",
    });
    return res;
  } catch (err) {
    Sentry.addBreadcrumb({
      category: "http",
      message: `${init?.method ?? "GET"} ${url} failed`,
      data: { durationMs: Date.now() - start },
      level: "error",
    });
    throw err;
  }
}
```

**When to reach for this:**

* You need **native + JS** crash capture in production EAS binaries
* Stack traces must resolve to **TypeScript source**, not Hermes bytecode offsets
* Release Health should gate store submissions alongside [Performance Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/performance/performance-basics/) budgets
* You want breadcrumbs for navigation and API without building a custom ring buffer

---

## Working Example

Full bootstrap with session context, auth-aware user scope, and error boundary integration.

```tsx
// src/observability/sentry.ts
import * as Sentry from "@sentry/react-native";
import * as Application from "expo-application";
import * as Updates from "expo-updates";
 
export function initSentry() {
  const version = Application.nativeApplicationVersion ?? "0.0.0";
  const build = Application.nativeBuildVersion ?? "0";
 
  Sentry.init({
    dsn: process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN,
    environment: process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_APP_ENV,
    release: `${version}+${build}`,
    dist: Updates.updateId ?? build,
    enableAutoSessionTracking: true,
    enableNative: true,
    enableNativeCrashHandling: true,
    tracesSampleRate: __DEV__ ? 1.0 : 0.15,
    integrations: [
      Sentry.reactNativeTracingIntegration(),
    ],
  });
}
 
export function setSentryUser(userId: string | null) {
  if (userId) {
    Sentry.setUser({ id: userId });
  } else {
    Sentry.setUser(null);
  }
}
 
export function captureWithContext(error: unknown, context?: Record<string, unknown>) {
  Sentry.withScope((scope) => {
    if (context) scope.setContext("extra", context);
    Sentry.captureException(error);
  });
}
```

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx
import { useEffect } from "react";
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
import * as Sentry from "@sentry/react-native";
import { initSentry, setSentryUser } from "@/observability/sentry";
import { useSentryRouteBreadcrumb } from "@/observability/useSentryRouteBreadcrumb";
import { useAuth } from "@/features/auth/useAuth";
 
initSentry();
 
function RootLayout() {
  const { userId } = useAuth();
  useSentryRouteBreadcrumb();
 
  useEffect(() => {
    setSentryUser(userId);
  }, [userId]);
 
  return (
    <Sentry.ErrorBoundary fallback={<CrashFallback />}>
      <Stack />
    </Sentry.ErrorBoundary>
  );
}
 
function CrashFallback() {
  return null; // your recovery UI
}
 
export default Sentry.wrap(RootLayout);
```

```ts
// Pair with auth logout - clear user scope
// setSentryUser(null) on logout - see ../auth-session/mobile-auth-basics/
```

---

## Source Maps on EAS

Hermes ships **bytecode** in release builds. Without uploaded maps, Sentry shows `index.android.bundle:1:234567`.

| Artifact | When | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hermes `.map` | Every EAS production build | JS stack → `.tsx` lines |
| iOS dSYM | Native iOS build | Native frame → Swift/ObjC |
| ProGuard mapping | Android release | Obfuscated Java → symbols |

```bash
# Verify release exists in Sentry before shipping OTA
sentry-cli releases list | grep "1.4.2+42"
```

* **`release`** in `Sentry.init` must **exactly match** the CLI upload release string
* **`dist`** differentiates OTA bundles sharing the same native `release` - use `Updates.updateId`
* Re-upload maps after **OTA-only** JS changes if your pipeline treats OTA as a new dist
* Failed map upload is a **release blocker** - treat like missing tests

> **Related:** [OTA Updates Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/ota-updates-basics/) - when JS changes ship without store review

---

## Release Health

Sentry **Release Health** tracks sessions and crash-free rates per `release` + `environment`.

```ts
// Sessions start automatically with enableAutoSessionTracking: true
// End on crash, or background beyond sessionTrackingIntervalMillis (default 30s)
 
Sentry.init({
  // ...
  enableAutoSessionTracking: true,
  sessionTrackingIntervalMillis: 30000,
});
```

* Compare **crash-free sessions** across `production` vs `preview` environments
* A bad OTA appears as a drop on the **same native release** with a new `dist`
* Align thresholds with [SLOs for Mobile Apps](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/observability/slos-for-mobile-apps/)
* Do not count **development** sessions in production SLO numerators - filter `environment`

## Breadcrumbs Best Practices

| Category | Source | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `navigation` | Expo Router pathname | `/checkout/payment` |
| `http` | Wrapped `fetch` | `POST /v1/orders 201` |
| `auth` | Login/logout handlers | `refresh_token_rotated` |
| `ui` | Primary user actions | `tap_place_order` |
| `console` | `Sentry.captureConsoleIntegration` | dev warnings only |

```ts
Sentry.addBreadcrumb({
  category: "auth",
  message: "token_refresh_failed",
  level: "warning",
  data: { reason: "invalid_grant" }, // no raw tokens
});
```

* Cap automated console breadcrumbs in production - noisy logs hide signal
* Redact **Authorization** headers in HTTP breadcrumbs
* Mirror breadcrumb categories in [Structured Logging On Device](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/observability/structured-logging-on-device/) for cross-vendor correlation

  await fetchFeed();

## FAQs

Does @sentry/react-native work in Expo Go?

* Partially - native crash capture requires a **development build** or store binary.
* Validate integrations on `eas build --profile development` before production.

Where should Sentry.init live with Expo Router?

* Top of `app/_layout.tsx` as a side effect, or a dedicated `instrumentation.ts` imported first.
* Must run before routed screens mount and before other global handlers overwrite ErrorUtils.

How do I avoid duplicate error reports?

* Use `Sentry.wrap` on the root component once.
* Do not call both `captureException` and rethrow from boundaries unless intentional.
* Chain `ErrorUtils` handlers - see [Global Error Handlers](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/error-resilience/global-error-handlers/).

What goes in release vs dist?

* **release** = native app version users see in the store (`1.4.2+42`).
* **dist** = OTA update id or build number - distinguishes JS bundles under the same release.

Dokumen: Structured Logging On Device
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/observability/structured-logging-on-device/

# Structured Logging On Device

Batching structured logs on device and **shipping on next foreground** (and on background flush). Mobile networks are unreliable; per-line streaming wastes battery. This cookbook builds a small buffer you own before adopting Datadog or a custom ingest API.

Highlights / Structured Logging On Device

* Structured logs are JSON lines with stable keys - grep-friendly in any backend
* Buffer on device; ship batches on foreground and before background - not per log line
* Cap buffer size and drop verbose levels first - unbounded logs OOM low-RAM Android
* Attach release, OTA id, sessionId, and route to every batch header
* Never persist access tokens or PII in log payloads - hash user ids
* Pair with crash reporters - logs uploaded on prior foreground explain native crashes

## Prerequisites

```bash
npx expo install @react-native-async-storage/async-storage expo-application expo-updates
```

> **Tooling:** These examples target **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4), **React Native 0.86.0**, and **React 19.2.3**.

---

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

**1. Log schema**

```ts
// src/logging/types.ts
export type LogLevel = "debug" | "info" | "warn" | "error";
 
export type StructuredLog = {
  ts: string;              // ISO-8601
  level: LogLevel;
  event: string;           // stable snake_case name: feed_fetch_failed
  message?: string;
  data?: Record<string, string | number | boolean | null>;
};
 
export type LogBatchHeader = {
  sessionId: string;
  release: string;
  otaUpdateId: string;
  route?: string;
  platform: "ios" | "android";
};
```

**2. Ring buffer with persistence**

```ts
// src/logging/buffer.ts
import AsyncStorage from "@react-native-async-storage/async-storage";
import type { StructuredLog } from "./types";
 
const STORAGE_KEY = "log_buffer_v1";
const MAX_LOGS = 200;
 
let memory: StructuredLog[] = [];
 
export async function appendLog(entry: StructuredLog) {
  memory.push(entry);
  if (memory.length > MAX_LOGS) {
    memory = memory.slice(-MAX_LOGS);
  }
  await AsyncStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY, JSON.stringify(memory));
}
 
export async function drainLogs(): Promise<StructuredLog[]> {
  const raw = await AsyncStorage.getItem(STORAGE_KEY);
  const logs: StructuredLog[] = raw ? JSON.parse(raw) : memory;
  memory = [];
  await AsyncStorage.removeItem(STORAGE_KEY);
  return logs;
}
```

**3. Logger facade**

```ts
// src/logging/logger.ts
import type { LogLevel, StructuredLog } from "./types";
import { appendLog } from "./buffer";
 
function write(level: LogLevel, event: string, data?: StructuredLog["data"], message?: string) {
  const entry: StructuredLog = {
    ts: new Date().toISOString(),
    level,
    event,
    message,
    data,
  };
  if (__DEV__) console[level === "debug" ? "log" : level](event, data ?? {});
  void appendLog(entry);
}
 
export const logger = {
  debug: (event: string, data?: StructuredLog["data"]) => write("debug", event, data),
  info: (event: string, data?: StructuredLog["data"]) => write("info", event, data),
  warn: (event: string, data?: StructuredLog["data"]) => write("warn", event, data),
  error: (event: string, data?: StructuredLog["data"], message?: string) =>
    write("error", event, data, message),
};
```

**4. Ship on foreground**

```tsx
// src/logging/useLogShipping.ts
import { useEffect, useRef } from "react";
import { AppState, type AppStateStatus } from "react-native";
import * as Application from "expo-application";
import * as Updates from "expo-updates";
import { drainLogs } from "./buffer";
import { getSessionId } from "@/observability/session";
 
async function shipBatch(route?: string) {
  const logs = await drainLogs();
  if (logs.length === 0) return;
 
  const header = {
    sessionId: await getSessionId(),
    release: `${Application.nativeApplicationVersion}+${Application.nativeBuildVersion}`,
    otaUpdateId: Updates.updateId ?? "embedded",
    route,
    platform: require("react-native").Platform.OS,
  };
 
  await fetch(`${process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL}/v1/logs/batch`, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
    body: JSON.stringify({ header, logs }),
  });
}
 
export function useLogShipping(route?: string) {
  const appState = useRef(AppState.currentState);
 
  useEffect(() => {
    const sub = AppState.addEventListener("change", (next: AppStateStatus) => {
      if (appState.current.match(/inactive|background/) && next === "active") {
        void shipBatch(route);
      }
      if (next === "background") {
        void shipBatch(route); // flush before suspend - may not complete on iOS
      }
      appState.current = next;
    });
    return () => sub.remove();
  }, [route]);
}
```

**When to reach for this:**

* You need **offline-tolerant** telemetry without blocking UI on every `fetch`
* Native crashes wipe in-memory state - persisted buffers from the **previous session** explain last actions
* You want vendor-neutral JSON before committing to Datadog / CloudWatch / custom ELK
* API failures need structured `event` names for dashboards - not unstructured `console.log`

---

## Working Example

Wire shipping at the app shell with auth-safe fields and sampling.

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
import { usePathname } from "expo-router";
import { useLogShipping } from "@/logging/useLogShipping";
 
export default function RootLayout() {
  const pathname = usePathname();
  useLogShipping(pathname);
  return <Stack />;
}
```

```ts
// src/api/client.ts - structured API errors
import { logger } from "@/logging/logger";
 
export async function apiGet<T>(path: string): Promise<T> {
  const start = Date.now();
  try {
    const res = await fetch(`${process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL}${path}`);
    if (!res.ok) {
      logger.warn("api_request_failed", {
        path,
        status: res.status,
        durationMs: Date.now() - start,
      });
      throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);
    }
    logger.info("api_request_ok", { path, durationMs: Date.now() - start });
    return res.json();
  } catch (err) {
    logger.error("api_request_error", { path, durationMs: Date.now() - start });
    throw err;
  }
}
```

```ts
// Auth events - no tokens
import { logger } from "@/logging/logger";
 
export function logAuthEvent(event: "login_success" | "logout" | "refresh_failed", userId?: string) {
  logger.info(event, { userId: userId ? hashId(userId) : null });
}
 
function hashId(id: string) {
  return id.slice(0, 8) + "…"; // replace with real hash in production
}
```

---

## Batching Rules

| Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- |
| **Max 200 lines** per device | Prevents AsyncStorage bloat on chatty screens |
| **Drop `debug` first** when over capacity | Keeps `error` and `warn` under pressure |
| **Ship on foreground** | Network usually available; user expects brief sync |
| **Ship on background** | Best-effort before suspend - iOS may kill task |
| **Idempotent ingest** | Server dedupes by `sessionId` + `ts` + `event` |

```ts
// src/logging/buffer.ts - drop debug when trimming
function trim(logs: StructuredLog[]) {
  if (logs.length <= MAX_LOGS) return logs;
  const errors = logs.filter((l) => l.level !== "debug");
  return errors.slice(-MAX_LOGS);
}
```

---

## Correlation with Crashes and Traces

```ts
// Include the same ids Sentry and OTel use
logger.info("checkout_started", {
  sessionId,
  release,
  otaUpdateId: Updates.updateId,
  traceId, // from opentelemetry-on-mobile when enabled
});
```

* Logs **without** shared ids are orphan narratives - always copy `sessionId` from [Observability Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/observability/observability-basics/)
* Upload batches **before** heavy crash reproduction attempts - device logs rotate quickly
* For [Performance Monitoring](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/observability/performance-monitoring/), log slow spans as `warn` when duration exceeds budget

---

## Privacy and Retention

* **No** emails, names, free-text user input, or card data in `data`
* Hash or truncate **user ids** - align with [Analytics & Privacy](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/observability/analytics-and-privacy/) retention policy
* Server-side retention: 30–90 days for mobile client logs unless compliance requires longer
* Honor **logout** by rotating `sessionId` and draining the buffer - see [Mobile Auth Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/auth-session/mobile-auth-basics/)

---

## FAQs

Why not log directly to the cloud from the device?

* Per-line HTTPS on every tap drains battery and fails offline.
* Batching amortizes TLS handshakes and survives brief offline windows.

Does AsyncStorage survive native crashes?

* Usually yes for writes that completed - last logs may explain the prior session.
* In-memory-only buffers are lost on every native crash.

Should I use console.log in production?

* `console` in release builds is often stripped or ignored.
* Structured logger writes to buffer **and** optional dev console.

How does this relate to Sentry breadcrumbs?

* Breadcrumbs ride with crash events - small ring, crash-time only.
* Structured logs are a **durable, queryable** stream - ship both, duplicate sparingly.

Dokumen: OTA Updates Best Practices
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/best-practices/

# OTA Updates Best Practices

A condensed summary of the 25 most important best practices drawn from every page in this section.

Highlights / OTA Updates Best Practices

* OTA ships JS and assets only - native modules and permissions need store builds
* runtimeVersion must match between eas build and eas update on every release
* Channels map to environments - preview soak before production on revenue paths
* Record last known-good update ID before every production publish
* Use eas update --environment on SDK 55+ - local .env is ignored
* Feature flags and OTA rollback are complementary incident tools

1. **OTA is JS and assets only:** Native modules, config plugins, permissions, entitlements, SDK upgrades, and app icons require `eas build` and store submission - OTA cannot add native symbols.
2. **Set explicit runtimeVersion policy:** Use `appVersion`, `nativeVersion`, or `fingerprint` consistently in `app.config` - document the choice in README and never mix policies across flavors without an ADR.
3. **Match runtime on build and update:** The `runtimeVersion` resolved by `eas build` must equal what `eas update` targets - verify with `npx expo config --type public` before every publish.
4. **Bump runtime when native changes:** New native dependency, plugin edit, or permission string means new store build and new runtime line - do not OTA JS that imports missing native modules.
5. **Configure updates.url and projectId:** Run `eas update:configure` after `eas init` - missing `updates.url` disables `expo-updates` silently in release builds.
6. **Wire channel headers to build profiles:** `updates.requestHeaders["expo-channel-name"]` must match `eas.json` `channel` for each profile - drive from `EAS_BUILD_PROFILE` in dynamic `app.config`.
7. **Use eas update --environment always:** On SDK 55+, update runners ignore local `.env` - pass `--environment production` (or preview) so OTA bundles match build env vars.
8. **Name channels for environments:** `development`, `preview`, `staging`, `production` - not engineer names; map channels to audiences in `docs/release-channels.md`.
9. **Linear promotion flow:** `development` → `preview` (QA) → `production` - no skipping preview for payment, auth, or checkout changes regardless of diff size.
10. **Preview builds for OTA sign-off:** QA tests on EAS `preview` profile binaries, not Expo Go - Expo Go cannot receive your production update configuration.
11. **CI-only production publish:** Prefer tagged GitHub Actions workflows for `eas update --channel production` - laptop publish is break-glass with second approver and postmortem.
12. **Record last known-good update ID:** Every production release ticket stores the previous bundle ID for `eas update:rollback` or `eas update:republish` - rollbacks without this are guesswork.
13. **Define rollback triggers before launch:** Crash-free drop, payment success drop, and auth error spike thresholds with owners - see Release & OTA Rules Tier 4.
14. **Practice rollback quarterly on preview:** Run `eas update:rollback` on the preview channel in a drill - target under 15 minutes from decision to verified channel head.
15. **Gate native-dependent JS with flags:** Remote kill switches plus `Application.nativeApplicationVersion` checks prevent crashes until store adoption crosses your threshold.
16. **Log updateId in production analytics:** `Updates.updateId`, `runtimeVersion`, and `channel` at session start - support and incident response depend on knowing the running bundle.
17. **checkAutomatically ON\_LOAD with fallback 0:** Check on cold start without blocking launch on slow networks - tune reload UX separately via expo-updates client API.
18. **Rebuild after first updates config:** Adding `expo-updates` wiring requires a new native binary - `eas update` alone does not enable updates on old installs.
19. **Treat bundle size regressions as releases:** Large OTA bundles hurt TTI - compare Metro output before production publish and link to performance budget rules.
20. **Backward-compatible API contracts:** Mobile users skip updates - JS shipped OTA must tolerate older API responses until store adoption is high; run contract tests in CI.
21. **Safe local storage migrations:** MMKV and SQLite schema bumps need tested upgrade paths from the previous production bundle - bad migrations brick installs and need rollback.
22. **Staged rollouts on production:** Use `--rollout-percentage` or `eas channel:rollout` after preview soak - monitor crash and payment metrics at each step before 100%.
23. **Tag Sentry with updateId:** Segment crash reports by bundle during rollouts - without cohort tags, percentage rollouts are blind.
24. **Track runtime distribution weekly:** Percentage of users per `runtimeVersion` - stale binaries stop receiving OTAs; enforce minimum native version when security requires.
25. **Two-track release checklist:** Store submission checklist for native changes and OTA checklist for preview soak, flags, rollback ID, and dashboards - attach both to every release ticket.

## FAQs

What is the default greenfield OTA stack?

`appVersion` runtime policy + `eas.json` channels per profile + `eas update:configure` + preview soak + CI production publish + `updateId` logging + quarterly rollback drill + Release & OTA Rules checklist.

Can I fix a native crash with OTA?

No - native crashes need a new store build. OTA fixes JavaScript logic and assets only. Roll back JS if the crash is from importing a missing native module, then ship binary.

Where do I start for first EAS Update setup?

[OTA Updates Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/ota-updates-basics/) for boundaries, then [expo-updates Configuration](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/expo-updates-configuration/) for `app.config`, then [Release Channels & Branches](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/release-channels-and-branches/) for promotion flow.

appVersion or fingerprint for runtime?

`appVersion` for most consumer apps. `fingerprint` when native project drifts without marketing version bumps - see [Runtime Version Policy](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/runtime-version-policy/).

How do rollouts relate to rollback?

[Rollouts](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/staged-rollouts/) limit blast radius before full exposure. [Rollback Runbook](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/rollback-runbook/) recovers after a bad publish - use both with shared monitoring dashboards.

Dokumen: expo-updates Configuration
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/expo-updates-configuration/

# expo-updates Configuration

Runtime version, update URL, and check-on-launch policies - the `app.config` cookbook for wiring **EAS Update** into Expo SDK 57 apps so binaries and OTA bundles stay compatible.

Highlights / expo-updates Configuration

* runtimeVersion policy in app.config must match what eas build and eas update resolve
* updates.url points at your EAS project - verify with npx expo config --type public
* checkAutomatically and fallbackToCacheTimeout trade freshness for offline startup
* Channel headers in requestHeaders must align with eas.json build profile channel
* Run eas update:configure once after eas init - rebuild native after first-time setup
* SDK 55+ requires eas update --environment - local .env is ignored on update runners

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
npx expo install expo-updates
npx eas init
npx eas update:configure
```

```ts
// app.config.ts
import type { ExpoConfig } from "expo/config";
 
const config: ExpoConfig = {
  name: "ShopApp",
  slug: "shop-app",
  version: "2.4.0",
  runtimeVersion: {
    policy: "appVersion",
  },
  extra: {
    eas: {
      projectId: "xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx",
    },
  },
  updates: {
    url: "https://u.expo.dev/xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx",
    checkAutomatically: "ON_LOAD",
    fallbackToCacheTimeout: 0,
    requestHeaders: {
      "expo-channel-name": "production",
    },
  },
};
 
export default config;
```

```bash
# Verify resolved public config
npx expo config --type public | jq '{runtimeVersion, updates}'
 
# Publish with EAS environment (SDK 55+)
eas update --channel production --environment production --message "Config verified"
```

**When to reach for this:**

* First-time EAS Update setup after `eas init`.
* Auditing why devices skip updates (`runtimeVersion` or channel mismatch).
* Tuning startup behavior - silent background check vs blocking fetch.
* White-label flavors that need per-variant `requestHeaders` and `projectId`.

**When to avoid:**

* Changing native permissions or plugins - config edit still needs `eas build`.
* Pointing production apps at `development` channel headers - use build profiles instead.
* Expecting `expo start` to apply OTA - updates are disabled in dev.

## Working Example

A production-ready `app.config.ts` with **profile-driven channel headers**, explicit runtime policy, and startup check policy.

**Step 1 - `eas.json` channels per build profile**

```json
{
  "cli": { "version": ">= 16.0.0" },
  "build": {
    "development": {
      "developmentClient": true,
      "distribution": "internal",
      "channel": "development"
    },
    "preview": {
      "distribution": "internal",
      "channel": "preview"
    },
    "production": {
      "channel": "production"
    }
  }
}
```

**Step 2 - Dynamic `app.config.ts`**

```ts
// app.config.ts
import type { ExpoConfig } from "expo/config";
 
const EAS_PROJECT_ID = "xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx";
 
const channel =
  process.env.EAS_BUILD_PROFILE === "preview"
    ? "preview"
    : process.env.EAS_BUILD_PROFILE === "development"
      ? "development"
      : "production";
 
const config: ExpoConfig = {
  name: "ShopApp",
  slug: "shop-app",
  version: "2.4.0",
  runtimeVersion: { policy: "appVersion" },
  extra: { eas: { projectId: EAS_PROJECT_ID } },
  updates: {
    url: `https://u.expo.dev/${EAS_PROJECT_ID}`,
    checkAutomatically: "ON_LOAD",
    fallbackToCacheTimeout: 0,
    requestHeaders: { "expo-channel-name": channel },
  },
  ios: { bundleIdentifier: "com.example.shopapp" },
  android: { package: "com.example.shopapp" },
};
 
export default config;
```

**Step 3 - First native build after configure**

```bash
eas build --profile preview --platform all
eas update --channel preview --environment preview --message "Smoke test channel wiring"
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* `runtimeVersion.policy: "appVersion"` ties OTA targeting to `expo.version`
* `updates.url` uses the EAS project UUID from `extra.eas.projectId`
* `requestHeaders["expo-channel-name"]` must match the profile's `channel` in `eas.json`
* `checkAutomatically: "ON_LOAD"` checks on every cold start; `fallbackToCacheTimeout: 0` never blocks launch on network

## Deep Dive

### runtimeVersion Options

| Policy | Resolves to | Best for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `appVersion` | `expo.version` string | Most consumer apps; simple mental model |
| `nativeVersion` | Platform build numbers | Teams that bump build number per native change |
| `fingerprint` | Hash of native project state | Monorepos with frequent native drift |
| `"1.0.0"` (static string) | Literal value | Brownfield with fixed native runtime |

```ts
// Explicit static runtime (advanced / brownfield)
runtimeVersion: "shop-native-2026-q1",
```

* Pick **one policy per app** - document it in README and release tickets
* Changing policy mid-flight strands devices - coordinate with a store release
* See [Runtime Version Policy](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/runtime-version-policy/) for selection guidance

### checkAutomatically Values

| Value | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `ON_LOAD` | Check every cold start (default recommendation) |
| `ON_ERROR_RECOVERY` | Check only after crash recovery |
| `WIFI_ONLY` | Check on launch when on Wi-Fi |
| `NEVER` | No automatic check - you call `checkForUpdateAsync` manually |

```ts
updates: {
  checkAutomatically: "ON_LOAD",
  fallbackToCacheTimeout: 0, // 0 = never block launch waiting for network
},
```

* `fallbackToCacheTimeout: 3000` blocks launch up to 3s for a fresh bundle - use sparingly
* Pair automatic checks with user-consent reload for disruptive updates - see [expo-updates (Client API)](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-sdk/expo-updates-client-api/)

### Channel Header Wiring

```text
eas.json build.profile.channel  →  embedded in binary at eas build
app.config updates.requestHeaders  →  sent on every update check
eas update --channel <name>     →  publishes bundle to that channel
```

* All three must agree - channel mismatch is the #1 "fix never arrived" incident
* `eas update:configure` scaffolds `updates.url` and `projectId` - it does not replace profile discipline
* White-label: separate `projectId`, channel, and bundle ID per app variant

### Environment Variables on Update Runners

```bash
# SDK 55+ - local .env is NOT used on EAS update runners
eas update --channel production --environment production
```

* Create matching EAS environments for `preview` and `production`
* Align `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` vars between `eas build` and `eas update` for the same channel
* Mismatched API URLs in OTA vs binary cause auth outages - treat env parity as a release gate

## Gotchas

* **Missing `updates.url`** - `Updates.isEnabled` is false. **Fix:** `eas update:configure` + rebuild.
* **runtimeVersion drift** - Build used `2.4.0`, update published under `2.5.0` after version bump without rebuild. **Fix:** Rebuild binaries or publish to matching runtime.
* **Hard-coded `production` header in dev profile** - Preview QA receives production OTAs. **Fix:** Drive header from `EAS_BUILD_PROFILE`.
* **First configure without rebuild** - Old binary lacks `expo-updates` native wiring. **Fix:** New `eas build` after adding updates config.
* **Blocking `fallbackToCacheTimeout` on slow networks** - Users stare at splash. **Fix:** Keep `0` unless you have a strong offline-update UX.
* **Publishing without `--environment`** - Stale or wrong API hosts baked into OTA bundle. **Fix:** Always pass `--environment` on SDK 55+.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `checkAutomatically: "ON_LOAD"` | Default freshness | You need fully manual control |
| `checkAutomatically: "NEVER"` + client API | Custom banner UX | Team forgets to implement checks |
| Static `runtimeVersion` string | Pinned brownfield host | Marketing version should drive targeting |
| `fingerprint` policy | Native changes without version bumps | Team lacks CI fingerprint validation |

## FAQs

Do I need to rebuild after changing checkAutomatically?

Yes - `checkAutomatically` and `fallbackToCacheTimeout` are embedded in the native manifest at build time. Changing them requires a new `eas build`.

Where does updates.url come from?

`eas update:configure` writes `https://u.expo.dev/<projectId>` using your `extra.eas.projectId`. Verify with `npx expo config --type public`.

Can I use app.config.js instead of .ts?

Yes. The same `updates` and `runtimeVersion` keys apply. Dynamic channel selection via `process.env.EAS_BUILD_PROFILE` is the common pattern.

How do I test configuration without production risk?

Build `preview` profile → publish `eas update --channel preview` → install internal build → confirm `Updates.channel` and `Updates.runtimeVersion` in logs.

Does expo-updates work in development builds?

Development clients can point at `development` channel, but `__DEV__` and dev tooling differ from production. Sign-off OTA behavior on `preview`/`production` profiles only.

## Related

* [Runtime Version Policy](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/runtime-version-policy/) - policy comparison
* [Release Channels & Branches](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/release-channels-and-branches/) - channel promotion
* [expo-updates (Client API)](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-sdk/expo-updates-client-api/) - programmatic check and reload

Highlights / OTA Updates Highlights Summary

* OTA ships JavaScript, TypeScript, and assets - not new native code
* runtimeVersion policy in app.config must match what eas build and eas update resolve

## [OTA Updates Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/ota-updates-basics/)

* OTA ships JavaScript, TypeScript, and assets - not new native code
* runtimeVersion must match between eas build and eas update or devices silently skip updates
* New native modules, config plugins, and permission strings require a store build
* Preview channel soak catches JS that assumes native APIs not yet in production binaries
* Feature flags kill bad JS paths faster than waiting for a second OTA
* Expo Go cannot receive production EAS Update payloads - test on preview builds

## [expo-updates Configuration](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/expo-updates-configuration/)

* runtimeVersion policy in app.config must match what eas build and eas update resolve
* updates.url points at your EAS project - verify with npx expo config --type public
* checkAutomatically and fallbackToCacheTimeout trade freshness for offline startup
* Channel headers in requestHeaders must align with eas.json build profile channel
* Run eas update:configure once after eas init - rebuild native after first-time setup
* SDK 55+ requires eas update --environment - local .env is ignored on update runners

## [Release Channels & Branches](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/release-channels-and-branches/)

* Channels map to environments - development, preview, staging, production
* eas.json build.channel embeds the channel in each binary at build time
* Branches hold update history; channels point at a branch head
* Promotion is republish or channel redirect - never skip preview on revenue paths
* eas update --environment is required on SDK 55+ for env parity with builds
* Production publish should be CI-only with audit trail in release tickets

## [Rollback Runbook](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/rollback-runbook/)

* Target < 15 minutes from rollback decision to channel serving known-good bundle
* eas update:rollback republishes a prior update or embedded bundle interactively
* Record last known-good update ID in every production release ticket
* Feature flags off first when logic errors - OTA rollback second for bundle defects
* runtimeVersion mismatch cannot be fixed by OTA - escalate to store build
* Monitor crash-free rate for 60 minutes after rollback completes

## [Runtime Version Policy](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/runtime-version-policy/)

* runtimeVersion is the compatibility key between eas build binaries and eas update bundles
* appVersion policy is simplest - ties runtime to expo.version marketing string
* nativeVersion uses platform build numbers - bumps on every native rebuild
* fingerprint hashes native project state - best when native drifts without version bumps
* Never mix policies across flavors in the same release train
* Track runtime distribution weekly - stale runtimes stop receiving OTAs silently

## [Staged Rollouts](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/staged-rollouts/)

* Per-update rollouts start with eas update --rollout-percentage=N
* Branch-based rollouts split traffic between two branches on one channel
* Only one rollout per branch or channel at a time - end before publishing conflicting updates
* Monitor crash-free rate and payment success at each percentage step
* Pair EAS rollouts with feature flags for intra-bundle kill switches
* Revert with eas update:revert-update-rollout or eas channel:rollout End

## [OTA Updates Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/best-practices/)

* OTA ships JS and assets only - native modules and permissions need store builds
* runtimeVersion must match between eas build and eas update on every release
* Channels map to environments - preview soak before production on revenue paths
* Record last known-good update ID before every production publish
* Use eas update --environment on SDK 55+ - local .env is ignored
* Feature flags and OTA rollback are complementary incident tools

Dokumen: OTA Updates Basics
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/ota-updates-basics/

# OTA Updates Basics

10 examples to get you started with **Over-The-Air (OTA) updates** on Expo SDK 57 - what EAS Update can change in minutes versus what still requires an App Store or Play Store submission.

Highlights / OTA Updates Basics

* OTA ships JavaScript, TypeScript, and assets - not new native code
* runtimeVersion must match between eas build and eas update or devices silently skip updates
* New native modules, config plugins, and permission strings require a store build
* Preview channel soak catches JS that assumes native APIs not yet in production binaries
* Feature flags kill bad JS paths faster than waiting for a second OTA
* Expo Go cannot receive production EAS Update payloads - test on preview builds

## Prerequisites

OTA updates require `expo-updates` in a **release or preview binary** - not Expo Go.

```bash
npx create-expo-app@latest MyOtaApp --template blank-typescript
cd MyOtaApp
npx expo install expo-updates
npx eas init
npx eas update:configure
```

> **Tooling:** These examples target **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4), **React Native 0.86.0**, and **React 19.2.3**.

---

## Basic Examples

### 1. Two Delivery Paths: OTA vs Store

Every mobile release decision starts with one question: **does this change touch native code?**

```text
JavaScript / assets change only     →  eas update (minutes)
Native shell / permissions / SDK    →  eas build + store submit (days)
```

* **OTA** replaces the JS bundle and downloadable assets on devices that already have a compatible binary
* **Store build** replaces the native shell - Hermes runtime, native modules, entitlements, icons
* Users on old store versions stay on their **runtime line** until they upgrade the binary
* See [Release & OTA Rules](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/release-and-ota-rules/) for the full promotion checklist

> **Related:** [expo-updates (Client API)](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-sdk/expo-updates-client-api/) - checking and applying updates from app code

---

### 2. Fix a React Component Bug (OTA-Safe)

Pure JavaScript logic errors are the classic OTA use case - no native boundary crossed.

```tsx
// src/screens/CheckoutScreen.tsx - typo fix ships OTA
export function CheckoutScreen() {
  const total = useCartTotal();
 
  return (
    <View>
      <Text>Total: {formatCurrency(total)}</Text>
      {/* Fixed: was dividing by 100 twice */}
      <PrimaryButton label="Pay now" onPress={submitPayment} />
    </View>
  );
}
```

```bash
# After preview soak
eas update --channel production --environment production --message "Fix checkout total display"
```

* Component trees, hooks, styles, and navigation structure are **OTA-safe**
* Ship to `preview` first; soak before `production` on revenue paths
* Pair with crash monitoring - OTA is fast, not risk-free

> **Related:** [Release Channels & Branches](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/release-channels-and-branches/) - staging → production promotion

---

### 3. Swap Image Assets (OTA-Safe)

Bundled images, fonts referenced from JS, and Lottie JSON ship with the update manifest.

```tsx
// src/components/HeroBanner.tsx
import heroImage from "@/assets/hero-summer.png";
 
export function HeroBanner() {
  return <Image source={heroImage} style={{ width: "100%", height: 200 }} />;
}
```

* Asset changes in the Metro bundle are **OTA-safe**
* **App icon and splash screen** are native - they require a new binary
* Large asset additions affect bundle size and TTI - watch performance budgets

---

### 4. Add a Native Module (Store Required)

Installing a package with native code changes `ios/` and `android/` output - OTA cannot add it.

```bash
# This sequence requires eas build + store submit, NOT eas update alone
npx expo install react-native-vision-camera
```

```ts
// app.config.ts - new plugin = native rebuild
export default {
  expo: {
    plugins: [
      [
        "react-native-vision-camera",
        { cameraPermissionText: "We need camera access for barcode scan." },
      ],
    ],
  },
};
```

* `npx expo prebuild` diff is the signal - if native project changes, plan a store build
* **Never** ship JS that imports the new module over OTA before binaries exist in stores
* Gate new native-dependent screens behind feature flags until store adoption crosses your threshold

> **Related:** [EAS Build Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/eas-build/eas-build-basics/) - cloud binaries that receive updates

---

### 5. Change Info.plist Permission Strings (Store Required)

Permission copy lives in native manifests - users see stale text if you OTA without rebuilding.

```json
{
  "expo": {
    "ios": {
      "infoPlist": {
        "NSCameraUsageDescription": "Scan barcodes to add items to your cart."
      }
    },
    "android": {
      "permissions": ["android.permission.CAMERA"]
    }
  }
}
```

* Any `infoPlist`, `permissions`, or `entitlements` change needs **eas build**
* App Review reads permission strings on the **binary**, not the JS bundle
* Document permission changes in store release notes, not only OTA changelogs

---

### 6. Bump Expo SDK (Store Required)

SDK upgrades change the native runtime, Hermes version, and default native dependencies.

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "expo": "~57.0.4",
    "react": "19.2.3",
    "react-native": "0.86.0"
  }
}
```

* After SDK upgrade: `eas build` for all profiles, then resume `eas update` on the **new runtime line**
* Old binaries on the previous runtime **stop receiving** updates on the new line
* Plan user messaging when minimum native version enforcement is required

> **Related:** [Runtime Version Policy](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/runtime-version-policy/) - `appVersion`, `nativeVersion`, and fingerprint strategies

---

### 7. runtimeVersion Is the Compatibility Gate

`runtimeVersion` tells EAS Update which JS bundles a binary may download. Mismatch = silent skip.

```ts
// app.config.ts
export default {
  expo: {
    version: "2.4.0",
    runtimeVersion: {
      policy: "appVersion",
    },
    updates: {
      url: "https://u.expo.dev/xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx",
    },
  },
};
```

```bash
# Build embeds runtime 2.4.0
eas build --profile production --platform all
 
# Update must target the same runtime
eas update --channel production --environment production
```

* `eas build` artifacts and `eas update` bundles must share the same resolved `runtimeVersion`
* Verify with `npx expo config --type public | jq '.runtimeVersion'`
* Wrong policy strands users on stale JS without an obvious error - test on preview devices

> **Related:** [expo-updates Configuration](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/expo-updates-configuration/) - full `app.config` cookbook

---

### 8. OTA vs Store Decision Table

Copy this table into your release runbook and require a checkbox per change.

| Change | OTA? | Store? | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JS bug fix | ✅ | - | Preview soak first |
| New React screen (no new native) | ✅ | - | Watch bundle size |
| New `expo install` native module | - | ✅ | Bump runtime; gate JS |
| Config plugin added/changed | - | ✅ | Prebuild diff required |
| App icon / adaptive icon | - | ✅ | Native asset pipeline |
| Push notification icon (Android) | - | ✅ | Native resource |
| Remote copy / theme tokens in JS | ✅ | - | No native touch |
| SQLite schema migration in JS | ✅ | ⚠️ | Test upgrade path; bad migration bricks |
| API breaking change | ✅ | ⚠️ | Old JS must tolerate old API |
| Hermes bytecode / bundle size | ✅ | - | Treat as release event |

* When a row says **⚠️**, OTA is technically possible but needs extra QA and rollback planning
* Revenue, auth, and payment rows default to **preview soak** regardless of "small" diffs

---

### 9. Gate JS Until Binaries Catch Up

OTA lets you ship JS fast; feature flags let you **control who executes it**.

```tsx
// src/features/barcode/useBarcodeScanner.ts
import * as Application from "expo-application";
 
const MIN_NATIVE_FOR_SCANNER = "2.4.0";
 
export function useBarcodeScannerEnabled(remoteFlag: boolean) {
  const nativeVersion = Application.nativeApplicationVersion ?? "0.0.0";
  const nativeReady = compareSemver(nativeVersion, MIN_NATIVE_FOR_SCANNER) >= 0;
  return remoteFlag && nativeReady;
}
```

* Remote flags disable bad paths **immediately** - faster than republishing an OTA
* `Application.nativeApplicationVersion` reflects the **store binary**, not the OTA bundle ID
* Server authorization still enforces access - flags are UX, not security

> **Related:** [Feature Flags for Safe Rollout](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/error-resilience/feature-flags-for-safe-rollout/) - kill switches alongside OTA

---

### 10. Know Which Bundle Is Running

Support and incident response need the update ID - not just the marketing version.

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx (dev/preview diagnostics only)
import * as Updates from "expo-updates";
import { useEffect } from "react";
 
export default function RootLayout() {
  useEffect(() => {
    if (__DEV__) return;
    console.info("[updates]", {
      updateId: Updates.updateId,
      runtimeVersion: Updates.runtimeVersion,
      channel: Updates.channel,
      isEmbeddedLaunch: Updates.isEmbeddedLaunch,
    });
  }, []);
 
  return <Stack />;
}
```

* `Updates.updateId` identifies the OTA bundle; `Updates.isEmbeddedLaunch` true means no OTA applied yet
* Log to analytics in preview/production - redact in public user-facing screens
* Keep **last known-good update ID** in release tickets for [Rollback Runbook](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/rollback-runbook/)

---

## FAQs

Can OTA change native code?

No. OTA replaces JavaScript bundles and downloadable assets. Native modules, permissions, entitlements, SDK version, and app icons require `eas build` and store submission.

Does Expo Go receive EAS Updates?

No. Expo Go uses a generic native shell without your `expo-updates` channel configuration. Test OTA on **preview** or **production** profile builds from EAS.

How fast can a JS fix reach users?

After publish, devices check on launch (per your `checkAutomatically` policy). Users may need one restart. Critical fixes can prompt reload via [expo-updates (Client API)](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-sdk/expo-updates-client-api/).

What if I OTA a change that needs native code?

The app crashes at import or first native call - often immediately on launch. Roll back the channel and ship a store build. Prevention: preview soak + runtime guards + [Release & OTA Rules](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/release-and-ota-rules/).

Do users on old store versions get new OTAs?

They receive OTAs for **their** `runtimeVersion` line only. Track runtime distribution weekly; enforce minimum native version when security requires it.

Dokumen: Release Channels & Branches
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/release-channels-and-branches/

# Release Channels & Branches

Staging → production promotion with EAS Update - a cookbook for **channels**, **branches**, and the linear promotion flow that keeps preview QA aligned with production behavior.

Highlights / Release Channels & Branches

* Channels map to environments - development, preview, staging, production
* eas.json build.channel embeds the channel in each binary at build time
* Branches hold update history; channels point at a branch head
* Promotion is republish or channel redirect - never skip preview on revenue paths
* eas update --environment is required on SDK 55+ for env parity with builds
* Production publish should be CI-only with audit trail in release tickets

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```json
// eas.json - channel per build profile
{
  "build": {
    "preview": { "distribution": "internal", "channel": "preview" },
    "production": { "channel": "production" }
  }
}
```

```bash
# Publish to preview branch (soak)
eas update --branch preview --channel preview --environment preview \
  --message "feat: checkout validation fix"
 
# After QA sign-off - publish same commit to production channel
eas update --branch production --channel production --environment production \
  --message "promote: checkout validation fix"
```

```bash
# Inspect what each channel serves
eas channel:view production
eas update:list --branch production --limit 5
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Setting up first `development` → `preview` → `production` flow.
* Promoting a soaked preview bundle to production users.
* Mapping Git branches to EAS Update branches for trunk-based teams.
* Auditing which bundle ID production channel currently serves.

**When to avoid:**

* Per-engineer channels (`jane-dev`) - use preview builds + branch updates instead.
* Direct production publish from a feature branch without preview soak on revenue paths.
* Sharing one production channel across two bundle IDs - white-label needs separate channels.

## Working Example

End-to-end **staging → preview → production** promotion with channel/branch tables and CI gate.

**Step 1 - Document the channel map**

```markdown
<!-- docs/release-channels.md -->
| Channel      | Binary profile | Audience        | Who may publish      |
|--------------|----------------|-----------------|----------------------|
| development  | development    | Engineers       | Any dev (local)      |
| preview      | preview        | QA + stakeholders | Tech lead on-call  |
| staging      | preview*       | Pre-prod soak   | Release manager      |
| production   | production     | Store users     | CI tag only          |
 
* staging uses preview profile binary with `expo-channel-name: staging` header override if needed
```

**Step 2 - Wire branches to channels**

```bash
# One-time: ensure channels point at intended branches
eas channel:create preview
eas channel:create production
eas channel:edit preview --branch preview
eas channel:edit production --branch production
```

**Step 3 - Feature work on preview**

```bash
git checkout -b fix/checkout-validation
# ... JS changes only (OTA-safe) ...
 
eas update --branch preview --channel preview --environment preview \
  --message "fix: card validation regex"
```

**Step 4 - QA on preview binary**

```bash
# QA installs eas build --profile preview artifact
# Maestro smoke + manual payment path on physical device
eas update:list --branch preview --limit 3
```

**Step 5 - Promote to production (CI preferred)**

```yaml
# .github/workflows/eas-update-production.yml (excerpt)
name: Promote OTA to production
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      message:
        required: true
jobs:
  update:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: expo/expo-github-action@v8
        with:
          eas-version: latest
          token: ${{ secrets.EXPO_TOKEN }}
      - run: eas update --branch production --channel production \
               --environment production \
               --message "${{ github.event.inputs.message }}"
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* **Branches** store update history; **channels** are the pointer apps query at runtime
* Preview soak happens on the **same channel** QA binaries embed via `requestHeaders`
* Production promotion is a deliberate second publish - not an accidental channel edit
* CI-only production publish leaves an audit trail (`eas update:list`, GitHub Actions logs)

## Deep Dive

### Channels vs Branches

```text
eas update --branch feature-x     →  writes bundle to branch "feature-x"
eas channel:edit preview --branch feature-x   →  preview channel now serves feature-x
App checks channel "preview"      →  receives head of branch feature-x
```

| Concept | Role |
| --- | --- |
| **Channel** | Named endpoint devices query (`expo-channel-name` header) |
| **Branch** | Git-like line of updates; holds bundle history |
| **Build profile** | Embeds default channel in binary via `eas.json` |

* `eas update --channel production` publishes to the branch currently linked to `production`
* Prefer explicit `--branch` when promoting so history stays traceable
* `eas channel:view <name>` shows branch mapping and current update ID

### Linear Promotion Flow

```text
development  →  preview (QA)  →  staging (optional soak)  →  production
     ↑              ↑                      ↑                        ↑
  engineer      internal build         24–48h soak              CI tag only
```

* **development:** rapid iteration; may break; not for stakeholders
* **preview:** release-like internal binary; Maestro smoke required
* **staging (optional):** longer soak for auth/payment; same binary class as preview
* **production:** store users; two-person rule or CI-only

### Mapping Git Branches to EAS Branches

```bash
# Trunk-based: publish from main to preview branch
git checkout main
eas update --branch preview --channel preview --environment preview
 
# GitFlow: publish from release/x.y to staging branch
git checkout release/2.4
eas update --branch staging --channel staging --environment staging
```

* EAS branches are **not** automatically tied to Git branches - you enforce mapping in CI
* Document which Git branch may publish to which EAS channel in CONTRIBUTING.md
* Reject direct `production` publish from unmerged feature branches

### Republish Promotion Pattern

When preview and production should run the **same bundle artifact**:

```bash
# Option A - cherry-pick commit and publish to production branch
git checkout main
git cherry-pick <preview-commit-sha>
eas update --branch production --channel production --environment production \
  --message "promote: <ticket-id>"
 
# Option B - channel redirect (advanced; use with care)
eas channel:edit production --branch preview
# Follow immediately with branch split if preview continues diverging
```

* Option A preserves clear Git history per channel
* Option B is faster but blurs branch semantics - document in runbook
* Always record **preview soak window** and **bundle ID** in the release ticket

## Gotchas

* **Channel header ≠ eas update channel** - Binary built with `preview` header never sees `production` updates. **Fix:** Rebuild or match publish channel to embedded header.
* **Skipping preview for "tiny" payment fix** - Incidents cost more than soak time. **Fix:** Minimum 24h preview on revenue paths per [Release & OTA Rules](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/release-and-ota-rules/).
* **Local `.env` on production publish** - Wrong API host in OTA bundle. **Fix:** `eas update --environment production` always.
* **Two apps, one channel** - Consumer app receives business app JS. **Fix:** Separate `projectId`, channel, and bundle ID per variant.
* **Friday production OTA without weekend on-call** - Rollback at 6 p.m. with no coverage. **Fix:** Policy in release rules.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Branch per Git feature | Parallel QA of features | Too many stale branches |
| Single `main` branch for all channels | Small team, linear flow | Need parallel soaks |
| `eas channel:rollout` | Gradual production exposure | Need full soak on preview first |
| Store-only releases | Native every sprint | Weekly JS-only fixes |

## FAQs

How many channels do we need?

Minimum: `development`, `preview`, `production`. Add `staging` when revenue paths need 48h soak. Avoid per-person channels.

Can preview and production share a branch?

Technically yes, but it erases promotion audit trails. Prefer separate branches and promote via explicit publish or documented channel edit.

How do I see what production is serving?

```bash
eas channel:view production
eas update:view <update-id>
```

Does eas update --channel differ from --branch?

`--channel` publishes to the branch linked to that channel. `--branch` targets a branch directly. Use both for clarity during promotion.

Should production be CI-only?

Strongly recommended. Break-glass laptop publish needs second approver, `eas update:list` screenshot, and postmortem requirement.

## Related

* [OTA Updates Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/ota-updates-basics/) - OTA vs store boundaries
* [expo-updates Configuration](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/expo-updates-configuration/) - `requestHeaders` wiring
* [Staged Rollouts](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/staged-rollouts/) - percentage rollouts on channels
* [Rollback Runbook](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/rollback-runbook/) - channel republish in minutes
* [EAS Build Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/eas-build/eas-build-basics/) - profiles that embed channels
