Dokumen: Performance Best Practices
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/performance/best-practices/

# Performance Best Practices

A condensed summary of the 25 most important best practices drawn from every page in this section.

Highlights / Performance Best Practices

* Measure on mid-tier Android - iPhone Pro hides jank and memory pressure
* Define TTI, FPS, bundle, and memory budgets with named owners before feature freeze
* Virtualize feeds - ScrollView for short static content only
* Profile navigation transitions in React DevTools before sprinkling memo
* Hermes sampling and Flashlight scores validate release builds, not Expo Go
* Performance regressions are rollback triggers - link to Performance Budget Rules

1. **Measure on mid-tier Android first:** Pixel 6a class exposes jank, memory pressure, and slow storage that iPhone Pro hides - if it passes reference Android, iOS is usually fine; the reverse is false.
2. **Define TTI before optimizing:** Cold start → primary tab interactive (not splash hide alone) - document the gate in `docs/performance-budgets.md` with a reference device.
3. **Publish budgets with named owners:** Bundle MB, TTI seconds, FPS floors, and memory ceilings - anonymous budgets are ignored in crunch week; see [Performance Budget Rules](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/performance-budget-rules/).
4. **Profile release-like builds:** Expo Go and dev client timings are not production - use EAS `preview` or release variants for TTI, bundle, and Flashlight scores.
5. **Separate JS FPS from UI FPS:** JS at 0 means taps queue even when UI FPS looks fine - scroll jank on feeds often involves both threads.
6. **Instrument TTI with marks:** `performance.now()` at root layout and primary screen interactive - ship analytics events in production, not only `console.info`.
7. **Keep root `_layout` imports minimal:** Heavy SDKs, charts, and editors belong in lazy routes - every root import is on the cold-start critical path.
8. **Hold splash until first meaningful frame:** Avoid splash hide → full-screen spinner → content; load one body font for TTI, defer the rest.
9. **Defer post-TTI work with InteractionManager:** Analytics, migrations, remote config, and secondary prefetch run after animations - cancel tasks on unmount.
10. **Analyze bundle size in CI:** `react-native-bundle-visualizer` on `--dev false` bundles - fail PRs over budget without ADR exception.
11. **Lazy-load heavy Expo Router screens:** `React.lazy` + `Suspense` for reports, maps, and editors - confirm treemap blocks leave the main bundle.
12. **Use narrow package imports:** Per-icon and per-function paths - full `lodash` and barrel re-exports dominate treemaps.
13. **Record React DevTools Profiler on navigation:** Tab switch, stack push/pop, modal open - fix unstable context and `screenOptions` before memoizing leaves.
14. **Stabilize list parents before row memo:** `useCallback` `renderItem`, module-scope `keyExtractor`, and `extraData` for selection - see [Lists Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/lists-scrolling/best-practices/).
15. **Default to FlatList for growing feeds:** ScrollView mounts every child - switch at ~20 rows or any pagination; evaluate FlashList when profiling proves mount cost.
16. **Run Hermes sampling on hot scenarios:** Fast fling, tab switch, cold start - export `.cpuprofile` to speedscope when JS CPU spikes without obvious React commits.
17. **Flashlight score the primary scroll scenario:** BAM aggregated score on reference Android - compare iterations across releases, not one demo on a flagship.
18. **Build a two-device matrix:** Mid-tier gate + budget floor device - flagship scores are informational only.
19. **Cap list memory and paginate with eviction:** Unbounded `data` arrays are the #1 session RAM leak - ring buffer or max items with persisted cursor.
20. **Clean up listeners in every `useEffect`:** AppState, NetInfo, navigation `addListener`, intervals - missing cleanup doubles work and retains closures.
21. **Clear caches on logout:** TanStack Query `clear()`, MMKV user scope, global image maps - stale cache is a memory and security defect.
22. **Soak-test memory for 10 minutes:** Realistic scroll, stack navigation, background/foreground - leaks appear late, not in 30-second smoke tests.
23. **Tune `windowSize` only after hygiene:** Lower reduces memory; too low causes blank rows - profile with Flashlight before changing defaults.
24. **Link regressions to rollback policy:** TTI > 15%, score drop > 10 points, or bundle overrun triggers release review - document in Performance Budget Rules.
25. **Fix measurement before micro-optimizations:** Repro script → DevTools commits → Hermes hotspots → bundle treemap - not random `useMemo` on presentational chips.

## FAQs

What is the default greenfield performance stack?

Written budgets + reference Android device + release `preview` builds + React DevTools Profiler for navigation + Hermes sampling for JS hotspots + Flashlight for scroll scores + Metro visualizer in CI.

Where do I start on a slow feed?

[Lists Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/lists-scrolling/best-practices/) first - keys, memo, `renderItem`. Then [React DevTools Profiler](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/performance/react-devtools-profiler/). Then [Hermes Sampling Profiler](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/performance/hermes-sampling-profiler/) if JS CPU remains high.

Expo Go good enough for perf review?

No - native shell, module graph, and dev overhead differ. Ship perf sign-off on **EAS preview/production** artifacts only.

How does this section relate to Expo Rules?

[Performance Budget Rules](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/performance-budget-rules/) owns **thresholds, CI gates, and owners**. This section owns **measurement tools and fix patterns**.

FlatList or FlashList for SDK 57?

FlatList for short and medium feeds with correct hygiene. FlashList when profiling shows recycling/mount cost dominates - benchmark with [Flashlight](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/performance/flashlight-benchmarking/) before migrating.

Dokumen: Bundle Size Analysis
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/performance/bundle-size-analysis/

# Bundle Size Analysis

Metro bundle visualizer and lazy route splitting - find what ships in the Hermes main bundle and defer heavy screens until after cold start.

Highlights / Bundle Size Analysis

* npx react-native-bundle-visualizer treemap shows which packages dominate Hermes bundle
* Measure production bundles - dev:false strips differently than Expo Go
* Expo Router lazy routes split heavy screens from the main TTI path
* Replace default imports with per-icon or per-function paths when treemap shows bloat
* Gate bundle size in CI - pair with Performance Budget Rules thresholds
* Lazy chunks still count toward TTI if loaded before primary interactive

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

**1. Generate production bundle + source map**

```bash
npx react-native bundle \
  --platform android \
  --dev false \
  --entry-file node_modules/expo-router/entry.js \
  --bundle-output ./.perf/index.android.bundle \
  --sourcemap-output ./.perf/index.android.bundle.map \
  --assets-dest ./.perf/assets
```

**2. Open treemap**

```bash
npx react-native-bundle-visualizer \
  --bundle ./.perf/index.android.bundle \
  --sourcemap ./.perf/index.android.bundle.map
```

**3. Triage top offenders**

| Treemap block | Common fix |
| --- | --- |
| `moment` / `date-fns/locale/*` | `dayjs` or narrow imports |
| `lodash` full | `lodash/es/map` or native helpers |
| `@expo/vector-icons` entire set | Per-family import or subset font |
| `charting` / `maps` / `editor` SDKs | Lazy route + dynamic `import()` |
| Duplicate `react` / nested copies | Align monorepo `metro.config.js` |

**4. Lazy-load heavy Expo Router screens**

```tsx
// app/(tabs)/analytics.tsx - lazy tab screen
import { Suspense, lazy } from "react";
import { ActivityIndicator, View } from "react-native";
 
const AnalyticsScreen = lazy(() => import("../../src/screens/AnalyticsScreen"));
 
export default function AnalyticsRoute() {
  return (
    <Suspense
      fallback={
        <View style={{ flex: 1, justifyContent: "center" }}>
          <ActivityIndicator />
        </View>
      }
    >
      <AnalyticsScreen />
    </Suspense>
  );
}
```

**5. CI size gate (sketch)**

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/check-bundle-size.sh
BUNDLE="./.perf/index.android.bundle"
MAX_BYTES=4500000  # ~4.3 MB raw - adjust to your gzip budget
 
SIZE=$(wc -c < "$BUNDLE")
if [ "$SIZE" -gt "$MAX_BYTES" ]; then
  echo "Bundle $SIZE exceeds $MAX_BYTES"
  exit 1
fi
```

**When to reach for this:**

* TTI regressed after adding a dependency.
* OTA update download size spiked.
* PR adds `import` from a heavy SDK on the root layout path.
* You need evidence for an ADR exception to [Performance Budget Rules](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/performance-budget-rules/).

## Working Example

Audit a bloated root import, split a heavy screen, and verify the treemap block moves out of the main path.

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx - keep root lean
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
import { QueryClientProvider } from "@tanstack/react-query";
import { queryClient } from "../src/lib/queryClient";
 
export default function RootLayout() {
  return (
    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
      <Stack screenOptions={{ headerShown: false }} />
    </QueryClientProvider>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// app/settings/reports.tsx - heavy screen NOT on TTI path
import { Suspense, lazy } from "react";
import { ActivityIndicator, StyleSheet, View } from "react-native";
 
const ReportsScreen = lazy(() =>
  import("../../src/screens/ReportsScreen").then((m) => ({ default: m.ReportsScreen })),
);
 
export default function ReportsRoute() {
  return (
    <Suspense fallback={<View style={styles.fallback}><ActivityIndicator /></View>}>
      <ReportsScreen />
    </Suspense>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  fallback: { flex: 1, alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "center" },
});
```

```tsx
// src/screens/ReportsScreen.tsx - heavy deps isolated to lazy chunk
import { StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
// Example heavy dep - only loads when user opens Reports
import { VictoryPie } from "victory-native";
 
export function ReportsScreen() {
  const data = [
    { x: "A", y: 35 },
    { x: "B", y: 25 },
    { x: "C", y: 40 },
  ];
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.screen}>
      <Text style={styles.title}>Reports</Text>
      <VictoryPie data={data} width={280} height={280} />
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  screen: { flex: 1, padding: 16, alignItems: "center" },
  title: { fontSize: 20, fontWeight: "700", marginBottom: 16 },
});
```

**Verification checklist**

1. Run visualizer **before** lazy split - note `victory-native` (or your SDK) area in main bundle.
2. Move screen behind `lazy()` - re-bundle; heavy block shrinks in main treemap.
3. Confirm **home tab TTI path** does not `import` the heavy module transitively through barrels.
4. Record main bundle bytes in release ticket - link to budget owner table.

## Import Hygiene

### Prefer narrow entry points

```tsx
// BAD - pulls entire library
import _ from "lodash";
import * as Icons from "@expo/vector-icons";
 
// BETTER
import debounce from "lodash/debounce";
import Ionicons from "@expo/vector-icons/Ionicons";
```

### Audit barrels

```tsx
// packages/ui/src/index.ts - re-exports everything
export * from "./charts"; // ← drags charts into any `from "@acme/ui"` import
 
// BETTER - explicit subpaths in package.json exports
// import { Button } from "@acme/ui/button";
```

### Metro monorepo resolution

Shared packages in monorepos duplicate dependencies easily - align `watchFolders` and `resolver` in `metro.config.js`. See [Shared Packages & Metro Resolution](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/shared-packages-and-metro-resolution/).

## Expo Router Lazy Loading Notes

| Pattern | TTI impact |
| --- | --- |
| `lazy()` screen module | Chunk loads on first navigation - good for settings/reports |
| Tab `lazy: true` (default) | Defers first mount until tab focus - good for cold start |
| `Link prefetch` | Loads chunk early - use only for likely next screen |
| Root `_layout` imports | **Always** on critical path - keep minimal |

```tsx
// Prefetch heavy detail route when user hovers card - optional trade-off
import { Link } from "expo-router";
 
<Link href="/reports" prefetch>
  Open reports
</Link>
```

## Scope: What Counts Toward Budget

Per [Performance Budget Rules](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/performance-budget-rules/):

* **Main Hermes bundle** at first open
* **Lazy chunks** loaded before primary interactive (accidental eager prefetch)
* **OTA artifact size** - separate gate, same analysis tooling

Assets (images, fonts) are separate but affect download - `expo-asset` bundled media appears in export output.

## Gotchas

* **Analyzing dev bundles** - `dev: true` includes dev tooling; always use `--dev false`.
* **Expo Go** - not your bundle graph; export from your app's entry.
* **Lazy without Suspense** - React 19 still needs a boundary for `lazy()` routes.
* **Transitive imports through hooks** - a hook imported in root layout pulls its dependency tree into main.

## FAQs

react-native-bundle-visualizer vs source-map-explorer?

Both map bytes to modules. `react-native-bundle-visualizer` is tuned for RN Metro output - start there. Use `source-map-explorer` if you already have web tooling in CI.

Does Hermes gzip match raw bundle bytes?

CI often gates **raw** or **gzip** - pick one and document it. Gzip ≈ 30–40% of raw for typical RN bundles; align with your 4 MB budget definition.

Can dynamic import() split any dependency?

Metro supports `import()` for async chunks. Native modules still **autolink** at build time - removing JS import does not remove native code unless you uninstall the package.

Do devDependencies affect bundle size?

No - only imports reachable from production entry count. They still affect install and CI time - see [Dead Code & Dependency Analysis](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/dead-code-and-dependency-analysis/).

How do fonts affect size?

Bundled `.ttf` files land in assets. Subset icon fonts and load display fonts after splash when possible - [Startup Time Optimization](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/performance/startup-time-optimization/).

Bundle shrank but TTI unchanged - why?

TTI includes native startup, bytecode load, and first-screen work - not JS bytes alone. Profile holistically with [Performance Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/performance/performance-basics/).

Dokumen: Performance Profiling Highlights Summary
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/performance/highlights-summary/

# Performance Profiling Highlights Summary

Every highlight bullet from the 8 pages in this section, gathered on one page and grouped by the page it came from.

Highlights / Performance Profiling Highlights Summary

* TTI is cold start until the primary screen is interactive - not splash dismissal alone
* Record a navigation transition - not idle home - to catch provider and tab re-renders
* Sampling profiler runs on device - no Chrome DevTools JS sampling in release
* Flashlight is BAM's Lighthouse-style audit - aggregated perf score for Android apps
* npx react-native-bundle-visualizer treemap shows which packages dominate Hermes bundle
* Leaks are retained references - listeners, timers, and closures holding screens

## [Performance Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/performance/performance-basics/)

* TTI is cold start until the primary screen is interactive - not splash dismissal alone
* 60 fps is the target; sustained 55 fps on lists is the audit floor on mid-tier Android
* JS FPS and UI FPS are separate - JS at 0 means taps queue until the thread clears
* Memory budgets are session ceilings - measure after 10 minutes on a reference device
* Measure on mid-tier Android - iPhone Pro hides jank and memory pressure
* Publish written budgets with owners before feature freeze - see Performance Budget Rules

## [React DevTools Profiler](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/performance/react-devtools-profiler/)

* Record a navigation transition - not idle home - to catch provider and tab re-renders
* Ranked chart shows which components committed; flame chart shows why parents dragged children
* Why did this render? highlights changed props, state, and context in React 19
* Fix unstable context values and inline props before sprinkling memo on leaf rows
* Pair Profiler with list hygiene - navigation often re-renders every visible FlatList row
* Profile release-like builds on device - Fast Refresh hides real commit costs

## [Hermes Sampling Profiler](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/performance/hermes-sampling-profiler/)

* Sampling profiler runs on device - no Chrome DevTools JS sampling in release
* Profile release or preview builds - dev transforms and Fast Refresh skew hotspots
* Export .cpuprofile and open in speedscope or RN DevTools Performance tab
* Look for long sync loops in renderItem, JSON.parse on fetch, and style flattening
* Enable Hermes profiling in native build flags before EAS production if needed
* Pair with React DevTools - sampling finds CPU; Profiler finds avoidable React commits

## [Flashlight Benchmarking](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/performance/flashlight-benchmarking/)

* Flashlight is BAM's Lighthouse-style audit - aggregated perf score for Android apps
* No in-app setup - CLI measures installed APK/AAB on real devices via adb
* flashlight test automates iterations; flashlight measure gives live CPU/FPS graphs
* Compare scores across Pixel 6a, Samsung A-series, and flagship - not one phone
* JS thread CPU at 100% correlates with JS FPS at 0 - watch the third graph
* Store reports per release SHA - BAM scores are regression gates, not one-off demos

## [Bundle Size Analysis](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/performance/bundle-size-analysis/)

* npx react-native-bundle-visualizer treemap shows which packages dominate Hermes bundle
* Measure production bundles - dev:false strips differently than Expo Go
* Expo Router lazy routes split heavy screens from the main TTI path
* Replace default imports with per-icon or per-function paths when treemap shows bloat
* Gate bundle size in CI - pair with Performance Budget Rules thresholds
* Lazy chunks still count toward TTI if loaded before primary interactive

## [Memory Leaks & List Churn](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/performance/memory-leaks-and-list-churn/)

* Leaks are retained references - listeners, timers, and closures holding screens
* FlatList churn: unbounded data arrays, unstable keys, and huge windowSize
* Always remove AppState, NetInfo, and navigation listeners in useEffect cleanup
* Global caches without eviction blow session memory - cap LRU or scope per user
* Images in lists need size limits and cache policy - not full-res URIs for thumbnails
* Profile soak tests - 10 minutes on reference Android, not 30-second smoke tests

## [Startup Time Optimization](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/performance/startup-time-optimization/)

* TTI = bytecode load + critical JS + first interactive frame - optimize each segment
* Keep app/\_layout.tsx imports minimal - heavy SDKs belong in lazy routes
* Hide splash only after fonts and auth gate resolve - avoid flash then spinner
* Hermes ships precompiled bytecode - smaller main bundle loads faster
* Defer analytics, migrations, and prefetch with InteractionManager after first paint
* Measure cold start on release builds - dev client startup is not comparable

## [Performance Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/performance/best-practices/)

* Measure on mid-tier Android - iPhone Pro hides jank and memory pressure
* Define TTI, FPS, bundle, and memory budgets with named owners before feature freeze
* Virtualize feeds - ScrollView for short static content only
* Profile navigation transitions in React DevTools before sprinkling memo
* Hermes sampling and Flashlight scores validate release builds, not Expo Go
* Performance regressions are rollback triggers - link to Performance Budget Rules

Reviewed by Chris St. John·Last updated Jul 18, 2026

Dokumen: Performance Basics

# Performance Basics

TTI, FPS, and memory budgets defined per app tier - the vocabulary every React Native team needs before profiling tools, CI gates, or release sign-off.

Highlights / Performance Basics

* TTI is cold start until the primary screen is interactive - not splash dismissal alone
* 60 fps is the target; sustained 55 fps on lists is the audit floor on mid-tier Android
* JS FPS and UI FPS are separate - JS at 0 means taps queue until the thread clears
* Memory budgets are session ceilings - measure after 10 minutes on a reference device
* Measure on mid-tier Android - iPhone Pro hides jank and memory pressure
* Publish written budgets with owners before feature freeze - see Performance Budget Rules

## Prerequisites

Every example below uses built-in React Native APIs and patterns that work on **Expo SDK 57** release builds. Scaffold a standard TypeScript app to try the instrumentation snippets.

```bash
npx create-expo-app@latest MyPerfApp --template blank-typescript
cd MyPerfApp
npx expo start
```

> **Tooling:** These examples target **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4), **React Native 0.86.0**, and **React 19.2.3**.

---

## Basic Examples

### 1. Define TTI for Your App

**Time to Interactive (TTI)** is the moment users can complete the primary action on your main screen - not when the splash hides, not when the first pixel paints.

```tsx
// src/perf/tti.ts - team-defined contract
export type TtiMilestone =
  | "app_launch" // process start / JS entry
  | "root_layout_mounted"
  | "primary_tab_layout"
  | "primary_data_ready"
  | "primary_interactive";
 
/**
 * Consumer feed app: cold start → home feed scrollable + pull-to-refresh works.
 * B2B form app: cold start → first input focused and keyboard-ready.
 * Document YOUR primary tab and gate in docs/performance-budgets.md.
 */
export const TTI_CONTRACT = {
  start: "app_launch" as const,
  end: "primary_interactive" as const,
  referenceDevice: "Pixel 6a class Android",
  budgetMs: 2500,
};
```

* TTI must be **defined per app** - "fast" without a definition is not measurable
* Exclude **dev client** and **Fast Refresh** timings from production budgets
* Pair TTI with a **reference device** - simulators and flagship phones lie
* See [Performance Budget Rules](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/performance-budget-rules/) for owner tables and CI gates

> **Related:** [Startup Time Optimization](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/performance/startup-time-optimization/) - deferring work that blocks TTI

---

### 2. Mark TTI with performance.now()

Instrument launch in root layout and mark interactive when the primary screen passes its data gate.

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx
import { useEffect, useRef } from "react";
import { Slot } from "expo-router";
 
const t0 = globalThis.performance?.now?.() ?? Date.now();
 
export default function RootLayout() {
  const reported = useRef(false);
 
  useEffect(() => {
    if (reported.current) return;
    reported.current = true;
    const rootMounted = globalThis.performance?.now?.() ?? Date.now();
    console.info("[perf] root_layout_mounted_ms", Math.round(rootMounted - t0));
  }, []);
 
  return <Slot />;
}
```

```tsx
// app/(tabs)/index.tsx - primary tab marks interactive
import { useEffect, useRef } from "react";
import { Pressable, StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
export default function HomeScreen() {
  const interactive = useRef(false);
 
  useEffect(() => {
    if (interactive.current) return;
    interactive.current = true;
    // In production: analytics.track("tti_primary_interactive", { ms: ... })
    console.info("[perf] primary_interactive");
  }, []);
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.screen}>
      <Text style={styles.title}>Home</Text>
      <Pressable style={styles.cta}>
        <Text style={styles.ctaText}>Primary action</Text>
      </Pressable>
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  screen: { flex: 1, padding: 16, justifyContent: "center" },
  title: { fontSize: 24, fontWeight: "700", marginBottom: 16 },
  cta: { backgroundColor: "#2563eb", padding: 14, borderRadius: 10, alignItems: "center" },
  ctaText: { color: "#fff", fontWeight: "600" },
});
```

* Start the clock at **JS entry** or first root `useEffect` - be consistent across releases
* End when **primary CTA is enabled** and list data (if any) is rendered - not skeleton-only
* Log to analytics in production; `console.info` is for local verification only

---

### 3. Understand JS FPS vs UI FPS

React Native runs two animation/render pipelines. Confusing them sends you optimizing the wrong thread.

| Metric | Thread | What it measures |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **JS FPS** | JavaScript (Hermes) | React render, business logic, fetch parsing |
| **UI FPS** | Native (main) | Layout, compositing, gestures, native animations |

```tsx
// Dev only - shake device → "Show Perf Monitor" in dev menu
// Watch both counters while scrolling a heavy FlatList
import { FlatList, StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
const ROWS = Array.from({ length: 500 }, (_, i) => ({ id: String(i), title: `Row ${i}` }));
 
export default function FpsDemo() {
  return (
    <FlatList
      data={ROWS}
      keyExtractor={(item) => item.id}
      renderItem={({ item }) => (
        <View style={styles.row}>
          <Text>{item.title}</Text>
        </View>
      )}
    />
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  row: { padding: 16, borderBottomWidth: StyleSheet.hairlineWidth, borderColor: "#e2e8f0" },
});
```

* **JS FPS at 0** - taps and navigation queue; the app feels frozen even if UI FPS looks fine
* **UI FPS drops** - layout thrash, heavy shadows, or native animation cost
* Scroll jank on feeds is often **both** - fix list hygiene first, then native visuals

> **Related:** [Lists & Scrolling basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/lists-scrolling/lists-basics/) - virtualization before FPS tuning

---

### 4. Set a Frame-Rate Budget

Target **60 fps** (16.7 ms per frame). For release audits on mid-tier Android, **≥ 55 fps sustained** on the primary list is a practical floor.

```tsx
// scripts/perf/frame-budget.ts - documentation constant for the team
export const FRAME_BUDGET = {
  targetFps: 60,
  frameBudgetMs: 1000 / 60, // ~16.7
  auditFloorFps: 55,
  primaryScenarios: [
    "home_feed_fast_fling",
    "tab_switch_animation",
    "modal_open_close",
    "pull_to_refresh",
  ],
} as const;
```

* Measure **sustained** scroll, not a two-second demo - momentum flings expose blank rows and JS spikes
* Tab transitions and modal open/close belong in the audit - navigation re-renders are a common regression
* FPS audits stay **manual or RUM** - CI rarely measures frames reliably

---

### 5. Define Memory Budgets by App Tier

Memory is a **session ceiling**, not a launch snapshot. Measure after realistic usage - 10 minutes browsing feeds, opening settings, returning from background.

| App tier | Example | Starter RAM ceiling (reference Android) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Light** | Settings, simple forms | ≤ 200 MB |
| **Standard** | Social feed, e-commerce | ≤ 350 MB |
| **Heavy** | Maps, media, offline packs | ≤ 500 MB with ADR |

```tsx
// src/perf/memory-budget.ts
export const MEMORY_BUDGET = {
  tier: "standard" as const,
  ceilingMb: 350,
  soakMinutes: 10,
  scenarios: ["scroll_home", "open_profile", "background_2min", "return_and_scroll"],
};
```

* **Leaks show up late** - a 120 MB launch can climb to 400 MB after list churn and uncleared listeners
* iOS and Android report memory differently - pick one **reference Android** for regression tracking
* Heavy tiers need an **ADR exception** linked from [Performance Budget Rules](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/performance-budget-rules/)

> **Related:** [Memory Leaks & List Churn](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/performance/memory-leaks-and-list-churn/) - patterns that blow session ceilings

---

### 6. Bundle Size as a Performance Metric

Larger Hermes bundles increase **parse/bytecode load time** and **heap pressure**. Treat main-bundle MB as part of TTI, not a separate concern.

```bash
# Export production bundle for size check (adjust entry for your app)
npx react-native bundle \
  --platform android \
  --dev false \
  --entry-file node_modules/expo-router/entry.js \
  --bundle-output /tmp/index.android.bundle \
  --assets-dest /tmp/assets
 
ls -lh /tmp/index.android.bundle
```

* Starter consumer target: **≤ 4 MB gzipped** main bundle at TTI - adjust per category
* Count **lazy chunks loaded before interactive** toward first-open budget
* See [Bundle Size Analysis](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/performance/bundle-size-analysis/) for Metro visualizer workflow

---

### 7. The Two-Thread Mental Model

Every tap crosses threads. Knowing the path prevents "we memoized everything but it's still slow."

```
User tap
  → Native gesture (UI thread)
  → Bridge / JSI event to JS thread
  → React render + your handlers (Hermes)
  → Reconciliation commit to native (Fabric)
  → Layout + paint (UI thread)
```

```tsx
import { Pressable, StyleSheet, Text } from "react-native";
 
export function SlowButton({ onPress }: { onPress: () => void }) {
  return (
    <Pressable
      style={styles.btn}
      onPress={() => {
        // Runs on JS thread - blocks other JS work until finished
        let sum = 0;
        for (let i = 0; i < 2_000_000; i++) sum += i;
        onPress();
      }}
    >
      <Text style={styles.label}>Tap me</Text>
    </Pressable>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  btn: { padding: 14, backgroundColor: "#2563eb", borderRadius: 8 },
  label: { color: "#fff", fontWeight: "600" },
});
```

* Long synchronous JS on press **drops JS FPS to 0** - defer with `InteractionManager` or native modules
* Reanimated worklets move per-frame work off the JS thread - see Animations section
* Fabric reduces bridge overhead but **does not** remove JS render cost

---

## Intermediate Examples

### 8. Defer Non-Critical Work After TTI

`InteractionManager` queues tasks until animations and transitions finish - the first lever for startup without rewriting features.

```tsx
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { InteractionManager, StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
export default function HomeWithDeferredInit() {
  const [ready, setReady] = useState(false);
 
  useEffect(() => {
    const task = InteractionManager.runAfterInteractions(() => {
      // Analytics init, feature flags, non-critical prefetch
      setReady(true);
    });
    return () => task.cancel();
  }, []);
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.screen}>
      <Text style={styles.title}>Home</Text>
      <Text style={styles.meta}>{ready ? "Telemetry on" : "Core UI only"}</Text>
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  screen: { flex: 1, padding: 16 },
  title: { fontSize: 22, fontWeight: "700" },
  meta: { marginTop: 8, color: "#64748b" },
});
```

* Run **fonts, analytics, remote config, and heavy migrations** after first interactive frame when possible
* Cancel the task on unmount - navigation away during startup should not fire deferred work
* Pair with [Startup Time Optimization](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/performance/startup-time-optimization/) for splash and bytecode strategy

---

### 9. Measure a Simple Scroll Scenario

Before advanced tools, reproduce a **fixed audit script** on a reference device every release.

```markdown
## Weekly scroll audit (5 minutes)
 
1. Cold start app on Pixel 6a (or team reference device).
2. Open primary feed tab.
3. Fast fling scroll for 15 seconds.
4. Record: UI FPS min, JS FPS min, any blank rows.
5. Open/close modal on feed - note parent re-render spikes in DevTools.
6. Compare to last RC - regressions > 10% trigger investigation.
```

* Same device, same build type (**release**), same network - variance destroys trust
* Blank rows during fling are **list height bugs**, not mysterious "React slowness"
* Escalate to [Flashlight Benchmarking](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/performance/flashlight-benchmarking/) when you need scored comparisons across devices

---

### 10. Publish Budgets with Named Owners

Anonymous budgets are ignored in crunch week. Copy the starter table into `docs/performance-budgets.md` and assign humans.

| Metric | Threshold (starter) | Owner role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Main JS bundle (Hermes) | ≤ 4 MB gzipped | Mobile platform lead |
| Cold start TTI (primary tab) | ≤ 2.5 s on reference Android | Feature squad lead |
| Scroll FPS (primary list) | ≥ 55 fps sustained | UI performance champ |
| Memory after 10 min session | ≤ 350 MB on reference Android | Mobile on-call |

```tsx
// src/perf/budgets.ts - import constants in CI scripts and docs
export const PERF_BUDGETS = {
  bundleGzipMb: 4,
  ttiMs: 2500,
  scrollFpsFloor: 55,
  memoryCeilingMb: 350,
} as const;
```

* **Tier 1** at kickoff, **Tier 2** in CI for bundle size, **Tier 3** manual device audit before store submit
* Link regressions to rollback policy in [Performance Budget Rules](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-rules/performance-budget-rules/)
* [Performance Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/performance/best-practices/) condenses the full section into 25 rules

---

## FAQs

What is a reasonable TTI budget for Expo SDK 57?

Many consumer apps target **≤ 2.5 s** cold start to primary-tab interactive on mid-tier Android. Heavy apps (maps, offline media) need higher ceilings with ADR justification - measure your baseline first.

Why measure on mid-tier Android instead of my iPhone?

Low-end and mid-tier Android exposes jank, slow storage, and memory pressure that flagship iPhones hide. If it passes on reference Android, iOS is usually fine; the reverse is false.

Does Expo Go reflect production performance?

No - Expo Go ships a generic native shell and different module graph. Profile **release builds** (EAS `preview` or `production`) for TTI, bundle size, and memory.

Is 60 fps always required?

60 fps is the ideal. For audits, **55 fps sustained** on the primary list is a practical release floor. Brief dips during image decode are acceptable; sustained JS FPS at 0 is not.

How does Hermes affect these metrics?

Hermes improves startup via **bytecode** and reduces parse cost versus JSC. It does not remove React render work or list churn - you still defer heavy JS and virtualize feeds.

Where do I start if the app feels slow?

1. Define TTI and reproduce on reference Android (release build).
2. Fix list virtualization and re-render hygiene on the primary feed.
3. Profile with [React DevTools Profiler](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/performance/react-devtools-profiler/) before random `memo`.

Dokumen: React DevTools Profiler

# React DevTools Profiler

Finding avoidable re-renders on navigation transitions - the cookbook workflow for Expo SDK 57 apps before you rewrite screens or add `memo` everywhere.

Highlights / React DevTools Profiler

* Record a navigation transition - not idle home - to catch provider and tab re-renders
* Ranked chart shows which components committed; flame chart shows why parents dragged children
* Why did this render? highlights changed props, state, and context in React 19
* Fix unstable context values and inline props before sprinkling memo on leaf rows
* Pair Profiler with list hygiene - navigation often re-renders every visible FlatList row
* Profile release-like builds on device - Fast Refresh hides real commit costs

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

**Setup (once per session)**

```bash
# Start app with dev client or debug build
npx expo start
# Press j in terminal → open React Native DevTools in browser
# Open Profiler tab → gear → enable "Record why each component rendered"
```

**Repro script - navigation transition**

1. Reload app (cold or warm).
2. Click **Record** in Profiler.
3. Navigate: Home tab → open stack screen → go back → switch tab → return.
4. Stop recording.
5. In **Ranked** view, sort by render duration - note top 5 components.
6. Click a hot row component → **Why did this render?** → check props/context changes.
7. Fix the **nearest stable owner** (layout provider, tab shell, list parent) before memoizing leaves.

**Stable navigation shell pattern**

```tsx
// app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx
import { Tabs } from "expo-router";
import { useMemo } from "react";
 
export default function TabLayout() {
  const screenOptions = useMemo(
    () => ({
      headerShown: false,
      tabBarActiveTintColor: "#2563eb",
    }),
    [],
  );
 
  return (
    <Tabs screenOptions={screenOptions}>
      <Tabs.Screen name="index" options={{ title: "Home" }} />
      <Tabs.Screen name="search" options={{ title: "Search" }} />
    </Tabs>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// src/ui/FeedRow.tsx - memo only after parent props are stable
import { memo } from "react";
import { Pressable, StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
export type FeedItem = { id: string; title: string };
 
export const FeedRow = memo(function FeedRow({
  item,
  onPress,
}: {
  item: FeedItem;
  onPress: (id: string) => void;
}) {
  return (
    <Pressable onPress={() => onPress(item.id)} style={styles.row}>
      <Text style={styles.title}>{item.title}</Text>
    </Pressable>
  );
});
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  row: { padding: 16, borderBottomWidth: StyleSheet.hairlineWidth, borderColor: "#e2e8f0" },
  title: { fontSize: 16, fontWeight: "600" },
});
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Tab switch causes the home feed to stutter though data did not change.
* Opening a modal re-renders hundreds of list rows in Profiler.
* A context provider at root updates on every navigation action.
* You are about to add `React.memo` to 40 components without evidence.

## Working Example

A minimal repro: unstable `screenOptions` and a new `renderItem` each render force the entire feed to commit on every tab blur/focus.

```tsx
import { memo, useCallback, useMemo, useState } from "react";
import {
  FlatList,
  ListRenderItem,
  Pressable,
  StyleSheet,
  Text,
  View,
} from "react-native";
 
type Post = { id: string; title: string };
 
const POSTS: Post[] = Array.from({ length: 120 }, (_, i) => ({
  id: String(i),
  title: `Post ${i + 1}`,
}));
 
const PostRow = memo(function PostRow({
  post,
  onOpen,
}: {
  post: Post;
  onOpen: (id: string) => void;
}) {
  return (
    <Pressable onPress={() => onOpen(post.id)} style={styles.row}>
      <Text style={styles.title}>{post.title}</Text>
    </Pressable>
  );
});
 
function Feed({ posts }: { posts: Post[] }) {
  const [opened, setOpened] = useState<string | null>(null);
 
  const onOpen = useCallback((id: string) => setOpened(id), []);
 
  const renderItem: ListRenderItem<Post> = useCallback(
    ({ item }) => <PostRow post={item} onOpen={onOpen} />,
    [onOpen],
  );
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.panel}>
      <Text style={styles.heading}>Feed {opened ? `(opened ${opened})` : ""}</Text>
      <FlatList
        data={posts}
        keyExtractor={(item) => item.id}
        renderItem={renderItem}
        extraData={opened}
        style={styles.list}
      />
    </View>
  );
}
 
/** Simulates tab shell remounting with fresh object literals - Profiler will light up. */
function UnstableShell({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  const [tab, setTab] = useState<"home" | "search">("home");
  // BAD: new object every render - triggers navigation subtree commits
  const headerStyle = { backgroundColor: tab === "home" ? "#eff6ff" : "#f8fafc" };
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.shell}>
      <View style={[styles.header, headerStyle]}>
        <Pressable onPress={() => setTab("home")}>
          <Text>Home</Text>
        </Pressable>
        <Pressable onPress={() => setTab("search")}>
          <Text>Search</Text>
        </Pressable>
      </View>
      {tab === "home" ? children : <Text style={styles.placeholder}>Search placeholder</Text>}
    </View>
  );
}
 
export default function ProfilerNavigationDemo() {
  const posts = useMemo(() => POSTS, []);
  return (
    <UnstableShell>
      <Feed posts={posts} />
    </UnstableShell>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  shell: { flex: 1 },
  header: { flexDirection: "row", gap: 16, padding: 16 },
  panel: { flex: 1 },
  heading: { paddingHorizontal: 16, fontWeight: "700" },
  list: { flex: 1 },
  row: { padding: 16 },
  title: { fontSize: 15 },
  placeholder: { padding: 16, color: "#64748b" },
});
```

**Profiler checklist for this screen**

| Symptom in recording | Likely cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Every `PostRow` commits on tab tap | Parent `Feed` re-rendered; unstable `renderItem` or missing `memo` | `useCallback` renderItem + `memo` row |
| `UnstableShell` commits all children | Inline `headerStyle` object | `useMemo` or `StyleSheet` |
| Rows commit when only `opened` changes | Expected - pass `extraData` | Ensure only affected rows need full tree work |
| Provider at root commits on navigation | Context value recreated | Split context; memoize `value` object |

## Navigation-Specific Hotspots

### Context providers at the root

```tsx
// BAD - new value every render
<AppContext.Provider value={{ theme, setTheme, cart, setCart }}>
 
// BETTER - split read/write or memoize value slices
const value = useMemo(() => ({ theme, cart }), [theme, cart]);
<AppContext.Provider value={value}>
```

Navigation often reads context in tab bars and headers. If the value object is fresh each render, **every screen under the provider commits**.

### Expo Router layouts

`_layout.tsx` files re-render when route segments change. Hoist heavy providers **below** the segment that changes, or split layouts so stack modals do not wrap the entire tab tree.

```tsx
// app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx - keep providers that do not need stack state here
// app/(tabs)/feed/_layout.tsx - stack-specific state stays in feed subtree
```

### List parents on stack push/pop

When a stack screen opens over a tab, the tab may stay mounted. If the feed parent subscribes to navigation focus events and calls `setState` on every blur, Profiler shows a spike on **all visible rows**. Debounce focus handlers and avoid storing navigation objects in React state.

## Reading Profiler Views

| View | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| **Flame graph** | Finding which parent dragged children into a commit |
| **Ranked** | Total time per component - start here for "who is slow" |
| **Timeline** | Correlating commits with gestures (scroll, tab switch) |

**React 19 "Why did this render?"** categories:

* **Props changed** - inline objects/functions from parent; fix parent stability.
* **State changed** - expected; narrow state ownership.
* **Context changed** - provider value identity; split or memoize.
* **Parent re-rendered** - child had no hook changes but parent forced reconciliation - add `memo` after parent is stable.

## Gotchas

* **Profiling in dev exaggerates render cost** - use Profiler for *relative* comparisons (before/after fix), not absolute ms budgets.
* **Strict Mode double render** - development may show duplicate commits; compare the same environment before and after.
* **Memo without stable props is useless** - Profiler will still show child commits if `renderItem` is a new function reference.
* **Do not profile only idle screens** - navigation transitions are where avoidable commits hide.

## FAQs

React Native DevTools vs standalone react-devtools?

Expo SDK 57 routes through **React Native DevTools** (press `j` in CLI). Use the embedded Profiler tab - the workflow matches React web DevTools for commits and ranked views.

How do I profile a release build?

DevTools attaches to debuggable builds. For release-like timing, use **Hermes sampling** and **Flashlight** alongside Profiler - see [Hermes Sampling Profiler](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/performance/hermes-sampling-profiler/) and [Flashlight Benchmarking](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/performance/flashlight-benchmarking/).

Should I memo every list row?

Only after `renderItem`, handlers, and parent context are stable. Otherwise Profiler shows rows committing anyway - see [List Performance Tuning](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/lists-scrolling/list-performance-tuning/).

Profiler shows Tabs layout re-rendering - is that normal?

Some re-render on focus is expected. Spikes that include the entire feed are not - stabilize `screenOptions`, `tabBarStyle`, and providers in `app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx`.

How does React 19 batching affect Profiler?

More automatic batching reduces duplicate commits from rapid `setState` - good. It does not fix unstable props from parents; referential equality rules are unchanged.

What commit time is "too slow"?

No universal ms threshold in Profiler - look for **unexpected commits** (all rows on modal open) and **ranked outliers** you can eliminate. Pair with FPS measurement on device for user-visible impact.

## Related

* [Performance Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/performance/performance-basics/) - TTI, FPS, and memory vocabulary
* [List Performance Tuning](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/lists-scrolling/list-performance-tuning/) - `memo`, `extraData`, stable `renderItem`
* [Props, State & Re-renders on Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/rn-fundamentals/props-state-and-re-renders-on-mobile/) - what triggers commits
* [Style Performance](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/style-performance/) - inline styles breaking memo equality
* [Tabs & Drawers](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/tabs-and-drawers/) - `lazy` tabs and mount behavior

Dokumen: Product Collaboration Best Practices
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/product-collaboration/best-practices/

# Product Collaboration Best Practices

A condensed summary of the **25 most important product collaboration practices** for Expo SDK 57 mobile teams - drawn from every page in this section.

Highlights / Product Collaboration Best Practices

* Device demos in refinement - stakeholders trust thumbs, not static artboards
* Feasibility notes on every net-new screen before sprint commit
* Platform parity documented - intentional divergence beats silent drift
* Estimates as ranges with OTA vs store path stated per ticket
* Crash-free and rollout % in weekly updates - not git jargon
* Motion classified before hi-fi lock - Reanimated vs static decided jointly

1. **Demo on real devices in refinement:** iOS + Android preview build or sim recording before sprint commit - [Product Collaboration Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/product-collaboration/product-collaboration-basics/).
2. **Figma is a hypothesis:** Handoff checklist includes safe areas, keyboard, and non-happy-path states - not only marketing frames.
3. **Engineer in design crit early:** Wireframe-stage attendance catches gesture and navigation issues before hi-fi investment.
4. **Feasibility comment per screen:** One engineer note on ticket - spike needed, fallback pattern, or clear - [Working with Design & Motion](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/product-collaboration/working-with-design-and-motion/).
5. **Safe area is layout:** `useSafeAreaInsets` - never magic `paddingTop: 44` copied from web mocks.
6. **Keyboard states in design review:** Primary CTA visible with keyboard up on smallest supported phone.
7. **Touch targets ≥48dp:** Enforce in design system components - dense Figma does not override HIG/Material - [Design Systems Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/design-systems-basics/).
8. **Platform parity is a decision:** Document intentional iOS/Android differences in ADR - [Platform Parity Decisions](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/product-collaboration/platform-parity-decisions/).
9. **Native chrome over custom imitation:** System back, share sheet, and pickers unless brand ADR says otherwise.
10. **Gestures flagged before pointing:** Swipe, drag, pull-to-refresh tickets link Gesture Handler feasibility - [Gesture Handler](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/react-native-gesture-handler/).
11. **Motion spec before hi-fi lock:** Trigger, duration, interrupt, reduced-motion fallback - [Animations Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/animations-basics/).
12. **Reanimated for gesture-linked UI:** Scroll-linked headers and swipe rows - not `Animated` with JS-thread scroll - [Reanimated 4](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/react-native-reanimated-4/).
13. **30-minute motion spikes:** GO / SIMPLIFY / DEFER verdict with screen recording on mid-tier Android.
14. **Phased delight is valid:** v1 static transitions + v1.1 motion - label in roadmap, not hidden descope.
15. **Estimates are ranges:** Engineering + discovery + release calendar - [Estimation & Risk on Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/product-collaboration/estimation-and-risk-on-mobile/).
16. **OTA vs store on every ticket:** JS-only OTA path stated; native changes trigger store timeline honesty.
17. **Store review buffer explicit:** +2–5 calendar days on binary releases - never promise users a date at merge.
18. **Native spikes are billable discovery:** 0.5–2 days with written outcome - not hidden padding.
19. **Risk register on epics:** Top three risks reviewed weekly with PM - likelihood, impact, owner.
20. **Debt in the portfolio board:** SDK upgrades and perf beside features with business risk - [Prioritizing Tech Debt vs Features](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/product-collaboration/prioritizing-tech-debt-vs-features/).
21. **Crash-free in stakeholder updates:** ≥99.5% target with plain-language impact - [Stakeholder Communication](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/product-collaboration/stakeholder-communication/).
22. **Trade-off memos:** Three options, recommendation, decision date - engineering recommends, PM decides.
23. **Yellow flag early:** Estimate bust same-day - revised range beats demo-day surprise.
24. **PR screenshots both platforms:** Unintentional parity drift is a bug; intentional drift is documented.
25. **Tokens over one-off pixels:** Color, spacing, and motion presets in design system - screens compose components, not literals - [Theming & Brand Flavors](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/theming-and-brand-flavors/).

## FAQs

What is the single highest-leverage habit?

Device demo in refinement - one 10-minute walkthrough prevents more rework than any process doc.

How do we onboard PMs to mobile constraints?

Share this best-practices page + [OTA Updates Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/ota-updates-basics/) - OTA vs store is the most common misconception.

Design team resists feasibility sessions?

Frame as protecting craft - fewer emergency simplifications post-sprint. 30 minutes at wireframe saves days of hi-fi rework.

How often to review platform parity ADRs?

When adding gestures, sheets, or OS upgrades (e.g. Android predictive back). Otherwise quarterly audit of screenshot pairs.

Minimum stakeholder update cadence?

Weekly mobile health message - release stage, crash-free, top issue, ask. Incidents get impact-first template same day.

* [Platform Parity Decisions](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/product-collaboration/platform-parity-decisions/) - ranked iOS/Android choices
* [Estimation & Risk on Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/product-collaboration/estimation-and-risk-on-mobile/) - ranges and store buffer
* [Prioritizing Tech Debt vs Features](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/product-collaboration/prioritizing-tech-debt-vs-features/) - debt portfolio framing

Dokumen: Platform Parity Decisions
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/product-collaboration/platform-parity-decisions/

# Platform Parity Decisions

Ranked decision guide for when **iOS and Android intentionally differ** in Expo SDK 57 apps - choose the best approach per scenario, document the call, and avoid silent drift that confuses users and QA.

Highlights / Platform Parity Decisions

* Platform parity is a product choice - not an accident of whichever dev finished first
* Follow HIG and Material where users expect native chrome - document exceptions in ADR
* Shared design tokens with platform-specific navigation patterns is the default stack
* Intentional divergence needs a ticket, screenshot pair, and PM sign-off - not silent drift
* Android predictive back and iOS edge swipe change custom gesture specs
* Store review and OS policy sometimes force platform-specific flows - record the constraint

## How to Use This List

* Default assumption: **shared business logic**, **platform-native chrome** where OS conventions differ (back, sheets, permissions).
* Each decision ranks options - pick **Best** unless compliance, timeline, or brand mandates override.
* Record chosen rank, date, and dissent in a short ADR or ticket comment - link iOS + Android screenshots.
* Revisit when adding **gesture-heavy** flows, **Material You** theming, or **Android 15 predictive back**.

---

## Decision 1: Back navigation on nested stacks

**Scenario:** Multi-step checkout inside a stack; users expect to go back without losing cart state.

| Rank | Choice | Approach |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Best | **Platform-native back** | iOS swipe-from-edge + header back; Android hardware/gesture back via Expo Router stack |
| 2nd | **Custom header back with shared logic** | One `onBack` handler; platform icons from design system |
| 3rd | **Floating universal back button** | Bottom-left FAB - acceptable only in games or immersive media |

**Wrong choice:** Disabling Android system back to force a centered "Back" text button - users churn when gesture back exits the app unexpectedly.

**Why best is best:** Users muscle-memory OS navigation. Router `router.back()` wired to both header and Android `BackHandler` preserves state without fighting the platform.

---

## Decision 2: Primary action placement in forms

**Scenario:** Long signup form; primary CTA must be obvious on both platforms.

| Rank | Choice | Approach |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Best | **Sticky footer CTA (shared)** | Full-width button above safe area; keyboard avoidance tested both OS |
| 2nd | **iOS top-right text action + Android FAB** | Documented divergence for power-user apps |
| 3rd | **Inline submit after last field only** | Acceptable for 2-field flows |

**Wrong choice:** iOS-only top-right "Done" with no Android equivalent hidden in overflow menu - Android users never find submit.

**Why best is best:** Sticky footer survives keyboard and dynamic type; one layout QA matrix. Platform-specific placement doubles design and test cost for marginal UX gain.

---

## Decision 3: Date and time selection

**Scenario:** Schedule appointment; pick date + time with validation.

| Rank | Choice | Approach |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Best | **Platform pickers** | `@react-native-community/datetimepicker` - spinner on iOS, calendar/dialog on Android |
| 2nd | **Unified bottom sheet custom picker** | Brand-critical scheduling apps with motion budget |
| 3rd | **Web-style inline calendar always visible** | Only on tablet layouts |

**Wrong choice:** Forcing iOS wheel picker styling on Android - feels foreign and fails TalkBack/VoiceOver expectations.

**Why best is best:** Native pickers ship fast, respect locale, and pass store accessibility scrutiny. Custom pickers need spikes - [Working with Design & Motion](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/product-collaboration/working-with-design-and-motion/).

---

## Decision 4: Share sheet and social actions

**Scenario:** User shares referral link or exports PDF from a detail screen.

| Rank | Choice | Approach |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Best | **`expo-sharing` + system share sheet** | OS-native targets (Messages, Drive, etc.) |
| 2nd | **Custom in-app share targets** | When analytics require channel tracking per tap |
| 3rd | **Copy link only** | MVP acceptable; expand before growth campaigns |

**Wrong choice:** Rebuilding the entire OS share sheet in RN - maintenance nightmare; never matches installed apps.

**Why best is best:** System sheets update with OS - new targets appear without app releases. Custom UI is product differentiation, not default.

---

## Decision 5: Tab bar vs navigation drawer

**Scenario:** App has 4–5 top-level destinations; PM wants "same as web sidebar."

| Rank | Choice | Approach |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Best | **Bottom tabs (phone)** | Expo Router `(tabs)` - thumb-reachable; Material/iOS tab bar conventions |
| 2nd | **Drawer on Android + tabs on iOS** | Document divergence; rare unless enterprise admin apps |
| 3rd | **Hamburger-only navigation** | Acceptable for 6+ destinations with clear IA |

**Wrong choice:** Permanent left sidebar on phone portrait - wastes horizontal space; fights one-handed use.

**Why best is best:** Mobile IA centers bottom tabs; tablet can use split view later. Web sidebar mental model does not transfer to 390px width.

---

## Decision 6: Modal presentation style

**Scenario:** Confirm destructive delete; need user attention without losing context.

| Rank | Choice | Approach |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Best | **Platform alert / action sheet** | `Alert.alert` simple; `@expo/react-native-action-sheet` for 3+ actions |
| 2nd | **Bottom sheet (shared)** | `@gorhom/bottom-sheet` - matches modern iOS sheet + Android bottom dialog |
| 3rd | **Centered web-style modal** | Desktop tablet only |

**Wrong choice:** Full-screen blocking modal with no dismiss gesture on Android - violates Material back expectations.

**Why best is best:** Destructive confirms map cleanly to platform dialogs. Sheets scale to rich content; centered modals feel web-imported on phones.

---

## Decision 7: Pull-to-refresh indicator

**Scenario:** Feed list refresh; brand has custom loading animation.

| Rank | Choice | Approach |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Best | **Platform refresh control** | `RefreshControl` with brand tint color token |
| 2nd | **Custom Lottie header** | Marketing-heavy apps; budget Reanimated + scroll sync |
| 3rd | **Manual refresh button only** | Offline-first lists where pull gesture conflicts with row swipe |

**Wrong choice:** Disabling pull-to-refresh on iOS only because custom animation was Android-only - users report "broken" on App Store reviews.

**Why best is best:** `RefreshControl` is one prop; tint aligns brand without custom scroll physics. Custom refresh needs [Gesture Conflict Resolution](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/gesture-conflict-resolution/).

---

## Decision 8: Typography and default fonts

**Scenario:** Brand uses custom font; body text must feel native.

| Rank | Choice | Approach |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Best | **Custom brand font + system fallback stack** | `expo-font` load; SF Pro / Roboto fallback for CJK and missing glyphs |
| 2nd | **Platform system font for body, brand for display** | Reduces bundle; slightly different cross-platform rhythm |
| 3rd | **Identical web font files both platforms** | Acceptable when marketing mandates pixel parity |

**Wrong choice:** Assuming Google Fonts web files render identically on iOS without testing diacritics and tabular nums.

**Why best is best:** Mobile readability and bundle size matter. Tokenized typography from [Design Systems Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/design-systems-basics/) documents which roles use brand vs system.

---

## Decision 9: Permissions prompts and pre-prompts

**Scenario:** Camera access for profile photo; store requires clear purpose strings.

| Rank | Choice | Approach |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Best | **In-app education screen → system prompt** | Same copy both platforms; `Info.plist` + `AndroidManifest` strings localized |
| 2nd | **iOS pre-prompt only (Android goes straight to system)** | Acceptable - Android has no official pre-prompt pattern |
| 3rd | **Custom fake "permission" UI that isn't system dialog** | Misleading; store rejection risk |

**Wrong choice:** Different permission rationale text per platform without legal review - compliance failure on enterprise contracts.

**Why best is best:** One education flow; native dialog is still OS-controlled. Document Android "don't ask again" path in support macros.

---

## Decision 10: Haptics on success and error

**Scenario:** Payment success, form error, toggle favorite - design spec includes haptic feedback.

| Rank | Choice | Approach |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Best | **iOS `expo-haptics` + Android short vibration fallback** | Map semantic events: success → notification success; error → error pattern |
| 2nd | **iOS haptics only; Android silent** | Documented divergence for low-priority delight |
| 3rd | **Identical long vibration both platforms** | Feels aggressive on iPhone; avoid |

**Wrong choice:** Calling haptics on every list scroll tick - battery drain and App Store "excessive feedback" complaints.

**Why best is best:** Semantic mapping preserves intent without pretending hardware is identical. Android vibration amplitude varies by OEM - keep patterns short.

---

## Decision 11: Dark mode and dynamic color

**Scenario:** App supports dark mode; Android Material You pulls wallpaper colors.

| Rank | Choice | Approach |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Best | **Shared semantic tokens + platform theme provider** | `useColorScheme` + [Theming & Brand Flavors](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/theming-and-brand-flavors/) |
| 2nd | **Identical hex palette both modes** | No dynamic color on Android 12+ |
| 3rd | **Light mode only** | Acceptable short-term; document debt |

**Wrong choice:** Hard-coded `#FFFFFF` backgrounds - Android dark mode and iOS smart invert break layouts.

**Why best is best:** Semantic `surface`, `textPrimary` tokens absorb platform theme without redrawing every screen in Figma.

---

## Decision 12: Push notification permission timing

**Scenario:** Marketing wants push opt-in at first launch; engineering prefers contextual prompt.

| Rank | Choice | Approach |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Best | **Contextual prompt after first value moment** | e.g. after first order - higher opt-in, same API both platforms |
| 2nd | **iOS provisional / Android notification channels** | Platform-specific APIs with shared product timing doc |
| 3rd | **Launch-day modal** | Only if compliance mandates; expect lower opt-in |

**Wrong choice:** iOS system prompt on cold start before login - Apple Human Interface Guidelines discourage; users tap Don't Allow permanently.

**Why best is best:** Timing is product policy; implementation uses `expo-notifications` once. Divergence is **when**, not **whether**, to ask.

---

## FAQs

Must iOS and Android look identical?

No - they must feel **coherent**. Shared IA, tokens, and copy; native navigation and system components can differ. Document intentional deltas in ADRs.

Who signs off on platform divergence?

PM + design lead + engineering lead. QA receives a **parity matrix** listing screens that differ - not a single golden screenshot.

How do we prevent accidental drift?

PR template requires iOS + Android screenshots for UI changes. CI preview builds on both platforms. Unintentional drift is a bug; intentional is documented.

What about tablet and foldable layouts?

Treat as separate decisions - phone parity first. Foldables may follow Android Material adaptive guidelines while iPad uses split navigation.

Does Expo Router force parity?

Router file structure is shared; presentation options (`presentation: "modal"`) can diverge per platform with `Platform.select` - still document the choice.

## Related

* [Product Collaboration Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/product-collaboration/product-collaboration-basics/) - design-to-mobile translation
* [Working with Design & Motion](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/product-collaboration/working-with-design-and-motion/) - motion feasibility per platform
* [Design Systems Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/design-systems-basics/) - shared tokens, platform chrome
* [Gesture Handler](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/react-native-gesture-handler/) - back gesture and pan conflicts
* [Theming & Brand Flavors](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/theming-and-brand-flavors/) - dark mode tokens
* [Expo Router Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/expo-router-basics/) - stack and tab patterns

Dokumen: Product Collaboration Basics
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/product-collaboration/product-collaboration-basics/

# Product Collaboration Basics

10 examples to get you started translating **designs into feasible mobile interactions** on Expo SDK 57 - what to validate before sprint commitment, how to talk to design and PM in mobile terms, and where web assumptions break on phones.

Highlights / Product Collaboration Basics

* Figma frames are hypotheses - validate on iOS and Android hardware before sprint commitment
* Safe areas, keyboard, and gesture back change layout math - not optional polish
* One feasibility note per screen beats a post-sprint 'we can't build that' surprise
* Motion specs need frame budget and fallback - see Animations & Gestures before pixels lock
* Design tokens from your system beat one-off hex values copied from web mocks
* Demo on device in refinement - stakeholders trust thumbs, not static artboards

## Prerequisites

Product collaboration assumes a standard **Expo SDK 57** app with design tokens and at least one preview build profile.

```bash
npx create-expo-app@latest MyProductApp --template blank-typescript
cd MyProductApp
npx eas init
```

> **Tooling:** These examples target **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4), **React Native 0.86.0**, and **React 19.2.3**. Pair with [Design Systems Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/design-systems-basics/) for tokens and [Animations Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/animations-basics/) for motion feasibility.

---

## Basic Examples

### 1. Design Handoff Is a Conversation, Not a File Drop

Treat Figma export as the **start** of refinement - not the end of design.

```markdown
## Handoff checklist (per screen)
- [ ] iOS + Android artboards OR explicit "platform follows HIG/Material"
- [ ] Safe area insets noted (notch, Dynamic Island, nav bar)
- [ ] Keyboard states: default, focused, error inline
- [ ] Loading, empty, error - not only happy path
- [ ] Engineer feasibility comment thread open before sprint planning
```

* PM schedules **15-minute feasibility pass** with engineer + designer before pointing
* "Looks good" on Figma ≠ "ships this sprint" on two platforms
* Record blockers in the ticket - "needs native module spike" is a valid outcome

> **Related:** [Working with Design & Motion](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/product-collaboration/working-with-design-and-motion/) - pre-pixel feasibility reviews

---

### 2. Safe Area Changes Every "Fixed" Header

Web mocks with `position: fixed` top bars ignore the notch and status bar.

```tsx
// src/screens/ProfileScreen.tsx
import { View, Text } from "react-native";
import { useSafeAreaInsets } from "react-native-safe-area-context";
 
export function ProfileScreen() {
  const insets = useSafeAreaInsets();
 
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1, paddingTop: insets.top }}>
      <Text accessibilityRole="header">Profile</Text>
      {/* Content scrolls under transparent header only if designed that way */}
    </View>
  );
}
```

* Show designers **two device frames**: iPhone with Dynamic Island + Android with punch-hole
* `paddingTop: 44` magic numbers fail on new hardware - use insets
* Sticky footers need `insets.bottom` for home indicator overlap

---

### 3. Bottom Sheets Are Not Web Modals

Centered modal dialogs from web often become **bottom sheets** or **full-screen flows** on mobile.

| Web pattern | Mobile default | When to diverge |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Centered dialog | Bottom sheet (`@gorhom/bottom-sheet`) | Short confirmations |
| Dropdown menu | Action sheet / context menu | Destructive actions need platform sheet |
| Hover tooltip | Long-press or info icon | No hover on touch |
| Multi-column form | Single column + steps | Keyboard reduces visible viewport |

* Flag **gesture dismiss** expectations - swipe-down vs tap-outside differs by platform
* See [Platform Parity Decisions](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/product-collaboration/platform-parity-decisions/) when iOS and Android intentionally differ

---

### 4. Keyboard Avoidance Is Part of the Design

A form that looks perfect in Figma may hide the primary CTA when the keyboard opens.

```tsx
import { KeyboardAvoidingView, Platform, ScrollView } from "react-native";
 
export function SignUpForm() {
  return (
    <KeyboardAvoidingView
      style={{ flex: 1 }}
      behavior={Platform.OS === "ios" ? "padding" : undefined}
      keyboardVerticalOffset={Platform.OS === "ios" ? 64 : 0}
    >
      <ScrollView keyboardShouldPersistTaps="handled">
        {/* fields + submit - designer reviews with keyboard up */}
      </ScrollView>
    </KeyboardAvoidingView>
  );
}
```

* Design review must include **keyboard-up screenshot** on smallest supported phone
* `android:windowSoftInputMode` may need config plugin - not pure JS
* Floating labels that animate need motion budget - [Reanimated 4](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/react-native-reanimated-4/)

---

### 5. Touch Targets Beat Pixel-Perfect Density

Figma at 100% zoom tempts 32px buttons; Apple HIG and Material recommend **44–48dp minimum**.

```tsx
// design-systems/PrimaryButton.tsx - enforce minimum touch target
import { Pressable, Text, StyleSheet } from "react-native";
 
type Props = { label: string; onPress: () => void };
 
export function PrimaryButton({ label, onPress }: Props) {
  return (
    <Pressable
      onPress={onPress}
      style={styles.hitSlop}
      accessibilityRole="button"
      accessibilityLabel={label}
    >
      <Text style={styles.label}>{label}</Text>
    </Pressable>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  hitSlop: {
    minHeight: 48,
    minWidth: 48,
    paddingHorizontal: 16,
    justifyContent: "center",
    alignItems: "center",
  },
  label: { fontSize: 16, fontWeight: "600" },
});
```

* Designers use **8px grid** from [Design Systems Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/design-systems-basics/) - engineers enforce `minHeight` in components
* Dense data tables on phone often need **card list** alternative - negotiate in refinement
* WCAG 2.5.5 (44×44) is a product decision, not a post-launch audit surprise

---

### 6. Gestures Need Engineering Early

Swipe-to-delete, drag-to-reorder, and pull-to-refresh compete for the same pan handlers.

```markdown
## Gesture feasibility (ticket template)
**Interaction:** Swipe row left → reveal Delete
**Libraries:** react-native-gesture-handler + Reanimated
**Conflicts:** Parent FlatList vertical scroll
**Spike:** 0.5 day if new pattern
**Fallback:** Long-press → action sheet
```

* If the mock shows **physics-based** drag, link [Gesture Handler](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/react-native-gesture-handler/) in the ticket
* "Same as iOS Mail" is not a spec - record threshold, haptics, and undo pattern
* Android back gesture can cancel incomplete swipes - test on API 35 emulator

---

### 7. States Beyond the Happy Path

Shippable screens need **loading, empty, error, offline, and permission-denied** - not only the marketing frame.

```tsx
type ViewState = "loading" | "empty" | "error" | "ready";
 
export function OrdersList({ state, orders }: { state: ViewState; orders: Order[] }) {
  if (state === "loading") return <OrdersSkeleton />;
  if (state === "empty") return <EmptyState title="No orders yet" cta="Browse catalog" />;
  if (state === "error") return <ErrorState onRetry={refetch} />;
  return <FlatList data={orders} renderItem={renderOrder} />;
}
```

* PM acceptance criteria: "user sees X when network fails" - not implied
* Skeleton vs spinner is a **design system** decision - one pattern per data density
* Permission strings (`NSCameraUsageDescription`) require store build - flag in estimation

---

### 8. Typography and Dynamic Type

Fixed `fontSize: 14` in Figma breaks when users enable **larger text** in system settings.

```tsx
import { Text, StyleSheet } from "react-native";
 
export function BodyText({ children }: { children: string }) {
  return (
    <Text
      style={styles.body}
      maxFontSizeMultiplier={1.3} // product cap - document in a11y ADR if lower than system
    >
      {children}
    </Text>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  body: { fontSize: 16, lineHeight: 24 }, // token: typography.body
});
```

* Designers deliver **type scale tokens**, not one-off sizes - [Theming & Brand Flavors](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/theming-and-brand-flavors/)
* Review **XL dynamic type** on iOS and **font scale 1.3** on Android before sign-off
* Truncation rules: `numberOfLines` vs expand - business copy decision

---

### 9. Native Pickers vs Custom Dropdowns

"Custom select" from web is often **half a sprint** on mobile; platform pickers ship faster.

| Requirement | Faster path | Slower path |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Date of birth | `@react-native-community/datetimepicker` | Custom calendar wheel |
| Country list | Searchable modal + `FlatList` | Figma custom dropdown with blur |
| Single choice (3–5 options) | Segmented control / radio group | Bottom sheet with illustrations |

* Document **intentional** custom UI in ADR when platform picker is rejected
* Custom pickers need a11y: screen reader order, focus trap, dismiss gesture
* PM trade-off table in refinement beats redesign mid-sprint

---

### 10. Device Demo Closes the Loop

End refinement with a **10-minute device walkthrough** - prototype, preview build, or Storybook on phone.

```bash
# Share preview with design + PM before sprint start
eas build --profile preview --platform all
# QR in refinement notes; same build for QA acceptance
```

```markdown
## Refinement done when
- [ ] Designer saw iOS + Android (sim or device)
- [ ] Engineer logged feasibility risks in ticket
- [ ] PM accepted fallback for any "spike pending" item
- [ ] Motion marked: Animated vs Reanimated vs static
```

* Stakeholders overweight Figma fidelity - **thumb demo** resets expectations
* Record screen recording for async PMs - 30 seconds beats a paragraph
* Ties to [Stakeholder Communication](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/product-collaboration/stakeholder-communication/) for release language

---

## FAQs

When should engineering join design reviews?

Before high-fidelity lock on net-new flows - ideally at wireframe. One engineer in weekly design crit catches mobile-specific issues early. Late joiners produce expensive pixel reworks.

How do we say "no" without blocking product?

Offer **ranked alternatives**: platform picker vs custom, bottom sheet vs full screen, phase 1 without animation. "No" with options is collaboration; "no" alone is a wall.

Do we need separate iOS and Android designs?

Not always - shared layout with platform chrome differences is common. Document intentional divergence in [Platform Parity Decisions](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/product-collaboration/platform-parity-decisions/); don't let drift happen by accident.

What if design uses web components as reference?

Translate patterns, don't copy DOM. Flexbox translates; hover, `vh`, and multi-column grids do not. Reference [Design Systems Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/design-systems-basics/) for RN component APIs.

How much buffer should estimates include for design churn?

Stable tokens and components: 10–15%. New gestures, camera, or motion: 25–40% plus spike day. See [Estimation & Risk on Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/product-collaboration/estimation-and-risk-on-mobile/).

Should PMs learn React Native?

They should learn **mobile constraints**: safe areas, store review, OTA vs binary, offline. Code literacy helps read feasibility notes - not a requirement to write JSX.

* [Stakeholder Communication](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/product-collaboration/stakeholder-communication/) - plain-language status updates
