Dokumen: Stakeholder Communication
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/product-collaboration/stakeholder-communication/

# Stakeholder Communication

A cookbook for explaining **crash rates, release status, and engineering trade-offs** in plain language - templates Expo SDK 57 leads paste into Slack, email, and exec updates without drowning non-engineers in jargon.

Highlights / Stakeholder Communication

* Stakeholders need outcomes and dates as ranges - not git commit hashes
* Crash-free rate and ANR rate are the mobile uptime metric - translate from Sentry/Crashlytics
* Release status: binary vs OTA vs in review - three different user-visible states
* Trade-off memos in one screen: option, cost, risk, recommendation
* Red/yellow/green without context causes panic - always pair status with next action
* Device demo clips beat paragraphs for design approval and incident comms

## Recipe

> Weekly product-health message - copy, fill blanks, send Monday 9am local.

```markdown
## Mobile health - week of <date>
 
**Release:** <version> - <In review | Rolling out 20% | Full production | OTA only>
**Crash-free sessions (7d):** <99.x%> - target ≥99.5% - <on track | investigating>
**Top crash:** <short signature> - <ticket> - owner <name> - ETA <range>
**Store:** <submitted | approved | not scheduled> - next binary <date range>
**Sprint:** <on track | at risk> - <one-line why>
 
**Needs from leadership:** <none | decision on scope X by Wednesday>
```

```bash
# Numbers source - run before writing update
# Sentry: Project → Releases → crash-free rate
# EAS: Dashboard → latest production build + OTA group
# Play Console / App Store Connect: rollout % and review status
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Weekly exec or product sync
* Post-incident stakeholder thread
* Pre-release go/no-go
* Scope negotiation when estimate busts
* Design sign-off when feasibility changes

---

## Working Example

### Crash rate: translate for PM and execs

| Engineer term | Stakeholder language |
| --- | --- |
| Crash-free sessions 98.2% | **1 in 55 sessions ends in a force-close** - above our 1-in-200 target |
| ANR rate 0.4% (Android) | App **freezes** on 4 in 1000 sessions - users may see "App isn't responding" |
| P95 launch time 2.8s | Slowest 5% of opens take **nearly 3 seconds** before interaction |
| OTA revert on channel `production` | **Instant rollback** of yesterday's JS fix - no App Store wait |
| New native build required | Users must **update from the store** - 3–7 day calendar minimum |

```markdown
## Incident summary (plain language)
**What users see:** App closes on the payment confirmation screen after tapping Pay.
**How many:** ~120 crashes in 24h (~0.3% of checkout sessions).
**Cause (initial):** JS error when card type missing - fix ready on preview.
**Fix path:** OTA to production after 4h preview soak - **no store submission**.
**Rollback:** Revert OTA channel if crash-free drops below 99% in first hour.
**Owner:** <name> - next update in #incidents at 3pm.
```

**Norms:**

* Lead with **user impact**, then scale, then technical cause
* State **fix delivery mechanism** early - OTA vs store sets expectations
* Never promise "fixed" until preview soak criteria met - say "fix candidate in preview"

### Release status ladder

```text
Stage 0: Development - internal only, preview builds
Stage 1: Store submitted - engineering done; calendar clock with Apple/Google
Stage 2: Approved / phased rollout - 1%→10%→100% Play; iOS manual release or phased
Stage 3: OTA on top of binary - JS changes only; runtimeVersion must match
```

```markdown
## Release note for #product (template)
**v2.14.0 (build 412)** - submitted to App Store <date>, Play <date>
**User-facing:** Loyalty card in wallet tab; improved search
**Not in this build:** Animated card flip - moved to v2.15 (needs Reanimated spike)
**OTA plan:** None until binary at 50% rollout
**Risk:** New camera permission string - first-time reviewers may ask questions (+1–2d)
```

* **"Engineering complete"** ≠ **"released"** - repeat until stakeholders internalize
* Link phased rollout % from store consoles - screenshots help async readers
* Cross-link [Estimation & Risk on Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/product-collaboration/estimation-and-risk-on-mobile/) when dates slip

### Trade-off memo (one screen)

```markdown
## Decision needed: Custom date picker vs platform picker
**Context:** Checkout reschedule screen - design wants branded wheel; eng estimates 5d + risk.
 
| Option | Time | Risk | UX |
|--------|------|------|-----|
| A. Platform picker | 1d | Low | Native feel both OS |
| B. Custom Reanimated wheel | 5–7d | Med jank on Android | Brand match |
| C. Ship web date input (defer) | 0d | High support burden | Poor mobile UX |
 
**Recommendation:** A for v1; B as fast-follow if NPS data shows pain.
**Decision by:** <date> - blocks sprint commit.
```

* Three options maximum - decision fatigue kills memos
* Engineering recommends; PM decides - document dissent if overruled
* Attach 15s screen recording per option when UX is the debate

### Sprint status without jargon

| Instead of | Write |
| --- | --- |
| "Blocked on native module" | "Waiting on proof that barcode scanner works in our build - spike ends Thursday" |
| "Reanimated conflict" | "Swipe-to-delete fights scroll - trying fix; fallback is long-press menu" |
| "Red on CI" | "Automated checks failed - fixing tonight; not a user-facing delay yet" |
| "Tech debt" | "Paying down upgrade required for store policy in August" |

```markdown
## Sprint 24 - at risk (not red)
**Still shipping:** Profile edit, push prefs
**At risk:** Gift card scan - hardware test Friday; may slip 2d
**Not started:** Motion polish - descoped to protect scan deadline
**Ask:** PM confirm scan is P0 over animation
```

### Design and feasibility updates

When engineering discovers a design is costly, use **change request** not blame:

```markdown
## Feasibility update: Hero parallax on home
**Design intent:** Background moves at 0.5× scroll speed.
**Finding:** Jank on Pixel 6a in spike - 42 FPS vs 60 target.
**Options:** (1) Static hero - 0d (2) Simplified fade - 1d (3) Full parallax - 3d + perf ticket
**Design partner:** @design - can we review (2) on device tomorrow 10am?
```

* Invite **device review** - aligns with [Working with Design & Motion](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/product-collaboration/working-with-design-and-motion/)
* Reference [Animations Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/animations-basics/) only in technical appendix - not exec summary

### Executive escalation (brief)

```markdown
## Escalation: Store rejection risk
**Issue:** Payment SDK requires privacy manifest update before April policy.
**Business impact:** Cannot ship revenue features until resolved.
**Cost:** 1 sprint upgrade (already requested Sprint 25).
**Decision:** Approve feature freeze Apr 1–14? Y/N
**If no:** Accept risk of removal from App Store <policy date>.
```

One screen, forced choice, consequence of inaction stated neutrally.

---

## Deep Dive

### Status color rules

| Color | Meaning | Required companion text |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Green | On track within agreed range | What's shipping this sprint |
| Yellow | Risk identified; mitigation active | Owner + date of next checkpoint |
| Red | Missed commitment or user harm | Exec decision or scope cut listed |

**Never** post red without owner and next update time - panic without agency destroys trust.

### Audience-specific depth

| Audience | Include | Omit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CEO | Revenue/release risk, calendar | Hermes, Metro, Reanimated |
| PM | Scope, dates, trade-offs | Gradle plugin internals |
| Design | Device clips, feasibility options | Crash stack traces |
| Support | Workaround steps, ETA plain | Git branch names |
| Engineering | Full technical detail | - |

### Cadence table

| Forum | Frequency | Format |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #product-mobile | Weekly | Health template |
| Sprint review | Biweekly | Demo on device + burndown |
| Incident channel | Per event | Impact-first template |
| Quarterly | Once | Debt + upgrade portfolio |

### Anti-patterns

| Anti-pattern | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| "Works on my machine" | Preview build QR in every UI update |
| Silent slip until demo day | Yellow flag when estimate range exceeded mid-sprint |
| Stack trace in #general | Link incident doc; plain language in channel |
| "QA will sign off" | Named QA status + device matrix |
| Undefined "soon" | Replace with date **range** |

---

## FAQs

How technical should weekly updates be?

Lead with business metrics (crash-free, rollout %, dates). Technical detail in linked doc or thread reply - interested engineers drill down; PMs stay oriented.

What crash-free target should we cite?

Common mobile SaaS target: **≥99.5%** crash-free sessions. Adjust per industry; state your target consistently so week-over-week comparisons matter.

How to communicate OTA vs store fix during incident?

"**OTA tonight**" means JS-only, users may need app restart. "**Store build**" means days minimum. Say which path and why - stakeholders often assume instant App Store updates.

PM wants daily ETA on in-review build?

Share **store console status** daily with same template; explain Apple does not expose precise review clocks. Ranges only - "approved between Wed–Fri."

How to push back on scope without sounding negative?

Trade-off memo with three options and a recommendation. "Yes, and here is what we defer" beats "no."

Dokumen: Working with Design & Motion
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/product-collaboration/working-with-design-and-motion/

# Working with Design & Motion

A cookbook for **feasibility reviews before pixels are final** - how Expo SDK 57 engineers and designers align on motion, gestures, and layout constraints without killing craft or missing sprint dates.

Highlights / Working with Design & Motion

* Feasibility review at wireframe saves more time than redesign at hi-fi
* Every motion spec needs: trigger, duration, easing, interrupt rule, and reduced-motion fallback
* Reanimated 4 for gesture-linked frames; Animated API for simple fades - decide before Figma lock
* Prototype on device in 30 minutes beats a week of pixel debate
* Design tokens constrain motion values - spring configs live in the system
* Say 'fallback pattern' in refinement - stakeholders accept phased delight

## Recipe

> Pre-hi-fi feasibility session card - 30 minutes, three attendees.

```markdown
## Motion feasibility - <screen name>
**Attendees:** Designer, engineer, PM (optional)
**Inputs:** Wireframe or lo-fi + interaction notes (not final pixels)
**Devices:** iPhone 16 sim + Pixel 6a or 8 (low-end Android mandatory for motion)
 
### Agenda (30 min)
1. Walk user path - 5 min
2. List interactions - scroll, swipe, shared element, keyboard - 5 min
3. Classify each: Static | Animated API | Reanimated | Native - 10 min
4. Flag spikes + fallbacks - 5 min
5. Write ticket notes + record 20s device clip - 5 min
```

```bash
# Engineer prep - have Reanimated starter running
npx expo install react-native-reanimated react-native-gesture-handler
npx expo start
# Open Performance monitor on Android: shake → Show Perf Monitor
```

**When to reach for this:**

* New onboarding with stepped transitions
* List row actions (swipe, drag-to-reorder)
* Hero / shared-element transitions
* Bottom sheet with nested scroll
* Marketing asks for "like Instagram" interactions

---

## Working Example

### Interaction classification matrix

Fill this in the session - paste into Jira/Linear:

| Interaction | Design intent | RN approach | Risk | Fallback |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Screen enter | Fade + slide up 250ms | `Animated` + `useNativeDriver` | Low | Instant navigate |
| Pull hero shrink | Collapsing header on scroll | Reanimated `useAnimatedScrollHandler` | Med Android FPS | Static header |
| Card → detail | Shared element transition | Reanimated shared transition | Med - router config | Cross-fade |
| Swipe row delete | iOS Mail pattern | Gesture Handler + Reanimated | High scroll conflict | Long-press menu |
| Skeleton shimmer | Loading placeholder | Reanimated loop or static gray | Low battery | Static skeleton |

* **Static** = no animation budget; ship first
* Link spikes to [Gesture Conflict Resolution](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/gesture-conflict-resolution/) when Risk = High

### Motion spec template for designers

```markdown
## Motion spec: Checkout success
**Trigger:** Payment API returns 200
**Enter:** Checkmark scale 0→1, spring (damping 15, stiffness 150), 400ms perceived
**Exit:** Auto-advance to receipt at 1200ms or tap Continue
**Interrupt:** Back gesture cancels animation → show receipt immediately
**Reduced motion:** Skip scale; show checkmark static + haptic only
**Haptic:** success notification (iOS); short vibrate (Android)
**Reference:** Not Lottie - vector draw in SVG or icon
```

Engineers map spring values to Reanimated `withSpring` - store presets in design system:

```tsx
// theme/motion.ts
export const motion = {
  springSnappy: { damping: 18, stiffness: 220 },
  springGentle: { damping: 22, stiffness: 120 },
  durationFast: 200,
  durationNormal: 300,
} as const;
```

Align with [Design Systems Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/design-systems-basics/) - motion tokens beside color tokens.

### 30-minute spike script

```tsx
// spikes/SwipeRowSpike.tsx - throwaway; answers GO / NO-GO
import Animated, { useAnimatedStyle, useSharedValue, withSpring } from "react-native-reanimated";
import { Gesture, GestureDetector } from "react-native-gesture-handler";
 
export function SwipeRowSpike() {
  const translateX = useSharedValue(0);
  const pan = Gesture.Pan()
    .activeOffsetX([-10, 10])
    .onUpdate((e) => { translateX.value = e.translationX; })
    .onEnd(() => { translateX.value = withSpring(0); });
 
  const style = useAnimatedStyle(() => ({ transform: [{ translateX: translateX.value }] }));
 
  return (
    <GestureDetector gesture={pan}>
      <Animated.View style={[{ height: 56, backgroundColor: "#eee" }, style]} />
    </GestureDetector>
  );
}
```

**Done when:**

* Screen recording attached: iOS + Android, FPS visible on Android
* Written verdict: **GO** (estimate range) | **SIMPLIFY** (fallback) | **SPIKE MORE** (time box +2h)
* PM acknowledges fallback in acceptance criteria

### Feasibility red flags (call out early)

| Red flag in Figma | Mobile reality |
| --- | --- |
| Parallax on every scroll screen | GPU + scroll thread contention |
| Blur behind sheets everywhere | `expo-blur` costly on old Android |
| Physics-based multi-card stack | Gesture conflicts + state complexity |
| Hover states | No hover - need pressed/focused |
| Video background autoplay | Battery + data; often needs native player |
| Custom cursor / drag handles | Touch targets and hitSlop differ |

Offer **ranked alternatives** - same pattern as [Product Collaboration Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/product-collaboration/product-collaboration-basics/).

### Reduced motion and accessibility

```tsx
import { useReducedMotion } from "react-native-reanimated";
 
export function useMotionPolicy() {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion();
  return {
    shouldAnimate: !reduced,
    enterDuration: reduced ? 0 : 300,
  };
}
```

* Design delivers **reduced-motion frame** alongside default - not engineer afterthought
* `AccessibilityInfo.isReduceMotionEnabled` on older paths if needed
* PM: reduced motion is not edge case - iOS Settings → Motion → Reduce Motion

### Review checklist before hi-fi lock

```markdown
## Hi-fi lock gate
- [ ] Safe areas on smallest phone frame
- [ ] Keyboard states documented
- [ ] Motion spec per non-static transition
- [ ] Reduced-motion variant approved
- [ ] Loading / empty / error frames exist
- [ ] Tokens used - no orphan hex values ([Design Systems](../design-systems/design-systems-basics.md))
- [ ] Engineer comment: no unresolved HIGH risk without spike ticket
- [ ] 20s device clip or preview QR attached
```

PM does not accept hi-fi lock without checklist - prevents "surprise" estimates.

### Collaborating with design system team

| Request | DS response |
| --- | --- |
| New button bounce | Add `motionPreset` to `PrimaryButton` |
| One-off marketing animation | Isolate in `campaign/` folder - not core DS |
| Shared element between catalog and detail | Document router config in DS motion ADR |

Prevents N custom animations in feature folders - see [Building an Internal Component Library](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/design-systems/building-an-internal-component-library/).

---

## Deep Dive

### When to insist on Reanimated 4

| Signal | Tool |
| --- | --- |
| Animation tied to scroll position | Reanimated |
| Gesture drives animation frame-by-frame | Reanimated + Gesture Handler |
| Simple opacity on mount | `Animated` |
| Layout enter/exit for list items | Reanimated Layout Animations |
| Keyboard height interpolation | Reanimated or `KeyboardAvoidingView` |

Full comparison: [Animations Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/animations-basics/) and [Reanimated 4](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/animations-gestures/react-native-reanimated-4/).

### Phased delivery language

```markdown
## Phased motion plan
**v1 (sprint N):** Static transitions, correct layout, haptics on success
**v1.1 (sprint N+1):** Swipe actions if spike GO
**v2:** Shared element - depends on Router upgrade
```

Stakeholders accept **phased delight** when labeled product strategy - not "cut scope" shame.

### Anti-patterns

| Anti-pattern | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| Motion review after hi-fi sign-off | Wireframe feasibility session |
| "Match iOS exactly on Android" | Platform parity doc per interaction |
| Lottie for simple fades | Vector + Reanimated - smaller bundle |
| No FPS check on Pixel A-series | Mandatory low-end Android in matrix |
| Designer-only prototype in Principle | RN spike - physics differ |

---

## FAQs

Who owns the motion spec - design or engineering?

Design owns intent (timing, feel, interrupt); engineering owns implementation map and fallbacks. Joint sign-off on feasibility doc.

How long should spikes take?

30 minutes to 0.5 day for motion/gesture questions. Stop with GO/NO-GO written verdict - no infinite polish on throwaway code.

Can we use Lottie for everything?

Lottie fits illustrated loaders and brand moments. Interaction-heavy UI (drags, scroll-linked) needs Reanimated - Lottie is not a gesture engine.

What if design insists on non-performant animation?

Show FPS recording on Pixel 6a. Trade-off memo: ship animation vs ship feature on time vs simplify. PM decides with data.

Do we need motion in the design system?

Yes for repeated patterns (button press, sheet enter, list skeleton). Campaign one-offs stay outside core tokens.

Dokumen: Project Setup Best Practices
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/best-practices/

# Project Setup Best Practices

A condensed summary of the 25 most important best practices drawn from every page in this section.

Highlights / Project Setup Best Practices

* Pin Expo SDK at scaffold with default@sdk-57 and verify with expo-doctor
* Keep app routes thin; put features under features/<name>/
* One react-native copy in monorepos - duplicate native deps crash at runtime
* Prefer SDK 57 auto Metro config before hand-tuning watchFolders
* Commit lockfiles; never commit ios/ and android/ under CNG
* White-label with app.config env variants, not forked feature code

1. **Scaffold with an SDK template pin:** `npx create-expo-app@latest --template default@sdk-57` - upgrading later costs more than starting on the supported SDK.
2. **Run expo-doctor on day one:** Fix version skew before the first feature PR - doctor catches config and dependency mismatches early.
3. **Commit lockfiles with the app:** CI and EAS must resolve the same tree as local dev - floating installs hide native/JS skew until TestFlight.
4. **Keep package.json scripts boring:** `start`, `ios`, `android`, `lint`, `typecheck` - every engineer should not memorize one-off Metro flags.
5. **Extend expo/tsconfig.base:** Strict TypeScript from the template - custom tsconfig drift breaks Expo Router typed routes and autolinking types.
6. **Use app.config.ts for environments:** Dynamic config beats duplicated `app.json` files - drive variants with `APP_VARIANT` or `BRAND` env vars.
7. **Pick the smallest template that fits:** `blank-typescript` for learning; `tabs` only when navigation is day-one scope - delete unused boilerplate immediately.
8. **Organize by feature, not layer-only:** `features/orders/` owns screens, hooks, and presenters - global `components/` is for design-system primitives only.
9. **One public export per feature:** Route files import `OrdersScreen` from `features/orders` - no cross-feature deep imports into `hooks/useOrder.ts`.
10. **Thin app/ directory:** Expo Router files re-export feature screens - business logic does not live beside `_layout.tsx`.
11. **Start monorepos with pnpm + Turborepo when sharing UI:** `apps/mobile` + `packages/ui` with `workspace:*` - add Nx when generators and affected graphs justify the complexity.
12. **Let SDK 57 configure Metro first:** Automatic monorepo detection beats hand-written `watchFolders` - customize only when doctor and builds prove a gap.
13. **Hoist or isolate pnpm symlinks consciously:** `nodeLinker: hoisted` avoids many Metro symlink bugs - document the choice in README for onboarding.
14. **Never duplicate react-native in the graph:** Two native copies cause "Invalid hook call" and obscure redboxes - `npx expo-doctor` and `why react-native` checks in CI.
15. **Declare peerDependencies in shared packages:** Workspace libraries should peer `react`, `react-native`, and `expo` - apps provide the single installed version.
16. **Use Nx tags for boundaries:** `scope:orders` cannot import `scope:billing` internals - enforce with `@nx/enforce-module-boundaries` in growing orgs.
17. **Run affected tasks in CI:** `nx affected -t lint,typecheck,test` keeps monorepo PRs fast - full-repo runs do not scale past a dozen packages.
18. **White-label with config, not forks:** `apps/acme` and `apps/globex` share `packages/core` - brand tokens inject via `BrandProvider`, not copy-paste screens.
19. **Separate EAS projectId per app binary:** White-label flavors need distinct credentials, env vars, and update channels - one projectId per bundle ID.
20. **Gitignore native folders under CNG:** Committed `ios/`/`android/` block SDK upgrades - regenerate on EAS Build or `expo prebuild --clean`.
21. **Document first-run verification:** A script that runs `expo-doctor`, `tsc --noEmit`, and a dev-client build - new hires prove the toolchain in one command.
22. **Ignore `.env.local`, commit `.env.example`:** Machine-specific secrets stay local - example env documents required `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` keys without values.
23. **Align Babel and Metro with the template:** Custom plugins belong in documented config - silent Babel drift breaks Fast Refresh and Reanimated.
24. **Choose Turborepo or Nx, not both orchestrators:** One task graph owner - mixing confuses `dev` scripts and cache keys.
25. **Revisit folder structure at ~15 engineers:** Layer-only layouts collapse under parallel feature teams - schedule a migration before import cycles force a rewrite.

## FAQs

When should we adopt a monorepo?

* When two or more apps or a shared UI package ships from the same team.
* Single-app teams should stay single-repo until duplication pain is measurable.

Turborepo or Nx for Expo?

* Turborepo for simpler caching and pnpm workspaces.
* Nx when you need generators, boundary enforcement, and affected graphs at scale.

Can multiple Expo apps share one node\_modules?

* Yes at the workspace root with pnpm - each app still needs its own `app.config` and EAS project.
* Metro must resolve one `react-native` instance.

## Related

* [Project Setup Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/project-setup-basics/) - layout, scripts, and first-run verification
* [create-expo-app Templates](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/create-expo-app-templates/) - picking the right starter
* [Folder Structure for Features](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/folder-structure-for-features/) - feature slices vs layers
* [Monorepo with Turborepo](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/monorepo-with-turborepo/) - shared packages and caching
* [Shared Packages & Metro Resolution](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/shared-packages-and-metro-resolution/) - watchFolders and symlinks

Dokumen: create-expo-app Templates
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/create-expo-app-templates/

# create-expo-app Templates

`create-expo-app` ships five first-party templates - each pins Expo SDK 57 when you pass `@sdk-57`. Picking the wrong starter costs days of migration; this page maps each template to the product shape it fits.

Highlights / create-expo-app Templates

* default@sdk-57 is the team default - Expo Router, TypeScript, and recommended scripts
* tabs@sdk-57 and default@sdk-57 are interchangeable for most apps - pick one and standardize
* blank-typescript@sdk-57 is for spikes and brownfield experiments without navigation wired
* bare-minimum@sdk-57 runs prebuild immediately - only when you need android/ and ios/ on day one
* Always suffix templates with @sdk-57 during the SDK transition - bare @latest may scaffold SDK 54

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
# Team default - multi-screen app with Expo Router + TypeScript
npx create-expo-app@latest ShopApp --template default@sdk-57 --yes
 
# Tab-first navigation starter (similar scope to default)
npx create-expo-app@latest ShopApp --template tabs@sdk-57 --yes
 
# Minimal spike - no router, TypeScript enabled
npx create-expo-app@latest Spike --template blank-typescript@sdk-57 --yes
 
# Native dirs on day one - runs prebuild during scaffold
npx create-expo-app@latest NativeDay1 --template bare-minimum@sdk-57 --yes
 
cd ShopApp && npx expo-doctor
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Choosing a starter before the first production commit - template swaps are painful once navigation and native dirs grow roots.
* Standardizing template choice across squads so every new repo boots the same scripts and folder layout.
* Deciding whether you need `bare-minimum` now or can stay managed and run `npx expo prebuild` later.
* Auditing an accidental SDK 54 scaffold - compare `package.json` against the template you intended.

## Working Example

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/new-expo-app.sh - org template picker with SDK 57 verification
set -euo pipefail
 
APP_NAME="${1:?Usage: ./new-expo-app.sh <AppName> [default|tabs|blank-typescript|bare-minimum]}"
KIND="${2:-default}"
 
case "$KIND" in
  default|tabs|blank-typescript|bare-minimum) TEMPLATE="${KIND}@sdk-57" ;;
  *) echo "Unknown template: $KIND" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac
 
npx create-expo-app@latest "$APP_NAME" --template "$TEMPLATE" --yes
cd "$APP_NAME"
 
# Fail fast if the scaffold drifted from SDK 57
EXPO_VER="$(node -p "require('./package.json').dependencies.expo")"
RN_VER="$(node -p "require('./package.json').dependencies['react-native']")"
test "$EXPO_VER" = "~57.0.4" || { echo "Expected expo ~57.0.4, got $EXPO_VER" >&2; exit 1; }
test "$RN_VER" = "0.86.0" || { echo "Expected react-native 0.86.0, got $RN_VER" >&2; exit 1; }
 
npx expo-doctor
npx tsc --noEmit
 
echo "✅ $APP_NAME scaffolded with $TEMPLATE"
```

After `default@sdk-57`, expect this layout:

```text
ShopApp/
├── app/
│   ├── _layout.tsx          # Expo Router root layout
│   ├── (tabs)/
│   │   ├── _layout.tsx      # Tab navigator
│   │   ├── index.tsx
│   │   └── explore.tsx
│   └── +not-found.tsx
├── assets/
├── app.json
├── package.json             # expo ~57.0.4, react-native 0.86.0, react 19.2.3
└── tsconfig.json
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* A single script encodes org policy - engineers pass `default`, `tabs`, `blank-typescript`, or `bare-minimum`; the `@sdk-57` suffix is never optional.
* Post-scaffold version assertions catch SDK drift before feature work starts.
* `expo-doctor` and `tsc --noEmit` as mandatory gates after every template choice.
* `default@sdk-57` ships file-based routing under `app/` - the layout you extend for production navigation.

## Deep Dive

### How It Works

* **`create-expo-app`** copies a versioned template from the Expo monorepo, writes `package.json`, installs dependencies, and generates starter source.
* The **`@sdk-57` suffix** pins the template's dependency graph - `expo` resolves to `~57.0.4` with matching `react-native` `0.86.0` and `react` `19.2.3`.
* **`default` and `tabs`** both enable Expo Router and TypeScript; they differ in starter navigation structure, not SDK capabilities.
* **`blank` / `blank-typescript`** ship a single `App.tsx` entry - no `app/` directory, no router - you add navigation manually.
* **`bare-minimum`** runs `npx expo prebuild` during setup, generating `android/` and `ios/` immediately.

### Template Comparison

| Template | Navigation | TypeScript | Native dirs (`android/`, `ios/`) | Best for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `default@sdk-57` | Expo Router, tab/stack starter | Yes | No (managed / CNG) | **Most production apps** - team default |
| `tabs@sdk-57` | Expo Router, tab layout emphasized | Yes | No | Apps where tab IA is decided day one |
| `blank@sdk-57` | None - single `App.js` | No | No | JS-only spikes, teaching RN primitives |
| `blank-typescript@sdk-57` | None - single `App.tsx` | Yes | No | Typed spikes, library experiments, brownfield probes |
| `bare-minimum@sdk-57` | None - single `App.tsx` | Yes | **Yes** (prebuild runs) | Custom native code or CI that compiles native on day one |

```bash
# Side-by-side comparison - scaffold into /tmp, inspect, delete
npx create-expo-app@latest /tmp/compare-default --template default@sdk-57 --yes
npx create-expo-app@latest /tmp/compare-blank --template blank-typescript@sdk-57 --yes
ls /tmp/compare-default/app        # Router present
ls /tmp/compare-blank/app 2>/dev/null || echo "blank: no app/ directory"
```

### Decision Flow

| Your situation | Template |
| --- | --- |
| New product app with multiple screens | `default@sdk-57` |
| Tab bar is the primary IA from sprint one | `tabs@sdk-57` (or `default` - nearly equivalent) |
| Prototype one screen, no navigation yet | `blank-typescript@sdk-57` |
| Embed RN inside existing native shell | `blank-typescript@sdk-57` or brownfield flow - not `bare-minimum` by default |
| Need `android/` and `ios/` committed immediately | `bare-minimum@sdk-57` |
| Physical device testing with stock Expo Go only | SDK 54 project (Expo Go constraint) - not SDK 57 templates |

### What Each Template Omits

| Template | You add later |
| --- | --- |
| `default` / `tabs` | State management, API client, feature folders under `src/features/` |
| `blank-typescript` | Expo Router (`npx expo install expo-router` + `app/` directory) or React Navigation |
| `bare-minimum` | Navigation, managed-workflow simplicity - you own native project maintenance |

### TypeScript Notes

```tsx
// blank-typescript@sdk-57 entry - no Router, single root component
import { StatusBar } from "expo-status-bar";
import { StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
export default function App() {
  return (
    <View style={styles.container}>
      <Text>Blank TypeScript starter on SDK 57.</Text>
      <StatusBar style="auto" />
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  container: { flex: 1, alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "center" },
});
```

```tsx
// default@sdk-57 - route files live under app/, not App.tsx
// app/(tabs)/index.tsx
import { StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
export default function HomeScreen() {
  return (
    <View style={styles.container}>
      <Text>Home tab - Expo Router file route.</Text>
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  container: { flex: 1, alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "center" },
});
```

Prefer `default@sdk-57` when the app will have more than one screen - retrofitting Expo Router into `blank-typescript` is doable but wastes the first sprint.

## Gotchas

* **Scaffolding without `@sdk-57`** - During the SDK 57 transition, bare `create-expo-app@latest` may create SDK 54 for Expo Go on physical devices. **Fix:** Pass `--template default@sdk-57` (or your chosen template with the suffix) for new production work.
* **Treating `tabs` and `default` as fundamentally different** - Both ship Expo Router and TypeScript with similar file counts. Teams waste time debating them. **Fix:** Pick one org-wide; the difference is starter layout, not capability.
* **Choosing `bare-minimum` for "just in case"** - Prebuild commits `android/` and `ios/`, increasing merge conflict surface and slowing managed upgrades. **Fix:** Start `default@sdk-57`; run `npx expo prebuild` when native dirs are actually required.
* **Staying on `blank` when the app grows past one screen** - Engineers bolt React Navigation into `App.tsx` and end up with a non-standard tree. **Fix:** Migrate to Expo Router early or start with `default@sdk-57`.
* **Assuming templates include state management or API layers** - No template ships Redux, TanStack Query, or feature folders. **Fix:** Add architecture after scaffold; see [Folder Structure for Features](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/folder-structure-for-features/).
* **Mixing template entry styles** - `default` uses `app/_layout.tsx`; `blank-typescript` uses `App.tsx`. Copy-pasting route code between them without restructuring fails. **Fix:** Match imports and entry points to the template you chose.
* **Skipping `expo-doctor` after template selection** - Template metadata can resolve incompatible native module peers. **Fix:** Run `npx expo-doctor` before the first feature PR.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default@sdk-57` | Standard multi-screen Expo apps | You need only a single-screen spike (`blank-typescript`) |
| `tabs@sdk-57` | Tab IA is fixed from day one | You want the general-purpose starter name (`default`) |
| `blank-typescript@sdk-57` | Minimal surface, no router yet | Production app with multiple screens |
| `bare-minimum@sdk-57` | Native directories required immediately | Managed workflow with CNG is acceptable |
| `--example` from `expo/examples` | Learning a specific integration (Router, SQLite) | Production scaffold - examples are demos, not maintained product templates |
| Internal template repo (fork of `default@sdk-57`) | Org-wide lint, CI, and design tokens baked in | One-off prototypes where official templates are faster |

## FAQs

What templates does create-expo-app ship?

Five first-party templates: `default`, `tabs`, `blank`, `blank-typescript`, and `bare-minimum`. Append `@sdk-57` to pin Expo SDK 57 at scaffold time.

Which template should most teams pick?

`default@sdk-57`. It includes Expo Router, TypeScript, and the recommended Expo CLI scripts. Use `blank-typescript@sdk-57` for minimal spikes and `bare-minimum@sdk-57` only when you need native directories immediately.

What is the difference between default and tabs?

Both target multi-screen apps with Expo Router and TypeScript. `default` is the general-purpose starter; `tabs` emphasizes tab navigation structure in the generated `app/` tree. For most teams they are interchangeable - standardize on one.

When should I choose blank-typescript?

When you need a typed minimal app without navigation wired - library spikes, RN learning exercises, or brownfield experiments. Add Expo Router or React Navigation when screens multiply.

When should I choose bare-minimum?

When you need `android/` and `ios/` directories on day one - custom native modules, existing native CI, or brownfield integration that cannot wait for a later `prebuild`. Otherwise start managed with `default@sdk-57`.

Why must I use @sdk-57 in the template name?

During the SDK 57 transition, `create-expo-app@latest` without `--template` may scaffold SDK 54 for Expo Go compatibility on physical devices. Production work targeting RN 0.86 should pass `@sdk-57` explicitly.

How do I verify the template pinned SDK 57?

```bash
node -p "require('./package.json').dependencies.expo"
node -p "require('./package.json').dependencies['react-native']"
npx expo-doctor
```

Expect `~57.0.4` and `0.86.0`.

Does default include TypeScript?

Yes. `default@sdk-57` and `tabs@sdk-57` ship TypeScript, `tsconfig.json`, and typed route files under `app/`. Use `blank@sdk-57` only when you explicitly want JavaScript without types.

Can I switch templates after scaffolding?

There is no automatic migration. Moving from `blank-typescript` to Expo Router means adding `app/`, dependencies, and config. Moving from managed to `bare-minimum` means running `prebuild` and committing native dirs. Pick the right template early.

What files does bare-minimum add?

`android/` and `ios/` directories generated by `npx expo prebuild` during setup, plus the same minimal `App.tsx` entry as `blank-typescript`. You maintain native projects from commit one.

Should I use --example instead of --template?

`--example` pulls demos from `expo/examples` - great for learning integrations. For production apps, use `default@sdk-57` or your org fork so upgrades track the maintained template.

Gotcha: why does my tabs template look like default?

They share the same SDK, Router, and TypeScript stack. The generated `app/` file names and tab layout differ slightly. Functionally they solve the same problem - do not re-scaffold to switch between them.

Do templates include testing or CI setup?

No. Templates ship app source, `app.json`, and Expo scripts. Add Jest, Maestro, EAS, and lint configs after scaffold - or use an internal template repo that extends `default@sdk-57`.

Can I scaffold into a monorepo subdirectory?

Yes:

```bash
npx create-expo-app@latest apps/mobile --template default@sdk-57 --yes
```

Install from the monorepo root afterward. See [Monorepo with Turborepo](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/monorepo-with-turborepo/).

What is the relationship between templates and Expo Go?

SDK 57 templates target RN 0.86. Physical iOS devices can only install the latest Expo Go from the App Store, which may lag SDK 57. Use a simulator, a matching Expo Go build from expo.dev/go, or a development build - not an older template SDK - for device testing.

## Related

* [Project Setup Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/project-setup-basics/) - standard app layout, scripts, and first-run verification after scaffold
* [create-expo-app Quickstart](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-platform/create-expo-app-quickstart/) - full scaffold workflow, flags, and SDK pin checklist
* [Folder Structure for Features](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/folder-structure-for-features/) - where feature code lives after you pick a template
* [Monorepo with Turborepo](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/monorepo-with-turborepo/) - scaffold `apps/mobile` with `default@sdk-57` inside a workspace

> **Stack versions:** This page was written for **React 19.2.3**, **React Native 0.86.0**, and **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4).

Dokumen: Folder Structure for Features
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/folder-structure-for-features/

# Folder Structure for Features

Feature slices group everything a product area needs in one directory; layer folders (`components/`, `hooks/`, `screens/` at the repo root) scatter related code across the tree. The split you pick on day one determines how painful the first 50 features feel.

Highlights / Folder Structure for Features

* Feature slices colocate screens, hooks, and components per product area - layers split by file type across the repo
* Keep app/ routes thin - import FeatureScreen from features/ and render it
* index.ts is each feature's public API - other features import from there, not deep paths
* Shared primitives live in components/ui/ - product-specific UI stays inside the feature folder
* Switch from layers to slices when cross-feature imports and god screens outnumber isolated changes

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```text
src/
├── components/
│   └── ui/                  # shared primitives (Button, Screen, TextField)
├── lib/                     # api client, storage, analytics helpers
├── features/
│   └── orders/
│       ├── index.ts         # public exports only
│       ├── screens/
│       │   └── OrdersScreen.tsx
│       ├── components/
│       │   └── OrderRow.tsx
│       ├── hooks/
│       │   └── useOrders.ts
│       └── types.ts
└── types/                   # truly global types (User, Session)
 
app/
└── (tabs)/
    └── orders/
        └── index.tsx        # export { OrdersScreen as default } from "@/features/orders"
```

```ts
// src/features/orders/index.ts
export { OrdersScreen } from "./screens/OrdersScreen";
export type { Order } from "./types";
```

```tsx
// app/(tabs)/orders/index.tsx - route stays one line when possible
export { OrdersScreen as default } from "@/features/orders";
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Onboarding engineers to a feature ("everything for Orders lives under `features/orders/`").
* Preventing god screens that import hooks from six unrelated folders.
* Drawing import boundaries so `features/inbox` never reaches into `features/orders/components/OrderRow.tsx`.
* Deciding whether a new screen belongs in a layer folder or a feature slice.

## Working Example

```tsx
// src/features/orders/types.ts
export type OrderStatus = "pending" | "shipped" | "delivered";
 
export type Order = {
  id: string;
  title: string;
  totalCents: number;
  status: OrderStatus;
};
```

```tsx
// src/features/orders/hooks/useOrders.ts
import { useCallback, useEffect, useState } from "react";
import type { Order } from "../types";
 
export function useOrders() {
  const [orders, setOrders] = useState<Order[]>([]);
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true);
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);
 
  const refresh = useCallback(async () => {
    try {
      setError(null);
      const response = await fetch("https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/todos?_limit=6");
      if (!response.ok) throw new Error("Failed to load orders");
      const data = (await response.json()) as Array<{ id: number; title: string; completed: boolean }>;
      setOrders(
        data.map((row) => ({
          id: String(row.id),
          title: row.title,
          totalCents: 1999,
          status: row.completed ? "delivered" : "pending",
        }))
      );
    } catch (e) {
      setError(e instanceof Error ? e.message : "Unknown error");
    } finally {
      setLoading(false);
    }
  }, []);
 
  useEffect(() => {
    refresh();
  }, [refresh]);
 
  return { orders, loading, error, refresh };
}
```

```tsx
// src/features/orders/components/OrderRow.tsx
import { Pressable, StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
import type { Order } from "../types";
 
type Props = {
  order: Order;
  onPress: (id: string) => void;
};
 
export function OrderRow({ order, onPress }: Props) {
  return (
    <Pressable style={styles.row} onPress={() => onPress(order.id)} accessibilityRole="button">
      <View style={styles.textBlock}>
        <Text style={styles.title} numberOfLines={1}>
          {order.title}
        </Text>
        <Text style={styles.meta}>
          ${(order.totalCents / 100).toFixed(2)} · {order.status}
        </Text>
      </View>
    </Pressable>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  row: { paddingVertical: 12, paddingHorizontal: 16 },
  textBlock: { gap: 4 },
  title: { fontSize: 16, fontWeight: "600", color: "#0f172a" },
  meta: { fontSize: 13, color: "#64748b" },
});
```

```tsx
// src/features/orders/screens/OrdersScreen.tsx
import { ActivityIndicator, FlatList, RefreshControl, StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
import { OrderRow } from "../components/OrderRow";
import { useOrders } from "../hooks/useOrders";
 
export function OrdersScreen() {
  const { orders, loading, error, refresh } = useOrders();
 
  if (loading && orders.length === 0) {
    return <ActivityIndicator style={styles.centered} />;
  }
 
  if (error) {
    return (
      <View style={styles.centered}>
        <Text style={styles.error}>{error}</Text>
      </View>
    );
  }
 
  return (
    <FlatList
      data={orders}
      keyExtractor={(item) => item.id}
      renderItem={({ item }) => <OrderRow order={item} onPress={() => {}} />}
      refreshControl={<RefreshControl refreshing={loading} onRefresh={refresh} />}
      contentContainerStyle={styles.list}
    />
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  centered: { flex: 1, justifyContent: "center", alignItems: "center" },
  list: { paddingVertical: 8 },
  error: { color: "#b91c1c", padding: 24, textAlign: "center" },
});
```

```ts
// tsconfig.json paths (Expo default template includes @/* → project root or src)
// "paths": { "@/*": ["./src/*"] }
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* **`features/orders/`** owns types, hooks, components, and the screen - a new engineer opens one folder to understand Orders.
* **`OrderRow`** is presentational; **`useOrders`** owns async work - the screen orchestrates, it does not fetch inline.
* **`index.ts`** exports only `OrdersScreen` and `Order` - internals stay private.
* **`app/(tabs)/orders/index.tsx`** re-exports the screen - Expo Router owns URLs; features own implementation.

## Deep Dive

### How It Works

* **Feature slices (vertical)** organize by product capability - `features/orders`, `features/inbox`. Changes to Orders touch files under one subtree.
* **Layers (horizontal)** organize by technical role - global `components/`, `hooks/`, `screens/`. Every feature sprinkles files across multiple top-level folders.
* **Expo Router `app/`** maps URLs to screens. Route files should stay thin entry points; heavy logic lives in `features/`.
* **`index.ts` public APIs** enforce import boundaries - cross-feature imports use `@/features/orders`, never `@/features/orders/components/OrderRow`.
* **Shared `components/ui/`** holds design-system primitives used by many features; feature `components/` holds product-specific composition.

### Feature Slice vs Layer Layout

| Approach | Structure | Strength | Weakness |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Feature slice** | `features/orders/{screens,hooks,components}` | Onboarding, refactors, and PRs stay local | Risk of duplicating similar list rows across features |
| **Layered** | `screens/`, `hooks/`, `components/` at root | Familiar to web devs; easy to find "all hooks" | Cross-folder imports explode; god screens emerge |
| **Hybrid (recommended)** | `components/ui/` + `features/*` + thin `app/` | Shared primitives without a global component graveyard | Requires discipline on `index.ts` exports |

```text
# Layered - fine for < 5 screens, painful at scale
src/
├── components/       # every feature's rows, cards, modals mixed together
├── hooks/
├── screens/
└── services/
 
# Feature slice - scales with team and feature count
src/
├── components/ui/
├── lib/
└── features/
    ├── orders/
    ├── inbox/
    └── settings/
```

### Import Rules

| Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- |
| Route files import from `@/features/<name>` only | Keeps navigation decoupled from feature internals |
| Features import other features via their `index.ts` | Prevents deep-path coupling |
| Never import sibling feature `components/` directly | OrderRow is not a shared primitive - duplicate or promote to `ui/` |
| `lib/` and `components/ui/` are the shared layer | Cross-cutting utilities and design tokens live here |

```ts
// ✅ Cross-feature import through public API
import type { Order } from "@/features/orders";
 
// ❌ Reaching into another feature's internals
import { OrderRow } from "@/features/orders/components/OrderRow";
```

### When to Migrate Layers → Slices

| Signal | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Screen files exceed ~200 lines of orchestration | Extract to `features/<name>/` with container/presenter split |
| PRs routinely touch 4+ top-level folders for one feature | Create a feature folder and move related files |
| `components/` has dozens of single-use wrappers | Move product-specific components into feature folders |
| Onboarding doc says "search the repo for Orders" | Colocate Orders under `features/orders/` |

Migrate one feature at a time - start with the noisiest god screen, not a big-bang rewrite.

### TypeScript Notes

```tsx
// src/components/ui/Screen.tsx - shared primitive, no feature imports
import type { ReactNode } from "react";
import { StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
type ScreenProps = {
  title: string;
  children: ReactNode;
};
 
export function Screen({ title, children }: ScreenProps) {
  return (
    <View style={styles.root}>
      <Text style={styles.title}>{title}</Text>
      <View style={styles.body}>{children}</View>
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  root: { flex: 1, padding: 16, gap: 12, backgroundColor: "#fff" },
  title: { fontSize: 24, fontWeight: "700" },
  body: { flex: 1, gap: 8 },
});
```

```tsx
// features/settings/screens/SettingsScreen.tsx - feature screen uses shared primitive
import { Screen } from "@/components/ui/Screen";
import { Text } from "react-native";
 
export function SettingsScreen() {
  return (
    <Screen title="Settings">
      <Text>Notifications, account, and privacy live here.</Text>
    </Screen>
  );
}
```

Keep `components/ui/` free of feature imports. If `Screen` needs feature data, pass it as props - do not import from `features/`.

## Gotchas

* **Global `components/` graveyard** - Every one-off card lands in `components/` because it is "reusable someday." **Fix:** Default to `features/<name>/components/`; promote to `ui/` only after the second consumer exists.
* **Fat route files in `app/`** - Business logic, fetch calls, and modals live in `app/(tabs)/orders/index.tsx`. **Fix:** Re-export from `features/orders`; keep routes under ~5 lines.
* **Deep imports across features** - `features/inbox` imports `features/orders/components/OrderRow`. **Fix:** Import types from `@/features/orders`; duplicate small presentational rows or extract shared UI to `components/ui/`.
* **No `index.ts` public API** - Fifty files per feature with no export boundary; everything is public. **Fix:** Export only screens and shared types from `index.ts`; treat other paths as private.
* **Layer folders plus feature folders** - `screens/OrdersScreen.tsx` and `features/orders/screens/OrdersScreen.tsx` both exist. **Fix:** Pick one scheme per app; hybrid confusion doubles search cost.
* **Shared hooks in the wrong layer** - `useOrders` in global `hooks/` but only Orders uses it. **Fix:** Colocate single-feature hooks under `features/orders/hooks/`; reserve global `hooks/` for truly shared behavior (`useAppTheme`).
* **Monorepo packages without feature boundaries** - Shared `@repo/ui` grows feature-specific props. **Fix:** Keep product features in the app; packages hold primitives only. See [Shared Packages & Metro Resolution](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/shared-packages-and-metro-resolution/).

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Feature slices (`features/*`) | Growing apps, multiple squads, frequent feature work | Single-screen spike - folder overhead not worth it |
| Layered (`components/`, `hooks/`, `screens/`) | Tiny apps with < 5 screens and one engineer | Cross-feature imports and god screens are already common |
| Domain packages in a monorepo (`packages/orders`) | Multiple apps share entire feature modules | One app - in-repo slices are simpler |
| Colocation only (no `features/` prefix) | Small teams prefer flat `src/orders/` | Large repos where feature name in path aids search |
| Route-driven only (`app/` holds everything) | Prototype due in days | Production apps - routes become god screens within weeks |

## FAQs

What is a feature slice?

A directory that contains everything one product area needs - screens, hooks, components, types - so engineers work in one subtree. Example: `src/features/orders/`.

What is a layered structure?

Top-level folders grouped by technical role: `components/`, `hooks/`, `screens/`, `services/`. Every feature spreads files across these folders instead of one slice.

What goes in app/ vs features/?

`app/` holds Expo Router route files - URL mapping and layout nesting. `features/` holds implementation - screens, hooks, and feature components. Route files should re-export feature screens.

What goes in components/ui/ vs features/\*/components/?

`components/ui/` - design-system primitives used by many features (Button, Screen, TextField). `features/*/components/` - product-specific UI used only inside that feature (OrderRow, InboxThread).

Why use index.ts in each feature?

It defines the public API. Other features and routes import `@/features/orders` - not deep paths. Internals can change without breaking consumers.

Can features import from other features?

Yes, but only through the other feature's `index.ts` - typically types or a single exported screen. Avoid importing internal components; that couples features silently.

When should I use layered folders instead?

Very small apps with few screens and one developer. Once PRs routinely touch multiple top-level folders for one feature, migrate to slices.

How do I migrate from layers to slices?

Pick the worst god screen. Create `features/<name>/`, move its screen, hooks, and components, add `index.ts`, and thin the route file. Repeat per feature - no big-bang rewrite required.

Where do API clients and auth live?

Cross-cutting infrastructure in `src/lib/` - `api.ts`, `storage.ts`, `analytics.ts`. Feature hooks call into `lib/`; `lib/` does not import from `features/`.

Should hooks be global or per-feature?

Per-feature when only one screen uses them (`useOrders` in `features/orders/hooks/`). Global in `src/hooks/` when shared across features (`useAppTheme`, `useSession`).

Gotcha: why did our global components/ folder become unmaintainable?

Single-use wrappers accumulate because "components/" feels like the right place for any JSX file. Default to feature-local components; promote to `ui/` only with a second real consumer.

How does this interact with container/presenter?

`features/<name>/screens/` holds containers (data, navigation). `features/<name>/components/` holds presenters (props-only UI). See [Container/Presenter on Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/container-presenter-on-mobile/).

Does Expo Router require features/?

No - Router only requires an `app/` directory. `features/` is an organizational convention that keeps routes thin and implementation testable.

How do path aliases like @/\* work?

Expo templates ship `tsconfig.json` with `"paths": { "@/*": ["./*"] }` or `"./src/*"`. Point `@/` at `src/` so `@/features/orders` resolves consistently. Metro respects the same paths when configured via `expo/tsconfig` or `babel-plugin-module-resolver` if needed.

What about tests - colocate or \_\_tests\_\_ folder?

Colocate `OrderRow.test.tsx` next to `OrderRow.tsx` inside the feature folder. Feature integration tests live in `features/orders/__tests__/` if you prefer grouping. Keep tests inside the slice you are testing.

# Project Setup Highlights Summary

Every highlight bullet from the 8 pages in this section, gathered on one page and grouped by the page it came from.

Highlights / Project Setup Highlights Summary

* Pin SDK 57 at scaffold time with default@sdk-57 - bare @latest may still resolve SDK 54
* default@sdk-57 is the team default - Expo Router, TypeScript, and recommended scripts
* Feature slices colocate screens, hooks, and components per product area - layers split by file type across the repo
* Expo SDK 52+ auto-configures Metro for monorepos - delete manual watchFolders if you migrated from older guides
* @nx/expo generators scaffold apps and libraries with consistent tsconfig, lint, and path aliases
* Expo SDK 52+ auto-configures Metro for workspaces - delete legacy watchFolders if your app still starts

## [Project Setup Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/project-setup-basics/)

* Pin SDK 57 at scaffold time with default@sdk-57 - bare @latest may still resolve SDK 54
* The default template centers on app/ (Expo Router), app.config.ts, and SDK-pinned package.json
* Scripts delegate to expo start so LAN, tunnel, and dev-client flags stay consistent across the team
* npx expo-doctor compares your graph to the SDK 57 matrix before Metro surfaces obscure errors
* tsconfig.json extends expo/tsconfig.base - add strict without fighting Metro path aliases
* app.config.ts is the manifest single source of truth for bundle IDs, icons, and plugins
* First-run verification: install → expo-doctor → tsc --noEmit → expo start

## [create-expo-app Templates](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/create-expo-app-templates/)

* default@sdk-57 is the team default - Expo Router, TypeScript, and recommended scripts
* tabs@sdk-57 and default@sdk-57 are interchangeable for most apps - pick one and standardize
* blank-typescript@sdk-57 is for spikes and brownfield experiments without navigation wired
* bare-minimum@sdk-57 runs prebuild immediately - only when you need android/ and ios/ on day one
* Always suffix templates with @sdk-57 during the SDK transition - bare @latest may scaffold SDK 54

## [Folder Structure for Features](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/folder-structure-for-features/)

* Feature slices colocate screens, hooks, and components per product area - layers split by file type across the repo
* Keep app/ routes thin - import FeatureScreen from features/ and render it
* index.ts is each feature's public API - other features import from there, not deep paths
* Shared primitives live in components/ui/ - product-specific UI stays inside the feature folder
* Switch from layers to slices when cross-feature imports and god screens outnumber isolated changes

## [Monorepo with Turborepo](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/monorepo-with-turborepo/)

* Expo SDK 52+ auto-configures Metro for monorepos - delete manual watchFolders if you migrated from older guides
* workspace:\* links apps/mobile to packages/ui via symlinks - edits are visible without publishing
* Duplicate react-native versions in one monorepo cause build and runtime failures - run pnpm why react-native
* turbo.json dev tasks should set cache: false and persistent: true for expo start
* Keep product features in the app - packages/ui holds primitives, not feature screens

## [Monorepo with Nx](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/monorepo-with-nx/)

* @nx/expo generators scaffold apps and libraries with consistent tsconfig, lint, and path aliases
* nx affected runs lint and typecheck only on projects touched since main - critical for multi-app repos
* Tag projects type:app, type:lib, scope:shared and enforce boundaries in ESLint - apps import libs, not each other
* Expo SDK 57 still auto-configures Metro - Nx orchestrates tasks, not bundler resolution
* Keep product features in apps/mobile - Nx libraries hold primitives and shared domain logic
* Use nx run mobile:start locally; wire nx affected -t lint in CI for monorepo-aware gates

## [Shared Packages & Metro Resolution](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/shared-packages-and-metro-resolution/)

* Expo SDK 52+ auto-configures Metro for workspaces - delete legacy watchFolders if your app still starts
* watchFolders tells Metro which directories outside the app root trigger rebundles on save
* extraNodeModules and nodeModulesPaths override where Metro resolves a package name - use only when auto-config fails
* pnpm isolated installs symlink packages differently than npm hoisting - wrong nodeLinker causes native build errors
* Duplicate react-native in one monorepo breaks builds - run pnpm why react-native after every major bump
* SDK 55+ enables autolinkingModuleResolution for monorepos automatically - Metro and native link the same module copy

## [Multiple Apps in One Repo](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/multiple-apps-in-one-repo/)

* Each white-label app is a separate Expo project under apps/ - same packages/core, different app.config.ts identity
* APP\_VARIANT or BRAND env vars drive bundle IDs, icons, and display names without forking source
* packages/core holds screens and navigation - apps only wire brand theme, config, and store metadata
* Each app keeps its own eas.json and EAS project - builds run from the app directory with root install
* Different bundle identifiers let QA install staging and production side by side on one device
* Never hard-code brand colors in scope:shared libs - inject theme from each app's entry point

## [Project Setup Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/best-practices/)

* Pin Expo SDK at scaffold with default@sdk-57 and verify with expo-doctor
* Keep app routes thin; put features under features//
* One react-native copy in monorepos - duplicate native deps crash at runtime
* Prefer SDK 57 auto Metro config before hand-tuning watchFolders
* Commit lockfiles; never commit ios/ and android/ under CNG
* White-label with app.config env variants, not forked feature code

Dokumen: Monorepo with Turborepo
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/monorepo-with-turborepo/

# Monorepo with Turborepo

A Turborepo monorepo lets multiple Expo apps share TypeScript config, ESLint rules, and a UI package while Turbo caches lint and typecheck tasks across CI. Expo SDK 57 detects workspaces automatically - you focus on package boundaries, not Metro wiring.

Highlights / Monorepo with Turborepo

* Expo SDK 52+ auto-configures Metro for monorepos - delete manual watchFolders if you migrated from older guides
* workspace:\* links apps/mobile to packages/ui via symlinks - edits are visible without publishing
* Duplicate react-native versions in one monorepo cause build and runtime failures - run pnpm why react-native
* turbo.json dev tasks should set cache: false and persistent: true for expo start
* Keep product features in the app - packages/ui holds primitives, not feature screens

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
mkdir mobile-monorepo && cd mobile-monorepo
pnpm init
 
# Workspace roots (create pnpm-workspace.yaml - see Working Example)
npx create-expo-app@latest apps/mobile --template default@sdk-57 --yes
 
mkdir -p packages/ui/src
pnpm add turbo -Dw
 
# Link UI package into the app (from apps/mobile/package.json)
# "@repo/ui": "workspace:*"
 
pnpm install
pnpm turbo run typecheck
pnpm turbo run dev --filter=mobile
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Two or more Expo apps (consumer + admin, white-label flavors) sharing components and utilities.
* A design-system package consumed by mobile and a future web admin.
* CI that runs lint/typecheck across apps and packages with remote caching.
* Colocating native modules or shared business logic without publishing to npm.

## Working Example

```yaml
# pnpm-workspace.yaml
packages:
  - "apps/*"
  - "packages/*"
```

```json
// package.json (root)
{
  "name": "mobile-monorepo",
  "private": true,
  "scripts": {
    "dev": "turbo run dev",
    "lint": "turbo run lint",
    "typecheck": "turbo run typecheck",
    "doctor": "turbo run doctor"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "turbo": "^2.5.0",
    "typescript": "^5.8.0"
  },
  "packageManager": "pnpm@10.0.0",
  "engines": {
    "node": ">=20"
  }
}
```

```json
// turbo.json
{
  "$schema": "https://turbo.build/schema.json",
  "tasks": {
    "dev": {
      "cache": false,
      "persistent": true
    },
    "lint": {
      "dependsOn": ["^lint"]
    },
    "typecheck": {
      "dependsOn": ["^typecheck"]
    },
    "doctor": {
      "cache": false
    }
  }
}
```

```json
// apps/mobile/package.json
{
  "name": "mobile",
  "private": true,
  "main": "expo-router/entry",
  "scripts": {
    "dev": "expo start",
    "android": "expo start --android",
    "ios": "expo start --ios",
    "lint": "expo lint",
    "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit",
    "doctor": "expo-doctor"
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "@repo/ui": "workspace:*",
    "expo": "~57.0.4",
    "expo-router": "~6.0.8",
    "react": "19.2.3",
    "react-native": "0.86.0"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@repo/typescript-config": "workspace:*",
    "typescript": "^5.8.0"
  }
}
```

```json
// packages/ui/package.json
{
  "name": "@repo/ui",
  "version": "0.0.0",
  "private": true,
  "exports": {
    "./button": "./src/button.tsx",
    "./screen": "./src/screen.tsx"
  },
  "scripts": {
    "lint": "eslint . --max-warnings 0",
    "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit"
  },
  "peerDependencies": {
    "react": "^19.2.3",
    "react-native": "0.86.0"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@repo/typescript-config": "workspace:*",
    "@types/react": "^19.0.0",
    "react": "19.2.3",
    "react-native": "0.86.0",
    "typescript": "^5.8.0"
  }
}
```

```tsx
// packages/ui/src/button.tsx
import type { ReactNode } from "react";
import { Pressable, StyleSheet, Text, type PressableProps } from "react-native";
 
type ButtonProps = PressableProps & {
  children: ReactNode;
  variant?: "primary" | "secondary";
};
 
export function Button({ children, variant = "primary", style, ...rest }: ButtonProps) {
  return (
    <Pressable style={[styles.base, variant === "primary" ? styles.primary : styles.secondary, style]} {...rest}>
      <Text style={styles.label}>{children}</Text>
    </Pressable>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  base: { paddingVertical: 12, paddingHorizontal: 20, borderRadius: 10, alignItems: "center" },
  primary: { backgroundColor: "#2563eb" },
  secondary: { backgroundColor: "#e2e8f0" },
  label: { fontSize: 16, fontWeight: "600", color: "#0f172a" },
});
```

```tsx
// apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/index.tsx
import { Button } from "@repo/ui/button";
import { StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
export default function HomeScreen() {
  return (
    <View style={styles.container}>
      <Text style={styles.title}>Shared UI from @repo/ui</Text>
      <Button variant="primary" onPress={() => {}}>
        Continue
      </Button>
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  container: { flex: 1, alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "center", gap: 16, padding: 24 },
  title: { fontSize: 20, fontWeight: "700" },
});
```

```js
// apps/mobile/metro.config.js - SDK 52+ default is usually enough
const { getDefaultConfig } = require("expo/metro-config");
 
module.exports = getDefaultConfig(__dirname);
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* **`pnpm-workspace.yaml`** declares `apps/*` and `packages/*` - Expo detects the monorepo and configures Metro automatically on SDK 57.
* **`workspace:*`** symlinks `@repo/ui` into `apps/mobile/node_modules` - Metro bundles source `.tsx` from the package without a separate build step.
* **`turbo.json`** runs `typecheck` and `lint` with `^` dependency ordering - shared packages check before apps.
* **`peerDependencies`** on `react` and `react-native` in `@repo/ui` prevent duplicate renderer copies inside the package.
* **Minimal `metro.config.js`** - no manual `watchFolders` when using `expo/metro-config` on SDK 52+.

## Deep Dive

### How It Works

* **Workspaces** let `apps/mobile` depend on local packages via symlinks instead of npm publishes.
* **Turborepo** builds a task graph from each workspace's `package.json` scripts and caches task outputs by input hash.
* **Expo Metro (SDK 52+)** auto-detects monorepos and watches workspace packages - manual `watchFolders` / `extraNodeModules` are only needed for legacy setups or non-standard layouts.
* **Metro bundles workspace TSX** directly - unlike Next.js, there is no `transpilePackages` equivalent; Babel processes linked source through the app's config.
* **EAS Build** runs from the app directory (`apps/mobile`) but installs dependencies from the monorepo root when configured with the correct working directory.

### Recommended Layout

```text
mobile-monorepo/
├── apps/
│   ├── mobile/              # Expo SDK 57 consumer app (default@sdk-57)
│   └── admin/               # optional second app
├── packages/
│   ├── ui/                  # shared primitives (Button, Screen)
│   ├── typescript-config/   # shared tsconfig bases
│   └── eslint-config/       # shared lint rules
├── pnpm-workspace.yaml
├── turbo.json
└── package.json
```

| Directory | Owns | Does not own |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `apps/mobile` | Routes (`app/`), feature folders, app config | Generic buttons usable by every app |
| `packages/ui` | Design-system primitives, shared styles | Feature screens, navigation, API clients |
| `packages/typescript-config` | `base.json`, `expo.json` extends | App-specific path aliases |

### turbo.json Tasks for Expo

| Task | `cache` | `persistent` | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dev` (`expo start`) | `false` | `true` | Long-running dev server |
| `typecheck` | default | - | Fast CI gate; cacheable |
| `lint` | default | - | Cacheable per package |
| `doctor` (`expo-doctor`) | `false` | - | Validates SDK 57 dependency graph |

```bash
# Run only the mobile app dev server
pnpm turbo run dev --filter=mobile
 
# Typecheck mobile and everything it depends on
pnpm turbo run typecheck --filter=mobile...
 
# Typecheck only packages changed since main
pnpm turbo run typecheck --filter="...[origin/main]"
```

### Duplicate Dependency Prevention

Expo monorepos fail when multiple copies of `react`, `react-native`, or native modules resolve:

```bash
pnpm why --depth=10 react-native
pnpm why --depth=10 react
```

| Problem | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| Two `react-native` versions | Align versions in root `package.json` `pnpm.overrides` or `resolutions` |
| Package missing `react` peer | Add `peerDependencies` in workspace packages; install peers in the app |
| Duplicate native modules | Enable `experiments.autolinkingModuleResolution` in `app.json` (SDK 54+; automatic in SDK 55+ monorepos) |

```json
// Root package.json - force single React 19 across workspaces (pnpm)
{
  "pnpm": {
    "overrides": {
      "react": "19.2.3",
      "react-native": "0.86.0"
    }
  }
}
```

### TypeScript Notes

```json
// packages/typescript-config/expo.json
{
  "$schema": "https://json.schemastore.org/tsconfig",
  "extends": "./base.json",
  "compilerOptions": {
    "jsx": "react-jsx",
    "moduleResolution": "bundler",
    "noEmit": true,
    "strict": true
  }
}
```

```json
// apps/mobile/tsconfig.json
{
  "extends": "@repo/typescript-config/expo.json",
  "compilerOptions": {
    "baseUrl": ".",
    "paths": {
      "@/*": ["./src/*"]
    }
  },
  "include": ["**/*.ts", "**/*.tsx", ".expo/types/**/*.ts", "expo-env.d.ts"]
}
```

Workspace packages need their own `tsconfig.json` with `"noEmit": true` for `turbo run typecheck`. Path aliases like `@/*` belong in each app - not in the shared base.

## Gotchas

* **Manual Metro monorepo config on SDK 57** - Copying pre-SDK-52 `watchFolders` recipes can conflict with Expo's automatic detection. **Fix:** Start with `getDefaultConfig(__dirname)` only; delete legacy resolver overrides and run `npx expo start --clear`.
* **Duplicate `react-native` versions** - Two versions in one monorepo cause native build and runtime errors. **Fix:** `pnpm why react-native`; add root overrides; never let packages pin different RN majors.
* **`workspace:*` with npm** - npm does not support the workspace protocol. **Fix:** Use pnpm (Turborepo's default recommendation), Yarn 4+, or Bun; or replace with `*` and accept weaker linking guarantees.
* **Feature screens in `packages/ui`** - Shared package imports `expo-router` and feature hooks; every app inherits unwanted navigation coupling. **Fix:** Keep features in `apps/mobile/src/features/`; packages hold primitives only.
* **Missing `exports` entries** - Adding `./card.tsx` without listing it in `package.json` `exports` breaks Metro resolution. **Fix:** Declare every subpath explicitly once `exports` is present.
* **pnpm isolated installs** - Strict isolation can break some React Native libraries. **Fix:** Use `nodeLinker: hoisted` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` if resolution errors appear (Expo supports isolated installs from SDK 54+, but hoisted is safer during setup).
* **EAS Build from wrong directory** - Build profile points at repo root without monorepo install config. **Fix:** Set EAS `workingDirectory` to `apps/mobile` and install from root per [Expo monorepo guide](https://docs.expo.dev/guides/monorepos/).

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Turborepo + pnpm workspaces | Multiple Expo apps, shared packages, CI caching | Single standalone app - monorepo overhead not worth it |
| Yarn/npm workspaces only | Simple linking without task orchestration | You need Turbo cache and `turbo run --filter` on CI |
| Nx monorepo | Generators, affected graph, polyglot repos with RN plugin | You want the lightest possible Expo + packages setup |
| Polyrepo + published npm packages | Teams are independent; semver boundaries matter | Rapid iteration on shared UI - publish cycles slow you down |
| Single app with `src/components/` | One product, one store listing | Two apps sharing 60%+ UI code |

## FAQs

Why use Turborepo with Expo?

Workspaces alone link packages. Turborepo adds a task graph, local caching, and remote caching so `lint` and `typecheck` skip unchanged packages on CI. Filtering (`--filter=mobile`) targets one app and its dependencies.

Do I need custom Metro config for monorepos on SDK 57?

Usually no. Expo auto-configures Metro when it detects workspace roots and you use `expo/metro-config`. If you migrated from a pre-SDK-52 guide, remove manual `watchFolders` and `extraNodeModules`, then run `npx expo start --clear`.

What does workspace:\* mean?

It tells pnpm to symlink the local `packages/ui` workspace into `apps/mobile/node_modules` instead of downloading from npm. The `*` means "whatever version exists in the workspace."

Do shared packages need a build step?

For Metro bundling, no - apps import raw `.tsx` from `@repo/ui`. For publishing to npm outside the monorepo, add a `build` task that emits `dist/`. Inside the monorepo, source imports are standard.

How do I scaffold the Expo app inside apps/?

```bash
npx create-expo-app@latest apps/mobile --template default@sdk-57 --yes
```

Run `pnpm install` from the monorepo root afterward so workspace links resolve.

Can I add a second Expo app?

Yes. Scaffold `apps/admin` with the same template, add `"@repo/ui": "workspace:*"`, and run `pnpm turbo run dev --filter=admin`. Share `packages/ui` and `packages/typescript-config` across both.

How do I run only one app?

```bash
pnpm turbo run dev --filter=mobile
pnpm turbo run typecheck --filter=mobile...
```

The trailing `...` includes workspace dependencies of `mobile`.

Gotcha: why does Metro fail to resolve @repo/ui?

Common causes: missing `exports` entry for the subpath, package not listed in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, or `pnpm install` not run from root. Verify `node_modules/@repo/ui` is a symlink to `packages/ui`.

How do I prevent duplicate react-native?

```bash
pnpm why --depth=10 react-native
```

Align all workspaces to `0.86.0`. Add root `pnpm.overrides` if a transitive dependency pulls a different major.

Should packages/ui use peerDependencies?

Yes. Declare `react` and `react-native` as peers so the app supplies a single copy. Install matching versions in the app's `dependencies`, not only in the package's `devDependencies`.

Where do feature folders live in a monorepo?

Inside each app: `apps/mobile/src/features/`. Shared packages hold primitives and utilities - not product feature screens. See [Folder Structure for Features](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/folder-structure-for-features/).

How does EAS Build work with monorepos?

Point the build at the app subdirectory and install from the monorepo root. EAS detects `pnpm-lock.yaml` at the root. Set the app's `eas.json` and working directory per Expo's monorepo documentation.

What turbo.json settings does expo start need?

```json
"dev": { "cache": false, "persistent": true }
```

Dev servers are long-running and should not be cached as completed tasks.

Turborepo vs Nx for React Native?

Turborepo is lighter - task caching and filtering with minimal config. Nx adds generators, affected commands, and RN-specific plugins at more setup cost. See [Monorepo with Nx](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/monorepo-with-nx/).

When is a monorepo the wrong choice?

Single app, single team, no shared packages. Monorepos add install complexity, duplicate-dependency risk, and tooling config. Start standalone; extract a monorepo when a second app or shared package is real - not speculative.

## Related

* [Shared Packages & Metro Resolution](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/shared-packages-and-metro-resolution/) - `watchFolders`, legacy Metro overrides, and symlink pitfalls
* [Multiple Apps in One Repo](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/multiple-apps-in-one-repo/) - white-label flavors sharing a core package
* [Monorepo with Nx](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/monorepo-with-nx/) - generators and affected builds as an alternative orchestrator
