Dokumen: Agent Skills Best Practices
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/skills/best-practices/

# Agent Skills Best Practices

A condensed summary of the 25 most important best practices drawn from every page in this section.

Highlights / Agent Skills Best Practices

* Pin React 19.2.3, RN 0.86.0, and Expo SDK 57 in every SKILL.md header
* Skills document workflows - human docs in eas-build, expo-router, and testing stay authoritative
* Guardrails block unsafe OTA, credential commits, and hand-edited CNG native dirs
* Every skill output ends with verifiable commands - expo-doctor, tsc, test, eas channel:view
* Split skills by decision domain - monolithic mobile skills produce dangerous automation
* Refresh skills after SDK bumps, postmortems, and runtimeVersion policy changes

1. **Skills are playbooks, not tutorials:** `SKILL.md` files tell agents *how to execute* - [Agent Skills Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/skills/agent-skills-basics/) defines structure; [EAS Build Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/eas-build/eas-build-basics/) teaches concepts.
2. **Pin the stack in every skill:** React **19.2.3**, RN **0.86.0**, Expo SDK **57** (`expo` ~57.0.4) - unpinned skills hallucinate deprecated APIs.
3. **One skill per decision domain:** Release, routing, native review, testing, upgrade, incident - never one mega-skill.
4. **Declare inputs before acting:** `eas.json`, `app.config.ts`, bundle IDs, `runtimeVersion`, last good `updateId` - agents guess without them.
5. **Outputs must be verifiable:** Commands and checklists, not prose summaries - reject skill runs that omit `npx expo-doctor`.
6. **Guardrails are the highest-value section:** OTA vs build boundaries, credential rules, rollout pause - see [EAS Release Skill](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/skills/eas-release-skill/).
7. **Invoke skills at decision points:** First production release, SDK upgrade, crash storm - not for reading introductory docs.
8. **Human docs remain source of truth:** Skills link to [Typed Routes](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/typed-routes/), [Maestro E2E](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/maestro-e2e/), [Config Plugins](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/native-modules/config-plugins/) - don't duplicate.
9. **Run `npx expo-doctor` after dependency changes:** Mandatory gate in [SDK Upgrade Skill](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/skills/sdk-upgrade-skill/) and every native-touching skill output.
10. **Use `npx expo install` in skills:** Never hand-pin `expo-*` versions - SDK 57 alignment drifts otherwise.
11. **Classify JS-only vs native-impacting before release:** Native module, plugin, or permission → `eas build` - OTA alone is unsafe.
12. **`runtimeVersion` in every OTA skill invocation:** Mismatch needs store binary - [Runtime Version Policy](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/runtime-version-policy/).
13. **Expo Router skills enable `typedRoutes`:** Regenerate with `npx expo start`; verify `npx tsc --noEmit` - [Expo Router Skill](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/skills/expo-router-skill/).
14. **Validate deep-link params at runtime:** Zod at screen entry - generated `Href` types don't prove malicious input.
15. **Native skills prefer config plugins:** CNG `prebuild --clean` erases hand-edited `ios/` - [Native Module Skill](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/skills/native-module-skill/).
16. **Idempotent plugins only:** Second `prebuild --clean` should produce empty git diff.
17. **App bridges → Expo Modules; TurboModules for RN libraries:** RN 0.86 New Architecture defaults - test on device.
18. **Testing skills respect the pyramid:** Many Jest, few Maestro - [Mobile Testing Skill](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/skills/mobile-testing-skill/).
19. **Maestro `appId` must match bundle ID:** Display name mismatches cause silent flow failures.
20. **E2E on EAS `e2e-test` builds:** Expo Go is not production-shaped - pair with EAS Workflows `type: maestro`.
21. **SDK upgrade skills use dedicated branches:** `prebuild --clean`, doctor, preview `eas build` matrix before production.
22. **Incident skills contain before diagnose:** Pause phased/staged rollout; assign IC - [Incident Triage Skill](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/skills/incident-triage-skill/).
23. **Tag crashes with buildNumber + updateId + route:** Triage without repro - [Observability Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/observability/best-practices/).
24. **OTA rollback < 15 minutes when JS regression:** Record known-good `updateId` in every release ticket - [Rollback Runbook](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/rollback-runbook/).
25. **Refresh skills after postmortems:** Every missed guardrail becomes a new bullet - version skills with semver in `createRunOncePlugin` spirit.

## FAQs

Where should SKILL.md files live?

App repo `.cursor/skills/` for project-specific `eas.json` conventions; org registry for shared incident and upgrade playbooks. Always pin SDK version.

Should agents edit eas.json without human approval?

Skill may draft diffs - human release captain approves before CI non-interactive runs. Guardrails block production track submit without explicit prompt.

How do skills relate to Expo's official upgrade assistant?

[SDK Upgrade Skill](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/skills/sdk-upgrade-skill/) orchestrates the same gates for agents - official release notes stay authoritative for breaking changes.

Can skills replace on-call runbooks?

No. Skills accelerate checklists; [Store Incident Response](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/store-operations/store-incident-response/) and rollback runbooks own production authority.

When is a skill stale?

After any SDK bump, `runtimeVersion` policy change, or postmortem action item. Run `npx expo-doctor` in the skill verification section on refresh.

Dokumen: EAS Release Skill
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/skills/eas-release-skill/

# EAS Release Skill

Build, submit, and OTA steps with guardrails - a cookbook-style **Agent Skill** for shipping **Expo SDK 57** binaries and updates without unsafe automation.

Highlights / EAS Release Skill

* Skill output is a ordered build → submit → OTA checklist - not a tutorial on EAS concepts
* Always classify changes as JS-only vs native-impacting before choosing eas update vs eas build
* runtimeVersion and channel must appear in every OTA skill invocation
* Submit profiles mirror build profiles - production credentials never land in git
* Verification ends with eas channel:view and npx expo-doctor
* Pair with EAS Build Basics and OTA Updates Basics for human-readable depth

## What This Skill Does

Produces an **executable release plan**: `eas.json` profile selection, cloud build commands, store submit steps, and optional `eas update` - each gated by `runtimeVersion`, credentials, and change classification.

## When to Invoke

* First production release or new `eas.json` profile
* Choosing **OTA vs store binary** for a hotfix
* Wiring `--auto-submit` or CI non-interactive submit
* Adding preview/internal distribution before production
* Post-merge release on `release/*` branches

## Inputs

| Input | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `eas.json` | Profiles, env, submit targets |
| `app.config.ts` | `version`, `runtimeVersion`, bundle IDs |
| Change list | JS-only vs native (modules, permissions, plugins) |
| Target channel/branch | `production`, `preview`, etc. |
| Last known-good `updateId` | Rollback anchor for OTA path |
| Platform scope | `ios`, `android`, `all` |

## Outputs

* Ordered command checklist with `--non-interactive` CI variants
* Risk callouts (credentials, phased rollout, track selection)
* Verification: `eas build:list`, `eas submit`, `eas channel:view`, `npx expo-doctor`
* Explicit **stop** if change is native-impacting but human requested OTA-only

## Guardrails

1. **Native change → `eas build`.** New `expo-*` module, permission, config plugin, or `expo-build-properties` edit is never OTA-only.
2. **`runtimeVersion` must match** live store binaries for OTA - see [Runtime Version Policy](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/runtime-version-policy/).
3. **Submit to internal/TestFlight first** - production Play track rollout is a separate console step ([EAS Submit](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/eas-build/eas-submit/)).
4. **Secrets in EAS environments** - not committed `.env` files ([Build Profiles & Flavors](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/eas-build/build-profiles-and-flavors/)).
5. **Pause phased/staged rollout** before hotfix binary when crash storm is active.
6. **Run `npx expo-doctor`** after any skill-generated dependency or plugin change.

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
# 1. Classify change
npx expo-doctor
git diff --name-only HEAD~1   # scan package.json, app.config.ts, plugins/
 
# 2. Cloud build (store-shaped)
eas build --profile production --platform all --non-interactive
 
# 3. Submit latest artifacts
eas submit --platform ios --latest --non-interactive
eas submit --platform android --latest --non-interactive
 
# 4. JS-only hotfix (same runtimeVersion)
eas update --channel production --message "fix: checkout validation copy"
 
# 5. Verify
eas channel:view production
eas build:list --limit 3
```

```json
// eas.json (excerpt - SDK 57)
{
  "build": {
    "development": {
      "developmentClient": true,
      "distribution": "internal"
    },
    "preview": {
      "distribution": "internal",
      "channel": "preview"
    },
    "production": {
      "channel": "production",
      "autoIncrement": true
    }
  },
  "submit": {
    "production": {
      "ios": { "ascAppId": "1234567890" },
      "android": {
        "serviceAccountKeyPath": "./secrets/play-service-account.json",
        "track": "internal"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

**When to reach for this skill:**

* Release captain needs a **single checklist** before Friday deploy
* Agent is asked to "ship the fix" without specifying OTA vs binary
* New engineer onboarding to EAS - skill enforces guardrails docs alone might skip

---

## Working Example

### Step 0 - Classify the change

```bash
npx expo-doctor
```

| Signal | Path |
| --- | --- |
| Only `.tsx`, hooks, copy | OTA candidate |
| `package.json` new `expo-camera` | **Build required** |
| `app.config.ts` plugin added | **Build required** |
| Hermes / RN version bump | **Build required** + `runtimeVersion` review |

### Step 1 - Build

```bash
eas build --profile production --platform all
# CI one-shot:
eas build --profile production --platform ios --auto-submit --non-interactive
```

* `developmentClient: true` → dev client, not store - [EAS Build Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/eas-build/eas-build-basics/)
* CNG teams: native dirs generated on server - [Prebuild Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/prebuild-basics/)

### Step 2 - Submit

```bash
eas submit --platform ios --latest
eas submit --platform android --latest
```

* Android `track: "internal"` in `eas.json` - promote in Play Console later
* iOS lands in TestFlight - phased release is App Store Connect step

### Step 3 - OTA (JS-only)

```bash
eas update --channel production --message "fix: cart total rounding"
eas channel:view production
```

* Record published `updateId` in release ticket - [Rollback Runbook](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/rollback-runbook/)
* Staged OTA rollout: [Staged Rollouts](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/staged-rollouts/)

### Step 4 - Verify

```bash
npx expo-doctor
eas build:list --limit 1
eas update:list --branch production --limit 3
```

## Decision: OTA vs Store Binary

```text
                    ┌─────────────────┐
                    │  Change landed  │
                    └────────┬────────┘
                             │
                    ┌────────▼────────┐
                    │ expo-doctor OK? │──no──► fix config/deps first
                    └────────┬────────┘
                             │ yes
                    ┌────────▼────────────────┐
                    │ Native-impacting change?  │
                    └────────┬────────────────┘
                         yes │      │ no
              ┌──────────────┘      └──────────────┐
              ▼                                    ▼
      eas build + submit                  runtimeVersion
      (new binary)                        matches store?
                                                    │
                                    yes ──► eas update
                                    no  ──► eas build (bump runtimeVersion)
```

## FAQs

Can the skill run eas submit to production Play track automatically?

Technically yes via `track: "production"` - guardrail: default to **internal** until QA signs off. Skill should warn when production track is requested.

Does --auto-submit skip TestFlight testing?

No - it uploads the binary. TestFlight distribution and App Review are still console steps unless your workflow promotes separately.

What if expo-doctor fails mid-release?

Stop. Skill output should not include submit/OTA until doctor passes. Fix skew with `npx expo install --fix` per [SDK Upgrade Skill](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/skills/sdk-upgrade-skill/).

Dokumen: Expo Router Skill
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/skills/expo-router-skill/

# Expo Router Skill

Route scaffolding, typed params, and deep-link wiring - an **Agent Skill** for adding screens safely on **Expo Router** with **Expo SDK 57** file-based routing.

Highlights / Expo Router Skill

* Skill scaffolds app/ files, typed Href builders, and scheme-based deep links for SDK 57
* experiments.typedRoutes: true is mandatory output - run tsc --noEmit to verify
* Dynamic routes use object hrefs with pathname + params - never raw string interpolation
* Deep links require scheme in app.config.ts plus optional universal links host
* Validate runtime URL params with Zod - generated types do not prove deep-link input
* Delegate navigation concepts to expo-router section docs - skill produces file tree + code

## What This Skill Does

Generates:

* `app/` route file tree (layouts, index, dynamic segments)
* `experiments.typedRoutes` config and href builder modules
* Deep link / universal link wiring in `app.config.ts`
* `tsc --noEmit` verification steps

## When to Invoke

* New feature needs routes under `app/` (tabs, stacks, modals)
* Adding dynamic route `/orders/[id]` with typed navigation
* Wiring `myapp://` or `https://` deep links to existing screens
* Refactoring string `router.push` calls to centralized `Href` builders
* Post-auth redirects and protected route groups

## Inputs

| Input | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Route map | Paths, groups `(auth)`, tab vs stack |
| Param shapes | `{ id: string }`, optional query fields |
| `app.config.ts` | `scheme`, `ios.bundleIdentifier`, linking |
| Existing `app/` tree | Avoid duplicate layouts |
| Deep link examples | `myapp://orders/42`, notification payloads |

## Outputs

* File tree diff (`app/...`)
* `app.config.ts` linking snippet
* `src/navigation/hrefs.ts` (or `routes.ts`) with typed builders
* Screen param validation stub (Zod)
* Commands: `npx expo start`, `npx tsc --noEmit`

## Guardrails

1. **Enable `experiments.typedRoutes: true`** - regenerate types after every `app/` change ([Typed Routes](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/typed-routes/)).
2. **Dynamic routes use object `href`** - `{ pathname: "/orders/[id]", params: { id } }`.
3. **Validate runtime params** - types don't prove malicious deep-link input.
4. **Keep routes thin** - re-export feature screens from `src/features/` ([Mobile Architecture Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/mobile-architecture-basics/)).
5. **Don't nest duplicate `_layout` providers** - one auth/session boundary at root.
6. **Test deep links on dev build** - Expo Go scheme handling differs from production.

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```ts
// app.config.ts
export default {
  scheme: "myapp",
  experiments: { typedRoutes: true },
} satisfies import("expo/config").ExpoConfig;
```

```tsx
// app/orders/[id].tsx
import { useLocalSearchParams } from "expo-router";
import { z } from "zod";
 
const paramsSchema = z.object({ id: z.string().min(1) });
 
export default function OrderDetailScreen() {
  const raw = useLocalSearchParams<{ id: string }>();
  const { id } = paramsSchema.parse(raw);
  // ...
}
```

```ts
// src/navigation/hrefs.ts
import type { Href } from "expo-router";
 
export const orderDetailHref = (id: string): Href => ({
  pathname: "/orders/[id]",
  params: { id },
});
```

```tsx
// Usage
import { Link, router } from "expo-router";
import { orderDetailHref } from "@/navigation/hrefs";
 
<Link href={orderDetailHref("42")}>Order 42</Link>
router.push(orderDetailHref("42"));
```

```bash
npx expo start    # regen .expo/types/router.d.ts
npx tsc --noEmit  # catch invalid href at compile time
```

**When to reach for this skill:**

* Product asks for three new screens with cross-links and shareable URLs
* Push notification payload maps to a route - need deep link wiring
* TypeScript CI fails after `app/` restructure

---

## Working Example

### 1. Scaffold route group

```text
app/
├── _layout.tsx           # root Stack or Slot
├── (tabs)/
│   ├── _layout.tsx
│   ├── index.tsx
│   └── orders/
│       ├── index.tsx
│       └── [id].tsx
└── (auth)/
    ├── _layout.tsx
    └── login.tsx
```

* Route groups `(tabs)` don't appear in URL - [Route Groups](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/route-groups-and-organizing-app/)
* Tab layout: [Tabs & Drawers](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/tabs-and-drawers/)

### 2. Root layout (auth gate sketch)

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx
import { Stack, useRouter, useSegments } from "expo-router";
import { useEffect } from "react";
import { useSession } from "@/features/auth/session";
 
export default function RootLayout() {
  const { session, isLoading } = useSession();
  const segments = useSegments();
  const router = useRouter();
 
  useEffect(() => {
    if (isLoading) return;
    const inAuth = segments[0] === "(auth)";
    if (!session && !inAuth) router.replace("/(auth)/login");
    if (session && inAuth) router.replace("/(tabs)");
  }, [session, isLoading, segments]);
 
  return <Stack screenOptions={{ headerShown: false }} />;
}
```

* Advanced patterns: [Protected Routes](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router-advanced/protected-routes-and-middleware/)

### 3. Deep links

```ts
// app.config.ts
export default {
  scheme: "myapp",
  ios: { bundleIdentifier: "com.example.myapp" },
  android: { package: "com.example.myapp" },
  // Optional universal links:
  // ios: { associatedDomains: ["applinks:myapp.com"] },
} satisfies import("expo/config").ExpoConfig;
```

| URL | Resolves to |
| --- | --- |
| `myapp://orders/42` | `app/orders/[id].tsx` with `id=42` |
| `myapp://(tabs)/orders` | orders list |

* Declarative links: [Link & href](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/link-and-href/)
* Imperative after mutation: `router.replace("/(tabs)")` post-login

### 4. Verify

```bash
npx expo start
npx tsc --noEmit
 
# iOS simulator deep link test
xcrun simctl openurl booted "myapp://orders/42"
```


## Skill Output Checklist

```markdown
- [ ] app/ tree documented
- [ ] experiments.typedRoutes: true in app.config.ts
- [ ] href builders exported from single module
- [ ] Zod (or equivalent) on dynamic params
- [ ] scheme / associatedDomains if deep links required
- [ ] npx tsc --noEmit in verification section
- [ ] No business logic duplicated in route files
```

## FAQs

Should the skill generate modal routes?

Yes when requested - use `presentation: "modal"` in layout options. See [Modal Routes](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router-advanced/modal-and-presentation-routes/) for SDK 57 presentation patterns.

Does typedRoutes catch invalid optional params?

Partially. Generated `Href` unions cover pathnames; optional search params still need runtime validation at screen entry.

Web vs native href differences?

Skill should use `expo-router` `Href` type - works on web and native. Platform-specific linking config belongs in `app.config.ts` only.

## [Agent Skills Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/skills/agent-skills-basics/)

* One user journey per Maestro file - appId must match installed bundle exactly
* EAS Workflows type: maestro jobs preferred over ad-hoc CI shell for SDK 57
* Outputs include npm run test:ci and maestro test commands with flaky-test controls

## [SDK Upgrade Skill](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/skills/sdk-upgrade-skill/)

* Ordered upgrade checklist: branch, expo install, prebuild --clean, doctor, device smoke
* npx expo-doctor is a hard gate - skill stops on failure before merge
* runtimeVersion and eas.json profiles must be reviewed on every SDK bump
* Native module and config plugin diffs require full eas build matrix before production
* Aligned with Expo official upgrade flow - not a substitute for reading SDK 57 release notes
* Outputs include rollback branch name and preview build verification commands

## [Incident Triage Skill](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/skills/incident-triage-skill/)

* Skill produces timed contain → diagnose → recover checklist with explicit IC roles
* Crash clusters need release tags: buildNumber, updateId, runtimeVersion, channel
* Decision tree: feature flag off → OTA rollback → pause rollout → store hotfix binary
* Native SIGABRT crashes cannot be fixed by eas update - skill must escalate to eas build
* Pair with Sentry symbolication gates and Rollback Runbook verification commands
* SDK 57: distinguish Hermes JS errors from native module regressions on RN 0.86 NA

## [Agent Skills Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/skills/best-practices/)

* Pin React 19.2.3, RN 0.86.0, and Expo SDK 57 in every SKILL.md header
* Skills document workflows - human docs in eas-build, expo-router, and testing stay authoritative
* Guardrails block unsafe OTA, credential commits, and hand-edited CNG native dirs
* Every skill output ends with verifiable commands - expo-doctor, tsc, test, eas channel:view
* Split skills by decision domain - monolithic mobile skills produce dangerous automation
* Refresh skills after SDK bumps, postmortems, and runtimeVersion policy changes

Dokumen: Mobile Testing Skill
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/skills/mobile-testing-skill/

# Mobile Testing Skill

Jest + Maestro plans from acceptance criteria - an **Agent Skill** that turns product AC into a **test pyramid slice** for **Expo SDK 57** apps.

Highlights / Mobile Testing Skill

* Skill converts acceptance criteria into Jest unit/component tests plus Maestro YAML flows
* jest-expo preset and transformIgnorePatterns are part of every SDK 57 output
* Mock native I/O at Jest boundaries - exercise real bridges in Maestro on EAS builds
* One user journey per Maestro file - appId must match installed bundle exactly
* EAS Workflows type: maestro jobs preferred over ad-hoc CI shell for SDK 57
* Outputs include npm run test:ci and maestro test commands with flaky-test controls

## What This Skill Does

From written acceptance criteria, produces:

* **Jest** unit and component tests (`jest-expo` + RNTL)
* **Maestro** YAML E2E flows for critical journeys
* CI wiring sketch (GitHub Actions or EAS Workflows)
* Explicit **what not to E2E** list (push down the pyramid)

## When to Invoke

* New feature ticket with AC but no test plan
* Regression after refactor - need targeted Jest + smoke Maestro
* PR asks "what should QA automate?"
* Setting up first Maestro flow on EAS `e2e-test` profile
* Converting manual test script to maintainable automation

## Inputs

| Input | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Acceptance criteria | Source of test cases |
| `appId` / bundle ID | Maestro `appId` field |
| Screen/route names | Stable selectors and navigation |
| `testID` policy | Team convention for Maestro `id:` taps |
| Build profile | `e2e-test` APK / simulator build |
| Mock boundaries | APIs, SecureStore, sensors |

## Outputs

* `*.test.ts(x)` files with RNTL queries (role/label first)
* `.maestro/<journey>.yml` flows
* `jest.setup.ts` additions if needed
* `eas.json` `e2e-test` profile snippet
* Commands: `npm run test:ci`, `maestro test .maestro/`

## Guardrails

1. **Many Jest, few Maestro** - pyramid discipline ([Mobile Testing Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/mobile-testing-basics/)).
2. **Query like users** - `getByRole`, `getByLabelText` before `testID` ([RNTL](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/react-native-testing-library/)).
3. **Mock at boundaries** - don't assert implementation details inside components.
4. **Maestro `appId` exact match** - bundle ID ≠ display name.
5. **Short independent flows** - one journey per YAML file ([Maestro E2E](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/maestro-e2e/)).
6. **E2E on real builds** - not Expo Go for production-shaped flows.

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

**Input AC (example):**

```markdown
- Guest can add item to cart from product list
- Cart badge shows item count
- Signed-in user sees saved address at checkout
```

**Skill output skeleton:**

```ts
// src/features/cart/cart.test.ts
import { addToCart } from "./cart-logic";
 
describe("addToCart", () => {
  it("increments quantity for existing sku", () => {
    expect(addToCart({ sku: "A1", qty: 1 }, { sku: "A1", qty: 2 })).toEqual({
      sku: "A1",
      qty: 3,
    });
  });
});
```

```tsx
// src/features/cart/CartBadge.test.tsx
import { render, screen } from "@testing-library/react-native";
import { CartBadge } from "./CartBadge";
 
it("shows count when items present", () => {
  render(<CartBadge count={3} />);
  expect(screen.getByLabelText("Cart, 3 items")).toBeTruthy();
});
```

```yaml
# .maestro/add-to-cart.yml
appId: com.example.shop
---
- launchApp
- tapOn: "Products"
- tapOn:
    id: "product-tile-A1"
- tapOn: "Add to cart"
- assertVisible:
    id: "cart-badge"
    text: "1"
```

```bash
npm run test:ci
maestro test .maestro/add-to-cart.yml
```

**When to reach for this skill:**

* Sprint planning - AC exists, tests don't
* Agent asked to "add tests" without specifying layers
* Flaky E2E - skill should propose moving assertions down to Jest

---

## Working Example

### 1. Map AC → pyramid

| AC | Layer | Artifact |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Add to cart logic | Unit | `cart-logic.test.ts` |
| Badge visible | Component | `CartBadge.test.tsx` |
| List → detail → cart | E2E | `.maestro/add-to-cart.yml` |
| Saved address at checkout | Integration + E2E | mocked API test + checkout flow |

### 2. Jest setup (SDK 57)

```bash
npx expo install jest-expo jest @types/jest @testing-library/react-native test-renderer --dev
```

```json
{
  "jest": {
    "preset": "jest-expo",
    "transformIgnorePatterns": [
      "node_modules/(?!((jest-)?react-native|@react-native(-community)?)|expo(nent)?|@expo(nent)?/.*|@expo-google-fonts/.*|react-navigation|@react-navigation/.*|@sentry/react-native|native-base|react-native-svg)"
    ],
    "setupFilesAfterEnv": ["<rootDir>/jest.setup.ts"]
  }
}
```

Full preset: [Jest Setup for Expo](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/jest-setup-for-expo/).

### 3. Maestro + EAS Workflow

```json
// eas.json excerpt
{
  "build": {
    "e2e-test": {
      "withoutCredentials": true,
      "ios": { "simulator": true },
      "android": { "buildType": "apk" }
    }
  }
}
```

```yaml
# .eas/workflows/e2e-test-android.yml
name: e2e-test-android
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: ["*"]
jobs:
  build_android_for_e2e:
    type: build
    params:
      platform: android
      profile: e2e-test
  maestro_test:
    needs: [build_android_for_e2e]
    type: maestro
    params:
      build_id: ${{ needs.build_android_for_e2e.outputs.build_id }}
      flow_path: [".maestro/add-to-cart.yml"]
```

### 4. Flaky controls

* Regex matchers: `assertVisible: "Welcome back.*"`
* `extendedWaitUntil` for slow network screens
* Avoid chaining five journeys in one YAML file

## FAQs

Should the skill generate Detox tests?

Default to Maestro for SDK 57 Expo teams. Mention Detox only when AC requires native synchronization Detox excels at - see [Detox E2E](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/detox-e2e/).

How many Maestro flows per feature?

One happy path + one critical failure path maximum per feature. More belongs in Jest.

Snapshot tests from the skill?

Only for small presentational components - not full screens. Prefer role/label assertions.

Dokumen: Native Module Skill
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/skills/native-module-skill/

# Native Module Skill

Config plugin and TurboModule scaffolding reviews - an **Agent Skill** for safely adding native surface area on **Expo SDK 57** / **React Native 0.86** with CNG and the New Architecture.

Highlights / Native Module Skill

* Skill reviews config plugin idempotency and TurboModule Codegen alignment for RN 0.86 NA
* CNG apps must use plugins - never hand-edit ios/ or android/ without a follow-up plugin
* Prefer create-expo-module for app-local bridges; TurboModules for RN-ecosystem libraries
* Output includes prebuild --clean diff review and npx expo-doctor gate
* New native dependency always triggers eas build - skill must flag OTA-only requests as unsafe
* Cross-check against Config Plugins and Writing a TurboModule human docs

## What This Skill Does

Reviews or scaffolds:

* **Config plugins** (`app.config.ts` + `plugins/with-*.ts`)
* **Expo Modules** via `create-expo-module` layout
* **TurboModule** Codegen specs when RN-ecosystem library patterns apply
* Prebuild diff checklist and `expo-doctor` verification

## When to Invoke

* Adding third-party SDK with manifest / plist / Gradle requirements
* Writing local `plugins/with-custom-feature.ts`
* Evaluating TurboModule vs Expo Modules API for a new bridge
* PR review: "is this plugin idempotent under `prebuild --clean`?"
* Before merging any change that touches `ios/` or `android/` manually

## Inputs

| Input | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `app.config.ts` | Current `plugins` array and order |
| Native requirement | Permissions, entitlements, Gradle flags |
| Package name | npm module or local `./modules/foo` |
| Architecture mode | New Architecture default on RN 0.86 |
| CNG policy | Generated vs checked-in native dirs |

## Outputs

* Plugin skeleton or review checklist (idempotency, ordering)
* `package.json` / autolinking notes
* `npx expo prebuild --clean` + `git diff ios/ android/` steps
* `npx expo-doctor` gate
* **Build required** flag - never approve OTA-only for native changes

## Guardrails

1. **Config plugins over manual native edits** - [Config Plugins](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/native-modules/config-plugins/).
2. **Plugin order matters** - document when multiple plugins touch `Info.plist` or `AndroidManifest.xml`.
3. **Idempotent plugins** - running `prebuild --clean` twice yields empty git diff.
4. **App bridges → `create-expo-module`** - TurboModules for RN-first libraries ([Writing a TurboModule](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/native-modules/writing-a-turbomodule/)).
5. **Test on New Architecture device build** - bridge fallback hides sync API bugs on RN 0.86.
6. **Native change → `eas build`** - skill rejects OTA-only release plans.

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```ts
// app.config.ts
import type { ExpoConfig } from "expo/config";
 
export default ({ config }: { config: ExpoConfig }): ExpoConfig => ({
  ...config,
  plugins: [
    [
      "expo-build-properties",
      {
        ios: { deploymentTarget: "15.1" },
        android: { minSdkVersion: 24, compileSdkVersion: 35 },
      },
    ],
    "./plugins/with-analytics-sdk",
  ],
});
```

```ts
// plugins/with-analytics-sdk.ts
import {
  ConfigPlugin,
  withInfoPlist,
  withAndroidManifest,
  createRunOncePlugin,
} from "expo/config-plugins";
 
const withAnalyticsSdk: ConfigPlugin = (config) => {
  config = withInfoPlist(config, (cfg) => {
    cfg.modResults.MyAnalyticsEnabled = true;
    return cfg;
  });
  config = withAndroidManifest(config, (cfg) => {
    // add manifest entries - keep idempotent
    return cfg;
  });
  return config;
};
 
export default createRunOncePlugin(
  withAnalyticsSdk,
  "with-analytics-sdk",
  "1.0.0"
);
```

```bash
npx expo prebuild --clean
git diff ios/ android/
npx expo-doctor
eas build --profile preview --platform all   # never OTA-only for this change
```

**When to reach for this skill:**

* Vendor SDK docs say "add this to `AndroidManifest.xml`" - skill converts to plugin
* Engineer pasted manual `ios/Podfile` edit - skill redirects to CNG-safe path
* Library README mentions TurboModule Codegen - skill picks Expo Module vs Turbo path

## Working Example

### Path A - Config plugin (most app teams)

**Review checklist the skill emits:**

```markdown
## Config plugin review
- [ ] Uses createRunOncePlugin with name + version
- [ ] No absolute paths; reads from config props
- [ ] Info.plist / manifest changes are merge-safe
- [ ] Documented plugin order relative to expo-build-properties
- [ ] prebuild --clean → review diff → second prebuild → empty diff
- [ ] expo-doctor passes
- [ ] eas build planned (OTA insufficient)
```

See [Patching Native Projects](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/native-modules/patching-native-projects/) when upstream lacks a plugin.

### Path B - Expo Module (app-local native bridge)

```bash
npx create-expo-module@latest expo-secure-counter
# Wire in app:
npx expo install ./modules/expo-secure-counter
```

* Autolinking: [Autolinking & expo-modules-core](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/native-modules/autolinking-and-expo-modules-core/)
* Prefer over TurboModule for **app-specific** Swift/Kotlin bridges

### Path C - TurboModule (RN ecosystem library)

```ts
// modules/my-turbo-lib/src/NativeMyTurboLib.ts
import type { TurboModule } from "react-native";
import { TurboModuleRegistry } from "react-native";
 
export interface Spec extends TurboModule {
  getConstants(): { value: string };
  process(input: string): string;
}
 
export default TurboModuleRegistry.getEnforcing<Spec>("MyTurboLib");
```

```json
// package.json codegenConfig excerpt
{
  "codegenConfig": {
    "name": "MyTurboLibSpec",
    "type": "modules",
    "jsSrcsDir": "src"
  }
}
```

* Skill verifies **New Architecture** test plan on device
* Third-party without Expo config: [Using Third-Party Libraries](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/native-modules/using-third-party-native-libraries/)

## Decision: Expo Module vs TurboModule

| Criterion | Expo Module | TurboModule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Owner | App team, single app | RN library, multi-consumer |
| Setup | `create-expo-module` | Codegen + `codegenConfig` |
| Config plugin | Often bundled | Usually `react-native.config.js` |
| Expo CNG fit | Excellent | Good with prebuild |
| Skill default | **Yes for app bridges** | When publishing RN package |

## FAQs

Can the skill approve a one-line Info.plist hand-edit?

Only as emergency hotfix with follow-up plugin ticket. CNG `prebuild --clean` will erase hand edits - skill must flag debt.

Does adding expo-camera need this skill?

Built-in config plugins often suffice. Invoke skill when combining multiple permission plugins or custom Gradle flags.

OTA after native module?

Never for users on old binaries without the module. Skill output always includes `eas build` and runtimeVersion review.

Dokumen: State Management Best Practices
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/state-management/best-practices/

# State Management Best Practices

A condensed summary of the 25 most important best practices drawn from every page in this section.

Highlights / State Management Best Practices

* Classify state before choosing a library: server, client, URL, form, secrets
* Default stack: TanStack Query + Zustand (or Context) + Expo Router params
* Never store API catalogs in global client stores - Query owns server state
* Wire focusManager and onlineManager for mobile lifecycle on day one
* Hydrate session and prefs before routing to avoid flash of wrong screen
* Document the team choice in an ADR before the third global store appears

1. **Classify state first:** Label every piece as server, client UI, URL/navigation, form, or secret - then match to a tool. Random library picks create overlapping caches.
2. **Query-first for API data:** TanStack Query owns lists, details, loading, errors, dedupe, and background refresh. Do not hand-roll `useEffect` fetch on the fifth networked screen.
3. **Keep client UI out of Query cache:** Theme toggles, wizard steps, and modal flags are not query keys. Misusing cache semantics serializes UI into server infrastructure.
4. **Default greenfield stack:** TanStack Query (server) + Zustand or split Context (client) + Expo Router search params (shareable filters). Add Redux only when an ADR requires it.
5. **useState for ephemeral screen UI:** Modal open, single-screen selection, and simple toggles stay local until another route genuinely needs the value.
6. **useReducer for coupled transitions:** Wizards, small multi-field forms, and step machines get one reducer - not five independent `useState` calls that drift out of sync.
7. **Split Context by update frequency:** Theme, session state, and actions live in separate contexts. One mega-context re-renders the list on every cart tick.
8. **Memoize provider values:** `useMemo` for state objects and `useCallback` for actions. Inline `{ signOut: () => ... }` in provider value breaks `React.memo` downstream.
9. **Reach for Zustand when selectors matter:** Global cart, preferences, and flags need fine-grained subscriptions. Select primitives - `useStore((s) => s.count)` - not the whole store.
10. **One store per domain:** `cartStore`, `preferencesStore` - not `appStore` with forty unrelated fields. Import cycles and test resets get painful fast.
11. **Redux Toolkit when audit matters:** Regulated workflows, mandated DevTools, and middleware ecosystems justify RTK. Not for a badge counter on day one.
12. **Do not run two server caches:** Pick TanStack Query or RTK Query for the same API - never both. Migration is slice-by-slice with a checklist.
13. **Wire mobile lifecycle for Query:** `onlineManager` + NetInfo and `focusManager` + AppState in bootstrap. Web defaults do not refetch on app foreground.
14. **Tune staleTime and gcTime deliberately:** Catalog reads tolerate minutes of staleness; balances and checkout totals do not. Document defaults in `createQueryClient`.
15. **Optimistic mutations with rollback:** Use `onMutate`, `cancelQueries`, snapshot `previous`, and restore on `onError`. Manual optimistic `useState` scales poorly across screens.
16. **Persist reads, not secrets:** `persistQueryClient` and Zustand `persist` for public catalog and prefs. Access tokens go to `expo-secure-store` - never AsyncStorage.
17. **Hydrate before routing:** Session and persisted prefs must finish loading before choosing auth vs app stacks. Pair with splash hold to avoid flash of login screen.
18. **Clear all layers on logout:** Secure token, Zustand slices, Query cache, and disk persister. Shared tablets leak PII when only one layer clears.
19. **URL state via Expo Router params:** Filters and tabs that marketing wants shareable belong in `useLocalSearchParams` - not a global store that breaks deep links.
20. **Forms stay colocated:** React Hook Form or screen-level reducer for inputs; `useMutation` on submit. Do not stream every keystroke into Zustand.
21. **Jotai for atomic UIs only when justified:** Builder and inspector panels benefit from derived atoms. Default hires know Zustand - document Jotai in an ADR if adopted.
22. **Test store boundaries:** Reset Zustand with `setState(initial, true)`; isolated `QueryClient` with `retry: false`. Mock network at service edge, not inside reducers.
23. **Measure before optimizing:** React DevTools Profiler on list scroll beats premature Jotai adoption. Fix provider storms before sprinkling `React.memo` on two hundred rows.
24. **Version persisted schemas:** Bump `name: "preferences-v3"` or Query `buster` on breaking API or shape changes. OTA without cache bust parses stale JSON into crashes.
25. **Record the decision in an ADR:** Before squad B installs MobX while squad A uses Redux, write [ADR: State Management Selection](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/adr-state-management-selection/) and link it from store modules.

## FAQs

What is the smallest stack for a new Expo SDK 57 app?

TanStack Query + `useState`/`useReducer` on screens. Add Zustand when a second route needs the same client state. Add Context for session if Zustand feels heavy for one user object.

When is Redux still correct?

Audit trails, time-travel debugging requirements, and existing org standards. See [Redux Toolkit](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/state-management/redux-toolkit/).

How do I know state is in the wrong layer?

Same API data edited in Zustand and Query; token in Query cache; filter in global store but not in URL when shareable. Run the checklist in [State Management Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/state-management/state-management-basics/).

Dokumen: Context Without Storms
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/state-management/context-without-storms/

# Context Without Storms

Split contexts, memoized providers, and selector patterns to avoid re-render storms. React Context is built-in and works for **infrequently changing** values - theme, locale, auth session. A single mega-context updating every second will tank list scroll performance on mid-range Android devices.

Highlights / Context Without Storms

* One Context value object forces every consumer to re-render on any field change
* Split by update frequency: ThemeContext vs SessionContext vs ActionsContext
* Memoize provider value with useMemo - stable action callbacks with useCallback
* use-context-selector or Zustand when many components need one slice
* Context fits theme, locale, and session - not API catalog caches
* Measure with React DevTools Profiler before adding a global store

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```tsx
// Split: state context + dispatch context (or actions-only context)
import { createContext, useCallback, useContext, useMemo, useState, type ReactNode } from "react";
 
type Theme = "light" | "dark";
 
const ThemeStateContext = createContext<Theme>("light");
const ThemeActionsContext = createContext<{ toggle: () => void } | null>(null);
 
export function ThemeProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  const [theme, setTheme] = useState<Theme>("light");
  const toggle = useCallback(() => setTheme((t) => (t === "light" ? "dark" : "light")), []);
  const actions = useMemo(() => ({ toggle }), [toggle]);
 
  return (
    <ThemeStateContext.Provider value={theme}>
      <ThemeActionsContext.Provider value={actions}>{children}</ThemeActionsContext.Provider>
    </ThemeStateContext.Provider>
  );
}
 
export function useTheme() {
  return useContext(ThemeStateContext);
}
 
export function useThemeActions() {
  const ctx = useContext(ThemeActionsContext);
  if (!ctx) throw new Error("useThemeActions must be used within ThemeProvider");
  return ctx;
}
```

**When to reach for this:**

* **Theme, locale, or accessibility** settings change rarely - Context is appropriate.
* **Session identity** (user id, signOut) is read by many screens but updates on login/logout only.
* You want **zero extra dependencies** before Zustand is justified.
* Consumers need **actions without subscribing to state** - split contexts pattern.
* Profiler shows **wide re-renders** from one provider - split or add selectors.

## Working Example

```tsx
// session/SessionProvider.tsx - split state vs actions; memoized value
import {
  createContext,
  useCallback,
  useContext,
  useMemo,
  useState,
  type ReactNode,
} from "react";
 
type User = { id: string; displayName: string };
 
type SessionState = {
  user: User | null;
  status: "loading" | "authenticated" | "anonymous";
};
 
type SessionActions = {
  signIn: (user: User) => void;
  signOut: () => void;
};
 
const SessionStateContext = createContext<SessionState | null>(null);
const SessionActionsContext = createContext<SessionActions | null>(null);
 
export function SessionProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  const [state, setState] = useState<SessionState>({ user: null, status: "loading" });
 
  const signIn = useCallback((user: User) => {
    setState({ user, status: "authenticated" });
  }, []);
 
  const signOut = useCallback(() => {
    setState({ user: null, status: "anonymous" });
  }, []);
 
  const actions = useMemo(() => ({ signIn, signOut }), [signIn, signOut]);
 
  return (
    <SessionStateContext.Provider value={state}>
      <SessionActionsContext.Provider value={actions}>{children}</SessionActionsContext.Provider>
    </SessionStateContext.Provider>
  );
}
 
export function useSessionState() {
  const ctx = useContext(SessionStateContext);
  if (!ctx) throw new Error("useSessionState requires SessionProvider");
  return ctx;
}
 
export function useSessionActions() {
  const ctx = useContext(SessionActionsContext);
  if (!ctx) throw new Error("useSessionActions requires SessionProvider");
  return ctx;
}
 
// --- Consumer: header only needs displayName ---
import { Text, View } from "react-native";
 
export function HeaderGreeting() {
  const { user, status } = useSessionState();
  if (status === "loading") return <Text>…</Text>;
  return <Text>Hello, {user?.displayName ?? "Guest"}</Text>;
}
 
// --- Consumer: settings only needs signOut - does NOT re-render when user displayName changes
// if you only import useSessionActions and never useSessionState
import { Pressable } from "react-native";
 
export function SignOutButton() {
  const { signOut } = useSessionActions();
  return (
    <Pressable onPress={signOut}>
      <Text>Sign out</Text>
    </Pressable>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// Selector hook pattern without extra library - subscribe to one field
import { useRef, useSyncExternalStore } from "react";
 
function useSessionSelector<T>(selector: (state: SessionState) => T): T {
  const state = useSessionState();
  const selectorRef = useRef(selector);
  selectorRef.current = selector;
 
  return useSyncExternalStore(
    () => () => {},
    () => selectorRef.current(state),
    () => selectorRef.current(state)
  );
}
 
// Usage: only re-renders when user.id changes (manual optimization - Zustand does this natively)
export function UserIdLabel() {
  const userId = useSessionSelector((s) => s.user?.id ?? "anon");
  return <Text>ID: {userId}</Text>;
}
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* **Split contexts** - components that only call `signOut` avoid re-renders when `displayName` changes (if they never touch state context).
* **`useMemo` / `useCallback`** stabilize the actions object - prevents child memo breakage.
* **Selector pattern** with `useSyncExternalStore` is a bridge before Zustand - see limitations in Deep Dive.
* **Session** is identity, not API cache - profile details still come from TanStack Query.

## Deep Dive

### Why Re-render Storms Happen

React re-renders all **consumers** of a context when `Provider value={...}` identity or content triggers an update. A common mistake:

```tsx
// ❌ New object every render - all consumers re-render
<AppContext.Provider value={{ user, cart, theme, setTheme }}>
```

Even if only `cart` changed, `theme` consumers re-render because the value object is new.

### Split Context Checklist

| Context | Holds | Update frequency |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ThemeStateContext` | `"light" | "dark"` | Rare |
| `SessionStateContext` | `user`, `status` | Login/logout |
| `SessionActionsContext` | `signIn`, `signOut` | Never (stable refs) |
| `QueryClientProvider` | Server cache | Per fetch - not React Context for data |

### Memoization Pattern

```tsx
const value = useMemo(
  () => ({ user, status }),
  [user, status]
);
```

Actions context should depend only on **stable callbacks** - never inline `() => signOut()` in the value object without `useCallback`.

### use-context-selector

For many subscribers needing different slices, `use-context-selector` avoids manual `useSyncExternalStore`:

```bash
npx expo install use-context-selector
```

```tsx
import { createContext, useContextSelector } from "use-context-selector";
 
const SessionContext = createContext<SessionState>({ user: null, status: "anonymous" });
 
export function useUserId() {
  return useContextSelector(SessionContext, (s) => s.user?.id);
}
```

### When to Graduate to Zustand

| Signal | Action |
| --- | --- |
| 5+ contexts nested at root | Flatten with Zustand slices |
| High-frequency updates (cart qty) | Zustand selectors |
| Profiler shows Context consumers > 20ms | Measure, then migrate hottest slice |

### Context vs Query

| Data | Tool |
| --- | --- |
| User session token / id | Context + secure store |
| User profile bio, avatar URL | `useQuery(["profile", id])` |
| Theme preference | Context or Zustand + persistence |

## Gotchas

* **Single context with { state, dispatch, extras }** - Every dispatch re-renders readers of `extras`. **Fix:** Split state and actions.
* **Inline functions in provider value** - `signOut: () => setUser(null)` breaks `React.memo`. **Fix:** `useCallback`.
* **Storing fetched arrays in Context** - Refetch updates re-render the tree. **Fix:** TanStack Query.
* **Provider inside FlatList renderItem** - N providers per row. **Fix:** One provider at `app/_layout.tsx`.
* **Default context value with real data** - `createContext({ user: guest })` masks missing provider. **Fix:** `null` + throw in hook.
* **useSyncExternalStore selector without store subscription** - Example above still re-renders when parent context updates - true fine-grained needs external store (Zustand/Jotai).
* **Passing entire API client in Context** - Stable but encourages fat context. **Fix:** Module singleton or DI - see [dependency injection](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/dependency-injection-in-rn/).

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Split Context | Theme, session, rare updates | Cart qty changing per second |
| use-context-selector | Many slices, stay dependency-free-ish | Team already standardized on Zustand |
| Zustand | Global client state + selectors | Two values total in the app |
| TanStack Query | Server lists and details | Theme toggle |
| Expo Router params | Shareable filter/tab state | Auth tokens |

## FAQs

Is React Context slow on React Native?

Context itself is fast - **unnecessary consumers** are slow. Split contexts, memoize values, and avoid putting high-frequency state in Context.

How many providers at root is too many?

Three to five well-scoped providers is normal (`Query`, `Session`, `Theme`, `SafeArea`). More than eight nested suggests consolidation.

Should I use Context for React Navigation theme?

Expo Router / React Navigation accept a `theme` prop on the root navigator - often simpler than custom Context for colors alone.

Context vs Zustand for auth?

Both work. Context + `expo-secure-store` adapter is common. Zustand helps when many selectors read auth-adjacent UI flags - see [ADR Decision 7](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/adr-state-management-selection/).

How do I test providers?

Wrap with `SessionProvider` in tests; mock secure store at boundary. Prefer testing hooks with `renderHook` and stubbed context values.

Does React 19 improve Context?

React 19 continues concurrent rendering - context consumers still re-render when value changes. Splitting and selectors remain best practice on RN 0.86.

Can I combine useReducer with Context?

Yes - `useReducer` in provider, split dispatch into actions context. Pattern matches Redux without the dependency.

What about React.memo on list items?

Memo helps only if props are stable. Fix the provider first - memo on 200 rows is a band-aid on a storm.

Should locale live in Context?

Yes - i18n direction and strings change infrequently. Pair with `expo-localization` for device default; persist user override in AsyncStorage.

How do I debug re-render storms?

React DevTools Profiler → record interaction → find cascading renders from one context provider. Flip one split at a time.

Is passing dispatch via Context OK?

`dispatch` is stable - safe in actions context. Consumers that only dispatch never need state context.

When is one combined context acceptable?

Prototypes and apps with <10 screens where profiler shows no list jank. Refactor before shipping long lists.

# State Management Highlights Summary

Every highlight bullet from the 9 pages in this section, gathered on one page and grouped by the page it came from.

Highlights / State Management Highlights Summary

* Classify state first: server, client UI, URL/navigation, form - then pick a tool
* useState fits toggles, counters, and single-screen selections
* One Context value object forces every consumer to re-render on any field change
* No provider tree - import useStore hook anywhere in the JS bundle
* Adopt when audit trails, middleware, and DevTools are organizational requirements
* Query owns API data - loading, error, cache, dedupe, and background refresh

## [State Management Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/state-management/state-management-basics/)

* Classify state first: server, client UI, URL/navigation, form - then pick a tool
* TanStack Query owns API data; Zustand or useState own client UI that survives screen changes
* Expo Router search params are URL state - prefer them over global stores for filters
* Intermittent networks need stale-while-revalidate, not spinners on every tab focus
* Default greenfield stack: Query + Zustand (or Context) + Router params
* One global store per domain beats a single god object for the whole app
* Secure tokens belong in expo-secure-store - not Query cache or Redux persist

## [useState & useReducer](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/state-management/usestate-and-usereducer/)

* useState fits toggles, counters, and single-screen selections
* useReducer groups related transitions - forms, wizards, and step machines
* Dispatch is stable in React 19 - safe to omit from effect deps
* Keep server data in TanStack Query - not in reducer initial state from fetch
* Colocate reducers beside the screen that owns the workflow
* useActionState is web-centric; mobile forms still use Hook Form or useReducer

## [Context Without Storms](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/state-management/context-without-storms/)

* One Context value object forces every consumer to re-render on any field change
* Split by update frequency: ThemeContext vs SessionContext vs ActionsContext
* Memoize provider value with useMemo - stable action callbacks with useCallback
* use-context-selector or Zustand when many components need one slice
* Context fits theme, locale, and session - not API catalog caches
* Measure with React DevTools Profiler before adding a global store

## [Zustand](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/state-management/zustand/)

* No provider tree - import useStore hook anywhere in the JS bundle
* Selectors prevent list screens from re-rendering on unrelated slice updates
* One store per domain: cart, preferences, onboarding flags
* persist middleware + AsyncStorage for non-secret preferences only
* devtools middleware works with Flipper / Redux DevTools adapters in dev
* Reset store state in tests with useStore.setState(initial)

## [Redux Toolkit](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/state-management/redux-toolkit/)

* Adopt when audit trails, middleware, and DevTools are organizational requirements
* createSlice reduces Redux boilerplate - immer-powered reducers by default
* RTK Query is optional - prefer TanStack Query unless already on Redux
* configureStore sets up DevTools and thunk middleware in one call
* One slice per feature domain - avoid a single orders-and-ui-and-auth monolith
* Test reducers as pure functions; integration tests use mock store factory

## [TanStack Query](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/state-management/tanstack-query/)

* Query owns API data - loading, error, cache, dedupe, and background refresh
* staleTime controls how long cached data stays fresh without refetching
* gcTime controls how long inactive cache remains in memory after unmount
* onlineManager + NetInfo and focusManager + AppState wire mobile lifecycle
* persistQueryClient with AsyncStorage or expo-sqlite for offline reads
* Mutations use onMutate for optimistic UI with automatic rollback on error

## [Jotai & Atomic State](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/state-management/jotai-and-atomic-state/)

* Atoms are minimal units of state - components subscribe only to atoms they use
* Derived atoms compute from other atoms without manual dependency arrays
* Fine-grained updates help canvas editors, builders, and multi-panel dashboards
* No provider required for atoms - Provider only for store scope in tests
* Prefer Zustand unless the team already thinks in atomic graphs
* Keep server data in TanStack Query - atoms for client UI composition

## [State Persistence & Hydration](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/state-management/state-persistence-and-hydration/)

* Cold start UX: show last good UI while stores rehydrate asynchronously
* Gate navigation on session hydration - not on every Zustand preference read
* expo-secure-store for access tokens; AsyncStorage for non-sensitive prefs
* persistQueryClient dehydrates server cache - clear on logout
* Avoid hydration flash with PersistGate pattern or splash hold until ready
* Version persisted schemas - migrate or bump storage keys on breaking changes

## [State Management Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/state-management/best-practices/)

* Classify state before choosing a library: server, client, URL, form, secrets
* Default stack: TanStack Query + Zustand (or Context) + Expo Router params
* Never store API catalogs in global client stores - Query owns server state
* Wire focusManager and onlineManager for mobile lifecycle on day one
* Hydrate session and prefs before routing to avoid flash of wrong screen
* Document the team choice in an ADR before the third global store appears

Dokumen: Redux Toolkit

# Redux Toolkit

Predictable state for large teams and time-travel debugging. Redux Toolkit (RTK) pays off when **compliance**, **middleware ecosystems**, or **existing Redux investment** demand centralized reducers. For greenfield Expo SDK 57 apps, default to TanStack Query + Zustand unless an ADR mandates RTK.

Highlights / Redux Toolkit

* Adopt when audit trails, middleware, and DevTools are organizational requirements
* createSlice reduces Redux boilerplate - immer-powered reducers by default
* RTK Query is optional - prefer TanStack Query unless already on Redux
* configureStore sets up DevTools and thunk middleware in one call
* One slice per feature domain - avoid a single orders-and-ui-and-auth monolith
* Test reducers as pure functions; integration tests use mock store factory

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
npx expo install @reduxjs/toolkit react-redux
```

```tsx
// src/app/store.ts
import { configureStore } from "@reduxjs/toolkit";
import { cartSlice } from "@/features/cart/cartSlice";
import { checkoutSlice } from "@/features/checkout/checkoutSlice";
 
export const store = configureStore({
  reducer: {
    cart: cartSlice.reducer,
    checkout: checkoutSlice.reducer,
  },
  devTools: __DEV__,
});
 
export type RootState = ReturnType<typeof store.getState>;
export type AppDispatch = typeof store.dispatch;
```

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx
import { Provider } from "react-redux";
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
import { store } from "@/app/store";
 
export default function RootLayout() {
  return (
    <Provider store={store}>
      <Stack />
    </Provider>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// features/cart/cartSlice.ts
import { createSlice, PayloadAction } from "@reduxjs/toolkit";
 
type CartItem = { productId: string; qty: number };
 
type CartState = { items: CartItem[] };
 
const initialState: CartState = { items: [] };
 
export const cartSlice = createSlice({
  name: "cart",
  initialState,
  reducers: {
    addItem(state, action: PayloadAction<CartItem>) {
      state.items.push(action.payload);
    },
    clearCart(state) {
      state.items = [];
    },
  },
});
 
export const { addItem, clearCart } = cartSlice.actions;
```

```tsx
// Typed hooks
import { TypedUseSelectorHook, useDispatch, useSelector } from "react-redux";
import type { AppDispatch, RootState } from "@/app/store";
 
export const useAppDispatch = () => useDispatch<AppDispatch>();
export const useAppSelector: TypedUseSelectorHook<RootState> = useSelector;
```

**When to reach for this:**

* **Regulated domains** need action logs and replay (fintech, healthcare workflows).
* **Multiple teams** already standardized on Redux patterns and training materials.
* **Middleware** requirements: analytics per action, crash breadcrumbs, offline queue integration.
* **RTK Query** is acceptable when **entire app** is on Redux - otherwise use TanStack Query.
* ADR explicitly ranks RTK over Zustand - see [ADR](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/adr-state-management-selection/).

## Working Example

```tsx
// checkoutSlice.ts - multi-step client workflow with explicit actions
import { createSlice, PayloadAction } from "@reduxjs/toolkit";
 
type Step = "cart" | "shipping" | "payment" | "done";
 
type CheckoutState = {
  step: Step;
  shippingId: string | null;
  error: string | null;
};
 
const initialState: CheckoutState = {
  step: "cart",
  shippingId: null,
  error: null,
};
 
export const checkoutSlice = createSlice({
  name: "checkout",
  initialState,
  reducers: {
    setStep(state, action: PayloadAction<Step>) {
      state.step = action.payload;
      state.error = null;
    },
    selectShipping(state, action: PayloadAction<string>) {
      state.shippingId = action.payload;
    },
    setError(state, action: PayloadAction<string>) {
      state.error = action.payload;
    },
    resetCheckout() {
      return initialState;
    },
  },
});
 
export const { setStep, selectShipping, setError, resetCheckout } = checkoutSlice.actions;
```

```tsx
// CheckoutScreen.tsx - server shipping methods via TanStack Query; steps via Redux
import { useQuery } from "@tanstack/react-query";
import { Pressable, Text, View } from "react-native";
import { useAppDispatch, useAppSelector } from "@/app/hooks";
import { addItem, clearCart } from "@/features/cart/cartSlice";
import { resetCheckout, selectShipping, setStep } from "@/features/checkout/checkoutSlice";
 
function fetchShippingMethods() {
  return Promise.resolve([
    { id: "standard", label: "Standard" },
    { id: "express", label: "Express" },
  ]);
}
 
export function CheckoutScreen() {
  const dispatch = useAppDispatch();
  const step = useAppSelector((s) => s.checkout.step);
  const shippingId = useAppSelector((s) => s.checkout.shippingId);
  const cartCount = useAppSelector((s) => s.cart.items.length);
 
  const { data: methods = [] } = useQuery({
    queryKey: ["shipping-methods"],
    queryFn: fetchShippingMethods,
    enabled: step === "shipping",
  });
 
  return (
    <View style={{ padding: 16, gap: 8 }}>
      <Text>Step: {step}</Text>
      <Text>Cart items: {cartCount}</Text>
 
      {step === "cart" && (
        <Pressable
          onPress={() => {
            dispatch(addItem({ productId: "demo", qty: 1 }));
            dispatch(setStep("shipping"));
          }}
        >
          <Text>Continue to shipping</Text>
        </Pressable>
      )}
 
      {step === "shipping" &&
        methods.map((m) => (
          <Pressable
            key={m.id}
            onPress={() => {
              dispatch(selectShipping(m.id));
              dispatch(setStep("payment"));
            }}
          >
            <Text style={{ fontWeight: shippingId === m.id ? "700" : "400" }}>{m.label}</Text>
          </Pressable>
        ))}
 
      {step === "payment" && (
        <Pressable
          onPress={() => {
            dispatch(clearCart());
            dispatch(resetCheckout());
          }}
        >
          <Text>Pay (demo)</Text>
        </Pressable>
      )}
    </View>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// checkoutSlice.test.ts
import { checkoutSlice, setStep } from "./checkoutSlice";
 
test("setStep clears error", () => {
  const state = checkoutSlice.reducer(
    { step: "cart", shippingId: null, error: "fail" },
    setStep("shipping")
  );
  expect(state.step).toBe("shipping");
  expect(state.error).toBeNull();
});
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* **RTK slices** encode checkout transitions - auditable action names in DevTools.
* **TanStack Query** still owns **shipping methods** from API - not duplicated in Redux.
* **Typed hooks** prevent dispatching wrong action shapes.
* **Reducer tests** run without React - fast CI signal.
* **resetCheckout** returns initial state on completion - clear domain boundary.

## Deep Dive

### configureStore Defaults

`configureStore` adds:

* Redux Thunk middleware for async logic
* DevTools integration in development
* Immutability and serializability checks (warn in dev)

Disable noisy checks for persist actions if needed:

```tsx
middleware: (getDefaultMiddleware) =>
  getDefaultMiddleware({
    serializableCheck: { ignoredActions: ["persist/PERSIST"] },
  }),
```

### RTK Query (Optional)

If the org mandates Redux for all data:

```tsx
import { createApi, fetchBaseQuery } from "@reduxjs/toolkit/query/react";
 
export const api = createApi({
  reducerPath: "api",
  baseQuery: fetchBaseQuery({ baseUrl: "https://api.example.com" }),
  endpoints: (builder) => ({
    getOrders: builder.query<Order[], void>({ query: () => "/orders" }),
  }),
});
 
// store reducer: { [api.reducerPath]: api.reducer }
// middleware: getDefaultMiddleware().concat(api.middleware)
```

**Prefer TanStack Query** on new Expo apps unless RTK is already everywhere - two cache layers fight each other.

### Time-Travel Debugging

1. Run app in dev with Redux DevTools (Flipper plugin or remote debugger).
2. Dispatch actions - state tree updates per slice.
3. Jump to prior action - reproduce bug reports with exact sequence.

Critical for **audit** scenarios where support must replay user steps.

### Entity Adapter (Lists)

```tsx
import { createEntityAdapter, createSlice } from "@reduxjs/toolkit";
 
const ordersAdapter = createEntityAdapter<Order>();
 
const ordersSlice = createSlice({
  name: "orders",
  initialState: ordersAdapter.getInitialState(),
  reducers: {
    ordersLoaded: ordersAdapter.setAll,
    orderUpdated: ordersAdapter.updateOne,
  },
});
```

Still prefer Query for server lists unless offline middleware requires normalized Redux entities.

### Listener Middleware

React to actions without coupling slices:

```tsx
import { createListenerMiddleware } from "@reduxjs/toolkit";
 
const listenerMiddleware = createListenerMiddleware();
 
listenerMiddleware.startListening({
  actionCreator: clearCart,
  effect: async (_action, listenerApi) => {
    listenerApi.dispatch(resetCheckout());
  },
});
```

## Gotchas

* **Fetching in components into Redux on every mount** - Duplicates Query. **Fix:** Query for server; Redux for client workflow only.
* **Giant root reducer** - One slice file per feature. **Fix:** `combineReducers` via `configureStore` reducer map.
* **Non-serializable values in state** - `Date`, class instances break DevTools. **Fix:** Store ISO strings; map in selectors.
* **useSelector without equality fn** - Returning new objects re-renders often. **Fix:** Select primitives or use `shallowEqual`.
* **redux-persist with tokens in AsyncStorage** - Security review failure. **Fix:** Secure store for secrets; see persistence guide.
* **Installing RTK "just in case"** - Bundle and boilerplate tax. **Fix:** ADR before adoption.
* **Two server caches** - RTK Query + TanStack Query for same endpoints. **Fix:** Pick one.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Redux Toolkit | Audit, middleware, team standards | Cart + theme only |
| Zustand | Lightweight global client state | Mandated action logs |
| TanStack Query | Server state (default) | Checkout step machine alone |
| useReducer + Context | Small shared UI | Cross-feature audited ledger |
| Event sourcing | Compliance immutable log | Typical consumer app |

## FAQs

RTK vs Zustand bundle size?

RTK + react-redux is larger than Zustand. Justified when DevTools and middleware are required - not for a badge counter.

Should new Expo apps start with Redux?

No - default Query + Zustand per [ADR Decision 10](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/adr-state-management-selection/). Adopt RTK when requirements appear.

RTK Query vs TanStack Query?

Feature parity is close. TanStack Query has stronger Expo/mobile docs in this site. RTK Query when reducers already own the app.

How do I type useSelector?

Export `RootState` from store; use `TypedUseSelectorHook<RootState>` - see recipe typed hooks.

Async thunks still?

`createAsyncThunk` works. Many teams use Query mutations instead of thunks for network - thunks for complex multi-slice orchestration.

Redux DevTools on physical device?

Use Flipper Redux plugin or remote JS debugging. Production builds disable DevTools via `devTools: __DEV__`.

How to test connected screens?

```tsx
import { Provider } from "react-redux";
import { configureStore } from "@reduxjs/toolkit";
 
const store = configureStore({ reducer: { cart: cartSlice.reducer } });
render(<Provider store={store}><CheckoutScreen /></Provider>);
```

Can slices live in feature folders?

Yes - `features/cart/cartSlice.ts` imported into `app/store.ts`. Keeps features modular.

Immer already inside createSlice?

Yes - mutate `state` in reducers; Immer produces immutable updates.

Logout sequence?

Dispatch `resetCheckout`, `clearCart`, and `api.util.resetApiState()` if using RTK Query; plus `queryClient.clear()` if TanStack Query coexists during migration.

Migrating from Redux to Zustand?

Slice-by-slice - move read-heavy UI to Query first, then client slices to Zustand. Run [refactoring checklist](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/refactoring-checklist/).

Expo Router with Redux?

Single `Provider` in `app/_layout.tsx`. Routes dispatch actions; avoid store imports in shared entity types.

## Related

* [useState & useReducer](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/state-management/usestate-and-usereducer/) - local workflow before Redux
