Dokumen: State Management Basics
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/state-management/state-management-basics/

# State Management Basics

10 examples to get you started with State Management - 7 basic and 3 intermediate. Mobile users lose signal constantly; classify state before picking a library.

Highlights / State Management Basics

* Classify state first: server, client UI, URL/navigation, form - then pick a tool
* TanStack Query owns API data; Zustand or useState own client UI that survives screen changes
* Expo Router search params are URL state - prefer them over global stores for filters
* Intermittent networks need stale-while-revalidate, not spinners on every tab focus
* Default greenfield stack: Query + Zustand (or Context) + Router params
* One global store per domain beats a single god object for the whole app
* Secure tokens belong in expo-secure-store - not Query cache or Redux persist

## Prerequisites

Scaffold a production-shaped Expo app with an explicit SDK 57 pin. State examples assume Expo Router and TypeScript.

```bash
npx create-expo-app@latest MyApp --template default@sdk-57
cd MyApp
npm install
```

Confirm the SDK pin before adding state libraries:

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "expo": "~57.0.4",
    "react": "19.2.3",
    "react-native": "0.86.0"
  }
}
```

Install the default server-state layer most teams adopt on day one:

```bash
npx expo install @tanstack/react-query @react-native-community/netinfo
```

> **Tooling:** These examples target **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4), **React Native 0.86.0**, and **React 19.2.3**.

---

## Basic Examples

### 1. Local State for Ephemeral UI

Modal open, sheet expanded, pressed tab index - state that dies when the screen unmounts belongs in **`useState`** on that screen.

```tsx
// app/(tabs)/catalog/index.tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { Modal, Pressable, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
export default function CatalogScreen() {
  const [filterOpen, setFilterOpen] = useState(false);
 
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1, padding: 16 }}>
      <Pressable onPress={() => setFilterOpen(true)}>
        <Text>Filters</Text>
      </Pressable>
 
      <Modal visible={filterOpen} animationType="slide" onRequestClose={() => setFilterOpen(false)}>
        <View style={{ flex: 1, padding: 24 }}>
          <Text>Filter sheet - local state only</Text>
          <Pressable onPress={() => setFilterOpen(false)}>
            <Text>Close</Text>
          </Pressable>
        </View>
      </Modal>
    </View>
  );
}
```

* **`filterOpen`** does not need Redux, Zustand, or Context - no other screen reads it
* Unmounting the screen resets state automatically - no manual cleanup
* If three sibling components on the **same screen** need it, lift state to a parent or a screen-level hook - still not global

> **Related:** [useState & useReducer](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/state-management/usestate-and-usereducer/) - when local state outgrows a single screen

---

### 2. Props vs Owned State

**Props** flow down; **state** is owned by the component that updates it. Mobile list items should stay presentational.

```tsx
// src/features/catalog/components/ProductRow.tsx
import { Pressable, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
type Props = {
  title: string;
  priceLabel: string;
  selected: boolean;
  onPress: () => void;
};
 
export function ProductRow({ title, priceLabel, selected, onPress }: Props) {
  return (
    <Pressable onPress={onPress} style={{ padding: 12, backgroundColor: selected ? "#e0f2fe" : "#fff" }}>
      <Text style={{ fontWeight: "600" }}>{title}</Text>
      <Text>{priceLabel}</Text>
    </Pressable>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// Parent owns selection state
import { useState } from "react";
import { FlatList } from "react-native";
import { ProductRow } from "@/features/catalog/components/ProductRow";
 
const PRODUCTS = [
  { id: "1", title: "Trail Pack", priceLabel: "$89" },
  { id: "2", title: "Day Pack", priceLabel: "$49" },
];
 
export function ProductList() {
  const [selectedId, setSelectedId] = useState<string | null>(null);
 
  return (
    <FlatList
      data={PRODUCTS}
      keyExtractor={(item) => item.id}
      renderItem={({ item }) => (
        <ProductRow
          title={item.title}
          priceLabel={item.priceLabel}
          selected={selectedId === item.id}
          onPress={() => setSelectedId(item.id)}
        />
      )}
    />
  );
}
```

* **`ProductRow`** has no `useState` - re-renders only when props change
* Parent **`selectedId`** is the single source of truth for highlight state
* Passing **`onPress`** keeps navigation and side effects in the container layer

> **Related:** [../component-patterns/container-presenter-on-mobile/container-presenter-on-mobile.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/container-presenter-on-mobile/) - split data hooks from JSX

---

### 3. Server State vs Client State

**Server state** comes from an API and goes stale. **Client state** is UI the user controls. Mixing them in one `useState` blob causes refetch bugs.

```tsx
// ❌ Anti-pattern - API data in useState with manual useEffect
const [orders, setOrders] = useState<Order[]>([]);
const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true);
 
useEffect(() => {
  fetch("/orders")
    .then((r) => r.json())
    .then(setOrders)
    .finally(() => setLoading(false));
}, []);
```

```tsx
// ✅ Server state in TanStack Query; client state stays local
import { useQuery } from "@tanstack/react-query";
import { useState } from "react";
 
function OrdersScreen() {
  const [sort, setSort] = useState<"newest" | "oldest">("newest");
 
  const { data: orders = [], isPending, isError, refetch } = useQuery({
    queryKey: ["orders"],
    queryFn: fetchOrders,
    staleTime: 60_000,
  });
 
  const sorted = [...orders].sort((a, b) =>
    sort === "newest" ? b.placedAt.localeCompare(a.placedAt) : a.placedAt.localeCompare(b.placedAt)
  );
 
  // render sorted, isPending, isError, refetch, setSort...
}
```

* **`orders`** are server-owned - cache, dedupe, and background refresh belong in Query
* **`sort`** is client-owned - no network round-trip when the user toggles
* Pull-to-refresh calls **`refetch()`** - not a manual `setOrders`

> **Related:** [TanStack Query](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/state-management/tanstack-query/) - cache policies for mobile | [../architecture-design/adr-state-management-selection/adr-state-management-selection.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/adr-state-management-selection/) - decision matrix

---

### 4. Global Client State (When Screens Share It)

Cart badge, theme mode, onboarding completion - state that **survives navigation** but is not API data fits a small global store or split Context.

```tsx
// src/features/cart/useCartStore.ts
import { create } from "zustand";
 
type CartItem = { productId: string; qty: number };
 
type CartStore = {
  items: CartItem[];
  add: (item: CartItem) => void;
  count: () => number;
};
 
export const useCartStore = create<CartStore>((set, get) => ({
  items: [],
  add: (item) => set((s) => ({ items: [...s.items, item] })),
  count: () => get().items.reduce((n, i) => n + i.qty, 0),
}));
```

```tsx
// Tab bar reads count via selector - not the whole store
import { useCartStore } from "@/features/cart/useCartStore";
import { Text, View } from "react-native";
 
export function CartTabIcon() {
  const count = useCartStore((s) => s.count());
  return (
    <View>
      <Text>Cart</Text>
      {count > 0 && <Text>{count}</Text>}
    </View>
  );
}
```

* **Zustand selectors** limit re-renders - tab icon updates without re-rendering the catalog list
* Do not put **fetched product catalog** in this store - that is server state
* Install with **`npx expo install zustand`** - pure JS, no native module

> **Related:** [Zustand](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/state-management/zustand/) - slices, devtools, and tests

---

### 5. URL State with Expo Router

Filters, tabs, and pagination that should restore on deep link belong in **route search params** - not a global store.

```tsx
// app/(tabs)/catalog/index.tsx
import { router, useLocalSearchParams } from "expo-router";
import { Pressable, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
type Params = { category?: string };
 
export default function CatalogRoute() {
  const { category = "all" } = useLocalSearchParams<Params>();
 
  return (
    <View style={{ padding: 16, gap: 8 }}>
      <Text>Category: {category}</Text>
      {(["all", "gear", "apparel"] as const).map((c) => (
        <Pressable key={c} onPress={() => router.setParams({ category: c })}>
          <Text style={{ fontWeight: category === c ? "700" : "400" }}>{c}</Text>
        </Pressable>
      ))}
    </View>
  );
}
```

* **`useLocalSearchParams`** reads the current route's query string equivalent
* **`router.setParams`** updates params without losing stack position - OS back restores prior filter
* Shareable links (`myapp://catalog?category=gear`) work when **`scheme`** is set in `app.config.ts`

> **Related:** [Typed Routes](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/typed-routes/) - typed params in SDK 57

---

### 6. Intermittent Networks and Stale Data

On mobile, assume the user is offline in an elevator. Show **last good data** with a subtle offline banner - not a blank screen.

```tsx
import NetInfo from "@react-native-community/netinfo";
import { onlineManager, useQuery } from "@tanstack/react-query";
import { useEffect } from "react";
import { Text, View } from "react-native";
 
onlineManager.setEventListener((setOnline) =>
  NetInfo.addEventListener((state) => setOnline(!!state.isConnected))
);
 
function ProductList() {
  const { data, isPending, isFetching, isError } = useQuery({
    queryKey: ["products"],
    queryFn: fetchProducts,
    staleTime: 5 * 60_000,
    gcTime: 24 * 60 * 60_000,
    retry: 2,
  });
 
  const showOfflineCache = !isPending && data && isError;
 
  return (
    <View>
      {showOfflineCache && <Text>Offline - showing saved results</Text>}
      {isFetching && !isPending && <Text>Updating…</Text>}
      {/* render data */}
    </View>
  );
}
```

* **`staleTime`** keeps cached data visible while a background refetch runs
* **`onlineManager`** tells Query when the device reconnects - triggers `refetchOnReconnect`
* **`gcTime`** (formerly `cacheTime`) controls how long unused cache survives in memory

> **Related:** [TanStack Query](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/state-management/tanstack-query/) - `focusManager` on AppState | [../error-resilience/network-failure-ux/network-failure-ux.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/error-resilience/network-failure-ux/) - offline UX patterns

---

### 7. Root Provider Tree (Minimal)

Wire server-state and session providers once in **`app/_layout.tsx`** - avoid nesting providers per screen.

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx
import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from "@tanstack/react-query";
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
import { useState } from "react";
import { SessionProvider } from "@/features/auth/SessionProvider";
 
export default function RootLayout() {
  const [queryClient] = useState(
    () =>
      new QueryClient({
        defaultOptions: {
          queries: { staleTime: 30_000, retry: 2 },
        },
      })
  );
 
  return (
    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
      <SessionProvider>
        <Stack screenOptions={{ headerShown: false }} />
      </SessionProvider>
    </QueryClientProvider>
  );
}
```

* **`QueryClient`** is created once per app session - `useState(() => new QueryClient())` avoids sharing between tests and prod accidentally in the same module
* **`SessionProvider`** exposes auth identity - tokens live behind `expo-secure-store`, not in Query cache
* Keep the tree **flat** - deep provider nesting slows cold start and complicates tests

> **Related:** [Context Without Storms](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/state-management/context-without-storms/) - split contexts when providers re-render too much

---

## Intermediate Examples

### 8. Splitting Server and Client in One Screen

A checkout screen combines **cart (client)**, **shipping options (server)**, and **selected method (client)**. Three buckets, three tools.

```tsx
import { useQuery } from "@tanstack/react-query";
import { useState } from "react";
import { useCartStore } from "@/features/cart/useCartStore";
 
export function CheckoutScreen() {
  const items = useCartStore((s) => s.items);
  const [shippingId, setShippingId] = useState<string | null>(null);
 
  const { data: methods = [], isPending } = useQuery({
    queryKey: ["shipping-methods", items.length],
    queryFn: () => fetchShippingMethods(items),
    enabled: items.length > 0,
  });
 
  // UI: cart summary from Zustand, methods from Query, selection from useState
}
```

* **Cart items** are client-global (Zustand) - user added them across screens
* **Shipping methods** depend on cart contents - Query key includes `items.length` for invalidation
* **`shippingId`** is ephemeral UI on this screen - `useState` until submit, then mutation

> **Related:** [../architecture-design/clean-architecture-on-mobile/clean-architecture-on-mobile.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/clean-architecture-on-mobile/) - use cases vs hooks

---

### 9. Last-Known-Good on Cold Start

Persist Query cache to AsyncStorage so catalog screens render immediately after process kill - hydrate before first paint when possible.

```tsx
// src/lib/queryPersister.ts
import AsyncStorage from "@react-native-async-storage/async-storage";
import { createAsyncStoragePersister } from "@tanstack/query-async-storage-persister";
 
export const asyncStoragePersister = createAsyncStoragePersister({
  storage: AsyncStorage,
  key: "REACT_QUERY_OFFLINE_CACHE",
});
```

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx (excerpt)
import { PersistQueryClientProvider } from "@tanstack/react-query-persist-client";
import { asyncStoragePersister } from "@/lib/queryPersister";
 
<PersistQueryClientProvider
  client={queryClient}
  persistOptions={{ persister: asyncStoragePersister, maxAge: 1000 * 60 * 60 * 24 }}
>
  {children}
</PersistQueryClientProvider>
```

```bash
npx expo install @react-native-async-storage/async-storage @tanstack/react-query-persist-client @tanstack/query-async-storage-persister
```

* **`maxAge`** caps how old persisted cache can be - pair with `staleTime` per query
* Show a **hydration gate** or skeleton only when no persisted data exists - see persistence guide
* Logout must **`queryClient.clear()`** and wipe the persister - stale user data is a security bug

> **Related:** [State Persistence & Hydration](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/state-management/state-persistence-and-hydration/) - cold-start without jank

---

### 10. Decision Checklist Before Adding a Library

Run this checklist when a teammate proposes Redux, Jotai, or another store.

```text
State checklist (answer before npm install):
 
1. Is it from an API?           → TanStack Query (or RTK Query if Redux already)
2. Is it shareable in a URL?    → Expo Router search params
3. Is it a multi-field form?    → React Hook Form + mutation on submit
4. Is it global client UI?      → Zustand or split Context
5. Is it ephemeral on one screen? → useState / useReducer
6. Is it a secret token?        → expo-secure-store + thin SessionProvider
7. Does compliance need audit?  → Redux Toolkit + DevTools
 
If two libraries answer the same "yes" - pick one and document in an ADR.
```

```tsx
// Document the team default in a comment or ADR link at the store boundary
/** @see docs/adr-state-management - server: Query, client: Zustand, URL: Router */
export const usePreferences = create<PreferencesStore>(/* ... */);
```

* **Seven questions** prevent installing three overlapping global stores
* New squads should read the ADR before introducing MobX, Jotai, or a second Query wrapper
* Revisit when requirements change - offline sync, collaborative editing, or mandated DevTools

> **Related:** [../architecture-design/adr-state-management-selection/adr-state-management-selection.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/adr-state-management-selection/) - ranked decisions | [Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/state-management/best-practices/) - section summary

Dokumen: useState & useReducer
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/state-management/usestate-and-usereducer/

# useState & useReducer

When component state is enough on mobile screens. Reach for **`useReducer`** when multiple fields update together - checkout steps, onboarding wizards, and validation-heavy forms. Keep API responses in TanStack Query; reducers own **client UI transitions** only.

Highlights / useState & useReducer

* useState fits toggles, counters, and single-screen selections
* useReducer groups related transitions - forms, wizards, and step machines
* Dispatch is stable in React 19 - safe to omit from effect deps
* Keep server data in TanStack Query - not in reducer initial state from fetch
* Colocate reducers beside the screen that owns the workflow
* useActionState is web-centric; mobile forms still use Hook Form or useReducer

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```tsx
// useState - ephemeral UI on one screen
const [expanded, setExpanded] = useState(false);
```

```tsx
// useReducer - related fields + explicit transitions
type State = { step: 0 | 1 | 2; email: string; error?: string };
type Action =
  | { type: "set_email"; email: string }
  | { type: "next" }
  | { type: "back" }
  | { type: "set_error"; error: string };
 
function reducer(state: State, action: Action): State {
  switch (action.type) {
    case "set_email":
      return { ...state, email: action.email, error: undefined };
    case "next":
      return state.step < 2 ? { ...state, step: (state.step + 1) as State["step"] } : state;
    case "back":
      return state.step > 0 ? { ...state, step: (state.step - 1) as State["step"] } : state;
    case "set_error":
      return { ...state, error: action.error };
    default:
      return state;
  }
}
 
const [state, dispatch] = useReducer(reducer, { step: 0, email: "" });
```

**When to reach for this:**

* State affects **one screen** (or one feature subtree) and unmounts with it.
* Several `useState` calls update in **lockstep** - one reducer replaces five `setX` calls.
* You need **predictable transitions** (wizard back/next) without a global store.
* Form has **few fields** (login) - reducer is enough; large forms use React Hook Form.
* You are **not** caching API lists - that belongs in Query.

## Working Example

```tsx
// OnboardingWizard.tsx - useReducer for steps; useState for a simple toggle
import { useReducer, useState } from "react";
import { Pressable, StyleSheet, Text, TextInput, View } from "react-native";
 
type WizardState = {
  step: 1 | 2 | 3;
  name: string;
  notifications: boolean;
  error?: string;
};
 
type WizardAction =
  | { type: "set_name"; name: string }
  | { type: "toggle_notifications" }
  | { type: "next" }
  | { type: "back" }
  | { type: "submit_error"; error: string }
  | { type: "reset" };
 
const initial: WizardState = { step: 1, name: "", notifications: true };
 
function wizardReducer(state: WizardState, action: WizardAction): WizardState {
  switch (action.type) {
    case "set_name":
      return { ...state, name: action.name, error: undefined };
    case "toggle_notifications":
      return { ...state, notifications: !state.notifications };
    case "next": {
      if (state.step === 1 && state.name.trim().length < 2) {
        return { ...state, error: "Name must be at least 2 characters" };
      }
      return state.step < 3 ? { ...state, step: (state.step + 1) as WizardState["step"], error: undefined } : state;
    }
    case "back":
      return state.step > 1 ? { ...state, step: (state.step - 1) as WizardState["step"], error: undefined } : state;
    case "submit_error":
      return { ...state, error: action.error };
    case "reset":
      return initial;
    default:
      return state;
  }
}
 
export function OnboardingWizard({ onComplete }: { onComplete: (payload: WizardState) => void }) {
  const [state, dispatch] = useReducer(wizardReducer, initial);
  const [submitting, setSubmitting] = useState(false);
 
  async function handleFinish() {
    setSubmitting(true);
    try {
      // await saveProfile(state) - mutation via Query in production apps
      onComplete(state);
      dispatch({ type: "reset" });
    } catch {
      dispatch({ type: "submit_error", error: "Could not save - try again" });
    } finally {
      setSubmitting(false);
    }
  }
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.container}>
      <Text style={styles.title}>Step {state.step} of 3</Text>
      {state.error && <Text style={styles.error}>{state.error}</Text>}
 
      {state.step === 1 && (
        <TextInput
          placeholder="Your name"
          value={state.name}
          onChangeText={(name) => dispatch({ type: "set_name", name })}
          style={styles.input}
        />
      )}
 
      {state.step === 2 && (
        <Pressable onPress={() => dispatch({ type: "toggle_notifications" })}>
          <Text>Notifications: {state.notifications ? "On" : "Off"}</Text>
        </Pressable>
      )}
 
      {state.step === 3 && <Text>Review: {state.name}</Text>}
 
      <View style={styles.row}>
        {state.step > 1 && (
          <Pressable style={styles.btnSecondary} onPress={() => dispatch({ type: "back" })}>
            <Text>Back</Text>
          </Pressable>
        )}
        {state.step < 3 ? (
          <Pressable style={styles.btn} onPress={() => dispatch({ type: "next" })}>
            <Text style={styles.btnLabel}>Next</Text>
          </Pressable>
        ) : (
          <Pressable style={styles.btn} onPress={handleFinish} disabled={submitting}>
            <Text style={styles.btnLabel}>{submitting ? "Saving…" : "Finish"}</Text>
          </Pressable>
        )}
      </View>
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  container: { padding: 20, gap: 12 },
  title: { fontSize: 22, fontWeight: "700" },
  error: { color: "#dc2626" },
  input: { borderWidth: 1, borderColor: "#cbd5e1", padding: 12, borderRadius: 8 },
  row: { flexDirection: "row", gap: 8, marginTop: 8 },
  btn: { backgroundColor: "#2563eb", padding: 14, borderRadius: 8, flex: 1 },
  btnSecondary: { padding: 14, borderRadius: 8, borderWidth: 1, borderColor: "#94a3b8" },
  btnLabel: { color: "#fff", fontWeight: "600", textAlign: "center" },
});
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* **`useReducer`** owns step, name, notifications, and validation error - one transition function.
* **`useState(submitting)`** stays separate - async pending is orthogonal to wizard data.
* **Validation runs in the reducer** on `next` - impossible states (step 4) never exist.
* **`reset`** returns a known initial object - testable and idempotent.
* **Network submit** stays outside the reducer - dispatch only records success/failure UI.

## Deep Dive

### When useState Is Enough

| Pattern | Example | Why useState |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Boolean UI | Modal open, accordion | One value, one setter |
| Single selection | Highlighted list row | Parent holds `selectedId` |
| Counter | Quantity stepper | `setQty((q) => q + 1)` is clear |
| Text filter (local) | Search box before debounced Query | Ephemeral until submit |

### When useReducer Wins

| Pattern | Example | Why reducer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Wizard / steps | Onboarding, KYC | `next`/`back` encode rules |
| Form with cross-field rules | Password + confirm | One action updates multiple fields |
| State machine | Upload: idle → uploading → done | Finite transitions |
| Undo batch | Draft editor | Single `RESET` action |

### Dispatch Stability (React 19)

`dispatch` from `useReducer` is **stable** for the component lifetime - omit it from `useEffect` dependency arrays. Same for `setState` from `useState`. The [react-hooks lint rules](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/linting-formatting/react-hooks-lint-rules/) document this.

### Lazy Initialization

```tsx
const [state, dispatch] = useReducer(reducer, props.initialStep, (step) => ({
  step,
  email: "",
  notifications: true,
}));
```

Pass a third argument when initial state is expensive to compute - runs once on mount.

### Colocation Rule

Keep `wizardReducer` in the same file as `OnboardingWizard` until a second screen needs identical transitions. Promote to `features/onboarding/wizardReducer.ts` only on reuse - not preemptively.

### Server Data Boundary

```tsx
// ❌ Do not hydrate reducer from fetch in useEffect
useEffect(() => {
  fetchProfile().then((p) => dispatch({ type: "load_profile", profile: p }));
}, []);
 
// ✅ Query owns profile; reducer owns edit draft
const { data: profile } = useQuery({ queryKey: ["profile"], queryFn: fetchProfile });
const [draft, dispatch] = useReducer(editReducer, profile ?? emptyDraft);
```

Sync draft from Query with a keyed remount or explicit `reset` when `profile.id` changes - not on every render.

## Gotchas

* **Many unrelated `useState` calls** - Five booleans for one form means missed updates. **Fix:** One `useReducer` or React Hook Form.
* **Mutating state inside reducer** - `state.items.push(x)` breaks React. **Fix:** Return new objects: `{ ...state, items: [...state.items, x] }`.
* **Reducer side effects** - Fetching inside `switch` makes testing hard. **Fix:** Side effects in event handlers; reducer stays pure.
* **Storing API lists in reducer** - Duplicates TanStack Query cache. **Fix:** Query for server data; reducer for UI-only draft.
* **Lifting reducer too high** - Wizard state in root Context re-renders the app. **Fix:** Keep reducer on the wizard screen until another route truly needs it.
* **Missing `default` case** - TypeScript exhaustiveness helps; runtime unknown actions should return `state`.
* **Functional updates with reducer** - Reducers already receive previous state - do not nest `setState` patterns inside.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `useState` | 1–2 independent values | Many coupled fields |
| `useReducer` | Wizards, small forms, state machines | Global cart across tabs |
| React Hook Form | Large forms, validation schemas | Single email field |
| Zustand | Global client state with selectors | Ephemeral modal on one screen |
| XState | Complex audited workflows | Simple three-step onboarding |

## FAQs

useState or useReducer for a login form?

Two fields (email, password) - `useState` is fine. If you add remember-me, MFA step, and inline validation, switch to `useReducer` or Hook Form.

Can I use useReducer with Context?

Yes - `useReducer` in a provider is the built-in global pattern. Split contexts or Zustand when consumers re-render too often - see [Context Without Storms](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/state-management/context-without-storms/).

Does useReducer replace Redux?

Only for **local** or **small shared** UI state. Redux Toolkit still wins for audited multi-feature domains and DevTools at scale - see [Redux Toolkit](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/state-management/redux-toolkit/).

How do I test a reducer?

Export `wizardReducer` and unit-test actions without rendering:

```tsx
expect(wizardReducer(initial, { type: "next" })).toEqual({ ...initial, error: "Name must be at least 2 characters" });
```

Should submitting be in the reducer?

Keep **`submitting`** as `useState` or derive from `useMutation` `isPending`. Async status is a side effect, not a pure transition.

What about React 19 useActionState?

`useActionState` targets Server Actions on web. Expo mobile apps use `useReducer` + TanStack Query `useMutation` for networked submits.

How many useState hooks is too many?

Rule of thumb: more than **four related values** on one screen → consider one reducer or a custom hook wrapping state.

Can I use immer with useReducer?

Yes via `useImmerReducer` from `use-immer`. Zustand + immer middleware is more common for global stores - see [Zustand](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/state-management/zustand/).

How do wizards interact with Expo Router?

Keep step index in reducer state for animated transitions. For shareable progress, mirror step in `router.setParams({ step: "2" })` - URL is optional UX, reducer is source of truth during the session.

Why not put everything in one big useState object?

`setState({ ...s, email })` works until two updates batch incorrectly or you forget a field. Reducers force explicit action names - easier to log and test.

How does this relate to container/presenter?

Container holds `useReducer` / `useState`; presenter receives props and callbacks only - see [container-presenter on mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/container-presenter-on-mobile/).

Performance on long lists?

Reducer state in a parent of a 500-row `FlatList` re-renders all rows. Move list data to Query; keep selection in reducer with `extraData` or row-level memoization.

## Related

* [State Management Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/state-management/state-management-basics/) - local vs global vs server classification
* [Context Without Storms](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/state-management/context-without-storms/) - when reducer moves to Context
* [TanStack Query](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/state-management/tanstack-query/) - server mutations on wizard submit
* [Zustand](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/state-management/zustand/) - when wizard state must survive unmount
* [../component-patterns/anti-patterns-god-screens/anti-patterns-god-screens.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/anti-patterns-god-screens/) - too many useState calls on one screen
* [../architecture-design/adr-state-management-selection/adr-state-management-selection.md](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/adr-state-management-selection/) - form state decision

Dokumen: Zustand
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/state-management/zustand/

# Zustand

Lightweight global stores with minimal boilerplate. Zustand fits **client UI state** that survives screen changes - cart, preferences, feature tour completion. Pair with TanStack Query for API data; do not duplicate server caches in Zustand.

Highlights / Zustand

* No provider tree - import useStore hook anywhere in the JS bundle
* Selectors prevent list screens from re-rendering on unrelated slice updates
* One store per domain: cart, preferences, onboarding flags
* persist middleware + AsyncStorage for non-secret preferences only
* devtools middleware works with Flipper / Redux DevTools adapters in dev
* Reset store state in tests with useStore.setState(initial)

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
npx expo install zustand
```

```tsx
// src/features/cart/cartStore.ts
import { create } from "zustand";
 
type CartItem = { productId: string; qty: number };
 
type CartState = {
  items: CartItem[];
  add: (item: CartItem) => void;
  remove: (productId: string) => void;
  totalQty: () => number;
};
 
export const useCartStore = create<CartState>((set, get) => ({
  items: [],
  add: (item) =>
    set((s) => {
      const existing = s.items.find((i) => i.productId === item.productId);
      if (existing) {
        return {
          items: s.items.map((i) =>
            i.productId === item.productId ? { ...i, qty: i.qty + item.qty } : i
          ),
        };
      }
      return { items: [...s.items, item] };
    }),
  remove: (productId) => set((s) => ({ items: s.items.filter((i) => i.productId !== productId) })),
  totalQty: () => get().items.reduce((n, i) => n + i.qty, 0),
}));
```

```tsx
// Consumer - selector limits re-renders
import { useCartStore } from "@/features/cart/cartStore";
 
const qty = useCartStore((s) => s.totalQty());
```

**When to reach for this:**

* **Multiple screens** read/write the same client state (cart badge, filters persisted locally).
* Context causes **profiler-visible** re-render storms - selectors fix it.
* You want **small bundle** (~1KB) without Redux ceremony.
* State updates are **synchronous** UI - not server cache with stale times.
* Team default from [ADR](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/adr-state-management-selection/) for global client UI.

## Working Example

```tsx
// stores/preferencesStore.ts - slice pattern + devtools in dev
import { create } from "zustand";
import { devtools } from "zustand/middleware";
 
type ThemeMode = "system" | "light" | "dark";
 
type PreferencesState = {
  theme: ThemeMode;
  hapticsEnabled: boolean;
  setTheme: (theme: ThemeMode) => void;
  toggleHaptics: () => void;
};
 
export const usePreferencesStore = create<PreferencesState>()(
  devtools(
    (set) => ({
      theme: "system",
      hapticsEnabled: true,
      setTheme: (theme) => set({ theme }, false, "preferences/setTheme"),
      toggleHaptics: () => set((s) => ({ hapticsEnabled: !s.hapticsEnabled }), false, "preferences/toggleHaptics"),
    }),
    { name: "PreferencesStore", enabled: __DEV__ }
  )
);
 
// stores/cartStore.ts - separate domain store
import { create } from "zustand";
 
type CartItem = { productId: string; title: string; qty: number };
 
type CartState = {
  items: CartItem[];
  add: (item: CartItem) => void;
  clear: () => void;
};
 
export const useCartStore = create<CartState>((set) => ({
  items: [],
  add: (item) => set((s) => ({ items: [...s.items, item] })),
  clear: () => set({ items: [] }),
}));
 
// --- UI ---
import * as Haptics from "expo-haptics";
import { Pressable, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
export function SettingsScreen() {
  const theme = usePreferencesStore((s) => s.theme);
  const hapticsEnabled = usePreferencesStore((s) => s.hapticsEnabled);
  const setTheme = usePreferencesStore((s) => s.setTheme);
  const toggleHaptics = usePreferencesStore((s) => s.toggleHaptics);
 
  function onToggleHaptics() {
    if (hapticsEnabled) void Haptics.selectionAsync();
    toggleHaptics();
  }
 
  return (
    <View style={{ padding: 16, gap: 12 }}>
      <Text>Theme: {theme}</Text>
      <Pressable onPress={() => setTheme(theme === "dark" ? "light" : "dark")}>
        <Text>Toggle theme</Text>
      </Pressable>
      <Pressable onPress={onToggleHaptics}>
        <Text>Haptics: {hapticsEnabled ? "On" : "Off"}</Text>
      </Pressable>
    </View>
  );
}
 
export function CartBadge() {
  const count = useCartStore((s) => s.items.reduce((n, i) => n + i.qty, 0));
  return <Text>Cart ({count})</Text>;
}
```

```tsx
// cartStore.test.ts
import { useCartStore } from "./cartStore";
 
const initial = useCartStore.getState();
 
beforeEach(() => {
  useCartStore.setState(initial, true);
});
 
test("add merges quantity", () => {
  useCartStore.getState().add({ productId: "1", title: "Pack", qty: 1 });
  useCartStore.getState().add({ productId: "1", title: "Pack", qty: 2 });
  expect(useCartStore.getState().items).toHaveLength(2); // or merge policy per product rules
});
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* **Separate stores per domain** - preferences changes do not touch cart subscribers.
* **`devtools` middleware** names actions for Redux DevTools in development only.
* **Selectors** on `useCartStore` keep tab badge updates cheap.
* **`setState(..., true)`** replaces entire state in tests - deterministic reset.
* **Haptics** stay in the component - store holds flags, not native side effects.

## Deep Dive

### Slices in One Store (Optional)

Combine related slices when they share devtools namespace:

```tsx
import { create } from "zustand";
 
type BearSlice = { bears: number; addBear: () => void };
type FishSlice = { fish: number; addFish: () => void };
 
type Store = BearSlice & FishSlice;
 
export const useBoundStore = create<Store>()((...a) => ({
  ...createBearSlice(...a),
  ...createFishSlice(...a),
}));
 
function createBearSlice(set: Parameters<typeof create<BearSlice>>[0]): BearSlice {
  return {
    bears: 0,
    addBear: () => set((s) => ({ bears: s.bears + 1 })),
  };
}
```

Prefer **multiple `create()` stores** until cross-slice transactions are required.

### persist Middleware

```tsx
import AsyncStorage from "@react-native-async-storage/async-storage";
import { create } from "zustand";
import { createJSONStorage, persist } from "zustand/middleware";
 
export const usePreferencesStore = create(
  persist<PreferencesState>(
    (set) => ({
      theme: "system",
      hapticsEnabled: true,
      setTheme: (theme) => set({ theme }),
      toggleHaptics: () => set((s) => ({ hapticsEnabled: !s.hapticsEnabled })),
    }),
    {
      name: "preferences-v1",
      storage: createJSONStorage(() => AsyncStorage),
      partialize: (s) => ({ theme: s.theme, hapticsEnabled: s.hapticsEnabled }),
    }
  )
);
```

* **`partialize`** excludes actions from disk - only serialize data fields.
* **Never persist tokens** - use `expo-secure-store` via custom storage adapter - see [State Persistence & Hydration](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/state-management/state-persistence-and-hydration/).
* Bump **`name`** (`preferences-v2`) when schema changes - or run migration in `onRehydrateStorage`.

### Devtools on Device

`devtools` middleware sends actions to Redux DevTools Extension when debugging JS via Flipper or remote desktop. Disable in production: `enabled: __DEV__`.

### subscribeWithSelector

```tsx
import { subscribeWithSelector } from "zustand/middleware";
 
useCartStore.subscribe(
  (s) => s.items.length,
  (len) => console.log("cart size", len)
);
```

Use for analytics side effects - not React renders.

### Immer (Optional)

```bash
npm install immer
```

```tsx
import { immer } from "zustand/middleware/immer";
 
create<CartState>()(
  immer((set) => ({
    items: [],
    add: (item) =>
      set((state) => {
        state.items.push(item);
      }),
  }))
);
```

## Gotchas

* **Selecting entire store** - `useCartStore()` without selector re-renders on every cart change. **Fix:** `useCartStore((s) => s.items.length)`.
* **Derived data in store without memoization** - `get().items.map(...)` in render via selector runs each time. **Fix:** Computed selector or `useMemo` on result.
* **Storing API responses** - Cache invalidation becomes manual. **Fix:** TanStack Query.
* **Side effects inside `set`** - Calling `fetch` in `add()` couples store to network. **Fix:** Component or thunk calls API, then `set`.
* **One giant store** - Import cycles and hot reload pain. **Fix:** `features/cart/cartStore.ts`, `features/settings/preferencesStore.ts`.
* **persist everything** - Large cart JSON slows cold start. **Fix:** `partialize`, TTL, or Query persistence for server reads.
* **Forgetting test reset** - Tests leak state order-dependent. **Fix:** `beforeEach(() => useCartStore.setState(initial, true))`.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Zustand | Global client UI + selectors | Server list cache |
| Context (split) | Theme/session, zero deps | High-frequency cart updates |
| Redux Toolkit | Audit + middleware ecosystem | Greenfield with only cart + theme |
| Jotai | Atomic derived UI graphs | Team unfamiliar with atoms |
| MMKV raw | Speed-critical persistence | You still need update semantics |

## FAQs

Does Zustand need a Provider?

No - stores are module singletons. Multiple React roots (rare in RN) would share the same store unless you pass `createStore` via context.

Zustand vs Redux Toolkit in 2026?

Default Zustand for client global state. Redux when DevTools, middleware, and organizational standards require centralized reducers - see [Redux Toolkit](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/state-management/redux-toolkit/).

How do I use Zustand with Expo Router?

Import hooks in any route file. Orchestrate navigation in the route; store holds data. Avoid importing `router` inside store modules.

Can Zustand replace TanStack Query?

No for server state. Zustand can hold optimistic UI flags; Query owns fetched entities and cache keys.

How big is the bundle impact?

Zustand is ~1–3KB gzipped - negligible vs a single image asset. Redux Toolkit is larger but includes RTK Query.

Async actions pattern?

Keep async in hooks or services:

```tsx
async function checkout() {
  set({ status: "pending" });
  try {
    await api.checkout(get().items);
    set({ status: "done", items: [] });
  } catch (e) {
    set({ status: "error" });
  }
}
```

TypeScript best practice?

Define `CartState` type explicitly; use `create<CartState>()(...)` with middleware for inferred middleware types.

How do I hydrate on app boot?

Use `persist` + `onRehydrateStorage` callback to gate UI - see [State Persistence & Hydration](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/state-management/state-persistence-and-hydration/).

Multiple components same selector?

Zustand uses `Object.is` on selector result - return primitives or stable references to avoid extra renders.

Integration with React Compiler?

Selectors are still recommended - compiler memoization does not replace cross-component store subscriptions.

Logout cleanup?

`useCartStore.setState({ items: [] })` plus `queryClient.clear()` - client and server caches must clear together.

Can I use Zustand with immer and devtools together?

Yes - middleware order matters: `devtools(persist(immer(...)))` - check Zustand docs for your middleware chain.

# App Store Connect Workflow

Metadata, screenshots, review notes, and expedited review - the **App Store Connect checklist** for shipping Expo SDK 57 IPAs built with EAS. Upload automation lives in [EAS Submit](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/eas-build/eas-submit/); this page covers everything reviewers and users see before and after binary processing.

Highlights / App Store Connect Workflow

* App Store Connect is the control plane - EAS Submit uploads binaries; humans own metadata and release
* Screenshots must match current UI - stale marketing assets trigger 2.3.3 rejections
* Review notes with demo credentials cut Guideline 2.1 false negatives
* Privacy Nutrition Labels must match PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy and runtime behavior
* Phased release defaults on - plan marketing around 7-day rollout
* Expedited review is rare - reserve for revenue-critical or security fixes with evidence

## How to Use This Checklist

* Run **Tier 1** before the first `eas submit` - missing agreements or tax forms block all releases.
* Complete **Tier 2** on every version bump - metadata drift is a top rejection cause.
* **Tier 3** is submission day - attach review notes and select release strategy.
* **Tier 4** is post-approval - phased release, pricing, and EU trader compliance.
* Pair with [App Store Review Guidelines](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ios-platform/app-store-review-guidelines/) for rejection context.

---

## Tier 1: Account & App Record (before first upload)

* **Apple Developer Program** membership active; team role includes App Manager or Admin
* **App Store Connect agreements** signed (Paid Applications if IAP; free apps still need base agreement)
* **Tax and banking** complete if selling digital goods or subscriptions
* **Bundle ID** registered in Certificates, Identifiers & Profiles - matches `ios.bundleIdentifier` in `app.config.ts`
* **App record created** in App Store Connect with correct primary language and SKU
* **ASC App ID** (`ascAppId`) copied into `eas.json` submit profile
* **App Privacy** questionnaire started - answers must match SDK inventory (see [Compliance: ATT & Privacy Labels](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/store-operations/compliance-att-and-privacy-labels/))
* **Privacy policy URL** public, HTTPS, no login wall
* **Export compliance** answered in Connect - encryption self-classification consistent with `ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption` in config
* **TestFlight** enabled - first upload processes through TestFlight before App Review selection

---

## Tier 2: Metadata & Creative (every release)

### Listing copy

* **App name** ≤ 30 characters; no competitor trademarks or keyword stuffing
* **Subtitle** ≤ 30 characters; describes primary value, not generic "best app ever"
* **Promotional text** updated (can change without new binary - use for timely campaigns)
* **Description** accurate - features listed must exist in the submitted build
* **Keywords** comma-separated, no spaces, no repeat of app name, ≤ 100 bytes total
* **Support URL** loads; **Marketing URL** optional but recommended
* **What's New** describes user-visible changes - not internal refactors or "bug fixes" only
* **Copyright** string current year and legal entity
* **Age rating** questionnaire re-run if content, chat, UGC, or gambling mechanics changed
* **Category** primary + secondary still accurate

### Screenshots & preview assets

* **6.7" (iPhone 15 Pro Max)** screenshot set required - other sizes optional but recommended
* **6.5"** and **5.5"** if supporting older devices in marketing
* **iPad Pro 12.9"** if `supportsTablet: true` in config
* Screenshots show **current build UI** - not Figma mocks or last year's redesign
* Status bar clean - full battery, reasonable time, no debug banners
* Localized screenshot sets per locale you ship (EN, DE, JA, etc.)
* **App Preview video** optional - must be screen capture, not motion graphics only
* **App icon** 1024×1024 without alpha channel uploaded in Connect (or pulled from build)

```bash
# Optional: Fastlane snapshot or custom Detox script → store/screenshots/ios/
# Commit locale folders: en-US/, de-DE/
```

### Pricing & availability

* **Price tier** or free confirmed
* **Territories** list matches legal/compliance sign-off (EU, UK, CN require extra forms)
* **Pre-orders** disabled unless intentionally configured
* **In-App Purchases** and subscriptions in **Ready to Submit** state if referenced in app

---

## Tier 3: Submission Day

### Build selection

* Correct **build number** selected - matches `ios.buildNumber` from EAS build you QA'd
* Build **processed** (not "Processing" or "Invalid Binary")
* No **ITMS** email errors - privacy manifest, entitlements, or icon issues resolved (see [iOS Privacy Manifests](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ios-platform/ios-privacy-manifests-and-required-reason-apis/))

### App Review Information

* **Sign-in required** toggle accurate
* **Demo account** username + password tested within last 24 hours
* **Contact info** - phone number that rings during US business hours if possible
* **Notes** field includes:
  + Step-by-step path to core feature
  + Hardware requirements (camera, NFC, Apple Watch companion)
  + Feature flags or A/B tests disabled for review
  + ATT behavior ("not shown" vs "shown on second launch")
  + Backend environment (production vs staging)
* **Attachment** optional - PDF with screenshots of hidden admin flows

```markdown
<!-- store/review-notes-ios.md - paste into Connect -->
Demo: reviewer@example.com / ReviewDemo2026!
Path: Sign In → Home → Scan tab → grant Camera → scan any barcode
Account deletion: Profile → Settings → Delete Account
No cross-app tracking; ATT not displayed.
```

### Compliance toggles on version record

* **IDFA / tracking** declaration matches app behavior
* **Encryption** export compliance answers consistent with prior submissions
* **Content rights** - third-party content licensed if app streams music/video/UGC
* **EU Digital Services Act** trader status complete if distributing in EU

### Submit for review

* **Release option** chosen:
  + **Manually release** after approval (safest for coordinated launches)
  + **Automatically release** after approval
  + **Scheduled release** date/time for marketing alignment
* **Phased release** enabled (recommended) - 7-day gradual rollout
* Click **Submit for Review** - status moves to **Waiting for Review**

---

## Tier 4: After Approval

* Confirm **Ready for Sale** or trigger manual release
* Monitor **Phased Release** progress (App Store Connect → Activity → phased release)
* Watch **Crashlytics / Sentry** for build number tied to phased cohort
* Respond to **App Review messages** within 24 hours if metadata dispute arises
* Update **TestFlight** groups - expire old builds per 90-day limit
* Archive screenshot PNGs in git tag `store/ios/2.4.0`

---

## Expedited Review Checklist

Apple grants **expedited review** sparingly - misuse burns credibility. Use only when delay causes measurable user harm or revenue loss.

### Before requesting

* Issue is **blocking live users** (checkout broken, auth outage) - not "we promised marketing a date"
* Fix is in **submitted or about-to-submit** binary - not a metadata-only hope
* Standard review already **waiting** or **rejected with fix uploaded**
* No policy gray area - expedite will not bypass Guideline 4.2 or 5.1.1 disputes

### Request package

* **App Store Connect → Contact Us → App Review → Expedited App Review Request**
* **Concise explanation** (≤ 1 paragraph): user impact, timeline, why standard queue is insufficient
* **Evidence**: crash rate graph, support ticket volume, press embargo date (if contractual)
* **No duplicate requests** - one open expedite per app at a time

```text
Subject: Expedited Review - ShopApp 2.4.1 auth fix
 
Users cannot complete checkout since 2026-07-08 14:00 UTC due to OAuth redirect regression.
~12,000 DAU affected; support tickets +340%. Fix in build 240013, submitted today.
Standard queue would miss contractual SLA with enterprise customers.
```

### After decision

* If **approved** - monitor review status hourly; be available for reviewer questions
* If **denied** - proceed on standard queue; do not re-request same day without new facts
* Document outcome in postmortem - expedite is emergency tool, not release planning

---

## FAQs

How long does App Review take?

* Median is 24–48 hours; first submission and holiday weeks run longer.
* **Waiting for Review** is queue time; **In Review** usually lasts minutes to hours.

Can I edit metadata while In Review?

* Some fields lock during review - plan copy changes before submit.
* Rejection resets some locks; expedited resubmit may need unchanged metadata.

TestFlight build vs App Store build - same IPA?

* Yes - production EAS IPA uploads once; you choose TestFlight vs App Review distribution in Connect.

What triggers ITMS-91053 before human review?

* Missing **Required Reason API** declarations in privacy manifest - fix in `app.config.ts` and rebuild.
* See [App Store Review Guidelines](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ios-platform/app-store-review-guidelines/).

Phased release vs manual release?

* **Phased** rolls to 100% of users over 7 days - pause if crashes spike.
* **Manual** lets you hold approved build until marketing go - then enable phased on release day.

Dokumen: Store Operations Best Practices
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/store-operations/best-practices/

# Store Operations Best Practices

A condensed summary of the **25 most important store operations habits** drawn from every page in this section - for teams shipping Expo SDK 57 apps through App Store Connect and Google Play Console.

Highlights / Store Operations Best Practices

* Version build numbers in git before every EAS production build
* TestFlight and Play internal are mandatory gates - not optional niceties
* Privacy inventory drives iOS labels and Play Data safety - one spreadsheet
* Phased and staged rollout are default; 100% day-one is the exception
* Review notes and demo accounts expire - rotate every release
* Incident runbooks name who can pause rollout before the outage happens

1. **Treat store ops as a pipeline:** Build → internal test → submit → phased release → monitor - not a Friday afternoon task after feature freeze.
2. **Increment `buildNumber` and `versionCode` every upload:** Stores reject duplicates; hotfixes on the same marketing `version` still need new integers.
3. **Tag git commits that produced store binaries:** Incidents trace to source; `eas build:list` alone is not enough for audits.
4. **Run `npx expo-doctor` on release branches:** SDK drift causes upload failures and native crashes reviewers see before you do.
5. **Smoke-test Release builds on physical devices:** Simulators hide push, biometrics, IAP, ATT, and performance - Guideline 2.1 lives on real hardware.
6. **Use TestFlight internal before App Review:** Same IPA as production; catches signing, entitlements, and privacy manifest issues cheaply.
7. **Use Play internal track before production:** Minutes-to-hours feedback; validates Data safety and `versionCode` monotonicity.
8. **Automate upload with EAS Submit:** Humans choose release timing; machines avoid Transporter typos and wrong IPA selection.
9. **Keep metadata in git:** `store/metadata.ts` and locale folders - Connect and Play copy paste from one source of truth.
10. **Automate screenshot pipelines per locale:** Fastlane Snapshot, Detox, or Maestro - stale screenshots trigger 2.3.3 rejections.
11. **Maintain review notes with working demo credentials:** Rotate passwords every release; expired accounts cause false rejections.
12. **Align App Privacy, Nutrition Labels, and Play Data safety:** One privacy inventory spreadsheet drives all three - see [Compliance: ATT & Privacy Labels](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/store-operations/compliance-att-and-privacy-labels/).
13. **Request ATT only when you truly track across other companies' apps:** False tracking declarations are Guideline 5.1.2 strikes; non-personalized ads when denied.
14. **Match permission strings and manifest entries to runtime behavior:** iOS `infoPlist` descriptions and Android `blockedPermissions` - see [Permissions & Play Policy](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/android-platform/permissions-and-play-policy/).
15. **Rebuild native for privacy manifest and ATT changes:** OTA cannot fix ITMS-91053 or missing `NSUserTrackingUsageDescription`.
16. **Default iOS phased release and Android staged rollout to ON:** Start Play at 5–10%; plan marketing around 7-day iOS curve.
17. **Monitor crash rate by build number during partial rollout:** Sentry and Play vitals sliced on `versionCode` - aggregate app stats hide regressions.
18. **Document who can pause phased release and halt Play rollout:** Vacation gaps delay containment - name primary and backup in runbook.
19. **Know rollback limits:** Stores are forward-only; you ship fixes, not downgrades - [Phased Release & Rollback](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/store-operations/phased-release-and-rollback/).
20. **Classify rejections by Guideline or policy topic:** Emotional replies waste cycles - use [Store Rejection Playbook](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/store-operations/store-rejection-playbook/) templates.
21. **Attach evidence to Resolution Center replies:** Screen recordings, test accounts, and manifest excerpts beat "we cannot reproduce."
22. **Escalate after two evidence-based round-trips:** Not after first denial - Apple App Review Board and Play appeals need facts.
23. **Reserve expedited review for measurable user harm:** Revenue promises alone burn credibility - [App Store Connect Workflow](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/store-operations/app-store-connect-workflow/).
24. **Run incident command for delisting and SEV1 crashes:** IC, scribe, comms, legal - not parallel Slack threads - [Store Incident Response](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/store-operations/store-incident-response/).
25. **Postmortem every SEV1/SEV2 store incident:** Update playbook, privacy inventory, and release checklist within five business days.

## FAQs

What is the minimum viable store ops for a solo dev?

* Production EAS profiles, version bump discipline, TestFlight + internal track, phased/staged rollout, privacy forms honest, review notes with demo login.

iOS first or Android first?

* Either works - ship the ready platform; keep API backward compatible if staggered by a week.

How often refresh screenshots?

* Every major UI release and localization add - automate generation in CI where possible.

Where does EAS Update fit?

* JS-only fixes on compatible runtime versions - never substitute for native compliance or crash-on-launch fixes.

Dokumen: Compliance: ATT & Privacy Labels
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/store-operations/compliance-att-and-privacy-labels/

# Compliance: ATT & Privacy Labels

Tracking transparency and nutrition labels - the cookbook for aligning **iOS App Tracking Transparency (ATT)**, **Privacy Nutrition Labels**, and **Google Play Data safety** with what your Expo SDK 57 app actually does at runtime. Policy context lives in [App Store Review Guidelines](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ios-platform/app-store-review-guidelines/) and [Permissions & Play Policy](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/android-platform/permissions-and-play-policy/).

Highlights / Compliance: ATT & Privacy Labels

* ATT applies when you track users across apps/websites owned by other companies - not all analytics
* NSUserTrackingUsageDescription is required before AppTrackingTransparency prompt
* Privacy Nutrition Labels and App Privacy in Connect must match PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy
* Play Data safety must tell the same story as iOS labels - auditors compare both
* IDFA access without ATT prompt is a fast rejection and policy violation
* Rebuild native after privacy manifest or ATT changes - not OTA

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
npx expo install expo-tracking-transparency
```

```ts
// app.config.ts - ATT string + honest tracking declaration
export default {
  expo: {
    ios: {
      bundleIdentifier: "com.example.shopapp",
      infoPlist: {
        NSUserTrackingUsageDescription:
          "ShopApp uses this identifier to measure ad campaign performance and limit duplicate offers.",
      },
      privacyManifests: {
        NSPrivacyTracking: false, // set true only if you track across other companies' apps/sites
        NSPrivacyTrackingDomains: [],
        NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypes: [
          {
            NSPrivacyCollectedDataType: "NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypeCrashData",
            NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypeLinked: false,
            NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypeTracking: false,
            NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypePurposes: [
              "NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypePurposeAppFunctionality",
            ],
          },
        ],
      },
    },
  },
};
```

```tsx
// features/ads/requestTrackingIfNeeded.ts
import * as TrackingTransparency from "expo-tracking-transparency";
import { Platform } from "react-native";
 
export async function requestTrackingIfNeeded(): Promise<boolean> {
  if (Platform.OS !== "ios") return true;
 
  const { status: current } = await TrackingTransparency.getTrackingPermissionsAsync();
  if (current === "granted") return true;
  if (current === "denied") return false;
 
  // Show your own pre-prompt explaining value BEFORE system dialog
  const { status } = await TrackingTransparency.requestTrackingPermissionsAsync();
  return status === "granted";
}
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Adding AdMob, Facebook SDK, AppsFlyer, or any SDK that reads IDFA.
* First App Store submission - Nutrition Labels and App Privacy questionnaire.
* Play Console **Data safety** redraft after SDK upgrade.
* Rejection citing Guideline **5.1.2** (tracking) or inaccurate privacy labels.
* Legal asks for **cross-store privacy parity** documentation.

---

## Working Example

### Step 1 - Inventory data collection

Build a **privacy inventory** spreadsheet from code and dependencies:

| Source | Data type | Linked to user? | Used for tracking? | Store surfaces |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your API | Email, name | Yes | No | Both |
| Sentry | Crash logs | No | No | iOS manifest + Play diagnostics |
| Firebase Analytics | Usage events | No\* | No\* | Labels + Data safety |
| AdMob | Advertising ID | Yes | Yes | ATT + ads declaration |

\*Verify SDK config - default Firebase settings may differ.

```bash
# Dependency audit starting points
grep -r "expo-" package.json
grep -r "analytics\|sentry\|ads\|tracking" app.config.ts features/
```

### Step 2 - iOS: ATT decision tree

```
Do you link user/device data with third-party data for advertising
OR share with data brokers
OR use IDFA for cross-app/website tracking (other companies)?
├── NO → NSPrivacyTracking: false; do NOT call ATT; declare analytics as non-tracking
└── YES → NSPrivacyTracking: true; NSUserTrackingUsageDescription; request ATT before IDFA
```

**ATT prompt rules:**

* Request **after** user understands context - use pre-prompt screen.
* Never gate core app features on accepting tracking.
* If user denies, **do not read IDFA** - ad SDKs must run in non-personalized mode.
* `expo-tracking-transparency` wraps `ATTrackingManager`.

### Step 3 - iOS: Privacy Nutrition Labels

App Store Connect → **App Privacy**:

1. Match categories to inventory (contact info, identifiers, usage data, diagnostics).
2. For each type: **linked to identity**, **used for tracking**, **purposes**.
3. Publish labels - preview on listing.

Align `NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypes` in `app.config.ts` with Connect answers - see [iOS Privacy Manifests](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ios-platform/ios-privacy-manifests-and-required-reason-apis/).

```ts
// Example: purchase history declared in manifest
{
  NSPrivacyCollectedDataType: "NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypePurchaseHistory",
  NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypeLinked: true,
  NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypeTracking: false,
  NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypePurposes: [
    "NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypePurposeAppFunctionality",
  ],
}
```

### Step 4 - Android: Data safety alignment

Play Console → **App content** → **Data safety**:

| iOS label claim | Play Data safety field |
| --- | --- |
| Contact info collected | Personal info → email/name |
| Identifiers → User ID | Device or other IDs |
| Diagnostics → crash data | App info and performance |
| Data used for tracking | **Advertising or marketing** + **Data sharing** |

* **Collected** vs **shared** must reflect SDK network calls - not just your API.
* **Ephemeral processing** only if you truly do not retain.
* **Deletion request** URL or in-app path if you collect personal data.

Full checklist: [Google Play Console Workflow](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/store-operations/google-play-console-workflow/).

### Step 5 - Permission strings match behavior

iOS `infoPlist` usage descriptions must describe **current** feature:

```ts
infoPlist: {
  NSCameraUsageDescription: "ShopApp uses the camera to scan product barcodes.",
  NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription: "ShopApp lets you choose a photo for your profile.",
  NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription: "ShopApp uses your location to find nearby stores.",
}
```

Android dangerous permissions - request in context; Data safety must mention location if `expo-location` runs.

### Step 6 - Verify before submit

```bash
npx expo prebuild --platform ios --clean
plutil -p ios/ShopApp/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy
npx expo config --type public | jq '.ios.infoPlist.NSUserTrackingUsageDescription'
```

**Manual QA script:**

* Fresh install → tracking SDKs **inactive** until consent flows complete
* Deny ATT → ads still work (non-personalized) or ads disabled gracefully
* Account deletion removes PII per privacy policy
* Connect **App Privacy** export matches Play **Data safety** PDF for legal

### Step 7 - Rebuild and submit

Privacy manifest and ATT strings are **native** - ship new binary via [EAS Submit](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/eas-build/eas-submit/).

---

## Cross-Store Alignment Matrix

| Topic | iOS | Android |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tracking consent | ATT prompt | No ATT; ads ID + UMP/consent SDK |
| Label UI | Nutrition Labels on App Store | Data safety section on Play |
| Manifest file | `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy` | Manifest permissions + Data safety form |
| Account deletion | Required if accounts created | Required by policy; link in Data safety |
| Kids / COPPA | Age rating + no tracking children | Target audience form |

---

## Common Mistakes

| Mistake | Consequence |
| --- | --- |
| Ad SDK in `package.json` but "no data collected" on forms | Rejection + regulatory risk |
| ATT prompt on launch before value explanation | Low opt-in + poor UX; review scrutiny |
| Reading IDFA when `NSPrivacyTracking: false` | Guideline 5.1.2 rejection |
| OTA-only "fix" for manifest | Stores still serve old non-compliant binary |
| iOS says no location; Android manifest has `ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION` | Play policy strike |

---

## FAQs

Is first-party analytics tracking?

* Analytics confined to your app, not linked to third-party ad networks for cross-app profiling, is generally **not** ATT tracking.
* Still declare usage/diagnostics data in labels and Data safety.

Do I need ATT for push notifications?

* No - push tokens are not IDFA.
* Declare device identifiers if you use token for cross-app ad profiling (unusual).

Expo Go and privacy testing?

* ATT and manifests apply to **store builds** - test on EAS production or preview dev client builds with matching entitlements.

What if labels were wrong in a live app?

* Update Connect and Play forms immediately.
* Ship compliant binary if SDK behavior must change.
* See [Store Incident Response](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/store-operations/store-incident-response/) for disclosure decisions.

Dokumen: Google Play Console Workflow
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/store-operations/google-play-console-workflow/

# Google Play Console Workflow

Data safety, content rating, and staged rollout - the **Google Play Console checklist** for Expo SDK 57 AABs uploaded via [EAS Submit](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/eas-build/eas-submit/). Runtime permissions and manifest hygiene are covered in [Permissions & Play Policy](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/android-platform/permissions-and-play-policy/); this page is the store-operator view from first app creation through production rollout.

Highlights / Google Play Console Workflow

* Play Console Dashboard tasks block production until policy forms are complete
* Data safety answers must match SDK behavior - mismatches cause rejection and user trust issues
* Content rating (IARC) is mandatory before any public track
* Staged rollout percentage is separate from internal/closed/open testing tracks
* versionCode must increase monotonically - Play rejects duplicate integers
* eas submit --track controls upload destination; rollout % is set in Console UI

## How to Use This Checklist

* **Tier 1** - one-time app setup and Play App Signing.
* **Tier 2** - policy forms that gate **every** track (internal included on first release).
* **Tier 3** - store listing and creative assets per release.
* **Tier 4** - upload, testing tracks, and production **staged rollout**.
* Re-run Tier 2 when adding SDKs that collect data, request dangerous permissions, or show ads.

---

## Tier 1: App Setup (before first upload)

* **Google Play Developer account** active; one-time registration fee paid
* **App created** in Play Console with default language and app name
* **`android.package`** in `app.config.ts` matches Play app ID - cannot change after first publish
* **Play App Signing** enabled - Google holds app signing key; you upload with upload key
* **Upload key** registered with EAS - see [Signing & Play App Signing](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/android-platform/signing-and-play-app-signing/)
* **Service account** for EAS Submit with **Release to testing tracks** (minimum) or **Release to production**
* **Service account JSON** path in `eas.json` - not committed to git
* **versionCode** scheme documented - monotonic integer every upload
* **Privacy policy URL** on public HTTPS page
* **Target API level** meets Play requirements for SDK 57 / RN 0.86 builds (verify in EAS build logs)

```json
// eas.json - submit to internal first
{
  "submit": {
    "production": {
      "android": {
        "serviceAccountKeyPath": "./secrets/play-service-account.json",
        "track": "internal"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

---

## Tier 2: Policy & Compliance (gates all tracks)

### Data safety form

* **Data safety** section opened in Play Console → **Start**
* Inventory all SDKs - analytics, crash, ads, auth, push, maps (grep `package.json` + `app.config.ts` plugins)
* For each data type collected:
  + **Collected or shared** answered honestly
  + **Purpose** matches actual use (analytics vs fraud prevention vs personalization)
  + **Encrypted in transit** - HTTPS for your API; SDK defaults documented
  + **Users can request deletion** - aligns with in-app account deletion if accounts exist
* **Location** - precise vs approximate matches `expo-location` usage
* **Photos and videos** - matches picker vs broad storage reads
* **Device or other IDs** - advertising ID, Firebase installation ID, etc.
* **Data safety labels** preview matches what users see on Play Store listing
* Cross-check with [Compliance: ATT & Privacy Labels](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/store-operations/compliance-att-and-privacy-labels/) for iOS parity

| Common Expo SDK | Data safety touchpoint |
| --- | --- |
| `expo-notifications` | Device ID, push token |
| `@sentry/react-native` | Crash logs, diagnostics |
| `expo-image-picker` | Photos (user-selected) |
| `expo-location` | Location (approximate/precise) |
| `react-native-google-mobile-ads` | Advertising ID, usage data |

### Content rating

* **Content rating** questionnaire started (IARC)
* Violence, gambling, user-generated content, and location sharing answered accurately
* **Received rating** (Everyone, Teen, Mature, etc.) applied to release
* Re-run questionnaire when adding chat, WebView user content, or loot mechanics

### Target audience & news apps

* **Target audience and content** - age groups selected; no appeal to children if not designed for them
* **News apps** declaration if applicable
* **COVID-19 apps** declaration if applicable (legacy form may still appear)
* **Government apps** declaration if applicable

### Ads & declarations

* **Contains ads** toggle matches reality (AdMob, mediation SDKs)
* **App access** - credentials provided if login required for review (like iOS review notes)
* **Ads ID** - declare if using advertising ID; respect **Privacy Sandbox** / opt-out flows

### Permissions alignment

* `AndroidManifest.xml` permissions (via prebuild) match Data safety - remove unused permissions with `blockedPermissions`
* Dangerous permissions have in-app rationale before system prompt
* See [Permissions & Play Policy](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/android-platform/permissions-and-play-policy/) for photo picker and notification patterns

---

## Tier 3: Store Listing (every release)

### Main store listing

* **App name** ≤ 30 characters
* **Short description** ≤ 80 characters - primary value prop
* **Full description** ≤ 4000 characters - features match submitted build
* **App icon** 512×512 PNG
* **Feature graphic** 1024×500 JPG or PNG (required for featuring)
* **Phone screenshots** - min 2, max 8; 16:9 or 9:16; current UI
* **7-inch tablet** and **10-inch tablet** screenshots if `supportsTablet` or layout targets tablets
* **Chromebook** / **Android XR** assets if distributing to those form factors
* **Video** optional - YouTube URL
* Localized listings per country/language you support

### Release notes

* **Release notes** per language - user-visible changes for this `versionCode`
* No keyword stuffing - Play may flag ASO abuse

### Pricing & distribution

* **Countries/regions** selected
* **Free or paid** consistent with billing setup
* **Managed Google Play** / enterprise constraints if B2B

---

## Tier 4: Upload, Tracks & Staged Rollout

### Build upload

* `eas build --profile production --platform android` produces **AAB**
* `android.versionCode` incremented in `app.config.ts`
* `eas submit --platform android --latest` succeeds
* Play Console shows release **Processing** → **Available to testers** or **In review**

### Testing track progression (recommended)

* **Internal testing** - up to 100 testers; minutes-to-hours processing
* **Closed testing (alpha)** - email lists, larger QA pool
* **Open testing (beta)** - public opt-in URL
* Sign-off checklist completed on each track before production
* See [Internal Testing Tracks](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/android-platform/internal-testing-tracks/)

### Production release

* Promote tested AAB to **Production** (or submit `track: "production"` via EAS)
* **Staged rollout** enabled - start **5–10%** for risky releases
* **Rollout percentage** owners documented (who can pause/halt)
* Monitor **Android vitals** - crash rate, ANR rate, startup time
* Increase rollout: 10% → 20% → 50% → 100% with go/no-go between steps
* **Halt rollout** procedure ready - see [Phased Release & Rollback](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/store-operations/phased-release-and-rollback/)

```markdown
## Staged rollout go/no-go (example)
| Gate | Threshold | Action |
|------|-----------|--------|
| Crash rate | < 1.1× baseline | Continue rollout |
| ANR rate | < 1.5× baseline | Pause at current % |
| 1-star spike | > 2× daily avg | Halt + triage |
```

### Post-release

* **Pre-launch report** reviewed (Accessibility, security, SDK warnings)
* **Policy status** green - no outstanding violations
* Archive AAB mapping file if using R8 mapping for crash deobfuscation
* Tag git `store/android/2.4.0-build240012`

---

## Dashboard Required Tasks (quick audit)

Open **Play Console → Dashboard** and clear every red item before expecting production visibility:

* Set up your app (initial wizard)
* Privacy policy
* App access (login credentials for reviewers)
* Ads declaration
* Content rating
* Target audience
* Data safety
* Store listing (at least default language)
* Select countries

---

## FAQs

Internal track vs production - same AAB?

* Yes - you promote the same artifact up tracks.
* `versionCode` must be unique across all tracks in the app.

Does eas submit set rollout percentage?

* No - EAS uploads to the track you specify.
* **Staged rollout %** is configured in Play Console **Production → Releases**.

Data safety vs permissions in manifest?

* Manifest declares what OS *can* grant; Data safety declares what you *collect/share*.
* Both must align - see [Permissions & Play Policy](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/android-platform/permissions-and-play-policy/).

Rejected for Data safety inaccuracy?

* Update form to match SDK reality or remove SDK.
* File appeal only with evidence (code paths, network logs) - see [Store Rejection Playbook](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/store-operations/store-rejection-playbook/).

Can I ship 100% immediately?

* Yes - toggle staged rollout to 100% for hotfixes or low-risk patches.
* Default to partial rollout for native migrations (RN upgrade, New Architecture flip).

## Related

* [Store Operations Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/store-operations/store-operations-basics/) - dual-store release flow
* [Permissions & Play Policy](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/android-platform/permissions-and-play-policy/) - runtime permissions cookbook
* [Internal Testing Tracks](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/android-platform/internal-testing-tracks/) - alpha/beta progression
* [Signing & Play App Signing](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/android-platform/signing-and-play-app-signing/) - upload key setup

# Store Operations Highlights Summary

Every highlight bullet from the 8 pages in this section, gathered on one page and grouped by the page it came from.

Highlights / Store Operations Highlights Summary

* Store ops starts after a production-shaped EAS build - not Expo Go or debug APKs
* App Store Connect is the control plane - EAS Submit uploads binaries; humans own metadata and release
* Play Console Dashboard tasks block production until policy forms are complete
* iOS phased release spreads to 100% over 7 days - you can pause or accelerate from App Store Connect
