* Parse rejection emails for Guideline numbers and ITMS codes - not emotional language

## [Store Operations Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/store-operations/store-operations-basics/)

* Store ops starts after a production-shaped EAS build - not Expo Go or debug APKs
* Bump ios.buildNumber and android.versionCode on every store upload - stores reject duplicates
* TestFlight and Play internal tracks validate signing and policy before App Review
* Metadata, privacy forms, and review notes live in git - not only in console UIs
* eas submit automates upload; humans still own release timing and rollout percentage
* Phased release on iOS and staged rollout on Play are your first rollback levers

## [App Store Connect Workflow](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/store-operations/app-store-connect-workflow/)

* App Store Connect is the control plane - EAS Submit uploads binaries; humans own metadata and release
* Screenshots must match current UI - stale marketing assets trigger 2.3.3 rejections
* Review notes with demo credentials cut Guideline 2.1 false negatives
* Privacy Nutrition Labels must match PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy and runtime behavior
* Phased release defaults on - plan marketing around 7-day rollout
* Expedited review is rare - reserve for revenue-critical or security fixes with evidence

## [Google Play Console Workflow](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/store-operations/google-play-console-workflow/)

* Play Console Dashboard tasks block production until policy forms are complete
* Data safety answers must match SDK behavior - mismatches cause rejection and user trust issues
* Content rating (IARC) is mandatory before any public track
* Staged rollout percentage is separate from internal/closed/open testing tracks
* versionCode must increase monotonically - Play rejects duplicate integers
* eas submit --track controls upload destination; rollout % is set in Console UI

## [Phased Release & Rollback](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/store-operations/phased-release-and-rollback/)

* iOS phased release spreads to 100% over 7 days - you can pause or accelerate from App Store Connect
* Play staged rollout is manual percentage - halt stops new installs without pulling existing users
* Neither store rolls back binaries automatically - you submit a prior or fixed build
* Crash spikes during partial rollout are the signal to pause - not Twitter alone
* OTA (EAS Update) can mitigate JS-only bugs; native regressions need new store build
* Document who has Console access to pause rollout before incident hour

## [Compliance: ATT & Privacy Labels](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/store-operations/compliance-att-and-privacy-labels/)

* ATT applies when you track users across apps/websites owned by other companies - not all analytics
* NSUserTrackingUsageDescription is required before AppTrackingTransparency prompt
* Privacy Nutrition Labels and App Privacy in Connect must match PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy
* Play Data safety must tell the same story as iOS labels - auditors compare both
* IDFA access without ATT prompt is a fast rejection and policy violation
* Rebuild native after privacy manifest or ATT changes - not OTA

## [Store Rejection Playbook](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/store-operations/store-rejection-playbook/)

* Parse rejection emails for Guideline numbers and ITMS codes - not emotional language
* Reproduce on Release build on device before replying - simulators miss native crashes
* Resolution Center replies need evidence: video, screenshots, test account, code pointers
* Metadata rejections fix in Connect; binary rejections need new EAS build
* Play appeals need Data safety evidence - form-only fixes without binary may suffice
* Escalate with facts after two failed round-trips - not after first denial

## [Store Incident Response](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/store-operations/store-incident-response/)

* Store incidents span delisting, policy strikes, broken live builds, and sudden guideline changes
* First hour: confirm scope, pause rollout, assign incident commander - not parallel Slack threads
* Removing app from sale is last resort - pause phased/staged rollout first when possible
* Legal and comms own external messaging; engineering owns technical timeline
* Post-incident: update privacy forms, rejection playbook entry, and on-call runbook
* Regulatory breaches may require user notification beyond store status pages

## [Store Operations Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/store-operations/best-practices/)

* Version build numbers in git before every EAS production build
* TestFlight and Play internal are mandatory gates - not optional niceties
* Privacy inventory drives iOS labels and Play Data safety - one spreadsheet
* Phased and staged rollout are default; 100% day-one is the exception
* Review notes and demo accounts expire - rotate every release
* Incident runbooks name who can pause rollout before the outage happens

Dokumen: Phased Release & Rollback
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/store-operations/phased-release-and-rollback/

# Phased Release & Rollback

Pausing iOS phased release and halting Play rollout - the cookbook for **containing bad releases** on Expo SDK 57 apps without waiting for full user exposure. Upload still flows through [EAS Submit](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/eas-build/eas-submit/); this page covers operator actions in App Store Connect and Play Console after a build is live or partially live.

Highlights / Phased Release & Rollback

* iOS phased release spreads to 100% over 7 days - you can pause or accelerate from App Store Connect
* Play staged rollout is manual percentage - halt stops new installs without pulling existing users
* Neither store rolls back binaries automatically - you submit a prior or fixed build
* Crash spikes during partial rollout are the signal to pause - not Twitter alone
* OTA (EAS Update) can mitigate JS-only bugs; native regressions need new store build
* Document who has Console access to pause rollout before incident hour

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```markdown
## Rollback decision tree (first 15 minutes)
1. Confirm bad build number in Sentry / Play Vitals matches live release
2. Classify: native crash (store build) vs JS logic (EAS Update candidate)
3. iOS: App Store Connect → pause phased release
4. Android: Play Console → halt staged rollout
5. If native: prepare hotfix build OR promote last-known-good versionCode / buildNumber
6. Post status page + in-app banner if auth/checkout broken
```

```bash
# Hotfix path - increment build numbers, rebuild, resubmit
# app.config.ts: ios.buildNumber + android.versionCode bumped
eas build --profile production --platform all
eas submit --platform ios --latest
eas submit --platform android --latest
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Crash-free rate drops > 0.5% during first day of rollout.
* ANR rate doubles on Android vitals at 20% staged rollout.
* Checkout or auth regression confirmed in production - not a flaky A/B test.
* Marketing pushed before engineering validated phased cohort metrics.
* You need to **stop new adopters** while deciding between OTA fix and hotfix binary.

---

## Working Example

### Scenario - 2.4.0 regression at partial rollout

**Symptoms:** iOS phased release day 2 (~28% users); Android at 20% staged rollout. Sentry shows 3.2% crash rate on `240012` (baseline 0.4%). Stack trace: null pointer in native module after RN 0.86 upgrade.

**Step 1 - Pause new exposure**

| Platform | Console path | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| iOS | App Store Connect → **Apps** → **ShopApp** → **Activity** → version **2.4.0** | **Pause Phased Release** |
| Android | Play Console → **Release** → **Production** → active release | **Halt rollout** (stops at current %) |

* **Pause iOS phased release** - users who already received update keep it; no new users get 2.4.0 until resumed or replaced.
* **Halt Play rollout** - same behavior; existing installs stay on bad build until they update again.

**Step 2 - Assess rollback options**

| Fix type | Tool | Time to users |
| --- | --- | --- |
| JS-only bug | EAS Update (runtime compatible) | Minutes–hours |
| Native crash | New store binary | 1–3+ days (review) |
| Server-side | API flag / config | Minutes |

This crash is **native** - OTA will not help. Proceed with hotfix **2.4.1** build `240013`.

**Step 3 - iOS: release strategy while paused**

1. Build and submit hotfix IPA via EAS.
2. Submit **2.4.1** for App Review - mention regression fix in review notes.
3. Options while waiting:
   * Leave **2.4.0 phased release paused** (limits blast radius).
   * If Apple approves **2.4.1** before pause expires, **release 2.4.1** with phased release enabled - do not resume 2.4.0.
4. **Cannot "downgrade"** users on iOS - users on 2.4.0 need forward fix 2.4.1.

```markdown
<!-- App Store Connect review note addendum -->
2.4.1 fixes crash on cold start (Sentry issue SHOP-4412) introduced in 2.4.0 build 240012.
2.4.0 phased release is paused. No new users receive 2.4.0.
```

**Step 4 - Android: halt + superseding release**

1. Play Console → **Production** → confirm rollout **halted** at 20%.
2. Upload hotfix AAB `versionCode 240013` via `eas submit`.
3. Create new production release with **100%** or restart **staged rollout at 5%** for the fix.
4. Google does not auto-replace installs - users on 2.4.0 pull 2.4.1 when they update.

```json
// eas.json - hotfix submit (same profiles, new versionCode in app.config.ts)
{
  "submit": {
    "production": {
      "android": {
        "serviceAccountKeyPath": "./secrets/play-service-account.json",
        "track": "production"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

**Step 5 - Resume safe rollout**

| Platform | When metrics clean | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| iOS | 2.4.1 approved | Release with **phased release ON**; monitor 48h |
| Android | 2.4.1 at 5% for 24h | Increase 5 → 20 → 50 → 100 |

**Step 6 - Postmortem hooks**

* Tag Sentry releases with `buildNumber` / `versionCode`.
* Add go/no-go checklist to [Store Operations Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/store-operations/store-operations-basics/) example 9.
* File incident doc if severity warranted - [Store Incident Response](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/store-operations/store-incident-response/).

---

## iOS Phased Release Reference

| Day (approx.) | % of auto-update users |
| --- | --- |
| Day 1 | 1% |
| Day 2 | 2% |
| Day 3 | 5% |
| Day 4 | 10% |
| Day 5 | 20% |
| Day 6 | 50% |
| Day 7 | 100% |

**Controls in App Store Connect:**

* **Pause Phased Release** - freeze percentage until resumed.
* **Release Update to All Users** - skip remaining phased days (use only when hotfix validated).
* **Turn off phased release** on next version - instant 100% (higher risk).

Users who **manually update** from the App Store may receive the build immediately regardless of phase - phased applies to automatic updates.

---

## Android Staged Rollout Reference

| Control | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| **Staged rollout 5%** | 5% of eligible new updaters receive release |
| **Increase percentage** | More users offered update; irreversible except halt |
| **Halt rollout** | Freeze at current %; no new users get release |
| **Full rollout 100%** | All eligible users offered update |

**Android vitals** (Play Console → **Quality** → **Android vitals**):

* **User-perceived crash rate**
* **ANR rate**
* Compare **versionCode** slices - not just aggregate app stats.

---

## EAS Update as Partial Mitigation

When the bug is **JavaScript-only** and runtime version policy allows:

```bash
eas update --branch production --message "fix: cart total rounding"
```

* Users on bad **native** build still need store hotfix if native code changed.
* Do not OTA over a crash-on-launch native regression - app never reaches JS bundle.
* Pair with feature flags to disable broken screens while update propagates.

---

## Rollback Limitations

| Expectation | Reality |
| --- | --- |
| "Roll back to 2.3.9 in stores" | Stores forward-only - submit 2.3.10 or 2.4.1 fix |
| "Pull binary from users' phones" | Not possible - only stop new installs |
| "Same versionCode re-upload" | Play rejects duplicate; iOS rejects duplicate build number |
| "Instant fix worldwide" | Review queue + phased/staged timing |

---

## FAQs

Pause phased release vs removing app from sale?

* **Pause phased** limits new updates to bad build - app stays available.
* **Remove from sale** is nuclear - use only for legal/policy crisis; see incident response doc.

Who can halt Play rollout?

* Users with **Release to production** permission.
* Document named backups - vacations cause delay.

Should first release use phased/staged?

* **Yes** for established apps with meaningful DAU.
* First-ever launch has no prior baseline - still consider 10% Android staged after internal track sign-off.

Expedited review for rollback hotfix?

* Request only with user-impact evidence - [App Store Connect Workflow](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/store-operations/app-store-connect-workflow/) expedited checklist.

Dokumen: Store Operations Basics
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/store-operations/store-operations-basics/

# Store Operations Basics

10 examples to get you started with Store Operations - 7 basic and 3 intermediate. Each example moves one step along the **build → test → submit → release → monitor** path for Expo SDK 57 apps on App Store Connect and Google Play Console.

Highlights / Store Operations Basics

* Store ops starts after a production-shaped EAS build - not Expo Go or debug APKs
* Bump ios.buildNumber and android.versionCode on every store upload - stores reject duplicates
* TestFlight and Play internal tracks validate signing and policy before App Review
* Metadata, privacy forms, and review notes live in git - not only in console UIs
* eas submit automates upload; humans still own release timing and rollout percentage
* Phased release on iOS and staged rollout on Play are your first rollback levers

## Prerequisites

Store operations assume you already ship binaries with EAS Build. Scaffold or confirm an Expo project pinned to SDK 57:

```bash
npx create-expo-app@latest MyStoreApp --template blank-typescript
cd MyStoreApp
npx expo install expo-dev-client
eas init
```

Confirm versions in `package.json`:

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "expo": "~57.0.4",
    "react": "19.2.3",
    "react-native": "0.86.0"
  }
}
```

Link the project to EAS and configure at least a `production` build profile in `eas.json`. Store uploads require **store distribution** builds - not `development` or simulator artifacts.

| Stage | iOS artifact | Android artifact |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Local QA | EAS internal / dev client | EAS internal APK or AAB |
| Pre-store | TestFlight IPA | Play internal AAB |
| Store submit | Production IPA | Production AAB |
| Live users | App Store release | Production track |

> **Tooling:** These examples target **Expo SDK 57**, **React Native 0.86**, and **React 19.2.3**. Automate uploads with [EAS Submit](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/eas-build/eas-submit/); policy details live in [App Store Review Guidelines](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ios-platform/app-store-review-guidelines/) and [Permissions & Play Policy](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/android-platform/permissions-and-play-policy/).

---

## Basic Examples

### 1. Version Bump in `app.config.ts`

Every store upload needs a **new build number** (iOS) and **versionCode** (Android). Marketing `version` can stay the same for hotfixes; native integers must always increase.

```ts
// app.config.ts
import type { ExpoConfig } from "expo/config";
 
const config: ExpoConfig = {
  expo: {
    name: "ShopApp",
    slug: "shop-app",
    version: "2.4.0",
    ios: {
      bundleIdentifier: "com.example.shopapp",
      buildNumber: "240012", // CFBundleVersion - increment every upload
    },
    android: {
      package: "com.example.shopapp",
      versionCode: 240012, // monotonic integer - increment every upload
    },
  },
};
 
export default config;
```

* **`version`** is user-facing semver on both stores
* **`buildNumber`** / **`versionCode`** must increase even for "same version" rebuilds
* CI can derive integers from `git rev-list --count HEAD` - document the scheme in README
* Run `npx expo config --type public` before build to catch typos

> **Related:** [App Store Connect Workflow](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/store-operations/app-store-connect-workflow/) - metadata tied to version strings

---

### 2. Production EAS Build for Both Platforms

Store submission starts with **release-shaped** binaries signed with production credentials.

```bash
# One command per platform (or both)
eas build --profile production --platform ios
eas build --profile production --platform android
 
# Verify build finished
eas build:list --limit 5
```

```json
// eas.json - minimum production profile
{
  "build": {
    "production": {
      "distribution": "store",
      "ios": { "simulator": false },
      "android": { "buildType": "app-bundle" }
    }
  }
}
```

* **`distribution: "store"`** produces App Store IPA and Play AAB - not ad-hoc internal links
* Download and smoke-test on physical devices before submit - simulators hide push, biometrics, and IAP
* Tag the git commit that produced the build - store incidents trace back to source

---

### 3. Pre-Store Gate with `expo-doctor`

Catch SDK drift and config mistakes before burning a review cycle.

```bash
npx expo-doctor
npx expo config --type public > /tmp/public-config.json
npm run typecheck
npm test -- --ci
```

```markdown
<!-- docs/release-gates.md - copy into every release PR -->
## Pre-submit gate
- [ ] expo-doctor green
- [ ] Release build installed on iOS + Android device
- [ ] Cold start, login, paywall, push tap, deep link, logout, account delete
- [ ] Privacy labels / Data safety match SDK inventory
- [ ] Review notes updated with demo credentials
```

* **`expo-doctor`** flags incompatible package versions against SDK 57
* Treat the device smoke test as non-negotiable - Guideline 2.1 rejections are often "crashes on launch"
* Keep gates in git so new engineers do not rely on tribal memory

---

### 4. TestFlight and Play Internal Before Public Review

Validate signing, entitlements, and policy forms on **real store pipelines** before production users or App Review see the build.

```bash
# iOS → TestFlight (same binary as App Store submit)
eas build --profile production --platform ios
eas submit --platform ios --latest
 
# Android → internal testing track
eas submit --platform android --profile production --latest
# eas.json submit.android.track: "internal"
```

| Track | Console path | Typical audience |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TestFlight internal | App Store Connect → TestFlight | Up to 100 ASC users, no Beta Review |
| TestFlight external | TestFlight → External testing | Up to 10k, Beta App Review |
| Play internal | Testing → Internal testing | Up to 100 emails, minutes to process |

* Internal tracks catch **wrong bundle ID**, **missing push entitlement**, and **Data safety** gaps cheaply
* External TestFlight and open beta add review latency - plan calendar accordingly
* See [TestFlight Distribution](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ios-platform/testflight-distribution/) and [Internal Testing Tracks](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/android-platform/internal-testing-tracks/)

---

### 5. Store Metadata Snapshot in the Repo

Listing copy, URLs, and keywords should not exist only in App Store Connect or Play Console - version them beside code.

```ts
// store/metadata.ts - single source for both stores
export const storeMetadata = {
  appName: "ShopApp",
  subtitle: "Scan, save, checkout fast",
  shortDescription:
    "Shop smarter with barcode scan, saved lists, and secure checkout.",
  fullDescription: `ShopApp helps you build grocery lists, compare prices, and check out in seconds.
 
• Barcode scanner for in-aisle adds
• Shared household lists
• Secure sign-in and account deletion in Settings`,
  keywords: ["grocery", "scanner", "shopping", "list"],
  privacyPolicyUrl: "https://example.com/privacy",
  supportUrl: "https://example.com/support",
  marketingUrl: "https://example.com",
} as const;
```

* Paste from this file into Connect and Play - reduces typo drift between platforms
* **Privacy policy URL** must load without login - reviewers and Play bots check this
* Localize in `store/metadata.en.ts`, `store/metadata.de.ts` when you add locales

> **Related:** [App Store Connect Workflow](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/store-operations/app-store-connect-workflow/) - full metadata checklist

### 6. Review Notes Template for App Review

Reviewers need working credentials, feature flags off, and reproduction paths - especially for login-gated Expo apps.

```markdown
<!-- store/review-notes-ios.md -->
## App Review notes (iOS)
 
**Demo account**
- Email: reviewer@example.com
- Password: ReviewDemo2026!
 
**How to test core flow**
1. Launch app → tap Sign In → use demo account above
2. Home → tap Scan → grant Camera when prompted → scan any UPC
3. Profile → Settings → Delete Account (required for account-creation apps)
 
**Backend**
- Production API; no VPN required
- Push notifications: send test from Profile → Notification test
 
**ATT / tracking**
- We do not track users across apps; ATT prompt is not shown
- Analytics: first-party only (Sentry crashes, no ad ID)
 
**Contact**
- engineering-mobile@example.com (responds within 4 business hours)
```

* Attach the same content in **App Store Connect → App Review Information → Notes**
* Update passwords every release - expired demo accounts cause false rejections
* Mention if features are geo-gated or require hardware (NFC, LiDAR)

### 7. `eas submit` to Both Stores

Automate upload after QA signs off - humans still choose **when** the build goes live.

```bash
eas submit --platform ios --latest
eas submit --platform android --latest
```

```json
// eas.json - submit profiles
{
  "submit": {
    "production": {
      "ios": {
        "appleId": "you@example.com",
        "ascAppId": "1234567890",
        "appleTeamId": "ABCDE12345"
      },
      "android": {
        "serviceAccountKeyPath": "./secrets/play-service-account.json",
        "track": "production"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

* iOS upload lands in **App Store Connect → TestFlight** first; you manually submit for review
* Android `track: "production"` uploads to production - use `internal` until policy forms pass
* Store API credentials in EAS Secrets or encrypted CI vaults - never commit JSON keys

> **Related:** [EAS Submit](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/eas-build/eas-submit/) - credential setup and CI wiring

## Intermediate Examples

### 8. Coordinated Dual-Store Release Branch

Ship iOS and Android from one release branch with a shared checklist and frozen dependencies.

```bash
git checkout -b release/2.4.0
# bump version + build numbers in app.config.ts
git commit -am "chore(release): 2.4.0 build 240012"
eas build --profile production --platform all --non-interactive
```

```yaml
# .github/workflows/release.yml (excerpt)
jobs:
  store-submit:
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/release/2.4.0'
    steps:
      - run: npx expo-doctor
      - run: eas submit --platform ios --latest --non-interactive
      - run: eas submit --platform android --latest --non-interactive
```

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Mobile lead | Merge release branch, trigger builds |
| QA | Sign TestFlight + internal track checklists |
| PM | Approve metadata and "What's New" copy |
| Eng on-call | Monitor crash rate first 24h after rollout |

* **Do not** cherry-pick unrelated features onto `release/*` - hotfixes get their own patch branch
* If one platform rejects, tag the approved build - do not rebuild both unnecessarily
* Record actual submit timestamps in `CHANGELOG.md`

### 9. Post-Submit Monitoring Dashboard

Store approval is not the finish line - watch crashes and ANRs as rollout percentage increases.

```ts
// lib/releaseHealth.ts - tag sessions with store build
import * as Application from "expo-application";
import Constants from "expo-constants";
 
export function releaseContext() {
  return {
    appVersion: Application.nativeApplicationVersion,
    buildNumber: Application.nativeBuildVersion,
    updateId: Constants.expoConfig?.updates?.checkAutomatically,
    platform: Application.applicationId,
  };
}
```

```markdown
## First 72 hours after live
- [ ] Crash-free sessions ≥ 99.5% (Sentry / Play Vitals)
- [ ] No spike in 1-star reviews mentioning "crash" or "login"
- [ ] iOS phased release day 1–2: hold at 1% if crashes climb
- [ ] Play staged rollout: pause at 20% if ANR rate doubles baseline
- [ ] Support inbox macro ready for "update app" replies
```

* Compare **build number** in crash reports to the build you promoted - OTA cannot fix native regressions
* Pair with [Phased Release & Rollback](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/store-operations/phased-release-and-rollback/) procedures
* Set PagerDuty thresholds before rollout - not after Twitter notices

### 10. Release Train Calendar (Build → Live)

A recurring calendar prevents "Friday submit" surprises and aligns marketing with phased rollout timing.

```markdown
<!-- docs/release-train.md -->
| Week | Activity | Owner |
|------|----------|-------|
| T-14 | Feature freeze on `main` | EM |
| T-10 | Cut `release/x.y.z`, bump build numbers | Mobile lead |
| T-7  | TestFlight + Play internal to QA | QA |
| T-5  | Metadata + privacy forms signed off | PM + Legal |
| T-3  | `eas submit` both platforms | Mobile lead |
| T-2  | iOS: submit for review; Android: production with 5% rollout | Mobile lead |
| T-0  | iOS: release with phased 7-day; Android: 20% → 50% → 100% | Mobile lead |
| T+1  | Go/no-go from crash dashboards | On-call |
```

* **iOS phased release** takes up to 7 days to reach 100% - plan marketing pushes after day 3–4 if metrics are clean
* **Play staged rollout** is manual percentage - document who can pause it (see incident runbook)
* EU **Digital Services Act** trader forms and age ratings must be complete before `T-3` or EU territories block

## FAQs

Can I ship the same marketing version twice?

* Yes - increment **buildNumber** / **versionCode** every upload.
* "What's New" copy can reference the same `version` string for a hotfix rebuild.

Does eas submit also release to users?

* **iOS:** Upload only - you still choose manual release, phased release, or scheduled date in App Store Connect.
* **Android:** `track` in `eas.json` determines destination; production uploads still need rollout % in Play Console unless you set 100%.

Expo Go vs development build vs store build?

* **Expo Go** cannot be submitted to stores.
* **Development builds** validate features; store ops uses **production** `distribution: "store"` profiles.

What if only Android is ready?

* Ship platforms independently - document version skew in support macros.
* Keep API backward compatibility when iOS trails Android by a week.

Where do privacy compliance tasks fit?

* Before submit: ATT, Nutrition Labels, Play Data safety - see [Compliance: ATT & Privacy Labels](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/store-operations/compliance-att-and-privacy-labels/).

Dokumen: Styling Best Practices
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/best-practices/

# Styling Best Practices

A condensed summary of the 25 most important best practices drawn from every page in this section.

Highlights / Styling Best Practices

* Cache static styles with StyleSheet.create; reserve inline for dynamic values
* Default flex direction is column - set row explicitly for horizontal layouts
* Apply safe area once at the screen root with react-native-safe-area-context
* Pair iOS shadow props with Android elevation via Platform.select
* Gate first paint until expo-font loads or hide splash on error
* Use semantic color tokens keyed off useColorScheme, not hardcoded hex in screens

1. **Cache static styles with `StyleSheet.create`:** Move layout, spacing, and color rules that do not change per render into a stylesheet - inline object literals allocate on every render and defeat native caching.
2. **Compose with style arrays:** Layer base, state, and overrides as `[styles.card, pressed && styles.cardPressed, props.style]` - order matters; document whether caller or component wins.
3. **Remember the column default:** React Native flex defaults to `column` - set `flexDirection: "row"` explicitly whenever you expect horizontal layout.
4. **Fill screens with `flex: 1`, not `height: "100%"`:** Percentage height needs a parent with defined height; `flex: 1` on the root view (inside safe area) is the reliable viewport fill pattern.
5. **Use `gap` for sibling spacing:** Prefer `gap` on flex containers over margin hacks on first/last child - fewer edge-case bugs when items mount and unmount.
6. **Wrap the app in `SafeAreaProvider` once:** Read insets via `useSafeAreaInsets` or `SafeAreaView` at the screen root - do not nest safe-area padding on every child.
7. **Pick safe-area edges deliberately:** Full-bleed hero images need `edges={['bottom']}` or manual bottom inset only - applying all edges on nested wrappers doubles padding.
8. **Plan for edge-to-edge Android (RN 0.86):** Status bar and navigation bar insets change on modern Android - test on API 35+ devices, not only classic inset models.
9. **Theme with semantic tokens:** Name colors `surface`, `textPrimary`, `borderSubtle` - map tokens to light/dark palettes instead of sprinkling `#111` and `#fff` through feature code.
10. **Sync chrome with `useColorScheme`:** Drive `StatusBar`, tab bars, and navigation headers from the active scheme - hardcoded light status bar icons vanish on dark backgrounds.
11. **Breakpoint on window width, not device class:** `useWindowDimensions().width >= 768` works for Android tablets and foldables - `Platform.isPad` alone is insufficient.
12. **Avoid web-only layout assumptions:** No media queries or `vh` - use hooks, percentage widths, and `flexWrap` for responsive phone/tablet layouts.
13. **Stabilize list wrapper styles:** `contentContainerStyle={{ padding: 16 }}` on `FlatList` recreates every parent render - hoist to `StyleSheet.create` or `useMemo`.
14. **Memoize row components, not just styles:** `memo(Row)` fails when parents pass fresh inline `style` objects - pass `styles.row` references from the stylesheet.
15. **Animate transform and opacity, not layout:** Driving `height` from `setState` every frame triggers Yoga layout each tick - use Reanimated for motion; reserve `LayoutAnimation` for discrete toggles.
16. **Shadow on a wrapper, clip on the inner view:** `overflow: "hidden"` on the same view that carries iOS `shadow*` props clips the shadow - split outer shadow wrapper and inner content.
17. **Always set `backgroundColor` on elevated surfaces:** iOS shadows and Android `elevation` need an opaque surface color - transparent cards produce invisible depth.
18. **Pair iOS shadow with Android elevation:** `shadowColor` is ignored on Android - use `Platform.select` in `StyleSheet.create` for cross-platform cards.
19. **Use `StyleSheet.hairlineWidth` for dividers:** `borderWidth: 1` looks heavy on retina screens - hairline width tracks pixel density.
20. **Load fonts before first meaningful paint:** `useFonts` + `SplashScreen.preventAutoHideAsync` - return `null` at the root until fonts load or error; never flash system font on brand screens.
21. **Register each font weight explicitly:** `fontWeight: "700"` with a single custom family often fails - load `Inter-Bold.ttf` and set `fontFamily: "Inter-Bold"` directly.
22. **Cap scaling on dense UI:** Apply `maxFontSizeMultiplier` on toolbars and chips; allow full dynamic type on body copy - accessibility without breaking layout.
23. **Define a typography scale in tokens:** Map `display`, `title`, `body`, and `label` to `fontSize` + `lineHeight` pairs - screens reference roles, not raw numbers.
24. **Profile before adopting a styling library:** NativeWind, Tamagui, and Unistyles solve scale problems - a handful of `StyleSheet` screens do not need the bundle and config cost.
25. **Audit public styles in code review:** New inline styles in list hot paths and one-off hex colors are regressions - enforce tokens and stylesheet usage in CI lint rules where possible.

## FAQs

When is inline style acceptable?

* Truly dynamic values: progress bar width, animated opacity, pressed-state toggles tied to gesture state.
* Everything else belongs in `StyleSheet.create` or a token module.

Should I use NativeWind for a new Expo SDK 57 app?

* Reach for it when you have a design system with many screens and utility-class ergonomics help velocity.
* Skip it for small apps where `StyleSheet` + tokens stay readable.

Why does my Android shadow not show?

* You likely set iOS-only `shadow*` props - add `elevation` and a solid `backgroundColor`.

How many safe-area wrappers should a screen have?

* One - typically the outermost layout view for that screen.
* Tab layouts may own top inset; child screens should not re-apply top padding.

What is the first responsive layout hook to learn?

* `useWindowDimensions()` - it re-renders on rotation and split-screen, unlike a one-shot `Dimensions.get()`.

Do dark mode tokens belong in StyleSheet?

* Define two token objects (`light`, `dark`) and select at runtime - or use a small `useTheme()` hook that returns the active palette.
* Avoid maintaining duplicate `StyleSheet.create` blocks per scheme unless profiling proves it necessary.

Dokumen: Dark Mode & Color Schemes
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/dark-mode-and-color-schemes/

# Dark Mode & Color Schemes

`useColorScheme`, dynamic palettes, and system sync.

Highlights / Dark Mode & Color Schemes

* useColorScheme returns 'light', 'dark', or null - branch styles from a token object
* Define semantic tokens (background, text, border) - not raw hex per component
* Appearance.setColorScheme overrides system choice for in-app toggle
* Expo userInterfaceStyle in app.json sets the app-level default and splash behavior
* StatusBar and navigation bar styles must follow the active scheme
* Test both schemes - automatic OS sync is the default users expect

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```tsx
import { useColorScheme, StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
const colors = {
  light: { background: "#ffffff", text: "#0f172a", muted: "#64748b", border: "#e2e8f0" },
  dark: { background: "#0f172a", text: "#f8fafc", muted: "#94a3b8", border: "#334155" },
} as const;
 
export function ThemedCard({ title, body }: { title: string; body: string }) {
  const scheme = useColorScheme() ?? "light";
  const theme = colors[scheme];
 
  return (
    <View style={[styles.card, { backgroundColor: theme.background, borderColor: theme.border }]}>
      <Text style={[styles.title, { color: theme.text }]}>{title}</Text>
      <Text style={[styles.body, { color: theme.muted }]}>{body}</Text>
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  card: { borderRadius: 12, borderWidth: 1, padding: 16, gap: 6 },
  title: { fontSize: 17, fontWeight: "600" },
  body: { fontSize: 15, lineHeight: 22 },
});
```

**When to reach for this:** Any screen that must respect the system light/dark setting - or offer an in-app override - without maintaining two separate component trees.

## Working Example

```tsx
import { useCallback, useMemo, useState } from "react";
import {
  Appearance,
  Pressable,
  StyleSheet,
  Text,
  useColorScheme,
  View,
} from "react-native";
import { StatusBar } from "expo-status-bar";
import { SafeAreaView } from "react-native-safe-area-context";
 
type Scheme = "light" | "dark";
type Preference = "system" | Scheme;
 
const palette = {
  light: {
    background: "#f8fafc",
    surface: "#ffffff",
    text: "#0f172a",
    subtext: "#475569",
    accent: "#2563eb",
    border: "#cbd5e1",
  },
  dark: {
    background: "#020617",
    surface: "#0f172a",
    text: "#f8fafc",
    subtext: "#94a3b8",
    accent: "#60a5fa",
    border: "#334155",
  },
} as const;
 
function useAppColorScheme(): Scheme {
  const system = useColorScheme();
  return system === "dark" ? "dark" : "light";
}
 
export default function SettingsAppearanceScreen() {
  const scheme = useAppColorScheme();
  const theme = palette[scheme];
  const [preference, setPreference] = useState<Preference>("system");
 
  const applyPreference = useCallback((next: Preference) => {
    setPreference(next);
    if (next === "system") {
      Appearance.setColorScheme(null); // follow OS again
    } else {
      Appearance.setColorScheme(next);
    }
  }, []);
 
  const styles = useMemo(() => makeStyles(theme), [theme]);
 
  return (
    <SafeAreaView style={styles.safe} edges={["top", "left", "right"]}>
      <StatusBar style={scheme === "dark" ? "light" : "dark"} />
 
      <Text style={styles.heading}>Appearance</Text>
      <Text style={styles.subheading}>
        System is {scheme}. Preference: {preference}.
      </Text>
 
      <View style={styles.card}>
        {(["system", "light", "dark"] as const).map((option) => (
          <Pressable
            key={option}
            onPress={() => applyPreference(option)}
            style={[styles.row, preference === option && styles.rowActive]}
          >
            <Text style={styles.rowLabel}>{option}</Text>
            {preference === option && <Text style={styles.check}>✓</Text>}
          </Pressable>
        ))}
      </View>
 
      <View style={[styles.preview, { backgroundColor: theme.surface }]}>
        <Text style={styles.previewTitle}>Preview card</Text>
        <Text style={styles.previewBody}>Semantic tokens swap with the active scheme.</Text>
      </View>
    </SafeAreaView>
  );
}
 
function makeStyles(theme: (typeof palette)[Scheme]) {
  return StyleSheet.create({
    safe: { flex: 1, backgroundColor: theme.background, padding: 16, gap: 12 },
    heading: { fontSize: 28, fontWeight: "700", color: theme.text },
    subheading: { fontSize: 15, color: theme.subtext },
    card: {
      backgroundColor: theme.surface,
      borderRadius: 12,
      borderWidth: StyleSheet.hairlineWidth,
      borderColor: theme.border,
      overflow: "hidden",
    },
    row: {
      flexDirection: "row",
      justifyContent: "space-between",
      alignItems: "center",
      paddingHorizontal: 16,
      paddingVertical: 14,
      borderBottomWidth: StyleSheet.hairlineWidth,
      borderBottomColor: theme.border,
    },
    rowActive: { backgroundColor: theme.background },
    rowLabel: { fontSize: 16, color: theme.text, textTransform: "capitalize" },
    check: { color: theme.accent, fontWeight: "700" },
    preview: {
      borderRadius: 12,
      padding: 16,
      gap: 6,
      borderWidth: StyleSheet.hairlineWidth,
      borderColor: theme.border,
    },
    previewTitle: { fontSize: 17, fontWeight: "600", color: theme.text },
    previewBody: { fontSize: 15, lineHeight: 22, color: theme.subtext },
  });
}
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* `useColorScheme()` reading the active system scheme (`"light"` | `"dark"` | `null`).
* Semantic **token objects** (`background`, `surface`, `text`) instead of hard-coded hex in components.
* `Appearance.setColorScheme()` for an in-app light/dark/system preference toggle.
* `StatusBar` from `expo-status-bar` switching `style` with the active scheme.
* `useMemo` to rebuild `StyleSheet` when the theme changes.

## Deep Dive

### How It Works

* **`useColorScheme`** is a React hook from `react-native` that subscribes to the OS appearance setting. It returns `"light"`, `"dark"`, or `null` (unknown / unavailable) and re-renders when the user toggles system dark mode.
* **`Appearance` API** - `Appearance.getColorScheme()` for one-shot reads; `Appearance.addChangeListener` for manual subscriptions; `Appearance.setColorScheme("dark" | "light" | null)` to override the app independently of the system (`null` restores system sync).
* **Semantic tokens** - Define colors by role (`textPrimary`, `borderSubtle`) not by value (`gray500`). Components reference roles; the palette maps roles to hex per scheme.
* **Expo `userInterfaceStyle`** - In `app.json` / `app.config.js`, `"userInterfaceStyle": "automatic"` follows the OS (default). `"light"` or `"dark"` locks the app regardless of system setting.
* **Native chrome** - Status bar, Android navigation bar, and iOS home indicator areas must use contrasting styles per scheme (see [Safe Areas & Notches](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/safe-areas-and-notches/)).

### useColorScheme vs Appearance

| API | Type | Use for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `useColorScheme()` | Hook - triggers re-render | Component styles, themed JSX |
| `Appearance.getColorScheme()` | Snapshot | Module-level one-time checks (rare) |
| `Appearance.addChangeListener` | Event subscription | Non-React code paths (prefer hook in components) |
| `Appearance.setColorScheme()` | Override | In-app theme picker (system / light / dark) |

```tsx
import { Appearance, useColorScheme } from "react-native";
 
// In a component - reactive
function Banner() {
  const scheme = useColorScheme() ?? "light";
  return <View style={{ backgroundColor: scheme === "dark" ? "#1e293b" : "#fff" }} />;
}
 
// Override for in-app toggle
Appearance.setColorScheme("dark");  // force dark
Appearance.setColorScheme(null);    // follow system again
```

### Token Structure Patterns

**Flat palette (small apps)**

```tsx
const colors = {
  light: { bg: "#fff", text: "#111", accent: "#2563eb" },
  dark: { bg: "#111", text: "#f8fafc", accent: "#60a5fa" },
};
```

**Semantic roles (recommended)**

```tsx
const tokens = {
  light: {
    backgroundPrimary: "#ffffff",
    textPrimary: "#0f172a",
    borderDefault: "#e2e8f0",
  },
  dark: {
    backgroundPrimary: "#0f172a",
    textPrimary: "#f8fafc",
    borderDefault: "#334155",
  },
};
```

**Context provider (shared access)**

```tsx
import { createContext, useContext, useMemo } from "react";
import { useColorScheme } from "react-native";
 
type Theme = (typeof palette)["light"];
 
const ThemeContext = createContext<Theme>(palette.light);
 
export function ThemeProvider({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  const scheme = useColorScheme() ?? "light";
  const theme = useMemo(() => palette[scheme], [scheme]);
  return <ThemeContext.Provider value={theme}>{children}</ThemeContext.Provider>;
}
 
export function useTheme() {
  return useContext(ThemeContext);
}
```

### Expo app.json Configuration

```json
{
  "expo": {
    "userInterfaceStyle": "automatic",
    "ios": { "userInterfaceStyle": "automatic" },
    "android": { "userInterfaceStyle": "automatic" }
  }
}
```

* `"automatic"` - follow OS (recommended default).
* `"light"` / `"dark"` - lock the app; `useColorScheme` still reports the forced value.
* Splash screen background should match the launch scheme to avoid a flash.

### TypeScript Notes

```tsx
import { ColorSchemeName, useColorScheme } from "react-native";
 
type Scheme = "light" | "dark";
 
function resolveScheme(name: ColorSchemeName): Scheme {
  return name === "dark" ? "dark" : "light";
}
 
function useResolvedScheme(): Scheme {
  return resolveScheme(useColorScheme());
}
 
// Typed palette - exhaustiveness checked
const palette: Record<Scheme, { background: string; text: string }> = {
  light: { background: "#fff", text: "#111" },
  dark: { background: "#111", text: "#fff" },
};
```

* `ColorSchemeName` is `"light" | "dark" | null | undefined`.
* Always handle `null` - default to `"light"` or your app's fallback.

## Gotchas

* **Hard-coded colors in `StyleSheet.create` at module scope** - Styles are frozen at load time; they do not react to scheme changes. **Fix:** Build styles inside the component with `useMemo`, or apply dynamic colors inline: `style={[styles.card, { backgroundColor: theme.surface }]}`.
* **Ignoring `null` from `useColorScheme`** - On some paths the hook returns `null`. **Fix:** `const scheme = useColorScheme() ?? "light"`.
* **Light status bar on a light background** - White-on-white status bar icons disappear. **Fix:** `StatusBar style="dark"` in light mode, `style="light"` in dark mode.
* **Forgetting images and icons** - Logos and illustrations designed for white backgrounds look wrong on dark surfaces. **Fix:** Provide `@2x` dark variants, use `tintColor`, or wrap in a themed container.
* **`Appearance.setColorScheme` without persisting preference** - User's choice resets on restart. **Fix:** Store preference in `AsyncStorage` / MMKV and apply on app launch before first paint.
* **Locked `userInterfaceStyle: "light"` in app.json while building dark UI** - Config contradicts your theme work. **Fix:** Use `"automatic"` unless you intentionally ship a single-scheme app.
* **Semi-transparent overlays** - `rgba(0,0,0,0.5)` works on light; on dark backgrounds the same overlay can look muddy. **Fix:** Define separate overlay tokens per scheme.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `useColorScheme` + token object | Default - zero deps, full control | You need complex theming with breakpoints and media queries |
| React Context `ThemeProvider` | Many nested components share tokens | One-off screens (inline branch is fine) |
| `Appearance.setColorScheme` | In-app light/dark/system toggle | Replacing token definitions - it only changes the active scheme |
| `@react-navigation/native` theme | Navigation chrome matches app colors | Non-navigation UI (still need your own tokens) |
| `react-native-unistyles` / Tamagui / NativeWind | Design-system scale, responsive + dark tokens | Simple apps with a dozen colors |
| `expo-system-ui` | Set root background color natively on scheme change | Component-level text colors |

## FAQs

What does useColorScheme return?

`"light"`, `"dark"`, or `null`. Treat `null` as unknown and fall back to `"light"` (or your app's default). The hook re-renders the component when the OS appearance changes.

How do I add an in-app dark mode toggle?

```tsx
import { Appearance } from "react-native";
 
Appearance.setColorScheme("dark");  // force dark
Appearance.setColorScheme("light"); // force light
Appearance.setColorScheme(null);    // follow system
```

Persist the user's choice and re-apply on cold start. `useColorScheme` reflects the effective scheme after override.

Should I use StyleSheet.create for themed styles?

Static keys (fontSize, fontWeight, borderRadius) can live in a static `StyleSheet`. Colors that change per scheme should be applied dynamically - either rebuild styles with `useMemo` when the scheme changes, or use `style={[styles.base, { color: theme.text }]}`.

What is userInterfaceStyle in app.json?

Expo config that sets the app-level appearance policy: `"automatic"` (follow OS), `"light"`, or `"dark"`. It affects splash screen and native shell defaults. Prefer `"automatic"` for most apps.

How do I theme the status bar?

```tsx
import { StatusBar } from "expo-status-bar";
 
<StatusBar style={scheme === "dark" ? "light" : "dark"} />
```

Light content (white icons) on dark backgrounds; dark content on light backgrounds.

Gotcha: Why do my colors not update when I toggle system dark mode?

You likely hard-coded colors in a module-level `StyleSheet.create`. Move color values to a palette keyed by scheme and apply them in render, or rebuild styles when `useColorScheme` changes.

Should I define separate components for light and dark?

No - branch styles, not trees. One component structure with theme tokens is easier to maintain than duplicated JSX for each scheme.

How do semantic tokens help?

Components reference `theme.text` instead of `#0f172a`. When you adjust the dark palette, every screen updates. Renaming `gray-700` to a role like `textSecondary` survives palette overhauls.

Does React Navigation respect dark mode?

Pass a `theme` and `darkTheme` to `NavigationContainer` using your token palette. Screen content still needs its own `useColorScheme` branching - navigation theming only covers headers, tabs, and cards built into the navigator.

How do I avoid a white flash on launch in dark mode?

Set splash `backgroundColor` to your dark `background` token in `app.json`. Use `expo-system-ui` to set the root view background. Apply theme before rendering the first screen.

Can I detect dark mode outside a React component?

`Appearance.getColorScheme()` returns the current value synchronously. For reactive UI, prefer `useColorScheme` in components or `Appearance.addChangeListener` in non-UI modules.

How do shadows and borders change in dark mode?

Shadows are less visible on dark backgrounds - rely more on border tokens (`borderColor: theme.border`) and subtle surface elevation. See [Shadows, Elevation & Borders](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/shadows-elevation-and-borders/).

What about images that only work on light backgrounds?

Use `scheme === "dark"` to swap `source`, apply a light `tintColor`, or place the image on a fixed `surface` container that stays light in both schemes (e.g., brand logo lockup).

Does useColorScheme work with Expo Router?

Yes - it is a standard React Native hook. Use it in any client screen or layout. It updates when the system appearance changes while the app is running.

How does dark mode interact with safe areas?

Safe area insets are independent of color scheme, but status bar contrast depends on both. Coordinate `StatusBar` style with your header background. See [Safe Areas & Notches](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/safe-areas-and-notches/).

## Related

* [Styling Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/styling-basics/) - StyleSheet vs inline styles and dynamic color application
* [Safe Areas & Notches](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/safe-areas-and-notches/) - status bar style on edge-to-edge screens
* [Shadows, Elevation & Borders](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/shadows-elevation-and-borders/) - platform shadows that need per-scheme tuning
* [Typography Scale & Font Loading](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/typography-scale-and-font-loading/) - readable text contrast in both schemes
* [Responsive & Adaptive Layout](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/responsive-and-adaptive-layout/) - layout tokens that may also vary by breakpoint

Dokumen: Flexbox Deep Dive
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/flexbox-deep-dive/

# Flexbox Deep Dive

The mobile layout workhorse - direction, flex, align, and common recipes.

Highlights / Flexbox Deep Dive

* React Native defaults to flexDirection: column - opposite of most web row-first layouts
* flex: 1 means grow to fill remaining space along the main axis
* justifyContent aligns on the main axis; alignItems on the cross axis
* gap replaces margin hacks between flex children (RN 0.71+)
* flexShrink: 0 prevents squashed icons and avatars in crowded rows
* The header–content–footer shell is three nested flex: 1 containers

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```tsx
import { StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
export function ScreenShell() {
  return (
    <View style={styles.screen}>
      <View style={styles.header}>
        <Text style={styles.title}>Inbox</Text>
      </View>
 
      <View style={styles.content}>
        <Text>Scrollable or list content goes here.</Text>
      </View>
 
      <View style={styles.footer}>
        <Text style={styles.footerText}>3 unread</Text>
      </View>
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  screen: { flex: 1, backgroundColor: "#fff" },
  header: {
    paddingHorizontal: 16,
    paddingVertical: 12,
    borderBottomWidth: StyleSheet.hairlineWidth,
    borderBottomColor: "#e2e8f0",
  },
  title: { fontSize: 20, fontWeight: "700" },
  content: { flex: 1, padding: 16 }, // grows - pushes footer down
  footer: {
    padding: 16,
    borderTopWidth: StyleSheet.hairlineWidth,
    borderTopColor: "#e2e8f0",
  },
  footerText: { textAlign: "center", color: "#64748b" },
});
```

**When to reach for this:** Any screen layout in React Native - rows, columns, toolbars, cards, and the classic header/content/footer shell all run through Yoga flexbox.

## Working Example

```tsx
import { ScrollView, StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
interface Task {
  id: string;
  title: string;
  done: boolean;
}
 
const TASKS: Task[] = [
  { id: "1", title: "Review flexbox PR", done: false },
  { id: "2", title: "Ship dark mode tokens", done: true },
  { id: "3", title: "Test foldable layout", done: false },
];
 
export default function TaskBoard() {
  return (
    <View style={styles.screen}>
      {/* Toolbar row */}
      <View style={styles.toolbar}>
        <Text style={styles.heading}>Tasks</Text>
        <View style={styles.badge}>
          <Text style={styles.badgeText}>{TASKS.filter((t) => !t.done).length}</Text>
        </View>
      </View>
 
      {/* Scrollable flex child */}
      <ScrollView contentContainerStyle={styles.list}>
        {TASKS.map((task) => (
          <View key={task.id} style={styles.row}>
            <View style={[styles.dot, task.done && styles.dotDone]} />
            <Text
              style={[styles.rowTitle, task.done && styles.rowTitleDone]}
              numberOfLines={1}
            >
              {task.title}
            </Text>
            <Text style={styles.rowMeta}>{task.done ? "Done" : "Open"}</Text>
          </View>
        ))}
      </ScrollView>
 
      {/* Bottom action bar */}
      <View style={styles.actionBar}>
        <View style={styles.actionPrimary}>
          <Text style={styles.actionPrimaryText}>Add task</Text>
        </View>
      </View>
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  screen: { flex: 1, backgroundColor: "#f8fafc" },
  toolbar: {
    flexDirection: "row",
    alignItems: "center",
    justifyContent: "space-between",
    paddingHorizontal: 16,
    paddingVertical: 12,
    gap: 8,
  },
  heading: { fontSize: 28, fontWeight: "700", color: "#0f172a" },
  badge: {
    minWidth: 28,
    height: 28,
    borderRadius: 14,
    backgroundColor: "#2563eb",
    alignItems: "center",
    justifyContent: "center",
    paddingHorizontal: 8,
  },
  badgeText: { color: "#fff", fontWeight: "700", fontSize: 13 },
  list: { padding: 16, gap: 10 },
  row: {
    flexDirection: "row",
    alignItems: "center",
    gap: 12,
    backgroundColor: "#fff",
    borderRadius: 12,
    padding: 14,
  },
  dot: {
    width: 10,
    height: 10,
    borderRadius: 5,
    backgroundColor: "#94a3b8",
    flexShrink: 0,
  },
  dotDone: { backgroundColor: "#22c55e" },
  rowTitle: { flex: 1, fontSize: 16, fontWeight: "600", color: "#0f172a" },
  rowTitleDone: { color: "#94a3b8", textDecorationLine: "line-through" },
  rowMeta: { fontSize: 13, color: "#64748b", flexShrink: 0 },
  actionBar: {
    padding: 16,
    borderTopWidth: StyleSheet.hairlineWidth,
    borderTopColor: "#cbd5e1",
    backgroundColor: "#fff",
  },
  actionPrimary: {
    backgroundColor: "#2563eb",
    borderRadius: 12,
    paddingVertical: 14,
    alignItems: "center",
  },
  actionPrimaryText: { color: "#fff", fontWeight: "600", fontSize: 16 },
});
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* `flex: 1` on the screen root so the layout fills the device viewport.
* `flexDirection: "row"` for toolbar and list rows - explicit, never assumed.
* `justifyContent: "space-between"` to pin title left and badge right.
* `flex: 1` on the title `Text` so it truncates while meta stays visible.
* `flexShrink: 0` on the dot and meta so icons do not get squashed.
* `gap` for consistent spacing between row children without margin math.
* `ScrollView` as a flex child that scrolls while the action bar stays pinned.

## Deep Dive

### How It Works

* React Native layout runs through **Yoga**, a flexbox implementation shared across iOS and Android.
* Every `View` is a flex container. The default `display` is flex; there is no block/inline split like the web.
* Default **`flexDirection` is `column`** - children stack vertically unless you set `row`.
* Default **`alignItems` is `stretch`** - children expand to the container's cross-axis width (in a column, that means full width).
* Default **`flexShrink` is 0** on children (differs from many browser defaults) - items keep their intrinsic size unless you allow shrinking.
* **`flex: 1`** is shorthand for `flexGrow: 1`, `flexShrink: 1`, `flexBasis: 0` - the child claims all remaining space along the main axis.
* Styles cross the JS/native boundary on update; deep flex trees with frequent style object recreation can add layout cost (see [Style Performance](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/style-performance/)).

### Main-Axis vs Cross-Axis

| `flexDirection` | Main axis (justifyContent) | Cross axis (alignItems) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `column` (default) | Vertical ↕ | Horizontal ↔ |
| `row` | Horizontal ↔ | Vertical ↕ |
| `column-reverse` | Vertical (reversed) | Horizontal |
| `row-reverse` | Horizontal (reversed) | Vertical |

```tsx
// Column (default): justifyContent = vertical, alignItems = horizontal
<View style={{ flex: 1, justifyContent: "center", alignItems: "center" }}>
  <Text>Centered</Text>
</View>
 
// Row: justifyContent = horizontal, alignItems = vertical
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", gap: 8 }}>
  <Icon />
  <Text style={{ flex: 1 }}>Label fills middle space</Text>
  <Chevron />
</View>
```

### Flex Properties at a Glance

| Property | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `flex: 1` | Grow to fill remaining space; shrink if needed |
| `flexGrow: 1` | Take extra space when siblings do not |
| `flexShrink: 1` | Allow shrinking below intrinsic size when crowded |
| `flexShrink: 0` | Never shrink - protect icons, badges, avatars |
| `flexBasis: "auto"` | Start from content size, then grow/shrink |
| `flexBasis: 0` | Ignore content size when distributing space |
| `alignSelf` | Override parent's `alignItems` for one child |

### Common Layout Recipes

**1. Header / scrollable content / footer**

```tsx
<View style={{ flex: 1 }}>
  <Header />
  <ScrollView style={{ flex: 1 }} contentContainerStyle={{ padding: 16 }} />
  <Footer />
</View>
```

**2. Horizontally spaced toolbar actions**

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", justifyContent: "space-between", alignItems: "center" }}>
  <BackButton />
  <Title />
  <MenuButton />
</View>
```

**3. Equal-width segments (tabs)**

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row" }}>
  {tabs.map((tab) => (
    <Pressable key={tab} style={{ flex: 1, alignItems: "center" }}>
      <Text>{tab}</Text>
    </Pressable>
  ))}
</View>
```

**4. Bottom-aligned card actions**

```tsx
<View style={{ flex: 1, justifyContent: "flex-end", padding: 16 }}>
  <PrimaryButton />
</View>
```

**5. Wrapping chip row**

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", flexWrap: "wrap", gap: 8 }}>
  {tags.map((tag) => (
    <Chip key={tag} label={tag} />
  ))}
</View>
```

### TypeScript Notes

```tsx
import type { FlexStyle, ViewStyle } from "react-native";
 
type Justify = FlexStyle["justifyContent"]; // "flex-start" | "center" | "space-between" | ...
 
interface RowProps {
  children: React.ReactNode;
  justify?: Justify;
  style?: ViewStyle;
}
 
function Row({ children, justify = "flex-start", style }: RowProps) {
  return (
    <View style={[{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", justifyContent: justify, gap: 8 }, style]}>
      {children}
    </View>
  );
}
```

* `FlexStyle` covers flex-specific keys; `ViewStyle` is the full view style type.
* Style arrays merge left-to-right: `[styles.base, isActive && styles.active]`.
* Falsy entries in style arrays (`false`, `null`, `undefined`) are ignored safely.

## Gotchas

* **Assuming row direction** - Pasting web snippets without `flexDirection: "row"` stacks items vertically. **Fix:** Set `flexDirection: "row"` explicitly for horizontal layouts.
* **Missing `flex: 1` on the screen root** - Content does not fill the viewport; footers float mid-screen. **Fix:** Apply `flex: 1` to the outermost `View` (inside your safe-area wrapper).
* **Using `height: "100%"` instead of `flex: 1`** - Percentage height requires a parent with explicit height; fails unpredictably in nested trees. **Fix:** Prefer `flex: 1` for fill-remaining-space layouts.
* **Truncated text in rows without `flex: 1`** - Long titles push siblings off-screen instead of ellipsizing. **Fix:** Give the `Text` `flex: 1` (and `numberOfLines`) inside a row; set `flexShrink: 0` on trailing icons.
* **`justifyContent: "center"` without `flex: 1`** - Centering only works within the container's content height, not the full screen. **Fix:** Give the container `flex: 1` so it spans available space.
* **`alignItems: "center"` shrinking row children** - Children shrink to content width; a `width: "100%"` child may not stretch. **Fix:** Use `alignSelf: "stretch"` on the child that must be full width, or use `alignItems: "stretch"` on the parent.
* **Padding on `ScrollView` instead of `contentContainerStyle`** - Scroll indicators and bounce behave oddly on iOS. **Fix:** Put padding and `gap` on `contentContainerStyle`; keep `style={{ flex: 1 }}` on the `ScrollView` itself.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Yoga flexbox (`View`) | Default for all RN layout - rows, columns, fill space | You need absolute positioning overlays (use `position: "absolute"`) |
| `FlatList` / `SectionList` | Long virtualized lists with homogeneous rows | Short static content - `ScrollView` + `map` is simpler |
| `react-native-reanimated` layout animations | Animated flex changes, entering/exiting layouts | Static screens with no motion requirements |
| Percentage widths (`width: "50%"`) | Simple two-column splits | Precise multi-column grids - calculate dp from `useWindowDimensions` |
| CSS Grid (web-only targets) | Expo web with responsive grid | iOS/Android production layouts - flex is the portable choice |

## FAQs

What is the default flex direction in React Native?

`column` - children stack top to bottom. This is the opposite of many web nav bars that implicitly flow in a row. Always set `flexDirection: "row"` when you want horizontal layout.

What does flex: 1 actually mean?

It is shorthand for `flexGrow: 1`, `flexShrink: 1`, `flexBasis: 0`. The child grows to consume all remaining space along the parent's main axis and can shrink if space is tight. Put `flex: 1` on the screen root and on content areas between fixed headers/footers.

When should I use justifyContent vs alignItems?

* `justifyContent` - alignment along the **main** axis (vertical in a column, horizontal in a row).
* `alignItems` - alignment along the **cross** axis (horizontal in a column, vertical in a row).

Center a single child in a full screen: `flex: 1`, `justifyContent: "center"`, `alignItems: "center"`.

How do I keep a footer pinned to the bottom?

```tsx
<View style={{ flex: 1 }}>
  <ScrollView style={{ flex: 1 }} />
  <Footer />
</View>
```

The `ScrollView` with `flex: 1` takes all space above the footer. The footer renders at its natural height below.

Why does my row text not truncate with ellipsis?

`numberOfLines` needs a bounded width. In a row, give the `Text` `flex: 1` so it competes for space, and `flexShrink: 0` on trailing icons so they keep their size.

What is flexShrink: 0 for?

It prevents a child from shrinking below its intrinsic size when the row is crowded. Use it on avatars, icons, badges, and fixed-width buttons so they do not get squashed.

Does gap work in React Native flex layouts?

Yes - `gap`, `rowGap`, and `columnGap` are supported in React Native 0.71+. They add space between flex children without margin on first/last items. Works in `View` and `ScrollView` `contentContainerStyle`.

How do I space items evenly across a row?

* `justifyContent: "space-between"` - first at start, last at end, equal space between.
* `justifyContent: "space-around"` - equal space around each item.
* `justifyContent: "space-evenly"` - perfectly even gaps including edges.

For toolbar back/title/menu, `space-between` is the most common.

Can I nest flex containers?

Yes - flex is recursive. A column screen can contain row toolbars, row list items, and column cards. Each `View` establishes its own flex context with independent main/cross axes.

Gotcha: Why does centering only work sometimes?

`justifyContent: "center"` centers within the container's own height. If the container wraps its content (no `flex: 1`), centering has no extra space to work with. Add `flex: 1` to the container.

How does flexWrap work?

`flexWrap: "wrap"` lets row children flow to the next line when they exceed the container width. Combine with `gap` for chip grids and tag clouds. Set explicit widths on children or use percentage basis for even columns.

What is alignSelf?

It overrides the parent's `alignItems` for a single child. Example: parent has `alignItems: "center"` but one child needs full width - set `alignSelf: "stretch"` on that child.

Should I use margin or gap between flex children?

Prefer `gap` for uniform spacing between siblings. Use margin when one item needs asymmetric spacing (e.g., push a button to the right with `marginLeft: "auto"` in a row - though `justifyContent: "space-between"` is cleaner).

How does flex interact with ScrollView?

Give the `ScrollView` `style={{ flex: 1 }}` so it fills space between siblings. Put padding and `gap` on `contentContainerStyle`. Add `contentContainerStyle={{ flexGrow: 1 }}` when you need the scroll content to fill the viewport (e.g., center empty-state text).

Where do I learn responsive breakpoints and tablet layouts?

Flex distributes space within a container; breakpoints decide *which* flex tree to render. See [Responsive & Adaptive Layout](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/responsive-and-adaptive-layout/) and [Dimensions & Responsive Layout](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/rn-fundamentals/dimensions-and-responsive-layout/).

## Related

* [Styling Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/styling-basics/) - `StyleSheet.create`, inline styles, and the RN styling mental model
* [Safe Areas & Notches](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/safe-areas-and-notches/) - insets around your flex screen shell
* [Responsive & Adaptive Layout](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/responsive-and-adaptive-layout/) - breakpoints that change flex trees on tablet

Dokumen: Styling & Layout Highlights Summary
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/highlights-summary/

# Styling & Layout Highlights Summary

Every highlight bullet from the 9 pages in this section, gathered on one page and grouped by the page it came from.

Highlights / Styling & Layout Highlights Summary

* React Native styles are JavaScript objects - no CSS cascade, classes, or selectors
* React Native defaults to flexDirection: column - opposite of most web row-first layouts
* Use react-native-safe-area-context - not the deprecated core SafeAreaView
* useColorScheme returns 'light', 'dark', or null - branch styles from a token object
* There are no CSS media queries - use useWindowDimensions and app-defined breakpoints
* StyleSheet.create registers styles once - inline objects allocate on every render

## [Styling Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/styling-basics/)

* React Native styles are JavaScript objects - no CSS cascade, classes, or selectors
* StyleSheet.create validates properties and sends cached IDs to the native layer
* Flexbox defaults to column direction - the opposite of most web layouts
* Combine styles with arrays; later entries override earlier ones
* useColorScheme reads the system light/dark preference for dynamic palettes
* SafeAreaView from react-native-safe-area-context clears notches and home indicators
* Platform.select is the idiomatic way to branch iOS shadow vs Android elevation

## [Flexbox Deep Dive](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/flexbox-deep-dive/)

* React Native defaults to flexDirection: column - opposite of most web row-first layouts
* flex: 1 means grow to fill remaining space along the main axis
* justifyContent aligns on the main axis; alignItems on the cross axis
* gap replaces margin hacks between flex children (RN 0.71+)
* flexShrink: 0 prevents squashed icons and avatars in crowded rows
* The header–content–footer shell is three nested flex: 1 containers

## [Safe Areas & Notches](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/safe-areas-and-notches/)

* Use react-native-safe-area-context - not the deprecated core SafeAreaView
* Wrap the app root in SafeAreaProvider once; read insets via hook or SafeAreaView
* edges prop controls which sides get padding - omit bottom above tab bars
* RN 0.86 enables edge-to-edge Android by default - content draws behind system bars
* useSafeAreaInsets for granular padding; SafeAreaView for whole-screen wrappers
* Double safe-area padding is the most common layout bug - one owner per axis

## [Dark Mode & Color Schemes](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/dark-mode-and-color-schemes/)

* useColorScheme returns 'light', 'dark', or null - branch styles from a token object
* Define semantic tokens (background, text, border) - not raw hex per component
* Appearance.setColorScheme overrides system choice for in-app toggle
* Expo userInterfaceStyle in app.json sets the app-level default and splash behavior
* StatusBar and navigation bar styles must follow the active scheme
* Test both schemes - automatic OS sync is the default users expect

## [Responsive & Adaptive Layout](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/responsive-and-adaptive-layout/)

* There are no CSS media queries - use useWindowDimensions and app-defined breakpoints
* 768 dp is the common tablet threshold; 600 dp matches Material compact-to-medium
* Adaptive layout changes structure (split view), not just spacing
* Foldables and split-screen shrink window width - test narrow states
* Combine breakpoints with flexbox - dimensions pick the tree, flex distributes space
* Safe area insets are orthogonal to breakpoints - handle both

## [Style Performance](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/style-performance/)

* StyleSheet.create registers styles once - inline objects allocate on every render
* A new style reference crosses the JS/native boundary even when values are unchanged
* Static style arrays are cheap; dynamic entries inside renderItem are not
* Layout thrash happens when width, flex, or position flip every frame - batch updates
* Pressable style callbacks should return StyleSheet IDs, not fresh object literals
* Profile with React DevTools and Hermes sampling before sprinkling useMemo on styles

## [Shadows, Elevation & Borders](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/shadows-elevation-and-borders/)

* iOS uses shadowColor, shadowOffset, shadowOpacity, and shadowRadius - Android ignores them
* Android elevation draws a material shadow from the view background - set backgroundColor
* overflow: hidden on iOS clips shadow spread - apply shadow to a wrapper View
* StyleSheet.hairlineWidth gives a crisp 1-device-pixel border on both platforms
* borderRadius with overflow hidden is the standard recipe for rounded image masks
* Platform.select inside StyleSheet.create keeps one file for cross-platform cards

## [Typography Scale & Font Loading](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/typography-scale-and-font-loading/)

* Load custom fonts with expo-font useFonts before rendering branded text
* Gate the splash screen until fonts resolve - avoid FOUT with SplashScreen.preventAutoHideAsync
* Define a typography scale as tokens (display, title, body, caption) not ad-hoc font sizes
* fontFamily must match the key passed to useFonts exactly - including weight variants
* allowFontScaling respects system accessibility settings - cap with maxFontSizeMultiplier on dense UI
* lineHeight is in dp; pair with fontSize for readable multi-line body copy

## [Styling Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/best-practices/)

* Cache static styles with StyleSheet.create; reserve inline for dynamic values
* Default flex direction is column - set row explicitly for horizontal layouts
* Apply safe area once at the screen root with react-native-safe-area-context
* Pair iOS shadow props with Android elevation via Platform.select
* Gate first paint until expo-font loads or hide splash on error
* Use semantic color tokens keyed off useColorScheme, not hardcoded hex in screens
