Dokumen: Typography Scale & Font Loading
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/typography-scale-and-font-loading/

# Typography Scale & Font Loading

`expo-font`, custom families, and accessible text sizing.

Highlights / Typography Scale & Font Loading

* Load custom fonts with expo-font useFonts before rendering branded text
* Gate the splash screen until fonts resolve - avoid FOUT with SplashScreen.preventAutoHideAsync
* Define a typography scale as tokens (display, title, body, caption) not ad-hoc font sizes
* fontFamily must match the key passed to useFonts exactly - including weight variants
* allowFontScaling respects system accessibility settings - cap with maxFontSizeMultiplier on dense UI
* lineHeight is in dp; pair with fontSize for readable multi-line body copy

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
npx expo install expo-font expo-splash-screen
```

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx (Expo Router root) or App.tsx
import { useFonts } from "expo-font";
import * as SplashScreen from "expo-splash-screen";
import { useEffect } from "react";
import { Text, View } from "react-native";
import { typography } from "./theme/typography";
 
SplashScreen.preventAutoHideAsync();
 
export default function RootLayout() {
  const [loaded, error] = useFonts({
    "Inter-Regular": require("./assets/fonts/Inter-Regular.ttf"),
    "Inter-SemiBold": require("./assets/fonts/Inter-SemiBold.ttf"),
  });
 
  useEffect(() => {
    if (loaded || error) SplashScreen.hideAsync();
  }, [loaded, error]);
 
  if (!loaded && !error) return null;
 
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1 }}>
      <Text style={typography.title}>Typography ready</Text>
      <Text style={typography.body}>Inter loads before first paint.</Text>
    </View>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// theme/typography.ts
import { StyleSheet } from "react-native";
 
export const typography = StyleSheet.create({
  title: {
    fontFamily: "Inter-SemiBold",
    fontSize: 24,
    lineHeight: 32,
    letterSpacing: -0.3,
    color: "#0f172a",
  },
  body: {
    fontFamily: "Inter-Regular",
    fontSize: 16,
    lineHeight: 24,
    color: "#334155",
  },
  caption: {
    fontFamily: "Inter-Regular",
    fontSize: 12,
    lineHeight: 16,
    color: "#64748b",
  },
});
```

**When to reach for this:** Brand fonts, consistent heading hierarchy, or accessibility-safe text - you need custom families loaded before UI renders and a token scale instead of magic numbers scattered in screens.

## Working Example

```tsx
import { useFonts } from "expo-font";
import * as SplashScreen from "expo-splash-screen";
import { useEffect } from "react";
import { PixelRatio, StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
SplashScreen.preventAutoHideAsync();
 
const FONT_SCALE = PixelRatio.getFontScale();
 
type TextVariant = "display" | "title" | "body" | "caption" | "label";
 
const variantStyles: Record<TextVariant, object> = {
  display: typography.display,
  title: typography.title,
  body: typography.body,
  caption: typography.caption,
  label: typography.label,
};
 
function AppText({
  variant = "body",
  children,
  maxScale = 1.35,
}: {
  variant?: TextVariant;
  children: React.ReactNode;
  maxScale?: number;
}) {
  return (
    <Text
      style={variantStyles[variant]}
      allowFontScaling
      maxFontSizeMultiplier={maxScale}
    >
      {children}
    </Text>
  );
}
 
export default function TypographyScreen() {
  const [fontsLoaded, fontError] = useFonts({
    "Inter-Regular": require("./assets/fonts/Inter-Regular.ttf"),
    "Inter-SemiBold": require("./assets/fonts/Inter-SemiBold.ttf"),
    "Inter-Bold": require("./assets/fonts/Inter-Bold.ttf"),
  });
 
  useEffect(() => {
    if (fontsLoaded || fontError) SplashScreen.hideAsync();
  }, [fontsLoaded, fontError]);
 
  if (!fontsLoaded && !fontError) return null;
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.screen}>
      <AppText variant="display">Good morning</AppText>
      <AppText variant="title">Your tasks today</AppText>
      <AppText variant="body">
        System font scale is {FONT_SCALE.toFixed(2)}×. Body copy scales with accessibility
        settings up to the configured cap.
      </AppText>
      <AppText variant="caption">Last synced 2 min ago</AppText>
      <View style={styles.chip}>
        <AppText variant="label" maxScale={1.2}>
          3 overdue
        </AppText>
      </View>
    </View>
  );
}
 
const typography = StyleSheet.create({
  display: {
    fontFamily: "Inter-Bold",
    fontSize: 34,
    lineHeight: 40,
    letterSpacing: -0.5,
    color: "#0f172a",
  },
  title: {
    fontFamily: "Inter-SemiBold",
    fontSize: 22,
    lineHeight: 28,
    color: "#0f172a",
  },
  body: {
    fontFamily: "Inter-Regular",
    fontSize: 16,
    lineHeight: 24,
    color: "#334155",
  },
  caption: {
    fontFamily: "Inter-Regular",
    fontSize: 13,
    lineHeight: 18,
    color: "#64748b",
  },
  label: {
    fontFamily: "Inter-SemiBold",
    fontSize: 12,
    lineHeight: 16,
    letterSpacing: 0.6,
    textTransform: "uppercase",
    color: "#475569",
  },
});
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  screen: { flex: 1, padding: 24, gap: 12, backgroundColor: "#f8fafc" },
  chip: {
    alignSelf: "flex-start",
    marginTop: 8,
    paddingHorizontal: 10,
    paddingVertical: 4,
    borderRadius: 6,
    backgroundColor: "#fee2e2",
  },
});
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* `useFonts` loads multiple weights as separate family keys - the Expo SDK 57 pattern for static TTF files
* Splash screen stays visible until fonts load or error, preventing flash of system font
* Typography tokens (`display`, `title`, `body`, `caption`, `label`) centralize size, line height, and family
* `AppText` wrapper applies `allowFontScaling` and per-variant `maxFontSizeMultiplier` caps
* `PixelRatio.getFontScale()` surfaces the current accessibility multiplier for layout debugging

## Deep Dive

### Loading Fonts with expo-font

`expo-font` ships with Expo SDK 57 and wraps native font registration on iOS and Android.

| API | Use case |
| --- | --- |
| `useFonts(map)` | React hook - returns `[loaded, error]`; best for root layout gating |
| `Font.loadAsync(map)` | Imperative preload in bootstrap routines alongside `Asset.loadAsync` |
| `Font.isLoaded(name)` | Check a single family before rendering a lazy subtree |

```tsx
import * as Font from "expo-font";
 
// Imperative batch (e.g. before navigation mounts)
await Font.loadAsync({
  "Inter-Regular": require("./assets/fonts/Inter-Regular.ttf"),
});
```

Install aligned to SDK 57:

```bash
npx expo install expo-font expo-splash-screen
```

Font files must live under `assets/` and be statically `require()`'d - Metro bundles them at build time.

### Splash Screen Gate

Without a gate, React renders immediately with the system font, then swaps when custom fonts arrive (**flash of unstyled text**).

```tsx
import * as SplashScreen from "expo-splash-screen";
 
SplashScreen.preventAutoHideAsync();
 
// In root component
useEffect(() => {
  if (loaded || error) SplashScreen.hideAsync();
}, [loaded, error]);
 
if (!loaded && !error) return null;
```

* Call `preventAutoHideAsync` at module scope before the first render.
* Return `null` (or a minimal placeholder) while `loaded` is false.
* Hide splash on **error** too - otherwise the app stalls on a frozen splash screen.

### Font Family vs fontWeight

React Native does **not** map `fontWeight: "600"` to a custom TTF automatically. Each weight/style is usually a separate file registered under its own family name.

```tsx
// Works - explicit family per file
{ fontFamily: "Inter-SemiBold", fontSize: 18 }
 
// Unreliable with custom fonts - may fall back to system bold
{ fontFamily: "Inter-Regular", fontWeight: "600", fontSize: 18 }
```

| Approach | Pros | Cons |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Separate files per weight (`Inter-Bold`, etc.) | Predictable on iOS and Android | More files to load |
| Single variable font (when supported) | One file | Verify RN/Expo support for your font format |
| System font (`fontFamily: undefined`) | Zero load time, native feel | No brand typography |

### Typography Scale Tokens

Define a fixed ramp - do not pick `fontSize` per screen ad hoc.

| Token | Typical `fontSize` / `lineHeight` | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `display` | 32–40 / 38–48 | Hero headings |
| `title` | 20–24 / 26–32 | Screen titles, card headers |
| `body` | 15–17 / 22–26 | Paragraphs, list primary text |
| `caption` | 11–13 / 14–18 | Timestamps, metadata |
| `label` | 11–12 / 14–16 | Chips, badges, overlines |

```tsx
export const fontSize = {
  xs: 12,
  sm: 14,
  md: 16,
  lg: 20,
  xl: 24,
  "2xl": 32,
} as const;
 
// lineHeight ≈ 1.4–1.5 × fontSize for body; tighter for display
```

Pair tokens with `letterSpacing` and `textTransform` on labels - keep numeric rhythm in one module.

### Accessible Text Sizing

iOS and Android expose **font scale** accessibility settings. React Native respects them by default on `Text`.

| Prop | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `allowFontScaling` | `true` | When `false`, ignores system font scale |
| `maxFontSizeMultiplier` | unlimited | Caps how large text can grow (iOS/Android) |
| `adjustsFontSizeToFit` | `false` | Shrinks text to fit `numberOfLines` box (iOS) |

```tsx
<Text allowFontScaling maxFontSizeMultiplier={1.3} style={typography.body}>
  Accessible body copy
</Text>
 
// Dense UI - toolbar, tab labels
<Text maxFontSizeMultiplier={1.1} numberOfLines={1}>
  Dashboard
</Text>
```

Use `PixelRatio.getFontScale()` to log or adapt layouts at extreme scales (e.g. switch list rows to two lines).

**Do not** disable `allowFontScaling` app-wide - it breaks accessibility. Cap selectively on chips, nav bars, and fixed-height buttons.

### lineHeight and Vertical Rhythm

* `lineHeight` is in **density-independent pixels**, not unitless like CSS `line-height: 1.5`.
* Rule of thumb: `lineHeight = fontSize × 1.4` for body, tighter for large display type.
* `Text` inside a row with `alignItems: "center"` may look off if line heights differ - normalize variants.

```tsx
body: {
  fontSize: 16,
  lineHeight: 24, // 1.5× - comfortable paragraph
},
display: {
  fontSize: 34,
  lineHeight: 40, // ~1.18× - tight hero
},
```

### Combining with Images and Assets

Load fonts in the same bootstrap routine as image preloading:

```tsx
import { Asset } from "expo-asset";
import * as Font from "expo-font";
 
export async function loadResources() {
  await Promise.all([
    Asset.loadAsync([require("./assets/logo.png")]),
    Font.loadAsync({
      "Inter-Regular": require("./assets/fonts/Inter-Regular.ttf"),
    }),
  ]);
}
```

See the images and assets article for splash coordination with `Asset.loadAsync`.

### TypeScript Notes

```tsx
import type { TextStyle } from "react-native";
 
export type TypographyVariant = "display" | "title" | "body" | "caption";
 
export const typography: Record<TypographyVariant, TextStyle> = StyleSheet.create({
  display: { fontFamily: "Inter-Bold", fontSize: 34, lineHeight: 40 },
  title: { fontFamily: "Inter-SemiBold", fontSize: 22, lineHeight: 28 },
  body: { fontFamily: "Inter-Regular", fontSize: 16, lineHeight: 24 },
  caption: { fontFamily: "Inter-Regular", fontSize: 13, lineHeight: 18 },
});
```

* `TextStyle` includes `fontFamily`, `fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`, `fontVariant`.
* Font map keys in `useFonts` are strings - use the same string in `fontFamily`.
* `require()` of `.ttf` / `.otf` returns a number (asset module ID) at build time.

## Gotchas

* **Flash of system font** - Rendering text before `useFonts` resolves. **Fix:** Gate root layout with splash screen + `return null` until `loaded`.
* **fontWeight with custom family** - `fontFamily: "Inter"` + `fontWeight: "700"` often ignores the custom file. **Fix:** Register each weight as its own family name and reference it directly.
* **Wrong font family string** - `fontFamily` must match the `useFonts` key exactly (`"Inter-SemiBold"`, not `"Inter SemiBold"`). **Fix:** Copy keys from the load map.
* **Missing font file in bundle** - Dynamic `require` paths fail Metro static analysis. **Fix:** Static `require("./assets/fonts/Inter-Regular.ttf")` only.
* **Uncapped scaling breaks layouts** - Large accessibility fonts overflow toolbars and chips. **Fix:** `maxFontSizeMultiplier` on dense components; allow full scaling on body copy.
* **lineHeight too small** - Descenders clip on Android with tight line heights. **Fix:** Increase `lineHeight` or add `paddingVertical` on single-line badges.
* **Splash never hides on font error** - Waiting only for `loaded`. **Fix:** `if (loaded || error) SplashScreen.hideAsync()` and show a fallback system-font UI.
* **Variable font assumptions** - Not all variable font files work identically across platforms. **Fix:** Test on both iOS and Android devices; fall back to static weights if weights do not resolve.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `useFonts` hook at root | Expo Router / single root layout | Fonts needed only in one lazy screen (still preload at root for consistency) |
| `Font.loadAsync` in bootstrap | Shared loader with `Asset.loadAsync` | You prefer hook-driven splash gating |
| System fonts only | Utilities, internal tools, fastest ship | Brand guidelines require custom type |
| `@expo-google-fonts/*` packages | Popular open fonts without bundling files | Corporate licensed fonts not on Google Fonts |
| `expo-google-fonts` + `useFonts` | Quick Inter/Roboto setup | You already ship licensed OTF/TTF assets |
| Tamagui / NativeWind text tokens | Design system with themed typography | One screen with two text styles |

## FAQs

How do I install expo-font in Expo SDK 57?

```bash
npx expo install expo-font expo-splash-screen
```

* `expo-font` is included in the Expo SDK - `expo install` pins a compatible version.
* Import `useFonts` from `expo-font` in your root layout.
* Place `.ttf` or `.otf` files under `assets/fonts/` and static `require()` them.

What is the difference between useFonts and Font.loadAsync?

* `useFonts` is a React hook that triggers re-render when loading completes - ideal for component trees.
* `Font.loadAsync` returns a Promise - ideal for imperative bootstrap before `registerRootComponent`.
* Both accept the same map of family name → `require()` asset.

Why must I load each font weight separately?

* React Native selects fonts by **family name**, not CSS-style weight synthesis.
* Each TTF file registers under the key you provide in `useFonts`.
* Reference `"Inter-Bold"` in `fontFamily`, not `"Inter"` with `fontWeight: "700"`.

How do I prevent the flash of unstyled text?

```tsx
SplashScreen.preventAutoHideAsync();
// ...
if (!loaded && !error) return null;
```

* Keep the splash visible until fonts load.
* Do not render branded `Text` until `loaded` is true.
* Hide splash on error so the app does not hang.

What is a typography scale?

* A fixed set of text styles (display, title, body, caption) with paired `fontSize` and `lineHeight`.
* Centralized in `theme/typography.ts` as `StyleSheet.create` or plain objects.
* Screens reference tokens - not raw `fontSize: 17` literals.

Should allowFontScaling be true or false?

* Default `true` for almost all user-facing copy - respects accessibility settings.
* Set `false` only for decorative text or fixed-size icons implemented as text (rare).
* Prefer `maxFontSizeMultiplier` over disabling scaling entirely.

What does maxFontSizeMultiplier do?

* Caps how much the system font scale can enlarge text.
* `1.0` means no scaling; `1.3` allows up to 30% larger than the style's `fontSize`.
* Apply lower caps on nav bars, chips, and buttons; keep body copy at `1.5` or higher.

Gotcha: Why does my custom font work on iOS but not Android?

* Family name mismatch - Android is stricter about the exact `fontFamily` string.
* Font file not included in the bundle - verify static `require()` path.
* Using `fontWeight` instead of the correct family file - load and reference each weight explicitly.

How do I set lineHeight correctly?

* Use dp values, not unitless multipliers: `lineHeight: 24` with `fontSize: 16`.
* Body text: ~1.4–1.5× `fontSize`; display headings: ~1.1–1.2×.
* If glyphs clip, increase `lineHeight` or add vertical padding.

Can I use Google Fonts without downloading files?

* `@expo-google-fonts/inter` and similar packages wrap `useFonts` with pre-bundled assets.
* Install: `npx expo install @expo-google-fonts/inter expo-font`.
* Corporate apps with licensed fonts still use local `require()` of OTF/TTF files.

How does font scale affect layout?

* Larger text increases line boxes and can reflow flex rows.
* Use `numberOfLines`, `flexShrink: 1`, and multi-line toolbars at high scales.
* `PixelRatio.getFontScale()` helps debug layout at accessibility settings.

Should I use adjustsFontSizeToFit?

* Shrinks text to fit a fixed box when `numberOfLines` is set - mostly iOS.
* Useful for dynamic labels in fixed-width tabs.
* Do not rely on it for body paragraphs - let text wrap naturally.

How do I type typography tokens in TypeScript?

```tsx
const typography = StyleSheet.create({ ... }) satisfies Record<string, TextStyle>;
```

* Export a union type for variant names: `type Variant = keyof typeof typography`.
* Prop-type wrapper components with `variant: Variant` for autocomplete.

Do fonts slow app startup?

* Each TTF adds decode and registration time at launch.
* Load only weights you use - omit thin/black weights if unused.
* Batch with splash gate so users see splash, not a font swap.

How do nested Text components inherit fonts?

* Nested `Text` inherits parent `fontSize`, `fontFamily`, `color`, and `lineHeight` unless overridden.
* Inline links inside body copy can omit `fontFamily` if the parent body style already sets it.
* Override only the keys that differ (color, fontFamily for monospace snippets).

* [Style Performance](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/style-performance/) - stable typography tokens vs inline text styles
* [Responsive & Adaptive Layout](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/responsive-and-adaptive-layout/) - adapting layouts when font scale is high
* [Dark Mode & Color Schemes](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/dark-mode-and-color-schemes/) - text color tokens per color scheme
* [Images & Assets](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/rn-fundamentals/images-and-assets/) - `useFonts` alongside `Asset.loadAsync`

# Team & Onboarding Best Practices

A condensed summary of the **25 most important team and onboarding practices** for Expo SDK 57 mobile teams - drawn from every page in this section.

Highlights / Team & Onboarding Best Practices

* Day one: Node 20, npm ci, expo-doctor, Metro green - before feature tickets
* Week one ships a capstone PR with navigation, test, and preview build evidence
* Codebase tour is tiered and buddy-led - not a solo file tree binge
* Leveling uses a mobile skills matrix - Router, EAS, device matrix, release hygiene
* Pairing rotates driver/navigator; PRs include iOS + Android screenshots for UI
* Onboarding docs improve every hire - record confusion as doc PRs

1. **Machine setup before tickets:** Node 20 LTS, `npm ci`, `npx expo-doctor`, and `npx expo start` green on day one - [Onboarding Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/team/onboarding-basics/).
2. **Pin SDK 57 explicitly:** `expo` ~57.0.4, React 19.2.3, RN 0.86.0 - new hires do not bump SDK in week one - [Project Setup Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/project-setup-basics/).
3. **CONTRIBUTING.md is canonical:** Clone path, env template, branch rules, and preview label documented - not scattered Slack pins.
4. **Same scripts locally and in CI:** `lint`, `typecheck`, `test`, `start` - hires learn one command surface - [Mobile CI/CD Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/mobile-ci-cd-basics/).
5. **Week-one capstone is mandatory:** One E2E feature - route, screen, test, merged PR - [First-Week Learning Path](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/team/first-week-learning-path/).
6. **Expo Router tour early:** Thin `app/` routes re-exporting `features/` - mental model before deep refactors - [Expo Router Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/expo-router-basics/).
7. **Buddy assignment day one:** Named buddy for 90-minute codebase tour and first two PRs - not "ask anyone."
8. **Tiered codebase checklist:** Tier 1 day one, Tier 2 before capstone, Tier 3–4 week two - [Codebase Tour Checklist](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/team/codebase-tour-checklist/).
9. **Trace one feature slice together:** Tap → hook → API → client - whiteboard path beats reading every file.
10. **Preview build in week one:** Every hire triggers or installs an EAS `preview` build on hardware - [EAS Build Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/eas-build/eas-build-basics/).
11. **Expo Go vs dev client documented:** README states which - custom native modules require dev client, not guesswork.
12. **EAS login and org invite day one:** Humans use `eas login`; CI uses `EXPO_TOKEN` robot - never commit tokens.
13. **`.env.example` committed:** `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` only - production secrets in EAS environments.
14. **Standard simulator names:** iPhone 16 + Pixel 8 API 35 - pairing and screenshots stay comparable.
15. **PR evidence for UI:** iOS and Android screenshots or recording - sim-only review is insufficient for shipping confidence - [Pairing & Mob on Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/team/pairing-and-mob-on-mobile/).
16. **Rotate driver every 25 minutes:** Mob and pair sessions - one keyboard hogging hides bus factor.
17. **Device lab checkout sheet:** Physical devices for camera, push, biometrics - logged out between uses.
18. **Leveling matrix over tenure:** Junior vs mid defined by Router, Query, EAS, tests - [Junior → Mid RN Leveling](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/team/junior-mid-rn-leveling/).
19. **One competency per sprint growth plan:** Gap plans are focused - not unfocused "learn React Native."
20. **Tiny merged PR by day two:** Builds CI literacy before capstone scope - confidence from green checks.
21. **Record week-one confusion as doc PRs:** README path maps and tour notes improve the next hire - onboarding is a product.
22. **Pair on `app.config.ts` and `eas.json` first time:** Credentials and bundle IDs are not solo experimentation.
23. **Defer SDK upgrades and native plugins:** Week one is read-and-ship - platform changes need staff pairing.
24. **Release pairing for first submit shadow:** Observer on `eas submit` + rollback doc - [EAS Submit](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/eas-build/eas-submit/).
25. **Written week-one retro to lead:** Three bullets - clearest doc, most confusing folder, proposed doc fix - closes the feedback loop.

## FAQs

How long should onboarding take before "normal" velocity?

Expect full sprint capacity by week three. Week one is learning-shaped workload - capstone, not backlog avalanche.

One buddy or rotating buddies?

One primary buddy for two weeks; optional rotate for domain experts (CI, design system) in week two.

Remote hire without device lab?

Ship one team device or reimburse short-term rental. Require preview APK/IPA install on personal phone with staging accounts from vault.

Contractor onboarding - same path?

Same machine and tour checklist; scope leveling matrix to contract length. Capstone still proves merge and CI literacy.

Biggest onboarding mistake?

Assigning production tickets before Metro green and codebase tour Tier 1 - produces silent struggle and revert-heavy PRs.

Dokumen: Codebase Tour Checklist
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/team/codebase-tour-checklist/

# Codebase Tour Checklist

A tiered checklist for **where routes, features, native config, and CI live** in an Expo SDK 57 app - use on day two with a buddy, not as a solo scavenger hunt.

Highlights / Codebase Tour Checklist

* Tier 1: day-one paths - app/, package.json, app.config.ts, CONTRIBUTING.md
* Tier 2: feature slices, shared API client, env and EAS config
* Tier 3: native plugins, testing layout, observability hooks
* Tier 4: CI workflows, release channels, monorepo boundaries
* Check off with a buddy - annotate repo wiki with your team's actual paths
* Failed items become doc PRs - onboarding improves when confusion is recorded

## How to Use This Checklist

* Complete **Tier 1** before your first PR; **Tier 2** before capstone feature; **Tier 3–4** in week two.
* Replace placeholder paths (`features/orders/`) with your repo's real names - grep if README is stale.
* Mark each item **✓ found**, **? unclear**, or **✗ missing** - escalate `✗` to platform lead.
* Record answers in your onboarding PR or internal wiki - the next hire inherits your notes.
* Re-run Tier 4 when joining a new squad or after a major architecture migration.

---

## Tier 1 - Day One (1–8)

*You can run Metro and find the home screen without asking Slack.*

1. **Repository entry README** - clone command, Node version, `npm ci` vs `pnpm`, link to Slack channels.

   * **Look for:** `engines.node`, `#mobile` or `#app` channel, link to EAS project
   * **Ask if missing:** "Where is the canonical getting-started doc?"
2. **`package.json` scripts** - how lint, typecheck, test, and start are invoked.

   * **Look for:** `expo start`, `typecheck`, `lint`, `test` - same scripts CI calls
   * **Related:** [Project Setup Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/project-setup-basics/)
3. **SDK pin** - `expo`, `react`, `react-native` versions match SDK 57 matrix.

   * **Look for:** `"expo": "~57.0.4"`, `"react": "19.2.3"`, `"react-native": "0.86.0"`
   * **Verify:** `npx expo-doctor` passes on clean clone
4. **`app/` directory** - file-based routes (Expo Router).

   * **Look for:** `_layout.tsx`, `index.tsx`, `(tabs)/` or route groups
   * **Rule:** Route files stay thin - re-export feature screens
   * **Related:** [Expo Router Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/expo-router-basics/)
5. **Root layout `app/_layout.tsx`** - providers, fonts, splash, root navigator.

   * **Look for:** QueryClient, theme, auth gate, `Stack` / `Tabs` from `expo-router`
   * **Signal:** All global wrappers should be here or one imported provider file
6. **`app.config.ts` or `app.json`** - bundle IDs, icons, plugins, `extra` for env.

   * **Look for:** `ios.bundleIdentifier`, `android.package`, `plugins: []`, `extra.eas.projectId`
   * **Related:** [Project Setup Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/project-setup-basics/)
7. **Environment template** - `.env.example` with `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` vars documented.

   * **Look for:** Staging API URL, feature flag keys safe for client bundle
   * **Never:** Private API secrets in `EXPO_PUBLIC_`
8. **`CONTRIBUTING.md`** - branch flow, commit style, PR template, preview build label.

   * **Look for:** `needs-preview` label rules, CODEOWNERS mention, conventional commits

---

## Tier 2 - First PR (9–16)

*You can trace one user action from tap to network.*

9. **Feature folder convention** - where screen logic lives outside `app/`.

   * **Look for:** `features/<name>/screens|hooks|api|components/`
   * **Alt patterns:** `src/modules/`, FSD `entities/` + `features/`
   * **Related:** [Folder Structure for Features](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/folder-structure-for-features/)
10. **Shared API client** - single HTTP wrapper with auth headers and base URL.

    * **Look for:** `shared/api/client.ts`, `lib/api.ts`, or `createApiClient()` factory
    * **Trace:** Screen → hook → `ordersApi.getById` → `client.get`
11. **Auth/session gate** - how signed-out users are redirected.

    * **Look for:** `Redirect` in `app/_layout.tsx`, `(auth)/` route group, or `useAuth()` guard
    * **Ask:** Where is refresh token stored? (`expo-secure-store` pattern)
12. **State strategy** - what lives in TanStack Query vs Zustand vs context.

    * **Look for:** `useQuery` for server data; store only for UI session state
    * **Smell:** `fetch` inside Zustand actions duplicating query cache
13. **Design system entry** - buttons, typography, theme tokens.

    * **Look for:** `shared/ui/`, `@/components`, or external package import
    * **Ask:** Storybook or on-device catalog URL if it exists
14. **`eas.json` build profiles** - development, preview, production.

    * **Look for:** `developmentClient`, `distribution: internal`, `channel` per profile
    * **Related:** [EAS Build Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/eas-build/eas-build-basics/)
15. **TypeScript paths** - `@/` alias mapping in `tsconfig.json`.

    * **Look for:** `"paths": { "@/*": ["./*"] }"` or monorepo package names
    * **Verify:** Jump-to-definition from route to feature screen works in IDE
16. **Test colocation** - `*.test.tsx` beside components or `__tests__` folder policy.

    * **Look for:** `jest.config.js`, `jest.setup.ts`, `jest-expo` preset
    * **Run:** `npm test -- --listTests | head`

---

## Tier 3 - Week Two (17–24)

*You can reason about native behavior and debug production-shaped builds.*

17. **Config plugins** - native changes without hand-editing `ios/` / `android/`.

    * **Look for:** `plugins: ["expo-router", "./plugins/withCustom"]` in app config
    * **Ask:** When was last `npx expo prebuild` and is CNG adopted?
18. **`ios/` and `android/` presence** - managed vs bare vs generated native dirs.

    * **Managed/CNG:** folders gitignored - EAS generates at build
    * **Bare:** folders committed - local `pod install` required
    * **Related:** [Prebuild Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cng-prebuild/prebuild-basics/)
19. **Deep linking config** - scheme, universal links, intent filters.

    * **Look for:** `scheme` in app config, `apple-app-site-association`, Android intent filters
    * **Related:** [Deep Linking Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/deep-linking/deep-linking-basics/)
20. **Push notifications wiring** - token registration and cold-start route.

    * **Look for:** `expo-notifications` setup, `app/_layout.tsx` notification response listener
    * **Ask:** Which environment sends test pushes?
21. **Analytics and error reporting** - Sentry, Datadog, Amplitude, etc.

    * **Look for:** init in root layout or `AppProviders`, `captureException` usage pattern
    * **Ask:** PII rules - what is forbidden in breadcrumbs?
22. **OTA updates** - channels and `runtimeVersion` policy.

    * **Look for:** `expo-updates` config, `eas update` channel names in docs
    * **Related:** [OTA Updates Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/ota-updates-basics/)
23. **Maestro / E2E folder** - smoke flows and when CI runs them.

    * **Look for:** `.maestro/smoke.yml`, `appId` matching bundle identifier
    * **Related:** [Mobile Testing Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/mobile-testing-basics/)
24. **Internationalization** - locale files and date/number formatting.

    * **Look for:** `i18n/`, `locales/`, `expo-localization` usage
    * **Smell:** Hard-coded strings in feature screens without extraction

---

## Tier 4 - Release Literacy (25–30)

*You know how code becomes a store binary and who to ping when it breaks.*

25. **CI workflow location** - GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, or EAS Workflows.

    * **Look for:** `.github/workflows/pr-checks.yml`, `.eas/workflows/`
    * **Trace:** PR open → which jobs run → required checks for merge
26. **PR vs release pipelines** - separate triggers and secrets.

    * **Look for:** `pull_request` for lint/tsc/test; `tags: v*` for `eas build`
    * **Related:** [Mobile CI/CD Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/mobile-ci-cd-basics/)
27. **`EXPO_TOKEN` and secrets docs** - where robot credentials live (not in repo).

    * **Look for:** GitHub org secrets runbook, 1Password vault name
    * **Never:** Tokens in workflow YAML plaintext
28. **Store submission path** - who runs `eas submit` and TestFlight / Play tracks.

    * **Look for:** `submit` profile in `eas.json`, internal testing doc links
    * **Related:** [EAS Submit](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/eas-build/eas-submit/)
29. **Monorepo boundaries** - if applicable, which workspace is the mobile app.

    * **Look for:** `apps/mobile/`, `packages/ui`, `turbo.json` pipeline filters
    * **Related:** [Monorepo with Turborepo](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/monorepo-with-turborepo/)
30. **CODEOWNERS and on-call** - who must approve `app/`, native, or release changes.

    * **Look for:** `.github/CODEOWNERS`, PagerDuty / on-call schedule link
    * **Ask:** Hotfix process outside business hours

---

## Tour Session Template

Use this 60-minute agenda with a buddy:

```markdown
## Codebase tour - <hire> + <buddy> - <date>
 
### Tier 1 (20m)
- [ ] README clone path verified
- [ ] app/_layout.tsx walked
- [ ] app.config.ts bundle IDs noted
 
### Tier 2 (25m)
- [ ] Traced: <pick one feature> tap → API
- [ ] eas.json profiles explained
- [ ] Test command run together
 
### Tier 3–4 (15m sketch)
- [ ] CI PR checks named
- [ ] Preview build label demonstrated
- [ ] Open questions logged below
 
### Open questions → doc PRs
1.
2.
```

## FAQs

Our paths do not match the checklist - now what?

Update your team wiki with a path map table. Send a doc PR adding a `## Repository map` section to README linking real folders.

How deep on Tier 4 for juniors?

Awareness only in week one - "PR checks live here, releases tagged there." Hands-on release duty comes after first preview build.

Brownfield repo with native apps?

Add items for host app entry point, RN bundle URL, and bridge modules - see [Brownfield Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/brownfield/brownfield-basics/).

Dokumen: First-Week Learning Path
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/team/first-week-learning-path/

# First-Week Learning Path

A cookbook for a new hire's **first five days** - learn **Expo Router**, trigger **EAS Build**, and ship **one end-to-end feature** before week two backlog work.

Highlights / First-Week Learning Path

* Days 1–2: run the app, tour app/ routes, ship a one-line UI PR
* Days 3–4: trace one feature slice from route → hook → API → test
* Day 5: trigger a preview EAS build and install on a physical device
* Capstone: one small E2E feature - screen, navigation, test, preview build
* Pair with a buddy for first merge - review norms matter as much as syntax
* End week with a written 'what confused me' note - feed back into onboarding docs

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - the minimum path from clone to merged PR with a device build.

```bash
# Day 1 - green path
git clone <repo> && cd <repo> && npm ci
npx expo-doctor && npm run typecheck
npx expo start
 
# Day 3 - trace + change
# app/(tabs)/explore.tsx → features/explore/screens/ExploreScreen.tsx
 
# Day 5 - preview on device
eas build --profile preview --platform android --non-interactive
```

```text
Week arc:
  Mon  → Machine + Metro + read CONTRIBUTING.md
  Tue  → Expo Router tour + tiny UI PR merged
  Wed  → Feature slice trace + unit test
  Thu  → Navigation + RNTL component test
  Fri  → Preview build on phone + capstone PR
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Onboarding a junior or web-transfer engineer onto an existing Expo SDK 57 app.
* Standardizing what "productive in week one" means across squads.
* Replacing ad-hoc "read the whole repo" guidance with a shippable outcome.

## Working Example

Assume a team app with tabs, a `features/` folder, and `eas.json` preview profile. The capstone feature: **add a "Tips" row on Explore that navigates to `/tips`**.

### Day 1 - Machine and mental model

```bash
npm ci
npx expo-doctor
cp .env.example .env.local
npx expo start
```

Read in order:

1. `CONTRIBUTING.md` - branch naming, PR template, preview label rules
2. `app/_layout.tsx` - providers and root navigator
3. `app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx` - tab bar configuration
4. [Expo Router Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/expo-router-basics/) - file = route

**Deliverable:** Post in onboarding thread: screenshot of sim running + `expo-doctor` green.

### Day 2 - Tiny merged PR (Router)

Add a subtitle on an existing screen - practice branch → PR → CI without product risk.

```tsx
// app/(tabs)/explore.tsx - thin route file
import { ExploreScreen } from "@/features/explore/screens/ExploreScreen";
 
export default ExploreScreen;
```

```tsx
// features/explore/screens/ExploreScreen.tsx
import { Text, View } from "react-native";
 
export function ExploreScreen() {
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1, padding: 16 }}>
      <Text accessibilityRole="header">Explore</Text>
      <Text>Welcome - week one</Text>
    </View>
  );
}
```

```bash
git checkout -b onboarding/jane-explore-subtitle
npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test
git push -u origin HEAD
# Open PR - expect PR checks green in <10 min
```

**Deliverable:** One merged PR with passing CI. Read a teammate's review comment aloud in pairing.

### Day 3 - Feature slice trace

With your buddy, draw this path on a whiteboard for **one existing feature** (auth, cart, profile):

```text
app/orders/[id].tsx
  → features/orders/screens/OrderDetailScreen.tsx
    → features/orders/hooks/useOrder.ts
      → features/orders/api/ordersApi.ts
        → shared/api/client.ts
```

Grep exercise:

```bash
rg "useOrder" --type ts
rg "ordersApi" app features
```

Add a **unit test** for a pure formatter in the feature:

```tsx
// features/orders/lib/formatOrderTotal.test.ts
import { formatOrderTotal } from "./formatOrderTotal";
 
it("formats USD total", () => {
  expect(formatOrderTotal(1299, "USD")).toBe("$12.99");
});
```

**Deliverable:** Diagram photo + one new test file in the PR or capstone branch.

> **Related:** [Folder Structure for Features](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/folder-structure-for-features/) - scaling past starter layout

### Day 4 - Capstone UI + navigation

Add the Tips flow - route, screen, link.

```tsx
// app/tips.tsx
import { TipsScreen } from "@/features/tips/screens/TipsScreen";
 
export default TipsScreen;
```

```tsx
// features/tips/screens/TipsScreen.tsx
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
import { ScrollView, Text } from "react-native";
 
export function TipsScreen() {
  return (
    <>
      <Stack.Screen options={{ title: "Tips" }} />
      <ScrollView contentContainerStyle={{ padding: 16 }}>
        <Text>Ship small PRs. Run expo-doctor often.</Text>
      </ScrollView>
    </>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// features/explore/screens/ExploreScreen.tsx (excerpt)
import { Link } from "expo-router";
import { Pressable, Text } from "react-native";
 
<Link href="/tips" asChild>
  <Pressable accessibilityRole="link">
    <Text>View onboarding tips →</Text>
  </Pressable>
</Link>
```

Component test:

```tsx
// features/explore/screens/ExploreScreen.test.tsx
import { render, screen } from "@testing-library/react-native";
import { ExploreScreen } from "./ExploreScreen";
 
it("shows link to tips", () => {
  render(<ExploreScreen />);
  expect(screen.getByRole("link", { name: /tips/i })).toBeTruthy();
});
```

**Deliverable:** Navigation works in sim; test passes locally and in CI.

> **Related:** [Expo Router Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/expo-router-basics/) - `Link` and `href`

### Day 5 - EAS preview on device

Trigger a preview build and install on a physical Android device (or iOS if UDID registered).

```bash
eas login
eas build --profile preview --platform android --non-interactive
# Open EAS dashboard URL - scan QR on device
```

```json
// eas.json - confirm preview profile exists
{
  "build": {
    "preview": {
      "distribution": "internal",
      "channel": "preview",
      "android": { "buildType": "apk" }
    }
  }
}
```

On PR, add label `needs-preview` if your team automates builds - [Preview Builds on PRs](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/preview-builds-on-prs/).

**Capstone PR checklist:**

* New route `app/tips.tsx` + feature screen
* Link from Explore
* Unit or component test
* Screenshot from physical device in PR description
* `npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test` green

**Deliverable:** Merged capstone PR + proof of preview build on hardware.

## Deep Dive

### What to defer past week one

| Topic | Defer why | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SDK upgrade | High blast radius | Month two with buddy |
| Native modules / config plugins | Needs dev client literacy | When assigned ticket |
| Store submit | Credentials + policy | After first preview build |
| Monorepo Turbo filters | CI complexity | When touching shared packages |
| Maestro E2E authoring | Capstone uses RNTL | Week two or three |

### Buddy session agenda (90 minutes)

```markdown
1. 10m - Pull main, expo-doctor, demo Metro shortcuts
2. 20m - Walk app/_layout.tsx and one tab stack
3. 20m - Open Sentry / analytics (read-only) if applicable
4. 20m - Pair on capstone navigation bug if any
5. 20m - Review PR description template and preview label
```

### Written retro (private to lead)

```markdown
## Week one retro - <name>
- Clearest doc:
- Most confusing folder:
- Tool that surprised me:
- One doc PR I will send:
```

Feed "confusing folder" answers into [Codebase Tour Checklist](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/team/codebase-tour-checklist/) updates.

### Success metrics for leads

| Signal | Healthy week one | Investigate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PRs merged | ≥2 (tiny + capstone) | Zero merges - blocker |
| CI failures | Self-fixed after first | Same lint error day 4 |
| Device build | Preview installed | Sim-only at Friday |
| Questions | Specific, timed | Silent until day 10 |

## FAQs

What if CI fails on day two?

Fix CI before feature work - ask buddy to pair on `npx expo customize tsconfig.json` or missing env vars. Do not skip gates.

Capstone too big for juniors?

Drop the test requirement to one pure function test; keep navigation + preview build. Merge split PRs: UI first, link second.

No physical device available?

Use Android emulator with Play image or iOS simulator build profile. Still run `eas build` once to learn the dashboard.

Monorepo clone - different path?

Run install from app workspace root documented in README. Week-one capstone stays inside one app package - see [Monorepo with Turborepo](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/monorepo-with-turborepo/).

# Team & Onboarding Highlights Summary

Every highlight bullet from the 6 pages in this section, gathered on one page and grouped by the page it came from.

Highlights / Team & Onboarding Highlights Summary

* Pin Node 20 LTS and SDK 57 before cloning - mismatched peers break Metro on hour one
* Days 1–2: run the app, tour app/ routes, ship a one-line UI PR
* Tier 1: day-one paths - app/, package.json, app.config.ts, CONTRIBUTING.md

## [Onboarding Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/team/onboarding-basics/)

* Pin Node 20 LTS and SDK 57 before cloning - mismatched peers break Metro on hour one
* Xcode + CocoaPods for iOS simulators; Android Studio SDK 35 for emulators
* EAS CLI links your laptop to cloud builds - eas login once, eas build:configure in the repo
* npx expo-doctor is the first command after npm install - catches skew before obscure red screens
* Expo Go is fine for day one; dev clients are the path to native modules and E2E
* Document machine setup in CONTRIBUTING.md so every hire reproduces the same green path

## [First-Week Learning Path](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/team/first-week-learning-path/)

* Days 1–2: run the app, tour app/ routes, ship a one-line UI PR
* Days 3–4: trace one feature slice from route → hook → API → test
* Day 5: trigger a preview EAS build and install on a physical device
* Capstone: one small E2E feature - screen, navigation, test, preview build
* Pair with a buddy for first merge - review norms matter as much as syntax
* End week with a written 'what confused me' note - feed back into onboarding docs

## [Codebase Tour Checklist](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/team/codebase-tour-checklist/)

* Tier 1: day-one paths - app/, package.json, app.config.ts, CONTRIBUTING.md
* Tier 2: feature slices, shared API client, env and EAS config
* Tier 3: native plugins, testing layout, observability hooks
* Tier 4: CI workflows, release channels, monorepo boundaries
* Check off with a buddy - annotate repo wiki with your team's actual paths
* Failed items become doc PRs - onboarding improves when confusion is recorded

## [Junior → Mid RN Leveling](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/team/junior-mid-rn-leveling/)

* Junior: ship UI with Router, RNTL tests, and green PR checks on guidance
* Mid: own feature slices, preview builds, Query cache, and thin Maestro smokes
* Mobile-specific axes: navigation, offline, permissions, device matrix, release hygiene
* Leveling is evidence-based - merged PRs, not years of tenure
* Gap plans pair one competency per sprint - avoid unfocused 'learn RN' goals
* Web React experience accelerates UI work - does not replace native literacy

## [Pairing & Mob on Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/team/pairing-and-mob-on-mobile/)

* One driver, one navigator - rotate every 25 minutes in mob sessions
* Share simulators via screen share + named device profiles - avoid 'works on my phone'
* Device lab: checkout sheet, charged devices, wipe guest accounts between sessions
* PR reviews require sim or device evidence for UI, gestures, and safe areas
* Remote pairing: Tandem / VS Code Live Share for code; QuickTime for iOS sim mirror
* Mob on release days - RC install, smoke flows, and rollback paths together

## [Team & Onboarding Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/team/best-practices/)

* Day one: Node 20, npm ci, expo-doctor, Metro green - before feature tickets
* Week one ships a capstone PR with navigation, test, and preview build evidence
* Codebase tour is tiered and buddy-led - not a solo file tree binge
* Leveling uses a mobile skills matrix - Router, EAS, device matrix, release hygiene
* Pairing rotates driver/navigator; PRs include iOS + Android screenshots for UI
* Onboarding docs improve every hire - record confusion as doc PRs

Dokumen: Junior → Mid RN Leveling
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/team/junior-mid-rn-leveling/

# Junior → Mid RN Leveling

A cookbook **skills matrix** for **mobile-specific competencies** on Expo SDK 57 teams - define what junior looks like, what mid owns, and how to close gaps with evidence.

Highlights / Junior → Mid RN Leveling

* Junior: ship UI with Router, RNTL tests, and green PR checks on guidance
* Mid: own feature slices, preview builds, Query cache, and thin Maestro smokes
* Mobile-specific axes: navigation, offline, permissions, device matrix, release hygiene
* Leveling is evidence-based - merged PRs, not years of tenure
* Gap plans pair one competency per sprint - avoid unfocused 'learn RN' goals
* Web React experience accelerates UI work - does not replace native literacy

## Recipe

> Quick-reference leveling card - copy into eng ladder or performance rubric.

```text
Junior RN (L3) - "ships with support"
  ✓ Expo Router screens + Link navigation
  ✓ RNTL tests for happy path
  ✓ PR checks green; fixes own lint/tsc failures
  ✓ Runs app on sim + one physical device
  ✓ Asks for review before touching native config
 
Mid RN (L4) - "owns vertical slices"
  ✓ Feature folder end-to-end: route → API → test → preview build
  ✓ TanStack Query patterns; no duplicate fetch in global store
  ✓ Debugs Metro, Hermes redboxes, and flaky CI
  ✓ Triggers preview EAS build; reads eas.json profiles
  ✓ Authors 1–3 Maestro smoke steps or equivalent E2E
  ✓ Participates in on-call / release rotation with checklist
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Calibrating promotion discussions beyond vague "strong engineer."
* Building growth plans for web-to-mobile transfers.
* Staffing tickets - juniors on bounded UI; mids on cross-layer features.

## Working Example

### Competency matrix

Rate **A** (autonomous), **G** (guided), **N** (not yet) per quarter. Mid bar = **A** on all mid rows, **G+** on most junior rows.

| Competency | Junior (L3) | Mid (L4) | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Expo Router** | G - adds screens in existing groups | A - route groups, modals, typed params | Merged PRs touching `app/` |
| **React / RN UI** | G - lists, forms, loading states | A - perf-aware lists, keyboard, a11y roles | Reviewer notes; RNTL queries by role |
| **TypeScript** | G - props types, fixes tsc errors | A - narrow unions at route boundaries | Zero tsc suppressions in owned files |
| **Testing** | G - one component test per PR | A - hook tests + MSW integration | CI coverage on owned feature folder |
| **Networking** | G - calls existing API hooks | A - designs Query keys, error UX, retry policy | [TanStack Query on Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/networking-api/tanstack-query-on-mobile/) patterns |
| **Navigation edge cases** | N - back stack surprises | G - deep links, auth redirects | Manual test matrix documented in PR |
| **Native / EAS** | N - uses provided dev client | G - triggers preview build, reads logs | EAS dashboard screenshot in PR |
| **Permissions** | N - copies existing pattern | G - camera/location flows with denial path | Screenshots of OS dialogs in QA notes |
| **Offline / NetInfo** | N - aware | G - empty/offline UI states | Unit test with mocked NetInfo |
| **Performance** | N - avoids obvious rerenders | G - FlashList, memo boundaries | Profiler before/after on hot list |
| **CI/CD literacy** | G - fixes PR check failures | A - knows preview vs release lanes | [Mobile CI/CD Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/mobile-ci-cd-basics/) quiz pass |
| **Release hygiene** | N | G - runtimeVersion awareness, no secrets in bundle | Checklist sign-off on RC |
| **Debugging** | G - Metro cache, basic redbox | A - symbolicated traces, device logs | Postmortem participation |
| **Communication** | G - daily standup, asks early | A - estimates slices, flags native risk in planning | Ticket breakdown quality |

### Junior → mid gap plan (12 weeks)

One competency focus per sprint - not "learn everything."

```markdown
## <Engineer> - Q3 leveling plan
 
| Sprint | Focus | Success signal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Router + thin routes | 2 screens via feature re-export |
| 2 | RNTL by role/label | 80% new UI has test |
| 3 | TanStack Query reads | Remove one Zustand fetch duplication |
| 4 | Error + loading UX | Standard ErrorView on owned feature |
| 5 | Preview EAS build | Solo `eas build --profile preview` |
| 6 | Physical device QA | Device matrix row in PR template |
| 7 | Deep link or auth redirect | One `Redirect` / guard flow owned |
| 8 | Maestro smoke slice | 3-step YAML flow in CI optional job |
| 9 | List performance | Migrate one ScrollView → FlashList |
| 10 | Offline empty state | NetInfo mock test + UI |
| 11 | Release shadow | Buddy on RC checklist |
| 12 | Mid packet review | Matrix all A/G on mid rows |
```

### Ticket sizing guide

| Level | Appropriate tickets | Avoid until mid |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Junior | New row UI, copy, icon, isolated hook, test fixes | SDK bump, new config plugin, store submit |
| Mid | New feature slice, API integration, navigation restructure | Solo SDK major upgrade without staff engineer |
| Senior+ | Cross-app modules, native bridges, CI architecture | - |

```text
Junior ticket example:
  "Add order status badge to OrderRow - uses existing useOrder hook"
 
Mid ticket example:
  "Add order cancellation flow - new route, mutation, error states, preview build"
```

### Web transfer acceleration map

| Web skill | Maps to mobile | Gap to close |
| --- | --- | --- |
| React hooks | Same mental model | RN primitives (`View`, `Pressable`) |
| CSS layout | Flexbox similar | No cascade - StyleSheet / NativeWind |
| React Router | Expo Router file routes | Imperative `router.push`, mobile back stack |
| Browser DevTools | React DevTools | Flipper / React Native DevTools, sim logs |
| `fetch` + SWR | TanStack Query | Offline, app backgrounding, token refresh |
| Jest + RTL | RNTL | `jest-expo`, native module mocks |
| Deploy to Vercel | EAS Build + stores | Code signing, phased rollout |

### Promotion packet (evidence list)

Mid promotion should cite **artifacts**, not adjectives:

```markdown
## Mid promotion evidence - <name>
 
### Delivery
- 3 feature slices owned E2E (link PRs)
- 1 preview-build-driven QA cycle led
 
### Quality
- RNTL tests on owned features - <count> tests added
- Zero P1 bugs traced to missing loading/error state in owned code
 
### Mobile craft
- Maestro smoke: <link or flow file>
- Device matrix completed on RC <version>
 
### Collaboration
- Onboarded 1 hire on codebase tour
- Release checklist buddy on <date>
 
### Growth edges (honest)
- Still G on: push notification cold start
- Plan: pair with <senior> in Q4
```

## Deep Dive

### Signals that are *not* leveling

| Signal | Why it fails |
| --- | --- |
| "Knows React for 5 years" | Web tenure ≠ native release literacy |
| "Merged 100 PRs" | Count without scope - typo fixes ≠ feature ownership |
| "Works late" | Hours ≠ autonomy on EAS or device matrix |
| "Strong opinions on Redux" | Architecture debates without shipping evidence |

### Signals that *are* leveling

* **Autonomous preview build** when native-adjacent UI changes
* **Query cache** designed so sibling screens do not double-fetch
* **Reviewer trust** on owned feature folder - fewer nit comments over time
* **Incident participation** with actionable notes ("missing offline gate")

### Staff calibration questions

Use in leveling meetings:

1. Can they ship a feature without daily routing help?
2. Do their PRs include device evidence when gestures or safe areas change?
3. Can they explain why OTA cannot fix their last change?
4. Did they catch a native risk in planning before sprint commit?

### Recommended learning by gap

| Gap | Resource in this docs site |
| --- | --- |
| Router | [Expo Router Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/expo-router-basics/) |
| EAS | [EAS Build Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/eas-build/eas-build-basics/) |
| Testing | [Mobile Testing Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/mobile-testing-basics/) |
| CI | [Mobile CI/CD Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/mobile-ci-cd-basics/) |
| Structure | [Folder Structure for Features](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/folder-structure-for-features/) |
| Performance | [Performance Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/performance/performance-basics/) |

## FAQs

Junior with strong web background - start at mid?

UI velocity may be mid-level; native/EAS/permissions likely junior. Split matrix rows - do not skip device and release literacy.

How many mid engineers per squad?

Common ratio: 2 mid : 1 senior : 1–2 junior for a product squad of 4–5. Adjust when release load is high.

Contractor on 6-month term?

Use matrix for scope boundaries, not promotion. Contractors can be "mid scope" without L4 title.

Expo Go only team - defer EAS?

No - mid bar still requires preview build literacy. Use org's shared dev client if personal EAS access is limited.

Dokumen: Onboarding Basics
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/team/onboarding-basics/

# Onboarding Basics

10 examples for **day-one machine setup** - Xcode, Android Studio, EAS CLI, simulators, and SDK 57 pin - so a new teammate runs the app before lunch.

Highlights / Onboarding Basics

* Pin Node 20 LTS and SDK 57 before cloning - mismatched peers break Metro on hour one
* Xcode + CocoaPods for iOS simulators; Android Studio SDK 35 for emulators
* EAS CLI links your laptop to cloud builds - eas login once, eas build:configure in the repo
* npx expo-doctor is the first command after npm install - catches skew before obscure red screens
* Expo Go is fine for day one; dev clients are the path to native modules and E2E
* Document machine setup in CONTRIBUTING.md so every hire reproduces the same green path

## Prerequisites

Clone the team repo and confirm the SDK contract in `package.json` before installing native tooling. If the project uses the default template, expect Expo Router and managed workflow (no committed `ios/` / `android/` until prebuild or EAS).

```bash
git clone git@github.com:your-org/your-app.git
cd your-app
node -v   # expect 20.x
cat package.json | grep '"expo"'
```

Target stack for this section:

```json
{
  "engines": { "node": ">=20.0.0" },
  "dependencies": {
    "expo": "~57.0.4",
    "react": "19.2.3",
    "react-native": "0.86.0"
  }
}
```

> **Tooling:** These examples target **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4), **React Native 0.86.0**, and **React 19.2.3**. See [Project Setup Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/project-setup-basics/) for scaffold flags and folder layout.

---

## Basic Examples

### 1. Node 20 and Package Manager

Install **Node 20 LTS** with `nvm`, `fnm`, or `mise` - SDK 57 tooling and EAS CLI expect it.

```bash
# nvm example
nvm install 20
nvm use 20
node -v   # v20.x.x
 
npm install
# or: corepack enable && pnpm install
```

```json
{
  "engines": {
    "node": ">=20.0.0"
  }
}
```

* **One lockfile** in the repo - use the same package manager the team documents in `CONTRIBUTING.md`
* **`npm ci`** on CI; locally `npm install` is fine after clone
* If `engines` fails, fix Node before chasing Metro errors - wrong Node causes cryptic `transform` failures

> **Related:** [Project Setup Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/project-setup-basics/) - lockfile and `.gitignore` hygiene

---

### 2. SDK 57 Pin Verification

The `expo` package version is the compatibility contract for every `expo-*` module.

```bash
npm install
npx expo-doctor
npx expo install --check
```

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "expo": "~57.0.4",
    "react": "19.2.3",
    "react-native": "0.86.0"
  }
}
```

* **`npx expo-doctor`** compares your graph to the SDK 57 matrix - run it on day one and after every `git pull`
* **`npx expo install <pkg>`** resolves peer versions - never hand-pick `expo-camera` without it
* Mismatch symptom: red screen mentioning native module version or Hermes parse errors
* New hires should not bump SDK in week one unless assigned - pin first, upgrade later

> **Related:** [create-expo-app Templates](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/create-expo-app-templates/) - `default@sdk-57` scaffold

---

### 3. Environment Variables and Secrets

Copy the example env file before first run - missing API URLs cause silent blank screens.

```bash
cp .env.example .env.local
```

```bash
# .env.example (committed)
EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL=https://api.staging.example.com
# EAS secrets - not in .env for production builds
```

```ts
// app.config.ts - surface public vars via extra when needed
export default {
  expo: {
    extra: {
      apiUrl: process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL,
    },
  },
};
```

* **`EXPO_PUBLIC_*`** vars embed in the JS bundle - never put private keys here
* Production secrets live in **EAS Environment Variables**, not laptop `.env` files
* Ask your lead for **1Password / vault** links to `EXPO_TOKEN`, staging accounts, and TestFlight invites
* Restart Metro after changing env vars: `npx expo start -c`

---

### 4. First Run - Metro and Expo Go

Confirm JavaScript boots before installing multi-gigabyte native IDEs.

```bash
npx expo start
# press i for iOS simulator (requires Xcode)
# press a for Android emulator (requires Android Studio)
# scan QR with Expo Go on a physical device
```

```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "start": "expo start",
    "ios": "expo start --ios",
    "android": "expo start --android"
  }
}
```

* **Expo Go** is fastest for Router and UI work - limited native modules
* **`expo start -c`** clears Metro cache when imports look stale after branch switches
* If the project uses **expo-dev-client**, day-one may require a development build - check `eas.json` for `development` profile
* Success criteria: home screen loads, no redbox, `tsc --noEmit` passes

> **Related:** [Expo Router Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-router/expo-router-basics/) - file-based routes in `app/`

---

### 5. Xcode and iOS Simulator (macOS)

iOS development requires **Xcode** from the Mac App Store and command-line tools.

```bash
xcode-select --install
sudo xcodebuild -license accept
xcode-select -p
# /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer
 
# List simulators
xcrun simctl list devices available
 
# Open Simulator app
open -a Simulator
```

```bash
npx expo start --ios
# or: npx expo run:ios
```

* Install **Xcode 16+** compatible with SDK 57 - match what CI/EAS uses when documented
* First `run:ios` may trigger **CocoaPods** (`pod install`) if `ios/` exists or after prebuild
* **Apple Silicon:** simulators are `arm64` - faster than Rosetta x86 images
* Windows/Linux teammates use **EAS Build** for iOS artifacts - no local compile required

---

### 6. Android Studio and Emulator

Android builds need **Android Studio** with SDK Platform 35 and a virtual device (AVD).

```bash
# After Android Studio install - set ANDROID_HOME
export ANDROID_HOME=$HOME/Library/Android/sdk   # macOS
export PATH=$PATH:$ANDROID_HOME/emulator:$ANDROID_HOME/platform-tools
 
adb devices
emulator -list-avds
```

**Android Studio → SDK Manager:**

* **SDK Platforms:** Android 15 (API 35) - matches RN 0.86 defaults
* **SDK Tools:** Android SDK Build-Tools, Platform-Tools, Emulator

```bash
npx expo start --android
```

* Create an AVD with **Google Play** image when testing Play Services features
* **`adb reverse`** helps Metro reach localhost APIs: `adb reverse tcp:8081 tcp:8081`
* Enable **USB debugging** on physical Android devices for on-device dev

---

### 7. EAS CLI and Expo Account

**EAS CLI** links your machine to Expo's cloud build service - required for store-shaped binaries.

```bash
npm install -g eas-cli@latest
# or project-local: npx eas-cli@latest
 
eas login
eas whoami
 
cd your-app
eas build:configure   # creates eas.json if missing
```

```json
// eas.json (minimal starter)
{
  "cli": { "version": ">= 16.0.0" },
  "build": {
    "development": {
      "developmentClient": true,
      "distribution": "internal"
    },
    "preview": {
      "distribution": "internal"
    },
    "production": {}
  }
}
```

* **`eas login`** uses your Expo account - request org invite from mobile lead
* **`eas build:configure`** wires project ID in `app.config.ts` via `extra.eas.projectId`
* CI uses **`EXPO_TOKEN`** robot account - humans use `eas login`; never commit tokens
* First cloud build: `eas build --profile development --platform ios --local` optional; default is cloud

> **Related:** [EAS Build Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/eas-build/eas-build-basics/) - profiles, credentials, first build

---

## Intermediate Examples

### 8. Development Client vs Expo Go

When the app adds custom native modules or config plugins, **Expo Go is not enough** - install a dev client.

```bash
npx expo install expo-dev-client
eas build --profile development --platform ios
# Install IPA via QR from EAS dashboard
npx expo start --dev-client
```

```json
{
  "build": {
    "development": {
      "developmentClient": true,
      "distribution": "internal",
      "ios": { "simulator": true }
    }
  }
}
```

* **Development profile** includes `expo-dev-client` and native code from config plugins
* **Simulator builds** (`ios.simulator: true`) install faster for iOS-only UI work
* Rebuild dev client when native deps change - JS-only changes still hot-reload
* Document which profile new hires should install in onboarding doc

> **Related:** [EAS Build Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/eas-build/eas-build-basics/) - `developmentClient: true`

---

### 9. Simulator and Emulator Shortcuts

Standardize device names so pairing sessions and screenshots match.

```bash
# iOS - boot named simulator
xcrun simctl boot "iPhone 16"
open -a Simulator
 
# Android - start AVD by name
emulator -avd Pixel_8_API_35 &
 
# Expo targets specific device
npx expo run:ios --device "iPhone 16"
npx expo run:android --device Pixel_8_API_35
```

```json
// package.json - team shortcuts (optional)
{
  "scripts": {
    "ios:16": "expo run:ios --device 'iPhone 16'",
    "android:pixel": "expo run:android --device Pixel_8_API_35"
  }
}
```

* **Same device class in design reviews** - avoid "works on my iPhone SE" surprises
* Reset simulators when Keychain or push state gets corrupted: `xcrun simctl erase all` (destructive)
* Physical devices: register UDIDs for iOS internal distribution in EAS credentials

---

### 10. Day-One Verification Checklist

Run this script block before opening your first PR - catches 90% of onboarding drift.

```bash
node -v                    # 20.x
npm ci
npx expo-doctor
npm run typecheck          # or: npx tsc --noEmit
npm run lint
npm test -- --passWithNoTests
npx expo start
```

```markdown
## CONTRIBUTING.md excerpt - Machine setup
1. Node 20 via nvm
2. Clone + `npm ci`
3. `cp .env.example .env.local` (ask #mobile for values)
4. `npx expo-doctor` - must pass
5. `npx expo start` - iOS sim + Android emu smoke
6. `eas login` + org invite
7. Install dev client from EAS `development` profile if repo has expo-dev-client
```

* Add **`npx expo customize tsconfig.json`** if typed routes fail on clean clone
* Screenshot passing `expo-doctor` in your onboarding PR if your team tracks hire checklists
* Escalate to platform channel when doctor fails on fresh clone - likely repo drift, not hire error

> **Related:** [Project Setup Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/project-setup/best-practices/) - conventions that survive week two

---

## FAQs

Do I need both Xcode and Android Studio?

For full-stack mobile teams, yes on macOS - you will touch both platforms in review. Windows/Linux hires can skip Xcode and use EAS for iOS binaries.

Expo Go or dev client on day one?

Expo Go if `package.json` has no `expo-dev-client`. If the README mentions a development build QR, install that first - Expo Go will not load custom native code.

How long does first `eas build` take?

20–40 minutes cloud-side. Start it after lunch on day one while reading the codebase tour - do not block morning Metro setup on it.

What if expo-doctor fails on a fresh clone?

Post output in #mobile with your OS version. Do not manually bump packages - run `npx expo install --fix` only when the lead confirms.

Dokumen: Pairing & Mob on Mobile
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/team/pairing-and-mob-on-mobile/

# Pairing & Mob on Mobile

A cookbook for **simulator sharing**, **device lab etiquette**, and **review norms** on Expo SDK 57 teams - mobile pairing fails when only one person sees the screen.

Highlights / Pairing & Mob on Mobile

* One driver, one navigator - rotate every 25 minutes in mob sessions
* Share simulators via screen share + named device profiles - avoid 'works on my phone'
* Device lab: checkout sheet, charged devices, wipe guest accounts between sessions
* PR reviews require sim or device evidence for UI, gestures, and safe areas
* Remote pairing: Tandem / VS Code Live Share for code; QuickTime for iOS sim mirror
* Mob on release days - RC install, smoke flows, and rollback paths together

## Recipe

> Quick-reference session card - paste into calendar invite.

```markdown
## Pairing session - <feature>
- Driver: <name> (keyboard)
- Navigator: <name> (reads aloud, watches sim)
- Device: iPhone 16 sim + Pixel 8 API 35 emu
- Branch: feature/<ticket>
- Rotate: 25 min
- Done when: PR opened with screenshot + test output
```

```bash
# Shared verification before ending session
npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test
npx expo start --dev-client   # if native modules
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Onboarding week-one capstone and first EAS preview install.
* Debugging gesture conflicts, keyboard overlap, or safe-area bugs.
* Release candidate walkthrough before store submit.
* Teaching EAS dashboard and credential flows - never solo on production keys.

## Working Example

### Remote pairing setup

| Tool | Use for | Mobile tip |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Zoom / Meet | Sim mirror, face cam | Share **window** not full screen - hide notifications |
| VS Code Live Share | Same buffer, shared terminal | Driver runs Metro; navigator watches sim on stream |
| QuickTime (macOS) | Crisp iOS sim video | File → New Movie Recording → pick Simulator window |
| scrcpy | Android device mirror | `scrcpy --stay-awake` for physical device sessions |

```bash
# Driver - standard start
npx expo start --clear
 
# Navigator - verify on second platform without stopping Metro
# press a / i in shared terminal with driver consent
```

**Norms:**

* Navigator **asks before** keyboard takeover - "mind if I drive for the repro?"
* Keep **one Metro** instance - second `expo start` causes port confusion
* Mute when not speaking; unmute to read error messages aloud - silent debugging wastes mob time

### Simulator sharing checklist

```markdown
## Before session
- [ ] Same Node 20 + `npm ci` completed both machines
- [ ] Same git branch checked out
- [ ] Named simulators: iPhone 16, Pixel_8_API_35
- [ ] .env.local values confirmed (staging API)
 
## During session
- [ ] Redbox reproduced on both iOS and Android once for UI bugs
- [ ] Font scale 100% default; test XL if a11y ticket
- [ ] Dark mode toggled if theme-related
 
## After session
- [ ] PR description includes both platform screenshots
- [ ] No uncommitted `app.config.ts` experiments left on driver machine
```

Standard device names tie back to [Onboarding Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/team/onboarding-basics/) - team scripts `npm run ios:16` reduce pairing friction.

### Device lab etiquette

Physical devices beat simulators for camera, push, biometrics, and performance.

```markdown
## Device lab shelf - team norms
 
### Checkout
- Sign device out in #device-lab or sheet: name, date, ticket
- Note OS version sticker on cradle (iOS 18.2, Android 15)
 
### Hygiene
- Log out of personal Apple/Google accounts before return
- Clear app data for staging builds when testing auth flows
- Charge to 80%+ before check-in; cable stays with cradle
 
### Shared staging accounts
- Use team vault credentials - never personal 2FA-only accounts
- Rotate passwords quarterly; document in 1Password vault
 
### Broken / flaky devices
- Red tag "do not use" + Slack post - flaky hardware wastes mob hours
```

```bash
# iOS internal build install - buddy verifies UDID registered
eas device:create
eas build --profile preview --platform ios
 
# Android APK sideload
eas build --profile preview --platform android
# QR from EAS dashboard - both observe install success
```

> **Related:** [EAS Build Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/eas-build/eas-build-basics/) - internal distribution | [Internal Distribution](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/eas-build/internal-distribution/)

### Mob programming format (3+ people)

```text
Roles rotate each slice:
  Driver     - types
  Navigator  - strategy, reads tickets
  Researcher - docs, Sentry, Expo forums
  Device op  - physical device + screenshots (optional fifth)
```

**25-minute slices:**

1. **Repro** - show bug on sim + device
2. **Hypothesis** - navigator states theory before code
3. **Change** - smallest diff
4. **Verify** - tests + both platforms
5. **Retro 2m** - what slowed us down?

```markdown
## Mob rules (mobile)
- No parallel Metro on different branches mid-session
- Production EAS credentials: senior only, group observes
- Merge only after everyone saw green tests on stream
```

### PR review norms (mobile-specific)

Require evidence beyond green CI:

| Change type | Reviewer expects |
| --- | --- |
| Layout / spacing | iOS + Android screenshots; note device class |
| Gestures / sheets | Screen recording or paired repro steps |
| Navigation | Deep link path or back-stack behavior described |
| Permissions | Screenshot of allow/deny dialogs |
| Native-adjacent | Preview `build_id` or dev client version noted |
| Performance | Before/after if list or animation touched |

**Review comment templates:**

```markdown
<!-- Request device evidence -->
Thanks - please add Android screenshot; iOS safe area looks correct.
 
<!-- Request preview build -->
This adds a config plugin - please trigger `needs-preview` and paste EAS link.
 
<!-- Approve with device note -->
Verified on iPhone 16 sim + Pixel 8 emu - LGTM.
```

**SLA norms:**

* First review within **1 business day** for onboarding PRs
* **Pair review** (sync 15m) when PR touches `app/_layout.tsx`, `app.config.ts`, or `eas.json`

### Pairing on EAS and release

Never solo on first production credential touch - mob the checklist.

```markdown
## Release pairing checklist (45m)
- [ ] Confirm RC `build_id` matches QA sign-off sheet
- [ ] Driver shares EAS dashboard read-only; navigator reads steps aloud
- [ ] `eas submit` only after Maestro smoke green
- [ ] Rollback doc open: OTA roll-back + staged rollout pause links
- [ ] Post submit links in #releases thread
```

> **Related:** [Mobile CI/CD Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/mobile-ci-cd-basics/) - release vs PR lanes

## Deep Dive

### When pairing beats async review

| Scenario | Pair | Async OK |
| --- | --- | --- |
| First-week onboarding capstone | ✓ |  |
| Hermes redbox only on device | ✓ |  |
| Copy change in static Text |  | ✓ |
| New Expo config plugin | ✓ |  |
| Typo in test fixture |  | ✓ |
| Flaky Maestro in CI | ✓ |  |
| API type fix |  | ✓ |

### Anti-patterns

| Anti-pattern | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| "Let me share later" screenshots | Block merge until evidence in PR |
| Driver hogs keyboard 2h | Hard rotate 25m |
| Sim-only review for camera ticket | Mandatory device lab checkout |
| Two people run different `expo start` | One Metro; driver owns terminal |
| Mob of 6 on tiny typo | Split - pair for code, async for review |

### Inclusion and time zones

* Rotate driver so junior does not only navigate for a month
* Record **short** repro clips (under 2 min) for APAC/EU async - not hour-long mob recordings
* Document decisions in PR thread - verbal-only agreements exclude absent teammates

### Suggested cadence by team size

| Team size | Pairing cadence |
| --- | --- |
| 3–4 engineers | 2–3 paired sessions / week |
| 5–8 | Weekly mob on release + ad-hoc pairs |
| 9+ | Feature-area pairing pods; monthly cross-pod mob |

## FAQs

Pairing feels slow - how do we justify it?

Onboarding capstones and native bugs are faster paired than three async review rounds. Track time-to-merge for paired vs solo tickets one sprint.

No device lab budget?

Minimum: one team Android + one iOS device passed between squads. Simulators cover 80%; pairing on shared hardware for the 20%.

Remote-only team?

QuickTime sim mirror + scrcpy + strict screenshot PR template. Quarterly in-person or device-ship week for tactile QA.

How is mob different from standup?

Mob produces merged code or a repro recording. Standup syncs status - do not mob entire backlog in standup block.

* [First-Week Learning Path](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/team/first-week-learning-path/) - buddy capstone
* [Codebase Tour Checklist](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/team/codebase-tour-checklist/) - paired tour agenda
