Dokumen: Architecture Decision Records
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/tech-leadership/architecture-decision-records/

# Architecture Decision Records

Mobile **ADR** examples for decisions every Expo lead faces: **OTA vs store**, **custom native module vs Expo SDK**, and how to write records that survive SDK 57 → 58 upgrades. ADRs are **short, dated, and linked** - not wiki essays nobody reads.

Highlights / Architecture Decision Records

* ADRs are short, dated, and reversible - not design novels in Confluence
* Mobile ADRs must name release clock: OTA, store binary, or both
* Record runtimeVersion impact and rollback path in every shipping ADR
* Native vs SDK decisions include maintenance owner and upgrade cost
* Link to ranked ADRs in architecture-design for navigation and state
* Supersede - don't edit history - when SDK or policy flips the decision

## Recipe

> Quick-reference ADR skeleton - copy into `docs/adr/` or `.adr/` in the repo.

```markdown
# ADR-NNNN: <Title>
 
- **Status:** proposed | accepted | superseded by ADR-XXXX
- **Date:** YYYY-MM-DD
- **Deciders:** @mobile-lead, @platform
- **Release clock:** OTA | store binary | backend | none
 
## Context
What problem and constraints? (team size, brownfield, compliance)
 
## Decision
We will <choice> because <one paragraph>.
 
## Consequences
### Positive
- …
### Negative
- …
### Rollback / reversal
- OTA: `eas update --roll-back --channel <ch>`
- Store: ship <version> binary; feature flag <name> off
 
## Alternatives considered
| Option | Rejected because |
| --- | --- |
| … | … |
```

```bash
# Repo layout
docs/adr/
  0001-ota-vs-store-for-checkout-copy.md
  0002-expo-camera-vs-custom-scanner.md
  README.md   # index with status table
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Two engineers argue the same OTA vs rebuild question every sprint.
* You add a third-party native SDK - need a paper trail for audit and onboarding.
* Store rejection forces a policy change - future hires must know **why** moderation exists.
* Squads disagree on navigation or state - point to [ranked ADRs](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/adr-navigation-library-choice/) and record your override.

## Working Example

### ADR-0007: Checkout error copy via OTA (not store)

```markdown
# ADR-0007: Checkout error copy via OTA
 
- **Status:** accepted
- **Date:** 2026-03-12
- **Deciders:** @mobile-lead, @pm-checkout
- **Release clock:** OTA (`production` channel)
 
## Context
Support needs clearer card-decline messaging before weekend campaign.
No API, native, or `runtimeVersion` change. Live binary: `2.4.1` (runtimeVersion `2.4.0`).
 
## Decision
Ship copy change with `eas update` to `production` after staging channel QA.
Do not cut store release `2.4.2` for text-only change.
 
## Consequences
### Positive
- Same-day ship; rollback in minutes
- Avoids store review queue during campaign
### Negative
- Users on ancient sideload builds off channel may not receive update
### Rollback
`eas update --roll-back --channel production`
Known-good update ID: recorded in release ticket MOB-4821
 
## Alternatives considered
| Option | Rejected because |
| --- | --- |
| Store submit 2.4.2 | 2–5 day review for zero native benefit |
| Backend-driven copy only | Offline checkout still needs local strings |
```

### ADR-0008: Barcode scan - `expo-camera` vs custom Vision module

```markdown
# ADR-0008: Barcode scan - expo-camera vs custom Vision module
 
- **Status:** accepted
- **Date:** 2026-04-02
- **Deciders:** @mobile-lead, @android-lead, @ios-lead
- **Release clock:** store binary (new native dependency)
 
## Context
Warehouse app needs Code 128 scan at 30 fps on mid-tier Android.
`expo-camera` barcode API meets MVP; custom ML Kit wrapper promised 2× speed.
 
## Decision
Use **expo-camera** `CameraView` barcode scanning for v1.
Revisit custom module only if field metrics show >5% scan failure on Pixel 6a class.
 
## Consequences
### Positive
- Config plugin + Expo SDK upgrade path maintained by Expo
- One less Swift/Kotlin module for juniors to maintain
### Negative
- May not match dedicated scanner hardware latency
- Still requires **dev client** rebuild - not OTA-able as native add
### Rollback
Feature flag `warehouse_scan_v1` off; prior manual entry flow remains
 
## Alternatives considered
| Option | Rejected because |
| --- | --- |
| Custom TurboModule + ML Kit | 2 eng-months maintenance; no field data yet |
| WebView + browser scan | Poor offline; store WebView policy risk |
| Third-party RN scanner (unmaintained) | Last commit 18 months ago; RN 0.86 untested |
```

### ADR-0009: Push notifications - Expo Notifications vs vendor SDK

```markdown
# ADR-0009: Push - Expo Notifications vs OneSignal SDK
 
- **Status:** accepted
- **Date:** 2026-05-18
- **Deciders:** @mobile-lead, @growth
- **Release clock:** store binary if switching later
 
## Context
Growth wants A/B rich push; engineering wants minimal native surface.
 
## Decision
**expo-notifications** + server-side campaign tooling for v1.
OneSignal evaluated - defer until marketing needs in-app IAM beyond product scope.
 
## Consequences
### Positive
- Aligns with EAS credentials and Expo push token flow
- Smaller native binary vs dual SDK
### Negative
- Advanced segmentation lives in our backend, not vendor UI
### Rollback
Stay on expo-notifications; no vendor SDK to remove
 
## Alternatives considered
| Option | Rejected because |
| --- | --- |
| OneSignal RN SDK | Extra native dep + duplicate FCM/APNs wiring |
| Firebase only (no Expo wrapper) | Loses unified Expo push DX for managed workflow |
```

### ADR index table

```markdown
# ADR index
 
| ID | Title | Status | Clock |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0007 | Checkout copy OTA | accepted | OTA |
| 0008 | expo-camera scan | accepted | store |
| 0009 | expo-notifications | accepted | store |
| 0010 | Expo Router (greenfield) | accepted | - |
```

Link architectural choices to existing ranked docs:

* Navigation: [ADR: Navigation Library Choice](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/adr-navigation-library-choice/)
* State: [ADR: State Management Selection](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/adr-state-management-selection/)

Record **only the team-specific override** - do not duplicate entire ranked pages.

### When to write vs when to skip

| Situation | ADR? |
| --- | --- |
| Button color OTA | No - ticket comment suffices |
| First OTA to production channel | **Yes** - establishes rollback ritual |
| New native module | **Yes** - maintenance owner required |
| Expo Router on new app | **Yes** - links ranked ADR + template choice |
| Zustand vs Context for one screen | No - reverse quickly |
| SDK 57 → 58 upgrade strategy | **Yes** - supersede prior SDK ADRs |

## Gotchas

* **ADR without rollback line** - Acceptable decision becomes irreversible in incidents. **Fix:** Every `accepted` ADR names OTA roll-back or store version pin.
* **Editing old ADRs in place** - Git history lies. **Fix:** `Status: superseded by ADR-0012` and new file.
* **"We decided in Slack"** - Onboarding repeats the debate. **Fix:** Slack thread link in ADR context; decision lives in repo.
* **Ignoring runtimeVersion** - ADR says OTA but binary mismatch bricks users. **Fix:** Mandate `runtimeVersion` line in Context.
* **Native ADR without owner** - Module rots when author leaves. **Fix:** Named `@ios-lead` / `@android-lead` in Deciders.

49454e4f4d5f434e4f5904434556494d4345131c1a56181a181c1a1d

## Alternatives

| Format | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Markdown in `docs/adr/` | Default for RN teams | Org mandates ADR tooling (e.g. Log4brains) |
| Nygard template (Context/Decision/Consequences) | Cross-team architecture | Need mobile-specific clock fields - extend template |
| RFC with comment period | Large org, many stakeholders | Two-pizza team - overhead kills velocity |
| Wiki only | Never for decisions | Repo ADRs are versioned with code |

## FAQs

How long should a mobile ADR be?

One to two pages. If longer, split into ADR (decision) + cookbook (how-to). Link [Native vs JavaScript Trade-offs](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/tech-leadership/native-vs-javascript-trade-offs/) for framework depth.

Who approves ADRs?

Tech lead + one affected specialist (iOS, Android, backend). Product signs policy-sensitive ADRs (IAP, UGC, health).

ADR number vs date ordering?

Use monotonic IDs (`0008`) - dates slip; IDs stay sortable. Index table shows status at a glance.

Do ADRs replace expo-doctor or CI?

No. ADRs document **why** you accepted a native dependency; CI still blocks skewed installs.

How do ADRs relate to architecture-design section?

**architecture-design** holds ranked decision frameworks. **tech-leadership ADRs** hold **your team's recorded choice** and exceptions.

* [ADR: State Management Selection](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/adr-state-management-selection/) - Query-first stack

Dokumen: Technical Leadership Best Practices
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/tech-leadership/best-practices/

# Technical Leadership Best Practices

A condensed summary of the **25 most important technical leadership practices** for Expo SDK 57 mobile teams - drawn from every page in this section. Protect quality without becoming the bottleneck.

Highlights / Technical Leadership Best Practices

* Classify every ship: OTA, store binary, backend - before promising dates
* ADRs for native, OTA production, and navigation/state commits
* Review standards scale quality - lead reviews boundaries, not every line
* Disagree-and-commit with written dissent and revisit triggers
* Mentor week-one outcomes: Metro, sims, merged tiny PR, preview build
* Native code is a budget line - default JavaScript until ranked doc says otherwise

1. **Classify changes by release clock:** JS-only OTA vs native store binary vs backend dependency - before sprint commitment - [Tech Lead Basics on Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/tech-leadership/tech-lead-basics-on-mobile/).
2. **Maintain a three-clock dependency map:** Align mobile leads with backend and release managers on [Release Train Calendar](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/release-train-calendar/) - not surprise Friday API breaks.
3. **Risk budget store submits:** Cap store releases per sprint; track rejections as process debt - velocity without guardrails ships rollback weekends.
4. **OTA requires runtimeVersion discipline:** Mismatch needs new binary - document rollback `updateId` every production OTA - [Runtime Version Policy](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/runtime-version-policy/).
5. **Preview builds on native-touching PRs:** Expo Go hides custom native modules - [Preview Builds on PRs](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/preview-builds-on-prs/).
6. **Write ADRs for irreversible choices:** OTA-to-production policy, new native modules, navigation/state commits - short markdown in repo - [Architecture Decision Records](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/tech-leadership/architecture-decision-records/).
7. **Supersede ADRs - never silent edits:** Status field + new file preserves onboarding truth.
8. **Point to ranked architecture docs:** Team ADR records **your** choice; frameworks live in [architecture-design](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/best-practices/).
9. **Default native boundary to Expo SDK:** Custom TurboModules need maintenance owners and cost worksheet - [Native vs JavaScript Trade-offs](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/tech-leadership/native-vs-javascript-trade-offs/).
10. **Enforce PR review checklist:** Perf lists, a11y labels, native `expo install`, thin routes - [Code Review Standards for RN](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/tech-leadership/code-review-standards-for-rn/).
11. **Require device evidence on UI PRs:** iOS + Android screenshot or recording - sim-only Pro Max review lies on Android-majority apps.
12. **Small PRs over hero reviews:** Target under 400 lines; same-day review beats weekly mega-diffs.
13. **CODEOWNERS on `app.config.ts` and `eas.json`:** Native config mistakes are org-wide - not junior solo experimentation.
14. **Time-box technical disagreements:** Owner, decide-by date ≤ 5 days, ranked ADR or spike - no 50-message Slack limbo - [Handling Technical Disagreements](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/tech-leadership/handling-technical-disagreements/).
15. **Disagree-and-commit in writing:** Dissent preserved; one implementation after commit; revisit trigger named.
16. **Navigation debates use ranked ADR:** Greenfield SDK 57 defaults Expo Router; brownfield exceptions documented - [ADR: Navigation Library Choice](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/adr-navigation-library-choice/).
17. **State debates classify first:** Server → Query; client UI → Zustand; URL → Router params - [ADR: State Management Selection](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/adr-state-management-selection/).
18. **Mentor structured week one:** Metro green, tiny merged PR, preview on device - not production tickets day one - [Mentoring Junior Mobile Devs](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/tech-leadership/mentoring-junior-mobile-devs/).
19. **Safe first PR scope:** Copy, tests, a11y - defer solo native config until mid-level evidence - [Junior → Mid RN Leveling](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/team/junior-mid-rn-leveling/).
20. **Buddy + capstone path:** Use [First-Week Learning Path](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/team/first-week-learning-path/) - not "read the repo."
21. **Teach debugging ladder:** Redbox → DevTools → expo-doctor → preview build → native logs paired.
22. **Pair on first EAS build and submit shadow:** Release literacy before on-call rotation - [Onboarding Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/team/onboarding-basics/).
23. **Review architecture boundaries - delegate feature diffs:** Lead on native, release, and cross-squad contracts; mids own feature quality.
24. **Run refactoring checklist before major release:** God modules block parallel PRs and SDK upgrades - [Refactoring Checklist](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/refactoring-checklist/).
25. **Improve onboarding from every hire retro:** Confusion → doc PR - leadership is a feedback loop into [team](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/team/best-practices/) practices.

## FAQs

How do I avoid becoming the sole approver?

Publish checklists and ranked ADRs so mids block boundary violations. You approve exceptions and release PRs - not every `Text` color change.

Startup with no ADR culture - minimum viable?

Three ADRs: navigation choice, state stack, OTA vs store policy. Expand when native modules appear.

EM vs tech lead on disagree-and-commit?

Tech lead owns technical option scoring; EM breaks ties on calendar risk and staffing. Both sign compliance-sensitive ADRs.

Contractors and leadership practices?

Same review checklist and ADR stack; scope mentoring to contract length. No solo `eas.json` edits without staff review.

Biggest tech-lead failure mode on mobile?

Optimizing PR count without release-clock literacy - fast merges that OTA native changes or miss store review buffers.

Dokumen: Code Review Standards for RN
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/tech-leadership/code-review-standards-for-rn/

# Code Review Standards for RN

Performance, accessibility, and **native-boundary** review checklist for Expo SDK 57 PRs. Standardize what reviewers verify so quality scales without the tech lead on every diff.

Highlights / Code Review Standards for RN

* Mobile review is device evidence + boundary checks - not style-only LGTM
* Perf: list virtualization, stable renderItem, root layout import weight
* A11y: label, role, state, font scaling - VoiceOver/TalkBack spot check
* Native boundary: expo install, config plugins, OTA vs build classification
* Router: thin routes, params typed, no business logic in app/
* Block merge on missing rollback notes for release and native PRs

## Recipe

> Quick-reference PR review card - paste into `.github/pull_request_template.md`.

```markdown
## Mobile review checklist
 
### Evidence (UI / gesture / a11y changes)
- [ ] iOS screenshot or recording attached
- [ ] Android screenshot or recording attached
- [ ] VoiceOver OR TalkBack spot-check noted (which flow)
 
### Performance
- [ ] Lists use FlashList/FlatList - not ScrollView for long feeds
- [ ] `renderItem` / `keyExtractor` stable (useCallback or module scope)
- [ ] No new heavy imports in `app/_layout.tsx` without lazy route
 
### Accessibility
- [ ] `accessibilityLabel` on icon-only controls
- [ ] `accessibilityRole` matches behavior (button vs link)
- [ ] Dynamic type: layout survives large font (or `maxFontSizeMultiplier` justified)
 
### Native boundary
- [ ] New deps added via `npx expo install <pkg>`
- [ ] `app.config.ts` / config plugin changes called out in description
- [ ] Classified: JS-only (OTA OK) vs requires `eas build`
- [ ] `npx expo-doctor` green (CI link)
 
### Architecture
- [ ] Route file thin - logic in `features/`
- [ ] No deep imports across feature boundaries
- [ ] Server state in TanStack Query - not duplicated in Zustand
 
### Release (if touching eas.json, runtimeVersion, channels)
- [ ] Rollback steps in ticket / PR comment
- [ ] runtimeVersion bump justified
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Review quality varies wildly across reviewers.
* Perf regressions merge because "it looked fine on iPhone 16 Pro."
* Juniors add native packages without config plugin awareness.
* You are formalizing [Pairing & Mob on Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/team/pairing-and-mob-on-mobile/) norms into CI-enforceable habits.

## Working Example

### Performance review - feed PR

```tsx
// ❌ Reviewer blocks - ScrollView map of 200 orders
export function OrdersScreenBad() {
  const { data } = useOrders();
  return (
    <ScrollView>
      {data?.map((o) => <OrderRow key={o.id} order={o} />)}
    </ScrollView>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// ✅ Approve path - virtualized list + stable renderItem
import { FlashList } from "@shopify/flash-list";
import { useCallback } from "react";
 
export function OrdersScreen() {
  const { data } = useOrders();
  const renderItem = useCallback(
    ({ item }: { item: Order }) => <OrderRow order={item} />,
    []
  );
 
  return (
    <FlashList
      data={data ?? []}
      renderItem={renderItem}
      keyExtractor={(o) => o.id}
      estimatedItemSize={72}
    />
  );
}
```

**Reviewer questions:**

* Did Profiler run on **mid-tier Android** reference device?
* Does parent re-create `renderItem` every render (inline arrow)?
* Any new context provider above the list?

See [Performance Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/performance/best-practices/) and [Memory Leaks & List Churn](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/performance/memory-leaks-and-list-churn/).

### Accessibility review - custom pressable

```tsx
// ❌ Block - icon-only, no name, wrong role
<Pressable onPress={onSave}>
  <Icon name="check" />
</Pressable>
```

```tsx
// ✅ Approve - name, role, state
<Pressable
  onPress={onSave}
  accessibilityRole="button"
  accessibilityLabel="Save changes"
  accessibilityState={{ disabled: !dirty, busy: saving }}
>
  <Icon name="check" accessible={false} />
</Pressable>
```

**Reviewer spot-check (30 seconds):**

* Enable VoiceOver on iOS sim (⌘F5) - focus order logical?
* TalkBack on Android emu - double-tap activates?

See [accessibilityLabel & accessibilityRole](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/accessibility/accessibilitylabel-and-accessibilityrole/).

### Native-boundary review - new camera dependency

```diff
// package.json - reviewer verifies expo install, not raw npm major
+ "expo-camera": "~17.0.10"
```

```ts
// app.config.ts - plugin stanza present
plugins: [
  [
    "expo-camera",
    {
      cameraPermission: "Allow $(PRODUCT_NAME) to scan warehouse barcodes.",
    },
  ],
],
```

**Reviewer checklist:**

| Question | Pass criteria |
| --- | --- |
| OTA safe? | **No** - native module; PR labels `requires-build` |
| Permission strings human-readable? | Yes - store review reads these |
| Expo Go test claimed? | Flag misleading - needs dev client |
| ADR or ticket links native choice? | [Architecture Decision Records](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/tech-leadership/architecture-decision-records/) |

### Architecture review - route thickness

```tsx
// ❌ Block - fetch + branching in app/ route
// app/(tabs)/orders.tsx
export default function OrdersRoute() {
  const [filter, setFilter] = useState("open");
  const { data } = useQuery({ queryKey: ["orders", filter], queryFn: () => fetchOrders(filter) });
  return <FlatList data={data} ... />;
}
```

```tsx
// ✅ Approve - thin route
// app/(tabs)/orders.tsx
export { OrdersScreen as default } from "@/features/orders/screens/OrdersScreen";
```

Aligns with [Mobile Architecture Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/mobile-architecture-basics/) and [Feature-Sliced Design for RN](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/feature-sliced-design-for-rn/).

### Review severity rubric

| Severity | Examples | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Block** | Missing permission plugin; ScrollView feed; secret in `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` | Must fix before merge |
| **Request changes** | Unstable list props; missing a11y label; deep feature import | Fix or ticket + follow-up |
| **Comment** | Naming, optional refactor, docs | Author discretion |
| **Praise** | Tests, rollback notes, device matrix evidence | Reinforce behavior |

## Gotchas

* **Sim-only iOS Pro Max** - Layout and perf lie. **Fix:** Require Android emu evidence for UI PRs.
* **"LGTM" on `package.json` only PR** - Native drift without plugin. **Fix:** Native-boundary section mandatory when lockfile changes include `expo-*` native packages.
* **Reviewing Expo Go screenshot for reanimated worklet bug** - Dev client differs. **Fix:** Preview build link in PR.
* **Approving Zustand cache of API list** - Duplicate source of truth. **Fix:** Point to [ADR: State Management Selection](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/adr-state-management-selection/).
* **Skipping rollback on `eas.json` channel change** - Wrong users get update. **Fix:** Release subsection required.

## Alternatives

| Approach | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PR template checklist | Default - low friction | Fully automated visual diff only teams |
| Danger / custom bot | Enforce screenshot labels | Small team - maintenance cost |
| Pair review only | Complex native migration | Daily feature throughput |
| CODEOWNERS on `app.config.ts` | Multi-squad monorepo | Solo maintainer overhead |

## FAQs

Should reviewers run the branch locally?

For **native config** and **gesture** PRs - yes. For copy-only TSX, device evidence in PR is enough if CI is green.

How long should mobile review take?

Target **same business day** for PRs under 400 lines. If longer, author should split or schedule review pairing.

Do we need both VoiceOver and TalkBack every PR?

Alternate per PR is fine; **both platforms** must be covered across the sprint - not all iOS.

What about auto-generated files?

Skip reviewing `.expo/types` line-by-line; **do** verify `tsc` passes and route params match usage.

Junior reviewer vs senior - same checklist?

Same checklist; seniors escalate architecture and native-boundary items. Juniors focus on a11y and list patterns first - [Junior → Mid RN Leveling](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/team/junior-mid-rn-leveling/).

## Related

* [Native Modules Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/native-modules/native-modules-basics/) - native boundary primer

# Technical Leadership Highlights Summary

## [Tech Lead Basics on Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/tech-leadership/tech-lead-basics-on-mobile/)

* Three clocks: OTA (minutes), store binary (days), backend API - leads own the dependency map
* Velocity without guardrails ships store rejections and rollback weekends
* Classify every change: JS-only, native-impacting, policy-sensitive - before promising a date
* Risk budget: one store submit per sprint unless incident lane is pre-approved
* Preview builds on PRs catch native drift; Expo Go alone hides custom native modules
* Protect main with CI gates - speed comes from small PRs, not skipped checks

## [Architecture Decision Records](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/tech-leadership/architecture-decision-records/)

* ADRs are short, dated, and reversible - not design novels in Confluence
* Mobile ADRs must name release clock: OTA, store binary, or both
* Record runtimeVersion impact and rollback path in every shipping ADR
* Native vs SDK decisions include maintenance owner and upgrade cost
* Link to ranked ADRs in architecture-design for navigation and state
* Supersede - don't edit history - when SDK or policy flips the decision

## [Code Review Standards for RN](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/tech-leadership/code-review-standards-for-rn/)

* Mobile review is device evidence + boundary checks - not style-only LGTM
* Perf: list virtualization, stable renderItem, root layout import weight
* A11y: label, role, state, font scaling - VoiceOver/TalkBack spot check
* Native boundary: expo install, config plugins, OTA vs build classification
* Router: thin routes, params typed, no business logic in app/
* Block merge on missing rollback notes for release and native PRs

## [Native vs JavaScript Trade-offs](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/tech-leadership/native-vs-javascript-trade-offs/)

* Default to JavaScript + Expo SDK until measured perf or OS API gaps force native
* Every native path adds build time, OTA lockout, and Swift/Kotlin bus factor
* Third-party SDKs are native debt with vendor upgrade schedules
* TurboModules pay off at sustained high-frequency bridge traffic - not one-off calls
* Record maintenance owner and escape hatch in ADR before merging native code
* Revisit when SDK 58 ships - Expo may absorb your custom module

## [Mentoring Junior Mobile Devs](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/tech-leadership/mentoring-junior-mobile-devs/)

* Week one: Metro green, named sim profiles, one merged tiny PR before feature scope
* Teach Expo Router thin routes early - prevents god-screen refactors
* Safe first PRs: copy, styles, tests - not app.config or native deps solo
* Debugging ladder: redbox → React DevTools → native logs → preview build
* Pair on first eas build and store-adjacent files - never solo experimentation
* Growth tied to evidence matrix - [Junior → Mid RN Leveling](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/team/junior-mid-rn-leveling/)

## [Handling Technical Disagreements](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/tech-leadership/handling-technical-disagreements/)

* Disagreements stuck in Slack need a time-boxed decision forum - not endless threads
* Navigation and state are multi-year tax - escalate with ranked ADRs, not opinions
* Disagree-and-commit: record dissent, owner ships, revisit trigger named
* Prototype budget: 2–3 days max for spikes - binary choice after metrics or ADR
* Staff engineer dissent on compliance/native - override needs written risk acceptance
* Post-decision: no relitigation until revisit date or production incident

## [Technical Leadership Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/tech-leadership/best-practices/)

* Classify every ship: OTA, store binary, backend - before promising dates
* ADRs for native, OTA production, and navigation/state commits
* Review standards scale quality - lead reviews boundaries, not every line
* Disagree-and-commit with written dissent and revisit triggers
* Mentor week-one outcomes: Metro, sims, merged tiny PR, preview build
* Native code is a budget line - default JavaScript until ranked doc says otherwise

Dokumen: Mentoring Junior Mobile Devs
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/tech-leadership/mentoring-junior-mobile-devs/

# Mentoring Junior Mobile Devs

Simulator skills, debugging, and **safe first PRs** for engineers new to Expo SDK 57. Mobile mentoring fails when juniors fight Metro day three while seniors expect feature velocity - structure the first two weeks deliberately.

Highlights / Mentoring Junior Mobile Devs

* Week one: Metro green, named sim profiles, one merged tiny PR before feature scope
* Teach Expo Router thin routes early - prevents god-screen refactors
* Safe first PRs: copy, styles, tests - not app.config or native deps solo
* Debugging ladder: redbox → React DevTools → native logs → preview build
* Pair on first eas build and store-adjacent files - never solo experimentation
* Growth tied to evidence matrix - [Junior → Mid RN Leveling](../team/junior-mid-rn-leveling.md)

## Recipe

> Quick-reference mentor card - assign buddy + milestones.

```text
Week 1 milestones:
  Day 1  Metro green + expo-doctor (iPhone 16 + Pixel 8 emu)
  Day 2  Tiny UI PR merged (subtitle, test, screenshots)
  Day 3  Trace one feature: app/ route → features/ screen → hook
  Day 4  Fix one lint/a11y review comment with TalkBack check
  Day 5  Install preview EAS build on personal device
 
Safe first PR types:
  ✅ Copy, spacing, RNTL test, accessibilityLabel
  ✅ New screen behind existing tab pattern (buddy reviews route)
  ⚠️  New npm dependency (buddy + lead review)
  🚫 Solo app.config.ts / eas.json / config plugin / native module
```

```bash
# Mentor runs this with mentee on day 1
npx expo-doctor
npx expo start
# Press i → iOS   Press a → Android
# Shift+I / Shift+A → pick standard team devices
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Hiring web React devs onto mobile squads.
* Intern or bootcamp graduate joining mid-sprint.
* Senior IC asked to "buddy" without a written path - use [First-Week Learning Path](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/team/first-week-learning-path/) as spine.

## Working Example

### Simulator skills curriculum

| Day | Skill | Exercise |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Boot simulators | `npx expo start` → `i` / `a`; screenshot both platforms |
| 2 | Device picker | `Shift+I` choose iPhone SE - layout still readable |
| 3 | Reload vs dev menu | `r` reload; dev menu → Fast Refresh verify |
| 4 | Accessibility | VoiceOver ⌘F5; navigate one form with labels |
| 5 | Physical device | Install preview build; compare safe area to sim |

Deep reference: [iOS Simulator & Android Emulator](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/expo-cli/ios-simulator-and-android-emulator/).

```bash
# Standard team device names (document in CONTRIBUTING.md)
xcrun simctl list devices available | grep "iPhone 16"
# Android: Pixel 8 API 35 in AVD Manager
```

### Safe first PR - "Explore subtitle"

**Scope:** One TSX file in `features/`, thin route re-export, one RNTL test, PR screenshots.

```tsx
// features/explore/screens/ExploreScreen.tsx - mentee edits here only
import { Text, View } from "react-native";
 
export function ExploreScreen() {
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1, padding: 16 }}>
      <Text accessibilityRole="header">Explore</Text>
      <Text>Discover tips curated for you.</Text>
    </View>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// __tests__/ExploreScreen.test.tsx
import { render, screen } from "@testing-library/react-native";
import { ExploreScreen } from "@/features/explore/screens/ExploreScreen";
 
test("shows curated subtitle", () => {
  render(<ExploreScreen />);
  expect(screen.getByText(/curated for you/i)).toBeTruthy();
});
```

**Mentor review teaches:**

* PR template checklist from [Code Review Standards for RN](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/tech-leadership/code-review-standards-for-rn/)
* Why route file stays one line - [Mobile Architecture Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/mobile-architecture-basics/)
* Attach iOS + Android screenshots before requesting review

### Debugging ladder (teach in order)

```text
1. Read the redbox / LogBox - full message, file, line
2. React DevTools - props/state wrong vs layout wrong
3. Metro terminal - transform / resolution errors
4. npx expo-doctor - version skew
5. eas build preview - reproduces native-only failures
6. Xcode / Android Studio logs - last resort; pair only
```

```tsx
// Common junior mistake - mentor demo fix
// ❌ Inline renderItem invalidates list memo
<FlashList renderItem={({ item }) => <Row item={item} />} ... />
 
// ✅ Module-level or useCallback
const renderItem = useCallback(({ item }: { item: Item }) => <Row item={item} />, []);
```

Pair on first **Hermes** `undefined is not a function` - teach `npm why <pkg>` and lockfile hygiene, not random cache clears.

### PRs to defer until mid-level

| Topic | Why wait | Mentor alternative |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `app.config.ts` plugins | Store rejection risk | Pair read-only walkthrough |
| `eas.json` credentials | Org-wide blast radius | Shadow `eas build:list` |
| Native module install | Dev client + OTA rules | Watch lead merge similar PR |
| Navigation restructure | Dual back stacks | Bugfix in existing stack first |
| TanStack Query cache design | Global data bugs | Add field to existing query |

Align promotion evidence with [Junior → Mid RN Leveling](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/team/junior-mid-rn-leveling/).

### Weekly mentor sync (15 minutes)

```markdown
## Mentee: @name - week 2
 
Shipped:
- PR #412 Explore subtitle (merged)
- Preview build on Android device
 
Stuck:
- useLocalSearchParams typing - read typed routes doc
 
Next:
- Add Tips row + Link to /tips (capstone)
 
Mentor action:
- Pair 30m on Query hook Thursday
```

Feed "stuck" items into onboarding doc PRs - [Onboarding Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/team/onboarding-basics/).

## Gotchas

* **"Works on my machine"** - Junior uses Expo Go; app needs dev client. **Fix:** Day-one README clarity; preview build by day five.
* **Throwing juniors on hotfix Friday** - No rollback literacy. **Fix:** Hotfixes shadowed; first solo fix is Monday OTA with template.
* **Review nitpicks without teaching** - Style comments without "why" do not build mobile judgment. **Fix:** One teaching comment per review (a11y, perf, or boundary).
* **Skipping Android** - iOS-only habit on Android-majority user base. **Fix:** Both screenshots required from week one.

## Alternatives

| Approach | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Buddy + written path | Default | "Sink or swim" on legacy brownfield |
| Mob programming week one | Complex domain (fintech) | Simple CRUD - overkill |
| Formal training budget | Large hiring wave | One hire - use internal docs |
| Rotating mentors | Broad exposure | Needs continuity for first PRs |

## FAQs

Web React hire - what transfers?

Component thinking, hooks, and testing mindset transfer. **New:** Metro, simulators, native boundaries, store release clocks, platform a11y services.

How hands-on should mentors be?

**Pair** on days 1–5 for environment and first merge; **review** with teaching comments week 2–4; **delegate** bounded features by week 3–6 if capstone merged.

Junior wants to learn native modules immediately?

Redirect to Expo SDK modules first. Custom native is mid+ competency unless hired as platform engineer - see [Native vs JavaScript Trade-offs](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/tech-leadership/native-vs-javascript-trade-offs/).

What if buddy is too busy?

Lead assigns alternate buddy for **reviews** within 24h; do not leave first PR idle - kills confidence.

Dokumen: Tech Lead Basics on Mobile
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/tech-leadership/tech-lead-basics-on-mobile/

# Tech Lead Basics on Mobile

Balancing **ship velocity** with **store-review risk** on Expo SDK 57 teams. Mobile tech leads own the **release clock map** - when OTA is enough, when a store build is mandatory, and when product dates must yield to Apple or Google policy.

Highlights / Tech Lead Basics on Mobile

* Three clocks: OTA (minutes), store binary (days), backend API - leads own the dependency map
* Velocity without guardrails ships store rejections and rollback weekends
* Classify every change: JS-only, native-impacting, policy-sensitive - before promising a date
* Risk budget: one store submit per sprint unless incident lane is pre-approved
* Preview builds on PRs catch native drift; Expo Go alone hides custom native modules
* Protect main with CI gates - speed comes from small PRs, not skipped checks

## Recipe

> Quick-reference lead card - paste into sprint planning or release retro.

```text
Change classification (every ticket):
  [ ] JS-only, same runtimeVersion     → OTA candidate
  [ ] Native module / plugin / permission → eas build required
  [ ] Store policy (payments, UGC, health) → legal + review buffer
  [ ] Backend contract change            → coordinate Clock C first
 
Velocity rules:
  - PRs < 400 lines when possible - review same day
  - UI PRs include iOS + Android screenshot or recording
  - No Friday store submit without Monday rollback owner
  - One incident hotfix lane documented in CONTRIBUTING.md
```

```bash
# Before promising "ship tomorrow"
npx expo-doctor
eas build:list --limit 3          # last binary age + runtimeVersion
eas channel:list                  # production channel ↔ runtimeVersion
git diff main -- package.json app.config.ts eas.json
```

**When to reach for this:**

* You are the default decision-maker on release path (OTA vs store) and review throughput.
* Product asks for a date before engineering classifies native impact.
* Crash rate or store rejection rate is climbing while PR velocity stays high.
* Onboarding a new squad lead onto an existing EAS + Expo Router app.

## Working Example

### Sprint planning - classify the backlog

| Ticket | Ship path | Review risk | Lead call |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Copy fix on checkout | OTA → `production` | Low | Ship after QA on staging channel |
| New `expo-camera` scan flow | Store binary | Medium - camera permission strings | Build preview Mon; submit Wed |
| In-app subscription UI | Store binary | **High** - IAP guidelines | Pair with [App Store Review Guidelines](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ios-platform/app-store-review-guidelines/); +3 day buffer |
| Backend required field | OTA **after** API live | Medium - old binaries | Backend prod Tue; OTA Wed with flag off |
| SDK 57 → 58 bump | Store binary | High - regression surface | Dedicated sprint; no feature coupling |

Document the table in the sprint ticket or release notes - "we'll OTA it" without classification is how teams ship broken `runtimeVersion` pairings.

### Release decision tree

```text
Need to ship a fix?
  │
  ├─ Touches ios/, android/, app.config plugins, native deps?
  │    └─ YES → eas build + submit (Clock A). OTA cannot help.
  │
  ├─ JS/TS/assets only AND runtimeVersion unchanged on live binary?
  │    └─ YES → eas update on channel (Clock B). Rollback in minutes.
  │
  └─ Store policy change (login, payments, medical claims)?
       └─ YES → review checklist + human review buffer before submit.
```

```json
// eas.json - separate profiles so velocity does not shortcut production credentials
{
  "build": {
    "preview": {
      "distribution": "internal",
      "channel": "preview"
    },
    "production": {
      "channel": "production",
      "autoIncrement": true
    }
  }
}
```

### Review throughput without skipping gates

```yaml
# .github/workflows/pr.yml - fast feedback, same gates as main
name: PR checks
on: pull_request
jobs:
  quality:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: "20", cache: "npm" }
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx expo-doctor
      - run: npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test
```

* **Small PRs** merge faster than heroic review marathons - split native config from UI when possible.
* **Named reviewers** for `app.config.ts`, `eas.json`, and `plugins/` - not drive-by approval.
* **Preview label** triggers EAS preview build - see [Preview Builds on PRs](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/preview-builds-on-prs/).

### Store-review risk budget

```markdown
## Release risk ledger - sprint 24
 
| Risk spent | Item | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 unit | IAP copy change | Approved day 2 |
| 1 unit | New photo upload (UGC) | Rejected - missing moderation ADR |
| 0 (OTA) | Button color | Shipped same day |
 
Budget: 2 store submits / sprint. Over budget → defer to next train or OTA-only week.
```

Leads track **rejections as process debt** - each rejection costs more calendar time than an extra day of QA. Pair with [Release Train Calendar](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/cicd/release-train-calendar/) for the three-clock model.

### When to slow down velocity

| Signal | Lead action |
| --- | --- |
| Crash-free rate drops after OTA | Roll back channel; freeze OTA until root cause |
| `expo-doctor` warnings in CI | Block merge - skew becomes Friday fire |
| Reviewer skips device evidence on UI PR | Reinstate screenshot rule from [Pairing & Mob on Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/team/pairing-and-mob-on-mobile/) |
| Product wants Friday submit + new native module | Renegotiate date or descope native - not both |
| Two squads ship conflicting `app.config` plugins | Architecture sync - see [Mobile Architecture Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/architecture-design/mobile-architecture-basics/) |

## Gotchas

* **"We'll hotfix with OTA" after adding a native package** - OTA does not ship Hermes bytecode for new `.so` / framework linkage. **Fix:** Rebuild binary; communicate delay early.
* **Expo Go green, dev client red** - Juniors demo in Go; production uses custom native modules. **Fix:** Preview build in Definition of Done for native-touching work.
* **Velocity = skipping typecheck** - Merged `any` and broken routes compound into review-week refactors. **Fix:** Same CI on PR and main; no admin bypass.
* **Single approver on store metadata** - Wrong privacy nutrition label triggers rejection unrelated to code quality. **Fix:** Checklist row for App Store Connect / Play Console fields.
* **Backend deploy after mobile** - New required JSON field bricks old app versions. **Fix:** Tolerant readers first; see release train dependency matrix.

## Alternatives

| Approach | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OTA-first culture | Mature `runtimeVersion` discipline; few native changes | Team frequently adds native modules |
| Store train only (no OTA) | Regulated apps banning remote JS | You need same-day copy fixes |
| Feature flags + OTA | Decouple binary live from feature visible | Flag system itself needs governance |
| Code freeze weeks | Major SDK upgrade or holiday moratorium | Every sprint - trains stop moving |

## FAQs

How do I explain OTA vs store to product in one sentence?

**OTA** updates JavaScript on the binary users already installed - minutes to rollback. **Store** ships a new installable app - required for native changes and the only path for new users on old OS versions.

What is a healthy PR merge rate for a 6-person mobile squad?

Aim for **2–4 merged PRs per engineer per week**, mostly under 400 lines. One store release every 2–4 weeks plus OTA in between beats daily mega-merges.

Should the tech lead review every PR?

No - you review **architecture boundaries**, **native config**, and **release PRs**. Delegate feature PRs to mids; audit checklist compliance weekly.

When is Friday store submit acceptable?

When Monday **rollback owner** is named, OTA rollback path is tested, and the change is not a first-time policy-sensitive feature (IAP, health, kids category).

How does this relate to web tech lead habits?

Web leads optimize deploy frequency; mobile leads optimize **clock alignment** and **review risk**. Continuous deploy does not exist for Clock A - plan accordingly.

## Related

Dokumen: Testing Best Practices
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/best-practices/

# Testing Best Practices

A condensed summary of the 25 most important best practices drawn from every page in this section.

Highlights / Testing Best Practices

* Follow the pyramid: many unit/component tests, few E2E flows
* Use jest-expo preset and mock native modules at service boundaries
* Query RNTL by role and label - not testID-only
* Prefer Maestro for YAML E2E; Detox when gray-box sync is required
* Contract-test API schemas before store builds
* Run smoke E2E on physical devices in release candidates

1. **Follow the testing pyramid:** Many fast unit and component tests, fewer integration tests, minimal E2E - E2E belongs on critical paths only.
2. **Use jest-expo as the preset:** Aligns transforms and mocks with Expo SDK 57 - custom Jest config from web tutorials breaks on native imports.
3. **Centralize setup in jest.setup.ts:** Matchers, reanimated mocks, and NetInfo stubs live once - not copy-pasted per test file.
4. **Fix transformIgnorePatterns when packages fail:** Opt specific `node_modules` into transpilation - document the list when adding native-heavy deps.
5. **Mock at service boundaries:** Mock `api/client`, not every `expo-*` module - over-mocking hides integration bugs.
6. **Avoid false confidence from empty mocks:** `jest.mock('expo-camera', () => ({}))` lets tests pass while production crashes - return realistic shapes.
7. **Query like users do:** RNTL priority is role, label, then text - `testID` is escape hatch, not default.
8. **Use userEvent over fireEvent:** Press sequences match real interaction - `fireEvent` skips accessibility and timing paths.
9. **Wait for async UI with findBy or waitFor:** Assertions immediately after `press` flake on mobile - network and animations need async matchers.
10. **Test presenters without providers when possible:** Pure props-in JSX-out components run in milliseconds - reserve MSW for integration tests.
11. **Snapshot only stable primitives:** Buttons and badges, not entire screens - snapshot churn trains teams to click-through approve.
12. **Colocate tests beside source:** `Button.test.tsx` next to `Button.tsx` - distant `__tests__` folders stop being updated.
13. **Run tests in CI on every PR:** `npm test -- --ci` with coverage optional - local-only testing does not scale past five engineers.
14. **Separate unit and contract scripts:** `test:contract` for Zod fixtures - fast signal without booting the full app.
15. **Contract-test API responses with Zod:** Shared schemas between client and tests - backend shape changes fail CI before QA.
16. **Add Pact when multiple teams own APIs:** Consumer-driven contracts complement schema tests - use when mobile and backend release independently.
17. **Start Maestro with three smoke flows:** Launch, sign-in, and primary tab - YAML flows are cheap to maintain vs Detox for many teams.
18. **Pin appId in Maestro to bundle identifier:** Wrong `appId` launches the wrong binary silently - match `app.config` ios.bundleIdentifier / android.package.
19. **Run Maestro on EAS build artifacts in CI:** Flows against release-like binaries - Expo Go is not a store submission stand-in.
20. **Reach for Detox when sync is the bug:** Gray-box synchronization helps gesture-heavy flows - accept native build setup cost.
21. **Use Storybook for visual states, not navigation:** Catalog loading/error/empty variants - on-device Storybook beats screenshotting production screens.
22. **Gate Storybook behind STORYBOOK\_ENABLED:** Swap entry in dev only - production bundles must not ship story routes.
23. **Flake policy: fix or quarantine:** Quarantined E2E must have owner and expiry - retry loops hide product bugs.
24. **Test offline and airplane mode paths:** NetInfo mocks in unit tests; real device check before release - mobile users lose signal constantly.
25. **Pre-submission checklist:** Unit + component green, smoke Maestro on physical device, contract tests, and manual payment/permission flows once per RC.

## FAQs

How many E2E tests are enough?

* Three to eight smoke flows covering revenue and auth paths.
* Add more only when a specific regression repeats in production.

Maestro or Detox for Expo SDK 57?

* Default Maestro for speed and YAML maintainability.
* Detox when you need tight native synchronization and already pay native CI cost.

Should we test Expo Router layouts?

* Use RNTL `renderRouter` for integration tests on critical stacks.
* Do not E2E every deep link - contract-test param parsing instead.

## Related

* [Mobile Testing Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/mobile-testing-basics/) - pyramid tour and intro examples
* [Jest Setup for Expo](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/jest-setup-for-expo/) - presets and mocks
* [React Native Testing Library](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/react-native-testing-library/) - queries and async
* [Mocking Native Modules](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/mocking-native-modules/) - boundary mocks
* [Maestro E2E](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/maestro-e2e/) - YAML flows and CI
* [Contract Tests for APIs](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/contract-tests-for-apis/) - Zod and Pact

# Testing Highlights Summary

Every highlight bullet from the 9 pages in this section, gathered on one page and grouped by the page it came from.

Highlights / Testing Highlights Summary

* The pyramid is wide at the bottom: many fast unit tests, fewer E2E flows
* `jest-expo` preset mocks Expo SDK modules so Jest runs without a simulator
* Query like a user: role and label before `testID`
* `jest-expo` auto-mocks most Expo modules - you override only what your test asserts
* Flows are YAML files in `.maestro/` - readable by QA and engineers alike
* Detox synchronizes with the RN bridge - it waits for animations, network, and timers to idle

## [Mobile Testing Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/mobile-testing-basics/)

* The pyramid is wide at the bottom: many fast unit tests, fewer E2E flows
* jest-expo preset mocks most Expo modules so Jest runs in Node without a simulator
* React Native Testing Library queries mirror how users find UI - label and role before testID
* Mock native modules at the boundary; never assert on implementation details inside components
* Maestro YAML flows are cheap smoke tests; Detox fits when you need native synchronization
* Contract tests catch API shape drift before a store build ships to production users

## [Jest Setup for Expo](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/jest-setup-for-expo/)

* `jest-expo` preset mocks Expo SDK modules so Jest runs without a simulator
* Install with `npx expo install` so versions match Expo SDK 57
* `transformIgnorePatterns` is the fix when Jest cannot parse ESM in node\_modules
* Keep tests out of `app/` - use `__tests__` or colocated `*.test.tsx` files
* Snapshots are for small presentational components - not full screens

## [React Native Testing Library](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/react-native-testing-library/)

* Query like a user: role and label before `testID`
* `screen` keeps queries scoped to the last `render` call
* Use `findBy*` and `waitFor` for async state - never bare `setTimeout`
* `userEvent` is async - always `await` press and type
* Importing from `@testing-library/react-native` registers Jest matchers automatically

## [Mocking Native Modules](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/mocking-native-modules/)

* `jest-expo` auto-mocks most Expo modules - you override only what your test asserts
* Manual mocks live in `__mocks__/` adjacent to the module or via `jest.mock` inline
* Mock at your app's boundary (hooks/services), not every `node_modules` import
* Reset mocks in `afterEach` - leaked implementations cause order-dependent flakes
* A passing Jest suite does not prove native code works - complement with Maestro or device QA

## [Maestro E2E](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/maestro-e2e/)

* Flows are YAML files in `.maestro/` - readable by QA and engineers alike
* `appId` must match the installed bundle ID / application ID exactly
* EAS Workflows can build an APK/simulator app then run Maestro in one pipeline
* Regex matchers (`.*`, `Welcome!`) absorb minor copy and timing variance
* Keep flows short and independent - one user journey per file

## [Detox E2E](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/detox-e2e/)

* Detox synchronizes with the RN bridge - it waits for animations, network, and timers to idle
* Expo SDK 54+ uses `expo-detox-config-plugin` after prebuild - Expo Go cannot run Detox
* E2E tests live in `e2e/` and run through the `detox` CLI, not plain `jest`
* `testID` props are the stable selectors Detox matchers rely on
* Release/simulator builds bundle JS - rebuild after app code changes
* Reach for Detox when Maestro flakes on async native work; Maestro wins on YAML speed

## [Visual Regression & Storybook](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/visual-regression-and-storybook/)

* Storybook 10+ swaps the app entry when `STORYBOOK_ENABLED=true` - zero Storybook code in production
* Portable stories (`composeStories`) reuse CSF files in Jest without duplicating props
* On-device Storybook is the source of truth for RN - web Storybook misses native layout
* Visual regression uses Maestro `takeScreenshot` + baseline diff - no built-in Chromatic for RN yet
* Set `onDeviceUI: false` when capturing screenshots so the Storybook chrome stays out of frame
* Pair stories with contract tests - pixels catch layout drift, schemas catch API drift

## [Contract Tests for APIs](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/contract-tests-for-apis/)

* Contract tests fail in Jest before a bad API response reaches a simulator
* Pact records consumer expectations and verifies providers against shared pact files
* Zod schema tests are lighter - validate fixtures and parsers without a mock server
* Mobile apps are Pact consumers - backends verify they still satisfy published contracts
* Store pact JSON in git or a Pact Broker - never only on a developer laptop
* Pair contracts with MSW in RNTL - same shapes, different test layer

## [Testing Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/best-practices/)

* Follow the pyramid: many unit/component tests, few E2E flows
* Use jest-expo preset and mock native modules at service boundaries
* Query RNTL by role and label - not testID-only
* Prefer Maestro for YAML E2E; Detox when gray-box sync is required
* Contract-test API schemas before store builds
* Run smoke E2E on physical devices in release candidates

Dokumen: Jest Setup for Expo
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/jest-setup-for-expo/

# Jest Setup for Expo

`jest-expo` gives Expo SDK 57 projects a working Jest preset: native modules are mocked, TypeScript transforms are configured, and you can run unit and component tests on every commit without booting a simulator.

Highlights / Jest Setup for Expo

* `jest-expo` preset mocks Expo SDK modules so Jest runs without a simulator
* Install with `npx expo install` so versions match Expo SDK 57
* `transformIgnorePatterns` is the fix when Jest cannot parse ESM in node\_modules
* Keep tests out of `app/` - use `\_\_tests\_\_` or colocated `\*.test.tsx` files
* Snapshots are for small presentational components - not full screens

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
npx expo install jest-expo jest @types/jest @testing-library/react-native test-renderer --dev
```

```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "test": "jest --watchAll",
    "test:ci": "jest --ci --coverage=false"
  },
  "jest": {
    "preset": "jest-expo",
    "transformIgnorePatterns": [
      "node_modules/(?!((jest-)?react-native|@react-native(-community)?)|expo(nent)?|@expo(nent)?/.*|@expo-google-fonts/.*|react-navigation|@react-navigation/.*|@sentry/react-native|native-base|react-native-svg)"
    ],
    "setupFilesAfterEnv": ["<rootDir>/jest.setup.ts"]
  }
}
```

```ts
// jest.setup.ts
import "@testing-library/react-native";
 
afterEach(() => {
  jest.clearAllMocks();
});
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Every Expo app that ships features - run tests in CI before EAS builds.
* Component and hook tests with `@testing-library/react-native` (see [React Native Testing Library](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/react-native-testing-library/)).
* Pure TypeScript utilities (formatters, reducers, API mappers) with no native imports.
* Snapshot tests for small, stable presentational components - not navigation trees.

## Working Example

```bash
# From project root (Expo SDK 57)
npx expo install jest-expo jest @types/jest @testing-library/react-native test-renderer --dev
```

```json
// package.json (excerpt)
{
  "scripts": {
    "test": "jest --watchAll",
    "test:ci": "jest --ci --coverage=false --changedSince=origin/main",
    "test:update-snapshots": "jest -u --coverage=false"
  },
  "jest": {
    "preset": "jest-expo",
    "transformIgnorePatterns": [
      "node_modules/(?!((jest-)?react-native|@react-native(-community)?)|expo(nent)?|@expo(nent)?/.*|@expo-google-fonts/.*|react-navigation|@react-navigation/.*|@sentry/react-native|native-base|react-native-svg)"
    ],
    "setupFilesAfterEnv": ["<rootDir>/jest.setup.ts"],
    "collectCoverageFrom": [
      "**/*.{ts,tsx}",
      "!**/__tests__/**",
      "!**/coverage/**",
      "!**/node_modules/**",
      "!**/.expo/**",
      "!**/expo-env.d.ts"
    ]
  }
}
```

```ts
// jest.setup.ts
import "@testing-library/react-native";
 
// Reset module mocks between tests when you use jest.mock at file scope.
afterEach(() => {
  jest.clearAllMocks();
});
```

```json
// tsconfig.json (excerpt - enables Jest globals in TypeScript)
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "types": ["jest"]
  }
}
```

```tsx
// src/components/greeting.tsx
import { StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
 
export function Greeting({ name }: { name: string }) {
  return (
    <View style={styles.container}>
      <Text accessibilityRole="header">Hello, {name}</Text>
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  container: { padding: 16 },
});
```

```tsx
// __tests__/greeting-test.tsx
import { render, screen } from "@testing-library/react-native";
import { Greeting } from "../src/components/greeting";
 
describe("<Greeting />", () => {
  test("renders the name", () => {
    render(<Greeting name="Alex" />);
    expect(screen.getByRole("header", { name: "Hello, Alex" })).toBeOnTheScreen();
  });
 
  test("matches snapshot for stable markup", () => {
    const { toJSON } = render(<Greeting name="Alex" />);
    expect(toJSON()).toMatchSnapshot();
  });
});
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* `jest-expo` preset - zero custom Babel config for standard Expo projects.
* `transformIgnorePatterns` - transpiles ESM packages Jest would otherwise skip.
* `jest.setup.ts` - imports RNTL once so Jest matchers (`toBeOnTheScreen`) are registered.
* `*-test.tsx` naming - recognized by `jest-expo` without extra `testMatch` config.
* Snapshot on a leaf component - not the whole app shell.

## Deep Dive

### How It Works

* **`jest-expo` preset** extends Jest with Expo-aware transforms, module name mappers, and built-in mocks for most `expo-*` and React Native internals.
* **Test Renderer** (via `@testing-library/react-native`) renders components to a JS tree - no native view hierarchy, no simulator.
* **`transformIgnorePatterns`** tells Jest which `node_modules` packages to run through Babel; without it, imports from `react-native`, `expo-router`, or navigation packages throw syntax errors.
* **`setupFilesAfterEnv`** runs after the test framework installs - ideal for global matchers, mock resets, and shared `jest.mock` setup.
* **Fake timers** in setup are optional; enable per-file when testing `setTimeout`, animations, or debounced search.

### Jest Config at a Glance

| Option | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `preset: "jest-expo"` | Base Expo/RN transform + native mocks |
| `transformIgnorePatterns` | Allow-list ESM packages for Babel |
| `setupFilesAfterEnv` | Global test setup (`jest.setup.ts`) |
| `collectCoverageFrom` | Files included in coverage reports |
| `moduleNameMapper` | Alias `@/` paths (add if using `tsconfig` paths) |

### Module Path Aliases

When `tsconfig.json` maps `@/*` to `./src/*`, mirror it in Jest:

```json
"jest": {
  "preset": "jest-expo",
  "moduleNameMapper": {
    "^@/(.*)$": "<rootDir>/src/$1"
  }
}
```

### Snapshot Discipline

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Snapshot leaf components with stable props | Snapshot entire screens with live data |
| Review snapshot diffs in PRs | Auto-approve snapshot updates without reading |
| Pair snapshots with behavior assertions | Rely on snapshots alone for navigation flows |
| Delete obsolete snapshots when components are removed | Keep thousand-line snapshots "just in case" |

Expo's own docs recommend **Maestro E2E** over snapshot tests for full UI flows - snapshots complement, not replace, integration and E2E coverage.

### TypeScript Notes

```ts
// jest.setup.ts - typed mock helpers for native modules
import "@testing-library/react-native";
 
type ExpoLocationMock = {
  requestForegroundPermissionsAsync: jest.Mock;
  getCurrentPositionAsync: jest.Mock;
};
 
export function getLocationMock(): ExpoLocationMock {
  return jest.requireMock("expo-location") as ExpoLocationMock;
}
```

* Add `"jest"` to `compilerOptions.types` so `describe`, `it`, and `expect` type-check.
* Install `@types/jest` via `expo install` to stay aligned with the SDK's Jest version.
* Prefer `jest.MockedFunction<typeof fn>` over `any` when typing mocked imports.

## Gotchas

* **Tests inside `app/` with Expo Router** - Every file under `app/` must be a route or layout. **Fix:** Put tests in `__tests__/` at the project root or colocate `*.test.tsx` next to `src/components/`.
* **"Cannot use import statement outside a module"** - A dependency ships ESM and Jest skips transpiling it. **Fix:** Add the package to `transformIgnorePatterns` (or use the full Expo-recommended regex above).
* **Forgetting `test-renderer`** - `@testing-library/react-native` depends on the standalone `test-renderer` package (not deprecated `react-test-renderer`). **Fix:** `npx expo install test-renderer --dev`.
* **Matchers like `toBeOnTheScreen` not found** - RNTL extends Jest only after you import from `@testing-library/react-native`. **Fix:** Add `import "@testing-library/react-native"` to `jest.setup.ts`.
* **Snapshots that never fail** - Giant snapshots of screens with timestamps, random IDs, or fetched data create noise. **Fix:** Snapshot presentational components with fixed props; test data-driven UI with queries and assertions.
* **Running `jest` without `jest-expo`** - Plain Jest does not mock `expo-constants`, `expo-font`, or native modules. **Fix:** Always set `"preset": "jest-expo"` in `package.json` or `jest.config.js`.
* **Watch mode in CI** - `--watchAll` hangs CI runners. **Fix:** Use `"test:ci": "jest --ci --coverage=false"` in pipelines and pre-merge checks.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `jest-expo` + Jest | Unit/component tests for Expo apps | You need real native UI synchronization (use Detox or Maestro) |
| Vitest | Shared monorepo already standardized on Vitest for web packages | Expo RN preset and native mocks are Jest-first today |
| Manual `react-native` Jest preset | Bare RN without Expo | You are on Expo SDK - `jest-expo` is the maintained path |
| Maestro / Detox E2E | Full flows, gestures, native chrome | Testing a pure `formatCurrency()` function |

## FAQs

What do I install for Jest on Expo SDK 57?

```bash
npx expo install jest-expo jest @types/jest @testing-library/react-native test-renderer --dev
```

Always use `expo install` for version alignment with SDK 57 - do not pin Jest versions manually from npm.

Where does Jest config live?

* `package.json` under a `"jest"` key is the Expo default and works for most apps.
* A standalone `jest.config.js` is fine for larger teams - still set `preset: "jest-expo"`.
* Do not duplicate config in both places; pick one source of truth.

What file names does jest-expo recognize as tests?

* `*.test.ts`, `*.test.tsx`, `*.spec.ts`, `*.spec.tsx`
* `*-test.ts`, `*-test.tsx` (Expo docs convention)
* Files under `__tests__/` directories

No extra `testMatch` is required with the default preset.

Do I still need react-test-renderer?

No. `react-test-renderer` does not support React 19. Install the standalone `test-renderer` package as a dev dependency alongside `@testing-library/react-native`.

How do I fix transformIgnorePatterns for pnpm or Bun?

pnpm and Bun add store path segments inside `node_modules`. Expo documents alternate regex patterns - copy the variant for your package manager from [Unit testing with Jest](https://docs.expo.dev/develop/unit-testing/) rather than the npm/Yarn regex.

What belongs in jest.setup.ts?

* `import "@testing-library/react-native"` for matchers
* Global `afterEach(() => jest.clearAllMocks())` when using spies
* Shared mocks only if every test file needs them - prefer per-file `jest.mock` for module-specific behavior

Should I enable coverage in CI?

* Turn on `collectCoverage` locally or on main-branch builds first.
* Exclude `app/`, generated types, and `.expo/` via `collectCoverageFrom`.
* Add `coverage/` to `.gitignore` - never commit HTML reports.

Can I test Expo Router screens with this setup?

Yes - after `jest-expo` and RNTL are configured, use `expo-router/testing-library` and `renderRouter`. See [React Native Testing Library](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/react-native-testing-library/) for query patterns; keep test files outside `app/`.

When are snapshots worth it?

* Small components with stable structure (badges, empty states, error banners).
* Not for screens that embed navigation, fetching, or animation state.
* Expo recommends E2E (Maestro) for full UI regression - see [Maestro E2E](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/maestro-e2e/).

How do I run only changed tests?

```json
"test:ci": "jest --ci --coverage=false --changedSince=origin/main"
```

Pair with `--passWithNoTests` on fresh branches if your CI policy allows zero-test PRs.

jest-expo mocks everything - is that enough?

`jest-expo` mocks most Expo modules with safe defaults. Custom native modules, third-party SDKs, and nuanced permission flows need manual mocks. See [Mocking Native Modules](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/mocking-native-modules/).

How do I mock expo-font or expo-splash-screen in setup?

```ts
jest.mock("expo-font", () => ({
  loadAsync: jest.fn(() => Promise.resolve()),
  isLoaded: jest.fn(() => true),
}));
 
jest.mock("expo-splash-screen", () => ({
  preventAutoHideAsync: jest.fn(() => Promise.resolve()),
  hideAsync: jest.fn(() => Promise.resolve()),
}));
```

Place app-wide mocks in `jest.setup.ts`; feature-specific mocks stay in the test file.

What test scripts should package.json expose?

| Script | When |
| --- | --- |
| `test` | Local dev with `--watchAll` |
| `test:ci` | CI - no watch, fail on errors |
| `test:update-snapshots` | Intentional snapshot refresh (`jest -u`) |

Never run watch mode on EAS or GitHub Actions runners.

## Related

* [Mobile Testing Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/mobile-testing-basics/) - unit → component → integration → E2E pyramid
* [React Native Testing Library](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/react-native-testing-library/) - queries, async, and user-centric assertions
* [Mocking Native Modules](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/mocking-native-modules/) - manual mocks beyond `jest-expo` defaults
* [Maestro E2E](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/testing/maestro-e2e/) - YAML flows when Jest is not enough
* [Container/Presenter on Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/component-patterns/container-presenter-on-mobile/) - presenters are ideal Jest + RNTL targets
* [GitHub Actions Integration](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/git/github-actions-integration/) - wire `test:ci` into PR checks

> **Stack versions:** This page was written for **React 19.2.3**, **React Native 0.86.0**, and **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4).
