Dokumen: Crash Spike Triage
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/troubleshooting/crash-spike-triage/

# Crash Spike Triage

A cookbook for **Sentry clustering**, **bisecting releases**, and **sizing user impact** when crash-free sessions drop after a store rollout or OTA publish. Assumes production is wired per [Sentry for React Native](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/observability/sentry-for-react-native/) and release identity per [Observability Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/observability/observability-basics/).

Highlights / Crash Spike Triage

* Cluster by fingerprint and release tags before reading individual stack traces
* Bisect OTA update id vs native build - wrong layer wastes the rollback window
* Crash-free sessions beats raw event count for user impact sizing
* Compare phased rollout % to crash cohort size - small rollout can still be SEV2
* Symbolicated stacks required - unsymbolicated Hermes frames are not triage
* Document suspect update group id in the incident channel within 10 minutes

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```bash
# 1. Confirm spike (Sentry UI or API)
#    Filter: environment=production, last 1h vs 24h baseline
 
# 2. Segment by native release
#    Group by: release (e.g. 2.4.0+240012)
 
# 3. Segment by OTA dist within top release
#    Group by: dist (expo-updates updateId)
 
# 4. Open top issue cluster - note fingerprint + first seen
 
# 5. Correlate with deploy timeline
eas update:list --branch production --limit 5
# App Store Connect: phased release % / Play: staged rollout %
 
# 6. Contain (parallel with triage)
#    Pause rollout / eas update:rollback / kill switch
 
# 7. Size impact
#    crash-free sessions delta × DAU estimate = affected users
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Sentry alert: crash-free sessions dropped >2% absolute vs 7-day baseline
* Support ticket volume for "app closes" correlates with alert window
* Release Health shows new issue fingerprint with steep `first seen` ramp

**When to escalate instead of bisecting:**

* Spike across **all** releases and OTA ids simultaneously → backend or CDN incident
* Native-only SIGABRT with no new OTA → store build rollback path, not channel revert
* Unsymbolicated stacks only → fix source map upload first - see [EAS Build Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/eas-build/eas-build-basics/)

---

## Working Example

A **45-minute triage drill** for a crash spike on production after an OTA publish.

### T+0 - Confirm the spike is real (5 min)

```text
Baseline (7d):  99.4% crash-free sessions
Current (1h):   96.8% crash-free sessions
Delta:          -2.6% absolute  →  exceeds rollback trigger
```

Sentry Release Health filters:

| Filter | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `environment` | `production` |
| `release` | `2.4.0+240012` (latest live native) |
| Time range | Last 1 hour vs previous 24 hours |

* Ignore dev and preview environments in production numerators - see [SLOs for Mobile Apps](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/observability/slos-for-mobile-apps/)
* Compare **sessions**, not raw event count - one loop crash generates hundreds of events

---

### T+5 - Cluster issues (10 min)

Open **Issues** sorted by event volume in the alert window.

```text
Top cluster:
  Fingerprint: checkout-screen-null-ref
  First seen:  2026-07-09 14:02 UTC
  Events:      4,200 (82% of spike)
  Releases:    2.4.0+240012 only
  Dist:        abc123-update-group (single OTA id)
```

Sentry query patterns:

```text
is:unresolved release:2.4.0+240012 dist:abc123-update-group
```

| Cluster pattern | Interpretation |
| --- | --- |
| One fingerprint, one `dist` | Bad OTA bundle - rollback channel |
| One fingerprint, all `dist` on one `release` | Native regression in that binary |
| Many fingerprints, one `dist` | Bad OTA with multiple bugs - still rollback |
| Many fingerprints, all releases | Backend, config, or third-party SDK outage |

* **Breadcrumbs** on the top event: last navigation route, API failures, flag state
* If fingerprint is `NativeModule` / `SIGABRT`, skip OTA bisect - open native war room

---

### T+15 - Bisect releases (10 min)

Timeline on a whiteboard or incident doc:

```markdown
| UTC Time | Event |
|----------|-------|
| 13:45 | Backend deploy v892 - no mobile change |
| 14:02 | eas update --channel production (group abc123) |
| 14:05 | Sentry alert fired |
| 14:08 | iOS phased at 25% - build 240012 |
```

**Bisect decision tree:**

```text
Crash only on dist abc123?
  YES → Suspect OTA. eas update:view abc123. Rollback per OTA Emergency Rollback.
  NO  → Crash on all dist values for release 2.4.0+240012?
          YES → Suspect native binary. Pause phased release. Hotfix build.
          NO  → Crash on multiple native releases?
                  YES → Backend / shared dependency. Engage API on-call.
```

```bash
# OTA bisect
eas update:list --branch production --limit 5
eas update:view <suspect-group-id>
 
# Git bisect (after identifying suspect SHA)
git log --oneline <last-good-sha>..<suspect-sha> -- app/ src/
```

* `eas update:list` timestamp should precede Sentry `first seen` by minutes (OTA propagation)
* Store rollout % alone does not explain OTA-only dist clustering

---

### T+25 - Size user impact (5 min)

```ts
// Rough impact estimate for IC / exec comms
type ImpactEstimate = {
  crashFreeDelta: number;      // e.g. -0.026 (99.4% → 96.8%)
  sessionsLastHour: number;  // from Sentry Release Health
  dau: number;               // from analytics
};
 
function estimateAffectedUsers(e: ImpactEstimate): number {
  const crashedSessions = e.sessionsLastHour * e.crashFreeDelta;
  // Scale to DAU if spike is sustained - conservative for exec comms
  return Math.round(Math.min(crashedSessions, e.dau * e.crashFreeDelta));
}
```

| Input | Source |
| --- | --- |
| `crashFreeDelta` | Sentry Release Health |
| `sessionsLastHour` | Sentry Release Health |
| Phased rollout % | App Store Connect / Play Console - [Phased Release & Rollback](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/store-operations/phased-release-and-rollback/) |
| OTA adoption % | Analytics tag `otaUpdateId` cohort size |

**Example comms line for IC:**

```text
~2.6% session crash rate on production; top cluster affects checkout on OTA abc123.
iOS phased at 25% (~40k users). Containment: OTA rollback in progress.
```

* Under-reporting beats exaggerating - give ranges ("tens of thousands") if analytics lags
* Payment route crashes use revenue metrics, not just crash-free rate

---

### T+30 - Contain while triage finishes (parallel)

| Finding | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Single bad OTA `dist` | [OTA Emergency Rollback](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/troubleshooting/ota-emergency-rollback/) |
| Bad native build | Pause phased / halt staged; flag off |
| Isolated feature | Remote kill switch first |
| Backend correlation | Page API team; mobile holds rollouts |

```bash
eas update:rollback
eas channel:view production
```

Monitor 60 minutes post-containment - crash-free should recover toward baseline. If not, second cluster or wrong layer - re-bisect.

---

## Sentry Configuration for Triage

Ensure these are set at init - otherwise bisect fails silently:

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx
import * as Sentry from "@sentry/react-native";
import * as Application from "expo-application";
import * as Updates from "expo-updates";
 
Sentry.init({
  dsn: process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN,
  release: `${Application.nativeApplicationVersion}+${Application.nativeBuildVersion}`,
  dist: Updates.updateId ?? Application.nativeBuildVersion ?? "embedded",
  environment: process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_APP_ENV,
  enableAutoSessionTracking: true,
});
```

| Tag | Purpose in triage |
| --- | --- |
| `release` | Native build bisect |
| `dist` | OTA bundle bisect |
| `environment` | Exclude preview from production alerts |
| `transaction` / route | Screen-level clustering |

* Upload source maps on every EAS production build - unsymbolicated stacks block fingerprint accuracy
* Tag [Staged Rollouts](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/staged-rollouts/) cohorts during percentage OTA publishes

---

## Common Triage Mistakes

| Mistake | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| Chasing every event individually | Sort by fingerprint; top 3 clusters usually explain >90% |
| Rolling back OTA for native SIGABRT | Check issue platform and stack - native frames skip JS rollback |
| Ignoring phased rollout % | 5% rollout × high crash rate still hits revenue if checkout |
| No `dist` tag | Wire `Updates.updateId` before next incident |
| Declaring victory at 30 min | Watch Release Health for 60 min - slow OTA adoption masks recovery |

---

## FAQs

How do I cluster in Sentry during an incident?

Issues → sort by Events in time window → open top issue → check **First Seen**, **Releases**, and **Dist** distribution. Use Discover queries to group by `dist` when the Issues UI is noisy. Same fingerprint = same root cause candidate.

OTA rollback did not fix crashes - now what?

Re-check `dist` on incoming events - if `dist` unchanged, clients have not picked up rollback yet (wait or force reload policy). If `dist` changed but crashes persist, suspect native layer or second bug. Re-cluster from T+0.

What rollback trigger should we use?

Common mobile thresholds: crash-free -2% absolute, payment success -1% absolute, auth errors +3% relative. Define in [SLOs for Mobile Apps](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/observability/slos-for-mobile-apps/) and [Rollback Runbook](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/rollback-runbook/) before launch.

## Related

* [Sentry for React Native](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/observability/sentry-for-react-native/) - init, source maps, release health
* [Observability Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/observability/best-practices/) - tag every signal
* [OTA Emergency Rollback](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/troubleshooting/ota-emergency-rollback/) - channel revert under pressure
* [Rollback Runbook](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/rollback-runbook/) - full OTA rollback playbook

Dokumen: Mobile Incident Basics
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/troubleshooting/mobile-incident-basics/

# Mobile Incident Basics

Ten examples for **severity levels**, **comms channels**, and a **first-15-minutes checklist** - the foundation every Expo SDK 57 on-call rotation needs before a crash spike, bad OTA, or store delisting. Pair with [Observability Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/observability/observability-basics/) for signal taxonomy and [Rollback Runbook](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/ota-updates/rollback-runbook/) for OTA containment.

Highlights / Mobile Incident Basics

* Mobile incidents need a single incident commander - not parallel Slack threads
* Severity ties to user impact and revenue path - not how loud the alert is
* First 15 minutes: confirm scope, contain blast radius, assign roles
* Tag every signal with release, OTA update id, and channel before triage
* Containment beats root cause in minute zero - pause rollout, flip flags, rollback OTA
* Runbooks live in the repo next to the code - not buried in Slack search

## Prerequisites

Your team should already ship with release identity on every crash and log - see [Sentry for React Native](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/observability/sentry-for-react-native/). These examples assume **EAS Update** channels and **Sentry Release Health** are wired for production.

> **Tooling:** These examples target **Expo SDK 57** (`expo` ~57.0.4), **React Native 0.86.0**, and **React 19.2.3**.

---

## Basic Examples

### 1. Define Mobile Severity Levels

Web-style P1/P2 labels fail on mobile because **store adoption**, **OTA propagation**, and **offline users** stretch blast radius. Use impact-based severity:

```ts
// docs/incident-severity.ts - copy into your runbook repo
export type IncidentSeverity = "SEV1" | "SEV2" | "SEV3" | "SEV4";
 
export type SeverityCriteria = {
  sev: IncidentSeverity;
  userImpact: string;
  revenuePath: boolean;
  example: string;
};
 
export const MOBILE_SEVERITY_MATRIX: SeverityCriteria[] = [
  {
    sev: "SEV1",
    userImpact: "App unusable for majority OR removed from store OR data breach",
    revenuePath: true,
    example: "Play suspension; auth down for all users on live build",
  },
  {
    sev: "SEV2",
    userImpact: "Critical path broken for >25% of active users",
    revenuePath: true,
    example: "Checkout crash on iOS 2.4.0 phased release",
  },
  {
    sev: "SEV3",
    userImpact: "Regression with workaround; partial rollout or single platform",
    revenuePath: false,
    example: "Settings tab crash on Android preview channel",
  },
  {
    sev: "SEV4",
    userImpact: "Internal-only, policy warning, or sub-threshold metric drift",
    revenuePath: false,
    example: "Sentry noise on dev profile; App Store metadata deadline",
  },
];
```

* **SEV1** pages exec, legal, and comms - not just engineering
* **SEV2** is the default production crash spike with payment or auth involvement
* **SEV3** can wait for business hours if a kill switch exists
* Re-evaluate severity every 30 minutes - OTA propagation can escalate SEV3 → SEV2 quickly

---

### 2. Incident Commander and Roles

One person decides; everyone else executes. Parallel Slack threads without an IC waste the first 15 minutes.

```markdown
## Role assignment (paste into #incident-YYYYMMDD)
 
| Role | Owner | Responsibility |
|------|-------|----------------|
| **Incident Commander (IC)** | @oncall-mobile | Severity, timeline, go/no-go on rollback |
| **Tech Lead** | @mobile-lead | Triage, bisect, hotfix branch |
| **Comms** | @support-lead | Status page, support macros, social |
| **Scribe** | volunteer | Decision log with timestamps |
| **Store Ops** | @release-mgr | Pause phased release, Play halt - [Store Incident Response](../store-operations/store-incident-response.md) |
```

* IC does **not** need to be the best debugger - they need authority to pause releases
* Scribe captures: decision, who approved, UTC timestamp, link to dashboard snapshot
* Rotate IC after 4 hours on SEV1 - fatigue causes bad rollback calls

---

### 3. Comms Channels (Internal vs External)

Mobile incidents span engineering, support, executives, and app store status. Separate channels by audience:

```markdown
## Comms map
 
| Channel | Audience | Content rules |
|---------|----------|---------------|
| `#incident-YYYYMMDD` | Engineering + IC | Technical facts, commands run, hypotheses |
| `#incident-comms` | Support + PM + Comms | Approved customer-facing language only |
| PagerDuty / Opsgenie | On-call | Alert → acknowledge → join incident channel |
| Status page | Customers | No root cause until confirmed; no blame |
| Exec email | C-suite | Business impact, ETA range, what we are doing now |
```

```text
# Internal (engineering) - OK
Suspect OTA group abc123 published 14:02 UTC. Crash-free dropped 99.4% → 96.1%.
Running eas channel:view production. IC: @jane.
 
# External (status page) - OK
We are investigating reports of ShopApp closing unexpectedly on some devices.
Next update in 30 minutes or sooner.
 
# External - NEVER
Caused by @bob's deploy. Rolling back now.
```

* Engineering channel is noisy - that's fine; comms channel is curated
* Support macros must match status page wording - mismatched messages create ticket storms
* For store delisting, legal owns external copy - see [Store Outage & Policy Incident](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/troubleshooting/store-outage-and-policy-incident/)

---

### 4. First-15-Minutes Checklist

Containment before root cause. This checklist fits on one screen:

```markdown
## T+0 to T+15 (mobile production)
 
- [ ] **Acknowledge** alert; IC assigned (single name in channel topic)
- [ ] **Confirm scope:** platform(s), build number, OTA update id, channel, % users
- [ ] **Correlate timing:** OTA publish, store rollout %, backend deploy, feature flag change
- [ ] **Contain blast radius:**
  - [ ] Pause iOS phased release / halt Play staged rollout
  - [ ] Flip remote kill switch for suspected surface
  - [ ] Start OTA rollback if JS bundle suspect - [OTA Emergency Rollback](./ota-emergency-rollback.md)
- [ ] **Open dashboards:** Sentry Release Health, payment success, auth errors, OTA apply rate
- [ ] **Notify** comms + exec if SEV1/SEV2
- [ ] **Do not** merge hotfix to main until IC confirms containment path
```

```bash
# Scope confirmation commands (run in parallel)
eas channel:view production
eas update:list --branch production --limit 3
# Sentry: filter by release + dist (OTA update id)
```

* If you cannot name the **OTA update id** or **build number** in 5 minutes, observability gaps are the incident - fix tagging first
* Containment at T+10 beats perfect RCA at T+45

---

### 5. Correlate Release, OTA, and Backend

Mobile spikes often look like backend outages until you segment by client version.

```ts
// Log at session start - support and incidents depend on this
import * as Application from "expo-application";
import * as Updates from "expo-updates";
 
export function getIncidentCorrelationTags() {
  return {
    nativeRelease: `${Application.nativeApplicationVersion}+${Application.nativeBuildVersion}`,
    otaUpdateId: Updates.updateId ?? "embedded",
    channel: Updates.channel ?? "none",
    runtimeVersion: Updates.runtimeVersion ?? "unknown",
  };
}
```

| Signal shift pattern | Likely layer |
| --- | --- |
| Spike only on one `otaUpdateId` | Bad OTA - rollback channel |
| Spike on one `nativeRelease` only | Bad store build - pause rollout |
| All versions, all platforms | Backend or third-party API |
| Spike after flag change | Remote config - revert flag |

* [Observability Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/observability/best-practices/) - tag every report with release identity
* [SLOs for Mobile Apps](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/observability/slos-for-mobile-apps/) - define rollback triggers before launch week

---

### 6. Containment Levers by Layer

Know which lever fixes which failure - wrong lever wastes hours.

| Layer | Containment lever | Time to effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Remote config / flags** | Disable feature in LaunchDarkly / Firebase | Seconds–minutes |
| **OTA (JS bundle)** | `eas update:rollback` on channel | 5–15 minutes |
| **Store rollout** | Pause phased / halt staged % | Minutes |
| **Backend** | Roll back API deploy, circuit breaker | Minutes |
| **Native binary** | New `eas build` + expedited review | Hours–days |

```bash
# OTA containment (JS regression)
eas update:rollback
eas channel:view production
```

* OTA cannot fix native SIGABRT - do not burn 30 minutes on channel revert for a native-only crash
* Feature flags first when logic is isolated; OTA rollback when bundle-wide regression

---

### 7. Incident Channel Hygiene

Structured updates reduce duplicate work and prevent IC from re-answering the same question.

```text
## Status template (post every 15–30 min)
 
**SEV:** SEV2
**IC:** @jane
**Impact:** Checkout crash on iOS build 240012 (~18% phased users)
**Containment:** Phased release paused; flag `newCheckout` off
**Next:** Bisect OTA vs native - see Crash Spike Triage
**ETA:** Next update 15:45 UTC
```

* Pin the latest status message in the incident channel
* Link to Sentry issue cluster URL - not screenshots of stack traces
* `@channel` only for severity changes or containment confirmation - not every hypothesis

---

### 8. When to Page Exec and Legal

Not every crash warrants CEO email. Use explicit triggers:

```markdown
## Exec / legal notification triggers
 
| Trigger | Notify |
|---------|--------|
| App removed from App Store or Play | Exec + Legal immediately (SEV1) |
| PII exposure or regulatory breach allegation | Legal immediately |
| Payment success down >5% abs for >15 min | Exec + Finance |
| Auth down >25% users | Exec |
| SEV3 optional feature crash | Engineering only |
```

* Exec updates need **business impact** and **customer-facing status** - not stack traces
* Legal reviews any customer email about data incidents before send

---

### 9. Handoff to Deeper Runbooks

The first 15 minutes route to specialized playbooks - don't improvise under pressure.

| Symptom | Next runbook |
| --- | --- |
| Crash-free rate cliff after OTA | [Crash Spike Triage](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/troubleshooting/crash-spike-triage/) |
| Need channel revert now | [OTA Emergency Rollback](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/troubleshooting/ota-emergency-rollback/) |
| `eas build` failing on release cut | [Native Build Failure War Room](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/troubleshooting/native-build-failure-war-room/) |
| Store removal or policy strike | [Store Outage & Policy Incident](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/troubleshooting/store-outage-and-policy-incident/) |
| Incident resolved | [Post-Mortem Template for Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/troubleshooting/post-mortem-template-for-mobile/) |

---

### 10. Post-Incident Minimum (Same Day)

Before the team disperses, capture enough for tomorrow's post-mortem:

```markdown
## Same-day capture (scribe owns)
 
- [ ] Incident start/end UTC
- [ ] Final severity
- [ ] Affected releases: native builds + OTA ids
- [ ] Containment actions with timestamps
- [ ] Customer-visible duration
- [ ] Link to Sentry cluster / EAS update group
- [ ] Schedule post-mortem within 5 business days (SEV1/SEV2)
```

* "We'll write it up later" loses decision rationale - scribe notes beat memory
* Blameless post-mortems still require factual timelines - see [Post-Mortem Template for Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/troubleshooting/post-mortem-template-for-mobile/)

---

## FAQs

Who should be Incident Commander?

The on-call mobile engineer or release manager with authority to pause store rollouts and approve OTA rollback. IC does not need to be the person who wrote the buggy code - they need decision authority and calm under alert noise.

Is a crash spike always SEV2?

No. A spike on an optional tab affecting <1% of sessions with a kill switch available may be SEV3. Payment or auth regression on the live production build is SEV2 or SEV1 depending on scope. Use the severity matrix in Example 1, not alert volume alone.

What if we cannot tell OTA from native?

Filter Sentry by `dist` (OTA update id) and `release` (native version+build). If crashes span all OTA ids on one native build, suspect native. If isolated to one update id, suspect JS bundle. See [Crash Spike Triage](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/troubleshooting/crash-spike-triage/).

Dokumen: TypeScript in RN Best Practices
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/typescript-rn/best-practices/

# TypeScript in RN Best Practices

A condensed summary of the 25 most important best practices drawn from every page in this section.

Highlights / TypeScript in RN Best Practices

* Extend expo/tsconfig.base and enable strict incrementally in brownfield apps
* Use discriminated unions instead of optional fields per variant
* Validate fetch responses with Zod at the network boundary
* Type styles as StyleProp<ViewStyle>, not bare ViewStyle
* Enable experiments.typedRoutes and regenerate .expo/types in CI
* Wrap native modules with requireNativeModule<T> and runtime parsers

1. **Extend `expo/tsconfig.base`:** Expo SDK 57 projects should start from the official base config - it includes the right `jsx`, module resolution, and paths for Metro and native module typings.
2. **Turn on `strict` for greenfield screens:** New `.tsx` files should compile under full strictness from day one; brownfield apps phase flags in module by module instead of flipping everything at once.
3. **Name every component's props:** Export a `ComponentNameProps` interface (or type) beside the component - inline object types do not scale across refactors and Storybook stories.
4. **Prefer discriminated unions for variants:** Model `{ variant: "a"; aField: string } | { variant: "b"; bField: number }` instead of optional fields on every branch - TypeScript narrows correctly inside each case.
5. **Avoid `React.FC` in new code:** Type the function parameter directly - `React.FC` adds implicit `children` noise and is deprecated idiomatically in React 19 projects.
6. **Reuse RN prop types with `ComponentProps`:** Extend primitives via `ComponentProps<typeof Pressable>` and `Omit` only the keys you replace - hand-rolled prop lists drift when RN adds accessibility or platform props.
7. **Type press handlers from `PressableProps`:** Use `PressableProps["onPress"]` instead of hand-writing `GestureResponderEvent` signatures that may miss optional parameters.
8. **Push generics to list components:** Declare `FlatList<Place>` and `SectionList<Place>` at the list boundary - casting `data as Place[]` inside shared lists hides caller mistakes.
9. **Use `readonly T[]` for display props:** Prevent callers from mutating arrays you render - props are a contract, not a mutable shared buffer.
10. **Enable Expo Router typed routes:** Set `experiments.typedRoutes: true` in `app.config` and include `.expo/types/**/*.ts` so `Href` and `router.push` catch invalid paths at compile time.
11. **Regenerate route types in CI:** Run `npx expo customize tsconfig.json` before `tsc --noEmit` - without generated types, every `href` degrades to `string`.
12. **Pass dynamic routes as object hrefs:** Use `{ pathname: "/user/[id]", params: { id } }` - string literals like `"/user/[id]"` fail typed-route checks because params are missing.
13. **Match bracket names exactly:** A file `[id].tsx` requires `params: { id }`, not `{ userId }` - param keys must mirror the filesystem segment.
14. **Validate URL params with Zod:** Typed routes prove path shape, not value safety - parse `useLocalSearchParams` output before using IDs in fetch calls.
15. **Treat `fetch` JSON as `unknown`:** `res.json()` does not validate - assign to `unknown`, then `Schema.parse(data)`; never `as MyInterface` at the boundary.
16. **Model API envelopes explicitly:** Parse `{ items, nextCursor }` wrappers, not bare arrays - backends add pagination fields without a major version bump.
17. **Use `.nullable()` for SQL nulls:** Backend `avatarUrl: null` fails `.optional()` schemas - distinguish absent keys (optional) from present nulls (nullable).
18. **Coerce numbers at the boundary:** Gateways sometimes stringify numeric fields - `z.coerce.number()` belongs in the Zod schema, not repeated `Number()` calls in screens.
19. **Type styles as `StyleProp<ViewStyle>`:** Callers need to pass style arrays and falsy guards - bare `ViewStyle` rejects `[styles.base, pressed && styles.active]`.
20. **Use `PressableProps["style"]` for pressable wrappers:** Pressable styles can be functions of `pressed` state - narrowing to `ViewStyle` breaks the callback form.
21. **Wrap native modules with typed `requireNativeModule`:** Declare a `NativeModule` interface and parse async returns with Zod - JSI bindings can still return unexpected shapes across OS versions.
22. **Use `requireOptionalNativeModule` in Expo Go paths:** Modules missing from Expo Go should degrade gracefully - optional require plus feature flags beats try/catch around every call.
23. **Phase strictness in brownfield apps:** Enable `noImplicitAny`, then `strictNullChecks`, then `strict` - one flag per sprint keeps PRs reviewable.
24. **Prefer `@ts-expect-error` over `@ts-ignore`:** Expect-error fails when the underlying mistake is fixed - ignore comments linger and hide real regressions.
25. **Typecheck in CI separately from lint:** Run `tsc --noEmit` on every PR - ESLint does not catch invalid route hrefs, Zod mismatches, or broken generic inference.

## FAQs

Is strict TypeScript worth it on a two-person Expo team?

* Yes for new files - strict catches null crashes and bad API shapes before they reach TestFlight.
* Brownfield repos can enable strict per folder rather than blocking a release on a thousand legacy errors.

Should I use Zod on every API call?

* At minimum on responses that drive navigation or billing - high-impact boundaries.
* Internal constants and static config can stay TypeScript-only without runtime parsers.

Do typed Expo Router routes replace Zod for params?

* No - typed routes validate path structure at compile time.
* Zod still validates runtime values (UUID format, enum tabs, numeric limits).

What is the fastest win for style typing?

* Replace every `style?: ViewStyle` prop with `style?: StyleProp<ViewStyle>` in shared components.
* Most style-related TS errors in RN codebases come from this single mismatch.

How do I type a wrapper around Pressable without losing ripple props?

* Start from `ComponentProps<typeof Pressable>`, omit `children` if you rename it, and spread `...pressableProps` last only when callers should override defaults.

Can I skip types on native module bridges?

* Only if the module is throwaway prototype code.
* Production bridges need typed surfaces - untyped native returns are the top source of silent production crashes after OS upgrades.

Should `.expo/types` be committed?

* No - regenerate in dev and CI with `expo customize tsconfig.json`.
* Committing generated route types creates merge conflicts on every folder rename.

What strict flag hurts brownfield apps the most?

* `strictNullChecks` - it surfaces the most real bugs but also the most legacy noise.
* Enable it after `noImplicitAny` on new modules first.

## Related

* [TypeScript in RN Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/typescript-rn/typescript-in-rn-basics/) - strict tsconfig and introductory typed examples
* [Typing Components & Props](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/typescript-rn/typing-components-and-props/) - unions, generics, and prop contracts
* [Typing Navigation & Route Params](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/typescript-rn/typing-navigation-and-route-params/) - Expo Router params and validation

Dokumen: Expo Router Typed Routes
Sumber: https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/typescript-rn/expo-router-typed-routes/

# Expo Router Typed Routes

Expo Router can generate TypeScript types from your `app/` file tree. When typed routes are enabled, `href` strings, `router.push` calls, and param hooks are checked against real routes - so a renamed screen file becomes a compile error instead of a runtime 404.

Highlights / Expo Router Typed Routes

* Enable `experiments.typedRoutes` in app config - default Expo Router templates on SDK 57 often ship with this already on
* Expo CLI regenerates route types when `npx expo start` runs - output lands in `.expo/types` and `expo-env.d.ts`
* `Href` autocomplete catches typos in `<Link href>` and `router.push` at compile time
* Dynamic routes require object hrefs with strictly typed `params` - string templates alone are not enough
* Run `npx expo customize tsconfig.json` on CI so typecheck works without starting Metro

## Recipe

> Quick-reference recipe card - copy-paste ready.

```json
// app.json - enable typed routes (beta; required on older scaffolds)
{
  "expo": {
    "experiments": {
      "typedRoutes": true
    }
  }
}
```

```bash
# Regenerate route types and tsconfig includes
npx expo customize tsconfig.json
npx expo start
```

```tsx
import { Link, router } from "expo-router";
 
// Autocomplete and compile-time validation
<Link href="/settings" />
router.push("/settings");
```

**When to reach for this:**

* Multi-screen Expo Router apps where broken links should fail in CI, not on a device.
* Teams that rename, move, or group routes frequently with `(tabs)` and `(auth)` segments.
* Dynamic segments like `app/user/[id].tsx` where param keys must match the file name.
* Imperative navigation (`router.push`, `router.replace`) shared across hooks and deep links.
* Monorepos that typecheck mobile without starting the Metro dev server.

## Working Example

Assume this file tree:

```
app/
  _layout.tsx
  index.tsx
  settings.tsx
  user/
    [id].tsx
```

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx
import { Stack } from "expo-router";
 
export default function RootLayout() {
  return (
    <Stack>
      <Stack.Screen name="index" options={{ title: "Home" }} />
      <Stack.Screen name="settings" options={{ title: "Settings" }} />
      <Stack.Screen name="user/[id]" options={{ title: "User" }} />
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// app/index.tsx - declarative links with generated Href types
import { View, Text, StyleSheet } from "react-native";
import { Link, router } from "expo-router";
 
export default function HomeScreen() {
  return (
    <View style={styles.screen}>
      <Text style={styles.title}>Home</Text>
 
      <Link href="/settings" style={styles.link}>
        Settings
      </Link>
 
      <Text
        style={styles.link}
        onPress={() => router.push({ pathname: "/user/[id]", params: { id: "42" } })}
      >
        User 42
      </Text>
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  screen: { flex: 1, padding: 24, gap: 12 },
  title: { fontSize: 22, fontWeight: "600" },
  link: { color: "#2563eb", fontSize: 16 },
});
```

```tsx
// app/user/[id].tsx - strongly typed params from the route path
import { View, Text, StyleSheet } from "react-native";
import { useLocalSearchParams } from "expo-router";
 
export default function UserScreen() {
  const { id } = useLocalSearchParams<"/user/[id]">();
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.screen}>
      <Text style={styles.title}>User {id}</Text>
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  screen: { flex: 1, padding: 24 },
  title: { fontSize: 22, fontWeight: "600" },
});
```

```json
// tsconfig.json - after `npx expo customize tsconfig.json`
{
  "extends": "expo/tsconfig.base",
  "compilerOptions": { "strict": true },
  "include": [
    "**/*.ts",
    "**/*.tsx",
    ".expo/types/**/*.ts",
    "expo-env.d.ts"
  ]
}
```

**What this demonstrates:**

* Static routes (`/settings`) autocomplete and reject typos like `/setings`.
* Dynamic routes use **object hrefs** with `pathname` and strictly typed `params`.
* `useLocalSearchParams<"/user/[id]">()` ties param names to the file-based segment.
* `tsconfig.json` includes `.expo/types` and `expo-env.d.ts` so `tsc --noEmit` sees generated types.
* Both `<Link href>` and `router.push` share the same generated `Href` union.

## Deep Dive

### How It Works

* **Metro + Expo CLI** scan the `app/` directory (or `src/app/` when using a top-level `src` layout) and build a route manifest.
* With `experiments.typedRoutes: true`, CLI writes generated declarations into **`.expo/types`** and a git-ignored **`expo-env.d.ts`** at the project root.
* The global **`Href`** type (and exported **`Route`**) represent every valid path in the project.
* `<Link href>`, `router.push`, `router.replace`, and `useRouter()` consume `Href` - invalid strings error in the IDE.
* Types refresh when the dev server starts; they are **not** committed to git by default.

### Setup Checklist

| Step | Command / file | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Enable experiment | `app.json` → `expo.experiments.typedRoutes: true` | Default Router templates on SDK 57 may already set this |
| tsconfig includes | `npx expo customize tsconfig.json` | Adds `.expo/types/**/*.ts` and `expo-env.d.ts` |
| Generate types | `npx expo start` (or customize on CI) | First run creates `expo-env.d.ts` and updates `.gitignore` |
| CI typecheck | `npx expo customize tsconfig.json && npx tsc --noEmit` | No Metro required for generation |
| Do not edit | `expo-env.d.ts` | Auto-generated; stays gitignored |

### Static vs Dynamic Hrefs

```tsx
import { Link } from "expo-router";
 
// Static - string href
<Link href="/settings" />
 
// Dynamic - object href with params matching the file segment name
<Link href={{ pathname: "/user/[id]", params: { id: userId } }} />
 
// Template strings work when the expression is typed as Href
const id = "42";
<Link href={`/user/${id}` as const} />
```

| Form | Supported | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"/settings"` | Yes | Static segments |
| `{ pathname: "/user/[id]", params: { id } }` | Yes | Required for dynamic segments |
| `"/user/[id]"` (string only) | No | Type error - params missing |
| `"./settings"` (relative) | No | Use absolute paths or `useSegments()` |

### Query Parameters

Query params are not in the file system - type them manually:

```tsx
import { useLocalSearchParams } from "expo-router";
 
// Query only
const { q } = useLocalSearchParams<{ q?: string }>();
 
// Route + query - first generic is the route, second is query shape
const { id, tab } = useLocalSearchParams<"/user/[id]", { tab?: "posts" | "about" }>();
```

### Relative Navigation with useSegments

Typed routes require absolute hrefs. Build tab-relative paths from the current segments:

```tsx
import { Link, useSegments } from "expo-router";
 
export function ProfileTabLink() {
  const [group] = useSegments(); // e.g. "(tabs)" or "(auth)"
  return <Link href={`/${group}/profile`}>Profile</Link>;
}
```

### TypeScript Notes

```tsx
import { type Href, type Route } from "expo-router";
 
// Href - valid navigation targets
const settings: Href = "/settings";
 
// Route - matches any valid route string in the project
const route: Route = "/user/123";
 
// Typed segments for a specific layout branch
import { useSegments } from "expo-router";
const segments = useSegments<"/(tabs)/profile">();
```

* Generated types apply in **`.tsx` files** - plain `.ts` modules may not get `Href` autocomplete unless they import the types explicitly.
* After moving or renaming route files, restart `expo start` if the IDE shows stale autocomplete.
* `expo-env.d.ts` also augments React Native Web types (e.g. `className` on `View`) when typed routes are enabled.

## Gotchas

* **Skipping `npx expo customize tsconfig.json`** - `tsc --noEmit` in CI cannot see `.expo/types` and every `href` becomes `string`. **Fix:** Run customize in CI before typecheck.
* **String href to dynamic routes** - `href="/user/[id]"` typechecks as invalid because `id` is missing. **Fix:** Use `{ pathname: "/user/[id]", params: { id } }`.
* **Wrong param key names** - File is `[id].tsx` but params use `{ userId: "1" }`. **Fix:** Param keys must match bracket segment names exactly.
* **Committing `expo-env.d.ts`** - It is regenerated per machine and clutters diffs. **Fix:** Leave it gitignored; regenerate in CI with `expo customize`.
* **Removing `.expo/types` from tsconfig** - Autocomplete silently breaks; invalid routes compile. **Fix:** Keep both `.expo/types/**/*.ts` and `expo-env.d.ts` in `include`.
* **Relative `./` hrefs** - Typed routes do not support relative paths. **Fix:** Absolute paths or `useSegments()`-built paths.
* **Stale types after a big route refactor** - IDE still suggests deleted routes. **Fix:** Restart the dev server; run `npx expo customize tsconfig.json` if `include` paths changed.

## Alternatives

| Alternative | Use When | Don't Use When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Generated typed routes (`experiments.typedRoutes`) | Expo Router file-based apps on SDK 57 | Plain React Navigation without Expo Router |
| Manual `href` union type | Tiny apps with 3–4 static routes | Apps with dynamic segments and route groups |
| `useLocalSearchParams<MyParams>()` only | Quick param typing without enabling the experiment | You also need link `href` validation across the codebase |
| Runtime param validation (Zod) | Params arrive from deep links / push notifications | You want compile-time link checking - use both together |
| React Navigation typed navigators | Brownfield apps on `@react-navigation/native` | Greenfield Expo Router projects with file-based routing |

## FAQs

How do I enable typed routes in Expo SDK 57?

* Set `"experiments": { "typedRoutes": true }` under `"expo"` in `app.json` or `app.config.js`.
* Run `npx expo customize tsconfig.json` and start the dev server once.
* Default `create-expo-app` Router templates often enable this already - verify `app.json` before changing.

Where are generated route types stored?

* `.expo/types/**/*.ts` - route manifest types.
* `expo-env.d.ts` at the project root - global augmentations (gitignored).
* Both are listed in `tsconfig.json` `include` after customization.

Why does CI typecheck fail without starting Metro?

* Types are generated by Expo CLI, not Metro alone.
* Run `npx expo customize tsconfig.json` on CI before `npx tsc --noEmit`.
* Commit the updated `tsconfig.json` - not `expo-env.d.ts`.

What is the difference between Href and Route?

* `Href` - targets you can pass to `<Link href>` and `router.push`.
* `Route` - broader union of valid route strings in the project.
* Both are generated from your `app/` directory structure.

How do I link to a dynamic route?

```tsx
<Link href={{ pathname: "/user/[id]", params: { id: "42" } }} />
```

* Use an object with `pathname` matching the file (`[id]` segment).
* `params` keys must match bracket names in the file path.

Can I use template strings for href?

```tsx
const id = "42";
router.push(`/user/${id}`);
```

* Works when TypeScript can verify the result is a valid `Href`.
* Cast with `as Href` only when you have already validated `id` (e.g. with Zod).

How do I type query parameters?

* Query params are not generated from the file tree.
* Pass a manual generic: `useLocalSearchParams<{ ref?: string }>()`.
* Combine route + query with two generics on `useLocalSearchParams`.

Do relative paths like ./settings work?

* No - typed routes require absolute paths.
* Use `useSegments()` to prefix the current tab or group segment.

Does typed routes work with a src/app directory?

* Yes - Expo Router supports a top-level `src/app` layout.
* Generation follows the same rules; types update when the dev server runs.

What happens if I edit expo-env.d.ts by hand?

* The next `expo start` overwrites your changes.
* Do not commit the file - treat it as a build artifact.

Do I still need Zod for route params?

* Typed routes catch invalid **links** at compile time.
* Deep links and push notifications can still deliver malformed param values at runtime.
* Pair generated types with Zod validation on the screen boundary for external entry points.

How do I type useRouter and router.push?

```tsx
import { useRouter } from "expo-router";
 
const router = useRouter();
router.push("/settings");
router.replace({ pathname: "/user/[id]", params: { id: "1" } });
```

* `useRouter()` returns a typed router when the experiment is enabled.
* The standalone `router` import from `expo-router` is also typed.

Typed routes broke after I renamed a route file - what now?

* Restart `npx expo start` to regenerate types.
* Fix compile errors - they point at stale `href` strings still using the old path.
* Run `npx tsc --noEmit` to find every callsite.

# TypeScript in RN Highlights Summary

Every highlight bullet from the 9 pages in this section, gathered on one page and grouped by the page it came from.

Highlights / TypeScript in RN Highlights Summary

* Extend `expo/tsconfig.base` and keep `strict: true` - Expo scaffolds already ship this layout
* Props interfaces document the public contract - keep them narrow and explicit
* Enable experiments.typedRoutes so Expo CLI generates Href and Route types
* Native module JS proxies default to loose types - declare contracts at the wrapper layer
* Treat every `res.json()` as `unknown` until a Zod schema parses it - compile-time types alone do not survive the wire
* `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` accepts a single style, an array, or falsy entries - match what RN components already accept

## [TypeScript in RN Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/typescript-rn/typescript-in-rn-basics/)

* Extend `expo/tsconfig.base` and keep `strict: true` - Expo scaffolds already ship this layout
* Name prop interfaces `ComponentNameProps`; avoid `React.FC` because it adds implicit `children`
* Use `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` when a component accepts style overrides or style arrays
* Type route params at the screen boundary - untyped `useLocalSearchParams()` hides missing keys
* Treat API JSON as `unknown` until Zod validates it; `z.infer` keeps runtime and compile-time in sync
* `Pick`, `Omit`, and `ComponentProps` derive shapes from one source instead of duplicate interfaces

## [Typing Components & Props](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/typescript-rn/typing-components-and-props/)

* Props interfaces document the public contract - keep them narrow and explicit
* Discriminated unions model variant components without optional-prop soup
* Generic components preserve item types through lists and render props
* Extend ViewProps or PressableProps instead of re-declaring layout props
* Omit and Pick build reusable base contracts shared across a design system
* React 19 function components infer children from props - type them when you restrict layout

## [Typing Navigation & Route Params](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/typescript-rn/typing-navigation-and-route-params/)

* Enable experiments.typedRoutes so Expo CLI generates Href and Route types
* Dynamic segments require Href objects with a params map - string paths alone fail
* Pass the route literal to useLocalSearchParams for strongly typed path params
* Query strings are not inferred from the file tree - type them with a second generic
* URL params arrive as strings - validate and coerce at the screen boundary
* Zod parse at the trust boundary catches deep links and stale bookmarks

## [Typing Native Module APIs](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/typescript-rn/typing-native-module-apis/)

* Native module JS proxies default to loose types - declare contracts at the wrapper layer
* requireNativeModule<T> attaches a TypeScript surface to JSI host objects
* Treat every native return as unknown until parsed - same trust model as fetch().json()
* Zod at the boundary converts NSDictionary/Bundle payloads into narrow TS types
* EventEmitter listeners receive untyped payloads - validate in the subscription callback
* Legacy NativeModules remain in brownfield code - wrap and deprecate behind typed facades

## [Typing API Responses & Zod](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/typescript-rn/typing-api-responses-and-zod/)

* Treat every `res.json()` as `unknown` until a Zod schema parses it - compile-time types alone do not survive the wire
* `z.infer<typeof Schema>` is the single source of truth for both runtime checks and TypeScript exports
* Use `safeParse` at UI boundaries and `parse` in trusted fetch helpers where you want exceptions to bubble
* Compose schemas with `.extend`, `.pick`, and `z.discriminatedUnion` so list and detail endpoints share field definitions
* Pair validated fetch helpers with TanStack Query so every screen reuses the same typed `queryFn`

## [Utility Types for RN](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/typescript-rn/utility-types-for-rn/)

* `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` accepts a single style, an array, or falsy entries - match what RN components already accept
* `ComponentProps<typeof Pressable>` forwards every native prop without maintaining a hand-written list
* Use `Omit` to replace `children` or `style` when your wrapper exposes a narrower API
* `PressableProps['style']` captures the function-style callback Pressable allows - do not narrow to `ViewStyle` alone
* Derive event types from handler props (`ComponentProps<typeof TextInput>['onChangeText']`) instead of guessing signatures

## [Expo Router Typed Routes](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/typescript-rn/expo-router-typed-routes/)

* Enable `experiments.typedRoutes` in app config - default Expo Router templates on SDK 57 often ship with this already on
* Expo CLI regenerates route types when `npx expo start` runs - output lands in `.expo/types` and `expo-env.d.ts`
* `Href` autocomplete catches typos in `<Link href>` and `router.push` at compile time
* Dynamic routes require object hrefs with strictly typed `params` - string templates alone are not enough
* Run `npx expo customize tsconfig.json` on CI so typecheck works without starting Metro

## [Gradual Typing in Brownfield Apps](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/typescript-rn/gradual-typing-in-brownfield-apps/)

* Rename `.js` → `.ts` / `.tsx` file by file - `allowJs: true` lets JS and TS coexist during migration
* Enable `strictNullChecks` first; it catches the most real mobile bugs (undefined params, missing API fields)
* Use `// @ts-expect-error` with a ticket comment - it fails the build when the underlying error is fixed
* Type boundaries (API clients, navigation params, native bridges) before leaf UI files
* Track progress with `tsc --noEmit` error count per folder - shrink the blast radius sprint over sprint

## [TypeScript in RN Best Practices](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/typescript-rn/best-practices/)

* Extend expo/tsconfig.base and enable strict incrementally in brownfield apps
* Use discriminated unions instead of optional fields per variant
* Validate fetch responses with Zod at the network boundary
* Type styles as StyleProp<ViewStyle>, not bare ViewStyle
* Enable experiments.typedRoutes and regenerate .expo/types in CI
* Wrap native modules with requireNativeModule<T> and runtime parsers

# TypeScript in RN Basics

10 examples to get you started with TypeScript in RN - 7 basic and 3 intermediate.

Highlights / TypeScript in RN Basics

* Extend `expo/tsconfig.base` and keep `strict: true` - Expo scaffolds already ship this layout
* Name prop interfaces `ComponentNameProps`; avoid `React.FC` because it adds implicit `children`
* Use `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` when a component accepts style overrides or style arrays
* Type route params at the screen boundary - untyped `useLocalSearchParams()` hides missing keys
* Treat API JSON as `unknown` until Zod validates it; `z.infer` keeps runtime and compile-time in sync
* `Pick`, `Omit`, and `ComponentProps` derive shapes from one source instead of duplicate interfaces

## Prerequisites

Expo projects scaffold with TypeScript by default. Start from the blank TypeScript template so `tsconfig.json`, Metro, and the SDK pin are already aligned.

```bash
npx create-expo-app@latest MyTypedApp --template blank-typescript
cd MyTypedApp
```

Confirm the SDK and React pins in `package.json`:

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "expo": "~57.0.4",
    "react": "19.2.3",
    "react-native": "0.86.0"
  }
}
```

Conventions used throughout:

1. Every React Native screen file is `.tsx`. Plain `.ts` is for schemas, API clients, and shared types.
2. `strict: true` in `tsconfig.json` - the default when you extend Expo's base config.
3. Import types from `react-native` (`StyleProp`, `ViewStyle`, `GestureResponderEvent`) instead of redeclaring them.

> **Tooling:** Run `npx tsc --noEmit` in CI to catch type errors before a native build. Pair it with ESLint's `@typescript-eslint` rules for unused variables and unsafe `any`.

---

## Basic Examples

### 1. Strict tsconfig for Expo

Extend Expo's published base config instead of hand-rolling compiler options that drift from the SDK.

```json
{
  "extends": "expo/tsconfig.base",
  "compilerOptions": {
    "strict": true
  },
  "include": ["**/*.ts", "**/*.tsx", ".expo/types/**/*.ts", "expo-env.d.ts"]
}
```

* `expo/tsconfig.base` ships with Expo SDK 57 and already sets `jsx`, `moduleResolution`, and paths Metro expects
* `strict: true` enables `strictNullChecks`, `noImplicitAny`, and related flags - catch `undefined` route params and untyped API payloads early
* The `.expo/types/**/*.ts` include picks up **generated route types** when typed routes are enabled
* Do not disable `strict` to silence errors - fix the boundary (props, params, fetch) or add a narrow escape hatch with a comment

> **Related:** [Gradual Typing in Brownfield Apps](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/typescript-rn/gradual-typing-in-brownfield-apps/) - tightening strictness without blocking feature work | [Expo Router Typed Routes](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/typescript-rn/expo-router-typed-routes/) - generated types land in `.expo/types`

---

### 2. Typing Component Props

Define the shape of a component's props as a TypeScript interface and destructure in the parameter list.

```tsx
import { View, Text, StyleSheet } from "react-native";
 
interface ProfileHeaderProps {
  name: string;
  subtitle: string;
}
 
function ProfileHeader({ name, subtitle }: ProfileHeaderProps) {
  return (
    <View style={styles.header}>
      <Text style={styles.name}>{name}</Text>
      <Text style={styles.subtitle}>{subtitle}</Text>
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  header: { padding: 16, alignItems: "center" },
  name: { fontSize: 20, fontWeight: "600" },
  subtitle: { fontSize: 14, color: "#6b7280", marginTop: 4 },
});
```

* Name the interface `<ComponentName>Props` - easy to find with search and safe to extend later
* Prefer **`interface`** for component props; declaration merging makes extending straightforward
* Never use `React.FC` - it adds an implicit `children` prop you often do not want and is falling out of favor in 2026
* Export the props interface when the component lives in a design system - consumers can `extends` or `Pick` from it

> **Related:** [Typing Components & Props](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/typescript-rn/typing-components-and-props/) - generics, discriminated unions, and reusable prop contracts

---

### 3. Optional Props and Union Literals

Mark props optional with `?`, then supply defaults in the destructure so callers can omit them safely.

```tsx
import { Pressable, Text, StyleSheet } from "react-native";
 
interface ActionButtonProps {
  label: string;
  variant?: "primary" | "secondary";
  disabled?: boolean;
  onPress: () => void;
}
 
function ActionButton({
  label,
  variant = "primary",
  disabled = false,
  onPress,
}: ActionButtonProps) {
  return (
    <Pressable
      style={[styles.base, variant === "primary" ? styles.primary : styles.secondary]}
      disabled={disabled}
      onPress={onPress}
    >
      <Text style={styles.label}>{label}</Text>
    </Pressable>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  base: { paddingHorizontal: 20, paddingVertical: 12, borderRadius: 8 },
  primary: { backgroundColor: "#2563eb" },
  secondary: { backgroundColor: "#e5e7eb" },
  label: { fontWeight: "600", color: "#fff" },
});
```

* `variant?: ...` makes the prop optional; TypeScript adds `undefined` to its type
* Default values in the destructure (`variant = "primary"`) fill in when the caller omits the prop
* A **union literal type** (`"primary" | "secondary"`) restricts callers to valid options - autocomplete works in the editor
* Do not use `defaultProps` - it is deprecated for function components in React 19

> **Related:** [Typing Components & Props](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/typescript-rn/typing-components-and-props/) - variant props and discriminated unions for mode-specific fields

---

### 4. StyleProp for Reusable Style Props

When a component accepts a `style` override, type it with `StyleProp` so callers can pass a single object or an array.

```tsx
import { View, Text, StyleSheet, type StyleProp, type ViewStyle } from "react-native";
 
interface CardProps {
  title: string;
  style?: StyleProp<ViewStyle>;
}
 
function Card({ title, style }: CardProps) {
  return (
    <View style={[styles.card, style]}>
      <Text style={styles.title}>{title}</Text>
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  card: {
    margin: 16,
    padding: 20,
    borderRadius: 12,
    backgroundColor: "#fff",
  },
  title: { fontSize: 18, fontWeight: "600" },
});
 
// Usage - single object or array both type-check
// <Card title="Hello" style={{ marginTop: 24 }} />
// <Card title="Hello" style={[styles.card, isActive && styles.active]} />
```

* `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` accepts a style object, an array of styles, `false`, or `undefined` - matching how RN merges style arrays
* Use `TextStyle` and `ImageStyle` for text and image wrappers respectively; do not reuse `ViewStyle` on `Text`
* Merge with `[styles.card, style]` so the caller's override wins without replacing your base layout
* For `Pressable`, type `style` as `StyleProp<ViewStyle> | ((state) => StyleProp<ViewStyle>)` when you need pressed-state styling

> **Related:** [Utility Types for RN](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/typescript-rn/utility-types-for-rn/) - `StyleProp`, `ComponentProps`, and style-safe helpers | [Styling Basics](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/styling-layout/styling-basics/) - `StyleSheet.create` and the RN styling model

---

### 5. Typing useState

Let inference do the work, and add an explicit generic when the initial value does not carry the full type.

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { View, Text, ActivityIndicator, StyleSheet } from "react-native";
 
interface User {
  id: string;
  name: string;
}
 
export default function UserPanel() {
  const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
  const [user, setUser] = useState<User | null>(null);
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false);
 
  if (loading) {
    return <ActivityIndicator style={styles.centered} />;
  }
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.centered}>
      <Text>Count: {count}</Text>
      <Text>{user?.name ?? "No user loaded"}</Text>
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  centered: { flex: 1, justifyContent: "center", alignItems: "center" },
});
```

* Skip the generic when `useState(initial)` has enough info - `useState(0)` is already `number`
* Supply `useState<User | null>(null)` when the value could later be richer - otherwise TypeScript pins it to `null`
* Unions like `User | null` make the "not loaded yet" state explicit - consumers must narrow before using fields
* Do **not** store derived values in state; compute during render from simpler state

> **Related:** [Props, State & Re-renders on Mobile](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/rn-fundamentals/props-state-and-re-renders-on-mobile/) - when state updates trigger native re-renders

---

### 6. Typing Pressable Handlers

Use React Native's exported event types so handler parameters stay typed without `any`.

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import {
  Pressable,
  Text,
  StyleSheet,
  type GestureResponderEvent,
} from "react-native";
 
export default function LikeButton() {
  const [liked, setLiked] = useState(false);
 
  const handlePress = (event: GestureResponderEvent) => {
    setLiked((prev) => !prev);
    console.log("pressed at", event.nativeEvent.pageX, event.nativeEvent.pageY);
  };
 
  return (
    <Pressable
      style={({ pressed }) => [styles.button, pressed && styles.pressed]}
      onPress={handlePress}
    >
      <Text style={styles.label}>{liked ? "Liked" : "Like"}</Text>
    </Pressable>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  button: { padding: 12, borderRadius: 8, backgroundColor: "#2563eb" },
  pressed: { opacity: 0.85 },
  label: { color: "#fff", fontWeight: "600" },
});
```

* `GestureResponderEvent` is the standard type for `onPress`, `onPressIn`, and `onPressOut` on `Pressable` and `TouchableOpacity`
* Read touch coordinates from `event.nativeEvent` - the shape is stable across iOS and Android
* If you keep the handler inline, you can skip the annotation - TypeScript infers it from `onPress`'s signature
* For long-press menus, type `onLongPress` the same way; for `TextInput`, use `NativeSyntheticEvent<TextInputChangeEventData>`

> **Related:** [Typing Components & Props](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/typescript-rn/typing-components-and-props/) - callback props and event handler contracts

---

### 7. Utility Types (Pick, Omit, Partial)

Derive new types from existing ones instead of writing duplicate interfaces that drift.

```ts
interface Device {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  platform: "ios" | "android";
  lastSeenAt: string;
}
 
type DeviceSummary = Pick<Device, "id" | "name">;
type NewDevice = Omit<Device, "id" | "lastSeenAt">;
type DevicePatch = Partial<Omit<Device, "id">>;
```

* `Pick<T, K>` keeps only the listed keys; `Omit<T, K>` removes them - compose both to express API shapes
* `Partial<T>` makes every property optional; handy for PATCH endpoints and form drafts
* `Required<T>` and `Readonly<T>` round out the most-used utilities for immutable config objects
* Changing the source interface automatically flows through - no hand-synced duplicates across screens

> **Related:** [Utility Types for RN](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/typescript-rn/utility-types-for-rn/) - `ComponentProps`, `StyleProp`, and RN-specific helpers

## Intermediate Examples

### 8. Typed Route Params with Expo Router

Type search params at the screen boundary so missing or mistyped keys fail at compile time.

```tsx
import { View, Text, StyleSheet } from "react-native";
import { useLocalSearchParams } from "expo-router";
 
type ProductParams = {
  id: string;
  preview?: string;
};
 
export default function ProductScreen() {
  const { id, preview } = useLocalSearchParams<ProductParams>();
 
  return (
    <View style={styles.screen}>
      <Text style={styles.title}>Product {id}</Text>
      {preview ? <Text style={styles.badge}>Preview mode</Text> : null}
    </View>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  screen: { flex: 1, padding: 24 },
  title: { fontSize: 22, fontWeight: "600" },
  badge: { marginTop: 8, color: "#2563eb" },
});
```

* `useLocalSearchParams<Params>()` types the return value - optional keys use `?` in the params type
* Params arrive as **strings** from the URL; parse numbers with `Number(id)` or validate with Zod before use
* For dynamic segments like `app/product/[id].tsx`, keep param names aligned with the file name (`id` matches `[id]`)
* Prefer **generated typed routes** (`experiments.typedRoutes` in `app.json`) for links that stay in sync with the file tree

> **Related:** [Typing Navigation & Route Params](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/typescript-rn/typing-navigation-and-route-params/) - React Navigation stacks and param validation | [Expo Router Typed Routes](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/typescript-rn/expo-router-typed-routes/) - generated `Href` types and keeping them current

---

### 9. Typed fetch with Zod

Guarantee at runtime that API responses match the TypeScript type you ship to screens.

```ts
import { z } from "zod";
 
const UserSchema = z.object({
  id: z.string(),
  name: z.string(),
  email: z.string().email(),
});
 
type User = z.infer<typeof UserSchema>;
 
async function fetchUser(id: string): Promise<User> {
  const res = await fetch(`https://api.example.com/users/${id}`);
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);
  const json: unknown = await res.json();
  return UserSchema.parse(json);
}
```

* Typing a response as `Promise<User>` is a **lie** if you never validate - mobile APIs change without warning
* A Zod schema validates at runtime **and** infers the TypeScript type, so there is only one thing to maintain
* Treat the raw response as `unknown` until it passes the schema - no accidental `any` leaking into UI components
* On slow networks, pair validated fetch helpers with TanStack Query so every screen shares the same typed `queryFn`

> **Related:** [Typing API Responses & Zod](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/typescript-rn/typing-api-responses-and-zod/) - error shapes, schema composition, and offline caches

---

### 10. ComponentProps for Extending RN Primitives

Reuse a built-in component's prop surface when wrapping `Pressable`, `Text`, or `TextInput`.

```tsx
import {
  Pressable,
  Text,
  StyleSheet,
  type ComponentProps,
} from "react-native";
 
type PressableProps = ComponentProps<typeof Pressable>;
 
interface LinkButtonProps extends Omit<PressableProps, "children"> {
  label: string;
}
 
function LinkButton({ label, style, ...pressableProps }: LinkButtonProps) {
  return (
    <Pressable style={[styles.link, style]} {...pressableProps}>
      <Text style={styles.label}>{label}</Text>
    </Pressable>
  );
}
 
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  link: { paddingVertical: 8 },
  label: { color: "#2563eb", fontWeight: "600" },
});
```

* `ComponentProps<typeof Pressable>` captures every prop `Pressable` accepts - `onPress`, `disabled`, `accessibilityRole`, and more
* `Omit<..., "children">` removes props you replace with your own API (`label` instead of free-form `children`)
* Spread `...pressableProps` last so callers can override defaults without re-listing every RN prop
* The same pattern works for `TextInput`, `ScrollView`, and third-party components that forward refs

> **Related:** [Utility Types for RN](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/typescript-rn/utility-types-for-rn/) - `ComponentProps`, `StyleProp`, and composition patterns | [Typing Native Module APIs](https://docs.wahwei/reactnative.codeguides.io/typescript-rn/typing-native-module-apis/) - bridging untyped native returns into safe TS boundaries
